      x = q * padicNorm p q * distToNearestInt (q * ξ)} = 0

statements.name: Bugeaud08.problem_10_8.variants.quadratic
statements.doc:
The quadratic case of Problem 10.8. de Mathan and Teulié [dMT04] solved the
$p$-adic Littlewood conjecture for quadratic real numbers.
statements.statement:
theorem problem_10_8.variants.quadratic (ξ : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime)
    (hξ : (minpoly ℚ ξ).natDegree = 2) :
    sInf {x : ℝ | ∃ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q ∧
      x = q * padicNorm p q * distToNearestInt (q * ξ)} = 0

statements.name: Bugeaud08.problem_10_8.variants.exceptional_set_dimH_zero
statements.doc:
The exceptional set for Problem 10.8 has Hausdorff dimension zero (Einsiedler
and Kleinbock [EK07].
statements.statement:
theorem problem_10_8.variants.exceptional_set_dimH_zero (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    dimH {ξ : ℝ | Filter.atTop.liminf
      (fun q : ℕ ↦ q * padicNorm p q * distToNearestInt (q * ξ)) ≠ 0} = 0

problems.title: Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Mahler's Z-numbers
problems.doc:
See also FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/Mahler32.lean.

*References:*
  - [Bug12] Bugeaud, Yann. "Distribution modulo one and Diophantine approximation."
    Vol. 193. Cambridge University Press, 2012. Chapter 10.
  - [Mah68] Mahler, Kurt. "An unsolved problem on the powers of 3/2."
    Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society 8.2 (1968): 313-321.
  - [FLP95] Flatto, Leopold, Jeffrey C. Lagarias, and Andrew D. Pollington.
    "On the range of fractional parts $\{\xi(p/q)^n\}$."
    Acta Arithmetica 70.2 (1995): 125-147.

statements.name: Bugeaud09.problem_10_9
statements.doc:
Problem 10.9. There are no real numbers $\xi$ such that $0 \le \{\xi (3/2)^n\} < 1/2$
for every positive integer $n$, i.e. no Z-number exists. Posed by Mahler [Mah68].
statements.statement: theorem problem_10_9 : type_of% Mahler32.mahler_conjecture

statements.name: Bugeaud09.problem_10_9.variants.measure_zero
statements.doc: Mahler [Mah68] proved that the set of Z-numbers has Lebesgue measure zero.
statements.statement:
theorem problem_10_9.variants.measure_zero :
    MeasureTheory.volume {ξ : ℝ | IsZNumber ξ} = 0

statements.name: Bugeaud09.problem_10_9.variants.dimH_lt_one
statements.doc:
Flatto, Lagarias, and Pollington [FLP95] proved that the set of Z-numbers has
Hausdorff dimension strictly less than $1$.
statements.statement:
theorem problem_10_9.variants.dimH_lt_one :
    dimH {ξ : ℝ | IsZNumber ξ} < 1

problems.title: Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Automatic Expansions in Two Bases
problems.doc:
Problem 10.32 asks whether some irrational real number has automatic expansions in two
multiplicatively independent bases. The answer is no. Adamczewski and Faverjon [AF20] proved
it with the multivariate Mahler method, in a form that is stronger than the question asked:
the base-$b$ digit sequence may be $k$-automatic for an arbitrary $k \ge 2$, not only for
$k = b$.

The definitions used here are in `FormalConjecturesForMathlib`:
`Nat.MultiplicativelyIndependent` and `Nat.MultiplicativelyIndependentFamily`,
`AutomaticSequence.IsAutomatic`, `AutomaticSequence.IsAutomaticInBase` and
`AutomaticSequence.IsBroadlyAutomaticInBase`.

*References:*
  - [AF20](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.08283) Adamczewski, Boris, and Colin Faverjon.
    "Mahler's method in several variables and finite automata." arXiv:2012.08283 (2020).
    Appendix A, Conjectures A.2 and A.3, both proved there from Part (i) of Theorem 1.1.
  - [AS03] Allouche, Jean-Paul, and Jeffrey Shallit. "Automatic Sequences: Theory,
    Applications, Generalizations." Cambridge University Press, 2003. Chapter 13,
    Open Problems 7, p. 403, is the problem that Problem 10.32 modifies.
  - [Bug12] Bugeaud, Yann. "Distribution modulo one and Diophantine approximation."
    Vol. 193. Cambridge University Press, 2012. Chapter 10.
  - [Cob69] Cobham, Alan. "On the base-dependence of sets of numbers recognizable by finite
    automata." Mathematical Systems Theory 3 (1969): 186-192.
  - [LvdP82] Loxton, John H., and Alfred J. van der Poorten. "Arithmetic properties of the
    solutions of a class of functional equations." Journal für die reine und angewandte
    Mathematik 330 (1982): 159-172. Its transcendence method was the first attack on the
    problem; Nishioka later reported a gap in its main proof.

statements.name: Bugeaud32.adamczewski_faverjon
statements.doc:
**Adamczewski–Faverjon** [AF20, Conjecture A.3], proved there from Part (i) of Theorem 1.1.
Let $b_1, \dots, b_r$ be multiplicatively independent positive integers, and for every $i$ let
$\xi_i$ be a real number that is automatic in base $b_i$. Then $\xi_1, \dots, \xi_r$ are
algebraically independent over $\mathbb{Q}$, unless one of them is rational.

Two points of fidelity. The hypothesis is the *joint* multiplicative independence of
$b_1, \dots, b_r$ that [AF20] defines on p. 3 (no nonzero integer tuple $(n_i)$ has
$\prod_i b_i^{n_i} = 1$), not the weaker pairwise condition; it is what the proof feeds to
Part (i) of Theorem 1.1, via the multiplicative independence of $1/b_1, \dots, 1/b_r$.
Automaticity is the broad notion that the proof of Conjecture A.3 uses: the base-$b_i$ digits
of $\xi_i$ are $k$-automatic for some $k \ge 2$, which need not be $b_i$.
statements.statement:
theorem adamczewski_faverjon {r : ℕ} (b : Fin r → ℕ) (hb : ∀ i, 2 ≤ b i)
    (hind : Nat.MultiplicativelyIndependentFamily b)
    (ξ : Fin r → ℝ) (hauto : ∀ i, IsBroadlyAutomaticInBase (b i) (ξ i))
    (hirr : ∀ i, Irrational (ξ i)) :
    AlgebraicIndependent ℚ ξ

statements.name: Bugeaud32.problem_10_32.variants.strong
statements.doc:
Problem 10.32, strong form. No irrational real number is automatic in two multiplicatively
independent bases, in the broad sense that its digit sequence in each of the two bases is
`k`-automatic for some `k`. This is [AF20, Conjecture A.2], with the broad notion of
automaticity that its proof provides.
statements.statement:
theorem problem_10_32.variants.strong (ξ : ℝ) (hξ : Irrational ξ) (b₁ b₂ : ℕ)
    (hb₁ : 2 ≤ b₁) (hb₂ : 2 ≤ b₂) (hind : Nat.MultiplicativelyIndependent b₁ b₂)
    (h₁ : IsBroadlyAutomaticInBase b₁ ξ) (h₂ : IsBroadlyAutomaticInBase b₂ ξ) : False

statements.name: Bugeaud32.problem_10_32
statements.doc:
Problem 10.32. Is there an irrational real number whose expansions in two multiplicatively
independent bases can both be generated by a finite automaton? The answer is no, by [AF20].
statements.statement:
theorem problem_10_32 :
    ¬ ∃ ξ : ℝ, Irrational ξ ∧ ∃ b₁ b₂ : ℕ, 2 ≤ b₁ ∧ 2 ≤ b₂ ∧
      Nat.MultiplicativelyIndependent b₁ b₂ ∧
      IsAutomaticInBase b₁ ξ ∧ IsAutomaticInBase b₂ ξ

problems.title: Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Simultaneously Small Entropies
problems.doc:
A real number can be described by its continued fraction expansion and by its expansion in an
integer base. Problem 10.53 asks for an irrational number for which both descriptions have small
block complexity. Temur [Tem26] answered it, in the stronger form that asks for every base at
once, by an explicit construction.

*References:*
  - [Bug12] Bugeaud, Yann. "Distribution modulo one and Diophantine approximation."
    Vol. 193. Cambridge University Press, 2012. Chapter 10.
  - [Tem26](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16362) Temur, Faruk. "Simultaneously small continued
    fraction entropy and base $b$ entropy." arXiv preprint arXiv:2609.16362 (2026).
  - [BBFKW10] Broderick, Ryan, Yann Bugeaud, Lior Fishman, Dmitry Kleinbock, and Barak Weiss.
    "Schmidt's game, fractals, and numbers normal to no base."
    Mathematical Research Letters 17.2 (2010): 307-321.

statements.name: Bugeaud53.problem_10_53
statements.doc:
Problem 10.53. There is an irrational real number $\xi$ such that $E(\xi) < \log 2$ and
$E(\xi, b) < \log b$ for some integer $b \ge 2$. Answered by Temur [Tem26].
statements.statement:
theorem problem_10_53 :
    ∃ ξ : ℝ, Irrational ξ ∧ cfEntropy ξ < (Real.log 2 : EReal) ∧
      ∃ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b ∧ baseEntropy b ξ < (Real.log b : EReal)

statements.name: Bugeaud53.problem_10_53.variants.all_bases
statements.doc:
Problem 10.53, in the stronger form that asks for every base at once: there is an irrational
real number $\xi$ such that $E(\xi) < \log 2$ and $E(\xi, b) < \log b$ for every integer
$b \ge 2$. Answered by Temur [Tem26].
statements.statement:
theorem problem_10_53.variants.all_bases :
    ∃ ξ : ℝ, Irrational ξ ∧ cfEntropy ξ < (Real.log 2 : EReal) ∧
      ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → baseEntropy b ξ < (Real.log b : EReal)

statements.name: Bugeaud53.problem_10_53.variants.uncountable
statements.doc:
There are uncountably many numbers as in Problem 10.53. This follows from a result of Broderick,
Bugeaud, Fishman, Kleinbock and Weiss [BBFKW10] applied to the Gauss-Cantor set
$\{[0; 1, a_1, 1, a_2, \ldots] : a_j \in \{1, 2\}\}$, as observed in [Tem26].
statements.statement:
theorem problem_10_53.variants.uncountable :
    ¬ {ξ : ℝ | Irrational ξ ∧ cfEntropy ξ < (Real.log 2 : EReal) ∧
      ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → baseEntropy b ξ < (Real.log b : EReal)}.Countable

statements.name: Bugeaud53.problem_10_53.variants.temur
statements.doc:
Temur [Tem26], Theorem 1. There is an irrational $\xi \in (0, 1)$ all of whose partial quotients
are $1$ or $2$, such that
$$\lVert b^k \xi \rVert > 154^{-2^b} \quad (b \ge 2,\ k \ge 0),$$
where $\lVert \cdot \rVert$ denotes the distance to the nearest integer. The bound on the partial
quotients gives $E(\xi) \le (\log 2) / 4$, and the displayed inequality forces the base $b$
expansion of $\xi$ to omit a block of zeros, which gives $E(\xi, b) < \log b$ for every
$b \ge 2$. Temur's $\xi$ is moreover computable.
statements.statement:
theorem problem_10_53.variants.temur :
    ∃ ξ : ℝ, Irrational ξ ∧ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, partQuot ξ n = 1 ∨ partQuot ξ n = 2) ∧
      (∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → ∀ k : ℕ,
        (154 : ℝ) ^ (-(2 ^ b) : ℤ) < distToNearestInt ((b : ℝ) ^ k * ξ)) ∧
      cfEntropy ξ ≤ ((Real.log 2 / 4 : ℝ) : EReal) ∧
      ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → baseEntropy b ξ < (Real.log b : EReal)

problems.title: Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Pisot orbits on the Cantor set
problems.doc:
Problem 10.61, proposed by Mendès France [MF67, Problème 1, p. 41]. For a Pisot number
$\alpha > 2$ put
$$C(\alpha) = \left\{ (\alpha - 1) \sum_{k \ge 1} \varepsilon_k \alpha^{-k} :
\varepsilon_k \in \{0, 1\} \right\}.$$
The problem asks to prove that $(\xi \alpha^n)_{n \ge 1}$ is not uniformly distributed
modulo one for any $\xi \in C(\alpha)$. In the language of [MF67] this reads
$C(\alpha) \cap B(\alpha) = \emptyset$, where $B(\alpha)$ is the set of $\xi$ for which
$(\xi \alpha^n)$ is uniformly distributed modulo one.

The problem is open. It is easy for an integer base and settled for two quadratic
$\alpha$; the general Pisot case is what remains. [Ste26] reduces it to a statement about
shift-invariant measures of the full two-shift, and proves that every true instance admits
a finite certificate, so the difficulty is uniformity in $\alpha$ rather than any single
$\alpha$. The variants below state the criterion and the instances of [Ste26] that concern
Problem 10.61 directly; the reduction itself is not stated here, since it needs the symbolic
model.

Deleting the term $n = 0$ does not change uniform distribution modulo one, so the
statements indexed from $n = 1$ agree with the ones of [Ste26], which are indexed from
$n = 0$. Where an orbit is confined away from an interval the stronger form, for every
$n \ge 0$, is stated.

*References:*
  - [Bug12] Bugeaud, Yann. "Distribution modulo one and Diophantine approximation."
    Vol. 193. Cambridge University Press, 2012. Chapter 10, Problem 10.61, p. 222.
  - [MF67] Mendès France, Michel. "Nombres normaux. Applications aux fonctions
    pseudo-aléatoires." Journal d'Analyse Mathématique 20 (1967): 1-56.
  - [Kok35] Koksma, Jurjen F. "Ein mengentheoretischer Satz über die Gleichverteilung
    modulo Eins." Compositio Mathematica 2 (1935): 250-258.
  - [Ste26] Stephan, Ralf. "Criteria for the non-equidistribution of $(\xi \alpha^n)$ on
    the Cantor set $C(\alpha)$." Preprint, 2026.
    https://doi.org/10.13140/RG.2.2.13923.52001

statements.name: Bugeaud61.problem_10_61
statements.doc:
Problem 10.61. Let $\alpha > 2$ be a Pisot number. For every $\xi \in C(\alpha)$ the
sequence $(\xi \alpha^n)_{n \ge 1}$ is not uniformly distributed modulo one.
statements.statement:
theorem problem_10_61 (α : ℝ) (hα : IsPisot α) (hα2 : 2 < α) :
    ∀ ξ ∈ pisotCantorSet α, ¬ IsEquidistributedModuloOne fun n : ℕ => ξ * α ^ (n + 1)

statements.name: Bugeaud61.problem_10_61.variants.almost_every
statements.doc:
The hypothesis $\xi \in C(\alpha)$ cannot be dropped: by Koksma's metric theorem [Kok35],
for a fixed $\alpha > 1$ the sequence $(\xi \alpha^n)_{n \ge 1}$ is uniformly distributed
modulo one for Lebesgue-almost every $\xi$. Problem 10.61 asks a null set of starting
points to defeat an almost-everywhere law.
statements.statement:
theorem problem_10_61.variants.almost_every (α : ℝ) (hα : 1 < α) :
    ∀ᵐ ξ ∂(MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ),
      IsEquidistributedModuloOne fun n : ℕ => ξ * α ^ (n + 1)

statements.name: Bugeaud61.problem_10_61.variants.covering_criterion
statements.doc:
The covering criterion, [Ste26, Theorem C(i)], at a quadratic setup: $\alpha > 1$ is a root
of $X^2 - aX - b$ whose conjugate $\beta = a - \alpha$ is non-zero of modulus less than
one. If the Route A exponent $A(\alpha)$ formed from $\alpha$ and $\rho = |\beta|$ is
below $1$, then Problem 10.61 holds at $\alpha$.

[Ste26] states the criterion for a Pisot number of any degree $d \ge 2$, but proves it only
in this degree-two case.
statements.statement:
theorem problem_10_61.variants.covering_criterion {a b : ℤ} {α : ℝ}
    (hroot : α ^ 2 = a * α + b) (hα : 1 < α) (hβ : (a : ℝ) - α ≠ 0)
    (hconj : |(a : ℝ) - α| < 1) (hA : routeAExponent α |(a : ℝ) - α| < 1) :
    ∀ ξ ∈ pisotCantorSet α, ¬ IsEquidistributedModuloOne fun n : ℕ => ξ * α ^ (n + 1)

statements.name: Bugeaud61.problem_10_61.variants.covering_criterion_range
statements.doc:
The exact range of the covering criterion, [Ste26, Theorem C(ii)]: at a quadratic setup of
norm $-b$ one has $A(\alpha) < 1$ if and only if
$(\log_2 \alpha - 1)(\log_2(\alpha / |b|) - 1) > 1$, which for units reads $\alpha > 4$.
The criterion therefore never reaches the slice $2 < \alpha \le 4$, and says nothing about
a quadratic $\alpha$ with $A(\alpha) \ge 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem problem_10_61.variants.covering_criterion_range {a b : ℤ} {α : ℝ}
    (hroot : α ^ 2 = a * α + b) (hα : 1 < α) (hconj : |(a : ℝ) - α| < 1) (hb : b ≠ 0) :
    routeAExponent α |(a : ℝ) - α| < 1 ↔
      1 < (Real.logb 2 α - 1) * (Real.logb 2 α - Real.logb 2 |(b : ℝ)| - 1)

statements.name: Bugeaud61.problem_10_61.variants.two_add_sqrt_five
statements.doc:
[Ste26, Theorem D] at $\alpha = 2 + \sqrt 5$, the smallest $\alpha$ the covering criterion
reaches: Problem 10.61 holds there in the strong form. There is one open interval
$J \subseteq (0, 1)$, the same for every $\xi \in C(\alpha)$ and every $n \ge 0$, that
$\{\xi \alpha^n\}$ misses.
statements.statement:
theorem problem_10_61.variants.two_add_sqrt_five :
    ∃ x r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ Set.Ioo (x - r) (x + r) ⊆ Set.Ioo 0 1 ∧
      ∀ ξ ∈ pisotCantorSet (2 + Real.sqrt 5), ∀ n : ℕ,
        Int.fract (ξ * (2 + Real.sqrt 5) ^ n) ∉ Set.Ioo (x - r) (x + r)

statements.name: Bugeaud61.problem_10_61.variants.two_add_sqrt_three
statements.doc:
[Ste26, Theorem D] at $\alpha = 2 + \sqrt 3$: Problem 10.61 holds there, by a
confinement-gap certificate in exact $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt 3]$ arithmetic. This $\alpha$ lies
in the slice $2 < \alpha \le 4$, which the covering criterion does not reach.
statements.statement:
theorem problem_10_61.variants.two_add_sqrt_three :
    ∀ ξ ∈ pisotCantorSet (2 + Real.sqrt 3),
      ¬ IsEquidistributedModuloOne fun n : ℕ => ξ * (2 + Real.sqrt 3) ^ (n + 1)

problems.title: Equidistributed Sequences
problems.doc:
Corollary 4.2 of Chapter 1 states that the sequence $(x^n), n = 1, 2, ... ,$ is equidistributed modulo 1 for
almost all x > 1. And a little bit further down:
"one does not know whether sequences such as $(e^n)$, $(π^n)$, or even $((\frac 3 2)^n)$"
are equidistributed modulo 1 or not.

*References:*
  - [Uniform Distribution of Sequences](https://store.doverpublications.com/products/9780486149998)
by *L. Kuipers* and *H. Niederreiter*, 1974
  - [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equidistributed_sequence)
  - [Mat80] de Mathan, Bernard. "Numbers contravening a condition in density modulo 1."
    Acta Mathematica Hungarica 36.3-4 (1980): 237-241.
  - [Pol79] Pollington, Andrew Douglas. "On the density of sequence $\{n_ {k}\xi\} $."
    Illinois Journal of Mathematics 23.4 (1979): 511-515.

statements.name: Equidistribution.isAccumulationPoint_exists_subsequence_tendsto
statements.doc:
If a point `x` is an accumulation point of a sequence `s_0, s_1, ...` then
there is a subsequence of `s` that tends to `x`
statements.statement:
theorem isAccumulationPoint_exists_subsequence_tendsto
    (x : ℝ) (s : ℕ → ℝ) (hx : IsAccumulationPoint x s) :
    ∃ (u : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono u ∧ Filter.atTop.Tendsto (s ∘ u) (𝓝 x)

statements.name: Equidistribution.isEquidistributedModuloOne_three_halves_pow
statements.doc: The sequence `(3/2)^n` is equidistributed modulo `1`.
statements.statement:
theorem isEquidistributedModuloOne_three_halves_pow :
    IsEquidistributedModuloOne (fun n => (3 / 2 : ℝ)^n)

statements.name: Equidistribution.isEquidistributedModuloOne_transcendental_three_halves_pow
statements.doc:
It is not true that for every transcendental number `x` the sequence `x * (3 / 2) ^ n` is
equidistributed modulo `1`. The sequence `(3 / 2) ^ n` is lacunary, so by the theorem of
Pollington [Pol79] and de Mathan [Mat80] the set of real numbers `x` for which `x * (3 / 2) ^ n`
is not even dense modulo `1` has Hausdorff dimension `1`. This set is uncountable, so it contains
transcendental numbers. Alternatively, an elementary nested-interval construction (see issue
#5003) gives a Cantor set of `x` with `Int.fract (x * (3 / 2) ^ (8 * j)) ∈ [0, 1 / 10]` for all
`j`, which already rules out equidistribution for uncountably many, hence some transcendental,
`x`. By Koksma's metric theorem (Kuipers–Niederreiter, Chapter 1, Section 4), the sequence
`x * (3 / 2) ^ n` is equidistributed modulo `1` for almost all `x`.
statements.statement:
theorem isEquidistributedModuloOne_transcendental_three_halves_pow :
    ¬ ∀ x : ℝ, Transcendental ℚ x →
      IsEquidistributedModuloOne (fun n ↦ x * (3 / 2 : ℝ) ^ n)

statements.name: Equidistribution.isAccumulationPoint_three_halves_pow_infinite
statements.doc: The sequence `(3/2)^n` has infinitely many accumulation points modulo `1`.
statements.statement:
theorem isAccumulationPoint_three_halves_pow_infinite :
    {x | IsAccumulationPoint x (fun n => Int.fract <| (3 / 2 : ℝ)^n)}.Infinite

statements.name: Equidistribution.isAccumulationPoint_three_halves_pow
statements.doc: Find an accumulation point of the sequence `(3/2)^n` modulo `1`.
statements.statement:
theorem isAccumulationPoint_three_halves_pow :
    IsAccumulationPoint isAccumulationPoint_three_halves_pow.answer
      (fun n => Int.fract <| (3 / 2 : ℝ)^n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1)

statements.name: Erdos1.erdos_1
statements.doc:
If $A\subseteq\{1, ..., N\}$ with $|A| = n$ is such that the subset sums $\sum_{a\in S}a$ are
distinct for all $S\subseteq A$ then
$$
  N \gg 2 ^ n.
$$

This conjecture is false. A machine-checked disproof constructs sum-distinct sets for which
$N / 2^n$ tends to zero.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1 : ¬ ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (N : ℕ) (A : Finset ℕ) (_ : IsSumDistinctSet A N),
    N ≠ 0 → C * 2 ^ A.card < N

statements.name: Erdos1.erdos_1.variants.weaker
statements.doc: The trivial lower bound is $N \gg 2^n / n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1.variants.weaker : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (N : ℕ) (A : Finset ℕ)
    (_ : IsSumDistinctSet A N), N ≠ 0 → C * 2 ^ A.card / A.card < N

statements.name: Erdos1.erdos_1.variants.lb
statements.doc:
Erdős and Moser [Er56] proved
$$
  N \geq (\tfrac{1}{4} - o(1)) \frac{2^n}{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

[Er56] Erdős, P., _Problems and results in additive number theory_. Colloque sur la Th\'{E}orie des Nombres, Bruxelles, 1955 (1956), 127-137.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1.variants.lb : ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)),
    ∀ (N : ℕ) (A : Finset ℕ) (h : IsSumDistinctSet A N),
      (1 / 4 - o A.card) * 2 ^ A.card / (A.card : ℝ).sqrt ≤ N

statements.name: Erdos1.erdos_1.variants.lb_strong
statements.doc:
A number of improvements of the constant $\frac{1}{4}$ have been given, with the current
record $\sqrt{2 / \pi}$ first provided in unpublished work of Elkies and Gleason.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1.variants.lb_strong : ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)),
    ∀ (N : ℕ) (A : Finset ℕ) (h : IsSumDistinctSet A N),
      (√(2 / π) - o A.card) * 2 ^ A.card / (A.card : ℝ).sqrt ≤ N

statements.name: Erdos1.erdos_1.variants.real
statements.doc:
A generalisation of the problem to sets $A \subseteq (0, N]$ of real numbers, such that the subset
sums all differ by at least $1$ is proposed in [Er73] and [ErGr80].

The positive statement is false: every natural-number counterexample to `erdos_1` embeds into
$\mathbb{R}$, and distinct integer subset sums differ by at least one.

[Er73] Erdős, P., _Problems and results on combinatorial number theory_. A survey of combinatorial theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971) (1973), 117-138.

[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., _Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory_. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1.variants.real : ¬ ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (N : ℕ) (A : Finset ℝ)
    (_ : IsSumDistinctRealSet A N), N ≠ 0 → C * 2 ^ A.card < N

statements.name: Erdos1.erdos_1.variants.least_N_3
statements.doc:
The minimal value of $N$ such that there exists a sum-distinct set with three
elements is $4$.

https://oeis.org/A276661
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1.variants.least_N_3 :
    IsLeast { N | ∃ A, IsSumDistinctSet A N ∧ A.card = 3 } 4

statements.name: Erdos1.erdos_1.variants.least_N_4
statements.doc:
The minimal value of $N$ such that there exists a sum-distinct set with four
elements is $7$.

https://oeis.org/A276661
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1.variants.least_N_4 :
    IsLeast { N | ∃ A, IsSumDistinctSet A N ∧ A.card = 4 } 7

statements.name: Erdos1.erdos_1.variants.least_N_5
statements.doc:
The minimal value of $N$ such that there exists a sum-distinct set with five
elements is $13$.

https://oeis.org/A276661
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1.variants.least_N_5 :
    IsLeast { N | ∃ A, IsSumDistinctSet A N ∧ A.card = 5 } 13

statements.name: Erdos1.erdos_1.variants.least_N_9
statements.doc:
The minimal value of $N$ such that there exists a sum-distinct set with nine
elements is $161$.

https://oeis.org/A276661
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1.variants.least_N_9 :
    IsLeast { N | ∃ A, IsSumDistinctSet A N ∧ A.card = 9 } 161

problems.title: Erdős Problem 2
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/2](https://www.erdosproblems.com/2)
- [Ho15] Hough, B., *Solution of the minimum modulus problem for covering systems*. Ann. of Math.
  (2) **181** (2015), 361-382.
- [BBMST22] Balister, P., Bollobás, B., Morris, R., Sahasrabudhe, J. and Tiba, M., *On the Erdős
  Covering Problem: the density of the uncovered set*. Invent. Math. **228** (2022), 377-414.
- [PALOMAR-2026-10-05-000002](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-05-000002&version=1)

Erdős asked whether the smallest modulus in a distinct covering system can be arbitrarily large.
Hough [Ho15] proved that the answer is no, and Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, and Tiba
[BBMST22] later gave a simpler proof with an improved explicit upper bound.

statements.name: Erdos2.erdos_2
statements.doc:
Can the smallest modulus of a covering system be arbitrarily large?

This problem has a negative answer: there is a universal bound on the least modulus of any
distinct covering system.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_2 :
    ¬ ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ, ∀ i, ∃ m : ℕ,
      c.moduli i = Ideal.span {(m : ℤ)} ∧ B < m

problems.title: Erdős Problem 3
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/3](https://www.erdosproblems.com/3)
- [BlSi20] Bloom, Thomas F. and Sisask, Olof, *Breaking the logarithmic barrier in Roth's theorem
  on arithmetic progressions*. arXiv:2007.03528 (2020).
- [Go01] Gowers, W. T., *A new proof of Szemerédi's theorem*. Geom. Funct. Anal. (2001), 465-588.
- [GrTa17] Green, Ben and Tao, Terence, *New bounds for Szemerédi's theorem, III: a
  polylogarithmic bound for $r_4(N)$*. Mathematika (2017).
- [KeMe23] Kelley, Zander and Meka, Raghu, *Strong bounds for 3-progressions*. 2023 IEEE 64th
  Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science (FOCS) (2023).
- [LSS24] Leng, James, Sah, Ashwin and Sawhney, Mehtaab, *Improved bounds for Szemerédi's
  theorem*. arXiv:2402.17995 (2024).
- [OAI26] OpenAI, *Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions*. OpenAI Math Release
  preprint (2026).
  https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf

statements.name: Erdos3.erdos_3
statements.doc:
If $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ has $\sum_{n \in A}\frac 1 n = \infty$, then must $A$ contain arbitrarily
long arithmetic progressions?

Yes. This was proved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26]; see the linked Lean
proof.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_3 : ∀ A : Set ℕ,
    (¬ Summable fun a : A ↦ 1 / (a : ℝ)) →
    ∃ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ S ⊆ A, S.IsAPOfLength k

statements.name: Erdos3.erdos_3.variants.kelley_meka
statements.doc:
There are $\beta > 0$ and $c > 0$ such that $r_3(N) \ll N \exp(-c (\log N)^{\beta})$.

Proved by Kelley and Meka [KeMe23].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_3.variants.kelley_meka : ∃ β > (0 : ℝ), ∃ c > (0 : ℝ),
    (fun N ↦ (r 3 N : ℝ)) ≪ fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ) * Real.exp (-c * Real.log N ^ β)

statements.name: Erdos3.erdos_3.variants.three
statements.doc:
The case of $3$-term progressions: if $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ has $\sum_{n \in A}\frac 1 n = \infty$,
then $A$ contains a non-trivial $3$-term arithmetic progression.

Proved by Bloom and Sisask [BlSi20].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_3.variants.three : ∀ A : Set ℕ,
    (¬ Summable fun a : A ↦ 1 / (a : ℝ)) → ∃ S ⊆ A, S.IsAPOfLength 3

statements.name: Erdos3.erdos_3.variants.green_tao
statements.doc:
There is $c > 0$ such that $r_4(N) \ll N (\log N)^{-c}$.

Proved by Green and Tao [GrTa17].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_3.variants.green_tao : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ),
    (fun N ↦ (r 4 N : ℝ)) ≪ fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ (-c)

statements.name: Erdos3.erdos_3.variants.gowers
statements.doc:
For every $k \geq 3$ there is $c_k > 0$ such that $r_k(N) \ll_k N (\log \log N)^{-c_k}$.

Proved by Gowers [Go01].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_3.variants.gowers (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ),
    (fun N ↦ (r k N : ℝ)) ≪ fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log N) ^ (-c)

statements.name: Erdos3.erdos_3.variants.leng_sah_sawhney
statements.doc:
For every $k \geq 5$ there is $c_k > 0$ such that $r_k(N) \ll_k N \exp(-(\log \log N)^{c_k})$.

Proved by Leng, Sah and Sawhney [LSS24].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_3.variants.leng_sah_sawhney (k : ℕ) (hk : 5 ≤ k) : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ),
    (fun N ↦ (r k N : ℝ)) ≪
      fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ) * Real.exp (-Real.log (Real.log N) ^ c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 4
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/4](https://www.erdosproblems.com/4)

statements.name: Erdos4.erdos_4
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for any $C > 0$, there infinitely many $n$ such that:
$$
  p_{n + 1} - p_n > C \frac{\log\log n\log\log\log\log n}{(\log\log\log n) ^ 2}\log n
$$
statements.statement: theorem erdos_4 : (∀ C > 0, Erdos4For C)

statements.name: Erdos4.erdos_4.variants.rankin
statements.doc: Rankin's theorem: there exists a positive constant $C$ such that `Erdos4For C` holds.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_4.variants.rankin :
    ∃ C > 0, Erdos4For C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/5](https://www.erdosproblems.com/5)
- [BFM16] Banks, William D. and Freiberg, Tristan and Maynard, James, *On limit points of the
  sequence of normalized prime gaps*. Proc. Lond. Math. Soc. (3) (2016), 515-539.
- [Er55] Erdős, Paul, *Some remarks on number theory*. Riveon Lematematika (1955), 45-48.
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [Er85c] Erdős, P., *On some of my problems in number theory I would most like to see solved*.
  Number theory (Ootacamund, 1984) (1985), 74-84.
- [Er97c] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*. The mathematics of Paul Erdős,
  I (1997), 47-67.
- [GPY09] Goldston, Daniel A. and Pintz, János and Yıldırım, Cem Y., *Primes in tuples. I*.
  Ann. of Math. (2) (2009), 819-862.
- [HiMa88] Hildebrand, Adolf and Maier, Helmut, *Gaps between prime numbers*. Proc. Amer. Math.
  Soc. (1988), 1-9.
- [Me20] Merikoski, Jori, *Limit points of normalized prime gaps*. J. Lond. Math. Soc. (2) (2020),
  99-124.
- [Pi16] Pintz, János, *Polignac numbers, conjectures of Erdős on gaps between primes, arithmetic
  progressions in primes, and the bounded gap conjecture*. From arithmetic to zeta-functions
  (2016), 367-384.
- [Ri56] Ricci, Giovanni, *Recherches sur l'allure de la suite $\{p_{n+1}-p_n/\log p_n\}$*.
  Colloque sur la Théorie des Nombres, Bruxelles, 1955 (1956), 93-106.
- [We31] Westzynthius, E., *Über die Verteilung der Zahlen, die zu den n ersten Primzahlen
  teilerfremd sind*. Commentat. Phys. Math. (1931), 1-37.

statements.name: Erdos5.erdos_5
statements.doc:
Let $C\geq 0$. Is there an infinite sequence of $n_i$ such that
$$\lim_{i\to \infty}\frac{p_{n_i+1}-p_{n_i}}{\log n_i}=C?$$

We formalise "an infinite sequence of $n_i$" as a strictly monotone sequence of indices
`n : ℕ → ℕ`. Note that the numerator is the gap between the two *consecutive* primes
$p_{n_i}$ and $p_{n_i+1}$, which is `primeGap (n i)`, and not the gap between the primes
indexed by two consecutive members of the sequence.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_5 : ∀ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C →
    ∃ n : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono n ∧ Tendsto (fun i => normalizedGap (n i)) atTop (𝓝 C)

statements.name: Erdos5.erdos_5.variants.limit_point_set
statements.doc:
Let $S$ be the set of limit points of $(p_{n+1}-p_n)/\log n$. This problem asks whether
$S=[0,\infty]$.

Since $\infty\in S$ is known (see `erdos_5.variants.westzynthius`), the open content is the
equality of the finite part of $S$ with $[0,\infty)$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_5.variants.limit_point_set : limitPointSet = Ici 0

statements.name: Erdos5.erdos_5.variants.westzynthius
statements.doc: $\infty\in S$ by Westzynthius' result [We31] on large prime gaps.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_5.variants.westzynthius :
    ∃ n : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono n ∧ Tendsto (fun i => normalizedGap (n i)) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos5.erdos_5.variants.goldston_pintz_yildirim
statements.doc: $0\in S$ by the work of Goldston, Pintz, and Yildirim [GPY09] on small prime gaps.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_5.variants.goldston_pintz_yildirim : (0 : ℝ) ∈ limitPointSet

statements.name: Erdos5.erdos_5.variants.erdos_ricci
statements.doc: Erdős [Er55] and Ricci [Ri56] independently showed that $S$ has positive Lebesgue measure.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_5.variants.erdos_ricci : 0 < volume limitPointSet

statements.name: Erdos5.erdos_5.variants.hildebrand_maier
statements.doc: Hildebrand and Maier [HiMa88] showed that $S$ contains arbitrarily large (finite) numbers.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_5.variants.hildebrand_maier : ∀ C : ℝ, ∃ x ∈ limitPointSet, C < x

statements.name: Erdos5.erdos_5.variants.hildebrand_maier_measure
statements.doc:
[HiMa88] in fact prove the stronger statement that there is a constant $c>0$ with
$\lambda([0,T]\cap S)\geq cT$ for all sufficiently large $T$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_5.variants.hildebrand_maier_measure : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ T : ℝ in atTop,
    ENNReal.ofReal (c * T) ≤ volume (limitPointSet ∩ Icc 0 T)

statements.name: Erdos5.erdos_5.variants.pintz
statements.doc: Pintz [Pi16] showed that there exists some small constant $c>0$ such that $[0,c]\subset S$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_5.variants.pintz : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), Icc 0 c ⊆ limitPointSet

statements.name: Erdos5.erdos_5.variants.banks_freiberg_maynard
statements.doc:
Banks, Freiberg, and Maynard [BFM16] showed that at least $12.5\%$ of $[0,\infty)$ belongs
to $S$.

This is [BFM16, Theorem 1.1]: for any nine nonnegative reals
$\beta_1\leq\beta_2\leq\cdots\leq\beta_9$, at least one of the differences $\beta_j-\beta_i$
with $i<j$ belongs to $S$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_5.variants.banks_freiberg_maynard (β : Fin 9 → ℝ) (hβ : ∀ i, 0 ≤ β i)
    (hβmono : Monotone β) : ∃ i j, i < j ∧ β j - β i ∈ limitPointSet

statements.name: Erdos5.erdos_5.variants.banks_freiberg_maynard_measure
statements.doc:
The $12.5\%$ claim itself, as deduced in [BFM16, Corollary 1.2]:
$\lambda([0,T]\cap S)\geq (1-o(1))T/8$ as $T\to\infty$.

Note that the constant $1/8$ is only attained asymptotically and ineffectively; the bound
[BFM16] obtain for *all* $T>0$ is the weaker $\lambda([0,T]\cap S)>T/22$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_5.variants.banks_freiberg_maynard_measure : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ T : ℝ in atTop,
    ENNReal.ofReal ((1 - ε) * T / 8) ≤ volume (limitPointSet ∩ Icc 0 T)

statements.name: Erdos5.erdos_5.variants.merikoski
statements.doc:
Merikoski [Me20] showed that at least $1/3$ of $[0,\infty)$ belongs to $S$.

This is [Me20, Theorem 1]: for any reals $\beta_1\leq\beta_2\leq\beta_3\leq\beta_4$, at least
one of the differences $\beta_j-\beta_i$ with $i<j$ belongs to $S$. Note that, in contrast with
`erdos_5.variants.banks_freiberg_maynard`, the $\beta_i$ are not required to be nonnegative.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_5.variants.merikoski (β : Fin 4 → ℝ) (hβmono : Monotone β) :
    ∃ i j, i < j ∧ β j - β i ∈ limitPointSet

statements.name: Erdos5.erdos_5.variants.merikoski_measure
statements.doc:
The $1/3$ claim itself [Me20, Corollary 2]: $\lambda([0,T]\cap S)\geq T/3$ for all $T>0$.

Unlike the $1/8$ of [BFM16], this bound holds uniformly in $T$ with no error term.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_5.variants.merikoski_measure : ∀ T > (0 : ℝ),
    ENNReal.ofReal (T / 3) ≤ volume (limitPointSet ∩ Icc 0 T)

statements.name: Erdos5.erdos_5.variants.merikoski_bounded_gaps
statements.doc:
Merikoski [Me20] showed that $S$ has bounded gaps.

This is [Me20, Corollary 3]: there is a (ineffective) constant $C\geq 0$ such that
$S\cap[T,T+C]\neq\emptyset$ for all $T\geq 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_5.variants.merikoski_bounded_gaps :
    ∃ C ≥ (0 : ℝ), ∀ T ≥ (0 : ℝ), (limitPointSet ∩ Icc T (T + C)).Nonempty

statements.name: Erdos5.erdos_5.variants.dense
statements.doc:
In [Er65b], [Er85c], and [Er97c] Erdős asks whether $S$ is everywhere dense (but Weisenberg
notes that clearly $S$ is closed so this is equivalent to asking whether $S=[0,\infty]$).
statements.statement: theorem erdos_5.variants.dense : Ici (0 : ℝ) ⊆ closure limitPointSet

problems.title: Erdős Problem 6
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/6](https://www.erdosproblems.com/6)
- [BFT15] Banks, William D. and Freiberg, Tristan and Turnage-Butterbaugh, Caroline L., Consecutive primes in tuples. Acta Arith. (2015), 261-266.
- [Ma15] Maynard, James, Small gaps between primes. Ann. of Math. (2) (2015), 383-413.

statements.name: Erdos6.erdos_6
statements.doc:
There are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n < d_{n+1} < d_{n+2}$, where $d$
denotes the prime gap function.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_6 :
    {n | primeGap n < primeGap (n + 1) ∧ primeGap (n + 1) < primeGap (n + 2)}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos6.erdos_6.variants.increasing
statements.doc:
For all $m$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n < d_{n+1} < \dots < d_{n+m}$,
where $d$ denotes the prime gap function.

Proved by Banks, Freiberg, and Turnage-Butterbaugh [BFT15] with an application of the
Maynard-Tao machinery concerning bounded gaps between primes [Ma15]
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_6.variants.increasing (m : ℕ) :
    {n | ∀ i ∈ Finset.range m, primeGap (n + i) < primeGap (n + i + 1)}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos6.erdos_6.variants.decreasing
statements.doc:
For all $m$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n > d_{n+1} > \dots > d_{n+m}$,
where $d$ denotes the prime gap function.

Proved by Banks, Freiberg, and Turnage-Butterbaugh [BFT15] with an application of the
Maynard-Tao machinery concerning bounded gaps between primes [Ma15]
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_6.variants.decreasing (m : ℕ) :
    {n | ∀ i ∈ Finset.range m, primeGap (n + i) > primeGap (n + i + 1)}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 7
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/7](https://www.erdosproblems.com/7)

statements.name: Erdos7.erdos_7
statements.doc: Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are odd (and greater than 1)?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_7 :
    ∃ (C : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ), ∀ i,
      ¬ C.moduli i ≤ Ideal.span {2} ∧ C.moduli i ≠ ⊤

problems.title: Erdős Problem 9
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/9](https://www.erdosproblems.com/9)

statements.name: Erdos9.erdos_9.variants.infinite
statements.doc:
The set is known to be infinite. In [Er77c] Erdős credits Schinzel with proving that there are
infinitely many odd integers not of this form, but gives no reference.

[Er77c] Erdős, P., _Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III._.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_9.variants.infinite : Erdos9A.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos9.erdos_9
statements.doc:
Is the upper density of the set of odd numbers that cannot be expressed as a prime plus
two powers of 2 positive?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_9 : 0 < Erdos9A.upperDensity

problems.title: Erdős Problem 10
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/10](https://www.erdosproblems.com/10)
- [Cr71] Crocker, R., On the sum of a prime and of two powers of two. Pacific J. Math. 36 (1971),
  103-107.
- [Ga75] Gallagher, P. X., Primes and powers of 2. Acta Arith. 29 (1976), 353-370.
- [GrSo98] Granville, A. and Soundararajan, K., A binary additive problem of Erdős and the
  order of $2$ mod $p^2$. Ramanujan J. 2 (1998), 283-298.

statements.name: Erdos10.erdos_10
statements.doc:
Is there some $k$ such that every large integer is the sum of a prime and at most $k$
powers of $2$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_10 : ∃ k, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, n ∈ sumPrimeAndTwoPows k

statements.name: Erdos10.erdos_10.variants.gallagher
statements.doc:
Gallagher [Ga75] has shown that for any $ϵ > 0$ there exists $k(ϵ)$
such that the set of integers which are the sum of a prime and at most $k(ϵ)$
many powers of $2$ has lower density at least $1 - ϵ$.

Ref: Gallagher, P. X., _Primes and powers of 2_.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_10.variants.gallagher (ε : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ k, 1 - ε ≤ (sumPrimeAndTwoPows k).lowerDensity

statements.name: Erdos10.erdos_10.variants.granville_soundararajan_odd
statements.doc:
Granville and Soundararajan [GrSo98] have conjectured that at most $3$
powers of $2$ suffice for all odd integers, and hence at most $4$ powers of $2$
suffice for all even integers.

Ref: Granville, A. and Soundararajan, K., _A Binary Additive Problem of Erdős and the Order of $2$ mod $p^2$_
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_10.variants.granville_soundararajan_odd :
    {n : ℕ | Odd n ∧ 1 < n} ⊆ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 3 ∧
      {n : ℕ | Even n ∧ n ≠ 0} ⊆ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 4

statements.name: Erdos10.erdos_10.variants.grechuk_example
statements.doc:
Bogdan Grechuk has observed that `1117175146` is not the sum of a prime
and at most $3$ powers of $2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_10.variants.grechuk_example :
    1117175146 ∉ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 3

statements.name: Erdos10.erdos_10.variants.two_pows
statements.doc: There are infinitely many even integers not the sum of a prime and $2$ powers of $2$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_10.variants.two_pows :
    Set.Infinite <| {n : ℕ | Even n} \ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 2

statements.name: Erdos10.erdos_10.variants.grechuk
statements.doc:
Bogdan Grechuk has observed that $1117175146$ is not the sum of a prime and at most $3$
powers of $2$, and pointed out that parity considerations, coupled with the fact that there
are many integers not the sum of a prime and $2$ powers of $2$ suggest that there exist
infinitely many even integers which are not the sum of a prime and at most $3$ powers of $2$.

This follows from Crocker's construction [Cr71] of infinitely many odd $t \equiv 15 \pmod{16}$
which are not the sum of a prime and $2$ powers of $2$: each such $t + 1$ is even and not the
sum of a prime and at most $3$ powers of $2$.

The linked Lean formalisation is by Daryxx, see comment section.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_10.variants.grechuk :
    Set.Infinite <| {n : ℕ | Even n} \ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 11
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/11](https://www.erdosproblems.com/11)

statements.name: Erdos11.erdos_11
statements.doc: Is every large odd integer $n$ the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_11 :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, Odd n → ∃ k l : ℕ, Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2 ^ l

statements.name: Erdos11.erdos_11.variants.all_odd
statements.doc:
Every odd $n > 1$ is the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2. This is the form in
earlier versions of erdosproblems.com/11 and the hypothesis of [GrSo98]. It is stronger than
`erdos_11`, which asks only about large $n$: a single exception would refute it.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_11.variants.all_odd (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l : ℕ, Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2 ^ l

statements.name: Erdos11.erdos_11.variants.not_four_dvd
statements.doc:
Erdős often asked this under the weaker assumption that $n > 1$
is not divisible by 4.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_11.variants.not_four_dvd (n : ℕ) (hn : ¬ 4 ∣ n) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l : ℕ , Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2^l

statements.name: Erdos11.erdos_11.variants.two_pow_two
statements.doc: Is every odd $n > 1$ the sum of a squarefree number and two powers of 2?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_11.variants.two_pow_two (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l m : ℕ , Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2^l + 2^m

statements.name: Erdos11.erdos_11.variants.finite_bound1
statements.doc: Every odd $1 < n < 10^7$ is the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_11.variants.finite_bound1 (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (h : n < 10^7) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l : ℕ , Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2^l

statements.name: Erdos11.erdos_11.variants.finite_bound2
statements.doc: Every odd $1 < n < 2^50$ is the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_11.variants.finite_bound2 (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (h : n < 2^50) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l : ℕ , Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2^l

statements.name: Erdos11.erdos_11.variants.granville_soundararajan
statements.doc:
Suppose that every odd $n > 1$ is the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2. Then the set of
primes $p$ such that $2^p \not\equiv 2 \pmod{p^2}$ (the non-Wieferich primes) is infinite.
This follows from Theorem 1 in [GrSo98].
[GrSo98] Granville, A. and Soundararajan, K., A Binary Additive Problem of Erdős and the Order of $2$ mod $p^2$. The Ramanujan Journal (1998), 283-298.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_11.variants.granville_soundararajan (H : type_of% erdos_11.variants.all_odd) :
    {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ ¬ 2 ^ p ≡ 2 [MOD p ^ 2]}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 12
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/12](https://www.erdosproblems.com/12)

statements.name: Erdos12.isGood_example
statements.doc:
The set of $p ^ 2$ where $p \cong 3 \mod 4$ is prime is an example of a good set.
Formal proof provided by AlphaProof
statements.statement:
theorem isGood_example :
    IsGood {p ^ 2 | (p : ℕ) (_ : p ≡ 3 [MOD 4]) (_ : p.Prime)}

statements.name: Erdos12.erdos_12.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $A$ be an infinite set such that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$
such that $a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$. Is there such an $A$ with
$\liminf \frac{|A \cap \{1, \dotsc, N\}|}{N^{1/2}} > 0$ ?

The DeepMind prover agent has found a formal proof of this statement.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_12.parts.i : ∃ (A : Set ℕ), IsGood A ∧
    (0 : ℝ) < Filter.atTop.liminf
      (fun N => (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard / (N : ℝ).sqrt)

statements.name: Erdos12.erdos_12.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $A$ be an infinite set such that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$
such that $a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$. Does there exist some absolute constant $c > 0$
such that there are always infinitely many $N$
with $|A \cap \{1, \dotsc, N\}| < N^{1−c}$?

The DeepMind prover agent has found a formal disproof of this statement.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_12.parts.ii : ¬ ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (A : Set ℕ), IsGood A →
    {N : ℕ| (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard < (N : ℝ) ^ (1 - c)}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos12.erdos_12.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Let $A$ be an infinite set such that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$
such that $a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$. Is it true that $∑_{n \in A} \frac{1}{n} < \infty$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_12.parts.iii :
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ), IsGood A → Summable (fun (n : A) ↦ (1 / n : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos12.erdos_12.variants.erdos_sarkozy_density_0
statements.doc:
Erdős and Sárközy proved that such an $A$ must have density 0.
[ErSa70] Erd\H os, P. and Sárk\"ozi, A., On the divisibility properties of sequences of integers.
    Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) (1970), 97-101
statements.statement: theorem erdos_12.variants.erdos_sarkozy_density_0 (A : Set ℕ) (hA : IsGood A) : A.HasDensity 0

statements.name: Erdos12.erdos_12.variants.erdos_sarkozy
statements.doc:
Given any function $f(x)\to \infty$ as $x\to \infty$ there exists a set $A$ with the property
that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$ such that $a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$, such that there are
infinitely many $N$ such that $$\lvert A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert > \frac{N}{f(N)}.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_12.variants.erdos_sarkozy (f : ℕ → ℕ) (hf : atTop.Tendsto f atTop) :
    ∃ A, IsGood A ∧ {N : ℕ | (N : ℝ) / f N < (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos12.erdos_12.variants.example
statements.doc:
An example of an $A$ with the property that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$ such that
$a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$ and such that
$$\liminf \frac{\lvert A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}{N^{1/2}}\log N > 0$$
is given by the set of $p^2$, where $p\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ is prime.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_12.variants.example (A : Set ℕ)
    (hA : A = {p ^ 2 | (p : ℕ) (_ : p.Prime) (_ : p ≡ 3 [MOD 4])}) :
    IsGood A ∧ 0 < atTop.liminf (fun (N : ℕ) ↦ (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard * (N : ℝ).log / √N)

statements.name: Erdos12.erdos_12.variants.schoen
statements.doc:
Let $A$ be a set of natural numbers with the property that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$ such
that $a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$. If all elements in $A$ are pairwise coprime then
$$\lvert A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \ll N^{2/3}$$
for infinitely many $N$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_12.variants.schoen (A : Set ℕ) (hA : IsGood A) (hA' : A.Pairwise Nat.Coprime) :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), {N : ℕ | (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard ≤ C * (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ)}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos12.erdos_12.variants.baier
statements.doc:
Let $A$ be a set of natural numbers with the property that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$ such
that $a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$. If all elements in $A$ are pairwise coprime then
$$\lvert A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \ll N^{2/3}/\log N$$
for infinitely many $N$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_12.variants.baier (A : Set ℕ) (hA : IsGood A) (hA' : A.Pairwise Nat.Coprime) :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ),
      {N : ℕ | (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard ≤ C * (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ) / (N : ℝ).log}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 13
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/13](https://www.erdosproblems.com/13)

statements.name: Erdos13.erdos_13
statements.doc:
If $A \subseteq \{1, ..., N\}$ is a set with no $a, b, c \in A$ such that $a | (b+c)$ and
$a < \min(b,c)$, then $|A| \le N/3 + O(1)$. This has been solved by Bedert [Be23].

[Be23] Bedert, B., _On a problem of Erdős and Sárközy about sequences with no term dividing
the sum of two larger terms_. arXiv:2301.07065 (2023).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_13 : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ, ∀ A ⊆ Icc 1 N, IsForbiddenTripleFree A →
    (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) / 3 + C

statements.name: Erdos13.erdos_13.variants.general
statements.doc:
A general version asks, for a fixed $r \in \mathbb{N}$, if a set
$A \subseteq \{1, ..., N\}$ has no $a \in A$ and $b_1, ..., b_r \in A$ such that
$a | (b_1 + ... + b_r)$ and $a < \min(b_1, ..., b_r)$, then is it true that
$|A| \le N/(r+1) + O(1)$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_13.variants.general : ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ,
    ∀ A ⊆ Icc 1 N,
    (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ (b : Fin r → ℕ), (∀ i, b i ∈ A) → (∀ i, a < b i) →
      ¬ (a ∣ ∑ i, b i)) →
    (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) / (r + 1) + C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 14
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/14](https://www.erdosproblems.com/14)

statements.name: Erdos14.erdos_14.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$. Let $B ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ be the set of integers which are representable
in exactly one way as the sum of two elements from $A$. Is it true that for all
$\epsilon > 0$ and large $N$, $|\{1,\ldots,N\} \setminus B| \gg_\epsilon N^{1/2 - \epsilon}$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_14.parts.i :
    ∀ A, ∀ ε > 0, nonUniqueSumCount A ≫ almostSquareRoot ε

statements.name: Erdos14.erdos_14.parts.ii
statements.doc: Is it possible that $|\{1,\ldots,N\} \setminus B| = o(N^\frac{1}{2})$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_14.parts.ii :
    ∃ (A : Set ℕ), IsLittleO atTop (nonUniqueSumCount A) squareRoot

problems.title: Erdős Problem 15: Convergence of Series with Primes
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/15](https://www.erdosproblems.com/15)

statements.name: Erdos15.erdos_15
statements.doc:
Is it true that $\sum_{n=1}^\infty(-1)^n\frac{n}{p_n}$ converges,
where $p_n$ is the sequence of primes?

Note: In the problem statement, $p_n$ is the $n$-th prime, indexed such that $p_1=2, p_2=3, \ldots$.
We 0-index here to reflect how Nat.nth works.

Note: convergence here is convergence of the sequence of partial sums, which is what the
problem asks about. `Summable` would be the wrong notion: it is unconditional summability,
equivalent over $\mathbb{R}$ to absolute convergence, and $\sum_n n/p_n$ diverges.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_15 :
    ∃ l : ℝ, Tendsto (fun N => ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N,
      (-1 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) * (k + 1) / (k.nth Nat.Prime)) atTop (𝓝 l)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 16
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/16](https://www.erdosproblems.com/16)
- [Ch23] Chen, Yong-Gao, A conjecture of Erdős on $p+2^k$. arXiv:2312.04120 (2023).
- [Er50] Erdős, P., On integers of the form $2^k+p$ and some related problems. Summa Brasil. Math.
  (1950), 113-123.
- [Ro34] Romanoff, N. P., Über einige Sätze der additiven Zahlentheorie. Math. Ann. (1934), 668-678.

statements.name: Erdos16.erdos_16
statements.doc:
Is the set of odd integers not of the form $2^k+p$ the union of an infinite arithmetic progression
and a set of density $0$?

Erdős called this conjecture "rather silly".

Chen [Ch23] has proved the answer is no.

This was formalized in Lean by Chin using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_16 :
    ¬ ∃ A B : Set ℕ, Erdos16Set = A ∪ B ∧
      (∃ a d : ℕ, d > 0 ∧ A = { x | ∃ m : ℕ, x = a + m * d }) ∧
      density_zero B

statements.name: Erdos16.erdos_16.variant.romanoff
statements.doc: Romanoff [Ro34] showed that the set of odd integers of this form has positive density.

statements.name: Erdos16.erdos_16.variant.erdos
statements.doc:
Using covering congruences Erdős [Er50] proved that the set of odd integers which are not of this
form contains an infinite arithmetic progression.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_16.variant.erdos :
    ∃ a d : ℕ, d > 0 ∧ { x | ∃ m : ℕ, x = a + m * d } ⊆ Erdos16Set

problems.title: Erdős Problem 17
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/17](https://www.erdosproblems.com/17)

statements.name: Erdos17.erdos_17
statements.doc: **Erdős Problem 17.** Are there infinitely many cluster primes?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_17 : {p : ℕ | IsClusterPrime p}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos17.erdos_17.variants.upper_BES
statements.doc:
In 1999 Blecksmith, Erdős, and Selfridge [BES99] proved the upper bound
$$\pi^{\mathcal{C}}(x) \ll_A x(\log x)^{-A}$$ for every real $A > 0$.

[BES99] Blecksmith, Richard and Erd\H os, Paul and Selfridge, J. L., Cluster primes. Amer. Math. Monthly (1999), 43--48.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_17.variants.upper_BES {A : ℝ} (hA : 0 < A) :
  (fun x ↦ (clusterPrimeCount x : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun x ↦ x / (log x) ^ A

statements.name: Erdos17.erdos_17.variants.upper_Elsholtz
statements.doc:
In 2003, Elsholtz [El03] refined the upper bound to
$$\pi^{\mathcal{C}}(x) \ll x\,\exp\!\bigl(-c(\log\log x)^2\bigr)$$
for every real $0 < c < 1/8$.

[El03] Elsholtz, Christian, On cluster primes. Acta Arith. (2003), 281--284.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_17.variants.upper_Elsholtz :
  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    ∀ c ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (1 / 8),
      IsBigOWith C atTop (fun x ↦ (clusterPrimeCount x : ℝ))
        (fun x ↦ x * exp (-c * (log (log x)) ^ 2))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 18
problems.doc:
*Reference:*
* [erdosproblems.com/18](https://www.erdosproblems.com/18)
* [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. (1980). Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number
Theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique, 28. Université de Genève. (See the
sections on Egyptian fractions or practical numbers).
* [Vo85] Vose, Michael D., Egyptian fractions. Bull. London Math. Soc. (1985), 21-24.

statements.name: Erdos18.factorial_isPractical
statements.doc: $h(n!)$ is well-defined since $n!$ is practical for $n ≥ 1$.
statements.statement: theorem factorial_isPractical (n : ℕ) : Nat.IsPractical n.factorial

statements.name: Erdos18.erdos_18a
statements.doc:
**Conjecture 1.**
Are there infinitely many practical numbers $m$ such that $h(m) < (\log \log m)^{O(1)}$?

More precisely: does there exist a constant $C > 0$ such that for infinitely many
practical numbers $m$, we have $h(m) < (\log \log m)^C$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_18a :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ᶠ m in atTop, Nat.IsPractical m ∧
      (practicalH m : ℝ) < (log (log m)) ^ C

statements.name: Erdos18.erdos_18b
statements.doc:
**Conjecture 2.**
Is it true that $h(n!) < n^{o(1)}$? That is, for all $\varepsilon > 0$,
is $h(n!) < n^\varepsilon$ for sufficiently large $n$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_18b :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (practicalH n.factorial : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) ^ ε

statements.name: Erdos18.erdos_18c
statements.doc:
**Conjecture 3.**
Or perhaps even $h(n!) < (\log n)^{O(1)}$?

Erdős offered \$250 for a proof or disproof.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_18c :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (practicalH n.factorial : ℝ) < (log n) ^ C

statements.name: Erdos18.erdos_18_upper_bound
statements.doc:
**Erdős's Theorem.**
Erdős proved that $h(n!) < n$ for all $n \ge 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_18_upper_bound :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, practicalH (Nat.factorial n) < n

statements.name: Erdos18.erdos_18_vose
statements.doc:
**Vose's Theorem.**
Vose proved the existence of infinitely many practical numbers $m$ such that
$h(m) \ll (\log m)^{1/2}$. This gives a positive answer to a weaker form of Conjecture 1.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_18_vose :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ᶠ m in atTop, Nat.IsPractical m ∧
      (practicalH m : ℝ) < C * (log m) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 19
problems.doc:
The Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture: if $G$ is an edge-disjoint union of $n$ copies of $K_n$,
is $\chi(G) = n$?

We model $G$ by a family of $n$ vertex sets of size $n$ (the copies of $K_n$) which pairwise
share at most one vertex and which cover the vertex type. Two copies of $K_n$ are
edge-disjoint exactly when their vertex sets share at most one vertex.

*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/19](https://www.erdosproblems.com/19)
* [Hi81] Hindman, N., *On a conjecture of Erdős, Faber, and Lovász about $n$-colorings*.
  Canad. J. Math. (1981).
* [Ka92] Kahn, J., *Coloring nearly-disjoint hypergraphs with $n + o(n)$ colors*.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1992).
* [KKKMO21] Kang, D. Y., Kelly, T., Kühn, D., Methuku, A. and Osthus, D., *A proof of the
  Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture*. Ann. of Math. (2023).
  [arXiv:2101.04698](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04698)

statements.name: Erdos19.EFLConfig.le_chromaticNumber
statements.doc: The graph $G$ contains a copy of $K_n$, so $n \le \chi(G)$.
statements.statement: theorem le_chromaticNumber : (n : ℕ∞) ≤ C.graph.chromaticNumber

statements.name: Erdos19.EFLConfig.colorable_of_sharedColoring
statements.doc:
If the shared vertices can be coloured with $n$ colours so that shared vertices in a common
clique get distinct colours, then $G$ is $n$-colourable.
statements.statement:
theorem colorable_of_sharedColoring (c : V → Fin n)
    (hc : ∀ i u v, u ∈ C.A i → v ∈ C.A i → C.IsShared u → C.IsShared v → c u = c v → u = v) :
    C.graph.Colorable n

statements.name: Erdos19.EFLConfig.card_sharedSet_le
statements.doc:
There are at most $\binom{n}{2}$ shared vertices, since two cliques share at most one
vertex.
statements.statement: theorem card_sharedSet_le : C.sharedSet.card ≤ n.choose 2

statements.name: Erdos19.erdos_19
statements.doc: If $G$ is an edge-disjoint union of $n$ copies of $K_n$, then is $\chi(G) = n$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_19 :
    ∀ (V : Type) (n : ℕ) (C : EFLConfig V n), C.graph.chromaticNumber = n

statements.name: Erdos19.erdos_19.variants.lt_ten
statements.doc: Hindman [Hi81] proved the Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture for $n < 10$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_19.variants.lt_ten :
    ∀ (V : Type) (n : ℕ) (C : EFLConfig V n), n < 10 → C.graph.chromaticNumber = n

statements.name: Erdos19.erdos_19.variants.kahn
statements.doc: Kahn [Ka92] proved that $\chi(G) \le (1 + o(1))n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_19.variants.kahn :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ (V : Type) (C : EFLConfig V n),
      C.graph.Colorable ⌊(1 + ε) * n⌋₊

statements.name: Erdos19.erdos_19.variants.large_n
statements.doc:
Kang, Kelly, Kühn, Methuku and Osthus [KKKMO21] proved the Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture for
all sufficiently large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_19.variants.large_n :
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ (V : Type) (C : EFLConfig V n), C.graph.chromaticNumber = n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 20
problems.doc:
*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/20](https://www.erdosproblems.com/20)
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunflower_(mathematics))
* [ErRa60] Erdős, Paul and Rado, Richard. Intersection theorems for systems of sets.
  J. London Math. Soc. 35 (1960), 85--90.

statements.name: Erdos20.erdos_20
statements.doc: Is it true that $f(n,k) < c_k^n$ for some constant $c_k>0$ and for all $n > 0$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_20 : ∃ (c : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ n k, n > 0 → f n k < (c k) ^ n

statements.name: Erdos20.erdos_20.variants.erdos_rado_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős and Rado [ErRa60] proved the factorial upper bound for the $k$-sunflower
threshold: any family of $n$-uniform sets with more than $(k-1)^n \, n!$ members
contains a $k$-sunflower, hence $f(n,k) \le (k-1)^n \, n! + 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_20.variants.erdos_rado_bound :
    ∀ n k, n > 0 → 2 ≤ k → f n k ≤ (k - 1) ^ n * n.factorial + 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 21
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/21](https://www.erdosproblems.com/21)
- [Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
- [Er90] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. A tribute to Paul Erdős (1990),
  467-478.
- [Er92b] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics*.
  Matematiche (Catania) (1992), 231-240.
- [Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability
  (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
- [ErLo75] Erdős, P. and Lovász, L., *Problems and results on $3$-chromatic hypergraphs and some
  related questions*. (1975), 609--627.
- [Ka92b] Kahn, Jeff, *On a problem of Erdős and Lovász: random lines in a projective plane*.
  Combinatorica (1992), 417-423.
- [Ka94] Kahn, Jeff, *On a problem of Erdős and Lovász. II. $n(r)=O(r)$*. J. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (1994), 125-143.
- [Tr14] A. Tripathi, *A result on intersecting families with maximum transversal size*.
  arXiv:1409.4610 (2014).
- [BaWa21] J. Barát and I. M. Wanless, *Intersecting and 2-intersecting hypergraphs with maximal
  covering number: the Erdős-Lovász theme revisited*. J. Combin. Des. (2021), 260-286.

statements.name: Erdos21.erdos_21
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that there is an intersecting family $\mathcal{F}$ of sets of size $n$
(so $A\cap B\neq\emptyset$ for all $A,B\in \mathcal{F}$) with $\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert=f(n)$
such that any set $S$ with $\lvert S\rvert \leq n-1$ is disjoint from at least one
$A\in \mathcal{F}$.

Is it true that
$$f(n) \ll n?$$

Conjectured by Erdős and Lovász [ErLo75], who proved that
$$\frac{8}{3}n-3\leq f(n) \ll n^{3/2}\log n$$
for all $n$. The upper bound was improved by Kahn [Ka92b] to $f(n) \ll n\log n$. (The upper
bound constructions in both cases are formed by taking a random set of lines from a projective
plane of order $n-1$, assuming $n-1$ is a prime power.)

This problem was solved by Kahn [Ka94] who proved the upper bound $f(n) \ll n$. The Erdős-Lovász
lower bound of $\frac{8}{3}n-O(1)$ has not been improved, and it has been speculated (see e.g.
[Ka94]) that the correct answer is $3n+O(1)$.

It is trivial that $f(1)=1$ and $f(2)=3$. The values $f(3)=6$ and $f(4)=9$ were established by
Tripathi [Tr14]. Barát and Wanless [BaWa21] proved that $f(5)=13$, and that $13\leq f(6)\leq 18$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_21 : ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, f n ≤ C * n

statements.name: Erdos21.erdos_21.variants.lower
statements.doc: Erdős and Lovász [ErLo75] proved that $\frac{8}{3}n-3\leq f(n)$ for all $n$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_21.variants.lower (n : ℕ) : (8 / 3 : ℝ) * n - 3 ≤ f n

statements.name: Erdos21.erdos_21.variants.three_n
statements.doc: It has been speculated (see e.g. [Ka94]) that the correct answer is $3n+O(1)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_21.variants.three_n : ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    f n ≤ 3 * n + C ∧ 3 * n ≤ f n + C

statements.name: Erdos21.erdos_21.variants.small_values
statements.statement: theorem erdos_21.variants.small_values : f 1 = 1 ∧ f 2 = 3 ∧ f 3 = 6 ∧ f 4 = 9 ∧ f 5 = 13

problems.title: Erdős Problem 22
problems.doc:
The central problem of Ramsey–Turán theory: writing $\mathrm{rt}(n; k, \ell)$ for the maximum
number of edges of a $K_k$-free graph on $n$ vertices whose largest independent set has size
less than $\ell$, is it true that for every $\epsilon > 0$ and all sufficiently large $n$
$$\mathrm{rt}(n; 4, \epsilon n) \geq n^2/8?$$

Conjectured by Bollobás and Erdős [BoEr76], who constructed such a graph with
$(1/8 + o(1))n^2$ edges. Together with the matching upper bound
$\mathrm{rt}(n; 4, \epsilon n) \leq (1/8 + o(1))n^2$ of Szemerédi [Sz72], this determines the
Ramsey–Turán density of $K_4$ to be $1/8$. The conjecture as stated was proved by Fox, Loh,
and Zhao [FLZ15].

*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/22](https://www.erdosproblems.com/22)
* [BoEr76] Bollobás, B. and Erdős, P., *On a Ramsey-Turán type problem*. J. Combin. Theory
  Ser. B 21 (1976), 166--168.
* [Sz72] Szemerédi, E., *On graphs containing no complete subgraph with 4 vertices*
  (Hungarian). Mat. Lapok 23 (1972), 113--116.
* [FLZ15] Fox, J., Loh, P.-S., and Zhao, Y., *The critical window for the classical
  Ramsey-Turán problem*. Combinatorica 35 (2015), 435--476.

statements.name: Erdos22.erdos_22
statements.doc:
Let $\epsilon > 0$ and let $n$ be sufficiently large depending on $\epsilon$. Is there a graph
on $n$ vertices with at least $n^2/8$ many edges which contains no $K_4$, such that the largest
independent set has size at most $\epsilon n$?

This is true, as proved by Fox, Loh, and Zhao [FLZ15].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_22 :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
      ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 ∧
        (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ ε * n ∧ (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 8 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card

statements.name: Erdos22.erdos_22.variants.szemeredi_upper
statements.doc:
The matching upper bound, due to Szemerédi [Sz72]: a $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices whose
independence number is sublinear in $n$ has at most $(1/8 + o(1))n^2$ edges. That is, for every
$\epsilon > 0$ there is a $\delta > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$, every
$K_4$-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $\alpha(G) \leq \delta n$ has at most
$(1/8 + \epsilon)n^2$ edges.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_22.variants.szemeredi_upper (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
      ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 →
        (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ δ * n →
        (G.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) ≤ (1 / 8 + ε) * n ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos22.erdos_22.variants.bollobas_erdos_lower
statements.doc:
The construction of Bollobás and Erdős [BoEr76]: for every $\epsilon > 0$ and $\delta > 0$,
for all sufficiently large $n$ there is a $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices with independence
number at most $\delta n$ and at least $(1/8 - \epsilon)n^2$ edges. Together with
`erdos_22.variants.szemeredi_upper` this shows that the Ramsey–Turán density of $K_4$ is $1/8$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_22.variants.bollobas_erdos_lower (ε δ : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
      ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 ∧
        (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ δ * n ∧ (1 / 8 - ε) * n ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card

statements.name: Erdos22.erdos_22.variants.fox_loh_zhao
statements.doc:
The quantitative strengthening proved by Fox, Loh, and Zhao [FLZ15]: there is a constant
$C > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$ there exists a $K_4$-free graph on $n$
vertices with at least $n^2/8$ edges whose largest independent set has size at most
$$C \cdot \frac{(\log\log n)^{3/2}}{(\log n)^{1/2}} \cdot n.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_22.variants.fox_loh_zhao :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
      ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 ∧
        (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤
          C * (Real.log (Real.log n)) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) / (Real.log n) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) * n ∧
        (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 8 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 23
problems.doc:
*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/23](https://www.erdosproblems.com/23)
* [OEIS A389646](https://oeis.org/A389646)
* [Balogh-Clemen-Lidicky, Max Cuts in Triangle-free Graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14179)
* [McKay, Extremal graphs for bipartization of triangle-free graphs](https://users.cecs.anu.edu.au/~bdm/data/graphs.html)

statements.name: Erdos23.erdos_23.variants.n5
statements.doc:
Every triangle-free graph on $25$ vertices can be made bipartite by removing at most $25$
edges.

This is the $n = 5$ case of Erdős Problem 23.  It follows from the high-density range of
Balogh-Clemen-Lidicky together with McKay's complete catalogue of the 23-vertex extremal
graphs for bipartization of triangle-free graphs.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_23.variants.n5 :
    ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)), G.CliqueFree 3 → ∃ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)),
        H ≤ G ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card ≤ 25

statements.name: Erdos23.erdos_23.variants.n5_tight
statements.doc:
There exists a triangle-free graph on $25$ vertices such that at least $25$ edges must be
removed to make it bipartite.  The balanced blow-up of $C_5$ with five parts of size $5$
witnesses this.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_23.variants.n5_tight :
    ∃ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)), G.CliqueFree 3 ∧ ∀ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)),
        H ≤ G → H.IsBipartite → 25 ≤ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card

statements.name: Erdos23.erdos_23
statements.doc: Can every triangle-free graph on $5n$ vertices be made bipartite by deleting at most $n^2$ edges?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_23 :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Type) [Fintype V], Fintype.card V = 5 * n →
      ∀ (G : SimpleGraph V), G.CliqueFree 3 →
        ∃ (H : SimpleGraph V),
          H ≤ G ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card ≤ n^2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 24
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/24](https://www.erdosproblems.com/24)
- [Er90] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. A tribute to Paul Erdős (1990),
  467-478.
- [Er97b] Erdős, Paul, *Some old and new problems in various branches of combinatorics*. Discrete
  Math. (1997), 227-231.
- [Er92b] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics*.
  Matematiche (Catania) (1992), 231-240.
- [Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability
  (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
- [Gr12] Grzesik, Andrzej, *On the maximum number of five-cycles in a triangle-free graph*.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (2012), 1061-1066.
- [HHKNR13] Hatami, Hamed and Hladký, Jan and Kráľ, Daniel and Norine, Serguei and Razborov,
  Alexander, *On the number of pentagons in triangle-free graphs*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A
  (2013), 722-732.

statements.name: Erdos24.erdos_24
statements.doc:
Does every triangle-free graph on $5n$ vertices contain at most $n^5$ copies of $C_5$?

Győri proved this with $1.03n^5$, which has been improved by Füredi. The answer is yes, as proved
independently by Grzesik [Gr12] and Hatami, Hladky, Král, Norine, and Razborov [HHKNR13].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_24 :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (5 * n))), G.CliqueFree 3 →
      G.copyCount (cycleGraph 5) ≤ n ^ 5

problems.title: Erdős Problem 25: Logarithmic density of size-dependent congruences
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/25](https://www.erdosproblems.com/25)

statements.name: Erdos25.erdos_25
statements.doc:
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an arbitrary sequence of integers, each with an associated residue class
$a_i \pmod{n_i}$. Let $A$ be the set of integers $n$ such that for every $i$ either $n < n_i$ or
$n \not\equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}$. Must the logarithmic density of $A$ exist?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_25 :
    ∀ (seq_n : ℕ → ℕ) (seq_a : ℕ → ℤ), (∀ i, 0 < seq_n i) → StrictMono seq_n →
      ∃ d, Set.HasLogDensity
        { x : ℕ | ∀ i, (x : ℤ) < seq_n i ∨ ¬((x : ℤ) ≡ seq_a i [ZMOD seq_n i]) } d

problems.title: Erdős Problem 26
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/26](https://www.erdosproblems.com/26)
- [Te19](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1908.00488) G. Tenenbaum,
  _Some of Erdős' unconventional problems in number theory, thirty-four years later_,
  arXiv:1908.00488 [math.NT] (2019)

statements.name: Erdos26.erdos_26
statements.doc:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ be infinite such that $\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a} = \infty$. Must
there exist some $k\geq 1$ such that almost all integers have a divisor of the form $a+k$
for some $a\in A$?

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_26 : ¬ ∀ A : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono A → IsThick A →
    ∃ k, IsBehrend (A · + k)

statements.name: Erdos26.erdos_26.variants.rusza
statements.doc: If we allow for $\sum_{a\in A} \frac{1}{a} < \infty$ then Rusza has found a counter-example.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_26.variants.rusza : ∃ A : ℕ → ℕ,
    StrictMono A ∧ ¬IsThick A ∧ ∀ k, ¬IsBehrend (A · + k)

statements.name: Erdos26.erdos_26.variants.tenenbaum
statements.doc:
Tenenbaum asked the weaker variant where for every $\epsilon>0$ there is
some $k=k(\epsilon)$ such that at least $1-\epsilon$ density of all integers have a
divisor of the form $a+k$ for some $a\in A$.

The DeepMind prover agent has found a formal disproof of this statement.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_26.variants.tenenbaum : ¬ ∀ᵉ (A : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono A → IsThick A →
    (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ k, IsWeaklyBehrend (A · + k) ε)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 28
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/28](https://www.erdosproblems.com/28)

statements.name: Erdos28.erdos_28
statements.doc:
If $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ is such that $A + A$ contains all but finitely many integers then
 $\limsup 1_A ∗ 1_A(n) = \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_28 (A : Set ℕ) (h : (A + A)ᶜ.Finite) :
    limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => (sumRep A n : ℕ∞)) atTop = (⊤ : ℕ∞)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 29
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/29](https://www.erdosproblems.com/29)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Er89d] Erdős, P., *Some old and new problems on additive and combinatorial number theory*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics: Proceedings of the Third International Conference (New York, 1985)
  (1989), 181-186.
- [Er95] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and
  geometry*. Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
- [Er97c] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*. The mathematics of Paul Erdős,
  I (1997), 47-67.
- [JPSZ24] Jain, V. and Pham, H. T. and Sawhney, M. and Zakharov, D., *An explicit economical
  additive basis*. arXiv:2405.08650 (2024).

statements.name: Erdos29.erdos_29
statements.doc:
Is there an explicit construction of a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that $A+A=\mathbb{N}$ but
$1_A\ast 1_A(n)=o(n^\epsilon)$ for every $\epsilon>0$?

The existence of such a set was asked by Sidon to Erdős in 1932. Erdős (eventually) proved the
existence of such a set using probabilistic methods. This problem asks for a constructive
solution. An explicit construction was given by Jain, Pham, Sawhney, and Zakharov [JPSZ24].

The formal statement records the existence of such a set; the linked formal proof exhibits an
explicit construction.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_29 : ∃ A : Set ℕ, A + A = Set.univ ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
    (fun n : ℕ => (sumRep A n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ ε

problems.title: Erdős Problem 30
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/30](https://www.erdosproblems.com/30)
- [ErTu41] Erdős, P. and Turán, P., *On a problem of Sidon in additive number theory, and on
  some related problems*. J. London Math. Soc. 16 (1941), 212-215.
- [Li69] Lindström, B., *An inequality for $B_2$-sequences*. J. Combinatorial Theory 6 (1969),
  211-212.
- [Si38] Singer, J., *A theorem in finite projective geometry and some applications to number
  theory*. Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 43 (1938), 377-385.
- [BFR23] Balogh, J., Füredi, Z. and Roy, S., *An upper bound on the size of Sidon sets*.
  Amer. Math. Monthly 130 (2023), 437-445.
- [OB22] O'Bryant, K., *On the size of finite Sidon sets*.
  [arXiv:2207.07800](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07800) (2022).
- [CHO25] Carter, D., Hunter, Z. and O'Bryant, K., *On the diameter of finite Sidon sets*.
  Acta Math. Hungar. 175 (2025), 108-126.

See also [Ben Green's Open Problem 31](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf)
(formalised in `FormalConjectures/GreensOpenProblems/31.lean`).

statements.name: Erdos30.erdos_30
statements.doc: Is it true that, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $h(N) = \sqrt N + O_{\varepsilon}(N^\varepsilon)$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_30 :
    ∀ᵉ (ε > 0), (fun N => h N - (N : Real).sqrt) =O[atTop] fun N => (N : ℝ)^(ε : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos30.erdos_30.variants.O_one
statements.doc:
A stronger conjecture: is it true that $h(N) = \sqrt N + O(1)$?
Erdős thought this was perhaps too optimistic.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_30.variants.O_one :
    (fun N => h N - (N : ℝ).sqrt) =O[atTop] fun _ => (1 : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos30.erdos_30.variants.erdos_turan
statements.doc:
Erdős and Turán [ErTu41] proved $h(N) \le \sqrt N + O(N^{1/4})$.

This is an upper bound only. A statement with `=O` would also assert the lower bound
$h(N) \ge \sqrt N - O(N^{1/4})$, which is not part of this result.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_30.variants.erdos_turan :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, (h N : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ).sqrt + C * (N : ℝ) ^ (4⁻¹ : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos30.erdos_30.variants.lindstrom
statements.doc:
The proofs of Erdős–Turán [ErTu41] and Lindström [Li69] in fact give, for all $N$,
$h(N) \le N^{1/2} + N^{1/4} + 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_30.variants.lindstrom (N : ℕ) :
    (h N : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ).sqrt + (N : ℝ) ^ (4⁻¹ : ℝ) + 1

statements.name: Erdos30.erdos_30.variants.balogh_furedi_roy
statements.doc:
Balogh, Füredi and Roy [BFR23] proved $h(N) \le N^{1/2} + 0.998 N^{1/4}$ for all sufficiently
large $N$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_30.variants.balogh_furedi_roy :
    ∀ᶠ N in atTop, (h N : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ).sqrt + (0.998 : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (4⁻¹ : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos30.erdos_30.variants.obryant
statements.doc: O'Bryant [OB22] proved $h(N) \le N^{1/2} + 0.99703 N^{1/4}$ for all sufficiently large $N$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_30.variants.obryant :
    ∀ᶠ N in atTop, (h N : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ).sqrt + (0.99703 : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (4⁻¹ : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos30.erdos_30.variants.carter_hunter_obryant
statements.doc:
Carter, Hunter and O'Bryant [CHO25] proved $h(N) \le N^{1/2} + 0.98183 N^{1/4} + O(1)$.
This is the current record upper bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_30.variants.carter_hunter_obryant :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ N in atTop,
      (h N : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ).sqrt + (0.98183 : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (4⁻¹ : ℝ) + C

statements.name: Erdos30.erdos_30.variants.singer
statements.doc: Singer's construction [Si38] shows $h(N) \ge (1 - o(1)) N^{1/2}$ for all $N$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_30.variants.singer :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (1 - ε) * (N : ℝ).sqrt ≤ h N

statements.name: Erdos30.erdos_30.variants.isEquivalent_sqrt
statements.doc:
Combining Singer's lower bound [Si38] with the Erdős–Turán upper bound [ErTu41]:
$h(N) \sim N^{1/2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_30.variants.isEquivalent_sqrt :
    (fun N => (h N : ℝ)) ~[atTop] fun N => (N : ℝ).sqrt

statements.name: Erdos30.erdos_30.variants.elementary_difference_count
statements.doc:
The counting argument of Erdős and Turán [ErTu41]: a Sidon set $A \subseteq \{0, \dots, N\}$
has $|A|(|A| - 1) \le 2N$, because the $|A|(|A|-1)/2$ positive differences of $A$ are distinct
and lie in $\{1, \dots, N\}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_30.variants.elementary_difference_count (A : Finset ℕ) (N : ℕ)
    (hS : IsSidon (A : Set ℕ)) (hA : A ⊆ Finset.range (N + 1)) :
    A.card * (A.card - 1) ≤ 2 * N

statements.name: Erdos30.erdos_30.variants.distinct_sums_card
statements.doc:
For a Sidon set $A$, $|A + A| = |A|(|A|+1)/2$: the sums $a + b$ with $a \le b$ are pairwise
distinct [ErTu41].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_30.variants.distinct_sums_card (A : Finset ℕ) (hS : IsSidon (A : Set ℕ)) :
    (A + A).card = A.card * (A.card + 1) / 2

statements.name: Erdos30.erdos_30.variants.distinct_sums_in_range
