statements.doc: If $A \subseteq \{0, \dots, N\}$ then $A + A \subseteq \{0, \dots, 2N\}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_30.variants.distinct_sums_in_range (A : Finset ℕ) (N : ℕ)
    (hA : A ⊆ Finset.range (N + 1)) :
    A + A ⊆ Finset.range (2 * N + 1)

statements.name: Erdos30.erdos_30.variants.erdos_turan_counting
statements.doc:
The counting bound of Erdős and Turán [ErTu41] in its sum form: a Sidon set
$A \subseteq \{0, \dots, N\}$ has $|A|(|A| + 1)/2 \le 2N + 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_30.variants.erdos_turan_counting (A : Finset ℕ) (N : ℕ)
    (hS : IsSidon (A : Set ℕ)) (hA : A ⊆ Finset.range (N + 1)) :
    A.card * (A.card + 1) / 2 ≤ 2 * N + 1

statements.name: Erdos30.erdos_30.variants.lindstrom_weak
statements.doc:
A weak form of Lindström's bound [Li69], following from
`erdos_30.variants.elementary_difference_count`: a Sidon set $A \subseteq \{0, \dots, N\}$
has $|A| \le \lfloor \sqrt{2N} \rfloor + 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_30.variants.lindstrom_weak (A : Finset ℕ) (N : ℕ)
    (hS : IsSidon (A : Set ℕ)) (hA : A ⊆ Finset.range (N + 1)) :
    A.card ≤ Nat.sqrt (2 * N) + 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 31
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/31](https://www.erdosproblems.com/31)
- [Er56] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in additive number theory*. Colloque sur la Théorie des
  Nombres, Bruxelles, 1955 (1956), 127-137.
- [Er59] Erdős, P., *Über einige Probleme der additiven Zahlentheorie*. Sammelband zu Ehren des 250.
  Geburtstages Leonhard Eulers (1959), 116-119.
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [Er73] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of combinatorial
  theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971) (1973), 117-138.
- [Lo54] Lorentz, G. G., *On a problem of additive number theory*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (1954), 838-841.

statements.name: Erdos31.erdos_31
statements.doc:
Given any infinite set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ there is a set $B$ of density $0$ such that $A+B$ contains all except finitely many integers.

Conjectured by Erdős and Straus. Proved by Lorentz [Lo54].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_31 : ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite →
    ∃ B : Set ℕ, B.HasDensity 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ A + B

problems.title: Erdős Problem 32
problems.doc:
*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/32](https://www.erdosproblems.com/32)
* [Erd54] Erdős, Paul, Some results on additive number theory. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1954),
 847-853.
* [Guy04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437
* [Ru98c] Ruzsa, Imre Z., On the additive completion of primes. Acta Arith. (1998), 269-275.

statements.name: Erdos32.erdos_32.variants.log_squared
statements.doc:
Erdős proved in [Erd54] that there exists an additive complement $A$ to the primes with
$|A \cap \{1, \ldots, N\}| = O((\log N)^2)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_32.variants.log_squared : ∃ A : Set ℕ,
    IsAdditiveComplementToPrimes A ∧
    (fun N => (((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (· ∈ A)).card : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      fun N => (Real.log N) ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos32.erdos_32.variants.liminf_gt_one
statements.doc:
Must every additive complement $A$ to the primes satisfy
$\liminf_{N \to \infty} \frac{|A \cap \{1, \ldots, N\}|}{\log N} > 1$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_32.variants.liminf_gt_one : ∀ A : Set ℕ,
    IsAdditiveComplementToPrimes A →
    (1 : EReal) < liminf (fun N => (((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (· ∈ A)).card / Real.log N : EReal))
      atTop

statements.name: Erdos32.erdos_32
statements.doc:
Does there exist a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that $|A \cap \{1, \ldots, N\}| = o((\log N)^2)$
and every sufficiently large integer can be written as $p + a$ for some prime $p$ and $a \in A$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_32 : ∃ A : Set ℕ,
    IsAdditiveComplementToPrimes A ∧
    (fun N => (((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (· ∈ A)).card : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      fun N => (Real.log N) ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos32.erdos_32.variants.log_bound
statements.doc:
Can the bound $O(\log N)$ be achieved for an additive complement to the primes? [Guy04] writes
that Erdős offered \$50 for the solution.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_32.variants.log_bound : ∃ A : Set ℕ,
    IsAdditiveComplementToPrimes A ∧
    (fun N => (((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (· ∈ A)).card : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      fun N => Real.log N

statements.name: Erdos32.erdos_32.variants.ruzsa
statements.doc:
Ruzsa proved that any additive complement $A$ to the primes must satisfy
$\liminf_{N \to \infty} \frac{|A \cap \{1, \ldots, N\}|}{\log N} \geq e^\gamma$,
where $\gamma$ is the Euler-Mascheroni constant.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_32.variants.ruzsa : ∀ A : Set ℕ,
    IsAdditiveComplementToPrimes A →
    (Real.exp Real.eulerMascheroniConstant : EReal) ≤
      liminf (fun N => (((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (· ∈ A)).card / Real.log N : EReal)) atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 33
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/33](https://www.erdosproblems.com/33)

statements.name: Erdos33.erdos_33
statements.doc:
Let `A ⊆ ℕ` be a set such that every integer can be written as `n^2 + a`
for some `a` in `A` and `n ≥ 0`. What is the smallest possible value of
`lim sup n → ∞ |A ∩ {1, …, N}| / N^(1/2)`?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_33 : ⨅ A : {A : Set ℕ | AdditiveBasisCondition A}, Filter.atTop.limsup (fun N =>
    (A.1 ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard / (√N : EReal)) = erdos_33.answer

statements.name: Erdos33.erdos_33.variants.one_mem_lowerBounds
statements.doc:
Erdos observed that this value is finite and > 1. This records the lower bound `> 1`,
i.e. that `1` is a strict lower bound for every admissible `A`; the finiteness is
`erdos_33.variants.vanDoorn`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_33.variants.one_mem_lowerBounds :
    1 < ⨅ A : {A : Set ℕ | AdditiveBasisCondition A}, Filter.atTop.limsup (fun N =>
      (A.1 ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard / (√N : EReal))

statements.name: Erdos33.erdos_33.variants.vanDoorn
statements.doc:
The smallest possible value of `lim sup n → ∞ |A ∩ {1, …, N}| / N^(1/2)`
is at most `2φ^(5/2) ≈ 6.66`, with `φ` equal to the golden ratio. Proven by
Wouter van Doorn.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_33.variants.vanDoorn :
    ⨅ A : {A : Set ℕ | AdditiveBasisCondition A}, Filter.atTop.limsup (fun N =>
    (A.1 ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard / (√N : EReal)) ≤ ↑(2 * (φ ^ ((5 : ℝ) / 2)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 34
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/34](https://www.erdosproblems.com/34)
- [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III*. Number theory day
  (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [He86] Hegyvári, N., *On consecutive sums in sequences*. Acta Math. Hungar. (1986),
  193--200.
- [Ko15] Konieczny, J., *On consecutive sums in permutations*. arXiv:1504.07156 (2015).

statements.name: Erdos34.erdos_34
statements.doc:
For any permutation $\pi\in S_n$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ let $S(\pi)$ count the number of distinct consecutive sums, that is, sums of the shape $\sum_{u\leq i\leq v}\pi(i)$. Is it true that
$$
S(\pi) = o(n^2)
$$
for all $\pi\in S_n$?

Hegyvári [He86] gave a counterexample.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_34 :
    ¬ ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ p : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
      ((consecutiveSums n p).card : ℝ) < c * (n : ℝ) ^ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 35
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/35](https://www.erdosproblems.com/35)
- [Er56] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in additive number theory*. Colloque sur la Théorie des
  Nombres, Bruxelles, 1955 (1956), 127-137.
- [Er36c] Erdős, P., *On the arithmetical density of the sum of two sequences, one of which forms
  a basis for the integers*. Acta. Arith. (1936), 197-200.
- [Pl70] Plünnecke, H., *Eine zahlentheoretische Anwendung der Graphentheorie*. J. Reine. Angew.
  Math. (1970), 171-183.

statements.name: Erdos35.erdos_35
statements.doc:
Let $B\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an additive basis of order $k$ with $0\in B$. Is it true that for
every $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ we have
$$d_s(A+B)\geq \alpha+\frac{\alpha(1-\alpha)}{k},$$
where $\alpha=d_s(A)$ and
$$d_s(A) = \inf \frac{\lvert A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}{N}$$
is the Schnirelmann density?

Erdős [Er36c] proved this is true with $k$ replaced by $2k$ in the denominator (in a stronger form
that only considers $A\cup (A+b)$ for some $b\in B$, see [38](https://www.erdosproblems.com/38)).

Ruzsa has observed that this follows immediately from the stronger fact proved by Plünnecke
[Pl70] that (under the same assumptions, and for $\alpha>0$)
$$d_S(A+B)\geq \alpha^{1-1/k}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_35 : ∀ (B : Set ℕ) (k : ℕ), 0 ∈ B → B.IsAddBasisOfOrder k →
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, schnirelmannDensity A +
      schnirelmannDensity A * (1 - schnirelmannDensity A) / k ≤ schnirelmannDensity (A + B)

statements.name: Erdos35.erdos_35.variants.plunnecke
statements.doc:
Plünnecke [Pl70] proved that if $B\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ is an additive basis of order $k$ with
$0\in B$ then $d_S(A+B)\geq d_s(A)^{1-1/k}$ for every $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ with $d_s(A)>0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_35.variants.plunnecke (B : Set ℕ) (k : ℕ) (h0 : 0 ∈ B) (hB : B.IsAddBasisOfOrder k)
    (A : Set ℕ) (hA : 0 < schnirelmannDensity A) :
    schnirelmannDensity A ^ (1 - (k : ℝ)⁻¹) ≤ schnirelmannDensity (A + B)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 36
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/36](https://www.erdosproblems.com/36)
 - [Wikipedial: Minimum overlap problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_overlap_problem)

statements.name: Erdos36.minimum_overlap.variants.lower.erdos_1955
statements.doc:
A lower bound of $\frac 1 4$.
See [Some remarks on number theory (in Hebrew)](https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1955-13.pdf)
by *Paul Erdős*, Riveon Lematematika 9, p.45-48,1955
statements.statement:
theorem minimum_overlap.variants.lower.erdos_1955 :
    (1 : ℝ) / 4 ≤ atTop.liminf MinOverlapQuotient

statements.name: Erdos36.minimum_overlap.variants.lower.scherk_1955
statements.doc:
A lower bound of $1 - frac{1}{\sqrt 2}$.
Scherk (written communication), see
[On the minimal overlap problem of Erdös](https://eudml.org/doc/206397)
by *Leo Moser*, Аста Аrithmetica V, p. 117-119, 1959
statements.statement:
theorem minimum_overlap.variants.lower.scherk_1955 :
    1 - (√2)⁻¹ < atTop.liminf MinOverlapQuotient

statements.name: Erdos36.minimum_overlap.variants.lower.swierczkowski_1958
statements.doc:
A lower bound of $\frac{4 - \sqrt{6}}{5}$.
See [On the intersection of a linear set with the translation of its complement](https://bibliotekanauki.pl/articles/969027)
by *Stanisław Świerczkowski1*, Colloquium Mathematicum 5(2), p. 185-197, 1958
statements.statement:
theorem minimum_overlap.variants.lower.swierczkowski_1958 :
    (4 - 6 ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2)) / 5 < atTop.liminf MinOverlapQuotient

statements.name: Erdos36.minimum_overlap.variants.lower.haugland_1996
statements.doc: A lower bound of $\sqrt{4 - \sqrt{15}}$.
statements.statement:
theorem minimum_overlap.variants.lower.haugland_1996 :
    (4 - 15 ^((1 : ℝ) / 2)) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2) < atTop.liminf MinOverlapQuotient

statements.name: Erdos36.minimum_overlap.variants.lower.white_2022
statements.doc:
A lower bound of $0.379005$: the minimum overlap constant is at least $0.379005$.
See [Erdős' minimum overlap problem](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.05704)
by *Ethan Patrick White*, 2022
statements.statement:
theorem minimum_overlap.variants.lower.white_2022 :
    0.379005 ≤ atTop.liminf MinOverlapQuotient

statements.name: Erdos36.minimum_overlap.variants.upper.erdos_1955
statements.doc:
The example (with $N$ even), $A = \{\frac N 2 + 1, \dots, \frac{3N}{2}\}$
shows an upper bound of $\frac 1 2$.
statements.statement:
theorem minimum_overlap.variants.upper.erdos_1955 :
    atTop.limsup MinOverlapQuotient ≤ (1 : ℝ) / 2

statements.name: Erdos36.minimum_overlap.variants.upper.MRS_1956
statements.doc:
An upper bound of $\frac 2 5$.
See [Minimal overlapping under translation.](https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bulletin-of-the-american-mathematical-society/volume-62/issue-6)
by *T. S. Motzkin*, *K. E. Ralston* and *J. L. Selfridge*,
in "The summer meeting in Seattle" by *V. L. Klee Jr.*, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.62, p. 558, 1956
statements.statement:
theorem minimum_overlap.variants.upper.MRS_1956 :
    atTop.limsup MinOverlapQuotient ≤ (2 : ℝ) / 5

statements.name: Erdos36.minimum_overlap.variants.upper.haugland_1996
statements.doc:
An upper bound of $0.38200298812318988$.
See [Advances in the Minimum Overlap Problem](https://doi.org/10.1006%2Fjnth.1996.0064)
by *Jan Kristian Haugland*, Journal of Number Theory Volume 58, Issue 1, p 71-78, 1996
statements.statement:
theorem minimum_overlap.variants.upper.haugland_1996 :
    atTop.limsup MinOverlapQuotient ≤ 0.38200298812318988

statements.name: Erdos36.minimum_overlap.variants.upper.haugland_2022
statements.doc:
An upper bound of $0.3809268534330870$.
See [The minimum overlap problem](https://www.neutreeko.net/mop/index.htm)
by *Jan Kristian Haugland*
statements.statement:
theorem minimum_overlap.variants.upper.haugland_2022 :
    atTop.limsup MinOverlapQuotient ≤ 0.3809268534330870

statements.name: Erdos36.erdos_36.variants.lower
statements.doc: Find a better lower bound!
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_36.variants.lower:
    ∃ (c : ℝ), 0.379005 < c ∧ c ≤ atTop.liminf MinOverlapQuotient ∧ c =
      erdos_36.variants.lower.answer

statements.name: Erdos36.erdos_36.variants.upper
statements.doc: Find a better upper bound!
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_36.variants.upper :
    ∃ (c : ℝ), c < 0.380926853433087 ∧ atTop.limsup MinOverlapQuotient ≤ c ∧ c =
      erdos_36.variants.upper.answer

statements.name: Erdos36.erdos_36.variants.exists
statements.doc: The limit of `MinOverlapQuotient` exists and it is less than $0.385694$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_36.variants.exists : ∃ c, atTop.Tendsto MinOverlapQuotient (𝓝 c) ∧ c < 0.385694

statements.name: Erdos36.erdos_36
statements.doc: Find the value of the limit of `MinOverlapQuotient`!
statements.statement: theorem erdos_36 : atTop.Tendsto MinOverlapQuotient (𝓝 erdos_36.answer)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 38
problems.doc:
*Reference:*
- [erdosproblems.com/38](https://www.erdosproblems.com/38)
- [Er56](Erdős, P., Problems and results in additive number theory.
  Colloque sur la Théorie des Nombres, Bruxelles, 1955 (1956), 127-137.)

statements.name: Erdos38.erdos_38
statements.doc:
Does there exist $B \subset \mathbb{N}$ which is not an additive basis,
but is such that for every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of Schnirelmann density $\alpha$
and every $N$ there exists $b \in B$ such that
$$
  \lvert (A \cup (A+b)) \cap \{1, \ldots, N\} \rvert \geq (\alpha + f(\alpha)) N
$$
where $f(\alpha) > 0$ for $0 < \alpha < 1$?

Note: here Erdős seems to use a slightly weaker notion of an additive basis (see [Er56] at the top
of page 135). In particular, for this problem, a set is an additive basis of order $k$ if every
natural number can be written as a sum of _at most_ $k$ elements of the set, rather than as a sum of
_precisely_ $k$ elements.

A positive [solution](https://github.com/spicylemonade/erdos-38) was given by GPT 5.5 Pro
(prompted by gebyjaff, cleanup by Liam Price); in fact a sparse random set $B$ has this property,
with $f(\alpha)\gg \alpha (1-\alpha)^2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_38 :
    ∃ B : Set ℕ, ¬ B.IsWeakAddBasis ∧ ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, (∀ α, 0 < α → α < 1 → f α > 0) ∧
      ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ),
        let α := schnirelmannDensity A
        ∃ b ∈ B, (Ioc 0 N ∩ (A ∪ (A + {b}))).ncard ≥ (α + f α) * N

problems.title: Erdős Problem 39
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/39](https://www.erdosproblems.com/39)

statements.name: Erdos39.erdos_39
statements.doc:
Is there an infinite Sidon set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ such that
$\lvert A\cap \{1\ldots,N\}\rvert \gg_\epsilon N^{1/2-\epsilon}$
for all $\varepsilon > 0$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_39 : ∃ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite ∧ IsSidon A ∧
    ∀ᵉ  (ε  > (0 : ℝ)),
    (· ^ (1 / 2 - ε) : ℕ → ℝ) =O[atTop] fun N => (((Set.Icc 1 N) ∩ A).ncard : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 40
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/40](https://www.erdosproblems.com/40)

statements.name: Erdos40.erdos_40
statements.doc:
For what functions $g(N) → \infty$ is it true that
$$\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \gg \frac{N^{1/2}}{g(N)}$$
implies $\limsup 1_A\ast 1_A(n)=\infty$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_40 :
    {g : ℕ → ℝ | Tendsto g atTop atTop ∧ Erdos40For g} = erdos_40.answer

statements.name: Erdos40.erdos_40.variants.weaker
statements.doc:
Is there any function $g(N) → \infty$ such that
$$\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \gg \frac{N^{1/2}}{g(N)}$$
implies $\limsup 1_A\ast 1_A(n)=\infty$?

This is a weaker form of Erdős Problem 40, which asks for all such $g$. Establishing
the implication for even one $g(N) → \infty$ already answers Erdős Problem 28
positively, because a basis of order $2$ satisfies
$\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \gg N^{1/2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_40.variants.weaker :
    ∃ g : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto g atTop atTop ∧ Erdos40For g

statements.name: Erdos40.erdos_40.variants.implies_erdos_28
statements.doc:
Establishing the property in Erdős Problem 40 for any one function $g(N) → \infty$
implies the Erdős-Turán conjecture, see Erdős Problem 28.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_40.variants.implies_erdos_28 (g : ℕ → ℝ) (hg : Tendsto g atTop atTop)
    (h_erdos_40 : Erdos40For g) : type_of% Erdos28.erdos_28

problems.title: Erdős Problem 41
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/41](https://www.erdosproblems.com/41)

statements.name: Erdos41.erdos_41
statements.doc:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that the triple sums $a+b+c$ are all distinct
for $a,b,c \in A$ (aside from the trivial coincidences). Is it true that
$$\liminf_{N \to \infty} \frac{\lvert A \cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}{N^{1/3}}=0?$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_41 (A : Set ℕ) (h_triple : NtupleCondition A 3) (h_infinite : A.Infinite) :
    Filter.atTop.liminf (fun N => (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard / (N : ℝ)^(1/3 : ℝ)) = 0

statements.name: Erdos41.erdos_41.variants.pairwise
statements.doc:
Erdős proved that if the pairwise sums $a+b$ are all distinct aside from the trivial
coincidences, then
$$\liminf_{N \to \infty} \frac{\lvert A \cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}{N^{1/2}}=0.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_41.variants.pairwise (A : Set ℕ) (hA₂ : NtupleCondition A 2) (hA : A.Infinite) :
    Filter.atTop.liminf (fun N => (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard / (N : ℝ).sqrt) = 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 42: Maximal Sidon Sets and Disjoint Difference Sets
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/42](https://www.erdosproblems.com/42)

This problem asks whether maximal Sidon sets can coexist with other Sidon sets that have
disjoint difference sets (apart from 0).

statements.name: Erdos42.erdos_42
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 42**: Let M ≥ 1 and N be sufficiently large in terms of M. Is it true that for every
maximal Sidon set `A ⊆ {1,…,N}` there is another Sidon set `B ⊆ {1,…,N}` of size M such that
`(A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0}`?

This was proved for all $M$ by GPT 5.5 Pro (prompted by Sandhu), see discussion thread for more details.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_42 :
    ∀ M ≥ 1, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (_ : IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N),
    ∃ᵉ (B : Set ℕ), B ⊆ Set.Icc 1 N ∧ IsSidon B ∧ B.ncard = M ∧
    ((A - A) ∩ (B - B)) = {0}

statements.name: Erdos42.erdos_42.variants.constructive
statements.doc:
A variant asking for explicit bounds on how large N needs to be in terms of M.

This version provides a constructive function f such that for all M ≥ 1 and N ≥ f(M),
every maximal Sidon set A ⊆ {1,…,N} has another Sidon set B ⊆ {1,…,N} of size M with
disjoint difference sets (apart from 0).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_42.variants.constructive :
    ∃ (f : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ (M N : ℕ) (_ : 1 ≤ M) (_ : f M ≤ N),
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (_ : IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N), ∃ᵉ (B : Set ℕ),
      B ⊆ Set.Icc 1 N ∧ IsSidon B ∧ B.ncard = M ∧
      ((A - A) ∩ (B - B)) = {0}

statements.name: Erdos42.example_maximal_sidon
statements.doc: The set `{1, 2, 4}` is a maximal Sidon set in `{1, ..., 4}`.
statements.statement: theorem example_maximal_sidon : IsMaximalSidonSetIn {1, 2, 4} 4

statements.name: Erdos42.example_difference_set
statements.doc: The difference set of `{1, 2, 4}` is `{0, 1, 2, 3}`.
statements.statement: theorem example_difference_set : ({1, 2, 4} : Set ℕ) - {1, 2, 4} = {0, 1, 2, 3}

statements.name: Erdos42.maximal_sidon_contains_zero
statements.doc: For any maximal Sidon set, the difference set contains 0.
statements.statement:
theorem maximal_sidon_contains_zero (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (hA : IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N) : 0 ∈ A - A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 43
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/43](https://www.erdosproblems.com/43)

statements.name: Erdos43.erdos_43.parts.i
statements.doc:
If $A$ and $B$ are Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$(A-A)\cap(B-B)=\{0\}$, is it true that
$$\binom{\lvert A\rvert}{2}+\binom{\lvert B\rvert}{2}\leq\binom{f(N)}{2}+O(1)?$$

The answer is no; the Erdős Problems page notes that this follows from the solution to
Erdős Problem 42.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_43.parts.i :
    ¬ ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, ∀ (A B : Finset ℕ),
      A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) →
      IsSidon (B : Set ℕ) →
      (A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0} →
      ((A.card.choose 2 + B.card.choose 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ ((f N).choose 2 : ℝ) + C

statements.name: Erdos43.erdos_43.parts.ii
statements.doc:
If $A$ and $B$ are equal-sized Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$(A-A)\cap(B-B)=\{0\}$, can the bound be improved to
$$\binom{\lvert A\rvert}{2}+\binom{\lvert B\rvert}{2}
    \leq (1-c+o(1))\binom{f(N)}{2}$$
for some constant $c>0$?

The answer is no; the Erdős Problems page records a negative answer due to Barreto.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_43.parts.ii :
    ¬ ∃ᵉ (c > 0), ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[Filter.atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, ∀ (A B : Finset ℕ),
      A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) →
      IsSidon (B : Set ℕ) →
      A.card = B.card →
      (A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0} →
      ((A.card.choose 2 + B.card.choose 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤
        (1 - c + o N) * ((f N).choose 2 : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 44: Extending Sidon Sets
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/44](https://www.erdosproblems.com/44)
- [Si38] Singer, James, A theorem in finite projective geometry and some applications to number
  theory. Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. (1938), 377--385.

statements.name: Erdos44.maxSidonSubsetCard_icc_bound
statements.doc: The maximum size of a Sidon set in `{1, ..., N}` is less than or equal to `2 * √N`.
statements.statement:
theorem maxSidonSubsetCard_icc_bound (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    maxSidonSubsetCard (Icc 1 N) ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt N

statements.name: Erdos44.erdos_44
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 44:** Let N ≥ 1 and `A ⊆ {1,…,N}` be a Sidon set. Is it true that, for any ε > 0,
there exist M = M(ε) and `B ⊆ {N+1,…,M}` such that `A ∪ B ⊆ {1,…,M}` is a Sidon set
of size at least `(1−ε)M^{1/2}`?

This problem asks whether any Sidon set can be extended to achieve a density
arbitrarily close to the optimal density for Sidon sets.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_44 : ∀ᵉ (N ≥ (1 : ℕ)) (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) →
    ∀ᵉ (ε > (0 : ℝ)), ∃ᵉ (M > N) (B ⊆ Finset.Icc (N + 1) M),
      IsSidon (A ∪ B : Set ℕ) ∧ (1 - ε) * Real.sqrt M ≤ (A ∪ B).card

statements.name: Erdos44.erdos_44.variants.empty_start
statements.doc:
The case where we start with an empty set (constructing large Sidon sets).

The answer is yes. Singer [Si38] constructed Sidon sets of size $q + 1$ in
$\{1, \ldots, q^2 + q + 1\}$ for every prime $q$. Since $p_{n+1}/p_n \to 1$ for consecutive primes,
this gives Sidon sets of size $(1 - o(1))M^{1/2}$ in $\{1, \ldots, M\}$ for every $M$; see
[erdosproblems.com/30](https://www.erdosproblems.com/30).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_44.variants.empty_start : ∀ᵉ (ε > (0 : ℝ)), ∀ᶠ (M : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ᵉ (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 M), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) ∧ (1 - ε) * Real.sqrt M ≤ A.card

statements.name: Erdos44.example_sidon_set
statements.doc: The set `{1, 2, 4, 8, 13}` is a Sidon set in `{1, ..., 13}`.
statements.statement: theorem example_sidon_set : IsSidon ({1, 2, 4, 8, 13} : Set ℕ)

statements.name: Erdos44.sidon_set_lower_bound
statements.doc: For any `N`, there exists a Sidon set of size at least `√N/2`.
statements.statement:
theorem sidon_set_lower_bound (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    ∃ᵉ (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) ∧ Real.sqrt N / 2 ≤ A.card

statements.name: Erdos44.greedy_sidon_construction
statements.doc:
The greedy construction gives a Sidon set `A ⊆ {1, ..., N}` of size at least $N^{1/3}$,
stated here as $N \le |A|^3$. See Section 1 of [arXiv:2103.15850](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.15850).
statements.statement:
theorem greedy_sidon_construction (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    ∃ᵉ (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) ∧ N ≤ A.card ^ 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 45
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/45](https://www.erdosproblems.com/45)
- [Er95] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and geometry*.
  Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
- [Er96b] Erdős, Paul, *Some problems I presented or planned to present in my short talk*. Analytic
  number theory, Vol. 1 (Allerton Park, IL, 1995) (1996), 333-335.
- [Cr03] Croot, III, Ernest S., *On a coloring conjecture about unit fractions*. Ann. of Math. (2)
  (2003), 545-556.
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.

statements.name: Erdos45.erdos_45
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 2$. Is there an integer $n_k$ such that, if $D=\{ 1<d<n_k : d\mid n_k\}$, then for any
$k$-colouring of $D$ there is a monochromatic subset $D'\subseteq D$ such that
$\sum_{d\in D'}\frac{1}{d}=1$?

This follows from the colouring result of Croot [Cr03]. Croot's result allows for
$n_k \leq e^{C^k}$ for some constant $C>1$ (simply taking $n_k$ to be the lowest common multiple of
some interval $[1,C^k]$). Sawhney has observed that there is also a doubly exponential lower bound,
and hence this bound is essentially sharp.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_45 :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ colouring : ℕ → Fin k,
      ∃ colour : Fin k, ∃ D' ⊆ {d ∈ n.divisors | 1 < d ∧ d < n},
        (∀ d ∈ D', colouring d = colour) ∧ D'.reciprocalSum = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 46
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/46](https://www.erdosproblems.com/46)
- [Cr03] Croot, III, Ernest S., *On a coloring conjecture about unit fractions*. Ann. of Math. (2)
  (2003), 545-556.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).

statements.name: Erdos46.erdos_46
statements.doc:
Does every finite colouring of the integers have a monochromatic solution to
$1=\sum \frac{1}{n_i}$ with $2\leq n_1<\cdots <n_k$?

The answer is yes, as proved by Croot [Cr03] - indeed, there are infinitely many disjoint such
monochromatic solutions.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_46 :
    -- For any finite colouring of the integers
    ∀ (𝓒 : ℕ → ℕ), (Set.range 𝓒).Finite →
      -- there are integers `2 ≤ n₁ < ⋯ < n_k`
      ∃ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ S, 2 ≤ n) ∧
        -- whose reciprocals sum to `1`
        ∑ n ∈ S, (1 / n : ℚ) = 1 ∧
        -- and which all have the same colour
        (𝓒 '' (S : Set ℕ)).Subsingleton

statements.name: Erdos46.erdos_46.variants.infinitely_many_disjoint
statements.doc: Croot [Cr03] proved more: there are infinitely many disjoint such monochromatic solutions.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_46.variants.infinitely_many_disjoint :
    ∀ (𝓒 : ℕ → ℕ), (Set.range 𝓒).Finite →
      ∃ S : ℕ → Finset ℕ, (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (S i) (S j)) ∧
        ∀ i, (∀ n ∈ S i, 2 ≤ n) ∧ ∑ n ∈ S i, (1 / n : ℚ) = 1 ∧
          (𝓒 '' (S i : Set ℕ)).Subsingleton

statements.name: Erdos46.erdos_46.variants.positive_rat
statements.doc: In [ErGr80] they also ask for a monochromatic representation of any $\frac{a}{b}>0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_46.variants.positive_rat :
    ∀ (𝓒 : ℕ → ℕ), (Set.range 𝓒).Finite → ∀ q : ℚ, 0 < q →
      ∃ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ S, 2 ≤ n) ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, (1 / n : ℚ) = q ∧
        (𝓒 '' (S : Set ℕ)).Subsingleton

problems.title: Erdős Problem 47
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/47](https://www.erdosproblems.com/47)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my forgotten problems in number theory*. Hardy-Ramanujan J. (1992),
  34-50.
- [Er95] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and geometry*.
  Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
- [Er96b] Erdős, Paul, *Some problems I presented or planned to present in my short talk*. Analytic
  number theory, Vol. 1 (Allerton Park, IL, 1995) (1996), 333-335.
- [Er97c] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*. The mathematics of Paul Erdős, I
  (1997), 47-67.
- [Bl21] Bloom, T. F., *On a density conjecture about unit fractions*. arXiv:2112.03726
  (2021).
- [LiSa24] Liu, Y. and Sawhney, M., *On further questions regarding unit fractions*.
  arXiv:2404.07113 (2024).

statements.name: Erdos47.erdos_47
statements.doc:
If $\delta>0$ and $N$ is sufficiently large in terms of $\delta$, and $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is such that $\sum_{a\in A}\frac{1}{a}>\delta \log N$ then must there exist $S\subseteq A$ such that $\sum_{n\in S}\frac{1}{n}=1$?

Bloom [Bl21] proved this in the affirmative.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_47 :
    ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℕ,
      A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      δ * Real.log (N : ℝ) < A.reciprocalSum →
      ∃ S : Finset ℕ, S ⊆ A ∧ S.reciprocalSum = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 48
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/48](https://www.erdosproblems.com/48)

statements.name: Erdos48.erdos_48
statements.doc: Are there infinitely many integers $n, m$ such that $ϕ(n) = σ(m)$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_48 :
    {(n, m) : ℕ × ℕ | n.totient = σ 1 m}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 49
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/49](https://www.erdosproblems.com/49)
- [Er95] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and
  geometry*. Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
- [Er95c] Erdős, Paul, *Some problems in number theory*. Octogon Math. Mag. (1995), 3-5.
- [Ta24d] Tao, Terence, *Monotone nondecreasing sequences of the Euler totient function*.
  Matematica (2024), 793-820.

statements.name: Erdos49.erdos_49
statements.doc:
Let $A=\{a_1<\cdots<a_t\}\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be such that $\phi(a_1)<\cdots<\phi(a_t)$.
The primes are such an example. Are they the largest possible? Can one show that
$\lvert A\rvert<(1+o(1))\pi(N)$ or even $\lvert A\rvert=o(N)$?

Erdős remarks that the last conjecture is probably easy, and that similar questions can be asked
about $\sigma(n)$.

Solved by Tao [Ta24d], who proved that
$$ \lvert A\rvert \leq \left(1+O\left(\frac{(\log\log x)^5}{\log x}\right)\right)\pi(x).$$

In [Er95c] Erdős further asks about the situation when $\phi(a_1)\leq \cdots \leq \phi(a_t)$.

See also [415](https://www.erdosproblems.com/415).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_49 : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (f N : ℝ) ≤ (1 + ε) * Nat.primeCounting N

statements.name: Erdos49.erdos_49.variants.little_o
statements.doc: The weaker statement $\lvert A\rvert=o(N)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_49.variants.little_o :
    (fun N : ℕ ↦ (f N : ℝ)) =o[atTop] fun N ↦ (N : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos49.erdos_49.variants.tao
statements.doc:
Tao [Ta24d] proved that
$\lvert A\rvert \leq \left(1+O\left(\frac{(\log\log N)^5}{\log N}\right)\right)\pi(N)$, even for
sets on which $\phi$ is merely non-decreasing.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_49.variants.tao : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, 10 ≤ N →
    (g N : ℝ) ≤ (1 + C * (Real.log (Real.log N) ^ 5 / Real.log N)) *
      Nat.primeCounting N

statements.name: Erdos49.erdos_49.variants.primes_maximal
statements.doc: Are the primes the largest possible example, i.e. is $f(N) = \pi(N)$ for all $N \geq 2$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_49.variants.primes_maximal :
    ∀ N : ℕ, 2 ≤ N → f N = Nat.primeCounting N

problems.title: Erdős Problem 50
problems.doc:
*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/50](https://www.erdosproblems.com/50)
* [Er95] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and geometry.
Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
* [Sch38] Schoenberg, I. J. "On asymptotic distributions of arithmetical functions."
Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 39.2 (1936): 315-330.

statements.name: Erdos50.erdos_50_schoenberg
statements.doc:
Schoenberg [Sch38] proved that the asymptotic distribution function of $\varphi(n)/n$ exists.
That is, for any $c \in [0, 1]$, the proportion of integers $n \le N$ satisfying $\varphi(n)/n < c$
approaches a limit as $N \to \infty$. This limit function is the cumulative distribution function
of the values of $\varphi(n)/n$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_50_schoenberg : ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, IsDistributionOfPhiRatio f

statements.name: Erdos50.erdos_50_singular
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er95] proved that the distribution function of $\varphi(n)/n$ is purely singular on
$[0, 1]$: it is continuous there, but its derivative is zero almost everywhere on $[0, 1]$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_50_singular (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : IsDistributionOfPhiRatio f) :
    IsPurelySingularOn f (Icc 0 1)

statements.name: Erdos50.erdos_50
statements.doc:
Let $f$ be the asymptotic distribution function of $\varphi(n)/n$, so that for each $c \in [0,1]$,
$f(c)$ is the natural density of $\{n : \varphi(n) < cn\}$. Is it true that there is no $x$ such
that the derivative $f'(x)$ exists and is positive?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_50 : ∀ᵉ (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : IsDistributionOfPhiRatio f),
    ¬∃ x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∃ y > 0, HasDerivWithinAt f y (Icc 0 1) x

problems.title: Erdős Problem 51
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/51](https://www.erdosproblems.com/51)

statements.name: Erdos51.erdos_51
statements.doc:
Is there an infinite set $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $a \in A$,
there is an integer n such that $\phi(n)=a$, and
yet if $n_a$ is the smallest such integer, then $\frac{n_a}{a} → \infty$ as $a → ∞$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_51 : ∃ A : Set ℕ, ∃ n : A → ℕ,
      A.Infinite ∧
      (∀ a : A, IsLeast (φ ⁻¹' {(a : ℕ)}) (n a)) ∧
      Tendsto (fun a : A => (n a : ℝ) / (a : ℝ)) atTop atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 52
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/52](https://www.erdosproblems.com/52)

statements.name: Erdos52.erdos_52
statements.doc:
Let $A$ be a finite set of integers. Is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$
$\max( \lvert A+A\rvert,\lvert AA\rvert)\gg_\epsilon \lvert A\rvert^{2-\epsilon}?$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_52 : ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ε < 1 → ∃ (C : ℝ), 0 < C ∧ ∀ (A : Finset ℤ),
    (max (A + A).card (A * A).card : ℝ) ≥ C * (A.card : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 53
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/53](https://www.erdosproblems.com/53)
- [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III*. Number theory
  day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [ErSz83] Erdős, P. and Szemerédi, E., *On sums and products of integers*. Studies in pure
  mathematics (1983), 213-218.
- [Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991),
  397-406.
- [Er97] Erdős, Paul, *Problems in number theory*. New Zealand J. Math. (1997), 155-160.
- [Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
- [Ch03] Chang, M.-C., *The Erdős-Szemerédi problem on sum set and product set*. Annals of Math.
  (2003), 939-957.

statements.name: Erdos53.erdos_53
statements.doc:
Let $A$ be a finite set of integers. Is it true that, for every $k$, if $\lvert A\rvert$ is
sufficiently large depending on $k$, then there are least $\lvert A\rvert^k$ many integers which
are either the sum or product of distinct elements of $A$?

Asked by Erdős and Szemerédi [ErSz83]. Solved in this form by Chang [Ch03].

Erdős and Szemerédi proved that there exist arbitrarily large sets $A$ such that the number of
integers which are the sum or product of distinct elements of $A$ is at most
$$\exp\left(c \frac{(\log \lvert A\rvert)^2}{\log\log\lvert A\rvert}\right)$$
for some constant $c>0$. (erdosproblems.com multiplies by $\log\log\lvert A\rvert$;
[ErSz83, Theorem 2] divides by it.)

See also [52](https://www.erdosproblems.com/52).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_53 : ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset ℤ, N ≤ A.card →
    A.card ^ k ≤ (sumsAndProducts A).card

statements.name: Erdos53.erdos_53.variants.upper
statements.doc:
Erdős and Szemerédi [ErSz83] proved that there exist arbitrarily large sets $A$ such that the
number of integers which are the sum or product of distinct elements of $A$ is at most
$$\exp\left(c \frac{(\log \lvert A\rvert)^2}{\log\log\lvert A\rvert}\right)$$
for some constant $c>0$. (erdosproblems.com multiplies by $\log\log\lvert A\rvert$;
[ErSz83, Theorem 2] divides by it.)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_53.variants.upper : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ A : Finset ℤ, N ≤ A.card ∧
    ((sumsAndProducts A).card : ℝ) ≤
      Real.exp (c * Real.log A.card ^ 2 / Real.log (Real.log A.card))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 56
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/56](https://www.erdosproblems.com/56)

statements.name: Erdos56.erdos_56
statements.doc:
Suppose $A \subseteq \{1,\dots,N\}$ is such that there are no $k+1$ elements of $A$ which are
relatively prime. An example is the set of all multiples of the first $k$ primes.
Is this the largest such set?  To avoid trivial counterexamples, we must insist that $N$ be at
least the $k$th prime.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_56 : ¬ ∀ᵉ (k > 0) (N ≥ (k-1).nth Nat.Prime),
    (MaxWeaklyDivisible N k = (FirstPrimesMultiples N k).card)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 57
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/57](https://www.erdosproblems.com/57)
- [ErHa66] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., *On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems*.
  Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1966), 61-99.
- [LiMo20] Liu, Hong and Montgomery, Richard, *A solution to Erdős and Hajnal's odd cycle problem*.
  arXiv:2010.15802 (2020).

statements.name: Erdos57.erdos_57
statements.doc:
If $G$ is a graph with infinite chromatic number and $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ are lengths of the odd
cycles of $G$ then $\sum \frac{1}{a_i} = \infty$.

Conjectured by Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa66], and solved by Liu and Montgomery [LiMo20].

The linked formal proof (Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol) states the conclusion as
`¬ Summable (oddCycleReciprocal G)`, where `oddCycleReciprocal G n` is `n⁻¹` if `n` is an odd
cycle length of `G` and `0` otherwise; this is the indicator form of the sum below.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_57 :
    ∀ {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ →
      ¬ Summable (fun (a : G.oddCycleLengths) ↦ 1 / (a : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 58
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/58](https://www.erdosproblems.com/58)
- [Er90] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite unsolved problems. A tribute to Paul Erdős (1990), 467-478.
- [GaHuMa21] Gao, Jun and Huo, Qingyi and Ma, Jie, *A strengthening on odd cycles in graphs of given
  chromatic number*. SIAM J. Discrete Math. (2021), 2317-2327.
- [Gy92] Gyárfás, A., *Graphs with k odd cycle lengths*. Discrete Math. (1992), 41-48.

statements.name: Erdos58.erdos_58
statements.doc:
If $G$ is a graph which contains odd cycles of $\leq k$ different lengths then $\chi(G)\leq 2k+2$,
with equality if and only if $G$ contains $K_{2k+2}$.

Conjectured by Bollobás and Erdős. Proved by Gyárfás [Gy92].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_58 :
    ∀ {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ),
      G.oddCycleLengths.Finite →
      G.oddCycleLengths.ncard ≤ k →
        G.chromaticNumber ≤ (2 * k + 2 : ℕ∞) ∧
        (G.chromaticNumber = (2 * k + 2 : ℕ∞) ↔
          (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin (2 * k + 2))).IsContained G)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 59
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/59](https://www.erdosproblems.com/59)
- [EFR86] Erdős, P., Frankl, P. and Rödl, V., *The asymptotic number of graphs not containing a
  fixed subgraph and a problem for hypergraphs having no exponent*. Graphs Combin. (1986),
  113-121.
- [MoSa16] Morris, R. and Saxton, D., *The number of $C_{2\ell}$-free graphs*. Adv. Math. (2016),
  534-580. [arXiv:1309.2927](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.2927)
- [Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference "Paul
  Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).

statements.name: Erdos59.erdos_59
statements.doc:
Is it true that the number of graphs on $n$ vertices which do not contain $G$ is
$$\leq 2^{(1+o(1))\mathrm{ex}(n;G)}?$$

The answer is no, already for $G=C_6$ (see `erdos_59.variants.morris_saxton`). Graphs are
labelled, and $G$ ranges over finite graphs containing a cycle, as in [MoSa16]; for some forests
the answer is trivially no (for the path with two edges the free graphs include all matchings,
about $2^{\Theta(n\log n)}$ of them).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_59 :
    ¬ ∀ (k : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin k)), ¬ H.IsAcyclic →
      ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
        (numFree H n : ℝ) ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ ((1 + ε) * (extremalNumber n H : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos59.erdos_59.variants.erdos_frankl_rodl
statements.doc: If $G$ is not bipartite the answer is yes, proved by Erdős, Frankl, and Rödl [EFR86].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_59.variants.erdos_frankl_rodl {k : ℕ} (H : SimpleGraph (Fin k))
    (hH : ¬ H.IsBipartite) :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (numFree H n : ℝ) ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ ((1 + ε) * (extremalNumber n H : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos59.erdos_59.variants.morris_saxton
statements.doc:
The answer is no for $G=C_6$, the cycle on 6 vertices. Morris and Saxton [MoSa16, Proposition
1.4] have proved there are at least
$$2^{(1+c)\mathrm{ex}(n;C_6)}$$
such graphs for infinitely many $n$, for some constant $c>0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_59.variants.morris_saxton :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (2 : ℝ) ^ ((1 + c) * (extremalNumber n (cycleGraph 6) : ℝ)) ≤
        (numFree (cycleGraph 6) n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos59.erdos_59.variants.c4
statements.doc: In [Va99] the specific case of $G=C_4$ is also asked.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_59.variants.c4 :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (numFree (cycleGraph 4) n : ℝ) ≤
        (2 : ℝ) ^ ((1 + ε) * (extremalNumber n (cycleGraph 4) : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos59.erdos_59.variants.big_o
statements.doc:
It is still possible (and conjectured by Morris and Saxton) that the weaker bound of
$$2^{O(\mathrm{ex}(n;G))}$$
holds for all $G$ containing a cycle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_59.variants.big_o :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin k)), ¬ H.IsAcyclic →
      ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
        (numFree H n : ℝ) ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ (C * (extremalNumber n H : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 60
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/60](https://www.erdosproblems.com/60)
- [HeMaYa21] He, J. and Ma, J. and Yang, T., *Some extremal results on 4-cycles*. Journal of
  Combinatorial Theory B (2021).

statements.name: Erdos60.erdos_60
statements.doc:
Does every graph on $n$ vertices with $>\mathrm{ex}(n;C_4)$ edges contain $\gg n^{1/2}$ many
copies of $C_4$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_60 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, c > 0 ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
        ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
          (extremalNumber n (cycleGraph 4) < G.edgeFinset.card) →
          (c * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) ≤ ({ H' : G.Subgraph | Nonempty (H'.coe ≃g cycleGraph 4) }.ncard : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos60.erdos_60.variants.he_ma_yang
statements.doc:
He, Ma, and Yang [HeMaYa21] proved the conjecture when $n = q^2 + q + 1$ for some $q = 2^k$: they
showed that for large even $q$ every graph on $q^2 + q + 1$ vertices with
$\frac{1}{2}q(q+1)^2 + 1$ edges contains at least $q - 1$ copies of $C_4$, and
$\mathrm{ex}(q^2 + q + 1; C_4) = \frac{1}{2}q(q+1)^2$ when $q = 2^k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_60.variants.he_ma_yang :
    ∃ c : ℝ, c > 0 ∧
      ∀ (q : ℕ) (_hq : q.isPowerOfTwo),
        ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (q^2 + q + 1))) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
          (extremalNumber (q^2 + q + 1) (cycleGraph 4) < G.edgeFinset.card) →
          (c * Real.sqrt ((q^2 + q + 1) : ℝ) ≤ ({ H' : G.Subgraph | Nonempty (H'.coe ≃g cycleGraph 4) }.ncard : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos60.erdos_60.variants.two_copies
statements.doc: Erdős and Simonovits conjectured that at least 2 copies of $C_4$ are guaranteed.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_60.variants.two_copies :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
        (extremalNumber n (cycleGraph 4) < G.edgeFinset.card) →
        (2 ≤ { H' : G.Subgraph | Nonempty (H'.coe ≃g cycleGraph 4) }.ncard)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 61 -- Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/61](https://www.erdosproblems.com/61)

statements.name: Erdos61.erdos_61
statements.doc:
The Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture states that there is a constant $c(H) > 0$ for each
$H$ such that we can take $f(n) = n^{c(H)}$ in the above formulation.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_61 :
    ∀ {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (H : SimpleGraph α),
      ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), IsErdosHajnalLowerBound H (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ c)

statements.name: Erdos61.erdos_61.variants.erha89
statements.doc:
Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa89] proved that we can take $f(n) = \exp(c_H \sqrt{\log n})$
for some constant $c_H > 0$ depending on $H$.

[ErHa89] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., Ramsey-type theorems. Discrete Appl. Math. (1989), 37-52.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_61.variants.erha89 :
    ∀ {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (H : SimpleGraph α),
      ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), IsErdosHajnalLowerBound H (fun n : ℕ => exp (c * sqrt (log n)))

statements.name: Erdos61.erdos_61.variants.bnss23
statements.doc:
Bucić, Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour [BNSS23] improved this to
$f(n) = \exp(c_H \sqrt{\log n \log \log n})$ for some constant $c_H > 0$ depending on $H$.

[BNSS23] Bucić, M. and Nguyen, T. and Scott, A. and Seymour, P., A loglog step towards Erdos-Hajnal
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_61.variants.bnss23 :
    ∀ {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (H : SimpleGraph α),
      ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), IsErdosHajnalLowerBound H (fun n : ℕ => exp (c * sqrt (log n * log (log n))))

statements.name: Erdos61.erdos_61.variants.p5
statements.doc:
Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour [NSS23] proved the conjecture for $H = P_5$, the path on five
vertices: every $P_5$-free graph on $n$ vertices has a clique or independent set of
polynomial size.

[NSS23] Nguyen, T., Scott, A. and Seymour, P., Induced subgraph density. VII. The
five-vertex path. [arXiv:2312.15333](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.15333)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_61.variants.p5 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), IsErdosHajnalLowerBound (pathGraph 5) (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ c)

statements.name: Erdos61.erdos_61.variants.c5
statements.doc:
Chudnovsky, Scott, Seymour, and Spirkl [CSSS23] proved the conjecture for $H = C_5$, the
cycle on five vertices: every graph with no induced five-cycle has a clique or independent
set of polynomial size.

[CSSS23] Chudnovsky, M., Scott, A., Seymour, P. and Spirkl, S., Erdős–Hajnal for graphs with
no 5-hole. Proc. Lond. Math. Soc. (3) 126 (2023), 997–1014.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_61.variants.c5 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), IsErdosHajnalLowerBound (cycleGraph 5) (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 63
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/63](https://www.erdosproblems.com/63)
- [dBEr51] de Bruijn, N. G. and Erdős, P., *A colour problem for infinite graphs and a problem
  in the theory of relations*. Indag. Math. (1951), 369--373.
- [ErHa66] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., *On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems*.
  Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1966), 61-99.
- [LiMo20] Liu, Hong and Montgomery, Richard, *A solution to Erdős and Hajnal's odd cycle problem*.
  arXiv:2010.15802 (2020).
- [Re24] Reiher, C., *Graphs of large girth*. arXiv:2403.13571 (2024).

statements.name: Erdos63.erdos_63
statements.doc:
Does every graph with infinite chromatic number contain a cycle of length $2^n$ for infinitely
many $n$?

Conjectured by Mihók and Erdős. Solved affirmatively following the work of Liu and Montgomery
[LiMo20].

The linked formal proof (Codex) states the conclusion as `{n | HasCycleLength G (2 ^ n)}.Infinite`,
with `HasCycleLength G m` unfolding to `m ∈ G.cycleLengths`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_63 :
    ∀ {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ →
      ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n ≥ N, 2 ^ n ∈ G.cycleLengths

problems.title: Erdős Problem 64
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/64](https://www.erdosproblems.com/64)

statements.name: Erdos64.erdos_64
statements.doc:
Does every finite graph with minimum degree at least $3$
contain a cycle of length $2^k$ for some $k \geq 2$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_64 :
    ∀ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V) [Fintype V] [DecidableRel G.Adj],
        G.minDegree ≥ 3 → ∃ (k : ℕ) (v : V) (c : G.Walk v v),
            k ≥ 2 ∧ c.IsCycle ∧ c.length = 2^k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 65
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/65](https://www.erdosproblems.com/65)
- [GKS84] Gyárfás, A., Komlós, J. and Szemerédi, E., On the distribution of cycle lengths in graphs.
  J. Graph Theory (1984), 441-462.
- [GPSV85] Gyárfás, A., Prömel, H. J., Szemerédi, E. and Voigt, B., On the sum of the reciprocals
  of cycle lengths in sparse graphs. Combinatorica (1985), 41-52.
- [LiMo20] Liu, H. and Montgomery, R., A solution to Erdős and Hajnal's odd cycle problem.
  arXiv:2010.15802 (2020).

statements.name: Erdos65.erdos_65.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices and $kn$ edges, and $a_1<a_2<\cdots$ be the lengths of
cycles in $G$. Assume $n>0$. Is it true that
$$\sum\frac{1}{a_i}\gg \log k?$$

Gyárfás, Komlós, and Szemerédi [GKS84] have proved that this sum is $\gg \log k$, so that only
the second question remains.

The bound is stated for all sufficiently large $k$: [GKS84, Theorem 4'] proves it for $k \geq b$,
where $b$ is a constant. The case of $k$ slightly larger than $1$ is a separate problem, studied
in [GPSV85].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_65.parts.i :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℝ in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        0 < n →
        Fintype.card V = n →
        (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) = k * n →
        (∑ᶠ a ∈ G.cycleLengths, (1 : ℝ) / a) ≥ c * Real.log k

statements.name: Erdos65.erdos_65.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is the sum $\sum\frac{1}{a_i}$ minimised when $G$ is a complete bipartite graph?

This problem is #65 in Extremal Graph Theory in the graphs problem collection.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_65.parts.ii :
    ∀ (k : ℝ) (hk : 0 < k),
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        0 < n →
        Fintype.card V = n →
        (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) = k * n →
        ∀ (A B : Type) [Fintype A] [Fintype B],
          Fintype.card (A ⊕ B) = n →
          ((completeBipartiteGraph A B).edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) = k * n →
          (∑ᶠ a ∈ (completeBipartiteGraph A B).cycleLengths, (1 : ℝ) / a) ≤
            (∑ᶠ a ∈ G.cycleLengths, (1 : ℝ) / a)

statements.name: Erdos65.erdos_65.variants.liu_montgomery
statements.doc:
Liu and Montgomery [LiMo20, Corollary 1.2] have proved the asymptotically sharp lower bound of
$\geq (\tfrac{1}{2}-o(1))\log k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_65.variants.liu_montgomery :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℝ in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        0 < n →
        Fintype.card V = n →
        (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) = k * n →
        (∑ᶠ a ∈ G.cycleLengths, (1 : ℝ) / a) ≥ (1 / 2 - ε) * Real.log k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 66
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/66](https://www.erdosproblems.com/66)

statements.name: Erdos66.erdos_66
statements.doc:
Is there and $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ is such that
$$\lim_{n\to \infty}\frac{1_A\ast 1_A(n)}{\log n}$$
exists and is $\ne 0$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_66 : ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (c : ℝ), c ≠ 0 ∧
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ (sumRep A n : ℝ) / Real.log n) atTop (𝓝 c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 67
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/67](https://www.erdosproblems.com/66)
- [Ta16] Tao, Terence, The Erdős discrepancy problem. Discrete Anal. (2016), Paper No. 1, 29.

statements.name: Erdos67.erdos_67
statements.doc:
**The Erdős discrepancy problem**

If $f\colon \mathbb N \rightarrow \{-1, +1\}$ then is it true that for every $C>0$ there
exist $d, m \ge 1$ such that $$\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq k\leq m}f(kd)\right\rvert > C?$$
This is true, and was proved by Tao [Ta16]
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_67 (f : ℕ → ({-1, 1} : Finset ℝ)) (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C) : ∃ᵉ (d ≥ 1) (m ≥ 1),
    C < |∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m, (f (k * d)).1|

statements.name: Erdos67.erdos_67.variants.complex
statements.doc:
**The Erdős discrepancy problem (complex variant)**

If $f\colon \mathbb N \rightarrow S^1 ⊆ ℂ$ then is it true that for every $C>0$ there
exist $d, m \ge 1$ such that $$\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq k\leq m}f(kd)\right\rvert > C?$$
This is true, and was proved by Tao [Ta16]
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_67.variants.complex (f : ℕ → Metric.sphere (0 : ℂ) 1) (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C) :
    ∃ᵉ (d ≥ 1) (m ≥ 1), C < ‖∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m, (f (k * d)).1‖

problems.title: Erdős Problem 68
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/68](https://www.erdosproblems.com/68)

statements.name: Erdos68.erdos_68
statements.doc:
Is
$$\sum_{n=2}^\infty \frac{1}{n!-1}$$
irrational?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_68 :
    Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, 1 / ((n + 2).factorial - 1 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos68.sum_factorial_inv_eq_geometric
statements.doc: $$\sum_{n=2}^\infty \frac{1}{n!-1} = \sum_{n=2}^\infty \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{1}{(n!)^k}$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 69
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/69](https://www.erdosproblems.com/69)

statements.name: Erdos69.erdos_69
statements.doc:
Is
$$
\sum_{n\geq 2}\frac{\omega(n)}{2^n}
$$
irrational? (Here $\omega(n)$ counts the number of distinct prime divisors of $n$.)
statements.statement: theorem erdos_69 : Irrational <| ∑' n, ω (n + 2) / 2 ^ (n + 2)

statements.name: Erdos69.erdos_69.variants.specialisation_of_erdos_257
statements.doc:
Tao observed that `erdos_69` is a special case of `erdos_257`, since
$$
\sum_{n\geq 2}\frac{\omega(n)}{2^n} = \sum_p \frac{1}{2^p - 1}.
$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 70
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/70](https://www.erdosproblems.com/70)
- [ErRa56] Erdős, P. and Rado, R., *A partition calculus in set theory*,
  Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. **62** (1956), 427–489, Theorem 31.
- [Er87] Erdős, P., *Some problems on finite and infinite graphs*,
  Logic and combinatorics (Arcata, Calif., 1985), Contemp. Math. **65** (1987), 223–228.

The 3-uniform (triple) partition relation $\mathfrak{c} \to (\beta, n)^3_2$, where
$\mathfrak{c}$ denotes the order type of the real numbers with their usual order (written
$\lambda$ in [ErRa56]). This is the triple analogue of `OrdinalCardinalRamsey` used in
Problems 590–592; the file also contains the analogous relation for an ordinal in place
of the real line.

statements.name: Erdos70.erdos_70
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 70**: Let $\mathfrak{c}$ be the order type of the real numbers,
let $\beta$ be a countable ordinal, and let $2 \le n < \omega$.
Is it true that $\mathfrak{c} \to (\beta, n)^3_2$?

Note: The cases $n \le 3$ are trivially true (compare `omega_three`), so the
genuine content of the conjecture begins at $n = 4$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_70 :
    ∀ᵉ (β : Ordinal.{0}) (n : ℕ) (_ : β.card ≤ ℵ₀) (_ : 2 ≤ n),
      RealCardinalRamsey3 β n

statements.name: Erdos70.erdos_70.variants.erdos_rado
statements.doc:
**Erdős–Rado partial result**: $\mathfrak{c} \to (\omega + n, 4)^3_2$ for any
$2 \le n < \omega$, where $\mathfrak{c}$ is the order type of the real numbers.
Positive partial answer to Problem 70 with $\beta = \omega + n$ and the blue side
fixed at $4$ [ErRa56, Theorem 31].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_rado (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    RealCardinalRamsey3 (ω + n) 4

statements.name: Erdos70.erdos_70.variants.omega_times_two_four
statements.doc:
**First open case beyond Erdős–Rado**: $\mathfrak{c} \to (\omega \cdot 2, 4)^3_2$,
where $\mathfrak{c}$ is the order type of the real numbers.

Erdős and Rado proved $\mathfrak{c} \to (\omega + n, 4)^3_2$ for every finite $n \ge 2$
(see `erdos_rado`), which covers all red ordinals below $\omega \cdot 2 = \omega + \omega$.
This variant asks whether the result extends to $\beta = \omega \cdot 2$, the simplest
countable ordinal not covered by their theorem.
statements.statement:
theorem omega_times_two_four :
    RealCardinalRamsey3 (ω * 2) 4

statements.name: Erdos70.erdos_70.variants.omega_three
statements.doc:
**Trivial boundary case**: $\mathfrak{c} \to (\omega, 3)^3_2$, stated for the initial
ordinal $\mathfrak{c}.\mathrm{ord}$ of the cardinality of the continuum.

This is trivially true because in a 3-uniform hypergraph, a \"blue clique of size 3\"
consists of a single 3-element subset ($\binom{3}{3} = 1$), so the blue alternative
merely asks for one blue triple to exist. The proof splits into two cases:
- If any blue triple exists, it is itself a blue-monochromatic set of cardinality 3.
- If no blue triple exists, all triples are red, and since $\omega \le \mathfrak{c}$,
  any subset of order type $\omega$ is red-monochromatic.

The problem becomes non-trivial only for $n \ge 4$; see `omega_times_two_four` for
the simplest genuinely open case.
statements.statement:
theorem omega_three :
    OrdinalCardinalRamsey3 (𝔠).ord ω 3

statements.name: Erdos70.erdos_70.variants.omega_one
statements.doc:
**The relation at $\omega_1$**: $\mathfrak{c} \to (\omega_1, n)^3_2$ for finite $n \ge 2$,
where $\omega_1 = \aleph_1$ is the first uncountable ordinal.

Note that $\omega_1$ is *not* a countable ordinal, so this is not directly an instance of the
main Erdős problem (which asks for *countable* $\beta$). Under CH, $\omega_1 = \mathfrak{c}.\mathrm{ord}$,
making this a self-referential question about $\mathfrak{c}.\mathrm{ord} \to
(\mathfrak{c}.\mathrm{ord}, n)^3_2$.
statements.statement:
theorem omega_one :
    ∀ᵉ (n : ℕ) (_ : 2 ≤ n),
      OrdinalCardinalRamsey3 (𝔠).ord (Cardinal.aleph 1).ord n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 71
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/71](https://www.erdosproblems.com/71)
- [Bo77] Bollobás, Béla, *Cycles modulo $k$*. Bull. London Math. Soc. (1977), 97-98.
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*.
  (1982), 59--79.
- [Er95] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and
  geometry*. Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
- [Er97b] Erdős, Paul, *Some old and new problems in various branches of combinatorics*.
  Discrete Math. (1997), 227-231.

statements.name: Erdos71.erdos_71
statements.doc:
Is it true that for every infinite arithmetic progression $P$ which contains even numbers
there is some constant $c=c(P)$ such that every graph with average degree at least $c$
contains a cycle whose length is in $P$?

In [Er82e] Erdős credits this conjecture to himself and Burr. This has been proved by
Bollobás [Bo77]. The best dependence of the constant $c(P)$ is unknown.

The infinite arithmetic progression is encoded as a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ satisfying
`P.IsAPOfLength ⊤` (which forces a positive common difference), and "contains even numbers"
as the existence of an even element. The average degree of a finite simple graph is
`SimpleGraph.averageDegree`, i.e. $(\sum_v \deg v)/|V| \in \mathbb{Q}$, and a cycle whose
length is in $P$ is a cycle walk `w` with `w.length ∈ P`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_71 :
    ∀ P : Set ℕ, P.IsAPOfLength ⊤ → (∃ n ∈ P, Even n) →
      ∃ c : ℚ, ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
        [DecidableRel G.Adj], c ≤ G.averageDegree →
          ∃ (v : V) (w : G.Walk v v), w.IsCycle ∧ w.length ∈ P

problems.title: Erdős Problem 72
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/72](https://www.erdosproblems.com/72)
- [Er94b] Erdős, Paul, *Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and combinatorial geometry*.
  Math. Pannon. (1994), 261-269.
- [Er95] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and
  geometry*. Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
- [Er97b] Erdős, Paul, *Some old and new problems in various branches of combinatorics*. Discrete
  Math. (1997), 227-231.
- [Er97c] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*. The mathematics of Paul
  Erdős, I (1997), 47-67.
- [Bo77] Bollobás, Béla, *Cycles modulo $k$*. Bull. London Math. Soc. (1977), 97-98.
- [Ve05] Verstraete, Jacques, *Unavoidable cycle lengths in graphs*. J. Graph Theory (2005),
  151-167.
- [LiMo20] Liu, Hong and Montgomery, Richard, *A solution to Erdős and Hajnal's odd cycle
  problem*. arXiv:2010.15802 (2020).

statements.name: Erdos72.erdos_72
statements.doc:
Is there a set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ of density $0$ and a constant $c>0$ such that every graph on
sufficiently many vertices with average degree $\geq c$ contains a cycle whose length is in $A$?

Bollobás [Bo77] proved that such a $c$ does exist if $A$ is an infinite arithmetic progression
containing even numbers (see [71](https://www.erdosproblems.com/71)).

Erdős was 'almost certain' that if $A$ is the set of powers of $2$ then no such $c$ exists
(although he conjectured that $n$ vertices and average degree $\gg (\log n)^{C}$ suffices for
some $C=O(1)$). If $A$ is the set of squares (or the set of $p\pm 1$ for $p$ prime) then he had
no guess.

Solved by Verstraëte [Ve05], who gave a non-constructive proof that such a set $A$ exists.

Liu and Montgomery [LiMo20] proved that in fact this is true when $A$ is the set of powers of $2$
(more generally any set of even numbers which doesn't grow too quickly) - in particular this
contradicts the previous belief of Erdős.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_72 : ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.HasDensity 0 ∧ ∃ c : ℚ, 0 < c ∧
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), c ≤ G.averageDegree →
      ∃ (v : Fin n) (w : G.Walk v v), w.IsCycle ∧ w.length ∈ A

statements.name: Erdos72.erdos_72.variants.powers_of_two
statements.doc:
Liu and Montgomery [LiMo20] proved that there is a constant $c > 0$ such that every graph on
sufficiently many vertices with average degree $\geq c$ contains a cycle whose length is a power
of $2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_72.variants.powers_of_two : ∃ c : ℚ, 0 < c ∧
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), c ≤ G.averageDegree →
      ∃ (v : Fin n) (w : G.Walk v v), w.IsCycle ∧ ∃ k : ℕ, w.length = 2 ^ k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 73
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/73](https://www.erdosproblems.com/73)
- [Re99] Reed, B., Mangoes and Blueberries. Combinatorica (1999), 267-296.

statements.name: Erdos73.erdos_73
statements.doc:
Let $k\ge 0$. Let $G$ be a graph such that every subgraph $H$ contains an independent set of size
$\ge (n-k)/2$, where $n$ is the number of vertices of $H$. Must $G$ be the union of a bipartite
graph and $O_k(1)$ many vertices?

Proved by Reed [Re99].

The linked formal proof (Alexeev and Codex, following Reed's mangoes-and-blueberries argument)
states the hypothesis as `∀ H : G.Subgraph, H.verts.ncard ≤ 2 * H.coe.indepNum + k` and the
conclusion as `(G.induce Dᶜ).IsBipartite`, for graphs on `Fin n` (and, equivalently, on any
finite vertex type); this implies the statement below.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_73 :
    ∀ (k : ℕ), ∃ (C : ℕ),
      ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        (∀ (S : Finset V), ∃ (I : Finset V), I ⊆ S ∧ (G.induce (I : Set V)).edgeSet = ∅ ∧
          (I.card : ℝ) ≥ (S.card - k : ℝ) / 2) →
        ∃ (D : Finset V), D.card ≤ C ∧
          (G.induce (D : Set V)ᶜ).Colorable 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 74
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/74](https://www.erdosproblems.com/74)

statements.name: Erdos74.erdos_74
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)\to \infty$ possibly very slowly.
Is there a graph of infinite chromatic number such that every finite subgraph on $n$
vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most $f(n)$ edges?

The answer is no. A machine-checked disproof constructs a function $f(n) \to \infty$ for which
every graph satisfying this local deletion bound has finite chromatic number.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_74 : ¬ ∀ f : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto f atTop atTop →
    (∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ n, G.maxSubgraphEdgeDistToBipartite n ≤ f n)

statements.name: Erdos74.erdos_74.variants.sqrt
statements.doc:
Is there a graph of infinite chromatic number such that every finite subgraph on $n$
vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most $\sqrt{n}$ edges?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_74.variants.sqrt :
    ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ n, G.maxSubgraphEdgeDistToBipartite n ≤ (n : ℝ).sqrt

problems.title: Erdős Problem 75
problems.doc:
*Reference:*
* [erdosproblems.com/75] (https://www.erdosproblems.com/75)

statements.name: Erdos75.erdos_75
statements.doc:
Is there a graph of chromatic number `ℵ_ 1` with `ℵ_ 1` vertices such that for all
`ε > 0`, if `n` is sufficiently large and `H` is a subgraph on `n` vertices,
then `H` contains an independent set of size `> n ^ (1 - ε)`?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_75 :
    ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V),
      G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 ∧
      #V = ℵ_ 1 ∧
      ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ),
        ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∀ (H : G.Subgraph),
            H.verts.ncard = n →
            ∃ (I : Finset V),
              (I : Set V) ⊆ H.verts ∧
              G.IsIndepSet (I : Set V) ∧
              (I.card : ℝ) > (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 77
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/77](https://www.erdosproblems.com/77)
- [BBCGHMST24] Balister, P. and Bollobás, B. and Campos, M. and Griffiths, S. and Hurley, E. and
  Morris, R. and Sahasrabudhe, J. and Tiba, M., Upper bounds for multicolour Ramsey numbers.
  arXiv:2410.17197 (2024).
- [CGMS23] Campos, Marcelo and Griffiths, Simon and Morris, Robert and Sahasrabudhe, Julian, An
  exponential improvement for diagonal Ramsey. arXiv:2303.09521 (2023).
- [Er88] Erdős, P, Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and graph theory. Discrete Math.
  (1988), 81-92.
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory. Quaestiones
  Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [GNNW24] Gupta, P. and Ndiaye, N. and Norin, S. and Wei, L., Optimizing the CGMS upper bound on
  Ramsey numbers. arXiv:2407.19026 (2024).

statements.name: Erdos77.erdos_77
statements.doc:
If $R(k)$ is the Ramsey number for $K_k$, the minimal $n$ such that every $2$-colouring of the edges
of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of $K_k$, then find the value of
$$\lim_{k\to \infty}R(k)^{1/k}.$$

This problem is #3 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_77 :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun k : ℕ ↦ (SimpleGraph.diagonalRamsey k : ℝ) ^ (1 / (k : ℝ)))
      Filter.atTop (𝓝 erdos_77.answer)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 78
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/78](https://www.erdosproblems.com/78)
- [Co15] Cohen, Gil, *Two-source dispersers for polylogarithmic entropy and improved Ramsey
  graphs*. arXiv:1506.04428 (2015).
- [Er47] Erdős, P., *Some remarks on the theory of graphs*. Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (1947),
  292-294.
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [Er88] Erdős, P, Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and graph theory. Discrete Math.
  (1988), 81-92.
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory. Quaestiones
  Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [Er95] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and
  geometry*. Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
- [Er97c] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*. The mathematics of Paul
  Erdős, I (1997), 47-67.
- [Li23b] Li, Xin, *Two source extractors for asymptotically optimal entropy, and (many) more*.
  arXiv:2303.06802 (2023).
- [Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference "Paul
  Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).

statements.name: Erdos78.erdos_78
statements.doc:
Let $R(k)$ be the Ramsey number for $K_k$. Give a constructive proof that $R(k) > C^k$ for some
constant $C > 1$.

Equivalently, give an explicit construction of graphs on $n$ vertices which contain no clique
and no independent set of size $\geq c \log n$, for some constant $c > 0$.

We formalise "explicit" as: the adjacency relation of the graph on $n$ vertices is decided by a
single algorithm that runs in time polynomial in $n$ (see `explicitGraph`). This is the weakest
reasonable notion ("weakly explicit"); even this is open. The strongly explicit version, with time
polynomial in $\log n$, is `erdos_78.variants.strongly_explicit`.

This problem is #4 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_78 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ adj : List Bool × ℕ × ℕ → Bool, IsPolyTime adj ∧
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, NoHomogeneousSet (explicitGraph adj n) ⌈c * log n⌉₊

statements.name: Erdos78.erdos_78.variants.nonconstructive
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er47] gave a simple probabilistic, non-constructive proof that $R(k) > C^k$ for some
constant $C > 1$. In fact $R(k) > 2^{k/2}$ for all $k \geq 3$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_78.variants.nonconstructive :
    ∃ C > (1 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k in atTop, C ^ k < (SimpleGraph.diagonalRamsey k : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos78.erdos_78.variants.little_o_sqrt
statements.doc:
Erdős also asked for an explicit construction of graphs on $n$ vertices whose largest clique and
independent set have size $o(n^{1/2})$. Such constructions are now known; see [Co15] for the
history.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_78.variants.little_o_sqrt :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, f =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ √(n : ℝ)) ∧
      ∃ adj : List Bool × ℕ × ℕ → Bool, IsPolyTime adj ∧
        ∀ᶠ n in atTop, NoHomogeneousSet (explicitGraph adj n) ⌈f n⌉₊

statements.name: Erdos78.erdos_78.variants.cohen
statements.doc:
Cohen [Co15] constructed explicit graphs on $n$ vertices with no clique and no independent set
of size $2^{(\log \log n)^C}$, for some constant $C > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_78.variants.cohen :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∃ adj : List Bool × ℕ × ℕ → Bool, IsPolyTime adj ∧
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
        NoHomogeneousSet (explicitGraph adj n) ⌈(2 : ℝ) ^ (log (log n)) ^ C⌉₊

statements.name: Erdos78.erdos_78.variants.li
statements.doc:
Li [Li23b] improved this to explicit graphs on $n$ vertices with no clique and no independent set
of size $(\log n)^C$, for some constant $C > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_78.variants.li :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∃ adj : List Bool × ℕ × ℕ → Bool, IsPolyTime adj ∧
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, NoHomogeneousSet (explicitGraph adj n) ⌈(log n) ^ C⌉₊

statements.name: Erdos78.erdos_78.variants.strongly_explicit
statements.doc:
The strongly explicit version of `erdos_78`: an explicit family of graphs on $n$ vertices with no
clique and no independent set of size $\geq c \log n$, where each adjacency query is answered in
time polynomial in $\log n$ (see `stronglyExplicitGraph`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_78.variants.strongly_explicit :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ adj : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ → Bool, IsPolyTime adj ∧
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, NoHomogeneousSet (stronglyExplicitGraph adj n) ⌈c * log n⌉₊

statements.name: Erdos78.erdos_78.variants.li_strongly_explicit
statements.doc:
The construction of Li [Li23b] is strongly explicit: there are graphs on $n$ vertices with no
clique and no independent set of size $(\log n)^C$, for some constant $C > 0$, whose adjacency
queries are answered in time polynomial in $\log n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_78.variants.li_strongly_explicit :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∃ adj : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ → Bool, IsPolyTime adj ∧
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, NoHomogeneousSet (stronglyExplicitGraph adj n) ⌈(log n) ^ C⌉₊

problems.title: Erdős Problem 79
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/79](https://www.erdosproblems.com/79)
- [EFRS93] Erdős, P., Faudree, R. J., Rousseau, C. C. and Schelp, R. H., Ramsey size linear graphs.
  Combin. Probab. Comput. (1993), 389-399.
- [Wi24] Wigderson, Y., Infinitely many minimally non-Ramsey size linear graphs.
  arXiv:2409.05931 (2024).

statements.name: Erdos79.erdos_79
statements.doc:
We say $G$ is Ramsey size linear if $R(G,H)\ll m$ for all graphs $H$ with $m$ edges and
no isolated vertices.

Are there infinitely many graphs $G$ which are not Ramsey size linear but such that all of
its proper subgraphs are?

Asked by Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau, and Schelp [EFRS93]. $K_4$ was long the only known example.
Wigderson [Wi24] proved that there are infinitely many such graphs.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_79 :
    ∀ (N : ℕ), ∃ (n : ℕ) (_ : N ≤ n) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      ¬ G.IsRamseySizeLinear ∧
      ∀ H : G.Subgraph, H < ⊤ → H.coe.IsRamseySizeLinear

problems.title: Erdős Problem 80
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/80](https://www.erdosproblems.com/80)
- [erdosproblems.com/600](https://www.erdosproblems.com/600), stated in
  `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/600.lean`
- [FoLo12] Fox, Jacob and Loh, Po-Shen, On a problem of Erdős and Rothschild on edges in
  triangles. Combinatorica (2012), 619--628.

600 asks the same question from the other side. `Erdos600.eFunction n r` is the least edge
count forcing some edge into `r` triangles; `f c n` here is the largest book forced once the
edge count is at least $cn^2$. So `r ≤ f c n` and `Erdos600.eFunction n r ≤ c * n^2` say the
same thing, and the two functions are inverse to each other in that sense. Both are built on
`SimpleGraph.trianglesContaining`, which 600 introduced.

statements.name: Erdos80.erdos_80.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $c>0$ and let $f_c(n)$ be the maximal $m$ such that every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and
at least $cn^2$ edges, where each edge is contained in at least one triangle, must contain a
book of size $m$, that is, an edge shared by at least $m$ different triangles. Estimate
$f_c(n)$. In particular, is it true that $f_c(n)>n^\epsilon$ for some $\epsilon>0$?

The answer is no. Fox and Loh [FoLo12] proved that $f_c(n) \leq n^{O(1/\log\log n)}$ for every
fixed $c < 1/4$, so no $\epsilon > 0$ works for, say, $c = 1/8$. For $c > 1/4$ the situation is
different: $f_c(n) \geq n/6$, see [erdosproblems.com/80](https://www.erdosproblems.com/80).

The bound $c < 1/2$ is what makes the hypothesis satisfiable: a simple graph on $n$ vertices
has at most $n(n-1)/2$ edges, so no graph has $cn^2$ of them once $c \geq 1/2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_80.parts.i :
    ¬ ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → c < 1 / 2 →
      ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (n : ℝ) ^ ε < f c n

statements.name: Erdos80.erdos_80.parts.ii
statements.doc:
The weaker question from the same problem: is $f_c(n) \gg \log n$?

Same feasibility bound on `c` as above.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_80.parts.ii :
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → c < 1 / 2 →
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f c n : ℝ)) ≫ (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 81
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/81](https://www.erdosproblems.com/81)
- [EOZ93] Erdős, Paul and Ordman, Edward T. and Zalcstein, Yechezkel,
  *Clique partitions of chordal graphs*. Combin. Probab. Comput. (1993), 409–415.
- [CEO94] Chen, Guan-Tao and Erdős, Paul and Ordman, Edward T.,
  *Clique partitions of split graphs*. Combinatorics, graph theory, algorithms and applications
  (Beijing, 1993) (1994), 21–30.

statements.name: Erdos81.erdos_81
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a chordal graph on $n$ vertices - that is, $G$ has no induced cycles of
length greater than $3$. Can the edges of $G$ be partitioned into $n^2/6+O(n)$ many cliques?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_81 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.IsChordal →
      ∃ P : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), G.IsCliqueEdgePartition P ∧
        (P.card : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 6 + C * n

statements.name: Erdos81.erdos_81.variants.split
statements.doc:
Chen, Erdős, and Ordman [CEO94] have shown that any split graph can be partitioned
into $\frac{3}{16}n^2+O(n)$ many cliques.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_81.variants.split :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.IsSplitGraph →
      ∃ P : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), G.IsCliqueEdgePartition P ∧
        (P.card : ℝ) ≤ 3 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 16 + C * n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 82
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/82](https://www.erdosproblems.com/82)

statements.name: Erdos82.erdos_82
statements.doc: $F(n) / \log n \to \infty as n \to \infty$
statements.statement: theorem erdos_82 : Tendsto (fun n => F n / Real.log n) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos82.erdos_82.variants.F_upper_bound
statements.doc:
$F(n) \le O(n^{1/2} \ln ^ {3/4} n)$

Theorem 1.4 from [AKS07]

[AKS07] Alon, N. and Krivelevich, M. and Sudakov, B., Large nearly regular induced subgraphs. arXiv:0710.2106 (2007).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_82.variants.F_upper_bound :
    (fun n => (F n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n => Real.sqrt n * (Real.log n) ^ (3 / 4 : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 83
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/83](https://www.erdosproblems.com/83)
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [Er90] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. A tribute to Paul Erdős (1990),
  467-478.
- [Er92e] Erdős, Pál, *Some Unsolved problems in Geometry, Number Theory and Combinatorics*.
  Eureka (1992), 44-48.
- [Er95] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and
  geometry*. Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
- [ErKoRa61] Erdős, P. and Ko, Chao and Rado, R., *Intersection theorems for systems of finite
  sets*. Quart. J. Math. Oxford Ser. (2) (1961), 313-320.
- [AhKh97] Ahlswede, Rudolf and Khachatrian, Levon H., *The complete intersection theorem for
  systems of finite sets*. European J. Combin. (1997), 125-136.

statements.name: Erdos83.erdos_83
statements.doc:
Suppose that we have a family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[4n]$ such that $\lvert A\rvert=2n$
