for all $A\in\mathcal{F}$ and for every $A,B\in \mathcal{F}$ we have
$\lvert A\cap B\rvert \geq 2$. Then
$$\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert \leq \frac{1}{2}\left(\binom{4n}{2n}-\binom{2n}{n}^2\right).$$

Conjectured by Erdős, Ko, and Rado [ErKoRa61]. This inequality would be best possible, as shown
by taking $\mathcal{F}$ to be the collection of all subsets of $[4n]$ of size $2n$ containing at
least $n+1$ elements from $[2n]$.

Proved by Ahlswede and Khachatrian [AhKh97], who more generally showed the following. Let
$2\leq t\leq k\leq m$ and let $r\geq 0$ be such that
$$\frac{1}{r+1}\leq \frac{m-2k+2t-2}{(t-1)(k-t+1)}< \frac{1}{r}.$$
The largest possible family of subsets of $[m]$ of size $k$, such that the pairwise
intersections have size at least $t$, is the family of all subsets of $[m]$ of size $k$ which
contain at least $t+r$ elements from $\{1,\ldots,t+2r\}$.

The number $\binom{4n}{2n}-\binom{2n}{n}^2$ is even, so the bound is an integer.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_83 (n : ℕ) (F : Finset (Finset (Fin (4 * n)))) (hF : ∀ A ∈ F, A.card = 2 * n)
    (hinter : ∀ A ∈ F, ∀ B ∈ F, 2 ≤ (A ∩ B).card) :
    F.card ≤ ((4 * n).choose (2 * n) - (2 * n).choose n ^ 2) / 2

statements.name: Erdos83.erdos_83.variants.extremal
statements.doc:
The bound in [erdős_83](https://www.erdosproblems.com/83) is attained by the family of all
subsets of $[4n]$ of size $2n$ containing at least $n+1$ elements from $[2n]$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_83.variants.extremal (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ F : Finset (Finset (Fin (4 * n))), (∀ A ∈ F, A.card = 2 * n) ∧
      (∀ A ∈ F, ∀ B ∈ F, 2 ≤ (A ∩ B).card) ∧
      F.card = ((4 * n).choose (2 * n) - (2 * n).choose n ^ 2) / 2

statements.name: Erdos83.erdos_83.variants.ahlswede_khachatrian
statements.doc:
The complete intersection theorem of Ahlswede and Khachatrian [AhKh97]: for $2\leq t\leq k\leq m$,
every family of $k$-subsets of $[m]$ with pairwise intersections of size at least $t$ is at most
as large as one of the families of all $k$-subsets of $[m]$ containing at least $t+r$ elements of
$\{1,\ldots,t+2r\}$, $r \geq 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_83.variants.ahlswede_khachatrian (m k t : ℕ) (ht : 2 ≤ t) (htk : t ≤ k)
    (hkm : k ≤ m) (F : Finset (Finset (Fin m))) (hF : ∀ A ∈ F, A.card = k)
    (hinter : ∀ A ∈ F, ∀ B ∈ F, t ≤ (A ∩ B).card) :
    ∃ r : ℕ, F.card ≤ ({A : Finset (Fin m) | A.card = k ∧
      t + r ≤ (A.filter fun i : Fin m => (i : ℕ) < t + 2 * r).card} : Finset _).card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 85
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/85](https://www.erdosproblems.com/85)

statements.name: Erdos85.erdos_85
statements.doc: Is it true that, for all large $n$, $f(n + 1) \ge f(n)$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_85 : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, f n ≤ f (n + 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 86
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/86](https://www.erdosproblems.com/86)
- [BHLL14] Balogh, József and Hu, Ping and Lidický, Bernard and Liu, Hong, *Upper bounds on the size
  of 4- and 6-cycle-free subgraphs of the hypercube*. European J. Combin. (2014), 75-85.
- [BHN95] Brass, Peter and Harborth, Heiko and Nienborg, Hauke, *On the maximum number of edges in a
  {$C_4$}-free subgraph of {$Q_n$}*. J. Graph Theory (1995), 17--23.
- [Ba12b] R. Baber, *Turán densities of hypercubes*. arXiv:1201.3587 (2012).
- [Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991),
  397-406.

statements.name: Erdos86.erdos_86
statements.doc: Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph (so that $Q_n$ has $2^n$ vertices and $n2^{n-1}$ edges). Is it true that every subgraph of $Q_n$ with $$\geq \left(\frac{1}{2}+o(1)\right)n2^{n-1}$$ many edges contains a $C_4$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_86 :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ H : SimpleGraph (Fin n → Bool),
      H ≤ hypercube n →
        (1 / 2 + ε) * n * 2 ^ (n - 1 : ℕ) ≤ (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) →
          cycleGraph 4 ⊑ H

problems.title: Erdős Problem 87
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/87](https://www.erdosproblems.com/87)
- [Er95] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and geometry.
  Resenhas (1995), 165-186.

statements.name: Erdos87.erdos_87.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $0 < \epsilon < 1$. Is it true that, if $k$ is sufficiently large, then
$$R(G) > (1-\epsilon)^k R(k)$$
for every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\chi(G)=k$?

The restriction $\epsilon < 1$ excludes negative bases in $(1-\epsilon)^k$.

This problem is #12 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_87.parts.i :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ε < 1 → ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = (k : ℕ∞) →
        (SimpleGraph.diagonalGraphRamsey G : ℝ) >
          (1 - ε) ^ k * (SimpleGraph.diagonalRamsey k : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos87.erdos_87.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Even stronger, is there some $c > 0$ such that, for all large $k$,
$$R(G) > c R(k)$$
for every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\chi(G)=k$?

This problem is #13 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_87.parts.ii :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = (k : ℕ∞) →
        (SimpleGraph.diagonalGraphRamsey G : ℝ) > c * (SimpleGraph.diagonalRamsey k : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 88
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/88](https://www.erdosproblems.com/88)
- [Er92b] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics*.
  Matematiche (Catania) (1992), 231-240.
- [Er95] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and
  geometry*. Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
- [Er97d] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent problems and results in graph theory*. Discrete Math. (1997),
  81-85.
- [KSSS22] Kwan, M. and Sah, A. and Sauermann, L. and Sawhney, M., *Anticoncentration in Ramsey
  graphs and a proof of the Erdős-McKay conjecture*. Forum Math. Pi 11 (2023), e21.
  [arXiv:2208.02874](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.02874)

statements.name: Erdos88.erdos_88
statements.doc:
For any $\epsilon>0$ there exists $\delta=\delta(\epsilon)>0$ such that if $G$ is a graph on $n$
vertices with no independent set or clique of size $\geq \epsilon\log n$ then $G$ contains an
induced subgraph with $m$ edges for all $m\leq \delta n^2$.

This was conjectured by Erdős and McKay and proved by Kwan, Sah, Sauermann, and Sawhney
[KSSS22]. Erdős' original formulation also assumed that $G$ has $\gg n^2$ edges. By an old result
of Erdős and Szemerédi this follows from the other condition, so it is omitted here.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_88 :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ δ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (G.cliqueNum : ℝ) < ε * Real.log n → (G.indepNum : ℝ) < ε * Real.log n →
        ∀ m : ℕ, (m : ℝ) ≤ δ * n ^ 2 →
          ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), (G.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).edgeSet.ncard = m

statements.name: Erdos88.erdos_88.variants.erdos_mckay
statements.doc:
Erdős and McKay proved the statement of `erdos_88` with $\delta n^2$ replaced by
$\delta (\log n)^2$. Since $(\log n)^2 \leq n^2$, this weaker bound also follows from
`erdos_88`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_88.variants.erdos_mckay :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ δ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (G.cliqueNum : ℝ) < ε * Real.log n → (G.indepNum : ℝ) < ε * Real.log n →
        ∀ m : ℕ, (m : ℝ) ≤ δ * Real.log n ^ 2 →
          ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), (G.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).edgeSet.ncard = m

statements.name: Erdos88.erdos_88.variants.kwan_sah_sauermann_sawhney
statements.doc:
Kwan, Sah, Sauermann, and Sawhney [KSSS22, Theorem 1.1] proved the following stronger statement.
Fix $C > 0$ and $\eta > 0$, and let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with no independent set or
clique of size $\geq C \log_2 n$, where $n$ is sufficiently large with respect to $C$ and $\eta$.
Then for every integer $0 \leq m \leq (1 - \eta) e(G)$ there is an induced subgraph of $G$ with
exactly $m$ edges.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_88.variants.kwan_sah_sauermann_sawhney :
    ∀ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ η > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (G.cliqueNum : ℝ) < C * Real.logb 2 n → (G.indepNum : ℝ) < C * Real.logb 2 n →
        ∀ m : ℕ, (m : ℝ) ≤ (1 - η) * G.edgeSet.ncard →
          ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), (G.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).edgeSet.ncard = m

### AI disclosure

Lean 4 code in this file was drafted with assistance from OpenAI Codex.
The mathematical content and references are the author's own work.

statements.name: Erdos89.erdos_89
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er46] asked whether every set of $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$
determines $\gg \frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}$ many distinct distances.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_89 :
    (fun (n : ℕ) => n/(n : ℝ).log.sqrt) =O[atTop]
      (fun n => (minimalDistinctDistances ℝ² n : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos89.erdos_89.variants.n_dvd_log_n
statements.doc:
Guth and Katz [GuKa15] proved that there are always $\gg \frac{n}{\log n}$
many distinct distances.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_89.variants.n_dvd_log_n :
    (fun (n : ℕ) => n/(n : ℝ).log) =O[atTop]
      (fun n => (minimalDistinctDistances ℝ² n : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos89.erdos_89.variants.grid_upper_bound
statements.doc:
The square grid construction, going back to Erdős and Moser, shows that
$\frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}$ is the correct order if the conjecture is true:
there are configurations whose number of distinct distances is
$O(\frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}})$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_89.variants.grid_upper_bound :
    (fun n => (minimalDistinctDistances ℝ² n : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun (n : ℕ) => n/(n : ℝ).log.sqrt)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 90: The unit distance problem
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/90](https://www.erdosproblems.com/90)

The conjecture asks whether every set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ determines at most
$n^{1 + O(1/\log\log n)}$ unit distances. It was **disproved** in May 2026: an internal model at
OpenAI produced a construction beating the conjectured bound, with the proof digested and
human-verified in two arXiv papers:

* W. Sawin, [*An explicit lower bound for the unit distance problem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20579)
  (2026), giving $u(n) \ge n^{1.014114}/C$ for infinitely many $n$;
* N. Alon, T. F. Bloom, W. T. Gowers, D. Litt, W. Sawin, A. Shankar, J. Tsimerman, V. Wang and
  M. Matchett Wood, [*Remarks on the disproof of the unit distance conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20695)
  (2026), giving the qualitative form $u(n) \ge n^{1+\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon > 0$.

This file records the main statement (`erdos_90`), the two constructive disproof variants, the
logical implications between them, and the load-bearing reductions of Sawin's proof
(`sawin_lattice_reduction` and `sawin_totally_real_tower`) as further benchmark challenges.

statements.name: Erdos90.erdos_90
statements.doc:
Does every set of $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ contain at most
$n^{1+O(\frac{1}{\log\log n})}$ many pairs which are distance $1$ apart?

This was
[disproved](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/74c24085-19b0-4534-9c90-465b8e29ad73/unit-distance-proof.pdf)
by an internal model at OpenAI, which constructed (for infinitely many $n$) a set $P$ of $n$ points
in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that the number of unit distance pairs in $P$ is at least $n^{1+c}$, where
$c > 0$ is an absolute constant.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_90 : ¬ ∃ (O : ℕ → ℝ) (hO : O =O[atTop] (fun n => 1 / (n : ℝ).log.log)),
    (fun n => (maxUnitDistances n : ℝ)) =ᶠ[atTop] fun (n : ℕ) => (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + O n)

statements.name: Erdos90.erdos_90.variants.polynomial_lower_bound
statements.doc:
**Constructive form of the disproof.** There is an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that
infinitely many $n$ admit a configuration realising at least $n^{1+c}$ unit distances.

This is the qualitative content of Theorem 1.1 of Alon–Bloom–Gowers–Litt–Sawin–Shankar–
Tsimerman–Wang–Matchett Wood, [*Remarks on the disproof of the unit distance conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20695)
(2026). An explicit bound $c \ge 0.014114$ is given by Sawin, [*An explicit lower bound for the
unit distance problem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20579) (2026); see
`erdos_90.variants.sawin_explicit` below.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_90.variants.polynomial_lower_bound :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ),
      {n : ℕ | (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + c) ≤ (maxUnitDistances n : ℝ)}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos90.erdos_90.variants.sawin_explicit
statements.doc:
**Sawin's explicit exponent.** The constructive disproof can be realised with $c \ge 0.014114$
(absorbing the implicit constant $C$ of Sawin's Theorem 1 into a slightly smaller exponent for
all large enough $n$). Reference: Theorem 1 of Sawin, [arXiv:2605.20579](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20579)
(2026).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_90.variants.sawin_explicit :
    {n : ℕ | (n : ℝ) ^ (1.014114 : ℝ) ≤ (maxUnitDistances n : ℝ)}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos90.sawin_lattice_reduction
statements.doc:
**Sawin's Lemma 2: lattice geometry of unit distances** (Sawin, [arXiv:2605.20579](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20579)).

Let $d \ge 1$, $R > 1$, and suppose $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^{2d}$ is an additive subgroup
all of whose nonzero vectors have norm at least $\rho > 0$ (so $\Lambda$ is a lattice; Sawin takes
$\rho$ to be the norm of a shortest nonzero vector of $\Lambda$), equipped with an additive
embedding $\pi : \Lambda \to \mathbb{R}^2$. Suppose $S \subseteq \Lambda$ is a finite set of
"matching" vectors satisfying $\|v\| \le 1$ and $\|\pi v\| = 1$ for every $v \in S$. Then there
is a finite point set $U \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ of size $\#U \le (2R/\rho + 1)^{2d}$ whose
unit-distance density is at least $(1 - 1/R)^{2d}\,\#S$, i.e.
$(1-1/R)^{2d}\,\#S\,\#U \le \#\{(u_1, u_2) \in U^2 : |u_1 - u_2| = 1\}$. The right-hand side
counts ordered pairs, so it equals twice `unitDistNum U`.

This pure geometry-of-numbers reduction is the elementary heart of the disproof.
statements.statement:
theorem sawin_lattice_reduction
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (R : ℝ) (hR : 1 < R)
    (Λ : Submodule ℤ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (2*d))))
    (ρ : ℝ) (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hΛ : ∀ v : Λ, v ≠ 0 → ρ ≤ ‖(v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (2*d)))‖)
    (π : Λ →+ ℝ²) (hπ : Function.Injective π)
    (S : Finset Λ)
    (hS_norm : ∀ v ∈ S, ‖(v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (2*d)))‖ ≤ 1)
    (hS_proj : ∀ v ∈ S, ‖π v‖ = 1) :
    ∃ U : Finset ℝ², 0 < U.card ∧ (U.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 * R / ρ + 1) ^ (2*d) ∧
      ((1 : ℝ) - 1/R) ^ (2*d) * (S.card : ℝ) * (U.card : ℝ) ≤
        2 * (unitDistNum U : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos90.sawin_totally_real_tower
statements.doc:
**Sawin's Lemmas 11–12 / Remarks Proposition 2.3: the totally real tower.**

There exist $rdBound : \mathbb{R}$ and a *single* infinite set $Q$ of rational primes
$q \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ such that for every $N$ one can find a totally real number field $F/\mathbb{Q}$
of degree $\ge N$ with bounded root discriminant $|disc F|^{1/[F:\mathbb{Q}]} \le rdBound$ in which
*every* prime $q \in Q$ splits completely.

The load-bearing feature is the quantifier order: $Q$ is fixed *before* $F$, so the same primes
split completely in fields of *unbounded* degree. (For a single fixed $F$, Chebotarev already
gives infinitely many completely split primes $\equiv 1 \pmod 4$, so a per-field statement would
be vacuous.) This uniform splitting in an unbounded tower is the key arithmetic input to the
disproof. It is proved as Lemmas 11–12 of Sawin, [arXiv:2605.20579](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20579),
and as Proposition 2.3 of the [Remarks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20695) paper, via the
Golod–Shafarevich inequality for pro-$2$ groups together with the Hajir–Maire–Ramakrishna (2003)
tower construction.

A "completely split" rational prime $q$ in $F$ is one for which $(q)$ is the product of exactly
$[F:\mathbb{Q}]$ distinct maximal ideals.
statements.statement:
theorem sawin_totally_real_tower :
    ∃ (rdBound : ℝ) (Q : Set ℕ), Q.Infinite ∧ (∀ q ∈ Q, q.Prime ∧ q % 4 = 1) ∧
      ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F) (_ : CharZero F) (_ : NumberField F)
        (_ : IsTotallyReal F),
        N ≤ Module.finrank ℚ F ∧
        (|(NumberField.discr F : ℝ)|) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / Module.finrank ℚ F) ≤ rdBound ∧
        ∀ q ∈ Q, ∃ (factors : Finset (Ideal (𝓞 F))),
          factors.card = Module.finrank ℚ F ∧
          ∀ p ∈ factors, p.IsMaximal ∧ (q : 𝓞 F) ∈ p

problems.title: Erdős Problem 91
problems.doc:
*Reference:*
- [Er87b] Erdős, P., Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry.
  Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985) (1987), 167-177.
- [Ko24c] Z. Kovács, A note on Erdős's mysterious remark. arXiv:2412.05190 (2024).

statements.name: Erdos91.erdos_91
statements.doc:
Suppose $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ has $\lvert A\rvert=n$ and minimises the number of distinct
distances between points in $A$. Prove that for large $n$ there are at least two
(and probably many) such $A$ which are non-similar.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_91 :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ¬ UniqueMinimizer n

statements.name: Erdos91.erdos_91.variants.three
statements.doc: For $n = 3$ the equilateral triangle is the only such set.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_91.variants.three : UniqueMinimizer 3

statements.name: Erdos91.erdos_91.variants.four
statements.doc:
For $n=4$ the square or two equilateral triangles sharing an edge give two
non-similar examples.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_91.variants.four : ¬ UniqueMinimizer 4

statements.name: Erdos91.erdos_91.variants.five
statements.doc:
For $n = 5$ the regular pentagon is the unique such set (which has two distinct distances).
Erdős mysteriously remarks in [Er90] this was proved by 'a colleague'. (In [Er87b] this is
described as 'a colleague from Zagreb (unfortunately I do not have his letter)'.)
A published proof of this fact is provided by Kovács [Ko24c].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_91.variants.five : UniqueMinimizer 5

statements.name: Erdos91.erdos_91.variants.six
statements.doc: In [Er87b] on p.171 Erdős says that there are at least two non-similar examples for $n = 6$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_91.variants.six: ¬ UniqueMinimizer 6

statements.name: Erdos91.erdos_91.variants.seven
statements.doc: In [Er87b] on p.171 Erdős says that there are at least two non-similar examples for $n = 7$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_91.variants.seven: ¬ UniqueMinimizer 7

statements.name: Erdos91.erdos_91.variants.eight
statements.doc: In [Er87b] on p.171 Erdős says that there are at least two non-similar examples for $n = 8$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_91.variants.eight: ¬ UniqueMinimizer 8

statements.name: Erdos91.erdos_91.variants.nine
statements.doc: In [Er87b] on p.171 Erdős says that there are at least two non-similar examples for $n = 9$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_91.variants.nine: ¬ UniqueMinimizer 9

problems.title: Erdős Problem 92
problems.doc:
Both questions here are disproved, by way of Erdős Problem 90. The source says so directly: this
is a stronger form of the unit distance conjecture, so the disproof of that conjecture disproves
these too. See `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«90»`.

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/92](https://www.erdosproblems.com/92)

statements.name: Erdos92.erdos_92.variants.weak
statements.doc:
Is it true that $f(n)\leq n^{o(1)}$?

The source records this as disproved: "This is a stronger form of the unit distance conjecture
(see [90]). As such the recent disproof of [90] also disproves this." That disproof is
`Erdos90.erdos_90`, which this repository already records as `research solved` with the answer
`False`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_92.variants.weak : ¬ ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ,
  o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ n, (f n : ℝ) ≤ n^(o n)

statements.name: Erdos92.erdos_92.variants.strong
statements.doc:
Or even $f(n) < n^{c/\log\log n}$ for some constant $c > 0$?

Also disproved, and by the weak form rather than separately: since $c/\log\log n \to 0$, the bound
$n^{c/\log\log n}$ is of the form $n^{o(1)}$, so this statement implies
`erdos_92.variants.weak` and is false whenever that one is.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_92.variants.strong :
    ¬ ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (f n : ℝ) ≤ n^(c / (n : ℝ).log.log)

statements.name: Erdos93.erdos_93
statements.doc:
If $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then they determine at least
$\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\rfloor$ distinct distances.

Solved by Altman [Al63].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_93 (A : Finset ℝ²) (hA : ConvexIndep (A : Set ℝ²)) :
    A.card / 2 ≤ distinctDistances A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 94
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/94](https://www.erdosproblems.com/94)
- [Er92e] Erdős, Pál, *Some Unsolved problems in Geometry, Number Theory and Combinatorics*. Eureka
  (1992), 44-48.
- [Er97c] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*. The mathematics of Paul Erdős, I
  (1997), 47-67.
- [LeTh95] Lefmann, Hanno and Thiele, Torsten, *Point sets with distinct distances*. Combinatorica
  (1995), 379-408.

statements.name: Erdos94.erdos_94
statements.doc:
Suppose $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ determine a convex polygon and the set of distances between
them is $\{u_1,\ldots,u_t\}$. Suppose $u_i$ appears as the distance between $f(u_i)$ many pairs of
points. Then
$$\sum_i f(u_i)^2 \ll n^3.$$

In [Er97c] Erdős claims that Fishburn solved this, but gives no reference.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_94 : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ P : Finset ℝ², ConvexIndep (P : Set ℝ²) →
    ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, (distanceMultiplicity P u : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ C * (P.card : ℝ) ^ 3

statements.name: Erdos94.erdos_94.variants.no_three_on_a_line
statements.doc:
Lefmann and Theile [LeTh95] prove a stronger version of this question, that
$$\sum_i f(u_i)^2 \ll n^3$$
under the weaker assumption that no three points are on a line.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_94.variants.no_three_on_a_line : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ P : Finset ℝ²,
    NonTrilinear (P : Set ℝ²) →
    ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, (distanceMultiplicity P u : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ C * (P.card : ℝ) ^ 3

statements.name: Erdos94.erdos_94.variants.regular_ngon
statements.doc:
Erdős and Fishburn also make the stronger conjecture that $\sum f(u_i)^2$ is maximal for the
regular $n$-gon (for large enough $n$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_94.variants.regular_ngon : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ P : Finset ℝ²,
    P.card = n → ConvexIndep (P : Set ℝ²) →
    ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, (distanceMultiplicity P u : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤
      ∑ u ∈ distanceSet (regularNGon n), (distanceMultiplicity (regularNGon n) u : ℝ) ^ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 95
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/95](https://www.erdosproblems.com/95)
- [Er92e] Erdős, Pál, *Some Unsolved problems in Geometry, Number Theory and Combinatorics*.
  Eureka (1992), 44-48.
- [Er95] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and
  geometry*. Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
- [Er97c] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*. The mathematics of Paul
  Erdős, I (1997), 47-67.
- [Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability
  (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
- [Al63] Altman, E., *On a problem of P. Erdős*. Amer. Math. Monthly (1963), 148-157.
- [GuKa15] Guth, Larry and Katz, Nets Hawk, *On the Erdős distinct distances problem in the
  plane*. Ann. of Math. (2) (2015), 155-190.

statements.name: Erdos95.erdos_95
statements.doc:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb{R}^2$ determine the set of distances $\{u_1,\ldots,u_t\}$. Suppose
$u_i$ appears as the distance between $f(u_i)$ many pairs of points. Then for all $\epsilon>0$
$$\sum_i f(u_i)^2 \ll_\epsilon n^{3+\epsilon}.$$

The case when the points determine a convex polygon was solved by Altman [Al63]. Note it is
trivial that $\sum f(u_i)=\binom{n}{2}$.

Solved by Guth and Katz [GuKa15] who proved the upper bound
$$\sum_i f(u_i)^2 \ll n^3\log n.$$

See also [94](https://www.erdosproblems.com/94).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_95 : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ P : Finset ℝ²,
    ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, (distanceMultiplicity P u : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤
      C * (P.card : ℝ) ^ (3 + ε)

statements.name: Erdos95.erdos_95.variants.guth_katz
statements.doc: Guth and Katz [GuKa15] proved the upper bound $\sum_i f(u_i)^2 \ll n^3\log n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_95.variants.guth_katz : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ P : Finset ℝ², 2 ≤ P.card →
    ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, (distanceMultiplicity P u : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤
      C * (P.card : ℝ) ^ 3 * Real.log P.card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 96
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/96](https://www.erdosproblems.com/96)

statements.name: Erdos96.erdos_96
statements.doc:
If $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then there are $O(n)$ many pairs which are
distance $1$ apart.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_96 :
    (fun n => (maxConvexUnitDistances n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n => (n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 97
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/97](https://www.erdosproblems.com/97)

statements.name: Erdos97.erdos_97
statements.doc: Does every convex polygon have a vertex with no other 4 vertices equidistant from it?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_97 :
    ∀ A : Finset ℝ², A.Nonempty → ConvexIndep A → ¬HasNEquidistantProperty 4 A

statements.name: Erdos97.erdos_97.variants.three_equidistant
statements.doc:
Erdős originally conjectured this (in [Er46b]) with no 3 vertices equidistant,
but Danzer found a convex polygon on 9 points such that every vertex has three
vertices equidistant from it (but this distance depends on the vertex).
Danzer's construction is explained in [Er87b].

[Er46b] Erdős, P., _On sets of distances of $n$ points_. Amer. Math. Monthly (1946), 248-250.
[Er87b] Erdős, P., _Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry_. Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985), 167-177.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_97.variants.three_equidistant :
    ∃ A : Finset ℝ², A.Nonempty ∧ ConvexIndep A ∧ HasNEquidistantProperty 3 A

statements.name: Erdos97.erdos_97.variants.k_equidistant
statements.doc:
Erdős also conjectured that there is a $k$ for which every convex polygon has a vertex
with no other $k$ vertices equidistant from it.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_97.variants.k_equidistant :
    ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset ℝ², A.Nonempty → ConvexIndep A → ¬HasNEquidistantProperty k A

statements.name: Erdos97.erdos_97.variants.three_unit_distance
statements.doc:
Fishburn and Reeds [FiRe92] have found a convex polygon on 20 points such that
every vertex has three vertices equidistant from it (and this distance is the same for all vertices).

[FiRe92] Fishburn, P. C. and Reeds, J. A., _Unit distances between vertices of a convex polygon_. Comput. Geom. (1992), 81-91.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_97.variants.three_unit_distance :
    ∃ A : Finset ℝ², A.Nonempty ∧ ConvexIndep A ∧ HasNUnitDistanceProperty 3 A

statements.name: Erdos97.erdos_97.variants.three_unit_distance_cut_min
statements.doc:
Fishburn and Reeds [FiRe92] also proved that the smallest $n$ for which there exists
a convex $n$-gon and a cut $\{A, B\}$ of its vertices such that $|\{b \in B : d(a, b) = 1\}| ≥ 3$
for all $a \in A$, and $|\{a \in A : d(a, b) = 1\}| ≥ 3$ for all $b \in B$, is $n = 20$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_97.variants.three_unit_distance_cut_min :
    sInf {n : ℕ | ∃ (V : Finset ℝ²) (A B : Finset ℝ²),
      n = V.card ∧ ConvexIndep V ∧ A.Nonempty ∧ B.Nonempty ∧ IsCut V A B ∧
      HasNUnitDistancePointsOn 3 B A ∧ HasNUnitDistancePointsOn 3 A B} = 20

problems.title: Erdős Problem 98
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [[Er75f](https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=411984)]
  Erdős, Paul, On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry.
  Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. (4) (1975), 99-108.
- [[Er83c](https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=706025)]

  Erdős, P., Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry.
  Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985) (1987), 167-177.
- [[Er90](https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=1117038)]
  Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite unsolved problems.
  A tribute to Paul Erdős (1990), 467-478.
- [[Er92b](https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=1275857)]
  Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics.
  Matematiche (Catania) (1992), 231-240.
- [[EFPR93](https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=1210096)]
  Erdős, Paul and Füredi, Zoltán and Pach, János and Ruzsa, Imre Z.,
  The grid revisited. Discrete Math. (1993), 189-196.
- [[Er94b](https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=1304854)]

- [erdosproblems.com/98](https://www.erdosproblems.com/98)

statements.name: Erdos98.erdos_98
statements.doc:
Let $h(n)$ be such that any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, with no three on a line
and no four on a circle, determine at least $h(n)$ distinct distances. Does
$h(n)/n\to \infty$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_98 :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((h n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ))) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos98.erdos_98.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős could not even prove $h(n)\geq n$. Pach has shown $h(n) < n^{\log_2 3}$.
Erdős, Füredi, and Pach [EFPR93] have improved this to
$h(n) < n\exp(c\sqrt{\log n})$ for some constant $c>0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_98.variants.upper_bound :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (h n : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) * Real.exp (c * Real.sqrt (Real.log (n : ℝ)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 99
problems.doc:
*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/99](https://www.erdosproblems.com/99)
* [BeFo99] Bezdek, Andr\'{a}s and Fodor, Ferenc, Minimal diameter of certain sets in the plane. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1999), 105-111.
* [Er94b] Erd\H{o}s, Paul, Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and combinatorial geometry. Math. Pannon. (1994), 261-269.

statements.name: Erdos99.erdos_99
statements.doc:
For sufficiently large n, is it the case that any set of n points with minimum distance $1$
that minimizes diameter must contain an equilateral triangle of side length 1?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_99 :
    ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℝ²,
      A.card = n → HasMinDist1 A →
      (IsMinOn (fun B: Finset ℝ² => diam (B : Set ℝ²)) {B : Finset ℝ² | B.card = n ∧ HasMinDist1 B} A) →
      ∃ᵉ (p ∈ A) (q ∈ A) (r ∈ A), FormsEquilateralTriangle p q r

problems.title: Erdős Problem 100
problems.doc:
*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/100](https://www.erdosproblems.com/100)
* [Kanold](No references found)
* [GuKa15](Guth, Larry and Katz, Nets Hawk, On the Erd\H{o}s distinct distances problem in the plane. Ann. of Math. (2) (2015), 155-190.)
* [Piepmeyer](No references found)

statements.name: Erdos100.erdos_100
statements.doc: Is the diameter of $A$ at least $Cn$ for some constant $C > 0$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_100 :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℝ²,
      A.card = n →
      DistancesSeparated A →
      diam (A : Set ℝ²) > C * n

statements.name: Erdos100.erdos_100.variants.strong
statements.doc: Stronger conjecture: diameter $\geq n - 1$ for sufficiently large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_100.variants.strong :
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℝ²,
      A.card = n →
      DistancesSeparated A →
      diam (A : Set ℝ²) ≥ n - 1

statements.name: Erdos100.erdos_100.variants.kanold
statements.doc:
From [Kanold]: diameter $\geq n^{3/4}$.
TODO: find reference
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_100.variants.kanold :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℝ²,
      A.card = n →
      DistancesSeparated A →
      diam (A : Set ℝ²) ≥ (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 4 : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos100.erdos_100.variants.guth_katz
statements.doc: From [GuKa15]: diameter $\gg n / \log n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_100.variants.guth_katz :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℝ²,
      A.card = n →
      DistancesSeparated A →
      diam (A : Set ℝ²) ≥ C * n / log n

statements.name: Erdos100.erdos_100_piepmeyer
statements.doc:
From [Piepmeyer]: 9 points with diameter $< 5$.
TODO: find reference
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_100_piepmeyer :
    ∃ A : Finset ℝ², A.card = 9 ∧ DistancesSeparated A ∧
      diam (A : Set ℝ²) < 5

problems.title: Erdős Problem 101
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/101](https://www.erdosproblems.com/101)

statements.name: Erdos101.erdos_101
statements.doc:
Given $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, no five of which are on a line, the number of
lines containing four points is $o(n^2)$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_101 : (fun n => (numLinesWithFourPointMax n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n => (n : ℝ)^2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 102
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/102](https://www.erdosproblems.com/102)

statements.name: Erdos102.erdos_102
statements.doc:
Let $c > 0$ and let $h_c(n)$ be such that for any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with at least
$cn^2$ lines that each contain more than three of the points, some line contains $h_c(n)$ of
the points. Is it true that, for fixed $c > 0$, $h_c(n) \to \infty$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_102 :
    ∀ c > 0, ∀ M : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (M : ℕ∞) ≤ h c n

statements.name: Erdos102.erdos_102.variants.five
statements.doc: It is not known whether $h_c(n) \geq 5$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_102.variants.five :
    ∀ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (5 : ℕ∞) ≤ h c n

statements.name: Erdos102.erdos_102.variants.upper_sqrt
statements.doc:
It is easy to see that $h_c(n) \ll_c n^{1/2}$: for all sufficiently small $c > 0$ there are
admissible configurations (e.g. grids) in which no line contains more than $C_c n^{1/2}$ points.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_102.variants.upper_sqrt :
    ∃ c₀ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ c ∈ Set.Ioc 0 c₀, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      h c n ≤ (⌈C * Real.sqrt n⌉₊ : ℕ∞)

statements.name: Erdos102.erdos_102.variants.hunter
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er95] suggested that perhaps $h_c(n) \gg_c n^{1/2}$. Zach Hunter pointed out that this is
false: the points of $\{1, \dots, m\}^d$ with $n \approx m^d$, randomly projected to
$\mathbb{R}^2$, meet every line in $\ll_d n^{1/d}$ points and determine $\gg_d n^2$ lines with
more than three points. This gives $h_c(n) \ll n^{1 / \log(1/c)}$; we state the underlying form:
for every $d \geq 1$ there is $c > 0$ with $h_c(n) \ll_d n^{1/d}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_102.variants.hunter :
    ∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      h c n ≤ (⌈C * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / (d : ℝ))⌉₊ : ℕ∞)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 103
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/103](https://www.erdosproblems.com/103)

statements.name: Erdos103.erdos_103
statements.doc:
Let $h(n)$ count the number of incongruent sets of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ which minimise
the diameter subject to the constraint that $d(x,y)\geq 1$ for all points $x\neq y$. Is it true
that $h(n)\to \infty$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_103 : Tendsto h atTop (nhds ⊤)

statements.name: Erdos103.erdos_103.variants.two_le
statements.doc: It is not even known whether $h(n)\geq 2$ for all large $n$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_103.variants.two_le : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, 2 ≤ h n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 104
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/104](https://www.erdosproblems.com/104)
- [El84] Elekes, G., *{$n$} points in the plane can determine $n^{3/2}$ unit circles*. Combinatorica
  (1984), 131.
- [Er75h] Erdős, P., *Some problems on elementary geometry*. Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. (1975), 2-3.
- [Er81d] Erdős, P., *Some applications of graph theory and combinatorial methods to number theory
  and geometry*. Algebraic methods in graph theory, Vol. I, II (Szeged, 1978) (1981), 137-148.
- [Er92e] Erdős, Pál, *Some Unsolved problems in Geometry, Number Theory and Combinatorics*. Eureka
  (1992), 44-48.
- [HaMe86] Harborth, Heiko and Mengersen, Ingrid, *Point sets with many unit circles*. Discrete
  Math. (1986), 193--197.

statements.name: Erdos104.erdos_104
statements.doc: Given $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ the number of distinct unit circles containing at least three points is $o(n^2)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_104 :
    (fun n : ℕ => (maxUnitCircleCount n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 105
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/105](https://www.erdosproblems.com/105)
- [Be83] Beck, József, *On the lattice property of the plane and some problems of Dirac, Motzkin
  and Erdős in combinatorial geometry*. Combinatorica (1983), 281-297.
- [ErPu95] Erdős, P. and Purdy, G., *Two combinatorial problems in the plane*. Discrete Comput.
  Geom. (1995), 441-443.
- [SzTr83] Szemerédi, Endre and Trotter, Jr., William T., *Extremal problems in discrete
  geometry*. Combinatorica (1983), 381-392.

statements.name: Erdos105.erdos_105
statements.doc:
Let $A,B\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be disjoint sets of size $n$ and $n-3$ respectively, with not all
of $A$ contained on a single line. Is there a line which contains at least two points from $A$
and no points from $B$?

This has been disproved by Xichuan in the comments, who has found three explicit
counterexamples.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_105 :
    ¬ ∀ A B : Finset ℝ², Disjoint A B → A.card = B.card + 3 →
      ¬ Collinear ℝ (A : Set ℝ²) →
      ∃ p ∈ A, ∃ q ∈ A, p ≠ q ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, b ∉ line[ℝ, p, q]

statements.name: Erdos105.erdos_105.variants.hickerson
statements.doc: A construction of Hickerson shows that this fails with $n-2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_105.variants.hickerson : ¬ ∀ A B : Finset ℝ², Disjoint A B →
    A.card = B.card + 2 → ¬ Collinear ℝ (A : Set ℝ²) →
    ∃ p ∈ A, ∃ q ∈ A, p ≠ q ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, b ∉ line[ℝ, p, q]

statements.name: Erdos105.erdos_105.variants.beck_szemeredi_trotter
statements.doc:
A result independently proved by Beck [Be83] and Szemerédi and Trotter [SzTr83] (see [211])
implies it is true with $n-3$ replaced by $cn$ for some constant $c>0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_105.variants.beck_szemeredi_trotter : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ),
    ∀ A B : Finset ℝ², Disjoint A B → (B.card : ℝ) ≤ c * A.card →
      ¬ Collinear ℝ (A : Set ℝ²) →
      ∃ p ∈ A, ∃ q ∈ A, p ≠ q ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, b ∉ line[ℝ, p, q]

statements.name: Erdos105.erdos_105.variants.sub_four
statements.doc:
It remains possible that this holds with $n-4$ (or in general with $n-O(1)$ or $(1-o(1))n$).

This fails with $n-4$ as well: Core_65536 gives an explicit counterexample in the
[forum](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/105#post-8033) (24 July 2026), with $|A| = 10$
and $|B| = 6$ and integer coordinates, in which every line through two points of $A$ contains a
point of $B$. The incidences have been verified in Lean.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_105.variants.sub_four :
    ¬ ∀ A B : Finset ℝ², Disjoint A B → A.card = B.card + 4 →
      ¬ Collinear ℝ (A : Set ℝ²) →
      ∃ p ∈ A, ∃ q ∈ A, p ≠ q ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, b ∉ line[ℝ, p, q]

problems.title: Erdős Problem 107
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/107](https://www.erdosproblems.com/107)
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy_ending_problem)

statements.name: Erdos107.erdos_107
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that any $f(n)$ points in $ℝ^2$, no three on a line,
contain $n$ points which form the vertices of a convex $n$-gon.
Prove that $f(n) = 2^{n-2} + 1$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_107 : ∀ n ≥ 3, f n = 2^(n - 2) + 1

statements.name: Erdos107.nonempty_cardSet
statements.doc:
For every $n ≥ 3$, there exists $N$ such that any $N$ points, no three on a line,
contain a convex $n$-gon.
statements.statement: theorem nonempty_cardSet : ∀ n ≥ 3, (cardSet n).Nonempty

statements.name: Erdos107.variants.ersz_bounds
statements.doc:
Erdős and Szekeres proved the bounds
$$
  2^{n-2} + 1 ≤ f(n) ≤ \binom{2n-4}{n-2} + 1
$$
([ErSz60] and [ErSz35] respectively).

[ErSz60] Erdős, P. and Szekeres, G., _On some extremum problems in elementary geometry_.
  Ann. Univ. Sci. Budapest. Eötvös Sect. Math. (1960/61), 53-62.

[ErSz35] Erdős, P. and Szekeres, G., _A combinatorial problem in geometry_.
  Compos. Math. (1935), 463-470.
statements.statement:
theorem ersz_bounds :
    ∀ n ≥ 3, 2^(n - 2) + 1 ≤ f n ∧ f n ≤ Nat.choose (2 * n - 4) (n - 2) + 1

statements.name: Erdos107.variants.su_bound
statements.doc:
Suk [Su17] proved
$$
  f(n) ≤ 2^{(1+o(1))n}.
$$

[Su17] Suk, Andrew, _On the Erdős-Szekeres convex polygon problem_.
  J. Amer. Math. Soc. (2017), 1047-1053.
statements.statement:
theorem su_bound :
    ∃ r : ℕ → ℝ, r =o[atTop] (fun n => (n : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ n ≥ 3, (f n : ℝ) ≤ 2^(n + r n)

statements.name: Erdos107.variants.hmpt_bound
statements.doc:
The current best bound is due to Holmsen, Mojarrad, Pach, and Tardos [HMPT20],
who prove
$$
  f(n) ≤ 2^{n+O(\sqrt{n\log n})}.
$$

[HMPT20] Holmsen, Andreas F. and Mojarrad, Hossein Nassajian and Pach, János and Tardos, Gábor,
  _Two extensions of the Erdős-Szekeres problem_. J. Eur. Math. Soc. (JEMS) (2020), 3981-3995.
statements.statement:
theorem hmpt_bound :
    ∃ r : ℕ → ℝ, r =O[atTop] (fun n => Real.sqrt (n * Real.log n)) ∧
      ∀ n ≥ 3, (f n : ℝ) ≤ 2^(n + r n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 108
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/108](https://www.erdosproblems.com/108)

statements.name: Erdos108.erdos_108
statements.doc:
For every r ≥ 4 and k ≥ 2 is there some finite f(k,r) such that every graph of chromatic number ≥ f(k,r)
contains a subgraph of girth ≥ r and chromatic number ≥ k?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_108 :
    ∀ r ≥ 4, ∀ k ≥ (2 : ℕ), ∃ (f : ℕ),
    ∀ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V) (_ : Nonempty V)
      (hchro : f ≤ SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber G),
    ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), (SimpleGraph.girth H.coe ≥ r) ∧
    (SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber H.coe ≥ k)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 109
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/109](https://www.erdosproblems.com/109)
- [MRR19] J. Moreira, F.K. Richter, and D. Robertson, A proof of a sumset conjecture of Erdős,
  Annals of Math. 189 (2019), 605-652.

statements.name: Erdos109.erdos_109
statements.doc:
Any $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of positive upper density contains a sumset $B+C$ where both $B$ and $C$
are infinite.

The Erdős sumset conjecture. Proved by Moreira, Richter, and Robertson [MRR19].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_109 (A : Set ℕ) (h : A.upperDensity > 0) :
    ∃ B C : Set ℕ, B.Infinite ∧ C.Infinite ∧ B + C ⊆ A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 110
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/110](https://www.erdosproblems.com/110)
- [EHS82] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A. and Szemerédi, E., *On almost bipartite large chromatic graphs*.
  Theory and practice of combinatorics (1982), 117-123.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1982-11.pdf)
- [Er87] Erdős, P., *Some problems on finite and infinite graphs*. Logic and combinatorics
  (Arcata, Calif., 1985) (1987), 223-228. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-28.pdf)
- [Er95d] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems in combinatorial set theory*. Publ. Inst. Math.
  (Beograd) (N.S.) (1995), 61-65.
- [KoSh05] Komjáth, Péter and Shelah, Saharon, *Finite subgraphs of uncountably chromatic graphs*.
  J. Graph Theory (2005), 28--38.
- [La20] Lambie-Hanson, Chris, *On the growth rate of chromatic numbers of finite subgraphs*.
  Adv. Math. (2020), 107176, 13. [arXiv:1902.08177](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.08177)
- [dBEr51] de Bruijn, N. G. and Erdős, P., *A colour problem for infinite graphs and a problem in
  the theory of relations*. Indag. Math. (1951), 369--373.

statements.name: Erdos110.erdos_110
statements.doc:
Is there some $F(n)$ such that every graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ has, for all large
$n$, a subgraph with chromatic number $n$ on at most $F(n)$ vertices?

A question of Erdős, Hajnal, and Szemerédi (see [EHS82], [Er87, p. 225, Problem 6], [Er95d]).
The answer is no: Komjáth and Shelah [KoSh05] proved that it is consistent that the answer is no,
and Lambie-Hanson [La20, Theorem A] constructed a counterexample in ZFC. The statement below is
therefore the negation. Subgraphs need not be induced, and finiteness of `H.verts` is explicit
because `Set.ncard` is `0` on infinite sets. Graphs are taken in `Type 1`, the universe of the
vertex type in the linked proof's construction. A counterexample in `Type` would give one in
`Type 1` by `ULift`; conversely, Lambie-Hanson's graph has $2^{\aleph_1}$ vertices, so it also
exists in `Type`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_110 :
    ¬ ∃ F : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ (V : Type 1) (G : SimpleGraph V), Erdos737.ChromaticNumberAlephOne G →
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ H : G.Subgraph,
        H.verts.Finite ∧ H.verts.ncard ≤ F n ∧ H.coe.chromaticNumber = (n : ℕ∞)

statements.name: Erdos110.erdos_110.variants.lambie_hanson
statements.doc:
Lambie-Hanson's quantitative theorem [La20, Theorem A], of which `erdos_110` is a consequence:
for every $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ there is a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ such
that, for every $k \geq 3$, every finite subgraph with fewer than $f(k)$ vertices has chromatic
number less than $k$. (The graph constructed in [La20] has $2^{\aleph_1}$ vertices.)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_110.variants.lambie_hanson (f : ℕ → ℕ) :
    ∃ (V : Type 1) (G : SimpleGraph V), Erdos737.ChromaticNumberAlephOne G ∧
      ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k → ∀ H : G.Subgraph, H.verts.Finite → H.verts.ncard < f k →
        H.coe.chromaticNumber < (k : ℕ∞)

statements.name: Erdos110.erdos_110.variants.de_bruijn_erdos
statements.doc:
A theorem of de Bruijn and Erdős [dBEr51] implies that, if $G$ has infinite chromatic number,
then $G$ has a finite subgraph of chromatic number $n$ for every $n\geq 1$.

Infinite chromatic number is `G.chromaticNumber = ⊤`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_110.variants.de_bruijn_erdos {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (hG : G.chromaticNumber = ⊤) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    ∃ H : G.Subgraph, H.verts.Finite ∧ H.coe.chromaticNumber = (n : ℕ∞)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 111
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/111](https://www.erdosproblems.com/111)
- [Er81] Erdős, P., On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved. (1981)
- [EHS82] Erdős, P., Hajnal, A., and Szemerédi, E., On almost bipartite large chromatic graphs.
  Theory and practice of combinatorics (1982), 117–123.
- [Er87] Erdős, P., Some problems on finite and infinite graphs. (1987)
- [Er90] Erdős, P., Some of my favourite unsolved problems. (1990)
- [Er97d] Erdős, P., Some recent problems and results in graph theory. (1997)
- [Er97f] Erdős, P., Some unsolved problems. (1997)

See also Erdős Problem [74].

## Formalization notes

- **`bipartiteDistance G`**: the minimum number of edges to delete from a (finite) simple graph $G$
  to make it bipartite. Defined as the infimum over all spanning subgraphs $H \leq G$ with
  `H.IsBipartite` of the number of edges in `G.edgeSet \ H.edgeSet`.

- **`hG G n`**: for a graph $G$ on vertex type $V$, `hG G n` is the supremum over all sets $S$ of
  vertices of cardinality $n$ of `bipartiteDistance (G.induce S)`. This matches the problem's
  formulation: "any subgraph of $G$ on $n$ vertices can be made bipartite after deleting at most
  $h_G(n)$ edges."

statements.name: Erdos111.erdos_111
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 111** (Erdős, Hajnal, Szemerédi [EHS82]):

If $G$ is a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$, is it true that $h_G(n)/n \to \infty$?

Formally: for every graph $G$ (on a type $V$) with chromatic cardinal $\aleph_1$, the ratio
$h_G(n)/n$ tends to infinity: for every constant $C$, all sufficiently large $n$ satisfy
$h_G(n) > C \cdot n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_111 :
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 →
      Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (hG G n : ℝ) / n) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

statements.name: Erdos111.erdos_111.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
**Linear lower bound (ZFC, [EHS82])**: Every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ has
$h_G(n) \geq c \cdot n$ for some positive constant $c > 0$ and all sufficiently large $n$
(i.e., the *linear* lower bound $h_G(n) \gg n$ is known).

This follows from the fact that every graph with uncountable chromatic number contains
$\aleph_1$ vertex-disjoint odd cycles of some fixed odd length $\ell$: any induced subgraph
on $n$ vertices containing $\gg n / \ell$ such cycles requires removing $\gg n$ edges to
become bipartite.

This is a *strictly weaker* statement than the headline `erdos_111`, which asks for
$h_G(n)/n \to \infty$ (i.e., $h_G(n)$ grows *super-linearly* — the constant `c` could be
taken arbitrarily large for a fixed graph $G$). Whether the linear lower bound can be
improved to super-linear remains the open question.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_111.variants.lower_bound :
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 →
      ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
        ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop, c * n ≤ hG G n

statements.name: Erdos111.erdos_111.variants.upper_bound_existence
statements.doc:
**Upper bound existence (Erdős-Hajnal-Szemerédi [EHS82])**: There exists a graph $G$ with
chromatic number $\aleph_1$ such that $h_G(n) \ll n^{3/2}$, i.e., there is a constant $C > 0$
with $h_G(n) \leq C \cdot n^{3/2}$ for all $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_111.variants.upper_bound_existence :
    ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 ∧
      (fun n : ℕ => (hG G n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos111.erdos_111.variants.erdos_conjecture
statements.doc:
Erdős conjectured [Er81] that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a graph $G$ with
$\chi(G) = \aleph_1$ such that $h_G(n) \ll n^{1+\varepsilon}$.
The graph is chosen after $\varepsilon$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_111.variants.erdos_conjecture :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V),
      G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 ∧
        (fun n : ℕ => (hG G n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + ε))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 113
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/113](https://www.erdosproblems.com/113)
- [ErSi84] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M., *Cube-supersaturated graphs and related problems*.
  Progress in graph theory (Waterloo, Ont., 1982) (1984), 203-218.
- [Er90] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. A tribute to Paul Erdős (1990),
  467-478.
- [Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991),
  397-406.
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [Ja23b] Janzer, Oliver, *Disproof of a conjecture of Erdős and Simonovits on the Turán number
  of graphs with minimum degree 3*. Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN (2023), 8478--8494.

statements.name: Erdos113.erdos_113
statements.doc:
If $G$ is bipartite then $\mathrm{ex}(n;G)\ll n^{3/2}$ if and only $G$ is $2$-degenerate, that
is, $G$ contains no induced subgraph with minimal degree at least 3.

Conjectured by Erdős and Simonovits [ErSi84]. Erdős first offered \$250 for a proof and \$100 for
a counterexample, but in [Er93] offered \$500 for a counterexample. Disproved by Janzer [Ja23b]
who constructed, for any $\epsilon>0$, a $3$-regular bipartite graph $H$ such that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;H)\ll n^{\frac{4}{3}+\epsilon}.$$

See also [146](https://www.erdosproblems.com/146) and [147](https://www.erdosproblems.com/147).

The linked formal proof refutes the "only if" direction via Janzer's construction.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_113 : ¬ ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsBipartite →
    (((fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n G : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ)) ↔
      G.IsDegenerate 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 114
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/114](https://www.erdosproblems.com/114)
- [EHP58] Erdős, P., Herzog, F. and Piranian, G., *Metric properties of polynomials*.
  J. Analyse Math. (1958), 125-148.
- [ErHa99] Eremenko, A. and Hayman, W., *On the length of lemniscates*. Michigan Math. J. (1999),
  409-415. [arXiv:0805.2295](https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.2295)
- [Ta25] Tao, T., *The maximal length of the Erdős–Herzog–Piranian lemniscate in high degree*
  (2025). [arXiv:2512.12455](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.12455)

statements.name: Erdos114.erdos_114
statements.doc:
If $p(z) \in \mathbb{C}[z]$ is a monic polynomial of degree $n$, is the length of the curve
$\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \lvert p(z)\rvert = 1\}$ maximised when $p(z) = z^n - 1$?

We require $n \geq 1$. For $n = 0$ the only monic polynomial is $1$, whose level set is all of
$\mathbb{C}$, while $z^0 - 1 = 0$ has an empty level set.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_114 :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℂ[X], p.Monic → p.natDegree = n →
      lemniscateLength p ≤ lemniscateLength (X ^ n - 1)

statements.name: Erdos114.erdos_114.variants.large_n
statements.doc:
Tao [Ta25] proved that $z^n - 1$ maximises the length of the lemniscate for all sufficiently
large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_114.variants.large_n : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ p : ℂ[X], p.Monic → p.natDegree = n →
    lemniscateLength p ≤ lemniscateLength (X ^ n - 1)

statements.name: Erdos114.erdos_114.variants.two
statements.doc: Eremenko and Hayman [ErHa99] proved the case $n = 2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_114.variants.two (p : ℂ[X]) (hp : p.Monic) (hdeg : p.natDegree = 2) :
    lemniscateLength p ≤ lemniscateLength (X ^ 2 - 1)

statements.name: Erdos114.erdos_114.variants.one
statements.doc:
The case $n = 1$. A monic linear polynomial is $z - a$. Its lemniscate is a translate of the
lemniscate of $z - 1$, and translations preserve Hausdorff measure.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_114.variants.one (p : ℂ[X]) (hp : p.Monic) (hdeg : p.natDegree = 1) :
    lemniscateLength p ≤ lemniscateLength (X ^ 1 - 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 115
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/115](https://www.erdosproblems.com/115)
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Er90] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. A tribute to Paul Erdős (1990),
  467-478.
- [ErLe94] Erëmenko, A. and Lempert, L., *An extremal problem for polynomials*. Proc. Amer. Math.
  Soc. (1994), 191-193.
- [Po59a] Pommerenke, Ch., *On the derivative of a polynomial*. Michigan Math. J. (1959), 373-375.

statements.name: Erdos115.erdos_115
statements.doc:
If $p(z)$ is a polynomial of degree $n$ such that $\{z : \lvert p(z)\rvert\leq 1\}$ is connected
then is it true that
$$\max_{\substack{z\in\mathbb{C}\\ \lvert p(z)\rvert\leq 1}} \lvert p'(z)\rvert
\leq (\tfrac{1}{2}+o(1))n^2?$$

Eremenko and Lempert [ErLe94] have shown this is true, and in fact Chebyshev polynomials are the
extreme examples.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_115 :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ p : Polynomial ℂ, p.Monic → p.natDegree = n →
      IsConnected {z : ℂ | ‖p.eval z‖ ≤ 1} → ∀ z : ℂ, ‖p.eval z‖ ≤ 1 →
        ‖p.derivative.eval z‖ ≤ (1 / 2 + ε) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 116
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/116](https://www.erdosproblems.com/116)
- [EHP58] Erdős, P. and Herzog, F. and Piranian, G., *Metric properties of polynomials*. J.
  Analyse Math. (1958), 125-148.
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*. (1982),
  59--79.
- [Er90] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. A tribute to Paul Erdős (1990),
  467-478.
- [Er97c] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*. The mathematics of Paul Erdős,
  I (1997), 47-67.
- [Po61] Pommerenke, Ch., *On metric properties of complex polynomials*. Michigan Math. J. (1961),
  97-115.
- [KLR25] M. Krishnapur, E. Lundberg, and K. Ramachandran, *On the area of polynomial
  lemniscates*. arXiv:2503.18270 (2025).
- [Wa88] Wagner, Gerold, *On the area of lemniscate domains*. J. Analyse Math. (1988), 159-167.
- [Po28] G. Pólya, *Beitrag zue Verallgemeinerung des Verzerrungssatzes auf mehrfach
  zusammenhängende Gebiete*. S-B. Akad. Wiss. (1928), 228-232 and 280-282.

statements.name: Erdos116.erdos_116
statements.doc:
Let $p(z)=\prod_{i=1}^n (z-z_i)$ for $\lvert z_i\rvert \leq 1$. Is it true that
$$\lvert\{ z: \lvert p(z)\rvert <1\}\rvert>n^{-O(1)}$$
(or perhaps even $>(\log n)^{-O(1)}$)?

Conjectured by Erdős, Herzog, and Piranian [EHP58]. The lower bound $\gg n^{-4}$ follows from a
result of Pommerenke [Po61]. The lower bound $\gg (\log n)^{-1}$ was proved by Krishnapur,
Lundberg, and Ramachandran [KLR25].

Wagner [Wa88] proves, for $n\geq 3$, the existence of such polynomials with
$$\lvert\{ z: \lvert p(z)\rvert <1\}\rvert \ll_\epsilon (\log\log n)^{-1/2+\epsilon}$$
for all $\epsilon>0$. Krishnapur, Lundberg, and Ramachandran [KLR25] improved this upper bound to
$\ll (\log\log n)^{-1}$.

Pólya [Po28] showed the upper bound $\lvert\{ z: \lvert p(z)\rvert <1\}\rvert \leq \pi$ always
holds, and this is achieved only when the $z_i$ are identical.

statements.name: Erdos116.erdos_116.variants.log
statements.doc:
The lower bound $\lvert\{ z: \lvert p(z)\rvert <1\}\rvert \gg (\log n)^{-1}$ was proved by
Krishnapur, Lundberg, and Ramachandran [KLR25]; in particular the answer to the $(\log n)^{-O(1)}$
form of the question is also yes.

statements.name: Erdos116.erdos_116.variants.upper
statements.doc:
Krishnapur, Lundberg, and Ramachandran [KLR25] proved that there are polynomials with
$\lvert\{ z: \lvert p(z)\rvert <1\}\rvert \ll (\log\log n)^{-1}$, improving a result of Wagner
[Wa88].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_116.variants.upper : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, 3 ≤ n →
    ∃ z : Fin n → ℂ, (∀ i, ‖z i‖ ≤ 1) ∧
      volume {w : ℂ | ‖∏ i, (w - z i)‖ < 1} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C / Real.log (Real.log n))

statements.name: Erdos116.erdos_116.variants.polya
statements.doc: Pólya [Po28]: $\lvert\{ z: \lvert p(z)\rvert <1\}\rvert \leq \pi$ always holds.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_116.variants.polya (n : ℕ) (z : Fin n → ℂ) :
    volume {w : ℂ | ‖∏ i, (w - z i)‖ < 1} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal Real.pi

problems.title: Erdős Problem 118
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/118](https://www.erdosproblems.com/118)

*References:*
- [Sc99] Schipperus, R. *Countable partition ordinals.* Thesis, University of Colorado (1999).
- [Sc10] Schipperus, R. *Countable partition ordinals.* Ann. Pure Appl. Logic 161 (2010),
  1195–1215.
- [Da99] Darby, C. *Negative partition relations for ordinals $\omega^{\omega^\delta}$.*
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 76 (1999), 205–222.
- [La00] Larson, J. A. *An ordinal partition avoiding pentagrams.* J. Symbolic Logic 65
  (2000), 969–978.
- [HST10] Hajnal, A.; Larson, J. A. *Partition relations.* Handbook of set theory,
  Springer (2010), 129–213.

statements.name: Erdos118.erdos_118
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 118** (problem of Erdős and Hajnal). Let $\alpha$ be such that
$\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$. For every $n \ge 3$, must $\alpha \to (\alpha, n)^2$?

The original question is asked for cardinals, ordinals, and order types; we state the
ordinal version, which is the standard reading: ordinals $\alpha$ with
$\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$ are called *partition ordinals*.

The answer is **no**, shown independently by Schipperus [Sc99, Sc10] and Darby [Da99].
Larson [La00] gave the concrete counterexample $\alpha = \omega^{\omega^2}$, for which
$\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$ holds yet $\alpha \not\to (\alpha, 5)^2$. See Chapter 2.9 of
[HST10] for further background.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_118 :
    ¬ ∀ α : Ordinal.{0}, OrdinalRamsey α α 3 →
      ∀ n : ℕ, 3 ≤ n → OrdinalRamsey α α n

statements.name: Erdos118.erdos_118.variants.larson
statements.doc:
**Larson (2000).** The ordinal $\alpha = \omega^{\omega^2}$ is a partition ordinal,
$\omega^{\omega^2} \to (\omega^{\omega^2}, 3)^2$, yet
$\omega^{\omega^2} \not\to (\omega^{\omega^2}, 5)^2$ [La00], so the answer to the
Erdős–Hajnal question is negative already at $n = 5$.
statements.statement:
theorem larson : OrdinalRamsey (ω ^ ω ^ (2 : Ordinal)) (ω ^ ω ^ (2 : Ordinal)) 3 ∧
    ¬ OrdinalRamsey (ω ^ ω ^ (2 : Ordinal)) (ω ^ ω ^ (2 : Ordinal)) 5

problems.title: Erdős Problem 119
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/119](https://www.erdosproblems.com/119)
- [Be91] Beck, J., The modulus of polynomials with zeros on the unit circle: A problem of Erdős.
  Annals of Math. (1991), 609-651.
- [Er57] Erdős, Paul, Some unsolved problems. Michigan Math. J. (1957), 291-300.
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, Some unsolved problems. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Er64b] Erdős, P., Problems and results on diophantine approximations. Compositio Math. (1964),
  52-65.
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved. (1982), 59--79.
- [Er90] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite unsolved problems. A tribute to Paul Erdős (1990),
  467-478.
- [Er97f] Erdős, Paul, Some unsolved problems. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge,
  1993) (1997), 1-10.
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.
- [Li77] Linden, C. N., The modulus of polynomials with zeros on the unit circle. Bull. London Math.
  Soc. (1977), 65--69.
- [Va99] Various, Some of Paul's favorite problems. Booklet produced for the conference "Paul Erdős
  and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).
- [Wa80] Wagner, Gerold, On a problem of Erdős in {D}iophantine approximation. Bull. London Math.
  Soc. (1980), 81--88.

statements.name: Erdos119.erdos_119.parts.i
statements.doc:
Is it true that $\limsup M_n = \infty$?

This is Problem 4.1 in [Ha74] where it is attributed to Erdős.

The weaker conjecture that $\limsup M_n=\infty$ was proved by Wagner [Wa80], who show that there is
some $c>0$ with $M_n>(\log n)^c$ infinitely often.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_119.parts.i :
    ∀ (z : ℕ → ℂ) (hz : ∀ i : ℕ, ‖z i‖ = 1),
      atTop.limsup (fun n => (M z n : EReal)) = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos119.erdos_119.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is it true that there exists $c > 0$ such that for infinitely many $n$ we have $M_n > n^c$?

The second question was answered by Beck [Be91], who proved that there exists some $c>0$ such that
$\max_{n\leq N} M_n > N^c$.

statements.name: Erdos119.erdos_119.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Is it true that there exists $c > 0$ such that, for all large $n$, $\sum_{k \leq n} M_k > n^{1 + c}$?

The \$100 prize was offered for the third question in [Er97f]. This was resolved by GPT 5.6 and
Korsky (see the proof claims), who proved that $\sum_{k\leq n}M_k \gg \frac{n^{5/4}}{\sqrt{\log n}}$
(and hence for infinitely many $n$ we have $M_n> n^{1/4-o(1)}$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_119.parts.iii :
    ∀ (z : ℕ → ℂ) (hz : ∀ i : ℕ, ‖z i‖ = 1),
      ∃ (c : ℝ) (hc : c > 0), ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
        ∑ k ∈ range n, M z k > n ^ (1 + c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 120
problems.doc:
*Reference:*
- [erdosproblems.com/120](https://www.erdosproblems.com/120)
- [St20](http://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/fm/fm1/fm1111.pdf) Steinhaus, Hugo, Sur les distances des points dans les ensembles de measure positive. Fund. Math. (1920), 93-104.

statements.name: Erdos120.erdos_120
statements.doc:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be an infinite set. Must there be a set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$
of positive measure which does not contain any set of the shape $a * A + b$
for some $a,b \in \mathbb{R}$ and $a \neq 0$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_120 : ∀ A : Set ℝ, A.Infinite → Erdos120For A

statements.name: Erdos120.erdos_120.variants.finite_set
statements.doc: Steinhaus [St20] has proved Erdős 120 to be false whenever $A$ is a finite set.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_120.variants.finite_set {A : Set ℝ} (h : A.Finite) : ¬ Erdos120For A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 121
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/121](https://www.erdosproblems.com/121)
- [Er94b] Erdős, Paul, *Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and combinatorial geometry*.
  Math. Pannon. (1994), 261-269.
- [Er97] Erdős, Paul, *Problems in number theory*. New Zealand J. Math. (1997), 155-160.
- [Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
- [Er98] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my new and almost new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Number theory (Eger, 1996) (1998), 169-180.
- [ESS95] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, V. T., *On product representations of powers. I*.
  European J. Combin. (1995), 567-588.
- [Er38] P. Erdős, *On sequences of integers no one of which divides the product of two others
  and on related problems*. Tomsk. Gos. Univ. Ucen Zap. (1938), 74-82.
- [Ta24] Tao, T., *On product representations of squares*. arXiv:2405.11610 (2024).

statements.name: Erdos121.erdos_121
statements.doc:
Let $F_{k}(N)$ be the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that the product of no
$k$ many distinct elements of $A$ is a square. Is $F_5(N)=(1-o(1))N$?

Conjectured by Erdős, Sós, and Sárközy [ESS95], who proved
$F_2(N)=\left(\frac{6}{\pi^2}+o(1)\right)N$, $F_3(N) = (1-o(1))N$, and also established
asymptotics for $F_k(N)$ for all even $k\geq 4$ (in particular $F_k(N)\asymp N/\log N$ for all
even $k\geq 4$). Erdős [Er38] earlier proved that $F_4(N)=o(N)$ - indeed, if
$\lvert A\rvert \gg N$ and $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ then there is a non-trivial solution to
$ab=cd$ with $a,b,c,d\in A$.

This problem was answered in the negative by Tao [Ta24], who proved that for any $k\geq 4$ there
is some constant $c_k>0$ such that $F_k(N) \leq (1-c_k+o(1))N$.

See also [888](https://www.erdosproblems.com/888).
statements.statement: theorem erdos_121 : ¬ (fun N : ℕ => (F 5 N : ℝ)) ~[atTop] fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos121.erdos_121.variants.odd
statements.doc:
More generally, is $F_{2k+1}(N)=(1-o(1))N$? This is false for all $k \geq 2$ by Tao's
theorem [Ta24].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_121.variants.odd : ¬ ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k →
    (fun N : ℕ => (F (2 * k + 1) N : ℝ)) ~[atTop] fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos121.erdos_121.variants.tao
statements.doc:
Tao [Ta24] proved that for any $k\geq 4$ there is some constant $c_k>0$ such that
$F_k(N) \leq (1-c_k+o(1))N$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_121.variants.tao (k : ℕ) (hk : 4 ≤ k) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (F k N : ℝ) ≤ (1 - c) * N

statements.name: Erdos121.erdos_121.variants.three
statements.doc: Erdős, Sós, and Sárközy [ESS95] proved $F_3(N) = (1-o(1))N$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_121.variants.three : (fun N : ℕ => (F 3 N : ℝ)) ~[atTop] fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos121.erdos_121.variants.two
statements.doc: Erdős, Sós, and Sárközy [ESS95] proved $F_2(N)=\left(\frac{6}{\pi^2}+o(1)\right)N$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_121.variants.two :
    (fun N : ℕ => (F 2 N : ℝ)) ~[atTop] fun N : ℕ => 6 / Real.pi ^ 2 * N

problems.title: Erdős Problem 123
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/123](https://www.erdosproblems.com/123)
- [ChYu23b] Chen, Yong-Gao and Yu, Wang-Xing, On {$d$}-complete sequences of integers, {II}. Acta
  Arith. (2023), 161--181.
- [Er92b] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics.
  Matematiche (Catania) (1992), 231-240.
- [Er97] Erdős, Paul, Problems in number theory. New Zealand J. Math. (1997), 155-160.
- [Er97e] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite unsolved problems. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
- [ErLe96] Erdős, P. and Lewin, Mordechai, $d$-complete sequences of integers. Math. Comp. (1996),
  837-840.
- [MaCh16] Ma, Mi-Mi and Chen, Yong-Gao, On {$d$}-complete sequences of integers. J. Number Theory
  (2016), 1--12.

statements.name: Erdos123.erdos_123
statements.doc:
Let $a, b, c$ be three integers which are pairwise coprime. Is every large integer
the sum of distinct integers of the form $a^k b^l c^m$ ($k, l, m ≥ 0$), none of which
divide any other?

Equivalently: is the set $\{a^k b^l c^m : k, l, m \geq 0\}$ d-complete?

Note: For this not to reduce to the two-integer case, we need the integers
to be greater than one and distinct.

The prize of \$250 is offered by Erdős in [Er97] and [Er97e] for a 'proof or disproof'.

The main problem was resolved in the affirmative by GPT 5.6 (prompted by Snyder).

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_123 : ∀ a > 1, ∀ b > 1, ∀ c > 1, PairwiseCoprime a b c →
    IsDComplete (↑(powers a) * ↑(powers b) * ↑(powers c))

statements.name: Erdos123.erdos_123.variants.erdos_lewin_3_5_7
statements.doc: Erdős and Lewin [ErLe96] proved this conjecture when $a = 3$, $b = 5$, and $c = 7$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_123.variants.erdos_lewin_3_5_7 :
    IsDComplete (↑(powers 3) * ↑(powers 5) * ↑(powers 7))

statements.name: Erdos123.erdos_123.variants.powers_2_3
statements.doc:
A simpler case: the set of numbers of the form $2^k 3^l$ ($k, l ≥ 0$) is d-complete.

This was initially conjectured by Erdős in 1992, who called it a "nice and difficult"
problem, but it was quickly proven by Jansen and others using a simple inductive argument:
- If $n = 2m$ is even, apply the inductive hypothesis to $m$ and double all summands.
- If $n$ is odd, let $3^k$ be the largest power of $3$ with $3^k ≤ n$, and apply the
  inductive hypothesis to $n - 3^k$ (which is even).
statements.statement: theorem erdos_123.variants.powers_2_3 : IsDComplete (↑(powers 2) * ↑(powers 3))

statements.name: Erdos123.erdos_123.variants.powers_2_3_5_snug
statements.doc:
In [Er92b] Erdős makes the stronger conjecture (for $a=2$, $b=3$, and $c=5$) that, for any
$\epsilon>0$, all large integers $n$ can be written as the sum of distinct integers
$b_1<\cdots <b_t$ of the form $2^k3^l5^m$ where $b_t<(1+\epsilon)b_1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_123.variants.powers_2_3_5_snug :
    ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∃ A : Finset ℕ, (A : Set ℕ) ⊆ ↑(powers 2) * ↑(powers 3) * ↑(powers 5) ∧ IsSnug ε A ∧
        ∑ x ∈ A, x = n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 124
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/124](https://www.erdosproblems.com/124)
- [BEGL96] Burr, S. A. and Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Li, W. Wen-Ching, Complete sequences of sets of integer powers. Acta Arith. (1996), 133-138.

statements.name: Erdos124.erdos124.zero
statements.doc:
Let  $3 \le d_1 < d_2 < \dots < d_r$ be integers such that
$$\sum_{1 \le i \le r}\frac 1{d_i - 1} \ge 1.$$
Can all sufficiently large integers be written as a sum of the shape $\sum_i c_ia_i$
where $c_i \in \{0, 1\}$ and $a_i$ has only the digits $0, 1$ when written in base $d_i$?

Conjectured by Erdős [Er97], solved by Boris Alexeev using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
lemma erdos124.zero :
    ∀ D : Finset ℕ, (∀ d ∈ D, 3 ≤ d) → 1 ≤ ∑ d ∈ D, (d - 1 : ℚ)⁻¹ →
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ ∑ d ∈ D, sumsOfDistinctPowers d 0

statements.name: Erdos124.erdos124.ne_zero
statements.doc:
Let $k \ne 0$ and $3\leq d_1 < d_2 < \cdots < d_r$ be integers of gcd equal to $1$ such that
$$\sum_{1 \le i \le r}\frac 1{d_i - 1} \ge 1.$$
Can all sufficiently large integers be written as a sum of the shape $\sum_i c_ia_i$
where $c_i \in \{0, 1\}$ and $a_i$ is divisible by $d_i ^ k$ and has only the digits $0, 1$ when
written in base $d_i$?

Conjectured by Burr, Erdős, Graham, and Li [BEGL96]
statements.statement:
lemma erdos124.ne_zero :
    ∀ k ≠ 0, ∀ D : Finset ℕ, (∀ d ∈ D, 3 ≤ d) → 1 ≤ ∑ d ∈ D, (d - 1 : ℚ)⁻¹ → D.gcd id = 1 →
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ ∑ d ∈ D, sumsOfDistinctPowers d k

statements.name: Erdos124.erdos124.ne_zero_three_four_seven
statements.doc:
All sufficiently large integers can be written as $a + b + c$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are
divisible by $3$, $4$, and $7$ respectively, and after division by that base have only the
digits $0, 1$ in that base.

Proved by Burr, Erdős, Graham, and Li [BEGL96]
statements.statement:
lemma erdos124.ne_zero_three_four_seven :
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      n ∈ sumsOfDistinctPowers 3 1 + sumsOfDistinctPowers 4 1 + sumsOfDistinctPowers 7 1

statements.name: Erdos124.erdos124.converse
statements.doc:
Let $3\leq d_1 < d_2 < \cdots < d_r$ be integers such that all sufficiently large integers can be
written as a sum of the shape $\sum_i c_ia_i$ where $c_i \in \{0, 1\}$ and $a_i$ has only the digits
$0, 1$ when written in base $d_i$. Then
$$\sum_{1 \le i \le r}\frac 1{d_i - 1} \ge 1.$$

Reported by Burr, Erdős, Graham, and Li [BEGL96] as an observation of Pomerance
statements.statement:
lemma erdos124.converse {D : Finset ℕ} (hD₃ : ∀ d ∈ D, 3 ≤ d)
    (h : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ ∑ d ∈ D, sumsOfDistinctPowers d 0) : 1 ≤ ∑ d ∈ D, (d - 1 : ℚ)⁻¹

statements.name: Erdos124.erdos124.melfi_construction
statements.doc:
For any $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists an infinite sequence $2 \le d_0 < d_1 < \dots$ such
that the series $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{d_i - 1}$ converges to a value at most
$\varepsilon$, and yet for every $k \ne 0$ all sufficiently large integers can be written as
$\sum_{i \in I} a_i$ for some finite set $I$, where each $a_i$ is divisible by $d_i^k$ and has
only the digits $0, 1$ when written in base $d_i$.

The restriction $k \ne 0$ excludes the degenerate representation of $n$ as a sum of $n$ copies
of $1 = d_i^0$ taken from $n$ distinct bases.

Proved by Melfi [Me04, Proposition 1]
statements.statement:
lemma erdos124.melfi_construction {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ d : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono d ∧ 2 ≤ d 0 ∧
      Summable (fun i ↦ (d i - 1 : ℝ)⁻¹) ∧ ∑' i, (d i - 1 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ ε ∧ ∀ k ≠ 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∃ (I : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ i ∈ I, a i ∈ sumsOfDistinctPowers (d i) k) ∧
        ∑ i ∈ I, a i = n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 125
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/125](https://www.erdosproblems.com/125)

There are four possibilities for the density of $A+B$:
1. $A+B$ has zero upper and lower density (and hence also zero density).
2. $A+B$ has zero lower density, but positive upper density (and hence no density).
3. $A+B$ has positive upper and lower density that are equal (and hence positive density).
4. $A+B$ has positive upper and lower density that are unequal (and hence no density).

statements.name: Erdos125.erdos_125
statements.doc:
Case 3:
Does $A + B$ have positive upper and lower density that are equal?
This is the literal interpretation of "positive density" which was falsified.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_125 :
    ¬ (A + B).HasPosDensity

statements.name: Erdos125.erdos_125.variants.positive_lower_density
statements.doc:
Literature question:
Does $A + B$ have positive lower density?

This has been falsified.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_125.variants.positive_lower_density :
    ¬ 0 < (A + B).lowerDensity

statements.name: Erdos125.erdos_125.variants.positive_upper_density
statements.doc:
Literature question:
Does $A + B$ have positive upper density?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_125.variants.positive_upper_density :
    0 < (A + B).upperDensity

statements.name: Erdos125.erdos_125.variants.zero_density
statements.doc:
Case 1:
Does $A + B$ have zero upper and lower density?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_125.variants.zero_density :
    (A + B).upperDensity = 0 ∧ (A + B).lowerDensity = 0

statements.name: Erdos125.erdos_125.variants.zero_lower_positive_upper_density
statements.doc:
Case 2:
Does $A + B$ have zero lower density, but positive upper density?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_125.variants.zero_lower_positive_upper_density :
    (A + B).lowerDensity = 0 ∧ 0 < (A + B).upperDensity

statements.name: Erdos125.erdos_125.variants.positive_unequal_density
statements.doc:
Case 4:
Does $A + B$ have positive upper and lower density that are unequal?

This follows from the disproof `erdos_125.variants.positive_lower_density` above.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_125.variants.positive_unequal_density :
    ¬ (0 < (A + B).lowerDensity ∧ (A + B).lowerDensity < (A + B).upperDensity)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 126
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/126](https://www.erdosproblems.com/126)

statements.name: Erdos126.erdos_126
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that if $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ has $|A| = n$ then
$\prod_{a\neq b\in A}(a + b)$ has at least $f(n)$ distinct prime factors.
Is it true that $\frac{f(n)}{\log n} \to\infty$?

The answer is yes, and a machine-checked proof is available.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_126 : ∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ), IsMaximalAddFactorsCard f →
    Tendsto (fun n => f n / Real.log n) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos126.erdos_126.variants.IsBigO
statements.doc:
Erdős and Turán proved [ErTu34] in their first joint paper that
$$
  \log n \ll f(n) \ll \frac{n}{\log n}
$$

[ErTu34] Erdős, Paul and Turan, Paul, _On a Problem in the Elementary Theory of Numbers_. Amer. Math. Monthly (1934), 608-611.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_126.variants.IsBigO
    (f : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hf : IsMaximalAddFactorsCard f) :
    ((fun (n : ℕ) => Real.log n) =O[atTop] fun (n : ℕ) => (f n : ℝ)) ∧
      (fun (n : ℕ) => (f n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun (n : ℕ) => n / Real.log n

statements.name: Erdos126.erdos_126.variants.isLittleO
statements.doc: Erdős says that $f(n) = o(\frac{n}{\log n})$ has never been proved.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_126.variants.isLittleO
    (f : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hf : IsMaximalAddFactorsCard f) :
    (fun (n : ℕ) => (f n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) => n / Real.log n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 127
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/127](https://www.erdosproblems.com/127)
- [Er97b] Erdős, Paul, *Some old and new problems in various branches of combinatorics*. Discrete
  Math. (1997), 227-231.
- [Ed73] Edwards, C. S., *Some extremal properties of bipartite subgraphs*. Canadian J. Math.
  (1973), 475-485.
- [Al96] Alon, Noga, *Bipartite subgraphs*. Combinatorica (1996), 301-311.

statements.name: Erdos127.erdos_127
statements.doc:
Let $f(m)$ be maximal such that every graph with $m$ edges must contain a bipartite graph with
$$\geq \frac{m}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{8m+1}-1}{8}+f(m)$$
edges. Is there an infinite sequence of $m_i$ such that $f(m_i)\to \infty$?

Conjectured by Erdős, Kohayakava, and Gyárfás [Er97b]. Edwards [Ed73] proved that $f(m)\geq 0$
always. Note that $f(\binom{n}{2})= 0$, taking $K_n$. Solved by Alon [Al96], who showed
$f(n^2/2)\gg n^{1/2}$, and also showed that $f(m)\ll m^{1/4}$ for all $m$. The best possible
constant in $f(m)\leq Cm^{1/4}$ is unknown.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_127 : ∃ m : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto m atTop atTop ∧
    Tendsto (fun i => f (m i)) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos127.erdos_127.variants.edwards
statements.doc:
Edwards [Ed73] proved that every graph with $m$ edges contains a bipartite subgraph with at
least $\frac{m}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{8m+1}-1}{8}$ edges.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_127.variants.edwards {V : Type*} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    ∃ H : SimpleGraph V, H ≤ G ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧
      (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) / 2 + (√(8 * G.edgeSet.ncard + 1) - 1) / 8 ≤ H.edgeSet.ncard

statements.name: Erdos127.erdos_127.variants.alon_upper
statements.doc: Alon [Al96] showed that $f(m)\ll m^{1/4}$ for all $m$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_127.variants.alon_upper : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ m : ℕ, (f m : ℝ) ≤ C * (m : ℝ) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 128
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/128](https://www.erdosproblems.com/128)

statements.name: Erdos128.erdos_128
statements.doc:
Let G be a graph with n vertices such that every induced subgraph on ≥ $n/2$
vertices has more than $n^2/50$ edges. Must G contain a triangle?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_128 :
    ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      (∀ V' : Set V, 2 * V'.ncard + 1 ≥ Fintype.card V →
