        50 * (G.induce V').edgeSet.ncard > Fintype.card V ^ 2) → ¬ G.CliqueFree 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 130
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/130](https://www.erdosproblems.com/130)

statements.name: Erdos130.erdos_130
statements.doc:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be an infinite set which contains no three points on a
line and no four points on a circle. Consider the graph with vertices the points
in $A$, where two vertices are joined by an edge if and only if they are an
integer distance apart. How large can the chromatic number and clique number of
this graph be? In particular, can the chromatic number be infinite?

The chromatic number can be infinite: there is an infinite general-position set
whose integer-distance graph admits no finite proper colouring. How large the
*clique* number can be is not addressed here.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_130 :
    ∃ A : Set ℝ², A.Infinite ∧ InGeneralPosition A ∧
      (IntegerDistancePlaneGraph A).chromaticNumber = ⊤

problems.title: Erdős Problem 131
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/131](https://www.erdosproblems.com/131)
- [ELRSS99] Erdős, P. and Lev, V. and Rauzy, G. and Sándor, C. and Sárközy, A., *Greedy
  algorithm, arithmetic progressions, subset sums and divisibility*. Discrete Math. (1999),
  119-135.
- [PhZa24] Pham, H. T. and Zakharov, D., *Sharp bound for the Erdős–Straus non-averaging set
  problem*. [arXiv:2410.14624](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.14624) (2024).

statements.name: Erdos131.erdos_131.variants.pham_zakharov
statements.doc:
Every non-dividing set is non-averaging. Pham and Zakharov [PhZa24] proved that a
non-averaging subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ has size at most $N^{1/4 + o(1)}$, so
$F(N) \le N^{1/4 + o(1)}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_131.variants.pham_zakharov :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto f atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
      ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (F N : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 4 + f N)

statements.name: Erdos131.erdos_131.variants.elrss
statements.doc: Erdős, Lev, Rauzy, Sándor and Sárközy [ELRSS99] proved $F(N) < 3 N^{1/2} + 1$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_131.variants.elrss (N : ℕ) : (F N : ℝ) < 3 * Real.sqrt N + 1

statements.name: Erdos131.erdos_131
statements.doc:
Let $F(N)$ be the maximal size of $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that no $a \in A$ divides
the sum of any distinct elements of $A \setminus \{a\}$. Is it true that
$F(N) > N^{1/2 - o(1)}$?

The answer is no, by the bound of Pham and Zakharov [PhZa24]
(`erdos_131.variants.pham_zakharov`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_131 :
    ¬ ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto f atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
      ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (N : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2 - f N) < (F N : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 133
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/133](https://www.erdosproblems.com/133)
- [Er97b] Erdős, Paul, *Some old and new problems in various branches of combinatorics*. Discrete
  Math. (1997), 227-231.
- [HaSe84] Hanson, D. and Seyffarth, K., *$k$-saturated graphs of prescribed maximum degree*.
  Congr. Numer. (1984), 169-182.
- [FuSe94] Füredi, Zoltán and Seress, Ákos, *Maximal triangle-free graphs with restrictions on the
  degrees*. J. Graph Theory (1994), 11-24.
- [HaLe18] Haviv, Ishay and Levy, Dan, *Symmetric complete sum-free sets in cyclic groups*. Israel
  J. Math. (2018), 931-956.

statements.name: Erdos133.erdos_133
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that every triangle-free graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and diameter
$2$ contains a vertex with degree $\geq f(n)$. What is the order of growth of $f(n)$? Does
$f(n)/\sqrt{n}\to \infty$?

Asked by Erdős and Pach. The lower bound $f(n)\geq (1-o(1))\sqrt{n}$ follows from the fact that
a graph with maximum degree $d$ and diameter $2$ has at most $1+d+d(d-1)=d^2+1$ many vertices.

Hanson and Seyffarth [HaSe84] proved that $f(n)\leq (\sqrt{2}+o(1))\sqrt{n}$ using a Cayley graph
on $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, with the generating set given by some symmetric complete sum-free set
of size $\sim \sqrt{n}$. An alternative construction of such a complete sum-free set was given by
Haviv and Levy [HaLe18]. Füredi and Seress [FuSe94] proved that
$f(n)\leq (\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}+o(1))\sqrt{n}$. In particular $f(n)/\sqrt{n}\not\to\infty$.

The precise asymptotics of $f(n)$ are unknown; Alon believes that the truth is $f(n)\sim \sqrt{n}$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_133 : ¬ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : ℝ) / √n) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos133.erdos_133.variants.isTheta
statements.doc: The order of growth of $f(n)$ is $\sqrt{n}$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_133.variants.isTheta : (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] fun n ↦ √n

statements.name: Erdos133.erdos_133.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
The lower bound $f(n)\geq (1-o(1))\sqrt{n}$ follows from the fact that a graph with maximum degree
$d$ and diameter $2$ has at most $d^2+1$ many vertices.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_133.variants.lower_bound : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (1 - ε) * √n ≤ f n

statements.name: Erdos133.erdos_133.variants.hanson_seyffarth
statements.doc: Hanson and Seyffarth [HaSe84] proved that $f(n)\leq (\sqrt{2}+o(1))\sqrt{n}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_133.variants.hanson_seyffarth : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (f n : ℝ) ≤ (√2 + ε) * √n

statements.name: Erdos133.erdos_133.variants.furedi_seress
statements.doc: Füredi and Seress [FuSe94] proved that $f(n)\leq (\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}+o(1))\sqrt{n}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_133.variants.furedi_seress : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (f n : ℝ) ≤ (2 / √3 + ε) * √n

statements.name: Erdos133.erdos_133.variants.asymptotic
statements.doc: Is $f(n)\sim \sqrt{n}$? Alon believes that this is the truth.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_133.variants.asymptotic :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] fun n ↦ √n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 134
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/134](https://www.erdosproblems.com/134)
- [Er97b] Erdős, Paul, *Some old and new problems in various branches of combinatorics*. Discrete Math. (1997), 227-231.

statements.name: Erdos134.erdos_134
statements.doc:
Let $\epsilon,\delta>0$ and $n$ be sufficiently large in terms of $\epsilon$ and $\delta$.
Let $G$ be a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $<n^{1/2-\epsilon}$.
Can $G$ be made into a triangle-free graph with diameter $2$ by adding at most $\delta n^2$ edges?

Asked by Erdős and Gyárfás, who proved that this is the case when $G$ has maximum degree $\ll \log n/\log\log n$. A construction of Simonovits shows that this conjecture is false if we just have maximum degree $\leq Cn^{1/2}$, for some large enough $C$. In this note Alon solves this problem in a strong form, in particular proving that a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $<n^{1/2-\epsilon}$ can be made into a triangle-free graph with diameter $2$ by adding at most $O(n^{2-\epsilon})$ edges.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_134 :
    ∀ (ε δ : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hδ : 0 < δ),
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      G.CliqueFree 3 →
      (∀ v : Fin n, (G.degree v : ℝ) < Real.rpow (n : ℝ) ((1 : ℝ) / 2 - ε)) →
      ∃ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (_ : DecidableRel H.Adj),
        G ≤ H ∧
        H.CliqueFree 3 ∧
        (∀ x y : Fin n, x ≠ y → H.Adj x y ∨ ∃ z, H.Adj x z ∧ H.Adj z y) ∧
        ((H.edgeFinset \ G.edgeFinset).card : ℝ) ≤ δ * (n : ℝ) ^ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 136
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/136](https://www.erdosproblems.com/136)
- [Er97b] Erdős, Paul, *Some old and new problems in various branches of combinatorics*. Discrete
  Math. (1997), 227-231.
- [BCDP22] Bennett, P. and Cushman, R. and Dudek, A. and Pralat, P., *The Erdős-Gyárfás function
  $f(n,4,5)=\frac{5}{6}n+o(n)$ - so Gyárfás was right*. arXiv:2207.02920 (2022).
- [JoMu22] Joos, F. and Mubayi, D., *Ramsey theory constructions from hypergraph matchings*.
  arXiv:2208.12563 (2022).

statements.name: Erdos136.erdos_136
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be the smallest number of colours required to colour the edges of $K_n$ such that every
$K_4$ contains at least $5$ colours. Determine the size of $f(n)$.

Asked by Erdős and Gyárfás [Er97b], who proved $\frac56 (n - 1) < f(n) < n$ and $f(9) = 8$; Erdős
believed that the upper bound is closer to the truth. In fact $f(n) \sim \frac56 n$, as shown by
Bennett, Cushman, Dudek and Pralat [BCDP22]; Joos and Mubayi [JoMu22] found a shorter proof.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_136 : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 (5 / 6 : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 137
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/137](https://www.erdosproblems.com/137)

statements.name: Erdos137.erdos_137
statements.doc:
We say that $N$ is powerful if whenever $p\mid N$ we also have $p^2\mid N$.

Let $k\geq 3$. Can the product of any $k$ consecutive positive integers ever be powerful?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_137 : ∃ k ≥ 3, ∃ n, (∏ x ∈ Finset.Ioc n (n + k), x).Powerful

statements.name: Erdos137.erdos_137.variants.perfect_power
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 2$. Erdős and Selfridge [ES75] proved that the product of any $k$ consecutive
integers $N$ cannot be a perfect power.

[ES75] P. Erdös, J. L. Selfridge, "The product of consecutive integers is never a power",
  Illinois J. Math. 19(2): 292-301, 1975
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_137.variants.perfect_power (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 2) (n : ℕ) (x l : ℕ) (hl : 2 ≤ l) :
    (∏ x ∈ Finset.Ioc n (n + k), x) ≠ x ^ l

statements.name: Erdos137.erdos_137.variants.multiple_powerful_factors
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er82c] conjectures that, if $k$ is fixed, then for all $n$ sufficiently large and all
positive integers $m$, there must be at least $k$ distinct primes $p$ such that
$p\mid m(m+1)\cdots (m+n)$ and yet $p^2$ does not divide the right hand side.

[Er82c] Erdős, Paul, "Miscellaneous problems in number theory". Congr. Numer. (1982), 25-45.,
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_137.variants.multiple_powerful_factors (k : ℕ) : ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m),
    letI N := ∏ x ∈ Finset.Ioc m (m + n), x
    ∃ P : Finset ℕ, P.card = k ∧ ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime ∧
    p ∣ N ∧ ¬ p ^ 2 ∣ N

problems.title: Erdős Problem 138
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/138](https://www.erdosproblems.com/138)
- [Be68] Berlekamp, E. R., A construction for partitions which avoid long arithmetic progressions. Canad. Math. Bull. (1968), 409-414.
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory. Ann. Discrete Math. (1980), 89-115.
- [Er81] Erdős, P., On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved. Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
- [Go01] Gowers, W. T., A new proof of Szemerédi's theorem. Geom. Funct. Anal. (2001), 465-588.
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven
  Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
- [CFS26] Campos, M., Fox, J. and Schildkraut, C., A new lower bound for two-color van der Waerden
  numbers. [arXiv:2608.20824](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20824) (2026).
- [OAI26] OpenAI, *Quantitative Superexponential Bounds for van der Waerden Numbers*. OpenAI Math
  Release preprint (2026).
  https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/Quantitative-Superexponential-Bounds-for-van-der-Waerden-Numbers-September-23-2026/paper.pdf

statements.name: Erdos138.monoAP_guarantee_set_nonempty
statements.doc:
Asserts that for any number of colors `r` and any progression length `k`, there
always exists some number `N` large enough to guarantee a monochromatic arithmetic progression.
In other words, the set `monoAP_guarantee_set` is non-empty. This is the fundamental existence
result that allows for the definition of the van der Waerden numbers.
statements.statement: theorem monoAP_guarantee_set_nonempty (r k) : (monoAP_guarantee_set r k).Nonempty

statements.name: Erdos138.erdos_138
statements.doc:
In [Er80] Erdős asks whether
$$ \lim_{k \to \infty} (W(k))^{1/k} = \infty $$

Yes. This was proved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26], which shows
$W(k) > k^{k/100000}$ for all large $k$; see the linked Lean proof.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_138 : atTop.Tendsto (fun k => (W k : ℝ)^(1/(k : ℝ))) atTop

statements.name: Erdos138.erdos_138.variants.prime
statements.doc: When $p$ is prime Berlekamp [Be68] has proved $W(p+1) ≥ p^{2^p}$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_138.variants.prime (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) : p * (2 ^ p) ≤ W (p + 1)

statements.name: Erdos138.erdos_138.variants.upper
statements.doc: Gowers [Go01] has proved $$W(k) \leq 2^{2^{2^{2^{2^{k+9}}}}.$$
statements.statement: theorem erdos_138.variants.upper (k : ℕ) : W k ≤ 2 ^ (2 ^ (2 ^ 2 ^ 2 ^ (k + 9)))

statements.name: Erdos138.erdos_138.variants.quotient
statements.doc: In [Er81] Erdős asks whether $\frac{W(k+1)}{W(k)} \to \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_138.variants.quotient :
    atTop.Tendsto (fun k => ((W (k + 1) : ℚ)/(W k))) atTop

statements.name: Erdos138.erdos_138.variants.difference
statements.doc:
In [Er81] Erdős asks whether $W(k+1) - W(k) \to \infty$.

The DeepMind prover agent has found a formal proof of this statement.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_138.variants.difference :
    atTop.Tendsto (fun k => (W (k + 1) - W k)) atTop

statements.name: Erdos138.erdos_138.variants.dvd_two_pow
statements.doc:
In [Er80] Erdős asks whether $W(k)/2^k\to \infty$.

Campos, Fox and Schildkraut [CFS26] independently prove $W(k) \geq (1 - o(1)) k 2^{k-1}$, which
implies this; they report that their proof was generated with ChatGPT. (The related variant
`erdos_138.variants.difference`, $W(k+1) - W(k) \to \infty$, was solved separately in
[arxiv/2605.22763].)

Solved: a Lean 4 proof, derived from the Atlas proofs in
[facebookresearch/atlas-lean](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean), is linked in
`formal_proof`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_138.variants.dvd_two_pow :
    atTop.Tendsto (fun k => ((W k : ℚ)/ (2 ^ k))) atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 139
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/139](https://www.erdosproblems.com/139)

statements.name: Erdos139.erdos_139
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 139**:
Let $r_k(N)$ be the size of the largest subset of ${1,...,N}$ which does not contain a non-trivial
$k$-term arithmetic progression. Prove that $r_k(N) = o(N)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_139 (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 < k) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N => (r k N / N : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (𝓝 0)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 141
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/141](https://www.erdosproblems.com/141)
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primes_in_arithmetic_progression#Consecutive_primes_in_arithmetic_progression)

statements.name: Erdos141.erdos_141
statements.doc: Let $k≥3$. Are there $k$ consecutive primes in arithmetic progression?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_141 :
    ∀ k ≥ 3, ∃ (s : Set ℕ), s.IsAPAndPrimeProgressionOfLength k

statements.name: Erdos141.erdos_141.variants.first_cases
statements.doc: The existence of such progressions has been verified for $k≤10$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_141.variants.first_cases :
    (∀ k ≥ 3, k ≤ 10 → ∃ (s : Set ℕ), s.IsAPAndPrimeProgressionOfLength k)

statements.name: Erdos141.erdos_141.variants.eleven
statements.doc: Are there $11$ consecutive primes in arithmetic progression?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_141.variants.eleven :
    ∃ (s : Set ℕ), s.IsAPAndPrimeProgressionOfLength 11

statements.name: Erdos141.erdos_141.variants.infinite_three
statements.doc: It is open, even for $k=3$, whether there are infinitely many such progressions.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_141.variants.infinite_three :
    (consecutivePrimeArithmeticProgressions 3).Infinite

statements.name: Erdos141.erdos_141.variants.infinite_general_case
statements.doc: Fix a $k \geq 3$. Is it true that there are infinitely many arithmetic prime progressions of length $k$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_141.variants.infinite_general_case :
    ∀ k ≥ 3, (consecutivePrimeArithmeticProgressions k).Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 142
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/142](https://www.erdosproblems.com/142)

statements.name: Erdos142.erdos_142
statements.doc:
Prove an asymptotic formula for $r_k(N)$, the largest possible size of a subset
of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ that does not contain any non-trivial $k$-term arithmetic progression.
That is, find $f_k$ with $r_k(N) / f_k(N) \to 1$ as $N \to \infty$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_142 (k : ℕ) : (fun N => (r k N : ℝ)) ~[atTop] erdos_142.answer

statements.name: Erdos142.erdos_142.variants.lower
statements.doc:
Show that $r_k(N) = o_k(N / \log N)$, where $r_k(N)$ the largest possible size of a subset
of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ that does not contain any non-trivial $k$-term arithmetic progression.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_142.variants.lower (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 < k) :
    (fun N => (r k N : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun N : ℕ => N / (N : ℝ).log)

statements.name: Erdos142.erdos_142.variants.isTheta
statements.doc:
Determine the order of magnitude of $r_k(N)$, the largest possible size of a subset
of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ that does not contain any non-trivial $k$-term arithmetic progression.
That is, find $f_k$ with $r_k(N) \asymp_k f_k(N)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_142.variants.isTheta (k : ℕ) :
    (fun N => (r k N : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_142.variants.isTheta.answer

statements.name: Erdos142.erdos_142.variants.three
statements.doc:
Prove an asymptotic formula for $r_3(N)$, the largest possible size of a subset
of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ that does not contain any non-trivial $3$-term arithmetic progression.
That is, find $f$ with $r_3(N) / f(N) \to 1$ as $N \to \infty$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_142.variants.three : (fun N => (r 3 N : ℝ)) ~[atTop] erdos_142.variants.three.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 143
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/143](https://www.erdosproblems.com/143)

statements.name: Erdos143.erdos_143.parts.i
statements.doc:
Does this imply that
$$
\liminf \frac{|A \cap [1,x]|}{x} = 0?
$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_143.parts.i : ∀ (A : Set ℝ), WellSeparatedSet A →
    liminf (fun x => (A ∩ (Set.Icc 1 x)).ncard / x) atTop = 0

statements.name: Erdos143.erdos_143.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Or
$$
\sum_{x \in A} \frac{1}{x \log x} < \infty,
$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_143.parts.ii (A : Set ℝ) (h : WellSeparatedSet A) :
    Summable fun (x : A) ↦ 1 / (x * Real.log x)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 145
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/145](https://www.erdosproblems.com/145)

statements.name: Erdos145.erdos_145
statements.doc:
Let $s_1 < s_2 < \cdots$ be the sequence of squarefree numbers. Is it true that, for any
$\alpha\geq 0$,
$$
\lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{1}{x}\sum_{s_n\leq x}(s_{n+1}-s_n)^\alpha
$$
exists?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_145 :
    ∀ α ≥ (0 : ℝ), ∃ β : ℝ,
      atTop.Tendsto (fun x : ℝ ↦ 1 / x * ∑ n ∈ A x, (s (n + 1) - s n : ℝ) ^ α) (𝓝 β)

statements.name: Erdos145.erdos_145.variants.le_two
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er51] proved this for all $0\leq \alpha\leq 2$.

[Er51] Erdös, P., Some problems and results in elementary number theory.
  Publ. Math. Debrecen (1951), 103-109.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_145.variants.le_two {α : ℝ} (hα : α ∈ Set.Icc 0 2) :
    ∃ β : ℝ,
      atTop.Tendsto (fun x : ℝ ↦ 1 / x * ∑ n ∈ A x, (s (n + 1) - s n : ℝ) ^ α) (𝓝 β)

statements.name: Erdos145.erdos_145.variants.le_three
statements.doc:
Hooley [Ho73] extended this to all $0 \leq \alpha\leq 3$.

[Ho73] Hooley, Christopher, On the intervals between consecutive terms of sequences. Proc. Symp. Pure Math, vol. 24, pp. 129-140. 1973.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_145.variants.le_three {α : ℝ} (hα : α ∈ Set.Icc 0 3) :
    ∃ β : ℝ,
      atTop.Tendsto (fun x : ℝ ↦ 1 / x * ∑ n ∈ A x, (s (n + 1) - s n : ℝ) ^ α) (𝓝 β)

statements.name: Erdos145.erdos_145.variants.lt_eleven_thirds
statements.doc:
Greaves, Harman, and Huxley showed (in Chapter 11 of [GHH97]) that this is true for
$0 \leq \alpha < 11/3$.

[GHH97] Greaves, G. R. H. and Harman, G. and Huxley, M. N., Sieve Methods, Exponential Sums, and
  their Applications in Number Theory. (1997).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_145.variants.lt_eleven_thirds {α : ℝ} (hα : α ∈ Set.Ico 0 (11 / 3)) :
    ∃ β : ℝ,
      atTop.Tendsto (fun x : ℝ ↦ 1 / x * ∑ n ∈ A x, (s (n + 1) - s n : ℝ) ^ α) (𝓝 β)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 146
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/146](https://www.erdosproblems.com/146)
- [ErSi84] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M., *Cube-supersaturated graphs and related problems*.
  Progress in graph theory (1984), 203-218.
- [OpenAI26] OpenAI, *Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science*. (2026).

statements.name: Erdos146.erdos_146
statements.doc:
If $H$ is bipartite and is $r$-degenerate, that is, every induced subgraph of $H$ has minimum
degree $\leq r$, then
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \ll n^{2-1/r}.$$

The answer is no. OpenAI [OpenAI26] give a connected bipartite `2`-degenerate `H` and constants
`c, ε > 0` with $\mathrm{ex}(n;H)\geq cn^{3/2+\epsilon}$ for all large `n`, which exceeds the
conjectured $n^{2-1/2}=n^{3/2}$. See `erdos_146.variants.two_degenerate_counterexample`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_146 :
    ¬ ∀ (r q : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin q)),
      0 < r → H.IsBipartite → H.IsDegenerate r →
        Asymptotics.IsBigO atTop
          (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n H : ℝ))
          (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) - 1 / (r : ℝ)))

statements.name: Erdos146.erdos_146.variants.two_degenerate_counterexample
statements.doc:
The counterexample: a connected bipartite `2`-degenerate `H` whose extremal number exceeds
$n^{3/2+\epsilon}$ infinitely often, so the `r = 2` case of `erdos_146` fails.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_146.variants.two_degenerate_counterexample :
    ∃ (q : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin q)),
      H.Connected ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ H.IsDegenerate 2 ∧
      ∃ c ε : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ 0 < ε ∧
        ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
          c * (n : ℝ) ^ ((3 : ℝ) / 2 + ε) ≤ (extremalNumber n H : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 147
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/147](https://www.erdosproblems.com/147)
- [ErSi84] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M., *Cube-supersaturated graphs and related problems*.
  Progress in graph theory (Waterloo, Ont., 1982) (1984), 203-218.
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [Er97c] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*. The mathematics of Paul Erdős,
  I (1997), 47-67.
- [Ja23] Janzer, Oliver, *Rainbow Turán number of even cycles, repeated patterns and blow-ups of
  cycles*. Israel J. Math. (2023), 813--840.
- [Ja23b] Janzer, Oliver, *Disproof of a conjecture of Erdős and Simonovits on the Turán number
  of graphs with minimum degree 3*. Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN (2023), 8478--8494.

statements.name: Erdos147.erdos_147
statements.doc:
If $H$ is bipartite with minimum degree $r$ then there exists $\epsilon=\epsilon(H)>0$ such that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \gg n^{2-\frac{1}{r-1}+\epsilon}.$$

Conjectured by Erdős and Simonovits [ErSi84]. A probabilistic argument shows that there exists
some $\epsilon=\epsilon(H)>0$ such that $\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \gg n^{2-\frac{2}{r}+\epsilon}$.

This conjecture was disproved by Janzer [Ja23] for even $r\geq 4$. The case $r=3$ was disproved
by Janzer [Ja23b], who constructed, for any $\epsilon>0$, a $3$-regular bipartite graph $H$ such
that $\mathrm{ex}(n;H)\ll n^{\frac{4}{3}+\epsilon}$.

In [Ja23] Janzer conjectures that the above lower bound is sharp, in that for any $r\geq 3$ and
$\epsilon>0$ there exists an $r$-regular graph $H$ such that
$\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \ll n^{2-\frac{2}{r}+\epsilon}$. Janzer's result proves this for even
$r\geq 4$.

See also [113](https://www.erdosproblems.com/113), [146](https://www.erdosproblems.com/146), and
[714](https://www.erdosproblems.com/714).

The conjecture is stated for minimum degree $r \geq 2$ (for $r = 1$ the exponent
$2 - \frac{1}{r-1}$ is not meaningful).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_147 :
    ¬ ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [Nonempty V] (H : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel H.Adj],
      H.IsBipartite → 2 ≤ H.minDegree → ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧
        (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - 1 / ((H.minDegree : ℝ) - 1) + ε)) =O[atTop]
          fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n H : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos147.erdos_147.variants.janzer_even
statements.doc:
Janzer [Ja23] disproved the conjecture for even $r\geq 4$: for any even $r \geq 4$ and
$\epsilon>0$ there exists a nonempty $r$-regular bipartite graph $H$ such that
$\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \ll n^{2-\frac{2}{r}+\epsilon}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_147.variants.janzer_even (r : ℕ) (hr : 4 ≤ r) (heven : Even r) (ε : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ (q : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), 0 < q ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ H.IsRegularOfDegree r ∧
      (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n H : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
        fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - 2 / (r : ℝ) + ε)

statements.name: Erdos147.erdos_147.variants.cubic
statements.doc:
Janzer [Ja23b] constructed, for any $\epsilon>0$, a nonempty $3$-regular bipartite graph $H$
such that $\mathrm{ex}(n;H)\ll n^{\frac{4}{3}+\epsilon}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_147.variants.cubic (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ (q : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), 0 < q ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ H.IsRegularOfDegree 3 ∧
      (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n H : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
        fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (4 / 3 + ε : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos147.erdos_147.variants.janzer_conjecture
statements.doc:
Janzer [Ja23] conjectures that for any $r\geq 3$ and $\epsilon>0$ there exists a nonempty
$r$-regular graph $H$ such that $\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \ll n^{2-\frac{2}{r}+\epsilon}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_147.variants.janzer_conjecture : ∀ r : ℕ, 3 ≤ r → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
    ∃ (q : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), 0 < q ∧ H.IsRegularOfDegree r ∧
      (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n H : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
        fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - 2 / (r : ℝ) + ε)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 148
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/148](https://www.erdosproblems.com/148)
- [ElPl21] Elsholtz, Christian and Planitzer, Stefan, *Sums of four and more unit fractions and
  approximate parametrizations*. Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. (2021), 695-709.
- [Ko14] Konyagin, S. V., *Double exponential lower bound for the number of representations of
  unity by Egyptian fractions*. Math. Notes (2014), 277-281.
- [OEIS A006585](https://oeis.org/A006585)

statements.name: Erdos148.erdos_148
statements.doc:
Let $F(k)$ be the number of solutions to
$$ 1= \frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k},$$
where $1\leq n_1<\cdots<n_k$ are distinct integers. Find good estimates for $F(k)$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_148 : (fun k ↦ (F k : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_148.answer

statements.name: Erdos148.erdos_148.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
The current best bounds known are
$$2^{c^{\frac{k}{\log k}}}\leq F(k) \leq c_0^{(\frac{1}{5}+o(1))2^k},$$
where $c>0$ is some absolute constant and $c_0=1.5979102\ldots$ is the square of the 'Vardi
constant' $1.26408\cdots$. The lower bound is due to Konyagin [Ko14] and the upper bound to
Elsholtz and Planitzer [ElPl21]. (erdosproblems.com gives $c_0=1.26408\cdots$;
[ElPl21, Remark 3] gives $c_0=1.5979102\ldots$.)

[Ko14, Theorem 1] states the lower bound in the explicit form
$$F(k) \geq \exp\left(\exp\left(\left(\frac{(\log 2)(\log 3)}{3}+o(1)\right)
\frac{k}{\log k}\right)\right) \quad (k \to \infty),$$
which is the statement formalised here.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_148.variants.lower_bound :
    ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      exp (exp ((log 2 * log 3 / 3 + o k) * ((k : ℝ) / log k))) ≤ F k

statements.name: Erdos148.erdos_148.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
The current best bounds known are
$$2^{c^{\frac{k}{\log k}}}\leq F(k) \leq c_0^{(\frac{1}{5}+o(1))2^k},$$
where $c>0$ is some absolute constant and $c_0=1.5979102\ldots$ is the square of the 'Vardi
constant' $1.26408\cdots$. The lower bound is due to Konyagin [Ko14] and the upper bound to
Elsholtz and Planitzer [ElPl21]. (erdosproblems.com gives $c_0=1.26408\cdots$;
[ElPl21, Remark 3] gives $c_0=1.5979102\ldots$.)

[ElPl21, Corollary 3(2)] shows that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all $k \geq k(\varepsilon)$,
the number $f_k(1,1) \geq F(k)$ of solutions with $n_1 \leq \cdots \leq n_k$ is less than
$c_0^{(\frac{2}{5}+\varepsilon)2^{k-1}} = c_0^{(\frac{1}{5}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2})2^k}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_148.variants.upper_bound :
    ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      (F k : ℝ) ≤ c₀ ^ ((1 / 5 + o k) * 2 ^ k)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 150
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/150](https://www.erdosproblems.com/150)
- [Br24] Bradač, D., *On a question of Erdős and Nešetřil about minimal cuts in a graph*.
  arXiv:2409.02974 (2024).
- [Er88] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and graph theory*.
  Discrete Math. (1988), 81-92.
- [FKTV08] Fomin, Fedor V. and Kratsch, Dieter and Todinca, Ioan and Villanger, Yngve, *Exact
  algorithms for treewidth and minimum fill-in*. SIAM J. Comput. (2008), 1058-1079.
- [FoVi12] Fomin, Fedor V. and Villanger, Yngve, *Treewidth computation and extremal
  combinatorics*. Combinatorica (2012), 289-308.
- [GaMa18] Gaspers, Serge and Mackenzie, Simon, *On the number of minimal separators in graphs*.
  J. Graph Theory (2018), 653-659.

statements.name: Erdos150.erdos_150
statements.doc:
A minimal cut of a graph is a minimal set of vertices whose removal disconnects the graph. Let
$c(n)$ be the maximum number of minimal cuts a graph on $n$ vertices can have.

Does $c(n)^{1/n}\to \alpha$ for some $\alpha <2$?

It is unclear in [Er88] whether Erdős knew that the limit existed, which follows from a simple
argument first given in the literature (to the best of my knowledge) by Bradač [Br24].

That $\alpha<2$ was proved by Fomin, Kratsch, Todinca, and Villanger [FKTV08], who proved
$\alpha \leq 1.7087$. This was independently studied by Bradač [Br24] (unaware of this earlier
work), who proved that $\alpha \leq 2^{H(1/3)}\approx 1.8899$, where $H(\cdot)$ is the binary
entropy function.

This was formalized in Lean by Monticone using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_150 :
    ∃ α : ℝ, α < 2 ∧
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (maxMinimalCuts n : ℝ) ^ (1 / n : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 α)

statements.name: Erdos150.erdos_150.variants.erdos_nesetril
statements.doc:
Asked by Erdős and Nešetřil, who also ask whether $c(3m+2)=3^m$.

Note that the lower bound $1.4457\leq \alpha$ of Gaspers and Mackenzie [GaMa18] provides a
negative answer to the above question of Erdős and Nešetřil.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_150.variants.erdos_nesetril :
    ¬ ∀ m : ℕ, maxMinimalCuts (3 * m + 2) = 3 ^ m

statements.name: Erdos150.erdos_150.variants.seymour
statements.doc:
Seymour observed that $c(3m+2)\geq 3^m$, as seen by the graph of $m$ independent paths of length
$4$ joining two vertices.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_150.variants.seymour (m : ℕ) : 3 ^ m ≤ maxMinimalCuts (3 * m + 2)

statements.name: Erdos150.erdos_150.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
The current best-known bounds on $\alpha$ are
$$1.4457\leq \alpha \leq \frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}\approx 1.618.$$
The lower bound is due to Gaspers and Mackenzie [GaMa18].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_150.variants.lower_bound (α : ℝ)
    (hα : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (maxMinimalCuts n : ℝ) ^ (1 / n : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 α)) :
    1.4457 ≤ α

statements.name: Erdos150.erdos_150.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
The current best-known bounds on $\alpha$ are
$$1.4457\leq \alpha \leq \frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}\approx 1.618.$$
The upper bound is due to Fomin and Villanger [FoVi12] (with a simpler proof in [GaMa18]).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_150.variants.upper_bound (α : ℝ)
    (hα : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (maxMinimalCuts n : ℝ) ^ (1 / n : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 α)) :
    α ≤ (1 + Real.sqrt 5) / 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 151
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/151](https://www.erdosproblems.com/151)
- [Er88] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and graph theory*.
  Discrete Math. (1988), 81-92.
- [EGT92] Erdős, P. and Gallai, T. and Tuza, Zs., *Covering the cliques of a graph with
  vertices*. Discrete Math. (1992), 279-289.

statements.name: Erdos151.erdos_151
statements.doc:
For a graph $G$, let $\tau(G)$ denote the minimal number of vertices that include at least one
from each maximal clique of $G$ on at least two vertices. Let $H(n)$ be maximal such that every
triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices contains an independent set on $H(n)$ vertices.

If $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices, is $\tau(G)\leq n-H(n)$?

Erdős remarked that this is perhaps completely wrongheaded [Er88].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_151 :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), cliqueTransversalNumber G ≤ n - H n

statements.name: Erdos151.erdos_151.variants.cliqueFree_four
statements.doc: Erdős and Gallai made no progress on the question even when $G$ is $K_4$-free [Er88].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_151.variants.cliqueFree_four :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G.CliqueFree 4 →
      cliqueTransversalNumber G ≤ n - H n

statements.name: Erdos151.erdos_151.variants.cliqueFree_three
statements.doc:
If $G$ is triangle-free, then $\tau(G)\leq n-H(n)$: the complement of an independent set meets
every edge.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_151.variants.cliqueFree_three (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (hG : G.CliqueFree 3) : cliqueTransversalNumber G ≤ n - H n

statements.name: Erdos151.erdos_151.variants.sqrt_bound
statements.doc:
It is easy to see that $\tau(G)\leq n-\sqrt{n}$. We state this with $\lfloor\sqrt{n}\rfloor$:
with the real square root the bound fails for a single edge ($n = 2$, $\tau = 1$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_151.variants.sqrt_bound (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) :
    cliqueTransversalNumber G ≤ n - Nat.sqrt n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 152
problems.doc:
#TODO: Formalize the corresponding conjecture for infinite Sidon sets.

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/152](https://www.erdosproblems.com/152)

 - [ESS94] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, T., On Sum Sets of Sidon Sets, I. Journal of Number
    Theory (1994), 329-347.

statements.name: Erdos152.erdos_152
statements.doc:
Must `lim f n = ∞`?

This was proved formally by the DeepMind prover agent [DM26a].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_152 : Tendsto f atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos152.erdos_152.variants.square
statements.doc:
Must `f n ≫ n ^ 2`?

This stronger quadratic variant was also proved formally by the DeepMind prover agent [DM26b].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_152.variants.square :
    (fun n => f n : ℕ → ℝ) ≫ (fun n => n ^ 2 : ℕ → ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 153
problems.doc:
#TODO: Formalize the corresponding conjecture for infinite Sidon sets.

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/153](https://www.erdosproblems.com/153)
 - [ESS94] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, T., On Sum Sets of Sidon Sets, I. Journal of Number
    Theory (1994), 329-347.

statements.name: Erdos153.erdos_153
statements.doc:
Let $A$ be a finite Sidon set and $A+A=\{s_1<\cdots<s_t\}$. Is it true that
$$\frac{1}{t}\sum_{1\leq i<t}(s_{i+1}-s_i)^2 \to \infty$$
as $\lvert A\rvert\to \infty$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_153 : Tendsto f atTop atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 154
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/154](https://www.erdosproblems.com/154)
- [Li98] Lindström, Bernt, *Well distribution of Sidon sets in residue classes*.
  J. Number Theory (1998), 197-200.
- [Ko99] Kolountzakis, Mihail N., *On the uniform distribution in residue classes of dense sets
  of integers with distinct sums*. J. Number Theory (1999), 147-153.
- [ESS94] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, T., *On Sum Sets of Sidon Sets, I*.
  Journal of Number Theory (1994), 329-347.

statements.name: Erdos154.erdos_154
statements.doc:
Let $A\subset \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be a Sidon set with $\lvert A\rvert\sim N^{1/2}$. Must $A+A$ be
well-distributed over all small moduli? In particular, must about half the elements of $A+A$ be
even and half odd?

The answer is yes. Lindström [Li98] proved the analogous statement for $A$ itself (see
`erdos_154.variants.lindstrom`), later strengthened by Kolountzakis [Ko99]; well-distribution of
$A+A$ then follows using the Sidon property.

We state the question for the sumset: for any sequence of Sidon sets
$A_k\subseteq\{0,\ldots,N_k\}$ with $N_k\to\infty$ and $\lvert A_k\rvert\sim N_k^{1/2}$, and any
modulus $m\geq 2$, the proportion of elements of $A_k+A_k$ congruent to $i\pmod m$ (i.e. the count
divided by $\lvert A_k+A_k\rvert$) tends to $1/m$ for every residue $i<m$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_154 :
    ∀ (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) (N : ℕ → ℕ) (A : ℕ → Finset ℕ),
      Tendsto (fun k => (N k : ℝ)) atTop atTop →
      (∀ k, ∀ x ∈ A k, x ≤ N k) →
      (∀ k, IsSidon (A k : Set ℕ)) →
      Tendsto (fun k => ((A k).card : ℝ) / Real.sqrt (N k)) atTop (nhds 1) →
      ∀ i < m, Tendsto
        (fun k => (((A k + A k).filter (fun s => s % m = i)).card : ℝ) / ((A k + A k).card : ℝ))
        atTop (nhds (1 / m))

statements.name: Erdos154.erdos_154.variants.lindstrom
statements.doc:
Lindström's result for $A$ itself [Li98], later strengthened by Kolountzakis [Ko99]: for any
sequence of Sidon sets $A_k\subseteq\{0,\ldots,N_k\}$ with $N_k\to\infty$ and
$\lvert A_k\rvert\sim N_k^{1/2}$, and any modulus $m\geq 2$, the number of elements of $A_k$
congruent to $i\pmod m$, divided by $N_k^{1/2}$, tends to $1/m$ for every residue $i<m$.

Well-distribution of $A+A$ (the actual question, `erdos_154`) follows from this using the Sidon
property.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_154.variants.lindstrom :
    ∀ (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) (N : ℕ → ℕ) (A : ℕ → Finset ℕ),
      Tendsto (fun k => (N k : ℝ)) atTop atTop →
      (∀ k, ∀ x ∈ A k, x ≤ N k) →
      (∀ k, IsSidon (A k : Set ℕ)) →
      Tendsto (fun k => ((A k).card : ℝ) / Real.sqrt (N k)) atTop (nhds 1) →
      ∀ i < m, Tendsto
        (fun k => (((A k).filter (fun a => a % m = i)).card : ℝ) / Real.sqrt (N k))
        atTop (nhds (1 / m))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 155
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/155](https://www.erdosproblems.com/155)

statements.name: Erdos155.erdos_155
statements.doc:
Is it true that for every $k \geq 1$ we have
$$
F(N + k) \leq F(N) + 1
$$
for all sufficiently large $N$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_155 : ∀ k ≥ 1, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, F (N + k) ≤ F N + 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 156
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/156](https://www.erdosproblems.com/156)
- [ESS94] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, T., On Sum Sets of Sidon Sets, I. Journal of Number
  Theory (1994), 329-347.
- [Ru98b] Ruzsa, Imre Z., A small maximal Sidon set. Ramanujan J. (1998), 55-58.

statements.name: Erdos156.erdos_156
statements.doc:
Does there exist a maximal Sidon set $A\subset \{1,\ldots,N\}$ of size $O(N^{1/3})$?

A question of Erdős, Sárközy, and Sós [ESS94].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_156 :
    (fun N ↦ (minMaximalSidonSet N : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun N ↦ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 3 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos156.erdos_156.variants.greedy_lower_bound
statements.doc:
It is easy to prove that the greedy construction of a maximal Sidon set in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has size
$\gg N^{1/3}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_156.variants.greedy_lower_bound :
    (fun N ↦ ((Finset.greedySidonBelow N).card : ℝ)) ≫ (fun N ↦ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 3 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos156.erdos_156.variants.ruzsa_upper_bound
statements.doc: Ruzsa [Ru98b] constructed a maximal Sidon set of size $\ll (N\log N)^{1/3}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_156.variants.ruzsa_upper_bound :
    (fun N ↦ (minMaximalSidonSet N : ℝ)) ≪
      (fun N ↦ ((N : ℝ) * Real.log N) ^ (1 / 3 : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 157
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/157](https://www.erdosproblems.com/157)
- [ESS94] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, T., *On sum sets of Sidon sets, I*. Journal of Number
  Theory (1994), 329-347.
- [Er94b] Erdős, Paul, *Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and combinatorial geometry*.
  Math. Pannon. (1994), 261-269.
- [Pi23] Pilatte, C., *A solution to the Erdős–Sárközy–Sós problem on asymptotic Sidon bases of
  order 3*. Compositio Math. (2024), 1418-1432.

statements.name: Erdos157.erdos_157
statements.doc:
Does there exist an infinite Sidon set which is an asymptotic basis of order $3$?

Yes, as shown by Pilatte [Pi23].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_157 :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ IsSidon A ∧ A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 158
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/158](https://www.erdosproblems.com/158)
 - [ESS94] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, T., On Sum Sets of Sidon Sets, I. Journal of Number
    Theory (1994), 329-347.

statements.name: Erdos158.erdos_158
statements.doc: Let `A` be an infinite `B₂[2]` set. Must `liminf |A ∩ {1, ..., N}| * N ^ (- 1 / 2) = 0`?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_158 : ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → B2 2 A →
    liminf (fun N : ℕ => (A ∩ .Iio N).ncard * (N : ℝ) ^ (- 1 / 2 : ℝ)) atTop = 0

statements.name: Erdos158.erdos_158.variants.isSidon'
statements.doc:
Let `A` be an infinite Sidon set. Then
`liminf |A ∩ {1, ..., N}| * N ^ (- 1 / 2) * (log N) ^ (1 / 2) < ∞`. This is proved in [ESS94].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_158.variants.isSidon' {A : Set ℕ} (hAinf : A.Infinite) (hAsid : IsSidon A) :
    liminf (fun N ↦ ENNReal.ofReal ((A ∩ .Iio N).ncard * N ^ (- 1 / 2 : ℝ) * log N ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)))
      atTop < ⊤

statements.name: Erdos158.erdos_158.variants.isSidon
statements.doc:
As a corollary of `erdos_158.isSidon'`, we can prove that
`liminf |A ∩ {1, ..., N}| * N ^ (- 1 / 2) = 0` for any infinite Sidon set `A`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_158.variants.isSidon {A : Set ℕ} (hAinf : A.Infinite) (hAsid : IsSidon A) :
    liminf (fun N : ℕ => (A ∩ .Iio N).ncard * (N : ℝ) ^ (- 1 / 2 : ℝ)) atTop = 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 159
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/159](https://www.erdosproblems.com/159)
- [Er78] Erdős, P., Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory. Proc. Ninth Southeastern Conf. Combinatorics, Graph Theory and Computing (1978), 29-40.
- [Sp77] Spencer, J., Asymptotic lower bounds for Ramsey functions. Discrete Math. (1977), 69-76.

statements.name: Erdos159.erdos_159
statements.doc:
There exists some constant $c>0$ such that
$$R(C_4,K_n) \ll n^{2-c}.$$

The prize of $100 is offered in [Er78] for a proof or disproof.

This problem is #17 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_159 :
    ∃ (c : ℝ) (_ : 0 < c) (C : ℝ),
      ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n →
        (SimpleGraph.graphRamsey (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 4)
          (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)) : ℝ) ≤ C * (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 160
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/160](https://www.erdosproblems.com/160)

statements.name: Erdos160.erdos_160.known_upper
statements.doc:
On [Mathoverflow](https://mathoverflow.net/a/410815) user
[leechlattice](https://mathoverflow.net/users/125498/leechlattice) shows that
$h(n) \ll n^{\frac 2 3}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_160.known_upper :
    (fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3)

statements.name: Erdos160.erdos_160.better_upper
statements.doc: Estimate $h(n)$ by finding a better upper bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_160.better_upper :
    (fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] erdos_160.better_upper.answer ∧
    erdos_160.better_upper.answer =o[atTop] fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3)

statements.name: Erdos160.erdos_160.better_lower
statements.doc: Estimate $h(n)$ by finding a better lower bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_160.better_lower:
    (erdos_160.better_lower.answer =O[atTop] fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) ∧
    ∀ c > 0,
    (fun (n : ℕ) => exp (c * log n ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 12))) =O[atTop] (fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) →
    ∀ c > 0, (fun (n : ℕ) => exp (c * log n ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 12))) =o[atTop]
      erdos_160.better_lower.answer

statements.name: Erdos160.erdos_160.variants.known_lower
statements.doc:
The observation of Zachary Hunter in [that question](https://mathoverflow.net/q/410808)
coupled with the bounds of Kelley-Meka [KeMe23](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.05537) imply that
$$h(N) \gg \exp(c(\log N)^{\frac 1 {12}})$$
for some $c > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_160.variants.known_lower :
    ∃ c > 0, (fun (n : ℕ) => exp (c * log (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 12)))
    =O[atTop] fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 161
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/161](https://www.erdosproblems.com/161)
- [CFS11] Conlon, David and Fox, Jacob and Sudakov, Benny, Large almost monochromatic subsets in
  hypergraphs. Israel J. Math. (2011), 423--432.
- [Er90b] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on graphs and hypergraphs: similarities and differences
  . Mathematics of Ramsey theory (1990), 12-28.

statements.name: Erdos161.erdos_161.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $\alpha\in[0,1/2)$ and $n,t\geq 1$. Let $F^{(t)}(n,\alpha)$ be the smallest $m$ such that we can
$2$-colour the edges of the complete $t$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices such that if $X\subseteq
[n]$ with $\lvert X\rvert \geq m$ then there are at least $\alpha \binom{\lvert X\rvert}{t}$ many
$t$-subsets of $X$ of each colour. For fixed $n,t$ as we change $\alpha$ from $0$ to $1/2$ does
$F^{(t)}(n,\alpha)$ increase continuously or are there jumps? Only one jump?

Here growth is compared up to constant factors as $n\to\infty$. At $\alpha=0$,
each color must occur, following the source's Ramsey convention.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_161.parts.i :
    ∀ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t →
      {p | p.1 ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) (1 / 2) ∧ p.2 ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) (1 / 2) ∧
        (fun n ↦ (Hypergraph.balancedColoringThreshold n t p.1 : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop]
          (fun n ↦ (Hypergraph.balancedColoringThreshold n t p.2 : ℝ))} =
        erdos_161.parts.i.answer t

statements.name: Erdos161.erdos_161.parts.ii
statements.doc: For fixed $t\geq 3$, do all positive densities below $1/2$ give the same asymptotic order?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_161.parts.ii :
    ∀ t : ℕ, 3 ≤ t → ∀ α β : ℝ,
    0 < α → α < 1 / 2 → 0 < β → β < 1 / 2 →
    (fun n ↦ (Hypergraph.balancedColoringThreshold n t α : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop]
      (fun n ↦ (Hypergraph.balancedColoringThreshold n t β : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 162
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/162](https://www.erdosproblems.com/162)
- [Er90b] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on graphs and hypergraphs: similarities and
  differences*. Mathematics of Ramsey theory (1990), 12-28.

statements.name: Erdos162.erdos_162
statements.doc:
Let $\alpha > 0$ and $n \geq 1$. Let $F(n,\alpha)$ be the largest $k$ such that there exists some
2-colouring of the edges of $K_n$ in which any induced subgraph $H$ on at least $k$ vertices
contains more than $\alpha\binom{|H|}{2}$ many edges of each colour.

Prove that for every fixed $0 \leq \alpha \leq 1/2$, as $n \to \infty$,
$F(n,\alpha) \sim c_\alpha \log n$ for some constant $c_\alpha$.

We require $\alpha < 1/2$: at $\alpha = 1/2$ no colouring works for any `k ≤ n`
(see `erdos_162.variants.half`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_162 (α : ℝ) (h0 : 0 ≤ α) (h1 : α < 1 / 2) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, (fun n : ℕ ↦ (F n α : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ c * Real.log n)

statements.name: Erdos162.erdos_162.variants.bounds
statements.doc:
It is easy to show with the probabilistic method that there exist $c_1(\alpha), c_2(\alpha)$ such
that $c_1(\alpha)\log n < F(n,\alpha) < c_2(\alpha)\log n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_162.variants.bounds (α : ℝ) (h0 : 0 ≤ α) (h1 : α < 1 / 2) :
    ∃ c₁ c₂ : ℝ, 0 < c₁ ∧ c₁ < c₂ ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      c₁ * Real.log n < F n α ∧ (F n α : ℝ) < c₂ * Real.log n

statements.name: Erdos162.erdos_162.variants.half
statements.doc:
At $\alpha = 1/2$ the two colour counts in $H$ add up to $\binom{|H|}{2}$, so both cannot exceed
half of it. Hence $F(n, 1/2) = n + 1$, and the claim fails at $\alpha = 1/2$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_162.variants.half (n : ℕ) : F n (1 / 2) = n + 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 163
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/163](https://www.erdosproblems.com/163)
- [BuEr75] Burr, S. A. and Erdős, P., On the Ramsey number of graphs with small degree-ratio.
  Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai (1975).
- [Le17] Lee, C., Ramsey numbers of degenerate graphs. Ann. of Math. (2) 185 (2017), 791-829.

statements.name: Erdos163.erdos_163
statements.doc:
The Burr-Erdős conjecture: For any $d\geq 1$ if $H$ is a graph such that every subgraph
contains a vertex of degree at most $d$ then
$$R(H)\ll_d n.$$

Solved by Lee [Le17], who proved that $R(H) \leq 2^{2^{O(d)}}n$.

This problem is #9 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.

The linked formal proof (Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol) gives, for graphs `H` on `Fin n`, a natural
constant `C ≥ 1` with `RamseyFor H (C * n)` (every red/blue colouring of `K_{C n}` contains a
monochromatic copy of `H`); transporting along `Fintype.equivFin` gives the statement below.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_163 :
    ∀ (d : ℕ), 1 ≤ d →
      ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (H : SimpleGraph V),
        H.IsDegenerate d →
        (SimpleGraph.diagonalGraphRamsey H : ℝ) ≤ C * Fintype.card V

problems.title: Erdős Problem 164
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/164](https://www.erdosproblems.com/164)
- [Er76g] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. II*. J. Indian Math. Soc.
  (N.S.) (1976), 285-298.
- [Er86] Erdős, P., *Problémes et résultats en théorie des nombres*. (1986).
- [Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference "Paul
  Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).
- [ABLLPSTT26] B. Alexeev, K. Barreto, Y. Li, J. D. Lichtman, L. Price, J. I. Shah, Q. Tang, and
  T. Tao, *Primitive sets and Von Mangoldt Chains: Erdős problem #1196 and beyond*.
  arXiv:2605.00301 (2026).
- [Er35] Erdős, Paul, *Note on Sequences of Integers No One of Which is Divisible By Any Other*.
  J. London Math. Soc. (1935), 126-128.
- [Li23] Lichtman, J. D., *A proof of the Erdős primitive set conjecture*. arXiv:2202.02384 (2023).

statements.name: Erdos164.erdos_164
statements.doc:
A set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ is primitive if no member of $A$ divides another. Is the sum
$$\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n\log n}$$
maximised over all primitive sets when $A$ is the set of primes?

Erdős [Er35] proved that this sum always converges for a primitive set. Lichtman [Li23] proved
that the answer is yes. An alternative, simpler, proof is given by Alexeev, Barreto, Li, Lichtman,
Price, Shah, Tang, and Tao [ABLLPSTT26].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_164 :
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, (∀ a ∈ A, 2 ≤ a) → Erdos1196.IsPrimitive A →
      (∑' a : A, 1 / ((a : ℕ) * Real.log (a : ℕ))) ≤
        ∑' p : {p : ℕ | p.Prime}, 1 / ((p : ℕ) * Real.log (p : ℕ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 165
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/165](https://www.erdosproblems.com/165)
- [Er61] Erdős, P., *Graph theory and probability. II*. Canad. J. Math. (1961), 346-352.
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [Er90b] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on graphs and hypergraphs: similarities and
  differences*. Mathematics of Ramsey theory (1990), 12-28.
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [Er97c] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*. The mathematics of Paul Erdős,
  I (1997), 47-67.
- [Sh83] Shearer, J. B., *A note on the independence number of triangle-free graphs*. Discrete
  Math. (1983), 83-87.
- [Ki95] Kim, J. H., *The Ramsey number $R(3,t)$ has order of magnitude $t^2/\log t$*. Random
  Structures Algorithms (1995), 173-207.
- [CJMS25] Campos, M. and Jenssen, M. and Michelen, M. and Sahasrabudhe, J., *A new lower bound
  for the Ramsey numbers $R(3,k)$*. arXiv:2505.13371 (2025).
- [HHKP25] Hefty, Z. and Horn, P. and King, D. and Pfender, F., *Improving $R(3,k)$ in just two
  bites*. arXiv:2510.19718 (2025).

statements.name: Erdos165.erdos_165
statements.doc: Give an asymptotic formula for $R(3,k)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_165 :
    (fun k : ℕ ↦ (R(3, k) : ℝ)) ~[atTop] erdos_165.answer

statements.name: Erdos165.erdos_165.variants.conjecture
statements.doc:
Campos, Jenssen, Michelen and Sahasrabudhe [CJMS25] and Hefty, Horn, King and Pfender [HHKP25]
conjecture that $R(3,k) \sim \frac{k^2}{2\log k}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_165.variants.conjecture :
    (fun k : ℕ ↦ (R(3, k) : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun k : ℕ ↦ (k : ℝ) ^ 2 / (2 * Real.log k))

statements.name: Erdos165.erdos_165.variants.upper
statements.doc: Shearer [Sh83] proved $R(3,k) \leq (1+o(1))\frac{k^2}{\log k}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_165.variants.upper :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      (R(3, k) : ℝ) ≤ (1 + ε) * (k : ℝ) ^ 2 / Real.log k

statements.name: Erdos165.erdos_165.variants.lower
statements.doc:
Hefty, Horn, King and Pfender [HHKP25] proved $R(3,k) \geq (1/2+o(1))\frac{k^2}{\log k}$,
improving earlier bounds of Kim [Ki95] and Campos, Jenssen, Michelen and Sahasrabudhe [CJMS25].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_165.variants.lower :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      (1 / 2 - ε) * (k : ℝ) ^ 2 / Real.log k ≤ (R(3, k) : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 166
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/166](https://www.erdosproblems.com/166)
- [Sp77] Spencer, J., Asymptotic lower bounds for Ramsey functions. Discrete Math. (1977), 69-76.
- [AKS80] Ajtai, M., Komlós, J. and Szemerédi, E., A note on Ramsey numbers. J. Combin. Theory
  Ser. A (1980), 354-360.
- [MaVe23] Mattheus, S. and Verstraëte, J., The asymptotics of $r(4,t)$. Ann. of Math. (2024),
  941-965.

statements.name: Erdos166.erdos_166
statements.doc:
Prove that
$$R(4,k) \gg \frac{k^3}{(\log k)^{O(1)}}.$$

This is true, and was proved by Mattheus and Verstraëte [MaVe23], who showed that
$R(4,k) \gg \frac{k^3}{(\log k)^4}$.
This problem is #5 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.

The linked formal proof (Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol, via the construction of Bradač used for
Problem 920) gives `k ^ 3 / (log k) ^ c = O(R(4, k))` for a natural `c > 0`, with the Ramsey
number defined through `CliqueFree`/`IndepSetFree`; this implies the statement below.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_166 :
    ∃ (c C : ℝ), 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧
      ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in atTop,
        (SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey 4 k : ℝ) ≥
          C * (k : ℝ) ^ 3 / (Real.log k) ^ c

statements.name: Erdos166.erdos_166.variants.mattheus_verstraete
statements.doc:
Mattheus and Verstraëte [MaVe23] proved the explicit lower bound
$$R(4,k) \gg \frac{k^3}{(\log k)^4}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_166.variants.mattheus_verstraete :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in atTop,
      (SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey 4 k : ℝ) ≥ C * (k : ℝ) ^ 3 / (Real.log k) ^ 4

problems.title: Erdős Problem 168
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/168](https://www.erdosproblems.com/168)

statements.name: Erdos168.erdos_168.parts.i
statements.doc: What is the limit $F(N)/N$ as $N \to \infty$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_168.parts.i :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N => (F N / N : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (𝓝 erdos_168.parts.i.answer)

statements.name: Erdos168.erdos_168.parts.ii
statements.doc: Is the limit $F(N)/N$ as $N \to \infty$ irrational?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_168.parts.ii :
    Irrational (Filter.atTop.limsup (fun N => (F N / N : ℝ)))

statements.name: Erdos168.erdos_168.variants.limit_exists
statements.doc: The limit $F(N)/N$ as $N \to \infty$ exists. (proved by Graham, Spencer, and Witsenhausen)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_168.variants.limit_exists :
    ∃ x, Filter.Tendsto (fun N => (F N / N : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (𝓝 x)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 170
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/170](https://www.erdosproblems.com/170)

statements.name: Erdos170.erdos170
statements.doc: The problem is to determine the limit of the sequence $\frac{F(N)}{\sqrt{N}}$ as $N \to \infty$.
statements.statement: lemma erdos170 : Filter.Tendsto (fun N => F N / √N) Filter.atTop (𝓝 erdos170.answer)

statements.name: Erdos170.erdos170.existing_bounds
statements.doc:
The existence of the limit has been proved by Erdős and Gál [ErGa48].
The lower bound has been proven by Leech [Le56], who refined an argument of Rédei and Rényi.
The upper bound is due to Wichmann [Wi63].
statements.statement:
lemma erdos170.existing_bounds :
  ∃ x ∈ Set.Icc lower_bound upper_bound,
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N => F N / √N) Filter.atTop (𝓝 x)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 171
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/171](https://www.erdosproblems.com/171)
- [ErGr79] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory: van der Waerden's theorem and related topics*. Enseign. Math. (1979), 325-344.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [FuKa91] Furstenberg, H. and Katznelson, Y., *A density version of the Hales-Jewett Theorem*.
  Journal d'Analyse Mathématique (1991), 64-119.
- [Po12] Polymath, D. H. J., *A new proof of the density Hales–Jewett theorem*. Ann. Math.
  (2012), 1283-1327.

statements.name: Erdos171.erdos_171
statements.doc:
Is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$ and integer $t\geq 1$, if $N$ is sufficiently large and
$A$ is a subset of $[t]^N$ of size at least $\epsilon t^N$ then $A$ must contain a combinatorial
line $P$ (a set $P=\{p_1,\ldots,p_t\}$ where for each coordinate $1\leq j\leq t$ the $j$th
coordinate of $p_i$ is either $i$ or constant).

The 'density Hales-Jewett' problem. This was proved by Furstenberg and Katznelson [FuKa91]. A
new elementary proof, which gives quantitative bounds, was proved by the Polymath project
[Po12].

Combinatorial lines are Mathlib's `Combinatorics.Line (Fin t) (Fin N)` (which have at least one
non-constant coordinate).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_171 : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t → ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop,
    ∀ A : Finset (Fin N → Fin t), ε * t ^ N ≤ A.card →
      ∃ l : Combinatorics.Line (Fin t) (Fin N), ∀ i : Fin t, l i ∈ A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 172
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/172](https://www.erdosproblems.com/172)
- [OpenAI26] OpenAI, *Monochromatic finite sums and products in the positive integers*. OpenAI Math
  Release preprint (September 2026).
  [github.com/openai/math](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/Monochromatic-finite-sums-and-products-in-the-positive-integers-September-23-2026/paper.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos172.erdos_172
statements.doc:
Is it true that in any finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there exist arbitrarily large finite $A$ such that all sums
and products of distinct elements in $A$ are the same colour?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_172 :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (color : ℕ → Fin n) (m), ∃ (A : Finset ℕ), A.card ≥ m ∧ ∃ c, ∀ (S : Finset A),
    S.Nonempty → color (∑ x ∈ S, x) = c ∧ color (∏ x ∈ S, x) = c

problems.title: Erdős Problem 173
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/173](https://www.erdosproblems.com/173)
- [Sh76] Shader, L. E., *All right triangles are Ramsey in $E^2$!*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A
  (1976), 385-389.

statements.name: Erdos173.erdos_173
statements.doc:
In any $2$-colouring of $\mathbb{R}^2$, for all but at most one triangle $T$ (up to
congruence), there is a monochromatic congruent copy of $T$.

The colouring is arbitrary. No measurability is assumed. `≅` compares vertices with the same
label, so the conclusion allows a relabelling `σ`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_173 : ∀ (c : ℝ² → Fin 2) (T₁ T₂ : Triangle ℝ ℝ²),
    ¬ HasMonochromaticCopy c T₁ → ¬ HasMonochromaticCopy c T₂ →
      ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 3), T₁.points ∘ σ ≅ T₂.points

statements.name: Erdos173.erdos_173.variants.right_triangle
statements.doc:
Shader [Sh76] proved that in any $2$-colouring of $\mathbb{R}^2$, every right-angled triangle
has a monochromatic congruent copy.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_173.variants.right_triangle (c : ℝ² → Fin 2) (T : Triangle ℝ ℝ²)
    (hT : ∠ (T.points 0) (T.points 1) (T.points 2) = Real.pi / 2) :
    HasMonochromaticCopy c T

statements.name: Erdos173.erdos_173.variants.equilateral_exception
statements.doc:
The exceptional triangle can exist: colouring the plane in alternating half-open strips of
suitable width gives no monochromatic copy of some equilateral triangle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_173.variants.equilateral_exception : ∃ (c : ℝ² → Fin 2) (T : Triangle ℝ ℝ²),
    dist (T.points 0) (T.points 1) = dist (T.points 1) (T.points 2) ∧
    dist (T.points 1) (T.points 2) = dist (T.points 2) (T.points 0) ∧
    ¬ HasMonochromaticCopy c T

problems.title: Erdős Problem 174
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/174](https://www.erdosproblems.com/174)
- [EGMRSS73] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Montgomery, P. and Rothschild, B. L. and Spencer,
  J. and Straus, E. G., *Euclidean Ramsey Theorems I*. J. Comb. Th. A (1973), 341-363.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1973-08.pdf)
- [Er75f] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry*. Ann. Mat. Pura
  Appl. (4) (1975), 99-108. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-25.pdf)
- [FrRo90] Frankl, P. and Rödl, V., *A partition property of simplices in Euclidean space*.
  J. Amer. Math. Soc. (1990), 1-7.
- [Kr92] Kříž, Igor, *All trapezoids are Ramsey*. Discrete Math. (1992), 59-62.
- [LRW12] Leader, Imre and Russell, Paul A. and Walters, Mark, *Transitive sets in Euclidean
  Ramsey theory*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (2012), 382-396.
  [arXiv:1012.1350](https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.1350)

statements.name: Erdos174.erdos_174
statements.doc:
A finite set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is called Ramsey if, for any $k\geq 1$, there exists some
$d=d(A,k)$ such that in any $k$-colouring of $\mathbb{R}^d$ there exists a monochromatic copy
of $A$. Characterise the Ramsey sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

A copy of $A$ is a set congruent to $A$, as in [EGMRSS73, p. 344].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_174 (n : ℕ) :
    {A : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) | IsRamsey A} = erdos_174.answer n

statements.name: Erdos174.erdos_174.variants.spherical
statements.doc:
Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer, and Straus [EGMRSS73] proved that every Ramsey
set is 'spherical': it lies on the surface of some sphere.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_174.variants.spherical {n : ℕ} (A : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))
    (hA : IsRamsey A) : EuclideanGeometry.Cospherical A

statements.name: Erdos174.erdos_174.variants.graham
statements.doc: Graham has conjectured that every spherical set is Ramsey.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_174.variants.graham {n : ℕ} (A : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))
    (hA : A.Finite) (hs : EuclideanGeometry.Cospherical A) : IsRamsey A

statements.name: Erdos174.erdos_174.variants.leader_russell_walters
statements.doc:
Leader, Russell, and Walters [LRW12] have alternatively conjectured that a set is Ramsey if and
only if it is 'subtransitive': it can be embedded in some higher-dimensional set on which
rotations act transitively.

We use the definition of [LRW12]: a subset of a finite set whose symmetry group acts
transitively.

statements.name: Erdos174.erdos_174.variants.brick
statements.doc:
Sets known to be Ramsey include vertices of $k$-dimensional rectangles [EGMRSS73].

This is the case of the vertices `{x | ∀ i, x i = 0 ∨ x i = a i}` of a rectangular
parallelepiped [EGMRSS73, Cor. 21]; some $a_i$ may be $0$ [EGMRSS73, Cor. 22].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_174.variants.brick {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → ℝ) :
    IsRamsey {x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) | ∀ i, x i = 0 ∨ x i = a i}

statements.name: Erdos174.erdos_174.variants.simplex
statements.doc:
Sets known to be Ramsey include non-degenerate simplices [FrRo90].

A non-degenerate simplex is a set of affinely independent points.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_174.variants.simplex {n : ℕ} (A : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))
    (hA : AffineIndependent ℝ (Subtype.val : A → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) :
    IsRamsey A

statements.name: Erdos174.erdos_174.variants.trapezoid
statements.doc:
Sets known to be Ramsey include trapezoids [Kr92].

We state it for isosceles trapezoids with vertices $(\pm s, 0)$ and $(\pm t, h)$, $h\neq 0$.
A trapezoid that is not isosceles is not spherical, so it is not Ramsey by [EGMRSS73].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_174.variants.trapezoid (s t h : ℝ) (hh : h ≠ 0) :
    IsRamsey ({!₂[-s, 0], !₂[s, 0], !₂[-t, h], !₂[t, h]} :
      Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 175
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/175](https://www.erdosproblems.com/175)
- [Sa85] A. Sárközy, *On divisors of binomial coefficients, I*, J. Number Theory 20
  (1985), 70–80.
- [GrRa96] A. Granville and O. Ramaré, *Explicit bounds on exponential sums and the scarcity
  of squarefree binomial coefficients*, Mathematika 43 (1996), 73–107.
- [Ve95] G. Velammal, *Is the binomial coefficient $\binom{2n}{n}$ square free?*,
  Hardy-Ramanujan Journal 18 (1995), 23–45.

Sárközy proved the assertion for all sufficiently large `n`; Granville--Ramaré and Velammal
independently proved the full range `n ≥ 5`.

statements.name: Erdos175.erdos_175
statements.doc: Show that, for any $n\geq 5$, the binomial coefficient $\binom{2n}{n}$ is not squarefree.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_175 (n : ℕ) (hn : 5 ≤ n) :
    ¬ Squarefree ((2 * n).choose n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 178
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/178](https://www.erdosproblems.com/178)
- [ErGr79] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory: van der Waerden's theorem and related topics*. Enseign. Math. (1979), 325-344.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980).
- [Be81] Beck, József, *Balancing families of integer sequences*. Combinatorica (1981), 209-216.
- [Be17] Beck, József, *A discrepancy problem: balancing infinite dimensional vectors*. Number theory—Diophantine problems, uniform distribution and applications (2017), 61-82.

statements.name: Erdos178.erdos_178
statements.doc:
Let $A_1,A_2,\ldots$ be an infinite collection of infinite sets of integers, say
$A_i=\{a_{i1}<a_{i2}<\cdots\}$. Does there exist some $f:\mathbb{N}\to\{-1,1\}$ such that
$$\max_{m, 1\leq i\leq d} \left\lvert \sum_{1\leq j\leq m} f(a_{ij})\right\rvert \ll_d 1$$
for all $d\geq 1$?

Erdős remarks 'it seems certain that the answer is affirmative'. This was solved by Beck [Be81]. Recently Beck [Be17] proved that one can replace $\ll_d 1$ with $\ll d^{4+\epsilon}$ for any $\epsilon>0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_178 :
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ) (ha : ∀ i, StrictMono (a i)),
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℤ, (∀ n, f n = 1 ∨ f n = -1) ∧
      ∀ d : ℕ, ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ m i : ℕ, i < d →
        |∑ j ∈ range m, f (a i j)| ≤ ↑C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 180
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/180](https://www.erdosproblems.com/180)
- [ErSi82] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M., *Compactness results in extremal graph theory*.
  Combinatorica (1982), 275-288.
- [OpenAI26] OpenAI, *Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science*. (2026).

statements.name: Erdos180.erdos_180
statements.doc:
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite set of finite graphs then $\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})$ is the maximum
number of edges a graph on $n$ vertices can have without containing any subgraphs from
$\mathcal{F}$. Note that it is trivial that $\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})\leq \mathrm{ex}(n;G)$ for
every $G\in\mathcal{F}$. Is it true that, for every $\mathcal{F}$, there exists $G\in\mathcal{F}$
such that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;G)\ll_{\mathcal{F}}\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})?$$

This is the Erdős–Simonovits compactness conjecture. The answer is no: OpenAI [OpenAI26] give a
family of connected bipartite graphs, none of them acyclic, for which no single member controls
the family extremal number. See `erdos_180.variants.counterexample`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_180 :
    ¬ ∀ family : Finset FiniteGraph,
      family.Nonempty → IsCyclicFamily family → IsCompactFamily family

statements.name: Erdos180.erdos_180.variants.counterexample
statements.doc:
The counterexample: a nonempty family of connected bipartite graphs, none acyclic, that is not
compact.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_180.variants.counterexample :
    ∃ family : Finset FiniteGraph,
      family.Nonempty ∧
      (∀ forbidden ∈ family,
        forbidden.graph.Connected ∧ forbidden.graph.IsBipartite ∧
          ¬ forbidden.graph.IsAcyclic) ∧
      ¬ IsCompactFamily family

problems.title: Erdős Problem 181
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/181](https://www.erdosproblems.com/181)
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [Ti22] Tikhomirov, K., *A remark on the Ramsey number of the hypercube*. arXiv:2208.14568 (2022).
- [OpenAI26] OpenAI, *The hypercube Ramsey number has linear order*. OpenAI Math Release preprint
  (September 2026).
  [github.com/openai/math](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/The-hypercube-Ramsey-number-has-linear-order-September-23-2026/paper.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos181.erdos_181
statements.doc:
Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph (so that $Q_n$ has $2^n$ vertices and
$n2^{n-1}$ edges). Prove that $$R(Q_n) \ll 2^n.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_181 :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ,
      (diagonalGraphRamsey (hypercube n) : ℝ) ≤ C * 2 ^ n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 183
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/183](https://www.erdosproblems.com/183)
- [Er61] Erdős, P., *Graph theory and probability. II*. Canad. J. Math. (1961), 346-352.
- [OpenAI26] OpenAI, *Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science*. (2026).

statements.name: Erdos183.erdos_183
statements.doc:
Let $R(3;k)$ be the minimal $n$ such that if the edges of $K_n$ are coloured with $k$ colours
then there must exist a monochromatic triangle. Determine
$$\lim_{k\to \infty}R(3;k)^{1/k}.$$

There is no finite limit: $R(3;k)^{1/k}\to\infty$. This was established by OpenAI [OpenAI26]
along with the explicit superexponential lower bound in
`erdos_183.variants.explicit_lower_bound`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_183 :
    Tendsto (fun k : ℕ => (multicolourTriangleRamsey k : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (k : ℝ)))
      atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos183.erdos_183.variants.explicit_lower_bound
statements.doc:
The explicit bound behind `erdos_183`: for every $k\geq 2$,
$$R(3;k)\geq \left(\frac{k^{1/3}}{6e^{38}\log k}\right)^k.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_183.variants.explicit_lower_bound :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k →
      (((1 : ℝ) / (6 * Real.exp 38)) * (k : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3) / Real.log (k : ℝ)) ^ k ≤
        (multicolourTriangleRamsey k : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 184
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/184](https://www.erdosproblems.com/184)
- [BM22] Bucić, M. and Montgomery, R., Towards the Erdős-Gallai Cycle Decomposition Conjecture.
  arXiv:2211.07689 (2022).
- [CFS14] Conlon, David and Fox, Jacob and Sudakov, Benny, Cycle packing. Random Structures
  Algorithms (2014), 608-626.
- [EGP66] Erdős, Paul and Goodman, A. W. and Pósa, Lajos, The representation of a graph by set
  intersections. Canadian J. Math. (1966), 106-112.
- [Er71] Erdős, P., Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis. Combinatorial
  Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [OAI26a] OpenAI, *A linear cycle-and-edge decomposition of every graph*. OpenAI Math Release
  preprint (2026).
  https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/A-linear-cycle-and-edge-decomposition-of-every-graph-September-24-2026/main.pdf
- [Py85] Pyber, L., An Erdős-Gallai conjecture. Combinatorica (1985), 67-79.

statements.name: Erdos184.erdos_184
statements.doc:
Any graph on $n$ vertices can be decomposed into $O(n)$ many edge-disjoint cycles and edges.

This was proved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26a]; see the linked Lean
proof.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_184 :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ,
      (f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧
        IsDecomposition G D ∧
        (D.card : ℝ) ≤ f (Fintype.card V)

statements.name: Erdos184.erdos_184.variants.n_log_n
statements.doc: Erdős and Gallai [EGP66] proved that $O(n \log n)$ many cycles and edges suffices.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_184.variants.n_log_n :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ,
      (f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧
        IsDecomposition G D ∧
        (D.card : ℝ) ≤ f (Fintype.card V)

statements.name: Erdos184.erdos_184.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
The graph $K_{3,n-3}$ shows that at least $(1+c)n$ many cycles and edges are required, for some
constant $c>0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_184.variants.lower_bound :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      let G : SimpleGraph (Fin n) := fromRel (fun (i j : Fin n) => (i : ℕ) < 3 ∧ 3 ≤ (j : ℕ));
      ∀ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) →
        IsDecomposition G D →
        (1 + c) * (n : ℝ) ≤ (D.card : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos184.erdos_184.variants.covering
statements.doc:
In [Er71] Erdős suggests that only $n-1$ many cycles and edges are required if we do not
require them to be edge-disjoint. Pyber [Py85] proved this.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_184.variants.covering :
    ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
    ∃ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
      (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧
      (⋃ H ∈ D, H.edgeSet) = G.edgeSet ∧
      (D.card : ℝ) ≤ (Fintype.card V : ℝ) - 1

statements.name: Erdos184.erdos_184.variants.bucic_montgomery
statements.doc:
Before [OAI26a], the best bound was due to Bucić and Montgomery [BM22], who prove that
$O(n\log^* n)$ many cycles and edges suffice, where $\log^*$ is the iterated logarithm function.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_184.variants.bucic_montgomery :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ,
      (f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) * (Real.iteratedLog (n : ℝ) : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧
        IsDecomposition G D ∧
        (D.card : ℝ) ≤ f (Fintype.card V)

statements.name: Erdos184.erdos_184.variants.conlon_fox_sudakov
statements.doc:
Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov [CFS14] proved that $O_\epsilon(n)$ cycles and edges suffice if $G$ has
minimum degree at least $\epsilon n$, for any $\epsilon>0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_184.variants.conlon_fox_sudakov :
    ∀ ε > 0, ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ,
      (f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      (G.minDegree : ℝ) ≥ ε * (Fintype.card V : ℝ) →
      ∃ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧
        IsDecomposition G D ∧
        (D.card : ℝ) ≤ f (Fintype.card V)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 185
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/185](https://www.erdosproblems.com/185)
- [Er73] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of
  combinatorial theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971)
  (1973), 117-138.
- [FuKa91] Furstenberg, H. and Katznelson, Y., *A density version of the Hales-Jewett Theorem*.
  Journal d'Analyse Mathématique (1991), 64-119.

statements.name: Erdos185.erdos_185
statements.doc:
Let $f_3(n)$ be the maximal size of a subset of $\{0,1,2\}^n$ which contains no three points on
a line. Is it true that $f_3(n)=o(3^n)$?

Originally considered by Moser. It is trivial that $f_3(n)\geq R_3(3^n)$, the maximal size of a
subset of $\{1,\ldots,3^n\}$ without a three-term arithmetic progression. Moser showed that
$$f_3(n) \gg \frac{3^n}{\sqrt{n}}.$$

The answer is yes, which is a corollary of the density Hales-Jewett theorem, proved by
Furstenberg and Katznelson [FuKa91].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_185 : (fun n : ℕ => (f3 n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] fun n : ℕ => (3 : ℝ) ^ n

statements.name: Erdos185.erdos_185.variants.moser
statements.doc: Moser showed that $f_3(n) \gg \frac{3^n}{\sqrt{n}}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_185.variants.moser :
    (fun n : ℕ => (3 : ℝ) ^ n / √n) =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ => (f3 n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 186
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/186](https://www.erdosproblems.com/186)
- [Bo89] Bosznay, Á. P., *On the lower estimation of nonaveraging sets*. Acta Math. Hungar.
  (1989), 155-157.
- [ErSa90] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A., *On a problem of Straus*. Disorder in physical systems
  (1990), 55-66.
- [PhZa24] Pham, H. T. and Zakharov, D., *Sharp bound for the Erdős–Straus non-averaging set
  problem*. [arXiv:2410.14624](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.14624) (2024).

statements.name: Erdos186.erdos_186
statements.doc:
Let $F(N)$ be the maximal size of $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ which is 'non-averaging', so that
no $n\in A$ is the arithmetic mean of at least two elements in $A$. What is the order of growth
of $F(N)$?

It is known that $N^{1/4}\ll F(N) \ll N^{1/4+o(1)}$: the lower bound is due to Bosznay [Bo89] and
the upper bound to Pham and Zakharov [PhZa24, Theorem 1]. So $\log F(N)/\log N\to 1/4$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_186 :
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ Real.log (F N) / Real.log N) atTop (𝓝 (1 / 4))

statements.name: Erdos186.erdos_186.variants.pham_zakharov
statements.doc:
Pham and Zakharov [PhZa24, Theorem 1] proved that every non-averaging subset of
$\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has size at most $N^{1/4+o(1)}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_186.variants.pham_zakharov :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (F N : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 4 + ε)

statements.name: Erdos186.erdos_186.variants.bosznay
statements.doc: The lower bound $N^{1/4}\ll F(N)$ is due to Bosznay [Bo89].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_186.variants.bosznay :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, c * (N : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 4) ≤ F N

statements.name: Erdos186.erdos_186.variants.erdos_sarkozy
statements.doc: The original upper bound of Erdős and Sárközy [ErSa90] was $F(N)\ll (N\log N)^{1/2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_186.variants.erdos_sarkozy :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (F N : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.sqrt ((N : ℝ) * Real.log N)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 188
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/188](https://www.erdosproblems.com/188)
- [EGMRSS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Montgomery, P. and Rothschild, B. L. and Spencer, J.
  and Straus, E. G., Euclidean {R}amsey theorems. {II}. (1975), 529--557.
- [Ts17] Tsaturian, Sergei, A {E}uclidean {R}amsey result in the plane. Electron. J. Combin. (2017),
