  Paper No. 4.35, 9.

statements.name: Erdos188.erdos_188
statements.doc:
What is the smallest $k$ such that $\mathbb{R}^2$ can be red/blue coloured with no pair of red
points unit distance apart, and no $k$-term arithmetic progression of blue points with distance 1?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_188 : IsLeast s erdos_188.answer

statements.name: Erdos188.erdos_188.variants.nonempty
statements.doc:
Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory by Erdős & Graham (Page 14, 15):

It has been shown that there is a large $M$ so that it is possible to partition $\mathbb{E}^2$ into
two sets $A$ and $B$ so that $A$ contains no pair of points with distance 1 and $B$ contains no A.P.
of length $M$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_188.variants.nonempty : s.Nonempty

statements.name: Erdos188.erdos_188.variants.estimate
statements.doc:
Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory by Erdős & Graham (Page 15):

How small can $M$ be made? The only estimate currently known is that $M \le 10000000$ (more or less).
In the other direction, it has just been shown by R. Juhász [Ju (79)] that we must have $M \ge 5$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_188.variants.estimate : (∀ k, k ∈ s → 5 ≤ k) ∧ (∃ k ∈ s, k ≤ 10000000)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 189
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/189](https://www.erdosproblems.com/189)

statements.name: Erdos189.erdos_189
statements.doc:
If $\mathbb{R}^2$ is finitely coloured then must there exist some colour class which contains the
vertices of a rectangle of every area?

Graham, "On Partitions of 𝔼ⁿ", Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A 28, 89-91 (1980).
(See "Concluding Remarks" on page 96.)

Solved (with answer `False`, as formalised below) in:
Vjekoslav Kovač, "Coloring and density theorems for configurations of a given volume", 2023
https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.09973
In fact, Kovač's colouring is even Jordan measurable (the topological boundary of each
monochromatic region is Lebesgue measurable and has measure zero).

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev and Kovac using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_189 :
    ¬ Erdos189For
      (fun a b c d ↦
        line[ℝ, a, b].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, b, c].direction ∧
        line[ℝ, b, c].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, c, d].direction ∧
        line[ℝ, c, d].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, d, a].direction)
      (fun a b c d ↦ dist a b * dist b c)

statements.name: Erdos189.erdos_189.variants.square
statements.doc: Graham claims this is "easy to see".
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_189.variants.square :
    ¬ Erdos189For
      (fun a b c d ↦
        line[ℝ, a, b].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, b, c].direction ∧
        line[ℝ, b, c].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, c, d].direction ∧
        line[ℝ, c, d].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, d, a].direction ∧
        dist a b = dist b c)
      (fun a b c d ↦ dist a b * dist b c)

statements.name: Erdos189.erdos_189.variants.parallelogram
statements.doc: Seems to be open, as of January 2025.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_189.variants.parallelogram :
    ¬ Erdos189For
      (fun a b c d ↦
        line[ℝ, a, b] ∥ line[ℝ, c, d] ∧
        line[ℝ, a, d] ∥ line[ℝ, b, c])
      (fun a b c d ↦ dist a b * dist b c * (∡ a b c).sin)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 191
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/191](https://www.erdosproblems.com/191)
- [ErGr79] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory: van der Waerden's theorem and related topics*. Enseign. Math. (1979), 325-344.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*. (1982),
  59--79.
- [Ro03] Rödl, Vojtěch, *On homogeneous sets of positive integers*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A
  (2003), 229-240.
- [CFS13] Conlon, David and Fox, Jacob and Sudakov, Benny, *Two extensions of Ramsey's theorem*.
  Duke Math. J. (2013), 2903-2927.

statements.name: Erdos191.erdos_191
statements.doc:
Let $C>0$ be arbitrary. Is it true that, if $n$ is sufficiently large depending on $C$, then in
any $2$-colouring of $\binom{\{2,\ldots,n\}}{2}$ there exists some $X\subseteq \{2,\ldots,n\}$
such that $\binom{X}{2}$ is monochromatic and
$$\sum_{x\in X}\frac{1}{\log x}\geq C?$$

The answer is yes, which was proved by Rödl [Ro03]. In the same article Rödl also proved a lower
bound for this problem, constructing, for all $n$, a $2$-colouring of $\binom{\{2,\ldots,n\}}{2}$
such that if $X\subseteq \{2,\ldots,n\}$ is such that $\binom{X}{2}$ is monochromatic then
$$\sum_{x\in X}\frac{1}{\log x}\ll \log\log\log n.$$
In the same paper Rödl proves that the answer to the main problem is negative if we consider
$3$-colourings.

This bound is best possible, as proved by Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov [CFS13], who proved that, if
$n$ is sufficiently large, then in any $2$-colouring of $\binom{\{2,\ldots,n\}}{2}$ there exists
some $X\subseteq \{2,\ldots,n\}$ such that $\binom{X}{2}$ is monochromatic and
$$\sum_{x\in X}\frac{1}{\log x}\geq 2^{-8}\log\log\log n.$$

A $2$-colouring of the pairs of $\{2,\ldots,n\}$ is a graph `G` on this vertex set; a
monochromatic set is a clique or an independent set of `G`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_191 : ∀ C : ℝ, 0 < C → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Finset.Icc 2 n), ∃ X : Finset (Finset.Icc 2 n),
      (G.IsClique X ∨ G.IsIndepSet X) ∧ C ≤ ∑ x ∈ X, 1 / Real.log (x : ℕ)

statements.name: Erdos191.erdos_191.variants.conlon_fox_sudakov
statements.doc:
Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov [CFS13] proved that, if $n$ is sufficiently large, then in any
$2$-colouring of $\binom{\{2,\ldots,n\}}{2}$ there exists some $X\subseteq \{2,\ldots,n\}$ such
that $\binom{X}{2}$ is monochromatic and
$$\sum_{x\in X}\frac{1}{\log x}\geq 2^{-8}\log\log\log n.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_191.variants.conlon_fox_sudakov : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Finset.Icc 2 n), ∃ X : Finset (Finset.Icc 2 n),
      (G.IsClique X ∨ G.IsIndepSet X) ∧
        2 ^ (-8 : ℤ) * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log n)) ≤ ∑ x ∈ X, 1 / Real.log (x : ℕ)

statements.name: Erdos191.erdos_191.variants.rodl_upper
statements.doc:
Rödl [Ro03] constructed, for all $n$, a $2$-colouring of $\binom{\{2,\ldots,n\}}{2}$ such that
if $X\subseteq \{2,\ldots,n\}$ is such that $\binom{X}{2}$ is monochromatic then
$$\sum_{x\in X}\frac{1}{\log x}\ll \log\log\log n.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_191.variants.rodl_upper : ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Finset.Icc 2 n), ∀ X : Finset (Finset.Icc 2 n),
      G.IsClique X ∨ G.IsIndepSet X →
        ∑ x ∈ X, 1 / Real.log (x : ℕ) ≤ c * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log n))

statements.name: Erdos191.erdos_191.variants.three_colours
statements.doc:
Rödl [Ro03] proved that the answer to [erdős_191](https://www.erdosproblems.com/191) is negative
if we consider $3$-colourings: there is a constant $C$ such that for every $n$ some $3$-colouring
of $\binom{\{2,\ldots,n\}}{2}$ has $\sum_{x\in X}\frac{1}{\log x} < C$ for every monochromatic
$X$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_191.variants.three_colours : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ,
    ∃ c : Sym2 (Finset.Icc 2 n) → Fin 3, ∀ X : Finset (Finset.Icc 2 n),
      (∃ i : Fin 3, ∀ x ∈ X, ∀ y ∈ X, x ≠ y → c s(x, y) = i) →
        ∑ x ∈ X, 1 / Real.log (x : ℕ) < C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 192
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/192](https://www.erdosproblems.com/192)
- [ErGr79] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory: van der Waerden's theorem and related topics*. Enseign. Math. (1979), 325-344.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Ke92] Keränen, Veikko, *Abelian squares are avoidable on $4$ letters*. Automata, languages and
  programming (Vienna, 1992) (1992), 41-52.
- [FiPu23] Fici, Gabriele and Puzynina, Svetlana, *Abelian combinatorics on words: a survey*.
  Comput. Sci. Rev. (2023), Paper No. 100532, 21.

statements.name: Erdos192.erdos_192
statements.doc:
Let $A=\{a_1,a_2,\ldots\}\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be an infinite sequence such that $a_{i+1}-a_i$
is a positive unit vector (i.e. is of the form $(0,0,\ldots,1,0,\ldots,0)$). For which $d$ must
$A$ contain a three-term arithmetic progression?

This is true for $d\leq 3$ and false for $d\geq 4$.

This problem is equivalent to one on 'abelian squares' (see
[231](https://www.erdosproblems.com/231)). In particular $A$ can be interpreted as an infinite
string over an alphabet with $d$ letters (each letter describining which of the $d$ possible
steps is taken at each point). An abelian square in a string $s$ is a pair of consecutive blocks
$x$ and $y$ appearing in $s$ such that $y$ is a permutation of $x$. The connection comes from the
observation that $p,q,r\in A\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ form a three-term arithmetic progression if and
only if the string corresponding to the steps from $p$ to $q$ is a permutation of the string
corresponding to the steps from $q$ to $r$.

This problem is therefore equivalent to asking for which $d$ there exists an infinite string over
$\{1,\ldots,d\}$ with no abelian squares. An infinite string without abelian squares was
constructed when $d=4$ by Keränen [Ke92]. We refer to a recent survey by Fici and Puzynina
[FiPu23] for more background and related results.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_192 : {d : ℕ | ∀ a : ℕ → Fin d → ℝ, IsPositiveUnitWalk a →
    ∃ x ∈ Set.range a, ∃ y ∈ Set.range a, ∃ z ∈ Set.range a, x ≠ y ∧ ∀ j, x j + z j = 2 * y j} =
      erdos_192.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 193
problems.doc:
References:
- [erdosproblems.com/193](https://www.erdosproblems.com/193)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [GeRa79] Gerver, Joseph L. and Ramsey, L. Thomas, "On certain sequences of lattice points."
  Pacific J. Math. (1979), 357-363.
- [CaKa26] Cambie, Stijn and Kalviainen, Erik, "An infinite small-step Z³-walk with no
  collinear triple." [arXiv:2609.01766](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01766).

statements.name: Erdos193.erdos_193
statements.doc:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^3$ be a finite set and let $A = \lbrace a_1, a_2, \ldots \rbrace$ be
an infinite $S$-walk, so that $a_{i+1} - a_i \in S$ for all $i$. Must $A$ contain three collinear
points?

Cambie and Kalviainen [CaKa26] answered this question in the negative by constructing an infinite
walk in $\mathbb{Z}^3$ with a finite set of steps and no three collinear points.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_193 :
    ¬ ∀ S : Set (Fin 3 → ℤ), S.Finite →
      /- The statement's $A = \lbrace a_1, a_2, \ldots \rbrace$ is an infinite set.

      If the sequence only takes finitely many values, one value has to repeat infinitely many
      times, which would yield a trivial collinear triple (x, x, x). In this case, the conjecture
      would hold for degenerate S-walks. Another case is constant S-walks, which would render the
      conjecture trivially false (finite loop ranges have no 3 distinct points).

      Assuming the authors intend to stay away from these degenerate cases, we formalize this by
      requiring an infinite range (and require distinct points). -/
      ∀ a : ℕ → Fin 3 → ℤ, IsSWalk S a → (range a).Infinite →
      HasCollinearTriple ℚ (range (fun n ↦ (↑) ∘ a n : ℕ → Fin 3 → ℚ))

statements.name: Erdos193.erdos_193_z2
statements.doc: [GeRa79] showed that the answer is yes for $\mathbb{Z}^2$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_193_z2 :
    ∀ S : Set (Fin 2 → ℤ), S.Finite →
      ∀ a : ℕ → Fin 2 → ℤ, IsSWalk S a → (range a).Infinite →
      HasCollinearTriple ℚ (range (fun n ↦ (↑) ∘ a n : ℕ → Fin 2 → ℚ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 194
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/194](https://www.erdosproblems.com/194)
- [ABJ11] Ardal, H. and Brown, T. and Jungić, V., Chaotic orderings of the rationals and reals. Amer. Math. Monthly (2011), 921-925.

statements.name: Erdos194.erdos_194
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 3$. Must any ordering of $\mathbb{R}$ contain a monotone $k$-term arithmetic progression,
that is, some $x_1 <\cdots < x_k$ which forms an increasing or decreasing $k$-term arithmetic
progression?

The answer is no, even for $k=3$, as shown by Ardal, Brown, and Jungić [ABJ11].
-
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_194 :
  ¬ ∀ k ≥ 3, ∀ r : ℝ → ℝ → Prop, IsStrictTotalOrder ℝ r →
    ∃ s : List ℝ, s.IsAPOfLength k ∧ (s.Pairwise r ∨ s.Pairwise (flip r))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 195
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/195](https://www.erdosproblems.com/195)
- [Ad22] Adenwalla, S., Avoiding Monotone Arithmetic Progressions in Permutations of Integers.
  arXiv:2211.04451 (2022).
- [Ge19] Geneson, Jesse, Forbidden arithmetic progressions in permutations of subsets of the
  integers. Discrete Math. (2019), 1489-1491.

statements.name: Erdos195.erdos_195
statements.doc:
What is the largest $k$ such that in any permutation of $\mathbb{Z}$ there must exist a
monotone $k$-term arithmetic progression $x_1 < \cdots < x_k$?

Here a permutation of $\mathbb{Z}$ is a one-sided arrangement $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ of the
integers, i.e. a bijection $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, and a monotone $k$-term arithmetic
progression is a subsequence $a_{i_1}, \ldots, a_{i_k}$ with $i_1 < \cdots < i_k$ forming an
increasing or decreasing arithmetic progression.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_195 :
    erdos_195.answer = sSup {k : ℕ | ∀ f : ℕ ≃ ℤ, HasMonotoneAP f k}

statements.name: Erdos195.erdos_195.variants.leq_5_bound
statements.doc: Geneson [Ge19] proved that k ≤ 5.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_195.variants.leq_5_bound :
    5 ≥ sSup {k : ℕ | ∀ f : ℕ ≃ ℤ, HasMonotoneAP f k}

statements.name: Erdos195.erdos_195.variants.leq_4_bound
statements.doc: Adenwalla [Ad22] proved that k ≤ 4.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_195.variants.leq_4_bound :
    4 ≥ sSup {k : ℕ | ∀ f : ℕ ≃ ℤ, HasMonotoneAP f k}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 196
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/196](https://www.erdosproblems.com/196)
- [DEGS77] Davis, J. A. and Entringer, R. C. and Graham, R. L. and Simmons, G. J.,
  *On permutations containing no long arithmetic progressions*. Acta Arith. (1977), 81-90.
- [Ho26] Ho, Boon Suan, *A 4AP-free permutation of the positive integers*.
  [arXiv:2609.12780](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.12780)

statements.name: Erdos196.erdos_196
statements.doc:
Must every permutation of $\mathbb{N}$ contain a monotone 4-term arithmetic progression?

Here a monotone $k$-term arithmetic progression in a permutation $f$ is a set of indices
$i_1 < \cdots < i_k$ such that $f(i_1), \ldots, f(i_k)$ is an increasing or decreasing arithmetic
progression. [DEGS77] showed that every permutation of $\mathbb{N}$ contains a monotone 3-term
arithmetic progression, and that there are permutations with no monotone 5-term arithmetic
progression.

The answer is no: [Ho26] constructs an explicit permutation of the positive integers with no
monotone 4-term arithmetic progression. Independent constructions with Lean formalizations were
given shortly afterwards by Kruer and Kohlmeyer and, pseudonymously, in the repository
`coleski/erdos196`; the linked formal proof establishes the negation of this statement.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_196 : ¬ ∀ (f : ℕ ≃ ℕ), HasMonotoneAP f 4

problems.title: Erdős Problem 197
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/197](https://www.erdosproblems.com/197)

statements.name: Erdos197.erdos_197
statements.doc:
Can $\mathbb{N}$ be partitioned into two sets, each of which can be permuted to avoid monotone
3-term arithmetic progressions?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_197 :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, IsCompl A B ∧
      (∃ f : ℕ ≃ A, ¬HasMonotoneAP (Subtype.val ∘ f) 3) ∧
      (∃ g : ℕ ≃ B, ¬HasMonotoneAP (Subtype.val ∘ g) 3)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 198
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/198](https://www.erdosproblems.com/198)
- [Ba75] Baumgartner, James E., Partitioning vector spaces. J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. A (1975),
  231-233.

statements.name: Erdos198.baumgartner_strong
statements.doc:
Let $V$ be a vector space over the rationals and let $k$ be a fixed
positive integer. Then there is a set $X_k \subseteq V$ such that $X_k$ meets
every infinite arithmetic progression in $V$ but $X_k$ intersects every
$k$-element arithmetic progression in at most two points.

At the end of [Ba75] the author claims that by "slightly modifying the method of [his proof]", one
can prove this.
statements.statement:
lemma baumgartner_strong (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℚ V] (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ X : Set V,
      (∀ Y, Y.IsAPOfLength ⊤ → (X ∩ Y).Nonempty) ∧
      (∀ Y, IsAPOfLength Y k → (X ∩ Y).ncard ≤ 2)

statements.name: Erdos198.baumgartner_headline
statements.doc: The statement for which Baumgartner actually writes a proof.
statements.statement:
lemma baumgartner_headline (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℚ V] :
    ∃ X : Set V,
      (∀ Y, IsAPOfLength Y ⊤ → (X ∩ Y).Nonempty) ∧
      (∀ Y, IsAPOfLength Y 3 → (X ∩ Y).ncard ≤ 2)

statements.name: Erdos198.erdos_198
statements.doc:
The answer is no; Erdős and Graham report this was proved by Baumgartner, presumably referring to
the paper [Ba75], which does not state this exactly, but the following simple construction is
implicit in [Ba75].

Let $P_1,P_2,\ldots$ be an enumeration of all countably many infinite arithmetic progressions. We
choose $a_1$ to be the minimal element of $P_1\cap \mathbb{N}$, and in general choose $a_n$ to be an
element of $P_n\cap \mathbb{N}$ such that $a_n>2a_{n-1}$. By construction $A=\{a_1 < a_2 < \cdots\}$
contains at least one element from every infinite arithmetic progression, and is a lacunary set, so
is certainly Sidon.

AlphaProof has found the following explicit construction: $A = \{ (n+1)!+n : n\geq 0\}$. This is a
Sidon set, and intersects every arithmetic progression, since for any $a,d\in \mathbb{N}$,
$(a+d+1)!+(a+d)\in A$, and $d$ divides $(a+d+1)!+d$.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_198 : ¬ (∀ A : Set ℕ, IsSidon A → (∃ Y, IsAPOfLength Y ⊤ ∧ Y ⊆ Aᶜ))

statements.name: Erdos198.erdos_198.variants.concrete
statements.doc:
In fact one such sequence is $n! + n$.

This was found and proved by AlphaProof.

It also found $(n + 1)! + n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_198.variants.concrete :  ∃ (A : Set ℕ), A = {n ! + n | n} ∧
    IsSidon A ∧ (∀ Y, IsAPOfLength Y ⊤ → (A ∩ Y).Nonempty)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 199
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/199](https://www.erdosproblems.com/199)
- [Ba75] Baumgartner, James E., *Partitioning vector spaces*. J. Combinatorial Theory
  Ser. A (1975), 231-233.

statements.name: Erdos199.erdos_199
statements.doc:
If $A\subset \mathbb{R}$ does not contain a 3-term arithmetic progression then must $\mathbb{R}\backslash A$ contain an infinite arithmetic progression?

Baumgartner [Ba75] answered this in the negative.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_199 :
    ¬ ∀ A : Set ℝ, ThreeAPFree A →
      ∃ S : Set ℝ, S.IsAPOfLength ⊤ ∧ S ⊆ Aᶜ

problems.title: Erdős Problem 200
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/200](https://www.erdosproblems.com/200)

statements.name: Erdos200.erdos_200
statements.doc: Does the longest arithmetic progression of primes in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ have length $o(\log N)$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_200 :
    (fun n => (longestPrimeArithmeticProgressions n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n => log n)

statements.name: Erdos200.erdos_200.variants.upper
statements.doc: It follows from the prime number theorem that such a progression has length $\leq(1+o(1))\log N$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_200.variants.upper : ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)),
    ∀ n, longestPrimeArithmeticProgressions n ≤ (1 + o n) * log n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 202
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/202](https://www.erdosproblems.com/202)
- [BFV13] de la Bretèche, Régis and Ford, Kevin and Vandehey, Joseph, *On non-intersecting
  arithmetic progressions*. Acta Arith. (2013), 381-392.
- [Ch05] Chen, Yong-Gao, *On disjoint arithmetic progressions*. Acta Arith. (2005), 143-148.
- [Cr03b] Croot, III, Ernest S., *On non-intersecting arithmetic progressions*. Acta Arith.
  (2003), 233-238.
- [ErSz68] Erdős, P. and Szemerédi, E., *On a problem of P. Erdős and S. Stein*. Acta Arith.
  (1968), 85-90.
- [PaPh24] Park, Jinyoung and Pham, Huy Tuan, *A proof of the Kahn-Kalai conjecture*. J. Amer.
  Math. Soc. (2024), 235-243.

statements.name: Erdos202.erdos_202
statements.doc:
Let $n_1<\cdots < n_r\leq N$ with associated $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ such that the congruence classes are
disjoint (that is, every integer is $\equiv a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for at most one $1\leq i\leq r$). How
large can $r$ be in terms of $N$?

Let $f(N)$ be the maximum possible $r$, and let $L(N)=\exp(\sqrt{\log N\log\log N})$.

This was proved by GPT-5.4 Pro (prompted by Ho Boon Suan), using the argument of [BFV13] together
with the resolution of the Kahn-Kalai conjecture by Park and Pham [PaPh24], so that
$$f(N)= N L(N)^{-1+o(1)}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_202 : ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (f N : ℝ) = (N : ℝ) * scaleL N ^ (-1 + o N)

statements.name: Erdos202.erdos_202.variants.erdos_szemeredi
statements.doc: Erdős and Stein conjectured that $f(N)=o(N)$, which was proved by Erdős and Szemerédi [ErSz68].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_202.variants.erdos_szemeredi :
    (fun N => (f N : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 203
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/203](https://www.erdosproblems.com/203)

statements.name: Erdos203.erdos_203
statements.doc:
Is there an integer $m$ with $(m, 6) = 1$ such that none of $2^k \cdot 3^\ell \cdot m + 1$ are prime,
for any $k, \ell \ge 0$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_203 : ∃ m, m.Coprime 6 ∧ ∀ k l, ¬ (2^k * 3^l * m + 1).Prime

problems.title: Erdős Problem 204
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/204](https://www.erdosproblems.com/204)
- [Ad25] S. Adenwalla, A Question of Erdős and Graham on Covering Systems. arXiv:2501.15170 (2025).

statements.name: Erdos204.erdos_204
statements.doc:
Are there $n$ such that there is a covering system with moduli the divisors of $n$ which is 'as
disjoint as possible'?

That is, for all $d\mid n$ with $d>1$ there is an associated $a_d$ such that every integer is
congruent to some $a_d\pmod{d}$, and if there is some integer $x$ with
$$x\equiv a_d\pmod{d}\textrm{ and }x\equiv a_{d'}\pmod{d'}$$then $(d,d')=1$.

The density of such $n$ is zero. Erdős and Graham believed that no such $n$ exist.

Adenwalla [Ad25] has proved there are no such $n$.

This was formalized by van Doorn in Lean using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_204 : ¬ ∃ (n : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℤ),
    let D := {d : ℕ | d ∣ n ∧ d > 1}
    (∀ x : ℤ, ∃ d ∈ D, x ≡ a d [ZMOD d]) ∧
    (∀ d ∈ D, ∀ d' ∈ D, d ≠ d' → (∃ x : ℤ, x ≡ a d [ZMOD d] ∧ x ≡ a d' [ZMOD d']) →
      Nat.gcd d d' = 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 205
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/205](https://www.erdosproblems.com/205)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [Ro34] Romanoff, N. P., *Über einige Sätze der additiven Zahlentheorie*. Math. Ann. (1934),
  668-678.

statements.name: Erdos205.erdos_205.parts.i
statements.doc:
Is it true that all sufficiently large $n$ can be written as $2^k+m$ for some $k\geq 0$, where
$\Omega(m)<\log\log m$? (Here $\Omega(m)$ is the number of prime divisors of $m$ counted with
multiplicity.)

Barreto and Leeham, using ChatGPT and Aristotle, have proved a negative answer, which was
quantified by Tao and Alexeev (see the comments): in fact there are infinitely many $n$ such that,
for all $k$ with $2^k<n$, $n-2^k$ has at least
$$\gg \left(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right)^{1/2}$$
many prime factors.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_205.parts.i :
    ¬ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, IsRepresentable (fun m => Real.log (Real.log m)) n

statements.name: Erdos205.erdos_205.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is it true that all sufficiently large $n$ can be written as $2^k+m$ for some $k\geq 0$, where
$\Omega(m)<\log\log m$? (Here $\Omega(m)$ is the number of prime divisors of $m$ counted with
multiplicity.) What about $<\epsilon \log\log m$?

Barreto and Leeham, using ChatGPT and Aristotle, have proved a negative answer, which was
quantified by Tao and Alexeev (see the comments).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_205.parts.ii :
    ¬ ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      IsRepresentable (fun m => ε * Real.log (Real.log m)) n

statements.name: Erdos205.erdos_205.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Is it true that all sufficiently large $n$ can be written as $2^k+m$ for some $k\geq 0$, where
$\Omega(m)<\log\log m$? (Here $\Omega(m)$ is the number of prime divisors of $m$ counted with
multiplicity.) Or some more slowly growing function?

Barreto and Leeham, using ChatGPT and Aristotle, have proved a negative answer, which was
quantified by Tao and Alexeev (see the comments).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_205.parts.iii :
    ¬ ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, f =o[atTop] (fun m : ℕ => Real.log (Real.log m)) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, IsRepresentable f n

statements.name: Erdos205.erdos_205.variants.many_prime_factors
statements.doc:
In fact there are infinitely many $n$ such that, for all $k$ with $2^k<n$, $n-2^k$ has at least
$$\gg \left(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right)^{1/2}$$
many prime factors.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_205.variants.many_prime_factors : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ),
    {n : ℕ | ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ^ k < n →
      c * Real.sqrt (Real.log n / Real.log (Real.log n)) ≤ (Ω (n - 2 ^ k) : ℝ)}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos205.erdos_205.variants.odd_counterexamples
statements.doc:
The $n$ constructed in this way are divisible by a large power of $2$. It remains open whether
there exist arbitrarily large odd counterexamples.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_205.variants.odd_counterexamples :
    {n : ℕ | Odd n ∧ ¬ IsRepresentable (fun m => Real.log (Real.log m)) n}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 206
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/206](https://www.erdosproblems.com/206)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial
  number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980).
- [Cu22] Curtiss, D. R., *On Kellogg's Diophantine Problem*. Amer. Math. Monthly (1922),
  380-387.
- [Er50b] Erdős, Pál, *On a Diophantine equation*. Mat. Lapok (1950), 192-210.
- [Na23] Nathanson, M., *Underapproximation by Egyptian fractions*. J. Number Theory (2023),
  208-234.
- [Ch23b] Chu, H. V., *A threshold for the best two-term underapproximation by Egyptian
  fractions*. arXiv:2306.12564 (2023).
- [Ko24b] Kovač, V., *On eventually greedy best underapproximations by Egyptian fractions*.
  arXiv:2406.07218 (2024).

statements.name: Erdos206.erdos_206
statements.doc:
Let $x>0$ be a real number. For any $n\geq 1$ let
$$R_n(x) = \sum_{i=1}^n\frac{1}{m_i}<x$$
be the maximal sum of $n$ distinct unit fractions which is $<x$.

Is it true that, for almost all $x$, for sufficiently large $n$, we have
$$R_{n+1}(x)=R_n(x)+\frac{1}{m},$$
where $m$ is minimal such that $m$ does not appear in $R_n(x)$ and the right-hand side is
$<x$? (That is, are the best underapproximations eventually always constructed in a 'greedy'
fashion?)

Kovač [Ko24b] has proved that this is false - in fact as false as possible: the set of
$x\in (0,\infty)$ for which the best underapproximations are eventually 'greedy' has Lebesgue
measure zero.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_206 :
    ¬ ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume.restrict (Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ))), EventuallyGreedy x

problems.title: Erdős Problem 207
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/207](https://www.erdosproblems.com/207)
- [KSSS22b] Kwan, M. and Sah, A. and Sawhney, M. and Simkin, M., High-girth Steiner triple systems.
  arXiv:2201.04554 (2022).

statements.name: Erdos207.erdos_207
statements.doc:
For any $g\geq 2$, if $n$ is sufficiently large and $\equiv 1,3\pmod{6}$ then there exists a
3-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices such that

- every pair of vertices is contained in exactly one edge (i.e. the graph is a Steiner triple
system) and

- for any $2\leq j\leq g$ any collection of $j$ edges contains at least $j+3$ vertices.

Proved by Kwan, Sah, Sawhney, and Simkin [KSSS22b].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_207 :
    ∀ g : ℕ, 2 ≤ g → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    n % 6 = 1 ∨ n % 6 = 3 → ∃ H : Finset (Finset (Fin n)),
      H.IsBlockDesign 2 3 ∧ ∀ E ⊆ H,
        2 ≤ E.card → E.card ≤ g → E.card + 3 ≤ (E.biUnion id).card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 208
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/208](https://www.erdosproblems.com/208)

statements.name: Erdos208.erdos_208.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $s_1 < s_2 < \dots$ be the sequence of squarefree numbers. Is it true that
for any $\epsilon > 0$ and large $n$, $s_{n+1} - s_n \ll_\epsilon s_n^\epsilon$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_208.parts.i :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), (fun n => (s (n + 1) - s n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n => (s n : ℝ)^ε)

statements.name: Erdos208.erdos_208.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $s_1 < s_2 < \dots$ be the sequence of squarefree numbers. Is it true that
$s_{n + 1} - s_n \le (1 + o(1)) \cdot (\pi^2 / 6) \cdot \log (s_n) / \log (\log (s_n))$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_208.parts.ii : ∃ (c : ℕ → ℝ), (c =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      s (n + 1) - s n ≤ (1 + (c n)) * (π^2 / 6) * log (s n) / log (log (s n))

statements.name: Erdos208.erdos_208.variants.log_bound
statements.doc:
In [Er79] Erdős says perhaps $s_{n+1} - s_n \ll \log s_n$, but he is 'very doubtful'.

[Er79] Erdős, Paul, __Some unconventional problems in number theory__. Math. Mag. (1979), 67-70.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_208.variants.log_bound :
    (fun n ↦ (s (n + 1) - s n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ log (s n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 209
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/209](https://www.erdosproblems.com/209)
- [Er84] Erdős, P., *Research problems*. Period. Math. Hungar. (1984), 101-103.
- [ErPu95b] Erdős, Paul and Purdy, George, *Extremal problems in combinatorial geometry*.
  Handbook of combinatorics, Vol. 1, 2 (1995), 809-874.
- [FuPa84] Füredi, Z. and Palásti, I., *Arrangements of lines with a large number of triangles*.
  Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1984), 561-566.
- [Es16] Escudero, Juan García, *Gallai triangles in configurations of lines in the projective
  plane*. C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris (2016), 551-554.

statements.name: Erdos209.erdos_209
statements.doc:
Let $A$ be a finite collection of $d\geq 4$ non-parallel lines in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that
there are no points where at least four lines from $A$ meet. Must there exist a 'Gallai
triangle' (or 'ordinary triangle'): three lines from $A$ which intersect in three points, and
each of these intersection points only intersects two lines from $A$?

Füredi and Palásti [FuPa84] showed this is false when $d\geq 4$ is not divisible by $9$.
Escudero [Es16] showed this is false for all $d\geq 4$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_209 :
    ¬ ∀ d : ℕ, 4 ≤ d → ∀ A : Finset (AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²), A.card = d →
      (∀ L ∈ A, IsLine L) →
      ((A : Set (AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²)).Pairwise fun L₁ L₂ => ¬ L₁ ∥ L₂) →
      (∀ p : ℝ², pointMultiplicity A p ≤ 3) →
      HasGallaiTriangle A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 210
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/210](https://www.erdosproblems.com/210)
- [Mo51] Motzkin, T. S., *The lines and planes connecting the points of a finite set*.
  Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 70 (1951), 451–464.
- [KeMo58] Kelly, L. M. and Moser, W. O. J., *On the number of ordinary lines determined by
  n points*. Canadian Journal of Mathematics 10 (1958), 210–219.
- [CsSa93] Csima, J. and Sawyer, E. T., *There exist 6n/13 ordinary points*.
  Discrete & Computational Geometry 9 (1993), 187–202.
- [GrTa13] Green, B. and Tao, T., *On sets defining few ordinary lines*.
  Discrete & Computational Geometry 50 (2013), 409–468.

statements.name: Erdos210.erdos_210.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be the sharp guarantee such that, for any $n$ points in $\mathbb R^2$,
not all on a line, there are at least $f(n)$ lines which contain exactly two points
(called ordinary lines). Does $f(n)\to\infty$?
That $f(n)\to\infty$ was proved by Motzkin [Mo51].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_210.parts.i : Tendsto f atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos210.erdos_210.lower_bound
statements.doc:
Kelly and Moser [KeMo58] proved that $f(n)\geq 3n/7$ for all $n$.
Only $n\geq3$ have noncollinear configurations.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_210.lower_bound : ∀ n : ℕ, 3 ≤ n → 3 * n ≤ 7 * f n

statements.name: Erdos210.erdos_210.variants.csima_sawyer
statements.doc: Csima and Sawyer [CsSa93] proved $f(n)\geq6n/13$ when $n\geq8$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_210.variants.csima_sawyer : ∀ n : ℕ, 8 ≤ n → 6 * n ≤ 13 * f n

statements.name: Erdos210.erdos_210.variants.green_tao
statements.doc: Green and Tao [GrTa13] proved $f(n)\geq n/2$ for sufficiently large $n$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_210.variants.green_tao : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, n ≤ 2 * f n

statements.name: Erdos210.erdos_210.variants.green_tao_odd
statements.doc:
Green and Tao [GrTa13] proved $f(n)\geq3\lfloor n/4\rfloor$ for sufficiently
large odd $n$ [GrTa13, Theorem 2.2].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_210.variants.green_tao_odd :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, Odd n → 3 * (n / 4) ≤ f n

statements.name: Erdos210.erdos_210.variants.even_upper_bound
statements.doc:
Green and Tao [GrTa13, Proposition 2.1] give configurations attaining $n/2$
ordinary lines for sufficiently large even $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_210.variants.even_upper_bound :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, Even n → 2 * f n ≤ n

statements.name: Erdos210.erdos_210.variants.seven
statements.doc:
Kelly and Moser [KeMo58] give a seven-point configuration with three ordinary
lines, attaining their lower bound at $n=7$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_210.variants.seven : f 7 = 3

statements.name: Erdos210.erdos_210.variants.sylvester_gallai
statements.doc: The Sylvester–Gallai theorem states that $f(n)\geq1$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_210.variants.sylvester_gallai {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) : 1 ≤ f n

statements.name: Erdos210.erdos_210.upper_bound
statements.doc: An explicit near-pencil gives the linear upper bound $f(n)\leq n$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_210.upper_bound {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) : f n ≤ n

statements.name: Erdos210.erdos_210.parts.ii
statements.doc:
How fast does $f(n)$ tend to infinity? Kelly–Moser [KeMo58] and the near-pencil
construction show that its growth is linear.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_210.parts.ii :
    (fun n : ℕ => (f n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 211
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/211](https://www.erdosproblems.com/211)
- [Be83] Beck, József, *On the lattice property of the plane and some problems of Dirac,
  Motzkin and Erdős in combinatorial geometry*. Combinatorica (1983), 281-297.
- [SzTr83] Szemerédi, Endre and Trotter, Jr., William T., *Extremal problems in discrete
  geometry*. Combinatorica (1983), 381-392.
- [Er84] Erdős, P., *Research problems*. Period. Math. Hungar. (1984), 101-103.
- [BGS74] Burr, Stefan A. and Grünbaum, Branko and Sloane, N. J. A., *The orchard problem*.
  Geometriae Dedicata (1974), 397-424.
- [FuPa84] Füredi, Z. and Palásti, I., *Arrangements of lines with a large number of triangles*.
  Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1984), 561-566.

statements.name: Erdos211.erdos_211.variants.one_sixth
statements.doc:
Erdős speculates that there are at least $(1+o(1))kn/6$ determined lines [Er84].
The asymptotic bound is uniform over $1 \leq k < n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_211.variants.one_sixth :
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ (n k : ℕ), N ≤ n → 1 ≤ k → k < n →
    ∀ s : Finset ℝ², s.card = n →
      (∀ L : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ², IsLine L → (s.filter fun p => p ∈ L).card ≤ n - k) →
      (1 - ε) / 6 * (k : ℝ) * (n : ℝ) ≤ ((determinedLines s).card : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos211.erdos_211.variants.sharpness
statements.doc:
There are arbitrarily large configurations with no four collinear points and
$\sim n^2/6$ three-point lines, constructed by Burr, Grünbaum, and Sloane [BGS74]
and Füredi and Palásti [FuPa84]. The index need not equal the number of points.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_211.variants.sharpness :
  ∃ s : ℕ → Finset ℝ²,
    Tendsto (fun i => (s i).card) atTop atTop ∧
    (∀ (i : ℕ) (L : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²), IsLine L →
      ((s i).filter fun p => p ∈ L).card ≤ 3) ∧
    Tendsto (fun i =>
      (((determinedLines (s i)).filter fun L => ((s i).filter fun p => p ∈ L).card = 3).card : ℝ) /
        ((s i).card : ℝ) ^ 2) atTop (nhds (1 / 6 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos211.erdos_211
statements.doc:
Let $1\leq k<n$. Given $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, at most $n-k$ on any line,
there are $\gg kn$ many lines which contain at least two points.
Solved by Beck [Be83] and Szemerédi and Trotter [SzTr83].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_211 : MainBound

statements.name: Erdos211.erdos_211.variants.quadratic
statements.doc:
Given any $2n$ points with at most $n$ on a line there are $\gg n^2$ many lines
formed by the points. Solved by Beck [Be83] and Szemerédi and Trotter [SzTr83].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_211.variants.quadratic : QuadraticBound

problems.title: Erdős Problem 212
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/212](https://www.erdosproblems.com/212)

statements.name: Erdos212.erdos_212
statements.doc:
Is there a dense subset of ℝ^2 such that all pairwise distances
are rational?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_212 :
    ∃ u : Set ℂ, Dense u ∧ u.Pairwise fun c₁ c₂ => dist c₁ c₂ ∈ Set.range Rat.cast

problems.title: Erdős Problem 213
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/213](https://www.erdosproblems.com/213)

statements.name: Erdos213.erdos_213
statements.doc:
Let $n \geq 4$. Are there $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, no three on a line and no four on a circle,
such that all pairwise distances are integers?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_213 : ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 4 → Erdos213For n

statements.name: Erdos213.erdos_213.variants.KK08
statements.doc: The best construction to date, due to Kreisel and Kurz, has $n = 7$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_213.variants.KK08 : Erdos213For 7

problems.title: Erdős Problem 214
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/214](https://www.erdosproblems.com/214)
- [CsTo94] Csizmadia, György and Tóth, Géza, *Note on a Ramsey-type problem in geometry*.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1994), 302-306.
- [EGMRSS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Montgomery, P. and Rothschild, B. L. and Spencer, J.
  and Straus, E. G., *Euclidean Ramsey theorems. II*. (1975), 529-557.
- [Ju79] Juhász, Rozália, *Ramsey type theorems in the plane*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1979),
  152-160.

statements.name: Erdos214.erdos_214
statements.doc:
Let $S\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be such that no two points in $S$ are distance $1$ apart. Must the
complement of $S$ contain four points which form a unit square?

The answer is yes, proved by Juhász [Ju79], who proved more generally that the complement of $S$
must contain a congruent copy of any set of four points.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_214 :
    ∀ S : Set ℝ², UnitDistanceAvoiding S →
      ∃ p : Fin 4 → ℝ², (∀ i, p i ∈ Sᶜ) ∧ (p ≅ unitSquare)

statements.name: Erdos214.erdos_214.variants.juhasz
statements.doc:
The answer is yes, proved by Juhász [Ju79], who proved more generally that the complement of $S$
must contain a congruent copy of any set of four points.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_214.variants.juhasz : HasRedCopies 4

statements.name: Erdos214.erdos_214.variants.egmrss
statements.doc:
Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer, and Straus [EGMRSS75] had earlier showed that
$3\leq k\leq 10^{12}$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_214.variants.egmrss : 3 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ 10 ^ 12

statements.name: Erdos214.erdos_214.variants.juhasz_twelve_points
statements.doc: Juhász [Ju79] also improved the upper bound to $k\leq 11$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_214.variants.juhasz_twelve_points : ¬ HasRedCopies 12

statements.name: Erdos214.erdos_214.variants.csizmadia_toth
statements.doc: The upper bound was improved further by Csizmadia and Tóth [CsTo94] to $k\leq 7$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_214.variants.csizmadia_toth : ¬ HasRedCopies 8

statements.name: Erdos214.erdos_214.variants.bounds
statements.doc:
The best known bounds currently are
$$4\leq k\leq 7.$$
statements.statement: theorem erdos_214.variants.bounds : 4 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ 7

problems.title: Erdős Problem 215
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/215](https://www.erdosproblems.com/215)
- [Er83c] Erdős, Paul, *Combinatorial problems in geometry*. Math. Chronicle (1983), 35-54.
- [JaMa02] Jackson, Steve and Mauldin, R. Daniel, *Sets meeting isometric copies of the lattice
  $\mathbb{Z}^2$ in exactly one point*. Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA (2002), 15883-15887.

statements.name: Erdos215.erdos_215
statements.doc:
Does there exist $S\subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ such that every set congruent to $S$ (that is, $S$
after some translation and rotation) contains exactly one point from $\mathbb{Z}^2$?

An old question of Steinhaus. Erdős was 'almost certain that such a set does not exist'.

In fact, such a set does exist, as proved by Jackson and Mauldin [JaMa02]. Their construction
depends on the axiom of choice.

The plane is identified with $\mathbb{C}$: the sets congruent to $S$ are the sets $uS + t$ with
$\lvert u\rvert = 1$ and $t \in \mathbb{C}$, and $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is the set of Gaussian integers.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_215 : ∃ S : Set ℂ, ∀ u t : ℂ, ‖u‖ = 1 →
    ∃! z : ℂ, z ∈ (fun w => u * w + t) '' S ∧ ∃ a b : ℤ, z = a + b * Complex.I

problems.title: Erdős Problem 217
problems.doc: *Reference:* [Erdős Problem 217](https://www.erdosproblems.com/217)

statements.name: Erdos217.erdos_217
statements.doc:
For which $n$ do there exist $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, no three on a line and no four on
a circle, that determine $n-1$ distinct distances whose multiplicities are
$1,2,\ldots,n-1$? The condition $n>0$ excludes the empty configuration, since the
requested number $n-1$ of distances is nonnegative.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_217 : erdos_217.answer = {n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ ∃ P : Finset ℝ²,
    P.card = n ∧ InGeneralPosition (P : Set ℝ²) ∧
      (distanceSet P).card = n - 1 ∧
      (distanceSet P).image (distanceMultiplicity P) = Finset.Icc 1 (n - 1)}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 218
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/218](https://www.erdosproblems.com/218)

statements.name: Erdos218.erdos_218.variants.le
statements.doc:
The set of indices $n$ for which a prime gap is followed by a larger or equal prime gap has a
natural density of $\frac 1 2$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_218.variants.le : {n | primeGap n ≤ primeGap (n + 1)}.HasDensity <| 1 / 2

statements.name: Erdos218.erdos_218.variants.ge
statements.doc:
The set of indices $n$ for which a prime gap is preceded by a larger or equal prime gap has a
natural density of $\frac 1 2$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_218.variants.ge : {n | primeGap (n + 1) ≤ primeGap n}.HasDensity <| 1 / 2

statements.name: Erdos218.erdos_218.variants.infinite_equal_prime_gap
statements.doc:
There are infinitely many indices $n$ such that the prime gap at $n$ is equal to the prime gap
at $n+1$. This is equivalent to the existence of infinitely many arithmetic progressions of
length $3$, see `erdos_141.variants.infinite_three`.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_218.variants.infinite_equal_prime_gap : {n | primeGap n = primeGap (n + 1)}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 219
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/219](https://www.erdosproblems.com/219)

statements.name: Erdos219.erdos_219
statements.doc:
Are there arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions of primes?
Solution: yes.
Ref: Green, Ben and Tao, Terence, _The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions_
statements.statement: theorem erdos_219 : ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ l ∈ primeArithmeticProgressions, N ≤ ENat.card l

problems.title: Erdős Problem 220
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/220](https://www.erdosproblems.com/220)
- [Er40] Erdős, P., *The difference of consecutive primes*. Duke Math. J. (1940), 438--441.
- [Er73] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of
  combinatorial theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971)
  (1973), 117-138.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [MoVa86] Montgomery, H. L. and Vaughan, R. C., *On the distribution of reduced residues*. Ann. of
  Math. (2) (1986), 311-333.
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.

statements.name: Erdos220.erdos_220
statements.doc:
Let $n \geq 1$ and
$$A = \{a_1 < \cdots < a_{\phi(n)}\} = \{1 \leq m < n : (m, n) = 1\}.$$
Is it true that
$$\sum_{1 \leq k < \phi(n)} (a_{k+1} - a_k)^2 \ll \frac{n^2}{\phi(n)}?$$

A problem of Erdős [Er40, Er73, ErGr80], which is discussed in problem B40 of Guy's collection
[Gu04]. The answer is yes, as proved by Montgomery and Vaughan [MoVa86], who in fact proved that
$\sum_{1 \leq k < \phi(n)} (a_{k+1} - a_k)^\gamma \ll n^\gamma / \phi(n)^{\gamma - 1}$ for every
$\gamma \geq 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_220 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
      (sumSquaredGaps (sortedTotatives n) : ℝ) ≤ C * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / (n.totient : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 221
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/221](https://www.erdosproblems.com/221)
- [Lo54] Lorentz, G. G., *On a problem of additive number theory*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1954), 838-841.
- [Ru72] Ruzsa, Jr., I., *On a problem of P. Erdős*. Canad. Math. Bull. (1972), 309-310.

statements.name: Erdos221.erdos_221
statements.doc:
Is there a set $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ such that, for all large $N$,
$$\lvert A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \ll N/\log N$$
and such that every large integer can be written as $2^k+a$ for some
$k\geq 0$ and $a\in A$?

Lorentz [Lo54] proved there is such a set with, for all large $N$,
$$\lvert A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \ll \frac{\log\log N}{\log N}N$$
The answer is yes, proved by Ruzsa [Ru72].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_221 :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ,
      ((fun N => ({a ∈ A | a ≤ N}.ncard : ℝ)) ≪ (fun N => (N : ℝ) / Real.log N)) ∧
      ∀ᶠ N in atTop, ∃ k a, 0 ≤ k ∧ a ∈ A ∧ N = 2 ^ k + a

problems.title: Erdős Problem 224
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/224](https://www.erdosproblems.com/224)
- [DaGr62] Danzer, L. and Gr\"{u}nbaum, B., *\"{U}ber zwei Probleme
  bez\"{u}glich konvexer K\"{o}rper von P. Erd\H{o}s und von V. L. Klee*.
  Math. Z. (1962), 95-99.

statements.name: Erdos224.erdos_224
statements.doc:
If $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is any set of $2^d+1$ points then some three points in $A$ determine an obtuse angle.

The general case was proved by Danzer and Gr\"{u}nbaum [DaGr62].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_224 {d : ℕ} (A : Finset (ℝ^d)) (hcard : A.card = 2 ^ d + 1) :
    ∃ x y z : ℝ^d, x ∈ A ∧ y ∈ A ∧ z ∈ A ∧
      x ≠ y ∧ x ≠ z ∧ y ≠ z ∧ ObtuseAt x y z

problems.title: Erdős Problem 225
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/225](https://www.erdosproblems.com/225)
- [Er40b] Erdős, P., *Note on some elementary properties of polynomials*. Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (1940), 954-958.
- [Er57] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Michigan Math. J. (1957), 291-300.
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., *Research problems in function theory: new problems*. (1974), 155-180.
- [Kr74] Kristiansen, G. K., *Proof of an inequality for trigonometric polynomials*. Proc. Amer.
  Math. Soc. (1974), 49-57.
- [SaSh74] Saff, E. B. and Sheil-Small, T., *Coefficient and integral mean estimates for
  algebraic and trigonometric polynomials with restricted zeros*. J. London Math. Soc. (2)
  (1974/75), 16-22.
- [Kr76] Kristiansen, G. K., *Erratum to "Proof of a polynomial conjecture"*. Proc. Amer. Math.
  Soc. (1976), 377.

statements.name: Erdos225.erdos_225
statements.doc:
Let
$$ f(\theta) = \sum_{0\leq k\leq n}c_k e^{ik\theta}$$
be a trigonometric polynomial all of whose roots are real, such that
$\max_{\theta\in [0,2\pi]}\lvert f(\theta)\rvert=1$. Then
$$\int_0^{2\pi}\lvert f(\theta)\rvert \mathrm{d}\theta \leq 4.$$

This is Problem 4.20 in [Ha74], where it is attributed to Erdős.

This was solved independently by Kristiansen [Kr74] (only in the case when $c_k\in\mathbb{R}$)
and Saff and Sheil-Small [SaSh74] (for general $c_k\in \mathbb{C}$). (The original proof of
Kristiansen contained an error which was later fixed in [Kr76].)

"All roots real" refers to the zeros of $f$ as an entire function of $\theta\in\mathbb{C}$. We
normalise by $c_0c_n\neq 0$ and $n\geq 1$: a factor $e^{im\theta}$ affects neither the zeros nor
$\lvert f\rvert$ on the real line, while a single term $c_me^{im\theta}$ has no zeros and
$\int_0^{2\pi}\lvert f\rvert = 2\pi$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_225 :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℂ), 0 < n → c 0 ≠ 0 → c n ≠ 0 →
    (∀ z : ℂ, trigPoly n c z = 0 → z.im = 0) →
    (∀ θ ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) (2 * Real.pi), ‖trigPoly n c θ‖ ≤ 1) →
    (∃ θ ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) (2 * Real.pi), ‖trigPoly n c θ‖ = 1) →
    ∫ θ in (0 : ℝ)..(2 * Real.pi), ‖trigPoly n c θ‖ ≤ 4

problems.title: Erdős Problem 226
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/226](https://www.erdosproblems.com/226)
- [BaSc70] Barth, K. F. and Schneider, W. J., *Entire functions mapping
  countable dense subsets of the reals onto each other monotonically*.
  J. London Math. Soc. (2) (1970), 620--626.
- [BaSc71] Barth, K. F. and Schneider, W. J., *Entire functions mapping
  arbitrary countable dense sets and their complements onto each other*.
  J. London Math. Soc. (2) (1971/72), 482--488.
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., *Research problems in function theory: new problems*.
  (1974), 155--180.

statements.name: Erdos226.erdos_226
statements.doc:
Is there an entire non-linear function $f$ such that, for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$, $x$ is rational if and only if $f(x)$ is?

Barth and Schneider [BaSc70] proved the stronger result for countable dense subsets of
$\mathbb{R}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_226 :
    ∃ F : ℂ → ℂ, Differentiable ℂ F ∧ (∀ x : ℝ, (F x).im = 0) ∧
      (∀ g : AffineMap ℝ ℝ ℝ, (fun x : ℝ => (F x).re) ≠ g) ∧
      PreservesRationality (fun x : ℝ => (F x).re)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 228
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/228](https://www.erdosproblems.com/228)

statements.name: Erdos228.erdos_228
statements.doc:
Does there exist, for all large $n$, a polynomial $P$ of degree $n$, with coefficients $\pm1$, such
that $$\sqrt n \ll |P(z)| \ll \sqrt n$$ for all $|z|=1$, with the implied constants independent of
$z$ and $n$?

The answer is yes, proved by Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, and Tiba [BBMST19].

[BBMST19] Balister, P. and Bollob\'{A}s, B. and Morris, R. and Sahasrabudhe, J. and Tiba, M., _Flat Littlewood Polynomials Exist_. arXiv:1907.09464 (2019).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_228 :
    ∃ (c₁ : ℝ) (c₂ : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ p : Polynomial ℂ, p.degree = n ∧
    (∀ i ≤ n, p.coeff i = 1 ∨ p.coeff i = -1) ∧
    ∀ z : ℂ, ‖z‖ = 1 →
    ( √n < c₁ * ‖p.eval z‖ ∧ ‖p.eval z‖ < c₂ * √n )

problems.title: Erdős Problem 229
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/229](https://www.erdosproblems.com/229)
- [BaSc72] Barth, K. F. and Schneider, W. J., On a problem of Erd\H{o}s concerning the zeros of the
  derivatives of an entire function. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1972), 229--232.
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.

statements.name: Erdos229.erdos_229
statements.doc:
Let $(S_n)_{n \ge 1}$ be a sequence of sets of complex numbers, none of which have a finite
limit point. Does there exist an entire transcendental function $f(z)$ such that, for all $n \ge 1$, there
exists some $k_n \ge 0$ such that $f^{(k_n)}(z) = 0$ for all $z \in S_n$.

This is Problem 2.30 in [Ha74], where it is attributed to Erdős.

Solved in the affirmative by Barth and Schneider [BaSc72].

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_229 :
    letI := Polynomial.algebraPi ℂ ℂ ℂ
    ∀ (S : ℕ → Set ℂ), (∀ n, derivedSet (S n) = ∅) →
    ∃ (f : ℂ → ℂ), Transcendental (Polynomial ℂ) f ∧ Differentiable ℂ f ∧ ∀ n ≥ 1,
      ∃ k, ∀ z ∈ S n, iteratedDeriv k f z = 0

statements.name: Erdos229.theorem_1
statements.doc:
Let $\{S_k\}$ be any sequence of sets in the complex plane, each of which has no finite
limit point. Then there exists a sequence $\{n_k\}$ of positive integers and a
transcendental entire function $f(z)$ such that $f^{(n_k)}(z) = 0$ if $z \in S_k$.
statements.statement:
theorem theorem_1
    {S : ℕ → Set ℂ}
    (h : ∀ (k), derivedSet (S k) = ∅) :
  letI := Polynomial.algebraPi ℂ ℂ ℂ
  ∃ (f : ℂ → ℂ) (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    Differentiable ℂ f ∧ Transcendental (Polynomial ℂ) f ∧ ∀ k, 0 < n k ∧ ∀ {z} (_: z ∈ S k),
      iteratedDeriv (n k) f z = 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 230
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/230](https://www.erdosproblems.com/230)
- [Er57] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Michigan Math. J. (1957), 291-300.
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., *Research problems in function theory: new problems*. (1974), 155--180.
- [Er80h] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on polynomials and interpolation*. (1980), 383--391.
- [Ko80] Körner, T. W., *On a polynomial of Byrnes*. Bull. London Math. Soc. (1980), 219--224.
- [Ka80] Kahane, Jean-Pierre, *Sur les polynômes à coefficients unimodulaires*. Bull. London Math.
  Soc. (1980), 321-342.
- [BoBo09] Bombieri, Enrico and Bourgain, Jean, *On Kahane's ultraflat polynomials*. J. Eur. Math.
  Soc. (JEMS) (2009), 627-703.

statements.name: Erdos230.erdos_230
statements.doc:
Let $P(z)=\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}a_kz^k$ for some $a_k\in \mathbb{C}$ with $\lvert a_k\rvert=1$ for
$1\leq k\leq n$. Does there exist a constant $c>0$ such that, for $n\geq 2$, we have
$$\max_{\lvert z\rvert=1}\lvert P(z)\rvert \geq (1+c)\sqrt{n}?$$

This is Problem 4.31 in [Ha74], in which it is described as a conjecture of Erdős and Newman.
The lower bound of $\sqrt{n}$ is trivial from Parseval's theorem. Körner [Ko80] constructed, for
all $n\geq 2$, polynomials $P(z)=\sum_{k\leq n} a_kz^k$ with $\lvert a_k\rvert=1$ for
$1\leq k\leq n$ such that, for all $z$ with $\lvert z\rvert=1$,
$$(c_1-o(1))\sqrt{n} \leq \lvert P(z)\rvert \leq (c_2+o(1))\sqrt{n}$$
for some absolute constants $0<c_1\leq c_2$.

The answer is no (contrary to Erdős' initial guess). Kahane [Ka80] constructed 'ultraflat'
polynomials $P(z)=\sum a_kz^k$ with $\lvert a_k\rvert=1$ such that
$$P(z)=(1+o(1))\sqrt{n}$$
uniformly for all $z\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\lvert z\rvert=1$, where the $o(1)$ term $\to 0$ as
$n\to \infty$.

For more details see the paper [BoBo09] of Bombieri and Bourgain and where Kahane's construction
is improved to yield such a polynomial with
$$P(z)=\sqrt{n}+O(n^{\frac{7}{18}}(\log n)^{O(1)})$$
for all $z\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\lvert z\rvert=1$.

See also [228](https://www.erdosproblems.com/228) and
[1150](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1150).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_230 : ¬ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n →
    ∀ a : Fin n → ℂ, (∀ k, ‖a k‖ = 1) → (1 + c) * √n ≤ circleMax a

statements.name: Erdos230.erdos_230.variants.ultraflat
statements.doc:
Kahane [Ka80] constructed 'ultraflat' polynomials $P_n(z)=\sum_{k \leq n} a_kz^k$ with
$\lvert a_k\rvert=1$ such that $P_n(z)=(1+o(1))\sqrt{n}$ uniformly for all $z\in\mathbb{C}$ with
$\lvert z\rvert=1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_230.variants.ultraflat : ∃ a : (n : ℕ) → Fin n → ℂ, (∀ n k, ‖a n k‖ = 1) ∧
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ⨆ z : Metric.sphere (0 : ℂ) 1,
      |‖∑ k : Fin n, a n k * (z : ℂ) ^ ((k : ℕ) + 1)‖ / √n - 1|) atTop (𝓝 0)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 231
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/231](https://www.erdosproblems.com/231)
- [Er57] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Michigan Math. J. (1957), 291-300.
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Ke92] Keränen, Veikko, *Abelian squares are avoidable on $4$ letters*. Automata, languages and
  programming (Vienna, 1992) (1992), 41-52.
- [FiPu23] Fici, Gabriele and Puzynina, Svetlana, *Abelian combinatorics on words: a survey*.
  Comput. Sci. Rev. (2023), Paper No. 100532, 21.

statements.name: Erdos231.erdos_231
statements.doc:
Let $S$ be a string of length $2^k-1$ formed from an alphabet of $k$ characters. Must $S$ contain
an abelian square: two consecutive blocks $x$ and $y$ such that $y$ is a permutation of $x$?

Erdős initially conjectured that the answer is yes for all $k\geq 2$, but for $k=4$ this was
disproved by de Bruijn and Erdős. Erdős then asked if there is in fact an infinite string formed
from $\{1,2,3,4\}$ which contains no abelian squares? This is equivalent to
[192](https://www.erdosproblems.com/192), and such a string was constructed by Keränen [Ke92]. The
existence of this infinite string gives a negative answer to the problem for all $k\geq 4$.

Containing no abelian squares is a stronger property than being squarefree (the existence of
infinitely long squarefree strings over alphabets with $k\geq 3$ characters was established by
Thue). We refer to a recent survey by Fici and Puzynina [FiPu23] for more background and related
results.

As stated, the answer is negative for every $k \geq 2$: the strings $121$ and $1213121$ of
length $2^k - 1$ for $k = 2, 3$ contain no abelian square. See `erdos_231.variants.two_pow` for
strings of length $2^k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_231 :
    ¬ ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → ∀ S : List (Fin k), S.length = 2 ^ k - 1 → ContainsAbelianSquare S

statements.name: Erdos231.erdos_231.variants.two_pow
statements.doc:
Perhaps Erdős meant $2^k$, where indeed there is an example for $k=4$:
$$1213121412132124.$$
Every string of length $2^k$ over $k$ characters contains an abelian square for $k = 2, 3$, but
not for $k \geq 4$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_231.variants.two_pow :
    ¬ ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → ∀ S : List (Fin k), S.length = 2 ^ k → ContainsAbelianSquare S

statements.name: Erdos231.erdos_231.variants.two_pow_small
statements.doc: Every string of length $2^k$ over $k$ characters contains an abelian square for $k = 2, 3$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_231.variants.two_pow_small (k : ℕ) (hk : k = 2 ∨ k = 3) (S : List (Fin k))
    (hS : S.length = 2 ^ k) : ContainsAbelianSquare S

problems.title: Erdős Problem 232
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/232](https://www.erdosproblems.com/232)
- [ACMVZ23] Ambrus, Gergely and Csiszárik, Adrián and Matolcsi, Máté and Varga, Dániel and
  Zsámboki, Pál, *The density of planar sets avoiding unit distances*. Math. Program. (2023),
  [arXiv:2207.14179](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.14179).
- [Cr67] Croft, H. T., *Incidence incidents*. Eureka (1967), 22-26.
- [Er85] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results in combinatorial geometry*. Discrete geometry and
  convexity (New York, 1982), Ann. New York Acad. Sci. 440 (1985), 1-11.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1985-23.pdf)
- [Mo66] Moser, L., *Poorly formulated unsolved problems of combinatorial geometry*.
  Mimeographed (1966).

statements.name: Erdos232.erdos_232
statements.doc:
For $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ we define the upper density as
$$\overline{\delta}(A)=\limsup_{R\to \infty}\frac{\lambda(A \cap B_R)}{\lambda(B_R)},$$
where $\lambda$ is the Lebesgue measure and $B_R$ is the ball of radius $R$.

Estimate
$$m_1=\sup \overline{\delta}(A),$$
where $A$ ranges over all measurable subsets of $\mathbb{R}^2$ without two points distance $1$
apart. In particular, is $m_1\leq 1/4$?

A question of Moser [Mo66]; Erdős [Er85] conjectured $m_1<1/4$. The answer is yes: Ambrus,
Csiszárik, Matolcsi, Varga, and Zsámboki [ACMVZ23] proved that $m_1\leq 0.247$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_232 : m₁ ≤ 1 / 4

statements.name: Erdos232.erdos_232.variants.acmvz_set
statements.doc:
Ambrus, Csiszárik, Matolcsi, Varga, and Zsámboki [ACMVZ23, Theorem 1]: any Lebesgue measurable,
$1$-avoiding planar set has upper density at most $0.2470$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_232.variants.acmvz_set (A : Set ℝ²) (hA : NullMeasurableSet A volume)
    (hfree : Erdos214.UnitDistanceAvoiding A) : upperDensity A ≤ 247 / 1000

statements.name: Erdos232.erdos_232.variants.acmvz
statements.doc: Ambrus, Csiszárik, Matolcsi, Varga, and Zsámboki [ACMVZ23] proved that $m_1\leq 0.247$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_232.variants.acmvz : m₁ ≤ 247 / 1000

statements.name: Erdos232.erdos_232.variants.hexagonal_lower_bound
statements.doc:
A lower bound of $m_1\geq \pi/(8\sqrt{3})\approx 0.2267$ is given by taking the union of open
circular discs of radius $1/2$ at a regular hexagonal lattice suitably spaced apart
(see [ACMVZ23, Section 1]).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_232.variants.hexagonal_lower_bound :
    Real.pi / (8 * Real.sqrt 3) ≤ m₁

statements.name: Erdos232.erdos_232.variants.croft_lower_bound
statements.doc: Croft [Cr67] gives a small improvement of $m_1\geq 0.22936$ (see [ACMVZ23, Section 1]).
statements.statement: theorem erdos_232.variants.croft_lower_bound : 0.22936 ≤ m₁

problems.title: Erdős Problem 233
problems.doc:
*References:*
  - [erdosproblems.com/233](https://www.erdosproblems.com/233)
  - [A74741](https://oeis.org/A74741)
  - [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cram%C3%A9r%27s_conjecture)

statements.name: Erdos233.erdos_233
statements.doc:
A conjecture by Heath-Brown:
The sum of squares of the first $N$ gaps between consecutive primes behaves like $N * (log N)^2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_233 :
    (fun N => ((∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (primeGap n) ^ 2) : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N => N * (log N)^2

statements.name: Erdos233.erdos_233.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc: Cramér proved an upper bound of $O(N(\log N)^4)$ conditional on the Riemann hypothesis.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_233.variants.upper_bound (h : RiemannHypothesis) :
    (fun N => ((∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (primeGap n) ^ 2) : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N => N * (log N)^4

statements.name: Erdos233.erdos_233.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
The prime number theorem immediately implies a lower bound of $\gg N(\log N)^2$ for the sum of
squares of gaps between consecutive primes.

Formal proof linked here provided by AlphaProof.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_233.variants.lower_bound :
    (fun (N : ℕ) => N * (log N)^2) =O[atTop]
    (fun N => ((∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (primeGap n) ^ 2) : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 234
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/234](https://www.erdosproblems.com/234)

statements.name: Erdos234.erdos_234
statements.doc:
Is it true that for all `c ≥ 0`, the density `f c` of integers for which
`(p (n + 1) - p n) / log n < c` exists and is a continuous function of `c`?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_234 : ∃ f : ℝ≥0 → ℝ, Continuous f ∧
    ∀ c : ℝ≥0, HasDensity {n : ℕ | primeGap n / log n < c} (f c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 235
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/235](https://www.erdosproblems.com/235)
- [Ho65] Hooley, Christopher, _On the difference between consecutive numbers prime to $n$_. II.
  Publ. Math. Debrecen (1965), 39--49.

statements.name: Erdos235.erdos_235
statements.doc:
Let $N_k=2\cdot 3\cdots p_k$ and $\{a_1<a_2<\cdots <a_{\phi(N_k)}\}$ be the integers $<N_k$ which
are relatively prime to $N_k$. Then, for any $c\geq 0$, the limit
$$\frac{\#\{ a_i-a_{i-1}\leq c \frac{N_k}{\phi(N_k)} : 2\leq i\leq \phi(N_k)\}}{\phi(N_k)}$$
exists and is a continuous function of $c$.

Solved by Hooley [Ho65], who proved that these gaps have an exponential distribution: that is, if
$f(c)$ is the function in question, then
$$f(c)=(1+o(1))(1-e^{-c})$$
(where the $o(1)$ goes to $0$ uniformly as $k\to \infty$).

See also [234](https://www.erdosproblems.com/234) for a more difficult version of this problem using
actual primes.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_235 :
    ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, ContinuousOn f (Set.Ici (0 : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ c, 0 ≤ c → Tendsto (fun k ↦ proportion k c) atTop (𝓝 (f c))

statements.name: Erdos235.erdos_235.variants.hooley
statements.doc:
Hooley [Ho65] proved that the limit in `erdos_235` is $1-e^{-c}$.
For each fixed $c\geq 0$,
$$f(c)=(1+o(1))(1-e^{-c})$$
as $k\to\infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_235.variants.hooley (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    Tendsto (fun k ↦ proportion k c) atTop (𝓝 (1 - Real.exp (-c)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 236
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/236](https://www.erdosproblems.com/236)

statements.name: Erdos236.erdos_236
statements.doc: Let $f(n)$ count the number of solutions to $n=p+2^k$ for prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$. Show that $f(n)=o(\log n)$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_236: (fun n => (f n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n => Real.log (n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 237
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/237](https://www.erdosproblems.com/237)
- [ChDi22] Chen, Y.-G. and Ding, Y., *On a conjecture of Erdős*.
  [arXiv:2201.10727](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.10727) (2022).
- [Er50] Erdős, P., *On integers of the form $2^k+p$ and some related problems*.
  Summa Brasil. Math. (1950), 113-123.

statements.name: Erdos237.erdos_237
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be a set such that $\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \gg \log N$ for
all large $N$. Let $f(n)$ count the number of solutions to $n=p+a$ for $p$ prime and $a\in A$. Is
it true that $\limsup f(n)=\infty$?

The answer is yes, as proved by Chen and Ding [ChDi22].

Here `A` may contain $0$. This changes each $f(n)$ by at most one, so it does not affect the
answer.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_237 : ∀ A : Set ℕ,
    (fun N : ℕ ↦ Real.log N) =O[atTop] (fun N ↦ ((A ∩ .Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ)) →
    limsup (fun n ↦ (f A n : ℕ∞)) atTop = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos237.erdos_237.variants.infinite
statements.doc:
Chen and Ding [ChDi22] proved that the assumption
$\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \gg \log N$ can be replaced with the assumption that $A$ is
infinite.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_237.variants.infinite (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) :
    limsup (fun n ↦ (f A n : ℕ∞)) atTop = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos237.erdos_237.variants.pow_two
statements.doc: Erdős [Er50] proved the case $A=\{2^k : k\geq 0\}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_237.variants.pow_two :
    limsup (fun n ↦ (f (Set.range (2 ^ ·)) n : ℕ∞)) atTop = ⊤

problems.title: Erdős Problem 238
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/238](https://www.erdosproblems.com/238)

statements.name: Erdos238.erdos_238
statements.doc:
Let `c₁, c₂ > 0`. Is it true that for any sufficiently large `x`, there exists more than
`c₁ * log x` many consecutive primes `≤ x` such that the difference between any two is `> c₂`?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_238 : ∀ᵉ (c₁ > 0) (c₂ > 0), ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in atTop, ∃ (k : ℕ),
    c₁ * log x < k ∧ ∃ f : Fin k → ℕ, ∃ m, (∀ i, f i ≤ x ∧ f i = (m + i.1).nth Nat.Prime)
    ∧ ∀ i : Fin (k - 1), c₂ < primeGap (m + i.1)

statements.name: Erdos238.erdos_238.variants.small_c1
statements.doc: It is well-known that the conjecture above is true when `c₁` is sufficiently small.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_238.variants.small_c1 : ∀ c₂ > 0, ∀ᶠ c₁ in 𝓝[>] 0, ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in atTop, ∃ (k : ℕ),
    c₁ * log x < k ∧ ∃ f : Fin k → ℕ, ∃ m, (∀ i, f i ≤ x ∧ f i = (m + i.1).nth Nat.Prime)
    ∧ ∀ i : Fin (k - 1), c₂ < primeGap (m + i.1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 239
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/239](https://www.erdosproblems.com/239)
- [Ha68] Halász, G., Über die Mittelwerte multiplikativer zahlentheoretischer
  Funktionen. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1968), 365-403.
- [Wi67] Wirsing, E., Das asymptotische Verhalten von Summen über multiplikative Funk­tionen.
  Acta Math. Acad. Sei. Hung. (1967), 411-467.

statements.name: Erdos239.erdos_239
statements.doc:
Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to \{-1,1\}$ be a multiplicative function. Is it true that
$$ \lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n\leq N}f(n)$$ always exists?

The answer is yes, as proved by Wirsing [Wi67], and generalised by Halász [Ha68].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_239 :
    ∀ f : ℕ → ℝ,
    (∀ n ≥ 1, f n = 1 ∨ f n = -1) ∧
    (∀ m n, m.Coprime n → f (m * n) = f m * f n) ∧
    f 1 = 1 →
    ∃ L, Tendsto (fun N ↦ (∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f n) / N) atTop (𝓝 L)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 240
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/240](https://www.erdosproblems.com/240)
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1965-17.pdf)
- [Po18] Pólya, Georg, *Zur arithmetischen Untersuchung der Polynome*. Math. Z. (1918), 143-148.
- [Ti73] Tijdeman, R., *On integers with many small prime factors*. Compositio Math. 26 (1973),
  319-330. [numdam](https://www.numdam.org/item/CM_1973__26_3_319_0/)

statements.name: Erdos240.erdos_240
statements.doc:
Is there an infinite set of primes $P$ such that if $\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}$ is the set of integers
divisible only by primes in $P$ then $\lim a_{i+1}-a_i=\infty$?

The answer is yes, proved by Tijdeman [Ti73, Theorem 7]. The question was asked to Erdős by
Wintner [Er65b, p. 218]. See also Erdős Problem 368.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_240 :
    ∃ P : Set ℕ, P.Infinite ∧ P ⊆ {p : ℕ | p.Prime} ∧
      Tendsto (fun i ↦ a P (i + 1) - a P i) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos240.erdos_240.variants.tijdeman_epsilon
statements.doc:
Tijdeman [Ti73] resolved this question, proving that, for any $\epsilon>0$, there exists an
infinite set of primes $P$ such that, with $a_i$ defined as above,
$$a_{i+1}-a_i \gg a_i^{1-\epsilon}.$$
([Ti73, Theorem 7] is stated for $0<\epsilon<1$; for $\epsilon\geq 1$ the bound is trivial.)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_240.variants.tijdeman_epsilon (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ P : Set ℕ, P.Infinite ∧ P ⊆ {p : ℕ | p.Prime} ∧
      (fun i ↦ (a P i : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε)) =O[atTop] (fun i ↦ ((a P (i + 1) - a P i : ℕ) : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos240.erdos_240.variants.finite
statements.doc:
The limit is infinite for a finite set of primes, which follows from a theorem of Pólya [Po18],
that if $f(n)$ is a quadratic integer polynomial without repeated roots then as
$n\to \infty$ the largest prime factor of $f(n)$ also approaches infinity.
Erdős [Er65b, p. 218] also credits this to Pólya.

Here $P$ is nonempty: for $P=\emptyset$ the set of integers is $\{1\}$ and there are no gaps.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_240.variants.finite {P : Set ℕ} (hP : P.Finite) (hne : P.Nonempty)
    (hpr : P ⊆ {p : ℕ | p.Prime}) :
    Tendsto (fun i ↦ a P (i + 1) - a P i) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos240.erdos_240.variants.tijdeman_finite
statements.doc:
Tijdeman [Ti73] proved that, if $P$ is a finite set of primes, then
$$a_{i+1}-a_i \gg \frac{a_i}{(\log a_i)^C}$$
for some constant $C>0$ depending on $P$.

[Ti73, Theorem 1 and its Corollary] state this for the integers composed of all primes at most
$p$; it follows for every finite set of primes, since a subset of these integers has larger gaps.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_240.variants.tijdeman_finite {P : Set ℕ} (hP : P.Finite) (hne : P.Nonempty)
    (hpr : P ⊆ {p : ℕ | p.Prime}) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      (fun i ↦ (a P i : ℝ) / Real.log (a P i : ℝ) ^ C) =O[atTop]
        (fun i ↦ ((a P (i + 1) - a P i : ℕ) : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 241
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/30](https://www.erdosproblems.com/30)
- [erdosproblems.com/241](https://www.erdosproblems.com/241)
- [BoCh62] Bose, R. C. and Chowla, S., Theorems in the additive theory of numbers. Comment. Math.
  Helv. (1962/63), 141-147.
- [Gr01] Green, Ben, The number of squares and {$B_h[g]$} sets. Acta Arith. (2001), 365-390.
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
- [Wh24] White, Ethan Patrick, An optimal $L^2$ autoconvolution inequality. Canad. Math. Bull.
  67 (2024), 108-121. [doi:10.4153/S0008439523000565](https://doi.org/10.4153/S0008439523000565)

statements.name: Erdos241.erdos_241
statements.doc:
Is it true that $f(N)\sim N^{1/3}$?

Originally asked to Erdős by Bose.

This is discussed in problem C11 of Guy's collection [Gu04].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_241 :
    (fun N ↦ (f N 3 : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun N ↦ (N : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3))

statements.name: Erdos241.erdos_241.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
Bose and Chowla [BoCh62] provided a construction proving one half of this, namely
$(1+o(1))N^{1/3}\leq f(N)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_241.variants.lower_bound :
    ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ, ε =o[atTop] (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧
    ∀ᶠ N in atTop, (1 + ε N) * (N : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3) ≤ (f N 3 : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos241.erdos_241.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
Green [Gr01] proved the upper bound $f(N) \leq ((7/2)^{1/3}+o(1))N^{1/3}$
(note that $(7/2)^{1/3}\approx 1.519$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_241.variants.upper_bound :
    ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ, ε =o[atTop] (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧
    ∀ᶠ N in atTop, (f N 3 : ℝ) ≤ ((7 / 2 : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3) + ε N) * (N : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)

statements.name: Erdos241.erdos_241.variants.upper_bound_white
statements.doc:
Green's argument gives $f(N) \leq ((2/\mu_2^2)^{1/3}+o(1))N^{1/3}$, where
$\mu_2^2 = \inf \lVert g \ast g \rVert_2^2$ over $g \colon [-1/2,1/2] \to \mathbb{R}$ with
$\int g = 1$; Green used $\mu_2^2 \geq 4/7$. White [Wh24, Theorem 1 and Corollary 2] proved
$0.574636066 \leq \mu_2^2 \leq 0.574642912$, which gives the best upper bound known to date,
$f(N) \leq ((2/0.574636066)^{1/3}+o(1))N^{1/3}$ (note that $(2/0.574636066)^{1/3}\approx 1.5155$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_241.variants.upper_bound_white :
    ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ, ε =o[atTop] (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧
    ∀ᶠ N in atTop, (f N 3 : ℝ) ≤
      ((2 / 0.574636066 : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3) + ε N) * (N : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)

statements.name: Erdos241.erdos_241.variants.generalization
statements.doc:
More generally, Bose and Chowla [BoCh62] conjectured that the maximum size of
$A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with all $r$-fold sums distinct (aside from the trivial coincidences)
then $\lvert A\rvert \sim N^{1/r}.$
statements.statement: theorem erdos_241.variants.generalization (r : ℕ) (hr : r ≥ 2) :  BoseChowlaConjecture r

statements.name: Erdos241.erdos_241.variants.r_eq_2
statements.doc: This is known only for $r=2$ (see [erdosproblems.com/30]).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_241.variants.r_eq_2 :
    BoseChowlaConjecture 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 242
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/242](https://www.erdosproblems.com/242)
- [Si56] Sierpiński, W., Sur les décompositions de nombres rationnels en fractions primaires.
  Mathesis (1956), 16--32.

statements.name: Erdos242.erdos_242
statements.doc:
For every $n>2$ there exist distinct integers $1 ≤ x < y < z$
such that $\frac 4 n = \frac 1 x + \frac 1 y + \frac 1 z$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_242 (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 < n) :
    ∃ x y z : ℕ, 1 ≤ x ∧ x < y ∧ y < z ∧
      (4 / n : ℚ) = 1 / x + 1 / y + 1 / z

statements.name: Erdos242.erdos_242.variants.schinzel_generalization
statements.doc:
Schinzel conjectured (see [Si56]) the generalisation that, for any fixed $a$, if $n$ is sufficiently
large in terms of $a$ then there exist distinct integers $1\leq x < y < z$ such that
$\frac{a}{n} = \frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{1}{z}.$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_242.variants.schinzel_generalization
    (a : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ x y z : ℕ, 1 ≤ x ∧ x < y ∧ y < z ∧
      (a / n : ℚ) = 1 / x + 1 / y + 1 / z

problems.title: Erdős Problem 243
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/243](https://www.erdosproblems.com/243)

statements.name: Erdos243.erdos_243
statements.doc:
Let $a_1 < a_2 < \dots$ be a sequence of integers such that
$\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{a_n}{a_{n-1}^2} = 1$ and $\sum \frac{1}{a_n} \in \mathbb{Q}$.

Then, for all sufficiently large $n \ge 1$, $a_n = a_{n-1}^2 - a_{n-1} + 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_243 (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha₀ : StrictMono a)
    (ha₁ : Tendsto (fun n ↦ (a n : ℝ) / a (n - 1) ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 1))
    (ha₂ : Summable ((1 : ℚ) / a ·)) :
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, a n = a (n - 1) ^ 2 - a (n - 1) + 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 244
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/244](https://www.erdosproblems.com/244)

statements.name: Erdos244.erdos_244
statements.doc:
Let $C > 1$. Does the set of integers of the form $p + \lfloor C^k \rfloor$,
for some prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$, have density $>0$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_244 :
    ∀ C > (1 : ℝ), 0 < { p + ⌊C ^ k⌋₊ | (p) (k) (_ : p.Prime) }.lowerDensity

statements.name: Erdos244.erdos_244.variants.Romanoff
statements.doc:
Romanoff [Ro34] proved that the answer is yes if $C$ is an integer.

[Ro34] Romanoff, N. P., _Über einige Sätze der additiven Zahlentheorie_.
Math. Ann. (1934), 668-678.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_244.variants.Romanoff {C : ℕ} (hC : 1 < C) :
    0 < { p + ⌊C ^ k⌋₊ | (p) (k) (_ : p.Prime) }.lowerDensity

problems.title: Erdős Problem 245
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/245](https://www.erdosproblems.com/245)

statements.name: Erdos245.erdos_245
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that $|A\cap \{1, ..., N\}| = o(N)$.
Is it true that
$$
\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|(A + A)\cap \{1, ..., N\}|}{|A \cap \{1, ..., N\}|} \geq 3?
$$

The answer is yes, proved by Freiman [Fr73].

[Fr73] Fre\u{\i}man, G. A., _Foundations of a structural theory of set addition_. (1973), vii+108.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_245 :
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite →
      atTop.Tendsto (fun N ↦ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊ |>.ncard : ℝ) / N) (𝓝 0) →
      3 ≤ atTop.limsup
        fun N : ℝ ↦ ((A + A) ∩ Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊ |>.ncard : EReal)
          / (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊).ncard

statements.name: Erdos245.erdos_245.variants.two
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that $|A\cap \{1, ..., N\}| = o(N)$.
Then
$$
\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|(A + A)\cap \{1, ..., N\}|}{|A \cap \{1, ..., N\}|} \geq 2.
$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_245.variants.two (A : Set ℕ) (h_inf : A.Infinite)
    (hf : atTop.Tendsto (fun N ↦ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊ |>.ncard : ℝ) / N) (𝓝 0)) :
    2 ≤ atTop.limsup
      fun N : ℝ ↦ ((A + A) ∩ Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊ |>.ncard : EReal)
        / (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊).ncard

problems.title: Erdős Problem 246
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/246](https://www.erdosproblems.com/246)
- [Bi59] Birch, B. J., *Note on a problem of Erd\H{o}s*. Proc. Cambridge
  Philos. Soc. (1959), 370-373.
- [Ca60] Cassels, J. W. S., *On the representation of integers as the sums of
  distinct summands taken from a fixed set*. Acta Sci. Math. (Szeged) (1960),
  111-124.
- [FaCh17] Fang, Jin-Hui and Chen, Yong-Gao, *A quantitative form of the
  {E}rd\H{o}s-{B}irch theorem*. Acta Arith. (2017), 301--311.
- [He00b] Hegyv\'{a}ri, N., *On the completeness of an exponential type
