  sequence*. Acta Math. Hungar. (2000), 127--135.
- [Yu24] Yu, Wang-Xing, *On the representation of an exponential type sequence*.
  Publ. Math. Debrecen (2024), 253--261.

statements.name: Erdos246.erdos_246
statements.doc:
Let $(a,b)=1$. The set $\{a^kb^l: k,l\geq 0\}$ is complete - that is, every large integer is the sum of distinct integers of the form $a^kb^l$ with $k,l\geq 0$.

We state the nontrivial case $a,b\geq 2$, proved by Birch [Bi59].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_246 (a b : ℕ) (ha : 2 ≤ a) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hab : Nat.Coprime a b) :
    IsAddComplete (Gamma a b)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 247
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/247](https://www.erdosproblems.com/247)

statements.name: Erdos247.erdos_247
statements.doc:
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \cdots$ be a sequence of integers such that
$$
  \limsup \frac{n_k}{k} = \infty.
$$
Is
$$
  \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2^{n_k}}
$$
transcendental?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_247 : ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ), (StrictMono n) →
    atTop.limsup (fun k => (n k / k.succ : EReal)) = ⊤ →
    Transcendental ℚ (∑' k, (1 : ℝ) / 2 ^ n k)

statements.name: Erdos247.erdos_247.variants.strong_condition
statements.doc:
Erdős proved the answer is yes under the stronger condition that
$\limsup \frac{n_k}{k^t} = \infty$ for all $t\geq 1$.

[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R.,
_Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory_.
Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_247.variants.strong_condition (n : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hn : StrictMono n)
    (h : ∀ t ≥ (1 : ℝ),
      atTop.limsup (fun k => n k / (k.succ : ℝ) ^ t |>.toEReal) = ⊤) :
    Transcendental ℚ (∑' k, (1 : ℝ) / 2 ^ n k)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 248
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/248](https://www.erdosproblems.com/248)
- [TaTe25] T. Tao and J. Teräväinen, Quantitative correlations and some problems on prime factors of consecutive integers. arXiv:2512.01739 (2025).

statements.name: Erdos248.erdos_248
statements.doc:
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that $\omega(n + k) \ll k$ for all $k \geq 1$?
Here $\omega(n)$ is the number of distinct prime divisors of $n$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_248 : (∃ C > (0 : ℝ), { n | ∀ k ≥ 1, ω (n + k) ≤ C * k }.Infinite)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 249
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/249](https://www.erdosproblems.com/249)

statements.name: Erdos249.erdos_249
statements.doc:
Is
$$\sum_{n} \frac{\phi(n)}{2^n}$$
irrational? Here $\phi$ is the Euler totient function.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_249 : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (φ n) / (2 ^ n))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 250
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/250](https://www.erdosproblems.com/250)

statements.name: Erdos250.erdos_250
statements.doc:
Is
$$
  \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\sigma(n)}{2^n}
$$
irrational? Here $\sigma(n)$ is the sum of divisors function.

The answer is yes, as shown by Nesterenko [Ne96].

[Ne96] Nesterenko, Yu V., _Modular functions and transcendence questions_,
Mat. Sb. 187 *9* (1996), 1319--1348.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_250  : (∀ x, HasSum (fun (n : ℕ) => σ 1 n / (2 : ℝ) ^ n) x → Irrational x)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 251
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/251](https://www.erdosproblems.com/251)

statements.name: Erdos251.erdos_251
statements.doc: Is $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{p_n}{2^n}$ irrational? Here $p_n$ is the $n$-th prime ($p_1=2, p_2=3, \dots$).
statements.statement: theorem erdos_251 : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.nth Nat.Prime n) / (2 ^ n))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 252
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/252](https://www.erdosproblems.com/252)
 - [ErSt71] Erdös, P., and E. G. Straus. "Some number theoretic results." Pacific J. Math 36 (1971):
    635-646.
 - [ErSt74] Erdős, Paul, and Ernst Straus. "On the irrationality of certain series." Pacific journal
    of mathematics 55.1 (1974): 85-92.
 - [ErKa54] P. Erdős, M. Kac, Amer. Math. Monthly 61 (1954), Problem 4518.
 - [ScPu06] Schlage-Puchta, J. C., The irrationality of a number theoretical series. Ramanujan J.
    (2006), 455-460.
 - [FLC07] Friedlander, J. B. and Luca, F. and Stoiciu, M., On the irrationality of a divisor
    function series. Integers (2007).
 - [Pr22] Pratt, K., The irrationality of a divisor function series of Erdős and Kac.
    arXiv:2209.11124 (2022).

statements.name: Erdos252.erdos_252
statements.doc: Erdős Problem 252: irrationality of the sum for a given $k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_252 :
    ∀ k ≥ 1, Irrational (erdos_252_sum k)

statements.name: Erdos252.erdos_252.variants.k_eq_zero
statements.doc: `∑ σ 0 n / n!` is irrational. This is proved in [ErSt71].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_252.variants.k_eq_zero : Irrational (erdos_252_sum 0)

statements.name: Erdos252.erdos_252.variants.k_eq_one
statements.doc: `∑ σ 1 n / n!` is irrational. This is proved in [ErSt74].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_252.variants.k_eq_one : Irrational (erdos_252_sum 1)

statements.name: Erdos252.erdos_252.variants.k_eq_two
statements.doc: `∑ σ 2 n / n!` is irrational. This is proved in [ErKa54].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_252.variants.k_eq_two : Irrational (erdos_252_sum 2)

statements.name: Erdos252.erdos_252.variants.k_eq_three
statements.doc: `∑ σ 3 n / n!` is irrational. This is proved in [ScPu06] and [FLC07].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_252.variants.k_eq_three : Irrational (erdos_252_sum 3)

statements.name: Erdos252.erdos_252.variants.k_eq_four
statements.doc: `∑ σ 4 n / n!` is irrational. This is proved in [Pr22].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_252.variants.k_eq_four : Irrational (erdos_252_sum 4)

statements.name: Erdos252.erdos_252.variants.k_ge_five
statements.doc: For a fixed `k ≥ 5`, is `∑ σ k n / n!` irrational?.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_252.variants.k_ge_five :
    ∀ k ≥ 5, Irrational (erdos_252_sum k)

statements.name: Erdos252.erdos_252.variants.schinzel
statements.doc:
If Schinzel's conjecture is true, then `∑ σ k n / n!` is irrational for all `k`. This is proved
in [ScPu06].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_252.variants.schinzel (hs : ∀ (fs : Finset (Polynomial ℤ)),
    (∀ f ∈ fs, BunyakovskyCondition f) → SchinzelCondition fs →
    Infinite ↑{n | ∀ f ∈ fs, Prime (Polynomial.eval (↑n) f).natAbs}) :
    ∀ k, Irrational (erdos_252_sum k)

statements.name: Erdos252.erdos_252.variants.prime_tuples
statements.doc:
If the prime `k`-tuples conjecture is true, then `∑ σ k n / n!` is irrational. This is proved
in [FLC07].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_252.variants.prime_tuples {k : ℕ} (hk : 4 ≤ k) (hp : ∀ (a : Fin k → ℕ+)
    (b : Fin k → ℕ) (hab : ∀ p, p.Prime → ∃ n, ¬ p ∣ ∏ i, (a i * n + b i)),
    Set.Infinite {n | ∀ i : Fin k, (a i * n + b i).Prime} ) :
    Irrational (erdos_252_sum k)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 253
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/253](https://www.erdosproblems.com/253)

statements.name: Erdos253.erdos_253
statements.doc:
Let $a_1 < a_2 < \dotsc$ be an infinite sequence of positive integers such that
$\frac{a_{i+1}}{a_i} \to 1$. If every arithmetic progression contains infinitely many
integers which are the sum of distinct $a_i$ then every sufficiently large integer is
the sum of distinct $a_i$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_253 : ¬ ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, 0 < a 0 →
    RepresentsAPs a → (Filter.atTop.Tendsto (fun n ↦ (a <| n + 1 : ℝ) / a n) (𝓝 1)) →
      subsetSums (Set.range a) ∈ Filter.cofinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 254
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/254](https://www.erdosproblems.com/254)
- [Ca60] Cassels, J. W. S., On the representation of integers as the sums of distinct summands taken
  from a fixed set. Acta Sci. Math. (Szeged) (1960), 111-124.

statements.name: Erdos254.erdos_254
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be such that $\lvert A\cap [1,2x]\rvert -\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert \to
\infty\textrm{ as }x\to \infty$ and $\sum_{n\in A} \{ \theta n\}=\infty$ for every $\theta\in
(0,1)$, where $\{x\}$ is the distance of $x$ from the nearest integer. Then every sufficiently large
integer is the sum of distinct elements of $A$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_254 :
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
      (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦ (A ∩ Icc 1 (2 * x)).ncard - (A ∩ Icc 1 x).ncard) atTop atTop) ∧
      (∀ θ : ℝ, 0 < θ → θ < 1 → ¬ Summable (fun n : A ↦ distToNearestInt (θ * (n : ℝ)))) →
        ∀ᶠ m in atTop, IsSumOfDistinct A m

statements.name: Erdos254.erdos_254.variants.cassels
statements.doc:
Cassels [Ca60] proved this under the alternative hypotheses $\lim \frac{\lvert A\cap [1,2x]\rvert
-\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{\log\log x}=\infty$ and $\sum_{n\in A} \{ \theta n\}^2=\infty$ for every
$\theta\in (0,1)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_254.variants.cassels :
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
      (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦ (((A ∩ Icc 1 (2 * x)).ncard : ℝ) -
        ((A ∩ Icc 1 x).ncard : ℝ)) / Real.log (Real.log x)) atTop atTop) ∧
      (∀ θ : ℝ, 0 < θ → θ < 1 → ¬ Summable (fun n : A ↦ (distToNearestInt (θ * (n : ℝ)))^2)) →
        ∀ᶠ m in atTop, IsSumOfDistinct A m

problems.title: Erdős Problem 257
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/257](https://www.erdosproblems.com/257)

statements.name: Erdos257.erdos_257
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set. Is
$$
\sum_{n\in A} \frac{1}{2^n - 1}
$$
irrational?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_257 : ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite →
    Irrational (∑' n : A, (1 : ℝ) / (2 ^ n.1 - 1))

statements.name: Erdos257.erdos_257.variants.tsum_top_eq
statements.doc:
Show that
$$
\sum_{n} \frac{1}{2^n - 1} = \sum_{n} \frac{d(n)}{2^n},
$$
where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_257.variants.tsum_top_eq :
    ∑' n, 1 / (2 ^ n - 1 : ℝ) = ∑' n, n.divisors.card / (2 ^ n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos257.erdos_257.variants.tsum_top
statements.doc:
Show that
$$
\sum_{n} \frac{d(n)}{2^n}
$$
is irrational.

[Er48] Erdős, P., _On arithmetical properties of Lambert series_. J. Indian Math. Soc. (N.S.) (1948), 63-66.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_257.variants.tsum_top :
    Irrational <| ∑' n, n.divisors.card / (2 ^ n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos257.erdos_257.variants.summable_reciprocal_support
statements.doc:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be infinite with $\sum_{a \in A} 1/a < \infty$.
For every integer base $b \ge 2$, the series
$$
\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{b^a - 1}
$$
is irrational. No pairwise coprimality assumption is needed. Exponent zero
contributes zero under Lean's real-division convention.

Erdős stated the coprimality-free result in *On the irrationality of certain
series*, Math. Student 36 (1968), p. 222. A proof and formalisation appear in
W. Cook,
*Reciprocal Mersenne Subseries*:
https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos/blob/598cd7bac8b73dcfef3687f46922c1ef6da766ae/docs/papers/full-text/erdos257-mersenne-reasoning-surface.md
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_257.variants.summable_reciprocal_support
    (b : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hA : A.Infinite)
    (hsum : Summable fun a : A => 1 / (a : ℝ)) :
    Irrational (∑' n : A, 1 / ((b : ℝ) ^ (n : ℕ) - 1))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 258
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/258](https://www.erdosproblems.com/258)
- [Ch26] P. Chojecki and GPT-5.4 Pro, [Erdős problem 258](https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos258.pdf) (2026)
- [St26] ster-oc, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 258](https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=mathlib-v4.28.0&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ster-oc/2b7adcf9d753cf6e29d782f7374cc57e/raw/689a8483895cbe147634dfbf2d7b1db93a3b5b5f/Erdos258.lean) (2026)

statements.name: Erdos258.erdos_258
statements.doc:
Let $a_n \to \infty$ be a sequence of non-zero natural numbers. Is
$\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{(a_1 ... a_n)}$ irrational, where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$?

This was proved affirmatively by Chojecki and GPT-5.4 Pro [Ch26], and formalised in Lean
by ster-oc [St26].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_258 : ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) →
    Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
    Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n + 1), a i))

statements.name: Erdos258.erdos_258.variants.monotone
statements.doc:
Let $2 \leq a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \cdots$ be a monotone sequence with $a_n \to \infty$.
Is $\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{a_1 \cdots a_n}$ irrational, where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$?

Solution: True (proved by Erdős and Straus [ErSt71], Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.13).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_258.variants.monotone :
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) → Monotone a →
    Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
    Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n + 1), a i))

statements.name: Erdos258.erdos_258.variants.constant
statements.doc:
Is $\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{t^n}$ irrational, where $t ≥ 2$ is an integer.

Solution: True (proved by Erdős, see Erdős Problems website)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_258.variants.constant : ∀ t ≥ (2 : ℕ),
    Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / t^(n + 1)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 259
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/259](https://www.erdosproblems.com/259)

statements.name: Erdos259.erdos_259
statements.doc:
Is $\sum_{n} \mu(n)^2\frac{n}{2^n}$ irrational?

This is true, and was proved by Chen and Ruzsa.

[ChRu99] Chen, Yong-Gao and Ruzsa, Imre Z., On the irrationality of certain series. Period. Math. Hungar. (1999), 31--37.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_259 : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (μ n) ^ 2 * n / (2 ^ n))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 260
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/260](https://www.erdosproblems.com/260)
- [Wang, *Sparse Polynomial-Weighted Expansions*]
  (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24972)

statements.name: Erdos260.erdos_260
statements.doc:
Let $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be an increasing sequence such that $\frac{a_n}{n} \to \infty$.
Is the sum $\sum_{n}^{\infty} \frac{a_n}{2^{a_n}}$ irrational?

For a proof, see [Wang, *Sparse Polynomial-Weighted Expansions*]
(https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24972).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_260 :
                  ∀ a : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ s : ℝ,
                  StrictMono a →
                  Tendsto (fun n => (a n : ℝ ) / n ) atTop atTop →
                  HasSum (fun n => (a n : ℝ ) / 2 ^ a n) s → Irrational s

problems.title: Erdős Problem 261
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/261](https://www.erdosproblems.com/261)
 - [BoLo90] Borwein, Peter and Loring, Terry A., Some questions of Erdős and Graham on numbers
    of the form $\sum g_n/2^{g_n}$. Math. Comp. (1990), 377--394.
 - [Er88c] Erdős, P., On the irrationality of certain series: problems and results. New advances
    in transcendence theory (Durham, 1986) (1988), 102--109.
 - [TUZ20] Tengely, Szabolcs and Ulas, Maciej and Zygadlo, Jakub, On a Diophantine equation of
    Erdős and Graham. J. Number Theory (2020), 445--459.
 - [PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000016](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000016&version=1)

statements.name: Erdos261.erdos_261.variants.borwein_loring
statements.doc:
For every positive integer $m$, if $n = 2^{m+1} - m - 2$, then
$$\frac{n}{2^n} = \sum_{n < k \le n + m} \frac{k}{2^k}.$$

This construction is due to Borwein and Loring [BoLo90].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_261.variants.borwein_loring (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) :
    let n := 2 ^ (m + 1) - m - 2
    n / (2 ^ n : ℚ) = ∑ k ∈ Finset.Ioc n (n + m), k / (2 ^ k : ℚ)

statements.name: Erdos261.erdos_261.variants.borwein_loring_property
statements.doc:
The Borwein--Loring construction gives the required property when $m \ge 2$. This lower
bound ensures that the representation contains at least two terms.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_261.variants.borwein_loring_property (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) :
    Erdos261Prop (2 ^ (m + 1) - m - 2)

statements.name: Erdos261.erdos_261.parts.i
statements.doc:
Are there infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that there exist some $t \ge 2$ and
distinct integers $a_1, \ldots, a_t \ge 1$ satisfying
$$\frac{n}{2^n} = \sum_{1 \le k \le t} \frac{a_k}{2^{a_k}}?$$

In [Er88c], Erdős notes that Cusick had a simple proof that infinitely many such $n$ exist.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_261.parts.i : {n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ Erdos261Prop n}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos261.erdos_261.variants.le_10000
statements.doc:
Tengely, Ulas, and Zygadlo [TUZ20] verified that every positive integer $n \le 10000$ has
the required property.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_261.variants.le_10000 {n : ℕ} (hn_pos : 0 < n) (hn : n ≤ 10000) :
    Erdos261Prop n

statements.name: Erdos261.erdos_261.parts.ii
statements.doc: Do all positive integers $n$ have the required property?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_261.parts.ii : ∀ n > 0, Erdos261Prop n

statements.name: Erdos261.erdos_261.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Is there a rational number $x$ such that
$$x = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{a_k}{2^{a_k}}$$
has at least $2^{\aleph_0}$ representations by pairwise distinct positive integers $a_k$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_261.parts.iii : ∃ x : ℚ,
    𝔠 ≤ #{a : ℕ → ℕ | Erdos261InfiniteRepresentation x a}

statements.name: Erdos261.erdos_261.variants.two_representations
statements.doc:
In [Er88c], Erdős asks the weaker question of whether there exists a rational $x$ with at
least two representations
$$x = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{a_k}{2^{a_k}}$$
by pairwise distinct positive integers $a_k$.

The answer is yes: Z. Rafik (erdosproblems.com forum, 27 Apr 2026) observed that
$4/2^4 = 5/2^5 + 6/2^6$ and $\sum_{m \ge 1} m/2^m = 2$, so $7/4$ is represented both by
$\mathbb{N}_{>0} \setminus \{4\}$ and by $\mathbb{N}_{>0} \setminus \{5, 6\}$. It is generally believed that
"two" here is a misprint for $2^{\aleph_0}$ (see `erdos_261.parts.iii`, which remains open).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_261.variants.two_representations : ∃ x : ℚ,
    2 ≤ #{a : ℕ → ℕ | Erdos261InfiniteRepresentation x a}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 263
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/263](https://www.erdosproblems.com/263)

statements.name: Erdos263.erdos_263.parts.i
statements.doc: Is $a_n = 2^{2^n}$ an irrationality sequence in the above sense?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_263.parts.i : IsIrrationalitySequence (fun n : ℕ => 2 ^ 2 ^ n)

statements.name: Erdos263.erdos_263.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Must every irrationality sequence $a_n$ in the above sense
satisfy $a_n^{1/n} \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$?

The answer is no. [Liam Price's construction](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/263#post-6338)
gives a strictly increasing irrationality sequence with $\liminf a_n^{1/n} = 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_263.parts.ii :
    ¬ (∀ a : ℕ → ℕ,
      IsIrrationalitySequence a →
        atTop.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (a n : ℝ) ^ (1 / (n : ℝ))) atTop)

statements.name: Erdos263.erdos_263.variants.folklore
statements.doc:
A folklore result states that any $a_n$ satisfying $\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n^{\frac{1}{2^n}} = \infty$
has $\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converging to an irrational number.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_263.variants.folklore (a : ℕ -> ℕ)
    (ha : atTop.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (a n : ℝ) ^ (1 / (2 ^ n : ℝ))) atTop) :
    Irrational <| ∑' n, (1 : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos263.erdos_263.variants.sub_doubly_exponential
statements.doc:
Kovač and Tao [KoTa24] proved that any strictly increasing sequence $a_n$ such that
$\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converges and $\lim \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n^2} = 0$ is not
an irrationality sequence in the above sense.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series.
         arXiv:2406.17593 (2024).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_263.variants.sub_doubly_exponential (a: ℕ -> ℕ)
    (ha' : StrictMono a)
    (ha'' : Summable (fun n : ℕ => 1 / (a n : ℝ)))
    (ha''' : atTop.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (a (n + 1) : ℝ) / a n ^ 2) (𝓝 0)) :
    ¬ IsIrrationalitySequence a

statements.name: Erdos263.erdos_263.variants.super_doubly_exponential
statements.doc:
On the other hand, if there exists some $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $a_n$ satisfies
$\liminf \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n^{2+\varepsilon}} > 0$, then $a_n$ is an irrationality sequence
by the above folklore result `erdos_263.variants.folklore`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_263.variants.super_doubly_exponential (a: ℕ -> ℕ)
    (ha : ∀ n : ℕ, a n > 0)
    (ha' : StrictMono a)
    (ha'' : ∃ ε : ℝ, ε > 0 ∧
      Filter.atTop.liminf (fun n : ℕ => (a (n + 1) : ℝ) / a n ^ (2 + ε)) > 0) :
    IsIrrationalitySequence a

statements.name: Erdos263.erdos_263.variants.super_doubly_exponential_eventual
statements.doc:
The same folklore result with the growth hypothesis stated as an eventual lower bound
$a_{n+1} \geq c\, a_n^{2+\varepsilon}$. Unlike the real-valued `liminf` in
`erdos_263.variants.super_doubly_exponential`, this form also covers sequences such as
$a_n = 2^{(n+1)!}$, for which the ratio $a_{n+1} / a_n^{2+\varepsilon}$ tends to $+\infty$ and the
real `liminf` defaults to $0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_263.variants.super_doubly_exponential_eventual (a : ℕ → ℕ)
    (ha : ∀ n : ℕ, a n > 0)
    (ha' : StrictMono a)
    (ha'' : ∃ ε c : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ 0 < c ∧
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, c * (a n : ℝ) ^ (2 + ε) ≤ (a (n + 1) : ℝ)) :
    IsIrrationalitySequence a

statements.name: Erdos263.erdos_263.variants.doubly_exponential_all_but_countable
statements.doc:
Koizumi [Ko25] showed that $a_n = \lfloor \alpha^{2^n} \rfloor$ is an irrationality sequence
for all but countably many $\alpha > 1$, in the nondecreasing sense `IsWeakIrrationalitySequence`.
The strictly increasing predicate would fail on the whole interval $1 < \alpha < 4/3$, where
$a_0 = a_1 = 1$.

[Ko25] Koizumi, J., Irrationality of the reciprocal sum of doubly exponential sequences,
       arXiv:2504.05933 (2025).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_263.variants.doubly_exponential_all_but_countable :
    ∀ᶠ (α : ℝ) in .cocountable, α > 1 →
      IsWeakIrrationalitySequence (fun n : ℕ => ⌊α ^ 2 ^ n⌋₊)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 264
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/264](https://www.erdosproblems.com/264)

statements.name: Erdos264.erdos_264.parts.i
statements.doc:
Is $2^n$ an example of an irrationality sequence? Kovač and Tao proved that it is not [KoTa24]

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series. arXiv:2406.17593 (2024).
statements.statement: theorem erdos_264.parts.i : ¬IsIrrationalitySequence (2 ^ ·)

statements.name: Erdos264.erdos_264.parts.ii
statements.doc: Is $n!$ an example of an irrationality sequence?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_264.parts.ii : IsIrrationalitySequence Nat.factorial

statements.name: Erdos264.erdos_264.variants.example
statements.doc: One example is $2^{2^n}$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_264.variants.example : IsIrrationalitySequence (fun n ↦ 2 ^ (2 ^ n))

statements.name: Erdos264.erdos_264.variants.ko_tao_neg
statements.doc:
Kovač and Tao [KoTa24] generally proved that any strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
$a_n$ such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converges and
$$
  \liminf_{n \to \infty} (a_n^2 \sum_{k > n} \frac{1}{a_k^2}) > 0
$$
is not an irrationality sequence.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series. arXiv:2406.17593 (2024).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_264.variants.ko_tao_neg {a : ℕ → ℕ} (h₁ : StrictMono a) (h₂ : 0 ∉ Set.range a)
    (h₃ : Summable ((1 : ℝ) / a ·))
    (h₄ : ∃ C > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, C ≤ a n ^ 2 * ∑' k : Set.Ioi n, (1 : ℝ) / a k ^ 2) :
    ¬IsIrrationalitySequence a

statements.name: Erdos264.erdos_264.variants.ko_tao_pos
statements.doc:
On the other hand, Kovač and Tao [KoTa24] do prove that for any function $F$ with
$\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{F(n + 1)}{F(n)} = \infty$ there exists such an irrationality sequence with $a_n \sim F(n)$.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series. arXiv:2406.17593 (2024).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 266
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/266](https://www.erdosproblems.com/266)

statements.name: Erdos266.erdos_266
statements.doc:
Let $a_n$ be an infinite sequence of positive integers such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converges.
There exists some integer $t \ge 1$ such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n + t}$ is irrational.

This was disproven by Kovač and Tao in [KoTa24].

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series.
         [arXiv:2406.17593](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17593) (2024).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_266 :
    ¬ ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), ((∀ n : ℕ, a n ≥ 1) ∧ Summable ((1 : ℝ) / a ·) →
      ∃ t ≥ (1 : ℕ), Irrational <| ∑' n, (1 : ℝ) / ((a n) + t))

statements.name: Erdos266.erdos_266.variants.all_rationals
statements.doc:
In fact, Kovač and Tao proved in [KoTa24] that there exists a strictly increasing
sequence $a_n$ of positive integers such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n + t}$ converges to a rational
number for all $t \in \mathbb{Q}$ such that $t \ne -a_n$ for any $n$.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series.
         [arXiv:2406.17593](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17593) (2024).

Lean formalization by Ben Keene, with AI assistance.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_266.variants.all_rationals:
    ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a ∧ a 0 ≥ 1 ∧
      (∀ t : ℚ, (¬ ∃ n : ℕ, t = -(a n)) →
        (∃ q : ℚ, HasSum (fun n : ℕ => ((1 : ℝ) / ((a n) + t))) q))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 267
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/267](https://www.erdosproblems.com/267)

statements.name: Erdos267.erdos_267
statements.doc:
Let $F_1=F_2=1$ and $F_{n+1} = F_n + F_{n-1}$ be the Fibonacci sequence.
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an infinite sequence with $\frac{n_{k+1}}{n_k} \ge c > 1$. Must
$\sum_k \frac 1 {F_{n_k}}$ be irrational?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_267 : ∀ᵉ (n : ℕ → ℕ) (c > (1 : ℚ)), StrictMono n → (∀ k, c ≤ n (k+1) / n k) →
    Irrational (∑' k, 1 / (Nat.fib <| n k))

statements.name: Erdos267.erdos_267.variants.generalisation_ratio_limit_to_infinity
statements.doc:
Let $F_1=F_2=1$ and $F_{n+1} = F_n + F_{n-1}$ be the Fibonacci sequence.
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an infinite sequence with $\frac {n_k}{k} \to \infty$. Must
$\sum_k \frac 1 {F_{n_k}}$ be irrational?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_267.variants.generalisation_ratio_limit_to_infinity : ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    StrictMono n → Filter.Tendsto (fun k => (n (k+1) / k.succ : ℝ)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
    Irrational (∑' k, 1 / (Nat.fib <| n k))

statements.name: Erdos267.erdos_267.variants.specialization_pow_two
statements.doc:
Good [Go74] and Bicknell and Hoggatt [BiHo76] have shown that $\sum_n \frac 1 {F_{2^n}}$ is irrational.


Formal proof provided by AlphaProof
Ref:
* [Go74] Good, I. J., _A reciprocal series of Fibonacci numbers_
* [BiHo76] Hoggatt, Jr., V. E. and Bicknell, Marjorie, _A reciprocal series of Fibonacci numbers with subscripts $2\sp{n}k$_
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_267.variants.specialization_pow_two :
    Irrational <| ∑' k, 1 / (Nat.fib <| 2^k)

statements.name: Erdos267.erdos_267.variants.fibonacci_inverse_sum
statements.doc:
The sum $\sum_n \frac 1 {F_{n}}$ itself was proved to be irrational by André-Jeannin.

Ref: André-Jeannin, Richard, _Irrationalité de la somme des inverses de certaines suites récurrentes_.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_267.variants.fibonacci_inverse_sum :
    Irrational <| ∑' k, 1 / (Nat.fib k)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 268
problems.doc:
*Reference:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/268](https://www.erdosproblems.com/268)
 - [KoTa24] Kova\vC, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series.

statements.name: Erdos268.erdos_268
statements.doc:
Let `X` be the set of points in `Fin d → ℝ` of the shape
`fun i : Fin d => ∑' n : A, (1 : ℝ) / (n + i)` for some infinite subset `A ⊆ ℕ` such that
`1 / n` is summable over `A`. `X` has nonempty interior. This is proved in [KoTa24].
-
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_268 (d : ℕ) : (interior {x : Fin d → ℝ | ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧
    Summable (fun n : A => (1 : ℝ) / n ) ∧
    x = fun i : Fin d => ∑' n : A, (1 : ℝ) / (n + i)}).Nonempty

problems.title: Erdős Problem 269
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/269](https://www.erdosproblems.com/269)

statements.name: Erdos269.erdos_269.variants.rational
statements.doc:
Let $P$ be a finite set of primes with $|P| \ge 2$ and let
$\{a_1 < a_2 < \dots\}$ be the set of positive integers whose prime factors
are all in $P$. Is the sum
$$ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{[a_1,\ldots,a_n]} $$
rational?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_269.variants.rational :
    ∀ᵉ (P : Finset ℕ) (h : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) (h_card : P.card ≥ 2),
    ∃ (q : ℚ), q = (series (P : Set ℕ))

statements.name: Erdos269.erdos_269.variants.irrational
statements.doc:
Let $P$ be a finite set of primes with $|P| \ge 2$ and let
$\{a_1 < a_2 < \dots\}$ be the set of positive integers whose prime factors
are all in $P$. Is the sum
$$ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{[a_1,\ldots,a_n]} $$
irrational?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_269.variants.irrational :
    ∀ᵉ (P : Finset ℕ) (h : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) (h_card : P.card ≥ 2),
    Irrational (series (P : Set ℕ))

statements.name: Erdos269.erdos_269.variants.infinite
statements.doc:
This theorem addresses the case where the set of primes $P$ is infinite. In this case the sum is
irrational.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_269.variants.infinite (P : Set ℕ) (h : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) (h_inf : P.Infinite) :
  Irrational (series P)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 270
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/270](https://www.erdosproblems.com/270)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Ha75] Hansen, E. R., *A Table of Series and Products*. Prentice-Hall (1975), 87.
- [CrKo25] T. Crmarić and V. Kovač, *On the irrationality of certain super-polynomially decaying
  series*. arXiv:2504.18712 (2025).
- [Ko26] V. Kovač, [solution of the linear case](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/270#post-7469)
  (2026).

statements.name: Erdos270.erdos_270
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$. Is it true that
$$\sum_{n\geq 1} \frac{1}{(n+1)\cdots (n+f(n))}$$
is irrational?

Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] write 'the answer is almost surely in the affirmative if $f(n)$ is
assumed to be nondecreasing'. The case $f(n)=n$ was subsequently settled by Crmarić and Kovač
[Ko26]. Hansen [Ha75] has
shown that
$$\sum_n \frac{1}{\binom{2n}{n}}=\sum_n \frac{n!}{(n+1)\cdots (n+n)}=\frac{1}{3}+\frac{2\pi}{3^{5/2}}$$
is transcendental.

Crmarić and Kovač [CrKo25] have shown that the answer to this question is no in a strong sense:
for any $\alpha \in (0,\infty)$ there exists a function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that
$f(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to\infty$ and
$$\sum_{n\geq 1} \frac{1}{(n+1)\cdots (n+f(n))}=\alpha.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_270 :
    ¬ ∀ f : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto f atTop atTop → Irrational (series f)

statements.name: Erdos270.erdos_270.variants.every_value
statements.doc:
Crmarić and Kovač [CrKo25]: for any $\alpha \in (0,\infty)$ there exists a function
$f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that $f(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to\infty$ and
$$\sum_{n\geq 1} \frac{1}{(n+1)\cdots (n+f(n))}=\alpha.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_270.variants.every_value (α : ℝ) (hα : 0 < α) :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto f atTop atTop ∧
      HasSum (fun n : ℕ => (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc (n + 2) (n + 1 + f (n + 1)), (i : ℝ))⁻¹) α

statements.name: Erdos270.erdos_270.variants.monotone
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_270.variants.monotone :
    ∀ f : ℕ → ℕ, Monotone f → Tendsto f atTop atTop → Irrational (series f)

statements.name: Erdos270.erdos_270.variants.linear
statements.doc:
The case $f(n)=n$ has a positive answer, as observed by Crmarić and Kovač [Ko26]:
$\sum_{n\geq 1} n!/(2n)!$ is irrational.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_270.variants.linear : Irrational (series id)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 272
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/272](https://www.erdosproblems.com/272)

statements.name: Erdos272.erdos_272
statements.doc:
Let $N\geq 1$. What is the largest $t$ such that there are
$A_1,\ldots,A_t\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $A_i\cap A_j$ a non-empty
arithmetic progression for all $i\neq j$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_272 :
    ∀ N ≥ 1, maxArithInterCard N = erdos_272.answer N

statements.name: Erdos272.erdos_272.variants.isBigO_sq
statements.doc: Simonovits and Sós have shown that $t\ll N^2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_272.variants.isBigO_sq :
    (fun N ↦ (maxArithInterCard N : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N ↦ (N : ℝ) ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos272.erdos_272.variants.szabo
statements.doc:
Szabo showed that the maximal $t$ is equal to
$$
  \frac{N^2}{2} + O(N^{5/3}\log^3N).
$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_272.variants.szabo :
    (fun N ↦ (maxArithInterCard N - N ^ 2 / 2 : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      fun N : ℕ ↦ N ^ ((5 : ℝ) /  3) * (Real.log N) ^ 3

statements.name: Erdos272.erdos_272.variants.szabo_strong
statements.doc:
Szabo asks whether the maximal $t$ is given by
$$
  \frac{N^2}{2} + O(N)
$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_272.variants.szabo_strong :
    (fun N ↦ (maxArithInterCard N - N ^ 2 / 2 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 273
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/273](https://www.erdosproblems.com/273)

statements.name: Erdos273.erdos_273
statements.doc: Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are of the form $p-1$ for some primes $p \geq 5$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_273 : ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ, ∀ i, ∃ (p : ℕ), p.Prime ∧ 5 ≤ p ∧
    c.moduli i = Ideal.span {↑(p - 1)}

statements.name: Erdos273.erdos_273.variants.three
statements.doc: Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are of the form $p-1$ for some primes $p \geq 3$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_273.variants.three : ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℕ, ∀ i, ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ 3 ≤ p ∧
    c.moduli i = Ideal.span {↑(p - 1)}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 274
problems.doc:
*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/274](https://www.erdosproblems.com/274)
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herzog%E2%80%93Sch%C3%B6nheim_conjecture)
* [arXiv:1803.08301](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08301)
* [arXiv:1803.03569](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03569)
* [PMC7247885](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7247885/)
* [arXiv:1804.11103](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11103)

statements.name: Erdos274.erdos_274
statements.doc:
If $G$ is a group, can there exist an exact covering of $G$ by more than one coset
of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one of the cosets.)

The conjectured answer is no: in every such exact covering, two of the subgroups have
the same cardinality.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_274 : ∃ (G : Type*) (_ : Group G),
    1 < ENat.card G ∧ ∃ (ι : Type*) (_ : Fintype ι) (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι),
    1 < Fintype.card ι ∧ ∀ i j, i ≠ j → #(P.parts i) ≠ #(P.parts j)

statements.name: Erdos274.erdos_274.variants.abelian
statements.doc:
If `G` is a finite abelian group then there cannot exist an exact covering of `G` by more
than one cosets of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one
of the cosets.)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_274.variants.abelian {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [CommGroup G]
    (hG : 1 < Fintype.card G) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι)
    (hι : 1 < Fintype.card ι) :
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ #(P.parts i) = #(P.parts j)

statements.name: Erdos274.herzog_schonheim
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a group, and let $A = \{a_1G_1, \dots, a_kG_k\}$ be a finite system of left cosets of
subgroups $G_1, \dots, G_k$ of $G$.

Herzog and Schönheim conjectured that if $A$ forms a partition of $G$ with $k > 1$, then the
indices $[G:G_1], \dots, [G:G_k]$ cannot be distinct.
statements.statement:
theorem herzog_schonheim {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : 1 < ENat.card G) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (hι : 1 < Fintype.card ι) (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι) :
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ (P.parts i).index = (P.parts j).index

problems.title: Erdős Problem 275
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/275](https://www.erdosproblems.com/275)
- [CrVE70] R.B. Crittenden and C.L. Vanden Eynden, *Any n arithmetic progressions covering the first
  2^n integers cover all integers*, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 24 (1970), 475-481.

statements.name: Erdos275.erdos_275
statements.doc:
If a finite system of $r$ congruences $\{ a_i\pmod{n_i} : 1\leq i\leq r\}$ (the $n_i$ are not
necessarily distinct) covers $2^r$ consecutive integers then it covers all integers.

This is best possible as the system $2^{i-1}\pmod{2^i}$ shows. This was proved independently by
Selfridge and Crittenden and Vanden Eynden [CrVE70].

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_275 (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → ℤ) (n : Fin r → ℕ)
    (H : ∃ k : ℤ, ∀ x ∈ Ico k (k + 2 ^ r), ∃ i, x ≡ a i [ZMOD n i]) (x : ℤ) :
    ∃ i, x ≡ a i [ZMOD n i]

problems.title: Erdős Problem 276
problems.doc:
*References:*
[erdosproblems.com/276](https://www.erdosproblems.com/276)

statements.name: Erdos276.erdos_276
statements.doc:
Is there an infinite Lucas sequence $a_0, a_1, \ldots$ where $a_{n+2} = a_{n+1} + a_n$ for
$n \ge 0$ such that all $a_k$ are composite, and yet no integer has a common factor with every
term of the sequence?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_276 :
    ∃ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
    IsLucasSequence a ∧ (∀ k, (a k).Composite) ∧ (∀ n > 1, ∃ k, Nat.gcd n (a k) = 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 277
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/277](https://www.erdosproblems.com/277)
- [Ha79] Haight, J. A., Covering systems of congruences, a negative result. Mathematika (1979),
  53--61.

statements.name: Erdos277.erdos_277
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for every $c$, there exists an $n$ such that $\sigma(n)>cn$ but there is no
covering system whose moduli all divide $n$?

This was answered affirmatively by Haight [Ha79].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_277 :
   ∀ c : ℝ, ∃ n : ℕ, (σ 1 n : ℝ) > c * n ∧
      ∀ (m : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ), ∃ i, (n : ℤ) ∉ m.moduli i

problems.title: Erdős Problem 279
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/279](https://www.erdosproblems.com/279)

statements.name: Erdos279.erdos_279
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 3$. Is there a choice of congruence classes $a_p\pmod{p}$ for every prime $p$
such that all sufficiently large integers can be written as $a_p+tp$ for some prime $p$
and integer $t\geq k$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_279 :  ∀ k : Nat, k ≥ 3 →
    ∃ a : Nat → Nat, ∃ N : Nat, (∀ p : Nat, p.Prime → a p < p) ∧
    ∀ n ≥ N, ∃ p : Nat, ∃ t ≥ k, p.Prime ∧ n = a p + t * p

problems.title: Erdős Problem 280
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/280](https://www.erdosproblems.com/280)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial
  number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).

statements.name: Erdos280.erdos_280
statements.doc:
Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots $ be an infinite sequence of integers with associated $a_k\pmod{n_k}$, such that for some $\epsilon>0$ we have $n_k>(1+\epsilon)k\log k$ for all $k$. Then
$$
\#\{ m<n_k : m\not\equiv a_i\pmod{n_i} \textrm{ for }1\leq i\leq k\}\neq o(k).
$$

Cambie observed that this is false.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_280 :
    ¬ ∀ (n a : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono n → (∀ i, 1 ≤ i → a i < n i) →
      (∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧
        ∀ k, 1 ≤ k → (n k : ℝ) > (1 + ε) * (k : ℝ) * Real.log (k : ℝ)) →
      ¬ Tendsto
        (fun k : ℕ => (uncoveredCount n a k : ℝ) / (k : ℝ))
        atTop (nhds 0)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 281
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/281](https://www.erdosproblems.com/281)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [DaEr36] Davenport, H. and Erdős, P., *On sequences of positive integers*. Acta
  Arithmetica (1936), 147-151.
- [HaRo66] Halberstam, H. and Roth, K. F., *Sequences. Vol. I*. (1966), xx+291.

statements.name: Erdos281.erdos_281
statements.doc:
Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots$ be an infinite sequence such that, for any choice of congruence classes
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$, the set of integers not satisfying any of the congruences $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ has
density $0$. Is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$ there exists some $k$ such that, for every
choice of congruence classes $a_i$, the density of integers not satisfying any of the congruences
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ is less than $\epsilon$?

The answer is yes; the linked Lean proof formalizes Somani's argument.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_281 :
    ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono n → (∀ i, 0 < n i) →
      (∀ a : ResidueChoice n, Set.HasIntDensity (avoidAll n a) 0) →
        ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
          ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ a : ResidueChoice n,
            ∃ d : ℝ, Set.HasIntDensity (avoidPrefix n a k) d ∧ d < ε

problems.title: Erdős Problem 282
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)

statements.name: Erdos282.erdos_282
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set and consider the following
greedy algorithm for a rational $x\in (0,1)$: choose the minimal $n\in A$ not used
so far such that $n\geq 1/x$ and repeat with $x$ replaced by $x-\frac{1}{n}$. If this
terminates after finitely many steps then this produces a representation of
$x$ as the sum of distinct unit fractions with denominators from $A$.

Does this process always terminate if $x$ has odd denominator and $A$ is the
set of odd numbers?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_282 {x : ℚ} (hx : x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) (hx_den : Odd x.den) :
    greedyUnitFractionRem { n | Odd n } x =ᶠ[atTop] 0

statements.name: Erdos282.erdos_282.variants.general
statements.doc: More generally, for which pairs $x$ and $A$ does this process terminate?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_282.variants.general (x : ℚ) (A : Set ℕ) :
      greedyUnitFractionRem A x =ᶠ[atTop] 0 ↔ (x, A) ∈ erdos_282.variants.general.answer

statements.name: Erdos282.erdos_282.variants.fibonacci
statements.doc: In 1202 Fibonacci observed that this process terminates for any $x$ when $A=\mathbb{N}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_282.variants.fibonacci {x : ℚ} (hx : x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) :
    greedyUnitFractionRem .univ x =ᶠ[atTop] 0

statements.name: Erdos282.erdos_282.variants.graham
statements.doc:
Graham has shown that $\frac{m}{n}$ is the sum of distinct unit fractions
with denominators $\equiv a\pmod{d}$ if and only if
$$\left(\frac{n}{(n,a,d)},\frac{d}{(a,d)}\right)=1.$$
Does the greedy algorithm always
terminate in such cases?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_282.variants.graham :
    ∀ x : ℚ, x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1 → ∀ a d : ℕ, 1 < d →
      (x.den / x.den.gcd (a.gcd d)).gcd (d / a.gcd d) = 1 →
      greedyUnitFractionRem { n | n ≡ a [MOD d] } x =ᶠ[atTop] 0

statements.name: Erdos282.erdos_282.variants.sq
statements.doc:
Graham has also shown that $x$ is the sum of distinct unit fractions with
square denominators if and only if $x\in [0,\pi^2/6-1)\cup [1,\pi^2/6)$. Does the
greedy algorithm for this always terminate? Erdős and Graham believe not - indeed, perhaps it
fails to terminate almost always.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_282.variants.sq :
    ∀ x : ℚ, (x : ℝ) ∈ Set.Ico 0 (π ^ 2 / 6 - 1) ∪ Set.Ico 1 (π ^ 2 / 6) →
      greedyUnitFractionRem { n | IsSquare n } x =ᶠ[atTop] 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 283
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/283](https://www.erdosproblems.com/283)
- [Al19] Alekseyev, Max A., On partitions into squares of distinct integers whose
reciprocals sum to 1. (2019), 213--221.
- [Ca60] Cassels, J. W. S., On the representation of integers as the sums of distinct summands taken from a fixed set. Acta Sci. Math. (Szeged) (1960), 111-124.
- [Gr63] Graham, R. L., A theorem on partitions. J. Austral. Math. Soc. (1963), 435-441.
- [vD25] W. van Doorn, Partitions with prescribed sum of rationals: asymptotic bounds. arXiv:2502.02200 (2025).

statements.name: Erdos283.erdos_283
statements.doc:
Let $p\colon \mathbb{Z} \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ be a polynomial (with rational coefficients,
taking integer values at all integers) whose leading coefficient is positive and such that there
exists no $d≥2$ with $d ∣ p(n)$ for all $n≥1$. Is it true that,
for all sufficiently large $m$, there exist integers $1≤n_1<\dots < n_k$ such that
$$1=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}$$
and
$$m=p(n_1)+\cdots+p(n_k)$$?

GPT 5.5 Pro (prompted by Price) has given a proof that the answer is yes, for the stronger version
with $1$ replaced by any rational $\alpha>0$.

This was formalized in Lean by Ammanamanchi using Opus 4.6 and GPT 5.5 Pro.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_283 : ∀ p : ℚ[X], Condition p

statements.name: Erdos283.erdos_283.variants.graham
statements.doc: Graham [Gr63] has proved this when $p(x)=x$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_283.variants.graham : Condition X

statements.name: Erdos283.erdos_283.variants.graham_alpha
statements.doc:
Graham also conjectures that this remains true with $1$ replaced by an arbitrary rational $\alpha>0$
(provided $m$ is taken sufficiently large depending on $\alpha$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_283.variants.graham_alpha :
  ∀ (p : ℚ[X]) (α : ℚ),
    (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ z : ℤ, p.eval (n : ℚ) = z) →
    0 < p.leadingCoeff →
    (¬ ∃ (d : ℤ), d ≥ 2 ∧ ∀ (n : ℤ), n ≥ 1 → ∃ z : ℤ, p.eval (n : ℚ) = d * z) →
    α > 0 →
    ∀ᶠ (m : ℕ) in atTop,
      ∃ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ S, 1 ≤ n) ∧
        (∑ n ∈ S, (1 / (n : ℚ))) = α ∧
        (∑ n ∈ S, p.eval (n : ℚ)) = (m : ℚ)

statements.name: Erdos283.erdos_283.variants.cassels
statements.doc:
Cassels [Ca60] has proved that these conditions on the polynomial imply every sufficiently large
integer is the sum of $p(n_i)$ with distinct $n_i$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_283.variants.cassels :
  ∀ (p : ℚ[X]),
    (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ z : ℤ, p.eval (n : ℚ) = z) →
    0 < p.leadingCoeff →
    (¬ ∃ (d : ℤ), d ≥ 2 ∧ ∀ (n : ℤ), n ≥ 1 → ∃ z : ℤ, p.eval (n : ℚ) = d * z) →
    ∀ᶠ (m : ℕ) in atTop,
      ∃ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ S, 1 ≤ n) ∧
        (∑ n ∈ S, p.eval (n : ℚ)) = (m : ℚ)

statements.name: Erdos283.erdos_283.variants.burr
statements.doc: Burr has proved this if $p(x)=x^k$ with $k\geq 1$ and if we allow $n_i=n_j$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_283.variants.burr :
  ∀ (k : ℕ), k ≥ 1 →
    ∀ᶠ (m : ℕ) in atTop,
      ∃ M : Multiset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ M, 1 ≤ n) ∧
        (M.map (fun n ↦ 1 / (n : ℚ))).sum = 1 ∧
        (M.map (fun n ↦ (n : ℤ)^k)).sum = (m : ℤ)

statements.name: Erdos283.erdos_283.variants.alekseyev
statements.doc: Alekseyev [Al19] has proved this when $p(x)=x^2$, for all $m>8542$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_283.variants.alekseyev :
  ∀ (m : ℕ), m > 8542 →
    ∃ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ S, 1 ≤ n) ∧
      (∑ n ∈ S, (1 / (n : ℚ))) = 1 ∧
      (∑ n ∈ S, (n : ℤ)^2) = (m : ℤ)

statements.name: Erdos283.erdos_283.variants.van_doorn_linear
statements.doc:
van Doorn [vD25] has investigated the question of what 'sufficiently large' means for $p(x)=x$.
van Doorn has also proved the original conjecture for many linear and quadratic polynomials.
For example, if $p(x) = x + b$ with $1 \leq b \leq 5000$, then the conjecture is true.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_283.variants.van_doorn_linear :
  ∀ b : ℤ, 1 ≤ b → b ≤ 5000 → Condition (X + C (b : ℚ))

statements.name: Erdos283.erdos_283.variants.van_doorn_quadratic
statements.doc:
van Doorn [vD25] has proved the original conjecture for many linear and quadratic polynomials.
For example, if $p(x) = x^2 + b$ with $1 \leq b \leq 800$, then the conjecture is true.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_283.variants.van_doorn_quadratic :
  ∀ b : ℤ, 1 ≤ b → b ≤ 800 → Condition (X^2 + C (b : ℚ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 284
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/284](https://www.erdosproblems.com/284)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique 28 (1980).
- [Cr01] Croot, III, Ernest S., *On unit fractions with denominators in short intervals*. Acta
  Arith. 99 (2001), 99-114. [arXiv:math/9904181](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9904181)

statements.name: Erdos284.erdos_284
statements.doc:
Let $f(k)$ be the maximal value of $n_1$ such that there exist $n_1<n_2<\cdots <n_k$ with
$$1=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}.$$
Is it true that
$$f(k)=(1+o(1))\frac{k}{e-1}?$$

Asked by Erdős and Graham [ErGr80, p. 33]. We state it as $f(k)/k\to 1/(e-1)$, which is
equivalent. Essentially solved by Croot [Cr01], who showed that for any $N>1$ there exists some
$k\geq 1$ and
$$N<n_1<\cdots <n_k \leq (e+o(1))N$$
with $1=\sum \frac{1}{n_i}$. See also [erdosproblems.com/286](https://www.erdosproblems.com/286).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_284 :
    Tendsto (fun k : ℕ ↦ (f k : ℝ) / k) atTop (nhds (1 / (Real.exp 1 - 1)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 285
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/285](https://www.erdosproblems.com/285)

statements.name: Erdos285.erdos_285
statements.doc:
Let $f(k)$ be the minimal value of $n_k$ such that there exist $n_1 < n_2 < \dots < n_k$ with
$$
  1 = \frac{1}{n_1} + \cdots + \frac{1}{n_k}.
$$
Is it true that
$$
  f(k) = (1 + o(1)) \frac{e}{e - 1} k ?
$$

Proved by Martin [Ma00].

[Ma00] Martin, Greg, _Denser Egyptian fractions_. Acta Arith. (2000), 231-260.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_285 :
    ∀ᵉ (f : ℕ → ℕ)
    (S : Set ℕ)
    (hS : S = {k | ∃ (n : Fin k.succ → ℕ), StrictMono n ∧ 0 ∉ Set.range n ∧
      1 = ∑ i, (1 : ℝ) / n i })
    (h : ∀ k ∈ S,
      IsLeast
        { n (Fin.last k) | (n : Fin k.succ → ℕ) (_ : StrictMono n) (_ : 0 ∉ Set.range n)
          (_ : 1 = ∑ i, (1 : ℝ) / n i) }
        (f k)),
    ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)),
      ∀ k ∈ S, f k = (1 + o k) * rexp 1 / (rexp 1 - 1) * (k + 1)

statements.name: Erdos285.erdos_285.variants.lb
statements.doc: It is trivial that $f(k)\geq (1 + o(1)) \frac{e}{e - 1}k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_285.variants.lb (f : ℕ → ℕ)
    (S : Set ℕ)
    (hS : S = {k | ∃ (n : Fin k.succ → ℕ), StrictMono n ∧ 0 ∉ Set.range n ∧
      1 = ∑ i, (1 : ℝ) / n i })
    (h : ∀ k ∈ S,
      IsLeast
        { n (Fin.last k) | (n : Fin k.succ → ℕ) (_ : StrictMono n) (_ : 0 ∉ Set.range n)
          (_ : 1 = ∑ i, (1 : ℝ) / n i) }
        (f k)) :
    ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)),
      ∀ k ∈ S, (1 + o k) * rexp 1 / (rexp 1 - 1) * (k + 1) ≤ f k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 286
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/286](https://www.erdosproblems.com/286)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Cr01] Croot, III, Ernest S., *On unit fractions with denominators in short intervals*. Acta
  Arith. (2001), 99-114.

statements.name: Erdos286.erdos_286
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 2$. Is it true that there exists an interval $I$ of width $(e-1+o(1))k$ and integers
$n_1<\cdots<n_k\in I$ such that
$$1=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}?$$

The answer is yes, proved by Croot [Cr01].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_286 : ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto o atTop (nhds 0) ∧
    ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, ∃ a b : ℝ, b - a = (exp 1 - 1 + o k) * k ∧
      ∃ S : Finset ℕ, S.card = k ∧ 0 ∉ S ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, (1 : ℝ) / n = 1 ∧
        ∀ n ∈ S, (n : ℝ) ∈ Set.Icc a b

problems.title: Erdős Problem 287
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/287](https://www.erdosproblems.com/287)

statements.name: Erdos287.erdos_287
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq2$. Is it true that, for any distinct integers
$1 < n_1 < \cdots < n_k$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{n_i} = 1$,
we must have $\max(n_{i+1} - n_i) \geq 3$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_287 :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (s : Fin k → ℕ),
    StrictMono s → 1 < s ⟨0, by omega⟩ →
    ∑ i : Fin k, 1/ (s i : ℝ) = 1 →
    3 ≤ max_gap k s

statements.name: Erdos287.erdos_287.variants.gap_at_least_two
statements.doc:
The lower bound of $\geq 2$ is equivalent to saying that $1$ is not the sum of reciprocals of
consecutive integers, proved by Erdős [Er32].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_287.variants.gap_at_least_two :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (_ : 2 ≤ k) (s : Fin k → ℕ),
    StrictMono s → 1 < s ⟨0, by omega⟩ →
    ∑ i : Fin k, 1 / (s i : ℝ) = 1 →
    2 ≤ max_gap k s

statements.name: Erdos287.erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture
statements.doc:
For all large $N$, there exists a prime $p \in [N, 2N]$ such that $\frac{p+1}{2}$ is also prime.

This is an open conjecture. If true, it would imply `erdos_287` for all but at most finitely
many exceptions (see `erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture_implies`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture :
    ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N →
      ∃ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p ∧ N ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 * N ∧ Nat.Prime ((p + 1) / 2)

statements.name: Erdos287.erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture_implies
statements.doc:
The conjecture `erdos_287` would follow for all but at most finitely many exceptions if it were
known that, for all large $N$, there exists a prime $p \in [N, 2N]$ such that $\frac{p+1}{2}$
is also prime.

More precisely: if the prime conjecture holds, then there exists $k_0$ such that for all
$k \geq k_0$, any Egyptian fraction representation of $1$ with $k$ terms and all terms $> 1$
must have $\max(n_{i+1} - n_i) \geq 3$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture_implies : type_of% erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture →
    ∃ (k₀ : ℕ), ∀ᵉ (k : ℕ) (hk₀ : k₀ ≤ k) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (s : Fin k → ℕ),
      StrictMono s → 1 < s ⟨0, by omega⟩ →
      ∑ i : Fin k, 1 / (s i : ℝ) = 1 →
      3 ≤ max_gap k s

problems.title: Erdős Problem 288
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/288](https://www.erdosproblems.com/288)

statements.name: Erdos288.erdos_288
statements.doc:
Is it true that there are only finitely many pairs of intervals $I_1$, $I_2$ such that
$$
\sum_{n_1 \in I_1} \frac{1}{n_1} + \sum_{n_2 \in I_2} \frac{1}{n_2} \in \mathbb{N}?
$$

statements.name: Erdos288.erdos_288.variants.i2_card_eq_1
statements.doc: This is still open even if $|I_2| = 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_288.variants.i2_card_eq_1 : Set.Finite { (I, n₂) : (ℕ+ × ℕ+) × ℕ+ |
    I.1 ≤ I.2 ∧ ∃ n : ℕ+, ∑ n₁ ∈ Set.Icc I.1 I.2, (n₁⁻¹ : ℚ) + (n₂⁻¹ : ℚ) = n }

statements.name: Erdos288.erdos_288.variants.k_intervals
statements.doc: It is perhaps true with two intervals replaced by any $k$ intervals.

statements.name: Erdos288.erdos_288.variants.exists_k_gt_2
statements.doc: Is it true for any $k > 2$ that only finitely many $k$ intervals satisfy this condition?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_288.variants.exists_k_gt_2 :
    ∃ k > 2, Set.Finite { I : Fin k → ℕ+ × ℕ+ |
      ∀ j, (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧
        ∃ n : ℕ+, (∑ j : Fin k, ∑ nⱼ ∈ Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2, (nⱼ⁻¹ : ℚ)) = n }

problems.title: Erdős Problem 289
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/289](https://www.erdosproblems.com/289)
- [Ku+26] Kung, P.-N., Song, L., Hwang, D., Yoon, J., Li, C.-L., Severini, S., Olšák, M.,
  Lockhart, E., Le, Q. V., Gokturk, B., Luong, T., Pfister, T., & Peng, N. (2026). _LEAP:
  Supercharging LLMs for Formal Mathematics with Agentic Frameworks_.
  [arXiv:2606.03303](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03303).

statements.name: Erdos289.erdos_289
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $k$, there exist finite intervals
$I_1, \dotsc, I_k \subset \mathbb{N}$, distinct, not overlapping or adjacent, with
$|I_i| \geq 2$ for $1 \leq i \leq k$ such that
$$
1 = \sum_{i=1}^k \sum_{n \in I_i} \frac{1}{n}?
$$
Here two intervals are adjacent if their union is again an interval, so any two of the
$I_i$ must be separated by at least one integer.

This is true: a formal proof in Lean 4 was produced by the LEAP prover agent [Ku+26]
(see the linked `formal_proof`). We note that other recent solutions were also posted ahead of
this one (see [erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/289/proof-claims](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/289/proof-claims));
this formalization follows an independent, different proof path.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_289 :
    (∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, ∃ I : Fin k → ℕ × ℕ,
    (∀ i, (I i).1 < (I i).2) ∧
    (∀ i j, i ≠ j → (I i).2 + 1 < (I j).1 ∨ (I j).2 + 1 < (I i).1) ∧
    ∑ i, ∑ n ∈ .Icc (I i).1 (I i).2, (n⁻¹ : ℚ) = 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 290
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/290](https://www.erdosproblems.com/290)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980), p.34.
- [vD24] van Doorn, W., *On the non-monotonicity of the denominator of generalized harmonic sums*.
  arXiv:2411.03073 (2024).

statements.name: Erdos290.erdos_290
statements.doc:
Let $a\geq 1$. Must there exist some $b>a$ such that
$$\sum_{a\leq n\leq b}\frac{1}{n}=\frac{r_1}{s_1}\textrm{ and }
\sum_{a\leq n\leq b+1}\frac{1}{n}=\frac{r_2}{s_2},$$
with $(r_i,s_i)=1$ and $s_2<s_1$? If so, how does this $b(a)$ grow with $a$?

This was resolved in the affirmative by van Doorn [vD24], who proved $b=b(a)$ always exists, and in
fact $b(a) \ll a$. Indeed, if $a\in (3^k,3^{k+1}]$ then one can take $b=2\cdot 3^{k+1}-1$. van Doorn
also proves that $b(a)>a+(1/2-o(1))\log a$, and considers various generalisations of the original
problem.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_290 :
    (∀ a : ℕ, 1 ≤ a → ∃ b : ℕ, a < b ∧ harmonicDen a (b + 1) < harmonicDen a b)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 291
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/291](https://www.erdosproblems.com/291)
- [ErGr80, p.34] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Sh16] P. Shiu, The denominators of harmonic numbers. arXiv:1607.02863 (2016).
- [WuYa22] Wu, Bing-Ling and Yan, Xiao-Hui, On the denominators of harmonic numbers. {IV}. C. R.
  Math. Acad. Sci. Paris (2022), 53--57.

statements.name: Erdos291.erdos_291.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $n\geq 1$ and define $L_n$ to be the least common multiple of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $a_n$ by
$\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}\frac{1}{k}=\frac{a_n}{L_n}$.

Is it true that $(a_n,L_n)=1$ occurs for infinitely many $n$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_291.parts.i :
    { n : ℕ | Nat.gcd (a n) (L n) = 1 }.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos291.erdos_291.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is it true that $(a_n,L_n)>1$ occurs for infinitely many $n$?

Steinerberger has observed that the answer to the second question is trivially yes: for example, any
$n$ which begins with a $2$ in base $3$ has $3\mid (a_n,L_n)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_291.parts.ii :
    { n : ℕ | Nat.gcd (a n) (L n) > 1 }.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos291.erdos_291.variants.steinerberger_generalization
statements.doc:
More generally, if the leading digit of $n$ in base $p$ is $p-1$ then $p\mid (a_n,L_n)$. There is
in fact a necessary and sufficient condition: a prime $p\leq n$ divides $(a_n,L_n)$ if and only if
$p$ divides the numerator of $1+\cdots+\frac{1}{k}$, where $k$ is the leading digit of $n$ in base
$p$. This can be seen by writing $a_n = \frac{L_n}{1}+\cdots+\frac{L_n}{n}$ and observing that the
right-hand side is congruent to $1+\cdots+1/k$ modulo $p$. (The previous claim about $p-1$ follows
immediately from Wolstenholme's theorem.)

statements.name: Erdos291.erdos_291.variants.shiu_heuristic_asymptotic
statements.doc:
This leads to a heuristic prediction (see for example a preprint of Shiu [Sh16]) of
$\asymp\frac{x}{\log x}$ for the number of $n\in [1,x]$ such that $(a_n,L_n)=1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_291.variants.shiu_heuristic_asymptotic :
    Asymptotics.IsTheta atTop
      (fun x : ℕ ↦ ((((Finset.Icc 1 x).filter (fun n ↦ Nat.gcd (a n) (L n) = 1)).card : ℝ)))
      (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ) / Real.log x)

statements.name: Erdos291.erdos_291.variants.shiu_heuristic_density_zero
statements.doc:
In particular, there should be infinitely many $n$, but the set of such $n$ should have
density zero. Unfortunately this heuristic is difficult to turn into a proof.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_291.variants.shiu_heuristic_density_zero :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦
      ((((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (fun n ↦ Nat.gcd (a n) (L n) = 1)).card : ℝ) / (N : ℝ)))
      atTop (nhds 0)

statements.name: Erdos291.erdos_291.variants.wu_yan
statements.doc:
Wu and Yan [WuYa22] have proved, conditional on $\frac{1}{\log p}$ being linearly independent
over $\mathbb{Q}$ for any finite collection of primes $p$ (itself a consequence of Schanuel's
conjecture), that the set of $n$ for which $(a_n,L_n)>1$ has upper density $1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_291.variants.wu_yan
    (h_indep : LinearIndependent ℚ (fun p : {p : ℕ // p.Prime} ↦ 1 / Real.log (p : ℝ))) :
    atTop.limsup (fun N : ℕ ↦
      ((((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (fun n ↦ Nat.gcd (a n) (L n) > 1)).card : ℝ) /
        (N : ℝ) : EReal)) = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 292
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/292](https://www.erdosproblems.com/292)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Ma00] Martin, Greg, *Denser Egyptian fractions*. Acta Arith. (2000), 231-260.

statements.name: Erdos292.erdos_292
statements.doc:
Let $A$ be the set of $n\in \mathbb{N}$ such that there exist $1\leq m_1<\cdots <m_k=n$ with
$\sum\tfrac{1}{m_i}=1$. Explore $A$. In particular, does $A$ have density $1$?

Straus observed that $A$ is closed under multiplication. Furthermore, it is easy to see that $A$
does not contain any prime power.

The answer is yes, as proved by Martin [Ma00], who in fact proved that if
$B=\mathbb{N}\backslash A$ then, for all large $x$,
$$\frac{\lvert B\cap [1,x]\rvert}{x}\asymp \frac{\log\log x}{\log x},$$
and also gave an essentially complete description of $B$ as those integers which are small
multiples of prime powers.

van Doorn has observed that if $n\in A$ (with $n>1$) then $2n\in A$ also, since if
$\sum \frac{1}{m_i}=1$ then $\frac{1}{2}+\sum\frac{1}{2m_i}=1$ also.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_292 : A.HasDensity 1

statements.name: Erdos292.erdos_292.variants.martin
statements.doc:
Martin [Ma00] proved that if $B=\mathbb{N}\backslash A$ then
$\frac{\lvert B\cap [1,x]\rvert}{x}\asymp \frac{\log\log x}{\log x}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_292.variants.martin :
    (fun x : ℕ ↦ ((Aᶜ ∩ Set.Icc 1 x).ncard : ℝ) / x) =Θ[atTop]
      fun x ↦ Real.log (Real.log x) / Real.log x

statements.name: Erdos292.erdos_292.variants.mul
statements.doc: Straus observed that $A$ is closed under multiplication.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_292.variants.mul : ∀ m ∈ A, ∀ n ∈ A, m * n ∈ A

statements.name: Erdos292.erdos_292.variants.prime_pow
statements.doc: $A$ does not contain any prime power.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_292.variants.prime_pow : ∀ n ∈ A, ¬ IsPrimePow n

statements.name: Erdos292.erdos_292.variants.two_mul
statements.doc: van Doorn observed that if $n\in A$ (with $n>1$) then $2n\in A$ also.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_292.variants.two_mul : ∀ n ∈ A, 1 < n → 2 * n ∈ A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 294
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/294](https://www.erdosproblems.com/294)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [LiSa24] Liu, Y. and Sawhney, M., *On further questions regarding unit fractions*.
  [arXiv:2404.07113](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.07113) (2024).

statements.name: Erdos294.erdos_294
statements.doc:
Let $N\geq 1$ and let $t(N)$ be the least integer $t$ such that there is no solution to
$$1=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}$$
with $t=n_1<\cdots <n_k\leq N$. Estimate $t(N)$.

Solved by Liu and Sawhney [LiSa24, Theorem 1.6] (up to $(\log\log N)^{O(1)}$), who proved that
$$\frac{N}{(\log N)(\log\log N)^3(\log\log\log N)^{O(1)}}\ll t(N) \ll \frac{N}{\log N}.$$
The unspecified $O(1)$ exponent is the real number `K`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_294 :
    (∃ K : ℝ, (fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ) / (Real.log N * Real.log (Real.log N) ^ 3 *
        Real.log (Real.log (Real.log N)) ^ K)) ≪ (fun N : ℕ => (t N : ℝ))) ∧
    ((fun N : ℕ => (t N : ℝ)) ≪ (fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ) / Real.log N))

statements.name: Erdos294.erdos_294.variants.erdos_graham_upper
statements.doc:
Erdős and Graham [ErGr80, p. 35] could show that $t(N)\ll\frac{N}{\log N}$. They gave no proof;
one is in [LiSa24, Section 4].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_294.variants.erdos_graham_upper :
    (fun N : ℕ => (t N : ℝ)) ≪ (fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ) / Real.log N)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 295
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/295](https://www.erdosproblems.com/295)

statements.name: Erdos295.exists_k
statements.doc:
Helper lemma: for each $N$, there exists $k$ and $n_1 < ... < n_k$ such that
$N ≤ n_1 < ⋯ < n_k$ with $\frac 1 {n_1} + ... + \frac 1 {n_k} = 1$.
statements.statement:
lemma exists_k (N : ℕ) : ∃ (k : ℕ) (n : Fin k → ℕ),
    (∀ i, N ≤ n i) ∧ StrictMono n ∧ ∑ i, (1 / n i : ℝ) = 1

statements.name: Erdos295.erdos_295
statements.doc:
Let $k(N)$ denote the smallest $k$ such that there exists
$N ≤ n_1 < ⋯ < n_k$ with $\frac 1 {n_1} + ... + \frac 1 {n_k} = 1$

Is it true that $\lim_{N \to \infty} k(N) - (e - 1)N = \infty$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_295 :
    Filter.atTop.Tendsto (fun N => k N - (rexp 1 - 1)*N) Filter.atTop

statements.name: Erdos295.erdos_295.variants.erdos_straus
statements.doc:
Erdős and Straus have proved the existence of some constant $c>0$
such that $-c < k(N)-(e-1)N \ll \frac N {\log N}$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_295.variants.erdos_straus :
    ∃ᵉ (C > 0) (O > 0), ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      (k N - (rexp 1 - 1)*N) ∈ Set.Ioc (-C) (O * N / (N : ℝ).log)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 296
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/296](https://www.erdosproblems.com/296)
- [Bl21] Bloom, T. F., *On a density conjecture about unit fractions*.
  arXiv:2112.03726 (2021).

statements.name: Erdos296.erdos_296
statements.doc:
Let $N\geq 1$ and let $k(N)$ be maximal such that there are $k$ disjoint $A_1,\ldots,A_k\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $\sum_{n\in A_i}\frac{1}{n}=1$ for all $i$. Estimate $k(N)$. Is it true that $k(N)=o(\log N)$?

Hunter and Sawhney observed that Bloom's theorem [Bl21], together with the greedy
argument, gives $k(N)=(1-o(1))\log N$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_296 :
    (∀ N k : ℕ, HasDisjointUnitDecomps N k → (k : ℚ) ≤ recipSum (Finset.Icc 1 N)) ∧
      (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε < 1 → ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop,
        HasDisjointUnitDecomps N ⌊(1 - ε) * Real.log N⌋₊)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 298
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/298](https://www.erdosproblems.com/298)
- [Bl21] Bloom, T. F., On a density conjecture about unit fractions. arXiv:2112.03726 (2021).

statements.name: Erdos298.erdos_298
statements.doc:
Does every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of positive density contain some finite $S \subset A$ such that
$\sum_{n \in S} \frac{1}{n} = 1$?

The answer is yes, proved by Bloom [Bl21] (even if 'positive density' is interpreted as 'positive
upper density', which is likely what Erdős intended).

The theorem below uses the positive-upper-density interpretation; the literal natural-density
interpretation is recorded separately.

This was formalized in Lean 3 by Bloom and Mehta.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_298 : (∀ (A : Set ℕ), 0 ∉ A → 0 < A.upperDensity →
    ∃ (S : Finset ℕ), ↑S ⊆ A ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, (1 / n : ℚ) = 1)

statements.name: Erdos298.erdos_298.variants.natural_density
statements.doc: The literal natural-density interpretation of Erdős Problem 298 follows from [Bl21].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_298.variants.natural_density : (∀ (A : Set ℕ), 0 ∉ A →
    A.HasPosDensity →
    ∃ (S : Finset ℕ), ↑S ⊆ A ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, (1 / n : ℚ) = 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 299
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/298](https://www.erdosproblems.com/298)
- [erdosproblems.com/299](https://www.erdosproblems.com/299)
- [Bl21] Bloom, T. F., On a density conjecture about unit fractions. arXiv:2112.03726 (2021).

statements.name: Erdos299.erdos_299
statements.doc:
Is there an infinite sequence $a_1 < a_2 < \dots$ such that $a_{i+1} - a_i = O(1)$ and no finite
sum of $\frac{1}{a_i}$ is equal to 1?

There does not exist such a sequence, which follows from the positive solution to
[erdosproblems.com/298] by Bloom [Bl21].

This was formalized in Lean 3 by Bloom and Mehta.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_299 : ¬ (∃ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
    StrictMono a ∧ (∀ n, 0 < a n) ∧
    (fun n ↦ (a (n + 1) : ℝ) - a n) =O[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ S : Finset ℕ, ∑ i ∈ S, (1 : ℝ) / a i ≠ 1)

statements.name: Erdos299.erdos_299.variants.density
statements.doc:
The corresponding question is also false if one replaces sequences such that $a_{i+1} - a_i = O(1)$
with sets of positive density, as follows from [Bl21].

The statement is as follows:
If $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ has positive upper density (and hence certainly if $A$ has positive
density) then there is a finite $S \subset A$ such that $\sum_{n \in S} \frac{1}{n} = 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_299.variants.density : ∀ (A : Set ℕ), 0 ∉ A → 0 < A.upperDensity →
    ∃ S : Finset ℕ, ↑S ⊆ A ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, (1 : ℝ) / n = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 300
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/300](https://www.erdosproblems.com/300)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference "Paul
  Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).
- [Cr03] Croot, III, Ernest S., *On a coloring conjecture about unit fractions*. Ann. of Math. (2)
  (2003), 545-556.
- [LiSa24] Liu, Y. and Sawhney, M., *On further questions regarding unit fractions*.
  arXiv:2404.07113 (2024).

statements.name: Erdos300.erdos_300
statements.doc:
Let $A(N)$ denote the maximal cardinality of $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that
$\sum_{n\in S}\frac{1}{n}\neq 1$ for all $S\subseteq A$. Estimate $A(N)$.

Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] believe the answer is $A(N)=(1+o(1))N$. Croot [Cr03] disproved this,
showing the existence of some constant $c<1$ such that $A(N)<cN$ for all large $N$. It is
trivial that $A(N)\geq (1-\frac{1}{e}+o(1))N$. Liu and Sawhney [LiSa24] have proved that
$A(N)=(1-1/e+o(1))N$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_300 : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => (A N : ℝ) / N) atTop (𝓝 (1 - 1 / Real.exp 1))

statements.name: Erdos300.erdos_300.variants.erdos_graham
statements.doc:
Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] believed that $A(N)=(1+o(1))N$; this was disproved by Croot
[Cr03].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_300.variants.erdos_graham :
    ¬ Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => (A N : ℝ) / N) atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 302
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/302](https://www.erdosproblems.com/302)
- [BrRo91] Brown, Tom C. and Rödl, Voijtech, Monochromatic solutions to equations with unit
  fractions. Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. (1991), 387-392.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [va25](https://github.com/Woett/Mathematical-shorts/blob/main/Two-colouring%20and%20density%20lead%20to%20solutions%20to%20an%20equation%20in%20unit%20fractions.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos302.erdos_302.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $f(N)$ be the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that there are no
solutions to
$$\frac{1}{a}= \frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}$$
with distinct $a,b,c\in A$? Estimate $f(N)$.

The colouring version of this is [303], which was solved by Brown and Rödl [BrRo91].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_302.parts.i (f : ℕ → ℕ) (hf : ∀ N, IsMaxNoTripleCard N (f N)) :
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => (f N : ℝ) / N) atTop (𝓝 erdos_302.parts.i.answer)

statements.name: Erdos302.erdos_302.parts.ii
statements.doc:
In particular, is $f(N)=(\tfrac{1}{2}+o(1))N$?

This is false: it is contradicted by Cambie's lower bound of $(5/8+o(1))N$ recorded below,
since $5/8 > 1/2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_302.parts.ii (f : ℕ → ℕ) (hf : ∀ N, IsMaxNoTripleCard N (f N)) :
    ¬ Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => (f N : ℝ) / N) atTop (𝓝 ((1 : ℝ) / 2))

statements.name: Erdos302.erdos_302.variants.lower_half
statements.doc:
One can take either $A$ to be all odd integers in $[1,N]$ or all integers in $[N/2,N]$ to show
$f(N)\geq (1/2+o(1))N$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_302.variants.lower_half (f : ℕ → ℕ) (hf : ∀ N, IsMaxNoTripleCard N (f N))
    (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ((1 : ℝ) / 2 - ε) * N ≤ f N

statements.name: Erdos302.erdos_302.variants.lower_five_eighths
statements.doc:
Stijn Cambie has observed that
$$f(N)\geq (5/8+o(1))N,$$
taking $A$ to be all odd integers $\leq N/4$ and all integers in $[N/2,N]$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_302.variants.lower_five_eighths (f : ℕ → ℕ) (hf : ∀ N, IsMaxNoTripleCard N (f N))
    (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ((5 : ℝ) / 8 - ε) * N ≤ f N

statements.name: Erdos302.erdos_302.variants.upper_nine_tenths
statements.doc:
Wouter van Doorn has proved [va25] that
$$f(N) \leq (9/10+o(1))N.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_302.variants.upper_nine_tenths (f : ℕ → ℕ) (hf : ∀ N, IsMaxNoTripleCard N (f N))
    (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (f N : ℝ) ≤ ((9 : ℝ) / 10 + ε) * N

statements.name: Erdos302.erdos_302.variants.upper_0_8461739827964010
statements.doc:
Kenta Kitamura (KitaKen1 on GitHub) has given a Lean proof
([erdos-302-upper-bound](https://github.com/KitaKen1/erdos-302-upper-bound)) that
$$f(N) \leq (0.8461739827964010+o(1))N.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_302.variants.upper_0_8461739827964010 (f : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hf : ∀ N, IsMaxNoTripleCard N (f N)) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (f N : ℝ) ≤ ((8461739827964010 : ℝ) / 10000000000000000 + ε) * N

problems.title: Erdős Problem 303
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/303](https://www.erdosproblems.com/303)
- [BrRo91] Brown, Tom C. and Rödl, Voijtech, Monochromatic solutions to equations with unit
  fractions. Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. (1991), 387-392.

statements.name: Erdos303.erdos_303
statements.doc:
Is it true that in any finite colouring of the integers there exists a monochromatic solution
to $\frac 1 a = \frac 1 b + \frac 1 c$ with distinct $a, b, c$?

This is true, as proved by Brown and Rödl [BrRo91].

This was formalized in Lean by Yuan using Seed-Prover.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_303 :
    -- For any finite colouring of the integers
    ∀ (𝓒 : ℤ → ℤ), (Set.range 𝓒).Finite →
      -- There exists integers `a, b, c`
      ∃ (a b c : ℤ),
      -- that are non-zero and distinct.
      [a, b, c, 0].Nodup ∧
      -- `a, b, c` satisfy the equation
      (1/a : ℝ) = 1/b + 1/c ∧
      -- `a, b, c` have the same color
      (𝓒 '' {a, b, c}).Subsingleton

problems.title: Erdős Problem 304
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/304](https://www.erdosproblems.com/304)

[OAI26a] OpenAI, *Short Egyptian fractions*. OpenAI Math Release preprint (2026).
https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/Short-Egyptian-fractions-September-25-2026/Short-Egyptian-fractions-September-25-2026.pdf

statements.name: Erdos304.erdos_304.variants.upper_1950
statements.doc:
In 1950, Erdős [Er50c] proved the upper bound $$N(b) \ll \log b / \log \log b$$.
[Er50c] Erdős, P., Az ${1}/{x_1} + {1}/{x_2} + \ldots + {1}/{x_n} =A/B$ egyenlet eg\'{E}sz sz\'{A}m\'{u} megold\'{A}sairól. Mat. Lapok (1950), 192-210.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_304.variants.upper_1950 :
    (fun b => (smallestCollectionTo b : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun b => Real.log b / Real.log (Real.log b))

statements.name: Erdos304.erdos_304.variants.lower_1950
statements.doc:
In 1950, Erdős [Er50c] proved the lower bound $$\log \log b \ll N(b)$$.
[Er50c] Erdős, P., Az ${1}/{x_1} + {1}/{x_2} + \ldots + {1}/{x_n} =A/B$ egyenlet eg\'{E}sz sz\'{A}m\'{u} megold\'{A}sairól. Mat. Lapok (1950), 192-210.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_304.variants.lower_1950 :
    (fun b : ℕ => Real.log (Real.log b)) =O[atTop]
      (fun b => (smallestCollectionTo b : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos304.erdos_304.variants.upper_1985
statements.doc:
In 1985 Vose [Vo85] proved the upper bound $$N(b) \ll \sqrt{\log b}$$.
[Vo85] Vose, Michael D., Egyptian fractions. Bull. London Math. Soc. (1985), 21-24.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_304.variants.upper_1985 :
    (fun b => (smallestCollectionTo b : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun b => Real.sqrt (Real.log b))

statements.name: Erdos304.upper_bound
statements.doc:
Is it true that $$N(b) \ll \log \log b$$?

Yes. This was proved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26a]; see the linked
Lean proof.
statements.statement:
theorem upper_bound :
    (fun b : ℕ => (smallestCollectionTo b : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun b : ℕ => Real.log (Real.log b))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 305
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/305](https://www.erdosproblems.com/305)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [BlEr76] Bleicher, M. N. and Erdős, P., *Denominators of unit fractions*. J. Number Th. (1976),
  157-168.
- [Yo88] Yokota, H., *On a problem of Bleicher and Erdős*. J. Number Theory (1988), 198-207.
- [LiSa24] Liu, Y. and Sawhney, M., *On further questions regarding unit fractions*.
  arXiv:2404.07113 (2024).

statements.name: Erdos305.erdos_305
statements.doc:
For integers $1\leq a<b$ let $D(a,b)$ be the minimal value of $n_k$ such that there exist
integers $1\leq n_1<\cdots <n_k$ with
$$\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}.$$
Estimate $D(b)=\max_{1\leq a<b}D(a,b)$. Is it true that
$$D(b) \ll b(\log b)^{1+o(1)}?$$

Bleicher and Erdős [BlEr76] have shown that $D(b)\ll b(\log b)^2$. If $b=p$ is a prime then
$D(p) \gg p\log p$.

This was solved by Yokota [Yo88], who proved that
$$D(b)\ll b(\log b)(\log\log b)^4(\log\log\log b)^2.$$
This was improved by Liu and Sawhney [LiSa24] to
$$D(b)\ll b(\log b)(\log\log b)^3(\log\log\log b)^{O(1)}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_305 : ∃ δ : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto δ atTop (nhds 0) ∧
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ b : ℕ in atTop,
      (Dmax b : ℝ) ≤ C * b * (log b) ^ (1 + δ b)

statements.name: Erdos305.erdos_305.variants.bleicher_erdos
statements.doc: Bleicher and Erdős [BlEr76] have shown that $D(b)\ll b(\log b)^2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_305.variants.bleicher_erdos : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    ∀ᶠ b : ℕ in atTop, (Dmax b : ℝ) ≤ C * b * (log b) ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos305.erdos_305.variants.prime_lower_bound
statements.doc: If $b=p$ is a prime then $D(p) \gg p\log p$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_305.variants.prime_lower_bound : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
    ∀ᶠ p : ℕ in atTop, p.Prime → c * p * log p ≤ Dmax p

statements.name: Erdos305.erdos_305.variants.yokota
statements.doc: Yokota [Yo88] proved that $D(b)\ll b(\log b)(\log\log b)^4(\log\log\log b)^2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_305.variants.yokota : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ b : ℕ in atTop,
    (Dmax b : ℝ) ≤ C * b * log b * log (log b) ^ 4 * log (log (log b)) ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos305.erdos_305.variants.liu_sawhney
statements.doc: Liu and Sawhney [LiSa24] proved that $D(b)\ll b(\log b)(\log\log b)^3(\log\log\log b)^{O(1)}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_305.variants.liu_sawhney : ∃ C K : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ b : ℕ in atTop,
