statements.name: Erdos409.erdos_409.parts.ii
statements.doc: Can infinitely many $n$ reach the same prime under the iteration $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_409.parts.ii :
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime), { n | ∃ i, (φ · + 1)^[i] n = p }.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos409.erdos_409.parts.iii
statements.doc: What is the density of $n$ which reach any fixed prime under the iteration $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_409.parts.iii (p : ℕ) (h : p.Prime) :
    { n | ∃ i, (φ · + 1)^[i] n = p }.HasDensity erdos_409.parts.iii.answer

statements.name: Erdos409.erdos_409.variants.sigma
statements.doc:
If the iteration $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ starting at $n > 1$ reaches a prime, how many
iterations are needed before a prime is reached?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_409.variants.sigma (n : ℕ) (hn : n > 1)
    (hterm : ∃ i, (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime) :
    IsLeast { i | (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } erdos_409.variants.sigma.answer

statements.name: Erdos409.erdos_409.variants.sigma_termination
statements.doc:
If $n > 1$ then the iteration $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ necessarily reaches a prime.
Note: this is open — it is not clear that the σ iteration always terminates,
since it is non-decreasing (unlike the φ iteration which is strictly decreasing).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_409.variants.sigma_termination (n : ℕ) (hn : n > 1) :
    ∃ i, (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime

statements.name: Erdos409.erdos_409.variants.sigma_isTheta
statements.doc:
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ before a prime

    (h : ∀ n > 1, IsLeast { i | (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) :
    (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_409.variants.sigma_isTheta.answer

statements.name: Erdos409.erdos_409.variants.sigma_isBigO
statements.doc:
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ before a prime

statements.statement:
theorem erdos_409.variants.sigma_isBigO (c : ℕ → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ n > 1, IsLeast { i | (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) :
    (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] erdos_409.variants.sigma_isBigO.answer

statements.name: Erdos409.erdos_409.variants.sigma_isLittleO
statements.doc:
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ before a prime
is reached. Find the simplest function $g(n)$ such that $c(n) = o(g(n))$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_409.variants.sigma_isLittleO (c : ℕ → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ n > 1, IsLeast { i | (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) :
    (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] erdos_409.variants.sigma_isLittleO.answer

statements.name: Erdos409.erdos_409.variants.sigma_prime_termination
statements.doc: Is it true that iterates of $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ always reach a prime?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_409.variants.sigma_prime_termination :
    ∀ n > 1, ∃ i, (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime

problems.title: Erdős Problem 410
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/410](https://www.erdosproblems.com/410)

statements.name: Erdos410.erdos_410
statements.doc:
Let $σ_1(n) = σ(n)$, the sum of divisors function, and $σ_k(n) = σ(σ_{k-1}(n))$.

Is it true that $\lim_{k → ∞} σ_k(n)^{\frac 1 k} = ∞$?

This is problem (iii) from
Erdos, Granville, Pomerance, Spiro
"On the normal behavior of the iterates of some arithmetical functions"
(page 169 of the book "Analytic Number Theory", 1990).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_410 : ∀ n > 1,
    Tendsto (fun k : ℕ ↦ ((sigma 1)^[k] n : ℝ) ^ (1 / (k : ℝ))) atTop atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 412
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/412](https://www.erdosproblems.com/412)

Reviewed by @b-mehta on 2025-05-27

statements.name: Erdos412.erdos_412
statements.doc:
Let $σ_1(n)=σ(n)$, the sum of divisors function, and $σ_k(n) = σ(σ_{k-1}(n))$.
Is it true that, for every $m, n ≥ 2$, there exist some $i, j$ such that $σ_i(m) = σ_j(n)$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_412 : ∀ᵉ (m ≥ 2) (n ≥ 2), ∃ i j, (σ 1)^[i] m = (σ 1)^[j] n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 413
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/413](https://www.erdosproblems.com/413)
- [A5236](https://oeis.org/A5236)
- [La26] Lau, C. F., *On the Number of Prime Factors of Consecutive Integers*.
  [arXiv:2604.15042](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15042) (2026).

Erdős called a natural number `n` a *barrier* for `ω`, the number of distinct prime divisors,
if `m + ω(m) ≤ n` for all `m < n`. He believed there should be infinitely many such barriers, and
even posed a relaxed variant asking whether there is some `ε > 0` for which infinitely many `n`
satisfy `m + ε · ω(m) ≤ n` for every `m < n`.

statements.name: Erdos413.erdos_413.parts.i
statements.doc: Are there infinitely many barriers for `ω`?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_413.parts.i :
    { n | IsBarrier (fun m => ω m) n }.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos413.erdos_413.variants.hasPosDensity_barrier_expProd
statements.doc:
Erdős proved that the barrier set for `expProd` is infinite and even has positive density.

`HasPosDensity` is the right reading rather than positive lower density. In [Er79d] this is
Theorem 1, "the density of integers satisfying (2) is positive", where `d₀(n) = ∏ αᵢ` is
`expProd`. The averaging argument there bounds the density below, but Erdős states the existence
separately on the last page: "With a little more trouble, I can prove that the density of
integers `n` for which `n` is a barrier for `d₀(n)` exists." He goes further, that if `αᵢ` is the
density of `n` with `max_{m<n} (m + d₀(m)) = n + i`, then every `αᵢ` exists and they sum to `1`.

[Er79d] Erdős, P., *Some unconventional problems in number theory*.
Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1979), 71-80.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_413.variants.hasPosDensity_barrier_expProd :
    { n | IsBarrier (fun m => expProd m) n }.HasPosDensity

statements.name: Erdos413.erdos_413.variants.bigOmega
statements.doc: Erdős believed there should be infinitely many barriers for `Ω`, the total prime multiplicity.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_413.variants.bigOmega :
    { n | IsBarrier (fun m => Ω m) n }.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos413.erdos_413.variants.bigOmega_largest_barrier_lt_100k
statements.doc: Selfridge computed that the largest `Ω`-barrier below `10^5` is `99840`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_413.variants.bigOmega_largest_barrier_lt_100k :
    IsGreatest {n : ℕ | n < 10 ^ 5 ∧ IsBarrier (fun m => Ω m) n} 99840

statements.name: Erdos413.erdos_413.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Does there exist some $\epsilon > 0$ such that there are infinitely many
$\epsilon$-barriers for $\omega$? Lau [La26, Theorem 1.3] gives a positive answer.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_413.parts.ii :
    (∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), { n | IsBarrier (fun n => ε * ω n) n }.Infinite)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 414
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/414](https://www.erdosproblems.com/414)

statements.name: Erdos414.erdos_414
statements.doc:
Let $h_1(n) = h(n)$ and $h_k(n) = h(h_{k-1}(n))$. Is it true, for any $m,n$, there exist
$i$ and $j$ such that $h_i(m) = h_j(n)$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_414 : ∀ᵉ  (m > 0) (n > 0), ∃ i j, h^[i] m = h^[j] n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 416
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/416](https://www.erdosproblems.com/416)
- [OAI26a] OpenAI, *An asymptotic formula for the number of totients*. OpenAI Math Release
  preprint (2026).
  https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/An-asymptotic-formula-for-the-number-of-totients-September-25-2026/An-asymptotic-formula-for-the-number-of-totients-September-25-2026.pdf

statements.name: Erdos416.erdos_416.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let `V(x)` count the number of `n≤x` such that `ϕ(m)=n` is solvable. Does `V(2x)/V(x)→2` ?

Yes. This was proved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26a]; see the linked
Lean proof, which gives `V(cx)/V(x)→c` for every fixed `c>0`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_416.parts.i :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun x => (V (2 * x) / V (x))) Filter.atTop (𝓝 2)

statements.name: Erdos416.erdos_416.variants.regularly_varying
statements.doc:
Let `V(x)` count the number of `n≤x` such that `ϕ(m)=n` is solvable. Then `V(cx)/V(x)→c` for
every fixed `c>0`, which answers a question of Erdős and Hall. This was proved by an internal
OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26a]; see the linked Lean proof.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_416.variants.regularly_varying (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun x => V (c * x) / V x) Filter.atTop (𝓝 c)

statements.name: Erdos416.erdos_416.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let `V(x)` count the number of `n≤x` such that `ϕ(m)=n` is solvable.
Is there an asymptotic formula for `V(x)`?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_416.parts.ii :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun x => V x / erdos_416.parts.ii.answer x) atTop (𝓝 1)

statements.name: Erdos416.erdos_416.variants.Pillai
statements.doc:
Let `V(x)` count the number of `n≤x` such that `ϕ(m)=n` is solvable.
Pillai proved `V(x)=o(x)`.
Ref: S. Sivasankaranarayana Pillai, _On some functions connected with $\phi(n)$_
statements.statement: theorem erdos_416.variants.Pillai : V =o[atTop] id

statements.name: Erdos416.erdos_416.variants.Erdos
statements.doc:
Let `V(x)` count the number of `n≤x` such that `ϕ(m)=n` is solvable.
Erdős proved V(x)=x(logx)^(−1+o(1)).
Ref: Erdős, P., _On the normal number of prime factors of $p-1$ and some related problems concerning Euler's $\varphi$-function._
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_416.variants.Erdos : ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, f =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ x in Filter.atTop, V x = x * x.log ^ (-1 + f x)

statements.name: Erdos416.erdos_416.variants.Maier_Pomerance
statements.doc:
Let `V(x)` count the number of `n≤x` such that `ϕ(m)=n` is solvable.
`V(x)=x/logx * e^((C+o(1))(log log log x)^2)`, for some explicit constant `C>0`.
Ref:Maier, Helmut and Pomerance, Carl, _On the number of distinct values of Euler's $\phi$-function_.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_416.variants.Maier_Pomerance :
    0 < erdos_416.variants.Maier_Pomerance.answer ∧ ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, f =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ) ∧
      ∀ᶠ x in Filter.atTop, (V x : ℝ) = x / x.log *
        (rexp <| (erdos_416.variants.Maier_Pomerance.answer + f x) * x.log.log.log ^ 2)

statements.name: Erdos416.erdos_416.variants.Ford
statements.doc:
Let `V(x)` count the number of `n≤x` such that `ϕ(m)=n` is solvable.
`V(x) ≍ x/log x*e^(C_1*(log log log x − log log log log x)^2+C_2 log log log x − C_3 log log log log x)`
Ref: Ford, Kevin, _The distribution of totients_.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_416.variants.Ford :
    let (C₁, C₂, C₃) : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ := erdos_416.variants.Ford.answer
    0 < C₁ ∧ 0 < C₂ ∧ 0 < C₃ ∧
    let G (x : ℝ) : ℝ := x / x.log * (rexp <| C₁ * (x.log.log.log - x.log.log.log.log) ^ 2
        + C₂* x.log.log.log - C₃ * x.log.log.log.log)
    V =Θ[atTop] G

problems.title: Erdős Problem 417
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/417](https://www.erdosproblems.com/417)
- [Er98] Erdős, Paul, Some of my new and almost new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory. Number theory (Eger, 1996) (1998), 169-180.

statements.name: Erdos417.erdos_417.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let$$V'(x)=\#\{\phi(m) : 1\leq m\leq x\}$$and$$V(x)=\#\{\phi(m) \leq x : 1\leq m\}.$$
Does $\lim V(x)/V'(x)$ exist?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_417.parts.i :
    ∃ L : ENNReal, Tendsto (fun x ↦
      ({ k | k ∈ range totient ∧ (k : ℝ) ≤ x }.ncard : ENNReal) /
      ((totient '' { m | 1 ≤ m ∧ (m : ℝ) ≤ x }).ncard : ENNReal))
      atTop (𝓝 L)

statements.name: Erdos417.erdos_417.parts.ii
statements.doc: Is it $>1$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_417.parts.ii :
    ∃ L > (1 : ENNReal), Tendsto (fun x ↦
      ({ k | k ∈ range totient ∧ (k : ℝ) ≤ x }.ncard : ENNReal) /
      ((totient '' { m | 1 ≤ m ∧ (m : ℝ) ≤ x }).ncard : ENNReal))
      atTop (𝓝 L)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 418
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/418](https://www.erdosproblems.com/418)
- [Wikipedia: Noncototient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noncototient)
- [BaLu05] Banks, William D. and Luca, Florian, Nonaliquots and {R}obbins numbers. Colloq. Math.
  (2005), 27--32.
- [BrSc95] Browkin, J. and Schinzel, A., On integers not of the form {$n-\phi(n)$}. Colloq. Math.
  (1995), 55-58.
- [ChZh11] Chen, Yong-Gao and Zhao, Qing-Qing, Nonaliquot numbers. Publ. Math. Debrecen (2011),
  439--442.
- [Er73b] Erdős, P., \"Über die Zahlen der Form $\sigma (n)-n$ und $n-\phi(n)$. Elem. Math.
  (1973), 83-86.
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
- [PoPo16] Pollack, Paul and Pomerance, Carl, Some problems of Erdős on the sum-of-divisors
  function. Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B (2016), 1-26.

statements.name: Erdos418.erdos_418
statements.doc:
Are there infinitely many integers not of the form $n - \phi(n)$?

Asked by Erdős and Sierpiński. Numbers not of the form we call non-cototients.

Browkin and Schinzel [BrSc95] provided an affirmative answer to this question, proving that any
integer of the shape $2^{k}\cdot 509203$ for $k\geq 1$ is a non-cototient.

This is discussed in problem B36 of Guy's collection [Gu04].

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_418 : { (n - n.totient : ℕ) | n }ᶜ.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos418.erdos_418.variants.conditional
statements.doc:
It follows from a slight strengthening of the Goldbach conjecture that every odd number can be
written as $n - \phi(n)$.
In particular, we assume that every even number greater than 6 can be written as the sum of two
*distinct* primes, in contrast to the usual Goldbach conjecture that every even number greater than
2 can be written as the sum of two primes.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_418.variants.conditional
    (goldbach : ∀ (n : ℕ), 6 < n → Even n → ∃ p q, p ≠ q ∧ p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ n = p + q)
    (m : ℕ) (h : Odd m) :
    ∃ n, m + n.totient = n

statements.name: Erdos418.erdos_418.variants.odd_noncototient
statements.doc:
The **Odd Noncototient Conjecture**: every non-cototient is even. Equivalently, every odd natural
number is of the form $n - \phi(n)$ for some $n$.

This is the unconditional form of `erdos_418.variants.conditional`, which derives the odd case from a
strengthening of the Goldbach conjecture. See [Wikipedia: Noncototient].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_418.variants.odd_noncototient :
    { (n - n.totient : ℕ) | n }ᶜ ⊆ { k | Even k }

statements.name: Erdos418.erdos_418.variants.sigma
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er73b] has shown that a positive density set of natural numbers cannot be written as
$\sigma(n)-n$ (numbers not of this form are called nonaliquot, or sometimes untouchable).

Here "positive density" means positive lower density: Banks and Luca [BaLu05] proved that the
set of nonaliquots has lower density at least $1/48$, Chen and Zhao [ChZh11] improved this to
$0.06$, and it is not known whether the natural density of the nonaliquots exists (Pollack and
Pomerance [PoPo16] give a heuristic predicting its value).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_418.variants.sigma :
    0 < { (σ 1 n - n : ℕ) | n }ᶜ.lowerDensity

statements.name: Erdos418.erdos_418.variants.soln
statements.doc:
A solution to erdos_418 was shown by Browkin and Schinzel [BrSc95] by showing that any integer of
the form $2^(k + 1)\cdot 509203$ is not of the form $n - \phi(n)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_418.variants.soln :
    { 2 ^ (k + 1) * 509203 | k } ⊆ { (n - n.totient : ℕ) | n }ᶜ

statements.name: Erdos418.erdos_418.variants.density
statements.doc: It is open whether the set of non-cototients has positive (lower) density.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_418.variants.density :
    0 < { (n - n.totient : ℕ) | n }ᶜ.lowerDensity

problems.title: Erdős Problem 419
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/419](https://www.erdosproblems.com/419)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [EGIP96] Erdős, Paul and Graham, S. W. and Ivić, Aleksandar and Pomerance, Carl,
  *On the number of divisors of $n!$*. (1996), 337--355.

statements.name: Erdos419.erdos_419
statements.doc:
If $\tau(n)$ counts the number of divisors of $n$, then what is the set of limit points of
$$
\frac{\tau((n+1)!)}{\tau(n!)}?
$$

The limit points are exactly $\{1\} \cup \{1+1/k : k \geq 1\}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_419 :
    {x : ℝ | MapClusterPt x atTop factorialDivisorRatio} = limitPointSet

problems.title: Erdős Problem 420
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/420](https://www.erdosproblems.com/420)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [EGIP96] Erdős, P. and Graham, S. W. and Ivić, A. and Pomerance, C., *On the number of divisors
  of $n!$*. Analytic number theory, Vol. 1 (Allerton Park, IL, 1995), Progr. Math. 138, Birkhäuser
  Boston (1996), 337-355.

In the solved variants, $K(n)$ is the least $K \geq 1$ with $\tau((n+K)!) \geq 2\tau(n!)$, so that
$K(n) > h$ if and only if $F(h, n) < 2$. These variants state Corollaries 2 and 3 of [EGIP96] as
printed; the stronger claims on erdosproblems.com are not stated.

statements.name: Erdos420.erdos_420.parts.i
statements.doc:
If $\tau(n)$ counts the number of divisors of $n$ then let
$$F(f,n)=\frac{\tau((n+\lfloor f(n)\rfloor)!)}{\tau(n!)}.$$
Is it true that
$$\lim_{n\to \infty}F((\log n)^C,n)=\infty$$
for large $C$?

"For large $C$" means for all sufficiently large real $C$. Since $(\log n)^C$ increases with $C$
for $n \geq 3$ and $F(f,n)$ is nondecreasing in $f(n)$, this is equivalent to asking for one
such $C$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_420.parts.i :
    ∀ᶠ C : ℝ in atTop, Tendsto (F fun m ↦ Real.log m ^ C) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos420.erdos_420.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is it true that $F(\log n,n)$ is everywhere dense in $(1,\infty)$?

This asks that every point of $(1,\infty)$ lies in the closure of the set of values
$F(\log n, n)$. Note that $F(f,n) \geq 1$ always (`Erdos420.one_le_F`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_420.parts.ii :
    Set.Ioi (1 : ℝ) ⊆ closure (Set.range (F fun m ↦ Real.log m))

statements.name: Erdos420.erdos_420.parts.iii
statements.doc:
More generally, if $f(n)\leq \log n$ is a monotonic function such that $f(n)\to \infty$ as
$n\to \infty$, then is $F(f,n)$ everywhere dense?

"Everywhere dense" means dense in $(1,\infty)$, as in `Erdos420.erdos_420.parts.ii`. Asking for
$f(n) \leq \log n$ for all $n$, rather than for all large $n$, gives an equivalent question.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_420.parts.iii :
    ∀ f : ℕ → ℝ, Monotone f → (∀ n, f n ≤ Real.log n) → Tendsto f atTop atTop →
      Set.Ioi (1 : ℝ) ⊆ closure (Set.range (F f))

statements.name: Erdos420.erdos_420.variants.log_frequently_lt_two
statements.doc:
Erdős, Graham, Ivić and Pomerance proved [EGIP96, Corollary 2] that $K(n)/\log n$ is unbounded,
with $K(n)$ as in the module docstring. Equivalently, for every $c > 0$ we have
$F(c\log n, n) < 2$ for infinitely many $n$. In particular
$\liminf F(c\log n, n) \leq 2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_420.variants.log_frequently_lt_two :
    ∀ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, F (fun m ↦ c * Real.log m) n < 2

statements.name: Erdos420.erdos_420.variants.rankin_frequently_lt_two
statements.doc:
Erdős, Graham, Ivić and Pomerance proved [EGIP96, Corollary 2] that for infinitely many $n$,
$$K(n) > \frac{\log n \cdot \log\log n \cdot \log\log\log\log n}{9(\log\log\log n)^3},$$
with $K(n)$ as in the module docstring. Equivalently,
$F(f,n) < 2$ for infinitely many $n$, where $f(n)$ is the right-hand side.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_420.variants.rankin_frequently_lt_two :
    ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, F (fun m ↦ Real.log m * Real.log (Real.log m) *
      Real.log (Real.log (Real.log (Real.log m))) /
        (9 * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log m)) ^ 3)) n < 2

statements.name: Erdos420.erdos_420.variants.pow_four_ninths
statements.doc:
Erdős, Graham, Ivić and Pomerance proved [EGIP96, Corollary 3] that for all sufficiently large
$n$ we have $K(n) < n^{4/9}$, with $K(n)$ as in the module docstring. Hence
$F(n^{4/9}, n) \geq 2$ for all large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_420.variants.pow_four_ninths :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, 2 ≤ F (fun m ↦ (m : ℝ) ^ (4 / 9 : ℝ)) n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 421
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/421](https://www.erdosproblems.com/421)
- [Pratt26] K. Pratt, [A proof of Erdős Problem 421](https://www.erdosproblems.com/static/421-Pratt.pdf).

statements.name: Erdos421.erdos_421
statements.doc:
There exists a sequence $1 \le d_1 < d_2 < \dots$ with density 1 such that all products
$\prod_{u \le i \le v} d_i$ are distinct. This was solved affirmatively; see [Pratt26].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_421 :
    ∃ (d : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono d ∧ 1 ≤ d 0 ∧ HasDensity (Set.range d) 1 ∧
    {(u, v) : ℕ × ℕ | u ≤ v}.InjOn fun (u, v) => ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc u v, d i

problems.title: Erdős Problem 422
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/422](https://www.erdosproblems.com/422)
- [OEIS A005185](https://oeis.org/A005185)

statements.name: Erdos422.erdos_422
statements.doc:
Let $f(1) = f(2) = 1$ and for $n > 2$
$$
f(n) = f(n - f(n - 1)) + f(n - f(n - 2)).
$$
Does $f(n)$ miss infinitely many integers?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_422 :
    ∀ f : ℕ+ → ℕ+, IsHofstadterQ f → Set.Infinite {n | ∀ x, f x ≠ n}

statements.name: Erdos422.erdos_422.variants.surjective
statements.doc: Is $f$ surjective?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_422.variants.surjective :
    ∀ f : ℕ+ → ℕ+, IsHofstadterQ f → f.Surjective

statements.name: Erdos422.erdos_422.variants.growth_rate
statements.doc: How does $f$ grow?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_422.variants.growth_rate :
    ∀ f : ℕ+ → ℕ+, IsHofstadterQ f →
    (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] erdos_422.variants.growth_rate.answer

statements.name: Erdos422.erdos_422.variants.eventually_const
statements.doc:
Does $f$ become stationary at some point?

No: see `IsHofstadterQ.not_eventuallyConst`. The statement is existential, so the answer does
not depend on whether $f(n)$ is well-defined for all $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_422.variants.eventually_const :
    ¬ ∃ f : ℕ+ → ℕ+, IsHofstadterQ f ∧ EventuallyConst f atTop

statements.name: Erdos422.erdos_422.variants.well_defined
statements.doc: Is $f(n)$ well-defined for all $n$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_422.variants.well_defined : ∃ f : ℕ+ → ℕ+, IsHofstadterQ f

problems.title: Erdős Problem 423
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/423](https://www.erdosproblems.com/423)
- [Er77c] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III*,
  Number theory day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976), 1977, pp. 43–72.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial
  number theory*, Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980).
- [Cu25] Cushman, A., *A Note on the Sum-Product Problem and the Convex Sumset Problem*.
  arXiv:2512.13849 (2025).
- [Ta26] Tang, Q., *The Hofstadter consecutive-sum sequence omits infinitely many positive
  integers*. arXiv:2603.09939 (2026).
- [Bolan] Bolan, M., *Hofstader–Ulam Sequence*,
  https://github.com/mjtb49/HofstaderUlam/blob/main/HofstaderUlamSequence.pdf
- [OEIS A005243](https://oeis.org/A005243)

statements.name: Erdos423.erdos_423
statements.doc:
Erdős Problem 423 [Er77c, p.71; ErGr80, p.83]:

Let $a(1) = 1$, $a(2) = 2$, and for $k \ge 3$ let $a(k)$ be the least integer greater
than $a(k-1)$ that is a sum of at least two consecutive terms of the sequence.
What is the asymptotic behaviour of this sequence? It seems likely that $a_n = n + o(n)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_423 :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsHofstadterSeq a →
    (fun n : ℕ => (a n : ℝ) - n) =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos423.erdos_423.variants.nondecreasing
statements.doc: Bolan and Tang [Ta26] independently proved that $a_n-n$ is nondecreasing.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_423.variants.nondecreasing :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsHofstadterSeq a →
    ∀ n m : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → n ≤ m → a n - n ≤ a m - m

statements.name: Erdos423.erdos_423.variants.unbounded
statements.doc: Bolan and Tang [Ta26] independently proved that $a_n-n\to\infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_423.variants.unbounded :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsHofstadterSeq a →
    ∀ M : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, M + n ≤ a n

statements.name: Erdos423.erdos_423.variants.infinite_complement
statements.doc:
Bolan and Tang [Ta26] independently proved that infinitely many positive integers do not occur in
the Hofstadter sequence.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_423.variants.infinite_complement :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsHofstadterSeq a → Set.Infinite (Set.range a)ᶜ

statements.name: Erdos423.erdos_423.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
Tang [Ta26] proved $a_n \ll n^{1/(c-1)+o(1)}$ whenever every finite convex set $A$ satisfies
$|A-A|\geq |A|^{c-o(1)}$. Using the bound of Cushman [Cu25] gives
$a_n\ll n^{688/413+o(1)}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_423.variants.upper_bound :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsHofstadterSeq a →
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), (fun n => (a n : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ ((688 : ℝ) / 413 + ε))

statements.name: Erdos423.erdos_423.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc: Tang [Ta26] proved the lower bound $a_n=n+\Omega(\log\log n)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_423.variants.lower_bound :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsHofstadterSeq a →
    (fun n : ℕ => Real.log (Real.log n)) =O[atTop]
      (fun n : ℕ => (a n : ℝ) - n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 424: Sequence generated by $a_i a_j - 1$
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/424](https://www.erdosproblems.com/424)
 - [A5244](https://oeis.org/A5244)
 - [Ben Green's Open Problem 63](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8 Problem 63)
 - [Ko26] Korsky, S., *A problem of Erdős on the sequence $a_ia_j - 1$*,
   [arXiv:2608.07910](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07910)

statements.name: Erdos424.erdos_424
statements.doc:
Let $a_1 = 2$ and $a_2 = 3$ and continue the sequence by appending to $a_1, \ldots, a_n$ all possible
values of $a_i a_j - 1$ with $i \neq j$.
Is it true that the set of integers which eventually appear has positive density?

As explained on [erdosproblems.com/424](https://www.erdosproblems.com/424), "positive density"
here means positive *lower* density: is there $c > 0$ such that for all large $x$ at least
$cx$ of the integers in $[1, x]$ appear? See `erdos_424.variants.exact_density` for the
literal reading.

The answer is yes: Korsky [Ko26] (with ChatGPT 5.6 Pro) proved that the set has positive lower
density. The linked formal proof (Alexeev and Codex) shows that there is `c > 0` with
`c * x ≤ #{n ∈ [1, x] | n ∈ generatedSet}` for all large `x`, which gives
`c / 2 ≤ generatedSet.lowerDensity`.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_424 : 0 < generatedSet.lowerDensity

statements.name: Erdos424.erdos_424.variants.exact_density
statements.doc:
A literal interpretation of "positive density": the natural density of `generatedSet` exists
(i.e. the lower and upper density agree) and is positive.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_424.variants.exact_density : generatedSet.HasPosDensity

problems.title: Erdős Problem 425
problems.doc: *Reference:* [Erdős Problem 425](https://www.erdosproblems.com/425)

statements.name: Erdos425.erdos_425.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $F(n)$ be the maximum size of a subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with distinct
pairwise products. Is there a constant $c > 0$ such that
$$F(n) = \pi(n) + (c + o(1)) n^{3/4}(\log n)^{-3/2}?$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_425.parts.i : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
    Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ =>
        ((pairProductExtremal n : ℝ) - (Nat.primeCounting n : ℝ)) /
          ((n : ℝ) ^ ((3 : ℝ) / 4) * (Real.log n) ^ (-(3 : ℝ) / 2)))
      atTop (𝓝 c)

statements.name: Erdos425.erdos_425.parts.ii
statements.doc:
If all products of $r$ distinct elements of $A \subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ are
distinct, must
$$|A| \leq \pi(n) + O\bigl(n^{(r+1)/(2r)}\bigr)?$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_425.parts.ii : ∀ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n → RProductsDistinct r A →
      (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (Nat.primeCounting n : ℝ) +
        C * (n : ℝ) ^ (((r : ℝ) + 1) / (2 * r))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 426
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/426](https://www.erdosproblems.com/426)
- [Er76b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Proceedings of the Fifth British Combinatorial Conference (1976), 169-192.
- [EnEr72] Entringer, R. C. and Erdős, Paul, *On the number of unique subgraphs of a graph*.
  J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. B (1972), 112-115.
- [HaSc73] Harary, Frank and Schwenk, Allen J., *On the number of unique subgraphs*.
  J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. B (1973), 156-160.
- [Br75] Brouwer, A. E., *Note: "On the number of unique subgraphs of a graph"
  (J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. B 13 (1972), 112-115) by R. C. Entringer and P. Erdős*.
  J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. B (1975), 184-185.
- [BrCh24] Bradač, D. and Christoph, M., *Unique subgraphs are rare*. arXiv:2410.16233 (2024).

statements.name: Erdos426.erdos_426
statements.doc:
We say $H$ is a unique subgraph of $G$ if there is exactly one way to find $H$ as a subgraph
(not necessarily induced) of $G$. Is there a graph on $n$ vertices with
$$\gg \frac{2^{\binom{n}{2}}}{n!}$$
many distinct unique subgraphs?

Bradač and Christoph [BrCh24] have proved the answer is no: if $f(n)$ is the maximum number of
unique subgraphs in a graph on $n$ vertices then
$$f(n) = o\left(\frac{2^{\binom{n}{2}}}{n!}\right).$$

The $\gg$ below is read as: some constant $c>0$ works for arbitrarily large $n$. The negation
of the proposition on the right is then exactly $f(n) = o(2^{\binom{n}{2}}/n!)$, the form in
which Bradač and Christoph [BrCh24] resolved the problem.

The linked file states the resolution in that negated form, as
`Tendsto fSeq atTop (nhds 0)`. It counts the isomorphism classes occurring as unique subgraphs,
whereas `uniqueSubgraphCount` counts their representatives $G\leq H$; uniqueness forces exactly
one representative per class, so the two counts agree.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_426 :
    ¬ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∃ H : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      c * ((2 : ℝ) ^ n.choose 2 / n.factorial) ≤ (uniqueSubgraphCount H : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 427
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/427](https://www.erdosproblems.com/427)

statements.name: Erdos427.erdos_427.variants.shiu
statements.doc:
**Shiu's theorem**: for any $k \geq 1$ and $(a, q) = 1$ there exist infinitely many $k$-tuples of consecutive primes
$p_m, \dots, p_{m + k - 1}$ all of which are congruent to $a$ modulo $q$.

This is stated ahead of `erdos_427` because the formal proof linked there assumes it, and the
`assuming` clause must name a declaration that already exists.

[Sh00] Shiu, D. K. L., _Strings of congruent primes_. J. London Math. Soc. (2) (2000), 359-373.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_427.variants.shiu : ShiuTheorem

statements.name: Erdos427.erdos_427
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 427**: is it true that, for every $n$ and $d$, there exists $k$ such that
$$
  d \mid p_{n + 1} + \cdots + p_{n + k},
$$
where $p_r$ denotes the $r$th prime?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_427 : erdos427

statements.name: Erdos427.erdos_427.variants.of_shiu
statements.doc: Cedric Pilatte has observed that a positive solution to Erdős Problem 427 follows from Shiu's theorem.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_427.variants.of_shiu (H : ShiuTheorem) : erdos427

problems.title: Erdős Problem 428
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/428](https://www.erdosproblems.com/428)

statements.name: Erdos428.erdos_428
statements.doc:
Is there a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that, for infinitely many $n$, all of $n-a$
are prime for all $a\in A$ with $0 < a < n$ and $$\liminf\frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{\pi(x)}>0?$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_428 :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ,
      (∃ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a → a < n → (n - a).Prime) ∧
      liminf (fun n ↦ primeDensityRatio A n) atTop > 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 429
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/429](https://www.erdosproblems.com/429)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*.
  Ann. Discrete Math. (1980), 89-115.
- [We24] D. Weisenberg, *Sparse Admissible Sets and a Problem of Erdős and Graham*.
  Integers (2024).

statements.name: Erdos429.erdos_429
statements.doc:
Is it true that, if $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is sparse enough and does not cover all residue
classes modulo $p$ for any prime $p$, then there exists some $n\in \mathbb{Z}$ such that $n+a$ is
prime for all $a\in A$?

Weisenberg [We24] has shown the answer is no: $A$ can be arbitrarily sparse and missing at
least one residue class modulo every prime $p$, and yet $A+n$ is not contained in the primes
for any $n\in \mathbb{Z}$. (Weisenberg gives several constructions of such an $A$.)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_429 :
    ¬ ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto f atTop atTop ∧
      ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → (∀ N, (A ∩ Set.Icc 1 N).ncard ≤ f N) →
        (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ b : ZMod p, ∀ a ∈ A, (a : ZMod p) ≠ b) →
        ∃ n : ℤ, ∀ a ∈ A, (n + a).toNat.Prime

problems.title: Erdős Problem 430
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/430](https://www.erdosproblems.com/430)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).

The question is equivalent to the first part of
[Erdős Problem 385](https://www.erdosproblems.com/385) (an observation of Sarosh Adenwalla
recorded on both problem pages).

statements.name: Erdos430.erdos_430
statements.doc:
Fix some integer $n$ and define a decreasing sequence in $[1,n)$ by $a_1=n-1$ and, for
$k\geq 2$, letting $a_k$ be the greatest integer in $[1,a_{k-1})$ such that all of the prime
factors of $a_k$ are $>n-a_k$.

Is it true that, for sufficiently large $n$, not all of this sequence can be prime?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_430 : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ¬ ∀ m ∈ terms n, m.Prime

problems.title: Erdős Problem 431
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/431](https://www.erdosproblems.com/431)
- [OAI26a] OpenAI, *The additive indecomposability of the primes*. OpenAI Math Release preprint
  (2026).
  https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/the-additive-indecomposability-of-the-primes-September-24-2026/paper.pdf

statements.name: Erdos431.erdos_431
statements.doc:
Are there two infinite sets $A$ and $B$ such that $A+B$ agrees with the primes up to finitely
many exceptions?

This was disproved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26a]; see the linked Lean
proof.

statements.name: Erdos431.erdos_431.variants.ostmann
statements.doc:
Ostmann's inverse Goldbach conjecture: if $A$ and $B$ each have at least two elements, then
$A+B$ differs from the primes in infinitely many elements.

This was proved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26a]; see the linked Lean
proof.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_431.variants.ostmann :
    ∀ A B : Set ℕ, A.Nontrivial → B.Nontrivial → ((A + B) ∆ {n | n.Prime}).Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 433
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Erdős Problem 433](https://www.erdosproblems.com/433)
- P. Erdős and R. L. Graham, *On a linear Diophantine problem of Frobenius*,
  Acta Arithmetica 21 (1972), 399–408.
- J. Dixmier, *Proof of a conjecture by Erdős and Graham on Frobenius' coin problem*,
  Proceedings of the AMS 109 (1990), 567–577.

statements.name: Erdos433.erdos_433
statements.doc:
For every fixed $k \geq 2$, Erdős and Graham conjectured that
$$g(k,n) \sim \frac{n^2}{k-1}.$$
The conjecture was proved by Dixmier [Di90].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_433 : ∀ k, 2 ≤ k →
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (g k n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) ^ 2 / ((k : ℝ) - 1))) atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 434
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/434](https://www.erdosproblems.com/434)
- [Ki02] Kiss, G., On the extremal Frobenius problem in a new aspect. Ann. Univ. Sci.
  Budapest. Eötvös Sect. Math. (2002), 139–142.

statements.name: Erdos434.erdos_434.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $k \le n$. What choice of $A\subseteq\{1, \dots, n\}$ (with $\text{gcd}(A) = 1$) of size $|A| = k$
maximises the number of integers not representable as the sum of finitely
many elements from $A$ (with repetitions allowed)?
Is it $\{n, n - 1, \dots, n - k + 1\}$?

The maximal choice is indeed $\{n, \dots, n - k + 1\}$, as proved by Kiss [Ki02].

The Lean theorem assumes $2 \le k$. When $k = 1 < n$, the proposed singleton $\{n\}$ does not
have gcd $1$; the gcd condition instead forces the unique admissible choice $A = \{1\}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_434.parts.i (n k : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (h : k ≤ n) :
    IsGreatest
      { Nat.NcardUnrepresentable S | (S : Finset ℕ) (_ : S ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n)
        (_ : #S = k) (_ : S.gcd id = 1) }
      (Nat.NcardUnrepresentable <| erdos_434.parts.i.answer n k)

statements.name: Erdos434.erdos_434.parts.ii
statements.doc:
For $2 \le k \le n$, the interval $A = \{n, n - 1, \dots, n - k + 1\}$ maximises the number
of integers not representable as the sum of finitely many elements from $A$ (with repetitions
allowed), as proved by Kiss [Ki02].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_434.parts.ii : ∀ᵉ (n ≥ 1) (k ≥ 2), k ≤ n →
    IsGreatest
      { Nat.NcardUnrepresentable S | (S : Finset ℕ) (_ : S ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n)
        (_ : #S = k) (_ : S.gcd id = 1)}
      (Nat.NcardUnrepresentable <| Set.Icc (n - k + 1 : ℕ) n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 435
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/435](https://www.erdosproblems.com/435)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [HwSo24] W. Hwang and K. Song, *The Frobenius problem for Numerical Semigroups generated by
  binomial coefficients*. arXiv:2412.17882 (2024).

statements.name: Erdos435.erdos_435
statements.doc:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $n\neq p^k$ for any prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$. What is the largest
integer not of the form
$$\sum_{1\leq i<n}c_i\binom{n}{i}$$
where the $c_i\geq 0$ are integers?

If $n=\prod p_k^{a_k}$ then the largest integer not of this form is
$$\sum_k \left( \sum_{1\leq d\leq a_k}\binom{n}{p_k^d}\right)(p_k-1)-n.$$
This was first proved by Hwang and Song [HwSo24]. Independently this was found in the comment
section by Peake and Cambie.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_435 (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0)
    (hpk : ∀ p k : ℕ, p.Prime → n ≠ p ^ k) :
    IsGreatest
      {m : ℤ | ¬ ∃ c : ℕ → ℕ, m = ∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n, (c i : ℤ) * (n.choose i : ℤ)}
      ((∑ p ∈ n.primeFactors,
        (∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n.factorization p), (n.choose (p ^ d) : ℤ)) * ((p : ℤ) - 1)) - n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 436
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/436](https://www.erdosproblems.com/436)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [LeLe62] Lehmer, D. H. and Lehmer, Emma, *On runs of residues*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1962),
  102-106.
- [LLMS62] Lehmer, D. H. and Lehmer, E. and Mills, W. H. and Selfridge, J. L., *Machine proof of a
  theorem on cubic residues*. Math. Comp. (1962), 407-415.
- [BiMi63] Bierstedt, R. G. and Mills, W. H., *On the bound for a pair of consecutive quartic
  residues of a prime*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1963), 628-632.
- [LLM63] Lehmer, D. H. and Lehmer, Emma and Mills, W. H., *Pairs of consecutive power residues*.
  Canadian J. Math. (1963), 172-177.
- [BLL64] Brillhart, John and Lehmer, D. H. and Lehmer, Emma, *Bounds for pairs of consecutive
  seventh and higher power residues*. Math. Comp. (1964), 397-407.
- [Gr64g] Graham, R. L., *On quadruples of consecutive $k$th power residues*. Proc. Amer. Math.
  Soc. (1964), 196-197.
- [Du65] Dunton, M., *Bounds for pairs of cubic residues*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1965),
  330-332.
- [Hi91] Hildebrand, Adolf, *On consecutive $k$th power residues. II*. Michigan Math. J. (1991),
  241-253.

statements.name: Erdos436.erdos_436.parts.i
statements.doc:
If $p$ is a prime and $k, m \geq 2$, let $r(k, m, p)$ be the minimal $r$ such that
$r, r + 1, \ldots, r + m - 1$ are all $k$th power residues modulo $p$, and let
$\Lambda(k, m) = \limsup_{p \to \infty} r(k, m, p)$. Is $\Lambda(k, 2)$ finite for all $k$?

A question of Lehmer and Lehmer [LeLe62]. Hildebrand [Hi91] proved that $\Lambda(k, 2)$ is finite
for all $k \geq 2$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_436.parts.i : ∀ k ≥ 2, Λ k 2 < ⊤

statements.name: Erdos436.erdos_436.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is $\Lambda(k, 3)$ finite for all odd $k$?

Lehmer, Lehmer, Mills and Selfridge [LLMS62] proved $\Lambda(3, 3) = 23532$. The question is open
for odd $k \geq 5$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_436.parts.ii : ∀ k ≥ 3, Odd k → Λ k 3 < ⊤

statements.name: Erdos436.erdos_436.variants.two_two
statements.doc: Lehmer and Lehmer [LeLe62] proved $\Lambda(2, 2) = 9$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_436.variants.two_two : Λ 2 2 = 9

statements.name: Erdos436.erdos_436.variants.three_two
statements.doc: Dunton [Du65] proved $\Lambda(3, 2) = 77$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_436.variants.three_two : Λ 3 2 = 77

statements.name: Erdos436.erdos_436.variants.four_two
statements.doc: Bierstedt and Mills [BiMi63] proved $\Lambda(4, 2) = 1224$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_436.variants.four_two : Λ 4 2 = 1224

statements.name: Erdos436.erdos_436.variants.five_two
statements.doc: Lehmer, Lehmer and Mills [LLM63] proved $\Lambda(5, 2) = 7888$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_436.variants.five_two : Λ 5 2 = 7888

statements.name: Erdos436.erdos_436.variants.six_two
statements.doc: Lehmer, Lehmer and Mills [LLM63] proved $\Lambda(6, 2) = 202124$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_436.variants.six_two : Λ 6 2 = 202124

statements.name: Erdos436.erdos_436.variants.seven_two
statements.doc: Brillhart, Lehmer and Lehmer [BLL64] proved $\Lambda(7, 2) = 1649375$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_436.variants.seven_two : Λ 7 2 = 1649375

statements.name: Erdos436.erdos_436.variants.three_three
statements.doc: Lehmer, Lehmer, Mills and Selfridge [LLMS62] proved $\Lambda(3, 3) = 23532$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_436.variants.three_three : Λ 3 3 = 23532

statements.name: Erdos436.erdos_436.variants.even_three
statements.doc: Lehmer and Lehmer [LeLe62] proved $\Lambda(k, 3) = \infty$ for all even $k$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_436.variants.even_three : ∀ k ≥ 2, Even k → Λ k 3 = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos436.erdos_436.variants.ge_four
statements.doc: Graham [Gr64g] proved $\Lambda(k, l) = \infty$ for all $k \geq 2$ and $l \geq 4$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_436.variants.ge_four : ∀ k ≥ 2, ∀ l ≥ 4, Λ k l = ⊤

problems.title: Erdős Problem 437
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/437](https://www.erdosproblems.com/437)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., _Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory_. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [BPZ24] Bui, Hung M. and Pratt, Kyle and Zaharescu, Alexandru, _A problem of
  Erdős-Graham-Granville-Selfridge on integral points on hyperelliptic curves_. Math. Proc.
  Cambridge Philos. Soc. (2024), 309--323.
- [Ta24] Tao, Terence, _A result of Bui–Pratt–Zaharescu, and Erdős problem #437_. Blog post
  (2024).

statements.name: Erdos437.erdos_437
statements.doc:
Let $1\leq a_1<\cdots<a_k\leq x$. How many of the partial products
$a_1,a_1a_2,\ldots,a_1\cdots a_k$ can be squares? Is it true that, for any $\epsilon>0$, there can
be more than $x^{1-\epsilon}$ squares?

The answer is yes, which follows from work of Bui, Pratt, and Zaharescu [BPZ24], as noted by
Tao [Ta24].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_437 :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (x : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε) < L x

statements.name: Erdos437.erdos_437.variants.little_o
statements.doc:
Erdős and Graham write it is 'trivial' that there are $o(x)$ many such squares, although this is
not quite trivial, using Siegel's theorem.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_437.variants.little_o :
    (fun x : ℕ ↦ (L x : ℝ)) =o[atTop] fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos437.erdos_437.variants.tao
statements.doc:
Tao [Ta24] shows that, if $u(x)=(\log x\log\log x)^{1/2}$, then
$$x\exp(-(2^{1/2}+o(1))u(x)) \leq L(x) \leq x\exp(-(2^{-1/2}+o(1))u(x)).$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_437.variants.tao :
    ∃ o₁ o₂ : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto o₁ atTop (nhds 0) ∧ Tendsto o₂ atTop (nhds 0) ∧
      ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
        x * exp (-(√2 + o₁ x) * √(log x * log (log x))) ≤ L x ∧
        L x ≤ x * exp (-((√2)⁻¹ + o₂ x) * √(log x * log (log x)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 438
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/438](https://www.erdosproblems.com/438)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [Er80c] Erdős, Paul, *Nine little known problems in combinatorial number theory*. Normat (1980),
  155-164, 180.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [LOS83] Lagarias, J. C. and Odlyzko, A. M. and Shearer, J. B., *On the density of sequences of
  integers the sum of no two of which is a square. II. General sequences*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A
  (1983), 123-139.
- [KLS02] Khalfalah, A. and Lodha, S. and Szemerédi, E., *Tight bound for the density of sequence
  of integers the sum of no two of which is a perfect square*. Discrete Math. (2002), 243-255.

statements.name: Erdos438.erdos_438
statements.doc:
How large can $A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, N\}$ be if $A + A$ contains no square numbers?

A problem of Erdős [Er80, Er80c, ErGr80]. Taking all integers $\equiv 1 \pmod 3$ gives
$|A| \ge N/3$, and Massias observed that all integers
$\equiv 1, 5, 9, 13, 14, 17, 21, 25, 26, 29, 30 \pmod{32}$ give $|A| \ge \frac{11}{32} N$.
Lagarias, Odlyzko and Shearer [LOS83] proved that $11/32$ is sharp for the modular version of the
problem, and Khalfalah, Lodha and Szemerédi [KLS02] proved that it is sharp in general: the
maximal such $A$ satisfies $|A| \le (\frac{11}{32} + o(1)) N$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_438 :
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ (extremalSize N : ℝ) / (N : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 ((11 : ℝ) / 32))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 440
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/440](https://www.erdosproblems.com/440)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., _Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory_. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [ErSz80] Erdős, Pál and Szemerédi, Endre, _Remarks on a problem of the American Mathematical
  Monthly_. Mat. Lapok (1980), 121-124.

statements.name: Erdos440.erdos_440.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be infinite and let $A(x)$ count the number of
indices for which $\mathrm{lcm}(a_i,a_{i+1})\leq x$. Is it true that $A(x) \ll x^{1/2}$?

The answer is yes: Tao has given a simple proof, and Erdős and Szemerédi [ErSz80] proved the
sharp bound $A(x)\leq (c+o(1))x^{1/2}$ (see `erdos_440.variants.erdos_szemeredi`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_440.parts.i :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a → (∀ i, 0 < a i) →
      (fun x : ℕ ↦ (count a x : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun x : ℕ ↦ √x

statements.name: Erdos440.erdos_440.parts.ii
statements.doc:
How large can
$$\liminf \frac{A(x)}{x^{1/2}}$$
be?

Taking $A=\mathbb{N}$ shows that $\liminf A(x)/x^{1/2}=1$ is possible. Erdős and Szemerédi
[ErSz80] proved that it is always $\leq 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_440.parts.ii :
    IsGreatest {l : ℝ | ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a ∧ (∀ i, 0 < a i) ∧
      l = liminf (fun x : ℕ ↦ (count a x : ℝ) / √x) atTop} erdos_440.parts.ii.answer

statements.name: Erdos440.erdos_440.variants.erdos_szemeredi
statements.doc:
Erdős and Szemerédi [ErSz80] proved that $A(x)\leq (c+o(1))x^{1/2}$ where
$$c=\sum_{n\geq 1}\frac{1}{n^{1/2}(n+1)}\approx 1.86,$$
and that this constant is best possible (this was later rediscovered by van Doorn).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_440.variants.erdos_szemeredi :
    IsGreatest {l : ℝ | ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a ∧ (∀ i, 0 < a i) ∧
      l = limsup (fun x : ℕ ↦ (count a x : ℝ) / √x) atTop} erdosSzemerediConstant

problems.title: Erdős Problem 441
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/441](https://www.erdosproblems.com/441)
- [Er51b] P. Erdős, *Problem*. Mat. Lapok (1951), 233.
- [Er65] Erdős, P., *Extremal problems in number theory*. Proc. Sympos. Pure Math., Vol. VIII
  (1965), 181-189.
- [Er73] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of
  combinatorial theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971)
  (1973), 117-138.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Er98] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my new and almost new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Number theory (Eger, 1996) (1998), 169-180.
- [Ch72b] Choi, S. L. G., *The largest subset in $[1,n]$ whose integers have pairwise L.C.M. not
  exceeding $n$*. Mathematika (1972), 221-230.
- [Ch98] Chen, Yong-Gao, *Sequences with bounded l.c.m. of each pair of terms*. Acta Arith.
  (1998), 71-95.
- [DaCh06] Dai, Li-Xia and Chen, Yong-Gao, *Sequences with bounded l.c.m. of each pair of terms.
  II*. Acta Arith. (2006), 315-326.
- [ChDa07] Chen, Yong-Gao and Dai, Li-Xia, *Sequences with bounded l.c.m. of each pair of terms.
  III*. Acta Arith. (2007), 125-133.
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.

statements.name: Erdos441.erdos_441
statements.doc:
Let $N\geq 1$. What is the size of the largest $A\subset \{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that $[a,b]\leq N$
for all $a,b\in A$, where $[a,b]$ is the least common multiple of $a$ and $b$?

Is it attained by choosing all integers in $[1,(N/2)^{1/2}]$ together with all even integers in
$[(N/2)^{1/2},(2N)^{1/2}]$?

Let $g(N)$ denote the size of the largest such $A$. The construction mentioned proves that
$g(N) \geq \left(\tfrac{9}{8}N\right)^{1/2}+O(1)$. Erdős [Er51b] proved
$g(N) \leq (4N)^{1/2}+O(1)$, which was improved by Choi [Ch72b]. Chen [Ch98] established the
asymptotic $g(N) \sim \left(\tfrac{9}{8}N\right)^{1/2}$. Chen and Dai [DaCh06] proved that
$$g(N)\leq \left(\tfrac{9}{8}N\right)^{1/2}+
O\left(\left(\frac{N}{\log N}\right)^{1/2}\log\log N\right).$$

In [ChDa07] the same authors prove that, infinitely often, Erdős' construction is not optimal: if
$B$ is that construction and $A$ is such that $\lvert A\rvert=g(N)$ then, for infinitely many
$N$, $\lvert A\rvert\geq \lvert B\rvert+t-2$, where $t\geq 0$ is defined such that the $t$-fold
iterated logarithm of $N$ is in $[0,1)$. (erdosproblems.com omits the $-2$; [ChDa07] proves
the bound with it.)

This is discussed in problems B26 and E2 of Guy's collection [Gu04].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_441 :
    ¬ ∀ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N → g N = (erdosConstruction N).card

statements.name: Erdos441.erdos_441.variants.chen_dai_infinitely_often
statements.doc:
Chen and Dai [ChDa07] proved that, infinitely often, Erdős' construction is not optimal: for
infinitely many $N$, $g(N) \geq \lvert B\rvert+t-2$, where $B$ is the construction and $t\geq 0$
is such that the $t$-fold iterated logarithm of $N$ is in $[0,1)$. (erdosproblems.com omits the
$-2$; [ChDa07] proves the bound with it.)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_441.variants.chen_dai_infinitely_often :
    ∃ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (erdosConstruction N).card + Real.iteratedLog N ≤ g N + 2

statements.name: Erdos441.erdos_441.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc: Erdős' construction proves that $g(N) \geq \left(\tfrac{9}{8}N\right)^{1/2}+O(1)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_441.variants.lower_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ, √(9 / 8 * N) - C ≤ g N

statements.name: Erdos441.erdos_441.variants.erdos_upper_bound
statements.doc: Erdős [Er51b] proved $g(N) \leq (4N)^{1/2}+O(1)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_441.variants.erdos_upper_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ, (g N : ℝ) ≤ √(4 * N) + C

statements.name: Erdos441.erdos_441.variants.chen
statements.doc: Chen [Ch98] established the asymptotic $g(N) \sim \left(\tfrac{9}{8}N\right)^{1/2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_441.variants.chen :
    (fun N : ℕ ↦ (g N : ℝ)) ~[atTop] fun N ↦ √(9 / 8 * N)

statements.name: Erdos441.erdos_441.variants.chen_dai_upper_bound
statements.doc:
Chen and Dai [DaCh06] proved that
$g(N)\leq \left(\tfrac{9}{8}N\right)^{1/2}+
O\left(\left(\frac{N}{\log N}\right)^{1/2}\log\log N\right)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_441.variants.chen_dai_upper_bound :
    (fun N : ℕ ↦ (g N : ℝ) - √(9 / 8 * N)) =O[atTop]
      fun N ↦ √(N / Real.log N) * Real.log (Real.log N)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 442
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/442](https://www.erdosproblems.com/442)

statements.name: Erdos442.erdos_442
statements.doc:
Let $\operatorname{Log} x := \max\{\log x, 1\}$,
$\operatorname{Log}_2x = \operatorname{Log} (\operatorname{Log} x)$, and
$\operatorname{Log}_3x = \operatorname{Log}(\operatorname{Log}(\operatorname{Log} x)).$
Is it true that if $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ is such that
$$
\frac{1}{\operatorname{Log}_2 x} \sum_{n\in A: n\leq x} \frac{1}{n}\to\infty
$$
then
$$
\left(\sum_{n\in A: n\leq x} \frac{1}{n}\right)^2 \sum_{n, m \in A: n < m \leq x}
\frac{1}{\operatorname{lcm}(n, m)}\to\infty
$$
as $x\to\infty$?

Tao [Ta24b] has shown this is false.

[Ta24b] Tao, T., _Dense sets of natural numbers with unusually large least common multiples_.
arXiv:2407.04226 (2024).

Note: the informal and formal statements follow the solution paper https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.04226
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_442 : ¬ ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
    Tendsto (fun (x : ℝ) =>
      1 / x.maxLogOne.maxLogOne * ∑ n ∈ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊ : Set ℕ), (1 : ℝ) / n) atTop atTop →
    Tendsto (fun (x : ℝ) => 1 / (∑ n ∈ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊ : Set ℕ), (1 : ℝ) / n) ^ 2 *
      ∑ nm ∈ A.bddProdUpper x, (1 : ℝ) / nm.1.lcm nm.2) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos442.erdos_442.variants.tao
statements.doc:
Tao resolved erdos_442 in the negative in Theorem 1 of https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.04226.
The following is a formalisation of that theorem with $C_0 = 1$.

Let $\operatorname{Log} x := \max\{\log x, 1\}$,
$\operatorname{Log}_2x = \operatorname{Log} (\operatorname{Log} x)$, and
$\operatorname{Log}_3x = \operatorname{Log}(\operatorname{Log}(\operatorname{Log} x)).$
There exists a set $A$ of natural numbers such that
$$
\sum_{n\in A: n\leq x} \frac{1}{n} =
  \exp\left(\left(\left(\frac{1}{2} + o(1)\right)\operatorname{Log}_2^{1/2}x \operatorname{Log}_3x\right)\right)
$$
and
$$
\sum_{n, m\in A: n, m\leq x} \frac{1}{\operatorname{lcm}(n, m)}\ll\left(\sum_{n\in A: n\leq x} \frac{1}{n}\right)^2
$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_442.variants.tao :
    ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (C: ℝ) (hC : 0 < C) (hf : f =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ)),
      ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in atTop,
        ∑ n ∈ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊ : Set ℕ), (1 : ℝ) / n =
          Real.exp ((1 / 2 + f x) * √x.maxLogOne.maxLogOne * x.maxLogOne.maxLogOne.maxLogOne) ∧
        |∑ nm ∈ ((A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊) ×ˢ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊)).toFinset, (1 : ℝ) / nm.1.lcm nm.2| ≤
          C * (∑ n ∈ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊ : Set ℕ), (1 : ℝ) / n) ^ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 443
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/443](https://www.erdosproblems.com/443)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [He25] Hegyvári, Norbert, *An elementary question of Erdős and Graham*.
  arXiv:2503.24201 (2025).

statements.name: Erdos443.erdos_443.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $m,n\geq 1$. What is
$$\# \{ k(m-k) : 1\leq k\leq m/2\} \cap \{ l(n-l) : 1\leq l\leq n/2\}?$$
Can it be arbitrarily large?

This was solved independently by Hegyvári [He25] and Cambie (unpublished), who show that if
$m>n$ then the set in question has size
$$\leq m^{O(1/\log\log m)},$$
and that for any integer $s$ there exist infinitely many pairs $(m,n)$ such that the set in
question has size $s$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_443.parts.i :
    ∀ s : ℕ, ∃ m n : ℕ, n < m ∧ s ≤ (A n ∩ A m).card

statements.name: Erdos443.erdos_443.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $m,n\geq 1$. What is
$$\# \{ k(m-k) : 1\leq k\leq m/2\} \cap \{ l(n-l) : 1\leq l\leq n/2\}?$$
Is it $\leq (mn)^{o(1)}$ for all sufficiently large $m,n$?

This was solved independently by Hegyvári [He25] and Cambie (unpublished), who show that if
$m>n$ then the set in question has size
$$\leq m^{O(1/\log\log m)},$$
and that for any integer $s$ there exist infinitely many pairs $(m,n)$ such that the set in
question has size $s$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_443.parts.ii :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ m n : ℕ, n₀ < n → n < m →
      ((A n ∩ A m).card : ℝ) < ((m : ℝ) * n) ^ ε

problems.title: Erdős Problem 444
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/444](https://www.erdosproblems.com/444)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [ErSa80] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A., *Some asymptotic formulas on generalized divisor functions.
  IV*. Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. (1980), 467-479.

statements.name: Erdos444.erdos_444
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be infinite and $d_A(n)$ count the number of $a\in A$ which divide $n$.
Is it true that, for every $k$,
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty} \frac{\max_{n<x}d_A(n)}{\left(\sum_{n\in A\cap[1,x)}\frac{1}{n}\right)^k}
=\infty?$$

This is asked in [ErGr80, p.88]. The answer is yes, proved by Erdős and Sárközy [ErSa80].

The maximum is over $1 \le n < x$, since every $a \in A$ divides $0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_444 : ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → ∀ k : ℕ,
    atTop.limsup (fun x : ℝ ↦ (((Ico 1 ⌈x⌉₊).sup (divisorCount A) /
      (∑ n ∈ Ico 1 ⌈x⌉₊ with n ∈ A, (n : ℝ)⁻¹) ^ k : ℝ) : EReal)) = ⊤

problems.title: Erdős Problem 445
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/445](https://www.erdosproblems.com/445)
- [He00] Heath-Brown, D. R., Arithmetic applications of {K}loosterman sums. Nieuw Arch. Wiskd. (5)
  (2000), 380--384.
- [MathOverflow](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/69509/small-residue-classes-with-small-reciprocal)

statements.name: Erdos445.erdos_445
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for any $c>1/2$, if $p$ is a sufficiently large prime then, for any
$n\geq 0$, there exist $a,b\in(n,n+p^c)$ such that $ab\equiv 1\pmod{p}$?

This is discussed in this MathOverflow question [MathOverflow].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_445 :
    ∀ c : ℝ, c > 1 / 2 →
      ∀ᶠ p : ℕ in atTop, p.Prime → ∀ n : ℕ, Erdos445Prop c p n

statements.name: Erdos445.erdos_445.variants.heilbronn
statements.doc: Heilbronn (unpublished) proved this for $c$ sufficiently close to $1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_445.variants.heilbronn :
    ∃ c₀ < 1, ∀ c : ℝ, c > c₀ →
      ∀ᶠ p : ℕ in atTop, p.Prime → ∀ n : ℕ, Erdos445Prop c p n

statements.name: Erdos445.erdos_445.variants.heath_brown
statements.doc: Heath-Brown [He00] used Kloosterman sums to prove this for all $c>3/4$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_445.variants.heath_brown :
    ∀ c : ℝ, c > 3 / 4 →
      ∀ᶠ p : ℕ in atTop, p.Prime → ∀ n : ℕ, Erdos445Prop c p n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 447
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/447](https://www.erdosproblems.com/447)
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [Kl71] Kleitman, Daniel, *Collections of subsets containing no two sets and their union*.
  Proceedings of the LA Meeting AMS (1971), 153-155.

statements.name: Erdos447.erdos_447.parts.i
statements.doc:
How large can a union-free collection $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[n]$ be? By union-free we mean
there are no solutions to $A\cup B=C$ with distinct $A,B,C\in \mathcal{F}$. Must
$\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert =o(2^n)$?

In [Er65b] Erdős reported that the estimate $\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert=o(2^n)$ was proved in
unpublished work by Sárközy and Szemerédi.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_447.parts.i :
    (fun n : ℕ => (maxUnionFree n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (2 : ℝ) ^ n)

statements.name: Erdos447.erdos_447.parts.ii
statements.doc:
How large can a union-free collection $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[n]$ be? By union-free we mean
there are no solutions to $A\cup B=C$ with distinct $A,B,C\in \mathcal{F}$. Perhaps even
$$\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert <(1+o(1))\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}?$$

Solved by Kleitman [Kl71], who proved
$$\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert <(1+o(1))\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_447.parts.ii :
    ∃ c : ℕ → ℝ, (c =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)) ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (maxUnionFree n : ℝ) < (1 + c n) * (n.choose (n / 2) : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 448
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/448](https://www.erdosproblems.com/448)
- [OEIS A397433](https://oeis.org/A397433): the integer sequence $\tau^+(n)$
  (the constant $\alpha$ in Ford's asymptotic is [OEIS A074738](https://oeis.org/A074738)).
- [Er79] Erdős, Paul, Some unconventional problems in number theory. Math. Mag. (1979), 67-70.
- [Er79e] Erdős, Paul, Some unconventional problems in number theory. Astérisque (1979), 73-82.
- [HaTe88] Hall, Richard R. and Tenenbaum, Gérald, Divisors. (1988), xvi+167.
- [ErTe81] Erdős, P., Tenenbaum, G., *Sur la structure de la suite des diviseurs d'un entier.*
  Ann. Inst. Fourier (Grenoble) **31** (1981), 17–37.
- [Fo08] Ford, Kevin, *The distribution of integers with a divisor in a given interval.*
  Ann. of Math. (2) **168** (2008), 367–433.
- [Te13] Tenenbaum, Gérald, *Some of Erdős' unconventional problems in number theory, thirty-four
  years later.* Erdős Centennial, Bolyai Soc. Math. Stud. **25** (2013), 651–681.

statements.name: Erdos448.erdos_448
statements.doc:
Let $\tau(n)$ count the divisors of $n$ and $\tau^+(n)$ count the number of $k$ such that $n$ has a
divisor in $[2^k, 2^{k+1})$. Is it true that, for all $\epsilon > 0$,
$$ \tau^+(n) < \epsilon \cdot \tau(n) $$
for almost all $n$?

This is false, and was disproved by Erdős and Tenenbaum [ErTe81], who showed that in fact the upper
density of the set of such $n$ is $\asymp \epsilon^{1-o(1)}$ (where the $o(1)$ in the exponent
$\to 0$ as $\epsilon \to 0$). A more precise result was proved by Hall and Tenenbaum [HaTe88]
(see Section 4.6), who showed that the upper density is $\ll \epsilon \log(2/\epsilon)$. Hall and
Tenenbaum further prove that $\tau^+(n)/\tau(n)$ has a distribution function. Erdős and Graham also
asked whether there is a good inequality known for $\sum_{n \leq x} \tau^+(n)$. This was provided by
Ford [Fo08] who proved
$$ \sum_{n \leq x} \tau^+(n) \asymp x\frac{(\log x)^{1-\alpha}}{(\log\log x)^{3/2}} $$
where
$$ \alpha = 1-\frac{1+\log\log 2}{\log 2} = 0.08607\cdots. $$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_448 :
    ¬ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
      {n : ℕ | (tauPlus n : ℝ) < ε * (n.divisors.card : ℝ)}.HasDensity 1

statements.name: Erdos448.erdos_448.variants.erdos_tenenbaum
statements.doc:
Quantitative form of the (negative) answer to `erdos_448`. Erdős and Tenenbaum [ErTe81] showed that
the upper density of $\{n : \tau^+(n) < \epsilon \cdot \tau(n)\}$ is in fact
$\asymp \epsilon^{1 - o(1)}$, where the $o(1)$ in the exponent tends to $0$ as $\epsilon \to 0$.
Equivalently, $\log(\text{upper density}) / \log \epsilon \to 1$ as $\epsilon \to 0^+$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_448.variants.erdos_tenenbaum :
    Tendsto
      (fun ε : ℝ =>
        Real.log ({n : ℕ | (tauPlus n : ℝ) < ε * (n.divisors.card : ℝ)}.upperDensity) / Real.log ε)
      (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 (1 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos448.erdos_448.variants.hall_tenenbaum_upper_bound
statements.doc:
A more precise result of Hall and Tenenbaum [HaTe88, §4.6]: the upper density of
$\{n : \tau^+(n) < \epsilon \cdot \tau(n)\}$ is $\ll \epsilon \cdot \log(2/\epsilon)$ as
$\epsilon \to 0^+$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_448.variants.hall_tenenbaum_upper_bound :
    (fun ε : ℝ => ({n : ℕ | (tauPlus n : ℝ) < ε * (n.divisors.card : ℝ)}).upperDensity)
      =O[𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)] (fun ε : ℝ => ε * Real.log (2 / ε))

statements.name: Erdos448.erdos_448.variants.hall_tenenbaum_distribution
statements.doc:
Hall and Tenenbaum [HaTe88] further prove that $\tau^+(n)/\tau(n)$ has a distribution function:
there is a distribution function `F` (non-decreasing, with $F(-\infty) = 0$ and $F(+\infty) = 1$)
such that, for every continuity point $z$ of `F`, the set $\{n : \tau^+(n)/\tau(n) \le z\}$ has
density `F z`. Tenenbaum [Te13] proved that `F` is continuous at $z = 1$ and asked to determine
its discontinuity points, if any.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_448.variants.hall_tenenbaum_distribution :
    ∃ F : ℝ → ℝ, Monotone F ∧ Tendsto F atBot (𝓝 0) ∧ Tendsto F atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      ∀ z : ℝ, ContinuousAt F z →
        {n : ℕ | (tauPlus n : ℝ) / (n.divisors.card : ℝ) ≤ z}.HasDensity (F z)

statements.name: Erdos448.erdos_448.variants.ford
statements.doc:
Erdős and Graham asked whether there is a good inequality for $\sum_{n \le x} \tau^+(n)$. This was
answered by Ford [Fo08], who proved
$$ \sum_{n \le x} \tau^+(n) \asymp x \cdot \frac{(\log x)^{1 - \alpha}}{(\log\log x)^{3/2}}, $$
where $\alpha = 1 - \frac{1 + \log\log 2}{\log 2} = 0.08607\ldots$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_448.variants.ford :
    (fun x : ℕ => ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 x, (tauPlus n : ℝ))
      =Θ[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ =>
        let α : ℝ := 1 - (1 + Real.log (Real.log 2)) / Real.log 2
        (x : ℝ) * Real.log (x : ℝ) ^ (1 - α)
          / Real.log (Real.log (x : ℝ)) ^ ((3 : ℝ) / 2))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 450
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/450](https://www.erdosproblems.com/450)

statements.name: Erdos450.erdos_450
statements.doc:
How large must $y=y(\epsilon,n)$ be such that the number of integers in
$(x,x+y)$ with a divisor in $(n,2n)$ is at most $\epsilon y$?

The bound is required for every $x$ and every window length at least $y$, and
$y(\epsilon,n)$ is the least such threshold (or $\infty$ if there is none).
A **linear** scale $y \le C(\epsilon) n$ is known to suffice for fixed $\epsilon$
and all large $n$ (see `erdos_450.linear_scale_suffices`).
statements.statement: theorem erdos_450 (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (n : ℕ) : windowThreshold ε n = erdos_450.answer

statements.name: Erdos450.erdos_450.linear_scale_suffices
statements.doc:
A translate-uniform **linear** scale suffices: there is a sufficient window
length `Y` with `Y ε n ≤ C(ε) · n`. This is an upper bound on the optimal scale,
not the exact threshold asked for in `erdos_450`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_450.linear_scale_suffices :
    ∃ Y : ℝ → ℕ → ℕ,
      (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, (Y ε n : ℝ) ≤ C * n) ∧ IsSufficientScale Y

problems.title: Erdős Problem 452
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/452](https://www.erdosproblems.com/452)

statements.name: Erdos452.erdos_452
statements.doc:
Determine the largest length of an interval in $[x,2x]$ on which
$\omega(n) > \log\log n$ everywhere.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_452 : largeOmegaIntervalLength = erdos_452.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 453
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/453](https://www.erdosproblems.com/453)
- [Er70b] Erdős, P., *Some applications of graph theory to number theory*. Proc. Second Chapel Hill
  Conf. on Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Univ. North Carolina, Chapel Hill, N.C.,
  1970) (1970), 136-145.
- [Er74b] Erdős, P., *Remarks on some problems in number theory*. Math. Balkanica (1974), 197-202.
- [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III*. Number theory day
  (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.
- [Po79] Pomerance, Carl, *The prime number graph*. Math. Comp. (1979), 399-408.

statements.name: Erdos453.erdos_453
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $n$, there exists some $i<n$ such that
$$
p_n^2 < p_{n+i}p_{n-i},
$$
where $p_k$ is the $k$th prime?

Pomerance proved that the answer is no.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_453 : ¬ EventuallyHasPrimeWitness

problems.title: Erdős Problem 454
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/454](https://www.erdosproblems.com/454)
 - [Po79] Pomerance, Carl, The prime number graph. Math. Comp. (1979), 399-408.

statements.name: Erdos454.erdos_454
statements.doc: Is it true that `limsup (fun n => (f n - 2 * n.nth Prime : ℕ∞)) atTop = ⊤`?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_454 : limsup (fun n => (f n - 2 * n.nth Prime : ℕ∞)) atTop = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos454.erdos_454.variants.two_le_limsup
statements.doc: `limsup (fun n => (f n - 2 * n.nth Prime : ℕ∞)) atTop ≥ 2`, and this is proved in [Po79].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_454.variants.two_le_limsup : 2 ≤ limsup (fun n => (f n - 2 * n.nth Prime : ℕ∞)) atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 455
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/455](https://www.erdosproblems.com/455)
 - [Ri76] Richter, Bernd, Über die Monotonie von Differenzenfolgen. Acta Arith. (1976), 225-227.

statements.name: Erdos455.erdos_455
statements.doc:
Let `q : ℕ → ℕ` be a strictly increasing sequence of primes such that
`q (n + 2) - q (n + 1) ≥ q (n + 1) - q n`. Must `lim q n / (n ^ 2) = ∞`?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_455: ∀ q : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono q →
    (∀ n, (q n).Prime ∧ q (n + 2) - q (n + 1) ≥ q (n + 1) - q n) →
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (q n : ℝ) / n ^ 2) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos455.erdos_455.variants.liminf
statements.doc:
Let `q : ℕ → ℕ` be a strictly increasing sequence of primes such that
`q (n + 2) - q (n + 1) ≥ q (n + 1) - q n`. Then `liminf q n / (n ^ 2) > 0.352`, and this is proved in
[Ri76].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_455.variants.liminf : ∀ q : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono q →
    (∀ n, (q n).Prime ∧ q (n + 2) - q (n + 1) ≥ q (n + 1) - q n) →
    liminf (fun n : ℕ => (q n : ℝ≥0∞) / n ^ 2) atTop > 0.352

problems.title: Erdős Problem 456
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/456](https://www.erdosproblems.com/456)
- [Er79e] Erdős, Paul, Some unconventional problems in number theory. Astérisque (1979), 73--82.

statements.name: Erdos456.erdos_456.parts.i
statements.doc: Is it true that $m_n<p_n$ for almost all $n$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_456.parts.i :
    Tendsto (fun N ↦ (count (fun n ↦ m n < p n) N : ℝ) / (N : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1)

statements.name: Erdos456.erdos_456.parts.ii
statements.doc: Does $p_n/m_n \to \infty$ for almost all $n$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_456.parts.ii :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, Tendsto (fun N ↦ (count (· ∈ A) N : ℝ) / (N : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n ↦ (p n : ℝ) / (m n : ℝ)) (atTop ⊓ 𝓟 A) atTop

statements.name: Erdos456.erdos_456.parts.iii
statements.doc: Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p-1$ is the only $n$ for which $m_n=p$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_456.parts.iii :
    { q | q.Prime ∧ ∀ n, m n = q ↔ n = q - 1 }.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos456.erdos_456.variants.linniks_theorem
statements.doc: Linnik's theorem implies that $p_n\leq n^{O(1)}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_456.variants.linniks_theorem :
    ∃ L : ℝ, (fun n ↦ (p n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ L)

statements.name: Erdos456.erdos_456.variants.mn_leq_pn
statements.doc: It is trivial that $m_n \leq p_n$ always.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_456.variants.mn_leq_pn (n : ℕ) :
    m n ≤ p n

statements.name: Erdos456.erdos_456.variants.infinitely_many_n
statements.doc: Erdős [Er79e] writes it is 'easy to show' that for infinitely many $n$ we have $m_n < p_n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_456.variants.infinitely_many_n :
    { n | m n < p n }.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos456.erdos_456.variants.m_div_n
statements.doc: Erdős [Er79e] writes it is 'easy to show' that $m_n/n \to \infty$ for almost all $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_456.variants.m_div_n :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, Tendsto (fun N ↦ (count (· ∈ A) N : ℝ) / N) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n ↦ (m n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)) (atTop ⊓ 𝓟 A) atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 457
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/457](https://www.erdosproblems.com/457)

statements.name: Erdos457.erdos_457
statements.doc:
Is there some $\epsilon > 0$ such that there are infinitely
many $n$ where all primes $p \le (2 + \epsilon) \log n$ divide
$$
  \prod_{1 \le i \le \log n} (n + i)?
$$

This was formalized in Lean by Baretto and van Doorn using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_457 : ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ),
    { (n : ℕ) | ∀ (p : ℕ), p ≤ (2 + ε) * Real.log n → p.Prime →
      p ∣ ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 ⌊Real.log n⌋₊, (n + i) }.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos457.erdos_457.variants.qnk
statements.doc:
More generally, let $q(n, k)$ denote the least prime which
does not divide $\prod_{1 \le i \le k}(n + i)$. This
problem asks whether $q(n, \log n) \ge (2 + \epsilon) \log n$
infinitely often.

This follows from `erdos_457`: if every prime $p \le (2 + \epsilon) \log n$
divides $\prod_{1 \le i \le \log n} (n + i)$, then $q(n, \log n)$, the least
prime not dividing this product, must exceed $(2 + \epsilon) \log n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_457.variants.qnk : ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ),
    { (n : ℕ) | (2 + ε) * Real.log n ≤ q n (Real.log n) }.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos457.erdos_457.variants.one_sub
statements.doc:
Taking $n$ to be the product of primes
between $\log n$ and $(2 + o(1)) \log n$ gives an example where
$$
  q(n, \log n) \ge (2 + o(1)) \log n.
$$
Can one prove that $q(n, \log n) < (1 - \epsilon) (\log n)^2$
for all large $n$ and some $\epsilon > 0$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_457.variants.one_sub : ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ),
    ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, q n (Real.log n) < (1 - ε) * Real.log n ^ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 458
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/458](https://www.erdosproblems.com/458)

statements.name: Erdos458.erdos_458
statements.doc:
Let $\operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, n)$ denote the least common multiple of $\{1, \dots, n\}$.
Let $p_k$ be the $k$-th prime.
Is it true that for all $k \geq 1$, $\operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, p_{k+1}-1) < p_k \cdot \operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, p_k)$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_458 :
    ∀ k : ℕ, lcm_upto ((k + 1).nth Prime - 1)
     < k.nth Prime * lcm_upto (k.nth Prime)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 459
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/459](https://www.erdosproblems.com/459)
- [ErGr80] P. Erdős and R. L. Graham, *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*, Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique 28 (1980), p.91.
- [OEIS A289280](https://oeis.org/A289280)

statements.name: Erdos459.erdos_459
statements.doc:
Let $f(u)$ be the largest $v$ such that no $m\in (u,v)$ is composed entirely of primes dividing
$uv$. Estimate $f(u)$.

The estimate $u + 2 \le f(u) \le u^2$ holds for every $u \ge 2$. The upper bound is attained
when $u$ is prime, and the lower bound when $u = 2^k - 2$ with $k \ge 2$; Cambie further showed
that $f(n) = (1 + o(1))n$ for almost all $n$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_459 {u : ℕ} (hu : 2 ≤ u) : u + 2 ≤ f u ∧ f u ≤ u ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos459.erdos_459.variants.upper_tight
statements.doc: The upper bound $f u ≤ u ^ 2$ is attained exactly when `u` is prime: $f p = p ^ 2$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_459.variants.upper_tight {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : f p = p ^ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 461
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/461](https://www.erdosproblems.com/461)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).

statements.name: Erdos461.erdos_461
statements.doc:
Let $s_t(n)$ be the $t$-smooth component of $n$ - that is, the product of all primes $p$ (with
multiplicity) dividing $n$ such that $p<t$. Let $f(n,t)$ count the number of distinct possible
values for $s_t(m)$ for $m\in [n+1,n+t]$. Is it true that
$$f(n,t)\gg t$$
(uniformly, for all $t$ and $n$)?

Erdős and Graham report they can show
$$f(n,t) \gg \frac{t}{\log t}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_461 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ n t : ℕ, c * (t : ℝ) ≤ (f n t : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 462
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/462](https://www.erdosproblems.com/462)

statements.name: Erdos462.erdos_462
statements.doc:
Let $p(n)$ denote the least prime factor of $n$. Is there a constant $C>0$ such that
$$\sum_{x\leq n\leq x+C\sqrt{x}(\log x)^2}\frac{p(n)}{n}\gg 1$$
for all sufficiently large $x$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_462 :
    ∃ C c : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
      c ≤ ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc x
        ⌊(x : ℝ) + C * Real.sqrt x * (Real.log x) ^ 2⌋₊, (n.minFac : ℝ) / n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 463
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/463](https://www.erdosproblems.com/463)

statements.name: Erdos463.erdos_463
statements.doc:
Is there a function $f$ with $f(n)\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ such that,
for all large $n$, there is a composite number $m$ such that
$$
n + f(n) < m < n + p(m)
$$
Here $p(m)$ is the least prime factor of $m$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_463 : ∃ (f : ℕ → ℕ) (_ : Tendsto f atTop atTop),
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∃ m, m.Composite ∧
        n + f n < m ∧ m < n + m.minFac

problems.title: Erdős Problem 464
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/464](https://www.erdosproblems.com/464)
- [Er75i] Erdős, P., *Répartition modulo $1$*. (1975), iv+258.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial
  number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980).
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*.
  (1982), 59--79.
- [AkMo04] Akhunzhanov, R. K. and Moshchevitin, N. G., *On the chromatic number of a distance
  graph associated with a lacunary sequence*. Dokl. Akad. Nauk (2004), 295-296.
- [Du06] Dubickas, Artūras, *On the fractional parts of lacunary sequences*. Math. Scand. (2006),
  136-146.
- [Ka01] Katznelson, Y., *Chromatic numbers of Cayley graphs on $\mathbb{Z}$ and recurrence*.
  Combinatorica (2001), 211-219.
- [PeSc10] Peres, Yuval and Schlag, Wilhelm, *Two Erdős problems on lacunary sequences: chromatic
  number and Diophantine approximation*. Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. (2010), 295-300.
- [Po79b] Pollington, A. D., *On the density of sequence $\{n_k\xi\}$*. Illinois J. Math. (1979),
  511-515.
- [dM80] de Mathan, B., *Numbers contravening a condition in density modulo $1$*. Acta Math.
  Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1980), 237-241 (1981).

statements.name: Erdos464.erdos_464
statements.doc:
Let $A=\{n_1<n_2<\cdots\}\subset \mathbb{N}$ be a lacunary sequence (so there exists some
$\epsilon>0$ with $n_{k+1}\geq (1+\epsilon)n_k$ for all $k$). Must there exist an irrational
