statements.name: Erdos663.erdos_663
statements.doc:
Let $k \geq 2$, and let $q(n,k)$ denote the least prime which does not divide
$\prod_{1 \leq i \leq k}(n+i)$. Is it true that, if $k$ is fixed and $n$ is sufficiently
large, then $q(n,k) < (1+o(1))\log n$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_663 : ∀ k ≥ 2, ∃ error : ℕ → ℝ,
    error =o[atTop] (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      let P : ℕ := ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i)
      ∃ q : ℕ, q.Prime ∧ ¬ q ∣ P ∧ (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ¬ p ∣ P → q ≤ p) ∧
        (q : ℝ) < (1 + error n) * Real.log n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 664
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/664](https://www.erdosproblems.com/664)
- [Er81] Erdős, P., _On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved_.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
- [Er97f] Erdős, Paul, _Some unsolved problems_. Combinatorics, geometry and probability
  (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.

statements.name: Erdos664.erdos_664
statements.doc:
Let $c<1$ be some constant and $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ be such that
$\lvert A_i\rvert >c\sqrt{n}$ for all $i$ and $\lvert A_i\cap A_j\rvert\leq 1$ for all $i\neq j$.

Must there exist some set $B$ such that $B\cap A_i\neq \emptyset$ and
$\lvert B\cap A_i\rvert \ll_c 1$ for all $i$?

The answer is no, proved by Alon: if $q$ is a large prime power and $n=m=q^2+q+1$ then there
exist $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that
$\lvert A_i\rvert \geq \tfrac{2}{5}\sqrt{n}$ for all $i$ and $\lvert A_i\cap A_j\rvert\leq 1$ for
all $i\neq j$, and yet if $B$ has non-empty intersection with all $A_i$ then there exists $A_j$
such that $\lvert B\cap A_j\rvert \gg \log n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_664 :
    ¬ ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → c < 1 → ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin m → Finset (Fin n)),
      (∀ i, c * √n < (A i).card) → (∀ i j, i ≠ j → (A i ∩ A j).card ≤ 1) →
        ∃ B : Finset (Fin n), (∀ i, (B ∩ A i).Nonempty) ∧
          ∀ i, (B ∩ A i).card ≤ K

statements.name: Erdos664.erdos_664.variants.two_fifths
statements.doc: Alon's counterexample already works for $c=2/5$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_664.variants.two_fifths :
    ¬ ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin m → Finset (Fin n)),
      (∀ i, 2 / 5 * √n < (A i).card) → (∀ i j, i ≠ j → (A i ∩ A j).card ≤ 1) →
        ∃ B : Finset (Fin n), (∀ i, (B ∩ A i).Nonempty) ∧
          ∀ i, (B ∩ A i).card ≤ K

statements.name: Erdos664.erdos_664.variants.block_design
statements.doc:
In [Er81] the condition $\lvert A_i\cap A_j\rvert\leq 1$ for all $i\neq j$ is replaced by every
two points in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ being contained in exactly one $A_i$, that is,
$A_1,\ldots,A_m$ is a pairwise balanced block design. The bound $\lvert A_i\rvert>c\sqrt{n}$ is
kept, only the condition $c<1$ is omitted. This weaker version remains open, although Alon
conjectures the answer there to also be no.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_664.variants.block_design :
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin m → Finset (Fin n)),
      (∀ i, c * √n < (A i).card) → (∀ x y : Fin n, x ≠ y → ∃! i, x ∈ A i ∧ y ∈ A i) →
        ∃ B : Finset (Fin n), (∀ i, (B ∩ A i).Nonempty) ∧
          ∀ i, (B ∩ A i).card ≤ K

problems.title: Erdős Problem 665
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/665](https://www.erdosproblems.com/665)
- [Er97f] Erdős, Paul, Some unsolved problems. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge,
  1993) (1997), 1-10.
- [ErLa82] Erdős, P. and Larson, J., On pairwise balanced block designs with the sizes of blocks as
  uniform as possible. Annals of Discrete Mathematics (1982), 129-134.
- [ShSi85] S. S. Shrikhande and N. M. Singhi, On a problem of Erdős and Larson. Combinatorica
  (1985), 351-358.

statements.name: Erdos665.erdos_665
statements.doc:
A pairwise balanced design for $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ is a collection of sets $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq
\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that $2\leq \lvert A_i\rvert <n$ and every pair of distinct elements $x,y\in
\{1,\ldots,n\}$ is contained in exactly one $A_i$. Is there a constant $C>0$ and, for all large $n$,
a pairwise balanced design such that
$$\lvert A_i\rvert > n^{1/2}-C$$
for all $1\leq i\leq m$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_665 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∃ H : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), H.IsPairwiseBalancedDesign ∧
      ∀ e ∈ H, e.card < n ∧ Real.sqrt n - C < e.card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 666
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/666](https://www.erdosproblems.com/666)
- [BDT93] Brouwer, A. E. and Dejter, I. J. and Thomassen, C., *Highly symmetric subgraphs of
  hypercubes*. J. Algebraic Combin. (1993), 25-29.
- [Ch92] Chung, Fan R. K., *Subgraphs of a hypercube containing no small even cycles*. J. Graph
  Theory (1992), 273-286.
- [Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991),
  397-406.

statements.name: Erdos666.erdos_666
statements.doc:
Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph (so that $Q_n$ has $2^n$ vertices and $n2^{n-1}$
edges). Is it true that, for every $\epsilon>0$, if $n$ is sufficiently large, every subgraph of
$Q_n$ with
$$\geq \epsilon  n2^{n-1}$$
many edges contains a $C_6$?

The answer to this problem is no: Chung [Ch92] and Brouwer, Dejter, and Thomassen [BDT93]
constructed an edge-partition of $Q_n$ into four subgraphs, each containing no $C_6$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_666 :
    ¬ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ H : SimpleGraph (Fin n → Bool), H ≤ hypercube n →
      ε * n * 2 ^ (n - 1 : ℕ) ≤ (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) → (cycleGraph 6 ⊑ H)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 667
problems.doc:
A problem of Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau, and Schelp on the growth exponent of the largest clique
that is guaranteed inside a locally dense graph.

*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/667](https://www.erdosproblems.com/667)
* [Er97f] P. Erdős, _Some unsolved problems_. In: Combinatorics, Geometry and Probability
  (Cambridge, 1993), Cambridge Univ. Press (1997), 1-10.
* [EFRS94] P. Erdős, R. J. Faudree, C. C. Rousseau and R. H. Schelp,
  _A local density condition for triangles_. Discrete Math. 127 (1994), 153-161.

statements.name: Erdos667.erdos_667
statements.doc:
Let $p, q \geq 1$ be fixed integers. Define $H(n) = H(n; p, q)$ to be the largest $m$ such that any
graph on $n$ vertices where every set of $p$ vertices spans at least $q$ edges must contain a
complete graph on $m$ vertices. Is
$$ c(p, q) = \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{\log H(n)}{\log n} $$
a strictly increasing function of $q$ for $1 \leq q \leq \binom{p-1}{2} + 1$?

A problem of Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau, and Schelp. When $q = 1$ this corresponds exactly to the
classical Ramsey problem, and hence $\tfrac{1}{p-1} \leq c(p, 1) \leq \tfrac{2}{p+1}$ for
$p \geq 3$. It is easy to see that if $q = \binom{p-1}{2} + 1$ then $c(p, q) = 1$.

erdosproblems.com/667 also states that Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp showed
$c(p, \binom{p-1}{2}) \leq 1/2$. This cannot hold for all $p$: for $p = 6$, $q = 10$, the
complement of a $(6, 10)$-locally dense graph is $C_6$-free, so Bondy–Simonovits together with
$\alpha(F) \geq n^2 / (2e(F) + n)$ gives $c(6, 10) \geq 2/3$. That remark is therefore not
formalised here.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_667 :
    ∀ p : ℕ, StrictMonoOn (c p) (Set.Icc 1 (Nat.choose (p - 1) 2 + 1))

statements.name: Erdos667.erdos_667.variants.monotoneOn
statements.doc:
That $c(p, q)$ is *nondecreasing* in $q$ for fixed $p$ is a straightforward consequence of the
definitions: enlarging $q$ shrinks the family of $(p, q)$-locally dense graphs, which can only
increase the guaranteed clique size $H(n)$, and hence the exponent.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_667.variants.monotoneOn (p : ℕ) :
    MonotoneOn (c p) (Set.Icc 1 (Nat.choose (p - 1) 2 + 1))

statements.name: Erdos667.erdos_667.variants.endpoint
statements.doc:
The right endpoint: when $q = \binom{p-1}{2} + 1$ one has $c(p, q) = 1$
(stated as "easy to see" on erdosproblems.com/667).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_667.variants.endpoint (p : ℕ) (hp : 2 ≤ p) :
    c p (Nat.choose (p - 1) 2 + 1) = 1

statements.name: Erdos667.erdos_667.variants.ramsey_bounds
statements.doc:
The case $q = 1$ is the classical Ramsey problem, giving the bounds
$\tfrac{1}{p-1} \leq c(p, 1) \leq \tfrac{2}{p+1}$ for $p \geq 3$. (For $p = 2$ the condition
forces $G$ to be complete, so $c(2, 1) = 1$ and the upper bound fails.)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_667.variants.ramsey_bounds (p : ℕ) (hp : 3 ≤ p) :
    1 / ((p : ℝ) - 1) ≤ c p 1 ∧ c p 1 ≤ 2 / ((p : ℝ) + 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 668
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/668](https://www.erdosproblems.com/668)
- [A385657](https://oeis.org/A385657)
- [AMP25] B. Alexeev, D. Mixon, and H. Parshall, *The Erdős unit distance problem for small point
  sets*. arXiv:2412.11914 (2025).
- [EHSVZ25] P. Engel, O. Hammond-Lee, Y. Su, D. Varga, and P. Zsámboki, *Diverse beam search to
  find densest-known planar unit distance graphs*. arXiv:2406.15317 (2025).
- [Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability
  (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.

statements.name: Erdos668.erdos_668.parts.i
statements.doc:
Is it true that the number of incongruent sets of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ which maximise the
number of unit distances tends to infinity as $n\to\infty$?

The actual maximal number of unit distances is the subject of
[Erdős Problem 90](https://www.erdosproblems.com/90).

Two sets of points are congruent if an isometry of the plane maps one onto the other.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_668.parts.i :
    ∀ m : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ A : Fin m → Finset ℝ²,
      (∀ i, (A i).card = n ∧ unitDistNum (A i) = maxUnitDistances n) ∧
      ∀ i j, i ≠ j → ¬ ∃ f : ℝ² ≃ᵢ ℝ², f '' A i = A j

statements.name: Erdos668.erdos_668.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is it always $>1$ for $n>3$?

In fact this is $=1$ also for $n=4$, the unique example given by two equilateral triangles joined
by an edge.

Computational evidence of Engel, Hammond-Lee, Su, Varga, and Zsámboki [EHSVZ25] and Alexeev,
Mixon, and Parshall [AMP25] suggests that this count is $=1$ for various other $5\leq n\leq 21$
(although these calculations were checking only up to graph isomorphism, rather than
congruency).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_668.parts.ii :
    ¬ ∀ n : ℕ, 3 < n → ∃ A B : Finset ℝ², A.card = n ∧ B.card = n ∧
      unitDistNum A = maxUnitDistances n ∧ unitDistNum B = maxUnitDistances n ∧
      ¬ ∃ f : ℝ² ≃ᵢ ℝ², f '' A = B

statements.name: Erdos668.erdos_668.variants.four_points
statements.doc:
For $n=4$ there is, up to congruence, exactly one set of points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ which maximises
the number of unit distances: two unit equilateral triangles $abc$ and $bcd$ joined by the edge
$bc$, with $a\neq d$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_668.variants.four_points :
    ∃ a b c d : ℝ², dist a b = 1 ∧ dist a c = 1 ∧ dist b c = 1 ∧ dist b d = 1 ∧ dist c d = 1 ∧
      ({a, b, c, d} : Finset ℝ²).card = 4 ∧
      ∀ B : Finset ℝ², B.card = 4 →
        (unitDistNum B = maxUnitDistances 4 ↔ ∃ f : ℝ² ≃ᵢ ℝ², f '' {a, b, c, d} = B)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 669
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/669](https://www.erdosproblems.com/669)
- [BGS74] Burr, Stefan A. and Grünbaum, Branko and Sloane, N. J. A., *The orchard problem*.
  Geometriae Dedicata (1974), 397-424.
- [Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability
  (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.

statements.name: Erdos669.erdos_669.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $F_k(n)$ be minimal such that for any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ there exist at most
$F_k(n)$ many distinct lines passing through at least $k$ of the points, and $f_k(n)$ similarly
but with lines passing through exactly $k$ points.

Estimate $f_k(n)$ and $F_k(n)$ - in particular, determine $\lim F_k(n)/n^2$ and
$\lim f_k(n)/n^2$.

This part asks for $\lim F_k(n)/n^2$ for $k \geq 3$ (the case $k = 2$ is trivial). The
original question [Er97f, Problem 16] asks for the limits "if they exist", so the answer allows
nonexistence: the answer at $k$ is `some x` if the limit exists and equals $x$, and `none`
otherwise.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_669.parts.i :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k → ∀ x : ℝ,
      erdos_669.parts.i.answer k = some x ↔
        Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (maxLinesAtLeast k n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 x)

statements.name: Erdos669.erdos_669.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $F_k(n)$ be minimal such that for any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ there exist at most
$F_k(n)$ many distinct lines passing through at least $k$ of the points, and $f_k(n)$ similarly
but with lines passing through exactly $k$ points.

Estimate $f_k(n)$ and $F_k(n)$ - in particular, determine $\lim F_k(n)/n^2$ and
$\lim f_k(n)/n^2$.

This part asks for $\lim f_k(n)/n^2$ for $k \geq 3$ (the case $k = 2$ is trivial). The
original question [Er97f, Problem 16] asks for the limits "if they exist", so the answer allows
nonexistence: the answer at $k$ is `some x` if the limit exists and equals $x$, and `none`
otherwise.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_669.parts.ii :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k → ∀ x : ℝ,
      erdos_669.parts.ii.answer k = some x ↔
        Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (maxLinesExactly k n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 x)

statements.name: Erdos669.erdos_669.variants.exactly_le_atLeast
statements.doc: Trivially $f_k(n)\leq F_k(n)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_669.variants.exactly_le_atLeast (k n : ℕ) :
    maxLinesExactly k n ≤ maxLinesAtLeast k n

statements.name: Erdos669.erdos_669.variants.k_two
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_669.variants.k_two (n : ℕ) :
    maxLinesExactly 2 n = n.choose 2 ∧ maxLinesAtLeast 2 n = n.choose 2

statements.name: Erdos669.erdos_669.variants.burr_grunbaum_sloane_exactly
statements.doc:
The problem with $k=3$ is the classical 'Orchard problem' of Sylvester. Burr, Grünbaum, and Sloane
[BGS74] have proved that
$$f_3(n)=\frac{n^2}{6}-O(n)$$
and
$$F_3(n)=\frac{n^2}{6}-O(n).$$

This is the statement for $f_3$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_669.variants.burr_grunbaum_sloane_exactly :
    (fun n : ℕ => (maxLinesExactly 3 n : ℝ) - (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 6) =O[atTop]
      (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos669.erdos_669.variants.burr_grunbaum_sloane_atLeast
statements.doc:
The problem with $k=3$ is the classical 'Orchard problem' of Sylvester. Burr, Grünbaum, and Sloane
[BGS74] have proved that
$$f_3(n)=\frac{n^2}{6}-O(n)$$
and
$$F_3(n)=\frac{n^2}{6}-O(n).$$

This is the statement for $F_3$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_669.variants.burr_grunbaum_sloane_atLeast :
    (fun n : ℕ => (maxLinesAtLeast 3 n : ℝ) - (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 6) =O[atTop]
      (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos669.erdos_669.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc: There is a trivial upper bound of $F_k(n) \leq \binom{n}{2}/\binom{k}{2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_669.variants.upper_bound (k n : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    (maxLinesAtLeast k n : ℝ) ≤ (n.choose 2 : ℝ) / (k.choose 2 : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos669.erdos_669.variants.limit_le
statements.doc:
There is a trivial upper bound of $F_k(n) \leq \binom{n}{2}/\binom{k}{2}$, and hence
$$\lim F_k(n)/n^2 \leq \frac{1}{k(k-1)}.$$
See also [101](https://www.erdosproblems.com/101).

Here the limit is assumed to exist and is called `L`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_669.variants.limit_le (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (L : ℝ)
    (hL : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (maxLinesAtLeast k n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 L)) :
    L ≤ 1 / ((k : ℝ) * ((k : ℝ) - 1))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 670
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/670](https://www.erdosproblems.com/670)
- [Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability
  (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
- [Ho26] Ho, B. S., *Erdős's diameter conjecture for separated distances fails in high
  dimensions*. [arXiv:2604.15305](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15305) (2026).

statements.name: Erdos670.erdos_670
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a set of $n$ points such that all pairwise distances differ by
at least $1$. Is the diameter of $A$ at least $(1+o(1))n^2$?

The quantifiers in the source are ambiguous. Following the remarks on erdosproblems.com, this is
the regime where $d$ is fixed and the $o(1)$ term tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$, at a rate
which may depend on $d$. The case $d = 1$ was proved by Erdős
(`Erdos670.erdos_670.variants.dim_one`), so the question is open for $d \geq 2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_670 :
    ∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), A.card = n → HasSeparatedDistances A →
        (1 - ε) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ Metric.diam (A : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))

statements.name: Erdos670.erdos_670.variants.dim_one
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er97f] proved the claim when $d = 1$: if $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a set of $n$ points
such that all pairwise distances differ by at least $1$, then the diameter of $A$ is at least
$(1+o(1))n^2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_670.variants.dim_one :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)), A.card = n → HasSeparatedDistances A →
        (1 - ε) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ Metric.diam (A : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)))

statements.name: Erdos670.erdos_670.variants.choose_two
statements.doc:
The trivial lower bound: if $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is a set of $n \neq 2$ points such that all
pairwise distances differ by at least $1$, then the diameter of $A$ is at least $\binom{n}{2}$.

For $n \geq 3$, take a closest pair $a, b$ and a third point $c$. Then
$1 \leq \lvert d(a, c) - d(b, c)\rvert \leq d(a, b)$, so every distance is at least $1$. The
$\binom{n}{2}$ distances are at least $1$ apart, so the largest one is at least $\binom{n}{2}$.
For $n = 2$ the hypothesis is vacuous, and two points at distance $1/2$ show that the bound fails.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_670.variants.choose_two (d : ℕ) (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))
    (hA : HasSeparatedDistances A) (hn : A.card ≠ 2) :
    (A.card.choose 2 : ℝ) ≤ Metric.diam (A : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))

statements.name: Erdos670.erdos_670.variants.ho
statements.doc:
Ho [Ho26] showed that the claim fails if $n$ grows with $d$: there exist infinitely many $n$
and, with $d = n^2 - n$, a set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ of $n$ points such that all pairwise
distances differ by at least $1$, with diameter at most
$$
\left(1-\frac{1}{\pi^2}+o(1)\right)n^2\approx 0.898n^2.
$$
Ho's construction uses $n = q + 1$ points in dimension $q^2 + q = n^2 - n$, for every prime power
$q$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_670.variants.ho :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∃ A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n ^ 2 - n))), A.card = n ∧
        HasSeparatedDistances A ∧
        Metric.diam (A : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n ^ 2 - n)))) ≤
          (1 - 1 / Real.pi ^ 2 + ε) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos670.erdos_670.variants.uniform_in_dim
statements.doc:
The version of the problem where the $o(1)$ term must be uniform in the dimension $d$ has a
negative answer. This follows from `Erdos670.erdos_670.variants.ho` (Ho [Ho26]).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_670.variants.uniform_in_dim :
    ¬ ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ d : ℕ,
      ∀ A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), A.card = n → HasSeparatedDistances A →
        (1 - ε) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ Metric.diam (A : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 672
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/672](https://www.erdosproblems.com/672)

statements.name: Erdos672.erdos_672
statements.doc:
Can the product of an arithmetic progression of positive integers $n, n + d, ..., n + (k - 1)d$
of length $k ≥ 4$, with $(n, d) = 1$, be a perfect power?

Erdős believed not, i.e. that `Erdos672With k l` holds for all $k ≥ 4$ and $l > 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_672 :
    ∃ᵉ (k ≥ 4) (l > 1), ¬ Erdos672With k l

statements.name: Erdos672.erdos_672.variants.euler
statements.doc: According to https://www.erdosproblems.com/672, Euler proved this.
statements.statement:
lemma erdos_672.variants.euler :
    Erdos672With 4 2

statements.name: Erdos672.erdos_672.variants.oblath
statements.doc:
According to https://www.erdosproblems.com/672, Obláth proved this.

[Ob51] Oblath, Richard, Eine Bemerkung über Produkte aufeinander folgender Zahlen.
J. Indian Math. Soc. (N.S.) (1951), 135-139.
statements.statement:
lemma erdos_672.variants.oblath :
    Erdos672With 5 2 ∧ Erdos672With 3 3 ∧ Erdos672With 3 4 ∧ Erdos672With 3 5

problems.title: Erdős Problem 673
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/673](https://www.erdosproblems.com/673)
- [Er79e] Erdős, Paul, _Some unconventional problems in number theory_. Astérisque (1979), 73-82.
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, _Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved_. (1982),
  59--79.

statements.name: Erdos673.erdos_673.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $1=d_1<\cdots <d_{\tau(n)}=n$ be the divisors of $n$ and
$$G(n) = \sum_{1\leq i<\tau(n)}\frac{d_i}{d_{i+1}}.$$
Is it true that $G(n)\to \infty$ for almost all $n$?

The answer is yes: Tao observed that $\tau(n/m)/m\leq G(n)\leq \tau(n)$ for any $m\mid n$ with
$m>1$, so that $G(n)$ behaves very similarly to $\tau(n)$. In [Er82e] Erdős recalls this
conjecture and observes that it is indeed trivial that $G(n)\to \infty$ for almost all $n$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_673.parts.i : ∀ C : ℝ, {n : ℕ | C < G n}.HasDensity 1

statements.name: Erdos673.erdos_673.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Can one prove an asymptotic formula for $\sum_{n\leq X}G(n)$?

Indeed $\sum_{n\leq X}G(n)\sim X\log X$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_673.parts.ii :
    (fun X : ℕ ↦ ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 X, G n) ~[atTop] fun X : ℕ ↦ (X : ℝ) * log X

statements.name: Erdos673.erdos_673.variants.average
statements.doc: Erdős writes it is 'easy' to prove $\frac{1}{X}\sum_{n\leq X}G(n)\to \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_673.variants.average :
    Tendsto (fun X : ℕ ↦ (∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 X, G n) / X) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos673.erdos_673.variants.tao
statements.doc:
Tao observed that, for any divisor $m\mid n$ with $m>1$,
$\frac{\tau(n/m)}{m} \leq G(n) \leq \tau(n)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_673.variants.tao (n m : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hm : 1 < m) (hmn : m ∣ n) :
    ((n / m).divisors.card : ℝ) / m ≤ G n ∧ G n ≤ n.divisors.card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 674
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/674](https://www.erdosproblems.com/674)
- [Ko40] Ko, Chao, *Note on the Diophantine equation $x^xy^y=z^z$*. J. Chinese Math. Soc.
  (1940), 31-39.

statements.name: Erdos674.erdos_674
statements.doc:
Are there any integer solutions to $x^xy^y=z^z$ with $x,y,z>1$?

Ko [Ko40] proved there are none if $(x,y)=1$, but there are in fact infinitely many solutions in
general - for example, $x=2^{12}3^6$, $y = 2^83^8$, and $z = 2^{11}3^7$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_674 : solutionSet.Nonempty

statements.name: Erdos674.erdos_674.variants.infinite
statements.doc: There are in fact infinitely many integer solutions to $x^xy^y=z^z$ with $x,y,z>1$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_674.variants.infinite : solutionSet.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 675
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/675](https://www.erdosproblems.com/675)
- [Er79] Erdős, Paul, *Some unconventional problems in number theory*. Math. Mag. (1979), 67-70.
- [Ho26] Ho, B. S., *A squarefree lower bound for Erdős Problem 675*.
  [PDF](https://boonsuan.github.io/erdos675_squarefree.pdf) (2026).

statements.name: Erdos675.erdos_675.parts.i
statements.doc:
A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ has the translation property if, for every $n$, there is an
integer $t_n \geq 1$ such that, for all $1 \leq a \leq n$, $a \in A$ if and only if
$a + t_n \in A$. Does the set of sums of two squares $\{x^2 + y^2 : x, y \in \mathbb{N}\}$
have the translation property?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_675.parts.i :
    HasTranslationProperty {m : ℕ | ∃ x y : ℕ, m = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2}

statements.name: Erdos675.erdos_675.parts.ii
statements.doc:
If we partition all primes into $P\sqcup Q$, such that each set contains $\gg x/\log x$ many
primes $\leq x$ for all large $x$, then can the set of integers only divisible by primes from
$P$ have the translation property?

We read "can" as: is there such a partition for which this set (which contains $1$) has the
translation property?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_675.parts.ii :
    ∃ P : Set ℕ, P ⊆ {p : ℕ | p.Prime} ∧
      (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ) / Real.log x) =O[atTop] (fun x ↦ ((P ∩ Set.Iic x).ncard : ℝ)) ∧
      (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ) / Real.log x) =O[atTop]
        (fun x ↦ ((({p : ℕ | p.Prime} \ P) ∩ Set.Iic x).ncard : ℝ)) ∧
      HasTranslationProperty (composedOf P)

statements.name: Erdos675.erdos_675.parts.iii
statements.doc:
If $A$ is the set of squarefree numbers then how fast does the minimal such $t_n$ grow? Is it
true that $t_n>\exp(n^c)$ for some constant $c>0$?

We ask for the inequality for all sufficiently large $n$, since $t_1 = 1$.

Ho [Ho26] proved that the answer is yes: for every fixed $0 < c < 25/72$, $t_n > \exp(n^c)$ for
all sufficiently large $n$ (Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 3.2); see also the
[forum discussion](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/675#post-6002).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_675.parts.iii :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      Real.exp ((n : ℝ) ^ c) < (minTranslation {m : ℕ | Squarefree m} n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos675.erdos_675.variants.squarefree
statements.doc:
Elementary sieve theory implies that the set of squarefree numbers has the translation property
(as remarked on erdosproblems.com).
statements.statement: theorem erdos_675.variants.squarefree : HasTranslationProperty {m : ℕ | Squarefree m}

statements.name: Erdos675.erdos_675.variants.brun
statements.doc:
Let $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be a set of pairwise coprime integers with
$$\sum_{b \in B,\ b < x} \frac{1}{b} = o(\log \log x).$$
Then $A = \{n : b \nmid n \text{ for all } b \in B\}$ has the translation property.
As remarked on erdosproblems.com, this follows from Brun's sieve, and Erdős did not know what
happens if the condition on the sum is weakened or dropped.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_675.variants.brun (B : Set ℕ) (hB : B.Pairwise Nat.Coprime)
    (hsum : (fun x : ℕ ↦ ∑ b ∈ Finset.range x with b ∈ B, (1 : ℝ) / (b : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      fun x : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log (x : ℝ))) :
    HasTranslationProperty {n : ℕ | ∀ b ∈ B, ¬ b ∣ n}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 676
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/676](https://www.erdosproblems.com/676)
- [Er79] Erdős, Paul, *Some unconventional problems in number theory*.
  Math. Mag. (1979), 67–70.
- [Er79d] Erdős, P., *Some unconventional problems in number theory*.
  Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1979), 71–80.
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*.
  Ann. Discrete Math. (1980), 89–115.

statements.name: Erdos676.erdos_676
statements.doc:
Is every sufficiently large integer of the form $ap^2+b$ for some prime $p$ and integers
$a \geq 1$ and $0 \leq b < p$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_676 : ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
    ∃ a p b : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ 1 ≤ a ∧ b < p ∧ n = a * p ^ 2 + b

problems.title: Erdős Problem 677
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/677](https://www.erdosproblems.com/677)

statements.name: Erdos677.erdos_677
statements.doc:
Denote by $M(n, k)$ the least common multiple of the finite set $\{n+1, \dotsc, n+k\}$.
Is it true that for all $m \geq n + k$, we get $M(m, k) \neq M(n, k)$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_677 :
    ∀ (m n k : ℕ), k > 0 → m ≥ n + k → lcmInterval m k ≠ lcmInterval n k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 678
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/678](https://www.erdosproblems.com/678)
- [Ca24] S. Cambie, Resolution of an Erdős' problem on least common multiples. arXiv:2410.09138
  (2024).
- [Er79] Erdős, Paul, Some unconventional problems in number theory. Math. Mag. (1979), 67-70.
- [Er92e] Erdős, Pál, Some Unsolved problems in Geometry, Number Theory and Combinatorics. Eureka
  (1992), 44-48.

statements.name: Erdos678.erdos_678
statements.doc:
Write $M(n, k)$ be the least common multiple of $\{n+1, \dotsc, n+k\}$.
Let $k$ be sufficiently large. Are there infinitely many $m, n$ with $m \geq n + k$ such that
$$
M(n, k) > M(m, k + 1)
$$?
The answer is yes, as proved in a strong form by Cambie [Ca24].
[Ca24] S. Cambie, Resolution of an Erdős' problem on least common multiples. arXiv:2410.09138 (2024).

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle, on top of the PNT+ project.

For a fixed $k$ there are only finitely many such pairs, so "infinitely many" is read here as
ranging over $k$ as well: for every sufficiently large $k$ at least one pair $(m, n)$ occurs.
See `erdos_678.variants.infinitely_many_triples` for the reading in which the infinitude is
stated directly, and `erdos_678.variants.not_infinitely_many_pairs` for why it cannot be asked
of a single $k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_678 :
    ∀ᶠ k in atTop, {(m, n) | n + k ≤ m ∧ lcmInterval m (k + 1) < lcmInterval n k}.Nonempty

statements.name: Erdos678.erdos_678.variants.infinitely_many_triples
statements.doc:
The pairs $(m, n)$ with $m \geq n + k$ and $M(n, k) > M(m, k + 1)$ are infinite in number once
$k$ is allowed to vary, which is the sense in which Cambie's result answers the question.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_678.variants.infinitely_many_triples :
    {(k, m, n) | 3 ≤ k ∧ n + k ≤ m ∧ lcmInterval m (k + 1) < lcmInterval n k}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos678.erdos_678.variants.not_infinitely_many_pairs
statements.doc:
For a fixed sufficiently large $k$ only finitely many pairs occur: $M(m, k + 1) \geq m + 1$
bounds $m$ by $M(n, k)$, and for large $n$ the inequality reverses. So the question cannot be
read as asking for infinitely many pairs at a single $k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_678.variants.not_infinitely_many_pairs :
    ¬ ∀ᶠ k in atTop, {(m, n) | n + k ≤ m ∧ lcmInterval m (k + 1) < lcmInterval n k}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 679
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/679](https://www.erdosproblems.com/679)
- [Er79d] P. Erdős, Some unconventional problems in number theory.
  Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 33 (1979), 71–80.

statements.name: Erdos679.erdos_679.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $\epsilon>0$ and $\omega(n)$ count the number of distinct prime factors of $n$.
Are there infinitely many values of $n$ such that
$$\omega(n-k) < (1+\epsilon)\frac{\log k}{\log\log k}$$
for all $k<n$ which are sufficiently large depending on $\epsilon$ only?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_679.parts.i :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ K : ℕ, ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ k : ℕ, K < k → k < n →
        (ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors (n - k) : ℝ) <
          (1 + ε) * log k / log (log k)

statements.name: Erdos679.erdos_679.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Can one show the stronger version with
$$\omega(n-k) < \frac{\log k}{\log\log k}+O(1)$$
is false?

DottedCalculator disproved this strengthening. For every additive constant $C$ and cutoff $K$,
all sufficiently large $n$ admit $K<k<n$ violating the bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_679.parts.ii (C : ℝ) (K : ℕ) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ k < n, K < k ∧
      log (k : ℝ) / log (log k) + C ≤
        (ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors (n - k) : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 680
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/680](https://www.erdosproblems.com/680)

statements.name: Erdos680.erdos_680.parts.i
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $n$, there exists some $k$ such that
$$
p(n+k)>k^2+1,
$$
where $p(m)$ denotes the least prime factor of $m$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_680.parts.i :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in .atTop, ∃ k ≠ 0, (n + k).minFac > k^2 + 1

statements.name: Erdos680.erdos_680.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Can one prove this is false if we replace $k^2+1$ by $e^{(1+\epsilon)\sqrt{k}}+C_\epsilon$, for all
$\epsilon>0$, where $C_\epsilon>0$ is some constant?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_680.parts.ii : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ C > 0,
    ¬ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ k ≠ 0,
    Nat.minFac (n + k) > exp ((1 + ε) * √k) + C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 681
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/681](https://www.erdosproblems.com/681)

statements.name: Erdos681.erdos_681
statements.doc:
**Erdős problem 681.**
Is it true that for all large $n$ there exists $k$
such that $n + k$ is composite and $p(n+k) > k^2$,
where $p(m)$ is the least prime factor of $m$ ?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_681 :
    ∀ᶠ n in .atTop, ∃ k > 0, (n + k).Composite ∧ ∀ p, IsLPF p (n + k) → p > k ^ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 682
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/682](https://www.erdosproblems.com/682)
- [Er79d] Erdős, P., Some unconventional problems in number theory. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar.
  (1979), 71-80.
- [GaTa25] A. Gafni and T. Tao, Rough numbers between consecutive primes. arXiv:2508.06463 (2025).

statements.name: Erdos682.erdos_682
statements.doc:
Is it true that for almost all $n$ there exists some $m\in (p_n,p_{n+1})$ such that
$$p(m) \geq p_{n+1}-p_n,$$
where $p(m)$ denotes the least prime factor of $m$?

This was solved in the affirmative by Gafni and Tao [GaTa25].

This was formalized in Lean by Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_682 :
    {n | ∃ m ∈ Set.Ioo (p n) (p (n + 1)), p (n + 1) - p n ≤ m.minFac}.HasDensity 1

statements.name: Erdos682.erdos_682.variants.exceptional_count
statements.doc:
Gafni and Tao [GaTa25, Theorem 1.1] proved that the number of exceptional gaps
$(p_n,p_{n+1})$ with $p_n\in [X,2X]$ is
$$\ll \frac{X}{(\log X)^2}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_682.variants.exceptional_count :
    (fun X : ℕ ↦ ({n | p n ∈ Set.Icc X (2 * X) ∧
        ∀ m ∈ Set.Ioo (p n) (p (n + 1)), m.minFac < p (n + 1) - p n}.ncard : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      fun X : ℕ ↦ (X : ℝ) / Real.log X ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos682.erdos_682.variants.dickson_counterexample
statements.doc:
Erdős first thought this should be true for all large $n$, but found a (conditional)
counterexample: Dickson's conjecture says there are infinitely many $d$ such that
$$2183+30030d\textrm{ and }2201+30030d$$
are both prime, and then they must necessarily be consecutive primes. These give a counterexample
since $30030=2\cdot 3 \cdot 5\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13$ and every integer in $[2184,2200]$ is
divisible by at least one of these primes.

This was formalized in Lean by Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_682.variants.dickson_counterexample (d : ℕ) (h₁ : (2183 + 30030 * d).Prime)
    (h₂ : (2201 + 30030 * d).Prime) : ∃ n, p n = 2183 + 30030 * d ∧ p (n + 1) = 2201 + 30030 * d ∧
      ∀ m ∈ Set.Ioo (p n) (p (n + 1)), m.minFac < p (n + 1) - p n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 683
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/683](https://www.erdosproblems.com/683)
- [Er34] Erdős, Paul, A Theorem of Sylvester and Schur. J. London Math. Soc. (1934), 282--288.
- [Er55d] Erdős, P., On consecutive integers. Nieuw Arch. Wisk. (3) (1955), 124--128.
- [Er79d] Erdős, P., Some unconventional problems in number theory. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1979), 71-80.

statements.name: Erdos683.erdos_683
statements.doc:
Let $P(n, k)$ be the largest prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$.
There exists $c > 0$ such that $P(n, k) \ge \min(n - k + 1, k^{1 + c})$ for all $0 < k \le n/2$.

Erdős stated this for $1 \le k \le n$ with the bound $\min(n-k+1, k^{1+c})$ [Er79d]. The
minimum is needed even for $k \le n/2$: at $n = 2k$ every prime factor of $\binom{2k}{k}$ is at
most $2k$, so $P(n, k) \ge k^{1+c}$ fails for large $k$. The range $k \le n/2$ is natural
(cf. [#961](https://www.erdosproblems.com/961) and the
[discussion](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/discuss/683)).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_683 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 →
      (P n k : ℝ) ≥ min (↑(n - k + 1) : ℝ) ((k : ℝ) ^ (1 + c))

statements.name: Erdos683.erdos_683.variant.sylvester_schur
statements.doc: Sylvester and Schur [Er34] proved that $P(n, k) > k$ for $k \le n/2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_683.variant.sylvester_schur :
    ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 → P n k > k

statements.name: Erdos683.erdos_683.variant.erdos_log
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er55d] improved this to $P(n, k) \gg \min(n - k + 1, k \log k)$ for $k \le n/2$. The
minimum cannot be dropped: at $n = 2k$ one has $P(n, k) \le 2k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_683.variant.erdos_log :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 →
      (P n k : ℝ) ≥ min (↑(n - k + 1) : ℝ) (c * k * Real.log k)

statements.name: Erdos683.erdos_683.variant.exp_sqrt
statements.doc:
Standard heuristics suggest that $P(n, k) > \min(n - k + 1, e^{c\sqrt{k}})$ for some constant
$c > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_683.variant.exp_sqrt :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 →
      (P n k : ℝ) > min (↑(n - k + 1) : ℝ) (Real.exp (c * Real.sqrt k))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 684
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/684](https://www.erdosproblems.com/684)
- [APSSV26] Alexeev, B., Putterman, M., Sawhney, M., Sellke, M., and Valiant, G.,
  *Short proofs in combinatorics and number theory*. arXiv:2603.29961 (2026), Theorem 2.1.

statements.name: Erdos684.erdos_684.upper_bound
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be the smallest $0 \leq k \leq n$ for which the factor of
$\binom{n}{k}$ supported on primes at most $k$ exceeds $n^2$. Give bounds for $f(n)$.

An internal OpenAI model [APSSV26] has given an elementary argument which shows
$f(n) \ll (\log n)^2$. This statement gives the nonoptimal constant $514$.
The existence formulation avoids defining the minimum for small inputs.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_684.upper_bound :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ k ≤ n,
      (k : ℝ) ≤ 514 * (log (n : ℝ)) ^ 2 ∧ n ^ 2 < smallPrimePart n k

statements.name: Erdos684.erdos_684.lower_bound
statements.doc:
The elementary argument of an internal OpenAI model [APSSV26] constructs arbitrarily
large $n$ such that $f(n) \geq (1/2-o(1))\log n$. The following weaker form has coefficient
$1/8$: for arbitrarily large $n>1$, the small-prime part equals one for every
$k \leq (\log n)/8$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_684.lower_bound :
    ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, 1 < n ∧
      ∀ k : ℕ, (k : ℝ) ≤ log (n : ℝ) / 8 → smallPrimePart n k = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 685
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/685](https://www.erdosproblems.com/685)
- [Er79d] Erdős, P., *Some unconventional problems in number theory*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci.
  Hungar. (1979), 71-80.

statements.name: Erdos685.erdos_685.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $\epsilon > 0$ and let $n$ be large depending on $\epsilon$. Is it true that for all
$n^{\epsilon} < k \leq n^{1-\epsilon}$ the number of distinct prime divisors of $\binom{n}{k}$ is
$$(1+o(1))\, k \sum_{k < p < n} \frac{1}{p}?$$

The $o(1)$ is uniform in $k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_685.parts.i :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ δ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ k : ℕ,
      (n : ℝ) ^ ε < (k : ℝ) → (k : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε) →
        |(ω (n.choose k) : ℝ) - (k : ℝ) * primeRecipSum k n| ≤
          δ * ((k : ℝ) * primeRecipSum k n)

statements.name: Erdos685.erdos_685.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for some constant $c > 0$, the number of distinct prime divisors of
$\binom{n}{k}$ is
$$(1+o(1))\, k \sum_{k < p < n} \frac{1}{p}$$
even for all $(\log n)^c \leq k \leq n^{1-\epsilon}$?

Here $\epsilon > 0$ is as in the first question, and the $o(1)$ is uniform in $k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_685.parts.ii :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ δ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ k : ℕ,
      Real.log (n : ℝ) ^ c ≤ (k : ℝ) → (k : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε) →
        |(ω (n.choose k) : ℝ) - (k : ℝ) * primeRecipSum k n| ≤
          δ * ((k : ℝ) * primeRecipSum k n)

statements.name: Erdos685.erdos_685.variants.trivial_lower_bound
statements.doc:
For $1 \leq k \leq n - 1$ the number of distinct prime divisors of $\binom{n}{k}$ satisfies
$$\omega\left(\binom{n}{k}\right) \geq \frac{\log \binom{n}{k}}{\log n}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_685.variants.trivial_lower_bound :
    ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k → k < n →
      Real.log (n.choose k : ℝ) / Real.log (n : ℝ) ≤ (ω (n.choose k) : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 686
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/686](https://www.erdosproblems.com/686)
- [Er79d] Erdős, P., *Some unconventional problems in number theory*. Acta Math.
  Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1979), 71-80.

statements.name: Erdos686.erdos_686
statements.doc:
Can every integer $N≥2$ be written as
$$N=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}$$
for some $k≥2$ and $m≥n+k$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_686 :
    ∀ N ≥ (2 : ℕ), ∃ᵉ (k ≥ 2) (n : ℕ) (m ≥ n + k),
      (N : ℚ) = (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (m + i)) / (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i))

statements.name: Erdos686.erdos_686.variants.square
statements.doc:
Can every square $N≥2$ be written as
$$N=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}$$
for some $k≥2$ and $m≥n+k$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_686.variants.square :
    ∀ N ≥ (2 : ℕ),  (IsSquare N) → ∃ᵉ (k ≥ 2) (n : ℕ) (m ≥ n + k),
      (N : ℚ) = (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (m + i)) / (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i))

statements.name: Erdos686.erdos_686.variants.four
statements.doc:
Can $4$ be written as
$$4=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}$$
for some $k≥2$ and $m≥n+k$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_686.variants.four :
    ∃ᵉ (k ≥ 2) (n : ℕ) (m ≥ n + k),
      (4 : ℚ) = (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (m + i)) / (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i))

statements.name: Erdos686.erdos_686.variants.four_two
statements.doc:
The number $4$ cannot be written as
$$4=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq 2}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq 2}(n+i)}$$
for $m≥n+2$!
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_686.variants.four_two :
    ¬ ∃ᵉ (n : ℕ) (m ≥ n + 2),
      (4 : ℚ) = (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 2, (m + i)) / (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 2, (n + i))

statements.name: Erdos686.erdos_686.variants.four_three
statements.doc:
The number $4$ cannot be written as
$$4=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq 3}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq 3}(n+i)}$$
for $m≥n+3$!

See [comment section on erdosproblems.com](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/686#post-4599)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_686.variants.four_three :
    ¬ ∃ᵉ (n : ℕ) (m ≥ n + 3),
      (4 : ℚ) = (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 3, (m + i)) / (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 3, (n + i))

statements.name: Erdos686.erdos_686.variants.nine
statements.doc:
Can $9$ be written as
$$9=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}$$
for some $k≥2$ and $m≥n+k$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_686.variants.nine :
    ∃ᵉ (k ≥ 2) (n : ℕ) (m ≥ n + k),
      (9 : ℚ) = (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (m + i)) / (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i))

statements.name: Erdos686.erdos_686.variants.twenty_five
statements.doc:
Can $25$ be written as
$$25=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}$$
for some $k≥2$ and $m≥n+k$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_686.variants.twenty_five :
    ∃ᵉ (k ≥ 2) (n : ℕ) (m ≥ n + k),
      (25 : ℚ) = (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (m + i)) / (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i))

statements.name: Erdos686.erdos_686.variants.non_square
statements.doc:
Can every non-square $N≥2$ be written as
$$N=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}$$
for some $k≥2$ and $m≥n+k$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_686.variants.non_square :
    ∀ N ≥ (2 : ℕ), (¬ IsSquare N) → ∃ᵉ (k ≥ 2) (n : ℕ) (m ≥ n + k),
      (N : ℚ) = (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (m + i)) / (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 687
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/687](https://www.erdosproblems.com/687)
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 46](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.46):
  the same question; see `Green46` in `FormalConjectures.GreensOpenProblems.«46»`.
- [OEIS A058989](https://oeis.org/A058989): the values $Y(p_n)$, where $p_n$ is the $n$-th prime.
- [OEIS A048670](https://oeis.org/A048670): Jacobsthal's function of $\prod_{p \leq p_n} p$,
  which is $Y(p_n) + 1$.
- [Er79d] Erdős, P., *Some unconventional problems in number theory*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci.
  Hungar. 33 (1979), 71-80.
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  6 (1980), 89-115.
- [Er96b] Erdős, Paul, *Some problems I presented or planned to present in my short talk*.
  Analytic number theory, Vol. 1 (Allerton Park, IL, 1995), Progr. Math. 138 (1996), 333-335.
- [Iw78] Iwaniec, Henryk, *On the problem of Jacobsthal*. Demonstratio Math. 11 (1978), 225-232.
  [doi:10.1515/dema-1978-0121](https://doi.org/10.1515/dema-1978-0121)
- [MaPo90] Maier, Helmut and Pomerance, Carl, *Unusually large gaps between consecutive primes*.
  Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 322 (1990), 201-237.
- [FGKMT18] Ford, Kevin and Green, Ben and Konyagin, Sergei and Maynard, James and Tao, Terence,
  *Long gaps between primes*. J. Amer. Math. Soc. 31 (2018), 65-105.
  [arXiv:1412.5029](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.5029)
- [OAI26a] OpenAI, *A quadratic bound for Jacobsthal's function*. OpenAI Math Release preprint
  (2026).
  https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/A-quadratic-bound-for-Jacobsthals-function-September-25-2026/paper.pdf

statements.name: Erdos687.erdos_687.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $Y(x)$ be the maximal $y$ such that there exists a choice of congruence classes $a_p$ for
all primes $p\leq x$ such that every integer in $[1,y]$ is congruent to at least one of the
$a_p\pmod{p}$. Give good estimates for $Y(x)$.

We formalise this as determining $Y(x)$ up to constant factors.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_687.parts.i :
    (fun x : ℕ ↦ (Y x : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_687.parts.i.answer

statements.name: Erdos687.erdos_687.parts.ii
statements.doc:
In particular, can one prove that $Y(x)=o(x^2)$?

Yes: an internal OpenAI model proved $h(k) \ll k^2$ for Jacobsthal's function $h$ [OAI26a]
(see `Erdos970.erdos_970`). Since $Y(x) + 1$ is Jacobsthal's function of $\prod_{p \leq x} p$,
which has $\pi(x) \ll x/\log x$ prime factors, this gives $Y(x) \ll x^2/(\log x)^2$.
The linked Lean proof is by 30k30, from the bound of [OAI26a].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_687.parts.ii :
    (fun x : ℕ ↦ (Y x : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ) ^ 2)

statements.name: Erdos687.erdos_687.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Or, even stronger, can one prove that $Y(x)\ll x^{1+o(1)}$?

We read $Y(x)\ll x^{1+o(1)}$ as $Y(x) = O(x^{1+\varepsilon})$ for every fixed
$\varepsilon > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_687.parts.iii :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), (fun x : ℕ ↦ (Y x : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ) ^ (1 + ε))

statements.name: Erdos687.erdos_687.variants.iwaniec
statements.doc: Iwaniec's upper bound for Jacobsthal's function [Iw78] gives $Y(x) \ll x^2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_687.variants.iwaniec :
    (fun x : ℕ ↦ (Y x : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ) ^ 2)

statements.name: Erdos687.erdos_687.variants.fgkmt
statements.doc:
Ford, Green, Konyagin, Maynard and Tao [FGKMT18] proved
$$Y(x) \gg \frac{x \log x \log\log\log x}{\log\log x}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_687.variants.fgkmt :
    (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ) * Real.log x * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log x)) /
      Real.log (Real.log x)) =O[atTop] (fun x : ℕ ↦ (Y x : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos687.erdos_687.variants.maier_pomerance
statements.doc:
Maier and Pomerance [MaPo90] conjectured that $Y(x) \ll x(\log x)^{2+o(1)}$ (in this form it is
stated in [FGKMT18]).

We read this as $Y(x) = O(x(\log x)^{2+\varepsilon})$ for every fixed $\varepsilon > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_687.variants.maier_pomerance :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), (fun x : ℕ ↦ (Y x : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ) * Real.log x ^ (2 + ε))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 688
problems.doc:
*Reference:*
- [erdosproblems.com/688](https://www.erdosproblems.com/688)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, _A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory_. Ann. Discrete Math. (1980), 89-115.

statements.name: Erdos688.erdos_688.parts.i
statements.doc: Estimate $\epsilon_n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_688.parts.i :
    epsilonFunction =Θ[atTop] erdos_688.parts.i.answer

statements.name: Erdos688.erdos_688.parts.ii
statements.doc: In particular, is it true that $\epsilon_n = o(1)$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_688.parts.ii :
    epsilonFunction =o[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (1 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos688.erdos_688.variants.lglglg_over_lglg_is_big_o
statements.doc:
Erdős claims in [Er80] (p. 106) that it is not difficult to prove
$\epsilon_n \gg \frac{\log\log\log n}{\log\log n}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_688.variants.lglglg_over_lglg_is_big_o :
    (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (log (log (log (n : ℝ)))) / (log (log (n : ℝ))))
      =O[atTop] epsilonFunction

problems.title: Erdős Problem 689
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/689](https://www.erdosproblems.com/689)
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 45](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.45)
- [Ch26] Chojecki, P., *A greedy matching proof of Erdős's two-fold residue-class problem*.
  [ulam.ai/research/erdos689.pdf](https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos689.pdf) (April 2026).
- [PALOMAR-2026-09-20-000002](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-09-20-000002&version=1)

statements.name: Erdos689.erdos_689
statements.doc:
Let `n` be sufficiently large. Is there some choice of congruence class `a_p` for all primes
`2 ≤ p ≤ n` such that every integer in `[1,n]` satisfies at least two of the congruences
`≡ a_p (mod p)`?

Yes: this follows from the greedy-matching reduction of Chojecki [Ch26] combined with an
unconditional Fourier-analytic proof of the required three-prime counting estimate.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_689 :
    ∀ᶠ n in .atTop, ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n,
      2 ≤ (Finset.Icc 1 n |>.filter fun p => p.Prime ∧ a p ≡ m [MOD p]).card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 690
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/690](https://www.erdosproblems.com/690)
- [Er79e] Erdős, Paul, _Some unconventional problems in number theory_. Astérisque (1979), 73-82.
- [Ca25] S. Cambie, _Resolution of Erdős' problems about unimodularity_. arXiv:2501.10333 (2025).
- [WC26] S. Wang and D. Crapis, _A Complete Answer to Erdős Problem 690_. arXiv:2605.08542 (2026).

statements.name: Erdos690.erdos_690
statements.doc:
Let $d_k(p)$ be the density of those integers whose $k$th smallest prime factor is $p$ (i.e. if
$p_1<p_2<\cdots$ are the primes dividing $n$ then $p_k=p$).

For fixed $k\geq 1$ is $d_k(p)$ unimodular in $p$? That is, it first increases in $p$ until its
maximum then decreases.

The answer is no in general: Cambie [Ca25] has shown that $d_k(p)$ is unimodular for
$1\leq k\leq 3$ and is not unimodular for $4\leq k\leq 20$.

The densities $d_k(p)$ exist (see `erdos_690.variants.hasDensity`), so the statement quantifies
over any function `d` recording them.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_690 :
    ¬ ∀ k ≥ 1, ∀ d : ℕ → ℝ,
      (∀ p, p.Prime → (kthPrimeFactorSet k p).HasDensity (d p)) → IsUnimodalOnPrimes d

statements.name: Erdos690.erdos_690.variants.hasDensity
statements.doc:
For every $k\geq 1$ and prime $p$, the set of integers whose $k$th smallest prime factor is
$p$ has a natural density.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_690.variants.hasDensity (k p : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hp : p.Prime) :
    ∃ δ : ℝ, (kthPrimeFactorSet k p).HasDensity δ

statements.name: Erdos690.erdos_690.variants.cambie_unimodal
statements.doc: Cambie [Ca25] has shown that $d_k(p)$ is unimodular for $1\leq k\leq 3$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_690.variants.cambie_unimodal (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hk' : k ≤ 3)
    (d : ℕ → ℝ) (hd : ∀ p, p.Prime → (kthPrimeFactorSet k p).HasDensity (d p)) :
    IsUnimodalOnPrimes d

statements.name: Erdos690.erdos_690.variants.cambie_not_unimodal
statements.doc: Cambie [Ca25] has shown that $d_k(p)$ is not unimodular for $4\leq k\leq 20$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_690.variants.cambie_not_unimodal (k : ℕ) (hk : 4 ≤ k) (hk' : k ≤ 20)
    (d : ℕ → ℝ) (hd : ∀ p, p.Prime → (kthPrimeFactorSet k p).HasDensity (d p)) :
    ¬ IsUnimodalOnPrimes d

statements.name: Erdos690.erdos_690.variants.large_k
statements.doc:
Is $d_k(p)$ unimodular for any $k\geq 21$?

The answer is no: $d_k(p)$ is not unimodal for any $k \geq 4$ [WC26] (arXiv preprint).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_690.variants.large_k :
    ¬ ∃ k ≥ 21, ∀ d : ℕ → ℝ,
      (∀ p, p.Prime → (kthPrimeFactorSet k p).HasDensity (d p)) → IsUnimodalOnPrimes d

problems.title: Erdős Problem 691
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/691](https://www.erdosproblems.com/691)

statements.name: Erdos691.erdos_691
statements.doc:
Given $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, let
$M_A = \{n \geq 1 : a \mid n \text{ for some } a \in A\}$. Find a necessary and sufficient
condition on $A$ for $M_A$ to have density $1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_691 :
    erdos_691.answer = fun A ↦ (multiples A).HasDensity 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 692
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/692](https://www.erdosproblems.com/692)
- [Er79e] Erdős, Paul, Some unconventional problems in number theory. Astérisque (1979), 73-82.
- [Ob1] Erdős, P., *Oberwolfach Mathematical Problems, Volume 1*. Mathematisches
  Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach (Various).
- [Fo08] Ford, Kevin, *The distribution of integers with a divisor in a given interval*.
  Ann. of Math. (2) (2008), 367-433.
- [Ca25] Cambie, S., *Resolution of Erdős' problems about unimodularity*.
  arXiv:2501.10333 (2025).

statements.name: Erdos692.erdos_692.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $\delta_1(n,m)$ be the density of the set of integers with exactly one divisor in $(n,m)$.
Is $\delta_1(n,m)$ unimodular for $m>n+1$ (i.e. increases until some $m$ then decreases
thereafter)?

Cambie has calculated that unimodularity fails even for $n=2$ and $n=3$.

This was formalized in Lean by Monticone using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_692.parts.i :
    ¬ ∀ δ : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ, (∀ a b, IsDelta₁ a b (δ a b)) → ∀ n, UnimodularOn (δ n) (n + 1)

statements.name: Erdos692.erdos_692.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $\delta_1(n,m)$ be the density of the set of integers with exactly one divisor in $(n,m)$.
For fixed $n$, where does $\delta_1(n,m)$ achieve its maximum?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_692.parts.ii (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ δ : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ, (∀ a b, IsDelta₁ a b (δ a b)) →
      IsGreatest (δ n '' Set.Ioi (n + 1)) (δ n erdos_692.parts.ii.answer)

statements.name: Erdos692.erdos_692.variants.erdos_upper_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős proved that
$$\delta_1(n,m) \ll \frac{1}{(\log n)^c}$$
for all $m$, for some constant $c>0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_692.variants.erdos_upper_bound :
    ∀ δ : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ, (∀ a b, IsDelta₁ a b (δ a b)) →
      ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ m, δ n m ≤ C / Real.log n ^ c

statements.name: Erdos692.erdos_692.variants.cambie_three
statements.doc:
Cambie has calculated that unimodularity fails even for $n=2$ and $n=3$. For example,
$$\delta_1(3,6)= 0.35\quad \delta_1(3,7)\approx 0.33\quad \delta_1(3,8)\approx 0.3619.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_692.variants.cambie_three :
    ∀ δ : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ, (∀ a b, IsDelta₁ a b (δ a b)) →
      δ 3 7 < δ 3 6 ∧ δ 3 7 < δ 3 8

statements.name: Erdos692.erdos_692.variants.cambie_local_maxima
statements.doc:
Cambie [Ca25] has shown that, for fixed $n$, the sequence $\delta_1(n,m)$ has superpolynomially
many local maxima $m$. A local maximum is a maximal run of equal values of the sequence that is
strictly larger than the values just before and just after the run.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_692.variants.cambie_local_maxima (k : ℕ) :
    ∀ δ : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ, (∀ a b, IsDelta₁ a b (δ a b)) →
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (n : ℕ∞) ^ k ≤ (localMaxima (δ n) (n + 1)).encard

problems.title: Erdős Problem 694
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/694](https://www.erdosproblems.com/694)

statements.name: Erdos694.erdos_694
statements.doc:
Let $f_\max(n)$ be the largest $m$ such that $\phi(m) = n$, and
$f_\min(n)$ be the smallest such $m$, where $\phi$ is Euler's
totient function. Investigate
$$
  \max_{n\leq x}\frac{f_\max(n)}{f_\min(n)}.
$$

GPT-5.5 Pro (prompted by Price) has proved (see also the comments for a summary) that
$$
\max_{n\leq x}\frac{f_{\max}(n)}{f_{\min}(n)}=(e^\gamma+o(1))\log\log x.
$$

A Lean formalisation of the reduction exists, conditional on Mertens' product theorem and
Linnik's theorem; see the
[formal proof](https://github.com/Shashi456/erdos-formalizations/blob/main/Erdos/P694/Proof.lean).

The extrema are only required on nonempty fibres of the totient (values such as $3$ have no
preimage), and the identity is asked for sufficiently large $x$: at $x = 1$ the maximum is
$f_\max(1) / f_\min(1) = 2$ while $\log \log 1 = 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_694 : ∀ᵉ (fmax : ℕ → ℕ) (fmin : ℕ → ℕ),
      (∀ n, (∃ m, Nat.totient m = n) → IsGreatest (Nat.totient ⁻¹' {n}) (fmax n)) →
      (∀ n, (∃ m, Nat.totient m = n) → IsLeast (Nat.totient ⁻¹' {n}) (fmin n)) →
      ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto o atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
        ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
          sSup { (fmax n : ℝ) / fmin n | (n : ℕ) (_ : n ≤ x) (_ : ∃ m, Nat.totient m = n) } =
            (exp eulerMascheroniConstant + o x) * log (log (x : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos694.erdos_694.variants.carmichael
statements.doc:
Carmichael has asked whether there is an integer $n$ for which $\phi(m) = n$ has
exactly one solution, that is $\frac{f_\max(n)}{f_\min(n)} = 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_694.variants.carmichael :
    ∃ n > 0, ∃! m, Nat.totient m = n

statements.name: Erdos694.erdos_694.variants.inf_unique
statements.doc:
Erdős has proved that if there exists an integer $n$ for which $\phi(m) = n$ has
exactly one solution, then there must be infinitely many such $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_694.variants.inf_unique (h : ∃ n > 0, ∃! m, Nat.totient m = n) :
    { n | ∃! m, Nat.totient m = n }.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 695
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/695](https://www.erdosproblems.com/695)

statements.name: Erdos695.erdos_695
statements.doc:
Let $q_1 < q_2 < \cdots$ be a sequence of primes such that $q_{i + 1} \equiv 1 \pmod{q_i}$. Is it
true that
$$
\lim_{k \to \infty} q_k^{1/k} = \infty?
$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_695 :
    ∀ {q : ℕ → ℕ},
      StrictMono q →
      (∀ i, (q i).Prime) →
      (∀ i, q (i + 1) % q i = 1) →
      Tendsto (fun k => (q k : ℝ) ^ (1 / k : ℝ)) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos695.erdos_695.variants.upperBound
statements.doc:
Is there a sequence of primes $q_1 < q_2 < \cdots$ such that $q_{i + 1} \equiv 1 \pmod{q_i}$ and
$$
q(k) \leq \exp(k (\log k)^{1 + o(1)})?
$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_695.variants.upperBound :
    ∃ q : ℕ → ℕ,
      StrictMono q ∧
      (∀ i, (q i).Prime) ∧
      (∀ i, q (i + 1) % q i = 1) ∧
      ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ,
        (o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)) ∧
        -- We use `(k + 1)` here as the informal statement is 1-indexed.
        ∀ k, q k ≤ exp ((k + 1) * log (k + 1) ^ (1 + o k))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 696
problems.doc:
*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/696](https://www.erdosproblems.com/696)
* [Lean proof](https://github.com/davidturturean/erdos-696/blob/4fa1bf2c6ff6f2e0c7024f814614c7455404fdd3/Erdos696/Main.lean#L35), assuming
  the Siegel-Walfisz theorem, the Brun-Titchmarsh inequality, and Mertens' theorem as custom axioms.

statements.name: Erdos696.erdos_696
statements.doc:
Is it true that $H(n)/h(n)\to \infty$ for almost all $n$?

Formalised as: for every threshold $M$, the set of $n$ with $h(n) > 0$ and $H(n)/h(n) > M$
has natural density $1$. This is false: in fact, $H(n)/h(n) = 2 + o(1)$ for almost all $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_696 :
    ¬ ∀ M : ℝ,
      {n : ℕ | (h n : ℝ) > 0 ∧ (H n : ℝ) / (h n : ℝ) > M}.HasDensity 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 697
problems.doc:
*Reference:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/697](https://www.erdosproblems.com/697)
 - [Ha92] Hall, R. R., On some conjectures of Erdős in Astérisque. I. J. Number Theory (1992),
    313--319.

statements.name: Erdos697.density_exists
statements.doc:
For each $m$ and $\alpha$, the density of the set of integers which are divisible by
some $d \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$ with $1 < d < \exp (m ^ \alpha)$ exists.
statements.statement:
theorem density_exists (m : ℕ) (α : ℝ) : ∃ δ, HasDensity
    {n : ℕ | ∃ d, d ≡ 1 [MOD m] ∧ (d : ℝ) ∈ Set.Ioo 1 (exp (m ^ α)) ∧ d ∣ n} δ

statements.name: Erdos697.erdos_697.variants.delta_lt
statements.doc:
$\delta < \frac{m ^ \alpha + 1}{m}$. This shows that
$lim_{m\rightarrow\infty} \delta (m, \alpha) = 0$ for $\alpha < 1$.
At $m = 0$, both sides are 0, so the strict bound requires $m > 0$.
#TODO: prove this theorem.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_697.variants.delta_lt (m : ℕ) (α : ℝ) (hm : 0 < m) : δ m α < (m ^ α + 1) / m

statements.name: Erdos697.erdos_697.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $\beta = \frac{1}{\log 2}$. Then $lim_{m\rightarrow\infty} \delta (m, \alpha) = 0$ if
$\alpha < \beta$. This is proved in [Ha92].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_697.parts.i {α : ℝ} (hα : α < 1 / log (2 : ℝ)) : Tendsto (δ · α) atTop (𝓝 0)

statements.name: Erdos697.erdos_697.parts.ii
statements.doc:
$lim_{m\rightarrow\infty} \delta (m, \alpha) = 1$ if $\beta < \alpha$.
This is proved in [Ha92].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_697.parts.ii {α : ℝ} (hα : 1 / log (2 : ℝ) < α) : Tendsto (δ · α) atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 698
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/698](https://www.erdosproblems.com/698)
- [ErSz78] Erdős, P. and Szekeres, G., *Some number theoretic problems on binomial
  coefficients*. Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. (1978), 97-99.
- [Be11] Bergman, George M., *On common divisors of multinomial coefficients*. Bull. Aust.
  Math. Soc. (2011), 138--157.

statements.name: Erdos698.erdos_698
statements.doc:
Is there some $h(n)\to \infty$ such that for all $2\leq i<j\leq n/2$
$$\textrm{gcd}\left( \binom{n}{i},\binom{n}{j}\right) \geq h(n)?$$

This was resolved by Bergman [Be11], who proved that for any $2\leq i<j\leq n/2$
$$\textrm{gcd}\left( \binom{n}{i},\binom{n}{j}\right) \gg n^{1/2}\frac{2^i}{i^{3/2}},$$
where the implied constant is absolute.

The linked formal proof (van Doorn and Aristotle, see `erdos_698.variants.bergman`) gives the
explicit bound $\gcd > \frac{2^i \sqrt n}{4 i \sqrt{i - 1}}$, so $h(n) = \lfloor \sqrt n / 4 \rfloor$
works since $i \sqrt{i - 1} \le 2^i$ for $i \ge 2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_698 :
    ∃ h : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto h atTop atTop ∧
      ∀ n i j : ℕ, 2 ≤ i → i < j → j ≤ n / 2 →
        h n ≤ Nat.gcd (n.choose i) (n.choose j)

statements.name: Erdos698.erdos_698.variants.erdos_szekeres
statements.doc:
A problem of Erdős and Szekeres, who observed that
$$\textrm{gcd}\left( \binom{n}{i},\binom{n}{j}\right) \geq \frac{\binom{n}{i}}{\binom{j}{i}}
\geq 2^i$$
(in particular the greatest common divisor is always $>1$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_698.variants.erdos_szekeres (n i j : ℕ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) (hij : i < j)
    (hj : j ≤ n / 2) :
    (n.choose i : ℝ) / (j.choose i : ℝ) ≤ (Nat.gcd (n.choose i) (n.choose j) : ℝ) ∧
      (2 : ℝ) ^ i ≤ (n.choose i : ℝ) / (j.choose i : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos698.erdos_698.variants.erdos_szekeres_sharp
statements.doc: This inequality is sharp for $i=1$, $j=p$, and $n=2p$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_698.variants.erdos_szekeres_sharp (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hp2 : 2 < p) :
    (Nat.gcd ((2 * p).choose 1) ((2 * p).choose p) : ℝ) =
        ((2 * p).choose 1 : ℝ) / (p.choose 1 : ℝ) ∧
      ((2 * p).choose 1 : ℝ) / (p.choose 1 : ℝ) = (2 : ℝ) ^ 1

statements.name: Erdos698.erdos_698.variants.bergman
statements.doc:
This was resolved by Bergman [Be11], who proved that for any $2\leq i<j\leq n/2$
$$\textrm{gcd}\left( \binom{n}{i},\binom{n}{j}\right) \gg n^{1/2}\frac{2^i}{i^{3/2}},$$
where the implied constant is absolute.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_698.variants.bergman :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ n i j : ℕ, 2 ≤ i → i < j → j ≤ n / 2 →
      c * (Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) * (2 : ℝ) ^ i / ((i : ℝ) * Real.sqrt (i : ℝ))) ≤
        (Nat.gcd (n.choose i) (n.choose j) : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 699
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/699](https://www.erdosproblems.com/699)

statements.name: Erdos699.sylvester_schur
statements.doc: Sylvester and Schur: for $1 \le i \le n/2$ there is a prime $p > i$ dividing `n.choose i`.
statements.statement:
theorem sylvester_schur (n i : ℕ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) (hi_half : i ≤ n / 2) :
    ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ i < p ∧ p ∣ Nat.choose n i

statements.name: Erdos699.erdos_699
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 699.** Is it true that for every $1 \le i < j \le n / 2$ there exists a prime
$p \ge i$ with $p \mid \gcd\big(\binom{n}{i}, \binom{n}{j}\big)$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_699 :
    ∀ n i j : ℕ,
      1 ≤ i →
      i < j →
      j ≤ n / 2 →
      ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ i ≤ p ∧ p ∣ Nat.gcd (Nat.choose n i) (Nat.choose n j)

statements.name: Erdos699.erdos_szekeres_strengthening
statements.doc:
Erdős and Szekeres conjectured that, apart from a finite exceptional set of triples `(n, i, j)`,
one can always take `p > i` in the prime divisor statement.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_szekeres_strengthening :
    ∃ E : Finset (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ), ∀ n i j : ℕ,
      1 ≤ i →
      i < j →
      j ≤ n / 2 →
      (n, i, j) ∉ E →
      ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ i < p ∧ p ∣ Nat.gcd (Nat.choose n i) (Nat.choose n j)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 700
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/700](https://www.erdosproblems.com/700)

A problem of Erdős and Szekeres [ErSz78].

*References:*
 * [ErSz78] Erdős, P. and Szekeres, G., _Some number theoretic problems on binomial coefficients_,
   Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. (1978), 97-99.
 * [OEIS A091963](https://oeis.org/A091963)
 * Guy, R. K., _Unsolved Problems in Number Theory_, B31, B33.

statements.name: Erdos700.erdos_700.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $f(n) = \min_{1 < k \le n/2} \gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$ and let $P(n)$ be the largest prime
dividing $n$.

**(a)** Characterise those composite $n$ such that $f(n) = n/P(n)$.

Erdős–Szekeres [ErSz78] note that $f(n) = n/P(n)$ when $n$ is a product of two primes
(`erdos_700.variants.prime_mul`), with $n = 30$ a further example. The characterisation itself is
open; we state it as the (unknown) set of all composite `n` with `f n = n / P n`.

This follows the largest-prime reading on erdosproblems.com. In [ErSz78, p. 98], the first prose
line below (7) reads: "where $P(n)$ is the greatest prime power which divides $n$."
The paper's reading is stated with $Q(n)$ in `erdos_700.variants.prime_power_divisor`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_700.parts.i :
    {n : ℕ | ¬ n.Prime ∧ 1 < n ∧ f n = n / P n} = erdos_700.parts.i.answer

statements.name: Erdos700.erdos_700.variants.prime_power_divisor
statements.doc:
Characterise those composite $n$ such that $f(n) = n/Q(n)$, where $Q(n)$ is the largest
prime-power divisor of $n$. This is the reading of part (a) in Erdős–Szekeres
[ErSz78, pp. 98–99](https://combinatorica.hu/~p_erdos/1978-46.pdf).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_700.variants.prime_power_divisor :
    {n : ℕ | ¬ n.Prime ∧ 1 < n ∧ f n = n / Q n} = erdos_700.variants.prime_power_divisor.answer

statements.name: Erdos700.erdos_700.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $f(n) = \min_{1 < k \le n/2} \gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$.

**(b)** Are there infinitely many composite $n$ such that $f(n) > n^{1/2}$?

Erdős–Szekeres [ErSz78] could not prove this. (Since $f(n) \ge p(n)$, the least prime factor of
$n$, there are infinitely many $n$ — those of the form $p^2$ — with $f(n) \ge n^{1/2}$; the
question asks for the strict inequality.) Here $f(n) > n^{1/2}$ is written as `(f n) ^ 2 > n`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_700.parts.ii :
    {n : ℕ | ¬ n.Prime ∧ 1 < n ∧ (f n) ^ 2 > n}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos700.erdos_700.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Let $f(n) = \min_{1 < k \le n/2} \gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$.

**(c)** Is it true that, for every composite $n$, $f(n) \ll_A n/(\log n)^A$ for every $A > 0$?

Erdős–Szekeres [ErSz78] prove the weaker bound $f(n) \le (1 + o(1)) n/\log n$ (the case $A = 1$).
Here $f(n) \ll_A n/(\log n)^A$ is spelled out as: for every `A > 0` there is a constant `C`
(depending on `A`) with `f(n) ≤ C · n/(log n)^A` for every composite `n`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_700.parts.iii :
    (∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ¬ n.Prime → 1 < n →
      (f n : ℝ) ≤ C * (n : ℝ) / (Real.log n) ^ A)

statements.name: Erdos700.erdos_700.variants.prime_pow
statements.doc:
`f(p^a) = p` for a prime `p` and `a ≥ 2` (recorded by Erdős–Szekeres [ErSz78]). In particular,
since `(p^a) / P(p^a) = p^{a-1}`, the prime power `p^a` is a "hit" (`f(n) = n / P(n)`) if and only
if `a = 2`.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_700.variants.prime_pow (p a : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (ha : 2 ≤ a) : f (p ^ a) = p

statements.name: Erdos700.erdos_700.variants.prime_mul
statements.doc:
`f(pq) = p` for distinct primes `p < q` (recorded by Erdős–Szekeres [ErSz78]); in particular
`pq` is always a "hit" (`f(pq) = pq / P(pq) = p`). Proof via Lucas' theorem:
`p ∤ C(pq,k) ⟹ p ∣ k` (and the same for `q`),
so any `k` with `gcd(pq, C(pq,k)) = 1` must be a multiple of `pq`, of which there are none in
`(1, pq/2]`; the witness `k = q` gives `gcd(pq, C(pq,q)) = p`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_700.variants.prime_mul (p q : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p < q) :
    f (p * q) = p

problems.title: Erdős Problem 701
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/701](https://www.erdosproblems.com/701)

statements.name: Erdos701.erdos_701
statements.doc:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of sets closed under taking subsets (i.e. if
$B\subseteq A\in\mathcal{F}$ then $B\in \mathcal{F}$). There exists some element $x$ such that
whenever $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq \mathcal{F}$ is an intersecting subfamily we have
$$\lvert \mathcal{F}'\rvert \leq \lvert \{ A\in \mathcal{F} : x\in A\}\rvert.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_701 : ∀ {X : Type} [Nonempty X] [Fintype X],
    ∀ (F : Set (Set X)), IsLowerSet F →
      ∃ x : X, ∀ᵉ (F' ⊆ F),
        F'.Intersecting →
          (#F' ≤ #{ A : Set X | A ∈ F ∧ x ∈ A })

problems.title: Erdős Problem 702
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/702](https://www.erdosproblems.com/702)
- [Er75f] Erdős, Paul, _On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry_. Ann. Mat.
  Pura Appl. (4) (1975), 99-108.
- [Er76b] Erdős, P., _Problems and results in graph theory and combinatorial analysis_.
  Proceedings of the Fifth British Combinatorial Conference (Univ. Aberdeen, Aberdeen, 1975)
  (1976), 169-192.
- [Er81] Erdős, P., _On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved_.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, _Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved_. (1982),
  59--79.
- [Fr77] Frankl, Péter, _On families of finite sets no two of which intersect in a singleton_.
  Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. (1977), 125-134.

statements.name: Erdos702.erdos_702
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 4$. If $\mathcal{F}$ is a family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=k$
for all $A\in \mathcal{F}$ and $\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert >\binom{n-2}{k-2}$ then there are
$A,B\in\mathcal{F}$ such that $\lvert A\cap B\rvert=1$.

A conjecture of Erdős and Sós. Katona (unpublished) proved this when $k=4$, and Frankl [Fr77]
proved this for all $k\geq 4$.

Frankl's theorem is for $n$ sufficiently large in terms of $k$, and this is the form stated here.
Without this assumption the statement is false, see `erdos_702.variants.all_n_false`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_702 (k : ℕ) (hk : 4 ≤ k) :
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ 𝓕 : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), 𝓕.IsUniform k →
      (n - 2).choose (k - 2) < 𝓕.card → ∃ A ∈ 𝓕, ∃ B ∈ 𝓕, (A ∩ B).card = 1

statements.name: Erdos702.erdos_702.variants.all_n_false
statements.doc:
The statement does not hold for all $n$. For $k=4$ and $n=5$, the family of all $4$-subsets of
$\{1,\ldots,5\}$ has $5>\binom{3}{2}$ members, and any two of them meet in at least $3$ elements.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_702.variants.all_n_false :
    ¬ ∀ k : ℕ, 4 ≤ k → ∀ (n : ℕ) (𝓕 : Finset (Finset (Fin n))), 𝓕.IsUniform k →
      (n - 2).choose (k - 2) < 𝓕.card → ∃ A ∈ 𝓕, ∃ B ∈ 𝓕, (A ∩ B).card = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 703
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/703](https://www.erdosproblems.com/703)
- [Er75f] Erdős, Paul, _On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry_. Ann. Mat.
  Pura Appl. (4) (1975), 99-108.
- [Er76b] Erdős, P., _Problems and results in graph theory and combinatorial analysis_.
  Proceedings of the Fifth British Combinatorial Conference (Univ. Aberdeen, Aberdeen, 1975)
  (1976), 169-192.
- [Er81] Erdős, P., _On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved_.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, _Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved_. (1982),
  59--79.
- [FrFu84b] Frankl, P. and Füredi, Z., _On hypergraphs without two edges intersecting in a given
  number of vertices_. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1984), 230-236.
- [Fr77b] Frankl, P., _An intersection problem for finite sets_. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar.
  (1977), 371-373.
- [FrRo87] Frankl, Peter and Rödl, Vojtech, _Forbidden intersections_. Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (1987), 259-286.

statements.name: Erdos703.erdos_703
statements.doc:
Let $r\geq 1$ and define $T(n,r)$ to be maximal such that there exists a family $\mathcal{F}$ of
subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ of size $T(n,r)$ such that $\lvert A\cap B\rvert\neq r$ for all
$A,B\in \mathcal{F}$.

Estimate $T(n,r)$ for $r\geq 2$. In particular, is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$ there
exists $\delta>0$ such that for all $\epsilon n<r<(1/2-\epsilon) n$ we have
$$T(n,r)<(2-\delta)^n?$$

The answer is yes, proved by Frankl and Rödl [FrRo87].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_703 :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧
      ∀ (n r : ℕ), ε * n < r → r < (1 / 2 - ε) * n → (T n r : ℝ) < (2 - δ) ^ n

statements.name: Erdos703.erdos_703.variants.zero
statements.doc: It is trivial that $T(n,0)=2^{n-1}$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_703.variants.zero (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : T n 0 = 2 ^ (n - 1)

statements.name: Erdos703.erdos_703.variants.frankl_furedi
statements.doc:
Frankl and Füredi [FrFu84b] proved that, for fixed $r$ and $n$ sufficiently large in terms of
$r$, the maximal $T(n,r)$ is achieved by taking
$$\mathcal{F} = \left\{ A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\} : \lvert A\rvert> \frac{n+r}{2}\textrm{ or }
\lvert A\rvert < r\right\}$$
when $n+r$ is odd, and
$$\mathcal{F} = \left\{ A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\} : \lvert A\backslash \{1\}\rvert\geq
\frac{n+r}{2}\textrm{ or }\lvert A\rvert < r\right\}$$
when $n+r$ is even.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_703.variants.frankl_furedi (r : ℕ) : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
    T n r = if (n + r) % 2 = 1 then
      ((univ : Finset (Finset (Fin n))).filter fun A ↦
        (n + r : ℝ) / 2 < A.card ∨ A.card < r).card
    else
      ((univ : Finset (Finset (Fin n))).filter fun A ↦
        (n + r : ℝ) / 2 ≤ (A.filter fun i : Fin n ↦ (i : ℕ) ≠ 0).card ∨
          A.card < r).card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 704
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/704](https://www.erdosproblems.com/704)
- [Da26] Davies, J., *Measurable obstructions for unmeasurable colourings*. Preprint (2026).
  [arXiv:2610.12301](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12301)
- [Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
- [FrWi81] Frankl, P. and Wilson, R. M., *Intersection theorems with geometric consequences*.
  Combinatorica (1981), 357-368.
- [LaRo72] Larman, D. G. and Rogers, C. A., *The realization of distances within sets in
  Euclidean space*. Mathematika (1972), 1-24.
- [Pr20] Prosanov, R., *A new proof of the Larman-Rogers upper bound for the chromatic number of
  the Euclidean space*. Discrete Appl. Math. (2020), 115-120.
- [Ra00] Raigorodskii, A. M., *On the chromatic number of a space*. Uspekhi Mat. Nauk (2000),
  147-148.

statements.name: Erdos704.erdos_704.parts.i
statements.doc:
Does $\chi(G_n)$ grow exponentially in $n$?

Yes: Frankl and Wilson [FrWi81] proved an exponential lower bound and Larman and Rogers
[LaRo72] proved an exponential upper bound. Here exponential growth means that there are
constants $1 < c \leq C$ such that $c^n \leq \chi(G_n) \leq C^n$ for all large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_704.parts.i :
    (∃ c > (1 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ k : ℕ, (unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k → c ^ n ≤ (k : ℝ)) ∧
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∃ k : ℕ, (unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k ∧ (k : ℝ) ≤ C ^ n

statements.name: Erdos704.erdos_704.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $G_n$ be the unit distance graph in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with two vertices joined by an edge if
and only if the distance between them is $1$. Does
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\chi(G_n)^{1/n}$$
exist?

This generalises the Hadwiger–Nelson problem (Erdős Problem 508), the case $n = 2$. The
chromatic number is finite (see `Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.cube_colouring`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_704.parts.ii :
    ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((unitDistanceGraph n).chromaticNumber.toNat : ℝ) ^ (1 / (n : ℝ)))
      atTop (𝓝 L)

statements.name: Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.cube_colouring
statements.doc:
The trivial colouring (by tiling with cubes) gives
$$\chi(G_n) \leq (2 + \sqrt{n})^n.$$
In particular $\chi(G_n)$ is finite for every $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_704.variants.cube_colouring :
    ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ k : ℕ, (unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k ∧
      (k : ℝ) ≤ (2 + Real.sqrt n) ^ n

statements.name: Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.frankl_wilson
statements.doc:
Frankl and Wilson [FrWi81] proved
$$\chi(G_n) \geq (1 + o(1)) 1.2^n.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_704.variants.frankl_wilson :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ k : ℕ, (unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k → (1 - ε) * 1.2 ^ n ≤ (k : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.raigorodskii
statements.doc:
Raigorodskii [Ra00] proved
$$\chi(G_n) \geq (1.239\cdots + o(1))^n.$$
We state the weaker bound with the truncated constant $1.239$: for every $0 < c < 1.239$ we
have $\chi(G_n) \geq c^n$ for all large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_704.variants.raigorodskii :
    ∀ c ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1.239, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ k : ℕ, (unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k → c ^ n ≤ (k : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.davies_lower
statements.doc:
Davies [Da26, Theorem 1.4] proved
$$\chi(G_n) \geq (2 + o(1))^n,$$
improving the bound of Raigorodskii (see `Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.raigorodskii`): for every
$0 < c < 2$ we have $\chi(G_n) \geq c^n$ for all large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_704.variants.davies_lower :
    ∀ c ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 2, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ k : ℕ, (unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k → c ^ n ≤ (k : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.larman_rogers
statements.doc:
Larman and Rogers [LaRo72] proved
$$\chi(G_n) \leq (3 + o(1))^n.$$
Prosanov [Pr20] has given an alternative proof of this bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_704.variants.larman_rogers :
    ∀ C > (3 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∃ k : ℕ, (unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k ∧ (k : ℝ) ≤ C ^ n

statements.name: Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.davies_upper
statements.doc:
Davies [Da26, Theorem 1.5] proved
$$\chi(G_n) \leq (3\sqrt{3}/2 + o(1))^n,$$
improving the bound of Larman and Rogers (see `Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.larman_rogers`).
(The abstract of [Da26] prints $3\sqrt{3}/4$; Theorem 1.5 has $3\sqrt{3}/2 \approx 2.598$.)
