statements.statement:
theorem erdos_704.variants.davies_upper :
    ∀ C > 3 * Real.sqrt 3 / 2, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∃ k : ℕ, (unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k ∧ (k : ℝ) ≤ C ^ n

statements.name: Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.larman_rogers_conjecture
statements.doc:
Larman and Rogers [LaRo72] conjecture that the truth may be
$$\chi(G_n) = (2^{3/2} + o(1))^n,$$
that is, $\chi(G_n)^{1/n} \to 2^{3/2}$.

This is false: by `Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.davies_upper` [Da26] we have
$\limsup \chi(G_n)^{1/n} \leq 3\sqrt{3}/2 < 2^{3/2}$. Whether the limit exists remains open
(`Erdos704.erdos_704.parts.ii`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_704.variants.larman_rogers_conjecture :
    ¬ Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((unitDistanceGraph n).chromaticNumber.toNat : ℝ) ^ (1 / (n : ℝ)))
      atTop (𝓝 ((2 : ℝ) ^ ((3 : ℝ) / 2)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 705
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/705](https://www.erdosproblems.com/705)
- [OD99] P. O'Donnell, High girth unit-distance graphs. PhD Dissertation, Rutgers University (1999).

statements.name: Erdos705.erdos_705
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a finite unit distance graph in $\mamthbb{R}^2$.
Is there some $k$ such that if $G$ has girth $≥ k$, then $\chi(G) ≤ 3$?

The general case was solved by O'Donnell [OD99], who constructed finite unit distance graphs with
chromatic number $4$ and arbitrarily large girth.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_705:
  ¬ ∃ k, ∀ V : Set ℝ², V.Finite →
    (UnitDistancePlaneGraph V).girth ≥ k → (UnitDistancePlaneGraph V).chromaticNumber ≤ 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 706
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/706](https://www.erdosproblems.com/706)
- [Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.

statements.name: Erdos706.erdos_706
statements.doc:
Let $L(r)$ be such that if $G$ is a graph formed by taking a finite set of points $P$ in
$\mathbb{R}^2$ and some set $A\subset (0,\infty)$ of size $r$, where the vertex set is $P$ and
there is an edge between two points if and only if their distance is a member of $A$, then
$\chi(G)\leq L(r)$.

Estimate $L(r)$. In particular, is it true that $L(r)\leq r^{O(1)}$?

The case $r=1$ is the Hadwiger-Nelson problem, for which it is known that
$5\leq L(1)\leq 7$.

See also [508](https://www.erdosproblems.com/508), [704](https://www.erdosproblems.com/704),
and [705](https://www.erdosproblems.com/705).

Here $L(r)\leq r^{O(1)}$ is read as: there is $C$ with $\chi(G)\leq r^C$ for all large $r$. Small
$r$ must be excluded, since $L(1)\geq 5 > 1^C$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_706 :
    ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ᶠ r : ℕ in atTop, ∀ (P : Finset ℝ²) (A : Finset ℝ), A.card = r →
      (∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a) →
      (SimpleGraph.DistancePlaneGraph (A : Set ℝ) (P : Set ℝ²)).chromaticNumber ≤
        (r ^ C : ℕ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 707: Embedding Sidon Sets in Perfect Difference Sets
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/707](https://www.erdosproblems.com/707)
- [arxiv/2510.19804](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.19804) Boris Alexeev and Dustin G. Mixon, Forbidden
  Sidon subsets of perfect difference sets, featuring a human-assisted proof (2025)
- [Ha47] Marshall Hall, Jr., Cyclic projective planes, Duke Math. J. 14 (1947), 1079–1090.

Let `A ⊆ ℕ` be a finite Sidon set. Is there some set `B` with `A ⊆ B` which is a perfect
difference set modulo `p^2 + p + 1` for some prime power `p`?

This problem is related to Erdős Problem 329 about the maximum density of Sidon sets.
If this conjecture is true, it would imply that the maximum density of Sidon sets is 1.

statements.name: Erdos707.erdos_707
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 707**: It is false that any finite Sidon set can be embedded in a perfect
different set modulo some $n$.

As described in [arxiv/2510.19804], a counterexample is provided in [Ha47], see below.
The proof of this has been formalized.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using ChatGPT.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_707 : (∀ (A : Set ℕ) (h : A.Finite), IsSidon A →
    ∃ᵉ (B : Set ℕ) (n > 0), A ⊆ B ∧ IsPerfectDifferenceSet B n) ↔ False

statements.name: Erdos707.erdos_707.variants.prime_power
statements.doc:
It is false that any finite Sidon set can be embedded in a perfect
difference set modulo `p^2 + p + 1` for some prime power `p`.

As described in [arxiv/2510.19804], a counterexample is provided in [Ha47], see below.
The proof of this has been formalized.
-
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_707.variants.prime_power : (∀ (A : Set ℕ) (h : A.Finite), IsSidon A →
    ∃ (B : Set ℕ) (p : ℕ), IsPrimePow p ∧ A ⊆ B ∧
    IsPerfectDifferenceSet B (p^2 + p + 1)) ↔ False

statements.name: Erdos707.erdos_707.variants.prime
statements.doc:
It is false that any finite Sidon set can be embedded in a perfect
difference set modulo `p^2 + p + 1` for some prime `p`.

As described in [arxiv/2510.19804], a counterexample is provided in [Ha47], see below.
The proof of this has been formalized.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_707.variants.prime : (∀ (A : Set ℕ) (h : A.Finite), IsSidon A →
    ∃ᵉ (B : Set ℕ) (p : ℕ), p.Prime ∧ A ⊆ B ∧ IsPerfectDifferenceSet B (p^2 + p + 1)) ↔ False

statements.name: Erdos707.erdos_707.variants.counterexample_prime
statements.doc:
Alexeev and Mixon [arxiv/2510.19804] have disproved this conjecture, proving that $\{1,2,4,8\}$
cannot be extended to a perfect difference set modulo $p^2+p+1$
for any prime $p$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_707.variants.counterexample_prime (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A = {1, 2, 4, 8}) :
   Finite A ∧ IsSidon A ∧
   ∀ (B : Set ℕ) (p : ℕ),
    Prime p → A ⊆ B → ¬IsPerfectDifferenceSet B (p ^ 2 + p + 1)

statements.name: Erdos707.erdos_707.variants.counterexample_mian_chowla
statements.doc:
Alexeev and Mixon [arxiv/2510.19804] have disproved this conjecture,
showing that $\{1, 2, 4, 8, 13\}$ cannot be extended to any perfect difference set modulo a
positive integer. The modulus `0` is excluded, as in `erdos_707`: `IsPerfectDifferenceSet B 0`
describes an infinite perfect difference set in `ℤ`, and every finite Sidon set extends to one.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_707.variants.counterexample_mian_chowla (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A = {1, 2, 4, 8, 13}) :
   Finite A ∧ IsSidon A ∧
   ∀ (B : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → A ⊆ B → ¬IsPerfectDifferenceSet B n

statements.name: Erdos707.erdos_707.variants.counterexample_hall
statements.doc:
This conjecture was actually first disproved by Hall in 1947 [Ha47], long before Erdős asked
this question.
A counterexample for any modulus from from [Ha47] in the paragraph following Theorem 4.3, where it
was given as $\{-8, -6, 0, 1, 4\}$, but this can be shifted to natural numbers
as pointed out in [arxiv/2510.19804].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_707.variants.counterexample_hall (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A = {1, 3, 9, 10, 13}) :
   Finite A ∧ IsSidon A ∧
   ∀ (B : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → A ⊆ B → ¬IsPerfectDifferenceSet B n

statements.name: Erdos707.erdos_707.variants.perfect_difference_set_size_bound
statements.doc: A perfect difference set modulo `n` must have size `≤ √n + 1`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_707.variants.perfect_difference_set_size_bound (B : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ)
    (hB : IsPerfectDifferenceSet B n) : B.ncard ≤ n.sqrt + 1

statements.name: Erdos707.erdos_707.variants.singer_construction
statements.doc:
The Singer construction gives perfect difference sets for `n = p^2 + p + 1` where `p` is a
prime power.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_707.variants.singer_construction (p : ℕ) (hp : IsPrimePow p) :
    ∃ (B : Set ℕ), IsPerfectDifferenceSet B (p^2 + p + 1) ∧ B.ncard = p + 1

statements.name: Erdos707.erdos_707.variants.example_sidon_set
statements.doc: The set `{1, 2, 4}` is a Sidon set.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_707.variants.example_sidon_set : IsSidon ({1, 2, 4} : Set ℕ)

statements.name: Erdos707.erdos_707.variants.example_embedding
statements.doc: The set `{1, 2, 4}` can be embedded in a perfect difference set modulo 7.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_707.variants.example_embedding : ∃ (B : Set ℕ), {1, 2, 4} ⊆ B ∧
    IsPerfectDifferenceSet B 7

statements.name: Erdos707.erdos_707.variants.small_sidon_sets
statements.doc: For small Sidon sets, we can check the conjecture directly.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_707.variants.small_sidon_sets (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Finite) (h : A.ncard ≤ 3)
    (hSidon : IsSidon A) : ∃ (B : Set ℕ) (p : ℕ), IsPrimePow p ∧ A ⊆ B ∧
    IsPerfectDifferenceSet B (p^2 + p + 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 709
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/709](https://www.erdosproblems.com/709)
- [ErSu59] P. Erdős and J. Surányi, Bemerkungen zu einer Aufgabe eines mathematischen
  Wettbewerbs, Mat. Lapok 10 (1959), 39–48.
- [Er92c] P. Erdős, Some of my forgotten problems in number theory, Hardy–Ramanujan J. 15
  (1992), 34–50.
- [vD26] W. van Doorn, On the length of an interval that contains distinct multiples of the
  first $n$ positive integers, Integers (2026), #A7.

statements.name: Erdos709.erdos_709.variants.singleton
statements.doc: Erdős Problem 709 holds for a singleton input: the multiplier `1` suffices.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_709.variants.singleton : Works 1 1

statements.name: Erdos709.erdos_709
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that, for any $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}\subseteq [2,\infty)\cap\mathbb{N}$
of size $n$, in any interval $I$ of $f(n)\max(A)$ consecutive integers there exist distinct
$x_1,\ldots,x_n\in I$ such that $a_i\mid x_i$.

Obtain good bounds for $f(n)$, or even an asymptotic formula.

We read "good bounds" as determining the order of magnitude of $f(n)$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_709 : f =Θ[atTop] erdos_709.answer

statements.name: Erdos709.erdos_709.variants.ersu_lower
statements.doc:
A problem of Erdős and Surányi [ErSu59], who proved
$$(\log n)^c \ll f(n) \ll n^{1/2}$$
for some constant $c>0$.

This is the lower bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_709.variants.ersu_lower :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log n ^ c) =O[atTop] f

statements.name: Erdos709.erdos_709.variants.ersu_upper
statements.doc:
A problem of Erdős and Surányi [ErSu59], who proved
$$(\log n)^c \ll f(n) \ll n^{1/2}$$
for some constant $c>0$.

This is the upper bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_709.variants.ersu_upper :
    f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos709.erdos_709.variants.van_doorn_lower
statements.doc:
The lower bound here can be improved, using van Doorn's lower bound for [711] from [vD26], to
$$\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\ll f(n).$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_709.variants.van_doorn_lower :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log n / Real.log (Real.log n)) =O[atTop] f

problems.title: Erdős Problem 710
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/710](https://www.erdosproblems.com/710)
- [ErPo80] Erdős, P. and Pomerance, C., *Matching the natural numbers up to $n$ with distinct
  multiples in another interval*. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch. Indag. Math. 42 (1980), 147-161.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-13.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos710.erdos_710
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that in $(n,n+f(n))$ there exist distinct integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$
such that $k\mid a_k$ for all $1\leq k\leq n$. Obtain an asymptotic formula for $f(n)$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_710 : (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] erdos_710.answer

statements.name: Erdos710.erdos_710.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős and Pomerance [ErPo80] proved
$$\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{e}}+o(1)\right)n\left(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right)^{1/2}
\leq f(n) \leq (1.7398\cdots+o(1))n(\log n)^{1/2}.$$

This is the lower bound [ErPo80, Theorem 2].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_710.variants.lower_bound :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (2 / Real.sqrt (Real.exp 1) - ε) * n *
        Real.sqrt (Real.log n / Real.log (Real.log n)) ≤ (f n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos710.erdos_710.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős and Pomerance [ErPo80] proved
$$\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{e}}+o(1)\right)n\left(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right)^{1/2}
\leq f(n) \leq (1.7398\cdots+o(1))n(\log n)^{1/2}.$$

This is the upper bound. Here $1.7398\cdots = \sqrt{r}/(1-r)$, where $r$ is the solution of
$e^{-r} = r$ [ErPo80, (11), p. 154].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_710.variants.upper_bound :
    ∃ r : ℝ, Real.exp (-r) = r ∧ ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (f n : ℝ) ≤ (Real.sqrt r / (1 - r) + ε) * n * Real.sqrt (Real.log n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 711
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/711](https://www.erdosproblems.com/711)
- [ErPo80] Erdős, P. and Pomerance, C.,
  *Matching the natural numbers up to $n$ with distinct multiples in another interval* (1980).
- [Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my forgotten problems in number theory*.
  Hardy-Ramanujan J. (1992), 34–50.
- [vD26] van Doorn, W.,
  [*On the length of an interval that contains distinct multiples of the first $n$ positive
  integers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.16972). Integers 26 (2026), #A7.

statements.name: Erdos711.erdos_711.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $f(n,m)$ be minimal such that $(m,m+f(n,m))$ contains distinct integers
$a_1,\ldots,a_n$ with $k \mid a_k$ for $1 \leq k \leq n$. Prove that
$\max_m f(n,m) \leq n^{1+o(1)}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_711.parts.i : ∃ error : ℕ → ℝ,
    error =o[atTop] (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ m, ∃ L,
      HasDivisibleDistinctTuple n m L ∧ (L : ℝ) ≤ Real.rpow n (1 + error n)

statements.name: Erdos711.erdos_711.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Prove that $\max_m (f(n,m)-f(n,n)) \to \infty$.

This was proved by van Doorn [vD26], who obtained the stronger lower bound
$f(n,m)-f(n,n) \gg n\log n/\log\log n$ for a suitable $m=m(n)$ and all large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_711.parts.ii : ∀ B : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
    ∃ m Lm Ln : ℕ, IsMinimalIntervalLength n m Lm ∧
      IsMinimalIntervalLength n n Ln ∧ B ≤ Lm - Ln

problems.title: Erdős Problem 712
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/712](https://www.erdosproblems.com/712)
- [Er81] Erdős, P., On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.

statements.name: Erdos712.erdos_712
statements.doc:
Determine, for any $k>r>2$, the limiting value as $n\to\infty$ of
$$\frac{\mathrm{ex}_r(n,K_k^r)}{\binom{n}{r}},$$
where $\mathrm{ex}_r(n,K_k^r)$ is the largest number of $r$-edges which can placed on $n$ vertices
so that there exists no set of $k$ vertices which is covered by all $\binom{k}{r}$ possible
$r$-edges.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_712 :
    ∀ k r : ℕ, 2 < r → r < k →
      Tendsto (fun n ↦ (Hypergraph.cliqueExtremalNumber n r k : ℝ) / n.choose r)
        atTop (𝓝 (erdos_712.answer k r))

statements.name: Erdos712.erdos_712.variants.limit_exists
statements.doc:
The normalized extremal numbers have a limit in $[0,1]$. This existence result does
not determine the value asked for in Erdős Problem 712.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_712.variants.limit_exists (r k : ℕ) :
    ∃ π ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Hypergraph.cliqueExtremalNumber n r k : ℝ) / n.choose r)
        atTop (𝓝 π)

statements.name: Erdos712.erdos_712.variants.graph_case
statements.doc:
Turán's theorem gives the graph case:
$\mathrm{ex}_2(n,K_k)/\binom{n}{2}\to 1-1/(k-1)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_712.variants.graph_case (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Hypergraph.cliqueExtremalNumber n 2 k : ℝ) / n.choose 2)
      atTop (𝓝 (1 - 1 / ((k : ℝ) - 1)))

statements.name: Erdos712.erdos_712.variants.graph_case_div_sq
statements.doc:
With denominator $n^2$, Turán's graph limit is
$\frac12(1-1/(k-1))$. The factor $\frac12$ comes from the normalization.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_712.variants.graph_case_div_sq (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Hypergraph.cliqueExtremalNumber n 2 k : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) ^ 2)
      atTop (𝓝 ((1 / 2) * (1 - 1 / ((k : ℝ) - 1))))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 713
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/713](https://www.erdosproblems.com/713)
- [Er67d] Erdős, P., *Some recent results on extremal problems in graph theory. {R}esults*. (1967),
  117--123 (English); pp. 124--130 (French).
- [ErSi70] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M., *Some extremal problems in graph theory*. Combinatorial
  theory and its applications, I-III (Proc. Colloq., Balatonfüred, 1969) (1970), 377-390.
- [FrFu87] Frankl, P. and Füredi, Z., *Exact solution of some Turán-type problems*. J. Combin.
  Theory Ser. A (1987), 226--262.
- [FuGe21] Füredi, Zoltán and Gerbner, Dániel, *Hypergraphs without exponents*. J. Combin. Theory
  Ser. A (2021), Paper No. 105517, 9.

statements.name: Erdos713.erdos_713.parts.i
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for every bipartite graph $G$, there exists some $\alpha\in [1,2)$ and $c>0$ such that $$\mathrm{ex}(n;G)\sim cn^\alpha?$$

The condition that $G$ have at least two edges excludes degenerate forbidden graphs whose
extremal number is eventually zero, for which the displayed asymptotic with $c>0$ is impossible.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_713.parts.i :
    ∀ (q : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), G.IsBipartite → 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
      ∃ α c : ℝ, α ∈ Set.Ico 1 2 ∧ 0 < c ∧
        Asymptotics.IsEquivalent atTop
          (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n G : ℝ))
          (fun n : ℕ => c * (n : ℝ) ^ α)

statements.name: Erdos713.erdos_713.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Must $\alpha$ be rational?

The same nondegeneracy condition on $G$ is used as in part (i). Rationality means that the real
number $\alpha$ lies in the image of the canonical embedding $\mathbb{Q}\to\mathbb{R}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_713.parts.ii :
    ∀ (q : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), G.IsBipartite → 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
      ∀ α c : ℝ, α ∈ Set.Ico 1 2 → 0 < c →
        Asymptotics.IsEquivalent atTop
          (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n G : ℝ))
          (fun n : ℕ => c * (n : ℝ) ^ α) →
        α ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℚ → ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 714
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/714](https://www.erdosproblems.com/714)
- [Br66] Brown, W. G., *On graphs that do not contain a Thomsen graph*. Canad. Math. Bull. (1966),
  281-285.
- [ERS66] Erdős, P. and Rényi, A. and Sós, V. T., *On a problem of graph theory*. Studia Sci. Math.
  Hungar. (1966), 215--235.
- [KST54] Kövari, T. and Sós, V. T. and Turán, P., *On a problem of K. Zarankiewicz*. Colloq. Math.
  (1954), 50-57.

statements.name: Erdos714.erdos_714
statements.doc: Is it true that $$\mathrm{ex}(n; K_{r,r}) \gg n^{2-1/r}?$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_714 :
    ∀ r : ℕ, 2 ≤ r → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) - 1 / (r : ℝ)) ≤
        (extremalNumber n (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin r) (Fin r)) : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 716
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/716](https://www.erdosproblems.com/716)
- [BES73] Brown, W. G. and Erdős, P. and S\'os, V. T., Some extremal problems on {$r$}-graphs.
  (1973), 53--63.
- [RuSz78] Ruzsa, I. Z. and Szemer\'{e}di, E., Triple systems with no six points carrying three
  triangles. Combinatorics (Proc. Fifth Hungarian Colloq., Keszthely, 1976), Vol. II (1978), 939-945.

statements.name: Erdos716.erdos_716
statements.doc:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the family of all $3$-uniform hypergraphs with $6$ vertices and $3$ $3$-edges.
Is it true that
$$\mathrm{ex}_3(n,\mathcal{F})=o(n^2)?$$

The answer is yes, proved by Ruzsa and Szemerédi [RuSz78] (this is known as the Ruzsa-Szemerédi
problem).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_716 :
    (fun n ↦ (Hypergraph.configurationExtremalNumber n 3 6 3 : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 717
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/717](https://www.erdosproblems.com/717)
- [ErFa81] Erdős, Paul and Fajtlowicz, Siemion, *On the conjecture of Hajós*. Combinatorica 1
  (1981), 141-143. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-17.pdf)
- [FLS13] Fox, Jacob and Lee, Choongbum and Sudakov, Benny, *Chromatic number, clique
  subdivisions, and the conjectures of Hajós and Erdős-Fajtlowicz*. Combinatorica 33 (2013),
  181-197. [arXiv:1107.1920](https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.1920)

statements.name: Erdos717.erdos_717
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with chromatic number $\chi(G)$ and let $\sigma(G)$ be the
maximal $k$ such that $G$ contains a subdivision of $K_k$. Is it true that
$$\chi(G) \ll \frac{n^{1/2}}{\log n}\sigma(G)?$$

The answer is yes, proved by Fox, Lee, and Sudakov [FLS13, Theorem 1.1]. We read $\ll$ as: there
is an absolute constant $C > 0$ with this inequality for all graphs on $n \geq 2$ vertices
(for $n = 1$, $\log n = 0$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_717 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        2 ≤ Fintype.card V →
        (G.chromaticNumber.toNat : ℝ) ≤
          C * (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V : ℝ) / Real.log (Fintype.card V : ℝ)) *
            (cliqueSubdivisionNumber G : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos717.erdos_717.variants.erdos_fajtlowicz
statements.doc:
Erdős and Fajtlowicz [ErFa81, Theorem 3] showed that for almost all graphs on $n$ vertices
$$\chi(G) \gg \frac{n^{1/2}}{\log n}\sigma(G).$$
As in [ErFa81, p. 141], "almost all" means all but $o(2^{\binom{n}{2}})$ labelled graphs on $n$
vertices.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_717.variants.erdos_fajtlowicz :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ =>
        (Nat.card {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n) //
          ¬ (C * (Real.sqrt n / Real.log n) * (cliqueSubdivisionNumber G : ℝ) <
            (G.chromaticNumber.toNat : ℝ))} : ℝ) / 2 ^ n.choose 2) atTop (𝓝 0)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 719
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/719](https://www.erdosproblems.com/719)

statements.name: Erdos719.erdos_719
statements.doc:
Let $r\geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{ex}_r(n;K_{r+1}^r)$ be the maximum number of $r$-edges that can
be placed on $n$ vertices without forming a $K_{r+1}^r$ (the $r$-uniform complete graph on
$r+1$ vertices). Is every
$r$-hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices the union of at most $\mathrm{ex}_{r}(n;K_{r+1}^r)$ many copies
of $K_r^r$ and $K_{r+1}^r$, no two of which share a $K_r^r$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_719 :
    ∀ r : ℕ, 2 ≤ r → ∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
    H.IsUniform r → ∃ D : Finset (Finset (Fin n)),
      H.IsCompleteHypergraphDecomposition r D ∧
        D.card ≤ Hypergraph.cliqueExtremalNumber n r (r + 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 720
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/720](https://www.erdosproblems.com/720)
- [Er76c] Erdős, P., _Some recent problems and results in graph theory, combinatorics and number
  theory_. Proceedings of the Seventh Southeastern Conference on Combinatorics, Graph Theory,
  and Computing (Louisiana State Univ., Baton Rouge, La., 1976) (1976), 3-14.
- [EFRS78b] Erdős, P. and Faudree, R. J. and Rousseau, C. C. and Schelp, R. H., _The size Ramsey
  number_. Period. Math. Hungar. (1978), 145-161.
- [Er78] Erdős, Paul, _Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory_. Proceedings of the Ninth Southeastern Conference on Combinatorics, Graph Theory, and
  Computing (Florida Atlantic Univ., Boca Raton, Fla., 1978) (1978), 29-40.
- [Er81] Erdős, P., _On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved_.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, _Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved_. (1982),
  59--79.
- [Be83b] Beck, József, _On size Ramsey number of paths, trees, and circuits. I_. J. Graph
  Theory (1983), 115-129.

statements.name: Erdos720.erdos_720.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $\hat{R}(G)$ denote the size Ramsey number, the minimal number of edges $m$ such that there
is a graph $H$ with $m$ edges such that in any $2$-colouring of the edges of $H$ there is a
monochromatic copy of $G$.

Is it true that, if $P_n$ is the path of length $n$, then $\hat{R}(P_n)/n\to \infty$?

The answer is no: Beck [Be83b] proved that in fact $\hat{R}(P_n)\ll n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_720.parts.i :
    ¬ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (sizeRamseyNumber (pathGraph (n + 1)) : ℝ) / n) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos720.erdos_720.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is it true that, if $P_n$ is the path of length $n$, then $\hat{R}(P_n)/n^2 \to 0$?

The answer is yes: Beck [Be83b] proved that in fact $\hat{R}(P_n)\ll n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_720.parts.ii :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (sizeRamseyNumber (pathGraph (n + 1)) : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) ^ 2) atTop
      (nhds 0)

statements.name: Erdos720.erdos_720.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Is it true that, if $C_n$ is the cycle with $n$ edges, then $\hat{R}(C_n) =o(n^2)$?

The answer is yes: Beck [Be83b] proved that in fact $\hat{R}(C_n)\ll n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_720.parts.iii :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (sizeRamseyNumber (cycleGraph n) : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) ^ 2) atTop
      (nhds 0)

statements.name: Erdos720.erdos_720.variants.beck
statements.doc: Beck [Be83b] proved that $\hat{R}(P_n)\ll n$ and $\hat{R}(C_n)\ll n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_720.variants.beck :
    ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      sizeRamseyNumber (pathGraph (n + 1)) ≤ C * n ∧
        sizeRamseyNumber (cycleGraph n) ≤ C * n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 721
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/721](https://www.erdosproblems.com/721)
- [Gr22] Green, B., *New lower bounds for van der Waerden numbers*.
  [arXiv:2102.01543](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.01543).
- [Hu22] Hunter, Z., *Improved lower bounds for van der Waerden numbers*.
  [arXiv:2111.01099](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.01099).
- [Sc21] Schoen, T., *A subexponential upper bound for van der Waerden numbers W(3,k)*.
  [arXiv:2006.02877](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.02877).

statements.name: Erdos721.erdos_721.upper_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős Problem 721, upper bound: prove that $W(3,k) < \exp(k^c)$ for some
constant $c<1$.

The first to show that $W(3,k) < \exp(k^c)$ for some $c<1$ was Schoen [Sc21].
Source: [erdosproblems.com/721](https://www.erdosproblems.com/721).
The exponent is fixed independently of $k$, and the bound holds for all
sufficiently large $k$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_721.upper_bound : SubexponentialUpperBound

statements.name: Erdos721.erdos_721.lower_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős Problem 721, lower bound: Hunter [Hu22] improved this to
$W(3,k) \geq \exp\left(c\frac{(\log k)^2}{\log\log k}\right)$
for some constant $c>0$.

Source: [erdosproblems.com/721](https://www.erdosproblems.com/721).
This eventual bound uses a nonforcing interval of length $N$ and the
successor $N+1$ as a lower bound for the least forcing integer.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_721.lower_bound : HunterLowerBound

problems.title: Erdős Problem 722
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/722](https://www.erdosproblems.com/722)
- [Ha61] Hanani, Haim, The existence and construction of balanced incomplete block designs. Ann.
  Math. Statist. (1961), 361-386.
- [Ke14] P. Keevash, The existence of designs. arXiv:1401.3665 (2014).
- [Wi72] Wilson, Richard M., An existence theory for pairwise balanced designs. {II}. The structure
  of {PBD}-closed sets and the existence conjectures. J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. A (1972), 246-273.

statements.name: Erdos722.erdos_722
statements.doc:
Let $k>r$ and $n$ be sufficiently large in terms of $k$ and $r$. Does there always exist a block
$r-(n,k,1)$ design (or Steiner system with parameters $(n,k,r)$), provided the trivial necessary
divisibility conditions $\binom{k-i}{r-i}\mid \binom{n-i}{r-i}$ are satisfied for every $0\leq i<r$?
That is, can one find a family of $\binom{n}{r}\binom{k}{r}^{-1}$ many subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$,
all of size $k$, such that any $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ of size $r$ is contained in exactly one
set in the family?

This was proved by Keevash [Ke14] for all $(r,k)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_722 :
    ∀ r k : ℕ, 1 ≤ r → r < k → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    (∀ i < r, (k - i).choose (r - i) ∣ (n - i).choose (r - i)) →
      ∃ H : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), H.IsBlockDesign r k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 723: The prime power conjecture.
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/723](https://www.erdosproblems.com/723)

statements.name: Erdos723.erdos_723
statements.doc: If there is a finite projective plane of order $n$ then must $n$ be a prime power?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_723 :
    ∀ {P L : Type} (_: Membership P L) (_ : Fintype P) (_ : Fintype L),
      ∀ pp : ProjectivePlane P L, IsPrimePow pp.order

statements.name: Erdos723.erdos_723.variants.prime_power_is_projplane_order
statements.doc: These always exist if $n$ is a prime power.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_723.variants.prime_power_is_projplane_order :
    ∀ n, IsPrimePow n → ∃ (P L : Type) (_ : Membership P L) (_ : Fintype P) (_ : Fintype L)
      (pp : ProjectivePlane P L), pp.order = n

statements.name: Erdos723.erdos_723.variants.leq_11
statements.doc: This conjecture has been proved for $n \leq 11$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_723.variants.leq_11 {P L : Type} [Membership P L] [Fintype P] [Fintype L] :
    ∀ pp : ProjectivePlane P L, pp.order ≤ 11 → IsPrimePow pp.order

statements.name: Erdos723.erdos_723.variants.eq_12
statements.doc: It is open whether there exists a projective plane of order 12.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_723.variants.eq_12 :
    ∃ (P L : Type) (_ : Membership P L) (_ : Fintype P) (_ : Fintype L) (pp : ProjectivePlane P L),
      pp.order = 12

statements.name: Erdos723.erdos_723.variants.bruck_ryser
statements.doc:
Bruck and Ryser have proved that if $n \equiv 1 (\mod 4)$ or $n \equiv 2 (\mod 4)$ then $n$ must be
the sum of two squares.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_723.variants.bruck_ryser {P L : Type} [Membership P L] [Fintype P] [Fintype L]
    (n : ℕ) (pp : ProjectivePlane P L) (hpp : pp.order = n) :
    (n ≡ 1 [MOD 4] ∨ n ≡ 2 [MOD 4]) → ∃ a b, n = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 724
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/724](https://www.erdosproblems.com/724)
- [OEIS A001438](https://oeis.org/A001438)
- [Be83c] Beth, Thomas, *Eine Bemerkung zur Abschätzung der Anzahl orthogonaler lateinischer
  Quadrate mittels Siebverfahren*. Abh. Math. Sem. Univ. Hamburg (1983), 284-288.
- [BPS60] Bose, R. C. and Shrikhande, S. S. and Parker, E. T., *Further results on the
  construction of mutually orthogonal Latin squares and the falsity of Euler's conjecture*.
  Canadian J. Math. (1960), 189-203.
- [CES60] Chowla, S. and Erdős, P. and Straus, E. G., *On the maximal number of pairwise
  orthogonal Latin squares of a given order*. Canadian J. Math. (1960), 204-208.
- [Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
- [Wi74] Wilson, Richard M., *Concerning the number of mutually orthogonal Latin squares*.
  Discrete Math. (1974), 181-198.

statements.name: Erdos724.erdos_724
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be the maximum number of mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order $n$. Is it true
that
$$f(n) \gg n^{1/2}?$$
This question is from [Er81].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_724 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) ≤ (maxMOLS n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos724.erdos_724.variants.euler_conjecture
statements.doc:
Euler conjectured that $f(n) = 1$ when $n \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$. This is false: Bose, Parker, and
Shrikhande [BPS60] proved $f(n) \geq 2$ for $n \geq 7$, so for example $f(10) \geq 2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_724.variants.euler_conjecture :
    ¬ ∀ n : ℕ, n ≡ 2 [MOD 4] → maxMOLS n = 1

statements.name: Erdos724.erdos_724.variants.bose_parker_shrikhande
statements.doc: Bose, Parker, and Shrikhande [BPS60] proved that $f(n) \geq 2$ for all $n \geq 7$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_724.variants.bose_parker_shrikhande :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 7 ≤ n → 2 ≤ maxMOLS n

statements.name: Erdos724.erdos_724.variants.chowla_erdos_straus
statements.doc:
Chowla, Erdős, and Straus [CES60] proved that
$$f(n) \gg n^{1/91}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_724.variants.chowla_erdos_straus :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 91) ≤ (maxMOLS n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos724.erdos_724.variants.wilson
statements.doc:
Wilson [Wi74] proved that
$$f(n) \gg n^{1/17}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_724.variants.wilson :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 17) ≤ (maxMOLS n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos724.erdos_724.variants.beth
statements.doc:
Beth [Be83c] proved that
$$f(n) \gg n^{1/14.8}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_724.variants.beth :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 14.8) ≤ (maxMOLS n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos724.erdos_724.variants.le_sub_one
statements.doc:
For $n \geq 2$ there are at most $n - 1$ mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order $n$:
$$f(n) \leq n - 1.$$
This is classical; see OEIS A001438.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_724.variants.le_sub_one :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → maxMOLS n ≤ n - 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 725
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/725](https://www.erdosproblems.com/725)
- [Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*.
  Combinatorica 1 (1981), 25-42. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-16.pdf)
- [ErKa46] Erdős, P. and Kaplansky, I., *The asymptotic number of Latin rectangles*.
  Amer. J. Math. 68 (1946), 230-236. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1946-12.pdf)
- [Ya51] Yamamoto, K., *On the asymptotic number of Latin rectangles*.
  Jpn. J. Math. 21 (1951), 113-119.

statements.name: Erdos725.erdos_725
statements.doc:
Give an asymptotic formula for the number of $k\times n$ Latin rectangles.

The formula $F(k,n)$ must satisfy $L(k,n)\sim F(k,n)$ as $n\to\infty$ for every choice of
$k=k(n)\leq n$, so it also covers Latin squares ($k=n$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_725 (k : ℕ → ℕ) (hk : ∀ n, k n ≤ n) :
    (fun n ↦ (L (k n) n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] fun n ↦ erdos_725.answer (k n) n

statements.name: Erdos725.erdos_725.variants.erdos_kaplansky
statements.doc:
Erdős and Kaplansky [ErKa46] proved the count is
$$\sim e^{-\binom{k}{2}}(n!)^k$$
when $k=o((\log n)^{3/2-\epsilon})$.

Here $\epsilon>0$ is fixed.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_725.variants.erdos_kaplansky (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (k : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hk : (fun n ↦ (k n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] fun n ↦ Real.log n ^ (3 / 2 - ε)) :
    (fun n ↦ (L (k n) n : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
      fun n ↦ Real.exp (-((k n).choose 2 : ℝ)) * (n.factorial : ℝ) ^ k n

statements.name: Erdos725.erdos_725.variants.yamamoto
statements.doc:
Yamamoto [Ya51] extended this to $k\leq n^{1/3-o(1)}$.

As in [Ya51, p. 113], we assume $k<n^{1/3-\delta}$ with $n^{-\delta}\to 0$, where $\delta$
may be a positive constant or a function of $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_725.variants.yamamoto (δ : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hδ : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (-δ n)) atTop (nhds 0)) (k : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hk : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (k n : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 3 - δ n)) :
    (fun n ↦ (L (k n) n : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
      fun n ↦ Real.exp (-((k n).choose 2 : ℝ)) * (n.factorial : ℝ) ^ k n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 726
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/726](https://www.erdosproblems.com/726)
- [EGRS75] Erdős, P., and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., On the prime factors of
  $(\sp{2n}\sb{n})$. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.

statements.name: Erdos726.erdos_726
statements.doc:
As $n\to \infty$ ranges over integers
$\sum_{p\leq n}1_{n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}}\frac{1}{p}\sim \frac{\log\log n}{2}$?

A conjecture of Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus [EGRS75].

By $n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}$ we mean $n\equiv r\pmod{p}$ for some integer $r$ with $p/2<r<p$.
The remainder `n % p` is computed in `ℕ` before casting to `ℝ`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_726 :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ ∑ p ∈ (range (n + 1)).filter
        (fun p : ℕ ↦ p.Prime ∧ (p : ℝ) / 2 < ((n % p : ℕ) : ℝ)),
      (1 : ℝ) / (p : ℝ))
    ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)) / 2)

statements.name: Erdos726.erdos_726.variants.mertens_estimate
statements.doc: The classical estimate of Mertens states that $\sum_{p\leq n}\frac{1}{p}\sim \log\log n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_726.variants.mertens_estimate :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ ∑ p ∈ (range (n + 1)).filter (fun p ↦ p.Prime), (1 : ℝ) / ((p : ℕ) : ℝ))
    ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 727
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/727](https://www.erdosproblems.com/727)

statements.name: Erdos727.erdos_727
statements.doc: Let $k ≥ 2$. Does $((n+k)!)^2∣(2n)!$ hold for infinitely many $n$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_727 : ∀ k ≥ 2,
    Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | (Nat.factorial (n + k)) ^ 2 ∣ Nat.factorial (2 * n)}

statements.name: Erdos727.erdos_727.variants.k_2
statements.doc:
It is open even for $k = 2$.
Let $k = 2$. Does $((n+k)!)^2∣(2n)!$ hold for infinitely many n?

statements.name: Erdos727.erdos_727.variants.k_1
statements.doc:
Balakran proved this holds for $k = 1$.

Let $k = 1$. Does $((n+k)!)^2∣(2n)!$ for infinitely many $n$?

statements.name: Erdos727.erdos_727.variants.k_1_2
statements.doc:
Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus observe that the method of Balakran can be further used to prove
that there are infinitely many $n$ such that $(n+k)!(n+1)!∣(2n)!$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 728
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/728](https://www.erdosproblems.com/728)

statements.name: Erdos728.erdos_728
statements.doc:
Let $\varepsilon$ be sufficiently small and $C, C' > 0$. Are there integers $a, b, n$ such that
$$a, b > \varepsilon n\quad a!\, b! \mid n!\, (a + b - n)!, $$
and
$$C \log n < a + b - n < C' \log n ?$$

Note that the website currently displays a simpler (trivial) version of this problem because
$a + b$ isn't assumed to be in the $n + O(\log n)$ regime.

Barreto and ChatGPT-5.2 have proved that, for any $0 < C_1 < C_2$, there are infinitely many
$a, b, n$ with $b = n/2$, $a = n/2 + O(\log n)$, and $C_1 \log n < a + b - n < C_2 \log n$ such
that $a! b! \mid n! (a + b - n)!$

This appears to answer the question in the spirit it was intended.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_728 :
    ∀ᶠ ε : ℝ in 𝓝[>] 0, ∀ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ C' > C,
      ∃ a b n : ℕ,
        0 < n ∧
        ε * n < a ∧
        ε * n < b ∧
        a ! * b ! ∣ n ! * (a + b - n)! ∧
        a + b > n + C * log n ∧
        a + b < n + C' * log n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 729
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/729](https://www.erdosproblems.com/729)
- [EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., *On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$*. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.
- [Er68c] Erdős, P., *Aufgabe 557*. Elemente Math. (1968), 111-113.

statements.name: Erdos729.erdos_729
statements.doc:
Let $C>0$ be a constant. Are there infinitely many integers $a,b,n$ with $a+b> n+C\log n$ such
that the denominator of $$\frac{n!}{a!b!}$$contains only primes $\ll_C 1$?

Erdős [Er68c] proved that if $a!b!\mid n!$ then $a+b\leq n+O(\log n)$. This has been proved in the affirmative by Barreto and Leeham, using ChatGPT and Aristotle, with a modification of the argument used for [728].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_729 :
    ∀ (C : ℝ) (hC : C > 0),
      ∃ K ≥ 3, Set.Infinite { T : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ |
        let (a, b, n) := T
        a > 0 ∧ b > 0 ∧ n > 0 ∧
        (a : ℝ) + b > n + C * Real.log n ∧
        ∀ p, p.Prime → p > K →
          padicValNat p ((n.factorial / (a.factorial * b.factorial) : ℚ).den) = 0 }

problems.title: Erdős Problem 730
problems.doc:
*References:*
  - [erdosproblems.com/730](https://www.erdosproblems.com/730)
  - [A129515](https://oeis.org/A129515)
  - [PALOMAR-2026-08-22-000001](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-08-22-000001&version=1):
    a Lean 4 proof that there are infinitely many such pairs, checked by Comparator
    against the statement `S.Infinite` below and registered with the Palomar registry.
    The proof follows an argument posted on the erdosproblems.com forum
    (Liam Price, 24 June 2026), which shows that there are infinitely many
    consecutive pairs $(n, n+1)$.

statements.name: Erdos730.erdos_730
statements.doc:
Are there infinitely many pairs of integers $n < m$ such that $\binom{2n}{n}$
and $\binom{2m}{m}$ have the same set of prime divisors?

Yes: there are infinitely many consecutive pairs $(n, n+1)$. The formal proof
registered as [PALOMAR-2026-08-22-000001] proves `S.Infinite` for this `S`.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_730 : S.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos730.erdos_730.variants.explicit_pairs
statements.doc: For example, $(87,88)$ and $(607,608)$ are such pairs.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_730.variants.explicit_pairs :
    {(87, 88), (607, 608)} ⊆ S

statements.name: Erdos730.erdos_730.variants.delta_ne_one
statements.doc:
There are examples where $(n, m) ∈ S$ with $m ≠ n + 1$.

(Found by AlphaProof, although it was implicit already in [A129515])
statements.statement: theorem erdos_730.variants.delta_ne_one : ∃ (n m : ℕ), (n, m) ∈ S ∧ m ≠ n + 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 731
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/731](https://www.erdosproblems.com/731)
- [EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G.,
  *On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$*. Math. Comp. 29 (1975), 83-92.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-27.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos731.erdos_731
statements.doc:
Find some reasonable function $f(n)$ such that, for almost all integers $n$, the least integer
$m$ such that $m\nmid \binom{2n}{n}$ satisfies
$$m\sim f(n).$$

Here "almost all" means natural density $1$, and $m \sim f(n)$ means that for every
$\varepsilon>0$ the set of $n$ with $|m/f(n)-1|<\varepsilon$ has density $1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_731 : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ),
    {n : ℕ | |(leastNonDivisor n : ℝ) / erdos_731.answer n - 1| < ε}.HasDensity 1

statements.name: Erdos731.erdos_731.variants.egrs75
statements.doc:
A problem of Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus [EGRS75], who say it is 'not hard to show that',
for almost all $n$, the minimal such $m$ satisfies
$$m=\exp((\log n)^{1/2+o(1)}).$$

[EGRS75, (8), p. 91] states this as: for every $\varepsilon>0$, for all $n$ outside a set of
density $0$, $\exp((\log n)^{1/2-\varepsilon}) < m < \exp((\log n)^{1/2+\varepsilon})$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_731.variants.egrs75 : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ),
    {n : ℕ | Real.exp (Real.log n ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2 - ε)) < (leastNonDivisor n : ℝ) ∧
      (leastNonDivisor n : ℝ) < Real.exp (Real.log n ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2 + ε))}.HasDensity 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 732
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/732](https://www.erdosproblems.com/732)

statements.name: Erdos732.erdos_732.parts.i
statements.doc:
Call a sequence $1< X_1\leq \cdots \leq X_m\leq n$ block-compatible if there is a pairwise balanced
block design $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that $\lvert A_i\rvert=X_i$ for $1\leq
i\leq m$. (A pairwise block design means that every pair in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ is contained in exactly
one of the $A_i$.) Are there necessary and sufficient conditions for $(X_i)$ to be block-compatible?
Is there some constant $c>0$ such that for all large $n$ there are
$$\geq \exp(c n^{1/2}\log n)$$
many block-compatible sequences for $\{1,\ldots,n\}$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_732.parts.i :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (s : List ℕ), s ∈ Hypergraph.blockSizeProfiles n ↔ erdos_732.parts.i.answer n s

statements.name: Erdos732.erdos_732.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is there some constant $c>0$ such that for all large $n$ there are at least
$\exp(c n^{1/2}\log n)$ block-compatible sequences?

Alon has proved there are at least $2^{(\frac{1}{2}+o(1))n^{1/2}\log n}$ many sequences
which are block-compatible for $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_732.parts.ii :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    Real.exp (c * Real.sqrt n * Real.log n) ≤ (Hypergraph.blockSizeProfiles n).card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 733
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/733](https://www.erdosproblems.com/733)
- [Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-16.pdf)
- [SzTr83] Szemerédi, E. and Trotter, Jr., W. T., *Extremal problems in discrete geometry*.
  Combinatorica (1983), 381-392.

statements.name: Erdos733.erdos_733
statements.doc:
Call a sequence $1<X_1\leq\cdots\leq X_m\leq n$ line-compatible if there is a set of $n$ points in
$\mathbb{R}^2$ such that there are $m$ lines $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_m$ containing at least two
points, and the number of points on $\ell_i$ is exactly $X_i$.

Prove that there are at most
$$\exp(O(n^{1/2}))$$
many line-compatible sequences.

Asked by Erdős [Er81] and proved by Szemerédi and Trotter [SzTr83]. We take the lines $\ell_i$ to
be distinct but not necessarily all the lines determined by the points, as on erdosproblems.com;
[Er81] uses all the determined lines (`allLinesSequences`), so this bound implies his. Finiteness
of the set is part of the statement, since `Set.ncard` of an infinite set is $0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_733 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ,
      (compatibleSequences n).Finite ∧
        ((compatibleSequences n).ncard : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp (C * Real.sqrt n)

statements.name: Erdos733.erdos_733.variants.limit_exists
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er81] writes that it is 'easy' to prove there are at least
$$\exp(cn^{1/2})$$
many such sequences for some constant $c>0$, but expected proving the upper bound to be
difficult. Once it is done, he asked for the existence and value of
$$\lim_{n\to \infty}\frac{\log f(n)}{n^{1/2}},$$
where $f(n)$ counts the number of line-compatible sequences. Does this limit exist?

In [Er81], $f(n)$ counts the sequences of the numbers of points on all the lines determined by
$n$ points, i.e. `(allLinesSequences n).ncard`; this set is finite, as a subset of
`compatibleSequences n`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_733.variants.limit_exists :
    ∃ c : ℝ, Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log ((allLinesSequences n).ncard : ℝ) / Real.sqrt n)
      atTop (𝓝 c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 734
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/734](https://www.erdosproblems.com/734)
- [Er81] Erdős, P., On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
- [dBEr48] de Bruijn, N. G. and Erdős, P., On a combinatorial problem. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch.,
  Proc. (1948), 1277--1279 = Indagationes Math. 10, 421--423.

statements.name: Erdos734.erdos_734
statements.doc:
Find, for all large $n$, a non-trivial pairwise balanced block design $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq
\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that, for all $t$, there are $O(n^{1/2})$ many $i$ such that $\lvert
A_i\rvert=t$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_734 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∃ H : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), H.IsPairwiseBalancedDesign ∧
      (∀ e ∈ H, e.card < n) ∧ ∀ t : ℕ,
        ({e ∈ H | e.card = t}.card : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.sqrt n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 735
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/735](https://www.erdosproblems.com/735)
- [Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*.
  Combinatorica 1 (1981), 25-42. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-16.pdf)
- [ABKPR08] Ackerman, E., Buchin, K., Knauer, C., Pinchasi, R. and Rote, G., *There are not too
  many magic configurations*. Discrete Comput. Geom. 39 (2008), 3-16.
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-007-9023-0)

statements.name: Erdos735.erdos_735
statements.doc:
Given any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ when can one give positive weights to the points such that
the sum of the weights of the points along every line containing at least two points is the same?

This is a problem of Murty [Er81], who conjectured that this is only possible in one of
four cases: all points on a line, no three points on a line, $n-1$ points on a line, and a
triangle, the angle bisectors, and the incentre (or a projective equivalent). Ackerman, Buchin,
Knauer, Pinchasi and Rote [ABKPR08] proved this conjecture. Conversely, every set in these four
cases is magic.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_735 : {S : Finset ℝ² | IsMagic S} = erdos_735.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 737
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/737](https://www.erdosproblems.com/737)
- [EHS74] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A. and Shelah, S., *On some general properties of chromatic
  numbers*. Topics in topology (Proc. Colloq., Keszthely, 1972) (1974), 243-255.
- [Th83] Thomassen, Carsten, *Cycles in graphs of uncountable chromatic number*. Combinatorica
  (1983), 133-134.

statements.name: Erdos737.erdos_737
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$. Must there exist an edge $e$ such that, for
all large $n$, $G$ contains a cycle of length $n$ containing $e$?

The answer is yes, proved by Thomassen [Th83]. Erdős, Hajnal, and Shelah [EHS74] proved that $G$
must contain all sufficiently large cycles (see Erdős Problem 594).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_737 :
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), ChromaticNumberAlephOne G →
      ∃ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
        CycleThroughEdgeOfLength G e n

statements.name: Erdos737.erdos_737.variants.uncountable
statements.doc:
The title and abstract of [Th83] state the result for graphs of uncountable chromatic number,
that is, graphs with no proper colouring by `ℕ`. This is stronger than `erdos_737`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_737.variants.uncountable :
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), IsEmpty (G.Coloring ℕ) →
      ∃ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
        CycleThroughEdgeOfLength G e n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 740: Infinitary version of chromatic number and odd cycles
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/740](https://erdosproblems.com/740)

statements.name: Erdos740.erdos_740
statements.doc:
Let $\mathfrak{m}$ be an infinite cardinal and $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\mathfrak{m}$.
Let $r\geq 1$. Must $G$ contain a subgraph of chromatic number $\mathfrak{m}$ which does not contain
any odd cycle of length $\leq r$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_740 :
    ∀ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ℵ₀ ≤ G.chromaticCardinal →
        ∀ (r : ℕ),
          ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), H.coe.chromaticCardinal = G.chromaticCardinal ∧
            NoShortOddCycle H.coe r

problems.title: Erdős Problem 741
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/741](https://www.erdosproblems.com/741)
 - [Er94b] Erdős, Paul, Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and combinatorial geometry.
    Math. Pannon. (1994), 261-269.

statements.name: Erdos741.erdos_741.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be such that $A+A$ has positive upper density.
Can one always decompose $A=A_1\sqcup A_2$ such that $A_1+A_1$ and $A_2+A_2$
both have positive upper density?

This was proved by the DeepMind prover agent.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_741.parts.i : ∀ A : Set ℕ, 0 < upperDensity (A + A) → ∃ A₁ A₂,
    A = A₁ ∪ A₂ ∧ Disjoint A₁ A₂ ∧ 0 < upperDensity (A₁ + A₁)
    ∧ 0 < upperDensity (A₂ + A₂)

statements.name: Erdos741.erdos_741.variants.lower
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be such that $A+A$ has positive lower density.
Can one always decompose $A=A_1\sqcup A_2$ such that $A_1+A_1$ and $A_2+A_2$
both have positive lower density?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_741.variants.lower : ∀ A : Set ℕ, 0 < lowerDensity (A + A) → ∃ A₁ A₂,
    A = A₁ ∪ A₂ ∧ Disjoint A₁ A₂ ∧ 0 < lowerDensity (A₁ + A₁)
    ∧ 0 < lowerDensity (A₂ + A₂)

statements.name: Erdos741.erdos_741.variants.exact_density
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be such that $A+A$ has positive density in the literal sense that its
natural density exists and is positive.
Can one always decompose $A=A_1\sqcup A_2$ such that $A_1+A_1$ and $A_2+A_2$
both have positive density in this sense?

This was disproved by the DeepMind prover agent.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_741.variants.exact_density :
    ¬ ∀ A : Set ℕ, HasPosDensity (A + A) → ∃ A₁ A₂,
    A = A₁ ∪ A₂ ∧ Disjoint A₁ A₂ ∧ HasPosDensity (A₁ + A₁)
    ∧ HasPosDensity (A₂ + A₂)

statements.name: Erdos741.erdos_741.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is there a basis $A$ of order $2$ such that if $A=A_1\sqcup A_2$ then $A_1+A_1$ and $A_2+A_2$
cannot both have bounded gaps?

This was proved by DeepMind prover agent.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_741.parts.ii : ∃ A : Set ℕ, IsAddBasisOfOrder (A ∪ {0}) 2 ∧ ∀ A₁ A₂,
    A = A₁ ∪ A₂ → Disjoint A₁ A₂ → ¬ (IsSyndetic (A₁ + A₁) ∧ IsSyndetic (A₂ + A₂))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 742
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/742](https://www.erdosproblems.com/742)
- [Pl75] Plesník, Ján, Critical graphs of given diameter. Acta Fac. Rerum Natur. Univ. Comenian.
  Math. 30 (1975), 71-93.
- [CaHa79] Caccetta, L. and Häggkvist, R., On diameter critical graphs.
  Discrete Math. 28 (1979), 223-229.
- [Fa87] Fan, Genghua, On diameter 2-critical graphs. Discrete Math. 67 (1987), 235-240.
- [Fü92] Füredi, Zoltán, The maximum number of edges in a minimal graph of diameter 2.
  J. Graph Theory 16 (1992), 81-98.

statements.name: Erdos742.erdos_742
statements.doc:
**Murty-Simon Conjecture**

Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with diameter $2$ such that deleting any edge increases the
diameter. Is it true that $G$ has at most $\lfloor n^2 / 4 \rfloor$ edges? Equality is conjectured
to hold for the complete balanced bipartite graph $K_{\lceil n/2 \rceil, \lfloor n/2 \rfloor}$.

The conjecture is resolved up to a finite check: Fan [Fa87] verified it for $n \leq 24$ and
$n = 26$, and Füredi [Fü92] proved it for all sufficiently large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_742 :
    ∀ (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj], IsDiameter2Critical G →
    G.edgeFinset.card ≤ (Fintype.card V) ^ 2 / 4

statements.name: Erdos742.variants.plesnik_bound
statements.doc:
Plesník [Pl75] proved the bound $|E(G)| < 3n(n-1)/8$ for any diameter-$2$-critical graph
on $n$ vertices.
statements.statement:
theorem plesnik_bound (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG : IsDiameter2Critical G) :
    (G.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) < 3 * (Fintype.card V : ℝ) * ((Fintype.card V : ℝ) - 1) / 8

statements.name: Erdos742.variants.fan_bound
statements.doc: Fan [Fa87] verified the Murty-Simon conjecture for all $n \leq 24$ and for $n = 26$.
statements.statement:
theorem fan_bound (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hn : Fintype.card V ≤ 24 ∨ Fintype.card V = 26) (hG : IsDiameter2Critical G) :
    G.edgeFinset.card ≤ (Fintype.card V) ^ 2 / 4

statements.name: Erdos742.variants.furedi_bound
statements.doc:
Füredi [Fü92] proved the Murty-Simon conjecture for all sufficiently large $n$, that is, there
exists $n_0$ such that every diameter-$2$-critical graph on $n \geq n_0$ vertices has at most
$\lfloor n^2 / 4 \rfloor$ edges.
statements.statement:
theorem furedi_bound : ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
    n₀ ≤ Fintype.card V → IsDiameter2Critical G →
      G.edgeFinset.card ≤ (Fintype.card V) ^ 2 / 4

problems.title: Erdős Problem 743
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/743](https://www.erdosproblems.com/743)
- [ABCHPT21] Allen, Peter and Böttcher, Julia and Clemens, Dennis and Hladký, Jan and Piguet,
  Diana and Taraz, Anusch, *The tree packing conjecture for trees of almost linear maximum
  degree*. arXiv:2106.11720 (2021).
- [Bo83] Bollobás, Béla, *Some remarks on packing trees*. Discrete Math. (1983), 203-204.
- [Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
- [Fi83] Fishburn, P. C., *Balanced integer arrays: a matrix packing theorem*. J. Combin. Theory
  Ser. A (1983), 98-101.
- [Fi83b] Fishburn, P. C., *Packing graphs with odd and even trees*. J. Graph Theory (1983),
  369-383.
- [GyLe78] Gyárfás, A. and Lehel, J., *Packing trees of different order into $K_n$*.
  Combinatorics (Proc. Fifth Hungarian Colloq., Keszthely, 1976), Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai
  18 (1978), 463-469.
- [JKKO19] Joos, Felix and Kim, Jaehoon and Kühn, Daniela and Osthus, Deryk, *Optimal packings
  of bounded degree trees*. J. Eur. Math. Soc. (JEMS) (2019), 3573-3647.
- [JaMo24] Janzer, Barnabás and Montgomery, Richard, *Packing the largest trees in the tree
  packing conjecture*. arXiv:2403.10515 (2024).

statements.name: Erdos743.erdos_743
statements.doc:
Let $T_2,\ldots,T_n$ be a collection of trees such that $T_k$ has $k$ vertices. Can we always
write $K_n$ as the edge disjoint union of the $T_k$?

A conjecture of Gyárfás, known as the tree packing conjecture. We state it as a packing. For
every $n$ and all trees $T_k$ on the vertex set `Fin k`, $2 \leq k \leq n$, there are injective
maps
$f_k : \{0, \ldots, k - 1\} \to \{0, \ldots, n - 1\}$ such that the graphs $f_k(T_k)$ are
pairwise edge-disjoint (see `IsPacking`). Every tree with $k$ vertices is isomorphic to a tree
on `Fin k`, so this covers every collection of trees.

A tree with $k$ vertices has $k - 1$ edges, and $\sum_{k=2}^{n} (k - 1) = \binom{n}{2}$ is the
number of edges of $K_n$. Hence the copies $f_k(T_k)$ of a packing cover every edge of $K_n$.
So a packing is the same as a decomposition of $K_n$ into copies of $T_2, \ldots, T_n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_743 :
    ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ T : (k : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin k),
      (∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 2 n, (T k).IsTree) → IsPacking n (Set.Icc 2 n) T

statements.name: Erdos743.erdos_743.variants.stars_or_paths
statements.doc:
Gyárfás and Lehel [GyLe78] proved that this holds if all but at most $2$ of the trees are stars,
or if all the trees are stars or paths. This variant is the second case: each tree is a star or a
path.

Here a star on `Fin k` is `starGraph c` for a centre `c`, and a path is a graph isomorphic to
`pathGraph k`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_743.variants.stars_or_paths (n : ℕ) (T : (k : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin k))
    (hT : ∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 2 n, (T k).IsTree ∧
      ((∃ c : Fin k, T k = starGraph c) ∨ Nonempty (T k ≃g pathGraph k))) :
    IsPacking n (Set.Icc 2 n) T

statements.name: Erdos743.erdos_743.variants.all_but_two_stars
statements.doc:
Gyárfás and Lehel [GyLe78] proved that this holds if all but at most $2$ of the trees are stars,
or if all the trees are stars or paths. This variant is the first case.

Here a star on `Fin k` is `starGraph c` for a centre `c`. The two trees that may fail to be
stars are $T_a$ and $T_b$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_743.variants.all_but_two_stars (n : ℕ) (T : (k : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin k))
    (hT : ∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 2 n, (T k).IsTree)
    (hstar : ∃ a b : ℕ, ∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 2 n, k ≠ a → k ≠ b → ∃ c : Fin k, T k = starGraph c) :
    IsPacking n (Set.Icc 2 n) T

statements.name: Erdos743.erdos_743.variants.fishburn
statements.doc: Fishburn [Fi83b] proved this for $n\leq 9$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_743.variants.fishburn (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ 9) (T : (k : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin k))
    (hT : ∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 2 n, (T k).IsTree) :
    IsPacking n (Set.Icc 2 n) T

statements.name: Erdos743.erdos_743.variants.bollobas
statements.doc:
Bollobás [Bo83] proved that the smallest $\lfloor n/\sqrt{2}\rfloor$ many trees can always be
packed greedily into $K_n$.

The smallest trees are $T_1, \ldots, T_m$ with $m = \lfloor n/\sqrt{2} \rfloor$. The tree $T_1$ is
a single vertex, so we only pack $T_2, \ldots, T_m$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_743.variants.bollobas (n : ℕ) (T : (k : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin k))
    (hT : ∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 2 ⌊(n : ℝ) / Real.sqrt 2⌋₊, (T k).IsTree) :
    IsPacking n (Set.Icc 2 ⌊(n : ℝ) / Real.sqrt 2⌋₊) T

statements.name: Erdos743.erdos_743.variants.bounded_degree
statements.doc:
Joos, Kim, Kühn, and Osthus [JKKO19] proved that this conjecture holds when the trees have
bounded maximum degree. That is, for every $d$ there is $N$ such that for all $n \geq N$ the
following holds. If $T_k$ is a tree with $k$ vertices and maximum degree at most $d$ for
$2 \leq k \leq n$, then $K_n$ decomposes into $T_2, \ldots, T_n$.

They even allow the first $o(n)$ trees to have arbitrary maximum degree.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_743.variants.bounded_degree (d : ℕ) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → ∀ T : (k : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin k),
      (∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 2 n, (T k).IsTree ∧ (T k).maxDegree ≤ d) →
        IsPacking n (Set.Icc 2 n) T

statements.name: Erdos743.erdos_743.variants.almost_linear_degree
statements.doc:
Allen, Böttcher, Clemens, Hladký, Piguet, and Taraz [ABCHPT21] proved that this conjecture holds
when all the trees have maximum degree $\leq c\frac{n}{\log n}$ for some constant $c>0$. That is,
there is $c > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$ the following holds. If $T_k$ is a tree
with $k$ vertices and maximum degree at most $cn/\log n$ for $2 \leq k \leq n$, then $K_n$
decomposes into $T_2, \ldots, T_n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_743.variants.almost_linear_degree :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ T : (k : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin k),
      (∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 2 n,
        (T k).IsTree ∧ ((T k).maxDegree : ℝ) ≤ c * (n : ℝ) / Real.log (n : ℝ)) →
        IsPacking n (Set.Icc 2 n) T

statements.name: Erdos743.erdos_743.variants.largest_trees
statements.doc:
Janzer and Montgomery [JaMo24] have proved that there exists some $c>0$ such that the largest $cn$
trees can be packed into $K_n$.

We state this for all sufficiently large $n$. The trees are $T_k$ with $n - cn < k \leq n$, and
we also require $2 \leq k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_743.variants.largest_trees :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ T : (k : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin k),
      (∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → k ≤ n → (n : ℝ) - c * n < k → (T k).IsTree) →
        IsPacking n {k : ℕ | 2 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ n ∧ (n : ℝ) - c * n < k} T

problems.title: Erdős Problem 745: Second-largest component of a random graph
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/745](https://www.erdosproblems.com/745)

At the stated parameter $p=1/n$, the second-largest component has order
$n^{2/3}$ in probability. The logarithmic bound applies to fixed
$p=\lambda/n$ with $\lambda>1$.

[Al97] Aldous, D., Brownian excursions, critical random graphs and the multiplicative
coalescent. Ann. Probab. 25 (1997), 812–854.

[KSS80] Komlós, J., Sulyok, M. and Szemerédi, E., Second largest component in a random
graph. Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. 15 (1980), 391–395.

statements.name: Erdos745.erdos_745
statements.doc:
In $G(n,1/n)$ the second-largest component has order $n^{2/3}$ in probability.
The two positive constants may depend on the probability tolerance.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_745 :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ c C : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ c < C ∧
      ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
        1 - ε ≤ criticalProbability n (fun G ↦
          c * (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ) ≤ (secondLargestComponentOrder G : ℝ) ∧
          (secondLargestComponentOrder G : ℝ) ≤ C * (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos745.erdos_745.variants.supercritical
statements.doc:
For fixed $\lambda>1$, every constant above
$(\lambda-1-\log\lambda)^{-1}$ gives a logarithmic upper bound with high probability.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_745.variants.supercritical (lam : ℝ) (hlam : 1 < lam) (A : ℝ)
    (hA : 1 / (lam - 1 - Real.log lam) < A) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ probability lam n (fun G ↦
      (secondLargestComponentOrder G : ℝ) ≤ A * Real.log (n : ℝ)))
      Filter.atTop (𝓝 1)

statements.name: Erdos745.erdos_745.variants.noncritical_asymptotic
statements.doc:
For each fixed $\lambda>0$ with $\lambda\ne1$, the second-largest component size,
divided by $\log n$, converges in probability to $(\lambda-1-\log\lambda)^{-1}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_745.variants.noncritical_asymptotic
    (lam : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lam) (hne : lam ≠ 1) :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ probability lam n (fun G ↦
      |(secondLargestComponentOrder G : ℝ) / Real.log (n : ℝ) -
        1 / (lam - 1 - Real.log lam)| < ε)) Filter.atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 747
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/747](https://www.erdosproblems.com/747)
- [JKV08] Johansson, Anders and Kahn, Jeff and Vu, Van, Factors in random graphs. Random Structures
  Algorithms (2008), 1-28.
- [Ka23] Kahn, Jeff, Asymptotics for Shamir's problem. Adv. Math. (2023), Paper No. 109019, 39.

statements.name: Erdos747.erdos_747
statements.doc:
How large should $\ell(n)$ be such that, almost surely, a random $3$-uniform hypergraph on $3n$
vertices with $\ell(n)$ edges must contain $n$ vertex-disjoint edges?

The precise asymptotic was given by Kahn [Ka23], proving that the threshold is $\sim n\log n$ (also
for the general problem over $r$-uniform hypergraphs).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_747 :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε < 1 →
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ Hypergraph.matchingProbability (3 * n) 3
      ⌊(1 + ε) * erdos_747.answer n⌋₊ n) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ Hypergraph.matchingProbability (3 * n) 3
      ⌊(1 - ε) * erdos_747.answer n⌋₊ n) atTop (𝓝 0)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 748
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/748](https://www.erdosproblems.com/748)
- [CaEr90] Cameron, P. J. and Erdős, P., _On the number of sets of integers with various
  properties_. (1990), 61-79.
- [Er94b] Erdős, Paul, _Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and combinatorial
  geometry_. Math. Pannon. (1994), 261-269.
- [Er98] Erdős, Paul, _Some of my new and almost new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory_. Number theory (Eger, 1996) (1998), 169-180.
- [Gr04] Green, Ben, _The Cameron-Erdős conjecture_. Bull. London Math. Soc. (2004), 769-778.
- [Sa03] Sapozhenko, A. A., _The Cameron-Erdős conjecture_. Dokl. Akad. Nauk (2003), 749-752.

statements.name: Erdos748.erdos_748
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ count the number of sum-free $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$, i.e. $A$ contains no
solutions to $a=b+c$ with $a,b,c\in A$. Is it true that
$$f(n)=2^{(1+o(1))\frac{n}{2}}?$$

The Cameron–Erdős conjecture. This is true, and in fact $f(n) \ll 2^{n/2}$, which was proved
independently by Green [Gr04] and Sapozhenko [Sa03].

The statement $f(n)=2^{(1+o(1))n/2}$ is formalised as $\log_2 f(n)/n\to 1/2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_748 :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ logb 2 (f n) / n) atTop (nhds (1 / 2))

statements.name: Erdos748.erdos_748.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
It is trivial to see that $f(n) \geq 2^{\frac{n}{2}}$, considering all subsets of
$(n/2,n]$. The source writes $[n/2,n]$, but for even $n$ that interval is not sum-free,
since $n/2 + n/2 = n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_748.variants.lower_bound (n : ℕ) :
    (2 : ℝ) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) ≤ (f n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos748.erdos_748.variants.green_sapozhenko
statements.doc: Green [Gr04] and Sapozhenko [Sa03] proved that $f(n) \ll 2^{n/2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_748.variants.green_sapozhenko :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, (f n : ℝ) ≤ C * 2 ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)

statements.name: Erdos748.erdos_748.variants.asymptotic
statements.doc:
In fact, both Green [Gr04] and Sapozhenko [Sa03] prove the stronger asymptotic
$f(n) \sim c_n 2^{n/2}$, where $c_n$ takes on one of two values depending on the parity of
$n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_748.variants.asymptotic :
    ∃ c₀ c₁ : ℝ, 0 < c₀ ∧ 0 < c₁ ∧
      Tendsto (fun m : ℕ ↦ (f (2 * m) : ℝ) / 2 ^ m) atTop (nhds c₀) ∧
      Tendsto (fun m : ℕ ↦ (f (2 * m + 1) : ℝ) / 2 ^ ((2 * m + 1 : ℝ) / 2)) atTop
        (nhds c₁)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 749
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/749](https://www.erdosproblems.com/749)

statements.name: Erdos749.erdos_749
statements.doc:
Let $\epsilon>0$. Does there exist $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$
such that the lower density of $A+A$ is at least $1-\epsilon$
and yet $1_A\ast 1_A(n) \ll_\epsilon 1$ for all $n$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_749 : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ),
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, 1 - ε ≤ lowerDensity (A + A) ∧
    ((Nat.cast (R := ℝ) ∘ sumRep A) ≪ (fun n => (1: ℝ)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 750
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/750](https://www.erdosproblems.com/750)
- [EHS82] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A. and Szemerédi, E., On almost bipartite large chromatic graphs.
  Theory and practice of combinatorics (1982), 117-123.
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., Problems and results in chromatic graph theory. Proof Techniques in Graph
  Theory (1969), 27-35.
- [Er94b] Erdős, Paul, _Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and combinatorial geometry_.
  Math. Pannon. (1994), 261-269.
- [Er95d] Erdős, Paul, On some problems in combinatorial set theory. Publ. Inst. Math. (Beograd)
  (N.S.) (1995), 61-65.
- [ErHa67b] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, András, On chromatic graphs. Mat. Lapok (1967), 1--4.
- [UlamErdos750](https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos750.pdf)
- [St85] Stiebitz, M., _Beiträge zur Theorie der färbungskritischen Graphen_. Habilitation,
  TH Ilmenau (1985).
- [SaSt89] Sachs, H. and Stiebitz, M., _On constructive methods in the theory of colour-critical
  graphs_. Discrete Math. (1989), 287-296.
- [MuSt19] Müller, T. and Stehlík, M., _Generalised Mycielski graphs and the Borsuk-Ulam theorem_.
  Electron. J. Combin. (2019), P4.8.

statements.name: Erdos750.erdos_750.variants.stiebitz
statements.doc:
**Stiebitz's theorem** [St85]: every graph in $M_r$ has chromatic number at least $r$. The
matching upper bound follows from the construction, so the chromatic number is exactly $r$.

See also [SaSt89] and [MuSt19].

The linked formal proof (Alexeev and Codex, via signed-biclique chains and a `ℤ_p`-Tucker
lemma) uses the same `IsRecursivelyBuiltMr`, except that its `genMyc s G` has `MycAdj s G`
directly as adjacency relation instead of `SimpleGraph.fromRel (MycAdj s G)`; the two graphs are
equal since `MycAdj` is symmetric and irreflexive.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_750.variants.stiebitz {V : Type u} (G : SimpleGraph V) (r : ℕ)
    (h : IsRecursivelyBuiltMr r G) : (r : ℕ∞) ≤ G.chromaticNumber

statements.name: Erdos750.erdos_750
statements.doc:
Let $f(m)$ be some function such that $f(m)\to \infty$ as $m\to \infty$. Does there exist a
graph $G$ of infinite chromatic number such that every subgraph on $m$ vertices contains
an independent set of size at least $\frac{m}{2}-f(m)$?

Note that in [Er94b] the function $f$ generalises a (proven) result for $f(m) = \epsilon m$,
where $\epsilon > 0$. Hence we should assume it is non-negative valued.

The existence of such a graph was proved [UlamErdos750] by GPT 5.5 Pro (prompted by Chojecki).
Indeed, this constructs a graph with infinite chromatic number such that every subgraph on $m$
vertices can be made bipartite after deleting at most $f(m)$ many vertices.

The proof in plby/lean-proofs uses the proof of `erdos_750.variants.stiebitz` linked above.
It produces a graph on a `V : Type`, which gives the statement below in any universe by
lifting `V`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_750 :
    ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ≥0) (hf : atTop.Tendsto f atTop),
      ∃ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ ∧
        ∀ (m : ℕ) (S : Set V), 0 < m → S.ncard = m →
          ∃ I ⊆ S, G.IsIndepSet I ∧ m / 2 - f m ≤ I.ncard

statements.name: Erdos750.erdos_750.variants.epsilon
statements.doc:
In [Er69b] Erdős conjectures this for $f(m)=\epsilon m$ for any fixed $\epsilon>0$. This follows
from a result of Erdős, Hajnal, and Szemerédi [EHS82], as described by Sellke in the comments.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_750.variants.epsilon :
    ∀ (ε : ℝ≥0), ε > 0 →
      ∃ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ ∧
        ∀ (m : ℕ) (S : Set V), 0 < m → S.ncard = m →
          ∃ I ⊆ S, G.IsIndepSet I ∧ m / 2 - ε * m ≤ I.ncard

statements.name: Erdos750.erdos_750.variants.c_gt_quarter
statements.doc: In [ErHa67b] Erdős and Hajnal prove this for $f(m)\geq cm$ for all $c>1/4$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_750.variants.c_gt_quarter :
    ∀ (c : ℝ≥0), c > 1 / 4 →
      ∃ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ ∧
        ∀ (m : ℕ) (S : Set V), 0 < m → S.ncard = m →
          ∃ I ⊆ S, G.IsIndepSet I ∧ m / 2 - c * m ≤ I.ncard

problems.title: Erdős Problem 751
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/751](https://www.erdosproblems.com/751)
- [Er94b] Erdős, Paul, Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and combinatorial geometry.
  Math. Pannon. (1994), 261--269.
- [BoVi98] Bondy, J. A. and Vince, A., Cycles in a graph whose lengths differ by one or two.
  J. Graph Theory (1998), 11--15.

statements.name: Erdos751.erdos_751.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\chi(G)=4$. If $m_1<m_2<\cdots$ are the lengths of the
cycles in $G$ then can $\min(m_{i+1}-m_i)$ be arbitrarily large?

The answer is no: Bondy and Vince [BoVi98] proved that every graph with minimum degree at least $3$
has two cycles whose lengths differ by at most $2$, and hence the same is true for every graph with
chromatic number $4$.

`erdos_751.variants.finite` below carries the Lean proof. It assumes a finite vertex type,
where this quantifies over any `V : Type`, and the two are joined by de Bruijn-Erdős: a graph
that is not $3$-colourable has a finite subgraph that is not $3$-colourable, and cycles of that
subgraph are cycles of the whole. Mathlib does not have de Bruijn-Erdős, so that step is not
formalised here.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_751.parts.i :
    ¬ ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = 4 ∧
      ∀ m ∈ G.cycleLengths, ∀ m' ∈ G.cycleLengths, m < m' → m + k ≤ m'

statements.name: Erdos751.erdos_751.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\chi(G)=4$. If $m_1<m_2<\cdots$ are the lengths of the
cycles in $G$ then can $\min(m_{i+1}-m_i)$ be arbitrarily large? Can this happen if the girth of
$G$ is large?

The answer is no: Bondy and Vince [BoVi98] proved that every graph with minimum degree at least $3$
has two cycles whose lengths differ by at most $2$, and hence the same is true for every graph with
chromatic number $4$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_751.parts.ii :
    ¬ ∀ k g : ℕ, ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = 4 ∧ g ≤ G.girth ∧
      ∀ m ∈ G.cycleLengths, ∀ m' ∈ G.cycleLengths, m < m' → m + k ≤ m'

statements.name: Erdos751.erdos_751.variants.bondy_vince
statements.doc:
Bondy and Vince [BoVi98] proved that every graph with minimum degree at least $3$ has two cycles
whose lengths differ by at most $2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_751.variants.bondy_vince {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG : 3 ≤ G.minDegree) :
    ∃ m ∈ G.cycleLengths, ∃ m' ∈ G.cycleLengths, m < m' ∧ m' ≤ m + 2

statements.name: Erdos751.erdos_751.variants.finite
statements.doc:
The finite case of `erdos_751.parts.i`, which is what the Lean proof establishes: a finite graph
with chromatic number at least $4$ has two cycles whose lengths differ by $1$ or $2$.

The proof reaches this through a $4$-critical subgraph, which supplies the $2$-connectivity and
the vertex count its Bondy-Vince step needs on top of minimum degree $3$. Those extra hypotheses
are why it does not also settle `erdos_751.variants.bondy_vince`, which asks for minimum degree
$3$ alone.

This was formalized in Lean by SpringSense Innovation Institute using ChatGPT.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_751.variants.finite {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG : (4 : ℕ∞) ≤ G.chromaticNumber) :
    ∃ m ∈ G.cycleLengths, ∃ m' ∈ G.cycleLengths, m < m' ∧ m' ≤ m + 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 753
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/753](https://www.erdosproblems.com/753)
- [Al92] Alon, Noga, *Choice numbers of graphs: a probabilistic approach*. Combin. Probab.
  Comput. (1992), 107-114.

statements.name: Erdos753.erdos_753
statements.doc:
The list chromatic number $\chi_L(G)$ is defined to be the minimal $k$ such that for any
assignment of a list of $k$ colours to each vertex of $G$ (perhaps different lists for different
vertices) a colouring of each vertex by a colour on its list can be chosen such that adjacent
vertices receive distinct colours.

Does there exist some constant $c>0$ such that
$$\chi_L(G)+\chi_L(G^c)> n^{1/2+c}$$
for every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices (where $G^c$ is the complement of $G$)?

A problem of Erdős, Rubin, and Taylor.

The answer is no: Alon [Al92] proved that, for every $n$, there exists a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices
such that
$$\chi_L(G)+\chi_L(G^c)\ll (n\log n)^{1/2},$$
where the implied constant is absolute.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_753 :
    ¬ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2 + c) <
        (listChromaticNumber G : ℝ) + (listChromaticNumber Gᶜ : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos753.erdos_753.variants.alon
statements.doc:
Alon [Al92] proved that, for every $n$, there exists a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices such that
$$\chi_L(G)+\chi_L(G^c)\ll (n\log n)^{1/2},$$
where the implied constant is absolute.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_753.variants.alon :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (listChromaticNumber G : ℝ) + (listChromaticNumber Gᶜ : ℝ) ≤
        C * ((n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ)) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 755
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/755](https://www.erdosproblems.com/755)
- [ErPu75] Erdős, Paul and Purdy, George, Some extremal problems in geometry. III.
  (1975), 291--308.
- [Er94b] Erdős, Paul, Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and
  combinatorial geometry. Math. Pannon. (1994), 261--269.
- [CDL25b] Clemen, Felix Christian, Dumitrescu, Adrian, and Liu, Dingyuan,
  The number of regular simplices in higher dimensions. arXiv:2507.19841 (2025).

statements.name: Erdos755.erdos_755
statements.doc:
Erdős asked whether every $n$-point set in
$\mathbb{R}^6$ spans at most $(1/27 + o(1)) n^3$ unit equilateral triangles.

Clemen, Dumitrescu, and Liu [CDL25b] proved the stronger any-size statement
$T_6(n) = (1/27 + o(1)) n^3$. The unit-triangle upper bound follows as a
corollary, since unit equilateral triangles are a subset of equilateral
triangles of any positive side length: $T_\mathrm{unit} \leq T_\mathrm{anysize}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_755 :
    ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ,
      o =o[atTop] (fun _ : ℕ => (1 : ℝ)) ∧
        ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
          (TUnit 6 n : ℝ) ≤ ((1 / 27 : ℝ) + o n) * (n : ℝ) ^ 3

statements.name: Erdos755.erdos_755.variants.any_size_cdl
statements.doc:
Clemen, Dumitrescu, and Liu [CDL25b] proved the stronger version where
equilateral triangles of all positive side lengths are counted.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_755.variants.any_size_cdl :
    (fun n : ℕ => (TAnySize 6 n : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
      (fun n : ℕ => (1 / 27 : ℝ) * (n : ℝ) ^ 3)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 756
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/756](https://www.erdosproblems.com/756)
- [Bh24] Bhowmick, K., *A problem of Erdős about rich distances*. arXiv:2407.01174 (2024).
- [CDL25] Clemen, F., Dumitrescu, A. and Liu, D., *On multiplicities of interpoint distances*.
  arXiv:2505.04283 (2025).
- [Er97b] Erdős, Paul, *Some old and new problems in various branches of combinatorics*.
  Discrete Math. (1997), 227-231.
- [ErPa90] Erdős, P. and Pach, J., *Variations on the theme of repeated distances*.
  Combinatorica (1990), 261-269.
- [HoPa34] Hopf, H. and Pannwitz, E., *Aufgabe 167*. Jber. Deutsch. Math. Verein. (1934), 114.

statements.name: Erdos756.erdos_756
statements.doc:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points. Can there be $\gg n$ many distinct distances
each of which occurs for more than $n$ many pairs from $A$?

The answer is yes: Bhowmick [Bh24] constructs a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that
