$\lfloor\frac{n}{4}\rfloor$ distances occur at least $n+1$ times.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_756 :
    (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (maxRichDistances n : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos756.erdos_756.variants.bhowmick
statements.doc:
Bhowmick [Bh24] constructs a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that
$\lfloor\frac{n}{4}\rfloor$ distances occur at least $n+1$ times.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_756.variants.bhowmick (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ A : Finset ℝ², A.card = n ∧ n / 4 ≤ (richDistances A (n + 1)).card

statements.name: Erdos756.erdos_756.variants.bhowmick_general
statements.doc:
More generally, they construct, for any positive integer $m$ and large $n$, a set of $n$ points
such that
$\lfloor \frac{n}{2(m+1)}\rfloor$ distances occur at least $n+m$ times.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_756.variants.bhowmick_general (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ A : Finset ℝ², A.card = n ∧
      n / (2 * (m + 1)) ≤ (richDistances A (n + m)).card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 757
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/757](https://www.erdosproblems.com/757)
 - [GyLe95] Gyárfás, András and Lehel, Jenő, Linear sets with five distinct differences among any
    four elements. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (1995), 108-118.

statements.name: Erdos757.erdos_757
statements.doc: What is the supremum of the set of admissible numbers?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_757 {A : Set ℝ} :
    erdos_757.answer = sSup {c | IsAdmissible c}

statements.name: Erdos757.erdos_757.variants.lowerBound
statements.doc: The supremum is strictly larger than `1 / 2`, which is proved in [GyLe95].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_757.variants.lowerBound {A : Set ℝ} : 1 / (2 : ℝ) < sSup {c | IsAdmissible c}

statements.name: Erdos757.erdos_757.variants.upperBound
statements.doc: In [GyLe95], the authors also prove that the supremum is smaller than `3 / 5`.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_757.variants.upperBound {A : Set ℝ} : sSup {c | IsAdmissible c} < 3 / (5 : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 760
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/760](https://www.erdosproblems.com/760)
- [AKS97] Alon, Noga and Krivelevich, Michael and Sudakov, Benny, *Subgraphs with a large
  cochromatic number*. J. Graph Theory (1997), 295-297.

statements.name: Erdos760.erdos_760
statements.doc:
The cochromatic number of $G$, denoted by $\zeta(G)$, is the minimum number of colours needed to
colour the vertices of $G$ such that each colour class induces either a complete graph or
independent set.

If $G$ is a graph with chromatic number $\chi(G)=m$ then must $G$ contain a subgraph $H$ with
$$
\zeta(H) \gg \frac{m}{\log m}?
$$

A problem of Erdős and Gimbel, who proved that there must exist a subgraph $H$ with
$$
\zeta(H) \gg \left(\frac{m}{\log m}\right)^{1/2}.
$$
The proposed bound would be best possible, as shown by taking $G$ to be a complete graph.

The answer is yes, proved by Alon, Krivelevich, and Sudakov.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_760 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (m : ℕ),
      G.chromaticNumber = (m : ℕ∞) →
        ∃ H : G.Subgraph, ∃ k : ℕ, ((k : ℕ∞) ≤ H.coe.cochromaticNumber) ∧
          (c * (m : ℝ) / Real.log (m : ℝ) ≤ (k : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos760.erdos_760.variants.erdos_gimbel
statements.doc:
A problem of Erdős and Gimbel, who proved that there must exist a subgraph $H$ with
$$
\zeta(H) \gg \left(\frac{m}{\log m}\right)^{1/2}.
$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_760.variants.erdos_gimbel :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (m : ℕ),
      G.chromaticNumber = (m : ℕ∞) →
        ∃ H : G.Subgraph, ∃ k : ℕ, ((k : ℕ∞) ≤ H.coe.cochromaticNumber) ∧
          (c * Real.sqrt ((m : ℝ) / Real.log (m : ℝ)) ≤ (k : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 761
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/761](https://www.erdosproblems.com/761)
- [ErGi93] Erdős, P. and Gimbel, J., *Some problems and results in cochromatic theory*.
  Quo vadis, graph theory? (1993), 261-264.

statements.name: Erdos761.erdos_761.parts.i
statements.doc:
The dichromatic number of $G$, denoted by $\delta(G)$, is the minimum number $k$ of colours
required such that, in any orientation of the edges of $G$, there is a $k$-colouring of the
vertices of $G$ such that there are no monochromatic oriented cycles.

Must a graph with large chromatic number have large dichromatic number?

This question is due to Erdős and Neumann-Lara. We read it for finite graphs: for every $k$ there
is $m$ such that every finite graph with $\chi(G)\geq m$ has $\delta(G)\geq k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_761.parts.i :
    ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      (m : ℕ∞) ≤ G.chromaticNumber → (k : ℕ∞) ≤ dichromaticNumber G

statements.name: Erdos761.erdos_761.parts.ii
statements.doc:
The cochromatic number of $G$, denoted by $\zeta(G)$, is the minimum number of colours needed to
colour the vertices of $G$ such that each colour class induces either a complete graph or empty
graph.

Must a graph with large cochromatic number contain a graph with large dichromatic number?

This question is due to Erdős and Gimbel. We read it for finite graphs and subgraphs: for every
$k$ there is $m$ such that every finite graph with $\zeta(G)\geq m$ has a subgraph $H$ with
$\delta(H)\geq k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_761.parts.ii :
    ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      (m : ℕ∞) ≤ G.cochromaticNumber →
        ∃ H : G.Subgraph, (k : ℕ∞) ≤ dichromaticNumber H.coe

statements.name: Erdos761.erdos_761.variants.parts_ii_imp_i
statements.doc:
A positive answer to the second question implies a positive answer to the first via the bound
mentioned in [760].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_761.variants.parts_ii_imp_i :
    (∀ k : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, ∀ (V : Type u) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      (m : ℕ∞) ≤ G.cochromaticNumber →
        ∃ H : G.Subgraph, (k : ℕ∞) ≤ dichromaticNumber H.coe) →
    ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, ∀ (V : Type u) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      (m : ℕ∞) ≤ G.chromaticNumber → (k : ℕ∞) ≤ dichromaticNumber G

problems.title: Erdős Problem 762
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/762](https://www.erdosproblems.com/762)
- [EGS90] Erdős, Paul and Gimbel, John and Straight, H. Joseph, *Chromatic number versus
  cochromatic number in graphs with bounded clique number*. European J. Combin. (1990), 235-240.
- [St24b] R. Steiner, *On the difference between the chromatic and cochromatic number*.
  arXiv:2408.02400 (2024).

statements.name: Erdos762.erdos_762
statements.doc:
The cochromatic number of $G$, denoted by $\zeta(G)$, is the minimum number of colours needed to
colour the vertices of $G$ such that each colour class induces either a complete graph or empty
graph.

Is it true that if $G$ has no $K_5$ and $\zeta(G)\geq 4$ then $\chi(G) \leq \zeta(G)+2$?

This has been disproved by Steiner [St24b], who constructed a graph $G$ with $\omega(G)=4$,
$\zeta(G)=4$, and $\chi(G)=7$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_762 :
    ¬ ∀ (V : Type*) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      G.CliqueFree 5 → 4 ≤ G.cochromaticNumber →
        G.chromaticNumber ≤ G.cochromaticNumber + 2

statements.name: Erdos762.erdos_762.variants.bounded_clique_number
statements.doc:
A conjecture of Erdős, Gimbel, and Straight [EGS90], who proved that for every $n>2$ there exists
some $f(n)$ such that if $G$ contains no clique on $n$ vertices then $\chi(G)\leq \zeta(G)+f(n)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_762.variants.bounded_clique_number (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 < n) :
    ∃ f : ℕ, ∀ (V : Type*) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      G.CliqueFree n → G.chromaticNumber ≤ G.cochromaticNumber + f

statements.name: Erdos762.erdos_762.variants.steiner
statements.doc:
This has been disproved by Steiner [St24b], who constructed a graph $G$ with $\omega(G)=4$,
$\zeta(G)=4$, and $\chi(G)=7$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_762.variants.steiner :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      G.cliqueNum = 4 ∧ G.cochromaticNumber = 4 ∧ G.chromaticNumber = 7

problems.title: Erdős Problem 763
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/763](https://www.erdosproblems.com/763)
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [Er70c] Erdős, P., *Some problems in additive number theory*. Amer. Math. Monthly (1970),
  619-621.
- [ErFu56] Erdős, P. and Fuchs, W. H. J., *On a problem of additive number theory*. J. London
  Math. Soc. (1956), 67-73.
- [MoVa90] Montgomery, H. L. and Vaughan, R. C., *On the Erdős-Fuchs theorems*. (1990), 331-338.

statements.name: Erdos763.erdos_763
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$. Can there exist some constant $c>0$ such that
$$\sum_{n\leq N} 1_A\ast 1_A(n) = cN+O(1)?$$

A conjecture of Erdős and Turán. Erdős and Fuchs [ErFu56] proved that the answer is no in a
strong form: in fact even
$$\sum_{n\leq N} 1_A\ast 1_A(n) = cN+o\left(\frac{N^{1/4}}{(\log N)^{1/2}}\right)$$
is impossible. The error term here was improved to $o(N^{1/4})$ by Jurkat (unpublished) and
Montgomery and Vaughan [MoVa90].

See also [764](https://www.erdosproblems.com/764) for a generalisation to more summands.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_763 : ¬ ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (c : ℝ), 0 < c ∧
    (fun N : ℕ ↦ (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), sumRep A n : ℝ) - c * N) =O[atTop]
      fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos763.erdos_763.variants.erdos_fuchs
statements.doc:
Erdős and Fuchs [ErFu56] proved that
$\sum_{n\leq N} 1_A\ast 1_A(n) = cN+o\left(\frac{N^{1/4}}{(\log N)^{1/2}}\right)$ is impossible.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_763.variants.erdos_fuchs : ¬ ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (c : ℝ), 0 < c ∧
    (fun N : ℕ ↦ (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), sumRep A n : ℝ) - c * N) =o[atTop]
      fun N ↦ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) / √(Real.log N)

statements.name: Erdos763.erdos_763.variants.montgomery_vaughan
statements.doc:
Jurkat (unpublished) and Montgomery and Vaughan [MoVa90] proved that even
$\sum_{n\leq N} 1_A\ast 1_A(n) = cN+o(N^{1/4})$ is impossible.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_763.variants.montgomery_vaughan : ¬ ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (c : ℝ), 0 < c ∧
    (fun N : ℕ ↦ (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), sumRep A n : ℝ) - c * N) =o[atTop]
      fun N ↦ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 764
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/764](https://www.erdosproblems.com/764)
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [Er70c] Erdős, P., *Some problems in additive number theory*. Amer. Math. Monthly (1970),
  619-621.
- [Va72] Vaughan, R. C., *On the addition of sequences of integers*. J. Number Theory (1972),
  1-16.

statements.name: Erdos764.erdos_764
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$. Can there exist some constant $c>0$ such that
$$\sum_{n\leq N} 1_A\ast 1_A\ast 1_A(n) = cN+O(1)?$$

The case of $1_A\ast 1_A(n)$ is the subject of [763](https://www.erdosproblems.com/763).

The answer is no, proved in a strong form by Vaughan [Va72], who showed that in fact
$$\sum_{n\leq N} 1_A\ast 1_A\ast 1_A(n) = cN+o\left(\frac{N^{1/4}}{(\log N)^{1/2}}\right)$$
is impossible. Vaughan proves a more general result that applies to any $h$-fold convolution,
with different main terms permitted.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_764 : ¬ ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (c : ℝ), 0 < c ∧
    (fun N : ℕ ↦ (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), tripleRep A n : ℝ) - c * N) =O[atTop]
      fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos764.erdos_764.variants.vaughan
statements.doc:
Vaughan [Va72] showed that
$\sum_{n\leq N} 1_A\ast 1_A\ast 1_A(n) = cN+o\left(\frac{N^{1/4}}{(\log N)^{1/2}}\right)$ is
impossible.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_764.variants.vaughan : ¬ ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (c : ℝ), 0 < c ∧
    (fun N : ℕ ↦ (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), tripleRep A n : ℝ) - c * N) =o[atTop]
      fun N ↦ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) / √(Real.log N)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 765
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/765](https://www.erdosproblems.com/765)
- [Er38] Erdős, P., *On sequences of integers no one of which divides the product of two others
  and on related problems*. Tomsk. Gos. Univ. Ucen Zap. (1938), 74-82.
- [Re58] Reiman, I., *Über ein Problem von K. Zarankiewicz*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 9
  (1958), 269-273.
- [ERS66] Erdős, P. and Rényi, A. and Sós, V. T., *On a problem of graph theory*. Studia Sci. Math.
  Hungar. (1966), 215--235.
- [Br66] Brown, W. G., *On graphs that do not contain a Thomsen graph*. Canad. Math. Bull. (1966),
  281-285.
- [Er75] Erdős, P., *Some recent progress on extremal problems in graph theory*. Congr. Numer.
  (1975), 3-14.
- [Fu83] Füredi, Z., *Graphs without quadrilaterals*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 34 (1983),
  187-190.
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [MaYa23] Ma, Jie and Yang, Tianchi, *Upper bounds on the extremal number of the 4-cycle*. Bull.
  Lond. Math. Soc. (2023), 1655--1667.

statements.name: Erdos765.erdos_765
statements.doc:
Give an asymptotic formula for $\mathrm{ex}(n; C_4)$.

Erdős and Klein [Er38] proved $\mathrm{ex}(n; C_4) \asymp n^{3/2}$, and Reiman [Re58] proved
$$\frac{1}{2\sqrt 2} \le \lim \frac{\mathrm{ex}(n; C_4)}{n^{3/2}} \le \frac12.$$
Erdős and Rényi [ERS66], and independently Brown [Br66], gave a construction showing that if
$n = q^2 + q + 1$ with $q$ a prime power then $\mathrm{ex}(n; C_4) \ge \frac12 q (q+1)^2$; together
with Reiman's upper bound this gives $\mathrm{ex}(n; C_4) \sim \frac12 n^{3/2}$. Füredi [Fu83] proved
$\mathrm{ex}(n; C_4) = \frac12 q (q+1)^2$ for $q > 13$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_765 :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 4) : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
      fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) / 2

statements.name: Erdos765.erdos_765.variants.second_term
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er93] conjectured that $\mathrm{ex}(n; C_4) = \frac{n^{3/2}}{2} + \frac n4 + O(n^{1/2})$ for all
$n$, having proved the upper bound $\mathrm{ex}(n; C_4) \le \frac{n^{3/2}}{2} + \frac n4 + O(n^{1/2})$
in [Er75]. This is false: Ma and Yang [MaYa23] proved that, for some absolute constant $c > 0$ and
a positive density set of $n$, $\mathrm{ex}(n; C_4) \le \frac{n^{3/2}}{2} + (\frac14 - c) n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_765.variants.second_term :
    ¬ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 4) : ℝ) -
      (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) / 2 - (n : ℝ) / 4) =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 766
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/766](https://www.erdosproblems.com/766)
- [Er64c] Erdős, P., *Extremal problems in graph theory*. Theory of Graphs and its Applications
  (Proc. Sympos. Smolenice, 1963) (1964), 29-36.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1964-06.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos766.erdos_766.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $f(n;k,l)=\min \mathrm{ex}(n;G)$, where $G$ ranges over all graphs with $k$ vertices and $l$
edges.

Give good estimates for $f(n;k,l)$ in the range $k<l\leq k^2/4$.

In [Er64c, p. 33] this question is asked for $f_1(n;k,l)$ (`Erdos766.forcingNumber`), which
forces at least one graph with $k$ vertices and $l$ edges rather than one fixed graph; we follow
the source. The question for the function of erdosproblems.com is
`Erdos766.erdos_766.variants.minExtremalNumber_estimate`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_766.parts.i :
    ∀ k l : ℕ, k < l → l ≤ k ^ 2 / 4 →
      (fun n ↦ (forcingNumber n k l : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_766.parts.i.answer k l

statements.name: Erdos766.erdos_766.parts.ii
statements.doc:
For fixed $k$ and large $n$ is $f(n;k,l)$ a strictly monotone function of $l$?

As in `Erdos766.erdos_766.parts.i`, $f$ is $f_1$ of [Er64c], and we use the range
$k<l\leq k^2/4$ in which the question is asked there; here `k ^ 2 / 4` is $\lfloor k^2/4\rfloor$.
The question for the function of erdosproblems.com is
`Erdos766.erdos_766.variants.minExtremalNumber_strictMonoOn`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_766.parts.ii :
    ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      StrictMonoOn (forcingNumber n k) (Set.Ioc k (k ^ 2 / 4))

statements.name: Erdos766.erdos_766.variants.dirac_erdos
statements.doc:
Dirac and Erdős proved independently that when $l=\lfloor k^2/4\rfloor+1$
$$f(n;k,l)\leq \lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+1.$$

[Er64c, p. 34] states this for every $k \leq n$. We assume $k \geq 3$, since for $k \leq 2$ there
is no graph with $k$ vertices and $\lfloor k^2/4\rfloor+1$ edges.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_766.variants.dirac_erdos (n k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
    forcingNumber n k (k ^ 2 / 4 + 1) ≤ n ^ 2 / 4 + 1

statements.name: Erdos766.erdos_766.variants.minExtremalNumber_estimate
statements.doc:
The estimate question of `Erdos766.erdos_766.parts.i` for the function
$\min \mathrm{ex}(n;G)$ of erdosproblems.com (`Erdos766.minExtremalNumber`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_766.variants.minExtremalNumber_estimate :
    ∀ k l : ℕ, k < l → l ≤ k ^ 2 / 4 →
      (fun n ↦ ((minExtremalNumber n k l).toNat : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop]
        erdos_766.variants.minExtremalNumber_estimate.answer k l

statements.name: Erdos766.erdos_766.variants.minExtremalNumber_strictMonoOn
statements.doc:
The monotonicity question of `Erdos766.erdos_766.parts.ii` for the function
$\min \mathrm{ex}(n;G)$ of erdosproblems.com (`Erdos766.minExtremalNumber`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_766.variants.minExtremalNumber_strictMonoOn :
    ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      StrictMonoOn (minExtremalNumber n k) (Set.Ioc k (k ^ 2 / 4))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 767
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/767](https://www.erdosproblems.com/767)
- [Er64c] Erdős, P., _Extremal problems in graph theory_. Theory of Graphs and its Applications
  (Proc. Sympos. Smolenice, 1963) (1964), 29-36.
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., _Problems and results in chromatic graph theory_. Proof Techniques in Graph
  Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
- [Er75] Erdős, P., _Some recent progress on extremal problems in graph theory_. Congr. Numer.
  (1975), 3-14.
- [Ji04] Jiang, Tao, _A note on a conjecture about cycles with many incident chords_. J. Graph
  Theory (2004), 180-182.

statements.name: Erdos767.erdos_767
statements.doc:
Let $g_k(n)$ be the maximal number of edges possible on a graph with $n$ vertices which does not
contain a cycle with $k$ chords incident to a vertex on the cycle. Is it true that
$$g_k(n)=(k+1)n-(k+1)^2$$
for $n$ sufficiently large?

The answer is yes: the conjectured equality was proved for $n\geq 3k+3$ by Jiang [Ji04].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_767 :
    ∀ k ≥ 1, ∀ n ≥ 3 * k + 3, g k n = (k + 1) * n - (k + 1) ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos767.erdos_767.variants.czipszer
statements.doc: Czipszer proved that $g_k(n)\leq (k+1)n$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_767.variants.czipszer (k n : ℕ) : g k n ≤ (k + 1) * n

statements.name: Erdos767.erdos_767.variants.posa
statements.doc: Pósa proved that $g_1(n)=2n-4$ for $n\geq 4$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_767.variants.posa (n : ℕ) (hn : 4 ≤ n) : g 1 n = 2 * n - 4

problems.title: Erdős Problem 769
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/769](https://www.erdosproblems.com/769)

statements.name: Erdos769.erdos_769
statements.doc:
Let $c(n)$ be minimal such that if $k\geq c(n)$ then the $n$-dimensional unit
cube can be decomposed into $k$ homothetic $n$-dimensional cubes. Give good
bounds for $c(n)$ — in particular, is it true that $c(n)\gg n^n$?

The `c(n) \gg n^n` conjecture is **false**: for odd `n`, one can tile the unit
`n`-cube into `k` homothetic cubes for every `k ≥ U(n)` with `U(n)/n^n → 0`, so
`c(n)/n^n → 0` along odd dimensions and no absolute constant lower-bounds it.

Determining good bounds for `c(n)` in general remains open.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_769 : ¬ Erdos769LowerBound

statements.name: Erdos769.erdos_769.variants.growth_rate
statements.doc:
What refuting $c(n)\gg n^n$ leaves open: give good bounds for $c(n)$. Asked here on the
scale the problem itself sets, $n^n$: does $c$ have a well-defined order
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log c(n)}{n\log n}?$$
The refuted conjecture would have forced this limit to be at least $1$.
The cutoff condition is restricted to positive dimensions: in dimension zero,
exact coverage permits only one tile, so no cutoff exists.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_769.variants.growth_rate :
    ∃ c : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < n → IsCutoff n (c n)) ∧
      ∃ γ : ℝ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Real.log (c n) / (n * Real.log n)) atTop (𝓝 γ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 770
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/770](https://www.erdosproblems.com/770)
 - [Er49d] Erdös, P. "On the strong law of large numbers." Transactions of the American Mathematical
    Society 67.1 (1949): 51-56.
 - [Ma66] Matsuyama, Noboru. "On the strong law of large numbers." Tohoku Mathematical Journal,
    Second Series 18.3 (1966): 259-269.

statements.name: Erdos770.Nat.Prime.h_eq_add_one
statements.doc: `n + 1` is prime iff `h n = n + 1`. This is described as 'easy to see' in [Er74b].
statements.statement: theorem Nat.Prime.h_eq_add_one {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 < n) : h n = n + 1 ↔ (n + 1).Prime

statements.name: Erdos770.erdos_770.variants.odd_h_unbounded
statements.doc:
For odd `n`, the values of `h n` form an unbounded set.
This is described as 'easy to see' in [Er74b].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_770.variants.odd_h_unbounded : Unbounded (· ≤ ·) (ENat.toNat '' (h '' Odd))

statements.name: Erdos770.erdos_770.parts.i
statements.doc: For every prime `p`, does the density of integers with `h n = p` exist?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_770.parts.i : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ a, HasDensity {n | h n = p} a

statements.name: Erdos770.erdos_770.parts.ii
statements.doc: Does `liminf h n = ∞`?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_770.parts.ii : liminf h atTop = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos770.erdos_770.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Is it true that if `p` is the greatest prime such that `p - 1 ∣ n` and `p > n ^ ε`, then
`h n = p`?

statements.name: Erdos770.erdos_770.variants.three
statements.doc: It is probably true that `h n = 3` for infinitely many `n`.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_770.variants.three : {n | h n = 3}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 771
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/771](https://www.erdosproblems.com/771)
- [Er89] Erdős, P., *Some problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. Graph theory and
  its applications: East and West (Jinan, 1986), Ann. New York Acad. Sci. 576 (1989), 132-145.
- [AlFr88] Alon, N. and Freiman, G., *On sums of subsets of a set of integers*. Combinatorica 8
  (1988), 297-306.

statements.name: Erdos771.erdos_771
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that, for every $m\geq 1$, there exists some
$S\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $\lvert S\rvert=f(n)$ such that $m\neq \sum_{a\in A}a$ for all
$A\subseteq S$.

Is it true that
$$f(n) = \left(\frac{1}{2}+o(1)\right)\frac{n}{\log n}?$$

The answer is yes: the lower bound is due to Erdős and Graham and the upper bound to Alon and
Freiman [AlFr88].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_771 :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) / (2 * Real.log n)

statements.name: Erdos771.erdos_771.variants.erdos_graham_lower
statements.doc:
Erdős and Graham proved the lower bound
$$f(n)\geq \left(\frac{1}{2}+o(1)\right)\frac{n}{\log n}.$$
Their proof is to note that we can assume that $m< \binom{n+1}{2}$ and then, for any $m$, take
$S=\{ kp : 1\leq k<\frac{n}{p}\}$ where $p$ is the least prime that does not divide $m$
(so $p<(2+o(1))\log n$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_771.variants.erdos_graham_lower :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (1 / 2 - ε) * ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n) ≤ f n

statements.name: Erdos771.erdos_771.variants.alon_freiman_upper
statements.doc:
The complementary bound
$$f(n) \leq \left(\frac{1}{2}+o(1)\right)\frac{n}{\log n}$$
was proved by Alon and Freiman [AlFr88], who chose $m$ as the least common multiple of
$\{1,\ldots,s\}$ where $s$ is maximal such that $m\leq \frac{n^2}{20(\log n)^2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_771.variants.alon_freiman_upper :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (f n : ℝ) ≤ (1 / 2 + ε) * ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 772
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/772](https://www.erdosproblems.com/772)
- [Er80e] Erdős, P., _Some applications of Ramsey's theorem to additive number theory_. European
  J. Combin. (1980), 43-46.
- [Er84d] Erdős, P., _Extremal problems in number theory, combinatorics and geometry_. Proceedings
  of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Vol. 1, 2 (Warsaw, 1983) (1984), 51-70.
- [AlEr85] Alon, Noga and Erdős, P., _An application of graph theory to additive number theory_.
  European J. Combin. (1985), 201-203.

statements.name: Erdos772.erdos_772.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 1$ and $H_k(n)$ be the maximal $r$ such that if $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ has
$\lvert A\rvert=n$ and $\| 1_A\ast 1_A\|_\infty \leq k$ then $A$ contains a Sidon set of size at
least $r$.

Is it true that $H_k(n)/n^{1/2}\to \infty$?

The answer is yes, and in fact $H_k(n) \gg_k n^{2/3}$, proved by Alon and Erdős [AlEr85].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_772.parts.i :
    ∀ k ≥ 1, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (H k n : ℝ) / √n) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos772.erdos_772.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is it true that $H_k(n) > n^{1/2+c}$ for some constant $c>0$?

The answer is yes, and in fact $H_k(n) \gg_k n^{2/3}$, proved by Alon and Erdős [AlEr85].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_772.parts.ii :
    ∀ k ≥ 1, ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 + c : ℝ) < H k n

statements.name: Erdos772.erdos_772.variants.alon_erdos
statements.doc: Alon and Erdős [AlEr85] proved that $H_k(n) \gg_k n^{2/3}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_772.variants.alon_erdos (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c * (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ) ≤ H k n

statements.name: Erdos772.erdos_772.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er84d] proved that $H_k(n) \ll n^{2/3}$, where the implied constant is absolute.

Since $1_A\ast 1_A$ counts ordered pairs, the bound needs $k\geq 4$: the construction of
Erdős has at most two unordered representations of each sum, hence at most four ordered ones,
while $k\leq 2$ forces $A$ itself to be Sidon and so $H_k(n)=n$. For $k=3$ the only collisions
are $a+b=2c$, so the Sidon subsets of $A$ are its $3$-term-progression-free subsets, which have
size $n^{1-o(1)}$, and the bound fails there too.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_772.variants.upper_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ k ≥ 4, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (H k n : ℝ) ≤ C * (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 773
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/773](https://www.erdosproblems.com/773)
- [AlEr85] Alon, Noga and Erdős, P., *An application of graph theory to additive number theory*.
  European J. Combin. (1985), 201-203.
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [LeTh95] Lefmann, Hanno and Thiele, Torsten, *Point sets with distinct distances*. Combinatorica
  (1995), 379--408.

statements.name: Erdos773.erdos_773
statements.doc: What is the size of the largest Sidon subset $A\subseteq\{1,2^2,\ldots,N^2\}$? Is it $N^{1-o(1)}$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_773 :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop,
      (N : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε) ≤
        (Finset.maxSidonSubsetCard
          (Finset.image (fun n : ℕ => n ^ 2) (Finset.Icc 1 N)) : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 774
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/774](https://www.erdosproblems.com/774)

statements.name: Erdos774.erdos_774
statements.doc:
Is every proportionately dissociated (infinite) set the union of a finite
number of dissociated sets?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_774 : ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite → A.IsProportionatelyDissociated →
    ∃ (T : Set (Set ℕ)), (∀ S ∈ T, S.IsDissociated) ∧ T.Finite ∧ A = ⋃₀ T

problems.title: Erdős Problem 775
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/775](https://www.erdosproblems.com/775)
- [Ga25] Gao, J., *On cliques in hypergraphs*. arXiv:2510.14804 (2025).
- [MoMo65] Moon, J. W. and Moser, L., *On cliques in graphs*. Israel J. Math. (1965), 23-28.
- [Sp71] Spencer, J. H., *On cliques in graphs*. Israel J. Math. (1971), 419-421.

statements.name: Erdos775.erdos_775
statements.doc:
Is there a $3$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices which contains at least $n-O(1)$ different
sizes of cliques (maximal complete subgraphs)?

The answer is no, as proved by Gao [Ga25]: more generally, for any $k\geq 3$, every $k$-uniform
hypergraph on $n$ vertices contains at most $n-f_k(n)$ different sizes of cliques, where
$f_k(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_775 :
    ¬ ∃ C : ℕ, ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ H : UniformHypergraph (Fin n) 3,
      n - C ≤ (UniformHypergraph.cliqueSizes H).ncard

statements.name: Erdos775.erdos_775.variants.gao
statements.doc:
The answer is no, as proved by Gao [Ga25]: more generally, for any $k\geq 3$, every $k$-uniform
hypergraph on $n$ vertices contains at most $n-f_k(n)$ different sizes of cliques, where
$f_k(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_775.variants.gao :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto f atTop atTop ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ H : UniformHypergraph (Fin n) 3,
        (UniformHypergraph.cliqueSizes H).ncard + f n ≤ n

statements.name: Erdos775.erdos_775.variants.spencer
statements.doc:
For graphs, Spencer [Sp71] constructed a graph which contains cliques of at least
$n-\log_2n+O(1)$ different sizes.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_775.variants.spencer :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (n : ℝ) - Real.logb 2 (n : ℝ) - C ≤ ((SimpleGraph.cliqueSizes G).ncard : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos775.erdos_775.variants.moon_moser
statements.doc:
For graphs, Spencer [Sp71] constructed a graph which contains cliques of at least
$n-\log_2n+O(1)$ different sizes, which Moon and Moser [MoMo65] showed to be best possible.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_775.variants.moon_moser :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      ((SimpleGraph.cliqueSizes G).ncard : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) - Real.logb 2 (n : ℝ) + C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 777
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/777](https://www.erdosproblems.com/777)
- [Gu83] Guy, R. K., *A miscellany of Erdős problems*. Amer. Math. Monthly (1983), 118-120.
- [AlFr85] Alon, N. and Frankl, P., *The maximum number of disjoint pairs in a family of
  subsets*. Graphs Combin. (1985), 13-21.
- [ADGS15] Alon, N., Das, S., Glebov, R. and Sudakov, B., *Comparable pairs in families of
  sets*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (2015), 164-185. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.4196)

statements.name: Erdos777.erdos_777.parts.i
statements.doc:
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ then we write $G_{\mathcal{F}}$ for the
graph on $\mathcal{F}$ where $A\sim B$ if $A$ and $B$ are comparable - that is, $A\subseteq B$ or
vice versa.

Is it true that, if $\epsilon>0$ and $n$ is sufficiently large, whenever
$m\leq (2-\epsilon)2^{n/2}$ the graph $G_\mathcal{F}$ has $<2^{n}$ many edges?

A problem of Daykin and Erdős [Gu83]; here $m=\lvert\mathcal{F}\rvert$. The answer is yes, which
follows from Theorem 1.4 and Corollary 1.5 of Alon, Das, Glebov, and Sudakov [ADGS15].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_777.parts.i :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n → ∀ 𝓕 : Finset (Finset (Fin n)),
      (𝓕.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 - ε) * (2 : ℝ) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) → comparableEdges 𝓕 < 2 ^ n

statements.name: Erdos777.erdos_777.parts.ii
statements.doc:
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ then we write $G_{\mathcal{F}}$ for the
graph on $\mathcal{F}$ where $A\sim B$ if $A$ and $B$ are comparable - that is, $A\subseteq B$ or
vice versa.

Is it true that if $G_{\mathcal{F}}$ has $\geq cm^2$ edges then $m\ll_c 2^{n/2}$?

The answer is no, by Alon and Frankl [AlFr85, Example 6.1]: for every $d\geq 1$ there are
families with $m\gg n^d2^{n/2}$ and at least $2^{-2d-1}\binom{m}{2}$ comparable pairs. Here
$m=\lvert\mathcal{F}\rvert$, and the question is read as: for every $c>0$ there is $C=C(c)$ such
that $m\leq C2^{n/2}$ for all $n$ and all such families, so the answer is the negation.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_777.parts.ii :
    ¬ ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ 𝓕 : Finset (Finset (Fin n)),
      c * (𝓕.card : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ comparableEdges 𝓕 →
        (𝓕.card : ℝ) ≤ C * (2 : ℝ) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)

statements.name: Erdos777.erdos_777.parts.iii
statements.doc:
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ then we write $G_{\mathcal{F}}$ for the
graph on $\mathcal{F}$ where $A\sim B$ if $A$ and $B$ are comparable - that is, $A\subseteq B$ or
vice versa.

Is it true that, for any $\epsilon>0$, there exists some $\delta>0$ such that if there are
$>m^{2-\delta}$ edges then $m<(2+\epsilon)^{n/2}$?

The answer is yes, proved by Alon and Frankl [AlFr85, Theorem 1.4, the case $k=1$]. Here
$m=\lvert\mathcal{F}\rvert$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_777.parts.iii :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ 𝓕 : Finset (Finset (Fin n)),
      (𝓕.card : ℝ) ^ (2 - δ) < comparableEdges 𝓕 →
        (𝓕.card : ℝ) < (2 + ε) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 779
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/779](https://www.erdosproblems.com/779)

statements.name: Erdos779.erdos_779
statements.doc:
A Conjecture of Marian Deaconescu, see p.120 in https://doi.org/10.2307/2975810

[Needed to index shift in order to avoid trivial case $n = 0$,
where the conjecture is trivially false.]
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_779 (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≥ 1): let P := ∏ i ∈ range (n + 1), nth Nat.Prime i
    ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ (P + p).Prime ∧ nth Nat.Prime n < p ∧ p < P

problems.title: Erdős Problem 780
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/780](https://www.erdosproblems.com/780)
- [Er76] Erdős, Paul, _Problems and results in combinatorial analysis_. Colloquio Internazionale
  sulle Teorie Combinatorie (Roma, 1973), Tomo II (1976), 3-17.
- [Lo78] Lovász, L., _Kneser's conjecture, chromatic number, and homotopy_. J. Combin. Theory
  Ser. A (1978), 319-324.
- [AFL86] Alon, N. and Frankl, P. and Lovász, L., _The chromatic number of Kneser hypergraphs_.
  Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. (1986), 359-370.

statements.name: Erdos780.erdos_780
statements.doc:
Suppose $n\geq kr+(t-1)(k-1)$ and the edges of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$
vertices are $t$-coloured. Prove that some colour class must contain $k$ pairwise disjoint edges.

In other words, this problem asks to determine the chromatic number of the Kneser hypergraph.
When $k=2$ this was conjectured by Kneser and proved by Lovász [Lo78]. The general case was
proved by Alon, Frankl, and Lovász [AFL86].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_780 (n k r t : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (ht : 1 ≤ t)
    (hn : k * r + (t - 1) * (k - 1) ≤ n) (c : {e : Finset (Fin n) // e.card = r} → Fin t) :
    ∃ (i : Fin t) (e : Fin k → {e : Finset (Fin n) // e.card = r}),
      (∀ j, c (e j) = i) ∧ Pairwise fun a b ↦ Disjoint (e a).1 (e b).1

statements.name: Erdos780.erdos_780.variants.sharp
statements.doc:
This would be best possible: if $n=kr-1+(t-1)(k-1)$ then decomposing $[n]$ as one set $X_1$ of
size $kr-1$ and $t-1$ sets $X_2,\ldots,X_{t}$ of size $k-1$, a colouring without $k$ pairwise
disjoint edges is given colouring all subsets of $X_1$ in colour $1$ and assigning an edge with
colour $2\leq i\leq t$ if $i$ is minimal such that $X_i$ intersects the edge.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_780.variants.sharp (k r t : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (ht : 1 ≤ t) :
    ∃ c : {e : Finset (Fin (k * r - 1 + (t - 1) * (k - 1))) // e.card = r} → Fin t,
      ¬ ∃ (i : Fin t) (e : Fin k → {e : Finset (Fin (k * r - 1 + (t - 1) * (k - 1))) //
          e.card = r}), (∀ j, c (e j) = i) ∧ Pairwise fun a b ↦ Disjoint (e a).1 (e b).1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 781
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/781](https://www.erdosproblems.com/781)
- [BEF90] Brown, T. C. and Erdős, P. and Freedman, A. R., _Quasi-progressions and descending
  waves_. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1990), 81-95.
- [AlSp89] Alon, N. and Spencer, Joel, _Ascending waves_. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1989),
  275-287.

statements.name: Erdos781.erdos_781.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $f(k)$ be the minimal $n$ such that any $2$-colouring of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ contains a
monochromatic $k$-term descending wave: a sequence $x_1<\cdots <x_k$ such that, for $1<j<k$,
$$x_j \geq \frac{x_{j+1}+x_{j-1}}{2}.$$
Estimate $f(k)$.

Brown, Erdős, and Freedman [BEF90] proved $k^2-k+1\leq f(k) \leq \frac{k^3-4k+9}{3}$. Resolved by
Alon and Spencer [AlSp89] who proved that in fact $f(k) \gg k^3$, so that $f(k)\asymp k^3$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_781.parts.i : (fun k ↦ (f k : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] fun k ↦ (k : ℝ) ^ 3

statements.name: Erdos781.erdos_781.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is it true that $f(k)=k^2-k+1$ for all $k$?

The answer is no, since $f(k)\gg k^3$ by Alon and Spencer [AlSp89].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_781.parts.ii : ¬ ∀ k ≥ 1, f k = k ^ 2 - k + 1

statements.name: Erdos781.erdos_781.variants.brown_erdos_freedman
statements.doc: Brown, Erdős, and Freedman [BEF90] proved $k^2-k+1\leq f(k) \leq \frac{k^3-4k+9}{3}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_781.variants.brown_erdos_freedman (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    k ^ 2 - k + 1 ≤ f k ∧ (f k : ℚ) ≤ (k ^ 3 - 4 * k + 9) / 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 782
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/782](https://www.erdosproblems.com/782)
- [BEF90] Brown, T. C. and Erdős, P. and Freedman, A. R., _Quasi-progressions and descending
  waves_. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 53 (1990), 81-95.
- [BFS03] Brown, T. C., Freedman, A. R. and Shiue, P. J.-S., _Progressions of squares_.
  Australas. J. Combin. 27 (2003), 187-192.
- [BEU26] Bremner, A., Elsholtz, C. and Ulas, M., _There are infinitely many Hilbert cubes of
  dimension 3 in the set of squares_. [arXiv:2604.05459](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05459) (2026).
- [CiGr07] Cilleruelo, J. and Granville, A., _Lattice points on circles, squares in arithmetic
  progressions and sumsets of squares_. Additive combinatorics (2007), 241-262.
- [DiEl12] Dietmann, R. and Elsholtz, C., _Hilbert cubes in progression-free sets and in the set
  of squares II_. [arXiv:1207.1461](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.1461) (2012).
- [So07] Solymosi, J., _Elementary additive combinatorics_. Additive combinatorics (2007), 29-38.

statements.name: Erdos782.erdos_782.parts.i
statements.doc:
Do the squares contain arbitrarily long quasi-progressions? That is, does there exist some
constant $C>0$ such that, for any $k$, the squares contain a sequence $x_1,\ldots,x_k$ where, for
some $d$ and all $1\leq i<k$,
$$x_i+d\leq x_{i+1}\leq x_i+d+C.$$

A question of Brown, Erdős, and Freedman [BEF90]. This is the first question. Here $C$ and $d$ are
positive integers; $d\geq 1$ excludes constant sequences.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_782.parts.i :
    ∃ C : ℕ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, ContainsQuasiProgression {n : ℕ | IsSquare n} C k

statements.name: Erdos782.erdos_782.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Do the squares contain arbitrarily large cubes
$$a+\left\{ \sum_i \epsilon_ib_i : \epsilon_i\in \{0,1\}\right\}?$$

A question of Brown, Erdős, and Freedman [BEF90]. This is the second question. The generators
$b_i$ are nonzero integers, as in [BEU26]. Solymosi [So07] conjectured that the answer is no, and
Cilleruelo and Granville [CiGr07] observed that the answer is no conditional on the
Bombieri-Lang conjecture.

statements.name: Erdos782.erdos_782.variants.no_four_term_ap
statements.doc:
It is a classical fact that the squares do not contain arithmetic progressions of length
$4$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_782.variants.no_four_term_ap :
    Set.IsAPOfLengthFree {n : ℕ | IsSquare n} 4

statements.name: Erdos782.erdos_782.variants.dietmann_elsholtz
statements.doc:
Dietmann and Elsholtz [DiEl12, Theorem 1] proved that, for all sufficiently large $N$, if
$a_0\geq 0$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ are distinct positive integers such that the Hilbert cube
$a_0+\{0,b_1\}+\cdots+\{0,b_d\}$ consists of squares in $[1,N]$, then $d\leq 7\log\log N$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_782.variants.dietmann_elsholtz :
    ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ N ≥ N₀, ∀ (d : ℕ) (a₀ : ℤ) (b : Fin d → ℤ),
      0 ≤ a₀ → Function.Injective b → (∀ i, 0 < b i) →
      hilbertCube a₀ b ⊆ {n : ℤ | IsSquare n ∧ 1 ≤ n ∧ n ≤ N} →
        (d : ℝ) ≤ 7 * Real.log (Real.log N)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 785
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/785](https://www.erdosproblems.com/785)
- [ChFa10] Fang, Jin-Hui and Chen, Yong-Gao, *On additive complements*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (2010), 1923-1927.
- [ChFa11] Chen, Yong-Gao and Fang, Jin-Hui, *On additive complements. II*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (2011), 881-883.
- [ChFa14] Fang, Jin-Hui and Chen, Yong-Gao, *On additive complements. III*. J. Number Theory
  (2014), 83-91.
- [ChFa15] Chen, Yong-Gao and Fang, Jin-Hui, *On a conjecture of Sárközy and Szemerédi*.
  Acta Arith. (2015), 47-58.
- [Da64] Danzer, L., *Über eine Frage von G. Hanani aus der additiven Zahlentheorie*.
  J. Reine Angew. Math. (1964), 392-394.
- [Er57] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Michigan Math. J. (1957), 291-300.
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Na59] Narkiewicz, Władysław, *Remarks on a conjecture of Hanani in additive number theory*.
  Colloq. Math. (1959/60), 161-165.
- [Ru17] Ruzsa, Imre Z., *Exact additive complements*. Q. J. Math. (2017), 227-235.
- [SaSz94] Sárközy, A. and Szemerédi, E., *On a problem in additive number theory*.
  Acta Math. Hungar. (1994), 237-245.

statements.name: Erdos785.erdos_785
statements.doc:
Let $A,B\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be infinite sets of positive integers such that $A+B$ contains all
large integers. Let $A(x)=\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert$ and similarly for $B(x)$. Is it true that if
$A(x)B(x)\sim x$ then
$$A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$$
as $x\to \infty$?

A conjecture of Erdős and Danzer. The answer is yes, proved by Sárközy and Szemerédi [SaSz94],
who actually proved that it is impossible for
$$A(x)B(x)-x=o(A(x)).$$

This was formalized in Lean by van Doorn using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_785 :
    ∀ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → B.Infinite → 0 ∉ A → 0 ∉ B → IsExactAdditiveComplement A B →
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.danzer
statements.doc:
Danzer [Da64] proved that exact additive complements exist (Hanani had earlier conjectured they
do not exist, as reported in [Er57] and [Er61]).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_785.variants.danzer :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ 0 ∉ B ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B

statements.name: Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi
statements.doc:
Sárközy and Szemerédi [SaSz94] proved that it is impossible for
$$A(x)B(x)-x=o(A(x)).$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    ¬ (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.chen_fang
statements.doc:
Chen and Fang [ChFa15] proved $A(x)B(x)-x\ll \min(A(x),B(x))^c$ cannot hold for any constant
$c>0$. In particular $A(x)B(x)-x\ll A(x)^c$ cannot hold when $A$ is the sparser of the two sets.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) :
    ¬ (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ => (min (counting A x) (counting B x) : ℝ) ^ c)

statements.name: Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.narkiewicz
statements.doc:
Narkiewicz [Na59] proved that, under the given assumptions (and perhaps swapping $A$ and $B$)
we must have $A(2x)/A(x)\to 1$ and $B(2x)/B(x)\to 2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_785.variants.narkiewicz (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting B (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 2)) ∨
    (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting B (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ))
        atTop (𝓝 2))

statements.name: Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_upper_bound
statements.doc:
Ruzsa [Ru17] has constructed, for any function $w(x)\to \infty$, such a pair of sets with
$$A(x)B(x)-x<w(x)$$
for infinitely many $x$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_upper_bound (w : ℕ → ℝ) (hw : Tendsto w atTop atTop) :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ 0 ∉ B ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B ∧
      ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) < w x

statements.name: Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_lower_bound
statements.doc:
Ruzsa [Ru17] proves that, if $a^*(x)=\max A \cap [1,x]$ and $A$ and $B$ satisfy the conditions
in the problem then (after possibly changing the roles of $A$ and $B$)
$$A(x)B(x)-x > (1-o(1))\frac{a^*(x)}{A(x)}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_lower_bound (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
        (1 - ε) * (aStar A x : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)
          < (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) ∨
    (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
        (1 - ε) * (aStar B x : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)
          < (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_limsup
statements.doc:
Chen and Fang [ChFa10] proved the stronger statement that $A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$ if $A$ and $B$
are infinite sets such that $A+B$ contains all large integers and
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}<\frac{5}{4}.$$
They later [ChFa14] improved $5/4$ to $3-\sqrt{3}\approx 1.268$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_limsup (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsAdditiveComplement A B)
    (hlim : limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
      < ((3 - Real.sqrt 3 : ℝ) : EReal)) :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.chen_conjecture
statements.doc: Chen conjectures that this should be true with $3/2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_conjecture :
    ∀ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → B.Infinite → 0 ∉ A → 0 ∉ B → IsAdditiveComplement A B →
      limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
          < ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) →
        Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_sharp
statements.doc:
This is sharp, as Chen and Fang [ChFa11] also proved that there exist such $A$ and $B$ with
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}=\frac{3}{2}$$
for which $A(x)B(x)-x=1$ for infinitely many $x$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_sharp :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ 0 ∉ B ∧ IsAdditiveComplement A B ∧
      limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
          = ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) ∧
      ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 786
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/786](https://www.erdosproblems.com/786)

statements.name: Erdos786.erdos_786.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $\epsilon > 0$. Is there some set $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ of density $> 1 - \epsilon$
such that $a_1\cdots a_r = b_1\cdots b_s$ with $a_i, b_j\in A$ can only hold when
$r = s$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_786.parts.i : ∀ ε > 0, ε ≤ 1 →
    ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (δ : ℝ), 0 ∉ A ∧ 1 - ε < δ ∧ A.HasDensity δ ∧ A.IsMulCardSet

statements.name: Erdos786.erdos_786.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is there some set $A\subset\{1, ..., N\}$ of size $\geq (1 - o(1))N$ such that
$a_1\cdots a_r = b_1\cdots b_s$ with $a_i, b_j\in A$ can only hold when
$r = s$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_786.parts.ii :
    ∃ (A : ℕ → Set ℕ) (f : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : f =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)),
    ∀ N, A N ⊆ Set.Icc 1 (N + 1) ∧ (1 - f N) * N ≤ (A N).ncard ∧ (A N).IsMulCardSet

statements.name: Erdos786.erdos_786.parts.i.example
statements.doc: An example of such a set with density $\frac 1 4$ is given by the integers $\equiv 2\pmod{4}$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_786.parts.i.example (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A = { n | n % 4 = 2 }) :
    A.HasDensity (1 / 4) ∧ A.IsMulCardSet

statements.name: Erdos786.erdos_786.parts.i.selfridge
statements.doc:
Let $\epsilon > 0$ be given. Then, for a sufficiently large prime `p`, take the sequence of
consecutive primes $p_1 < \cdots < p_k$ such that
$$
\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{p_i} < 1 < \sum_{i=1}^{k + 1} \frac{1}{p_i},
$$
and let $A$ be the set of all naturals divisible by exactly one of $p_1, ..., p_k$ (with
multiplicity $1$). Then $A$ has density $> \frac{1}{e} - \epsilon$ and has the property
that $a_1\cdots a_r = b_1\cdots b_s$ with $a_i, b_j\in A$ can only hold when $r = s$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_786.parts.i.selfridge (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 / rexp 1) :
    ∀ᶠ (p : ℕ) in atTop, p.Prime → ∃ k,
      ∑ q ∈ consecutivePrimesFrom p k, (1 : ℝ) / q < 1 ∧
        1 < ∑ q ∈ consecutivePrimesFrom p (k + 1), (1 : ℝ) / q ∧
          letI A := { n | ∑ q ∈ consecutivePrimesFrom p k, (n : ℕ).factorization q = 1 }
          ∃ δ, 1 / rexp 1 - ε < δ ∧ A.HasDensity δ ∧ A.IsMulCardSet

problems.title: Erdős Problem 787
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/787](https://www.erdosproblems.com/787)
- [Be25] Beker, A., *The Erdős-Moser sum-free set problem via improved bounds for
  $k$-configurations*. [arXiv:2501.10203](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.10203) (2025).
- [Ch71] Choi, S. L. G., *On a combinatorial problem in number theory*.
  Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) (1971), 629-642.
- [Er65] Erdős, P., *Extremal problems in number theory*. Proc. Sympos. Pure Math., Vol. VIII
  (1965), 181-189. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1965-02.pdf)
- [Er73] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of
  combinatorial theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo.,
  1971) (1973), 117-138. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1973-21.pdf)
- [Ru05] Ruzsa, Imre Z., *Sum-avoiding subsets*. Ramanujan J. (2005), 77-82.
- [Sa21] Sanders, Tom, *The Erdős-Moser sum-free set problem*. Canad. J. Math. (2021), 63-107.

statements.name: Erdos787.erdos_787
statements.doc:
Let $g(n)$ be maximal such that given any set $A\subset \mathbb{R}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=n$ there
exists some $B\subseteq A$ of size $\lvert B\rvert\geq g(n)$ such that $b_1+b_2\not\in A$ for all
$b_1\neq b_2\in B$.

Estimate $g(n)$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_787 : (fun n ↦ (g ℝ n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_787.answer

statements.name: Erdos787.erdos_787.variants.integers
statements.doc:
This function was considered by Erdős and Moser. Choi observed that, without loss of generality,
one can assume that $A\subset \mathbb{Z}$.

Here this means that sets of integers give the same value $g(n)$ as sets of reals.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_787.variants.integers (n : ℕ) : g ℤ n = g ℝ n

statements.name: Erdos787.erdos_787.variants.klarner
statements.doc: Klarner proved $g(n) \gg \log n$ (indeed, a greedy construction suffices).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_787.variants.klarner :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c * Real.log n ≤ (g ℝ n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos787.erdos_787.variants.choi
statements.doc:
Choi [Ch71] proved $g(n) \ll n^{2/5+o(1)}$.

Here this means that $g(n) \leq n^{2/5+\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all large $n$,
as in [Er73, p. 130].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_787.variants.choi :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (g ℝ n : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 5 + ε)

statements.name: Erdos787.erdos_787.variants.sanders
statements.doc:
The current best bounds known are
$$(\log n)^{1+c} \ll g(n) \ll \exp(\sqrt{\log n})$$
for some constant $c>0$, the lower bound due to Sanders [Sa21] and the upper bound due to
Ruzsa [Ru05].

This is the lower bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_787.variants.sanders :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, Real.log n ^ (1 + c) ≤ (g ℝ n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos787.erdos_787.variants.ruzsa
statements.doc:
The current best bounds known are
$$(\log n)^{1+c} \ll g(n) \ll \exp(\sqrt{\log n})$$
for some constant $c>0$, the lower bound due to Sanders [Sa21] and the upper bound due to
Ruzsa [Ru05].

This is the upper bound. [Ru05] proves it in the form $\exp(O(\sqrt{\log n}))$, which is the form
stated here.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_787.variants.ruzsa :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (g ℝ n : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp (C * Real.sqrt (Real.log n))

statements.name: Erdos787.erdos_787.variants.beker
statements.doc:
Beker [Be25] has proved
$$(\log n)^{1+\tfrac{1}{68}+o(1)} \ll g(n).$$

Here this means that $g(n) \geq (\log n)^{1+c}$ for every $c < 1/68$ and all large $n$
[Be25, Theorem 1.2].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_787.variants.beker :
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → c < 1 / 68 → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, Real.log n ^ (1 + c) ≤ (g ℝ n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 789
problems.doc:
In this problem, a function $h : \mathbb{N} \to\mathbb{N}$ is defined maximally by
some counting property.

The problem asks to estimate $h(n)$. This has been interpreted here as asking for $\Theta(h(n))$.
The principal version includes the unknown function `erdos_789.answer`.

Straus [Str66] proved that $h(n) \ll \sqrt{n}$. Erdős [Er62c] and Choi [Ch74b] proved that
$(n\log(n))^{1/3} \ll h(n)$. Korsky [Ko26] improved this to $h(n) \gg \sqrt{n\log\log n/\log n}$.
The variants record these bounds and the open question whether $h(n) = \Theta(\sqrt{n})$. The file
proves Korsky's bound, following [Ko26], and derives from it the Erdős–Choi bound and
$h(n) \neq O((n\log(n))^{1/3})$.

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/789](https://www.erdosproblems.com/789)
- [Str66] Straus, E. G., _On a problem in combinatorial number theory_. J. Math. Sci. (1966), 77--80.
- [Er62c] Erdős, Pál, _Some remarks on number theory_. {III}. Mat. Lapok (1962), 28--38.
- [Ch74b] Choi, S. L. G., _On an extremal problem in number theory_. J. Number Theory (1974), 105--111.
- [Ko26] Korsky, S., _A near-square-root bound for an additive problem of Erdős and Straus_ (2026).
  [Proof claim](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/789/proof-claims).

statements.name: Erdos789.erdos_789
statements.doc:
Let $h(n)$ be maximal such that if $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=n$
then there is $B\subseteq A$ with $\lvert B\rvert \geq h(n)$ such that if
$a_1+\cdots+a_r=b_1+\cdots+b_s$ with $a_i,b_i\in B$ then $r=s$.

Estimate $h(n)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_789 :
    (fun n ↦ (subsetSumThreshold n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_789.answer

statements.name: Erdos789.erdos_789.variants.sq
statements.doc:
Let $h(n)$ be maximal such that if $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=n$
then there is $B\subseteq A$ with $\lvert B\rvert \geq h(n)$ such that if
$a_1+\cdots+a_r=b_1+\cdots+b_s$ with $a_i,b_i\in B$ then $r=s$.

Is $h(n) = \Theta(\sqrt{n})$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_789.variants.sq :
    (fun n ↦ (subsetSumThreshold n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] fun n ↦ √n

statements.name: Erdos789.erdos_789.variants.isBigO_sq
statements.doc: Straus [Str66] proved that $h(n) \ll \sqrt{n}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_789.variants.isBigO_sq :
    (fun n ↦ (subsetSumThreshold n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ √n

statements.name: Erdos789.erdos_789.variants.sq_isBigO
statements.doc:
By the solved variant `erdos_789.variants.isBigO_sq`, in order to prove
`erdos_789.variants.sq` it suffices to show $\sqrt{n}=O(h(n))$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_789.variants.sq_isBigO :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ √n) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (subsetSumThreshold n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos789.erdos_789.variants.sqrt_loglog_div_log_isBigO
statements.doc: Korsky [Ko26] proved that $h(n) \gg \sqrt{n\log\log n/\log n}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_789.variants.sqrt_loglog_div_log_isBigO :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ √(n * Real.log (Real.log n) / Real.log n)) =O[atTop]
      fun n ↦ (subsetSumThreshold n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos789.erdos_789.variants.cube_root_linearithmic_isBigO
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er62c] and Choi [Ch74b] proved that $(n\log(n))^{1/3}\ll h(n)$. This also follows from
`erdos_789.variants.sqrt_loglog_div_log_isBigO`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_789.variants.cube_root_linearithmic_isBigO :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n * Real.log n) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)) =O[atTop]
      fun n ↦ (subsetSumThreshold n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos789.erdos_789.variants.isBigO_cube_root_linearithmic
statements.doc:
It is not true that $h(n) = O((n\log(n))^{1/3})$. This follows from
`erdos_789.variants.sqrt_loglog_div_log_isBigO` [Ko26].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_789.variants.isBigO_cube_root_linearithmic :
    ¬ (fun n ↦ (subsetSumThreshold n : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      fun n ↦ (n * Real.log n) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)

statements.name: Erdos789.erdos_789.variants.cube_root_linearithmic
statements.doc:
It is not true that $h(n) = \Theta((n\log(n))^{1/3})$. This follows from
`erdos_789.variants.isBigO_cube_root_linearithmic`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_789.variants.cube_root_linearithmic :
    ¬ (fun n ↦ (subsetSumThreshold n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop]
      fun n ↦ (n * Real.log n) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 793
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/793](https://www.erdosproblems.com/793)
- [Er38] Erdős, P., *On sequences of integers no one of which divides the product of two others
  and on related problems*. Tomsk. Gos. Univ. Ucen Zap. (1938), 74-82.
- [Er69] Erdős, Paul, *Some applications of graph theory to number theory*. The Many Facets of
  Graph Theory (Proc. Conf., Western Mich. Univ., Kalamazoo, Mich., 1968) (1969), 77-82.
- [Er70b] Erdős, P., *Some applications of graph theory to number theory*. Proc. Second Chapel Hill
  Conf. on Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Univ. North Carolina, Chapel Hill, N.C.,
  1970) (1970), 136-145.

statements.name: Erdos793.erdos_793
statements.doc:
Let $F(n)$ be the maximum possible size of a subset $A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, n\}$ such that
$a \nmid bc$ whenever $a, b, c \in A$ with $a \neq b$ and $a \neq c$. Is there a constant $c$ such
that
$$F(n) = \pi(n) + (c + o(1)) n^{2/3} (\log n)^{-2}?$$

A problem of Erdős [Er69, Er70b], who proved in [Er38] that
$F(n) = \pi(n) + O(n^{2/3} (\log n)^{-2})$. The answer is yes, with $c = 27/2$: this was proved by
GPT-5.6 Sol (prompted by Chojecki), refining the argument of [Er38]; see
`erdos_793.variants.constant`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_793 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((F n : ℝ) - Nat.primeCounting n) /
      ((n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3) / (log n) ^ 2)) atTop (𝓝 c)

statements.name: Erdos793.erdos_793.variants.constant
statements.doc:
The constant in Problem 793 is $c = 27/2$, i.e.
$$F(n) = \pi(n) + \left(\frac{27}{2} + o(1)\right) \frac{n^{2/3}}{(\log n)^2}.$$
Formalised by van Doorn and Aristotle, following the proof of GPT-5.6 Sol.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_793.variants.constant :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((F n : ℝ) - Nat.primeCounting n) /
      ((n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3) / (log n) ^ 2)) atTop (𝓝 (27 / 2))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 794
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/794](https://www.erdosproblems.com/794)
- [Er69] Erdős, Paul, *Some applications of graph theory to number theory*. The Many Facets of
  Graph Theory (Proc. Conf., Western Mich. Univ., Kalamazoo, Mich., 1968) (1969), 77-82.
- [FrFu84] Frankl, P. and Füredi, Z., *An exact result for $3$-graphs*. Discrete Math. (1984),
  323-328.

statements.name: Erdos794.erdos_794
statements.doc:
Is it true that every $3$-uniform hypergraph on $3n$ vertices with at least $n^3+1$ edges must
contain either a subgraph on $4$ vertices with $3$ edges or a subgraph on $5$ vertices with $7$
edges?

Harris has provided the following simple counterexample to the problem as stated: the
$3$-uniform graph on $\{1,\ldots,9\}$ with $28$ edges, formed by taking $27$ edges by choosing
one element each from $\{1,2,3\},\{4,5,6\},\{7,8,9\}$, and then adding the edge $\{1,2,3\}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_794 :
    ¬ ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ H : Finset (Finset (Fin (3 * n))), H.IsUniform 3 →
      n ^ 3 + 1 ≤ H.card → H.ContainsSubgraph 4 3 ∨ H.ContainsSubgraph 5 7

statements.name: Erdos794.erdos_794.variants.balogh
statements.doc:
Balogh has observed that this problem is probably misstated by Erdős - indeed, every graph with
$5$ vertices spanning $7$ edges contains a graph on $4$ vertices spanning $3$ edges, so the
second condition can be dropped.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_794.variants.balogh {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (H : Finset (Finset V))
    (hH : H.IsUniform 3) (h : H.ContainsSubgraph 5 7) : H.ContainsSubgraph 4 3

statements.name: Erdos794.erdos_794.variants.harris
statements.doc:
Harris has provided the following simple counterexample to the problem as stated: the
$3$-uniform graph on $\{1,\ldots,9\}$ with $28$ edges, formed by taking $27$ edges by choosing
one element each from $\{1,2,3\},\{4,5,6\},\{7,8,9\}$, and then adding the edge $\{1,2,3\}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_794.variants.harris :
    harrisHypergraph.IsUniform 3 ∧ harrisHypergraph.card = 28 ∧
      ¬ harrisHypergraph.ContainsSubgraph 4 3 ∧ ¬ harrisHypergraph.ContainsSubgraph 5 7

statements.name: Erdos794.erdos_794.variants.frankl_furedi
statements.doc:
This problem is then now asking how many edges a $3$-uniform hypergraph can have before it
contains $K_4$ minus an edge, and whether the critical edge density is $2/9$. In fact there is a
construction of Frankl and Füredi [FrFu84] showing it must be at least $2/7$, which is the
conjectured truth (although Turán conjectured before [Er69] that the edge density was $1/4$, and
so likely there is simply a typo in this problem's statement).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_794.variants.frankl_furedi (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ H : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), H.IsUniform 3 ∧
      ¬ H.ContainsSubgraph 4 3 ∧ (2 / 7 - ε) * (n.choose 3 : ℝ) ≤ (H.card : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 796
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/796](https://www.erdosproblems.com/796)

statements.name: Erdos796.erdos_796
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 2$ and let $g_k(n)$ be the largest possible size of
$A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that every $m$ has $<k$ solutions to
$m=a_1a_2$ with $a_1<a_2\in A$. Is it true that
$$g_3(n)=\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}n+(c+o(1))\frac{n}{\log n}$$
for some constant $c$?

The answer is yes: the rescaled error `normalizedError` converges.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_796 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, Tendsto normalizedError atTop (𝓝 c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 798
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/798](https://www.erdosproblems.com/798)
- [Al91] Alon, N., *Economical coverings of sets of lattice points*. Geom. Funct. Anal. (1991),
  224-230.

statements.name: Erdos798.erdos_798
statements.doc:
Let $t(n)$ be the minimum number of points in $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$ such that the $\binom{t}{2}$
lines determined by these points cover all points in $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$.

Estimate $t(n)$. In particular, is it true that $t(n)=o(n)$?

A problem of Erdős and Purdy, who proved $t(n) \gg n^{2/3}$.

Resolved by Alon [Al91] who proved $t(n) \ll n^{2/3}\log n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_798 :
    (fun n : ℕ => (t n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos798.erdos_798.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc: A problem of Erdős and Purdy, who proved $t(n) \gg n^{2/3}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_798.variants.lower_bound :
    (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (t n : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos798.erdos_798.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc: Resolved by Alon [Al91] who proved $t(n) \ll n^{2/3}\log n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_798.variants.upper_bound :
    (fun n : ℕ => (t n : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ) * Real.log n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 800
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/800](https://www.erdosproblems.com/800)
- [Al94] Alon, N., Subdivided graphs have linear Ramsey numbers. J. Graph Theory (1994), 343-347.

statements.name: Erdos800.erdos_800
statements.doc:
If $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices which has no two adjacent vertices of degree $\geq 3$ then
$$R(G)\ll n,$$
where the implied constant is absolute.

A problem of Burr and Erdős. Solved in the affirmative by Alon [Al94].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_800 :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      Fintype.card V = n →
      (∀ u v, G.Adj u v → ¬(3 ≤ G.degree u ∧ 3 ≤ G.degree v)) →
      (SimpleGraph.diagonalGraphRamsey G : ℝ) ≤ C * n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 801
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/801](https://www.erdosproblems.com/801)
- [Er79g] Erdős, Paul, *Some old and new problems in various branches of combinatorics*.
  Proceedings of the Tenth Southeastern Conference on Combinatorics, Graph Theory and Computing
  (Florida Atlantic Univ., Boca Raton, Fla., 1979) (1979), 19-37.
- [Al96b] Alon, Noga, *Independence numbers of locally sparse graphs and a Ramsey type problem*.
  Random Structures Algorithms (1996), 271-278.

statements.name: Erdos801.erdos_801
statements.doc:
If $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices containing no independent set on $>n^{1/2}$ vertices then there
is a set of $\leq n^{1/2}$ vertices containing $\gg n^{1/2}\log n$ edges.

Proved by Alon [Al96b].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_801 : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ √n →
      ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), (S.card : ℝ) ≤ √n ∧
        c * √n * Real.log n ≤ (G.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).edgeSet.ncard

problems.title: Erdős Problem 802
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/802](https://www.erdosproblems.com/802)
- [AEKS81] Ajtai, M. and Erdős, P. and Komlós, J. and Szemerédi, E., *On Turán's theorem for
  sparse graphs*. Combinatorica (1981), 313-317.
- [AKS80] Ajtai, Miklós and Komlós, János and Szemerédi, Endre, *A note on Ramsey numbers*.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1980), 354-360.
- [Al96b] Alon, Noga, *Independence numbers of locally sparse graphs and a Ramsey type problem*.
  Random Structures Algorithms (1996), 271-278.
- [Sh95] Shearer, James B., *On the independence number of sparse graphs*. Random Structures
  Algorithms (1995), 269-271.

statements.name: Erdos802.erdos_802
statements.doc:
Is it true that any $K_r$-free graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $t$ contains an
independent set on
$$\gg_r \frac{\log t}{t}n$$
many vertices?

A conjecture of Ajtai, Erdős, Komlós, and Szemerédi [AEKS81].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_802 : ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
    G.CliqueFree r →
      c * (log G.averageDegree / G.averageDegree) * n ≤ G.indepNum

statements.name: Erdos802.erdos_802.variants.aeks
statements.doc:
Ajtai, Erdős, Komlós, and Szemerédi [AEKS81] proved that any $K_r$-free graph on $n$ vertices
with average degree $t$ contains an independent set on
$$\gg_r \frac{\log\log(t+1)}{t}n$$
many vertices.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_802.variants.aeks : ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
    G.CliqueFree r →
      c * (log (log (G.averageDegree + 1)) / G.averageDegree) * n ≤ G.indepNum

statements.name: Erdos802.erdos_802.variants.shearer
statements.doc:
Shearer [Sh95] proved that any $K_r$-free graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $t$ contains
an independent set on
$$\gg_r \frac{\log t}{\log\log(t+1)t}n$$
many vertices.

We assume $t \geq 2$. For $t + 1$ slightly larger than $e$ the factor $\log\log(t+1)$ is close
to $0$, so the bound blows up and the statement is false without such a restriction.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_802.variants.shearer : ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
    G.CliqueFree r → 2 ≤ G.averageDegree →
      c * (log G.averageDegree / (log (log (G.averageDegree + 1)) * G.averageDegree)) * n ≤
        G.indepNum

statements.name: Erdos802.erdos_802.variants.r_eq_three
statements.doc:
Ajtai, Komlós, and Szemerédi [AKS80] proved the conjectured bound when $r = 3$: any
triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $t$ contains an independent set on
$$\gg \frac{\log t}{t}n$$
many vertices.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_802.variants.r_eq_three : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
    G.CliqueFree 3 →
      c * (log G.averageDegree / G.averageDegree) * n ≤ G.indepNum

statements.name: Erdos802.erdos_802.variants.alon
statements.doc:
Alon [Al96b] proved the conjectured bound under the stronger assumption that the induced graph
on every vertex neighbourhood has chromatic number $\leq r - 2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_802.variants.alon : ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
    (∀ v, (G.induce (G.neighborSet v)).Colorable (r - 2)) →
      c * (log G.averageDegree / G.averageDegree) * n ≤ G.indepNum

problems.title: Erdős Problem 803
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/803](https://www.erdosproblems.com/803)
- [ErSi70] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M., _Some extremal problems in graph theory_. Combinatorial
  theory and its applications, I-III (Proc. Colloq., Balatonfüred, 1969) (1970), 377-390.
- [Al08] Alon, Noga, _Problems and results in extremal combinatorics. II_. Discrete Math. (2008),
  4460-4472.
- [JaSu23] Janzer, Oliver and Sudakov, Benny, _Resolution of the Erdős-Sauer problem on regular
  subgraphs_. Forum Math. Pi (2023), Paper No. e19, 13.

statements.name: Erdos803.erdos_803
statements.doc:
We call a graph $H$ $D$-balanced (or $D$-almost-regular) if the maximum degree of $H$ is at most
$D$ times the minimum degree of $H$.

Is it true that for every $m\geq 1$, if $n$ is sufficiently large, any graph on $n$ vertices with
$\geq n\log n$ edges contains a $O(1)$-balanced subgraph with $m$ vertices and $\gg m\log m$ edges
(where the implied constants are absolute)?

A problem of Erdős and Simonovits [ErSi70]. Alon [Al08] proved this is false: for every $D>1$
and large $n$ there is a graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $\geq n\log n$ edges such that if $H$ is
a $D$-balanced subgraph then $H$ has $\ll m\sqrt{\log m}+\log D$ many edges.

See also [1077](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1077).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_803 :
    ¬ ∃ (D c : ℝ), 0 < c ∧ ∀ m ≥ 1, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (n : ℝ) * log n ≤ G.edgeSet.ncard →
        ∃ H : G.Subgraph, H.verts.ncard = m ∧ IsBalanced H.coe D ∧
          c * m * log m ≤ H.edgeSet.ncard

statements.name: Erdos803.erdos_803.variants.alon
statements.doc:
Alon [Al08] proved that for every $D>1$ and large $n$ there is a graph $G$ with $n$ vertices
and $\geq n\log n$ edges such that if $H$ is a $D$-balanced subgraph on $m$ vertices then $H$ has
$\ll m\sqrt{\log m}+\log D$ many edges.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_803.variants.alon :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ D : ℝ, 1 < D → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (n : ℝ) * log n ≤ G.edgeSet.ncard ∧
      ∀ H : G.Subgraph, IsBalanced H.coe D →
        (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ≤ C * (H.verts.ncard * √(log H.verts.ncard) + log D)

statements.name: Erdos803.erdos_803.variants.janzer_sudakov
statements.doc:
Janzer and Sudakov [JaSu23] have proved that, for any $k$, if $n$ is sufficiently large then
any graph on $n$ vertices with at least $n\log n$ edges contains a $O(1)$-balanced subgraph on
$m\geq k$ vertices with $\gg_k \frac{\sqrt{\log m}}{(\log\log m)^{3/2}}m$ many edges.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_803.variants.janzer_sudakov :
    ∃ D : ℝ, ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (n : ℝ) * log n ≤ G.edgeSet.ncard →
        ∃ H : G.Subgraph, k ≤ H.verts.ncard ∧ IsBalanced H.coe D ∧
          c * (√(log H.verts.ncard) / (log (log H.verts.ncard)) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ)) *
            H.verts.ncard ≤ H.edgeSet.ncard

problems.title: Erdős Problem 804
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/804](https://www.erdosproblems.com/804)
- [Er91] Erdős, P., _Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory_. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991),
  397-406.
- [AlSu07] Alon, Noga and Sudakov, Benny, _On graphs with subgraphs having large independence
  numbers_. J. Graph Theory (2007), 149-157.

statements.name: Erdos804.erdos_804.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $f(m,n)$ be maximal such that any graph on $n$ vertices in which every induced subgraph on
$m$ vertices has an independent set of size at least $\log n$ must contain an independent set of
size at least $f(n)$.

Estimate $f(n)$. In particular, is it true that $f((\log n)^2,n) \geq n^{1/2-o(1)}$?

The answer is no: Alon and Sudakov [AlSu07] proved that in fact
$$\frac{(\log n)^2}{\log\log n}\ll f((\log n)^2,n) \ll (\log n)^2.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_804.parts.i :
    ¬ ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 - ε : ℝ) ≤ f ⌊(log n) ^ 2⌋₊ n

statements.name: Erdos804.erdos_804.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is it true that $f((\log n)^3,n)\gg (\log n)^3$?

The answer is no: Alon and Sudakov [AlSu07] proved that in fact
$$f((\log n)^3,n)\asymp \frac{(\log n)^2}{\log\log n}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_804.parts.ii :
    ¬ ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c * (log n) ^ 3 ≤ f ⌊(log n) ^ 3⌋₊ n

statements.name: Erdos804.erdos_804.variants.alon_sudakov
statements.doc:
Alon and Sudakov [AlSu07] proved that
$$\frac{(\log n)^2}{\log\log n}\ll f((\log n)^2,n) \ll (\log n)^2$$
and
$$f((\log n)^3,n)\asymp \frac{(\log n)^2}{\log\log n}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_804.variants.alon_sudakov :
    ∃ c₂ C₂ c₃ C₃ : ℝ, 0 < c₂ ∧ 0 < C₂ ∧ 0 < c₃ ∧ 0 < C₃ ∧
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      c₂ * ((log n) ^ 2 / log (log n)) ≤ f ⌊(log n) ^ 2⌋₊ n ∧
      (f ⌊(log n) ^ 2⌋₊ n : ℝ) ≤ C₂ * (log n) ^ 2 ∧
      c₃ * ((log n) ^ 2 / log (log n)) ≤ f ⌊(log n) ^ 3⌋₊ n ∧
      (f ⌊(log n) ^ 3⌋₊ n : ℝ) ≤ C₃ * ((log n) ^ 2 / log (log n))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 805
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/805](https://www.erdosproblems.com/805)
- [Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991),
  397-406.
- [AlSu07] Alon, N. and Sudakov, B., *On graphs with subgraphs having large independence
  numbers*. J. Graph Theory 56 (2007), 149-157.
  [arXiv:0706.4099](https://arxiv.org/abs/0706.4099)
- [ABS21] Alon, N., Bucić, M. and Sudakov, B., *Large cliques and independent sets all over the
  place*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 149 (2021), 3145-3157.
  [arXiv:2004.04718](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.04718)

statements.name: Erdos805.erdos_805.parts.i
statements.doc:
For which functions $g(n)$ with $n>g(n)\geq (\log n)^2$ is there a graph on $n$ vertices in which
every induced subgraph on $g(n)$ vertices contains a clique of size $\geq \log n$ and an
independent set of size $\geq \log n$?

In particular, is there such a graph for $g(n)=(\log n)^3$?

This is the first part. A problem of Erdős and Hajnal [Er91]; see also
[erdosproblems.com/804](https://www.erdosproblems.com/804). The inequalities
on `g` are required for all large `n`, and a graph is required for all large `n`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_805.parts.i :
    {g : ℕ → ℕ | (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, Real.log n ^ 2 ≤ g n ∧ g n < n) ∧ HasRamseyGraphs g} =
      erdos_805.parts.i.answer

statements.name: Erdos805.erdos_805.parts.ii
statements.doc:
For which functions $g(n)$ with $n>g(n)\geq (\log n)^2$ is there a graph on $n$ vertices in which
every induced subgraph on $g(n)$ vertices contains a clique of size $\geq \log n$ and an
independent set of size $\geq \log n$?

In particular, is there such a graph for $g(n)=(\log n)^3$?

This is the second part. Erdős and Hajnal thought that there is no such graph for
$g(n)=(\log n)^3$ [AlSu07]; we state the positive proposition, with $g(n)=\lfloor(\log n)^3\rfloor$
and a graph required for all large $n$, as in the first part.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_805.parts.ii : HasRamseyGraphs (fun n ↦ ⌊Real.log n ^ 3⌋₊)

statements.name: Erdos805.erdos_805.variants.alon_sudakov
statements.doc:
Alon and Sudakov [AlSu07] proved that there is no such graph with
$$g(n)=\frac{c}{\log\log n}(\log n)^3$$
for some constant $c>0$.

Here `log` is the natural logarithm, as in [AlSu07], and the statement is for all large `n`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_805.variants.alon_sudakov :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ¬ ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      IsLocallyRamsey G ⌊c * Real.log n ^ 3 / Real.log (Real.log n)⌋₊ ⌈Real.log n⌉₊

statements.name: Erdos805.erdos_805.variants.alon_bucic_sudakov
statements.doc:
Alon, Bucić, and Sudakov [ABS21] construct such a graph with
$$g(n)\leq 2^{2^{(\log\log n)^{1/2+o(1)}}}.$$

Here all logarithms are to base $2$, as in [ABS21], so the cliques and independent sets have at
least $\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ vertices; this implies the natural-logarithm version of the problem.
The $o(1)$ is expressed as: for every $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ and all large $n$ there is such a graph
with $g(n)=\lceil 2^{2^{(\log_2\log_2 n)^{1/2+\varepsilon}}}\rceil$. This form, with the rounding,
follows from [ABS21, Theorem 2].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_805.variants.alon_bucic_sudakov :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε < 1 / 2 → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      IsLocallyRamsey G
        ⌈(2 : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) ^ (Real.logb 2 (Real.logb 2 n) ^ (1 / 2 + ε)))⌉₊
        ⌈Real.logb 2 n⌉₊

problems.title: Erdős Problem 806
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/806](https://www.erdosproblems.com/806)
- [ErNe77] Erdős, P. and Newman, D. J., *Bases for sets of integers*. J. Number Theory (1977),
  420-425.
- [ABS09] Alon, Noga and Bukh, Boris and Sudakov, Benny, *Discrete Kakeya-type problems and small
  bases*. Israel J. Math. (2009), 285-301.

statements.name: Erdos806.erdos_806
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $\lvert A\rvert \leq n^{1/2}$. Must there exist some
$B\subset\mathbb{Z}$ with $\lvert B\rvert=o(n^{1/2})$ such that $A\subseteq B+B$?

A problem of Erdős and Newman [ErNe77], who proved that there exist $A$ with
$\lvert A\rvert\asymp n^{1/2}$ such that if $A\subseteq B+B$ then
$$\lvert B\rvert \gg \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}n^{1/2}.$$

Resolved by Alon, Bukh, and Sudakov [ABS09], who proved that for any $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$
with $\lvert A\rvert \leq n^{1/2}$ there exists some $B$ such that $A\subseteq B+B$ and
$$\lvert B\rvert \ll \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}n^{1/2}.$$

See also [333](https://www.erdosproblems.com/333).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_806 : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∀ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n → (A.card : ℝ) ≤ √n →
      ∃ B : Finset ℤ, A.map Nat.castEmbedding ⊆ B + B ∧ (B.card : ℝ) ≤ ε * √n

statements.name: Erdos806.erdos_806.variants.alon_bukh_sudakov
statements.doc:
