Alon, Bukh, and Sudakov [ABS09] proved that for any $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ with
$\lvert A\rvert \leq n^{1/2}$ there exists some $B$ such that $A\subseteq B+B$ and
$\lvert B\rvert \ll \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}n^{1/2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_806.variants.alon_bukh_sudakov : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∀ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n → (A.card : ℝ) ≤ √n →
      ∃ B : Finset ℤ, A.map Nat.castEmbedding ⊆ B + B ∧
        (B.card : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.log (Real.log n) / Real.log n * √n

statements.name: Erdos806.erdos_806.variants.erdos_newman
statements.doc:
Erdős and Newman [ErNe77] proved that there exist $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with
$\lvert A\rvert\asymp n^{1/2}$ such that if $A\subseteq B+B$ then
$\lvert B\rvert \gg \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}n^{1/2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_806.variants.erdos_newman : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∃ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n ∧ c * √n ≤ A.card ∧ (A.card : ℝ) ≤ √n ∧
      ∀ B : Finset ℤ, A.map Nat.castEmbedding ⊆ B + B →
        c * Real.log (Real.log n) / Real.log n * √n ≤ B.card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 808
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/808](https://www.erdosproblems.com/808)
- [ErSz83] Erdős, P. and Szemerédi, E., *On sums and products of integers*. Studies in pure
  mathematics (1983), 213-218. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1983-18.pdf)
- [ARS20] Alon, Noga and Ruzsa, Imre and Solymosi, József, *Sums, products and ratios along the
  edges of a graph*. Publ. Mat. (2020), 143-155.
  [arXiv:1802.06405](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.06405)

statements.name: Erdos808.erdos_808
statements.doc:
Let $c,\epsilon>0$ and $n$ be sufficiently large. If $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ has $\lvert A\rvert=n$
and $G$ is any graph on $A$ with at least $n^{1+c}$ edges then
$$\max(\lvert A+_GA\rvert,\lvert A\cdot_G A\rvert) \geq \lvert A\rvert^{1+c-\epsilon},$$
where
$$A+_GA = \{ a+b : (a,b)\in G\}$$
and similarly for $A\cdot_GA$.

This strong conjecture of Erdős and Szemerédi [ErSz83] strengthens Erdős Problem 52
(`Erdos52.erdos_52`, the case of the complete graph). It was disproved by Alon, Ruzsa, and
Solymosi [ARS20, Theorem 3]: for arbitrarily large $m$ there are a set of integers $A$ with
$\lvert A\rvert=m$ and a graph on $A$ with $\gg m^{5/3}/(\log m)^{1/3}$ edges such that
$\lvert A+_GA\rvert+\lvert A\cdot_GA\rvert \ll (m\log m)^{4/3}$. The statement below is the
negation of the conjecture.

A set $A$ with a graph on it is given by a finite type `V`, a graph `G` on `V` and an injection
`a : V ↪ ℕ` (so $A$ is the image of `a` and $n$ is `Fintype.card V`). Here `ℕ` contains $0$; see
`erdos_808.variants.positive` for positive integers.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_808 :
    ¬ ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
      ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (a : V ↪ ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
        n₀ ≤ Fintype.card V →
        (Fintype.card V : ℝ) ^ (1 + c) ≤ (G.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) →
        (Fintype.card V : ℝ) ^ (1 + c - ε) ≤
          max ((edgeSums a G).card : ℝ) ((edgeProducts a G).card : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos808.erdos_808.variants.positive
statements.doc:
The conjecture already fails for positive integers: the set of integers constructed in
[ARS20, Theorem 3] consists of positive integers. This is `erdos_808` with the extra hypothesis
`∀ v, 0 < a v`, so it implies `erdos_808`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_808.variants.positive :
    ¬ ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
      ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (a : V ↪ ℕ), (∀ v, 0 < a v) →
        ∀ (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
          n₀ ≤ Fintype.card V →
          (Fintype.card V : ℝ) ^ (1 + c) ≤ (G.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) →
          (Fintype.card V : ℝ) ^ (1 + c - ε) ≤
            max ((edgeSums a G).card : ℝ) ((edgeProducts a G).card : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos808.erdos_808.variants.ars_lower_bound
statements.doc:
Alon, Ruzsa, and Solymosi do prove, however, that if $A$ has size $n$ and $G$ has $m$ edges then
$$\max(\lvert A+_GA\rvert,\lvert A\cdot_G A\rvert) \gg m^{3/2}n^{-7/4}.$$

This is [ARS20, Theorem 10]. It holds for any $n$-element set of real numbers, and [ARS20]
state it for $\lvert A+_GA\rvert+\lvert A\cdot_GA\rvert$, which is within a factor $2$ of the
maximum. It is written in multiplied-out form, so that $n=0$ needs no division.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_808.variants.ars_lower_bound :
    ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧
      ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (a : V ↪ ℝ) (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
        (G.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) ^ ((3 : ℝ) / 2) ≤
          K * (Fintype.card V : ℝ) ^ ((7 : ℝ) / 4) *
            max ((edgeSums a G).card : ℝ) ((edgeProducts a G).card : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 810
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/810](https://www.erdosproblems.com/810)
- [BEGS89] Burr, S. A., Erdős, P., Graham, R. L., and Sós, V. T.,
  *Maximal anti-Ramsey graphs and the strong chromatic number*.
  J. Graph Theory 13 (1989), no. 3, 263–282.
- [Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (1991), 397–406.

statements.name: Erdos810.erdos_810
statements.doc:
Does there exist some $\epsilon>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, there exists a
graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with at least $\epsilon n^2$ edges whose edges can be coloured with $n$
colours so that every $C_4$ receives four distinct colours?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_810 : ∃ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
    ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), ∃ color : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n,
      ε * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ∧ C4RainbowColoring G color

problems.title: Erdős Problem 812
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/812](https://www.erdosproblems.com/812)
- [BEFS89] Burr, S. A. and Erd\H{o}s, P. and Faudree, R. J. and Schelp, R. H., On the difference
  between consecutive {R}amsey numbers. Utilitas Math. (1989), 115--118.

statements.name: Erdos812.erdos_812.parts.i
statements.doc: Is it true that $\frac{R(n+1)}{R(n)}\geq 1+c$ for some constant $c>0$, for all large $n$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_812.parts.i :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (R (n + 1) : ℝ) / (R n : ℝ) ≥ 1 + c

statements.name: Erdos812.erdos_812.parts.ii
statements.doc: Is it true that $R(n+1)-R(n) \gg n^2$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_812.parts.ii :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (R (n + 1) : ℝ) - (R n : ℝ)) ≫ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ 2)

statements.name: Erdos812.erdos_812.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc: Burr, Erdős, Faudree, and Schelp [BEFS89] proved that $R(n+1)-R(n) \geq 4n-8$ for all $n\geq 2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_812.variants.lower_bound :
    ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → (R (n + 1) : ℤ) - (R n : ℤ) ≥ 4 * (n : ℤ) - 8

problems.title: Erdős Problem 813
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/813](https://www.erdosproblems.com/813)
- [Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991),
  397-406.
- [BuSu23] Bucić, M. and Sudakov, B., *Large independent sets from local considerations*.
  Combinatorica 43 (2023), 505-546. [arXiv:2007.03667](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.03667)

statements.name: Erdos813.erdos_813
statements.doc:
Let $h(n)$ be minimal such that every graph on $n$ vertices where every set of $7$ vertices
contains a triangle must contain a clique on at least $h(n)$ vertices. Estimate $h(n)$. In
particular, do there exist constants $c_1, c_2 > 0$ such that
$$n^{1/3+c_1} \ll h(n) \ll n^{1/2-c_2}?$$

The lower half has a positive answer (`Erdos813.erdos_813.variants.lower`); the upper half is
`Erdos813.erdos_813.variants.upper`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_813 :
    ∃ c₁ > (0 : ℝ), ∃ c₂ > (0 : ℝ),
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 3 + c₁ : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n ↦ (h n : ℝ)) ∧
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (h n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 - c₂ : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos813.erdos_813.variants.erdos_hajnal
statements.doc:
Erdős and Hajnal proved (see [Er91]) that
$$n^{1/3} \ll h(n) \ll n^{1/2}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_813.variants.erdos_hajnal :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 3 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n ↦ (h n : ℝ)) ∧
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (h n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos813.erdos_813.variants.bucic_sudakov
statements.doc:
Bucić and Sudakov [BuSu23] proved that $h(n) \gg n^{5/12-o(1)}$. Their result is stated for
graphs in which every $7$ vertices contain an independent set of size $3$; it applies to $h$
by taking complements.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_813.variants.bucic_sudakov :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (n : ℝ) ^ (5 / 12 - ε : ℝ) ≤ (h n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos813.erdos_813.variants.lower
statements.doc:
The lower half of `Erdos813.erdos_813` has a positive answer: there is a constant $c_1 > 0$
with $n^{1/3+c_1} \ll h(n)$. This follows from the bound $h(n) \gg n^{5/12-o(1)}$ of Bucić and
Sudakov [BuSu23], since $5/12 > 1/3$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_813.variants.lower :
    ∃ c₁ > (0 : ℝ), (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 3 + c₁ : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n ↦ (h n : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos813.erdos_813.variants.upper
statements.doc:
The upper half of `Erdos813.erdos_813`: is there a constant $c_2 > 0$ with
$h(n) \ll n^{1/2-c_2}$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_813.variants.upper :
    ∃ c₂ > (0 : ℝ), (fun n : ℕ ↦ (h n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 - c₂ : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 814
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/814](https://www.erdosproblems.com/814)
- [EFRS90] Erdős, P. and Faudree, R. J. and Rousseau, C. C. and Schelp, R. H., _Subgraphs of
  minimal degree k_. Discrete Math. (1990), 53--58.
- [Er91] Erdős, P., _Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory_. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991),
  397-406.
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, _Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory_.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [MNS17] Mousset, Frank and Noever, Andreas and Škorić, Nemanja, _Smaller subgraphs of minimum
  degree k_. Electron. J. Combin. (2017), Paper No. 4.9, 8.
- [Sa19] Sauermann, Lisa, _A proof of a conjecture of Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp on
  subgraphs of minimum degree k_. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (2019), 36--75.

statements.name: Erdos814.erdos_814
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 2$ and $G$ be a graph with $n\geq k-1$ vertices and
$$(k-1)(n-k+2)+\binom{k-2}{2}+1$$
edges. Does there exist some $c_k>0$ such that $G$ must contain an induced subgraph on at most
$(1-c_k)n$ vertices with minimum degree at least $k$?

The case $k=3$ was a problem of Erdős and Hajnal [Er91]. The question for general $k$ was a
conjecture of Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau, and Schelp [EFRS90], who proved that such a subgraph
exists with at most $n-c_k\sqrt{n}$ vertices. Mousset, Noever, and Skorić [MNS17] improved
this to $n-c_k\frac{n}{\log n}$. The full conjecture was proved by Sauermann [Sa19], who proved
this with $c_k \gg 1/k^3$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_814 :
    ∀ k ≥ 2, ∃ c > 0, ∀ n ≥ k - 1, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      G.edgeFinset.card = (k - 1) * (n + 2 - k) + (k - 2).choose 2 + 1 →
        ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), S.Nonempty ∧ (S.card : ℝ) ≤ (1 - c) * n ∧
          k ≤ (G.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).minDegree

statements.name: Erdos814.erdos_814.variants.at_least
statements.doc:
The conclusion holds as soon as $G$ has at least $(k-1)(n-k+2)+ inom{k-2}{2}+1$ edges
(Sauermann [Sa19]).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_814.variants.at_least :
    ∀ k ≥ 2, ∃ c > 0, ∀ n ≥ k - 1, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (k - 1) * (n + 2 - k) + (k - 2).choose 2 + 1 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
        ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), S.Nonempty ∧ (S.card : ℝ) ≤ (1 - c) * n ∧
          k ≤ (G.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).minDegree

statements.name: Erdos814.erdos_814.variants.sauermann
statements.doc: Sauermann [Sa19] proved this with $c_k \gg 1/k^3$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_814.variants.sauermann :
    ∃ C > 0, ∀ k ≥ 2, ∀ n ≥ k - 1, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (k - 1) * (n + 2 - k) + (k - 2).choose 2 + 1 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
        ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), S.Nonempty ∧ (S.card : ℝ) ≤ (1 - C / k ^ 3) * n ∧
          k ≤ (G.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).minDegree

problems.title: Erdős Problem 816
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/816](https://www.erdosproblems.com/816)
- [Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991),
  397-406.
- [ChMa25] K. Chen and J. Ma, *A problem of Erdős and Hajnal on paths with equal-degree
  endpoints*. arXiv:2503.19569 (2025).

statements.name: Erdos816.erdos_816
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a graph with $2n+1$ vertices and $n^2+n+1$ edges. Must $G$ contain two vertices of the
same degree which are joined by a path of length $3$?

A problem of Erdős and Hajnal. The example of $K_{n,n+1}$ shows that this fails if we only have
$n^2+n$ edges.

This is true, and was proved by Chen and Ma [ChMa25], who prove the stronger statement that,
provided $n\geq 600$, all graphs with $2n+1$ vertices and at least $n^2+n$ edges contain two
vertices of the same degree joined by a path of length $3$, except $K_{n,n+1}$.

For $n = 1$ the graph is a triangle, which contains no path of length $3$, so we assume $n \geq 2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_816 : ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n + 1)),
    G.edgeFinset.card = n ^ 2 + n + 1 → HasEqualDegreePathThree G

statements.name: Erdos816.erdos_816.variants.chen_ma
statements.doc:
Chen and Ma [ChMa25] proved that, provided $n\geq 600$, all graphs with $2n+1$ vertices and at
least $n^2+n$ edges contain two vertices of the same degree joined by a path of length $3$, except
$K_{n,n+1}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_816.variants.chen_ma : ∀ n : ℕ, 600 ≤ n →
    ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n + 1)), n ^ 2 + n ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
      ¬ Nonempty (G ≃g completeBipartiteGraph (Fin n) (Fin (n + 1))) →
        HasEqualDegreePathThree G

statements.name: Erdos816.erdos_816.variants.complete_bipartite
statements.doc: The example of $K_{n,n+1}$ shows that this fails if we only have $n^2+n$ edges.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_816.variants.complete_bipartite : ∀ n : ℕ,
    (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin n) (Fin (n + 1))).edgeFinset.card = n ^ 2 + n ∧
      ¬ HasEqualDegreePathThree (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin n) (Fin (n + 1)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 817
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/817](https://www.erdosproblems.com/817)
- [Co26] Costa, S., *A negative answer to the Erdős–Sárközy question*.
  [arXiv:2609.06303](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06303) (2026).

statements.name: Erdos817.erdos_817
statements.doc:
Let $k \geq 3$. Define $g_k(n)$ to be the minimal $N$ such that
$\{1, ..., N\}$ contains some $A$ of size $|A| = n$ such that
$$
  \langle A\rangle = \left\{\sum_{a \in A} \epsilon_a a : \epsilon_a \in\{0, 1\}\right\}
$$
contains no non-trivial $k$-term arithmetic progression. Estimate $g_k(n)$. In
particular, is it true that
$$
  g_3(n) \gg 3^n
$$

The answer is no: Costa [Co26, Corollary 1.2] proved that $\liminf_{n \to \infty} g_3(n)/3^n = 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_817 :
    ¬ (fun n => (3 ^ n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n => (g 3 n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos817.erdos_817.variants.bdd_power
statements.doc:
A problem of Erdős and Sárközy who proved
$$
  g_3(n) \gg \frac{3^n}{n^{O(1)}}.
$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_817.variants.bdd_power : ∃ O > (0 : ℝ),
    (fun (n : ℕ) => (3 ^ n : ℝ) / n ^ O) =O[atTop] fun n => (g 3 n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 818
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/818](https://www.erdosproblems.com/818)
- [So09d] Solymosi, József, *Bounding multiplicative energy by the sumset*. Adv. Math. (2009),
  402-408.

statements.name: Erdos818.erdos_818
statements.doc:
Let $A$ be a finite set of integers such that $\lvert A+A\rvert \ll \lvert A\rvert$. Is it true that
$$\lvert AA\rvert \gg \frac{\lvert A\rvert^2}{(\log \lvert A\rvert)^C}$$
for some constant $C>0$?

This was proved by Solymosi [So09d], in the strong form
$$\lvert AA\rvert \gg \frac{\lvert A\rvert^2}{\log \lvert A\rvert}.$$
See also [52].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_818 :
    ∀ K : ℝ, 0 < K → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
      ∀ A : Finset ℤ, 2 ≤ A.card → ((A + A).card : ℝ) ≤ K * (A.card : ℝ) →
        c * (A.card : ℝ) ^ 2 / (Real.log (A.card : ℝ)) ^ C ≤ ((A * A).card : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos818.erdos_818.variants.solymosi
statements.doc:
This was proved by Solymosi [So09d], in the strong form
$$\lvert AA\rvert \gg \frac{\lvert A\rvert^2}{\log \lvert A\rvert}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_818.variants.solymosi :
    ∀ K : ℝ, 0 < K → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
      ∀ A : Finset ℤ, 2 ≤ A.card → ((A + A).card : ℝ) ≤ K * (A.card : ℝ) →
        c * (A.card : ℝ) ^ 2 / Real.log (A.card : ℝ) ≤ ((A * A).card : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 819
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/819](https://www.erdosproblems.com/819)
- [Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991),
  397-406.
- [ErFr91] Erdős, P. and Freud, R., *On sums of a Sidon-sequence*. J. Number Theory 38 (1991),
  196-205.

statements.name: Erdos819.erdos_819
statements.doc:
Let $f(N)$ be maximal such that there exists $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$\lvert A\rvert=\lfloor N^{1/2}\rfloor$ such that $\lvert (A+A)\cap [1,N]\rvert=f(N)$.
Estimate $f(N)$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_819 : (fun N ↦ (f N : ℝ)) ~[atTop] erdos_819.answer

statements.name: Erdos819.erdos_819.variants.erdos_freud_lower
statements.doc:
Erdős and Freud [ErFr91] proved
$$\left(\frac{3}{8}-o(1)\right)N \leq f(N) \leq \left(\frac{1}{2}+o(1)\right)N.$$

This is the lower bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_819.variants.erdos_freud_lower :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (3 / 8 - ε) * N ≤ (f N : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos819.erdos_819.variants.erdos_freud_upper
statements.doc:
Erdős and Freud [ErFr91] proved
$$\left(\frac{3}{8}-o(1)\right)N \leq f(N) \leq \left(\frac{1}{2}+o(1)\right)N.$$

This is the upper bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_819.variants.erdos_freud_upper :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (f N : ℝ) ≤ (1 / 2 + ε) * N

problems.title: Erdős Problem 820
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/820](https://www.erdosproblems.com/820)
- [Er74b] Erdős, P., *Remarks on some problems in number theory*. Math. Balkanica (1974),
  197-202.
- [OEIS A263647](https://oeis.org/A263647): the $n$ with $(2^n-1, 3^n-1) = 1$.

statements.name: Erdos820.erdos_820
statements.doc:
Let $H(n)$ be the smallest integer $l$ such that there exists $k < l$ with $(k^n-1, l^n-1) = 1$.
Is it true that $H(n) = 3$ infinitely often? That is, is $(2^n-1, 3^n-1) = 1$ for infinitely
many $n$ (see `Erdos820.H_eq_three_iff`)?

The request to estimate $H(n)$ is open-ended and not formalised; the variants below state the
specific questions that are asked. See also Erdős Problem 770.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_820 : {n : ℕ | H n = 3}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos820.erdos_820.variants.log_log_exponent
statements.doc:
Is it true that there exists some constant $c > 0$ such that, for all $\epsilon > 0$,
$$
H(n) > \exp\left(n^{(c-\epsilon)/\log\log n}\right)
$$
for infinitely many $n$ and
$$
H(n) < \exp\left(n^{(c+\epsilon)/\log\log n}\right)
$$
for all large enough $n$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_820.variants.log_log_exponent :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ),
      (∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
        Real.exp ((n : ℝ) ^ ((c - ε) / Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)))) < (H n : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
        (H n : ℝ) < Real.exp ((n : ℝ) ^ ((c + ε) / Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ))))

statements.name: Erdos820.erdos_820.variants.two_pow_upper
statements.doc:
Let $K(n)$ be the smallest $k$ such that $(k^n-1, 2^n-1) = 1$. Does a similar upper bound hold
for $K(n)$? That is, is there a constant $c > 0$ such that, for all $\epsilon > 0$,
$$
K(n) < \exp\left(n^{(c+\epsilon)/\log\log n}\right)
$$
for all large enough $n$?

We read "similar" as an upper bound of the same shape, with its own constant $c$, which need
not be the same as in `Erdos820.erdos_820.variants.log_log_exponent`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_820.variants.two_pow_upper :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (K n : ℝ) < Real.exp ((n : ℝ) ^ ((c + ε) / Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ))))

statements.name: Erdos820.erdos_820.variants.erdos_lower
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er74b] proved that there exists a constant $c > 0$ such that
$$
H(n) > \exp\left(n^{c/(\log\log n)^2}\right)
$$
for infinitely many $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_820.variants.erdos_lower :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      Real.exp ((n : ℝ) ^ (c / Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)) ^ 2)) < (H n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 821
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/821](https://www.erdosproblems.com/821)
- [BaHa98] Baker, R. C. and Harman, G., Shifted primes without large prime factors. Acta Arith.
  (1998), 331--361.
- [Er35b] Erdős, P., On the normal number of prime factors of $p-1$ and some related problems
  concerning Euler's $\varphi$-function. Quart. J. Math. (1935), 205-213.
- [Er74b] Erdős, P., Remarks on some problems in number theory. Math. Balkanica (1974), 197-202.
- [Li22] J. D. Lichtman, Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli and shifted primes
  without large prime factors. arXiv:2211.09641 (2022).
- [LuPo11] Luca, Florian and Pollack, Paul, An arithmetic function arising from {C}armichael's
  conjecture. J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux (2011), 697--714.
- [OpenAI26] OpenAI, *Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers*.
  OpenAI Math Release preprint (September 2026).
  [github.com/openai/math](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/Weighted-Dilation-Graphs-Smooth-Shifted-Primes-and-Totient-Fibers-September-24-2026/paper.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos821.erdos_821
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for every $\epsilon>0$, there exist infinitely many $n$ such that
$g(n) > n^{1-\epsilon}$?

This was proved in [OpenAI26]; see the linked formal proof for more explanations.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_821 :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), { n : ℕ | (g n : ℝ) > (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε) }.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos821.erdos_821.variants.pillai
statements.doc: Pillai proved that $\limsup g(n)=\infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_821.variants.pillai :
    atTop.limsup (fun n : ℕ ↦ (g n : EReal)) = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos821.erdos_821.variants.erdos
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er35b] proved that there exists some constant $c>0$ such that $g(n) > n^c$ for infinitely
many $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_821.variants.erdos :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), { n : ℕ | (n : ℝ) ^ c < (g n : ℝ) }.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos821.erdos_821.variants.lichtman
statements.doc:
The best known bound is that there are infinitely many $n$ such that $g(n) > n^{0.71568\cdots}$,
obtained by Lichtman [Li22] as a consequence of proving that there are
$\geq \frac{x}{(\log x)^{O(1)}}$ many primes $p\leq x$ such that all prime factors of $p-1$ are
$\leq x^{0.2843\cdots}$ (which improves a number of previous exponents, most recently Baker and
Harman [BaHa98]).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_821.variants.lichtman :
    ∃ c > (0.71568 : ℝ), { n : ℕ | (n : ℝ) ^ c < (g n : ℝ) }.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 822
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/822](https://www.erdosproblems.com/822)
- [GIL24] Gabdullin, Mikhail R. and Iudelevich, Vitalii V. and Luca,
  Florian, Numbers of the form {$k+f(k)$}. J. Number Theory (2024), 58--85.

statements.name: Erdos822.erdos_822
statements.doc:
Does the set of integers of the form $n + \varphi(n)$ have positive (lower) density?

[GIL24] proved this was true.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_822 :
    0 < (Set.range fun n => n + Nat.totient n).lowerDensity

problems.title: Erdős Problem 823
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/823](https://www.erdosproblems.com/823)
- [Er59c] Erdős, P., *Remarks on number theory. II. Some problems on the $\sigma$ function*.
  Acta Arith. (1959), 171--177.
- [Er74b] Erdős, P., *Remarks on some problems in number theory*. Math. Balkanica (1974),
  197-202.
- [Po15b] Pollack, Paul, *Remarks on fibers of the sum-of-divisors function*. Analytic number
  theory, Springer, Cham (2015), 305-320.

statements.name: Erdos823.erdos_823
statements.doc:
Let $\alpha\geq 1$. Is there a sequence of integers $n_k,m_k$ such that $n_k/m_k\to \alpha$ and
$\sigma(n_k)=\sigma(m_k)$ for all $k\geq 1$, where $\sigma$ is the sum of divisors function?

The answer is yes, proved by Pollack [Po15b].

We take $n_k$ and $m_k$ to be positive integers.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_823 : ∀ α : ℝ, 1 ≤ α →
    ∃ n m : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ k, 0 < n k) ∧ (∀ k, 0 < m k) ∧ (∀ k, σ 1 (n k) = σ 1 (m k)) ∧
      Tendsto (fun k ↦ (n k : ℝ) / m k) atTop (𝓝 α)

statements.name: Erdos823.erdos_823.variants.totient
statements.doc:
For every $\alpha\geq 1$ there are sequences of integers $n_k,m_k$ such that $n_k/m_k\to \alpha$
and $\phi(n_k)=\phi(m_k)$ for all $k\geq 1$. Erdős [Er74b] writes it is 'easy to prove the
analogous result for $\phi(n)$'.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_823.variants.totient : ∀ α : ℝ, 1 ≤ α →
    ∃ n m : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ k, 0 < n k) ∧ (∀ k, 0 < m k) ∧ (∀ k, φ (n k) = φ (m k)) ∧
      Tendsto (fun k ↦ (n k : ℝ) / m k) atTop (𝓝 α)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 824
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/824](https://www.erdosproblems.com/824)
- [Er59c] Erdős, P., *Remarks on number theory. II. Some problems on the $\sigma$ function*.
  Acta Arith. (1959), 171--177.
- [Er74b] Erdős, P., *Remarks on some problems in number theory*. Math. Balkanica (1974),
  197-202.
- [PoPo16] Pollack, Paul and Pomerance, Carl, *Some problems of Erdős on the sum-of-divisors
  function*. Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B (2016), 1-26.
- [LiZh26] Li, Shisheng and Zhuang, Zhong, *Coprime pairs with equal sum of divisors, assuming
  smooth shifted primes*. Preprint (October 2026).
  [github.com/daizisheng/erdos-824](https://github.com/daizisheng/erdos-824/blob/b4b7099bb8ab9c1c7fc61dae18a73cdbe503fe5a/paper/erdos824.pdf)
- [OpenAI26] OpenAI, *Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers*.
  OpenAI Math Release preprint (September 2026).
  [github.com/openai/math](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/Weighted-Dilation-Graphs-Smooth-Shifted-Primes-and-Totient-Fibers-September-24-2026/paper.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos824.erdos_824
statements.doc:
Let $h(x)$ count the number of integers $1\leq a<b<x$ such that $(a,b)=1$ and
$\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)$, where $\sigma$ is the sum of divisors function. Is it true that
$h(x)>x^{2-o(1)}$?

That is, is it true that for every $\epsilon > 0$ we have $h(x) > x^{2-\epsilon}$ for all large
$x$? According to erdosproblems.com, Erdős [Er74b] proved that $\limsup h(x)/x = \infty$ and
claimed a similar proof for this problem.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_824 :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (x : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε) < (h x : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos824.erdos_824.variants.pollack_pomerance
statements.doc:
Pollack and Pomerance [PoPo16, Section 6] proved that $h(x)/x \to \infty$, answering a question
of Erdős [Er59c].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_824.variants.pollack_pomerance :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦ (h x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos824.erdos_824.variants.squarefree
statements.doc:
A similar question can be asked if the condition $(a,b)=1$ is replaced by the condition that $a$
and $b$ are squarefree. Let $h'(x)$ count the number of squarefree integers $1\leq a<b<x$ with
$\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)$. Is it true that $h'(x)>x^{2-o(1)}$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_824.variants.squarefree :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (x : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε) < (hSquarefree x : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 825
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/825](https://www.erdosproblems.com/825)

statements.name: Erdos825.erdos_825
statements.doc:
Is there an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that every integer $n$ with
$\sigma(n) > Cn$ is the distinct sum of proper divisors of $n$?

This has been solved in the affirmative by Larsen - in fact, for any $\epsilon>0$ there exists $L$
such that if $n$ has only prime divisors $>L$ and $\sigma(n)>(2+\epsilon)n$ then $n$ is the distinct
sum of proper divisors of $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_825 :
    ∃ (C : ℝ) (_ : C > 0),
      ∀ (n) (_ : σ 1 n > C * n),
        ∃ s ⊆ n.properDivisors, n = s.sum id

statements.name: Erdos825.erdos_825.variants.necessary_cond
statements.doc:
Show that if the constant $C > 0$ is such that every integer $n$ with
$\sigma(n) > Cn$ is the distinct sum of proper divisors of $n$, then we
must have $C > 2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_825.variants.necessary_cond (C : ℝ) (_hC : 0 < C)
    (h : ∀ (n : ℕ) (_ : σ 1 n > C * n),
        ∃ s ⊆ n.properDivisors, n = s.sum id) :
    2 < C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 826
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/826](https://www.erdosproblems.com/826)

statements.name: Erdos826.erdos_826
statements.doc:
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that, for all $k\geq 1$
$$
  \tau(n + k) \ll k?
$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_826 :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), { n | ∀ k ≥ 1, σ 0 (n + k) ≤ C * k }.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 827
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/827](https://www.erdosproblems.com/827)
- [Er75h] Erdős, P., *Some problems on elementary geometry*. Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. 2 (1975),
  2-3.
- [Er78c] Erdős, P., *Some more problems on elementary geometry*. Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. 5
  (1978), 52-54.
- [MaRo15] Martínez, L. and Roldán-Pensado, E., *Points defining triangles with distinct
  circumradii*. Acta Math. Hungar. 145 (2015), 136-141.
  [arXiv:1402.6276](https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.6276)

statements.name: Erdos827.erdos_827
statements.doc:
Let $n_k$ be minimal such that if $n_k$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ are in general position then
there exists a subset of $k$ points such that all $\binom{k}{3}$ triples determine circles of
different radii.

Determine $n_k$.

General position means that no three points are collinear and no four are concyclic, as in
[Er75h] (quoted in [MaRo15]).
statements.statement: theorem erdos_827 : n = erdos_827.answer

statements.name: Erdos827.erdos_827.variants.martinez_roldan_pensado
statements.doc:
In [Er78c] Erdős gave an argument for $n_k \leq k+2\binom{k-1}{2}\binom{k-1}{3}$, but this
argument is incorrect, as explained by Martínez and Roldán-Pensado [MaRo15], who give a corrected
argument that proves $n_k\ll k^9$.

[MaRo15, Theorem 1.1] assumes only that no four points lie on a line or a circle. That class
contains the sets in general position, so the bound holds for $n_k$ as defined here.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_827.variants.martinez_roldan_pensado :
    (fun k : ℕ ↦ (n k : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun k : ℕ ↦ (k : ℝ) ^ 9

statements.name: Erdos827.erdos_827.variants.n_four_le
statements.doc: Martínez and Roldán-Pensado [MaRo15, Theorem 1.2] show that $n_4 \leq 9$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_827.variants.n_four_le : n 4 ≤ 9

statements.name: Erdos827.erdos_827.variants.n_five_le
statements.doc: Martínez and Roldán-Pensado [MaRo15, Theorem 1.2] show that $n_5 \leq 37$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_827.variants.n_five_le : n 5 ≤ 37

problems.title: Erdős Problem 828
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/828](https://www.erdosproblems.com/828)

statements.name: Erdos828.erdos_828
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for any $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that
$$\phi(n) | n + a$$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_828 : ∀ a : ℤ, Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | ↑(φ n) ∣ n + a}

statements.name: Erdos828.erdos_828.variants.lehmer_conjecture
statements.doc: When $n > 1$, Lehmer conjectured that $\phi(n) | n - 1$ if and only if $n$ is prime.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_828.variants.lehmer_conjecture : ∀ n > 1, φ n ∣ n - 1 ↔ Prime n

statements.name: Erdos828.erdos_828.variants.phi_dvd_self_iff_pow2_pow3
statements.doc:
It is an easy exercise to show that $\phi(n) | n$ if and only if $n = 0, 1$ or $n = 2^a 3^b$ for
some $a > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_828.variants.phi_dvd_self_iff_pow2_pow3 {n : ℕ} :
    φ n ∣ n ↔ n ≤ 1 ∨ ∃ᵉ (a > 0) (b), n = 2 ^ a * 3 ^ b

problems.title: Erdős Problem 829
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
- [Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the
  work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.

statements.name: Erdos829.erdos_829
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 829 (open).**  Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be the set of perfect cubes.  Is
it true that $(1_A \ast 1_A)(n) \ll (\log n)^{O(1)}$?  That is, does there exist a natural
number $C$ such that the number of representations of $n$ as a sum of two cubes is
$O((\log n)^C)$ as $n \to \infty$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_829 :
    ∃ C : ℕ, (fun n : ℕ => (sumRep cubes n : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun n : ℕ => (Real.log n) ^ C)

statements.name: Erdos829.variants.mordell
statements.doc:
Mordell proved $\limsup_{n \to \infty} (1_A \ast 1_A)(n) = \infty$, where $A$ is the set of
perfect cubes.  Equivalently, the number of representations of $n$ as a sum of two cubes is
unbounded.
statements.statement: theorem mordell : limsup (fun n : ℕ => (sumRep cubes n : ℕ∞)) atTop = (⊤ : ℕ∞)

statements.name: Erdos829.variants.mahler
statements.doc:
Mahler proved $(1_A \ast 1_A)(n) \gg (\log n)^{1/4}$ for infinitely many $n$, where $A$ is
the set of perfect cubes.

[Ma35b] Mahler, K., _On the lattice points on curves of genus 1_. Proc. London Math. Soc.
  (2) (1935), 431-466.
statements.statement:
theorem mahler : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ),
    ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, C * (Real.log n) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 4) ≤ (sumRep cubes n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos829.variants.stewart
statements.doc:
Stewart improved Mahler's lower bound to $(1_A \ast 1_A)(n) \gg (\log n)^{11/13}$ for
infinitely many $n$, where $A$ is the set of perfect cubes.

[St08] Stewart, C. L., _Cubic Thue equations with many solutions_. Int. Math. Res. Not.
  IMRN (2008), Art. ID rnn040, 11.
statements.statement:
theorem stewart : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ),
    ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, C * (Real.log n) ^ ((11 : ℝ) / 13) ≤ (sumRep cubes n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 830
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/830](https://www.erdosproblems.com/830)
- [Er55b] Erdős, P., *On amicable numbers*. Publ. Math. Debrecen (1955), 108-111.
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.
- [Po15] Pomerance, Carl, *On amicable numbers*. (2015), 321-327.
- [Po81] Pomerance, Carl, *On the distribution of amicable numbers. II*. J. Reine Angew. Math.
  (1981), 183-188.

statements.name: Erdos830.erdos_830.parts.i
statements.doc:
**Erdos Problem 830, Part 1**
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$. Are there
infinitely many amicable pairs?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_830.parts.i : {(a, b) | IsAmicable a b}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos830.erdos_830.parts.ii
statements.doc:
**Erdos Problem 830, Part 2**
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then is it true that
$$A(x) > x^{1-o(1)}?$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_830.parts.ii : ∃ o : ℝ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ᶠ x in atTop,
    x ^ (1 - o x) < A x

statements.name: Erdos830.erdos_830.variants.erdos
statements.doc:
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then one can show that $A(x) = o(x)$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_830.variants.erdos : A =o[atTop] id

statements.name: Erdos830.erdos_830.variants.pomerance
statements.doc:
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then one can show that
$A(x) \leq x \exp(-(\log x)^{1/3})$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_830.variants.pomerance : ∀ᶠ x in atTop, A x ≤ x * rexp (- Real.nthRoot 3 x.log)

statements.name: Erdos830.erdos_830.variants.pomerance_stronger
statements.doc:
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then one can show that
$A(x) \leq x \exp(-(\tfrac{1}{2}+o(1))(\log x\log\log\log x)^{1/2})$.
(erdosproblems.com has $\log\log x$; [Po15, Theorem 1.1] has $\log\log\log x$.)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_830.variants.pomerance_stronger :
    ∃ o : ℝ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ x in atTop, A x ≤ x * rexp (- (1/ 2 + o x) * √(x.log * x.log.log.log))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 831
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/831](https://www.erdosproblems.com/831)
- [Er75h] Erdős, P., *Some problems on elementary geometry*. Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. (1975), 2-3.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-41.pdf)
- [Er92e] Erdős, Pál, *Some Unsolved problems in Geometry, Number Theory and Combinatorics*. Eureka
  (1992), 44-48.

statements.name: Erdos831.erdos_831
statements.doc:
Let $h(n)$ be maximal such that in any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ (with no three on a line and
no four on a circle) there are at least $h(n)$ many circles of different radii passing through
three points. Estimate $h(n)$.

Erdős asks this in [Er75h, pp. 2-3] (see also [Er92e]); see also Problems 104 and 506. We read
"estimate" as the order of magnitude `=Θ`. [Er75h] also asks how $h(n)$ changes if one only
assumes that the points are not all on a circle; this is not formalised.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_831 :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (h n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_831.answer

statements.name: Erdos831.erdos_831.variants.szekeres
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er75h, p. 2] attributes to E. Szekeres the observation that for three points
$x_1,x_2,x_3$ of the plane, not on a line, there is a unique point $x_4$ such that
$x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4$ are not on a circle and the four circles determined by the four triples of these
points have the same radius; one can take $x_4$ to be the orthocentre of the triangle
$x_1x_2x_3$.

Read literally this fails for a right-angled triangle, whose orthocentre is a vertex, so we assume
that the triangle has no right angle. We also require the four points to be in general position,
so that the four circles exist.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_831.variants.szekeres (x₁ x₂ x₃ : ℝ²)
    (hcol : ¬ Collinear ℝ ({x₁, x₂, x₃} : Set ℝ²)) (hright : ¬ IsRightAngled x₁ x₂ x₃) :
    ∃! x₄ : ℝ², x₄ ∉ ({x₁, x₂, x₃} : Set ℝ²) ∧
      InGeneralPosition ({x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄} : Set ℝ²) ∧
      (circleRadii ({x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄} : Set ℝ²)).ncard = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 832
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/832](https://www.erdosproblems.com/832)
- [AkSh16] Akolzin, Ilia and Shabanov, Dmitry, Colorings of hypergraphs with large number of colors.
  Discrete Math. (2016), 3020--3031.
- [Al85] Alon, Noga, Hypergraphs with high chromatic number. Graphs Combin. (1985), 387--389.
- [ChPe20] Cherkashin, Danila and Petrov, Fedor, Regular behavior of the maximal hypergraph
  chromatic number. SIAM J. Discrete Math. (2020), 1326--1333.

statements.name: Erdos832.erdos_832
statements.doc:
Let $r\geq 3$ and $k$ be sufficiently large in terms of $r$. Is it true that every $r$-uniform
hypergraph with chromatic number $k$ has at least
$$\binom{(r-1)(k-1)+1}{r}$$
edges, with equality only for the complete graph on $(r-1)(k-1)+1$ vertices?

This was disproved by Alon [Al85]. The validity of this conjecture for $r=3$ remains open.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_832 :
    ¬ ∀ r : ℕ, 3 ≤ r → ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
      H.IsUniform r → H.HasHypergraphChromaticNumber k →
      ((r - 1) * (k - 1) + 1).choose r ≤ H.card ∧
      (H.card = ((r - 1) * (k - 1) + 1).choose r →
        ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), S.card = (r - 1) * (k - 1) + 1 ∧ H = S.powersetCard r)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 833
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/833](https://www.erdosproblems.com/833)
- [ErLo75] Erdős, P. and Lovász, L., Problems and results on {$3$}-chromatic hypergraphs and some
  related questions. (1975), 609--627.

statements.name: Erdos833.erdos_833
statements.doc:
Does there exist an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, for all $r\geq 2$, in any $r$-uniform
hypergraph with chromatic number $3$ there is a vertex contained in at least $(1+c)^r$ many edges?

This was solved by Erdős and Lovász [ErLo75], who proved in particular that there is a vertex
contained in at least $\frac{2^{r-1}}{4r}$ many edges.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_833 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, 2 ≤ r →
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
      H.IsUniform r → H.HasHypergraphChromaticNumber 3 →
        ∃ v : Fin n, (1 + c) ^ r ≤ (H.hypergraphDegree v : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 834
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/834](https://www.erdosproblems.com/834)
- [Li25] R. Li, On an Erdős-Lovász problem: $3$-critical $3$-graphs of minimum degree $7$.
  arXiv:2512.24850 (2025).

statements.name: Erdos834.erdos_834.parts.i
statements.doc:
Does there exist a $3$-critical $3$-uniform hypergraph in which every vertex has degree
$\geq 7$, where criticality means that the transversal number is $3$ and deleting any edge
reduces it to $2$?

In the first formulation, the transversal notion of criticality, Li [Li25] proves that a
$3$-critical $3$-uniform hypergraph must have a vertex of degree $\leq 6$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_834.parts.i :
    ¬ ∃ (n : ℕ) (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
    H.IsUniform 3 ∧ (H : Set (Finset (Fin n))).HasFiniteTransversal 3 ∧
      ¬ (H : Set (Finset (Fin n))).HasFiniteTransversal 2 ∧
      (∀ e ∈ H, (H.erase e : Set (Finset (Fin n))).HasFiniteTransversal 2) ∧
      ∀ v : Fin n, 7 ≤ H.hypergraphDegree v

statements.name: Erdos834.erdos_834.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Does there exist a $3$-critical $3$-uniform hypergraph with minimum degree at least $7$,
where criticality means that deleting any edge or vertex reduces chromatic number $3$ to $2$?

In the second formulation, the chromatic notion of criticality, Li [Li25] provides an
explicit $3$-critical $3$-uniform hypergraph on $9$ vertices with minimum degree $7$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_834.parts.ii :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
    H.IsUniform 3 ∧ H.HasHypergraphChromaticNumber 3 ∧
      (∀ e ∈ H, (H.erase e).HypergraphColorable 2) ∧
      (∀ v : Fin n, (H.filter (fun e ↦ v ∉ e)).HypergraphColorable 2) ∧
      ∀ v : Fin n, 7 ≤ H.hypergraphDegree v

problems.title: Erdős Problem 835
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)
 - [MT25](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-835/blob/main/On_Problem_835.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos835.erdos_835
statements.doc:
Does there exist a $k>2$ such that the $k$-sized subsets of {1,...,2k} can be coloured with
$k+1$ colours such that for every $A\subset \{1,\ldots,2k\}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=k+1$ all $k+1$
colours appear among the $k$-sized subsets of $A$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_835 : ∃ k > 2, Property k

statements.name: Erdos835.erdos_835.variants.johnson
statements.doc:
Alternative statement of Erdős Problem 835 using the chromatic number of the Johnson graph.
This is equivalent to asking whether there exists $k > 2$ such that the chromatic number of the
Johnson graph $J(2k, k)$ is $k+1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_835.variants.johnson : ∃ l,
    -- making sure k > 2
    letI k := l + 3
    J(2 * k, k).chromaticNumber = k + 1

statements.name: Erdos835.johnsonGraph_2k_k_chromaticNumber_known_cases
statements.doc:
It is known that for $3 \leq k \leq 8$, the chromatic number of $J(2k, k)$ is greater than $k+1$,
see [Johnson graphs](https://aeb.win.tue.nl/graphs/Johnson.html).
statements.statement:
theorem johnsonGraph_2k_k_chromaticNumber_known_cases (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (hk' : k ≤ 8) :
    J(2 * k, k).chromaticNumber > k + 1

statements.name: Erdos835.johnsonGraph_18_9_chromaticNumber
statements.doc:
The smallest case not on this page is $k=9$:
But that one can be solved as well:
The chromatic number of $J(18, 9)$ is at least $11$.
statements.statement: theorem johnsonGraph_18_9_chromaticNumber : J(18, 9).chromaticNumber > 9 + 1

statements.name: Erdos835.indepNum_johnson_le_johnsonBound
statements.doc: Johnson's bound for the independence number of the Johnson graph.
statements.statement: lemma indepNum_johnson_le_johnsonBound : α(J(n, k)) ≤ johnsonBound n 4 k

statements.name: Erdos835.div_johnsonBound_le_chromaticNum_johnson
statements.doc: Johnson's bound for the chromatic number of the Johnson graph.
statements.statement:
lemma div_johnsonBound_le_chromaticNum_johnson :
    ⌈(n.choose k / johnsonBound n 4 k : ℚ≥0)⌉₊ ≤ χ(J(n, k))

statements.name: Erdos835.chromaticNumber_johnson_2k_k_lower_bound
statements.doc:
It is known that for $3 \leq k \leq 8$, the chromatic number of $J(2k, k)$ is greater than
$k+1$, see [Johnson graphs](https://aeb.win.tue.nl/graphs/Johnson.html).
statements.statement:
theorem chromaticNumber_johnson_2k_k_lower_bound (hk : 3 ≤ k) (hk' : k ≤ 8) :
    k + 1 < J(2 * k, k).chromaticNumber

statements.name: Erdos835.chromaticNumber_johnson_2k_k_lower_bound_odd
statements.doc:
It is also known that for $3 \leq k \leq 203$ odd, the chromatic number of $J(2k, k)$ is
greater than $k+1$, see [Johnson graphs](https://aeb.win.tue.nl/graphs/Johnson.html).
statements.statement:
theorem chromaticNumber_johnson_2k_k_lower_bound_odd (hk : 3 ≤ k) (hk' : k ≤ 300) (hk_odd : Odd k) :
    k + 1 < J(2 * k, k).chromaticNumber

statements.name: Erdos835.johnson_chromaticNumber_odd
statements.doc: It can be seen that the chromatic number of $J(2k,k)$ is $>k+1$ for all odd $k>2$.
statements.statement:
theorem johnson_chromaticNumber_odd (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 < k) (h : Odd k) :
    k + 1 < J(2 * k, k).chromaticNumber

statements.name: Erdos835.johnson_chromaticNumber_composite
statements.doc:
Ma and Tang have proved that the chromatic number of $J(2k,k)$ is $>k+1$ for all $k>2$ not of the
form $p-1$ for prime $p$.
statements.statement:
theorem johnson_chromaticNumber_composite (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 < k) (h : (k + 1).Composite) :
    k + 1 < J(2 * k, k).chromaticNumber

statements.name: Erdos835.johnson_chromaticNumber
statements.doc: Is the chromatic number of `J(2 * k, k)` always at least `k + 2`?
statements.statement:
theorem johnson_chromaticNumber :
    ∀ k ≥ 3, k + 2 ≤ J(2 * k, k).chromaticNumber

problems.title: Erdős Problem 836
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/836](https://www.erdosproblems.com/836)
- [ErLo75] Erdős, P. and Lovász, L., Problems and results on {$3$}-chromatic hypergraphs and some
  related questions. (1975), 609--627.
- [Pr26] Price, L., *A Linear Intersection Bound*. (2026).

statements.name: Erdos836.erdos_836.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $r\geq 2$ and let $G$ be an intersecting $r$-uniform hypergraph with chromatic number
$3$. Must $G$ contain $O(r^2)$ many vertices? Vertices are counted in the union of the edges,
so isolated vertices are excluded.

Alon has provided a counterexample to the first question: this hypergraph is intersecting,
its chromatic number is $3$, and it has $\asymp 4^r/\sqrt{r}$ many vertices.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_836.parts.i :
    ¬ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, 2 ≤ r →
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
      H.IsUniform r → H.HasHypergraphChromaticNumber 3 → (H : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Intersecting →
        ((H.biUnion id).card : ℝ) ≤ C * (r : ℝ) ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos836.erdos_836.parts.ii
statements.doc:
In an intersecting $r$-uniform hypergraph with chromatic number $3$, must there be two
distinct edges which meet in $\gg r$ many vertices?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_836.parts.ii :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, 2 ≤ r →
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
      H.IsUniform r → H.HasHypergraphChromaticNumber 3 → (H : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Intersecting →
        ∃ e ∈ H, ∃ f ∈ H, e ≠ f ∧ c * r ≤ ((e ∩ f).card : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 837
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/837](https://www.erdosproblems.com/837)

statements.name: Erdos837.erdos_837
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 2$ and $A_k\subseteq [0,1]$ be the set of $\alpha$ such that there exists some
$\beta(\alpha)>\alpha$ with the property that, if $G_1,G_2,\ldots$ is a sequence of $k$-uniform
hypergraphs with
$$\liminf \frac{e(G_n)}{\binom{\lvert G_n\rvert}{k}} >\alpha$$
then there exist subgraphs $H_n\subseteq G_n$ such that $\lvert H_n\rvert \to \infty$ and
$$\liminf \frac{e(H_n)}{\binom{\lvert H_n\rvert}{k}} >\beta,$$
and further that this property does not necessarily hold if $>\alpha$ is replaced by $\geq \alpha$.
What is $A_3$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_837 :
    {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Icc 0 1 ∧ ∃ β : ℝ, α < β ∧
    Hypergraph.HasDensityJump 3 α β true ∧ ¬ Hypergraph.HasDensityJump 3 α β false}
      = erdos_837.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 838
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/838](https://www.erdosproblems.com/838)
- [Er78c] Erdős, P., *Some more problems on elementary geometry*. Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. 5
  (1978), 52-54. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1978-44.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos838.erdos_838.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, with no three on a line,
determine at least $f(n)$ different convex subsets. Estimate $f(n)$ - in particular, does there
exist a constant $c$ such that
$$\lim \frac{\log f(n)}{(\log n)^2}=c?$$

A question of Erdős and Hammer [Er78c, pp. 52-53]. This is the first part. We read "estimate" as
asking for an asymptotic formula for $\log f(n)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_838.parts.i :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (f n)) ~[atTop] erdos_838.parts.i.answer

statements.name: Erdos838.erdos_838.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, with no three on a line,
determine at least $f(n)$ different convex subsets. Estimate $f(n)$ - in particular, does there
exist a constant $c$ such that
$$\lim \frac{\log f(n)}{(\log n)^2}=c?$$

A question of Erdős and Hammer [Er78c, p. 53]. This is the second part.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_838.parts.ii :
    ∃ c : ℝ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (f n) / Real.log n ^ 2) atTop (nhds c)

statements.name: Erdos838.erdos_838.variants.erdos_bounds
statements.doc:
Erdős proved in [Er78c] that there exist constants $c_1,c_2>0$ such that
$$n^{c_1\log n}<f(n)< n^{c_2\log n}.$$
Here $\log$ is the natural logarithm (another base only changes the constants), and $n\geq 2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_838.variants.erdos_bounds :
    ∃ c₁ c₂ : ℝ, 0 < c₁ ∧ 0 < c₂ ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n →
      (n : ℝ) ^ (c₁ * Real.log n) < f n ∧ (f n : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) ^ (c₂ * Real.log n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 839
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/839](https://www.erdosproblems.com/839)
- [Er78f] Erdős, P., *Problems in number theory and combinatorics*, Proc. Sixth Manitoba Conf. on
  Numerical Math. (1978), 35-58.
- [Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1992).

See also [Erdős Problem 359](https://www.erdosproblems.com/359) and
[Erdős Problem 867](https://www.erdosproblems.com/867).

statements.name: Erdos839.erdos_839.parts.i
statements.doc:
Erdős Problem 839 (Part 1) [Er78f][Er92c]:

Let $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
such that no $a_i$ is the sum of consecutive $a_j$ for $j < i$.
Is it true that $\limsup a_n / n = \infty$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_839.parts.i :
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 1 ≤ a n) → StrictMono a → SumOfConsecutiveFree a →
    atTop.limsup (fun n : ℕ => (a n : ℝ≥0∞) / n) = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos839.erdos_839.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Erdős Problem 839 (Part 2, stronger) [Er78f][Er92c]:

Let $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
such that no $a_i$ is the sum of consecutive $a_j$ for $j < i$.
Is it true that $\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac{1}{\log x} \sum_{a_n < x} \frac{1}{a_n} = 0$?

This is equivalent to asking whether the range $\{a_1,a_2,\ldots\}$ has logarithmic density zero
(see `Set.HasLogDensity`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_839.parts.ii :
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 1 ≤ a n) → StrictMono a → SumOfConsecutiveFree a →
    Set.HasLogDensity (Set.range a) 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 840
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/840](https://www.erdosproblems.com/840)
- [Er81h] Erdős, P., *Some problems and results on additive and multiplicative number theory*.
  Analytic number theory (Philadelphia, Pa., 1980), Lecture Notes in Math. 899 (1981), 171-182.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-33.pdf)
- [ErFr91] Erdős, P. and Freud, R., *On sums of a Sidon-sequence*. J. Number Theory 38 (1991),
  196-205.
- [Pi06] Pikhurko, O., *Dense edge-magic graphs and thin additive bases*. Discrete Math. 306
  (2006), 2097-2107.

statements.name: Erdos840.erdos_840
statements.doc:
Let $f(N)$ be the size of the largest quasi-Sidon subset $A\subset\{1,\ldots,N\}$, where we say
that $A$ is quasi-Sidon if
$$\lvert A+A\rvert=(1+o(1))\binom{\lvert A\rvert}{2}.$$
How does $f(N)$ grow?

Following [Er81h, p. 175], we ask for the largest $c$ such that there are quasi-Sidon sets
$A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, N\}$ with $\lvert A\rvert = (1+o(1))cN^{1/2}$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_840 : IsLUB {c : ℝ | IsQuasiSidonConstant c} erdos_840.answer

statements.name: Erdos840.erdos_840.variants.erdos_freud_lower
statements.doc:
Erdős and Freud [ErFr91] proved
$$\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}+o(1)\right)N^{1/2} \leq f(N) \leq \left(2+o(1)\right)N^{1/2}.$$
(Although both bounds were already given by Erdős in [Er81h].)

This is the lower bound. The lower bound is taking a genuine Sidon set $B\subset [1,N/3]$ of size
$\sim N^{1/2}/\sqrt{3}$ and taking the union with $\{N-b : b\in B\}$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_840.variants.erdos_freud_lower : IsQuasiSidonConstant (2 / Real.sqrt 3)

statements.name: Erdos840.erdos_840.variants.erdos_freud_upper
statements.doc:
Erdős and Freud [ErFr91] proved
$$\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}+o(1)\right)N^{1/2} \leq f(N) \leq \left(2+o(1)\right)N^{1/2}.$$
(Although both bounds were already given by Erdős in [Er81h].)

This is the upper bound.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_840.variants.erdos_freud_upper (c : ℝ) (hc : IsQuasiSidonConstant c) : c ≤ 2

statements.name: Erdos840.erdos_840.variants.pikhurko
statements.doc:
The upper bound was improved by Pikhurko [Pi06] to
$$f(N) \leq \left(\left(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{(\pi+2)^2}\right)^{-1/2}+o(1)\right)N^{1/2}$$
(the constant here is $=1.863\cdots$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_840.variants.pikhurko (c : ℝ) (hc : IsQuasiSidonConstant c) :
    c ≤ (1 / 4 + 1 / (Real.pi + 2) ^ 2) ^ (-(1 : ℝ) / 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 841
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/841](https://www.erdosproblems.com/841)
- [ErSe92] Erdős, Paul and Selfridge, J. L., Problems and Solutions: Solutions: 6655. Amer. Math.
  Monthly (1992), 791--794.
- [BPZ24] Bui, Hung M. and Pratt, Kyle and Zaharescu, Alexandru, A problem of
  Erdős-Graham-Granville-Selfridge on integral points on hyperelliptic curves. Math. Proc.
  Cambridge Philos. Soc. (2024), 309--323.
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.

statements.name: Erdos841.erdos_841
statements.doc:
Let $t_n$ be minimal such that $\{n+1,\ldots,n+t_n\}$ contains a subset whose product with $n$ is
a square number (and let $t_n=0$ if $n$ is itself square). Estimate $t_n$.

A problem of Erdős, Graham, and Selfridge. For example, $t_6=6$ since $6\cdot 8\cdot 12=24^2$. It
is trivial that $t_n\geq P(n)$, where $P(n)$ is the largest prime divisor of $n$.

Bui, Pratt, and Zaharescu [BPZ24] proved that the distribution of $t_n$ continues to follow
$P(n)$, in that for any fixed $c\in (0,1]$
$$\lim_{x\to \infty}\frac{\lvert \{ n\leq x : t_n\leq n^c\}\rvert}{x}
  = \lim_{x\to \infty}\frac{\lvert \{ n\leq x : P(n)\leq n^c\}\rvert}{x}.$$
The statement below is that the difference of the two counting functions is $o(x)$.

This was formalized in Lean by Codex.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_841 (c : ℝ) (hc : c ∈ Set.Ioc 0 1) :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦
      ((((Finset.Icc 1 x).filter fun n : ℕ ↦ (t n : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ c).card : ℝ) -
        ((Finset.Icc 1 x).filter fun n : ℕ ↦ (n.maxPrimeFac : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ c).card) / x)
      atTop (𝓝 0)

statements.name: Erdos841.erdos_841.variants.selfridge_large_prime
statements.doc:
Selfridge proved that $t_n=P(n)$ if $P(n)>\sqrt{2n}+1$.

This was formalized in Lean by Codex.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_841.variants.selfridge_large_prime (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n)
    (h : √(2 * n) + 1 < (n.maxPrimeFac : ℝ)) : t n = n.maxPrimeFac

statements.name: Erdos841.erdos_841.variants.selfridge_sqrt
statements.doc:
Selfridge proved that $t_n \ll n^{1/2}$ if $P(n)\leq\sqrt{2n}+1$.

This was formalized in Lean by Codex.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_841.variants.selfridge_sqrt :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, (n.maxPrimeFac : ℝ) ≤ √(2 * n) + 1 → (t n : ℝ) ≤ C * √n

statements.name: Erdos841.erdos_841.variants.many_small_values
statements.doc:
Bui, Pratt, and Zaharescu [BPZ24] proved that for at least $x^{1-o(1)}$ many $n\leq x$ we have
$$t_n \leq \exp(O(\sqrt{\log n\log\log n})).$$

This was formalized in Lean by Codex.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_841.variants.many_small_values : ∃ K : ℝ,
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦
      log (((Finset.Icc 1 x).filter fun n ↦
        (t n : ℝ) ≤ exp (K * √(log n * log (log n)))).card : ℝ) / log x) atTop (𝓝 1)

statements.name: Erdos841.erdos_841.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
Bui, Pratt, and Zaharescu [BPZ24] proved that for all non-square $n$
$$t_n \gg (\log\log n)^{6/5}(\log\log\log n)^{-1/5}.$$

This was formalized in Lean by Codex.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_841.variants.lower_bound : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ¬ IsSquare n →
      C * (log (log n) ^ ((6 : ℝ) / 5) * log (log (log n)) ^ (-(1 : ℝ) / 5)) ≤ t n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 842
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/842](https://www.erdosproblems.com/842)
- [Er92b] Erdős, Paul, _Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics_.
  Matematiche (Catania) (1992), 231-240.
- [FlSt92] Fleischner, Herbert and Stiebitz, Michael, _A solution to a colouring problem of
  P. Erdős_. Discrete Math. (1992), 39--48.

statements.name: Erdos842.erdos_842
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a graph on $3n$ vertices formed by taking $n$ vertex disjoint triangles and adding a
Hamiltonian cycle (with all new edges) between these vertices. Does $G$ have chromatic number at
most $3$?

The answer is yes, proved by Fleischner and Stiebitz [FlSt92].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_842 :
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V) (n : ℕ), IsTrianglesPlusHamiltonianCycle G n →
      G.chromaticNumber ≤ 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 844
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/844](https://www.erdosproblems.com/844)
- [AMS25] Alexeev, B., Mixon, D. and Sawin, W., *The independence and clique cover numbers of the
  squarefree graph*. arXiv:2507.01928 (2025).
- [Ch74] Chvátal, V., *Intersecting families of edges in hypergraphs having the hereditary
  property*. (1974), 61-66.

statements.name: Erdos844.erdos_844
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be such that, for all $a,b\in A$, the product $ab$ is not
squarefree.

Is the maximum size of such an $A$ achieved by taking $A$ to be the set of even numbers and
odd non-squarefree numbers?

A problem of Erdős and Sárközy.

Weisenberg has provided the following positive proof. It is clear that such a maximal $A$ must
contain all non-squarefree numbers. It therefore suffices to find the largest size of a subset
of all squarefree numbers in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that any two have at least one prime factor
in common. By the result of Chvátal [Ch74] discussed in [701] this is maximised by the set of
all even squarefree numbers.

An alternative proof was independently found by Alexeev, Mixon, and Sawin [AMS25].

This was formalized in Lean by Jennings using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_844 : ∀ N : ℕ,
    IsGreatest {k : ℕ | ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N,
      (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, ¬ Squarefree (a * b)) ∧ A.card = k}
      (evenOrOddNonSquarefree N).card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 845
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/845](https://www.erdosproblems.com/845)

statements.name: Erdos845.erdos_845
statements.doc:
Let $C > 0$. Is it true that the set of integers of the form $n = b_1 + \cdots + b_t$,
with $b_1 < \cdots < b_t$, where $b_i = 2^{k_i}3^{l_i}$ for $1 \leq i\leq t$ and
$b_t \leq Cb_1$ has density $0$?

van Doorn and Everts \cite{vDEv25} have disproved this with $C=6$ - in fact, they prove that all
integers can be written as such a sum in which $b_t<6b_1$.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_845 :
    ¬ ∀ᵉ (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C),
      let f : ℕ × ℕ → ℕ := fun (k, l) ↦ 2 ^ k * 3 ^ l
      { ∑ x ∈ B, f x | (B : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (h : B.Nonempty)
        (hB : B.sup f ≤ C * B.inf' h f) }.HasDensity 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 846
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/846](https://www.erdosproblems.com/846)

statements.name: Erdos846.erdos_846
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 846**
Let `A ⊂ ℝ²` be an infinite set for which there exists some `ϵ>0` such that in any subset of `A`
of size `n` there are always at least `ϵn` with no three on a line.
Is it true that `A` is the union of a finite number of sets where no three are on a line?

In other words, prove or disprove the following statement: every infinite `ε`-non-trilinear subset of the
plane is weakly non-trilinar.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_846 : ¬ ∀ᵉ (A : Set ℝ²) (ε > 0), A.Infinite → NonTrilinearFor A ε →
    WeaklyNonTrilinear A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 847
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/847](https://www.erdosproblems.com/847)
- [RRS24] Reiher, Christian and R\"odl, Vojt\v ech and Sales, Marcelo, Colouring versus density in integers and {H}ales-{J}ewett cubes. J. Lond. Math. Soc. (2) (2024)
  [arXiv:2311.08556](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.08556)

statements.name: Erdos847.erdos_847
statements.doc:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set for which there exists some $\epsilon > 0$ such that
in any subset of $A$ of size $n$ there is a subset of size at least $\epsilon n$ which contains no
three-term arithmetic progression.

Is it true that $A$ is the union of a finite number of sets which contain no three-term arithmetic
progression?

A negative answer was given by Reiher, Rödl, and Sales [RRS24], who proved that, for any
$0<\mu<1/2$, there exists $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that every finite colouring of $A$ contains
a three-term arithmetic progression, and yet every subset of $A$ of size $n$ contains a subset of
size $\geq \mu n$ without a three-term arithmetic progression.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_847 : ¬ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), Infinite A → HasFew3APs A →
    ∃ n, ∃ (S : Fin n → Set ℕ), (∀ i, ThreeAPFree (S i)) ∧ A = ⋃ i : Fin n, S i

problems.title: Erdős Problem 848
problems.doc:
Is the maximum size of a set $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that $ab + 1$ is never
squarefree (for all $a, b \in A$) achieved by taking those $n \equiv 7 \pmod{25}$?

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/848](https://www.erdosproblems.com/848)
 - [Er92b] Erdős, P. "Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics,
   and geometry." Resenhas do Instituto de Matemático e Estatística da Universidade
   de São Paulo 2.2 (1995): 165-186.
 - [Sa25] Sawhney, M. "Problem 848." (2025)
   https://www.math.columbia.edu/~msawhney/Problem_848.pdf
 - Full formal proof of asymptotic result: https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger

statements.name: Erdos848.erdos_848
statements.doc:
Is the maximum size of a set $A ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that $ab + 1$ is never squarefree
(for all $a, b ∈ A$) achieved by taking those $n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}$?

This asks whether `Erdos848 N` holds for all $N$ (formulated using `A ⊆ Finset.range N`).

This was solved for all sufficiently large $N$ by Sawhney in this note. In fact, Sawhney proves
something slightly stronger, that there exists some constant $c>0$ such that if
$\lvert A\rvert \geq (\frac{1}{25}-c)N$ and $N$ is large then $A$ is contained in either
$\{ n\equiv 7\pmod{25}\}$ or $\{n\equiv 18\pmod{25}\}$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_848 : ∀ N, Erdos848For N

statements.name: Erdos848.erdos_848.variants.asymptotic
statements.doc:
There exists $N₀$ such that for all $N ≥ N₀$, if $A ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ satisfies that $ab + 1$
is never squarefree for all $a, b ∈ A$, then $|A| ≤ |\{n ≤ N : n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}\}|$.

More precisely, Sawhney proves: there exist absolute constants $η > 0$ and $N₀$
such that for all $N ≥ N₀$, if $|A| ≥ (1/25 - η)N$ then $A ⊆ \{n : n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}\}$ or
$A ⊆ \{n : n ≡ 18 \pmod{25}\}$.

A complete formal Lean 4 proof is available at:
https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger
statements.statement: theorem erdos_848.variants.asymptotic : ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, Erdos848For N

problems.title: Erdős Problem 849
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/849](https://www.erdosproblems.com/849)

statements.name: Erdos849.erdos_849
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for every integer $t\geq1$, there is some integer $a$ such that ${n \choose k} = a$
with $1\leq k \le \frac{n}{2}$ has exactly $t$ solutions?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_849 :
    ∀ t ≥ 1, ∃ a : ℕ,
      {n : ℕ | ∃ k ≥ 1, 2 * k ≤ n ∧ choose n k = a}.ncard = t

problems.title: Erdős Problem 850
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/850](https://www.erdosproblems.com/850)

statements.name: Erdos850.erdos_850
statements.doc:
Can there exist two distinct integers $x$ and $y$ such that $x,y$ have the same prime factors,
$x+1,y+1$ have the same prime factors, and $x+2,y+2$ also have the same prime factors?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_850 :
    ∃ x y : ℕ, x ≠ y ∧ x.primeFactors = y.primeFactors
      ∧ (x + 1).primeFactors = (y + 1).primeFactors
      ∧ (x + 2).primeFactors = (y + 2).primeFactors

problems.title: Erdős Problem 851
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/851](https://www.erdosproblems.com/851)
- [Pr26] D. Price and GPT-5.2 Pro, [Erdős problem 851](https://www.overleaf.com/read/svgbjzpxxppv#4eea7e) (2026)

statements.name: Erdos851.erdos_851.variants.romanoff
statements.doc: The set of integers of the form `2^k+p` (where `p` is prime) has positive lower density.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_851.variants.romanoff : 0 < Set.lowerDensity twoPowAddPrimeSet

statements.name: Erdos851.erdos_851
statements.doc:
Let $\epsilon > 0$. Is there some $r \ll_\epsilon 1$ such that the density of integers of the
form $2^k+n$, where $k \geq 0$ and $n$ has at most $r$ prime divisors, is at least $1-\epsilon$?

This was proved affirmatively by Price and GPT-5.2 Pro [Pr26].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_851 (ε : ℝ) (hε : ε ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) : ∃ r,
    1 - ε ≤ (TwoPowAddSet r).lowerDensity

problems.title: Erdős Problem 852
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/852](https://www.erdosproblems.com/852)
- [Er85c] Erdős, P., *On some of my problems in number theory I would most like to see solved*.
  Number theory (Ootacamund, 1984) (1985), 74-84.
- [A001223](https://oeis.org/A001223)
- [A053597](https://oeis.org/A053597)
- [A078515](https://oeis.org/A078515)

statements.name: Erdos852.erdos_852.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $h(x)$ be maximal such that for
some $n < x$ the numbers $d_n, d_{n+1}, \ldots, d_{n+h(x)-1}$ are all distinct [Er85c]. Estimate
$h(x)$. In particular, is it true that
$$h(x) > (\log x)^c$$
for some constant $c > 0$?

The statement avoids defining $h$. Since $h(x)$ is the longest such run, $h(x) > y$ holds exactly
when some $n < x$ starts a run of $H > y$ distinct gaps. We state the question this way, with $x$
real. We read it as asking for one $c > 0$ such that the inequality holds for all large $x$.

The primes are indexed from $p_0 = 2$, as in `primeGap`. Shifting the index by one does not change
the question.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_852.parts.i :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop,
      ∃ n : ℕ, (n : ℝ) < x ∧ ∃ H : ℕ, (Real.log x) ^ c < (H : ℝ) ∧ DistinctGapRun n H

statements.name: Erdos852.erdos_852.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $h(x)$ be maximal such that for
some $n < x$ the numbers $d_n, d_{n+1}, \ldots, d_{n+h(x)-1}$ are all distinct [Er85c]. Estimate
$h(x)$. In particular, is it true that
$$h(x) = o(\log x)?$$

The statement avoids defining $h$. It says that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all large real $x$,
every run of $H$ distinct gaps $d_n, \ldots, d_{n+H-1}$ with $n < x$ satisfies
$H \leq \varepsilon \log x$. This is $h(x) \leq \varepsilon \log x$, because $h(x)$ is the longest
such run.

The indexing is as in `Erdos852.erdos_852.parts.i`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_852.parts.ii :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop,
      ∀ n : ℕ, (n : ℝ) < x → ∀ H : ℕ, DistinctGapRun n H → (H : ℝ) ≤ ε * Real.log x

statements.name: Erdos852.erdos_852.variants.tendsto_atTop
statements.doc:
Brun's sieve implies $h(x) \to \infty$ as $x \to \infty$ (remark on
[erdosproblems.com/852](https://www.erdosproblems.com/852)).

That is, for every $H$ and all large $x$ there is some $n < x$ such that $d_n, \ldots, d_{n+H-1}$
are all distinct. Since more values of $n$ are allowed as $x$ grows, this holds exactly when, for
every $H$, some $n$ has $d_n, \ldots, d_{n+H-1}$ all distinct.

This also follows from `Erdos6.erdos_6.variants.increasing`, because strictly increasing prime
gaps are distinct.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_852.variants.tendsto_atTop :
    ∀ H : ℕ, ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop, ∃ n : ℕ, (n : ℝ) < x ∧ DistinctGapRun n H

problems.title: Erdős Problem 853
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/853](https://www.erdosproblems.com/853)

statements.name: Erdos853.erdos_853.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $r(x)$ be the smallest even
integer $t$ such that $d_n = t$ has no solutions for $n \le x$.

Is it true that $r(x) \to \infty$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_853.parts.i : atTop.Tendsto r atTop

statements.name: Erdos853.erdos_853.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $r(x)$ be the smallest even
integer $t$ such that $d_n = t$ has no solutions for $n \le x$.

Is it true that $r(x) / \log x \to \infty$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_853.parts.ii :
    atTop.Tendsto (fun n ↦ r n / Real.log n) atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 854
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/854](https://www.erdosproblems.com/854)
- [Er85c] Erdős, P., *On some of my problems in number theory I would most like to see solved*.
  Number theory (Ootacamund, 1984), Lecture Notes in Math. 1122 (1985), 74-84.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1985-17.pdf)
- [Ob1] Erdős, P., *Oberwolfach Mathematical Problems*, Volume 1. Mathematisches
  Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach.
- [OEIS A389839](https://oeis.org/A389839): smallest even number which cannot be written as the
  difference of two consecutive numbers which are relatively prime to the $n$th primorial. It
  agrees with `minEvenNonGap k` for $k\geq 3$.
- [OEIS A048670](https://oeis.org/A048670): Jacobsthal's function of the product of the first $n$
  primes, which is the largest gap.

statements.name: Erdos854.erdos_854.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $n_k$ denote the $k$th primorial, i.e. the product of the first $k$ primes.

If $1=a_1<a_2<\cdots <a_{\phi(n_k)}=n_k-1$ is the sequence of integers coprime to $n_k$, then
estimate the smallest even integer not of the form $a_{i+1}-a_i$. Are there
$$\gg \max_i (a_{i+1}-a_i)$$
many even integers of the form $a_{j+1}-a_j$?

This is the first part. A problem of Erdős [Er85c, p. 80], who writes "integer" instead of "even
integer"; all differences $a_{i+1}-a_i$ are even, so only even integers are meaningful. Here
"estimate" is read as $\Theta$. Erdős first thought that for large $k$ every even $t \leq
\max_i(a_{i+1}-a_i)$ is a gap, but [Ob1] reports computations of Lacampagne and Selfridge showing
this fails for $n_6 = 30030$ (OEIS A389839 and A048670 give $20$ and $22$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_854.parts.i :
    (fun k ↦ (minEvenNonGap k : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_854.parts.i.answer

statements.name: Erdos854.erdos_854.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $n_k$ denote the $k$th primorial, i.e. the product of the first $k$ primes.

If $1=a_1<a_2<\cdots <a_{\phi(n_k)}=n_k-1$ is the sequence of integers coprime to $n_k$, then
estimate the smallest even integer not of the form $a_{i+1}-a_i$. Are there
$$\gg \max_i (a_{i+1}-a_i)$$
many even integers of the form $a_{j+1}-a_j$?

This is the second part. We read it as: there is an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that, for all
large $k$, the number of distinct gap values is at least $c$ times the largest gap.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_854.parts.ii :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (maxGap (kthPrimorial k) : ℝ) ≤ ((gapSet (kthPrimorial k)).card : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 855
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/855](https://www.erdosproblems.com/855)

This is an "eventually" formulation of the Second Hardy–Littlewood conjecture.

statements.name: Erdos855.erdos_855
statements.doc:
Erdős Problem 855 (Segal's conjecture): $\pi(x + y) \le \pi(x) + \pi(y)$
for all sufficiently large $x, y$, i.e. for all $x, y \ge N$ for some $N$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_855 :
    ∀ᶠ (xy : ℕ × ℕ) in atTop ×ˢ atTop, π (xy.1 + xy.2) ≤ π xy.1 + π xy.2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 856
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/856](https://www.erdosproblems.com/856)
- [Er70] Erdős, P., *Some extremal problems in combinatorial number theory*. Mathematical Essays
  Dedicated to A. J. Macintyre (1970), 123-133. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1970-21.pdf)
- [TaZh25b] Tang, Q. and Zhang, S., *Harmonic LCM patterns and sunflower-free capacity*.
  [arXiv:2512.20055](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.20055) (2025).

The problem is closely related to the sunflower problem
[erdosproblems.com/857](https://www.erdosproblems.com/857). The version with natural density in
place of the harmonic sum is [erdosproblems.com/536](https://www.erdosproblems.com/536).

statements.name: Erdos856.erdos_856
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 3$ and $f_k(N)$ be the maximum value of $\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}$, where $A$ ranges
over all subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ which contain no subset of size $k$ with the same pairwise
least common multiple.

Estimate $f_k(N)$.

This is the question of Erdős [Er70, p. 127]. We read "estimate" as
$f_k(N) = \Theta(\text{answer})$ as $N \to \infty$, for each fixed $k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_856 (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) :
    f k =Θ[atTop] erdos_856.answer k

statements.name: Erdos856.erdos_856.variants.erdos_upper
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er70, p. 127] notes that
$$f_k(N) \ll \frac{\log N}{\log\log N}.$$

The implied constant depends on $k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_856.variants.erdos_upper (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, f k N ≤ C * (Real.log N / Real.log (Real.log N))

statements.name: Erdos856.erdos_856.variants.tang_zhang_lower
statements.doc:
Tang and Zhang [TaZh25b, Theorem 1.2] proved that, for fixed $k\geq 3$ and as $N\to\infty$,
$$f_k(N) \geq (\log N)^{c_k - o(1)}, \qquad c_k = \frac{k-2}{e\,((k-2)!)^{1/(k-2)}}.$$

The $o(1)$ is stated with an arbitrary $\varepsilon > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_856.variants.tang_zhang_lower (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, Real.log N ^ (tangZhangExponent k - ε) ≤ f k N

statements.name: Erdos856.erdos_856.variants.tang_zhang_three_lower
statements.doc:
Tang and Zhang [TaZh25b, Corollary 1.7] proved, as $N\to\infty$,
$$(\log N)^{\log(1.551)-o(1)}\leq f_3(N)\ll(\log N)^{\frac{3}{2^{2/3}}-1+o(1)}.$$

This is the lower bound, with the $o(1)$ stated with an arbitrary $\varepsilon > 0$. Since
$\log(1.551) = 0.4389\ldots$, it implies the site's $(\log N)^{0.438}\leq f_3(N)$ for large $N$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_856.variants.tang_zhang_three_lower (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, Real.log N ^ (Real.log 1.551 - ε) ≤ f 3 N

statements.name: Erdos856.erdos_856.variants.tang_zhang_three_upper
statements.doc:
Tang and Zhang [TaZh25b, Corollary 1.7] proved, as $N\to\infty$,
$$(\log N)^{\log(1.551)-o(1)}\leq f_3(N)\ll(\log N)^{\frac{3}{2^{2/3}}-1+o(1)}.$$

This is the upper bound, with the $o(1)$ and the implied constant absorbed into an arbitrary
$\varepsilon > 0$. The site rounds the exponent to $0.889$, but $\frac{3}{2^{2/3}}-1=0.8898\ldots$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_856.variants.tang_zhang_three_upper (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, f 3 N ≤ Real.log N ^ (3 / (2 : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3) - 1 + ε)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 857
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/857](https://www.erdosproblems.com/857)

For fixed `n, k`, let `m(n, k)` be minimal such that every family of subsets of `[n]`
of size at least `m(n, k)` contains a `k`-sunflower.
The problem asks to estimate `m(n, k)`, ideally asymptotically.

statements.name: Erdos857.erdos_857
statements.doc: Estimate `m(n,k)`, or better give an asymptotic formula.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_857 :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k → Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (m n k : ℝ) / erdos_857.answer k n) atTop (nhds 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 858
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/858](https://www.erdosproblems.com/858)
- [Er70] Erdős, Paul, _Some extremal problems in combinatorial number theory_. Mathematical Essays
  Dedicated to A. J. Macintyre (1970), 123-133.
- [Al66] Alexander, Ralph, _Density and multiplicative structure of sets of integers_. Acta
  Arith. (1966/67), 321--332.
- [ESS68] Erdős, P. and Sárközi, A. and Szemerédi, E., _On the solvability of certain equations
  in sequences of positive upper logarithmic density_. J. London Math. Soc. (1968), 71--78.
- [Be35] Behrend, F., _On sequences of numbers not divisible by another_. London Math. Soc.
  Journal (1935), 42-45.

statements.name: Erdos858.erdos_858
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be such that there is no solution to $at=b$ with $a,b\in A$ and
the smallest prime factor of $t$ is $>a$. Estimate the maximum of
$$\frac{1}{\log N}\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}.$$

This has been solved by Chojecki and GPT-5.4 Pro, who show that for large $N$
$$\max_A \sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}=(c+o(1))\log N$$
where the maximum is over all $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with the stated property and
$c\approx 0.618\cdots$ is an explicit constant.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_858 : ∃ c : ℝ, Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ M N / log N) atTop (nhds c)

statements.name: Erdos858.erdos_858.variants.positive
statements.doc:
The limit $c\approx 0.618\cdots$ is positive: for any fixed large $N$ the maximum is bounded
