away from $0$ (Alexander [Al66], Erdős–Sárközi–Szemerédi [ESS68]).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_858.variants.positive :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ M N / log N) atTop (nhds c)

statements.name: Erdos858.erdos_858.variants.infinite
statements.doc:
Alexander [Al66] and Erdős, Sárközi, and Szemerédi [ESS68] proved that if $A$ is an infinite set
with this property then $\sum_{n\in A\cap [1,N]}\frac{1}{n}=o(\log N)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_858.variants.infinite (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (h0 : 0 ∉ A)
    (hadm : ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, ∀ t : ℕ, a * t = b → t.minFac ≤ a) :
    (fun N : ℕ ↦ ∑ n ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (· ∈ A), (1 : ℝ) / n) =o[atTop]
      fun N : ℕ ↦ log N

problems.title: Erdős Problem 859
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/859](https://www.erdosproblems.com/859)

statements.name: Erdos859.erdos_859.variants.erdos_upper_lower_bounds
statements.doc:
A weaker version of the problem proved by Erdos:
The density `dₜ` of `DivisorSumSet (t : ℕ)` is bounded from below by `1 / log (t) ^ c₃` and
from above by `1 / log (t) ^ c₄` for some positive constants `c₃` and `c₄`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_859.variants.erdos_upper_lower_bounds : ∃ᵉ (c₃ > (0 : ℝ)) (c₄ > (0 : ℝ)) (t₀ : ℕ),
    ∀ᶠ t in atTop, ∃ dₜ : ℝ, (DivisorSumSet t).HasDensity dₜ ∧
    1 / Real.log t ^ c₃ < dₜ ∧ dₜ < 1 / Real.log t ^ c₄

statements.name: Erdos859.erdos_859
statements.doc: The density of the divisor sum set is asymptotically equivalent to $c_1 / \log(t)^{c_2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_859 :
    ∃ c₁ > 0, ∃ c₂ > (0 : ℝ), ∃ d : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ t > 0, (DivisorSumSet t).HasDensity (d t)) ∧
      (fun (t : ℕ) ↦ d t) ~[atTop] (fun t ↦ c₁ / Real.log t ^ c₂)

statements.name: Erdos859.erdos_859.variants.trivial_case
statements.doc: A case where we can easily calculate the density of `DivisorSumSet t` is that of `t=0`.
statements.statement: lemma erdos_859.variants.trivial_case : DivisorSumSet 0 = Set.univ

statements.name: Erdos859.erdos_859.variants.positive_density
statements.doc:
An easy sanity check is to prove that for every natural number `t` the density `dₜ` is
a positive number.
Hint: investigate some multiplicative structure of `DivisorSumSet t`.
statements.statement:
lemma erdos_859.variants.positive_density (t : ℕ) :
    (DivisorSumSet t).HasPosDensity

problems.title: Erdős Problem 860
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/860](https://www.erdosproblems.com/860)
- [ErPo80] Erdős, P. and Pomerance, C., *Matching the natural numbers up to $n$ with distinct
  multiples in another interval*. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch. Indag. Math. 42 (1980), 147-161.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-13.pdf)
- [Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my forgotten problems in number theory*. Hardy-Ramanujan J. 15
  (1992), 34-50. [PDF](https://hrj.episciences.org/125/pdf)

statements.name: Erdos860.erdos_860
statements.doc:
Let $h(n)$ be such that, for any $m\geq 1$, in the interval $(m,m+h(n))$ there exist distinct
integers $a_i$ for $1\leq i\leq \pi(n)$ such that $p_i\mid a_i$, where $p_i$ denotes the $i$th
prime.

Estimate $h(n)$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_860 : (fun n ↦ (h n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_860.answer

statements.name: Erdos860.erdos_860.variants.erdos_pomerance_upper
statements.doc:
Erdős and Pomerance [ErPo80] proved that
$$h(n) \ll \frac{n^{3/2}}{(\log n)^{1/2}}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_860.variants.erdos_pomerance_upper :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (h n : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) / Real.sqrt (Real.log n)

statements.name: Erdos860.erdos_860.variants.erdos_selfridge_lower
statements.doc:
Erdős and Selfridge proved $h(n)>(3-o(1))n$.

[ErPo80, (19), p. 159] states this as $\limsup h(n)/n \geq 3$, that is, it holds for infinitely
many $n$. We state that form.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_860.variants.erdos_selfridge_lower :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (3 - ε) * n ≤ (h n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos860.erdos_860.variants.ruzsa
statements.doc: Ruzsa proved $h(n)/n\to \infty$, as reported in [Er92c, p. 36].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_860.variants.ruzsa :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (h n : ℝ) / n) atTop atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 862
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/862](https://www.erdosproblems.com/862)
- [Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my forgotten problems in number theory*. Hardy-Ramanujan J. (1992),
  34-50.
- [SaTh15] Saxton, David and Thomason, Andrew, *Hypergraph containers*. Invent. Math. (2015),
  925-992.

statements.name: Erdos862.erdos_862.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $A_1(N)$ be the number of maximal Sidon subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Is it true that
$$A_1(N) < 2^{o(N^{1/2})}?$$

A problem of Cameron and Erdős. This is resolved as a consequence of results of Saxton and
Thomason [SaTh15] - they prove that the number of Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is at least
$2^{(1.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}$. Since each Sidon set is contained in a maximal Sidon set, and each
maximal Sidon set contains at most $2^{(1+o(1))N^{1/2}}$ Sidon sets, it follows that
$$A_1(N) \geq 2^{(0.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_862.parts.i :
    ¬ (fun N : ℕ => Real.logb 2 (numMaximalSidonSets N : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos862.erdos_862.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $A_1(N)$ be the number of maximal Sidon subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Is it true that
$$A_1(N) > 2^{N^c}$$
for some constant $c>0$?

A problem of Cameron and Erdős. This is resolved as a consequence of results of Saxton and
Thomason [SaTh15] - they prove that the number of Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is at least
$2^{(1.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}$. Since each Sidon set is contained in a maximal Sidon set, and each
maximal Sidon set contains at most $2^{(1+o(1))N^{1/2}}$ Sidon sets, it follows that
$$A_1(N) \geq 2^{(0.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_862.parts.ii :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop,
      (2 : ℝ) ^ ((N : ℝ) ^ c) < (numMaximalSidonSets N : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos862.erdos_862.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
This is resolved as a consequence of results of Saxton and Thomason [SaTh15] - they prove that
the number of Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is at least $2^{(1.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}$. Since each
Sidon set is contained in a maximal Sidon set, and each maximal Sidon set contains at most
$2^{(1+o(1))N^{1/2}}$ Sidon sets, it follows that
$$A_1(N) \geq 2^{(0.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_862.variants.lower_bound (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop,
      (2 : ℝ) ^ (((0.16 : ℝ) - ε) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) ≤ (numMaximalSidonSets N : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 864
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/864](https://www.erdosproblems.com/864)
- [A389182](https://oeis.org/A389182)
- [ErFr91] Erdős, P. and Freud, R., *On sums of a Sidon-sequence*. J. Number Theory 38 (1991),
  196--205.
- [Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my forgotten problems in number theory*. Hardy-Ramanujan J. 15
  (1992), 34-50.

statements.name: Erdos864.erdos_864
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be a set such that there exists at most one $n$ with more than one
solution to $n=a+b$ (with $a\leq b\in A$). Estimate the maximal possible size of $|A|$. In
particular, is it true that
$$|A| \leq (1+o(1))\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} N^{1/2}?$$

A problem of Erdős and Freud [ErFr91] [Er92c]. For the analogous question with $n=a-b$ they prove
that $\lvert A\rvert\sim N^{1/2}$. This is a weaker form of Erdős Problem 840.

The condition on $A$ is `HasAtMostOneRepeatedSum`. We state the question as follows: for every
$\varepsilon > 0$ and all large $N$, every such set $A$ satisfies
$|A| \leq (1+\varepsilon)\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} N^{1/2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_864 :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N,
      HasAtMostOneRepeatedSum A →
        (#A : ℝ) ≤ (1 + ε) * (2 / Real.sqrt 3) * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos864.erdos_864.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős and Freud [ErFr91] [Er92c] prove that
$$\lvert A\rvert \geq (1+o(1))\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}N^{1/2}.$$
This is shown by taking a genuine Sidon set $B\subset [1,N/3]$ of size $\sim N^{1/2}/\sqrt{3}$
and taking the union with $\{N-b : b\in B\}$.

That is, for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all large $N$ there is a set $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$
with the property of `Erdos864.erdos_864` and $|A| \geq (1-\varepsilon)\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}N^{1/2}$.
So the constant $2/\sqrt{3}$ there cannot be replaced by a smaller one.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_864.variants.lower_bound :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N,
      HasAtMostOneRepeatedSum A ∧
        (1 - ε) * (2 / Real.sqrt 3) * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) ≤ #A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 865
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/865](https://www.erdosproblems.com/865)
- [CES75] Choi, S. L. G. and Erdős, P. and Szemerédi, E., Some additive and multiplicative problems
  in number theory. Acta Arith. (1975), 37--50.
- [Ci26] R. Cipollini, [A sharp $5/8$ bound for an Erdős–Sós pairwise-sums problem](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.29361)
  (2026).

statements.name: Erdos865.erdos_865
statements.doc:
There exists a constant $C>0$ such that, for all large $N$, if $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ has
size at least $\frac{5}{8}N+C$ then there are distinct $a,b,c\in A$ such that $a+b,a+c,b+c\in A$.

A problem of Erdős and Sós (also earlier considered by Choi, Erdős, and Szemerédi [CES75], but Erdős
had forgotten this).

This problem was solved in the affirmative by Cipollini and GPT Pro [Ci26].

This is true. The linked proof gives it in the contrapositive and with the constant cleared:
every triple-free $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ satisfies $8\lvert A\rvert\leq 5N+C$ for a fixed
$C$, for every $N$ rather than only for large $N$. It also shows the threshold is sharp, by
exhibiting triple-free sets of size $(5N+16)/8$ for every $N$ divisible by $8$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_865 :
    ∃ C > 0, ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in atTop,
      ∀ A ⊆ Icc 1 N, A.card ≥ (5 / 8 : ℝ) * N + C →
      ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, ∃ c ∈ A, a ≠ b ∧ a ≠ c ∧ b ≠ c ∧
      a + b ∈ A ∧ a + c ∈ A ∧ b + c ∈ A

statements.name: Erdos865.erdos_865.variants.k2
statements.doc:
It is a classical folklore fact that if $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,2N\}$ has size $\geq N+2$ then
there are distinct $a,b\in A$ such that $a+b\in A$, which establishes the $k=2$ case.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_865.variants.k2 (N : ℕ) :
    ∀ A ⊆ Icc 1 (2 * N), A.card ≥ N + 2 →
    ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, a ≠ b ∧ a + b ∈ A

statements.name: Erdos865.erdos_865.variants.sos
statements.doc:
Erdős and Sós conjectured that
$f_k(N)\sim \frac{1}{2}\left(1+\sum_{1\leq r\leq k-2}\frac{1}{4^r}\right) N$,
where $f_k(N)$ is the minimal size of a subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ guaranteeing $k$ elements
have all pairwise sums in the set.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_865.variants.sos :
    ∀ᵉ (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k),
    (fun N ↦ (f N k : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun N ↦ (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (1 + ∑ r ∈ Icc 1 (k - 2),
      (1 / 4 : ℝ) ^ r) * N)

statements.name: Erdos865.erdos_865.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
Choi, Erdős, and Szemerédi [CES75] have proved that, for all $k\geq 3$, there exists $\epsilon_k>0$
such that (for large enough $N$) $f_k(N)\leq \left(\frac{2}{3}-\epsilon_k\right)N$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_865.variants.upper_bound (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) :
    ∃ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, (f N k : ℝ) ≤ (2 / 3 - ε) * N

problems.title: Erdős Problem 867
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/867](https://www.erdosproblems.com/867)
- [CoPh96] Coppersmith, Don and Phillips, Steven, *On a question of Erdős on subsequence sums*.
  SIAM J. Discrete Math. (1996), 173-177.
- [Fr93] Freud, R., *Adding numbers - on a problem of P. Erdős*. James Cook Mathematical
  Notes (1993), 6199-6202.

statements.name: Erdos867.erdos_867
statements.doc:
Is it true that if $A=\{a_1<\cdots <a_t\}\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ has no solutions to
$$a_i+a_{i+1}+\cdots+a_j\in A$$
then
$$\lvert A\rvert \leq \frac{N}{2}+O(1)?$$

In fact this problem is false. Freud [Fr93] constructed a sequence with density $\geq 19/36$.
The current best bounds are due to Coppersmith and Phillips [CoPh96], who prove that the
maximal size of such an $A$ satisfies
$$\frac{13}{24}N -O(1)\leq \lvert A\rvert \leq \left(\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{512}\right)N+\log N.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_867 :
    ¬ ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ, ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A →
      (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) / 2 + C

statements.name: Erdos867.erdos_867.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc: Taking $A=(N/2,N]\cap \mathbb{N}$ shows $\lvert A\rvert \geq N/2-O(1)$ is possible.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_867.variants.lower_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A ∧
      ((N : ℝ) / 2 - C ≤ (A.card : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos867.erdos_867.variants.adenwalla
statements.doc:
Adenwalla has observed that
$$\lvert A\rvert \leq (\tfrac{2}{3}+o(1))N.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_867.variants.adenwalla (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A →
      (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 / 3 + ε) * (N : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos867.erdos_867.variants.freud
statements.doc: Freud [Fr93] constructed a sequence with density $\geq 19/36$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_867.variants.freud :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A ∧
      (((19 / 36 : ℝ) - ε) * (N : ℝ) ≤ (A.card : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos867.erdos_867.variants.coppersmith_phillips_lower_bound
statements.doc:
The current best bounds are due to Coppersmith and Phillips [CoPh96], who prove that the
maximal size of such an $A$ satisfies
$$\frac{13}{24}N -O(1)\leq \lvert A\rvert.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_867.variants.coppersmith_phillips_lower_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A ∧
      ((13 / 24 : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) - C ≤ (A.card : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos867.erdos_867.variants.coppersmith_phillips_upper_bound
statements.doc:
The current best bounds are due to Coppersmith and Phillips [CoPh96], who prove that the
maximal size of such an $A$ satisfies
$$\lvert A\rvert \leq \left(\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{512}\right)N+\log N.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_867.variants.coppersmith_phillips_upper_bound :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A →
      (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 / 3 - 1 / 512) * (N : ℝ) + Real.log (N : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 868
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/868](https://www.erdosproblems.com/868)
- [LaLa26] Larsen and Larsen, [Erdős problem 868](https://github.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-868/blob/main/868.pdf) (2026)

statements.name: Erdos868.erdos_868.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $A$ be an additive basis of order $2$, let $f(n)$ denote the number of ways in which
$n$ can be written as the sum of two elements from $A$. If $f(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, then
must $A$ contain a minimal additive basis of order $2$?

Larsen and Larsen [LaLa26] answered this in the negative.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_868.parts.i :
    ¬ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 →
      atTop.Tendsto (fun n => ncard_add_repr A 2 n) atTop → ∃ B ⊆ A,
      B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2

statements.name: Erdos868.erdos_868.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $A$ be an additive basis of order $2$, let $f(n)$ denote the number of ways in which
$n$ can be written as the sum of two elements from $A$. If $f(n) > \epsilon \log n$ for large $n$
and an arbitrary fixed $\epsilon > 0$, then must $A$ contain a minimal additive
basis of order $2$?

Larsen and Larsen [LaLa26] constructed a counterexample with $f(n) > c \log n$ for all large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_868.parts.ii :
    ¬ ∀ᵉ (A : Set ℕ) (ε > 0), A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 →
      (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ε * Real.log n < ncard_add_repr A 2 n) → ∃ B ⊆ A,
      B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2

statements.name: Erdos868.erdos_868.variants.fixed_ε
statements.doc:
Erdős and Nathanson proved that this is true if $f(n) > c \log n$ for all large $n$, for
some fixed constant $c > (\log \frac{4}{3})^{-1}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_868.variants.fixed_ε :
    ∀ᵉ (A : Set ℕ) (c > (Real.log (4 / 3))⁻¹), A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 →
      (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, c * Real.log n < ncard_add_repr A 2 n) → ∃ B ⊆ A,
      B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2

statements.name: Erdos868.erdos_868.variants.Hartter_Nathanson
statements.doc:
Härtter and Nathanson proved that there exist additive bases which do not contain
any minimal additive bases.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_868.variants.Hartter_Nathanson (o : ℕ) (ho : 1 < o) : ∃ (A : Set ℕ),
    A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o ∧ ∀ B ⊆ A, B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o →
    ∃ b ∈ B, (B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o

problems.title: Erdős Problem 869
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/869](https://www.erdosproblems.com/869)
- [ErNa88] Erdős, Paul and Nathanson, Melvyn B., *Partitions of bases into disjoint unions of
  bases*. J. Number Theory (1988), 1-9.
- [Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my forgotten problems in number theory*. Hardy-Ramanujan J. (1992),
  34-50.
- [La26] Larsen, D., *Three questions of Erdős–Nathanson on asymptotic bases of order 2*.
  [arXiv:2603.03472](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03472) (2026).

statements.name: Erdos869.erdos_869
statements.doc:
If $A_1, A_2$ are disjoint additive bases of order $2$ (i.e. $A_i + A_i$ contains all large
integers) then must $A = A_1 \cup A_2$ contain a minimal additive basis of order $2$ (one such that
deleting any element creates infinitely many $n \notin A + A$)?

A question of Erdős and Nathanson [ErNa88, Er92c]. The answer is no: Larsen [La26] constructed
disjoint bases $A_1, A_2$ of order $2$ such that $A_1 \cup A_2$ contains no minimal basis of
order $2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_869 :
    ¬ ∀ (A₁ A₂ : Set ℕ), Disjoint A₁ A₂ →
      A₁.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 → A₂.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 →
      ∃ D ⊆ A₁ ∪ A₂, D.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧
        ∀ d ∈ D, ¬ (D \ {d}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 871
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/871](https://www.erdosproblems.com/871)
- [ErNa88] Erdős, Paul and Nathanson, Melvyn B., *Partitions of bases into disjoint unions of bases*. J. Number Theory (1988), 1-9.
- [ErNa89] Erdős, Paul and Nathanson, Melvyn B., *Additive bases with many representations*. Acta Arith. (1989), 399-406.

statements.name: Erdos871.erdos_871
statements.doc:
Let $A$ be an additive basis of order $2$, and suppose $1_A\ast 1_A(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$. Can $A$ be partitioned into two disjoint additive bases of order $2$?

A question of Erdős and Nathanson [ErNa88], who proved this is true if $1_A\ast 1_A(n) > c\log n$ (for all large $n$) for some constant $c>(\log\frac{4}{3})^{-1}$. Erdős and Nathanson [ErNa89] also proved that for every $t$ there exists a basis $A$ of order $2$ such that $1_A\ast 1_A(n)\geq t$ for all large $n$ and yet $A$ cannot be partitioned into two disjoint additive bases. This has been disproved by Larsen using Claude Opus 4.5 - in fact only a small modification of the argument of [ErNa89] is required.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_871 :
    ¬ ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
      (∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, a + b = n) ∧
      (∀ t, ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∃ pairs : Finset (ℕ × ℕ),
        pairs.card ≥ t ∧
          ∀ p ∈ pairs, p.1 ∈ A ∧ p.2 ∈ A ∧ p.1 + p.2 = n ∧ p.1 ≤ p.2) →
      ∃ (B C : Set ℕ),
        (∀ x, x ∈ A ↔ x ∈ B ∨ x ∈ C) ∧
        Disjoint B C ∧
        (∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∃ a ∈ B, ∃ b ∈ B, a + b = n) ∧
        (∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∃ a ∈ C, ∃ b ∈ C, a + b = n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 872
problems.doc:
This file states Erdős Problem 872 for the primitive-set saturation game on $\{2, \dots, n\}$.
The game value `L n` is defined by a finite minimax recursion: Prolonger moves first and maximizes
the final size of the claimed primitive set, while Shortener minimizes it.

The problem statement does not fix the turn order. This file fixes Prolonger to move first,
following the convention used in the forum discussion of the problem. The choice is not cosmetic:
computational data suggests the Shortener-first value tracks $\pi(n)$ while the Prolonger-first
value grows linearly, and the questions below concern the Prolonger-first quantity.

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/872](https://www.erdosproblems.com/872)
- [erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/872](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/872)

statements.name: Erdos872.erdos_872.parts.i
statements.doc:
Erdős Problem 872, part (i) (weak form): there exists a constant $\epsilon > 0$ such that the
game length is at least $\epsilon \cdot n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_872.parts.i :
    ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (L n : ℝ) ≥ ε * n

statements.name: Erdos872.erdos_872.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Erdős Problem 872, part (ii) (strong form): for every $\epsilon > 0$, the game length is at
least $(1-\epsilon) \cdot n / 2$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

The forum thread (April-May 2026) records Shortener strategies giving
$L(n) \leq (23/48 + o(1)) \cdot n$ (described in the thread as accepted as correct, with a Lean
formalization in progress) and a claimed $L(n) \leq 0.19 \cdot n$, either of which would answer this
question negatively under the Prolonger-first convention.

The $23/48$ upper bound for `C`-respecting plays (following old-bielefelder's strategy in the
forum thread) was formalized in Lean 4 by Pommeret using Aristotle and Claude Opus 4.7, and
completed to a proof for the full minimax game value `L n` by Ilia Pauzner using Gemini 4 Argon.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_872.parts.ii :
    ¬ ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (L n : ℝ) ≥ (1 - ε) * n / 2

statements.name: Erdos872.erdos_872.trivial_upper_bound
statements.doc:
A trivial upper bound: a play can claim at most the $n - 1$ elements of $\{2, \dots, n\}$, so
$L(n) \leq n - 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_872.trivial_upper_bound (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    L n ≤ n - 1

statements.name: Erdos872.erdos_872.variants.prime_question
statements.doc:
Forum-related variant: how small can a maximal primitive subset of $\{2, \dots, n\}$ be?
The set of primes in $\{2, \dots, n\}$ is a maximal primitive subset of size $\pi(n)$, and the forum
thread asks whether this is the smallest possible for all $n \geq 2$. Equivalently: must every
completed play of the saturation game, by both players and regardless of strategy, claim at least
$\pi(n)$ elements? (Terminal positions of the game are exactly the maximal primitive subsets.)

The answer is yes. For each prime $q \le n$, let $q^k$ be the largest power of $q$ that is at most
$n$. Maximality gives an element of $A$ comparable with $q^k$ under divisibility, and no element is
comparable with two such prime powers, so $|A| \ge \pi(n)$. This argument was posted on the forum
by old-bielefelder (May 2026); the statement also appears as Theorem 2.3(i) of
[El23] S. Elsakhawy, *Independence and domination in divisor graph and mod-difference graphs*,
J. Egyptian Math. Soc. 31 (2023).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_872.variants.prime_question :
    ∀ n ≥ 2, ∀ A : Finset ℕ, Maximal (IsPrimitive n) A →
      ((Finset.Icc 2 n).filter Nat.Prime).card ≤ A.card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 873
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/873](https://www.erdosproblems.com/873)
- [Er92c] Erdős, P., Some of my forgotten problems in number theory. Hardy-Ramanujan J. 15
  (1992), 34-50.

statements.name: Erdos873.erdos_873
statements.doc:
Let $A = \{a_1 < a_2 < \dots\} \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and let $F(A,X,k)$ count the number of $i$
such that $[a_i,a_{i+1}, \dots ,a_{i+k−1}] < X$, where the left-hand side is the least common
multiple. Is it true that, for every $\epsilon > 0$, there exists some $k$ such that
$F(A,X,k) < X^\epsilon$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_873 : ∀ᵉ (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ε > (0 : ℝ)), 0 < a 0 → StrictMono a →
    ∃ k, ∀ X > 0, F a X k < (X^ε).toEReal

statements.name: Erdos873.erdos_873.variants.triple_upper_bound
statements.doc: The upper bound (2).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_873.variants.triple_upper_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), 0 < a 0 → StrictMono a →
        ∀ᶠ X : ℝ in Filter.atTop,
          (F a X 3 : EReal) ≤
            (C * X ^ (1 / 3 : ℝ) * Real.log X).toEReal

statements.name: Erdos873.erdos_873.variants.triple_lower_bound_infinitely_often
statements.doc: The infinitely-often lower bound (3).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_873.variants.triple_lower_bound_infinitely_often :
    ∃ (a : ℕ → ℕ) (c : ℝ),
      0 < a 0 ∧ StrictMono a ∧ 0 < c ∧
        ∀ X₀ : ℝ, ∃ X > X₀,
          (c * X ^ (1 / 3 : ℝ) * Real.log X).toEReal ≤ (F a X 3 : EReal)

statements.name: Erdos873.erdos_873.variants.supplement_all_scale
statements.doc:
There may be a sequence for which the lower bound in (3) holds for every $X$, that is, for
all sufficiently large $X$ rather than only for infinitely many $X$. (Asking it for every
$X > 0$ fails trivially: the lcm of three distinct positive integers is at least $4$, so
$F(A,X,3) = 0$ for $X \le 4$.)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_873.variants.supplement_all_scale :
    ¬ ∃ (a : ℕ → ℕ) (c : ℝ),
      0 < a 0 ∧ StrictMono a ∧ 0 < c ∧
        ∀ᶠ X : ℝ in Filter.atTop,
          (c * X ^ (1 / 3 : ℝ) * Real.log X).toEReal ≤ (F a X 3 : EReal)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 875
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/875](https://www.erdosproblems.com/875)
- [Er98] Erdős, P., *Some of my new and almost new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Number theory (Eger, 1996) (1998), 169-180.
- [Er62c] Erdős, P., *Some remarks on number theory. III* (in Hungarian). Mat. Lapok 13 (1962),
  28-38. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1962-22.pdf)
- [ENS91] Erdős, P., Nicolas, J.-L. and Sárközy, A., *Sommes de sous-ensembles*. J. Théor. Nombres
  Bordeaux 3 (1991), 55-72. [Numdam](https://www.numdam.org/item/JTNB_1991__3_1_55_0/)
- [DeFr99] Deshouillers, J.-M. and Freiman, G. A., *On an additive problem of Erdős and Straus,
  2*. Astérisque 258 (1999), 141-148. [Numdam](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1999__258__141_0/)

The finite version of this problem is [erdosproblems.com/874](https://www.erdosproblems.com/874).

statements.name: Erdos875.erdos_875
statements.doc:
Let $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}\subset \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that the sets
$$S_r = \{ a_1+\cdots +a_r : a_1<\cdots<a_r\in A\}$$
are disjoint for distinct $r\geq 1$. How fast can such a sequence grow? How small can
$a_{n+1}-a_n$ be? In particular, for which $c$ is it possible that $a_{n+1}-a_n\leq n^{c}$?

A problem of Deshouillers and Erdős [Er98] (an infinite version of
[874](https://www.erdosproblems.com/874)). Such sets are sometimes called admissible. We state the
last question: the set of such $c$ is `erdos_875.answer`. The bound is required for all large $n$,
since otherwise the first few $n$ would constrain the answer. The first two questions are not
formalised separately. Erdős also writes that it is not completely trivial to find such a sequence
with $a_{n+1}/a_n\to 1$ (not formalised).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_875 :
    {c : ℝ | ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ IsAdmissible A ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (gap A n : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ c} = erdos_875.answer

statements.name: Erdos875.erdos_875.variants.erdos_nicolas_sarkozy
statements.doc:
Erdős, Nicolas and Sárközy [ENS91, Theorem 2] constructed an infinite admissible set $A$ with
$$A(x)=\lvert\{a\in A: a\leq x\}\rvert \gg x^{5-2\sqrt6}.$$
The implied constant is positive and the inequality is required for all large $x$. This improves
a result of Erdős [Er62c], who obtained $A(x)\gg x^{c}$ for some unspecified $c>0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_875.variants.erdos_nicolas_sarkozy :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ IsAdmissible A ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
      ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, c * (x : ℝ) ^ (5 - 2 * Real.sqrt 6) ≤ (countingFunction A x : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos875.erdos_875.variants.polynomial_gaps
statements.doc:
Since $5-2\sqrt6=(5+2\sqrt6)^{-1}$, the result of [ENS91, Theorem 2] gives
$a_n\ll n^{5+2\sqrt6}$, hence $a_{n+1}-a_n\leq a_{n+1}\ll n^{5+2\sqrt6}$. So every
$c>5+2\sqrt6$ is possible in the main question.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_875.variants.polynomial_gaps (c : ℝ) (hc : 5 + 2 * Real.sqrt 6 < c) :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ IsAdmissible A ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (gap A n : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ c

statements.name: Erdos875.erdos_875.variants.deshouillers_freiman
statements.doc:
Deshouillers and Freiman [DeFr99, Theorem 1] proved a conjecture of Erdős on the finite version
([874](https://www.erdosproblems.com/874)): for all sufficiently large $N$, every admissible set
$A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ satisfies
$$\lvert A\rvert\leq 2\sqrt{N+\tfrac14}-1.$$
This is sharp: by Straus, the set of $k$ consecutive integers ending at $N$ is admissible if and
only if $k\leq 2\sqrt{N+\frac14}-1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_875.variants.deshouillers_freiman :
    ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N → ∀ A : Finset ℕ, (A : Set ℕ) ⊆ Set.Icc 1 N →
      IsAdmissible (A : Set ℕ) → (A.card : ℝ) ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt ((N : ℝ) + 1 / 4) - 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 876
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/876](https://www.erdosproblems.com/876)
- [Er62c] Erdős, P., *Some remarks on number theory. III* (in Hungarian). Mat. Lapok 13 (1962),
  28-38. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1962-22.pdf)
- [Er75b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Journées Arithmétiques
  de Bordeaux (Conf., Univ. Bordeaux, 1974), Astérisque 24-25 (1975), 295-310.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-30.pdf)
- [Er77c] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III*. Number theory day
  (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976), Lecture Notes in Math. 626 (1977), 43-72.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1977-27.pdf)
- [Er98] Erdős, P., *Some of my new and almost new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Number theory (Eger, 1996) (1998), 169-180.
- [DEM99] Deshouillers, J.-M., Erdős, P. and Melfi, G., *On a question about sum-free sequences*.
  Discrete Math. 200 (1999), 49-54.
- [LeOS77] Levine, E. and O'Sullivan, J., *An upper estimate for the reciprocal sum of a sum-free
  sequence*. Acta Arith. 34 (1977), 9-24.
- [Ab87] Abbott, H. L., *On sum-free sequences*. Acta Arith. 48 (1987), 93-96.

See also [erdosproblems.com/790](https://www.erdosproblems.com/790).

statements.name: Erdos876.erdos_876.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}\subset \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite sum-free set - that is, there are no
solutions to
$$a=b_1+\cdots+b_r$$
with $b_1<\cdots<b_r<a\in A$. How small can $a_{n+1}-a_n$ be? Is it possible that
$a_{n+1}-a_n<n$?

The gap question is discussed by Erdős in [Er98]. We state the second question. The inequality
$a_{n+1}-a_n<n$ is required for all large $n$, because it fails for $n=1$. The first question is
vaguer and is not formalised.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_876.parts.i :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ IsSubsetSumFree A ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, gap A n < n

statements.name: Erdos876.erdos_876.parts.ii
statements.doc:
In [Er75b] and [Er77c] Erdős asks to determine the maximum possible value of
$\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}$. Erdős had proved this is $<100$, and Sullivan had shown that this is
$<4$, and Sullivan conjectured the maximum is slightly larger than $2$ [Er77c, p. 52].

Here $A$ ranges over infinite sum-free sets, and the maximum is read as the supremum
`maxRecipSum`.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_876.parts.ii : maxRecipSum = erdos_876.parts.ii.answer

statements.name: Erdos876.erdos_876.variants.density_zero
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er62c, Theorem I] proved that a sum-free set has density zero (restated as
[DEM99, Theorem 1]).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_876.variants.density_zero (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hs : IsSubsetSumFree A) :
    A.HasDensity 0

statements.name: Erdos876.erdos_876.variants.recip_sum_lt
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er62c, Theorem II] proved that $\sum_{a\in A}1/a$ converges and is $<103$ for every
infinite sum-free set $A$; see also [Er75b, p. 302] and [DEM99, p. 49]. The later paper
[Er77c, p. 52] states the bound as $100$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_876.variants.recip_sum_lt (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hs : IsSubsetSumFree A) :
    ∃ s : ℝ, s < 103 ∧ HasSum (fun a : A ↦ (1 : ℝ) / (a : ℕ)) s

statements.name: Erdos876.erdos_876.variants.recip_sum_bounds
statements.doc:
Let $R$ be the supremum of $\sum_j 1/n_j$ over sum-free sequences $\{n_j\}$. Levine and O'Sullivan
[LeOS77] proved $R<4$ (and $R>2.035$), and Abbott [Ab87] improved the lower bound to $R>2.064$,
as reported in [DEM99, p. 50].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_876.variants.recip_sum_bounds : 2.064 < maxRecipSum ∧ maxRecipSum < 4

statements.name: Erdos876.erdos_876.variants.dem_ratio
statements.doc:
Deshouillers, Erdős and Melfi [DEM99, Theorem 3] constructed an infinite sum-free set with
$a_{n+1}/a_n\to 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_876.variants.dem_ratio :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ IsSubsetSumFree A ∧
      Tendsto (fun k : ℕ ↦ (Nat.nth (· ∈ A) (k + 1) : ℝ) / (Nat.nth (· ∈ A) k : ℝ))
        atTop (nhds 1)

statements.name: Erdos876.erdos_876.variants.dem_polynomial
statements.doc:
Deshouillers, Erdős and Melfi [DEM99, Theorem 4] proved that for every $\delta>0$ there is an
infinite sum-free set with $a_n\sim n^{3+\delta}$; we state the consequence $a_n\ll n^{3+\delta}$.
The site writes $a_n\sim n^{3+o(1)}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_876.variants.dem_polynomial (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ IsSubsetSumFree A ∧
      ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ k : ℕ, (Nat.nth (· ∈ A) k : ℝ) ≤ C * ((k : ℝ) + 1) ^ (3 + δ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 877
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/877](https://www.erdosproblems.com/877)
- [CaEr90] Cameron, P. J. and Erdős, P., _On the number of sets of integers with various
  properties_. (1990), 61-79.
- [Er98] Erdős, Paul, _Some of my new and almost new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory_. Number theory (Eger, 1996) (1998), 169-180.
- [LuSc01] Łuczak, Tomasz and Schoen, Tomasz, _On the number of maximal sum-free sets_. Proc.
  Amer. Math. Soc. (2001), 2205--2207.
- [BLST15] Balogh, József and Liu, Hong and Sharifzadeh, Maryam and Treglown, Andrew, _The
  number of maximal sum-free subsets of integers_. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (2015), 4713--4721.
- [BLST18] Balogh, József and Liu, Hong and Sharifzadeh, Maryam and Treglown, Andrew, _Sharp
  bound on the number of maximal sum-free subsets of integers_. J. Eur. Math. Soc. (JEMS) (2018),
  1885--1911.

statements.name: Erdos877.erdos_877
statements.doc:
Let $f_m(n)$ count the number of maximal sum-free subsets $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ - that is,
there are no solutions to $a=b+c$ in $A$ and $A$ is maximal with this property. Estimate $f(n)$
- is it true that $f_m(n)=o(2^{n/2})$?

A problem of Cameron and Erdős. Łuczak and Schoen [LuSc01] proved that there exists a constant
$c<1/2$ such that $f_m(n)<2^{cn}$, resolving this question. Balogh, Liu, Sharifzadeh, and
Treglown [BLST15] proved that $f_m(n)=2^{(\frac{1}{4}+o(1))n}$.

See [748](https://www.erdosproblems.com/748) for the non-maximal case.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_877 :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (fm n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (2 : ℝ) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)

statements.name: Erdos877.erdos_877.variants.luczak_schoen
statements.doc:
Łuczak and Schoen [LuSc01] proved that there exists a constant $c<1/2$ such that
$f_m(n)<2^{cn}$ for all large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_877.variants.luczak_schoen :
    ∃ c : ℝ, c < 1 / 2 ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (fm n : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ (c * n)

statements.name: Erdos877.erdos_877.variants.cameron_erdos
statements.doc: Cameron and Erdős [CaEr90] proved that $f_m(n)>2^{n/4}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_877.variants.cameron_erdos :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (2 : ℝ) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 4) < fm n

statements.name: Erdos877.erdos_877.variants.balogh_liu_sharifzadeh_treglown
statements.doc:
Balogh, Liu, Sharifzadeh, and Treglown [BLST15] proved that
$f_m(n)=2^{(\frac{1}{4}+o(1))n}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_877.variants.balogh_liu_sharifzadeh_treglown :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ logb 2 (fm n) / n) atTop (nhds (1 / 4))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 878
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/878](https://www.erdosproblems.com/878)
- [Er84e] Erdős, P., _On two unconventional number theoretic functions and on some
  related problems_. (1984), 113--121.
- [Ki26] Kitamura, K., _Erdős Problem #878 in Lean_,
  [GitHub repository](https://github.com/KitaKen1/erdos-878-lean/tree/d4a8eecf0606b3eee7342c2040a31c8c30eb5d76) (2026).

statements.name: Erdos878.erdos_878.parts.i
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for almost all $n$, $f(n)=o(n\log\log n)$ and
$F(n)\gg n\log\log n$?

The answer is yes; a Lean proof is given in [Ki26].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_878.parts.i :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.HasDensity 1 ∧
      (fun n : A ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
        (fun n : A ↦ (n : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ))) ∧
      (fun n : A ↦ (n : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ))) =O[atTop]
        (fun n : A ↦ (F n : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos878.erdos_878.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is it true that $\max_{n\le x}f(n)\sim x\log x/\log\log x$?

The answer is yes; a Lean proof is given in [Ki26].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_878.parts.ii :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦
        (maxUpTo f x : ℝ) / ((x : ℝ) * Real.log x / Real.log (Real.log x)))
        atTop (𝓝 1)

statements.name: Erdos878.erdos_878.parts.iii_all
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for all $x$, $\max_{n\le x}f(n)=\max_{n\le x}F(n)$?
Barreto noted that this is false at $x=210$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_878.parts.iii_all :
    ¬ ∀ x : ℕ, maxUpTo f x = maxUpTo F x

statements.name: Erdos878.erdos_878.parts.iii_eventually
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for all large $x$, $\max_{n\le x}f(n)=\max_{n\le x}F(n)$?

This is false, as formalized in Lean 4 by Ilia Pauzner using Gemini 4 Argon.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_878.parts.iii_eventually :
    ¬ ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, maxUpTo f x = maxUpTo F x

statements.name: Erdos878.erdos_878.parts.iv
statements.doc: Find an asymptotic formula for the number of $n<x$ such that $f(n)=F(n)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_878.parts.iv :
    (fun x : ℕ ↦
      (((Finset.Ico 1 x).filter fun n ↦ f n = F n).card : ℝ))
      ~[atTop] erdos_878.parts.iv.answer

statements.name: Erdos878.erdos_878.parts.v
statements.doc: Find an asymptotic formula for $H(x)=\sum_{n<x}f(n)/n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_878.parts.v :
    H ~[atTop] erdos_878.parts.v.answer

statements.name: Erdos878.erdos_878.parts.vi
statements.doc: Is it true that $H(x)\ll x\log\log\log\log x$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_878.parts.vi :
    H =O[atTop] fun x : ℕ ↦
        (x : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log (Real.log (x : ℝ))))

statements.name: Erdos878.erdos_878.variants.second_question_subsequence
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er84e] proved that $\max_{n\le x}f(n)\sim x\log x/\log\log x$
for a sequence of $x\to\infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_878.variants.second_question_subsequence :
    ∃ X : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto X atTop atTop ∧
      Tendsto (fun k : ℕ ↦
        (maxUpTo f (X k) : ℝ) /
          ((X k : ℝ) * Real.log (X k) / Real.log (Real.log (X k))))
        atTop (𝓝 1)

statements.name: Erdos878.erdos_878.variants.proposed_first_question_sharp
statements.doc:
For almost all $n$, $F(n)\sim \frac12 n\log\log n$.
A Lean proof is given in [Ki26].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_878.variants.proposed_first_question_sharp :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.HasDensity 1 ∧
      Tendsto (fun n : A ↦
        (F n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ))))
        atTop (𝓝 (1 / 2 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos878.erdos_878.variants.H_div_self_limsup_infinite
statements.doc: Erdős [Er84e] showed that $\limsup_{x\to\infty}H(x)/x=\infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_878.variants.H_div_self_limsup_infinite :
    ∀ C : ℝ, ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, C ≤ H x / (x : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos878.erdos_878.variants.H_div_self_liminf_finite
statements.doc: Erdős [Er84e] showed that $\liminf_{x\to\infty}H(x)/x<\infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_878.variants.H_div_self_liminf_finite :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, H x / (x : ℝ) ≤ C

statements.name: Erdos878.erdos_878.variants.H_upper_triple_log
statements.doc: Erdős [Er84e] proved that $H(x)\ll x\log\log\log x$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_878.variants.H_upper_triple_log :
    H =O[atTop] fun x : ℕ ↦
      (x : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log (x : ℝ)))

statements.name: Erdos878.erdos_878.variants.H_lower_quadruple_log_infinitely_often
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er84e] proved that $x\log\log\log\log x\ll H(x)$;
this entry records the infinitely-often consequence.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_878.variants.H_lower_quadruple_log_infinitely_often :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
      c * ((x : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log (Real.log (x : ℝ))))) ≤ H x

statements.name: Erdos878.erdos_878.variants.original_formula_17
statements.doc:
Formula (17) of [Er84e]: does $(x h(x)-m(x))/x\to\infty$?

The answer is yes; a Lean proof is given in [Ki26].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_878.variants.original_formula_17 :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦
        ((x * h x - m x : ℕ) : ℝ) / (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 881
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/881](https://www.erdosproblems.com/881)

statements.name: Erdos881.erdos_881
statements.doc:
Let `A ⊂ ℕ` be an additive basis of order `k` which is minimal in the sense that
if `B ⊂ A` is any infinite set, then `A \ B` is not a basis of order `k`.

Must there exist an infinite `B ⊂ A` such that `A \ B`
is an additive basis of order `k + 1`?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_881 :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ),
      IsMinimalAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder k A →
        ∃ (B : Set ℕ), B ⊆ A ∧ B.Infinite ∧
          (A \ B).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder (k + 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 882
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/882](https://www.erdosproblems.com/882)
- [Er98] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my new and almost new problems and results in combinatorial
  number theory*. Number theory (Eger, 1996) (1998), 169-180.
- [ELRSS99] Erdős, P., Lev, V., Rauzy, G., Sándor, C. and Sárközy, A., *Greedy algorithm,
  arithmetic progressions, subset sums and divisibility*. Discrete Math. (1999), 119-135.
- [Erdős Problem 1](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1) for the upper bound.
- [Alexeev] Boris Alexeev's sorry-free Lean 4 formalisation of the lower bound,
  [plby/lean-proofs](https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos882.lean).

statements.name: Erdos882.erdos_882
statements.doc:
What is the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that in the set
$$\left\{ \sum_{a\in S} a : \emptyset\neq S\subseteq A\right\}$$
no two distinct elements divide each other?

A problem of Erdős and Sárközy. The answer is $(1+o(1))\log_2 n$: the lower bound
$\lvert A\rvert > \log_2 n - 1$ is achieved by the construction of Erdős, Lev, Rauzy, Sándor
and Sárközy [ELRSS99] (see `erdos_882.variants.lower_bound`), while
[Erdős Problem 1](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1) gives
$\lvert A\rvert \leq \log_2 n + \tfrac{1}{2}\log_2\log n + O(1)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_882 :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (maxAntichainCard n : ℝ) / Real.logb 2 n)
      Filter.atTop (nhds 1)

statements.name: Erdos882.erdos_882.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős, Lev, Rauzy, Sándor and Sárközy [ELRSS99] proved that
$\lvert A\rvert > \log_2 n - 1$ is achievable, taking
$A = \{2^m - 2^{m-1}, 2^m - 2^{m-2}, \ldots, 2^m - 1\}$.

The key property of this construction is that distinct nonempty subsets have subset sums
which never divide one another.

The linked theorem `no_div` is phrased in terms of index sets $S \subseteq \{0, \ldots, m-1\}$,
i.e. $\sum_{i \in S_1} (2^m - 2^i) \nmid \sum_{i \in S_2} (2^m - 2^i)$ for distinct nonempty
$S_1, S_2$; it transfers to subsets of `A m` via the injectivity of $i \mapsto 2^m - 2^i$
(see `card_A`).
statements.statement: theorem erdos_882.variants.lower_bound (m : ℕ) : IsSubsetSumAntichain (A m)

statements.name: Erdos882.erdos_882.variants.lower_bound_explicit
statements.doc:
The lower bound of [ELRSS99] in quantitative form: for every $n \geq 1$ there is a subset-sum
antichain $A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, n\}$ with $\lvert A\rvert > \log_2 n - 1$, namely $A_m$
with $m = \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$ (by `erdos_882.variants.lower_bound`, `A_subset_Icc`
and `card_A`).

A sorry-free Lean 4 proof of this statement is the theorem `erdos_882` of [Alexeev].
That formalisation expresses the antichain condition as primitivity of the *set* of nonempty
subset sums (no element divides another one). For $A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, n\}$ this is
equivalent to `IsSubsetSumAntichain A`: if two distinct subsets had the same sum, then
removing their common elements would leave two disjoint nonempty subsets with a common sum
$t \geq 1$, so that $t$ and $2t$ would both be nonempty subset sums.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_882.variants.lower_bound_explicit (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    Real.logb 2 n - 1 < (maxAntichainCard n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos882.erdos_882.variants.sandor
statements.doc:
Sándor's construction (reported without reference in [Er98]) is claimed to achieve
$\lvert A\rvert = (1-o(1))\log_2 n$ with $A = \{2^i + m 2^m : 0 \leq i < m\}$ and
$n = 2^{m-1} + m 2^m$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_882.variants.sandor (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) :
    IsSubsetSumAntichain ((Finset.range m).image (fun i => 2 ^ i + m * 2 ^ m))

statements.name: Erdos882.erdos_882.variants.greedy
statements.doc: The greedy algorithm shows that $\lvert A\rvert \geq (1-o(1))\log_3 n$ is possible.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_882.variants.greedy :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop, (Real.logb 3 n - 1 : ℝ) ≤ (maxAntichainCard n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 883
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/883](https://www.erdosproblems.com/883)
- [ErSa97] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, G. N., On cycles in the coprime graph of integers.
  Electron. J. Combin. (1997), Research Paper 8.
- [Sa99] Sárközy, G. N., Complete tripartite subgraphs in the coprime graph of integers.
  Discrete Math. (1999), 227-238.

statements.name: Erdos883.erdos_883.parts.i
statements.doc:
For $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ let $G(A)$ be the graph with vertex set $A$, where two
integers are joined by an edge if they are coprime.

Is it true that if
$$|A| > \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + \lfloor n/3 \rfloor - \lfloor n/6 \rfloor$$
then $G(A)$ contains all odd cycles of length $\leq n/3 + 1$?

A problem of Erdős and Sárközy [ErSa97].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_883.parts.i :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Finset ℕ),
      A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n →
      n / 2 + n / 3 - n / 6 < A.card →
      ∀ l : ℕ, Odd l → 3 ≤ l → l ≤ n / 3 + 1 →
        l ∈ (coprimeGraph.induce (A : Set ℕ)).oddCycleLengths

statements.name: Erdos883.erdos_883.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for every $\ell\geq 1$, if $n$ is sufficiently large and
$$|A| > \lfloor n/2\rfloor + \lfloor n/3\rfloor - \lfloor n/6\rfloor$$
then $G(A)$ must contain a complete $(1,\ell,\ell)$ tripartite graph on $2\ell+1$ vertices?

The second question was solved by Sárközy [Sa99], who proved this with
$\ell \gg \log n/\log\log n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_883.parts.ii :
    ∀ l : ℕ, 1 ≤ l → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℕ,
      A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n →
      n / 2 + n / 3 - n / 6 < A.card →
      (SimpleGraph.completeMultipartiteGraph (fun i : Fin 3 ↦ Fin (![1, l, l] i))).IsContained
        (coprimeGraph.induce (A : Set ℕ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 884
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/884](https://www.erdosproblems.com/884)
- [Tao25](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/erdos-884.pdf)
- [Larsen](https://github.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-884/blob/main/884.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos884.erdos_884
statements.doc:
For a natural number n, let $1 = d_1 < \dotsc < d_{\tau(n)} = n$ denote the divisors of $n$
in increasing order.
Does it hold that
$\sum_{1 \le i < j \le \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_j - d_i} \ll 1 + \sum_{1 \le i < \tau(n)}
 \frac{1}{d_{i + 1} - d_i}$
for $n \to \infty$, i.e.
$\sum_{1 \le i < j \le \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_j - d_i} \in O \left( 1 + \sum_{1 \le i < \tau(n)}
 \frac{1}{d_{i + 1} - d_i} \right)$?

This conjecture has been **disproved**:
- In September 2025, Terence Tao gave a conditional _negative_ answer assuming the prime tuples
  conjecture, see `erdos_884_false_of_hardy_littlewood` for this implication.
- Daniel Larsen subsequently gave an
  [unconditional disproof](https://github.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-884/blob/main/884.pdf).

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/884](https://www.erdosproblems.com/884)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_884 :
    ¬ Erdos884Prop

statements.name: Erdos884.erdos_884_false_of_hardy_littlewood
statements.doc:
In September 2025, Terence Tao gave a conditional _negative_ answer to Erdős problem 884,
disproving it under the assumption of the *qualitative Hardy–Littlewood prime tuples
conjecture*, see Conjecture 1.1 and Theorem 1.1 of
[Tao25](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/erdos-884.pdf).

The qualitative conjecture states that for every admissible tuple $(h_1, \dotsc, h_k)$ of
integers, i.e. one which avoids at least one residue class modulo $p$ for every prime $p$,
there are infinitely many natural numbers $n$ such that $n + h_1, \dotsc, n + h_k$ are all
prime. Unlike the full Hardy–Littlewood conjecture, it does not give an asymptotic for the
number of such $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_884_false_of_hardy_littlewood
    (hHL : ∀ H : Finset ℤ, (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ a : ℤ, ∀ h ∈ H, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ a + h) →
      {n : ℕ | ∀ h ∈ H, Prime ((n : ℤ) + h)}.Infinite) :
    ¬Erdos884Prop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 885
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/885](https://www.erdosproblems.com/885)
- [ErRo97] Erdős, P. and Rosenfeld, M., The factor-difference set of integers. (1997)
- [Ji99] Jiménez-Urroz, J., A note on a conjecture of Erdős and {R}osenfeld. (1999)
- [Br19] Bremner, A., On a problem of Erdős related to common factor differences. (2019)

statements.name: Erdos885.erdos_885
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for every $k \geq 1$, there exist integers $N_1 < \dots < N_k$ such that
$|\cap_i D(N_i)| \geq k$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_885 : ∀ k ≥ 1,
    ∃ Ns : Finset ℕ,
      (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧
      Ns.card = k ∧
      (⋂ n ∈ Ns, factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ k

statements.name: Erdos885.erdos_885.variants.k_eq_2
statements.doc: Erdős and Rosenfeld [ErRo97] proved this is true for $k=2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_885.variants.k_eq_2 :
    ∃ Ns : Finset ℕ,
      (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧
      Ns.card = 2 ∧
      (⋂ n ∈ Ns, factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ 2

statements.name: Erdos885.erdos_885.variants.k_eq_3
statements.doc: Jiménez-Urroz [Ji99] proved this for $k=3$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_885.variants.k_eq_3 :
    ∃ Ns : Finset ℕ,
      (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧
      Ns.card = 3 ∧
      (⋂ n ∈ Ns, factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ 3

statements.name: Erdos885.erdos_885.variants.k_eq_4
statements.doc: Bremner [Br19] proved this for $k=4$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_885.variants.k_eq_4 :
    ∃ Ns : Finset ℕ,
      (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧
      Ns.card = 4 ∧
      (⋂ n ∈ Ns, factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ 4

problems.title: Erdős Problem 886
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/886](https://www.erdosproblems.com/886)
- [ErRo97] Erdős, Paul and Rosenfeld, Moshe, The factor-difference set of integers. Acta Arith.
  (1997), 353--359.

statements.name: Erdos886.erdos_886
statements.doc:
Let $\epsilon>0$. Is it true that, for all large $n$, the number of divisors of $n$ in
$(n^{1/2},n^{1/2}+n^{1/2-\epsilon})$ is $O_\epsilon(1)$?

Erdős attributes this conjecture to Ruzsa.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_886 :
    ∀ ε > 0, ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (Erdos886Divisors n ε 1).card ≤ K

statements.name: Erdos886.erdos_886.variants.rosenfeld_infinite
statements.doc:
Erdős and Rosenfeld [ErRo97] proved that there are infinitely many $n$ such that there are
four divisors of $n$ in $(n^{1/2},n^{1/2}+16n^{1/4})$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_886.variants.rosenfeld_infinite :
    Set.Infinite {n | 4 ≤ (Erdos886Divisors n (1/4) 16).card}

statements.name: Erdos886.erdos_886.variants.rosenfeld_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős and Rosenfeld [ErRo97] proved that, for any constant $C>0$, all large $n$ have at most
$1+C^2$ many divisors in $[n^{1/2}, n^{1/2}+Cn^{1/4}]$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_886.variants.rosenfeld_bound :
    ∀ C > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
    ((divisors n).filter (fun (d : ℕ) =>
      (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ (d : ℝ) ∧ (d : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) + C * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ))).card
      ≤ 1 + C ^ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 887
problems.doc:
*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/887](https://www.erdosproblems.com/887)
* [ErRo97] Erdős, Paul and Rosenfeld, Moshe, The factor-difference set of integers. Acta Arith. (1997), 353--359.

statements.name: Erdos887.erdos_887.parts.i
statements.doc:
Is there an absolute constant $K$ such that, for every $C > 0$, if $n$ is sufficiently large then
$n$ has at most $K$ divisors in $(n^{\frac{1}{2}}, n^{\frac{1}{2}} + C n^{\frac{1}{4}})$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_887.parts.i : ∀ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
    #{ d ∈ Ioo ⌊√n⌋₊ ⌈√n + C * n^((1 : ℝ) / 4)⌉₊ | d ∣ n } ≤ erdos_887.parts.i.answer

statements.name: Erdos887.erdos_887.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is there an absolute constant $K$ such that, for every $C > 0$, if $n$ is sufficiently large then
$n$ has at most $K$ divisors in $(n^{\frac{1}{2}}, n^{\frac{1}{2}} + C n^{\frac{1}{4}})$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_887.parts.ii : ∃ K, ∀ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
    #{ d ∈ Ioo ⌊√n⌋₊ ⌈√n + C * n^((1 : ℝ) / 4)⌉₊ | d ∣ n } ≤ K

statements.name: Erdos887.erdos_887.variants.rosenfeld_infinite
statements.doc:
A question of Erdős and Rosenfeld, who proved that there are infinitely many $n$ with (at least)
$4$ divisors in $(n^{\frac{1}{2}}, n^{\frac{1}{2}} + cn^{\frac{1}{4}})$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_887.variants.rosenfeld_infinite : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ),
    Infinite {n : ℕ | 4 ≤ #{ d ∈ Ioo ⌊√n⌋₊ ⌈√n + C * n^((1 : ℝ) / 4)⌉₊ | d ∣ n }}

statements.name: Erdos887.erdos_887.variants.rosenfeld_4
statements.doc:
Erdős and Rosenfeld ask whether $4$ is the best possible $K$ for the infinitude of $n$
with (at least) $K$ divisors in $(n^{\frac{1}{2}}, n^{\frac{1}{2}} + C n^{\frac{1}{4}})$, for some
constant $C > 0$. The constant cannot be taken to be $1$. Distinct divisors $d > \sqrt{n}$ give
distinct integers $d + n/d$, and a divisor in the interval has
$2\sqrt{n} < d + n/d < 2\sqrt{n} + C^2$, so for $C = 1$ there is at most one such divisor.

The answer is no. In a [forum post](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/887#post-7374)
(July 2026), m-czech showed that for $C = 31$ infinitely many $n$ have $5$ divisors in the
interval. The construction is $n = (x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 4)(x^2 - 16)(x^2 - 49)$ with
$z^2 = 56 x^2 + 65$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_887.variants.rosenfeld_4 :
    ¬ IsGreatest {K | ∃ C > (0 : ℝ),
      Infinite {n : ℕ | K ≤ #{ d ∈ Ioo ⌊√n⌋₊ ⌈√n + C * n^((1 : ℝ) / 4)⌉₊ | d ∣ n }}} 4

problems.title: Erdős Problem 888
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/888](https://www.erdosproblems.com/888)
- [Er98] Erdős, Paul, Some of my new and almost new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory. Number theory (Eger, 1996) (1998), 169-180.

statements.name: Erdos888.erdos_888
statements.doc:
What is the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that if
$a\leq b\leq c\leq d\in A$ are such that $abcd$ is a square then $ad=bc$?

This was proved by GPT-5.5 Pro (prompted by Chojecki).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_888 :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Nat.findGreatest (p n) n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop]
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log n) / Real.log n)

statements.name: Erdos888.erdos_888.variants.sarkozy
statements.doc:
Erdős claims that Sárközy proved that $\lvert A\rvert =o(n)$ (a proof of this
bound is provided by Tao in the comments).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_888.variants.sarkozy :
    (fun n ↦ (Nat.findGreatest (p n) n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (Nat.cast : ℕ → ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos888.erdos_888.variants.primes
statements.doc: The primes show that $\lvert A\rvert \gg n/\log n$ is possible.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_888.variants.primes :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Nat.findGreatest (p n) n : ℝ)) ≫ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) / Real.log n)

statements.name: Erdos888.erdos_888.variants.semiprimes
statements.doc:
Cambie and Weisenberg have noted in the comments that the set of semiprimes
also works, showing $(1+o(1))\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}n \leq \lvert A\rvert$ is achievable.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_888.variants.semiprimes :
    ∃ c : ℕ → ℝ, c =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (1 + c n) * ((n : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log n) / Real.log n) ≤ Nat.findGreatest (p n) n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 889
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/889](https://www.erdosproblems.com/889)

statements.name: Erdos889.erdos_889
statements.doc:
Let $v(n,k)$ count the prime factors of $n+k$ which
do not divide $n+i$ for $0\leq i < k$. Is it true that
$v_0(n)=\max_{k\geq 0}v(n,k)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_889 : Tendsto v₀ atTop (𝓝 ⊤)

statements.name: Erdos889.erdos_889.variants.v0_gt_1
statements.doc:
$v_0(n) > 1$ for all $n$ except $n$ = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 16

[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_889.variants.v0_gt_1 :
    ∀ n : ℕ, n ∉ ({0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 16} : Finset ℕ) → 1 < v₀ n

statements.name: Erdos889.erdos_889.variants.general
statements.doc:
Let $v_l(n) = \max_{k\geq l} v(n,k)$. For every fixed $l$,
$v_l(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$

[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_889.variants.general :
    ∀ l, Tendsto (v_l l) atTop (𝓝 ⊤)

statements.name: Erdos889.erdos_889.variants.v1_eq_1_finite
statements.doc:
Does $v_1(n) = 1$ have finite solutions?

[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_889.variants.v1_eq_1_finite :
    {n | v_l 1 n = 1}.Finite

statements.name: Erdos889.erdos_889.variants.V1_eq_1_finite
statements.doc:
Does $V_1(n) = 1$ have finite solutions?

This is a modification of `erdos_889.variants.v1_eq_1_finite`,
which might make it more amenable to attack according to [ErSe67].

Kenta Kitamura (KitaKen1 on GitHub) has given a Lean proof
([erdos-889-capital-v1-finite](https://github.com/KitaKen1/erdos-889-capital-v1-finite))
that there are only finitely many $n$ with $V_1(n) = 1$.

[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_889.variants.V1_eq_1_finite :
    {n | V_l 1 n = 1}.Finite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 890
problems.doc:
*Reference:*
- [erdosproblems.com/890](https://www.erdosproblems.com/890)
- [ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive
  integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.

statements.name: Erdos890.erdos_890.parts.a
statements.doc:
If $\omega_k(n)$ counts the number of distinct prime factors of $n$ which are $>k$, then is it true
that, for every $k\geq 1$,
$$\liminf_{n\to \infty}\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega_k(n+i)\leq k?$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_890.parts.a :
    ∀ k ≥ 1, liminf (fun n ↦ (∑ i ∈ range k, (ω_gt k (n + i) : EReal))) atTop ≤ k

statements.name: Erdos890.erdos_890.parts.b
statements.doc:
Is it true that
$$\limsup_{n\to \infty}\left(\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega(n+i)\right) \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}=1,$$
where $\omega$ counts the number of distinct prime factors without restriction?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_890.parts.b :
    ∀ k ≥ 1, limsup (fun n ↦ (∑ i ∈ range k, (ω (n + i) : EReal)) *
      (log (log n) / log n)) atTop = 1

statements.name: Erdos890.erdos_890.variants.liminf_lower_bound
statements.doc:
A question of Erdős and Selfridge [ErSe67], who observe that
$\liminf_{n\to \infty}\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega(n+i)\geq k+\pi(k)-1$ for every $k$. This follows from
Pólya's theorem that the set of $k$-smooth integers has unbounded gaps - indeed,
$n(n+1)\cdots (n+k-1)$ is divisible by all primes $\leq k$ and, provided $n$ is large, all but at
most one of $n,n+1,\ldots,n+k-1$ has a prime factor $>k$ by Pólya's theorem.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_890.variants.liminf_lower_bound (k : ℕ) :
    liminf (fun n ↦ (∑ i ∈ range k, (ω (n + i) : EReal))) atTop ≥ k + π k - 1

statements.name: Erdos890.erdos_890.variants.omega_limsup
statements.doc: It is a classical fact that $\limsup_{n\to \infty}\omega(n)\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}=1.$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_890.variants.omega_limsup :
    limsup (fun n ↦ (ω n : EReal) * (log (log n) / log n)) atTop = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 891
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/891](https://www.erdosproblems.com/891)
- [Po18] Pólya, Georg, Zur arithmetischen {U}ntersuchung der {P}olynome. Math. Z. (1918), 143--148.
- [Wikipedia] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture

statements.name: Erdos891.erdos_891
statements.doc:
Let $2=p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes and $k\geq 2$. Is it true that, for all sufficiently large
$n$, there must exist an integer in $[n,n+p_1\cdots p_k)$ with $>k$ many prime factors?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_891 :
    ∀ k ≥ 2, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
    ∃ m ∈ Ico n (n + ∏ i ∈ range k, i.nth Nat.Prime), k < ω m

statements.name: Erdos891.erdos_891.variants.schinzel
statements.doc:
Schinzel deduced from Pólya's theorem [Po18] (that the sequence of $k$-smooth integers has unbounded
gaps) that this is true with $p_1\cdots p_k$ replaced by $p_1\cdots p_{k-1}p_{k+1}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_891.variants.schinzel :
    ∀ k ≥ 2, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∃ m ∈ Ico n (n + (∏ i ∈ range (k - 1), i.nth Nat.Prime) * k.nth Nat.Prime),
      k < ω m

statements.name: Erdos891.erdos_891.variants.case_k_2
statements.doc:
This is unknown even for $k=2$ - that is, is it true that in every interval of $6$
(sufficiently large) consecutive integers there must exist one with at least $3$ prime factors?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_891.variants.case_k_2 :
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∃ m ∈ Ico n (n + 6), 3 ≤ ω m

statements.name: Erdos891.erdos_891.variants.weisenberg
statements.doc:
Weisenberg has observed that Dickson's conjecture implies the answer is no if we replace
$p_1\cdots p_k$ with $p_1\cdots p_k-1$. Indeed, let $L_k$ be the lowest common multiple of all
integers at most $p_1\cdots p_k$. By Dickson's conjecture [Wikipedia], there are infinitely many
$n'$ such that $\frac{L_k}{m}n'+1$ is prime for all $1\leq m < p_1\cdots p_k$. It follows that,
if $n=L_kn'+1$, then all integers in $[n,n+p_1\cdots p_k-1)$ have at most $k$ prime factors.

The statement is conditional on Dickson's conjecture, formalised as
`Dickson.dickson_conjecture`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_891.variants.weisenberg (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 2)
    (hdickson : type_of% Dickson.dickson_conjecture) :
    ∃ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∀ m ∈ Ico n (n + (∏ i ∈ range k, i.nth Nat.Prime) - 1),
      ω m ≤ k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 893
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/893](https://www.erdosproblems.com/893)
- [KoLu25] V. Kovač and F. Luca, On the number of divisors of Mersenne numbers. arXiv:2506.04883 (2025).

statements.name: Erdos893.erdos_893
statements.doc:
Does the limit $\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{f(2n)}{f(n)}$ tend to infinity?

(Other finite limits have been ruled out by [KoLu25], see below)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_893 :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (f (2 * n) : ℝ) / (f n : ℝ)) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos893.erdos_893.variants.unbounded
statements.doc:
Kovač and Luca [KoLu25] (building on a heuristic independently found by
Cambie (personal communication)) have shown that there is no finite limit, in that
$\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{f(2n)}{f(n)}$ is unbounded.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_893.variants.unbounded :
   ¬ BddAbove (Set.range fun n : ℕ => (f (2 * n) : ℝ) / f n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 894
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/894](https://www.erdosproblems.com/894)
- [Ka01] Katznelson, Y., *Chromatic numbers of Cayley graphs on $\mathbb{Z}$ and recurrence*.
  Combinatorica (2001), 211--219.
- [PeSc10] Peres, Yuval and Schlag, Wilhelm, *Two Erdős problems on lacunary sequences: chromatic
  number and Diophantine approximation*. Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. (2010), 295--300.

statements.name: Erdos894.erdos_894
statements.doc:
Let $A=\{n_1<n_2<\cdots\}\subset \mathbb{N}$ be a lacunary sequence (so there exists some
$\epsilon>0$ with $n_{k+1}\geq (1+\epsilon)n_k$ for all $k$). Is it true that there must exist a
finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ with no monochromatic solutions to $a-b\in A$?

Asked by Erdős in 1987, according to Katznelson [Ka01]. In other words, does the Cayley graph
defined on $\mathbb{Z}$ by a lacunary sequence have a finite chromatic number?

Katznelson observed that a positive solution to the problem follows from the answer to
[464](https://www.erdosproblems.com/464), which yields an irrational $\theta$ and $\delta>0$
such that $\inf_k \| \theta n_k\|>\delta$. In particular, the solution to
[464](https://www.erdosproblems.com/464) implies the answer to this question is yes, with the
best known quantitative bound, due to Peres and Schlag [PeSc10], being that there is a colouring
with no solutions using at most $\ll \epsilon^{-1}\log(1/\epsilon)$ colours.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_894 :
    ∀ n : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono n → (∀ k, 0 < n k) → IsLacunary n →
      ∃ (r : ℕ) (c : ℕ → Fin r), ∀ b k, c (b + n k) ≠ c b

problems.title: Erdős Problem 895
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/895](https://www.erdosproblems.com/895)
- [Er95d] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems in combinatorial set theory*. Publ. Inst. Math.
  (Beograd) (N.S.) (1995), 61-65.

statements.name: Erdos895.erdos_895
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $n$, if $G$ is a triangle-free graph on
$\{1,\ldots,n\}$ then there must exist three independent points $a,b,a+b$?

A problem of Erdős and Hajnal [Er95d]. The stated problem has been resolved by Barber (personal
communication) who verified using a SAT solver that this is true for all $n\geq 18$.

statements.name: Erdos895.erdos_895.variants.eighteen
statements.doc:
Barber's sharp form of [erdős_895](https://www.erdosproblems.com/895): every triangle-free graph on
$\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $n\geq 18$ contains three independent points $a,b,a+b$.

statements.name: Erdos895.erdos_895.variants.hindman
statements.doc:
Hajnal thought that there is in fact an independent set which is a Hindman set - that is, an
independent set of the shape
$$\left\{ \sum_{i\in S}a_i : S\subseteq \{1,\ldots,k\}\right\}$$
for some $a_1,\ldots,a_k$ (provided $n$ is sufficiently large depending on $k$).

The general question of an independent Hindman set remains open. Here the $a_i$ are taken to be
distinct positive integers and $S$ ranges over the nonempty subsets of $\{1,\ldots,k\}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_895.variants.hindman :
    ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Set.Icc 1 n), G.CliqueFree 3 →
      ∃ a : Fin k → ℕ, StrictMono a ∧ ∃ I : Set (Set.Icc 1 n), G.IsIndepSet I ∧
        Subtype.val '' I = {m | ∃ S : Finset (Fin k), S.Nonempty ∧ m = ∑ i ∈ S, a i}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 897
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/897](https://www.erdosproblems.com/897)
- [Ar25] Archivara Math Research Agent, [An Additive Counterexample: Erdős Problem 897](https://archivara.org/paper/df04f023-6ef0-4c52-bd12-18cdaa8f0741) (2025)
- [ArWu25] Aristotle, operated mostly by L. Wu, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 897](https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos897.lean) (2025)
- [Wi70] E. Wirsing, A characterization of $\log n$ as an additive arithmetic function.
  Symposia Math. (1970), 45-57.
- [Wi81] E. Wirsing, Additive and completely additive functions with restricted growth.
  Recent progress in analytic number theory, Vol. 2 (Durham, 1979), 231--280 (1981).

statements.name: Erdos897.erdos_897.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$ such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n (f(n+1)−f(n))/ \log n = ∞$?

The answer is no; this follows from a construction of Wirsing [Wi81], rediscovered by
Archivara [Ar25] and formalised in Lean by Aristotle [ArWu25].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_897.parts.i : ¬ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) →
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => ((f (n+1) - f n) / (n : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos897.erdos_897.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$) such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n f(n+1)/ f(n) = ∞$?

The answer is no; the same counterexample is formalised in Lean by Aristotle [ArWu25].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_897.parts.ii : ¬ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) →
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => (f (n+1) / f n : EReal)) = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos897.erdos_897.variants.log_growth
statements.doc:
Wirsing [Wi70] proved that if $|f(n+1)−f(n)| ≤ C$ then $f(n) = c \log n + O(1)$ for some constant
$c$. This is Erdős Problem 491; see `erdos_491`, whose linked formal proof gives this statement.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_897.variants.log_growth
    (f : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b)
    (C : ℝ) (hf' : ∀ n, |f (n+1) - f n| ≤ C) :
    ∃ c, ∃ (O : ℕ → ℝ), O =O[Filter.atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
      ∀ n, f n ≤ c*Real.log n + O n

statements.name: Erdos897.erdos_897.variants.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$) such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$ and $f(p^k) = f(p)$
or $f(p^k) = kf(p)$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n (f(n+1)−f(n))/ \log n = ∞$?

The known counterexample does not satisfy either of these extra hypotheses, so this variant remains
open.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_897.variants.parts.i : ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) →
    (∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p) ∨ (∀ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime → f (p^k) = k*f p) →
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => ((f (n+1) - f n) / (n : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos897.erdos_897.variants.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$) such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$ and $f(p^k) = f(p)$
or $f(p^k) = kf(p)$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n f(n+1)/f(n) = ∞$?

The known counterexample does not satisfy either of these extra hypotheses, so this variant remains
open.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_897.variants.parts.ii : ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) →
    (∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p) ∨ (∀ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime → f (p^k) = k*f p) →
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => (f (n+1) / f n : EReal)) = ⊤

problems.title: Erdős Problem 898
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/898](https://www.erdosproblems.com/898)
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*.
  (1982), 59--79.
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Mordell_inequality)

statements.name: Erdos898.erdos_898
statements.doc:
If $A,B,C\in \mathbb{R}^2$ form a triangle and $P$ is a point in the interior then, if $N$ is
where the perpendicular from $P$ to $AB$ meets the triangle, and similarly for $M$ and $L$,
$$
\overline{PA}+\overline{PB}+\overline{PC}\geq 2(\overline{PM}+\overline{PN}+\overline{PL}).
$$

Conjectured by Erdős in 1932 (according to [Er82e]) and proved by Mordell soon afterwards, now
known as the Erdős-Mordell inequality.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_898 (A B C P L M N : ℝ²) (hABC : AffineIndependent ℝ ![A, B, C])
    (hP : P ∈ interior (convexHull ℝ ({A, B, C} : Set ℝ²)))
    (hN : N ∈ line[ℝ, A, B]) (hPN : line[ℝ, P, N].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, A, B].direction)
    (hM : M ∈ line[ℝ, B, C]) (hPM : line[ℝ, P, M].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, B, C].direction)
    (hL : L ∈ line[ℝ, C, A]) (hPL : line[ℝ, P, L].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, C, A].direction) :
    dist P A + dist P B + dist P C ≥ 2 * (dist P M + dist P N + dist P L)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 899
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/899](https://www.erdosproblems.com/899)

statements.name: Erdos899.erdos_899
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that $|A\cap \{1, ..., N\}| = o(N)$.
Is it true that
$$
\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|(A - A)\cap \{1, ..., N\}|}{|A \cap \{1, ..., N\}|} = \infty?
$$

The answer is yes, proved by Ruzsa [Ru78].

[Ru78] Ruzsa, I. Z., _On the cardinality of {$A+A$}\ and {$A-A$}_. (1978), 933--938.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_899 : ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite →
    Tendsto (fun N => (A ∩ Icc 1 N |>.ncard : ℝ) / N) atTop (𝓝 0) →
    atTop.limsup (fun N => ((A - A : Set ℕ) ∩ Icc 1 N |>.ncard : EReal) /
      (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard) = ⊤

problems.title: Erdős Problem 900
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/900](https://www.erdosproblems.com/900)
- [AKS81] Ajtai, Miklós and Komlós, János and Szemerédi, Endre, *The longest path in a random
  graph*. Combinatorica 1 (1981), 1--12.
- [Er78] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory*. Proceedings of the Ninth Southeastern Conference on Combinatorics, Graph Theory, and
  Computing (1978), 29-40. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1978-36.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos900.erdos_900
statements.doc:
There is a function $f:(1/2,\infty)\to \mathbb{R}$ such that $f(c)\to 0$ as $c\to 1/2$ and
$f(c)\to 1$ as $c\to \infty$ and every random graph with $n$ vertices and $cn$ edges has (with
high probability) a path of length at least $f(c)n$.

Conjectured by Erdős [Er78, p. 32] and proved by Ajtai, Komlós, and Szemerédi [AKS81]. We take
the uniform random graph with $\lfloor cn\rfloor$ edges, count the length of a path in edges, read
"with high probability" as probability tending to $1$ as $n\to\infty$, and require $f(c)>0$ for
every $c>1/2$ (a path of linear length). The linked formal proof uses the same uniform model,
written as uniformly random $0/1$ vectors of weight $\lfloor cn\rfloor$ indexed by the pairs of
vertices.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_900 :
    ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, (∀ c : ℝ, 1 / 2 < c → 0 < f c) ∧
      Tendsto f (𝓝[>] (1 / 2)) (𝓝 0) ∧ Tendsto f atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      ∀ c : ℝ, 1 / 2 < c → Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦
        uniformEdgeProbability n ⌊c * n⌋₊ (HasLongPath n (f c))) atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 901
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/901](https://www.erdosproblems.com/901)
- [Be77] Beck, J., On a combinatorial problem of {P}. {E}rdős and {L}. {L}ovász. Discrete Math.
  (1977), 127--131.
- [Be78] Beck, J., On {$3$}-chromatic hypergraphs. Discrete Math. (1978), 127--137.
- [Er63b] Erdős, P., On a combinatorial problem. Nordisk Mat. Tidskr. (1963), 5--10, 40.
- [Er64e] Erdős, P., On a combinatorial problem. {II}. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1964),
  445--447.
- [ErLo75] Erdős, P. and Lovász, L., Problems and results on {$3$}-chromatic hypergraphs and some
  related questions. (1975), 609--627.
- [Pl09] Pluhár, András, Greedy colorings of uniform hypergraphs. Random Structures Algorithms
  (2009), 216--221.
- [RaSr00] Radhakrishnan, Jaikumar and Srinivasan, Aravind, Improved bounds and algorithms for
  hypergraph {$2$}-coloring. Random Structures Algorithms (2000), 4--32.

statements.name: Erdos901.erdos_901
statements.doc:
Let $m(n)$ be minimal such that there is an $n$-uniform hypergraph with $m(n)$ edges which is
$3$-chromatic. Estimate $m(n)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_901 :
    (fun n ↦ ((Hypergraph.minChromaticEdges n 3).toNat : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop]
    erdos_901.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 902
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/902](https://www.erdosproblems.com/902)
- [Er63c] Erdős, P., *On a problem in graph theory*. Math. Gaz. 47 (1963), 220-223.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1963-08.pdf)
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*.
  (1982), 59-79.
- [SzSz65] Szekeres, E. and Szekeres, G., *On a problem of Schütte and Erdős*. Math. Gaz. 49
  (1965), 290-293.

statements.name: Erdos902.erdos_902
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that there is a tournament (a complete directed graph) on $f(n)$
vertices such that every set of $n$ vertices is dominated by at least one other vertex.
Estimate $f(n)$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_902 : (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_902.answer

statements.name: Erdos902.erdos_902.variants.f_one
statements.doc:
It is easy to check that $f(1)=3$ and $f(2)=7$.

This is the statement for $f(1)$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_902.variants.f_one : f 1 = 3

statements.name: Erdos902.erdos_902.variants.f_two
statements.doc:
It is easy to check that $f(1)=3$ and $f(2)=7$.

This is the statement for $f(2)$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_902.variants.f_two : f 2 = 7

statements.name: Erdos902.erdos_902.variants.erdos_lower
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er63c] proved
$$2^{n+1}-1 \leq f(n) \ll n^22^n.$$

This is the lower bound.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_902.variants.erdos_lower (n : ℕ) : 2 ^ (n + 1) - 1 ≤ f n

statements.name: Erdos902.erdos_902.variants.erdos_upper
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er63c] proved
$$2^{n+1}-1 \leq f(n) \ll n^22^n.$$

This is the upper bound, in the form proved in [Er63c, (2)]:
$\limsup_n f(n)2^{-n}n^{-2} \leq \log 2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_902.variants.erdos_upper :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (f n : ℝ) ≤ (Real.log 2 + ε) * n ^ 2 * 2 ^ n

statements.name: Erdos902.erdos_902.variants.szekeres_f_three
statements.doc:
Szekeres and Szekeres [SzSz65] proved that $f(3)=19$ and
$$n2^n \ll f(n).$$

This is the statement for $f(3)$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_902.variants.szekeres_f_three : f 3 = 19

statements.name: Erdos902.erdos_902.variants.szekeres_lower
statements.doc:
