Szekeres and Szekeres [SzSz65] proved that $f(3)=19$ and
$$n2^n \ll f(n).$$

This is the lower bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_902.variants.szekeres_lower :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c * n * 2 ^ n ≤ (f n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 903
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/903](https://www.erdosproblems.com/903)
- [EFSW85] Erdős, P. and Fowler, Joel C. and S\'os, Vera T. and Wilson, Richard M., On {$2$}-designs.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1985), 131--142.
- [dBEr48] de Bruijn, N. G. and Erdős, P., On a combinatorial problem. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch.,
  Proc. (1948), 1277--1279 = Indagationes Math. 10, 421--423.

statements.name: Erdos903.erdos_903
statements.doc:
Let $n=p^2+p+1$ for some prime power $p$, and let $A_1,\ldots,A_t\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ be a
block design (so that every pair $x,y\in \{1,\ldots,n\}$ is contained in exactly one $A_i$). Is it
true that if $t>n$ then $t\geq n+p$?

This is true, and was proved by Erdős, Fowler, Sós, and Wilson [EFSW85].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_903 :
    ∀ p : ℕ, IsPrimePow p →
    ∀ H : Finset (Finset (Fin (p ^ 2 + p + 1))),
      H.IsPairwiseBalancedDesign → p ^ 2 + p + 1 < H.card →
        p ^ 2 + p + 1 + p ≤ H.card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 904
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/904](https://www.erdosproblems.com/904)
- [BoEr75] Bollobás, B. and Erdős, P., *Unsolved Problems*. Proc. Fifth British Combinatorial Conf. (1975), 678-680.
- [Er75] Erdős, P., *Some recent progress on extremal problems in graph theory*. Congr. Numer. (1975), 3-14.
- [Ed78] Edwards, C. S., *Complete subgraphs with largest sum of vertex degrees*. (1978), 293-306.
- [Fa92] Faudree, Ralph J., *Complete subgraphs with large degree sums*. J. Graph Theory (1992), 327-334.
- [BoNi05] Bollobás, Béla and Nikiforov, Vladimir, *The sum of degrees in cliques*. Electron. J. Combin. (2005), Note 21, 10.

statements.name: Erdos904.erdos_904
statements.doc:
Let $r\geq 2$ and let $t_r(n)$ be the Turán number (the maximal number of edges in a graph on $n$
vertices with no $K_{r+1}$).

If $G$ is a graph with $n$ vertices and $m\geq t_r(n)$ edges there exists a clique on $r$ vertices,
say $x_1,\ldots,x_r$, such that $$d(x_1)+\cdots+d(x_r)\geq \frac{2rm}{n}.$$

A conjecture of Bollobás and Erdős. This was conjectured in [Er75] only in the special case $r=3$. Edwards [Ed78] proved the conjecture for $2\leq r\leq 8$ (under the additional assumption that $n\geq r^2$). Faudree [Fa92] proved the conjecture for all $r\geq 2$ provided $n>\frac{r-1}{4}r^2$. The full conjecture was proved by Bollobás and Nikiforov [BoNi05].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_904 :
    ∀ (V : Type*) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
      (r : ℕ) (hr : r ∈ Set.Icc 1 (n V)) (hm : turanNumber (n V) r ≤ #G.edgeFinset),
      ∃ s, G.IsNClique r s ∧ 2 * r * #G.edgeFinset ≤ n V * ∑ v ∈ s, G.degree v

problems.title: Erdős Problem 905
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/905](https://www.erdosproblems.com/905)
- [KhNi79] Khadzhiivanov, N. G. and Nikiforov, S. V., *Solution of a problem of P. Erdős about the
  maximum number of triangles with a common edge in a graph*. C. R. Acad. Bulgare Sci. (1979),
  1315-1318.

statements.name: Erdos905.erdos_905
statements.doc:
Every graph with $n$ vertices and $>n^2/4$ edges contains an edge which is in at least $n/6$
triangles.

A conjecture of Bollobás and Erdős. This was proved independently by Edwards (unpublished) and
Khadzhiivanov and Nikiforov [KhNi79].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_905 (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hG : (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 4 < (#G.edgeFinset : ℝ)) :
    ∃ e ∈ G.edgeFinset, (n : ℝ) / 6 ≤ (#(G.trianglesContaining e) : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 906
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/906](https://www.erdosproblems.com/906)

statements.name: Erdos906.erdos_906
statements.doc:
Does there exists an entire non-zero transcendental function `f : ℂ → ℂ` such that for any
sequence `n₀ < n₁ < ...`, `{ z | ∃ k, iteratedDeriv (n k) f z = 0 }` is dense.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 907
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/907](https://www.erdosproblems.com/907)
- [dB51] de Bruijn, N. G., *Functions whose differences belong to a given class*. Nieuw Arch.
  Wiskunde (2) (1951), 194-218.

statements.name: Erdos907.erdos_907
statements.doc:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}$ be such that $f(x+h)-f(x)$ is continuous for every $h>0$. Is it
true that
$$f=g+h$$
for some continuous $g$ and additive $h$ (i.e. $h(x+y)=h(x)+h(y)$)?

A conjecture of Erdős from the early 1950s. Answered in the affirmative by de Bruijn [dB51].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_907 :
    ∀ f : ℝ → ℝ, (∀ h : ℝ, 0 < h → Continuous fun x => f (x + h) - f x) →
      ∃ g a : ℝ → ℝ, Continuous g ∧ (∀ x y, a (x + y) = a x + a y) ∧ f = g + a

problems.title: Erdős Problem 910
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/910](https://www.erdosproblems.com/910)
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*. (1982),
  59--79. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1982-33.pdf)
- [Er44] Erdős, P., *Some remarks on connected sets*. Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 50 (1944), 442-446.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1944-06.pdf)
- [Ru58] Rudin, M. E., *A connected subset of the plane*. Fund. Math. 46 (1958), 15-24.

statements.name: Erdos910.erdos_910.parts.i
statements.doc:
Does every connected set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ contain a connected subset which is not a point and not
homeomorphic to the original set?

Asked by Erdős [Er44, p. 445], see also [Er82e, p. 77]. Following [Er44, pp. 443 and 445], a
single point is not a connected set, so $X$ is required to have more than one point.

Erdős [Er82e, p. 77] reports that Rudin, assuming the continuum hypothesis, found counterexamples
to both questions of this problem. The theorem of [Ru58] (`erdos_910.variants.rudin_CH`) does not
say that Rudin's set is homeomorphic to its connected subsets with more than one point. A
counterexample that assumes the continuum hypothesis would not disprove this statement in ZFC.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_910.parts.i :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (X : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))), IsConnected X → X.Nontrivial →
      ∃ Y ⊆ X, IsConnected Y ∧ Y.Nontrivial ∧ ¬ Nonempty (Y ≃ₜ X)

statements.name: Erdos910.erdos_910.parts.ii
statements.doc:
If $n\geq 2$ does every connected set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ contain more than $2^{\aleph_0}$ many
connected subsets?

Erdős [Er82e, p. 77] asks this for connected sets of dimension greater than one; [Er44, p. 446]
asks, for these sets, for $2^{\mathfrak{c}}$ connected subsets. The condition $n\geq 2$ alone
would make the answer trivially no: a segment in $\mathbb{R}^2$ has only $2^{\aleph_0}$ connected
subsets, its intervals. So we require `1 < smallInductiveDimension X`, which agrees with the
covering dimension for subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$. As in `erdos_910.parts.i`, single points are not
counted as connected sets [Er44, p. 445].

Rudin's set $M$ [Ru58] has at most $2^{\aleph_0}$ connected subsets, since each one with more than
one point is $M$ minus a countable set. But $M$ lies in Rudin's continuum
$I=\bigcap_n\Gamma_n^*$, where each $\Gamma_n$ is a chain of $2$-cells whose links have diameter
less than $1/n$ [Ru58, 1.1-1.2], so $I$, and hence $M$, has dimension at most one. Rudin's set
therefore does not answer this question as Erdős states it.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_910.parts.ii :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (X : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))), IsConnected X →
      1 < smallInductiveDimension X →
      𝔠 < Cardinal.mk {Y : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) |
        Y ⊆ X ∧ IsConnected Y ∧ Y.Nontrivial}

statements.name: Erdos910.erdos_910.variants.rudin_CH
statements.doc:
Assume the continuum hypothesis. Rudin [Ru58, p. 15] constructed a connected subset $M$ of the
plane, with more than one point, such that $M\setminus N$ is at most countable for every connected
subset $N\subseteq M$ with more than one point.

This disproves a conjecture of Erdős [Er44, p. 443] that every connected set $C$ contains a
connected subset $C'$ such that $C\setminus C'$ has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. Erdős [Er82e,
p. 77] reports that Rudin's examples answer both questions of this problem in the negative; see
the docstrings of `erdos_910.parts.i` and `erdos_910.parts.ii`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_910.variants.rudin_CH :
    (ℵ₁ = 𝔠) → ∃ M : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), IsConnected M ∧ M.Nontrivial ∧
      ∀ N ⊆ M, IsConnected N → N.Nontrivial → (M \ N).Countable

problems.title: Erdős Problem 911
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/911](https://www.erdosproblems.com/911)
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*.
  (1982), 59--79.

statements.name: Erdos911.erdos_911
statements.doc:
Let $\hat{R}(G)$ denote the size Ramsey number, the minimal number of edges $m$ such that there is
a graph $H$ with $m$ edges that is Ramsey for $G$.

Is there a function $f$ such that $f(x)/x\to \infty$ as $x\to \infty$ such that, for all large $C$,
if $G$ is a graph with $n$ vertices and $e\geq Cn$ edges then
$$\hat{R}(G) > f(C) e?$$

Here $\hat{R}(G)$ is `sizeRamsey G G`, and $G$ has at least one vertex (for $n = 0$ the
inequality fails trivially).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_911 :
    ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, Tendsto (fun x ↦ f x / x) atTop atTop ∧
      ∃ C₀ : ℝ, ∀ C ≥ C₀, ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), 0 < n →
        C * n ≤ (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) →
          f C * G.edgeSet.ncard < (sizeRamsey G G : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 912
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/912](https://www.erdosproblems.com/912)
 - [Er82c] Erdős, P., Miscellaneous problems in number theory. Congr. Numer. (1982), 25-45.

statements.name: Erdos912.erdos_912.variants.selfridge
statements.doc: Erdős and Selfridge prove in [Er82c] that $h(n) \asymp \left(\frac{n}{\log n}\right)^{1/2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_912.variants.selfridge :
    (fun n => (h n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (fun n => (n / Real.log n) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos912.erdos_912
statements.doc:
Prove that there exists some $c>0$ such that
$$h(n) \sim c \left(\frac{n}{\log n}\right)^{1/2}$$
as $n\to \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_912 : ∃ c > 0,
    (fun n => (h n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun n => c * (n / Real.log n) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos912.erdos_912.variants.tao
statements.doc:
A heuristic of Tao using the Cramér model for the primes suggests this is true with
$c=\sqrt{2\pi}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_912.variants.tao :
    (fun n => (h n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun n => √(2 * Real.pi) * (n / Real.log n) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 913
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/913](https://www.erdosproblems.com/913)

Reviewed by @b-mehta on 2025-05-27

statements.name: Erdos913.erdos_913
statements.doc:
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that if
$$
  n(n + 1) = \prod_i p_i^{k_i}
$$
is the factorisation into distinct primes then all exponents $k_i$ are distinct?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_913 :
    { n | Set.InjOn (n * (n + 1)).factorization (n * (n + 1)).primeFactors }.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos913.erdos_913.variants.infinite_many_8p_sq_add_one_primes
statements.doc: It is likely that there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $8p^2 - 1$ is also prime.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_913.variants.infinite_many_8p_sq_add_one_primes :
    { p | p.Prime ∧ (8 * p ^ 2 - 1).Prime }.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos913.erdos_913.variants.conditional
statements.doc: If there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $8p^2 - 1$ is prime, then this is true.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_913.variants.conditional (h : { p | p.Prime ∧ (8 * p ^ 2 - 1).Prime }.Infinite) :
    { n | Set.InjOn (n * (n + 1)).factorization (n * (n + 1)).primeFactors }.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 914
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/914](https://www.erdosproblems.com/914)
- [CoHa63] Corrádi, K. and Hajnal, A., *On the maximal number of independent circuits in a graph*.
  Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1963), 423-439.
- [HaSz70] Hajnal, A. and Szemerédi, E., *Proof of a conjecture of P. Erdős*. (1970), 601-623.
- [KiKo08] Kierstead, H. A. and Kostochka, A. V., *A short proof of the Hajnal-Szemerédi theorem on
  equitable colouring*. Combin. Probab. Comput. (2008), 265-270.

statements.name: Erdos914.erdos_914
statements.doc:
Let $r\geq 2$ and $m\geq 1$. Every graph with $rm$ vertices and minimum degree at least $m(r-1)$
contains $m$ vertex disjoint copies of $K_r$.

When $r=2$ this follows from Dirac's theorem. Corrádi and Hajnal [CoHa63] proved this when $r=3$.
Hajnal and Szemerédi [HaSz70] proved this for all $r\geq 4$.

A shorter proof was given by Kierstead and Kostochka [KiKo08].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_914 {r m : ℕ} (hr : 2 ≤ r) (hm : 1 ≤ m) {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hV : Fintype.card V = r * m)
    (hdeg : m * (r - 1) ≤ G.minDegree) :
    ∃ K : Fin m → Finset V, (∀ i, G.IsNClique r (K i)) ∧
      Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint (K i) (K j)

statements.name: Erdos914.erdos_914.variants.equitable_colouring
statements.doc:
Equivalently, every graph with $rm$ vertices and maximum degree at most $m-1$ has a proper vertex
colouring with $m$ colours in which every colour class has exactly $r$ vertices (an equitable
colouring).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_914.variants.equitable_colouring {r m : ℕ} (hr : 2 ≤ r) (hm : 1 ≤ m) {V : Type*}
    [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hV : Fintype.card V = r * m)
    (hdeg : G.maxDegree ≤ m - 1) :
    ∃ C : G.Coloring (Fin m), ∀ i, (C.colorClass i).ncard = r

problems.title: Erdős Problem 915
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/915](https://www.erdosproblems.com/915)
- [BoEr62] Bollobás, Béla and Erdős, Pál, *Extremal problems in graph theory*. Mat. Lapok (1962),
  143--152.
- [Er67b] Erdős, Paul, *Extremal problems in graph theory*. A Seminar on Graph Theory (1967),
  54-59.
- [Ba60] P. Bártfai, *Solution of a problem posed by P. Erdős*. Mat. Lapok (1960), 175-176.
- [Bo66] Bollobás, B., *On graphs with at most three independent paths connecting any two
  vertices*. Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. (1966), 137--140.
- [Le73] Leonard, John L., *On a conjecture of Bollobás and Erdős*. Period. Math. Hungar. (1973),
  281--284.
- [Ma73] Mader, W., *Ein Extremalproblem des Zusammenhangs von Graphen*. Math. Z. (1973),
  223--231.
- [SoTh74] Sørensen, Bo Aagaard and Thomassen, Carsten, *On $k$-rails in graphs*. J.
  Combinatorial Theory Ser. B (1974), 143--159.

statements.name: Erdos915.erdos_915
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a graph with $1+n(m-1)$ vertices and $1+n\binom{m}{2}$ edges. Must $G$ contain two
points which are connected by $m$ disjoint paths?

A conjecture of Bollobás and Erdős [BoEr62]. This would be the best possible, as demonstrated by
$n$ copies of $K_m$ which share a single vertex (but are otherwise disjoint). It is unclear
whether disjoint here is to mean edge-disjoint or (internally) vertex-disjoint. The above
construction is valid for either interpretation.

This is the internally vertex-disjoint reading. It is trivial for $m = 2$, and was proved for
$m = 3$ by Bártfai [Ba60] and for $m = 4$ by Bollobás [Bo66]. Leonard [Le73] disproved this
conjecture for $m=5$, giving an explicit counterexample with $57$ vertices and $141$ edges, and
Mader [Ma73] disproved the conjecture in general for all $m \geq 6$. Sørensen and Thomassen
[SoTh74] proved that the conjectured bound of Bollobás and Erdős holds if the graph is
$3$-connected.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_915 :
    ¬ ∀ m n : ℕ, 2 ≤ m → 1 ≤ n → ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      Fintype.card V = 1 + n * (m - 1) → G.edgeSet.ncard = 1 + n * m.choose 2 →
        ∃ u v : V, u ≠ v ∧ ∃ P : Finset (G.Walk u v), P.card = m ∧ (∀ p ∈ P, p.IsPath) ∧
          (P : Set (G.Walk u v)).Pairwise InternallyDisjoint

statements.name: Erdos915.erdos_915.variants.edge_disjoint
statements.doc:
The edge-disjoint reading of [erdős_915](https://www.erdosproblems.com/915). Mader [Ma73] proved
that if a graph with $n$ vertices has more than
$$\frac{m}{2}(n-1)-\frac{1}{2}(e_0(G)+\cdots+e_{m-2}(G))$$
edges then $G$ contains two vertices connected by $m$ edge-disjoint paths (where $e_r(G)$ counts
the number of vertices of degree $\leq r$). In particular, this confirms (and is stronger than)
the conjecture.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_915.variants.edge_disjoint :
    ∀ m n : ℕ, 2 ≤ m → 1 ≤ n → ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      Fintype.card V = 1 + n * (m - 1) → G.edgeSet.ncard = 1 + n * m.choose 2 →
        ∃ u v : V, u ≠ v ∧ ∃ P : Finset (G.Walk u v), P.card = m ∧ (∀ p ∈ P, p.IsPath) ∧
          (P : Set (G.Walk u v)).Pairwise fun p q => List.Disjoint p.edges q.edges

problems.title: Erdős Problem 917
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/917](https://www.erdosproblems.com/917)
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph
  Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1969-13.pdf)
- [Er93] Erdős, P., *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*.
  Quaestiones Math. 16 (1993), 333-350.
- [Di52] Dirac, G. A., *A property of $4$-chromatic graphs and some remarks on critical graphs*.
  J. London Math. Soc. 27 (1952), 85-92.
- [To70] Toft, B., *On the maximal number of edges of critical $k$-chromatic graphs*. Studia Sci.
  Math. Hungar. 5 (1970), 461-470.
- [St87] Stiebitz, M., *Subgraphs of colour-critical graphs*. Combinatorica 7 (1987), 303-312.
- [LMY23] Luo, C., Ma, J. and Yang, T., *On the maximum number of edges in $k$-critical graphs*.
  Combin. Probab. Comput. 32 (2023), 900-911.
  [arXiv:2301.01656](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.01656)

The question is due to Erdős [Er69b, p. 28]; see also [Er93, p. 341]. See also
[erdosproblems.com/944](https://www.erdosproblems.com/944) and
[erdosproblems.com/1032](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1032).

statements.name: Erdos917.erdos_917.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 4$ and $f_k(n)$ be the largest number of edges in a graph on $n$ vertices which has
chromatic number $k$ and is critical (i.e. deleting any edge reduces the chromatic number).

Is it true that
$$f_k(n) \gg_k n^2?$$

This is the first part. It was proved by Toft [To70]. We read $\gg_k$ as: for each $k$ there is
$c > 0$ with $f_k(n) \geq cn^2$ for all large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_917.parts.i :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 4 ≤ k → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ (f k n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos917.erdos_917.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 4$ and $f_k(n)$ be the largest number of edges in a graph on $n$ vertices which has
chromatic number $k$ and is critical (i.e. deleting any edge reduces the chromatic number).

Is it true that
$$f_6(n)\sim n^2/4?$$

This is the second part.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_917.parts.ii :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f 6 n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 4)

statements.name: Erdos917.erdos_917.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 4$ and $f_k(n)$ be the largest number of edges in a graph on $n$ vertices which has
chromatic number $k$ and is critical (i.e. deleting any edge reduces the chromatic number).

More generally, is it true that, for $k\geq 6$,
$$f_k(n) \sim \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{\lfloor k/3\rfloor}\right)n^2?$$

This is the third part. It has a negative answer: the constructions in
`erdos_917.variants.lower_construction` disprove it for $k \not\equiv 0 \pmod 3$
(see `erdos_917.variants.not_asymptotic`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_917.parts.iii :
    ¬ ∀ k : ℕ, 6 ≤ k → (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f k n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] conjecturedValue k

statements.name: Erdos917.erdos_917.variants.lower_construction
statements.doc:
Constructions of Stiebitz [St87] show that, for $k\geq 6$, there exist infinitely many values of
$n$ such that
$$f_k(n) \geq \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{\lfloor k/3\rfloor+\delta_k}\right)n^2$$
where $\delta_k=0$ if $k\equiv 0\pmod{3}$, $\delta_k=1/7$ if $k\equiv 1\pmod{3}$, and
$\delta_k = 24/69$ if $k\equiv 2\pmod{3}$.

[LMY23] state the same bound in the form $(\frac12-\frac{3}{2k-\delta_k'})n^2$ with
$\delta_k'=0,8/7,44/23$, and credit the constructions to Toft [To70].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_917.variants.lower_construction (k : ℕ) (hk : 6 ≤ k) :
    ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      1 / 2 * (1 - 1 / (((k / 3 : ℕ) : ℝ) + delta k)) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ (f k n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos917.erdos_917.variants.not_asymptotic
statements.doc:
The constructions in `erdos_917.variants.lower_construction` disprove Erdős' conjectured asymptotic
$f_k(n) \sim \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{\lfloor k/3\rfloor}\right)n^2$ for $k\not\equiv 0\pmod{3}$,
$k \geq 6$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_917.variants.not_asymptotic (k : ℕ) (hk : 6 ≤ k) (h3 : ¬ 3 ∣ k) :
    ¬ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f k n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] conjecturedValue k

statements.name: Erdos917.erdos_917.variants.three_dvd
statements.doc:
The remaining case of the third question: is it true that, for $k\geq 6$ with $3 \mid k$,
$$f_k(n) \sim \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{\lfloor k/3\rfloor}\right)n^2?$$
For $k = 6$ this is `erdos_917.parts.ii`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_917.variants.three_dvd :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 6 ≤ k → 3 ∣ k → (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f k n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] conjecturedValue k

statements.name: Erdos917.erdos_917.variants.dirac
statements.doc:
In fact Dirac [Di52] proved
$$f_6(4n+2) \geq 4n^2+8n+3,$$
as witnessed by taking two disjoint copies of $C_{2n+1}$ and adding all edges between them.

We take $n \geq 1$, so that $C_{2n+1}$ is a cycle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_917.variants.dirac (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    4 * n ^ 2 + 8 * n + 3 ≤ f 6 (4 * n + 2)

statements.name: Erdos917.erdos_917.variants.erdos_three_dvd
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er69b] observed that Dirac's construction generalises to show that, if $3\mid k$, there are
infinitely many values of $n$ (those of the shape $mk/3$ where $m$ is odd) such that
$$f_k(n) \geq \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{k/3}\right)n^2 + n.$$

We take $m \geq 3$, so that the cycle $C_m$ exists.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_917.variants.erdos_three_dvd (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (h3 : 3 ∣ k) (m : ℕ)
    (hm : Odd m) (hm3 : 3 ≤ m) :
    conjecturedValue k (m * (k / 3)) + ((m * (k / 3) : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ (f k (m * (k / 3)) : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos917.erdos_917.variants.stiebitz_upper
statements.doc:
Stiebitz also proved the general upper bound
$$f_k(n) < \mathrm{ex}(n;K_{k-1})\sim \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{k-2}\right)n^2$$
for large $n$.

Here $k \geq 4$, as in [LMY23].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_917.variants.stiebitz_upper (k : ℕ) (hk : 4 ≤ k) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      f k n < SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin (k - 1)))

statements.name: Erdos917.erdos_917.variants.luo_ma_yang
statements.doc:
Luo, Ma, and Yang [LMY23] have improved this upper bound to
$$f_k(n) \leq \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{k-2}-\frac{1}{36(k-1)^2}+o(1)\right)n^2.$$

[LMY23, Theorem 1.1] proves the stronger bound
$f_k(n) \leq \mathrm{ex}(n;K_{k-1}) - \frac{n^2}{36(k-1)^2}$ for $k \geq 4$ and all large $n$, where
$\mathrm{ex}(n;K_{k-1})$ is the number of edges of the Turán graph $T_{k-2}(n)$. We state this form.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_917.variants.luo_ma_yang (k : ℕ) (hk : 4 ≤ k) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (f k n : ℝ) ≤
      (SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin (k - 1))) : ℝ) -
        (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / (36 * ((k : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 918
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/918](https://www.erdosproblems.com/918)
- [ErHa68b] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., On chromatic number of infinite graphs. (1968), 83--98.
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., Problems and results in chromatic graph theory. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.

statements.name: Erdos918.erdos_918.parts.i
statements.doc:
Is there a graph with $\aleph_2$ vertices and chromatic number $\aleph_2$ such that every
subgraph on $\aleph_1$ vertices has chromatic number $\leq\aleph_0$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_918.parts.i :
    ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ 2 ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 2 ∧
      ∀ (W : Set V) (_ : #W = ℵ₁), (G.induce W).chromaticCardinal ≤ ℵ₀

statements.name: Erdos918.erdos_918.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is there a graph with $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ vertices and chromatic number $\aleph_1$ such that
every subgraph on $\aleph_\omega$ vertices has chromatic number $\leq\aleph_0$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_918.parts.ii :
    ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ (ω + 1) ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₁ ∧
      ∀ (W : Set V) (_ : #W = ℵ_ ω), (G.induce W).chromaticCardinal ≤ ℵ₀

statements.name: Erdos918.erdos_918.variants.all_subgraphs.parts.i
statements.doc:
Is there a graph with $\aleph_2$ vertices and chromatic number $\aleph_2$ such that every
subgraph on $\aleph_1$ vertices has chromatic number $\leq\aleph_0$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_918.variants.all_subgraphs.parts.i :
    ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ 2 ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 2 ∧
      ∀ (H : G.Subgraph) (_ : #H.verts = ℵ₁), H.coe.chromaticCardinal ≤ ℵ₀

statements.name: Erdos918.erdos_918.variants.all_subgraphs.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is there a graph with $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ vertices and chromatic number $\aleph_1$ such that
every subgraph on $\aleph_\omega$ vertices has chromatic number $\leq\aleph_0$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_918.variants.all_subgraphs.parts.ii :
    ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ (ω + 1) ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₁ ∧
    ∀ (H : G.Subgraph) (_ : #H.verts = ℵ_ ω), H.coe.chromaticCardinal ≤ ℵ₀

statements.name: Erdos918.erdos_918.variants.erdos_hajnal
statements.doc:
A question of Erd\H{o}s and Hajnal [ErHa68b], who proved, assuming the generalized continuum
hypothesis, that for every finite $k \geq 1$ there is a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ and
$\aleph_k$ vertices where each subgraph on less than $\aleph_k$ vertices has chromatic number
$\leq \aleph_0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_918.variants.erdos_hajnal (hGCH : ∀ c : Cardinal.{u}, ℵ₀ ≤ c → 2 ^ c = Order.succ c)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) : ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V),
    #V = ℵ_ k ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₁ ∧
      ∀ (W : Set V) (_ : #W < ℵ_ k), (G.induce W).chromaticCardinal ≤ ℵ₀

statements.name: Erdos918.erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0.parts.i
statements.doc:
In [Er69b] the questions are stated with $= \aleph_0$ rather than $\leq\aleph_0$. This is
a likely typo since it can be shown that no such graph exists in this case.

This is the first question with induced subgraphs.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0.parts.i :
    ¬∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ 2 ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 2 ∧
      ∀ (W : Set V) (_ : #W = ℵ₁), (G.induce W).chromaticCardinal = ℵ₀

statements.name: Erdos918.erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0_all_subgraphs.parts.i
statements.doc:
In [Er69b] the questions are stated with $= \aleph_0$ rather than $\leq\aleph_0$. This is
a likely typo since it can be shown that no such graph exists in this case.

This is the first question with all subgraphs.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0_all_subgraphs.parts.i :
    ¬∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ 2 ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 2 ∧
      ∀ (H : G.Subgraph) (_ : #H.verts = ℵ₁), H.coe.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₀

statements.name: Erdos918.erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0.parts.ii
statements.doc:
In [Er69b] the questions are stated with $= \aleph_0$ rather than $\leq\aleph_0$. This is
a likely typo since it can be shown that no such graph exists in this case.

This is the second question with induced subgraphs.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0.parts.ii :
    ¬∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ (ω + 1) ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₁ ∧
      ∀ (W : Set V) (_ : #W = ℵ_ ω), (G.induce W).chromaticCardinal = ℵ₀

statements.name: Erdos918.erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0_all_subgraphs.parts.ii
statements.doc:
In [Er69b] the questions are stated with $= \aleph_0$ rather than $\leq\aleph_0$. This is

This is the second question with all subgraphs.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0_all_subgraphs.parts.ii :

      ∀ (H : G.Subgraph) (_ : #H.verts = ℵ_ ω), H.coe.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₀

problems.title: Erdős Problem 920
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/166](https://www.erdosproblems.com/166)
- [erdosproblems.com/920](https://www.erdosproblems.com/920)
- [erdosproblems.com/986](https://www.erdosproblems.com/986)
- [erdosproblems.com/1104](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1104)
- [Br26] D. Brada\v{c}, Nearly tight exponents for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers. arXiv:2605.28793
  (2026).
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., Problems and results in chromatic graph theory. Proof Techniques in Graph
  Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
- [GrYa68] Graver, Jack E. and Yackel, James, Some graph theoretic results associated with Ramsey's
  theorem. J. Combinatorial Theory (1968), 125--175.
- [MaVe23] Mattheus, S. and Verstraete, J., The asymptotics of $r(4,t)$. arXiv:2306.04007 (2023).

statements.name: Erdos920.erdos_920
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for $k\geq 4$, $f_k(n) \gg \frac{n^{1-\frac{1}{k-1}}}{(\log n)^{c_k}}$ for some
constant $c_k>0$?

This problem follows immediately from Mattheus and Verstraete's lower bound [MaVe23] for k = 4 and
Bradač's lower bound [Br26] for k ≥ 5.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_920 :
    ∀ k : ℕ, k ≥ 4 → ∃ c > 0,
      (fun n ↦ f k n) ≫ (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - 1 / ((k : ℝ) - 1)) / (log n) ^ c)

statements.name: Erdos920.erdos_920.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
Graver and Yackel [GrYa68] proved that
$f_k(n) \ll \left(n\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\right)^{1-\frac{1}{k-1}}.$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_920.variants.upper_bound (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 3) :
    (fun n ↦ f k n) ≪ (fun n ↦ ((n : ℝ) * log (log n) / log n) ^ (1 - 1 / ((k : ℝ) - 1)))

statements.name: Erdos920.erdos_920.variants.k_eq_3
statements.doc: It is known that $f_3(n)\asymp (n/\log n)^{1/2}$ (see [erdosproblems.com/1104]).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_920.variants.k_eq_3 :
    (fun n ↦ (f 3 n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (fun n ↦ ((n : ℝ) / log n) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos920.erdos_920.variants.lower_bound_k_eq_4
statements.doc:
The lower bound $R(4,m) \gg m^3/(\log m)^4$ of Mattheus and Verstraete [MaVe23]
(see [erdosproblems.com/166]) implies $f_4(n) \gg \frac{n^{2/3}}{(\log n)^{4/3}}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_920.variants.lower_bound_k_eq_4 :
    (fun n ↦ f 4 n) ≫ (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ) / (log n) ^ (4 / 3 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos920.erdos_920.variants.lower_bound_k_ge_5
statements.doc:
A positive answer to this question for all $k\geq 5$, i.e.
$f_k(n) \gg \frac{n^{1-\frac{1}{k-1}}}{(\log n)^{c_k}}$ for some constant $c_k>0$, follows from
the lower bound in [erdosproblems.com/986] given by Bradač [Br26].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_920.variants.lower_bound_k_ge_5 (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 5) :
    ∃ c > 0, (fun n ↦ f k n) ≫ (fun (n : ℕ) ↦
    (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - 1 / ((k : ℝ) - 1)) / (log n) ^ c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 921
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/921](https://www.erdosproblems.com/921)
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., Problems and results in chromatic graph theory. Proof Techniques in Graph
  Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
- [Ga63] Gallai, T., Kritische Graphen. I. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1963), 165-192.
- [KST84] Kierstead, H. A., Szemerédi, E. and Trotter, W. T., On coloring graphs with locally
  small chromatic number. Combinatorica (1984), 183-185.

statements.name: Erdos921.erdos_921
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 4$ and let $f_k(n)$ be the largest $m$ such that there is a graph on $n$ vertices
with chromatic number $k$ in which every odd cycle has length $> m$.
Then
$$f_k(n) \asymp n^{\frac{1}{k-2}}.$$

A question of Erdős and Gallai.

Proved for all $k\geq 4$ by Kierstead, Szemerédi, and Trotter [KST84].

The linked formal proof (Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol) states this as `f k n = Θ(n ^ (1 / (k - 2)))`,
where `f k n` is the largest `m` such that some graph on `n` vertices with chromatic number `k`
has no odd cycle of length at most `m`; the two eventual statements below are the two halves
of this estimate.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_921 :
    ∀ (k : ℕ), 4 ≤ k →
      ∃ (c₁ c₂ : ℝ), 0 < c₁ ∧ 0 < c₂ ∧
        (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
          (∃ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
            G.chromaticNumber = (k : ℕ∞) ∧
            ∀ l ∈ G.oddCycleLengths, c₁ * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / ((k : ℝ) - 2)) < (l : ℝ))) ∧
        (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
          ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
            G.chromaticNumber = (k : ℕ∞) →
            ∃ l ∈ G.oddCycleLengths, (l : ℝ) ≤ c₂ * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / ((k : ℝ) - 2)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 922
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/922](https://www.erdosproblems.com/922)
- [ErHa67b] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, András, *On chromatic graphs*. Mat. Lapok (1967), 1-4.
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph
  Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
- [Fo70b] Folkman, J. H., *An upper bound on the chromatic number of a graph*. (1970), 437-457.

statements.name: Erdos922.erdos_922
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 0$. Let $G$ be a graph such that every subgraph $H$ contains an independent set of size
$\geq (n-k)/2$, where $n$ is the number of vertices of $H$. Must $G$ have chromatic number at most
$k+2$?

A question of Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa67b]. The case $k=0$ is trivial, but they could not prove
this even for $k=1$.

This is true, and was proved by Folkman [Fo70b].

See also [73](https://www.erdosproblems.com/73).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_922 : ∀ (k : ℕ) (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
    (∀ S : Finset V, ∃ I : Finset V, I ⊆ S ∧ (G.induce (I : Set V)).edgeSet = ∅ ∧
      (I.card : ℝ) ≥ (S.card - k : ℝ) / 2) →
    G.chromaticNumber ≤ k + 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 923
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/923](https://www.erdosproblems.com/923)
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (1969), 27-35.
- [Ro77] Rödl, V., *On the chromatic number of subgraphs of a given graph*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1977), 370-371.

statements.name: Erdos923.erdos_923
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for every $k$, there is some $f(k)$ such that if $G$ has chromatic number
$\geq f(k)$ then $G$ contains a triangle-free subgraph with chromatic number $\geq k$?

This is true, as shown by Rödl [Ro77].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_923 : ∀ (V : Type*) (n : ℕ),
    ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph V, k ≤ G.chromaticNumber →
    ∃ H ≤ G, n ≤ H.chromaticNumber ∧ H.CliqueFree 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 926
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/926](https://www.erdosproblems.com/926)
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph
  Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [Er74c] Erdős, Paul, *Extremal problems on graphs and hypergraphs*. (1974), 75-84.
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [Fu91] Füredi, Zoltán, *On a Turán type problem of Erdős*. Combinatorica (1991), 75--79.
- [AKS03] Alon, Noga and Krivelevich, Michael and Sudakov, Benny, *Turán numbers of bipartite
  graphs and related Ramsey-type questions*. Combin. Probab. Comput. (2003), 477-494.

statements.name: Erdos926.erdos_926
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 4$. Is it true that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;H_k) \ll_k n^{3/2},$$
where $H_k$ is the graph on vertices $x,y_1,\ldots,y_k,z_1,\ldots,z_{\binom{k}{2}}$, where $x$ is
adjacent to all $y_i$ and each pair of $y_i,y_j$ is adjacent to a unique $z_i$.

It is trivial that $\mathrm{ex}(n;H_k)\gg n^{3/2}$ since $H_k$ contians a $C_4$ for $k\geq 3$.
Erdős [Er71] claimed a proof for $k=3$.

The answer is yes, proved by Füredi [Fu91], who proved that $\mathrm{ex}(n;H_k) \ll (kn)^{3/2}$.
This was improved to $\mathrm{ex}(n;H_k) \ll kn^{3/2}$ by Alon, Krivelevich, and Sudakov [AKS03].

Since each $H_k$ is 2-degenerate this is a special case of [146](https://www.erdosproblems.com/146).
The extremal number of the graph $H_k$ with the vertex $x$ omitted is the subject of
[1021](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1021).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_926 : ∀ k : ℕ, 4 ≤ k →
    (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n (H k) : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos926.erdos_926.variants.aks
statements.doc:
Alon, Krivelevich, and Sudakov [AKS03] proved $\mathrm{ex}(n;H_k) \ll kn^{3/2}$ with an
absolute implied constant.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_926.variants.aks : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ k : ℕ, 4 ≤ k → ∀ n : ℕ,
    (extremalNumber n (H k) : ℝ) ≤ C * k * (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 927
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/927](https://www.erdosproblems.com/927)
- [MoMo65] Moon, J. W. and Moser, L., *On cliques in graphs*. Israel J. Math. (1965), 23-28.
- [Er66b] Erdős, P., *On cliques in graphs*. Israel J. Math. (1966), 233--234.
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph
  Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [Sp71] Spencer, J. H., *On cliques in graphs*. Israel J. Math. (1971), 419-421.

statements.name: Erdos927.erdos_927
statements.doc:
Let $g(n)$ be the maximum number of different sizes of cliques that can occur in a graph on $n$
vertices. Estimate $g(n)$ - in particular, is it true that
$$g(n) = n - \log_2 n - \log_*(n) + O(1),$$
where $\log_*(n)$ is the number of iterated logarithms such that $\log \cdots \log n < 1$?

A quantity first considered by Moon and Moser [MoMo65], who proved
$n - \log_2 n - 2 \log \log n < g(n) \le n - \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$. Erdős [Er66b] improved the
lower bound to $n - \log_2 n - \log_*(n) - O(1) < g(n)$ and conjectured this was the correct order
of magnitude. This was disproved by Spencer [Sp71], who proved that in fact
$g(n) > n - \log_2 n - O(1)$.

Here $\log_2 n$ and $\log_*(n)$ are formalised as `Nat.log 2 n` and `Nat.iteratedLog 2 n`
(iterating `Nat.log 2` until the value is at most `1`); both differ from the quantities in the
problem by $O(1)$, so the statement is unaffected. See also `erdos_775.variants.spencer` and
`erdos_775.variants.moon_moser`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_927 :
    ¬ ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      g n + Nat.log 2 n + Nat.iteratedLog 2 n ≤ n + C ∧
        n ≤ g n + Nat.log 2 n + Nat.iteratedLog 2 n + C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 929
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/929](https://www.erdosproblems.com/929)
- [Er76d] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers
  and related questions*. Proceedings of the Fifth Manitoba Conference on Numerical Mathematics
  (Univ. Manitoba, Winnipeg, Man., 1975) (1976), 25-44.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1976-39.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos929.erdos_929.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 2$ be large and let $S(k)$ be the minimal $x$ such that there is a positive density set
of $n$ where
$$n+1,n+2,\ldots,n+k$$
are all divisible by primes $\leq x$.

Estimate $S(k)$ - in particular, is it true that $S(k)\geq k^{1-o(1)}$?

A problem of Erdős [Er76d, p. 26]. This is the first part. We read "estimate" as
$S(k) = \Theta(\text{answer})$ as $k \to \infty$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_929.parts.i : (fun k ↦ (S k : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_929.parts.i.answer

statements.name: Erdos929.erdos_929.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 2$ be large and let $S(k)$ be the minimal $x$ such that there is a positive density set
of $n$ where
$$n+1,n+2,\ldots,n+k$$
are all divisible by primes $\leq x$.

Estimate $S(k)$ - in particular, is it true that $S(k)\geq k^{1-o(1)}$?

This is the second part. We read $o(1)$ as an arbitrary $\varepsilon > 0$ for all large $k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_929.parts.ii :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, (k : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε) ≤ (S k : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos929.erdos_929.variants.rosser
statements.doc:
It follows from Rosser's sieve that $S(k)> k^{1/2-o(1)}$.

Erdős [Er76d, p. 26] states this for the index $\ell$ with $p_\ell = S(k)$. Since
$S(k) = p_\ell \geq \ell$, the bound transfers to $S(k)$. The $o(1)$ is stated with an arbitrary
$\varepsilon > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_929.variants.rosser :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, (k : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2 - ε) ≤ (S k : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos929.erdos_929.variants.trivial_upper
statements.doc: It is trivial that $S(k)\leq k+1$ since, for example, one can take $n\equiv 1\pmod{(k+1)!}$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_929.variants.trivial_upper (k : ℕ) : S k ≤ k + 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 930
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/930](https://www.erdosproblems.com/930)

statements.name: Erdos930.erdos_930
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for every $r$, there is a $k$ such that
if $I_1,\ldots,I_r$ are disjoint intervals of consecutive integers,
all of length at least $k$, then
$$
  \prod_{1\leq i\leq r}\prod_{m\in I_i}m
$$
is not a perfect power?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_930 :
    ∀ r > 0, ∃ k, ∀ I₁ I₂ : Fin r → ℕ,
      (∀ i : Fin r, 0 < I₁ i ∧ I₁ i + k ≤ I₂ i + 1) →
        (∀ i j : Fin r, i < j → I₂ i < I₁ j) →
          ¬ IsPower (∏ i : Fin r, ∏ m ∈ Icc (I₁ i) (I₂ i), m)

statements.name: Erdos930.erdos_930.variants.consecutive_strong
statements.doc:
Let $k$, $l$, $n$ be integers such that $k \ge 3$, $l \ge 2$ and $n + k \ge p^{(k)}$,
where $p^{(k)}$ is the least prime satisfying $p^{(k)} \ge k$.
Then there is a prime $p \ge k$ for which $l$ does not divide
the multiplicity of the prime factor $p$ in $(n + 1) \ldots (n + k)$.

Theorem 2 from [ErSe75].

[ErSe75] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., The product of consecutive integers is never a power. Illinois J. Math. (1975), 292-301.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_930.variants.consecutive_strong :
    ∀ k l n, 3 ≤ k → 2 ≤ l → nextPrime k ≤ n + k →
      ∃ p, k ≤ p ∧ p.Prime ∧
        ¬ (l ∣ Nat.factorization (∏ m ∈ Icc (n + 1) (n + k), m) p)

statements.name: Erdos930.erdos_930.variants.consecutive_integers
statements.doc:
Erdos and Selfridge [ErSe75] proved that the product of
consecutive integers is never a power (establishing the case $r=1$).

Theorem 1 from [ErSe75].

It is implied from `erdos_930.variants.consecutive_strong`.

[ErSe75] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., The product of consecutive integers is never a power. Illinois J. Math. (1975), 292-301.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_930.variants.consecutive_integers :
    ∀ n k, 0 ≤ n → 2 ≤ k →
      ¬ IsPower (∏ m ∈ Icc (n + 1) (n + k), m)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 931
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/931](https://www.erdosproblems.com/931)

statements.name: Erdos931.erdos_931
statements.doc:
Let $k_1 \geq k_2 \geq 3$. Are there only finitely many $n_2\geq n_1 + k_1$
such that
$$
  \prod_{1\leq i\leq k_1}(n_1 + i)\ \text{and}\ \prod_{1\leq j\leq k_2} (n_2 + j)
$$
have the same prime factors?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_931 : ∀ᵉ (k₁ : ℕ) (k₂ ≥ 3), k₂ ≤ k₁ →
    { (n₁, n₂) | n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ ∧
      (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors =
      (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors }.Finite

statements.name: Erdos931.erdos_931.variants.additional_condition
statements.doc:
Erdős thought perhaps if the two products have the same factors then
$n_2 > 2(n_1 + k_1)$.
It is an open question whether this is true when allowing a finite number of counterexamples.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_931.variants.additional_condition : ∀ᵉ (k₁ : ℕ) (k₂ ≥ 3), k₂ ≤ k₁ →
    {(n₁, n₂) | n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ ∧ n₂ ≤ 2 * (n₁ + k₁) ∧
      (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors =
      (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors}.Finite

statements.name: Erdos931.erdos_931.variants.additional_condition_nonempty
statements.doc: In fact there exist counterexamples, like this one found by AlphaProof.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_931.variants.additional_condition_nonempty : ∃ (k₁ k₂ : ℕ), ∃ (_h₁ : k₂ ≤ k₁), ∃ (_h₂ : 3 ≤ k₂),
  {(n₁, n₂) | n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ ∧ n₂ ≤ 2 * (n₁ + k₁) ∧
      (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors =
      (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors}.Nonempty

statements.name: Erdos931.erdos_931.variants.exists_prime
statements.doc:
Erdős was unable to prove that if the two products have the same factors
then there must exist a prime between $n_1$ and $n_2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_931.variants.exists_prime (k₁ k₂ n₁ n₂ : ℕ) (h₁ : k₂ ≤ k₁) (h₂ : 3 ≤ k₂)
    (h₃ : n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂) (h₄ : (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors =
      (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors) :
    ∃ (p : ℕ), p.Prime ∧ n₁ ≤ p ∧ p ≤ n₂

problems.title: Erdős Problem 932
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/932](https://www.erdosproblems.com/932)

statements.name: Erdos932.erdos_932
statements.doc:
Let $p_k$ denote the $k$th prime. For infinitely many $r$ there are at least two
integers $p_r < n < p_{r+1}$ all of whose prime factors are $< p_{r + 1} - p_r$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_932 :
    { r : ℕ | 2 ≤ (Finset.Ioo (r.nth Nat.Prime) (r.succ.nth Nat.Prime) |>.filter
      (fun m => m.maxPrimeFac < r.succ.nth Nat.Prime - r.nth Nat.Prime)).card }.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos932.erdos_932.variants.one_le
statements.doc: Erdős could show that the density of $r$ such that at least one such $n$ exists is $0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_932.variants.one_le :
    { r : ℕ | 1 ≤ (Finset.Ioo (r.nth Nat.Prime) (r.succ.nth Nat.Prime) |>.filter
      (fun m => m.maxPrimeFac < r.succ.nth Nat.Prime - r.nth Nat.Prime)).card }.HasDensity 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 933
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/933](https://www.erdosproblems.com/933)
- [Er76d] Erdős, P, Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and
  related questions. Proceedings of the Fifth Manitoba Conference on Numerical Mathematics (Univ.
  Manitoba, Winnipeg, Man., 1975) (1976), 25-44.

statements.name: Erdos933.erdos_933
statements.doc:
If $n(n+1)=2^k3^lm$, where $(m,6)=1$, then is it true that
$\limsup_{n\to \infty} \frac{2^k3^l}{n\log n}=\infty$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_933 :
    atTop.limsup (fun n : ℕ ↦
      ((((2 ^ k n * 3 ^ l n : ℕ) : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ))) : EReal)) = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos933.erdos_933.variants.mahler
statements.doc: Mahler proved (a more general result that implies in particular) that $2^k3^l<n^{1+o(1)}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_933.variants.mahler :
    ∃ c : ℕ → ℝ, (c =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ((2 ^ k n * 3 ^ l n : ℕ) : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + c n)

statements.name: Erdos933.erdos_933.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er76d] wrote 'it is easy to see' that for infinitely many $n$, $2^k 3^l > n\log n$.

Steinerberger has noted a simple proof of this fact follows from taking $n=2^{3^r}$ for any
integer $r\geq 1$, when $k=3^r$ and $l=r+1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_933.variants.lower_bound :
    Set.Infinite { n : ℕ | ((2 ^ k n * 3 ^ l n : ℕ) : ℝ) > (n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ) }

problems.title: Erdős Problem 934
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/934](https://www.erdosproblems.com/934)
- [Er88] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and graph theory*.
  Discrete Math. 72 (1988), 81-92.
- [BBPP83] Bermond, J.-C., Bond, J., Paoli, M. and Peyrat, C., *Graphs and interconnection
  networks: diameter and vulnerability*. Surveys in Combinatorics (Southampton, 1983), London Math.
  Soc. Lecture Note Ser. 82, Cambridge Univ. Press (1983), 1-30.
- [CGTT90] Chung, F. R. K., Gyárfás, A., Tuza, Z. and Trotter, W. T., *The maximum number of
  edges in $2K_2$-free graphs of bounded degree*. Discrete Math. 81 (1990), 129-135.
- [CCJK22] Cambie, S., Cames van Batenburg, W., de Joannis de Verclos, R. and Kang, R. J.,
  *Maximising line subgraphs of diameter at most $t$*. SIAM J. Discrete Math. 36 (2022),
  939-950. [arXiv:2103.11898](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.11898)
- [KMP26] Kumar, H., Mohar, B. and Pragada, S., *An improved bound for the strong clique index
  of graphs*. [arXiv:2607.02698](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.02698) (2026).
- [CvBK26] Cames van Batenburg, W. and Korsky, S., *Asymptotically attaining the Moore bound*.
  [arXiv:2608.03965](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03965) (2026).

statements.name: Erdos934.erdos_934
statements.doc:
Let $h_t(d)$ be minimal such that every graph $G$ with $h_t(d)$ edges and maximal degree
$\leq d$ contains two edges whose shortest path between them has length $\geq t$.

Estimate $h_t(d)$.

A problem of Erdős and Nešetřil [Er88]. Erdős wrote 'This problem seems to be interesting only
if there is a nice expression for $h_t(d)$.' We read "estimate" as asking for an exact
expression, as in that remark: `h t d = erdos_934.answer t d` for all `1 ≤ t` and all `d`.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_934 : ∀ t d : ℕ, 1 ≤ t → h t d = erdos_934.answer t d

statements.name: Erdos934.erdos_934.variants.h_one
statements.doc:
It is easy to see that $h_t(d)\leq 2d^t$ always and $h_1(d)=d+1$.

The site (and [CCJK22, p. 1]) states $h_1(d)=d+1$ without restriction; it fails for $d=2$ (the
triangle has three pairwise intersecting edges, so $h_1(2)=4$), hence we assume $d\neq 2$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_934.variants.h_one : ∀ d : ℕ, d ≠ 2 → h 1 d = d + 1

statements.name: Erdos934.erdos_934.variants.h_two
statements.doc:
Erdős and Nešetřil and Bermond, Bond, Paoli, and Peyrat [BBPP83] independently conjectured that
$h_2(d) \leq \tfrac{5}{4}d^2+1$, with equality for even $d$. This was proved by Chung, Gyárfás,
Tuza, and Trotter [CGTT90].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_934.variants.h_two :
    (∀ d : ℕ, 4 * h 2 d ≤ 5 * d ^ 2 + 4) ∧
      ∀ d : ℕ, Even d → 4 * h 2 d = 5 * d ^ 2 + 4

statements.name: Erdos934.erdos_934.variants.h_three_three
statements.doc: Cambie, Cames van Batenburg, de Joannis de Verclos, and Kang [CCJK22, Theorem 2] proved that $h_3(3)=23$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_934.variants.h_three_three : h 3 3 = 23

statements.name: Erdos934.erdos_934.variants.upper
statements.doc:
The same authors prove that for all $t\geq 1$ we have
$$h_t(d) \leq \tfrac{3}{2}d^t+1.$$
See [CCJK22, Theorem 6]. Here the inequality is stated as `2 * h t d ≤ 3 * d ^ t + 2`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_934.variants.upper :
    ∀ t d : ℕ, 1 ≤ t → 2 * h t d ≤ 3 * d ^ t + 2

statements.name: Erdos934.erdos_934.variants.lower_large_t
statements.doc:
The same authors prove that, if $t$ is large, then there are infinitely many $d$ such that
$h_t(d) \geq 0.629^td^t$. See [CCJK22, Proposition 5].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_934.variants.lower_large_t :
    ∃ t₀ : ℕ, ∀ t : ℕ, t₀ ≤ t →
      ∃ᶠ d : ℕ in atTop, ((629 : ℝ) / 1000) ^ t * (d : ℝ) ^ t ≤ (h t d : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos934.erdos_934.variants.kmp_h_three_four
statements.doc:
Cambie, Cames van Batenburg, de Joannis de Verclos, and Kang [CCJK22] conjectured that
$h_3(d) \leq d^3-d^2+d+2$ (with equality if $d-1$ is a prime power; the site writes "if and only
if", while [CCJK22, Conjecture 1] says "if"). Kumar, Mohar and Pragada [KMP26, Lemma 3.1]
refute the inequality: the odd graph $KG(7,3)$ has $35$ vertices, is $4$-regular, has $70$ edges
and any two of its edges are at distance less than $3$, so $h_3(4)\geq 71 > 54$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_934.variants.kmp_h_three_four : 71 ≤ h 3 4

statements.name: Erdos934.erdos_934.variants.ccjk_conjecture_false
statements.doc:
The inequality $h_3(d) \leq d^3-d^2+d+2$ conjectured in [CCJK22] is false [KMP26, Conjecture 1.9
and Lemma 3.1]. Here the inequality is stated as `h 3 d + d ^ 2 ≤ d ^ 3 + d + 2`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_934.variants.ccjk_conjecture_false :
    ¬ ∀ d : ℕ, h 3 d + d ^ 2 ≤ d ^ 3 + d + 2

statements.name: Erdos934.erdos_934.variants.kmp_liminf
statements.doc:
Kumar, Mohar and Pragada [KMP26, Theorem 1.11] proved
$$\liminf_{d\to\infty}\frac{h_3(d)}{d^3}\geq \frac{253}{225}.$$
In particular the conjecture of [CCJK22] that $h_t(d)\leq (1+o(1))d^t$ is false for $t=3$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_934.variants.kmp_liminf :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ d : ℕ in atTop, (253 / 225 - ε) * (d : ℝ) ^ 3 ≤ (h 3 d : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos934.erdos_934.variants.lower_liminf
statements.doc:
For every fixed $t\geq 2$, $\liminf_{d\to\infty} h_t(d)/d^t \geq 1$ [CvBK26, Corollary 1.2]. This
confirms, in a strong form, the conjecture of [CCJK22] that $h_t(d)\geq (1-o(1))d^t$ for
infinitely many $d$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_934.variants.lower_liminf :
    ∀ t : ℕ, 2 ≤ t → ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ d : ℕ in atTop,
      (1 - ε) * (d : ℝ) ^ t ≤ (h t d : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 935
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/935](https://www.erdosproblems.com/935)
- [Er76d] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers
  and related questions*. Proceedings of the Fifth Manitoba Conference on Numerical Mathematics
  (Univ. Manitoba, Winnipeg, Man., 1975) (1976), 25-44.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1976-39.pdf)
- [Fe26] Feng, T. et al., *Semi-Autonomous Mathematics Discovery with Gemini: A Case Study on the
  Erdős Problems*. [arXiv:2601.22401](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22401) (2026).

The powerful part $Q_2(m)$ of $m$ is `Erdos367.B 2 m`, the product of $p^a$ over the primes $p$
with $p^a \parallel m$ and $a \geq 2$. The second question is essentially the same as
[erdosproblems.com/367](https://www.erdosproblems.com/367).

statements.name: Erdos935.erdos_935.parts.i
statements.doc:
For any integer $n=\prod p^{k_p}$ let $Q_2(n)$ be the powerful part of $n$, so that
$$Q_2(n) = \prod_{\substack{p\\ k_p\geq 2}}p^{k_p}.$$
Is it true that, for every $\epsilon>0$ and $\ell\geq 1$, if $n$ is sufficiently large then
$$Q_2(n(n+1)\cdots(n+\ell))<n^{2+\epsilon}?$$

A problem of Erdős [Er76d, p. 32], who writes that if this is true then it seems very difficult to
prove. This is the first part.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_935.parts.i :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ ℓ → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ((Erdos367.B 2 (∏ m ∈ Finset.Icc n (n + ℓ), m) : ℕ) : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) ^ (2 + ε)

statements.name: Erdos935.erdos_935.parts.ii
statements.doc:
For any integer $n=\prod p^{k_p}$ let $Q_2(n)$ be the powerful part of $n$, so that
$$Q_2(n) = \prod_{\substack{p\\ k_p\geq 2}}p^{k_p}.$$
If $\ell\geq 2$ then is
$$\limsup_{n\to \infty}\frac{Q_2(n(n+1)\cdots(n+\ell))}{n^2}$$
infinite?

This is the second part. We write "infinite" as: for every $C$, $C n^2 < Q_2(\cdots)$ for infinitely
many $n$. The answer is yes, by the Pell equation construction of `erdos_935.variants.ell_two`
(the case $\ell = 2$); for larger $\ell$ the product for $\ell = 2$ divides the product for $\ell$,
and $Q_2$ does not decrease under divisibility.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_935.parts.ii :
    ∀ ℓ : ℕ, 2 ≤ ℓ → ∀ C : ℝ, ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      C * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 < ((Erdos367.B 2 (∏ m ∈ Finset.Icc n (n + ℓ), m) : ℕ) : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos935.erdos_935.parts.iii
statements.doc:
For any integer $n=\prod p^{k_p}$ let $Q_2(n)$ be the powerful part of $n$, so that
$$Q_2(n) = \prod_{\substack{p\\ k_p\geq 2}}p^{k_p}.$$
If $\ell\geq 2$ then is
$$\lim_{n\to \infty}\frac{Q_2(n(n+1)\cdots(n+\ell))}{n^{\ell+1}}=0?$$

This is the third part. The restriction $\ell \geq 2$ is needed: for $\ell = 1$ the Pell solutions of
`erdos_935.variants.mahler` give $Q_2(n(n+1)) = n(n+1)$ infinitely often.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_935.parts.iii :
    ∀ ℓ : ℕ, 2 ≤ ℓ → Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((Erdos367.B 2 (∏ m ∈ Finset.Icc n (n + ℓ), m) : ℕ) : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) ^ (ℓ + 1))
      atTop (nhds 0)

statements.name: Erdos935.erdos_935.variants.mahler
statements.doc:
A result of Mahler implies, for every $\ell\geq 1$,
$$\limsup_{n\to \infty}\frac{Q_2(n(n+1)\cdots(n+\ell))}{n^2}\geq 1.$$

Erdős [Er76d, pp. 31-32] derives this from the infinitely many solutions of $x^2-8y^2=1$, which
give consecutive powerful numbers. We write $\limsup \geq 1$ as: for every $\varepsilon > 0$,
$(1-\varepsilon) n^2 < Q_2(\cdots)$ for infinitely many $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_935.variants.mahler :
    ∀ ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ ℓ → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (1 - ε) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 < ((Erdos367.B 2 (∏ m ∈ Finset.Icc n (n + ℓ), m) : ℕ) : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos935.erdos_935.variants.ell_two
statements.doc:
The construction of van Doorn for [367] (also given by Aletheia [Fe26, §4.2]) proves the second
part in the affirmative: a construction via solutions to the Pell equation $x^2-8y^2=1$ implies
$$\limsup_{n\to \infty}\frac{Q_2(n(n+1)(n+2))}{n^2}=\infty.$$

This is the case $\ell = 2$, stated as in `erdos_935.parts.ii`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_935.variants.ell_two :
    ∀ C : ℝ, ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      C * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 < ((Erdos367.B 2 (∏ m ∈ Finset.Icc n (n + 2), m) : ℕ) : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 936
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/936](https://www.erdosproblems.com/936)

statements.name: Erdos936.erdos_936.variants.two_pow_add_one
statements.doc: Is $2^n + 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_936.variants.two_pow_add_one :
   EventuallyNotPowerful (2 ^ · + 1)

statements.name: Erdos936.erdos_936.variants.two_pow_sub_one
statements.doc: Is $2^n - 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_936.variants.two_pow_sub_one :
   EventuallyNotPowerful (2 ^ · - 1)

statements.name: Erdos936.erdos_936.variants.factorial_add_one
statements.doc: Is $n! + 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_936.variants.factorial_add_one :
   EventuallyNotPowerful (·! + 1)

statements.name: Erdos936.erdos_936.variants.factorial_sub_one
statements.doc: Is $n! - 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_936.variants.factorial_sub_one :
   EventuallyNotPowerful (·! - 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 937
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/937](https://www.erdosproblems.com/937)

*References:*
 * [BBC24] Bajpai, P., Bennett, M. A. and Chan, T. H., _Arithmetic progressions in squarefull /
   powerful numbers_, Int. J. Number Theory 20 (2024), 19-45.

statements.name: Erdos937.erdos_937
statements.doc:
Are there infinitely many four-term arithmetic progressions of coprime powerful numbers?
(A number $n$ is *powerful* if $p \mid n \to p^2 \mid n$; `Nat.Powerful`.)

Erdős [Er76d] asked this; the answer is **yes**: Bajpai, Bennett and Chan [BBC24] proved that
there are infinitely many four-term arithmetic progressions of pairwise coprime powerful numbers.
(Without coprimality this is easy, and by a theorem of Fermat there are no four *squares* in
arithmetic progression.)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_937 :
    {p : ℕ × ℕ | IsCoprimePowerfulAP4 p.1 p.2}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 938
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/938](https://www.erdosproblems.com/938)

statements.name: Erdos938.erdos_938
statements.doc:
Let $A=\{n_1 < n_2 < \cdots\}$ be the sequence of powerful numbers (if $p\mid n$ then $p^2\mid n$).
Are there only finitely many three-term progressions of consecutive terms $n_k,n_{k+1},n_{k+2}$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_938 : {P : Finset ℕ | (P : Set ℕ).IsAPOfLength 3 ∧ ∃ k,
    P = {nth Powerful k, nth Powerful (k + 1), nth Powerful (k + 2)}}.Finite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 939
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/939](https://www.erdosproblems.com/939)
- [Ni95] Nitaj, A., _On a conjecture of Erdős on 3-powerful numbers_. Bull. London Math. Soc.
  (1995), 317-318.
- [Co98] Cohn, J. H. E., _A conjecture of Erdős on 3-powerful numbers_. Math. Comp. (1998),
  439-440.
- [Wa24] Walsh, P., _A question of Erdős on 3-powerful numbers and an elliptic curve analogue
  of the Ankeny-Artin-Chowla conjecture_. arXiv:2404.03970 (2024).
- [LaPa67] Lander, L. J. and Parkin, T. R., _A counterexample to Euler's sum of powers
  conjecture_. Math. Comp. (1967), 101-103.

statements.name: Erdos939.erdos_939
statements.doc: If $r≥4$ then can the sum of $r-2$ coprime $r$-powerful numbers ever be itself $r$-powerful?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_939 : ∀ r ≥ 4, (Erdos939Sums r).Nonempty

statements.name: Erdos939.erdos_939.variants.finite
statements.doc:
If $r≥4$, are there at most finitely many sums of $r-2$ coprime $r$-powerful numbers
that are themselves $r$-powerful?

The answer is no: for every $r \ge 6$ there are infinitely many such sums, see
`erdos_939.variants.infinite_of_six_le`. (For $r = 4$ and $r = 5$ the question is open; for
$r = 4$ no example is known at all, see `erdos_939`.)
A construction in the site's comments, from GPT-5.5 Pro prompted by Price, gives infinitely
many for every $r \ge 6$. This statement quantifies over every $r \ge 4$, so it stays open at
$r = 4$ and $r = 5$. The category is unchanged because the construction is recorded in the
comments and not in the literature.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_939.variants.finite : ¬ ∀ r ≥ 4, (Erdos939Sums r).Finite

statements.name: Erdos939.erdos_939.variants.infinite_of_six_le
statements.doc:
For every $r \ge 6$ there are infinitely many sums of $r - 2$ coprime $r$-powerful numbers that
are themselves $r$-powerful.

A construction, found by GPT-5.5 Pro prompted by Liam Price and recorded in the comments on
[erdosproblems.com/939](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/939), expands
$(X+Y)^r = (X-Y)^r + \sum_{j \text{ odd}} 2\binom{r}{j} X^{r-j} Y^j$, splits the $j = 3$ term into
$\lfloor r/2 \rfloor - 2$ distinct pieces to obtain exactly $r - 2$ summands, and takes
$X = q^r$, $Y = B^r$ with $B$ divisible by all primes in the coefficients and $q > B$ a prime not
dividing $B$; varying $q$ gives infinitely many solutions.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_939.variants.infinite_of_six_le : ∀ r ≥ 6, (Erdos939Sums r).Infinite

statements.name: Erdos939.erdos_939.variants.triples
statements.doc:
Are there infinitely many triples of coprime $3$-powerful numbers $a, b, c$ such that $a + b = c$?

The answer is yes. Nitaj [Ni95] proved it, with $2^3\cdot 3^5\cdot 73^3 + 271^3 = 919^3$ as an
example. In Nitaj's construction at least two of $a, b, c$ are perfect cubes. Cohn [Co98]
constructed infinitely many triples of which none is a perfect cube, and Walsh [Wa24] gave a
further construction.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_939.variants.triples :
    {(a,b,c) | ({a, b, c} : Finset ℕ).Coprime ∧
      0 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧
      (3).Full a ∧ (3).Full b ∧ (3).Full c ∧
      a + b = c}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos939.erdos_939.variants.examples
statements.doc:
Cambie has found several examples of the sum of $r - 2$ coprime $r$-powerful numbers being itself
$r$-powerful. For example when $r=5$ we have
$$3^7\cdot 61^5 = 2^8\cdot3^{10}\cdot 5^7 + 2^{12}\cdot 23^6 + 11^5\cdot 13^5$$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_939.variants.examples : (∃ r ≥ 4, (Erdos939Sums r).Nonempty)

statements.name: Erdos939.erdos_939.variants.seven
statements.doc: Cambie has also found solutions when $r=7$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_939.variants.seven : (Erdos939Sums 7).Nonempty

statements.name: Erdos939.erdos_939.variants.eight
statements.doc:
Cambie has also found solutions when $r=8$.

The source adds that the $r=8$ solution works "even with the sum of $5$ $8$-powerful numbers".
That is a stronger result than this statement, which asks for the $r - 2 = 6$ summands of
`Erdos939Sums`.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_939.variants.eight : (Erdos939Sums 8).Nonempty

statements.name: Erdos939.erdos_939.variants.euler
statements.doc:
Euler had conjectured that the sum of $k - 1$ many $k$-th powers is never a
$k$-th power, but this is false for $k=5$, as Lander and Parkin [LaPa67] found
$$27^5+84^5+110^5+133^5=144^5$$.

The summands must be positive. Without that condition a set containing `0` would count, so the
negation would be satisfied by a sum of fewer than $k-1$ powers and would claim less than the
refutation of Euler's conjecture that this theorem records.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_939.variants.euler : ¬ (∀ k ≥ 4, ∀ S : Finset ℕ, S.card = k - 1 →
    (∀ s ∈ S, 0 < s) → ¬ (∃ q, ∑ s ∈ S, s ^ k = q ^k))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 940
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/940](https://www.erdosproblems.com/940)
- [BaBr94] Baker, R. C. and Brüdern, J., _On sums of two squarefull numbers_. Math. Proc.
  Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1994), 1-5.
- [He88] Heath-Brown, D. R., _Ternary quadratic forms and sums of three square-full numbers_.
  (1988), 137-163.

statements.name: Erdos940.erdos_940
statements.doc:
Let $r \ge 3$. Is it true that the set of integers which are the sum of at most $r$ $r$-powerful numbers
has density $0$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_940 :
    ∀ r ≥ 3,
      {n : ℕ | ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ), S.card ≤ r ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, r.Full s) ∧ n = S.sum}.HasDensity 0

statements.name: Erdos940.erdos_940.variants.two
statements.doc:
The set of integers which are the sum of at most two $2$-powerful numbers has density $0$.

Erdős called this 'easy'. Baker and Brüdern [BaBr94] gave the first proof in the literature.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_940.variants.two :
    {n : ℕ | ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ),
      S.card ≤ 2 ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, (2).Full s) ∧ n = S.sum}.HasDensity 0

statements.name: Erdos940.erdos_940.variants.three_cubes
statements.doc:
Is it true that the set of integers which are the sum of at most three cubes has density $0$?

The cubes are those of non-negative integers, which is what `Multiset ℕ` gives. This choice
decides the question: over `ℤ` a sum of three cubes is conjectured to represent every integer
that is not $\pm 4 \bmod 9$, which is density $7/9$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_940.variants.three_cubes :
    {n : ℕ | ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ), S.card ≤ 3 ∧ n = (Multiset.map (· ^ 3) S).sum}.HasDensity 0

statements.name: Erdos940.erdos_940.variants.large_integers
statements.doc:
Let $r \ge 3$. Are there infinitely many integers which are not the sum of at most $r$-many
$r$-powerful numbers?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_940.variants.large_integers :
    ∀ r ≥ 3, ¬ (∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ), S.card ≤ r ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, r.Full s) ∧ x = S.sum)

statements.name: Erdos940.erdos_940.variants.three_powerful
statements.doc:
Heath-Brown [He88] has proved that all large numbers are the sum of at most three
$2$-powerful numbers.

This is the case $r = 2$ of `Erdos1107.erdos_1107`, which asks the same question with $r + 1$
summands, and it is stated there as `Erdos1107.erdos_1107.variants.two`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_940.variants.three_powerful :
    ∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ), S.card ≤ 3 ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, (2).Full s) ∧ x = S.sum

problems.title: Erdős Problem 942
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/942](https://www.erdosproblems.com/942)

statements.name: Erdos942.erdos_942
statements.doc:
Is there some constant $c > 0$ such that $h(n) < (\log n)^{c + o(1)}$ and, for infinitely many $n$,
$h(n) > (\log n)^{c - o(1)}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_942 : ∃ c > 0, ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ), o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    (∀ᶠ n in atTop, erdos_942.h n < (Real.log n) ^ (c + o n)) ∧
    {n | erdos_942.h n > (Real.log n) ^ (c - o n)}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos942.erdos_942.variants.limsup
statements.doc: It is not hard to prove that $\limsup h(n) = \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_942.variants.limsup :
    atTop.limsup (((fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (n : ℕ∞)) ∘ erdos_942.h)) = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos942.erdos_942.variants.density
statements.doc:
It is not hard to prove that the density $\delta_l$ of integers for which $h(n) = l$ exists
and satisfies $$\sum_l \delta_l = 1$$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_942.variants.density :
    ∃ δ : ℕ → ℝ, ∀ l, {n | erdos_942.h n = l}.HasDensity (δ l) ∧
    ∑' l, δ l = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 943
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/943](https://www.erdosproblems.com/943)

statements.name: Erdos943.erdos_943
statements.doc: Let $A$ be the set of powerful numbers. Is is true that $1_A\ast 1_A(n)=n^{o(1)}$ for every $n$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_943 :
    ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ), o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (sumRep Powerful n) ≤ (n : ℝ)^(o n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 944
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/944](https://www.erdosproblems.com/944)

statements.name: Erdos944.erdos_944
statements.doc:
Let $k \ge 4$ and $r\ge 1$. Must there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$
 such that every vertex is critical, yet every critical set of edges has size $>r$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_944 :
    ∀ k ≥ 4, ∀ r ≥ 1, ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k r

statements.name: Erdos944.erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture
statements.doc:
Let $k \ge 4$. Must there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$
such that every vertex is critical, yet every critical set of edges has size $>1$?

This was conjectured by Dirac in 1970.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture :
    ∀ k ≥ 4, ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k 1

statements.name: Erdos944.erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_eq_5
statements.doc:
Dirac's conjecture was proved, for $k=5$: There exists a graph $G$ with chromatic number $5$, such
that every vertex is critical, yet every critical set of edges has size $>1$, or in other words:
has no critical edge.

[Br92] Brown, Jason I., A vertex critical graph without critical edges. Discrete Math. (1992), 99--101
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_eq_5 :
    ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 5 1

statements.name: Erdos944.erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_sub_one_not_prime
statements.doc:
Lattanzio [La02] proved there exist $k$-critical graphs without critical edges for all $k$ such that
$k - 1$ is not prime.

[La02] Lattanzio, John J., A note on a conjecture of {D}irac. Discrete Math. (2002), 323--330
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_sub_one_not_prime (k : ℕ) (hk : 4 ≤ k)
    (h : ¬ (k - 1).Prime) : ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k 1

statements.name: Erdos944.erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_ge_five
statements.doc:
Jensen [Je02] gave an construction for $k$-critical graphs without any critical edges for all $k ≥ 5$.

[Je02] Jensen, Tommy R., Dense critical and vertex-critical graphs. Discrete Math. (2002), 63--84.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_ge_five (k : ℕ) (hk : 5 ≤ k) :
    ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k 1

statements.name: Erdos944.erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_eq_four
statements.doc:
The case $k=4$ and $r=1$ was the remaining open case: Are there $4$-critical graphs
without any critical edges?

Answer: Yes. The Lean formalization linked below proves the existence of such a graph.
Together with Jensen's result for $k \ge 5$, this settles Dirac's conjecture for every
$k \ge 4$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_eq_four :
    ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 4 1

statements.name: Erdos944.erdos_944.variants.large_k_for_any_r
statements.doc:
Martinsson and Steiner [MaSt25] proved for every $r \ge 1$ if $k$ is sufficiently large, depending
on $r$, there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$ such that every vertex is critical,
yet every critical set of edges has size $>r$.

[MaSt25] Martinsson, Anders and Steiner, Raphael, Vertex-critical graphs far from edge-criticality. Combin. Probab. Comput. (2025), 151--157
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_944.variants.large_k_for_any_r (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) : ∀ᶠ k in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k r

problems.title: Erdős Problem 945
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/945](https://www.erdosproblems.com/945)
 - [ErMi52] Erdős, P. and Mirsky, L., The distribution of values of the divisor function {$d(n)$}. Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) (1952), 257--271.

statements.name: Erdos945.erdos_945
statements.doc: Is it true that $F(x) \leq (\log x)^{O(1)}$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_945 : Erdos945Prop

statements.name: Erdos945.erdos_945.variants.constant
statements.doc:
Is there a constant $C > 0$ such that, for all large $x$, every interval $[x, x+(\log x)C]$
contains two integers with the same number of divisors?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_945.variants.constant : Erdos945Constant

statements.name: Erdos945.erdos_945.variants.equivalence
statements.doc: The two ways of phrasing the conjecture are equivalent.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_945.variants.equivalence : Erdos945Prop ↔ Erdos945Constant

statements.name: Erdos945.erdos_945.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc: Erdős and Mirsky [ErMi52] proved that $\frac{(\log x)^{1/2}}{\log\log x}\ll F(x)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_945.variants.lower_bound :
    (fun (x : ℕ) => (log x).sqrt /(log x).log) =O[atTop] fun (n : ℕ) => (F n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos945.erdos_945.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc: Erdős and Mirsky [ErMi52] proved that $\log F(x) \ll \frac{(\log x)^{1/2}}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_945.variants.upper_bound :
    (fun (n : ℕ) => (F n : ℝ).log) =O[atTop] fun (x : ℕ) => (log x).sqrt /(log x).log

problems.title: Erdős Problem 946
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/946](https://www.erdosproblems.com/946)
 - [ErMi52] Erdős, P. and Mirsky, L., The distribution of values of the divisor function {$d(n)$}.
   Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) (1952), 257--271.
 - [Sp81] Spiro, C. A., The frequency with which an integral-valued, prime-independent,
   multiplicative or additive function of n divides a polynomial function of n.
 - [He84] Heath-Brown, D. R., The divisor function at consecutive integers.
   Mathematika 31 (1984), no. 2, 141--149.
 - [Hi85] Hildebrand, A., The divisor function at consecutive integers. Pacific J. Math.
   (1987), 307--319
 - [EPS87] Erdős, P., Pomerance, C., and Sarkőzy, A., On locally repeated values of
   arithmetic functions. III. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1987), 1--7.

statements.name: Erdos946.erdos_946
statements.doc:
There are infinitely many $n$ such that $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$. Proved in [He84].
Here τ is the divisor counting function, which is `σ 0` in mathlib.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_946 : {n : ℕ | σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 1)}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos946.erdos_946.variants.spiro_5040
statements.doc: There are infinitely many $n$ such that $τ(n) = τ(n + 5040)$. Proved in [Sp81].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_946.variants.spiro_5040 : {n : ℕ | σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 5040)}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos946.erdos_946.variants.heathbrown_lower_bound
statements.doc:
The number of $n \le x$ with $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$ is at least $x / (\log x)^7$ for all sufficiently
large $x$. Proved in [He84].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_946.variants.heathbrown_lower_bound :
    (fun x => x / (x.log)^7) =O[atTop] erdos946Count

statements.name: Erdos946.erdos_946.variants.hildebrand_lower_bound
statements.doc: Improved lower bound in [Hi85]: $Ω(x / (\log \log x)^3)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_946.variants.hildebrand_lower_bound :
    (fun x => x / (x.log.log)^3) =O[atTop] erdos946Count

statements.name: Erdos946.erdos_946.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc: Upper bound in [EPS87]: $O(x / \sqrt{\log \log x})$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_946.variants.upper_bound : erdos946Count =O[atTop] (fun x => x / √x.log.log )

problems.title: Erdős Problem 947
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/947](https://www.erdosproblems.com/947)
- [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III*. Number theory
  day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
- [Er50] Erdős, P., *On integers of the form $2^k+p$ and some related problems*. Summa Brasil.
  Math. (1950), 113-123.

statements.name: Erdos947.erdos_947
statements.doc:
There is no exact covering system - that is, a finite collection of congruence classes
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ with distinct $n_i$ such that every integer satisfies exactly one of these
congruence classes.

This is true, and was proved independently by Mirsky and Newman and by Davenport and Rado; the
Mirsky–Newman proof first appeared in [Er50]. See also [Er77c].

A `StrictCoveringSystem ℤ` is a finite family of congruence classes with distinct moduli
$n_i \geq 2$ covering $\mathbb{Z}$; the trivial exact covering system consisting of the single
class $0 \pmod 1$ is therefore excluded.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_947 : ¬ ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ, Pairwise (Disjoint on c.coset)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 948
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/948](https://www.erdosproblems.com/948)
- [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III*. Number theory day
  (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
- [ErGa91] Erdős, P. and Galvin, F., *Some Ramsey-type theorems*. Discrete Math. 87 (1991),
  261–269.

statements.name: Erdos948.erdos_948
statements.doc:
Is there a function $f(n)$ and a $k$ such that in any $k$-colouring of the integers there exists a
sequence $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ such that $a_n < f(n)$ for infinitely many $n$ and the set
$$\left\{ \sum_{i \in S} a_i : \textrm{finite nonempty } S \right\}$$
does not contain all colours?

A question of Erdős [Er77c] and Erdős and Galvin [ErGa91]. The answer is no: GPT-5.5 Pro (prompted
by Price) showed that for every $f$ there is a colouring of the integers such that the finite sums
of every such sequence use all colours. The linked formal proof (Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol) gives, for
every $f$ and $k \ge 1$, a colouring $c : \mathbb{Z} \to \{0, \ldots, k - 1\}$ such that for every
strictly increasing $a$ with $a_n < f(n)$ infinitely often and every colour, some nonempty finite
sum of the $a_i$ has that colour.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_948 :
    ¬ ∃ (f : ℕ → ℕ) (k : ℕ), 0 < k ∧ ∀ colouring : ℤ → Fin k,
      ∃ a : ℕ → ℤ, StrictMono a ∧ {n | a n < f n}.Infinite ∧
        ∃ c : Fin k, ∀ S : Finset ℕ, S.Nonempty → colouring (∑ i ∈ S, a i) ≠ c

statements.name: Erdos948.erdos_948.variants.monochromatic
statements.doc:
The original question asks for the set of finite sums to be monochromatic. Galvin showed that
this fails for $k = 2$, and it fails for every $k \ge 2$ by the negative answer to `erdos_948`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_948.variants.monochromatic :
    ¬ ∃ (f : ℕ → ℕ) (k : ℕ), 2 ≤ k ∧ ∀ colouring : ℤ → Fin k,
      ∃ a : ℕ → ℤ, StrictMono a ∧ {n | a n < f n}.Infinite ∧
        ∃ c : Fin k, ∀ S : Finset ℕ, S.Nonempty → colouring (∑ i ∈ S, a i) = c

problems.title: Erdős Problem 949
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/949](https://www.erdosproblems.com/949)

statements.name: Erdos949.erdos_949
statements.doc:
