Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a set containing no solutions to $a + b = c$.
Must there be a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R} \setminus S$ of cardinality continuum such that
$A + A \subseteq \mathbb{R}\setminus S$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_949 :
    ∀ S : Set ℝ, (∀ a ∈ S, ∀ b ∈ S, a + b ∉ S) → ∃ A ⊆ Sᶜ, #A = 𝔠 ∧ A + A ⊆ Sᶜ

statements.name: Erdos949.erdos_949.variants.sidon
statements.doc:
Let $S\sub \mathbb{R}$ be a Sidon set. Must there be a set $A\sub \mathbb{R}∖S$ of cardinality
continuum such that $A + A \sub \mathbb{R}∖S$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_949.variants.sidon :
    ∀ S : Set ℝ, IsSidon S → ∃ A ⊆ Sᶜ, #A = 𝔠 ∧ A + A ⊆ Sᶜ

problems.title: Erdős Problem 950
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/855](https://www.erdosproblems.com/855)
- [erdosproblems.com/950](https://www.erdosproblems.com/950)
- [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III. Number theory day
  (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
- [mathoverflow/508491](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/508491)

statements.name: Erdos950.erdos_950.parts.i
statements.doc: Is it true that $\liminf f(n)=1$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_950.parts.i :
    atTop.liminf (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : EReal)) = 1

statements.name: Erdos950.erdos_950.parts.ii
statements.doc: Is it true that $\limsup f(n)=\infty$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_950.parts.ii :
    atTop.limsup (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : EReal)) = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos950.erdos_950.parts.iii
statements.doc: Is it true that $f(n)=o(\log\log n)$ for all $n$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_950.parts.iii :
    f =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log n))

statements.name: Erdos950.erdos_950.variants.debruijn_erdos_turan
statements.doc:
This function was considered by de Bruijn, Erdős, and Turán, who showed that
$\sum_{n<x}f(n)\sim \sum_{n<x}f(n)^2\sim x$. They gave no proofs, but a proof of the (harder) second
claim is given by Gorodetsky here [mathoverflow/508491].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_950.variants.debruijn_erdos_turan :
    (fun x : ℕ ↦ ∑ n ∈ Finset.range x, f n) ~[atTop] (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ)) ∧
    (fun x : ℕ ↦ ∑ n ∈ Finset.range x, (f n) ^ 2) ~[atTop] (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos950.erdos_950.variants.weaker_pi
statements.doc:
Erdős writes that a 'weaker conjecture which is perhaps not quite inaccessible' is that,
for every $\epsilon>0$, if $x$ is sufficiently large there exists $y<x$ such that
$\pi(x)< \pi(y)+\epsilon \pi(x-y)$. Compare this to [855].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_950.variants.weaker_pi :
    ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∃ y < x,
      (π x : ℝ) < (π y : ℝ) + ε * (π (x - y) : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos950.erdos_950.variants.weaker_pi_implies_f
statements.doc:
He notes that if $\pi(x)< \pi(y)+O\left(\frac{x-y}{\log x}\right)$ for all $y<x-(\log x)^C$ for
some constant $C>0$ then $f(n)\ll \log\log\log n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_950.variants.weaker_pi_implies_f
    (h : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∃ K > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, ∀ y : ℕ,
      (y : ℝ) < x - (Real.log x) ^ C →
      (π x : ℝ) < (π y : ℝ) + K * ((x - y : ℝ) / Real.log x)) :
    f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log (Real.log n))

statements.name: Erdos950.erdos_950.variants.sum_primes
statements.doc:
The study of $f(p)$ is even harder, and Erdős could not prove that
$\sum_{p<x}f(p)^2\sim \pi(x)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_950.variants.sum_primes :
    (fun x : ℕ ↦ ∑ p ∈ (Finset.range x).filter Prime, (f p) ^ 2) ~[atTop]
      fun x ↦ (π x : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 951
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/951](https://www.erdosproblems.com/951)
 - [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III. Number theory day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ.,
    New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.

statements.name: Erdos951.erdos_951
statements.doc: If `1 < a 0 < ...` has property `Erdos951Prop`, is it true that `#{a i ≤ x} ≤ π x`?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_951 :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, 1 < a 0 → StrictMono a → Erdos951Prop a →
      ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, {i : ℕ | a i ≤ x}.ncard ≤ π ⌊x⌋₊

statements.name: Erdos951.erdos_951.variants.beurling
statements.doc:
Beurling conjectured that if `1 < a 0 < a 1 < ⋯` has property `Erdos951Prop` and the number
of reals in $[1, x]$ of the form $\prod_i a_i^{k_i}$ is $x + o(\log x)$, then `a` must be the
sequence of primes. Property `Erdos951Prop` makes distinct exponent vectors give distinct
Beurling integers, so counting the set `BeurlingIntegers a` counts the generalised integers.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_951.variants.beurling :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, IsBeurlingPrimes a → Erdos951Prop a →
    ((fun x => (BeurlingIntegers a ∩ .Iic x).ncard - x) =o[atTop] Real.log) →
    a = Nat.cast ∘ Nat.nth Nat.Prime

problems.title: Erdős Problem 952
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/952](https://www.erdosproblems.com/952)
- [Wikipedia](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaussian_moat)
- [OAI26a] OpenAI, *Bounded-Step Walks on Gaussian Primes*. OpenAI Math Release preprint (2026).
  https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/Bounded-Step-Walks-on-Gaussian-Primes-September-26-2026/paper.pdf

statements.name: Erdos952.erdos_952
statements.doc:
Is there an infinite sequence of distinct Gaussian primes $x_1,x_2,\ldots$
such that $\lvert x_{n+1}-x_n\rvert \ll 1$?

No. This was disproved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26a]; see the linked
Lean proof.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_952 :
  ¬ ∃ (x : ℕ → GaussianInt) (C : ℤ),
    Function.Injective x ∧
      ∀ n, Prime (x n) ∧ (x (n + 1) - x n).norm < C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 954
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/954](https://www.erdosproblems.com/954)
- [Er77c] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III*. Number theory
  day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976), Lecture Notes in Math. 626, Springer
  (1977), 43-72. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1977-27.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos954.erdos_954
statements.doc:
Let $0=a_0<a_1<a_2<\cdots$ be the sequence of integers defined by $a_0=0$ and $a_1=1$, and
$a_{k+1}$ is the smallest integer $n$ for which the number of solutions to $a_i+a_j \leq n$
(with $0\leq i\leq j\leq k$ and $j\geq 1$) is $<n$.

Is the number of solutions to $a_i+a_j \leq x$ equal to $x+O(x^{1/4+o(1)})$?

The sequence was constructed by Rosen [Er77c, p. 71]. We read $O(x^{1/4+o(1)})$ as
$O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and use the version with $a_0=0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_954 :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), (fun x : ℕ ↦ (solutionCount x : ℝ) - x) =O[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 4 + ε))

statements.name: Erdos954.erdos_954.variants.upper
statements.doc:
Erdős and Rosen could not even prove that the number of solutions to $a_i+a_j\leq x$ is at most
$(1+o(1))x$ [Er77c, p. 71].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_954.variants.upper :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (solutionCount x : ℝ) ≤ (1 + ε) * x

statements.name: Erdos954.erdos_954.variants.lower
statements.doc:
The number of solutions to $a_i+a_j\leq x$ is always at least $x$ by construction
[Er77c, p. 71].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_954.variants.lower : ∀ x : ℕ, x ≤ solutionCount x

problems.title: Erdős Problem 955
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/955](https://www.erdosproblems.com/955)
- [EGPS90] Erdős, P. and Granville, A. and Pomerance, C. and Spiro, C., On the normal behavior of
  the iterates of some arithmetic functions. Analytic number theory (Allerton Park, IL, 1989)
  (1990), 165-204.
- [Er73b] Erdős, P., Über die Zahlen der Form $\sigma(n) - n$ und $n - \phi(n)$. Elem. Math.
  (1973), 83--86.
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
- [PPT18] Pollack, Paul and Pomerance, Carl and Thompson, Lola, Divisor-sum fibers. Mathematika
  (2018), 330--342.
- [Po14b] Pollack, Paul, Some arithmetic properties of the sum of proper divisors and the sum of
  prime divisors. Illinois J. Math. (2014), 125--147.
- [PoPo16] Pollack, Paul and Pomerance, Carl, Some problems of Erdős on the sum-of-divisors
  function. Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B (2016), 1--26.
- [Tr15] Troupe, Lee, On the number of prime factors of values of the sum-of-proper-divisors
  function. J. Number Theory (2015), 120--135.
- [Tr20] Troupe, Lee, Divisor sums representable as the sum of two squares. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (2020), 4189--4202.

statements.name: Erdos955.erdos_955
statements.doc:
If $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ has density $0$ then $s^{-1}(A)$ must also have density $0$.

A conjecture of Erdős, Granville, Pomerance, and Spiro [EGPS90].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_955 :
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.HasDensity 0 → { x | s x ∈ A }.HasDensity 0

statements.name: Erdos955.erdos_955.variants.positive_density
statements.doc:
It is possible for $s(A)$ to have positive density even if $A$ has zero density (for example
taking $A$ to be the product of two distinct primes).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_955.variants.positive_density :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.HasDensity 0 ∧ (∃ d > 0, (s '' A).HasDensity d)

statements.name: Erdos955.erdos_955.variants.empty_preimage
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er73b] proved that there are sets $A$ of positive density such that $s^{-1}(A)$ is empty.

Here "positive density" means positive lower density: Erdős proved that the set of untouchable
numbers (those not of the form $s(n)$) has positive lower density [Er73b, Satz I]. Pollack and
Pomerance [PoPo16] conjecture that this set has a natural density and give a heuristic for its
value. The same result is stated as `erdos_418.variants.sigma` in Erdős Problem 418.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_955.variants.empty_preimage :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, 0 < A.lowerDensity ∧ { x | s x ∈ A } = ∅

statements.name: Erdos955.erdos_955.variants.pollack_primes
statements.doc: Pollack [Po14b] has shown that this is true if $A$ is the set of primes.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_955.variants.pollack_primes :
    { x | Nat.Prime (s x) }.HasDensity 0

statements.name: Erdos955.erdos_955.variants.troupe_unusually_many_prime_factors
statements.doc:
Troupe [Tr15] has shown that this is true if $A$ is the set of integers with unusually many prime
factors.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_955.variants.troupe_unusually_many_prime_factors :
    ∀ ε > 0, { x | (1 + ε) * Real.log (Real.log (s x)) <
      (ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors (s x) : ℝ) }.HasDensity 0

statements.name: Erdos955.erdos_955.variants.troupe_sum_of_two_squares
statements.doc:
Troupe [Tr20] has also shown this is true if $A$ is the set of integers which are the sum of two
squares.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_955.variants.troupe_sum_of_two_squares :
    { x | ∃ a b : ℕ, s x = a^2 + b^2 }.HasDensity 0

statements.name: Erdos955.erdos_955.variants.pollack_pomerance_thompson_bound
statements.doc:
Pollack, Pomerance, and Thompson [PPT18] prove that if $\epsilon(x)=o(1)$ and $A\subset \mathbb{N}$
has size at most $x^{1/2+\epsilon(x)}$ then $\#\{ n\leq x: s(n)\in A\} =o(x)$ as $x\to \infty$. It
follows that (using $s(n)\ll n\log\log n$) if $A$ grows like
$\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert\leq x^{1/2+o(1)}$ then $s^{-1}(A)$ has density $0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_955.variants.pollack_pomerance_thompson_bound :
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (ε : ℕ → ℝ),
      Tendsto ε atTop (𝓝 0) →
      (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (count (· ∈ A) n : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 / 2 : ℝ) + ε n)) →
      { x | s x ∈ A }.HasDensity 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 957
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/957](https://www.erdosproblems.com/957)
- [Du19] Dumitrescu, Adrian, *A product inequality for extreme distances*.
  Comput. Geom. 85 (2019), 101577.
  [PDF](https://adriandumitrescu.org/product-ineq.pdf)
- [ErPa90] Erdős, P. and Pach, J., *Variations on the theme of repeated distances*.
  Combinatorica 10 (1990), 261-269.

statements.name: Erdos957.erdos_957
statements.doc:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of size $n$ and let $\{d_1<\ldots<d_k\}$ be the set of
distinct distances determined by $A$. Let $f(d)$ be the number of times the distance $d$ is
determined. Is it true that
$$f(d_1)f(d_k) \leq (\tfrac{9}{8}+o(1))n^2?$$

A question of Erdős and Pach [ErPa90]. The answer is yes, proved by Dumitrescu [Du19]. Here
$f(d)$ counts unordered pairs of points of $A$ at distance $d$ (`distanceMultiplicity`), and
$o(1)$ is uniform over all $A$ of size $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_957 :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℝ², A.card = n →
      ∀ d₁ dₖ : ℝ, IsLeast (distanceSet A : Set ℝ) d₁ →
        IsGreatest (distanceSet A : Set ℝ) dₖ →
          (distanceMultiplicity A d₁ : ℝ) * distanceMultiplicity A dₖ ≤
            (9 / 8 + ε) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos957.erdos_957.variants.dumitrescu
statements.doc:
The original problem was solved by Dumitrescu [Du19, Theorem 1], who proved that
$$f(d_1)f(d_k)\leq \frac{9}{8}n^2+O(n).$$
Here a single constant $C$ in the error term $Cn$ works for all finite $A \subset \mathbb{R}^2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_957.variants.dumitrescu :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ A : Finset ℝ², ∀ d₁ dₖ : ℝ, IsLeast (distanceSet A : Set ℝ) d₁ →
      IsGreatest (distanceSet A : Set ℝ) dₖ →
        (distanceMultiplicity A d₁ : ℝ) * distanceMultiplicity A dₖ ≤
          9 / 8 * (A.card : ℝ) ^ 2 + C * (A.card : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 958
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/958](https://www.erdosproblems.com/958)
- [CDL25] Clemen, F., Dumitrescu, A. and Liu, D., *On multiplicities of interpoint distances*.
  arXiv:2505.04283 (2025).
- [PALOMAR-2026-10-05-000004](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-05-000004&version=1)

statements.name: Erdos958.erdos_958
statements.doc:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite set of size $n$, and let $\{d_1,\ldots,d_k\}$ be the set of
distances determined by $A$. Let $f(d)$ be the multiplicity of $d$, that is, the number of
unordered pairs from $A$ of distance $d$ apart.

Is it true that $k=n-1$ and $\{f(d_i)\}=\{n-1,\ldots,1\}$ if and only if $A$ is a set of
equidistant points on a line or a circle?

Erdős conjectured that the answer is no, and other such configurations exist.

This was proved by Clemen, Dumitrescu, and Liu [CDL25], who observed that equidistant points on a
short circular arc on a circle of radius $1$, together with the centre, are also an example.

The classification is asked for all sufficiently large $n$. Small exceptions such as
$\{(0,0), (1,0), (0,1), (0,-1)\}$ exist, so the negative answer asserts
counterexamples of arbitrarily large size, as in [CDL25].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_958 :
    ¬ ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ A : Finset ℝ², #A = n →
      ((#(distanceSet A) = n - 1 ∧
            (distanceSet A).image (distanceMultiplicity A) = Finset.Icc 1 (n - 1)) →
        (IsEquidistantOnLine A ∨ IsEquidistantOnCircle A))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 959
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/959](https://www.erdosproblems.com/959)

statements.name: Erdos959.erdos_959
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of size $n$ and let $\{d_1,\ldots,d_k\}$ be
the set of distinct distances determined by $A$. Let $f(d)$ be the number of times
the distance $d$ is determined, ordered so that
$f(d_1)\geq f(d_2)\geq \cdots \geq f(d_k)$. Estimate
$$\max (f(d_1)-f(d_2)),$$
where the maximum is taken over all $A$ of size $n$ (this is `extremalGap n`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_959 :
    (fun n ↦ (extremalGap n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_959.answer

statements.name: Erdos959.erdos_959.lower_bound
statements.doc:
A superlinear lower bound: there is a $c>0$ with
$$\text{extremalGap}(n)\geq n^{1 + c/\log\log n}$$
for all large $n$, so $\max (f(d_1)-f(d_2))$ grows faster than any linear function
of $n$. Determining the exact order remains open, which is `erdos_959`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_959.lower_bound :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N,
      (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + c / Real.log (Real.log n)) ≤ extremalGap n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 961
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/961](https://www.erdosproblems.com/961)
- [Ju74] Jutila, Matti, On numbers with a large prime factor. {II}. J. Indian Math. Soc. (N.S.) (1974), 125--130.
- [RaSh73](https://eudml.org/doc/urn:eudml:doc:205214) Ramachandra, K. and Shorey, T. N., On gaps between numbers with a large prime factor. Acta Arith. (1973), 99--111.

statements.name: Erdos961.erdos_961.sylvester_schur
statements.doc:
Sylvester and Schur [Er34] proved that every set of $k$ consecutive integers greater than $k$
contains an integer divisible by a prime greater than $k$, i.e. not $(k+1)$-smooth.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_961.sylvester_schur (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) : Erdos961Prop k k

statements.name: Erdos961.erdos_961.variants.well_defined
statements.doc: There exists $n$ such that `Erdos961Prop k n` holds.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_961.variants.well_defined (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k): ∃ n, Erdos961Prop k n

statements.name: Erdos961.erdos_961
statements.doc: It is conjectured that $f(k) \ll (\log k)^O(1)$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_961 : ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, f k < log k ^ C

statements.name: Erdos961.erdos_961.variants.erdos_upper_bound
statements.doc: Erdos [Er55d] proved $f(k) < 3 \frac{k}{\log k}$ for sufficiently large $k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_961.variants.erdos_upper_bound :
    ∀ᶠ k in atTop, f k < 3 * k / log k

statements.name: Erdos961.erdos_961.variants.jutila_ramachandra_shorey_upper_bound
statements.doc:
Jutila [Ju74], and Ramachandra--Shorey [RaSh73] proved a stronger upper bound
$f(k) \ll \frac{\log \log \log k}{\log \log k} \frac{k}{\log k}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_961.variants.jutila_ramachandra_shorey_upper_bound :
    (fun k => (f k : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun k => log (log (log k)) / log (log k) * (k / log k)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 962
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/962](https://www.erdosproblems.com/962)
- [Er65] Erdős, P., Extremal problems in number theory. Proc. Sympos. Pure Math., Vol. VIII (1965), 181-189.
- [Er76e] Erdős, P., Problems and results on consecutive integers. Publ. Math. Debrecen (1976), 271-282.
- [Tang](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-962/blob/main/On_Erd%C5%91s_Problem_962.pdf)
- [Tao](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/962)

statements.name: Erdos962.erdos_962
statements.doc:
Main conjecture:

$\log k(n) \le (\log n)^{(1/2 + o(1))}$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_962 :
    ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ,
      (∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, |ε n| < δ) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
        log (k n : ℝ)
          ≤ rpow (log n) ((1 : ℝ) / 2 + ε n)

statements.name: Erdos962.erdos_962.variants.tang_lower_bound
statements.doc:
Tang's lower bound [Tang]:

$\log k(n) \ge (1/\sqrt{2} - o(1)) * \sqrt{\log n * \log \log n}$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_962.variants.tang_lower_bound :
    ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ,
      (∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, |ε n| < δ) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
          (1 / sqrt 2 - ε n) *
              sqrt (log n * log (log n))
            ≤ log (k n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos962.erdos_962.variants.tao_upper_bound
statements.doc:
Tao's upper bound [Tao]:

$k(n) \le (1 + o(1)) * n^{1/2}$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_962.variants.tao_upper_bound :
    ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ,
      (∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, |ε n| < δ) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
          (k n : ℝ) ≤ (1 + ε n) * sqrt n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 963
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/963](https://www.erdosproblems.com/963)
- [Er65] Erdős, P., *Extremal problems in number theory*. Proc. Sympos. Pure Math., Vol. VIII
  (1965), 181-189. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1965-02.pdf)

A set `B` of real numbers is dissociated if all sums over its finite subsets are distinct. This is
`AddDissociated` in Mathlib.

statements.name: Erdos963.erdos_963.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that in any set $A\subset \mathbb{R}$ of size $n$ there is a
subset $B\subseteq A$ of size $\lvert B\rvert\geq k$ which is dissociated that is, the sums
$\sum_{b\in S}b$ are distinct for all $S\subseteq B$. Estimate $f(n)$ - in particular, is it true
that $f(n)\geq \lfloor \log_2 n\rfloor$?

This is the first part, a problem of Erdős [Er65, p. 188]. We read "estimate" as an asymptotic
equivalence $f(n)\sim$ `answer n`. The order of magnitude $\log n$ is easy (see
`erdos_963.variants.greedy` and the example $a_i=i$ in [Er65, p. 188]), so the question is the
constant.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_963.parts.i :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] erdos_963.parts.i.answer

statements.name: Erdos963.erdos_963.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that in any set $A\subset \mathbb{R}$ of size $n$ there is a
subset $B\subseteq A$ of size $\lvert B\rvert\geq k$ which is dissociated that is, the sums
$\sum_{b\in S}b$ are distinct for all $S\subseteq B$. Estimate $f(n)$ - in particular, is it true
that $f(n)\geq \lfloor \log_2 n\rfloor$?

This is the second part. Erdős [Er65, p. 188] asks whether the bound $\lfloor\log_3 n\rfloor$ can
be improved to $\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$. We state it for all $n\geq 1$, with
$\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ written as `Nat.log 2 n`.

As on the problem page, $A$ is any set of reals. [Er65] speaks of "given numbers" and uses the
example $a_i=i$. Allowing negative numbers makes the question harder. A dissociated set never
contains both $x$ and $-x$, and changing signs keeps a set dissociated. So the largest dissociated
subsets of $A$ and of $\{\lvert a\rvert : a\in A,\ a\neq 0\}$ have the same size, and the sets
$\{\pm a : a\in S\}$ (with $0$ added for odd $n$) show that $f(2m)=f(2m+1)$ is the least size of a
largest dissociated subset of a set of $m$ positive reals. Hence this statement asks for
$\lfloor\log_2 m\rfloor+1$ for $m$ positive reals. The question for positive reals with
$\lfloor\log_2\lvert A\rvert\rfloor$, one less, is `erdos_963.variants.positive`; it follows from
this statement.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_963.parts.ii : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → Nat.log 2 n ≤ f n

statements.name: Erdos963.erdos_963.variants.greedy
statements.doc:
Erdős noted that the greedy algorithm showed $f(n)\geq \lfloor \log_3 n\rfloor$
[Er65, p. 188].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_963.variants.greedy (n : ℕ) : Nat.log 3 n ≤ f n

statements.name: Erdos963.erdos_963.variants.positive
statements.doc:
The second part for sets of positive reals, with $\lfloor\log_2\lvert A\rvert\rfloor$ as in
[Er65, p. 188] and its example $a_i=i$: every set $A$ of positive reals has a dissociated subset
with at least $\lfloor\log_2 \lvert A\rvert\rfloor$ elements.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_963.variants.positive :
    ∀ A : Finset ℝ, (∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a) →
      ∃ B ⊆ A, Nat.log 2 A.card ≤ B.card ∧ AddDissociated (B : Set ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 964
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/964](https://www.erdosproblems.com/964)
- [Er86b] Erdős, P., *Some problems on number theory*. Proceedings of the seventeenth Southeastern
  international conference on combinatorics, graph theory, and computing (Boca Raton, Fla.,
  1986), Congr. Numer. 54 (1986), 225-244.
- [Eb25] Eberhard, S., *Ratios of consecutive values of the divisor function*.
  [arXiv:2505.00727](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00727) (2025).

statements.name: Erdos964.erdos_964
statements.doc:
Let $\tau(n)$ count the number of divisors of $n$. Is the sequence
$$\frac{\tau(n+1)}{\tau(n)}$$
everywhere dense in $(0,\infty)$?

The answer is yes, proved by Eberhard [Eb25].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_964 : Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ) ⊆ closure (tauRatio '' Set.Ici 1)

statements.name: Erdos964.erdos_964.variants.eberhard
statements.doc:
Eberhard [Eb25] proved that the ratios $\tau(n+1)/\tau(n)$ attain every positive rational value
infinitely many times. Since the positive rationals are dense in $(0,\infty)$, this implies
`erdos_964`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_964.variants.eberhard (q : ℚ) (hq : 0 < q) :
    {n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ tauRatio n = q}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 965
problems.doc:
For every 2-coloring of ℝ, is there an uncountable set $A ⊆ ℝ$ such that
all sums $a + b$ for $a, b ∈ A, a ≠ b$ have the same colour?

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/965](https://www.erdosproblems.com/965)
- [Er75b] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Journées Arithmétiques de Bordeaux (Conf., Univ. Bordeaux, Bordeaux, 1974) (1975), 295-310.
- [HLS17] Hindman, Neil and Leader, Imre and Strauss, Dona, Pairwise sums in colourings of the reals. Abh. Math. Semin. Univ. Hambg. (2017), 275--287.
- [Ko16] Komjáth, Péter, A certain 2-coloring of the reals. Real Anal. Exchange (2016), 227--231.
- [SWCol] Sokoup Dániel and Weiss, William, Sums and Anti-Ramsey Colourings of ℝ. https://danieltsoukup.github.io/academic/finset_colouring.pdf

statements.name: Erdos965.erdos_965
statements.doc:
Erdős asks in [Er75b] if for every 2-coloring of ℝ, there is an uncountable set $A ⊆ ℝ$ such that
all sums $a + b$ for $a, b ∈ A, a ≠ b$ have the same colour.

In [Ko16] Péter Komjáth constructed a counterexample.
The same result was proven independently in [SWCol] by Sokoup and Weiss.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_965 :
    ¬ ∀ f : ℝ → Fin 2, ∃ A : Set ℝ, ¬ A.Countable ∧
      ∀ᵉ (a ∈ A) (b ∈ A) (c ∈ A) (d ∈ A), a ≠ b → c ≠ d → f (a + b) = f (c + d)

statements.name: Erdos965.erdos_965.variants.generalization
statements.doc:
For every 2-coloring of ℝ, is there some $k ≥ 2$ and an uncountable set $A ⊆ ℝ$ such that all
sums $a_1 + \cdots + a_k$ of $k$ distinct elements of $A$ have the same colour?

In fact, in both [Ko16] and [SWCol] a single 2-coloring of ℝ is constructed such that for every
$k ≥ 2$ and every uncountable $A ⊆ ℝ$ the sums of $k$ distinct elements of $A$ are not
monochromatic.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_965.variants.generalization :
    ¬ ∀ f : ℝ → Fin 2, ∃ k ≥ 2, ∃ A : Set ℝ, ¬ A.Countable ∧ ∀ s t : Finset ℝ,
      ↑s ⊆ A → ↑t ⊆ A → s.card = k → t.card = k → f (s.sum id) = f (t.sum id)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 966
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/966](https://www.erdosproblems.com/966)
- [Er75b] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Journées
  Arithmétiques de Bordeaux (Conf., Univ. Bordeaux, Bordeaux, 1974) (1975), 295-310.

statements.name: Erdos966.erdos_966
statements.doc:
Let $k,r\geq 2$. Does there exist a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that contains no non-trivial
arithmetic progression of length $k+1$, yet in any $r$-colouring of $A$ there must exist a
monochromatic non-trivial arithmetic progression of length $k$?

Erdős [Er75b] reported that 'Spencer has recently shown that such a sequence exists', but gives
no reference.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_966 :
    ∀ k r : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → 2 ≤ r → ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.IsAPOfLengthFree (k + 1) ∧
      ∀ coloring : A → Fin r, ContainsMonoAPofLength coloring k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 967
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/967](https://www.erdosproblems.com/967)
- [ErIn64] Erdős, P. and Ingham, A. E., *Arithmetical Tauberian theorems*. Acta Arith. (1964),
  341-356.
- [Yi25] Yip, F., *On a problem of Erdős and Ingham*. arXiv:2512.16528 (2025).

statements.name: Erdos967.erdos_967
statements.doc:
Let $1<a_1<\cdots$ be a sequence of integers such that $\sum\frac{1}{a_i}<\infty$. Is it true
that, for every $t\in \mathbb{R}$,
$$1+\sum_{k}\frac{1}{a_k^{1+it}}\neq 0?$$

Yip [Yi25] has proved that this is not always true - in fact, for any real $t\neq 0$, there
exists a sequence of integers $1<a_1<\cdots$ such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_i}<\infty$ and
$1+\sum_{k}\frac{1}{a_k^{1+it}}=0$.

This was formalized in Lean by Wu using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_967 :
    ¬ ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a → 1 < a 0 → Summable (fun k : ℕ => 1 / (a k : ℝ)) →
      ∀ t : ℝ, 1 + (∑' k, summand t (a k)) ≠ 0

statements.name: Erdos967.erdos_967.variants.yip
statements.doc:
Yip [Yi25] has proved that this is not always true - in fact, for any real $t\neq 0$, there
exists a sequence of integers $1<a_1<\cdots$ such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_i}<\infty$ and
$1+\sum_{k}\frac{1}{a_k^{1+it}}=0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_967.variants.yip (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a ∧ 1 < a 0 ∧ Summable (fun k : ℕ => 1 / (a k : ℝ)) ∧
      (1 + (∑' k, summand t (a k)) = 0)

statements.name: Erdos967.erdos_967.variants.finite
statements.doc: It remains open whether this is true for every finite sequence of integers.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_967.variants.finite :
    ∀ A : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ A, 1 < n) → ∀ t : ℝ, 1 + (∑ n ∈ A, summand t n) ≠ 0

statements.name: Erdos967.erdos_967.variants.two_three_five
statements.doc:
A question of Erdős and Ingham [ErIn64]. The simplest case they could not decide this question
for was the finite sequence $\{2,3,5\}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_967.variants.two_three_five :
    ∀ t : ℝ, 1 + (∑ n ∈ ({2, 3, 5} : Finset ℕ), summand t n) ≠ 0

statements.name: Erdos967.erdos_967.variants.tauberian
statements.doc:
Their interest in this problem arose from their proof that the statement that there are no such
zeros is equivalent to the fact that, for any non-decreasing $f:\mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$
which is bounded on every bounded interval and is $=0$ for $x<1$, the relationship
$$f(x)+\sum_k f(x/a_k)=\left(1+\sum_k \frac{1}{a_k}+o(1)\right)x$$
implies $f(x)=(1+o(1))x$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_967.variants.tauberian (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : StrictMono a) (ha₀ : 1 < a 0)
    (hsum : Summable (fun k : ℕ => 1 / (a k : ℝ))) :
    (∀ t : ℝ, 1 + (∑' k, summand t (a k)) ≠ 0) ↔
      ∀ f : ℝ → ℝ, Monotone f → (∀ x : ℝ, 0 ≤ f x) → (∀ x < 1, f x = 0) →
        (∀ x y : ℝ, BddAbove (f '' Set.Icc x y)) →
        Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => (f x + ∑' k, f (x / (a k : ℝ))) / x) atTop
          (𝓝 (1 + ∑' k, 1 / (a k : ℝ))) →
        Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => f x / x) atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 968
problems.doc:
Let `uₙ = pₙ / n`, where `pₙ` is the `n`th prime. Does the set of `n` such that `uₙ < uₙ₊₁`
have positive lower density?

Erdős and Prachar also proved that `∑_{pₙ < x} |uₙ₊₁ - uₙ| ≍ (log x)^2`, and that the set of `n`
such that `uₙ > uₙ₊₁` has positive lower density. Erdős also asked whether there are infinitely many
increasing triples `uₙ < uₙ₊₁ < uₙ₊₂` or decreasing triples `uₙ > uₙ₊₁ > uₙ₊₂`.

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/968](https://www.erdosproblems.com/968)

[ErPr61] Erdős, P. and Prachar, K., _Sätze und Probleme über pₖ/k_. Abh. Math. Sem. Univ. Hamburg
(1961/62), 251–256.

[FMT18] Ford, K. and Maynard, J. and Tao, T., _Chains of large gaps between primes_. Irregularities
in the distribution of prime numbers, Springer (2018), 1–21.

[Ma15] Maynard, J., _Small gaps between primes_. Ann. of Math. (2015), 383–413.

[OAI26a] OpenAI, _Positive lower density of large prime gaps_. OpenAI Math Release preprint (2026).
https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/Positive-lower-density-of-large-prime-gaps-September-25-2026/main.pdf

statements.name: Erdos968.erdos_968
statements.doc:
Does the set `{n | u n < u (n+1)}` have positive lower density?

Yes. This was proved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26a]; see the linked
Lean proof.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_968 : 0 < {n : ℕ | u n < u (n + 1)}.lowerDensity

statements.name: Erdos968.erdos_968.variants.sum_abs_diff_isTheta_log_sq
statements.doc:
Erdős and Prachar proved `∑_{pₙ < x} |u (n+1) - u n| ≍ (log x)^2` (see [ErPr61]).

We encode `∑_{pₙ < x}` as a sum over `n < Nat.primeCounting' x` (the number of primes `< x`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_968.variants.sum_abs_diff_isTheta_log_sq :
    (fun x : ℕ =>
        ∑ n < Nat.primeCounting' x, |u (n + 1) - u n|) =Θ[atTop]
      fun x : ℕ => log x ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos968.erdos_968.variants.decreasing_steps_pos_lower_density
statements.doc:
Erdős and Prachar proved that the set `{n | u n > u (n+1)}` has positive lower density
(see [ErPr61]).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_968.variants.decreasing_steps_pos_lower_density :
    0 < {n : ℕ | u n > u (n + 1)}.lowerDensity

statements.name: Erdos968.erdos_968.variants.infinite_increasingTriples
statements.doc:
Erdős asked whether there are infinitely many solutions to `uₙ < uₙ₊₁ < uₙ₊₂`.

The answer is yes. Since `uₙ < uₙ₊₁` is equivalent to `pₙ₊₁ - pₙ > pₙ / n`, it suffices to have
infinitely many `n` with two consecutive prime gaps larger than `pₙ / n ∼ log n`. Ford, Maynard,
and Tao [FMT18] proved that for every fixed `k` there are infinitely many `n` with `k` consecutive
prime gaps all of size `≫ log pₙ · log log pₙ · log log log log pₙ / log log log pₙ`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_968.variants.infinite_increasingTriples :
    {n : ℕ | u n < u (n + 1) ∧ u (n + 1) < u (n + 2)}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos968.erdos_968.variants.infinite_decreasingTriples
statements.doc:
Erdős asked whether there are infinitely many solutions to `uₙ > uₙ₊₁ > uₙ₊₂`.

The answer is yes. Since `uₙ > uₙ₊₁` is equivalent to `pₙ₊₁ - pₙ < pₙ / n`, it suffices to have
infinitely many `n` with `pₙ₊₂ - pₙ` bounded, because `pₙ / n → ∞`. Maynard [Ma15] proved that
`liminf (pₙ₊₂ - pₙ) < ∞`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_968.variants.infinite_decreasingTriples :
    {n : ℕ | u n > u (n + 1) ∧ u (n + 1) > u (n + 2)}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 969
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Erdős Problem 969](https://www.erdosproblems.com/969)
- Moser, L. and MacLeod, R. A., *The error term for the squarefree integers*.
  Canadian Mathematical Bulletin **9** (1966), 303–306.
  https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-1966-039-4

statements.name: Erdos969.erdos_969
statements.doc:
Let $Q(x)$ count the squarefree integers in $[1,x]$, and define $E(x)$ by
$$Q(x)=\frac{6}{\pi^2}x+E(x).$$
Determine the order of magnitude of $E(x)$: an upper bound $E(x)=O(g(x))$ with a matching
oscillation bound $E(x)\ne o(g(x))$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_969 :
    let g := erdos_969.answer
    (fun x => |squarefreeCountingError x|) =O[atTop] g ∧
      ¬(fun x => |squarefreeCountingError x|) =o[atTop] g

statements.name: Erdos969.erdos_969.variants.prime_number_theorem
statements.doc: The prime number theorem implies $E(x)=o(\sqrt{x})$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_969.variants.prime_number_theorem :
    (fun x => |squarefreeCountingError x|) =o[atTop] (fun x : ℕ => (x : ℝ).sqrt)

statements.name: Erdos969.erdos_969.variants.evelyn_linfoot
statements.doc: Evelyn and Linfoot proved $E(x)=\Omega(x^{1/4})$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_969.variants.evelyn_linfoot :
    ¬(fun x => |squarefreeCountingError x|) =o[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ => (x : ℝ) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 970
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/970](https://www.erdosproblems.com/970)
- [FGKMT18] Ford, Kevin and Green, Ben and Konyagin, Sergei and Maynard, James and Tao, Terence,
  *Long gaps between primes*. J. Amer. Math. Soc. (2018), 65-105.
- [Iw78] Iwaniec, Henryk, *On the problem of {J}acobsthal*. Demonstratio Math. (1978), 225--231.
- [OAI26a] OpenAI, *A quadratic bound for Jacobsthal's function*. OpenAI Math Release preprint
  (2026).
  https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/A-quadratic-bound-for-Jacobsthals-function-September-25-2026/paper.pdf

statements.name: Erdos970.erdos_970
statements.doc:
Let $h(k)$ be Jacobsthal's function, defined to as the minimal $m$ such that, if $n$ has at most $k$ prime factors, then in any set of $m$ consecutive integers there exists an integer coprime to $n$. Determine the order of magnitude of $h(k)$. In particular, is it true that $$h(k) \ll k^2?$$

The bound $h(k) \ll k^2$ was proved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26a]; see
the linked Lean proof. The order of magnitude of $h(k)$ remains open.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_970 :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → (jacobsthalFunction k : ℝ) ≤ C * k ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos970.erdos_970.variants.iterated_log
statements.doc: The stronger bound $$h(k) \ll \frac{k^2}{(\log\log 3k)^2}$$ proved in [OAI26a].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_970.variants.iterated_log :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k →
      (jacobsthalFunction k : ℝ) ≤ C * k ^ 2 / (Real.log (Real.log (3 * k))) ^ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 971
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/971](https://www.erdosproblems.com/971)

statements.name: Erdos971.erdos_971
statements.doc:
Let `p(a, d)` be the least prime congruent to `a (mod d)`.
Does there exist a constant `c > 0` such that for all large `d`,
`p(a, d) > (1 + c) * φ(d) * log d` for `≫ φ(d)` many values of `a`?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_971 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ d in atTop,
      C * (d.totient : ℝ) ≤
        #{a < d | a.Coprime d ∧ (leastCongruentPrime a d : ℝ) > (1 + c) * d.totient * log d}

statements.name: Erdos971.erdos_971.variants.infinite_sequence
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er49c] proved that the statement in `erdos_971` holds for infinitely many values of `d`.

[Er49c] Erdős, P., _On some applications of Brun's method_. Acta Univ. Szeged. Sect. Sci. Math.
(1949), 57--63.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_971.variants.infinite_sequence :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ C > (0 : ℝ),
      {d : ℕ | C * (d.totient : ℝ) ≤
        #{a < d | a.Coprime d ∧ (leastCongruentPrime a d : ℝ) > (1 + c) * d.totient * log d}}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos971.erdos_971.variants.many_small
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er49c] proved that for any `ε > 0` we have `p(a, d) < ε * φ(d) * log d` for `≫_ε φ(d)` many
values of `a` (for all large `d`).

[Er49c] Erdős, P., _On some applications of Brun's method_. Acta Univ. Szeged. Sect. Sci. Math.
(1949), 57--63.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_971.variants.many_small :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ d in atTop,
      C * (d.totient : ℝ) ≤
        #{a < d | a.Coprime d ∧ (leastCongruentPrime a d : ℝ) < ε * d.totient * log d}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 972
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/972](https://www.erdosproblems.com/972)

statements.name: Erdos972.erdos_972
statements.doc:
**Erdős problem 972.**
Let $\alpha > 1$ be irrational. Are there infinitely many primes $p$
such that $\lfloor p\alpha \rfloor$ is also prime?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_972 : ∀ α > 1, Irrational α → (primeSet α).Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 973
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/973](https://www.erdosproblems.com/973)
- [Er92f] Erdős, L., On some problems of {P}. Turán concerning power sums of
  complex numbers. Acta Math. Hungar. (1992), 11--24.
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.
- [LYZ26] Luo, Yanping and Yang, Ruiyi and Zhu, Keheng, Exterior power sums.
  [arxiv/2607.22017](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22017)
- [TWHC26] Tan, Xiaojun and Wang, Qihang and Huang, Wei and Chen, Kun, Residual bounds for
  Schur-stable polynomials. [arxiv/2608.02043](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02043)
- [Tu84b] Turán, Paul, On a new method of analysis and its applications. (1984), xvi+584.
- [PALOMAR-2026-09-20-000008](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-09-20-000008&version=1)

statements.name: Erdos973.erdos_973
statements.doc:
Does there exist a constant $C>1$ such that, for every $n\geq 2$, there exists a sequence
$z_i\in \mathbb{C}$ with $z_1=1$ and $\lvert z_i\rvert \geq 1$ for all $1\leq i\leq n$ with
$\max_{2\leq k\leq n+1}\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq i\leq n}z_i^k\right\rvert < C^{-n}$?

This is Problem 7.3 in [Ha74], where it is attributed to Erdős.

The answer is no, by Luo, Yang and Zhu [LYZ26] (and via the residual-polynomial method of Tan,
Wang, Huang and Chen [TWHC26]): the maximum exceeds $e^{-\lambda n}$ for every fixed $\lambda>0$
once $n$ is large, so it decays subexponentially and no such $C$ exists. See
`erdos_973.variants.luo_yang_zhu` below.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_973 :
    ¬ ∃ C : ℝ, C > 1 ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → ∃ z : ℕ → ℂ,
        z 1 = 1 ∧
        (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) ∧
        (∀ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ < C ^ (-(n : ℝ)))

statements.name: Erdos973.erdos_973.variants.luo_yang_zhu
statements.doc:
The result of [LYZ26] that settles the problem: for every fixed $\lambda>0$ and all large enough
$n$, any $z_1,\dots,z_n$ with $\lvert z_j\rvert\geq 1$ satisfy
$\max_{2\leq k\leq n+1}\left\lvert\sum_j z_j^k\right\rvert > e^{-\lambda n}$.

This is sharper than `erdos_973.variants.tang`, whose bound $(2e)^{-(1+o(1))n}$ pins the rate at
$\log(2e) = 1 + \log 2$, still exponential decay.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_973.variants.luo_yang_zhu (lam : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lam) :
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ z : ℕ → ℂ,
      (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) →
      ∃ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1),
        Real.exp (-lam * n) < ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖

statements.name: Erdos973.erdos_973.variants.le_one
statements.doc:
Erdős proved (as described on p.35 of [Tu84b]) that such a sequence does exist with
$\lvert z_i\rvert\leq 1$. Indeed, Erdős' construction gives a value of $C\approx 1.32$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_973.variants.le_one :
    ∃ C : ℝ, C > 1 ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → ∃ z : ℕ → ℂ,
        z 1 = 1 ∧
        (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖z i‖ ≤ 1) ∧
        (∀ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ < C ^ (-(n : ℝ)))

statements.name: Erdos973.erdos_973.variants.m2_bounds
statements.doc:
In [Er92f] (a different) Erdős refines this analysis, proving that if
$M_2=\min_{z_j} \max_{2\leq k\leq n+1} \left\lvert \sum_{1\leq j\leq n}z_j^k\right\rvert$
where the minimum is taken over all $z_j\in \mathbb{C}$ with $\max \lvert z_j\rvert=1$, then
$(1.746)^{-n} < M_2 < (1.745)^{-n}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_973.variants.m2_bounds :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ M_2 : ℝ,
      IsGLB { M | ∃ z : ℕ → ℂ,
        (∀ j ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖z j‖ ≤ 1) ∧
        (∃ j ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖z j‖ = 1) ∧
        (∃ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), M = ‖∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, z j ^ k‖ ∧
          ∀ m ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, z j ^ m‖ ≤ M) } M_2 →
      (1.746 : ℝ) ^ (-(n : ℝ)) < M_2 ∧ M_2 < (1.745 : ℝ) ^ (-(n : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos973.erdos_973.variants.tang
statements.doc:
Tang notes in the comments that Theorem 6.1 of [Tu84b] implies that, if $\lvert z_i\rvert \geq 1$
for all $i$, then
$\max_{2\leq k\leq n+1}\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq i\leq n}z_i^k\right\rvert \geq (2e)^{-(1+o(1))n}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_973.variants.tang :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, f =o[atTop] (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ z : ℕ → ℂ,
      (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) →
      ∃ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1),
        ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ ≥
        (2 * Real.exp 1) ^ (-(1 + f n) * (n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 974
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/974](https://www.erdosproblems.com/974)
- [Ti66] Tijdeman, R., *On a conjecture of Turán and Erdős*. Indag. Math. (1966), 374-383.

statements.name: Erdos974.erdos_974
statements.doc:
Let $z_1,\ldots,z_n\in \mathbb{C}$ be a sequence such that $z_1=1$. Suppose that the sequence of
$$s_k=\sum_{1\leq i\leq n}z_i^k$$
contains infinitely many $(n-1)$-tuples of consecutive values of $s_k$ which are all $0$. Then
(essentially)
$$z_j=e(j/n),$$
where $e(x)=e^{2\pi ix}$.

A conjecture of Turán.

This is true (in the stronger form with only two such tuples) - in fact if $n$ is odd then the
$z_i$ must be exactly the $n$th roots of unity, and if $n$ is even they must be the vertices of
two regular $(n/2)$-gons with the same circumscribed circle centred at the origin. This was first
proved by Tijdeman [Ti66]. An independent proof of this was given in the comments section by Hu,
Tang, and Zhang.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_974 {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (z : Fin n → ℂ) (hz : z 0 = 1)
    (hs : Set.Infinite {k : ℕ | ∀ j < n - 1, ∑ i, z i ^ (k + j) = 0}) :
    IsTuranConfiguration z

statements.name: Erdos974.erdos_974.variants.two_tuples
statements.doc:
Erdős speculates that this may be true if there are two distinct $(n-1)$-tuples of consecutive
values of $s_k$ which are $0$. He does not elaborate on what the 'essentially' may mean precisely.

This is true (in the stronger form with only two such tuples) - in fact if $n$ is odd then the
$z_i$ must be exactly the $n$th roots of unity, and if $n$ is even they must be the vertices of
two regular $(n/2)$-gons with the same circumscribed circle centred at the origin. This was first
proved by Tijdeman [Ti66]. An independent proof of this was given in the comments section by Hu,
Tang, and Zhang.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_974.variants.two_tuples {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (z : Fin n → ℂ) (hz : z 0 = 1)
    {a b : ℕ} (hab : a ≠ b) (ha : ∀ j < n - 1, ∑ i, z i ^ (a + j) = 0)
    (hb : ∀ j < n - 1, ∑ i, z i ^ (b + j) = 0) :
    IsTuranConfiguration z

problems.title: Erdős Problem 975
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/975](https://www.erdosproblems.com/975)
 - [Va39] van der Corput, J. G., Une in\'egalit\'e{} relative au nombre des diviseurs. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch., Proc. (1939), 547--553.
 - [Er52b] Erd\"os, P., On the sum {$\sum^x_{k=1} d(f(k))$}. J. London Math. Soc. (1952), 7--15.
 - [Ho63] Hooley, Christopher, On the number of divisors of a quadratic polynomial. Acta Math. (1963), 97--114.
 - [Mc95] McKee, James, On the average number of divisors of quadratic polynomials. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1995), 389--392.
 - [Mc97] McKee, James, A note on the number of divisors of quadratic polynomials. (1997), 275--281.
 - [Mc99] McKee, James, The average number of divisors of an irreducible quadratic polynomial. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1999), 17--22.
 - [T] T. Tao, Erdos' divisor bound, https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/07/23/erdos-divisor-bound/

statements.name: Erdos975.erdos_975
statements.doc:
For an irreducible polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $f(n) \ge 1$ for sufficiently large $n$,
does there exists a constant $c = c(f) > 0$ such that
$\sum_{n \le x} \tau(f(n)) \approx c \cdot x \log x$?

Note that it is unclear whether the polynomial should have integer coefficients or merely be
integer-valued. We assume the former.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_975 :
    ∀ f : ℤ[X], f.natDegree ≠ 0 → Irreducible f → (∀ᶠ n in atTop, 1 ≤ f.eval n) →
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), Tendsto (fun x ↦ Erdos975Sum f x / (x * log x)) atTop (𝓝 c)

statements.name: Erdos975.erdos_975.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc: The correctness of the growth rate is shown in [Va39] (lower bound) and [Er52b] (upper bound).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_975.variants.upper_bound (f : ℤ[X]) (hf : Irreducible f)
    (hf_pos : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, 1 ≤ f.eval n) : Erdos975Sum f =O[atTop] (fun x ↦ x * log x)

statements.name: Erdos975.erdos_975.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc: Lower bound for the growth rate of `Erdos975Sum`, shown in [Va39].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_975.variants.lower_bound (f : ℤ[X]) (hf : Irreducible f) (hfdeg : f.natDegree ≠ 0)
    (hf_pos : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, 1 ≤ f.eval n) :
    (fun x ↦ x * log x) =O[atTop] Erdos975Sum f

statements.name: Erdos975.erdos_975.variants.quadratic
statements.doc:
When $f$ is an irreducible quadratic polynomial, the question is answered first by Hooley [Ho63].
More compact expression of the constant in terms of Hurwitz class numbers (when $a = 1$)
is given by McKey in [Mc95], [Mc97], [Mc99].

TODO: formalize Hurwitz class numbers and the expression of the constant in terms of them.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_975.variants.quadratic (f : ℤ[X]) (hf : Irreducible f)
    (hf_pos : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, 1 ≤ f.eval ↑n) (hf_degree : f.degree = 2) (c : ℝ) :
    c = erdos_975.variants.quadratic.answer → 0 < c ∧ Tendsto
      (fun x ↦ Erdos975Sum f x / (x * log x)) atTop (𝓝 c)

statements.name: Erdos975.erdos_975.variants.n2_plus_1_strong
statements.doc:
More concrete example for $f(n) = n^2 + 1$, where the asymptote is
$\sum_{n \le x} \tau(n^2 + 1) \sim \frac{3}{\pi} x \log x + O(x)$. See Tao's blog [T].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_975.variants.n2_plus_1_strong :
    (fun x ↦ Erdos975Sum (X ^ 2 + 1) x - (3 / π) * x * log x) =O[atTop] id

statements.name: Erdos975.erdos_975.variants.n2_plus_1
statements.doc: Asymptotics for `Erdos975Sum` with $f(X) = X^2 + 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_975.variants.n2_plus_1 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), Tendsto (fun x ↦ Erdos975Sum (X ^ 2 + 1) x / (x * log x)) atTop (𝓝 c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 976
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/976](https://www.erdosproblems.com/976)
- [Er52c] Erdős, P., *On the greatest prime factor of $\prod_{k=1}^x f(k)$*. J. London Math. Soc.
  27 (1952), 379-384.
- [Er65b] Erdős, P., *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [Na22] Nagell, T., Abh. Math. Sem. Hamburg 1 (1922), 179-194.
- [Ri34] Ricci, G., Annali di Mat. (1934), 295-303.
- [Te90] Tenenbaum, G., *Sur une question d'Erdős et Schinzel*. A tribute to Paul Erdős (1990),
  405-443.

statements.name: Erdos976.erdos_976
statements.doc:
Let $f\in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be an irreducible polynomial of degree $d\geq 2$. Let $F_f(n)$ be maximal
such that there exists $1\leq m\leq n$ with $f(m)$ is divisible by a prime $\geq F_f(n)$.
Equivalently, $F_f(n)$ is the greatest prime divisor of
$$\prod_{1\leq m\leq n}f(m).$$
Estimate $F_f(n)$.

We read "estimate" as determining the order of magnitude of $F_f(n)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_976 (f : ℤ[X]) (hf : Irreducible f) (hd : 2 ≤ f.natDegree) :
    (fun n ↦ (F f n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_976.answer f

statements.name: Erdos976.erdos_976.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $f\in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be an irreducible polynomial of degree $d\geq 2$, and let $F_f(n)$ be the
greatest prime divisor of $\prod_{1\leq m\leq n}f(m)$. Is it true that $F_f(n)\gg n^{1+c}$ for some
constant $c>0$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_976.parts.i :
    ∀ f : ℤ[X], Irreducible f → 2 ≤ f.natDegree →
      ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + c)) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (F f n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos976.erdos_976.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $f\in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be an irreducible polynomial of degree $d\geq 2$, and let $F_f(n)$ be the
greatest prime divisor of $\prod_{1\leq m\leq n}f(m)$. Is it true that $F_f(n)\gg n^d$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_976.parts.ii :
    ∀ f : ℤ[X], Irreducible f → 2 ≤ f.natDegree →
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ f.natDegree) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (F f n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos976.erdos_976.variants.nagell_ricci
statements.doc: Nagell [Na22] and Ricci [Ri34] proved that $F_f(n) \gg n\log n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_976.variants.nagell_ricci (f : ℤ[X]) (hf : Irreducible f)
    (hd : 2 ≤ f.natDegree) :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) * Real.log n) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (F f n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos976.erdos_976.variants.erdos
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er52c] improved the bound of Nagell and Ricci to
$$F_f(n) \gg n(\log n)^{\log\log\log n}.$$
More precisely, [Er52c] gives $F_f(n) > n(\log n)^{c\log\log\log n}$ for some constant
$c = c(f) > 0$; the site omits $c$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_976.variants.erdos (f : ℤ[X]) (hf : Irreducible f) (hd : 2 ≤ f.natDegree) :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ),
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) * Real.log n ^ (c * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log n)))) =O[atTop]
        fun n ↦ (F f n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos976.erdos_976.variants.tenenbaum
statements.doc:
In [Er65b] Erdős claimed a proof of $F_f(n) \gg n\exp((\log n)^c)$ for some constant $c>0$, but
never published it. A proof was provided by Tenenbaum [Te90].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_976.variants.tenenbaum (f : ℤ[X]) (hf : Irreducible f) (hd : 2 ≤ f.natDegree) :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) * Real.exp (Real.log n ^ c)) =O[atTop]
      fun n ↦ (F f n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 977
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/977](https://www.erdosproblems.com/977)
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [Sc62] Schinzel, A., *On primitive prime factors of $a^n-b^n$*. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc.
  (1962), 555-562.
- [St74b] Stewart, C. L., *The greatest prime factor of $a^n-b^n$*. Acta Arith. (1974/75),
  427-433.
- [St13] Stewart, Cameron L., *On divisors of Lucas and Lehmer numbers*. Acta Math. (2013),
  291-314.
- [MuWo02] Murty, Ram and Wong, Siman, *The $ABC$ conjecture and prime divisors of the Lucas and
  Lehmer sequences*. (2002), 43-54.
- [La21] L. Lai, *On the largest prime divisor of $n!+1$*. arXiv:2103.14894 (2021).

statements.name: Erdos977.erdos_977
statements.doc:
If $P(m)$ is the greatest prime divisor of $m$, then is it true that
$$\frac{P(2^n-1)}{n}\to \infty$$
as $n\to \infty$?

Schinzel [Sc62] proved that $P(2^n-1)>2n$ for $n>12$. In [Er65b] Erdős also asks about $P(n!+1)$.
Stewart [St74b] proved that this conjecture is true if we restrict $n$ to those integers with
$<\frac{1}{\log 2}\log\log n$ many prime factors.

This was proved in the affirmative by Stewart [St13], who proved that
$P(2^n-1)\gg n^{1+\frac{1}{104\log\log n}}$ for all large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_977 :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Nat.maxPrimeFac (2 ^ n - 1) : ℝ) / n) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos977.erdos_977.variants.schinzel
statements.doc: Schinzel [Sc62] proved that $P(2^n-1)>2n$ for $n>12$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_977.variants.schinzel :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 12 < n → 2 * n < Nat.maxPrimeFac (2 ^ n - 1)

statements.name: Erdos977.erdos_977.variants.stewart
statements.doc: Stewart [St13] proved that $P(2^n-1)\gg n^{1+\frac{1}{104\log\log n}}$ for all large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_977.variants.stewart : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    c * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + 1 / (104 * Real.log (Real.log n))) ≤ Nat.maxPrimeFac (2 ^ n - 1)

statements.name: Erdos977.erdos_977.variants.factorial
statements.doc:
In [Er65b] Erdős also asks about $P(n!+1)$: is it true that $P(n!+1)/n\to\infty$? This appears to
be open still. Murty and Wong [MuWo02] proved that $P(n!+1)>(1+o(1))n\log n$ assuming the abc
conjecture.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_977.variants.factorial :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Nat.maxPrimeFac (n.factorial + 1) : ℝ) / n) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos977.erdos_977.variants.lai
statements.doc:
The best-known unconditional result, due to Lai [La21], is that
$$\limsup \frac{P(n!+1)}{n} \geq 1+9\log 2\approx 7.238.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_977.variants.lai : ∀ C : ℝ, C < 1 + 9 * Real.log 2 →
    ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, C * n < Nat.maxPrimeFac (n.factorial + 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 978
problems.doc:
*Reference:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/978](https://www.erdosproblems.com/978)
 - [Ho67] Hooley, C., On the power free values of polynomials. Mathematika (1967), 21--26.
 - [Br11] Browning, T. D., Power-free values of polynomials. Arch. Math. (Basel) (2011), 139--150.
 - [Er53] Erdős, P., Arithmetical properties of polynomials. J. London Math. Soc. (1953), 416--425.
 - [OAI26a] OpenAI, *Squarefree values of quartics and power-free values of polynomials*. OpenAI
   Math Release preprint (2026).
   https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/Squarefree-values-of-quartics-and-power-free-values-of-polynomials-September-24-2026/manuscript.pdf

statements.name: Erdos978.erdos_978.variants.sub_one
statements.doc:
Let `f ∈ ℤ[X]` be an irreducible polynomial with positive leading coefficient. Suppose that the
degree `k` of `f` is larger than `2` and is not equal to a power of `2`. Then the set of `n` such
that `f n` is `(k - 1)`-th power free is infinite, and this is proved in [Er53].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_978.variants.sub_one {f : ℤ[X]} (hi : Irreducible f) (hd : 2 < f.natDegree)
    (hp : ∀ (x : ℕ), f.natDegree ≠ 2 ^ x) (hlc : 0 < f.leadingCoeff) :
    {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 1) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos978.erdos_978.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let `f ∈ ℤ[X]` be an irreducible polynomial with positive leading coefficient. Suppose that the
degree `k` of `f` is larger than `2`, is not equal to a power of `2`, and `f n` has no fixed
`(k - 1)`-th power divisors other than `1`. Then the set of `n` such that `f n` is `(k - 1)`-th
power free has positive density, and this is proved in [Ho67].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_978.parts.i {f : ℤ[X]} (hi : Irreducible f) (hd : 2 < f.natDegree)
    (hp2 : ∀ (x : ℕ), f.natDegree ≠ 2 ^ x) (hlc : 0 < f.leadingCoeff)
    (hp : ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∃ n : ℕ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 1) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ)) :
    HasPosDensity {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 1) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}

statements.name: Erdos978.erdos_978.variants.sub_two
statements.doc:
If the degree `k` of `f` is larger than or equal to `9`, and `f n` has no fixed `(k - 2)`-th
power divisors other than `1`, then the set of `n` such that `f n` is `(k - 2)`-th power free has
infinitely many elements. This result is proved in [Br11].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_978.variants.sub_two {f : ℤ[X]} (hi : Irreducible f) (hd : 9 ≤ f.natDegree)
    (hp : ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∃ n : ℕ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 2) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ)) :
    {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 2) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos978.erdos_978.variants.allow_fixed_divisors
statements.doc:
If $k > 3$ (and $k \neq 2^l$), then are there infinitely many $n$ for which $f(n)$ is
$(k-2)$-power-free?

This was disproved by the DeepMind prover agent.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_978.variants.allow_fixed_divisors :
    ¬ ∀ {f : ℤ[X]}, Irreducible f → f.natDegree > 3 →
    (¬ ∃ l : ℕ, f.natDegree = 2 ^ l) → 0 < f.leadingCoeff →
    (¬ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 1) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ)) →
    {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 2) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos978.erdos_978.parts.ii
statements.doc:
If $k>3$ (and $k \neq 2^l$), and for all primes $p$ there exists $n$ such that $p^{k-2}\nmid f(n)$,
then are there infinitely many $n$ for which $f(n)$ is $(k-2)$-power-free?

This was proved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26a]; see the linked Lean proof,
which gives positive density and does not need $k \neq 2^l$ or a positive leading coefficient.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_978.parts.ii :
    ∀ {f : ℤ[X]}, Irreducible f → f.natDegree > 3 →
    (¬ ∃ l : ℕ, f.natDegree = 2 ^ l) → 0 < f.leadingCoeff →
    (∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∃ n : ℕ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 2) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ)) →
    {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 2) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos978.erdos_978.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Does `n ^ 4 + 2` represent infinitely many squarefree numbers?

This was proved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26a]; see the linked Lean proof,
which gives positive density for every irreducible quartic with no fixed square divisor.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_978.parts.iii : {n : ℕ | Squarefree (n ^ 4 + 2)}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 979
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/979](https://www.erdosproblems.com/979)

statements.name: Erdos979.erdos_979
statements.doc:
Let $k ≥ 2$, and let $f_k(n)$ count the number of solutions to $n = p_1^k + \dots + p_k^k$,
where the $p_i$ are prime numbers. Is it true that $\limsup f_k(n) = \infty$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_979 :
    ∀ k ≥ 2, Filter.limsup (fun n => (solutionSet n k).encard) Filter.atTop = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos979.erdos_979.variants.k2
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er37b] proved that if $f_2(n)$ counts the number of solutions to $n = p_1^2 + p_2^2$, where $p_1$ and $p_2$ are prime numbers, then $\limsup f_2(n) = \infty$.

[Er37b] Erdős, Paul, On the Sum and Difference of Squares of Primes. J. London Math. Soc. (1937), 133--136.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_979.variants.k2 :
    Filter.limsup (fun n => (solutionSet n 2).encard) Filter.atTop = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos979.erdos_979.variants.k3
statements.doc: Erdős (unpublished)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_979.variants.k3 :
    Filter.limsup (fun n => (solutionSet n 3).encard) Filter.atTop = ⊤

problems.title: Erdős Problem 980
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/980](https://www.erdosproblems.com/980)
- [El67b] Elliott, P. D. T. A., *A problem of Erdős concerning power residue sums*.
  Acta Arith. 13 (1967/68), 131-149.
- [Er61e] Erdős, P., *Remarks on number theory. I*. Mat. Lapok (1961), 10-17.
- [Er65b] Erdős, P., *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [MaPo11] Martin, G. and Pollack, P., *The average least character nonresidue and further
  variations on a theme of Erdős*. [arXiv:1112.1175](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.1175) (2011).

statements.name: Erdos980.erdos_980
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 2$ and $n_k(p)$ denote the least $k$th power nonresidue of $p$. Is it true that
$$\sum_{p<x} n_k(p)\sim c_k \frac{x}{\log x}$$
for some constant $c_k>0$?

Erdős [Er65b] asked this; it is true, and was proved by Elliott [El67b]. As in [El67b], the sum
is over the primes $p \equiv 1 \pmod k$ (for each of which a $k$th power nonresidue exists).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_980 (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), residueSum k ~[atTop] fun x ↦ c * x / Real.log x

statements.name: Erdos980.erdos_980.variants.erdos_two
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er61e] proved this when $k=2$, with
$$c_2=\sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{p_k}{2^k},$$
where $p_k$ is the $k$th prime; the sum is over the odd primes $p < x$ [MaPo11, (1.1)].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_980.variants.erdos_two :
    residueSum 2 ~[atTop]
      fun x ↦ (∑' i : ℕ, (Nat.nth Nat.Prime i : ℝ) / 2 ^ (i + 1)) * x / Real.log x

problems.title: Erdős Problem 981
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/981](https://www.erdosproblems.com/981)
- [El69] Elliott, P. D. T. A., *A conjecture of Erdős concerning character sums*.
  Indag. Math. 31 (1969), 164–171.
- [TaZh25] [arxiv/2512.24631](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24631)
  **Average first-passage times for character sums** by *Quanyu Tang and Hao Zhang*

statements.name: Erdos981.erdos_981
statements.doc:
Let $\epsilon > 0$ and $f_\epsilon(p)$ be the smallest integer $m$
such that $\sum_{n\leq N} \left(\frac{n}{p}\right)<\epsilon N$ for all $N\geq m$. Prove that
$$\sum_{p<x}f_\epsilon(p)\sim c_\epsilon \frac{x}{\log x}$$
for some $c_\epsilon > 0$.

Proved by Elliott [El69].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_981 (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), Tendsto (fun x ↦ (∑ p : Nat.primesBelow ⌈x⌉₊, f ε p) * log x / x) atTop (𝓝 c)

statements.name: Erdos981.erdos_981.variants.first_time
statements.doc:
Let $\epsilon > 0$ and $f_\epsilon(p)$ be the smallest integer $m$ such that $\sum_{n\leq m} \left(\frac{n}{p}\right)<\epsilon m$. Prove that
$$\sum_{p<x}f_\epsilon(p)\sim c_\epsilon \frac{x}{\log x}$$
for some $c_\epsilon > 0$.

Proved by Tang and Zhang [TaZh25].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_981.variants.first_time (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), Tendsto (fun x ↦ (∑ p : Nat.primesBelow ⌈x⌉₊, f' ε p) * log x / x) atTop (𝓝 c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 982
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/982](https://www.erdosproblems.com/982)

statements.name: Erdos982.erdos_982
statements.doc:
If $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then some vertex has at least
$\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor$ different distances to other vertices.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_982 (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (p : Fin n → ℝ²) (hp : Function.Injective p)
    (hp' : EuclideanGeometry.IsConvexPolygon p) :
    ∃ (i : Fin n), { d : ℝ | ∃ j : Fin n, j ≠ i ∧ d = dist (p i) (p j) }.ncard ≥ n / 2

statements.name: Erdos982.erdos_982.variants.concyclic
statements.doc:
For distinct points on a common circle, every vertex has at least
$\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor$ different distances to the other vertices.
This does not require convexity or the assumption $3 \leq n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_982.variants.concyclic {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ℝ²) (hp : Function.Injective p)
    (c : ℝ²) (R : ℝ) (hR : ∀ j, dist (p j) c = R) (i : Fin n) :
    { d : ℝ | ∃ j : Fin n, j ≠ i ∧ d = dist (p i) (p j) }.ncard ≥ n / 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 983
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/983](https://www.erdosproblems.com/983)
- [Er70b] Erdős, P., *Some applications of graph theory to number theory*. Proc. Second Chapel
  Hill Conf. on Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Univ. North Carolina, Chapel
  Hill, N.C., 1970) (1970), 136-145. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1970-20.pdf)
- [Po79] Pomerance, C., *The prime number graph*. Math. Comp. 33 (1979), 399-408.
  [PDF](https://math.dartmouth.edu/~carlp/PDF/paper19.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos983.erdos_983.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $n\geq 2$ and $\pi(n)<k\leq n$. Let $f(k,n)$ be the smallest integer $r$ such that in any
$A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ of size $\lvert A\rvert=k$ there exist primes $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ such
that $>r$ many $a\in A$ are only divisible by primes from $\{p_1,\ldots,p_r\}$.

Is it true that
$$2\pi(n^{1/2})-f(\pi(n)+1,n)\to \infty$$
as $n\to \infty$?

This is the first part. The primes may depend on $A$. Erdős and Straus conjectured this
[Er70b, p. 138 and p. 140].

The answer is no: Liam Price and GPT-5.5 Pro showed on the
[forum](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/983#post-6104) that
$f(\pi(n)+1,n)=2\pi(n^{1/2})+1$ for infinitely many $n$; see the
[explanation](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/983#post-6525) by Nat Sothanaphan.
Write $p_k$ for the $k$-th prime. By [Po79, Corollary after Theorem 2.2] there are infinitely
many $N$ with $p_{N-i}p_{N+i}<p_N^2$ for $1\leq i<N$. Take $n=p_N^2-1$, so
$\pi(n^{1/2})=N-1$. Let $A$ consist of the products of adjacent primes on the path
$p_{2N-1},p_1,p_{2N-2},p_2,\ldots,p_{N+1},p_{N-1},p_N$, its two endpoint primes, and the
other primes up to $n$. Then $\lvert A\rvert=\pi(n)+1$, and for any $r\leq 2N-2$ primes at
most $r$ elements of $A$ are divisible only by those primes, so $f(\pi(n)+1,n)\geq 2N-1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_983.parts.i :
    ¬ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦
      2 * (Nat.primeCounting (Nat.sqrt n) : ℤ) - (f (Nat.primeCounting n + 1) n : ℤ))
      atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos983.erdos_983.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $n\geq 2$ and $\pi(n)<k\leq n$. Let $f(k,n)$ be the smallest integer $r$ such that in any
$A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ of size $\lvert A\rvert=k$ there exist primes $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ such
that $>r$ many $a\in A$ are only divisible by primes from $\{p_1,\ldots,p_r\}$.

In general, estimate $f(k,n)$, particularly when $\pi(n)+1<k=o(n)$.

This is the second part. We read "estimate" as an asymptotic formula `answer k n`, valid for
every function $k=k(n)$ with $\pi(n)+1<k(n)=o(n)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_983.parts.ii :
    ∀ k : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, Nat.primeCounting n + 1 < k n) →
      ((fun n : ℕ ↦ (k n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ))) →
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f (k n) n : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ erdos_983.parts.ii.answer (k n) n)

statements.name: Erdos983.erdos_983.variants.le_primeCounting
statements.doc: It is trivial that $f(k,n)\leq \pi(n)$ [Er70b, p. 138]. Here $\pi(n)<k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_983.variants.le_primeCounting {k n : ℕ} (hk : Nat.primeCounting n < k) :
    f k n ≤ Nat.primeCounting n

statements.name: Erdos983.erdos_983.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős and Straus [Er70b, p. 139, (14)] proved
$$f(\pi(n)+1,n)\leq 2\pi(n^{1/2})+1.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_983.variants.upper_bound (n : ℕ) :
    f (Nat.primeCounting n + 1) n ≤ 2 * Nat.primeCounting (Nat.sqrt n) + 1

statements.name: Erdos983.erdos_983.variants.erdos_straus
statements.doc:
Erdős and Straus proved [Er70b, pp. 138-140] that
$$f(\pi(n)+1,n)=2\pi(n^{1/2})+o_A\left(\frac{n^{1/2}}{(\log n)^A}\right)$$
for any $A>0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_983.variants.erdos_straus :
    ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A →
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f (Nat.primeCounting n + 1) n : ℝ) -
          2 * (Nat.primeCounting (Nat.sqrt n) : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.sqrt n / Real.log n ^ A)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 985
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/985](https://www.erdosproblems.com/985)

statements.name: Erdos985.erdos_985
statements.doc: Is it true that, for every prime $p$, there is a prime $q \leq p$ which is a primitive root modulo $p$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_985 : ∀ᵉ (p : ℕ) (hp_prime : p.Prime) (hp_nontrivial : p ≠ 2),
    ∃ q, q.Prime ∧ q < p ∧ orderOf (q : ZMod p) = p - 1

statements.name: Erdos985.erdos_985.variants.two_three_five_primitive_root
statements.doc: Heath-Brown proved that at least one of 2, 3, or 5 is a primitive root for infinitely many primes $p$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_985.variants.two_three_five_primitive_root :
    Set.Infinite
      {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧
      (orderOf (2 : ZMod p) = p - 1 ∨
       orderOf (3 : ZMod p) = p - 1 ∨
       orderOf (5 : ZMod p) = p - 1)}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 986
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/986](https://www.erdosproblems.com/986)
- [ChGr98] Chung, F. and Graham, R., *Erdős on Graphs: His Legacy of Unsolved Problems*.
  A K Peters, Ltd. (1998).
- [Br26] Bradač, D., Off-diagonal Ramsey numbers. arXiv:2605.28793 (2026).
- [Sp77] Spencer, J., Asymptotic lower bounds for Ramsey functions. Discrete Math. (1977), 69-76.
- [MaVe23] Mattheus, S. and Verstraëte, J., The asymptotics of $r(4,t)$. Ann. of Math. (2024),
  941-965.

statements.name: Erdos986.erdos_986
statements.doc:
For any fixed $s\geq 3$,
$$R(s,k) \gg \frac{k^{s-1}}{(\log k)^c}$$
for some constant $c=c(s)>0$.

According to Chung and Graham [ChGr98] this was first conjectured by Erdős in 1947.

Proved by Bradač [Br26], with $c=2s-4$.

The linked formal proof (Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol) gives `k ^ (s - 1) / (log k) ^ c = O(R(s, k))`
for a natural `c > 0`, with the Ramsey number defined through `CliqueFree`/`IndepSetFree`; this
implies the statement below.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_986 :
    ∀ (s : ℕ) (hs : 3 ≤ s),
      ∃ (c C : ℝ), 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧
        ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in atTop,
          (SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey s k : ℝ) ≥
            C * (k : ℝ) ^ (s - 1) / (Real.log k) ^ c

problems.title: Erdős Problem 987
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/987](https://www.erdosproblems.com/987)
- [APSSV26b] B. Alexeev, M. Putterman, M. Sawhney, M. Sellke, and G. Valiant,
  [Short proofs in combinatorics, probability, and number theory II](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.06609).
  arXiv:2604.06609 (2026).
- [Cl67] Clunie, J., On a problem of Erdős. J. London Math. Soc. (1967), 133--136.
- [Er64b] Erdős, P., Problems and results on diophantine approximations. Compositio Math. (1964),
  52-65.
- [Er65b] Erdős, P., Some remarks on number theory. Israel J. Math. (the actual reference
  cited by Clunie 1967 as [2]; the erdosproblems.com bibliography points to a different
  Erdős 1965 paper, "Some recent advances and current problems in number theory" (Lectures
  on Modern Mathematics III, 1965, 196-244), which does not appear to contain the
  exponential-sum log-bound proof).
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.
- [Li69] Lindström, B., An inequality for $B_2$-sequences. J. Combinatorial Theory (1969), 211-212.

statements.name: Erdos987.erdos_987.parts.i
statements.doc:
Question 1:

Is it true that $\limsup_{k \to \infty} A_k = \infty$?

Erdős [Er64b] remarks it is "easy to see" that $\limsup_k \sup_n |\sum_{j \le n} e(k x_j)| = \infty$.
Erdős [Er65b] later found a "very easy" proof that $A_k \gg \log k$ for infinitely many $k$.
Clunie [Cl67] proved that $A_k \gg k^{1/2}$ for infinitely many $k$, which implies the answer is
yes (Tao independently found a proof). This is Problem 7.21 in [Ha74].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_987.parts.i :
    ∀ (x : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : ∀ j : ℕ, x j ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1),
      atTop.limsup (fun k : ℕ => A x k) = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos987.erdos_987.variants.sup_limsup_infty
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er64b] remarks it is "easy to see" that for every infinite sequence
$x_1, x_2, \ldots \in (0, 1)$,
$$\limsup_{k \to \infty} \sup_n \left\lvert \sum_{j \le n} e(k x_j) \right\rvert = \infty.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_987.variants.sup_limsup_infty
    (x : ℕ → ℝ) (hx : ∀ j : ℕ, x j ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    atTop.limsup (fun k : ℕ =>
      ⨆ n : ℕ, ((‖∑ j ∈ range n, e ((k : ℝ) * x j)‖ : ℝ) : EReal)) = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos987.erdos_987.variants.log_lower_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er65b] proved that, for every infinite sequence $x_1, x_2, \ldots \in (0, 1)$,
$A_k \gg \log k$ for infinitely many $k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_987.variants.log_lower_bound
    (x : ℕ → ℝ) (_hx : ∀ j : ℕ, x j ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    ∃ c > 0, ∃ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, ((c * Real.log k : ℝ) : EReal) ≤ A x k

statements.name: Erdos987.erdos_987.variants.sqrt_lower_bound
statements.doc:
Clunie [Cl67] proved that, for every infinite sequence $x_1, x_2, \ldots \in (0, 1)$,
$A_k \gg k^{1/2}$ for infinitely many $k$. (Tao independently found a proof.)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_987.variants.sqrt_lower_bound
    (x : ℕ → ℝ) (hx : ∀ j : ℕ, x j ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    ∃ c > 0, ∃ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, ((c * Real.sqrt k : ℝ) : EReal) ≤ A x k

statements.name: Erdos987.erdos_987.variants.linear_upper_bound_weak
statements.doc:
**Linear upper bound (weakened).** A first weakened version of Clunie's `A_k ≤ k`: there
exists a sequence $x \in (0,1)$ with $A_k \le 2k$ for all $k \ge 1$. The witness is the
(shifted) van der Corput sequence. For the tighter $A_k \le k + 1$ bound see
`linear_upper_bound_clunie`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_987.variants.linear_upper_bound_weak :
    ∃ (x : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : ∀ j : ℕ, x j ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1),
      ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → A x k ≤ ((2 * k : ℝ) : EReal)

statements.name: Erdos987.erdos_987.variants.linear_upper_bound_clunie
statements.doc:
**Linear upper bound (tight via Clunie phase tracking).** Tighter than
`linear_upper_bound_weak`: there exists a sequence $x \in (0,1)$ with $A_k \le k + 1$ for all
$k \ge 1$, via the (shifted) van der Corput sequence. Whether the $+1$ can be eliminated to
recover Clunie's exact $A_k \le k$ under the strict $\mathrm{Ioo}\,0\,1$ hypothesis is open in
this formalization (see `linear_upper_bound`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_987.variants.linear_upper_bound_clunie :
    ∃ (x : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : ∀ j : ℕ, x j ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1),
      ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → A x k ≤ (((k : ℝ) + 1) : EReal)

statements.name: Erdos987.erdos_987.variants.linear_upper_bound
statements.doc:
Clunie [Cl67] proved that there exists an infinite sequence $\{z_\nu\}$ on the unit circle
with $A_\nu \le \nu$ for all $\nu \ge 1$. Translating $z_\nu = e(x_\nu)$, the natural domain of
$x_\nu$ is the half-open unit interval $\mathrm{Ico}\,0\,1$, matching the original
[Er64b]/[Cl67] statement (any unit complex number is allowed, including $z = 1$, i.e. $x = 0$).

**Note**: erdosproblems.com/987 phrases the problem with the *open* interval
$x_\nu \in (0, 1)$, which excludes $z = 1$ and is strictly stronger than what [Er64b]/[Cl67]
state; we align with the original papers here. The shifted-vdc $\le k + 1$ variant under the
open interval is preserved as `linear_upper_bound_clunie`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_987.variants.linear_upper_bound :
    ∃ (x : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : ∀ j : ℕ, x j ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1),
      ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → A x k ≤ ((k : ℝ) : EReal)

statements.name: Erdos987.erdos_987.variants.sqrt_log_upper_bound
statements.doc:
An internal OpenAI model (see [APSSV26b, §3]) proved that there exists an infinite sequence
$x_1, x_2, \ldots \in (0, 1)$ such that
$\sup_n \left\lvert \sum_{j \le n} e(k x_j) \right\rvert \ll (k \log k)^{1/2}$ for all $k \ge 1$
(in particular $A_k \ll (k \log k)^{1/2}$).

Note: the bound is restricted to $k \ge 2$ since $\log 1 = 0$ would make the RHS vanish at
$k = 1$, while the LHS $\|\sum_{j < n} e(x_j)\|$ can equal $1$ (e.g. for $n = 1$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_987.variants.sqrt_log_upper_bound :
    ∃ (x : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : ∀ j : ℕ, x j ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (C : ℝ) (_ : 0 < C),
      ∀ k n : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → ‖∑ j ∈ range n, e (k * x j)‖ ≤ C * Real.sqrt (k * Real.log k)

statements.name: Erdos987.erdos_987.parts.ii
statements.doc:
**Question 2 (parts.ii)**: Is it possible for $A_k = o(k)$? Yes — there exists a sequence
$(x_n) \in (0, 1)$ and a bound $b(k) = o(k)$ with $A x k \le b k$ eventually. A corollary of
`sqrt_log_upper_bound` (which gives a $\sqrt{k \log k}$ bound) plus the asymptotic
$\sqrt{k \log k} = o(k)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_987.parts.ii :
    ∃ (x : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : ∀ j : ℕ, x j ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (b : ℕ → ℝ),
      b =o[atTop] (fun k : ℕ => (k : ℝ)) ∧ ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, A x k ≤ ((b k : ℝ) : EReal)

statements.name: Erdos987.erdos_987.variants.finite_distinct_points
statements.doc:
Liu [Li69] showed that, for any $\epsilon > 0$, $A_k \gg k^{1 - \epsilon}$ infinitely often
under the additional assumption that there are only a finite number of distinct points. Clunie
observed in the Mathscinet review of [Li69] that under this assumption in fact $A_k = \infty$
infinitely often (the version stated here).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_987.variants.finite_distinct_points
    (x : ℕ → ℝ) (_hx : ∀ j : ℕ, x j ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1)
    (hfin : (Set.range x).Finite) :
    ∃ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, A x k = ⊤

problems.title: Erdős Problem 990
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/990](https://www.erdosproblems.com/990)
- [APSSV26b] B. Alexeev, M. Putterman, M. Sawhney, M. Sellke, and G. Valiant, *Short proofs in
  combinatorics, probability, and number theory II*. arXiv:2604.06609 (2026).
- [ErTu50] Erdős, P. and Turán, P., *On the distribution of roots of polynomials*. Ann. of Math. (2)
  (1950), 105-119.
- [Ha72b] Hayman, W. K., *Angular value distribution of power series with gaps*. Proc. London Math.
  Soc. (3) (1972), 590-624.

statements.name: Erdos990.erdos_990
statements.doc:
Let $f=a_0+\cdots+a_dx^d\in \mathbb{C}[x]$ be a polynomial. Is it true that, if $f$ has roots
$z_1,\ldots,z_d$ with corresponding arguments $\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_d\in [0,2\pi]$, then for all
intervals $I\subseteq [0,2\pi]$
$$
\left\lvert (\# \theta_i \in I) - \frac{\lvert I\rvert}{2\pi}d\right\rvert \ll
\left(n\log M\right)^{1/2},
$$
where $n$ is the number of non-zero coefficients of $f$ and
$$
M=\frac{\lvert a_0\rvert+\cdots +\lvert a_d\rvert}{(\lvert a_0\rvert\lvert a_d\rvert)^{1/2}}.
$$

An internal OpenAI model (see [APSSV26b]) has disproved the conjecture, constructing, for every
$n\geq 1$, a polynomial $f$ with $n$ non-zero coefficients such that $M<3$ and with a positive real
zero of multiplicity $n-1$, whence letting $I=[0,c/d]$ for a suitably small $c>0$,
$$
\left\lvert (\# \theta_i \in I) - \frac{\lvert I\rvert}{2\pi}d\right\rvert \geq n-1.
$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_990 :
    ¬ ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ f : ℂ[X], f.coeff 0 ≠ 0 → ∀ α β : ℝ, 0 ≤ α → α ≤ β → β ≤ 2 * π →
      |(rootArgCount f (Set.Icc α β) : ℝ) - (β - α) / (2 * π) * (f.natDegree : ℝ)| ≤
        C * Real.sqrt ((f.support.card : ℝ) * Real.log (M f))

statements.name: Erdos990.erdos_990.variants.erdos_turan
statements.doc: Erdős and Turán [ErTu50] proved such an upper bound with $n$ replaced by $d$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_990.variants.erdos_turan :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ f : ℂ[X], f.coeff 0 ≠ 0 → ∀ α β : ℝ, 0 ≤ α → α ≤ β → β ≤ 2 * π →
      |(rootArgCount f (Set.Icc α β) : ℝ) - (β - α) / (2 * π) * (f.natDegree : ℝ)| ≤
        C * Real.sqrt ((f.natDegree : ℝ) * Real.log (M f))

statements.name: Erdos990.erdos_990.variants.hayman
statements.doc:
Hayman [Ha72b] proved
$$
