\left\lvert (\# \theta_i \in I) - \frac{\lvert I\rvert}{2\pi}d\right\rvert \leq n-1,
$$
and noted this is essentially sharp since $f(x)=(x^{p}-1)^{n-1}$ has $n$ non-zero coefficients and
has $1$ as a positive real zero of multiplicity $n-1$ (although for this $f$ the parameter $M$
becomes very large).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_990.variants.hayman :
    ∀ f : ℂ[X], f.coeff 0 ≠ 0 → ∀ α β : ℝ, 0 ≤ α → α ≤ β → β ≤ 2 * π →
      |(rootArgCount f (Set.Icc α β) : ℝ) - (β - α) / (2 * π) * (f.natDegree : ℝ)| ≤
        (f.support.card : ℝ) - 1

statements.name: Erdos990.erdos_990.variants.counterexample
statements.doc:
An internal OpenAI model (see [APSSV26b]) has disproved the conjecture, constructing, for every
$n\geq 1$, a polynomial $f$ with $n$ non-zero coefficients such that $M<3$ and with a positive real
zero of multiplicity $n-1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_990.variants.counterexample :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∃ f : ℂ[X], f.coeff 0 ≠ 0 ∧ f.support.card = n ∧ M f < 3 ∧
      ∃ x : ℝ, 0 < x ∧ f.rootMultiplicity (x : ℂ) = n - 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 994
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/994](https://www.erdosproblems.com/994)
- [Er64b] Erdős, P., _Problems and results on diophantine approximations_. Compositio Math.
  (1964), 52-65.
- [Kh23] Khintchine, A., _Ein Satz über Kettenbrüche, mit arithmetischen Anwendungen_. Math. Z.
  (1923), 289--306.
- [Ma70] Marstrand, J. M., _On Khinchin's conjecture about strong uniform distribution_. Proc.
  London Math. Soc. (3) (1970), 540--556.

statements.name: Erdos994.erdos_994
statements.doc:
Let $E\subseteq (0,1)$ be a meaurable subset with Lebesgue measure $\lambda(E)$. Is it true that,
for almost all $\alpha$,
$$\lim_{n\to \infty}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}1_{\{k\alpha \}\in E}=\lambda(E)$$
for all $E$?

This is a conjecture of Khintchine [Kh23] (with the exceptional null set of $\alpha$ allowed to
depend on $E$). It is false, and was disproved by Marstrand [Ma70].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_994 :
    ¬ ∀ E ⊆ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, MeasurableSet E →
      ∀ᵐ α : ℝ, Tendsto (visitAverage E α) atTop (nhds (volume E).toReal)

statements.name: Erdos994.erdos_994.variants.simultaneous
statements.doc:
Read literally, with "for almost all $\alpha$" placed before "for all $E$", the statement is
trivially false: for any $\alpha$, removing the countable orbit $\{\{k\alpha\} : k\geq 1\}$ from
$(0,1)$ gives a measurable set of measure $1$ which is never visited.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_994.variants.simultaneous :
    ¬ ∀ᵐ α : ℝ, ∀ E ⊆ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, MeasurableSet E →
      Tendsto (visitAverage E α) atTop (nhds (volume E).toReal)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 995
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/995](https://www.erdosproblems.com/995)
- [Er49] Erdős, P., On the strong law of large numbers, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. (1949),
  329-334.

Let $n_1 < n_2 < \cdots$ be a lacunary sequence of integers and $f \in L^2([0,1])$ with
$\int_0^1 f = 0$. Estimate the growth of
$$S_N(\alpha) = \sum_{k \le N} f(\{\alpha n_k\})$$
for almost all $\alpha$, where $\{\cdot\}$ denotes the fractional part. In particular, is it
true that $S_N(\alpha) = o\!\left(N \sqrt{\log\log N}\right)$ for almost all $\alpha$?

Erdős [Er49] constructed a lacunary sequence and a mean-zero $f \in L^2([0,1])$ for which, for
every $\varepsilon > 0$, $\limsup_N S_N(\alpha) / (N (\log\log N)^{1/2 - \varepsilon}) = \infty$
for almost all $\alpha$, and believed this lower bound to be close to the truth.

The mean-zero hypothesis $\int_0^1 f = 0$ is the natural normalisation: otherwise the sum has a
linear main term coming from the average of $f$.

statements.name: Erdos995.erdos_995
statements.doc:
Erdős Problem 995:

For every lacunary sequence $(n_k)$ of integers and every $f \in L^2([0,1])$ with
$\int_0^1 f = 0$, is it true that for almost all $\alpha$,
$$\sum_{k < N} f(\{\alpha n_k\}) = o\!\left(N \sqrt{\log\log N}\right)?$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_995 :
    ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ), IsLacunary n → ∀ (f : ℝ → ℝ),
      MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)) →
      ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..1, f x = 0 →
      ∀ᵐ α ∂(volume.restrict (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)),
        partialSum n f α =o[atTop] fun N => (N : ℝ) * Real.sqrt (Real.log (Real.log N))

statements.name: Erdos995.erdos_995.variants.erdos_lower_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er49] showed the growth cannot be pushed below $N (\log\log N)^{1/2}$ by more than an
arbitrarily small power: there is a lacunary sequence and a mean-zero $f \in L^2([0,1])$ such
that for every $\varepsilon > 0$, for almost all $\alpha$,
$$\limsup_{N \to \infty} \frac{\sum_{k < N} f(\{\alpha n_k\})}{N (\log\log N)^{1/2 - \varepsilon}}
  = \infty.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_995.variants.erdos_lower_bound :
    ∃ (n : ℕ → ℕ), IsLacunary n ∧ ∃ (f : ℝ → ℝ),
      MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)) ∧
      ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..1, f x = 0 ∧
      ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ),
        ∀ᵐ α ∂(volume.restrict (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)),
          atTop.limsup (fun N => (((partialSum n f α N) /
            ((N : ℝ) * (Real.log (Real.log N)) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2 - ε)) : ℝ) : EReal)) = ⊤

problems.title: Erdős Problem 996
problems.doc:
*Reference:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/996](https://www.erdosproblems.com/996)
 - [Er49d] Erdös, P. "On the strong law of large numbers." Transactions of the American Mathematical
    Society 67.1 (1949): 51-56.
 - [Ma66] Matsuyama, Noboru. "On the strong law of large numbers." Tohoku Mathematical Journal,
    Second Series 18.3 (1966): 259-269.

statements.name: Erdos996.erdos_996
statements.doc:
Does there exists a positive constant `C` such that for all `f ∈ L²[0,1]` and all lacunary
sequences `n`, if `‖f - fₖ‖₂ = O(1 / log log log k ^ C)`, then for almost every `x`,
`lim ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, f (n k • x)) / N = ∫ t, f t ∂t`?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_996 :
    ∃ (C : ℝ), 0 < C ∧ ∀ (f : Lp ℂ 2 (haarAddCircle (T := 1))) (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    IsLacunary n →
    (fun k => (eLpNorm (⇑f - fourierPartial f k) 2 (haarAddCircle (T := 1))).toReal) =O[atTop]
    (fun k => 1 / (log (log (log k))) ^ C)
    →
    ∀ᵐ x, Tendsto (fun N => (∑ k ∈ .range N, f (n k • x)) / N) atTop
    (𝓝 (∫ t, f t ∂haarAddCircle))

statements.name: Erdos996.erdos_996.variants.log2
statements.doc: The following theorem is proved in [Ma66].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_996.variants.log2 : ∀ (C : ℝ), 0.5 < C →
    ∀ (f : Lp ℂ 2 (haarAddCircle (T := 1))) (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    IsLacunary n →
    (fun k => (eLpNorm (⇑f - fourierPartial f k) 2 (haarAddCircle (T := 1))).toReal) =O[atTop]
    (fun k => 1 / (log (log k)) ^ C)
    →
    ∀ᵐ x, Tendsto (fun N => (∑ k ∈ .range N, f (n k • x)) / N) atTop
    (𝓝 (∫ t, f t ∂haarAddCircle))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 997
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/997](https://www.erdosproblems.com/997)
- [APSSV26] B. Alexeev, M. Putterman, M. Sawhney, M. Sellke, and G. Valiant,
  [Short proofs in combinatorics and number theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29961).
  arXiv:2603.29961 (2026).
- [CLLW24] J. Champagne, T. Le, Y.-R. Liu, and T. D. Wooley, Well-distribution modulo one and the
  primes. arXiv:2406.19491 (2024).
- [Er64b] Erdős, P., Problems and results on diophantine approximations. Compositio Math. (1964),
  52-65.
- [Er85e] Erdős, P., Some problems and results in number theory. Number theory and combinatorics.
  Japan 1984 (Tokyo, Okayama and Kyoto, 1984) (1985), 65-87.
- [Hl55] Hlawka, Edmund, Zur formalen {T}heorie der {G}leichverteilung in kompakten {G}ruppen. Rend.
  Circ. Mat. Palermo (2) (1955), 33--47.
- [Mo26] P. Monticone, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 997](https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=mathlib-v4.28.0&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/pitmonticone/016f2ed66b4cd1c4c4b9998095170e60/raw/b7dfc05c525ae385b5835f89f1ada721443e4305/Erdos997.lean) (2026)

statements.name: Erdos997.erdos_997
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for every $\alpha$, the sequence $\{ \alpha p_n\}$ is not well-distributed,
if $p_n$ is the sequence of primes?

The answer is yes, by [APSSV26, Section 4]; a Lean formalisation is available in [Mo26].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_997 :
    ∀ α : ℝ, ¬ IsWellDistributed (fun n ↦ Int.fract (α * (n.nth Nat.Prime)))

statements.name: Erdos997.erdos_997.variants.lacunary
statements.doc:
Erdős proved that, if $n_k$ is a lacunary sequence, then the sequence $\{ \alpha n_k\}$ is not
well-distributed for almost all $\alpha$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_997.variants.lacunary (n : ℕ → ℕ) (h : IsLacunary n) :
    ∀ᵐ α, ¬ IsWellDistributed (fun k ↦ Int.fract (α * (n k : ℝ)))

statements.name: Erdos997.erdos_997.variants.irrational
statements.doc:
He also claimed in [Er64b] to have proved that there exists an irrational $\alpha$ for which
$\{\alpha p_n\}$ is not well-distributed. He later retracted this claim in [Er85e], saying "The
theorem is no doubt correct and perhaps will not be difficult to prove but I never was able to
reconstruct my 'proof' which perhaps never existed."

The existence of such an $\alpha$ was established by Champagne, Le, Liu, and Wooley [CLLW24].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_997.variants.irrational :
    ∃ α : ℝ, Irrational α ∧
      ¬ IsWellDistributed (fun n ↦ Int.fract (α * (n.nth Nat.Prime)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 999
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/999](https://www.erdosproblems.com/999)
- [Er64b] Erdős, P., _Problems and results on diophantine approximations_. Compositio Math.
  (1964), 52-65.
- [KoMa20] Koukoulopoulos, Dimitris and Maynard, James, _On the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture_.
  Ann. of Math. (2) (2020), 251--307.

statements.name: Erdos999.erdos_999
statements.doc:
For any function $f:\mathbb{N}\to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ the property that, for almost all
$\alpha$
$$\left\lvert \alpha-\frac{p}{q}\right\rvert < \frac{f(q)}{q}$$
has infinitely many solutions with $(p,q)=1$, is equivalent to
$$\sum_{q\geq 1}\phi(q)\frac{f(q)}{q}=\infty.$$

The Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture. It is easy to prove that the latter follows from the former.
Erdős proved this in the special case when $f(q)q$ is bounded. The full conjecture was proved by
Koukoulopoulos and Maynard [KoMa20].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_999 : ∀ f : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ q, 0 ≤ f q) →
    ((∀ᵐ x : ℝ, IsApproximable f x) ↔
      ¬ Summable fun q : ℕ ↦ (Nat.totient q : ℝ) * f q / q)

statements.name: Erdos999.erdos_999.variants.easy_direction
statements.doc:
It is easy to prove that divergence of the series follows from approximability almost
everywhere (the Borel–Cantelli lemma).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_999.variants.easy_direction (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : ∀ q, 0 ≤ f q)
    (h : ∀ᵐ x : ℝ, IsApproximable f x) :
    ¬ Summable fun q : ℕ ↦ (Nat.totient q : ℝ) * f q / q

statements.name: Erdos999.erdos_999.variants.erdos
statements.doc: Erdős [Er64b] proved the conjecture in the special case when $f(q)q$ is bounded.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_999.variants.erdos (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : ∀ q, 0 ≤ f q)
    (hb : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ q, f q * q ≤ C) :
    (∀ᵐ x : ℝ, IsApproximable f x) ↔
      ¬ Summable fun q : ℕ ↦ (Nat.totient q : ℝ) * f q / q

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1000
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1000](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1000)
- [Ca50b] Cassels, J. W. S., *Some metrical theorems in Diophantine approximation. I*. Proc.
  Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1950), 209-218.
- [Er64b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on diophantine approximations*. Compositio Math. (1964),
  52-65.
- [Ha] Haight, J. A., *Metric Diophantine approximation and related topics*. PhD thesis.

statements.name: Erdos1000.erdos_1000
statements.doc:
Let $A=\{n_1<n_2<\cdots\}$ be an infinite sequence of positive integers, and let $\phi_A(k)$
count the number of $1\leq m\leq n_k$ such that the fraction $\frac{m}{n_k}$ cannot be written
as $\frac{b}{n_j}$ for any integer $b$ and any $j<k$; equivalently,
$$
\frac{n_k}{(m,n_k)}\nmid n_j
$$
for all $1\leq j<k$.

Is there a sequence $A$ such that
$$
\lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k\leq N}\frac{\phi_A(k)}{n_k}=0?
$$

This was solved by Haight [Ha] who proved that such a sequence does exist (contrary to Erdős'
expectations).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1000 :
    ∃ n : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono n ∧ 0 < n 0 ∧
      Tendsto (phiAvg n) atTop (𝓝 0)

statements.name: Erdos1000.erdos_1000.variants.totient_le
statements.doc: It is trivial that $\phi_A(k)\geq \phi(n_k)$, where $\phi$ is the Euler totient function.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1000.variants.totient_le (n : ℕ → ℕ) (hn : StrictMono n) (hn0 : 0 < n 0)
    (k : ℕ) :
    (n k).totient ≤ phiSeq n k

statements.name: Erdos1000.erdos_1000.variants.liminf_eq_zero
statements.doc:
The study of $\phi_A$ was introduced by Cassels [Ca50b], who proved that there exist sequences
such that
$$
\liminf_{N\to \infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k\leq N}\frac{\phi_A(k)}{n_k}=0.
$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1000.variants.liminf_eq_zero :
    ∃ n : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono n ∧ 0 < n 0 ∧
      atTop.liminf (phiAvg n) = 0

statements.name: Erdos1000.erdos_1000.variants.not_tendsto_zero
statements.doc: Erdős [Er64b] proved that the limit of $\frac{\phi_A(k)}{n_k}$ as $k\to \infty$ cannot be $0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1000.variants.not_tendsto_zero (n : ℕ → ℕ) (hn : StrictMono n) (hn0 : 0 < n 0) :
    ¬ Tendsto (fun k : ℕ => (phiSeq n k : ℝ) / (n k : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 0)

statements.name: Erdos1000.erdos_1000.variants.limsup_eq_one
statements.doc:
In fact he proved that if $\liminf \frac{\phi_A(k)}{n_k}=0$ then
$\limsup \frac{\phi_A(k)}{n_k}=1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1000.variants.limsup_eq_one (n : ℕ → ℕ) (hn : StrictMono n) (hn0 : 0 < n 0)
    (h : atTop.liminf (fun k : ℕ => (phiSeq n k : ℝ) / (n k : ℝ)) = 0) :
    atTop.limsup (fun k : ℕ => (phiSeq n k : ℝ) / (n k : ℝ)) = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1001
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1001](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1001)
- [Er64b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on diophantine approximations*. Compositio Math.
  16 (1964), 52-65. [PDF](https://www.numdam.org/item/CM_1964__16__52_0.pdf)
- [EST58] Erdős, P. and Szüsz, P. and Turán, P., *Remarks on the theory of diophantine
  approximation*. Colloq. Math. 6 (1958), 119-126.
- [KeSo66] Kesten, H. and Sós, V. T., *On two problems of Erdős, Szüsz and Turán concerning
  diophantine approximations*. Acta Arith. 12 (1966/67), 183-192.
- [XiZa06] Xiong, Maosheng and Zaharescu, Alexandru, *A problem of Erdős-Szüsz-Turán on
  diophantine approximation*. Acta Arith. 125 (2006), 163-177.
- [Bo08] Boca, Florin P., *A problem of Erdős, Szüsz and Turán concerning Diophantine
  approximations*. Int. J. Number Theory 4 (2008), 691-708.

statements.name: Erdos1001.erdos_1001.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $S(N,A,c)$ be the measure of the set of those $\alpha\in (0,1)$ such that
$$\left\lvert \alpha-\frac{x}{y}\right\rvert< \frac{A}{y^2}$$
for some $N\leq y\leq cN$ and $(x,y)=1$. Does
$$\lim_{N\to \infty}S(N,A,c)=f(A,c)$$
exist?

This is a problem of Erdős, Szüsz, and Turán [EST58], restated in [Er64b, p. 62]. The existence
of the limit for all $A>0$ and $c\geq 1$ was proved by Kesten and Sós [KeSo66]. Boca [Bo08] and
Xiong and Zaharescu [XiZa06, Theorem 2] gave further proofs. We assume $A>0$ and $c\geq 1$,
since otherwise $S=0$. The second question, the explicit form of $f(A,c)$, is not stated here.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1001.parts.i (A c : ℝ) (hA : 0 < A) (hc : 1 ≤ c) :
    ∃ f : ℝ, Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ S N A c) atTop (𝓝 f)

statements.name: Erdos1001.erdos_1001.variants.est_formula
statements.doc:
Erdős, Szüsz, and Turán [EST58] proved that
$$f(A,c)=\frac{12 A\log c}{\pi^2}$$
when $0<A< \frac{c}{1+c^2}$. Here $c\geq 1$, since the range $N\leq y\leq cN$ is empty for
$c<1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1001.variants.est_formula (A c : ℝ) (hA : 0 < A) (hc : 1 ≤ c)
    (hAc : A < c / (1 + c ^ 2)) :
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ S N A c) atTop (𝓝 (12 * A * Real.log c / Real.pi ^ 2))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1002
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1002](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1002)
- [Ke60] Kesten, Harry, Uniform distribution {${\rm mod}\,1$}. Ann. of Math. (2) (1960), 445--471.

statements.name: Erdos1002.erdos_1002
statements.doc:
For any $0<\alpha<1$, let $f(\alpha,n)=\frac{1}{\log n}\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}(\tfrac{1}{2}-
\{ \alpha k\})$. Does $f(\alpha,n)$ have an asymptotic distribution function?

In other words, is there a non-decreasing function $g$ such that $g(-\infty)=0$, $g(\infty)=1$,
and $\lim_{n\to \infty}\lvert \{ \alpha\in (0,1): f(\alpha,n)\leq c\}\rvert=g(c)$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1002 :
    ∃ g : ℝ → ℝ, Monotone g ∧
    Tendsto g atBot (𝓝 0) ∧
    Tendsto g atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
    letI f :=  fun (α : ℝ) (n : ℕ) ↦
      (1 / log n) * ∑ k ∈ Icc (1 : ℕ) n, (1 / 2 - Int.fract (α * k))
    ∀ c : ℝ, Tendsto (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (volume { α | α ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ f α n ≤ c }).toReal)
      atTop (𝓝 (g c))

statements.name: Erdos1002.erdos_1002.variants.kesten
statements.doc:
Kesten [Ke60] proved that if $f(\alpha,\beta,n)=\frac{1}{\log n}\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}(\tfrac{1}{2}-
\{\beta+\alpha k\})$ then $f(\alpha,\beta,n)$ has asymptotic distribution function
$g(c)=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\rho c}\frac{1}{1+t^2}\mathrm{d}t$, where $\rho>0$ is an explicit
constant.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1002.variants.kesten :
    ∃ ρ > 0,
      let g := fun (c : ℝ) ↦ (1 / π) * ∫ t in Iic (ρ * c), 1 / (1 + t^2)
      ∀ c : ℝ, Tendsto (fun (n : ℕ) ↦
        (volume { p : ℝ × ℝ | let ⟨α, β⟩ := p; α ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ β ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧
          (1 / log n) * ∑ k ∈ Icc (1 : ℕ) n, (1 / 2 - Int.fract (β + α * k)) ≤ c }).toReal)
        atTop (𝓝 (g c))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1003
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1003](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1003)

statements.name: Erdos1003.erdos_1003
statements.doc:
Are there infinitely many solutions to $\phi(n) = \phi(n+1)$, where $\phi$ is the Euler totient
function?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1003 : Set.Infinite {n | φ n = φ (n + 1)}

statements.name: Erdos1003.erdos_1003.variants.Icc
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er85e] says that, presumably, for every $k \geq 1$ the equation
$$\phi(n) = \phi(n+1) = \cdots = \phi (n+k)$$ has infinitely many solutions.

[Er85e] Erdős, P., _Some problems and results in number theory_. Number theory and combinatorics. Japan 1984 (Tokyo, Okayama and Kyoto, 1984) (1985), 65-87.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1003.variants.Icc :
    ∀ k ≥ 1, {n | ∀ i ∈ Set.Icc 1 k, φ n = φ (n + i)}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos1003.erdos_1003.variants.eps87
statements.doc:
Erdős, Pomerance, and Sárközy [EPS87] proved that for all large $x$, the number
of $n \leq x$ with $\phi(n) = \phi(n+1)$ is at most $$\frac{x}{\exp((\log x)^{1/3})}$$.

[EPS87] Erd\H os, Paul and Pomerance, Carl and S\'ark\"ozy, Andr\'as, _On locally repeated values of certain arithmetic functions_. {II}. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1987), 1--7.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1003.variants.eps87 :  ∀ᶠ x in atTop,
    {(n : ℕ) | (n ≤ x) ∧ φ n = φ (n + 1)}.ncard ≤
      x / Real.exp ((x.log) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1004
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1004](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1004)

statements.name: Erdos1004.erdos_1004
statements.doc:
For any fixed c > 0, if x is sufficiently large then there exists n ≤ x such that
the values of φ(n+k) are all distinct for 1 ≤ k ≤ (log x)^c.
This is an open problem.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1004 :
    ∀ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∃ n ≤ x,
      IsDistinctTotientRun n ⌊(Real.log (x : ℝ)) ^ c⌋₊

statements.name: Erdos1004.erdos_1004.variants.le_of_isDistinctTotientRun
statements.doc:
Erdős, Pomerance, and Sárközy [EPS87] proved that if φ(n+k) are all distinct for 1 ≤ k ≤ K then
K ≤ n / exp(c (log n)^{1/3}) for some constant c > 0.
Here we state the existence of such a constant c.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1004.variants.le_of_isDistinctTotientRun :
    ∃ (c : ℝ) (hc : c > 0),
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ (K : ℕ), IsDistinctTotientRun n K →
        (K : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) / Real.exp (c * (Real.log n) ^ (1/3 : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1005
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1005](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1005)
- [Ma42] Mayer, A. E., *A mean value theorem concerning Farey series*. Quart. J. Math. Oxford
  Ser. (1942), 48-57.
- [Er43] Erdős, P., *A note on Farey series*. Quart. J. Math. Oxford Ser. (1943), 82-85.
- [vD25b] van Doorn, W., *Improved bounds for the Mayer-Erdős phenomenon on similarly ordered Farey
  fractions*. [arXiv:2509.00121](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.00121) (2025).

statements.name: Erdos1005.erdos_1005
statements.doc:
Let $\frac{a_1}{b_1}, \frac{a_2}{b_2}, \ldots$ be the Farey fractions of order $n \geq 4$. Let
$f(n)$ be the largest integer such that if $1 \leq k < l \leq k + f(n)$ then $\frac{a_k}{b_k}$ and
$\frac{a_l}{b_l}$ are similarly ordered, in other words $(a_k - a_l)(b_k - b_l) \geq 0$. Estimate
$f(n)$: in particular, is there a constant $c > 0$ such that $f(n) = (c + o(1)) n$ for all
large $n$?

Mayer [Ma42] proved that $f(n) \to \infty$ and Erdős [Er43] that $f(n) \gg n$. Van Doorn [vD25b]
proved $(1/12 - o(1)) n \le f(n) \le n / 4 + O(1)$ and conjectured that $f(n) = (1/4 + o(1)) n$,
which was proved by Cipollini and GPT-5.5; see `erdos_1005.variants.constant`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1005 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (f n : ℝ) / n) atTop (𝓝 c)

statements.name: Erdos1005.erdos_1005.variants.constant
statements.doc:
The constant in Problem 1005 is $c = 1/4$: $f(n) = (1/4 + o(1)) n$ (Cipollini and GPT-5.5;
formalised by Cipollini, van Doorn and Aristotle).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1005.variants.constant :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (f n : ℝ) / n) atTop (𝓝 (1 / 4))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1007
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1007](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1007)
- [ChNo16] Chaffee, Joe and Noble, Matt, *Dimension 4 and dimension 5 graphs with minimum edge
  set*. Australas. J. Combin. (2016), 327-333.
- [Ho13] House, Roger F., *A 4-dimensional graph has at least 9 edges*. Discrete Math. (2013),
  1783-1789.

statements.name: Erdos1007.erdos_1007
statements.doc:
The dimension of a graph $G$ is the minimal $n$ such that $G$ can be embedded in $\mathbb{R}^n$
such that every edge of $G$ is a unit line segment.

What is the smallest number of edges in a graph with dimension $4$?

Answer: The smallest number of edges is $9$, achieved solely by $K_{3,3}$, proved by House [Ho13]. An
alternative proof was given by Chaffee and Noble [ChNo16], who also prove that the smallest
number of edges in a graph of dimension $5$ is $15$ (achieved by $K_6$ and $K_{1,3,3}$).

statements.name: Erdos1007.erdos_1007.variants.dimension_four_extremal
statements.doc: The smallest number of edges in a graph of dimension $4$ is achieved solely by $K_{3,3}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1007.variants.dimension_four_extremal (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (hdim : G.HasDimension 4) (hcard : G.edgeSet.ncard = 9)
    (hdeg : ∀ v : Fin n, ∃ w : Fin n, G.Adj v w) :
    Nonempty (G ≃g completeBipartiteGraph (Fin 3) (Fin 3))

statements.name: Erdos1007.erdos_1007.variants.dimension_five
statements.doc: The smallest number of edges in a graph of dimension $5$ is $15$.

statements.name: Erdos1007.erdos_1007.variants.dimension_five_extremal
statements.doc: The smallest number of edges in a graph of dimension $5$ is achieved by $K_6$ and $K_{1,3,3}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1007.variants.dimension_five_extremal :
    ((SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin 6)).HasDimension 5 ∧
        (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin 6)).edgeSet.ncard = 15) ∧
      (K133.HasDimension 5 ∧ K133.edgeSet.ncard = 15)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1008
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1008](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1008)
- [CFS14b] Conlon, D. and Fox, J. and Sudakov, B., *Large subgraphs without complete bipartite
  graphs*. arXiv:1401.6711 (2014).
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.

statements.name: Erdos1008.erdos_1008
statements.doc:
Does every graph with $m$ edges contain a subgraph with $\gg m^{2/3}$ edges which contains
no $C_4$?

This problem was first solved in the affirmative by Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov [CFS14b]. A simple
proof is given by Hunter in the comments.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1008 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ H ≤ G, (cycleGraph 4).Free H ∧
        c * (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ) ≤ (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1008.erdos_1008.variants.three_quarters
statements.doc:
Originally asked by Bollobás and Erdős in 'a colloquium on graph theory at Tihany' with $m^{2/3}$
replaced by $m^{3/4}$. Folkman showed this is false with the counterexample $K_{n,n^2}$, which has
$n^3$ edges, and yet every subgraph with $>n^2+\binom{n}{2}$ edges contains a $C_4$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1008.variants.three_quarters :
    ¬ ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ H ≤ G, (cycleGraph 4).Free H ∧
        c * (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ^ (3 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1008.erdos_1008.variants.folkman
statements.doc:
Folkman's counterexample $K_{n,n^2}$, which has $n^3$ edges, and yet every subgraph with
$>n^2+\binom{n}{2}$ edges contains a $C_4$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1008.variants.folkman (n : ℕ) :
    ((completeBipartiteGraph (Fin n) (Fin (n ^ 2))).edgeSet.ncard = n ^ 3) ∧
      ∀ H ≤ completeBipartiteGraph (Fin n) (Fin (n ^ 2)),
        n ^ 2 + n.choose 2 < H.edgeSet.ncard → cycleGraph 4 ⊑ H

statements.name: Erdos1008.erdos_1008.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc: In [Er71] Erdős revises the conjecture to $m^{2/3}$, and notes $\gg m^{1/2}$ is trivial.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1008.variants.lower_bound :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ H ≤ G, (cycleGraph 4).Free H ∧
        c * (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1009
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1009](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1009)
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97--109.
- [Gy88] Győri, E., *On the number of edge-disjoint triangles in graphs of given size*. (1988),
  267--276.

statements.name: Erdos1009.erdos_1009
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for every $c>0$, there exists $f(c)$ such that every graph on $n$ vertices with
at least $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+k$ edges, where $k<c n$, contains at least $k-f(c)$ many edge
disjoint triangles?

Erdős [Er71] proved this for $c<1/2$ using a theorem of Erdős and Gallai, which says that every
graph on $n$ vertices with at least $(n-1)^2/4+2$ many edges, with chromatic number $3$, must
contain a triangle. In fact, Erdős proved this is true with $f(c)=0$ for $c<1/2$. At first Erdős
thought $f(c)=0$ for larger values of $c$ but this is false: an example of Sauer proves that
$f(2)\geq 1$.

This is true, and was proved by Győri [Gy88] who proved that this is true with $f(c)\ll c^2$,
and also that $f(c)=0$ if $c<2$ for odd $n$ or $c<3/2$ for even $n$.

A family of edge disjoint triangles is a finite set of $3$-cliques of $G$ any two of which share
at most one vertex.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1009 : ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ f : ℕ, ∀ (n k : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
    n ^ 2 / 4 + k ≤ G.edgeSet.ncard → (k : ℝ) < c * n →
      ∃ T : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), (∀ t ∈ T, G.IsNClique 3 t) ∧
        (T : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Pairwise (fun s t => (s ∩ t).card ≤ 1) ∧ k ≤ T.card + f

statements.name: Erdos1009.erdos_1009.variants.sauer
statements.doc:
Sauer gave an example of a graph on $n$ vertices with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+2n-6$ many edges
which contains only $2n-7$ many edge disjoint triangles: if $n=2r+4$ then $G$ is the complete
tripartite graph on $[r]\times [r]\times [4]$, with a $K_4$ on the $[4]$ vertices also.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1009.variants.sauer : ∀ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r → ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * r + 4)),
    G.edgeSet.ncard = (2 * r + 4) ^ 2 / 4 + 2 * (2 * r + 4) - 6 ∧
      ∀ T : Finset (Finset (Fin (2 * r + 4))), (∀ t ∈ T, G.IsNClique 3 t) →
        (T : Set (Finset (Fin (2 * r + 4)))).Pairwise (fun s t => (s ∩ t).card ≤ 1) →
          T.card ≤ 2 * (2 * r + 4) - 7

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1010
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1010](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1010)
- [Er62d] Erdős, P., *On a theorem of Rademacher-Turán*. Illinois J. Math. (1962), 122-127.
- [LoSi76] Lovász, L. and Simonovits, Miklós, *On the number of complete subgraphs of a graph*.
  (1976), 431-441.
- [NiKh81] Nikiforov, V. S. and Khadzhiivanov, N. G., *Solution of the problem of P. Erdős on the
  number of triangles in graphs with $n$ vertices and $[n^2/4]+l$ edges*. C. R. Acad. Bulgare
  Sci. (1981), 969-970.

statements.name: Erdos1010.erdos_1010
statements.doc:
Let $t<\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. Does every graph on $n$ vertices with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+t$ edges
contain at least $t\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ triangles?

Rademacher proved that every graph on $n$ vertices with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+1$ edges contains at
least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ triangles. Erdős [Er62d] proved that every graph on $n$ vertices with
$\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+t$ edges contains at least $t\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ triangles, for all $t<cn$,
for some constant $c>0$.

This is true, and was proved independently by Lovász and Simonovits [LoSi76] and Nikiforov and
Khadzhiivanov [NiKh81].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1010 : ∀ n t : ℕ, t < n / 2 → ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
    G.edgeFinset.card = n ^ 2 / 4 + t → t * (n / 2) ≤ (G.cliqueFinset 3).card

statements.name: Erdos1010.erdos_1010.variants.rademacher
statements.doc:
Rademacher proved that every graph on $n$ vertices with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+1$ edges contains at
least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ triangles.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1010.variants.rademacher : ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
    G.edgeFinset.card = n ^ 2 / 4 + 1 → n / 2 ≤ (G.cliqueFinset 3).card

statements.name: Erdos1010.erdos_1010.variants.erdos
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er62d] proved that every graph on $n$ vertices with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+t$ edges contains
at least $t\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ triangles, for all $t<cn$, for some constant $c>0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1010.variants.erdos : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ n t : ℕ, t < c * n →
    ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.edgeFinset.card = n ^ 2 / 4 + t →
      t * (n / 2) ≤ (G.cliqueFinset 3).card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1013
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1013](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1013)
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [GrYa68] Graver, J. E. and Yackel, J., *Some graph theoretic results associated with Ramsey's
  theorem*. J. Combinatorial Theory 4 (1968), 125-175.
- [DaIl22] Davies, E. and Illingworth, F., *The $\chi$-Ramsey problem for triangle-free graphs*.
  SIAM J. Discrete Math. 36 (2022), 1124-1134.
- [HHKP25] Hefty, Z., Horn, P., King, D. and Pfender, F., *Improving $R(3,k)$ in just two bites*.
  [arXiv:2510.19718](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.19718) (2025).

statements.name: Erdos1013.erdos_1013.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $h_3(k)$ be the minimal $n$ such that there exists a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with
chromatic number $k$. Find an asymptotic for $h_3(k)$, and also prove
$$\lim_{k\to \infty}\frac{h_3(k+1)}{h_3(k)}=1.$$

This is the first part.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1013.parts.i :
    (fun k ↦ (h3 k : ℝ)) ~[atTop] erdos_1013.parts.i.answer

statements.name: Erdos1013.erdos_1013.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $h_3(k)$ be the minimal $n$ such that there exists a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with
chromatic number $k$. Find an asymptotic for $h_3(k)$, and also prove
$$\lim_{k\to \infty}\frac{h_3(k+1)}{h_3(k)}=1.$$

This is the second part.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1013.parts.ii :
    Tendsto (fun k : ℕ ↦ (h3 (k + 1) : ℝ) / h3 k) atTop (nhds 1)

statements.name: Erdos1013.erdos_1013.variants.graver_yackel
statements.doc:
Graver and Yackel [GrYa68] proved
$$h_3(k)\gg \frac{\log k}{\log\log k}k^2.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1013.variants.graver_yackel :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (Real.log k / Real.log (Real.log k)) * k ^ 2 ≤ (h3 k : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1013.erdos_1013.variants.lower
statements.doc:
The upper bound $f(n) \leq (2+o(1))(n/\log n)^{1/2}$ of Davies and Illingworth [DaIl22] for the
function $f$ of [1104] gives
$$\left(\frac{1}{2}-o(1)\right)k^2\log k\leq h_3(k).$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1013.variants.lower :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      (1 / 2 - ε) * k ^ 2 * Real.log k ≤ (h3 k : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1013.erdos_1013.variants.upper
statements.doc:
The lower bound $f(n) \geq (1-o(1))(n/\log n)^{1/2}$ for the function $f$ of [1104], which follows
from the construction of Hefty, Horn, King, and Pfender [HHKP25], gives
$$h_3(k) \leq (2+o(1))k^2\log k.$$
The site states $(1+o(1))k^2\log k$, but the bounds recorded in [1104] give only $2+o(1)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1013.variants.upper :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      (h3 k : ℝ) ≤ (2 + ε) * k ^ 2 * Real.log k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1014
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1014](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1014)
- [Er71] Erdős, P., Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis. Combinatorial
  Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [OpenAI26] *On the ratio of $R(k,\ell)$ and $R(k,\ell+1)$*, proof due to an internal model at
  OpenAI (2026).
  https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/6dc7175d-d9e7-4b8d-96b8-48fe5798cd5b/Ramsey.pdf

statements.name: Erdos1014.erdos_1014
statements.doc:
Let $R(k,l)$ be the Ramsey number, so the minimal $n$ such that every graph on at least $n$
vertices contains either a $K_k$ or an independent set on $l$ vertices.

Prove, for fixed $k\geq 3$, that
$$\lim_{l\to \infty}\frac{R(k,l+1)}{R(k,l)}=1.$$

This has been
[solved](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/6dc7175d-d9e7-4b8d-96b8-48fe5798cd5b/Ramsey.pdf)
by an internal model at OpenAI.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1014 : ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k →
    Tendsto (fun l : ℕ ↦ (R(k, l + 1) : ℝ) / (R(k, l) : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1)

statements.name: Erdos1014.erdos_1014.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
That proof in fact shows that
$$R(k,l+1)\leq (1+O(l^{-c/k^2}))R(k,l)$$
for some constant $c>0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1014.variants.upper_bound :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ l : ℕ in atTop,
      (R(k, l + 1) : ℝ) ≤ (1 + C * (l : ℝ) ^ (-c / (k : ℝ) ^ 2)) * (R(k, l) : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1017
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1017](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1017)
- [EGP66] Erdős, Paul and Goodman, A. W. and Pósa, Lajos,
  *The representation of a graph by set intersections*. Canadian J. Math. (1966), 106–112.
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97–109.
- [GyKe17] Győri, Ervin and Keszegh, Balázs,
  *On the number of edge-disjoint triangles in $K_4$-free graphs*.
  Combinatorica (2017), 1113–1124.
- [Lo68] Lovász, L., *On covering of graphs*.
  Theory of Graphs (Proc. Colloq., Tihany, 1966) (1968), 231–236.

statements.name: Erdos1017.erdos_1017.lower_bound
statements.doc:
Let $f(n,k)$ be such that every graph on $n$ vertices and $k$ edges can be partitioned
into at most $f(n,k)$ edge-disjoint complete graphs. Estimate $f(n,k)$ for $k>n^2/4$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1017.lower_bound :
    ∀ n k : ℕ, k ≤ n.choose 2 → n * n < 4 * k →
      erdos_1017.lower_bound.answer n k ≤ f n k

statements.name: Erdos1017.erdos_1017.upper_bound
statements.doc:
Estimate an upper bound for $f(n,k)$, the worst-case number of complete subgraphs
needed to partition the edges of an $n$-vertex, $k$-edge graph, for
$n^2/4 < k \le \binom{n}{2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1017.upper_bound :
    ∀ n k : ℕ, k ≤ n.choose 2 → n * n < 4 * k →
      f n k ≤ erdos_1017.upper_bound.answer n k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1020
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1020](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1020)
- [BDE76] Bollobás, B. and Daykin, D. E. and Erdős, P., *Sets of independent edges of a hypergraph*.
  Quart. J. Math. Oxford Ser. (2) (1976), 25--32.
- [Er65d] Erdős, P., *A problem on independent {$r$}-tuples*. Ann. Univ. Sci. Budapest. Eötvös Sect.
  Math. (1965), 93--95.
- [ErGa59] Erdős, P. and Gallai, T., *On maximal paths and circuits of graphs*. Acta Math. Acad.
  Sci. Hungar. (1959), 337-356 (unbound insert).
- [FLM12] Frankl, Peter and Łuczak, Tomasz and Mieczkowska, Katarzyna, *On matchings in
  hypergraphs*. Electron. J. Combin. (2012), Paper 42, 5.
- [FRR12] Frankl, Peter and Rödl, Vojtech and Ruciński, Andrzej, *On the maximum number of edges in
  a triple system not containing a disjoint family of a given size*. Combin. Probab. Comput. (2012),
  141--148.
- [Fr17] Frankl, Peter, *Proof of the {E}rdős matching conjecture in a new range*. Israel J. Math.
  (2017), 421--430.
- [Fr87] Frankl, Peter, *The shifting technique in extremal set theory*. (1987), 81--110.
- [HLS12] Huang, Hao and Loh, Po-Shen and Sudakov, Benny, *The size of a hypergraph and its matching
  number*. Combin. Probab. Comput. (2012), 442--450.
- [Kl68] Kleitman, Daniel J., *Maximal number of subsets of a finite set no {$k$} of which are
  pairwise disjoint*. J. Combinatorial Theory (1968), 157--163.
- [KoKu23] Kolupaev, Dmitriy and Kupavskii, Andrey, *Erdős matching conjecture for almost perfect
  matchings*. Discrete Math. (2023), Paper No. 113304, 9.
- [LuMi14] Łuczak, Tomasz and Mieczkowska, Katarzyna, *On {E}rdős' extremal problem on matchings in
  hypergraphs*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (2014), 178--194.

statements.name: Erdos1020.erdos_1020
statements.doc:
Let $f(n;r,k)$ be the maximal number of edges in an $r$-uniform hypergraph which contains no set of $k$ many independent edges.

For all $r\geq 3$, $$f(n;r,k)=\max\left(\binom{rk-1}{r}, \binom{n}{r}-\binom{n-k+1}{r}\right).$$

Note: the source states the formula with no range on `n` or `k`, but some restriction
is needed: e.g. for `r = 3`, `k = 2`, `n = 4` no two disjoint triples fit in `4`
vertices, so the left-hand side is `4.choose 3 = 4` while the right-hand side is
`5.choose 3 = 10`. We require `k ≥ 1` and `n ≥ r*k - 1`: this is the smallest `n`
accommodating the construction counted by the first term (all `r`-subsets of a fixed
`(r*k - 1)`-set), and at `n = r*k - 1` the equality holds trivially, since the complete
`r`-uniform hypergraph has no `k`-matching. The source's commentary likewise calls the
case `n < k*r` trivial.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1020 (r : ℕ) (hr : 3 ≤ r) (n k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k)
    (hrk : r * k - 1 ≤ n) :
    f n r k = max ((r * k - 1).choose r)
      (n.choose r - (n - k + 1).choose r)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1021
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1021](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1021)
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [Er74c] Erdős, Paul, *Extremal problems on graphs and hypergraphs*. (1974), 75-84.
- [CoLe21] Conlon, David and Lee, Joonkyung, *On the extremal number of subdivisions*. Int. Math.
  Res. Not. IMRN (2021), 9122--9145.
- [Ja19] Janzer, Oliver, *Improved bounds for the extremal number of subdivisions*. Electron. J.
  Combin. (2019), Paper No. 3.3, 6.

statements.name: Erdos1021.erdos_1021
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for every $k \geq 3$, there is a constant $c_k > 0$ such that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n, G_k) \ll n^{3/2 - c_k},$$
where $G_k$ is the bipartite graph between $\{y_1, \ldots, y_k\}$ and
$\{z_1, \ldots, z_{\binom{k}{2}}\}$, with each $z_j$ joined to a unique pair of $y_i$?

A conjecture of Erdős and Simonovits [Er71, Er74c], who proved (in unpublished work) that one must
have $c_k \to 0$ as $k \to \infty$. The graph $G_k$ is the $1$-subdivision of $K_k$; for $k = 3$
it is the $6$-cycle. This was proved by Conlon and Lee [CoLe21] with $c_k = 6^{-k}$, improved to
$c_k = \frac{1}{4k - 6}$ by Janzer [Ja19]; see `erdos_1021.variants.janzer`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1021 :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n (cliqueSubdivision k) : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
        fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 - c)

statements.name: Erdos1021.erdos_1021.variants.janzer
statements.doc: Janzer [Ja19] proved that one can take $c_k = \frac{1}{4k - 6}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1021.variants.janzer (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n (cliqueSubdivision k) : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 - 1 / (4 * (k : ℝ) - 6))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1022
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1022](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1022)
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [Lo68] Lovász, L., *On covering of graphs*. Theory of Graphs (Proc. Colloq., Tihany, 1966)
  (1968), 231-236.
- [Wo13b] Wood, D. R., *Hypergraph colouring and degeneracy*. arXiv:1310.2972 (2013).

statements.name: Erdos1022.erdos_1022
statements.doc:
Is there a constant $c_t$, where $c_t\to \infty$ as $t\to \infty$, such that if $\mathcal{F}$
is a finite family of finite sets, all of size at least $t$, and for every set $X$ there are
$<c_t\lvert X\rvert$ many $A\in \mathcal{F}$ with $A\subseteq X$, then $\mathcal{F}$ has
chromatic number $2$ (in other words, has property B)?

This is false, and $c_t<2$ for all $t$: a counterexample is provided by Wood [Wo13b], who
constructs, for any $r\geq 2$, a triangle-free $2$-degenerate $r$-uniform hypergraph with
chromatic number $3$. A similar counterexample was found independently by KoishiChan in the
comments.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1022 :
    ¬ ∃ c : ℕ → ℝ, Filter.Tendsto c Filter.atTop Filter.atTop ∧
      ∀ t : ℕ, SparseImpliesPropertyB t (c t)

statements.name: Erdos1022.erdos_1022.variants.lt_two
statements.doc:
This is false, and $c_t<2$ for all $t$: a counterexample is provided by Wood [Wo13b], who
constructs, for any $r\geq 2$, a triangle-free $2$-degenerate $r$-uniform hypergraph with
chromatic number $3$. A similar counterexample was found independently by KoishiChan in the
comments.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1022.variants.lt_two :
    ∀ (t : ℕ) (c : ℝ), SparseImpliesPropertyB t c → c < 2

statements.name: Erdos1022.erdos_1022.variants.lovasz
statements.doc:
Erdős originally conjectured, in this language, that $c_2=1$, which he reports in [Er71] was
proved by Lovász.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1022.variants.lovasz :
    IsGreatest {c : ℝ | SparseImpliesPropertyB 2 c} 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1023
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1023](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1023)
- [Er71, p.105] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.

statements.name: Erdos1023.erdos_1023
statements.doc:
Let $F(n)$ be the maximal size of a family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that no set in
this family is the union of other members of the family. Is it true that there is a constant
$c>0$ such that
$$F(n)\sim c \frac{2^n}{n^{1/2}}?$$

Hunter observes in the comments that this follows from the solution to [447], which implies
$F(n)\sim \binom{n}{n/2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1023 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
      ((fun n : ℕ => (F n : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
        (fun n : ℕ => c * 2 ^ n / (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)))

statements.name: Erdos1023.erdos_1023.variants.erdos_kleitman
statements.doc:
Erdős and Kleitman proved in unpublished work that
$$F(n)\asymp \frac{2^n}{n^{1/2}}.$$
([Er71] has an exponent of $3/2$, but this is presumably a typo.)
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1023.variants.erdos_kleitman :
    (fun n : ℕ => (F n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (2 : ℝ) ^ n / (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos1023.erdos_1023.variants.hunter
statements.doc:
Hunter observes in the comments that this follows from the solution to [447], which implies
$F(n)\sim \binom{n}{n/2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1023.variants.hunter :
    (fun n : ℕ => (F n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (n.choose (n / 2) : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1024
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1024](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1024)
- [PhRo86] Phelps, K. T. and R\"odl, V., Steiner triple systems with minimum independence number. Ars
  Combin. (1986), 167--172.

statements.name: Erdos1024.erdos_1024
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be such that every $3$-uniform linear hypergraph on $n$ vertices contains an independent
set on $f(n)$ vertices. Estimate $f(n)$.

Phelps and Rödl [PhRo86] proved $f(n) \asymp (n\log n)^{1/2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1024 :
    (fun n ↦ (Hypergraph.linearIndependenceNumber n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop]
    erdos_1024.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1025
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1025](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1025)
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [ErHa58] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., *On the structure of set mappings*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci.
  Hungar. (1958), 111-133.
- [Sp72] Spencer, Joel, *Turán's theorem for $k$-graphs*. Discrete Math. (1972), 183--186.
- [CFS16] Conlon, David and Fox, Jacob and Sudakov, Benny, *Short proofs of some extremal results
  II*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (2016), 173--196.

statements.name: Erdos1025.erdos_1025
statements.doc:
Let $f$ be a function from all pairs of elements in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ to $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such
that $f(x,y)\neq x$ and $\neq y$ for all $x,y$. We call $X\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ independent
if whenever $x,y\in X$ we have $f(x,y)\not\in X$.

Let $g(n)$ be such that, in every function $f$, there is an independent set of size at least
$g(n)$. Estimate $g(n)$.

A question of Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa58], who could prove $n^{1/3} \ll g(n) \ll (n\log n)^{1/2}$.
Spencer [Sp72] proved $g(n)\gg n^{1/2}$. Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov [CFS16] proved
$g(n)\ll n^{1/2}$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1025 : (fun n : ℕ => (g n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] fun n : ℕ => √n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1026
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1026](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1026)
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [Ha57] Hanani, Haim, *On the number of monotonic subsequences*. Bull. Res. Council Israel
  Sect. F (1957/58), 11-13.
- [St95] Steele, J. Michael, *Variations on the monotone subsequence theme of Erdős and
  Szekeres*. (1995), 111-131.
- [TWY16] Tidor, J. and Wang, V. and Yang, B., *$1$-color avoiding paths, special tournaments,
  and incidence geometry*. arXiv:1608.04153 (2016).
- [Wa17] Wagner, Adam Zsolt, *Large subgraphs in rainbow-triangle free colorings*. J. Graph
  Theory (2017), 141-148.

statements.name: Erdos1026.erdos_1026
statements.doc:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ be a sequence of distinct real numbers. Determine
$$
\max\left(\sum x_{i_r}\right),
$$
where the maximum is taken over all monotonic subsequences.

This is as Erdős posed the problem in [Er71], which is rather ambiguous. Discussion between
several users in the comments section has led to the following precise possible question, as
posed by van Doorn:

What is the largest constant $c$ such that, for all sequences of $n$ real numbers
$x_1,\ldots,x_n$,
$$
\max\left(\sum x_{i_r}\right) > (c-o(1))\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum x_i
$$
(where again the maximum is taken over all monotonic subsequences)?

Cambie makes the stronger conjecture that if $x_1,\ldots,x_{k^2}$ are distinct positive real
numbers with $\sum x_i=1$ then there is always a monotonic subsequence with sum at least $1/k$.

This stronger conjecture appears to have been first proved by Tidor, Wang, and Yang [TWY16],
and is also implicit in work of Wagner [Wa17]. A proof was given and formalised by Aristotle
(see the comments), with an alternative proof provided by Chan. In particular, this shows that
$c=1$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1026 : IsGreatest admissibleConstants 1

statements.name: Erdos1026.erdos_1026.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc: A construction of Cambie in the comments shows that $c\leq 1$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1026.variants.upper_bound : 1 ∈ upperBounds admissibleConstants

statements.name: Erdos1026.erdos_1026.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
Hanani [Ha57] showed that every sequence is the disjoint union of at most
$(\sqrt{2}+o(1))\sqrt{n}$ many monotonic subsequences, whence $c\geq 1/\sqrt{2}$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1026.variants.lower_bound : 1 / Real.sqrt 2 ∈ admissibleConstants

statements.name: Erdos1026.erdos_1026.variants.hanani
statements.doc:
Hanani [Ha57] showed that every sequence is the disjoint union of at most
$(\sqrt{2}+o(1))\sqrt{n}$ many monotonic subsequences.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1026.variants.hanani (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, Function.Injective x →
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (I : Fin m → Finset (Fin n)),
        (∀ j, MonotoneOn x ↑(I j) ∨ AntitoneOn x ↑(I j)) ∧
        (Pairwise fun j k => Disjoint (I j) (I k)) ∧
        (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m)).biUnion I = Finset.univ ∧
        (m : ℝ) ≤ (Real.sqrt 2 + ε) * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1026.erdos_1026.variants.weighted_erdos_szekeres
statements.doc:
Cambie makes the stronger conjecture that if $x_1,\ldots,x_{k^2}$ are distinct positive real
numbers with $\sum x_i=1$ then there is always a monotonic subsequence with sum at least $1/k$.
This is a weighted-form of the Erdős-Szekeres theorem, and is also mentioned (as an open
question) in a survey on the latter by Steele [St95].

This stronger conjecture appears to have been first proved by Tidor, Wang, and Yang [TWY16],
and is also implicit in work of Wagner [Wa17]. A proof was given and formalised by Aristotle
(see the comments), with an alternative proof provided by Chan.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1026.variants.weighted_erdos_szekeres (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) (x : Fin (k ^ 2) → ℝ)
    (hx : Function.Injective x) (hx' : ∀ i, 0 < x i) (hsum : (∑ i, x i) = 1) :
    ∃ S ∈ monotonicSubsequenceSums x, 1 / (k : ℝ) ≤ S

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1027
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1027](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1027)
- [Er64e] Erdős, P., *On a combinatorial problem. II*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1964),
  445-447.
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.

statements.name: Erdos1027.erdos_1027
statements.doc:
Let $c>0$, and let $n$ be sufficiently large depending on $c$. Suppose that $\mathcal{F}$ is a
family of at most $c2^n$ many finite sets of size $n$. Let $X=\cup_{A\in \mathcal{F}}A$.

Must there exist $\gg_c 2^{\lvert X\rvert}$ many sets $B\subset X$ which intersect every set in
$\mathcal{F}$, yet contain none of them?

The existence of a single such $B$ is equivalent to $\mathcal{F}$ being $2$-chromatic (or having
property B), see [901](https://www.erdosproblems.com/901).

This is true, and a proof was given in the comment section by Koishi Chan.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1027 : ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ (α : Type) [DecidableEq α] (F : Finset (Finset α)),
      (∀ A ∈ F, A.card = n) → (F.card : ℝ) ≤ c * 2 ^ n →
        δ * 2 ^ (groundSet F).card ≤ (goodSets F).card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1028
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1028](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1028)
- [Er63d] Erdős, Pál, *On combinatorial questions connected with a theorem of Ramsey and van der
  Waerden*. Mat. Lapok (1963), 29-37.
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [ErSp71] Erdős, P. and Spencer, J., *Imbalances in $k$-colorations*. Networks (1971/72),
  379-385.

statements.name: Erdos1028.erdos_1028
statements.doc:
Let
$$H(n)=\min_f \max_{X\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}} \left\lvert \sum_{x<y\in X} f(x,y)\right\rvert,$$
where $f$ ranges over all functions $f:\{1,\ldots,n\}^2\to \{-1,1\}$. Estimate $H(n)$.

Erdős [Er63d] proved
$$\frac{n}{4}\leq H(n) \ll n^{3/2}.$$
Erdős and Spencer [ErSp71] proved that $H(n)\gg n^{3/2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1028 :
    (fun n => (H n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop]
      fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1028.erdos_1028.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er63d] proved
$$\frac{n}{4}\leq H(n) \ll n^{3/2}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1028.variants.lower_bound :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (n : ℝ) / 4 ≤ (H n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1028.erdos_1028.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er63d] proved
$$\frac{n}{4}\leq H(n) \ll n^{3/2}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1028.variants.upper_bound :
    (fun n => (H n : ℝ)) ≪ (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos1028.erdos_1028.variants.erdos_spencer
statements.doc: Erdős and Spencer [ErSp71] proved that $H(n)\gg n^{3/2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1028.variants.erdos_spencer :
    (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ)) ≪ (fun n => (H n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1029
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1029](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1029)
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [ErSz35] Erdős, P. and Szekeres, G., A combinatorial problem in geometry. Compos. Math. (1935),
  463-470.
- [Sp75] Spencer, J., Ramsey's theorem - a new lower bound. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1975),
  108-115.

statements.name: Erdos1029.erdos_1029
statements.doc:
If $R(k)$ is the Ramsey number for $K_k$, the minimal $n$ such that every $2$-colouring of the edges
of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of $K_k$, then
$$\frac{R(k)}{k2^{k/2}}\to \infty.$$

In [Er93] Erdős offers $100 for a proof of this and $1000 for a disproof, but says 'this last offer
is to some extent phoney: I am sure that this is true (but I have been wrong before).'
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1029 :
    Tendsto (fun k : ℕ ↦ (SimpleGraph.diagonalRamsey k : ℝ) /
      ((k : ℝ) * (2 : ℝ) ^ ((k : ℝ) / 2))) atTop atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1030
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1030](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1030)
- [BEFS89] Burr, S. and Erdős, P. and Faudree, R. J. and Schelp, R. H., On the difference between
  consecutive Ramsey numbers. Utilitas Math. (1989), 115-118.

statements.name: Erdos1030.erdos_1030
statements.doc:
Let $R(k,l)$ be the usual Ramsey number: the smallest $n$ such that if the edges of $K_n$ are
coloured red and blue then there exists either a red $K_k$ or a blue $K_l$.

Prove the existence of some $c>0$ such that
$$\lim_{k\to \infty}\frac{R(k+1,k)}{R(k,k)}> 1+c.$$

A problem of Erdős and Sós.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1030 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ L : ℝ,
      Tendsto (fun k : ℕ ↦
        (SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey (k + 1) k : ℝ) /
          (SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey k k : ℝ)) atTop (nhds L) ∧
      L > 1 + c

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1032
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1032](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1032)
- [Er93] Erdős, P., *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*.
  Quaestiones Math. 16 (1993), 333-350.
- [Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference
  "Paul Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).
- [Di52] Dirac, G. A., *A property of $4$-chromatic graphs and some remarks on critical graphs*.
  J. London Math. Soc. 27 (1952), 85-92.
- [Si72] Simonovits, M., *On colour-critical graphs*. Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. 7 (1972), 67-81.
- [To72] Toft, B., *Two theorems on critical $4$-chromatic graphs*. Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. 7
  (1972), 83-89.
- [Ma15] Markström, K. (ed.), *Problem collection from the IML programme: Graphs, Hypergraphs,
  and Computing*. [arXiv:1511.00270](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.00270) (2015). Problem 5.1
  (M. Simonovits).

See also [erdosproblems.com/917](https://www.erdosproblems.com/917) and
[erdosproblems.com/944](https://www.erdosproblems.com/944).

statements.name: Erdos1032.erdos_1032
statements.doc:
We say that a graph is $4$-chromatic critical if it has chromatic number $4$, and removing any edge
decreases the chromatic number to $3$.

Is there, for arbitrarily large $n$, a $4$-chromatic critical graph on $n$ vertices with minimum
degree $\gg n$?

This is a question of Erdős [Er93, p. 341] (see also [Va99, 3.60]). We read $\gg n$ as
$\geq cn$ for a fixed constant $c > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1032 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), IsKCritical G 4 ∧ c * (n : ℝ) ≤ (G.minDegree : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1032.erdos_1032.variants.five
statements.doc:
Is there, for arbitrarily large $n$, a $5$-chromatic critical graph on $n$ vertices with minimum
degree $\gg n$?

This problem is also open for $5$-chromatic critical graphs.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1032.variants.five :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), IsKCritical G 5 ∧ c * (n : ℝ) ≤ (G.minDegree : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1032.erdos_1032.variants.dirac_six
statements.doc:
Dirac gave an example of a $6$-chromatic critical graph with minimum degree $>n/2$.

Dirac's graphs join two disjoint odd cycles of length $n/2$ [Di52], [Ma15]. Here we state that
there are such graphs for infinitely many $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1032.variants.dirac_six :
    ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), IsKCritical G 6 ∧ (n : ℝ) / 2 < (G.minDegree : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1032.erdos_1032.variants.simonovits_toft
statements.doc:
Simonovits [Si72] and Toft [To72] independently constructed $4$-chromatic critical graphs with
minimum degree $\gg n^{1/3}$.

We state this as in [Ma15, Problem 5.1]: there are $4$-critical graphs on $n$ vertices with minimum
degree at least $c n^{1/3}$ for infinitely many $n$, for a fixed constant $c > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1032.variants.simonovits_toft :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
        IsKCritical G 4 ∧ c * (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3) ≤ (G.minDegree : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1033
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1033](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1033)
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*. (1982),
  59--79.
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [ErLa85] Erdős, Paul and Laskar, Renu, *A note on the size of a chordal subgraph*.
  Congr. Numer. (1985), 81--86.
- [Fa88] Fan, Genghua, *Degree sum for a triangle in a graph*. J. Graph Theory (1988), 249--263.

statements.name: Erdos1033.erdos_1033
statements.doc:
Let $h(n)$ be such that every graph on $n$ vertices with $>n^2/4$ many edges contains a triangle
whose vertices have degrees summing to at least $h(n)$. Estimate $h(n)$. In particular, is it
true that
$$h(n)\geq (2(\sqrt{3}-1)-o(1))n?$$

A conjecture of Bollobás and Erdős.

The answer is no. A blow-up of the butterfly graph, posted on the
[Erdős problems forum](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/1033) in June and July 2026 and
written up in [this note](https://woutercvb.github.io/Erdos1033_smalloptimization.pdf), gives
arbitrarily large graphs with more than $n^2/4$ edges in which every triangle has degree sum at
most $1.464n$, which is less than $2(\sqrt{3}-1)n$. Estimating the optimal value of $h(n)$ is
still open.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1033 :
    ¬ ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      n ^ 2 < 4 * #G.edgeFinset →
        ∃ t, G.IsNClique 3 t ∧
          (2 * (Real.sqrt 3 - 1) - ε) * n ≤ ∑ v ∈ t, (G.degree v : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1033.erdos_1033.variants.three_halves
statements.doc:
In [Er82e] it is asked whether $h(n)\geq \frac{3}{2}n$. The answer is no, since the construction
of Erdős and Laskar [ErLa85] gives $h(n) \leq 2(\sqrt{3}-1)n+O(1)$ and
$2(\sqrt{3}-1) < \frac{3}{2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1033.variants.three_halves :
    ¬ ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj], n ^ 2 < 4 * #G.edgeFinset →
      ∃ t, G.IsNClique 3 t ∧ 3 * n ≤ 2 * ∑ v ∈ t, G.degree v

statements.name: Erdos1033.erdos_1033.variants.fan
statements.doc:
Fan [Fa88] proved that $h(n) \geq \frac{21}{16}n$: every graph on $n$ vertices with $>n^2/4$
edges contains a triangle whose degrees sum to at least $\frac{21}{16}n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1033.variants.fan (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hG : n ^ 2 < 4 * #G.edgeFinset) :
    ∃ t, G.IsNClique 3 t ∧ 21 * n ≤ 16 * ∑ v ∈ t, G.degree v

statements.name: Erdos1033.erdos_1033.variants.erdos_laskar
statements.doc:
Erdős and Laskar [ErLa85] gave a construction showing that $h(n) \leq 2(\sqrt{3}-1)n+O(1)$:
for all large $n$ there is a graph on $n$ vertices with $>n^2/4$ edges in which every triangle
has degree sum at most $2(\sqrt{3}-1)n+O(1)$. The construction is made explicit in [Fa88].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1033.variants.erdos_laskar :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), n ^ 2 < 4 * #G.edgeFinset ∧
      ∀ t, G.IsNClique 3 t → ∑ v ∈ t, (G.degree v : ℝ) ≤ 2 * (Real.sqrt 3 - 1) * n + C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1034
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1034](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1034)
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [MaTa25] Ma, Jie and Tang, Quanyu, *On Erdős problem #1034*.
  [staff.ustc.edu.cn/~jiema/Erdos-1034.pdf](http://staff.ustc.edu.cn/~jiema/Erdos-1034.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos1034.erdos_1034
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with $>n^2/4$ many edges. Must there be a triangle $T$ in $G$
and vertices $y_1,\ldots,y_t$, where $t>(\frac{1}{2}-o(1))n$, such that every $y_i$ is joined to
at least two vertices of $T$?

A conjecture of Erdős and Faudree; a stronger version of [905].

This has been solved in the negative by Ma and Tang [MaTa25], who construct a graph with $n$
vertices and $>n^2/4$ edges in which every triangle has at most $(2-(5/2)^{1/2}+o(1))n$ vertices
adjacent to at least two of its vertices (note that $2-(5/2)^{1/2}\approx 0.4189$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1034 :
    ¬ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 4 < (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) →
        ∃ T : Finset (Fin n), G.IsNClique 3 T ∧ ∃ Y : Finset (Fin n),
          JoinedToTwo G T Y ∧ (1 / 2 - ε) * (n : ℝ) < (Y.card : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1034.erdos_1034.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős and Faudree asked about the threshold $h(n)$ such that every graph with $n$ vertices and
$>n^2/4$ edges contained a triangle and $h(n)$ other vertices which are connected to at least two
vertices of the triangle. The fact that every graph with $>n^2/4$ edges contains a book of size
$n/6$ shows that
$$(1/6-o(1))n \leq h(n).$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1034.variants.lower_bound (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 4 < (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) →
        ∃ T : Finset (Fin n), G.IsNClique 3 T ∧ ∃ Y : Finset (Fin n),
          JoinedToTwo G T Y ∧ (1 / 6 - ε) * (n : ℝ) ≤ (Y.card : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1034.erdos_1034.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
The construction of Ma and Tang [MaTa25] of a graph with $n$ vertices and $>n^2/4$ edges in which
every triangle has at most $(2-(5/2)^{1/2}+o(1))n$ vertices adjacent to at least two of its
vertices shows that, for the threshold $h(n)$ of `erdos_1034.variants.lower_bound`,
$$h(n) \leq (2-(5/2)^{1/2}+o(1))n.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1034.variants.upper_bound (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 4 < (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ∧
        ∀ T : Finset (Fin n), G.IsNClique 3 T → ∀ Y : Finset (Fin n),
          JoinedToTwo G T Y → (Y.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 - Real.sqrt (5 / 2) + ε) * (n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1034.erdos_1034.variants.k4_free
statements.doc:
Erdős suggested that the answer is different if $G$ has no $K_4$. In the comments Ma and Tang
sketch a proof that the conjecture remains false even if we assume that $G$ contains no $K_4$,
constructing a graph with $n$ vertices, $>n^2/4$ edges, and no $K_4$, in which every triangle has
at most $(2\sqrt{3}-3+o(1))n$ vertices adjacent to at least two of its vertices (note that
$2\sqrt{3}-3\approx 0.464$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1034.variants.k4_free (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 ∧
      (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 4 < (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ∧
        ∀ T : Finset (Fin n), G.IsNClique 3 T → ∀ Y : Finset (Fin n),
          JoinedToTwo G T Y → (Y.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 * Real.sqrt 3 - 3 + ε) * (n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1035
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1035](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1035)
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.

statements.name: Erdos1035.erdos_1035
statements.doc:
Is there a constant $c > 0$ such that every graph on $2^n$ vertices with minimum degree
$> (1-c) \cdot 2^n$ contains the $n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_n$?

This is Erdős's question [Er93, p. 345].

See also [576] for the extremal number of edges that guarantee a $Q_n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1035 :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 ^ n))) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      (∀ v, (G.degree v : ℝ) > (1 - c) * 2 ^ n) →
        (SimpleGraph.hypercube n).IsContained G

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1036
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1036](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1036)
- [AlHa91] Alon, N. and Hajnal, A., *Ramsey graphs contain many distinct induced subgraphs*.
  Graphs Combin. (1991), 1-6.
- [ErHa89b] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., *On the number of distinct induced subgraphs of a graph*.
  Discrete Math. (1989), 145-154.
- [Sh98] Shelah, Saharon, *Erdős and Rényi conjecture*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1998), 179-185.

statements.name: Erdos1036.erdos_1036
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices which does not contain a trivial (empty or complete) graph on
more than $c\log n$ vertices. Must $G$ contain at least $2^{\Omega_c(n)}$ many induced subgraphs
which are not pairwise isomorphic?

This is true, and was proved by Shelah [Sh98].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1036 :
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      G.IsCRamsey c →
        HasManyNonIsomorphicInducedSubgraphs G ((2 : ℝ) ^ (δ * (n : ℝ)))

statements.name: Erdos1036.erdos_1036.variants.alon_hajnal
statements.doc:
Alon and Hajnal [AlHa91] proved that $G$ must contain at least
$$\exp\left(n(\log n)^{-O(\log\log n)}\right)$$
many non-isomorphic induced subgraphs.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1036.variants.alon_hajnal :
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      G.IsCRamsey c →
        HasManyNonIsomorphicInducedSubgraphs G
          (Real.exp ((n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ) ^ (-(C * Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ))))))

statements.name: Erdos1036.erdos_1036.variants.erdos_hajnal
statements.doc:
Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa89b] proved that if neither $G$ nor its complement contains a balanced
complete bipartite graph $K_{k,k}$ on more than $c\log n$ vertices (as a not necessarily induced
subgraph) then $G$ contains at least $2^{\Omega_c(n)}$ many non-isomorphic induced subgraphs.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1036.variants.erdos_hajnal :
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      NoLargeBiclique G (c * Real.log (n : ℝ)) →
        HasManyNonIsomorphicInducedSubgraphs G ((2 : ℝ) ^ (δ * (n : ℝ)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1037
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1037](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1037)
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.

statements.name: Erdos1037.erdos_1037
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices in which every degree occurs at most twice, and the number of
distinct degrees is $>(\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon)n$. Must $G$ contain a trivial (empty or complete)
subgraph of size 'much larger' than $\log n$?

A question of Chen and Erdős.

The answer is no - Cambie, Chan, and Hunter have in the comment section given a simple
construction of a graph on $n$ vertices with at least $\frac{3}{4}n$ distinct degrees, every
degree appears at most twice, and the largest trivial subgraph has size $O(\log n)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1037 :
    ¬ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (∀ d : ℕ, {v : Fin n | (G.neighborSet v).ncard = d}.ncard ≤ 2) →
      ((1 / 2 + ε) * (n : ℝ) <
        ((Set.range fun v : Fin n => (G.neighborSet v).ncard).ncard : ℝ)) →
      ∃ s : Set (Fin n), G.IsHomogeneous s ∧ (C * Real.log (n : ℝ) < (s.ncard : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos1037.erdos_1037.variants.cambie_chan_hunter
statements.doc:
Cambie, Chan, and Hunter have in the comment section given a simple construction of a graph on
$n$ vertices with at least $\frac{3}{4}n$ distinct degrees, every degree appears at most twice,
and the largest trivial subgraph has size $O(\log n)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1037.variants.cambie_chan_hunter :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (∀ d : ℕ, {v : Fin n | (G.neighborSet v).ncard = d}.ncard ≤ 2) ∧
      (3 / 4 * (n : ℝ) ≤
        ((Set.range fun v : Fin n => (G.neighborSet v).ncard).ncard : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ s : Set (Fin n), G.IsHomogeneous s → ((s.ncard : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.log (n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1038
problems.doc:
*Reference:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/1038](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1038)
 - [Tao25] Tao, Terence. Sublevel Sets of Logarithmic Potentials. Terry Tao’s Blog, Dec. 2025
  (https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/erdos-1038-1.pdf)
 - [EHP58] Erdős, P., Herzog, F., Piranian, G. Metric properties of polynomials.
  J. Analyse Math. 6 (1958), 125--148.

statements.name: Erdos1038.erdos_1038.parts.i
statements.doc:
What is the infimum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all nonconstant monic polynomials `f` such
that all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]`?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1038.parts.i : erdos_1038.parts.i.answer =
    ⨅ f : {f : Polynomial ℝ // f.Monic ∧ f ≠ 1 ∧
    (f.roots.filter fun x => x ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1).card = f.natDegree},
    volume {x | |f.1.eval x| < 1}

statements.name: Erdos1038.erdos_1038.parts.ii
statements.doc:
The supremum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all monic polynomials `f` such that
all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]` is `2 * 2 ^ (1 / 2)`. This is proved in
[Tao25].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1038.parts.ii : 2 * 2 ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) =
    ⨆ f : {f : Polynomial ℝ // f.Monic ∧
    (f.roots.filter fun x => x ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1).card = f.natDegree},
    volume {x | |f.1.eval x| < 1}

statements.name: Erdos1038.erdos_1038.variants.inf_upperBound
statements.doc:
The infimum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all nonconstant monic polynomials `f` such that
all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]` is `< 1.835`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1038.variants.inf_upperBound : ⨅ f : {f : Polynomial ℝ // f.Monic ∧ f ≠ 1 ∧
    (f.roots.filter fun x => x ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1).card = f.natDegree},
    volume {x | |f.1.eval x| < 1} < 1.835

statements.name: Erdos1038.erdos_1038.variants.inf_lowerBound
statements.doc:
The infimum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all nonconstant monic polynomials `f` such that
all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]` is `≥ 2 ^ (4 / 3) - 1`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1038.variants.inf_lowerBound : 2 ^ (4 / 3 : ℝ) - 1 ≤
    ⨅ f : {f : Polynomial ℝ // f.Monic ∧ f ≠ 1 ∧
    (f.roots.filter fun x => x ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1).card = f.natDegree},
    volume {x | |f.1.eval x| < 1}

statements.name: Erdos1038.erdos_1038.variants.quadratic_sublevel_formula
statements.doc:
For a monic quadratic with roots at distance at most two, the sublevel measure
is $2\sqrt{1+d^2}$, where $2|d|$ is the distance between the roots. This gives
the degree-two case of the sublevel-set problem in [Tao25].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1038.variants.quadratic_sublevel_formula (m d : ℝ) (hd : |d| ≤ 1) :
    volume {x : ℝ | |(x - m) ^ 2 - d ^ 2| < 1} =
      ENNReal.ofReal (2 * Real.sqrt (1 + d ^ 2))

statements.name: Erdos1038.erdos_1038.variants.quadratic_upperBound
statements.doc:
The degree-two case of the supremum bound in [Tao25]: if $a,b\in[-1,1]$,
the sublevel set of $(x-a)(x-b)$ has measure at most $2\sqrt{2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1038.variants.quadratic_upperBound (a b : ℝ) (ha : |a| ≤ 1) (hb : |b| ≤ 1) :
    volume {x : ℝ | |(x-a)*(x-b)| < 1} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 * Real.sqrt 2)

statements.name: Erdos1038.erdos_1038.variants.quadratic_extremizer
statements.doc:
The admissible quadratic $x^2-1$, with roots $-1$ and $1$, attains the supremum
value $2\sqrt{2}$ in [Tao25].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1038.variants.quadratic_extremizer :
    volume {x : ℝ | |x ^ 2 - 1| < 1} = ENNReal.ofReal (2 * Real.sqrt 2)

statements.name: Erdos1038.erdos_1038.variants.sup_lowerBound
statements.doc:
The lower half of `erdos_1038.parts.ii`: the supremum is at least $2\sqrt{2}$, because the
admissible polynomial $x^2-1$ has sublevel measure exactly $2\sqrt{2}$. The matching upper bound
is proved in [Tao25].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1038.variants.sup_lowerBound : 2 * 2 ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤
    ⨆ f : {f : Polynomial ℝ // f.Monic ∧
    (f.roots.filter fun x => x ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1).card = f.natDegree},
    volume {x | |f.1.eval x| < 1}

statements.name: Erdos1038.erdos_1038.variants.inf_lt_two
statements.doc:
The infimum in `erdos_1038.parts.i` is strictly less than $2$, as observed in [EHP58]:
for $f(x)=(x+1)(x-1)^3$ the sublevel set $\{x : |f(x)| < 1\}$ is contained in
$(-1.108,-0.835)\cup(0,1.718)$, whose total length is $1.991$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1038.variants.inf_lt_two : ⨅ f : {f : Polynomial ℝ // f.Monic ∧ f ≠ 1 ∧
    (f.roots.filter fun x => x ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1).card = f.natDegree},
    volume {x | |f.1.eval x| < 1} < 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1041
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1041](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1041)

statements.name: Erdos1041.exists_connected_component_contains_two_roots
statements.doc:
**Erdős–Herzog–Piranian Component Lemma** (Metric Properties of Polynomials, 1958):
If $f$ is a monic degree $n$ polynomial with all roots in the unit disk,
then some connected component
of $\{z \mid |f(z)| < 1\}$ contains at least two roots with multiplicity.

See p. 139, above Problem 5:
[EHP58] Erdős, P. and Herzog, F. and Piranian, G., _Metric properties of polynomials_.
  J. Analyse Math. (1958), 125-148.
statements.statement:
theorem exists_connected_component_contains_two_roots :
    ∃ C, C ⊆ {z | ‖f.eval z‖ < 1} ∧ IsConnected C ∧
      2 ≤ (f.roots.filter (· ∈ C)).card

statements.name: Erdos1041.erdos_1041
statements.doc:
Let
$$ f(z) = \prod_{i=1}^{n} (z - z_i) \in \mathbb{C}[x] $$
with $|z_i| < 1$ for all $i$.

Conjecture: Must there always exist a path of length less than 2 in
$$ \{ z \in \mathbb{C} \mid |f(z)| < 1 \} $$
which connects two of the roots of $f$?

The answer is negative. ani gave a counterexample of degree seven on the
[Erdős problems forum](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/1041) on 7 September 2026.
The linked formalisation proves, for the member $s = 10^{-6}$ of ani's family, that every
connected subset of $\{ z \mid |f(z)| < 1 \}$ containing two distinct roots has
one-dimensional Hausdorff measure greater than $2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1041 :
    ¬ ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : ℂ[X]), n ≥ 2 → f.natDegree = n → f.Monic →
      f.rootSet ℂ ⊆ Metric.ball 0 1 →
      ∃ (z₁ z₂ : ℂ) (h : ({z₁, z₂} : Multiset ℂ) ≤ f.roots) (γ : Path z₁ z₂),
        Set.range γ ⊆ { z : ℂ | ‖f.eval z‖ < 1 } ∧ length (Set.range γ) < 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1043
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1043](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1043)
- [EHP58] Erdős, P. and Herzog, F. and Piranian, G., Metric properties of polynomials. J.
  Analyse Math. (1958), 125-148.
- [Po59] Pommerenke, Ch., On some problems by Erdős, Herzog and Piranian. Michigan Math. J.
  (1959), 221-225.
- [Po61] Pommerenke, Ch., On metric properties of complex polynomials. Michigan Math. J. (1961),
  97-115.

statements.name: Erdos1043.erdos_1043
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 1043**:
Let $f\in \mathbb{C}[x]$ be a monic polynomial.
Must there exist a straight line $\ell$ such that the projection of
$$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert\leq 1\}$$
onto $\ell$ has measure at most $2$?

Pommerenke [Po61] proved that the answer is no.

The projection onto the line $\ell = \mathbb{R} u$ is measured with the Lebesgue measure of that
line, so `volume` of the projected set is its length.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1043 :
    ¬ ∀ (f : ℂ[X]), f.Monic → f.degree ≥ 1 →
      ∃ (u : ℂ), ‖u‖ = 1 ∧
      volume ((ℝ ∙ u).orthogonalProjectionOnto '' levelSet f) ≤ 2

statements.name: Erdos1043.erdos_1043.variants.weak
statements.doc:
On the other hand, Pommerenke also proved there always exists a line such that the projection has
measure at most 3.3.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1043.variants.weak :
    ∀ (f : ℂ[X]), f.Monic → f.degree ≥ 1 →
      ∃ (u : ℂ), ‖u‖ = 1 ∧
      volume ((ℝ ∙ u).orthogonalProjectionOnto '' levelSet f) ≤ 3.3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1044
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1044](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1044)
- [EHP58] Erdős, P. and Herzog, F. and Piranian, G., *Metric properties of polynomials*.
  J. Analyse Math. (1958), 125-148.
- [Ta26] Tang, Quanyu, *On Erdős Problem 1044* (2026),
  [github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-1044](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-1044).

statements.name: Erdos1044.erdos_1044
statements.doc:
Let $f(z)=\prod_{i=1}^n(z-z_i)\in\mathbb{C}[x]$ where $\lvert z_i\rvert\leq 1$ for all $i$.
If $\Lambda(f)$ is the maximum of the lengths of the boundaries of the connected components of
$$
\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert<1\}
$$
then determine the infimum of $\Lambda(f)$.

A problem of Erdős, Herzog, and Piranian [EHP58].
