This has been resolved by Tang, who proved that the infimum of $\Lambda(f)$ over all such $f$
is $2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1044 :
    IsGLB {L : ℝ≥0∞ | ∃ f : ℂ[X], IsAdmissible f ∧ maxBoundaryLength f = L} erdos_1044.answer

statements.name: Erdos1044.erdos_1044.variants.infimum_eq_two
statements.doc:
This has been resolved by Tang, who proved that the infimum of $\Lambda(f)$ over all such $f$
is $2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1044.variants.infimum_eq_two :
    IsGLB {L : ℝ≥0∞ | ∃ f : ℂ[X], IsAdmissible f ∧ maxBoundaryLength f = L} 2

statements.name: Erdos1044.erdos_1044.variants.fixed_degree
statements.doc:
Tang also suggests that, if the degree $n$ is fixed, then the infimum over all such $f$ of
degree $n$ is attained by $f_n(z)=z^n-1$.

statements.name: Erdos1044.erdos_1044.variants.fixed_degree_of_le_two
statements.doc:
Tang also suggests that, if the degree $n$ is fixed, then the infimum over all such $f$ of
degree $n$ is attained by $f_n(z)=z^n-1$ (and proves this for $n=1$ and $n=2$).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1046
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1046](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1046)
- [EHP58] Erdős, P. and Herzog, F. and Piranian, G., *Metric properties of polynomials*. J.
  Analyse Math. (1958), 125-148.
- [Po59] Pommerenke, Ch., *On some problems by Erdős, Herzog and Piranian*. Michigan Math. J.
  (1959), 221-225.
- [BPS02] Barnard, Roger W. and Pearce, Kent and Solynin, Alexander Yu., *An isoperimetric
  inequality for logarithmic capacity*. Ann. Acad. Sci. Fenn. Math. (2002), 419-436.
- [Po28] Pólya, G., *Beitrag zur Verallgemeinerung des Verzerrungssatzes auf mehrfach
  zusammenhängende Gebiete*. S.-B. Preuss. Akad. Wiss. (1928), 280-282.
- [Ra95] Ransford, Thomas, *Potential theory in the complex plane*. London Mathematical Society
  Student Texts 28, Cambridge University Press (1995).

statements.name: Erdos1046.erdos_1046
statements.doc:
Let $f\in \mathbb{C}[x]$ be a monic polynomial and
$$E=\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert <1\}.$$
If $E$ is connected then is $E$ contained in a disc of radius $2$?

A problem of Erdős, Herzog, and Piranian [EHP58], who also ask, if
$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert\leq 1\}$ is connected, then what are the least possible diameter and
greatest possible width of this set, and conjecture the answer is $2$ in both cases. Their guess
that the width is always at most $2$ is false, as Pommerenke [Po59] gave an example with width
$>\sqrt{3}2^{1/3}\approx 2.18$.

The condition that $E$ is connected is equivalent to $E$ containing all zeros of $f'$.

The answer is yes, and in fact the centre of this disc can be taken to be
$\frac{z_1+\cdots+z_n}{n}$, where the $z_i$ are the roots of $f$, as shown by Pommerenke [Po59].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1046 : ∀ f : ℂ[X], f.Monic → IsConnected (lemniscate f) →
    ∃ c : ℂ, lemniscate f ⊆ ball c 2

statements.name: Erdos1046.erdos_1046.variants.centroid
statements.doc:
Pommerenke [Po59] showed that the centre of the disc can be taken to be the centroid
$\frac{z_1+\cdots+z_n}{n}$ of the roots $z_i$ of $f$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1046.variants.centroid : ∀ f : ℂ[X], f.Monic → IsConnected (lemniscate f) →
    lemniscate f ⊆ ball (f.roots.sum / f.natDegree) 2

statements.name: Erdos1046.erdos_1046.variants.diameter
statements.doc:
Erdős, Herzog, and Piranian [EHP58] conjecture that if $\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert\leq 1\}$ is
connected then its diameter is at least $2$.

The answer is yes, and connectedness is not needed. For monic $f$ of degree $n \geq 1$ the set
$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert\leq 1\}$ has logarithmic capacity $1$ [Ra95, Theorem 5.2.5], and Pólya
[Po28] proved $\mathrm{cap}(E) \leq \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{diam}(E)$ for every compact
$E \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, see [BPS02, (1.2)]. Hence the diameter is at least $2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1046.variants.diameter : ∀ f : ℂ[X], f.Monic →
    IsConnected (closedLemniscate f) → 2 ≤ Metric.ediam (closedLemniscate f)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1047
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1047](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1047)
- [EHP58] Erdős, P. and Herzog, F. and Piranian, G., *Metric properties of polynomials*.
  J. Analyse Math. (1958), 125-148.
- [Go66] Goodman, A. W., *On the convexity of the level curves of a polynomial*.
  Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1966), 358-361.
- [Po61] Pommerenke, Ch., *On metric properties of complex polynomials*. Michigan Math. J.
  (1961), 97-115.

statements.name: Erdos1047.erdos_1047
statements.doc:
Let $f\in \mathbb{C}[x]$ be a monic polynomial with $m$ distinct roots, and let $c>0$ be a
constant small enough such that $\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert\leq c\}$ has $m$ distinct connected
components.

Must all these components be convex?

A question of Grunsky, which was reported by Erdős, Herzog, and Piranian [EHP58].

The answer is no, as shown by Pommerenke [Po61], who showed that, if $k$ is sufficiently large,
and $f(z)=z^k(z-a)$ where $a$ is sufficiently close to $(1+\frac{1}{k})k^{\frac{1}{k+1}}$, then
$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert\leq 1\}$ has two components, and the component which contains $0$ is
not convex.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1047 :
    ¬ ∀ (f : ℂ[X]) (m : ℕ) (c : ℝ), f.Monic → (f.rootSet ℂ).ncard = m → 0 < c →
      (componentsIn (sublevelSet f c)).ncard = m →
        ∀ t ∈ componentsIn (sublevelSet f c), Convex ℝ t

statements.name: Erdos1047.erdos_1047.variants.pommerenke
statements.doc:
The answer is no, as shown by Pommerenke [Po61], who showed that, if $k$ is sufficiently large,
and $f(z)=z^k(z-a)$ where $a$ is sufficiently close to $(1+\frac{1}{k})k^{\frac{1}{k+1}}$, then
$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert\leq 1\}$ has two components, and the component which contains $0$ is
not convex.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1047.variants.pommerenke :
    ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in Filter.atTop, ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ a : ℝ,
      (1 + 1 / (k : ℝ)) * (k : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) < a →
        a < (1 + 1 / (k : ℝ)) * (k : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) + δ →
          (componentsIn (sublevelSet (X ^ k * (X - C (a : ℂ))) 1)).ncard = 2 ∧
          ¬ Convex ℝ (connectedComponentIn (sublevelSet (X ^ k * (X - C (a : ℂ))) 1) 0)

statements.name: Erdos1047.erdos_1047.variants.goodman
statements.doc:
Goodman [Go66] proved that one of the three components of
$$\{ z: \lvert (z^2+1)(z-2)^2\rvert < 5^{3/2}/4\}$$
is not convex.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1047.variants.goodman :
    (componentsIn (strictSublevelSet ((X ^ 2 + 1) * (X - C 2) ^ 2)
        ((5 : ℝ) ^ ((3 : ℝ) / 2) / 4))).ncard = 3 ∧
      ∃ t ∈ componentsIn (strictSublevelSet ((X ^ 2 + 1) * (X - C 2) ^ 2)
        ((5 : ℝ) ^ ((3 : ℝ) / 2) / 4)), ¬ Convex ℝ t

statements.name: Erdos1047.erdos_1047.variants.goodman_simple_roots
statements.doc: Goodman [Go66] constructed an example with simple roots, of degree $4$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1047.variants.goodman_simple_roots :
    ∃ (f : ℂ[X]) (c : ℝ), f.Monic ∧ f.natDegree = 4 ∧ (f.rootSet ℂ).ncard = 4 ∧ 0 < c ∧
      (componentsIn (sublevelSet f c)).ncard = 4 ∧
      ∃ t ∈ componentsIn (sublevelSet f c), ¬ Convex ℝ t

statements.name: Erdos1047.erdos_1047.variants.referee
statements.doc: The referee of the paper [Go66] also gave the example of $\lvert z(z^5-1)\rvert< 5\cdot 6^{-6/5}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1047.variants.referee :
    (componentsIn (strictSublevelSet (X * (X ^ 5 - 1))
        (5 * (6 : ℝ) ^ (-(6 : ℝ) / 5)))).ncard = 6 ∧
      ∃ t ∈ componentsIn (strictSublevelSet (X * (X ^ 5 - 1))
        (5 * (6 : ℝ) ^ (-(6 : ℝ) / 5))), ¬ Convex ℝ t

statements.name: Erdos1047.erdos_1047.variants.max_non_convex_components
statements.doc:
Goodman raises the question of the maximum number of non-convex components of
$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert < c\}$ that are possible as a function of the degree of $f$, where
$f$ ranges over all monic polynomials of degree $n$ and $c$ over all positive constants.

The maximum is $0$ for $n \le 1$, $1$ for $n = 2$, $2$ for $n = 3$, and $n$ for $n \ge 4$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1047.variants.max_non_convex_components (n : ℕ) :
    IsGreatest {k : ℕ | ∃ (f : ℂ[X]) (c : ℝ), f.Monic ∧ f.natDegree = n ∧ 0 < c ∧
      {t ∈ componentsIn (strictSublevelSet f c) | ¬ Convex ℝ t}.ncard = k}
      (erdos_1047.variants.max_non_convex_components.answer n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1048
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1048](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1048)
- [EHP58] Erdős, P. and Herzog, F. and Piranian, G., *Metric properties of polynomials*.
  J. Analyse Math. (1958), 125-148.
- [Po61] Pommerenke, Ch., *On metric properties of complex polynomials*. Michigan Math. J.
  (1961), 97-115.

statements.name: Erdos1048.erdos_1048
statements.doc:
If $f\in \mathbb{C}[x]$ is a monic polynomial with all roots satisfying
$\lvert z\rvert \leq r$ for some $0 < r < 2$, then must
$$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert <1\}$$
have a connected component with diameter $>2-r$?

A problem of Erdős, Herzog, and Piranian [EHP58].

Pommerenke [Po61] proved the answer is no for $r>1$, showing that if $f(z)=z^n-r^n$ then
$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert \leq 1\}$ has $n$ connected components, all with diameter
$\to 0$ as $n\to \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1048 :
    ¬ ∀ (r : ℝ) (f : ℂ[X]), 0 < r → r < 2 → f.Monic → f.degree ≥ 1 → (∀ z ∈ f.roots, ‖z‖ ≤ r) →
      ∃ z ∈ openLevelSet f, ENNReal.ofReal (2 - r) <
        Metric.ediam (connectedComponentIn (openLevelSet f) z)

statements.name: Erdos1048.erdos_1048.variants.pommerenke_ncard_components
statements.doc:
Pommerenke [Po61] proved the answer is no for $r>1$, showing that if $f(z)=z^n-r^n$ then
$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert \leq 1\}$ has $n$ connected components, all with diameter
$\to 0$ as $n\to \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1048.variants.pommerenke_ncard_components (r : ℝ) (hr : 1 < r) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (f : ℂ[X]) (hf : f = (X : ℂ[X]) ^ n - C ((r : ℂ) ^ n)) :
    {C : Set ℂ | ∃ z ∈ levelSet f, C = connectedComponentIn (levelSet f) z}.ncard = n

statements.name: Erdos1048.erdos_1048.variants.pommerenke_diam_tendsto_zero
statements.doc:
Pommerenke [Po61] proved the answer is no for $r>1$, showing that if $f(z)=z^n-r^n$ then
$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert \leq 1\}$ has $n$ connected components, all with diameter
$\to 0$ as $n\to \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1048.variants.pommerenke_diam_tendsto_zero (r : ℝ) (hr : 1 < r) (ε : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop, ∀ f : ℂ[X], f = (X : ℂ[X]) ^ n - C ((r : ℂ) ^ n) →
      ∀ z ∈ levelSet f,
        Metric.ediam (connectedComponentIn (levelSet f) z) < ENNReal.ofReal ε

statements.name: Erdos1048.erdos_1048.variants.r_le_one
statements.doc: On the other hand, if $0<r\leq 1$, then the answer is yes, as also shown by Pommerenke [Po61].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1048.variants.r_le_one (r : ℝ) (hr₀ : 0 < r) (hr₁ : r ≤ 1) (f : ℂ[X])
    (hmonic : f.Monic) (hdeg : f.degree ≥ 1) (hroots : ∀ z ∈ f.roots, ‖z‖ ≤ r) :
    ∃ z ∈ openLevelSet f, ENNReal.ofReal (2 - r) <
      Metric.ediam (connectedComponentIn (openLevelSet f) z)

statements.name: Erdos1048.erdos_1048.variants.diam_ge_two
statements.doc:
If $0\leq r\leq 1/2$ then the component which contains $0$ must have diameter $\geq 2$, which
$f(z)=z^n$ shows is best possible.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1048.variants.diam_ge_two (r : ℝ) (hr₀ : 0 ≤ r) (hr₁ : r ≤ 1 / 2) (f : ℂ[X])
    (hmonic : f.Monic) (hdeg : f.degree ≥ 1) (hroots : ∀ z ∈ f.roots, ‖z‖ ≤ r) :
    2 ≤ Metric.ediam (connectedComponentIn (levelSet f) 0)

statements.name: Erdos1048.erdos_1048.variants.diam_ge_two_is_best
statements.doc:
If $0\leq r\leq 1/2$ then the component which contains $0$ must have diameter $\geq 2$, which
$f(z)=z^n$ shows is best possible.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1048.variants.diam_ge_two_is_best (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    Metric.ediam (connectedComponentIn (levelSet ((X : ℂ[X]) ^ n)) 0) = 2

statements.name: Erdos1048.erdos_1048.variants.diam_gt_inv_r
statements.doc:
If $1/2<r\leq \frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}$ then the component which contains $0$ must have
diameter $>1/r$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1048.variants.diam_gt_inv_r (r : ℝ) (hr₀ : 1 / 2 < r)
    (hr₁ : r ≤ (Real.sqrt 5 - 1) / 2) (f : ℂ[X]) (hmonic : f.Monic) (hdeg : f.degree ≥ 1)
    (hroots : ∀ z ∈ f.roots, ‖z‖ ≤ r) :
    ENNReal.ofReal (1 / r) < Metric.ediam (connectedComponentIn (levelSet f) 0)

statements.name: Erdos1048.erdos_1048.variants.diam_gt_two_sub_sq
statements.doc:
If $\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}\leq r\leq 1$ then the component which contains $0$ must have
diameter $>2-r^2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1048.variants.diam_gt_two_sub_sq (r : ℝ) (hr₀ : (Real.sqrt 5 - 1) / 2 ≤ r)
    (hr₁ : r ≤ 1) (f : ℂ[X]) (hmonic : f.Monic) (hdeg : f.degree ≥ 1)
    (hroots : ∀ z ∈ f.roots, ‖z‖ ≤ r) :
    ENNReal.ofReal (2 - r ^ 2) < Metric.ediam (connectedComponentIn (levelSet f) 0)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1049
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1049](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1049)
- [Er48] Erdős, P., On arithmetical properties of Lambert series. J. Indian Math. Soc. (N.S.)
  (1948), 63-66.

statements.name: Erdos1049.erdos_1049
statements.doc:
Let $t>1$ be a rational number. Is
$\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{1}{t^n-1}=\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\tau(n)}{t^n}$ irrational, where
$\tau(n)$ counts the divisors of $n$?

A conjecture of Chowla.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1049 :
    ∀ t : ℚ, t > 1 → Irrational (∑' n : ℕ+, 1 / ((t : ℝ) ^ (n : ℕ) - 1))

statements.name: Erdos1049.erdos_1049.variants.geq_2_integer
statements.doc: Erdős [Er48] proved that this is true if $t\geq 2$ is an integer.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1049.variants.geq_2_integer :
     ∀ t : ℤ, t ≥ 2 → Irrational (∑' n : ℕ+, 1 / ((t : ℝ) ^ (n : ℕ) - 1))

statements.name: Erdos1049.lambert_series_eq_num_divisor_sum
statements.doc:
The classical Lambert series identity: $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{t^n - 1} =
\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\tau(n)}{t^n}$, where $\tau(n)$ counts the divisors of $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem lambert_series_eq_num_divisor_sum : ∀ t : ℚ,
     ∑' n : ℕ+, 1 / ((t : ℝ) ^ (n : ℕ) - 1) =
     ∑' n : ℕ+, (n : ℕ).divisors.card / ((t : ℝ) ^ (n : ℕ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1050
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1050](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1050)
- [Bo91] Borwein, Peter B., On the irrationality of {$\sum(1/(q^n+r))$}. J. Number Theory (1991), 253--259.
- [Bo92] Borwein, Peter B., On the irrationality of certain series. Math. Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc. (1992), 141--146.
- [Er48] Erdős, P., On arithmetical properties of Lambert series. J. Indian Math. Soc. (N.S.) (1948), 63-66.
- [Er88c] Erdős, P., On the irrationality of certain series: problems and results. New advances in transcendence theory (Durham, 1986) (1988), 102-109.

Is $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{2^n - 3}$ irrational?

The answer is **yes**, proved by P. B. Borwein [Bo91] (with a cleaner self-contained proof in [Bo92]),
specialized to $q = 2$, $r = -3$.

A formal Lean proof is given in an external repository,
[`gotrevor/lean-gallery`](https://github.com/gotrevor/lean-gallery), formalized by Trevor Morris with
Claude Code and Harmonic's Aristotle.

statements.name: Erdos1050.erdos_1050
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 1050.** The series $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{2^n - 3}$ is irrational.

The source sum runs over $n \ge 1$; as a `tsum` over `ℕ` (which starts at $0$) it is reindexed
$n \mapsto n + 1$, i.e. $\sum_{n=0}^\infty 1/(2^{n+1} - 3)$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1050 : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (1 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ (n + 1) - 3))

statements.name: Erdos1050.erdos_1050.variants.two_pow_sub_one
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 1050, variant [Er48].** Erdős proved that the related series
$\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{2^n - 1}$ (which equals the Lambert series $\sum_n \frac{\tau(n)}{2^n}$,
where $\tau$ is the divisor function) is irrational. This is the $q = 2$, $r = -1$ case of Borwein's
general theorem `Erdos1050.erdos_1050.variants.borwein` below.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1050.variants.two_pow_sub_one :
    Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (1 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ (n + 1) - 1))

statements.name: Erdos1050.erdos_1050.variants.borwein
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 1050, variant [Bo91].** Borwein's general theorem: for every integer $q \ge 2$
and rational $r \ne 0$ with $r \ne -q^n$ for all $n \ge 1$, the series $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{q^n + r}$
is irrational. Problem 1050 is the case $q = 2$, $r = -3$; the [Er48] variant is $q = 2$, $r = -1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1050.variants.borwein (q : ℤ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (r : ℚ) (hr : r ≠ 0)
    (hne : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → r ≠ -((q : ℚ) ^ n)) :
    Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (1 : ℝ) / ((q : ℝ) ^ (n + 1) + (r : ℝ)))

statements.name: Erdos1050.erdos_1050.variants.transcendental
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 1050, variant [Er88c] (open).** Erdős conjectured that
$\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{2^n + t}$ is *transcendental* for every integer $t \ne 0$ — strictly
stronger than the irrationality established by Borwein [Bo91]. This remains open.

Two exclusions make the series well-posed and the claim non-vacuous, exactly as in Borwein's theorem:
$t \ne -2^n$ for all $n \ge 1$ (so no denominator vanishes), and $t \ne 0$ (at $t = 0$ the series is
the rational $\sum_{n \ge 1} 2^{-n} = 1$, hence not transcendental).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1050.variants.transcendental :
    ∀ t : ℤ, t ≠ 0 → (∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → t ≠ -(2 : ℤ) ^ n) →
      Transcendental ℚ (∑' n : ℕ, (1 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ (n + 1) + (t : ℝ)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1051
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1051](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1051)
- [BKKKZ26] K. Barreto, J. Kang, S.-H. Kim, V. Kovač, and S. Zhang, Irrationality of rapidly
  converging series: a problem of Erdős and Graham. arXiv:2601.21442 (2026).
- [Er88c] Erdős, P., On the irrationality of certain series: problems and results. New advances in
  transcendence theory (Durham, 1986) (1988), 102-109.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Fe26] T. Feng et al, Semi-Autonomous Mathematics Discovery with Gemini: A Case Study on the Erdős
  Problems. arXiv:2601.22401 (2026).

statements.name: Erdos1051.erdos_1051
statements.doc:
Is it true that if $a_0 < a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ is a strictly increasing sequence
of integers with $\liminf a_n^{1/2^n} > 1$, then the series
$\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{1}{a_n \cdot a_{n+1}}$ is irrational?

This was solved in the affirmative by Aletheia [Fe26]. This was extended by Barreto, Kang, Kim,
Kovač, and Zhang [BKKKZ26], who essentially give a complete answer: if $\phi=\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}$
is the golden ratio and $1\leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ is a monotonically increasing sequence of
integers such that $\limsup a_n^{1/\phi^{n}}=\infty$ then $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{a_na_{n+1}}$
is irrational. Conversely, for any $1 < C < \infty$ there exists a sequence of integers
$1\leq a_1<\cdots$ such that $\lim a_n^{1/\phi^{n}}=C$ where this infinite sum is a rational number.

(Further, more general, results are available in [BKKKZ26].)

This was formalized in Lean by Baretto.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1051 :
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℤ), StrictMono a → GrowthCondition a →
      Irrational (ErdosSeries a)

statements.name: Erdos1051.erdos_1051.variants.rapid_growth
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er88c] notes that if the sequence grows rapidly to infinity (specifically, if
$a_{n+1} \geq C \cdot a_n^2$ for some constant $C > 0$), then the series is irrational.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1051.variants.rapid_growth (a : ℕ → ℤ) (h_mono : StrictMono a)
    (h_rapid : ∃ C > 0, ∀ n, (a (n + 1) : ℝ) ≥ C * (a n : ℝ) ^ 2) :
    Irrational (ErdosSeries a)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1052
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1052](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1052)

statements.name: Erdos1052.erdos_1052
statements.doc: Are there only finitely many unitary perfect numbers?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1052 :
    {n | IsUnitaryPerfect n}.Finite

statements.name: Erdos1052.even_of_isUnitaryPerfect
statements.doc:
All unitary perfect numbers are even.

Formal proof linked here provided by AlphaProof.
statements.statement: theorem even_of_isUnitaryPerfect (n : ℕ) (hn : IsUnitaryPerfect n) : Even n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1053
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1053](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1053)
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. Springer-Verlag, New York (2004).

statements.name: Erdos1053.erdos_1053
statements.doc:
Call a number $k$-perfect if $\sigma(n)=kn$, where $\sigma(n)$ is the sum of the divisors
of $n$. Must $k=o(\log\log n)$?

A question of Erdős, as reported in problem B2 of Guy's collection [Gu04].
The little-$o$ relation is taken as $n \to \infty$ within the positive integers for which
$\sigma(n) = kn$ for some $k$; on this set, $\sigma(n)/n$ is precisely that multiplier $k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1053 :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (σ 1 n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)) =o[atTop ⊓ 𝓟 {n : ℕ | ∃ k, Nat.IsPerfectFor n 1 k}]
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)))

statements.name: Erdos1053.erdos_1053.variants.guy
statements.doc:
Guy further writes 'It has even been suggested that there may be only finitely many $k$-perfect
numbers with $k\geq 3$.'
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1053.variants.guy :
    ∀ k ≥ 3, {n : ℕ | Nat.IsPerfectFor n 1 k}.Finite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1054
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1054](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1054)
- [PALOMAR-2026-10-05-000005](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-05-000005&version=1)

statements.name: Erdos1054.erdos_1054.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be the minimal integer $m$ such that $n$ is the sum of the $k$ smallest divisors
of $m$ for some $k\geq 1$. Is it true that $f(n)=o(n)$?

The strong claim that $f(n)=o(n)$ was disproved by Tao in the comments to
[468](https://www.erdosproblems.com/468), in which he proves that the upper density of
$\{ n : f(n)\leq \delta n\}$ is $\ll \delta^2$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1054.parts.i : ¬ (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos1054.erdos_1054.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be the minimal integer $m$ such that $n$ is the sum of the $k$ smallest divisors
of $m$ for some $k\geq 1$. Is it true that $f(n)=o(n)$ for almost all $n$?

No: combining the Tao–Kovač small-ratio bound $\#\{n \leq X : 0 < f(n) \leq \delta n\} \ll \delta^2 X$
with the fact that almost all odd integers are represented (or via the lower-density bound below),
$f(n)$ is not $o(n)$ along any density-one set $A$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1054.parts.ii : ¬ ∃ (A : Set ℕ), A.HasDensity 1 ∧
    (fun (n : A) ↦ (f ↑n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos1054.erdos_1054.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be the minimal integer $m$ such that $n$ is the sum of the $k$ smallest divisors
of $m$ for some $k\geq 1$. Is it true that $\limsup f(n)/n=\infty$?

Yes: for every $A \geq 1$, a positive lower density of odd integers satisfy $f(n) > A n$, so
$\limsup f(n)/n = \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1054.parts.iii : ∃ (A : Set ℕ), A.HasDensity 1 ∧
    atTop.limsup (fun n ↦ (f n : EReal) / n) = ⊤

statements.name: Erdos1054.f_undefined_at_2
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be the minimal integer $m$ such that $n$ is the sum of the $k$ smallest divisors
of $m$ for some $k\geq 1$. Show that $f$ is undefined at $n=2$, i.e. we get the junk value $0$.
statements.statement: theorem f_undefined_at_2 : f 2 = 0

statements.name: Erdos1054.f_undefined_at_3
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be the minimal integer $m$ such that $n$ is the sum of the $k$ smallest divisors
of $m$ for some $k\geq 1$. Show that $f$ is undefined at $n=5$, i.e. we get the junk value $0$.
statements.statement: theorem f_undefined_at_3 : f 5 = 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1055
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1055](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1055)

statements.name: Erdos1055.exists_p
statements.doc:
A prime $p$ is in class $1$ if the only prime divisors of $p+1$ are
$2$ or $3$. In general, a prime $p$ is in class $r$ if every prime factor
of $p+1$ is in some class $\leq r-1$, with equality for at least one prime factor.
Show that for each $r$ there exists a prime $p$ of class $r$.
statements.statement: theorem exists_p (r : ℕ+) : ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ IsOfClass r p

statements.name: Erdos1055.erdos_1055
statements.doc:
A prime $p$ is in class $1$ if the only prime divisors of $p+1$ are
$2$ or $3$. In general, a prime $p$ is in class $r$ if every prime factor
of $p+1$ is in some class $\leq r-1$, with equality for at least one prime factor.
Are there infinitely many primes in each class?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1055 (r) : {p | p.Prime ∧ IsOfClass r p}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos1055.erdos_1055.variants.erdos_limit
statements.doc:
A prime $p$ is in class $1$ if the only prime divisors of $p+1$ are
$2$ or $3$. In general, a prime $p$ is in class $r$ if every prime factor
of $p+1$ is in some class $\leq r-1$, with equality for at least one prime factor.
If $p_r$ is the least prime in class $r$, then how does $p_r^{1/r}$ behave?
Erdos conjectured that this tends to infinity.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1055.variants.erdos_limit :
    Filter.atTop.Tendsto (fun r ↦ (p r : ℝ) ^ (1 / r : ℝ)) Filter.atTop

statements.name: Erdos1055.erdos_1055.variants.selfridge_limit
statements.doc:
A prime $p$ is in class $1$ if the only prime divisors of $p+1$ are
$2$ or $3$. In general, a prime $p$ is in class $r$ if every prime factor
of $p+1$ is in some class $\leq r-1$, with equality for at least one prime factor.
If $p_r$ is the least prime in class $r$, then how does $p_r^{1/r}$ behave?
Selfridge conjectured that this is bounded.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1055.variants.selfridge_limit :
    ∃ M, ∀ r, (p r : ℝ) ^ (1 / r : ℝ) ≤ M

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1056
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1056](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1056)

statements.name: Erdos1056.erdos_1056
statements.doc:
Let $k ≥ 2$. Does there exist a prime $p$ and consecutive intervals $I_0,\dots,I_k$
such that $\prod\limits_{n{\in}I_i}n \equiv 1 \mod n$ for all $1 \le i \le k$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1056 :
    ∀ k ≥ 2, ∃ (p : ℕ) (_ : p.Prime) (boundaries : Fin (k + 1) → ℕ) (_ : StrictMono boundaries),
    AllModProdEqualsOne p boundaries

statements.name: Erdos1056.erdos_1056.variants.k2
statements.doc:
This is problem A15 in Guy's collection [Gu04], where he reports that in a letter in 1979
Erdős observed that $3 * 4 \equiv 5 * 6 * 7 \equiv 1 \mod 11$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1056.variants.k2 :
    AllModProdEqualsOne 11 ![3, 5, 8]

statements.name: Erdos1056.erdos_1056.variants.k3
statements.doc:
Makowski [Ma83] found, for $k=3$:
$2 * 3 * 4 * 5 \equiv 6 * 7 * 8 * 9 * 10 * 11 \equiv 12 * 13 * 14 * 15 \equiv 1 \mod 17$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1056.variants.k3 :
    AllModProdEqualsOne 17 ![2, 6, 12, 16]

statements.name: Erdos1056.erdos_1056.variants.noll_simmons
statements.doc:
Noll and Simmons asked, more generally, whether there are solutions to
$q_1! \equiv \dots \equiv q_k! \mod p$ for arbitrarily large $k$ (with $q_1 < \dots < q_k$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1056.variants.noll_simmons :
    ∀ᶠ k in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (_ : p.Prime) (Q : Fin k → ℕ) (_ : StrictMono Q) (_ : ∀ i, Q i < p),
    ∀ i j : Fin k, (Q i)! ≡ (Q j)! [MOD p]

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1057
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1057](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1057)
- [AGP94] Alford, W. R. and Granville, Andrew and Pomerance, Carl, There are infinitely many
  Carmichael numbers. Ann. of Math. (2) (1994), 703--722.
- [Er56c] Erdős, P., On pseudoprimes and Carmichael numbers. Publ. Math. Debrecen (1956),
  201--206.
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
- [Ha08] Harman, Glyn, Watt's mean value theorem and Carmichael numbers. Int. J. Number Theory
  (2008), 241--248.
- [Li22] J. D. Lichtman, Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli and shifted primes
  without large prime factors. arXiv:2211.09641 (2022).
- [Po89] Pomerance, Carl, Two methods in elementary analytic number theory. (1989), 135--161.

statements.name: Erdos1057.erdos_1057
statements.doc:
Is it true that $C(x)=x^{1-o(1)}$?

This is discussed in problem A13 of Guy's collection [Gu04].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1057 :
    Tendsto (fun x ↦ Real.log (carmichaelCounting x) / Real.log x) atTop (𝓝 1)

statements.name: Erdos1057.erdos_1057.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er56c] proved $C(x) < x \exp\left(-c \frac{\log x\log\log\log x}{\log\log x}\right)$
for some constant $c>0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1057.variants.upper_bound :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ x in atTop,
      carmichaelCounting x < x * Real.exp (-c * (Real.log x * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log x))) /
        Real.log (Real.log x))

statements.name: Erdos1057.erdos_1057.variants.pomerance
statements.doc:
Pomerance [Po89] gave a heuristic suggesting that this is the true order of growth, and in fact
$C(x)= x \exp\left(-(1+o(1))\frac{\log x\log\log\log x}{\log\log x}\right)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1057.variants.pomerance :
    Tendsto (fun x ↦
      -(Real.log (carmichaelCounting x / x) * Real.log (Real.log x)) /
      (Real.log x * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log x)))) atTop (𝓝 1)

statements.name: Erdos1057.erdos_1057.variants.agp_infinite
statements.doc: Alford, Granville, and Pomerance [AGP94] proved that $C(x)\to \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1057.variants.agp_infinite :
    Tendsto carmichaelCounting atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos1057.erdos_1057.variants.agp_lower_bound
statements.doc: Alford, Granville, and Pomerance [AGP94] proved that $C(x)>x^{2/7}$ for large $x$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1057.variants.agp_lower_bound :
    ∀ᶠ x in atTop, carmichaelCounting x > x ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1057.erdos_1057.variants.harman_lower_bound
statements.doc: The lower bound $C(x)> x^{0.33336704}$ was proved by Harman [Ha08].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1057.variants.harman_lower_bound :
    ∀ᶠ x in atTop, carmichaelCounting x > x ^ (0.33336704 : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1057.erdos_1057.variants.lichtman_lower_bound
statements.doc: This exponent was improved to $0.3389$ by Lichtman [Li22].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1057.variants.lichtman_lower_bound :
    ∀ᶠ x in atTop, carmichaelCounting x > x ^ (0.3389 : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1058
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1058](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1058)
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.
- [Lu01] Luca, Florian, *On a conjecture of Erdős and Stewart*. Math. Comp. (2001), 893-896.

statements.name: Erdos1058.erdos_1058
statements.doc:
Let $2=p_1<p_2<\cdots$ be the sequence of prime numbers. Are there only finitely many $n$ such
that $n\in [p_{k-1},p_k)$ and the only primes dividing $n!+1$ are $p_{k}$ and $p_{k+1}$?

A conjecture of Erdős and Stewart, as reported in problem A2 of Guy's collection [Gu04]. The only
known cases are $n=1,2,3,4,5$. Luca [Lu01] proved that indeed these are the only solutions.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1058 : {n | IsSolution n}.Finite

statements.name: Erdos1058.erdos_1058.variants.luca
statements.doc: Luca [Lu01] proved that $n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5$ are the only solutions.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1058.variants.luca : {n | IsSolution n} = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1059
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1059](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1059)

statements.name: Erdos1059.erdos_1059
statements.doc: Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p - k!$ is composite for each $k$ such that $1 ≤ k! < p$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1059 :
    Set.Infinite {p | p.Prime ∧ AllFactorialSubtractionsComposite p}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1060
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1060](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1060)

statements.name: Erdos1060.erdos_1060.parts.i
statements.doc:
The conjecture is about the function $f(n)$ which counts the number of solutions to
$k\sigma(k)=n$, where $\sigma(k)$ is the sum of divisors of $k$. The first bound is that $f(n)$ grows slower
than any power of $n^(\frac{1}{\log\log n})$. The second bound is that $f(n)$ is at most a power of
$\log n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1060.parts.i :
    ∃ h : ℕ → ℝ,
      h =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ 1 / log (log n)) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, #{k ≤ n | k * σ 1 k = n} ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ h n

statements.name: Erdos1060.erdos_1060.parts.ii
statements.doc: Part (ii) of Erdős Problem 1060: bound on the number of $k \le n$ with $k \sigma_1(k) = n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1060.parts.ii :
    ∃ (C : ℝ), (fun n ↦ (#{k ≤ n | k * σ 1 k = n} : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun n ↦ log n ^ C)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1061
problems.doc:
*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/1061](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1061)
 - [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., _Unsolved problems in number theory_. (2004), Problem B15.

statements.name: Erdos1061.erdos_1061
statements.doc:
How many (ordered) solutions are there to `σ(a) + σ(b) = σ(a + b)` with `a + b ≤ x`?
Is it true that this number is asymptotic to `c * x` for some constant `c > 0`?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1061 : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ S ~[atTop] (fun x : ℝ ↦ c * x)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1062
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1062](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1062)

statements.name: Erdos1062.erdos_1062.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Erdős asked whether the limiting density `f n / n` exists and, if so, whether it is
irrational.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1062.parts.ii :
    ∃ l, Tendsto (fun n => (f n : ℝ) / n) atTop (𝓝 l) ∧ Irrational l

statements.name: Erdos1062.erdos_1062.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc: The interval `[⌊n/3⌋, n]` is fork-free, and therefore `f n` is at least `⌈2n / 3⌉`.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1062.variants.lower_bound (n : ℕ) : ⌈(2 * n / 3 : ℝ)⌉₊ ≤ f n

statements.name: Erdos1062.erdos_1062.variants.lebensold_bounds
statements.doc:
Lebensold proved that for large `n`, the function `f n` lies between `0.6725 n` and
`0.6736 n`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1062.variants.lebensold_bounds :
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (0.6725 : ℝ) * n ≤ f n ∧ f n ≤ (0.6736 : ℝ) * n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1063
problems.doc:
*References:*
 * [erdosproblems.com/1063](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1063)
 * [ErSe83] Erdos, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Problem 6447. Amer. Math. Monthly (1983), 710.
 * [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., _Unsolved problems in number theory_. (2004), Problem B31.
 * [Mo85] Monier, Jean-Marie, _Problems and Solutions: Solutions of Advanced Problems: 6447_.
   Amer. Math. Monthly **92** (1985), 435-436.
 * [Ku+26] Kung, P.-N., Song, L., Hwang, D., Yoon, J., Li, C.-L., Severini, S., Olšák, M.,
   Lockhart, E., Le, Q. V., Gokturk, B., Luong, T., Pfister, T., & Peng, N. (2026). _LEAP:
   Supercharging LLMs for Formal Mathematics with Agentic Frameworks_.
   [arXiv:2606.03303](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03303).

statements.name: Erdos1063.erdos_1063.better_upper
statements.doc:
Estimate $n_k$ by finding a better upper bound than Cambie's
$n_k \leq k \cdot \operatorname{lcm}(1, \dotsc, k-1)$.

The comparator takes its least common multiple in `ℕ` and casts the result. Writing the
ascription as `((… ).lcm (fun n : ℕ => n) : ℝ)` instead puts it on the `Finset.lcm`
application, so the coercion lands on `n` and the `lcm` is taken in `ℝ`, where `lcm` of
non-zero elements is `1` and the whole comparator collapses to `k`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1063.better_upper :
    (fun k => (n k : ℝ)) =O[atTop] erdos_1063.better_upper.answer ∧
    erdos_1063.better_upper.answer =o[atTop] fun k =>
      (k : ℝ) * (((Finset.Icc 1 (k - 1)).lcm id : ℕ) : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1063.erdos_1063.variants.subexponential_upper_bound
statements.doc:
An improved upper bound
$n_k \ll \exp\left(\frac{k}{\log k}(\log \log k + \log \log \log k + \log 2)\right)$,
which is $o\bigl(k \cdot \operatorname{lcm}(1, \dotsc, k - 1)\bigr)$, was formally proved in
Lean 4 by the LEAP prover agent [Ku+26] (see the linked `formal_proof`).
This is an improvement over another upper bound propsed [here](https://github.com/pw/erdos1063-upper-bound/blob/a28481f5b4bda374086533397269c5b550c759b8/README.md).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1063.variants.subexponential_upper_bound :
    let upper_bound : ℕ → ℝ := fun k =>
      Real.exp ((k : ℝ) / Real.log k *
        (Real.log (Real.log k) + Real.log (Real.log (Real.log k)) + Real.log 2))
    (fun k => (n k : ℝ)) =O[atTop] upper_bound ∧
    upper_bound =o[atTop] fun k =>
      (k : ℝ) * (((Finset.Icc 1 (k - 1)).lcm id : ℕ) : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1063.erdos_1063.variants.exists_exception
statements.doc:
Erdős and Selfridge noted that, for $n \ge 2k$ with $k \ge 2$, at least one of the numbers
$n - i$ for $0 \le i < k$ fails to divide $\binom{n}{k}$ ([ErSe83]).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1063.variants.exists_exception {n k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) (h : 2 * k ≤ n) :
    ∃ i < k, ¬ (n - i) ∣ n.choose k

statements.name: Erdos1063.erdos_1063.variants.small_values
statements.doc: The initial values satisfy $n_2 = 4$, $n_3 = 6$, $n_4 = 9$, and $n_5 = 12$ ([Gu04], Problem B31).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1063.variants.small_values :
    n 2 = 4 ∧ n 3 = 6 ∧ n 4 = 9 ∧ n 5 = 12

statements.name: Erdos1063.erdos_1063.variants.monier_upper_bound
statements.doc:
Monier observed that $n_k \le k!$ for $k \ge 3$ ([Mo85]), since $\binom{k!}{k}$ is divisible
by $k! - i$ for $1 \le i < k$.

The hypothesis `3 ≤ k` is necessary. At $k = 2$ the bound is false: $n_2 = 4$ and $2! = 2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1063.variants.monier_upper_bound {k : ℕ} (hk : 3 ≤ k) :
    n k ≤ k !

statements.name: Erdos1063.erdos_1063.variants.cambie_upper_bound
statements.doc:
[Cambie observed](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1063) the improved bound
$n_k \le k \cdot \operatorname{lcm}(1, \dotsc, k - 1)$.

The hypothesis `3 ≤ k` is necessary here too. At $k = 2$ the right hand side is
$2 \cdot \operatorname{lcm}(1) = 2$, while $n_2 = 4$.

The source writes the bound as $k[2, 3, \dotsc, k-1]$. That agrees with the range used here,
because including $1$ does not change a least common multiple.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1063.variants.cambie_upper_bound {k : ℕ} (hk : 3 ≤ k) :
    n k ≤ k * (Finset.Icc 1 (k - 1)).lcm id

statements.name: Erdos1063.erdos_1063.variants.exp_upper_bound
statements.doc: The least common multiple bound implies $n_k \le \exp((1 + o(1))k)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1063.variants.exp_upper_bound :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto f atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
      ∀ k, (n k : ℝ) ≤ exp ((1 + f k) * k)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1064
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1064](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1064)

statements.name: Erdos1064.erdos_1064
statements.doc:
Let $ϕ(n)$ be the Euler's totient function, then the $n$ satisfies $ϕ(n)>ϕ(n - ϕ(n))$
have asymptotic density 1.
Reference: [LuPo02] Luca, Florian and Pomerance, Carl, On some problems of {M}\polhk akowski-{S}chinzel and {E}rd\H
os concerning the arithmetical functions {$\phi$} and
{$\sigma$}. Colloq. Math.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1064 : {n | φ n > φ (n - φ n)}.HasDensity 1

statements.name: Erdos1064.erdos_1064.variants.k2
statements.doc:
Let $ϕ(n)$ be the Euler's totient function, there exist infinitely many $n$
such that $ϕ(n)< ϕ(n - ϕ(n))$
Reference: [GLW01] Grytczuk, A. and Luca, F. and W\'ojtowicz, M., A conjecture of {E}rdős concerning inequalities for the
{E}uler totient function.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1064.variants.k2 : {n | φ n < φ (n - φ n)}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos1064.erdos_1064.variants.general_function
statements.doc:
For any function $f(n)=o(n)$,
we have $\phi(n)>\phi(n-\phi(n))+f(n)$ for almost all $n$.
Reference:
[LuPo02] Luca, Florian and Pomerance, Carl, On some problems of {M}\polhk akowski-{S}chinzel and {E}rd\H
os concerning the arithmetical functions {$\phi$} and
{$\sigma$}. Colloq. Math. (2002), 111--130.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1064.variants.general_function (f : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hf : (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ))) :
    {n : ℕ | φ (n - φ n) + f n < φ n}.HasDensity 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1065
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1065](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1065)

statements.name: Erdos1065.erdos_1065.parts.i
statements.doc:
Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p = 2^k * q + 1$
for some prime $q$ and $k ≥ 0$?

This is mentioned as B46
in [Unsolved Problems in Number Theory](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-26677-0)
by *Richard K. Guy*
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1065.parts.i :
    Set.Infinite {p | ∃ q k, p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ p = 2^k * q + 1}

statements.name: Erdos1065.erdos_1065.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p = 2^k 3^l q + 1$
for some prime $q$ and $k ≥ 0$, $l ≥ 0$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1065.parts.ii :
    Set.Infinite {p | ∃ q k l, p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ p = 2^k * 3^l * q + 1}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1066
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1066](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1066)
- [Cs98] Csizmadia, G., *On the independence number of minimum distance graphs*.
  Discrete Comput. Geom. 20 (1998), 179-187.
- [Er87b] Erdős, P., *Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry*.
  Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985) (1987), 167-177.
- [PaTo96] Pach, J. and Tóth, G., *On the independence number of coin graphs*.
  Geombinatorics 6 (1996), 30-33.
- [Po85] Pollack, R., *Increasing the minimum distance of a set of points*.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 40 (1985), 450.
- [Sw02] Swanepoel, K. J., *Independence numbers of planar contact graphs*.
  Discrete Comput. Geom. 28 (2002), 649-670.

statements.name: Erdos1066.erdos_1066
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a graph given by $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, where any two distinct points are at
least distance $1$ apart, and we draw an edge between two points if they are distance $1$ apart.

Let $g(n)$ be maximal such that any such graph always has an independent set on at least $g(n)$
vertices. Estimate $g(n)$, or perhaps $\lim \frac{g(n)}{n}$.

We ask for $\lim g(n)/n$. The limit exists by Fekete's lemma, since placing two configurations far
apart shows $g(a+b) \leq g(a)+g(b)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1066 :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (g n : ℝ) / n) atTop (𝓝 erdos_1066.answer)

statements.name: Erdos1066.erdos_1066.variants.pollack
statements.doc:
Such graphs are always planar. Pollack [Po85] noted that the Four colour theorem implies
$g(n)\geq n/4$, since the graph is planar.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1066.variants.pollack (n : ℕ) : (n : ℝ) / 4 ≤ (g n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1066.erdos_1066.variants.swanepoel
statements.doc:
This lower bound has been improved to $\frac{9}{35}n$ by Csizmadia [Cs98] and then
$\frac{8}{31}n$ by Swanepoel [Sw02].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1066.variants.swanepoel (n : ℕ) : (8 / 31 : ℝ) * n ≤ (g n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1066.erdos_1066.variants.pach_toth
statements.doc:
Erdős initially thought that $g(n)=n/3$, but Chung and Graham, and independently Pach, gave a
construction that shows $g(n)\leq \frac{6}{19}n$. Pach and Tóth [PaTo96] improved this to
$g(n)\leq \frac{5}{16}n$.

Since $g(1) = 1$, the bound cannot hold for all $n$, so it is stated for infinitely many $n$,
with $5/16$ replaced by $5/16+\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1066.variants.pach_toth :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (g n : ℝ) ≤ (5 / 16 + ε) * n

statements.name: Erdos1066.erdos_1066.variants.higher_dim
statements.doc:
Pollack [Po85] also reports a letter from Erdős which poses the more general problem of, given
$n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with minimum distance $1$, let $g_d(n)$ be maximal such that there
always exist at least $g_d(n)$ many points which have minimum distance $>1$. Is it true that
$g_d(n) \gg n/d$ in general?

We read this with a constant independent of $d$ and $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1066.variants.higher_dim :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ d n : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → c * n / d ≤ (gDim d n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1067
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1067](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1067)
- [BoPi24] N. Bowler and M. Pitz, A note on uncountably chromatic graphs. arXiv:2402.05984 (2024).
- [ErHa66] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems. Acta Math. Acad.
  Sci. Hungar. (1966), 61-99.
- [Ko13] Komjáth, Péter, A note on chromatic number and connectivity of infinite graphs. Israel
  J. Math. (2013), 499--506.
- [So15] Soukup, Dániel T., Trees, ladders and graphs. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (2015), 96--116.
- [Th17] Thomassen, Carsten, Infinitely connected subgraphs in graphs of uncountable chromatic
  number. Combinatorica (2017), 785--793.

statements.name: Erdos1067.erdos_1067
statements.doc:
Does every graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ contain an infinitely connected subgraph with
chromatic number $\aleph_1$?

Komjáth [Ko13] proved that it is consistent that the answer is no. This was improved by
Soukup [So15], who constructed a counterexample using no extra set-theoretical assumptions. A
simpler elementary example was given by Bowler and Pitz [BoPi24].

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle and Aleph Prover.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1067 :
    ¬ ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 →
      ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), H.coe.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 ∧ InfinitelyConnected H.coe

statements.name: Erdos1067.erdos_1067.variants.infinite_edge_connectivity
statements.doc:
Does every graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ contain an infinitely edge-connected subgraph
with chromatic number $\aleph_1$?

Thomassen [Th17] proved that the answer is yes: every graph of uncountable chromatic number has a
subgraph with infinite edge-connectivity and uncountable chromatic number.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1067.variants.infinite_edge_connectivity :
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 →
      ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), H.coe.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 ∧ InfinitelyEdgeConnected H.coe

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1068
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1068](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1068)

statements.name: Erdos1068.erdos_1068
statements.doc:
Does every graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ contain a countable subgraph which is
infinitely connected?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1068 :
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_  1 →
      ∃ s : Set V, s.Countable ∧ InfinitelyConnected (G.induce s)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1069
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1069](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1069)
- [Er87b] Erdős, P., *Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry*. Intuitive geometry
  (Siófok, 1985) (1987), 167-177.
- [Sa87] Sah, C.-H., *The rich line problem of P. Erdős*. (1987), 123-125.
- [SzTr83] Szemerédi, E. and Trotter, Jr., W. T., *Extremal problems in discrete geometry*.
  Combinatorica (1983), 381-392.

statements.name: Erdos1069.erdos_1069
statements.doc:
Given any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, the number of $k$-rich lines (lines which contain
$\geq k$ of the points) is, provided $k\leq n^{1/2}$,
$$\ll \frac{n^2}{k^3}.$$

Erdős [Er87b] describes this as a conjecture of himself, Croft, and Purdy. It was proved by
Szemerédi and Trotter [SzTr83]. We take $k \geq 2$, since for $k \leq 1$ there are infinitely
many $k$-rich lines.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1069 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (n k : ℕ) (s : Finset ℝ²), s.card = n → 2 ≤ k →
      (k : ℝ) ≤ Real.sqrt n →
        ((richLines s k).ncard : ℝ) ≤ C * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / (k : ℝ) ^ 3

statements.name: Erdos1069.erdos_1069.variants.lattice
statements.doc:
When $k=n^{1/2}$ the lattice points show that there can be $\geq(2+o(1))n^{1/2}$ many
$n^{1/2}$-rich lines: for $n=m^2$ the $m\times m$ grid has $2m$ lines with $m$ points each.
Erdős thought that perhaps this is best possible, but Sah [Sa87] gave a construction achieving
$\geq (3+o(1))n^{1/2}$ many $n^{1/2}$-rich lines.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1069.variants.lattice (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) :
    ∃ s : Finset ℝ², s.card = m ^ 2 ∧ 2 * m ≤ (richLines s m).ncard

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1070
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1070](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1070)
- [DuVa26] Dúcz, Á. and Varga, D., *A unit-distance graph in the plane with independence ratio
  below 1/4*. [arXiv:2606.28157](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28157) (2026).
- [Er87b] Erdős, P., *Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry*.
  Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985) (1987), 167-177.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-27.pdf)
- [MRVZ23] Matolcsi, M., Ruzsa, I. Z., Varga, D. and Zsámboki, P., *The fractional chromatic
  number of the plane is at least $4$*. [arXiv:2311.10069](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.10069)
  (2023).

If we also insist that no two points are distance $<1$ apart, we get
[erdosproblems.com/1066](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1066).

statements.name: Erdos1070.erdos_1070.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that, given any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, there exist $f(n)$ points
such that no two are distance $1$ apart. Estimate $f(n)$. In particular, is it true that
$f(n)\geq n/4$?

This is the first part, a problem of Erdős [Er87b, p. 171]. Since $f(n)=\Theta(n)$ is already
known, we ask for $\lim f(n)/n$. The limit exists by Fekete's lemma, since placing two
configurations far apart shows $f(a+b) \leq f(a)+f(b)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1070.parts.i :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : ℝ) / n) atTop (𝓝 erdos_1070.parts.i.answer)

statements.name: Erdos1070.erdos_1070.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that, given any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, there exist $f(n)$ points
such that no two are distance $1$ apart. Estimate $f(n)$. In particular, is it true that
$f(n)\geq n/4$?

This is the second part, read as the inequality for every $n$. The answer is no: Dúcz and Varga
[DuVa26, Theorem 1] construct a finite unit distance graph $G$ in the plane with
$\alpha(G) < |V(G)|/4$. For its vertex set $X$, `f_le X` gives
$f(|X|) \leq \alpha(U_X) \leq \alpha(G) < |X|/4$, where $U_X$ is the unit distance graph on $X$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1070.parts.ii : ¬ ∀ n : ℕ, (n : ℝ) / 4 ≤ (f n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1070.erdos_1070.variants.moser_spindle
statements.doc:
The Moser spindle shows $f(n)\leq \frac{2}{7}n\approx 0.285n$.

The Moser spindle has $7$ points and independence number $2$, so $m$ far-apart copies give the
bound for $n=7m$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1070.variants.moser_spindle (m : ℕ) : f (7 * m) ≤ 2 * m

statements.name: Erdos1070.erdos_1070.variants.matolcsi_ruzsa_varga_zsamboki_graphs
statements.doc:
Matolcsi, Ruzsa, Varga, and Zsámboki [MRVZ23, Section 3, after Theorem 2] showed that for every
$\varepsilon>0$ there is a finite unit distance graph $G\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ whose largest
independent set has size at most $(1/4+\varepsilon)|G|$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1070.variants.matolcsi_ruzsa_varga_zsamboki_graphs :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ X : Finset ℝ², X.Nonempty ∧
      ((UnitDistancePlaneGraph (X : Set ℝ²)).indepNum : ℝ) ≤ (1 / 4 + ε) * X.card

statements.name: Erdos1070.erdos_1070.variants.matolcsi_ruzsa_varga_zsamboki
statements.doc:
Matolcsi, Ruzsa, Varga, and Zsámboki [MRVZ23] have improved the upper bound to
$$f(n) \leq \left(\frac{1}{4}+o(1)\right)n.$$

This follows from the previous statement by taking disjoint copies of the graph far apart.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1070.variants.matolcsi_ruzsa_varga_zsamboki :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (f n : ℝ) ≤ (1 / 4 + ε) * n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1071
problems.doc:
*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/1071](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1071)
* [Da85] Danzer, L., _Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry_.
  Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985), 167-177.

statements.name: Erdos1071.erdos_1071.parts.i
statements.doc:
Can a finite set of disjoint unit segments in a unit square be maximal?
Solved affirmatively by [Da85], who gave an explicit construction.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle and ChatGPT.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1071.parts.i :
    ∃ S : Finset (ℝ² × ℝ²),
      Maximal (fun T : Finset (ℝ² × ℝ²) =>
        (∀ seg ∈ T, dist seg.1 seg.2 = 1 ∧
          seg.1 0 ∈ Icc 0 1 ∧ seg.1 1 ∈ Icc 0 1 ∧
          seg.2 0 ∈ Icc 0 1 ∧ seg.2 1 ∈ Icc 0 1) ∧
          (T : Set (ℝ² × ℝ²)).Pairwise SegmentsDisjoint) S

statements.name: Erdos1071.erdos_1071.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Is there a region $R$ with a maximal set of disjoint unit line segments that is countably infinite?
Here a unit line segment is a rotated and translated copy of the open interval $(0,1)$, and it is
required to be contained in $R$.
Solved affirmatively by [Fo99], who gave an explicit construction.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle and ChatGPT.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1071.parts.ii :
    ∃ (R : Set ℝ²) (S : Set (ℝ² × ℝ²)),
      IsOpen R ∧ IsConnected R ∧ S.Countable ∧ S.Infinite ∧
      Maximal (fun T : Set (ℝ² × ℝ²) =>
        (∀ seg ∈ T, dist seg.1 seg.2 = 1 ∧ openSegment ℝ seg.1 seg.2 ⊆ R) ∧
        T.Pairwise SegmentsDisjoint) S

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1072
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1072](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1072)

statements.name: Erdos1072.erdos_1072.parts.i
statements.doc: Is it true that there are infinitely many $p$ for which $f(p) = p − 1$?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1072.parts.i : Set.Infinite {p | p.Prime ∧ f p = p - 1}

statements.name: Erdos1072.erdos_1072.parts.ii
statements.doc: Is it true that $f(p)/p \to 0$ for $p \to \infty$ in a density 1 subset of the primes?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1072.parts.ii :
    ∃ (P : Set ℕ), P ⊆ {p | p.Prime} ∧ P.HasDensity 1 {p | p.Prime} ∧
      Tendsto (fun p => (f p / p : ℝ)) (atTop ⊓ principal P) (𝓝 0)

statements.name: Erdos1072.erdos_1072.variants.littleo
statements.doc:
Erdős, Hardy, and Subbarao [HaSu02], believed that the number of $p \le x$ for which $f(p)=p−1$
is $o(x/\log x)$.

[HaSu02] Hardy, G. E. and Subbarao, M. V., _A modified problem of Pillai and some related questions._
Amer. Math. Monthly (2002), 554--559.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1072.variants.littleo :
    (fun x ↦ (({p | p.Prime ∧ f p = p - 1} ∩ Icc 0 x).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun x ↦ x / Real.log x)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1073
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1073](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1073)

statements.name: Erdos1073.erdos_1073
statements.doc: Is it true that $A(x) \le x^{o(1)}$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1073 :
    ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ), o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ x, A x ≤ x ^ (o x)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1074
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1074](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1074)

statements.name: Erdos1074.erdos_1074.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $S$ be the set of all $m\geq 1$ such that there exists a prime $p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such
that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$. Does
$$
  \lim\frac{|S\cap[1, x]|}{x}
$$
exist?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1074.parts.i : ∃ c, EHSNumbers.HasDensity c

statements.name: Erdos1074.erdos_1074.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $S$ be the set of all $m\geq 1$ such that there exists a prime $p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such
that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$. What is
$$
  \lim\frac{|S\cap[1, x]|}{x}?
$$
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1074.parts.ii : EHSNumbers.HasDensity erdos_1074.parts.ii.answer

statements.name: Erdos1074.erdos_1074.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Similarly, if $P$ is the set of all primes $p$ such that there exists an $m$ with
$p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$, then does
$$
  \lim\frac{|P\cap[1, x]|}{\pi(x)}
$$
exist?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1074.parts.iii : ∃ c, PillaiPrimes.HasDensity c {p | p.Prime}

statements.name: Erdos1074.erdos_1074.parts.iv
statements.doc:
Similarly, if $P$ is the set of all primes $p$ such that there exists an $m$ with
$p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$, then what is
$$
  \lim\frac{|P\cap[1, x]|}{\pi(x)}?
$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1074.parts.iv :
    PillaiPrimes.HasDensity erdos_1074.parts.iv.answer {p | p.Prime}

statements.name: Erdos1074.erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_infinite
statements.doc:
Erdős, Hardy, and Subbarao proved that $S$ is infinite.

Formal proof linked here provided by AlphaProof.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_infinite : EHSNumbers.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos1074.erdos_1074.variants.PillaiPrimes_infinite
statements.doc: Erdős, Hardy, and Subbarao proved that $P$ is infinite.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1074.variants.PillaiPrimes_infinite : PillaiPrimes.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos1074.erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_one
statements.doc:
Regarding the first question, Hardy and Subbarao computed all EHS numbers up to $2^{10}$, and
write "...if this trend conditions we expect [the limit] to be around 0.5, if it exists. The
frequency with which the EHS numbers occur - most often in long sequences of consecutive integers -
makes us believe that their asymptotic density exists and is unity. Erdős, though initially
hesitant, later agreed with this view." That is, the conjecture is that $S$ has density $1$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_one : EHSNumbers.HasDensity 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1075
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1075](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1075)
- [Er64f] Erdős, P., On extremal problems of graphs and generalized graphs. Israel J. Math. (1964),
  183--190.

statements.name: Erdos1075.erdos_1075
statements.doc:
Let $r\geq 3$. There exists $c_r>r^{-r}$ such that, for any $\epsilon>0$, if $n$ is sufficiently
large, the following holds. Any $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with at least
$(1+\epsilon)(n/r)^r$ many edges contains a subgraph on $m$ vertices with at least $c_rm^r$ edges,
where $m=m(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1075 :
    ∀ r : ℕ, 3 ≤ r → ∃ c : ℝ, (r : ℝ)⁻¹ ^ r < c ∧
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ m : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto m atTop atTop ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ H : Finset (Finset (Fin n)),
        H.IsUniform r → (1 + ε) * ((n : ℝ) / r) ^ r ≤ H.card →
          ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), S.card = m n ∧
            c * (S.card : ℝ) ^ r ≤ (H.hypergraphInduce S).card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1077
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1077](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1077)

statements.name: Erdos1077.erdos_1077
statements.doc:
We call a graph $D$-balanced (or $D$-almost-regular) if the maximum degree is at most $D$ times the
minimum degree.

Let $ε, α > 0$ and $D$ and $n$ be sufficiently large. If $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with at
least $n^{1+α}$ edges, then must $G$ contain a $D$-balanced subgraph on $m > n^{1-α}$ vertices with
at least $εm^{1+α}$ edges?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1077 :
    ¬ ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ε < 1 → ∀ α > (0 : ℝ), α < 1 → ∀ᶠ D in atTop, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.edgeSet.ncard > (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + α) →
        ∃ (H : Subgraph G),
          letI m := H.verts.ncard
          IsBalanced H.coe D ∧
          m > (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - α) ∧
          H.edgeSet.ncard > ε * m ^ (1 + α)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1079
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1079](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1079)
- [Er75] Erdős, P., *Some recent progress on extremal problems in graph theory*. Congr. Numer.
  (1975), 3-14.
- [BoTh81] Bollobás, Béla and Thomason, Andrew, *Dense neighbourhoods and Turán's theorem*. J.
  Combin. Theory Ser. B (1981), 111--114.
- [Bo83b] Bondy, J. A., *Large dense neighbourhoods and Turán's theorem*. J. Combin. Theory Ser.
  B (1983), 109--111.

statements.name: Erdos1079.erdos_1079
statements.doc:
Let $r\geq 4$. If $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with at least $\mathrm{ex}(n;K_r)$ edges then
must $G$ contain a vertex with degree $d\gg_r n$ whose neighbourhood contains at least
$\mathrm{ex}(d;K_{r-1})$ edges?

As Erdős [Er75] says 'if true this would be a nice generalisation of Turán's theorem'. This is
true (unless $G$ it itself the Turán graph), and was proved by Bollobás and Thomason [BoTh81].
Bondy [Bo83b] showed that if $G$ has $>\mathrm{ex}(n;K_r)$ edges then the corresponding vertex
can be chosen to be of maximum degree in $G$.

The number of edges in the neighbourhood of $v$ is the number of edges of $G$ both of whose
endpoints are adjacent to $v$. Graphs on a single vertex are excluded, since there every degree
is $0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1079 : ∀ r : ℕ, 4 ≤ r → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n →
    ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), extremalNumber n (completeGraph (Fin r)) ≤ G.edgeSet.ncard →
      ∃ v : Fin n, c * n ≤ G.degree v ∧
        extremalNumber (G.degree v) (completeGraph (Fin (r - 1))) ≤
          {e ∈ G.edgeSet | ∀ x ∈ e, G.Adj v x}.ncard

statements.name: Erdos1079.erdos_1079.variants.bondy
statements.doc:
Bondy's strengthening [Bo83b]: if $G$ has more than $\mathrm{ex}(n;K_r)$ edges then some vertex
$v$ of maximum degree has $d(v) \geq n/2$ and its neighbourhood contains more than
$\mathrm{ex}(d(v);K_{r-1})$ edges.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1079.variants.bondy (r n : ℕ) (hr : 4 ≤ r) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hG : extremalNumber n (completeGraph (Fin r)) < G.edgeSet.ncard) :
    ∃ v : Fin n, G.degree v = G.maxDegree ∧ n ≤ 2 * G.degree v ∧
      extremalNumber (G.degree v) (completeGraph (Fin (r - 1))) <
        {e ∈ G.edgeSet | ∀ x ∈ e, G.Adj v x}.ncard

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1080
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1080](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1080)
- [DeSz92] de Caen, D. and Székely, L. A., The maximum size of {$4$}- and {$6$}-cycle free bipartite
  graphs on {$m,n$} vertices. (1992), 135--142.
- [Er75] Erdős, P., Some recent progress on extremal problems in graph theory. Congr. Numer. (1975),
  3-14.
- [LUW94] Lazebnik, F. and Ustimenko, V. A. and Woldar, A. J., New constructions of bipartite graphs
  on {$m,n$} vertices with many edges and without small cycles. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (1994),
  111--117.

statements.name: Erdos1080.erdos_1080
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph on $n$ vertices such that one part has $\lfloor n^{2/3}\rfloor$
vertices. Is there a constant $c>0$ such that if $G$ has at least $cn$ edges then $G$ must
contain a $C_6$?

The answer is no, as shown by De Caen and Székely [DeSz92], who in fact show a stronger result.
Let $f(n,m)$ be the maximum number of edges of a bipartite graph between $n$ and $m$ vertices which
does not contain either a $C_4$ or $C_6$. A positive answer to this question would then imply
$f(n,\lfloor n^{2/3}\rfloor)\ll n$. De Caen and Székely prove
$n^{10/9}\gg f(n,\lfloor n^{2/3}\rfloor) \gg n^{58/57+o(1)}$ for $m\sim n^{2/3}$. They also prove
more generally that, for $n^{1/2}\leq m\leq n$, $f(n,m) \ll (nm)^{2/3},$ which was also proved by
Faudree and Simonovits.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1080 :
    ¬ ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [Nonempty V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (X Y : Set V),
      IsBipartition G X Y → X.ncard = ⌊(Fintype.card V : ℝ) ^ (2/3 : ℝ)⌋₊ →
      G.edgeSet.ncard ≥ c * Fintype.card V →
        ∃ (v : V) (walk : G.Walk v v), walk.IsCycle ∧ walk.length = 6

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1081
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1081](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1081)
- [Er76e] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on consecutive integers*.
  Publ. Math. Debrecen 23 (1976), 271-282.
- [Od81] Odoni, R. W. K., *A problem of Erdős on sums of two squarefull numbers*.
  Acta Arith. 39 (1981), 145-162.
- [BlGr06] Blomer, V. and Granville, A., *Estimates for representation numbers of quadratic
  forms*. Duke Math. J. 135 (2006), 261-302.

statements.name: Erdos1081.erdos_1081
statements.doc:
Let $A(x)$ count the number of $n\leq x$ which are the sum of two squarefull numbers (a number
$m$ is squarefull if $p\mid m$ implies $p^2\mid m$). Is it true that
$$A(x) \sim c \frac{x}{\sqrt{\log x}}$$
for some $c>0$?

Odoni [Od81] proved this is false.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1081 :
    ¬ ∃ c > (0 : ℝ),
      (fun x : ℝ ↦ (A x : ℝ)) ~[atTop] fun x ↦ c * x / Real.sqrt (Real.log x)

statements.name: Erdos1081.erdos_1081.variants.blomer_granville
statements.doc:
Blomer and Granville [BlGr06] proved
$$A(x)= (\log\log x)^{O(1)}\frac{x}{(\log x)^{\alpha}}$$
where $\alpha=1-2^{-1/3}\approx 0.206299$: for some $C$ and all large $x$, $A(x)$ lies between
$(\log\log x)^{-C}$ and $(\log\log x)^{C}$ times $x/(\log x)^{\alpha}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1081.variants.blomer_granville :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop,
      x / Real.log x ^ alpha / Real.log (Real.log x) ^ C ≤ A x ∧
        (A x : ℝ) ≤ x / Real.log x ^ alpha * Real.log (Real.log x) ^ C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1082
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1082](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1082)

statements.name: Erdos1082.erdos_1082.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points with no three on a line.
Does $A$ determine at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ distinct distances?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1082.parts.i : ∀ (A : Finset ℝ²) (hA_n3c : NonTrilinear (A : Set ℝ²)),
    A.card / 2 ≤ distinctDistances A

statements.name: Erdos1082.erdos_1082.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points with no three on a line.
Must there exist a single point from which there are at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ distinct
distances?

This question has been answered negatively by Xichuan in the
[comments](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/1082), who gave a set of $42$ points in
$\mathbb{R}^2$, with no three on a line, such that each point determines only $20$ distinct distances.

A smaller counterexample has been formalised here: it comprised of $8$ points, where each point only
determines $3$ distances.

This counterexample has originally been found by Heiko Harborth.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1082.parts.ii :
    ¬ ∀ (A : Finset ℝ²) (hA : A.Nonempty) (hA_n3c : NonTrilinear (A : Set ℝ²)),
    ∃ (a : ℝ²) (ha : a ∈ A), A.card / 2 ≤ distinctDistancesFrom A a

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1083
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1083](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1083)
- [APST04] Aronov, Boris and Pach, János and Sharir, Micha and Tardos, Gábor, *Distinct distances in
  three and higher dimensions*. Combin. Probab. Comput. (2004), 283--293.
- [CEGSW90] Clarkson, Kenneth L. and Edelsbrunner, Herbert and Guibas, Leonidas J. and Sharir, Micha
  and Welzl, Emo, *Combinatorial complexity bounds for arrangements of curves and spheres*. Discrete
  Comput. Geom. (1990), 99--160.
- [Er46b] Erdős, P., *On sets of distances of {$n$} points*. Amer. Math. Monthly (1946), 248--250.
- [SoVu08] Solymosi, József and Vu, Van H., *Near optimal bounds for the {E}rdős distinct distances
  problem in high dimensions*. Combinatorica (2008), 113--125.

statements.name: Erdos1083.erdos_1083
statements.doc: Let $d\geq 3$, and let $f_d(n)$ be the minimal $m$ such that every set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ determines at least $m$ distinct distances. Estimate $f_d(n)$ - in particular, is it true that $$f_d(n)=n^{\frac{2}{d}-o(1)}?$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1083 :
    ∀ d : ℕ, 3 ≤ d → ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
        (minimalDistinctDistances (ℝ^d) n : ℝ) = (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) - o n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1084
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1084](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1084)
- [Ha74b] Harborth, Heiko, Lösung zu Problem 664A. Elem. Math. (1974), 14--15.

Let `f_2(n)` be the maximum number of pairs of points at distance exactly `1`
among any set of `n` points in `ℝ²`, under the condition that all pairwise
distances are at least `1`.

Estimate the growth of `f_2(n)`.

Status: open.

statements.name: Erdos1084.erdos_1084.variants.upper_d1
statements.doc: It is easy to check that $f_1(n) = n - 1$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1084.variants.upper_d1 : f 1 n = n - 1

statements.name: Erdos1084.erdos_1084.variants.easy_upper_d2
statements.doc: It is easy to check that $f_2(n) < 3n$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1084.variants.easy_upper_d2 (hn : n ≠ 0) : f 2 n < 3 * n

statements.name: Erdos1084.erdos_1084.variants.upper_d2
statements.doc: Erdős showed that there is some constant $c > 0$ such that $f_2(n) < 3n - c n^{1/2}$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1084.variants.upper_d2 : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n > 0, f 2 n < 3 * n - c * sqrt n

statements.name: Erdos1084.erdos_1084.variants.triangular_optimal_d2
statements.doc:
Erdős conjectured that the triangular lattice is best possible in 2D, in particular that
$f_2(3n^2 + 3n + 1) = 9n^2 + 3n$. Harborth [Ha74b] proved this, and more generally
$f_2(n) = \lfloor 3n - \sqrt{12n - 3} \rfloor$ for all $n \geq 2$.

Note: in [Er75f] is read $9n^2 + 6n$, but this seems to be a typo.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1084.variants.triangular_optimal_d2 : f 2 (3 * n ^ 2 + 3 * n + 1) = 9 * n ^ 2 + 3 * n

statements.name: Erdos1084.erdos_1084.variants.upper_lower_d3
statements.doc:
Erdős claims the existence of two constants $c_1, c_2 > 0$
such that $6n - c_1 n^{2/3} ≤ f_3(n) \le 6n - c_2 n^{2/3}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1084.variants.upper_lower_d3 :
    ∃ c₁ : ℝ, ∃ c₂ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      6 * n - c₁ * n ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ) ≤ f 3 n ∧ f 3 n ≤ 6 * n - c₂ * n ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1085
problems.doc:
Let f_d(n) be minimal such that, in any set of n points in ℝ^d, there exist at most f_d(n) pairs
of points which are distance 1 apart. Estimate f_d(n).

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1085](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1085)

statements.name: Erdos1085.erdos_1085.variants.lower_d2
statements.doc: Erdős showed $f_2(n) > n^{1+c/\log\log n}$ for some $c > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1085.variants.lower_d2 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + c / log (log n)) < f 2 n

statements.name: Erdos1085.erdos_1085.variants.upper_d2
statements.doc: Spencer, Szemerédi, and Trotter showed $f_2(n) = O(n^{4/3})$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1085.variants.upper_d2 : (fun n ↦ (f 2 n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (4/3 : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos1085.erdos_1085.variants.lower_d3
statements.doc: Erdős showed $f_3(n) = Ω(n^{4/3}\log\log n)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1085.variants.lower_d3 :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (4/3 : ℝ) * log (log n)) =O[atTop] (fun n ↦ (f 3 n : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos1085.erdos_1085.variants.upper_d3
statements.doc: Is the $n^{4/3}\log\log n$ lower bound in 3D also an upper bound?.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1085.variants.upper_d3 :
    (fun n ↦ (f 3 n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (4/3 : ℝ) * log (log n))

statements.name: Erdos1085.erdos_1085.variants.lower_d4_lenz
statements.doc:
Lenz showed that, for $d \ge 4$, $f_d(n) \ge \frac{p - 1}{2p} n^2 - O(1)$ where
$p = \lfloor\frac d2\rfloor$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1085.variants.lower_d4_lenz (hd : 4 ≤ d) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ↑(d / 2 - 1) / (2 * ↑(d / 2)) * n ^ 2 - C ≤ f d n

statements.name: Erdos1085.erdos_1085.variants.upper_d4_erdos
statements.doc:
Erdős showed that, for $d \ge 4$, $f_d(n) \le \left(\frac{p - 1}{2p} + o(1)\right) n^2$ where
$p = \lfloor\frac d2\rfloor$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1085.variants.upper_d4_erdos (hd : 4 ≤ d) :
    ∃ g : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto g atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
      ∀ n, f d n ≤ (↑(d / 2 - 1) / (2 * ↑(d / 2)) + g n) * n ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos1085.erdos_1085.variants.upper_lower_d5_odd
statements.doc:
Erdős and Pach showed that, for $d \ge 5$ odd, there exist constants $c_1(d), c_2(d) > 0$
such that $\frac{p - 1}{2p} n^2 + c_1 n^{4/3} \le f_d(n) \le \frac{p - 1}{2p} n^2 + c_2 n^{4/3}$ where
$p = \lfloor\frac d2\rfloor$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1085.variants.upper_lower_d5_odd (hd : 5 ≤ d) (hd_odd : Odd d) :
    ∃ c₁ > (0 : ℝ), ∃ c₂ : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      ↑(d / 2 - 1) / (2 * ↑(d / 2)) * n ^ 2 + c₁ * n ^ (4 / 3 : ℝ) ≤ f d n ∧
      f d n ≤ ↑(d / 2 - 1) / (2 * ↑(d / 2)) * n ^ 2 + c₂ * n ^ (4 / 3 : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1086
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1086](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1086)
- [ErPu71] Erdős, P. and Purdy, G., *Some extremal problems in geometry*. J. Combinatorial Theory
  Ser. A 10 (1971), 246-252.
- [RaSh17] Raz, O. E. and Sharir, M., *The number of unit-area triangles in the plane: theme and
  variations*. Combinatorica 37 (2017), 1221-1240.
  [arXiv:1501.00379](https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.00379)

statements.name: Erdos1086.erdos_1086
statements.doc:
Let $g(n)$ be minimal such that any set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains the vertices of
at most $g(n)$ many triangles with the same area. Estimate $g(n)$.

Only triangles of positive area are counted.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1086 : (fun n : ℕ ↦ (g n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_1086.answer

statements.name: Erdos1086.erdos_1086.variants.erdos_purdy_lower
statements.doc:
Erdős and Purdy [ErPu71] proved
$$n^2\log\log n \ll g(n) \ll n^{5/2}.$$

This is the lower bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1086.variants.erdos_purdy_lower :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.log (Real.log n)) =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (g n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1086.erdos_1086.variants.raz_sharir
statements.doc:
The upper bound of Erdős and Purdy [ErPu71] has been improved a number of times. The best known
bound is $g(n) \ll n^{20/9}$ by Raz and Sharir [RaSh17].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1086.variants.raz_sharir :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (g n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (20 / 9 : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1087
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1087](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1087)
- [ErPu71] Erdős, P. and Purdy, G., *Some extremal problems in geometry*. J. Combinatorial Theory
  Ser. A 10 (1971), 246-252.

statements.name: Erdos1087.erdos_1087
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that every set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains at most $f(n)$
many sets of four points which are 'degenerate' in the sense that some pair are the same distance
apart. Estimate $f(n)$ - in particular, is it true that $f(n)\leq n^{3+o(1)}$?

Here a set of four points is degenerate if two of its six pairwise distances are equal, and
$f(n)\leq n^{3+o(1)}$ is read as $f(n) \ll n^{3+\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1087 :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (3 + ε)

statements.name: Erdos1087.erdos_1087.variants.lower
statements.doc:
Erdős and Purdy [ErPu71] proved
$$n^3\log n \ll f(n) \ll n^{7/2}.$$

This is the lower bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1087.variants.lower :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ 3 * Real.log n) =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1087.erdos_1087.variants.upper
statements.doc:
Erdős and Purdy [ErPu71] proved
$$n^3\log n \ll f(n) \ll n^{7/2}.$$

This is the upper bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1087.variants.upper :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (7 / 2 : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1088
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1088](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1088)

statements.name: Erdos1088.erdos_1088
statements.doc:
Let $f_d(n)$ be the minimal $m$ such that any set of $m$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains a set of
$n$ points for which any two determined distances are distinct. Erdős Problem 1088 asks to
estimate $f_d(n)$. In particular, is it true that, for every fixed $n \geq 3$,
$$
f_d(n) = 2^{o(d)}
$$
as $d \to \infty$?

The little-$o$ condition is stated after taking the base-$2$ logarithm.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1088 :
    ∀ n ≥ 3,
      (fun d : ℕ ↦ Real.logb 2 (f d n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun d : ℕ ↦ (d : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1089
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1089](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1089)
- [Er75f] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry*. Ann. Mat. Pura
  Appl. (4) (1975), 99-108.
- [BBS83] Bannai, Eiichi and Bannai, Etsuko and Stanton, Dennis, *An upper bound for the
  cardinality of an $s$-distance subset in real Euclidean space. II*. Combinatorica (1983),
  147-152.

statements.name: Erdos1089.erdos_1089
statements.doc:
Let $g_d(n)$ be minimal such that every collection of $g_d(n)$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ determines
at least $n$ many distinct distances. Estimate $g_d(n)$. In particular, does
$$\lim_{d \to \infty} \frac{g_d(n)}{d^{n-1}}$$
exist?

A problem of Erdős [Er75f, p.105]. The answer is yes: for $n \ge 2$,
$$\binom{d+1}{n-1} + 1 \le g_d(n) \le \binom{d+n-1}{n-1} + 1,$$
where the upper bound is due to Bannai, Bannai and Stanton [BBS83] and the lower bound to a
construction of Aletheia (generalising constructions for Problem 502), so that
$g_d(n) / d^{n-1} \to 1/(n-1)!$ as $d \to \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1089 :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∃ L : ℝ,
      Tendsto (fun d : ℕ => (g d n : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) ^ (n - 1)) atTop (𝓝 L)

statements.name: Erdos1089.erdos_1089.variants.bounds_and_limit
statements.doc:
For $n \ge 2$ one has $\binom{d+1}{n-1} + 1 \le g_d(n) \le \binom{d+n-1}{n-1} + 1$ for all
$d \ge 1$, and $g_d(n) / d^{n-1} \to 1/(n-1)!$ as $d \to \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1089.variants.bounds_and_limit (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    (∀ d, 1 ≤ d → (d + 1).choose (n - 1) + 1 ≤ g d n ∧ g d n ≤ (d + n - 1).choose (n - 1) + 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun d : ℕ => (g d n : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) ^ (n - 1)) atTop
        (𝓝 ((1 : ℝ) / (n - 1).factorial))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1090
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1090](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1090)
- [Er75f] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry*. Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. (4) (1975), 99-108.

statements.name: Erdos1090.erdos_1090
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 3$. Does there exist a finite set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ such that, in any $2$-colouring of $A$, there exists a line which contains at least $k$ points from $A$, and all the points of $A$ on the line have the same colour?

Erdős [Er75f] says Graham and Selfridge proved the answer is yes when $k=3$. Hunter has observed that, for sufficiently large $n$, a generic projection of $[k]^n$ into $\mathbb{R}^2$ has this property, by the Hales-Jewett theorem.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1090 : ∀ (k : ℕ), ∀ (hk : 3 ≤ k),
    ∃ (A : Finset (Fin 2 → ℝ)), ∀ (C : A → Fin 2),
      ∃ (S : Finset (Fin 2 → ℝ)), ∃ (hSA : S ⊆ A),
        Collinear ℝ (S : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ)) ∧ S.card ≥ k ∧
          (∀ y ∈ A, y ∈ affineSpan ℝ (S : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ)) → y ∈ S) ∧
          ∃ c, ∀ x (hx : x ∈ S), C ⟨x, hSA hx⟩ = c

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1092
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Erdős Problem 1092](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1092)
- [Ro82] V. Rödl, *Nearly bipartite graphs with large chromatic number*, Combinatorica **2** (1982),
  377–383.

statements.name: Erdos1092.f_asymptotic_2
statements.doc:
Is it true that $f_2(n) \gg n$? Disproved by Rödl, who showed $f_r(n) = o(n)$ for all fixed
$r \geq 2$. A conjecture of Erdős, Hajnal, and Szemerédi.
