This seems to be closely related to, but distinct from, [744](https://www.erdosproblems.com/744).

Tang notes in the comments that Rödl [Ro82] constructed, for any $\epsilon>0$ and $k$, a graph
with chromatic number $\geq k$ such that every graph on $m$ vertices is bipartite after deleting at
most $\epsilon m$ edges.
statements.statement:
theorem f_asymptotic_2 :
    ¬ ∃ g : ℕ → ℕ, IsAdmissible 2 g ∧
      (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (g n : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos1092.f_asymptotic_general
statements.doc:
More generally, is $f_r(n)\gg_r n$ for every $r \geq 2$? Disproved by Rödl, who showed
$f_r(n) = o(n)$ for all fixed $r \geq 2$.
statements.statement:
theorem f_asymptotic_general :
    ¬ ∀ r : ℕ, 2 ≤ r → ∃ g : ℕ → ℕ, IsAdmissible r g ∧
      (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (g n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1093
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1093](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1093)

statements.name: Erdos1093.erdos_1093.parts.i
statements.doc: Are there infinitely many binomial coefficients with deficiency 1?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1093.parts.i :
    {x : ℕ × ℕ | let k := x.1; let n := x.2; 2 * k ≤ n ∧ deficiency n k = 1 ∧
      ∀ p, p.Prime → (p ∣ choose n k) → k < p}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos1093.erdos_1093.parts.ii
statements.doc: Are there only finitely many binomial coefficients with deficiency > 1?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1093.parts.ii :
    {x : ℕ × ℕ | let k := x.1; let n := x.2; 2 * k ≤ n ∧ deficiency n k > 1 ∧
      ∀ p, p.Prime → (p ∣ choose n k) → k < p}.Finite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1094
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1094](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1094)

statements.name: Erdos1094.erdos_1094
statements.doc:
For all $n\ge 2k$ the least prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$ is $\le\max(n/k,k)$, with only
finitely many exceptions.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1094 :
    {(n, k) : ℕ × ℕ | 0 < k ∧ 2 * k ≤ n ∧ (n.choose k).minFac > max (n / k) k}.Finite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1095
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1095](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1095)
- [EES74] Ecklund, Jr., E. F. and Erd\H{o}s, P. and Selfridge, J. L., A new function associated with
  the prime factors of {$(\sp{n}\sb{k})$}. Math. Comp. (1974), 647--649.
- [ELS93] Erdős, P. and Lacampagne, C. B. and Selfridge, J. L., Estimates of the least prime factor
  of a binomial coefficient. Math. Comp. (1993), 215--224.
- [GrRa96] Granville, Andrew and Ramaré, Olivier, Explicit bounds on exponential sums and the
  scarcity of squarefree binomial coefficients. Mathematika (1996), 73--107.
- [Ko99b] Konyagin, S. V., Estimates of the least prime factor of a binomial coefficient.
  Mathematika (1999), 41--55.
- [SSW20] Sorenson, Brianna and Sorenson, Jonathan and Webster, Jonathan, An algorithm and estimates
  for the {E}rdős-{S}elfridge function. (2020), 371--385.

statements.name: Erdos1095.erdos_1095.variants.lower_solved
statements.doc: The current record is $g(k) \gg \exp(c(\log k)^2)$ for some $c>0$, due to Konyagin [Ko99b]. -
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1095.variants.lower_solved :
    ∃ c > 0, (fun k : ℕ ↦ exp (c * log k ^ 2)) =O[atTop] fun k ↦ (g k : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1095.erdos_1095.variants.upper_conjecture
statements.doc: Ecklund, Erdős, and Selfridge [EES74] proved $g(k)\leq \exp((1+o(1))k)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1095.variants.upper_conjecture :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto f atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ᶠ k in atTop, g k ≤ exp (k * (1 + f k))

statements.name: Erdos1095.erdos_1095.variants.lower_conjecture
statements.doc:
Erdős, Lacampagne, and Selfridge [ELS93] write 'it is clear to every right-thinking person' that
$g(k)\geq\exp(c\frac{k}{\log k})$ for some constant $c>0$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1095.variants.lower_conjecture : ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ k in atTop, g k ≥ exp (c * k / log k)

statements.name: Erdos1095.erdos_1095.variants.log_equivalent
statements.doc: Sorenson, Sorenson, and Webster [SSWE20] give heuristic evidence that $\log g(k) \asymp \frac{k}{\log k}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1095.variants.log_equivalent :
    (fun k ↦ log (g k)) =Θ[atTop] (fun k ↦ (k : ℝ) / log k)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1096
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1096](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1096)
- [ErKo98] Erdős, P. and Komornik, V., Developments in non-integer bases.
  Acta Math. Hungar. (1998), 57--83.
- [Fe16] Feng, D.-J., On the topology of polynomials with bounded integer coefficients.
  J. Eur. Math. Soc. (2016), 181--193.

statements.name: Erdos1096.erdos_1096
statements.doc:
Let $1<q<1+\epsilon$ and consider the set of numbers of the shape
$\sum_{i\in S}q^i$ (for all finite $S$), ordered by size as
$0=x_1<x_2<\cdots$.

Is it true that, provided $\epsilon>0$ is sufficiently small, $x_{k+1}-x_k \to 0$?

This was solved affirmatively by Erdős and Komornik [ErKo98], who proved the conclusion
whenever $1<q<\sqrt{q_1}$, where $q_1$ is the second Pisot-Vijayaraghavan number.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1096 :
    ∃ ε > 0, ∀ q, 1 < q → q < 1 + ε →
    ∀ x : ℕ → ℝ, StrictMono x → Set.range x = { ∑ i ∈ S, q ^ i | S : Finset ℕ } →
    Tendsto (fun k => x (k + 1) - x k) atTop (𝓝 0)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1097
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1097](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1097)
- [Bo99] Bourgain, J., On the dimension of {K}akeya sets and related maximal
inequalities. Geom. Funct. Anal. (1999), 256--282
- [KaTa99] Katz, Nets Hawk and Tao, Terence, Bounds on arithmetic projections, and applications to the
{K}akeya conjecture. Math. Res. Lett. (1999), 625--630.
- [Le15] Lemm, Marius, New counterexamples for sums-differences. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (2015), 3863--3868.
- [GGTW25] B. Georgiev, J. Gómez-Serrano, T. Tao, and A. Wagner, Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale. arXiv:2511.02864 (2025).

statements.name: Erdos1097.erdos_1097
statements.doc:
The main conjecture: for any finite set of integers $A$ with $|A| = n$, the number of distinct
common differences in three-term arithmetic progressions is $O(n^{3/2})$.

This conjecture was resolved negatively by showing that the problem is exactly equivalent to
Bourgain's sums-differences question [Bo99], which was introduced as an arithmetic path towards
the Kakeya conjecture. Under this equivalence:
- The greatest achievable exponent for this problem is equal to the smallest constant $c$
  achievable for Bourgain's sums-differences question:
  $$|A -_G B| \ll \max(|A|, |B|, |A +_G B|)^c$$
- The $O(n^{3/2})$ prediction is disproved because the lower bound has been shown to satisfy
  $c \ge 1.77898$ (due to Zheng and AlphaEvolve [GGTW25], improving on Lemm [Le15]), which is
  strictly greater than $3/2 = 1.5$.
- The best known upper bound is $c \le 11/6 \approx 1.833$ (due to Katz and Tao [KaTa99]).
- While the specific $O(n^{3/2})$ prediction is resolved negatively, the general question of
  determining the exact optimal exponent $c$ remains open.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1097 : ¬ ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (A : Finset ℤ),
    (CommonDifferencesThreeTermAP A).ncard ≤ C * (A.card : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1097.erdos_1097.variants.weaker
statements.doc: A weaker bound has been proven: there are always at most $n^2$ such values of $d$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1097.variants.weaker :
    ∀ A, (CommonDifferencesThreeTermAP A).ncard ≤ A.card ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos1097.erdos_1097.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
A trivial lower bound: for sufficiently large `n` there exist sets $A$ with $|A| = n$ that contain at least $\Omega(n)$
distinct common differences of three-term arithmetic progressions.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1097.variants.lower_bound : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∃ (A : Finset ℤ),
    A.card = n ∧ c * (n : ℝ) ≤ (CommonDifferencesThreeTermAP A).ncard

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1098
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1098](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1098)
- [Ne76] Neumann, B. H., *A problem of Paul Erdős on groups*. J. Austral. Math. Soc. Ser. A (1976),
  467-472.

statements.name: Erdos1098.erdos_1098
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a group and $\Gamma=\Gamma(G)$ be the non-commuting graph, with vertices the elements
of $G$ and an edge between $g$ and $h$ if and only if $g$ and $h$ do not commute, $gh\neq hg$.

If $\Gamma$ contains no infinite complete subgraph, then is there a finite bound on the size of
complete subgraphs of $\Gamma$?

This was solved by Neumann [Ne76], who proved that $\Gamma$ contains no infinite complete subgraph
if and only if the centre of the group has finite index, and noted that if the centre has index $n$
then $\Gamma$ contains no complete subgraph on $>n$ vertices.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1098 :
    ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G],
      (∀ s : Set G, (nonCommutingGraph G).IsClique s → s.Finite) →
        ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ s : Finset G, (nonCommutingGraph G).IsClique (s : Set G) → s.card ≤ n

statements.name: Erdos1098.erdos_1098.variants.center_finiteIndex
statements.doc:
Neumann [Ne76] proved that $\Gamma$ contains no infinite complete subgraph if and only if the
centre of the group has finite index.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1098.variants.center_finiteIndex (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    (∀ s : Set G, (nonCommutingGraph G).IsClique s → s.Finite) ↔
      (Subgroup.center G).FiniteIndex

statements.name: Erdos1098.erdos_1098.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
Neumann [Ne76] noted that if the centre has index $n$ then $\Gamma$ contains no complete subgraph
on $>n$ vertices.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1098.variants.upper_bound (G : Type*) [Group G]
    [(Subgroup.center G).FiniteIndex] :
    (nonCommutingGraph G).CliqueFree ((Subgroup.center G).index + 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1099
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1099](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1099)
- [Er81h] Erdős, P., *Some problems and results on additive and multiplicative number theory*.
  Analytic number theory (Philadelphia, Pa., 1980) (1981), 171-182.
- [Vo84] Vose, Michael D., *Integers with consecutive divisors in small ratio*. J. Number Theory
  (1984), 233-238.
- [Te87] Tenenbaum, Gérald, *Sur un problème extrémal en arithmétique*. Ann. Inst. Fourier
  (1987), 1-18.

statements.name: Erdos1099.erdos_1099
statements.doc:
Let $1=d_1<\cdots<d_{\tau(n)}=n$ be the divisors of $n$, and for $\alpha>1$ let
$$h_\alpha(n) = \sum_i \left( \frac{d_{i+1}}{d_i}-1\right)^\alpha.$$
Is it true that
$$\liminf_{n\to \infty}h_\alpha(n) \ll_\alpha 1?$$

Erdős [Er81h] remarks that $n!$ or the least common multiple of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ would be good
candidates for an infinite sequence of $n$ with $h_\alpha(n)$ bounded.

The $\liminf$ is trivially $\geq 1$, just considering the term $i=1$. A positive answer to the
main question was provided by Vose [Vo84] by constructing a specific sequence. Tenenbaum [Te87]
proved that the two explicit sequences mentioned above satisfy this property.

The statement "$\liminf h_\alpha(n)$ is finite" is formalised as "$h_\alpha(n)\leq C$ for
infinitely many $n$".
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1099 :
    ∀ α : ℝ, 1 < α → ∃ C : ℝ, ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, h α n ≤ C

statements.name: Erdos1099.erdos_1099.variants.factorial
statements.doc:
Is $h_\alpha(n!)$ bounded? Tenenbaum [Te87, Théorème 1] proved that it is, for every
$\alpha > 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1099.variants.factorial : ∀ α : ℝ, 1 < α →
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, h α n.factorial ≤ C

statements.name: Erdos1099.erdos_1099.variants.lcm
statements.doc:
Is $h_\alpha(\mathrm{lcm}(1,\ldots,n))$ bounded? Tenenbaum [Te87, Théorème 1] proved that it
is, for every $\alpha > 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1099.variants.lcm : ∀ α : ℝ, 1 < α →
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, h α ((Finset.Icc 1 n).lcm id) ≤ C

statements.name: Erdos1099.erdos_1099.variants.ratio_sum
statements.doc:
Erdős remarks that this problem occurred to him when considering $\sum_i \frac{d_{i+1}}{d_i}$.
It is easy to see that $\sum_{i} \frac{d_{i+1}}{d_i}> \tau(n)+\log n$, and Erdős asked whether
$$\liminf \left(\sum_{i} \frac{d_{i+1}}{d_i}-\tau(n)-\log n\right)<\infty,$$
which follows from the affirmative answer to the main question.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1099.variants.ratio_sum : ∃ C : ℝ, ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∑ i : Fin (n.divisors.card - 1), ((Nat.nth (· ∣ n) (i + 1) : ℝ) / Nat.nth (· ∣ n) i) -
      n.divisors.card - Real.log n ≤ C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1100
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1100](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1100)
- [ErHa78] Erdős, P. and Hall, R. R., *On some unconventional problems on the divisors of
  integers*. J. Austral. Math. Soc. Ser. A 25 (1978), 479-485.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1978-26.pdf)
- [Er81h] Erdős, P., *Some problems and results on additive and multiplicative number theory*.
  Analytic number theory (Philadelphia, Pa., 1980) (1981), 171-182.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-33.pdf)
- [ErTe89] Erdős, P. and Tenenbaum, G., *Sur les fonctions arithmétiques liées aux diviseurs
  consécutifs*. J. Number Theory 31 (1989), 285-311.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1989-37.pdf)

The function $\tau_\perp(n)$ is called $\tau_r(n)$ in [Er81h] and $f(n)$ in [ErHa78] and [ErTe89].

statements.name: Erdos1100.erdos_1100.parts.i
statements.doc:
If $1=d_1<\cdots<d_{\tau(n)}=n$ are the divisors of $n$, then let $\tau_\perp(n)$ count the number
of $i$ for which $(d_i,d_{i+1})=1$.

Is it true that $\tau_\perp(n)/\omega(n)\to \infty$ for almost all $n$?

This is the first part, asked by Erdős and Hall [ErHa78, p. 483]. We read it as: for every $C$ the
set of $n$ with $\tau_\perp(n)\leq C\omega(n)$ has natural density $0$. This is equivalent to
$\tau_\perp(n)/\omega(n)\to\infty$ along a set of density $1$, and it avoids dividing by
$\omega(1)=0$.

The answer is yes. By [ErTe89, Corollary 2, p. 288], $\tau_\perp(n)\geq(\log n)^{\log 3-1+o(1)}$
for almost all $n$ (see `erdos_1100.variants.normal_order`), while $\omega(n)\sim\log\log n$ for
almost all $n$ (Hardy-Ramanujan).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1100.parts.i :
    ∀ C : ℝ, {n : ℕ | (tauPerp n : ℝ) ≤ C * (ω n : ℝ)}.HasDensity 0

statements.name: Erdos1100.erdos_1100.parts.ii
statements.doc:
If $1=d_1<\cdots<d_{\tau(n)}=n$ are the divisors of $n$, then let $\tau_\perp(n)$ count the number
of $i$ for which $(d_i,d_{i+1})=1$.

Is it true that
$$\tau_\perp(n)< \exp((\log n)^{o(1)})$$
for all $n$?

This is the second part. Erdős and Hall [ErHa78, p. 483] say it would be reasonable to expect
that for every $\epsilon>0$ one has $\tau_\perp(n)<\exp((\log n)^{\epsilon})$; the problem page
asks it as a question. We read $o(1)$ as: for every $\epsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$.
This is equivalent to a bound for all $n$ with an exponent that tends to $0$. A bound for all $n$
with a fixed small $\epsilon$ fails: for example $\tau_\perp(30)=4>\exp((\log 30)^{0.1})$.

The answer is no. Erdős and Tenenbaum [ErTe89, Theorem 4, p. 289] proved
$\max_{n\leq x}\tau_\perp(n)\geq\exp\bigl(((\log 2)^2+o(1))\log x/(\log\log x)^2\bigr)$ (see
`erdos_1100.variants.erdos_tenenbaum_max`). This gives infinitely many $n$ with
$\tau_\perp(n)>\exp((\log n)^{1/2})$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1100.parts.ii :
    ¬ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (tauPerp n : ℝ) < Real.exp (Real.log n ^ ε)

statements.name: Erdos1100.erdos_1100.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Let
$$g(k) = \max_{\omega(n)=k}\tau_\perp(n),$$
where $\omega(n)$ counts the number of distinct prime divisors of $n$, and $n$ is restricted to
squarefree integers. Determine the growth of $g(k)$.

This is the third part. We read "determine the growth" as $g(k)=\Theta(\texttt{answer}\ k)$. Known
bounds are $(\sqrt2+o(1))^k<g(k)<(2-c)^k$ [Er81h, p. 173] (see
`erdos_1100.variants.erdos_simonovits`), and $g(k)\leq 3\cdot(3\cdot 2^{-2/3})^k$
[ErTe89, Theorem 1] (see `erdos_1100.variants.erdos_tenenbaum_g`). So $g$ is at most exponential,
the lower bound announced in [Er81h] would make it exponential, and already the base of the
exponential is open.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1100.parts.iii :
    (fun k : ℕ ↦ (g k : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_1100.parts.iii.answer

statements.name: Erdos1100.erdos_1100.variants.omega_le
statements.doc:
It is trivial that $\tau_\perp(n)\geq \omega(n)$ [ErHa78, p. 480], [ErTe89, (1.9), p. 288]: each
prime divisor of $n$ is the larger member of a coprime pair of consecutive divisors.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1100.variants.omega_le : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → ω n ≤ tauPerp n

statements.name: Erdos1100.erdos_1100.variants.eq_omega
statements.doc:
There is equality $\tau_\perp(n)=\omega(n)$ for infinitely many $n$: Erdős and Hall [ErHa78, p. 480]
note equality when $n=p_1\cdots p_k$ and $p_i>p_1\cdots p_{i-1}$ for $2\leq i\leq k$. Such $n$
exist for every $k$, which we state.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1100.variants.eq_omega (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, Squarefree n ∧ ω n = k ∧ tauPerp n = k

statements.name: Erdos1100.erdos_1100.variants.erdos_hall
statements.doc:
Erdős and Hall [ErHa78, Theorem 1, p. 480] prove, for all $\epsilon>0$ and sufficiently large $x$,
$$\max_{n<x} \tau_\perp(n) > \exp((\log\log x)^{2-\epsilon}).$$
We write the maximum as: some $n<x$ has $\tau_\perp(n)$ above the bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1100.variants.erdos_hall : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop,
    ∃ n : ℕ, (n : ℝ) < x ∧ Real.exp (Real.log (Real.log x) ^ (2 - ε)) < (tauPerp n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1100.erdos_1100.variants.erdos_tenenbaum_max
statements.doc:
Erdős and Tenenbaum [ErTe89, Theorem 4, p. 289] improved this considerably: for $x\geq 3$,
$$\max_{n\leq x}\tau_\perp(n)\geq \exp\Bigl(\bigl((\log 2)^2+o(1)\bigr)
\frac{\log x}{(\log\log x)^2}\Bigr).$$
We write $o(1)$ as an arbitrarily small $\delta>0$ and the maximum as: some $n\leq x$ has
$\tau_\perp(n)$ above the bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1100.variants.erdos_tenenbaum_max : ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop,
    ∃ n : ℕ, (n : ℝ) ≤ x ∧
      Real.exp (((Real.log 2) ^ 2 - δ) * Real.log x / (Real.log (Real.log x)) ^ 2) ≤
        (tauPerp n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1100.erdos_1100.variants.normal_order
statements.doc:
Erdős and Tenenbaum [ErTe89, Corollary 2, p. 288] proved that for almost all $n$ (that is, on a set
of density $1$)
$$(\log n)^{\log 3-1+o(1)}\leq \tau_\perp(n)\leq (\log n)^{\log 2-1/2+o(1)}.$$
The paper credits the upper bound to an earlier work of the same authors (Bull. Soc. Math. France
111 (1983)). We write $o(1)$ as: for every $\epsilon>0$ the set of $n$ with
both bounds, with exponents shifted by $\mp\epsilon$, has density $1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1100.variants.normal_order : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
    {n : ℕ | Real.log n ^ (Real.log 3 - 1 - ε) ≤ (tauPerp n : ℝ) ∧
      (tauPerp n : ℝ) ≤ Real.log n ^ (Real.log 2 - 1 / 2 + ε)}.HasDensity 1

statements.name: Erdos1100.erdos_1100.variants.erdos_simonovits
statements.doc:
Erdős and Simonovits (see [Er81h, p. 173]) proved
$$(2^{1/2}+o(1))^k < g(k) < (2-c)^k$$
for some constant $c>0$. We write the lower bound as: every fixed $0\leq r<\sqrt2$ satisfies
$r^k<g(k)$ for all large $k$, and the upper bound for all large $k$.

[Er81h] announces this without proof, and [ErTe89, p. 291] calls the argument of Erdős and
Simonovits for squarefree $n$, which it uses for the upper bound, unpublished. The upper bound also
follows from `erdos_1100.variants.erdos_tenenbaum_g`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1100.variants.erdos_simonovits :
    (∀ r : ℝ, 0 ≤ r → r < Real.sqrt 2 → ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, r ^ k < (g k : ℝ)) ∧
      ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, (g k : ℝ) < (2 - c) ^ k

statements.name: Erdos1100.erdos_1100.variants.erdos_tenenbaum_g
statements.doc:
For squarefree $n$ with $\omega(n)=k$ the bound $f(n)\leq 3\tau(n)B_1^{\omega_1(n)}$ of
[ErTe89, Theorem 1, (1.3), p. 287], with $B_1=3\cdot 2^{-5/3}$, gives
$$g(k)\leq 3\left(3\cdot 2^{-2/3}\right)^k,$$
and $3\cdot 2^{-2/3}=1.88988\ldots<2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1100.variants.erdos_tenenbaum_g (k : ℕ) :
    (g k : ℝ) ≤ 3 * (3 / (2 : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3)) ^ k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1101
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1101](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1101)

statements.name: Erdos1101.erdos_1101.parts.i
statements.doc: 1. There is NO good sequence with polynomial growth.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1101.parts.i :
    ¬ ∃ u, IsGood u ∧ ∃ k : ℕ, (fun n => (u n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ k)

statements.name: Erdos1101.erdos_1101.parts.ii
statements.doc: 2. There is a good sequence with sub-exponential growth.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1101.parts.ii :
    ∃ u, IsGood u ∧ (fun n => Real.log (u n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n => (n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1102
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1102](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1102)

statements.name: Erdos1102.erdos_1102.density_zero_of_P
statements.doc:
If `A = {a₁ < a₂ < …}` has property P,
then `A` has natural density `0`.
Equivalently, `(a_j / j) → ∞` as `j → ∞`.
-
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1102.density_zero_of_P
    (A : ℕ → ℕ)
    (h_inc : StrictMono A)
    (hP : HasPropertyP (range A)) :
    Tendsto (fun j => (A j / j : ℝ)) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos1102.erdos_1102.exists_sequence_with_P
statements.doc:
Conversely, for any function `f : ℕ → ℕ` that goes to infinity,
there exists a strictly increasing sequence `A = {a₁ < a₂ < …}`
with property P such that `(a_j / j) ≤ f(j)` for all `j`.
-
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1102.exists_sequence_with_P
    (f : ℕ → ℕ) (h_inf : Tendsto f atTop atTop)
    (h_pos : ∀ n, f n ≠ 0) :
    ∃ A : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono A ∧
    HasPropertyP (range A) ∧
    ∀ j : ℕ, (A j : ℝ) / j ≤ f j

statements.name: Erdos1102.erdos_1102.upper_density_Q
statements.doc:
Every sequence with property Q has upper density at most `6 / π^2`.
-
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1102.upper_density_Q
    (A : ℕ → ℕ) (h_inc : StrictMono A)
    (hQ : HasPropertyQ (range A)) :
    limsup (fun j : ℕ  ↦ (j / A j : ℝ)) atTop ≤ 6 / Real.pi^2

statements.name: Erdos1102.erdos_1102.lower_density_Q_exists
statements.doc:
There exists an infinite sequence $A = {a₁ < a₂ < …} ⊂ \mathsf{SF}$ where
$\mathsf{SF} := \mathbb{N} \setminus \bigcup_{p} p^{2}\mathbb{N}$, i.e. the set of
squarefree numbers. The set `A` has property `Q` and natural density `6 / π^2`.
Equivalently, `(j / a_j) → 6/π^2` as `j → ∞`.
-
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1102.lower_density_Q_exists :
    ∃ A : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono A ∧
    (∀ j, Squarefree (A j)) ∧
    HasPropertyQ (range A) ∧
    Tendsto (fun j : ℕ  ↦ (j / A j : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 (6 / Real.pi^2))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1104
problems.doc: *Reference:* https://www.erdosproblems.com/1104

statements.name: Erdos1104.erdos_1104.variants.lower
statements.doc:
Lower bound (Hefty–Horn–King–Pfender 2025).
$$
(1 - o(1)) \sqrt{\frac{n}{\log n}} \le f(n),
$$
where $f(n)$ denotes the maximum chromatic number of a triangle-free graph on
$n$ vertices, formalized as `triangleFreeMaxChromatic n`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1104.variants.lower :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (1 - ε) * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) / Real.sqrt (Real.log (n : ℝ))
        ≤ (triangleFreeMaxChromatic n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1104.erdos_1104.variants.upper
statements.doc:
Upper bound (Davies–Illingworth 2022).
$$
f(n) \le (2 + o(1)) \sqrt{\frac{n}{\log n}},
$$
where $f(n)$ denotes the maximum chromatic number of a triangle-free graph on
$n$ vertices, formalized as `triangleFreeMaxChromatic n`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1104.variants.upper :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (triangleFreeMaxChromatic n : ℝ)
        ≤ (2 + ε) * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) / Real.sqrt (Real.log (n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1105
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1105](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1105)
- [PALOMAR-2026-10-13-000006](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-13-000006&version=1)
- [ESS75] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M. and Sós, V. T., Anti-{R}amsey theorems. (1975), 633--643.
- [MoNe05] Montellano-Ballesteros, J. J. and Neumann-Lara, V., An anti-{R}amsey theorem on cycles.
  Graphs Combin. (2005), 343--354.
- [SiSo84] Simonovits, Miklós and Sós, Vera T., On restricted colourings of {$K_n$}. Combinatorica
  (1984), 101--110.
- [Yu21] L.-T. Yuan, The anti-Ramsey number for paths. arXiv:2102.00807 (2021).

statements.name: Erdos1105.erdos_1105.parts.i
statements.doc:
The anti-Ramsey number $\mathrm{AR}(n,G)$ is the maximum possible number of colours in which the
edges of $K_n$ can be coloured without creating a rainbow copy of $G$ (i.e. one in which all edges
have different colours).

Let $C_k$ be the cycle on $k$ vertices. Is it true that
$\mathrm{AR}(n,C_k)=\left(\frac{k-2}{2}+\frac{1}{k-1}\right)n+O(1)$?

Montellano-Ballesteros and Neumann-Lara [MoNe05] gave an exact formula for $\mathrm{AR}(n,C_k)$,
which implies in particular that
$\mathrm{AR}(n,C_k)=\left(\frac{k-2}{2}+\frac{1}{k-1}\right)n+O(1).$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1105.parts.i :
    ∀ k, 3 ≤ k →
    ((fun n => (antiRamseyNum (cycleGraph k) n : ℝ) - ((k - 2 : ℝ) / 2 + 1 / (k - 1)) * n)
      =O[atTop] (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)))

statements.name: Erdos1105.erdos_1105.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $P_k$ be the path on $k$ vertices and $\ell=\lfloor\frac{k-1}{2}\rfloor$. If $n\geq k\geq 5$
then is $\mathrm{AR}(n,P_k)$ equal to $\max\left(\binom{k-2}{2}+1,
\binom{\ell-1}{2}+(\ell-1)(n-\ell+1)+\epsilon\right)$where $\epsilon=1$ if $k$ is odd and
$\epsilon=2$ otherwise?

A proof of the formula for $\mathrm{AR}(n,P_k)$ for all $n\geq k\geq 5$ has been announced by
Yuan [Yu21].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1105.parts.ii :
    ∀ (k n : ℕ), 5 ≤ k → k ≤ n →
    let ℓ := (k - 1) / 2
    let ε := if Odd k then 1 else 2
    antiRamseyNum (pathGraph k) n = max ((k - 2).choose 2 + 1) ((ℓ - 1).choose 2 +
      (ℓ - 1) * (n - ℓ + 1) + ε)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1106
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1106](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1106)
- [ScWi87] Schinzel, A. and Wirsing, E., Multiplicative properties of the partition function.
  Proc. Indian Acad. Sci. Math. Sci. (1987), 297--303.

statements.name: Erdos1106.erdos_1106.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $p(n)$ be the partition number of $n$ and $F(n)$ be the number of distinct prime factors of
$\prod_{i= 1} ^ {n} p(n)$, then $F(n)$ tends to infinity when $n$ tends to infinity.

The answer is yes: Schinzel and Wirsing [ScWi87] proved $F(n) \gg \log n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1106.parts.i :
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ #(∏ i ∈ Icc 1 n, partitionNumber i).primeFactors) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos1106.erdos_1106.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $p(n)$ be the partition number of $n$ and $F(n)$ be the number of distinct prime factors of
$\prod_{i= 1} ^ {n} p(n)$, $F(n)>n$ for sufficiently large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1106.parts.ii :
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, #(∏ i ∈ Icc 1 n, partitionNumber i).primeFactors > n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1107
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1107](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1107)
- [He88] Heath-Brown, D. R., Ternary quadratic forms and sums of three square-full numbers. (1988)

statements.name: Erdos1107.erdos_1107
statements.doc: Let $r \ge 2$. Is every large integer the sum of at most $r + 1$ many $r$-powerful numbers?
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1107 : ∀ r ≥ 2, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, SumOfRPowerful r n

statements.name: Erdos1107.erdos_1107.variants.two
statements.doc: Heath-Brown [He88] proved every large integer the sum of at most three $2$-powerful numbers.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1107.variants.two : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, SumOfRPowerful 2 n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1108
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1108](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1108)

statements.name: Erdos1108.erdos_1108.parts.i
statements.doc: For each $k \geq 2$, does the set $A = \left\{ \sum_{n\in S}n! : S\subset \mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}\text{ finite}\right\}$ of all finite sums of distinct factorials contain only finitely many $k$-th powers?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1108.parts.i : ∀ k ≥ 2,
    Set.Finite { a | a ∈ FactorialSums ∧ ∃ m : ℕ, m ^ k = a }

statements.name: Erdos1108.erdos_1108.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Does the set $A = \left\{ \sum_{n\in S}n! : S\subset \mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}\text{ finite}\right\}$ of all finite sums of distinct factorials contain only finitely many powerful numbers
(`Nat.Powerful`)?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1108.parts.ii :
     {a ∈ FactorialSums | a.Powerful}.Finite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1109
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1109](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1109)
- [ErSa87] P. Erdős and A. Sárközy, *On divisibility properties of integers of the form
  $a+a'$*, Acta Math. Hungar. (1987), 117--122.
- [Gy01] Katalin Gyarmati, *On divisibility properties of integers of the form $ab+1$*,
  Period. Math. Hungar. (2001), 71--79.
- [Ko04] S. V. Konyagin, *Problems of the set of square-free numbers*,
  Izv. Ross. Akad. Nauk Ser. Mat. (2004), 63--90.
- [Sa92c] G. N. Sárközy, *On a problem of P. Erdős*, Acta Math. Hungar.
  (1992), 271--282.

statements.name: Erdos1109.erdos_1109
statements.doc:
Let $f(N)$ be the size of the largest subset $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that
every $n\in A+A$ is squarefree. Estimate $f(N)$. In particular, is it true that
$f(N)\leq N^{o(1)}$, or even $f(N) \leq (\log N)^{O(1)}$?

This theorem formalizes the subpolynomial bound as `f(N) = O(N^ε)` for every `ε > 0`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1109 :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ),
      (fun N : ℕ => (f N : ℝ)) ≪ fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ) ^ ε

statements.name: Erdos1109.erdos_1109.variants.polylog
statements.doc: Is the stronger polylogarithmic bound $f(N) \leq (\log N)^{O(1)}$ true?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1109.variants.polylog :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ),
      (fun N : ℕ => (f N : ℝ)) ≪ fun N : ℕ => (Real.log N) ^ C

statements.name: Erdos1109.erdos_1109.variants.erdos_sarkozy_lower
statements.doc: Erdős and Sárközy [ErSa87] proved the lower bound $\log N \ll f(N)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1109.variants.erdos_sarkozy_lower :
    (fun N : ℕ => Real.log N) ≪ fun N : ℕ => (f N : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1109.erdos_1109.variants.erdos_sarkozy_upper
statements.doc: Erdős and Sárközy [ErSa87] proved the upper bound $f(N) \ll N^{3/4}\log N$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1109.variants.erdos_sarkozy_upper :
    (fun N : ℕ => (f N : ℝ)) ≪
      fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ) ^ ((3 : ℝ) / 4) * Real.log N

statements.name: Erdos1109.erdos_1109.variants.konyagin_lower
statements.doc:
Konyagin [Ko04] improved the lower bound to
$\log\log N(\log N)^2 \ll f(N)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1109.variants.konyagin_lower :
    (fun N : ℕ => Real.log (Real.log N) * (Real.log N) ^ 2) ≪
      fun N : ℕ => (f N : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1109.erdos_1109.variants.konyagin_upper
statements.doc: Konyagin [Ko04] improved the upper bound to $f(N) \ll N^{11/15+o(1)}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1109.variants.konyagin_upper :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), (fun N : ℕ => (f N : ℝ)) ≪
      fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ) ^ ((11 : ℝ) / 15 + ε)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1110
problems.doc: *Reference:* [Erdős Problem 1110](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1110)

statements.name: Erdos1110.erdos_1110
statements.doc:
Let $p>q\geq 2$ be two coprime integers. We call $n$ representable if it is the sum of
integers of the form $p^kq^l$, none of which divide each other.

If $\{p,q\}\neq \{2,3\}$ then what can be said about the density of non-representable
numbers? Are there infinitely many coprime non-representable numbers, that is, an infinite
family of pairwise coprime non-representable integers?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1110 :
    ∀ (p q : ℕ), q < p → 2 ≤ q →
      Nat.Coprime p q → ¬(p = 3 ∧ q = 2) →
      ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ A.Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧
        ∀ n ∈ A, ¬Representable p q n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1111
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1111](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1111)
- [ElEr85] El-Zahar, M. and Erdős, P., *On the existence of two non-neighboring subgraphs in a
  graph*. Combinatorica 5 (1985), 295-300.
- [NSS24] Nguyen, T., Scott, A. and Seymour, P., *On a problem of El-Zahar and Erdős*.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 165 (2024), 211-222. [arXiv:2303.13449](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.13449)
- [Wa80b] Wagon, S., *A bound on the chromatic number of graphs without certain induced
  subgraphs*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 29 (1980), 345-346.

statements.name: Erdos1111.erdos_1111
statements.doc:
If $G$ is a finite graph and $A,B$ are disjoint sets of vertices then we call $A,B$ anticomplete
if there are no edges between $A$ and $B$.

If $t,c\geq 1$ then there exists $d\geq 1$ such that if $\chi(G)\geq d$ and $\omega(G)<t$ then
there are anticomplete sets $A,B$ with $\chi(A)\geq \chi(B)\geq c$.

El-Zahar and Erdős [ElEr85] pose this as a question. Here $\chi(A)$ is the chromatic number of
the induced subgraph $G[A]$. Swapping $A$ and $B$, the conclusion says that both $\chi(A)$ and
$\chi(B)$ are at least $c$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1111 :
    ∀ t c : ℕ, 1 ≤ t → 1 ≤ c → ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧
      ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        (d : ℕ∞) ≤ G.chromaticNumber → G.CliqueFree t →
          ∃ A B : Set V, Anticomplete G A B ∧
            (c : ℕ∞) ≤ (G.induce A).chromaticNumber ∧
            (c : ℕ∞) ≤ (G.induce B).chromaticNumber

statements.name: Erdos1111.erdos_1111.variants.wagon
statements.doc:
El-Zahar and Erdős note that a result of Wagon [Wa80b] implies $d(t,2)\leq \binom{t}{2}+1$, where
$d(t,c)$ is the minimal $d$ in the problem.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1111.variants.wagon (t : ℕ) :
    ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ((t.choose 2 + 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ G.chromaticNumber → G.CliqueFree t →
        ∃ A B : Set V, Anticomplete G A B ∧
          2 ≤ (G.induce A).chromaticNumber ∧ 2 ≤ (G.induce B).chromaticNumber

statements.name: Erdos1111.erdos_1111.variants.el_zahar_erdos
statements.doc: El-Zahar and Erdős [ElEr85] proved the case $c = 3$: $d(t,3)$ exists for every $t$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1111.variants.el_zahar_erdos :
    ∀ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t → ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧
      ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        (d : ℕ∞) ≤ G.chromaticNumber → G.CliqueFree t →
          ∃ A B : Set V, Anticomplete G A B ∧
            3 ≤ (G.induce A).chromaticNumber ∧ 3 ≤ (G.induce B).chromaticNumber

statements.name: Erdos1111.erdos_1111.variants.three_three
statements.doc: El-Zahar and Erdős [ElEr85] proved $d(3,3)\leq 8$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1111.variants.three_three :
    ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      8 ≤ G.chromaticNumber → G.CliqueFree 3 →
        ∃ A B : Set V, Anticomplete G A B ∧
          3 ≤ (G.induce A).chromaticNumber ∧ 3 ≤ (G.induce B).chromaticNumber

statements.name: Erdos1111.erdos_1111.variants.nguyen_scott_seymour
statements.doc:
Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour [NSS24] prove that if $t,c\geq 1$ then there exists $d\geq 1$ such
that if $\chi(G)\geq d$ and $\omega(G)<t$ then there are anticomplete sets $A,B$ with
$\chi(B)\geq c$ and such that the minimum degree of the induced graph on $A$ is at least $c$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1111.variants.nguyen_scott_seymour :
    ∀ t c : ℕ, 1 ≤ t → 1 ≤ c → ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧
      ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        (d : ℕ∞) ≤ G.chromaticNumber → G.CliqueFree t →
          ∃ A B : Set V, Anticomplete G A B ∧
            A.Nonempty ∧ (∀ v ∈ A, c ≤ (A ∩ G.neighborSet v).ncard) ∧
            (c : ℕ∞) ≤ (G.induce B).chromaticNumber

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1113
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1113](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1113)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L., Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial
  Number Theory. Monographie de l'Enseignement Mathématique, No. 28 (1980).
- [Si60] Sierpiński, W., Elementary Theory of Numbers. Państwowe Wydawnictwo Naukowe,
  Warsaw (1960).
- [FFK08] Filaseta, M., Finch, C., and Kozek, M., On powers associated with Sierpiński numbers,
  Riesel numbers and Polignac's conjecture. Journal of Number Theory 128 (2008), 1916–1940.

A positive odd integer $k$ is a *Sierpiński number* if $k \cdot 2^n + 1$ is composite for all
$n \geq 0$. A *covering set* for $k$ is a finite set of primes $P$ such that every number of
the form $k \cdot 2^n + 1$ is divisible by at least one prime in $P$.

Sierpiński (1960) proved that infinitely many Sierpiński numbers exist using covering systems.
The smallest known Sierpiński number is 78557 (Selfridge). Erdős and Graham conjectured that
there exist Sierpiński numbers with no finite covering set. A negative answer would imply
infinitely many Fermat primes.

Note: The notion of a covering set for a Sierpiński number is closely related to a
`CoveringSystem` of $\mathbb{Z}$ (see
`FormalConjecturesForMathlib.NumberTheory.CoveringSystem`): a finite covering set of primes
for $k$ works because the exponents $n$ for which each prime divides $k \cdot 2^n + 1$ form
residue classes whose union covers all of $\mathbb{Z}$, i.e. a covering system.

See also Erdős Problems [203](https://www.erdosproblems.com/203) and
[276](https://www.erdosproblems.com/276).

statements.name: Erdos1113.erdos_1113.variants.infinitely_many_sierpinski
statements.doc:
Sierpiński [Si60] proved that there are infinitely many Sierpiński numbers, using covering
systems to construct suitable covering sets for any $k$ satisfying a certain congruence.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1113.variants.infinitely_many_sierpinski :
    Set.Infinite {k : ℕ | k.IsSierpinskiNumber}

statements.name: Erdos1113.erdos_1113
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 1113.** Do there exist Sierpiński numbers that possess no finite covering set
of primes?

Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] conjectured that the answer is yes. A negative answer would imply
that there are infinitely many Fermat primes.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1113 :
    ∃ k, k.IsSierpinskiNumber ∧ ¬ HasFinitePrimeCoveringSet k

statements.name: Erdos1113.erdos_1113.variants.filaseta_finch_kozek
statements.doc:
**Filaseta–Finch–Kozek conjecture (2008).** Every Sierpiński number is either a perfect power
or possesses a finite covering set of primes.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1113.variants.filaseta_finch_kozek :
    ∀ k, k.IsSierpinskiNumber →
      k.IsPerfectPower ∨ HasFinitePrimeCoveringSet k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1114
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1114](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1114)
- [Ba60b] Bálint, Elemér, *Proof of a conjecture of P. Erdős* (Hungarian: *Erdős Pál egy
  sejtésének bizonyítása*). Mat. Lapok 11 (1960), 33-40.
- [Lo76] Lorch, L., *Some monotonicity properties of polynomials with equally spaced zeros*.
  Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 27 (1976), 293-300.

statements.name: Erdos1114.erdos_1114
statements.doc:
Let $f(x)\in \mathbb{R}[x]$ be a polynomial of degree $n$ whose roots $\{a_0<\cdots<a_n\}$ are
all real and form an arithmetic progression.

The differences between consecutive zeros of $f'(x)$, beginning from the midpoint of $(a_0,a_n)$
towards the endpoints, are monotonically increasing.

Proved by Bálint [Ba60b]; some generalisations were given by Lorch [Lo76]. We take $f$ of
degree $N+1$ with the $N+1$ roots $a+jd$ ($0\le j\le N$, $d>0$), since the number of roots must
equal the degree, and read "increasing" as non-decreasing. Here `b k` is the zero of $f'$ in
$(a+kd,a+(k+1)d)$, which exists and is the only zero there by Rolle's theorem (see
`erdos_1114.variants.rolle`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1114 {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) {a d : ℝ} (hd : 0 < d) {f : ℝ[X]} {b : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hdegree : f.natDegree = N + 1)
    (hroots : ∀ j : ℕ, j ≤ N → f.eval (a + d * j) = 0)
    (hb : ∀ k : ℕ, k < N → b k ∈ Set.Ioo (a + d * k) (a + d * (k + 1)))
    (hderiv : ∀ k : ℕ, k < N → f.derivative.eval (b k) = 0) :
    RightGapMonotone N b ∧ GapSymmetric N b

statements.name: Erdos1114.erdos_1114.variants.rolle
statements.doc:
All the zeros of $f'(x)$ are all distinct real numbers in $(a_0,a_n)$ by Rolle's theorem.

Precisely, for $f$ as in `erdos_1114` (degree $N+1$, roots $a+jd$ for $0\le j\le N$), each
interval $(a+kd,a+(k+1)d)$ with $k<N$ contains exactly one zero of $f'$, and every zero of $f'$
lies in one of these intervals.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1114.variants.rolle {N : ℕ} {a d : ℝ} (hd : 0 < d) {f : ℝ[X]}
    (hdegree : f.natDegree = N + 1)
    (hroots : ∀ j : ℕ, j ≤ N → f.eval (a + d * j) = 0) :
    (∀ k : ℕ, k < N →
      ∃! x : ℝ, x ∈ Set.Ioo (a + d * k) (a + d * (k + 1)) ∧ f.derivative.eval x = 0) ∧
    (∀ x : ℝ, f.derivative.eval x = 0 →
      ∃ k : ℕ, k < N ∧ x ∈ Set.Ioo (a + d * k) (a + d * (k + 1)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1115
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1115](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1115)
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., *Research problems in function theory: new problems*. Proceedings of
  the Symposium on Complex Analysis (Canterbury, 1973), London Math. Soc. Lecture Note Ser. 12
  (1974), 155--180.
- [HaLi18] Hayman, W. K. and Lingham, E. F., *Research problems in function theory*.
  [arXiv:1809.07200](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200) (2018).
- [GoEr79] Gol'dberg, A. A. and Erëmenko, A. È., *On asymptotic curves of entire functions of
  finite order*. Mat. Sb. (N.S.) (1979), 555--581, 647. English translation: Math. USSR-Sb. 37
  (1980), 509--533. [Math-Net.Ru](https://www.mathnet.ru/eng/sm2401)
- [Ha60b] Hayman, W. K., *Slowly growing integral and subharmonic functions*. Comment. Math.
  Helv. 34 (1960), 75--84.

statements.name: Erdos1115.erdos_1115
statements.doc:
Let $f(z)$ be an entire function of finite order, and let $\Gamma$ be a rectifiable path on which
$f(z)\to \infty$. Let $\ell(r)$ be the length of $\Gamma$ in the disc $\lvert z\rvert<r$.

Find a path for which $\ell(r)$ grows as slowly as possible, and estimate $\ell(r)$ in terms of
$M(r)=\max_{\lvert z\rvert=r}\lvert f(z)\rvert$.

In particular, can such a path $\Gamma$ be found for which $\ell(r)\ll r$?

This is Problem 2.41 of [Ha74], where it is attributed to Erdős; see also [HaLi18, Problem 2.41].
The answer is no: Gol'dberg and Eremenko [GoEr79] proved that for every $\rho\in[0,\infty]$ there
is an entire function $f$ of order $\rho$ such that, for any asymptotic curve $\Gamma$ on which
$f\to\infty$, the length of $\Gamma$ in $\lvert z\rvert\leq r$ is not $O(r)$ (see also [HaLi18,
Updates 2.7 and 2.41]). The length in $\lvert z\rvert\leq r$ is at most the length in
$\lvert z\rvert<2r$, so $\ell(r)=O(r)$ for the open disc used here would make the length in the
closed disc $O(r)$ too.

We formalise the last question only: the first part asks for a best possible path and an estimate
in terms of $M(r)$ and has no precise claim to state, so it is not formalised. Reading choices:
$f$ is non-constant (a constant has no path on which $f\to\infty$, which would make the statement
trivially true); finite order is `Erdos516.OfFiniteOrder`; $\Gamma$ is given by its arc length
parametrisation `γ` (every rectifiable path on which $f\to\infty$ has infinite length and can be
reparametrised by arc length, without changing the curve traversed or the length in any disc);
$\ell(r)\ll r$ means $\ell(r)\le Cr$ for some $C$ and all large $r$.

[HaLi18, Problem 2.41] also report that Hayman [Ha60b] (and Piranian) showed that if
$\log M(r)=O((\log r)^2)$, one can take for $\Gamma$ a ray from the origin, so that $\ell(r)=r$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1115 :
    ¬ ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, Erdos516.OfFiniteOrder f → (¬ ∃ a : ℂ, ∀ z, f z = a) →
      ∃ γ : ℝ → ℂ, IsAsymptoticPath f γ ∧
        ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ r : ℝ in atTop, lengthInDisc γ r ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * r)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1116
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1116](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1116)
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., *Research problems in function theory: new problems*. Proceedings of
  the Symposium on Complex Analysis (Canterbury, 1973), London Math. Soc. Lecture Note Ser. 12
  (1974), 155--180.
- [To76] Toppila, Sakari, *On the counting function for the $a$-values of a meromorphic
  function*. Ann. Acad. Sci. Fenn. Ser. A I Math. 2 (1976), 565--572.
  [PDF](https://www.acadsci.fi/mathematica/Vol02/vol02pp565-572.pdf)
- [Go78] Gol'dberg, A. A., *Counting functions of sequences of $a$-points for entire
  functions*. Sibirsk. Mat. Zh. 19 (1978), 28--36, 236.
- [HaLi18] Hayman, W. K. and Lingham, E. F., *Research problems in function theory*.
  [arXiv:1809.07200](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200) (2018).

statements.name: Erdos1116.erdos_1116
statements.doc:
For a meromorphic function $f$ let $n(r,a)$ count the number of roots of $f(z)=a$ in the disc
$\lvert z\rvert <r$. Does there exist a meromorphic (or entire) $f$ such that for every
$a\neq b$
$$\limsup_{r\to \infty}\frac{n(r,a)}{n(r,b)}=\infty?$$

This is Problem 1.25 in [Ha74], where it is attributed to Erdős. Gol'dberg [Go78] and Toppila
[To76, Theorem 3] constructed such entire functions. We state this case, for finite
$a\neq b$, using `UnboundedCountRatio`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1116 :
    ∃ f : ℂ → ℂ, Differentiable ℂ f ∧
      ∀ a b : ℂ, a ≠ b → UnboundedCountRatio f a b

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1119
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1119](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1119)
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.
- [Er64g] Erdős, P., An interpolation problem associated with the continuum hypothesis.
  Michigan Math. J. (1964), 9--10.
- [KuSh17] Kumar, Ashutosh and Shelah, Saharon, On a question about families of entire
  functions. Fund. Math. (2017), 279--288.
- [ScWe24] Schilhan, Jonathan and Weinert, Thilo, Wetzel families and the continuum.
  J. Lond. Math. Soc. (2) (2024), Paper No. e12918, 27.

statements.name: Erdos1119.erdos_1119
statements.doc:
Let $\mathfrak{m}$ be an infinite cardinal with $\aleph_0 < \mathfrak{m} < \mathfrak{c} =
2^{\aleph_0}$. Let $\{f_\alpha\}$ be a family of entire functions such that, for every
$z_0 \in \mathbb{C}$, there are at most $\mathfrak{m}$ distinct values of $f_\alpha(z_0)$.
Must $\{f_\alpha\}$ have cardinality at most $\mathfrak{m}$?

This is Problem 2.46 in [Ha74], where it is attributed to Erdős. The question is
**independent of ZFC**: the headline statement is neither provable nor refutable from the
usual axioms of set theory, so its `sorry` cannot be filled either way.

The answer is yes if $\mathfrak{m}^+ < \mathfrak{c}$ (see
`erdos_1119.variants.easy_case`), so the question reduces to the case
$\mathfrak{m}^+ = \mathfrak{c}$, where it is undecidable: Kumar and Shelah [KuSh17]
produced a model of $\mathfrak{c} = \aleph_2$ in which the answer is yes (with
$\mathfrak{m} = \aleph_1$), while Schilhan and Weinert [ScWe24] produced a different
model of $\mathfrak{c} = \aleph_2$ in which the answer is no.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1119 :
    ∀ (m : Cardinal.{0}), ℵ₀ < m → m < 𝔠 →
    ∀ F : Set (ℂ → ℂ), (∀ f ∈ F, Differentiable ℂ f) →
      (∀ z₀ : ℂ, #{y : ℂ | ∃ f ∈ F, f z₀ = y} ≤ m) →
      #F ≤ m

statements.name: Erdos1119.erdos_1119.variants.easy_case
statements.doc:
The 'easy' case of Erdős Problem 1119: if moreover $\mathfrak{m}^+ < \mathfrak{c}$, then
any family of entire functions taking at most $\mathfrak{m}$ distinct values at each
point has cardinality at most $\mathfrak{m}$. In [Ha74] it is written that this is
'easy to see'.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1119.variants.easy_case (m : Cardinal.{0}) (hm : ℵ₀ < m)
    (hsucc : succ m < 𝔠) (F : Set (ℂ → ℂ))
    (hF : ∀ f ∈ F, Differentiable ℂ f)
    (hval : ∀ z₀ : ℂ, #{y : ℂ | ∃ f ∈ F, f z₀ = y} ≤ m) :
    #F ≤ m

statements.name: Erdos1119.erdos_1119.variants.erdos_wetzel
statements.doc:
Erdős's theorem [Er64g], answering a question of Wetzel: if $\mathfrak{c} > \aleph_1$,
then every family of entire functions taking only countably many distinct values at each
point $z_0 \in \mathbb{C}$ is itself countable.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1119.variants.erdos_wetzel (h : ℵ_ 1 < 𝔠) (F : Set (ℂ → ℂ))
    (hF : ∀ f ∈ F, Differentiable ℂ f)
    (hval : ∀ z₀ : ℂ, {y : ℂ | ∃ f ∈ F, f z₀ = y}.Countable) :
    F.Countable

statements.name: Erdos1119.erdos_1119.variants.erdos_wetzel_ch
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er64g] also showed that the previous statement fails under the continuum
hypothesis: if $\mathfrak{c} = \aleph_1$, then there is an **uncountable** family of
entire functions taking only countably many distinct values at each point
$z_0 \in \mathbb{C}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1119.variants.erdos_wetzel_ch (h : 𝔠 = ℵ_ 1) :
    ∃ F : Set (ℂ → ℂ), (∀ f ∈ F, Differentiable ℂ f) ∧
      (∀ z₀ : ℂ, {y : ℂ | ∃ f ∈ F, f z₀ = y}.Countable) ∧
      ¬ F.Countable

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1121
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1121](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1121)
- [BeLi16] Bezdek, Károly and Litvak, Alexander E., *Packing convex bodies by cylinders*.
  Discrete Comput. Geom. (2016), 725-738.
- [GoGo45] Goodman, A. W. and Goodman, R. E., *A circle covering theorem*. Amer. Math. Monthly
  (1945), 494-498.
- [Ha47] Hadwiger, H., *Nonseparable convex systems*. Amer. Math. Monthly (1947), 583-585.

statements.name: Erdos1121.erdos_1121
statements.doc:
If $C_1,\ldots,C_n$ are circles in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with radii $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ such that no line
disjoint from all the circles divides them into two non-empty sets then the circles can be
covered by a circle of radius $r=\sum r_i$.

This is true, and was proved by Goodman and Goodman [GoGo45] (whose proof also generalises to
higher dimensions). A generalisation to convex bodies was proved by Hadwiger [Ha47].

An alternative proof is given by Bezdek and Litvak [BeLi16].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1121 {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → ℝ²) (r : Fin n → ℝ) (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i)
    (hsep : ∀ (v : ℝ²) (t : ℝ), v ≠ 0 →
      (∀ i, ∀ p ∈ Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i), inner ℝ v p ≠ t) →
      (∀ i, inner ℝ v (c i) < t) ∨ (∀ i, t < inner ℝ v (c i))) :
    ∃ z : ℝ², (⋃ i, Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i)) ⊆ Metric.closedBall z (∑ i, r i)

statements.name: Erdos1121.erdos_1121.variants.higher_dimension
statements.doc:
The proof of Goodman and Goodman [GoGo45] also generalises to higher dimensions: if
$B_1,\ldots,B_n$ are balls in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with radii $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ such that no hyperplane
disjoint from all the balls divides them into two non-empty sets then the balls can be covered by
a ball of radius $r=\sum r_i$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1121.variants.higher_dimension {d n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (r : Fin n → ℝ) (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i)
    (hsep : ∀ (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (t : ℝ), v ≠ 0 →
      (∀ i, ∀ p ∈ Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i), inner ℝ v p ≠ t) →
      (∀ i, inner ℝ v (c i) < t) ∨ (∀ i, t < inner ℝ v (c i))) :
    ∃ z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
      (⋃ i, Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i)) ⊆ Metric.closedBall z (∑ i, r i)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1122
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1122](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1122)
- [Er46] Erdős, P., *On the distribution function of additive functions*. Annals of Math. (1946),
  1-20.
- [Ma22] Mangerel, Alexander P., *Additive functions in short intervals, gaps and a conjecture of
  Erdős*. Ramanujan J. (2022), 1023--1090.

statements.name: Erdos1122.erdos_1122
statements.doc:
Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to \mathbb{R}$ be an additive function (i.e. $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$ whenever
$(a,b)=1$). Let
$$A=\{ n \geq 1: f(n+1)< f(n)\}.$$
If $\lvert A\cap [1,X]\rvert =o(X)$ then must $f(n)=c\log n$ for some $c\in \mathbb{R}$?

The condition $\lvert A\cap [1,X]\rvert =o(X)$ says that $A$ has natural density $0$.

Partial progress was made by Mangerel [Ma22], who proved that this is true for completely
additive $f$ if
$$\lvert A\cap [1,X]\rvert \ll \frac{X}{(\log X)^{2+c}}$$
for some $c>0$, and if $f(p)$ does not have very large values (in a certain technical sense).

See also `erdos_491`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1122 : ∀ f : ℕ → ℝ,
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    {n | 1 ≤ n ∧ f (n + 1) < f n}.HasDensity 0 →
    ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ n > 0, f n = c * Real.log n

statements.name: Erdos1122.erdos_1122.variants.monotone
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er46] proved that $f(n)=c\log n$ for some $c\in\mathbb{R}$ if $A$ is empty, that is, if
$f(n) \leq f(n+1)$ for all $n \geq 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1122.variants.monotone (f : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b)
    (hmono : ∀ n ≥ 1, f n ≤ f (n + 1)) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ n > 0, f n = c * Real.log n

statements.name: Erdos1122.erdos_1122.variants.sub_tendsto_zero
statements.doc: Erdős [Er46] proved that $f(n)=c\log n$ for some $c\in\mathbb{R}$ if $f(n+1)-f(n)=o(1)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1122.variants.sub_tendsto_zero (f : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b)
    (hdiff : Tendsto (fun n ↦ f (n + 1) - f n) atTop (𝓝 0)) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ n > 0, f n = c * Real.log n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1125
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1125](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1125)
- [Er81b] Erdős, P., *My Scottish Book 'Problems'*. The Scottish Book (1981), 27-35.
- [Ke69] Kemperman, J. H. B., *On the regularity of generalized convex functions*. Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. (1969), 69-93.
- [La84] Laczkovich, M., *On Kemperman's inequality $2f(x)\leq f(x+h)+f(x+2h)$*. Colloq. Math. (1984), 109-115.

statements.name: Erdos1125.erdos_1125
statements.doc:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}$ be such that
$$2f(x) \leq f(x+h)+f(x+2h)$$
for every $x\in \mathbb{R}$ and $h>0$. Must $f$ be monotonic?

A problem of Kemperman [Ke69], who proved it is true if $f$ is measurable. Erdős [Er81b] wrote 'if it were my problem I would offer \$500 for it'. This was solved by Laczkovich [La84].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1125 : ∀ (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ x : ℝ, ∀ h : ℝ, h > 0 → 2 * f x ≤ f (x + h) + f (x + 2 * h)),
    Monotone f

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1126
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1126](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1126)
- [Er60c] Erdős, P., *Problem 310*. Colloq. Math., 311.
- [dB66] de Bruijn, N. G., *On almost additive functions*. Colloq. Math. (1966), 59-63.
- [Ju65] Jurkat, Wolfgang B., *On Cauchy's functional equation*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1965), 683-686.

statements.name: Erdos1126.erdos_1126
statements.doc:
If
$$f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$$
for almost all $x,y\in \mathbb{R}$ then there exists a function $g$ such that
$$g(x+y)=g(x)+g(y)$$
for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$ such that $f(x)=g(x)$ for almost all $x$.

Proved independently by de Bruijn [dB66] and Jurkat [Ju65].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1126 : ∀
    (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (h :
      ∀ᵐ (p : ℝ × ℝ) ∂(volume.prod volume),
        f (p.1 + p.2) = f p.1 + f p.2),
    ∃ h : ℝ → ℝ,
      (∀ x y, h (x + y) = h x + h y) ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂volume, f x = h x)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1128
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1128](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1128)

statements.name: Erdos1128.erdos_1128.prikryMills
statements.doc:
**Prikry–Mills counterexample** (key lemma):

There exists a 2-colouring $f$ of a set of cardinality $\aleph_1$ cubed such that
no countable box $A_1 \times B_1 \times C_1$ is monochromatic.

This is the unpublished result of Prikry and Mills (1978). The proof proceeds by
transfinite induction along $\omega_1$, which has uncountable cofinality, ensuring
every countable box is non-monochromatic.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1128.prikryMills :
    ∃ (X : Type) (_ : #X = aleph 1) (f : X → X → X → Fin 2),
      ∀ (A₁ B₁ C₁ : Set X),
        #A₁ = aleph 0 → #B₁ = aleph 0 → #C₁ = aleph 0 →
        ¬ IsMonochromaticBox f A₁ B₁ C₁

statements.name: Erdos1128.erdos_1128
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 1128** (disproved by Prikry–Mills, 1978):

Erdős asked whether every 2-colouring of $A \times B \times C$, where
$|A| = |B| = |C| = \aleph_1$, must contain a monochromatic countable box
$A_1 \times B_1 \times C_1$ with $|A_1| = |B_1| = |C_1| = \aleph_0$.

The answer is **No**: Prikry and Mills constructed a 2-colouring of $\omega_1^3$
with no monochromatic countable box.

Note: The positive statement asserts that every 2-colouring of every $\aleph_1^3$
contains a monochromatic countably infinite box. Since the answer is False, this
positive statement fails.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1128 :
    ¬ ∀ (A B C : Type) (_ : #A = aleph 1) (_ : #B = aleph 1) (_ : #C = aleph 1)
      (f : A → B → C → Fin 2),
      ∃ (A₁ : Set A) (B₁ : Set B) (C₁ : Set C),
        #A₁ = aleph 0 ∧ #B₁ = aleph 0 ∧ #C₁ = aleph 0 ∧
        IsMonochromaticBox f A₁ B₁ C₁

statements.name: Erdos1128.erdos_1128.variants.prikryMills_explicit
statements.doc:
**Explicit form of Prikry–Mills**:

There exists a 2-colouring of $\omega_1 \times \omega_1 \times \omega_1$ such that
for every countably infinite $A_1, B_1, C_1 \subseteq \omega_1$, the box
$A_1 \times B_1 \times C_1$ is not monochromatic.

This is the content of the Prikry–Mills theorem (1978, unpublished), stated
using Lean's ordinal type `{o : Ordinal // o < ω_ 1}` as the
representation of $\omega_1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1128.variants.prikryMills_explicit :
    ∃ (f : {o : Ordinal // o < ω_ 1} →
           {o : Ordinal // o < ω_ 1} →
           {o : Ordinal // o < ω_ 1} → Fin 2),
      ∀ (A₁ B₁ C₁ : Set {o : Ordinal // o < ω_ 1}),
        #A₁ = aleph 0 → #B₁ = aleph 0 → #C₁ = aleph 0 →
        ¬ IsMonochromaticBox f A₁ B₁ C₁

statements.name: Erdos1128.erdos_1128.variants.two_dimensional_false
statements.doc:
The claim that every 2-colouring of $\omega_1 \times \omega_1$ has an uncountable
monochromatic product rectangle is **false** in ZFC.

**Counterexample:** The ordering colouring $f(\alpha, \beta) = 0$ iff $\alpha < \beta$
has no uncountable monochromatic product rectangle $A_1 \times B_1$.

**Proof:** If $A_1 \times B_1$ were monochromatic with colour 0, then every element of
$A_1$ would be strictly less than every element of $B_1$, making $A_1$ bounded above in
$\omega_1$; but any bounded subset of $\omega_1$ is countable (since initial segments are
countable), contradicting $A_1$ being uncountable. The colour-1 case is symmetric with
the roles of $A_1$ and $B_1$ swapped.

Note: For 2-colourings of unordered pairs the analogous statement also fails: Sierpiński
showed $\omega_1 \not\to (\omega_1)^2_2$. The Erdős–Rado theorem gives
$(2^{\aleph_0})^+ \to (\aleph_1)^2_{\aleph_0}$ instead.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1128.variants.two_dimensional_false :
    ¬ ∀ (f : Omega1 → Omega1 → Fin 2),
        ∃ (A₁ B₁ : Set Omega1),
          ¬ A₁.Countable ∧ ¬ B₁.Countable ∧
          ∃ c : Fin 2, ∀ a ∈ A₁, ∀ b ∈ B₁, f a b = c

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1133
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1133](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1133)
- [Er67] Erdős, P., Problems and results on the convergence and divergence properties of the
  Lagrange interpolation polynomials and some extremal problems. Mathematica (Cluj) (1967), 65-73.
- [Ya26] Yang, J.-Q., *Erdős's Robust Polynomial Interpolation Problem: the Optimal Exponential
  Scale*. [arXiv:2609.14769](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14769) (2026).

statements.name: Erdos1133.erdos_1133
statements.doc:
Let $C>0$. There exists $\epsilon>0$ such that if $n$ is sufficiently large the following holds.

For any $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in [-1,1]$ there exist $y_1,\ldots,y_n\in [-1,1]$ such that, if $P$ is a
polynomial of degree $m<(1+\epsilon)n$ with $P(x_i)=y_i$ for at least $(1-\epsilon)n$ many
$1\leq i\leq n$, then $$\max_{x\in [-1,1]}\lvert P(x)\rvert >C.$$

Yang [Ya26, Theorem 2.1] proved this, including repeated nodes, by taking $\rho=0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1133 :
    ∀ C > (0 : ℝ), ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ x : Fin n → Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1,
        ∃ y : Fin n → Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1,
          ∀ P : Polynomial ℝ,
            (P.natDegree : ℝ) < (1 + ε) * (n : ℝ) →
            ((Finset.univ.filter (fun i ↦ P.eval (x i : ℝ) = (y i : ℝ))).card : ℝ) ≥
              (1 - ε) * (n : ℝ) →
            ∃ z ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1, |P.eval z| > C

statements.name: Erdos1133.erdos_1133.variants.weaker
statements.doc:
Erdős proved that, for any $C>0$, there exists $\epsilon>0$ such that if $n$ is sufficiently
large and $m=\lfloor (1+\epsilon)n\rfloor$ then for any $x_1,\ldots,x_m\in [-1,1]$ there is a
polynomial $P$ of degree $n$ such that $\lvert P(x_i)\rvert\leq 1$ for $1\leq i\leq m$ and
$\max_{x\in [-1,1]}\lvert P(x)\rvert>C$. The robust interpolation statement above also implies
this result. Erdős in [Er67] could not prove the robust statement even for $m=n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1133.variants.weaker :
    ∀ C > (0 : ℝ), ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      let m := ⌊(1 + ε) * (n : ℝ)⌋₊;
      ∀ x : Fin m → Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1,
        ∃ P : Polynomial ℝ,
          P.natDegree = n ∧
          (∀ i : Fin m, |P.eval (x i : ℝ)| ≤ 1) ∧
          ∃ z ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1, |P.eval z| > C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1134
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1134](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1134)
- [La16] Lagarias, Jeffrey C., *Erdős, Klarner, and the $3x+1$ problem*. Amer. Math. Monthly
  (2016), 753--776.
- [KlRa74] Klarner, D. A. and Rado, R., *Arithmetic properties of certain recursively defined
  sets*. Pacific J. Math. (1974), 445--463.
- [Kl82] Klarner, David A., *A sufficient condition for certain semigroups to be free*. J. Algebra
  (1982), 140--148.
- [Gu83b] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved Problems: Don't Try to Solve These Problems*. Amer. Math.
  Monthly (1983), 35--38+39--41.
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.

statements.name: Erdos1134.erdos_1134
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be the smallest set which contains $1$ and is closed under the
operations
$$x\mapsto 2x+1,\quad x\mapsto 3x+1,\quad x\mapsto 6x+1.$$
Does $A$ have positive lower density?

Lagarias [La16] reports that Erdős asked this in 1972, offering £10 for a solution. (Although
Hilton told Lagarias that this problem may have been formulated by Klarner, and that Erdős liked
it and offered a prize for its solution.)

Erdős had earlier proved (as reported in [KlRa74]) that if $A$ is the smallest set which contains
$1$ and is closed under the operations $x\mapsto m_ix+b_i$ for some (possibly infinite) collection
of $m_i\geq 1$ and $b_i\geq 0$ then, if $\sigma>0$ is such that $\sum \frac{1}{m_i^\sigma}=1$
then, for all large $X$, $\lvert A\cap [1,X]\rvert \ll X^{\sigma+o(1)}$. This result does not
help with the given problem since $\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{6}=1$.

This was answered in the negative soon afterwards by Crampin and Hilton (as reported in [Kl82]),
who proved that in fact, for all large $X$, $\lvert A\cap [1,X]\rvert \ll X^{\tau+o(1)}$ where
$\tau\approx 0.900626$ is the unique positive root of
$$6^{-\tau}+\sum_{k\geq 0}(3\cdot 2^k)^{-\tau}=1.$$
Their proof is given in [La16]. This problem is repeated by Guy [Gu83b] in an article called
'Don't Try to Solve These Problems'. This is Problem E36 in Guy's collection [Gu04].
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1134 : ¬ 0 < A.lowerDensity

statements.name: Erdos1134.erdos_1134.variants.sublinear
statements.doc:
The counting function of $A$ is sublinear: $\lvert A\cap [1,X]\rvert \ll X^{\tau+o(1)}$ with
$\tau < 1$, so in particular $\lvert A \cap [1, X]\rvert \ll X^{19/20}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1134.variants.sublinear :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ X : ℕ, ((A ∩ Set.Iic X).ncard : ℝ) ≤ C * (X : ℝ) ^ (19 / 20 : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1134.erdos_1134.variants.klarner
statements.doc:
Klarner has several (open) variants of this problem - see Section 8.9 of [La16]. For example, it
is unknown if the smallest set $A$ which contains $0$ and is closed under
$$x\mapsto 2x,\quad x\mapsto 3x+2,\quad x\mapsto 6x+3$$
has positive density.

The answer is negative: Kenta Kitamura (KitaKen1 on GitHub) has given a Lean proof
([erdos-1134-lean](https://github.com/KitaKen1/erdos-1134-lean)) that $A$ has natural density $0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1134.variants.klarner :
    ¬ 0 < (⋂₀ {S : Set ℕ | 0 ∈ S ∧
      ∀ x ∈ S, 2 * x ∈ S ∧ 3 * x + 2 ∈ S ∧ 6 * x + 3 ∈ S}).lowerDensity

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1135
problems.doc:
The Collatz conjecture states that for any positive integer $n$, there exists a natural
number $m$ such that the $m$-th term of the sequence is 1.

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1135](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1135)
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
- [La10] Lagarias, Jeffrey C., The {$3x+1$} problem: an overview. (2010), 3--29.
- [La16] Lagarias, Jeffrey C., Erdős, Klarner, and the {$3x+1$} problem. Amer. Math. Monthly
  (2016), 753--776.
- [La85] Lagarias, Jeffrey C., The {$3x+1$} problem and its generalizations. Amer. Math. Monthly
  (1985), 3--23.

This file points to the canonical formalization in
`FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.CollatzConjecture`.

statements.name: Erdos1135.erdos_1135
statements.doc:
The Collatz conjecture states that for any positive integer $n$, there exists a natural
number $m$ such that the $m$-th term of the sequence is 1.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1135 : type_of% CollatzConjecture.collatz_conjecture

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1136
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1136](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1136)
- [Mu11] Müller, Helmut, *Über ein additiv-zahlentheoretisches Problem von P. Erdős*.
  Mitt. Math. Ges. Hamburg (2011), 75-78.

statements.name: Erdos1136.erdos_1136
statements.doc:
Does there exist $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ with lower density $>1/3$ such that $a+b\neq 2^k$ for
any $a,b\in A$ and $k\geq 0$?

Müller [Mu11] settled this question in the affirmative: in fact one can take $A$ to be
the set of all integers congruent to $3\cdot 2^i\pmod{2^{i+2}}$ for any $i\geq 0$, which has
density $1/2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1136 :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, (1 / 3 : ℝ) < A.lowerDensity ∧ AvoidsPowersOfTwo A

statements.name: Erdos1136.erdos_1136.variants.multiples_of_three
statements.doc: Achieving density $1/3$ is trivial, taking $A$ to be all multiples of $3$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1136.variants.multiples_of_three :
    AvoidsPowersOfTwo {n : ℕ | 3 ∣ n} ∧ Set.HasDensity {n : ℕ | 3 ∣ n} (1 / 3)

statements.name: Erdos1136.erdos_1136.variants.mueller
statements.doc:
Müller [Mu11] settled this question in the affirmative: in fact one can take $A$ to be
the set of all integers congruent to $3\cdot 2^i\pmod{2^{i+2}}$ for any $i\geq 0$, which has
density $1/2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1136.variants.mueller :
    AvoidsPowersOfTwo muellerSet ∧ muellerSet.HasDensity (1 / 2)

statements.name: Erdos1136.erdos_1136.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
Müller also proved this is best possible, in that $A$ with the property in the question has
lower density at most $1/2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1136.variants.upper_bound (A : Set ℕ) (hA : AvoidsPowersOfTwo A) :
    A.lowerDensity ≤ 1 / 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1137
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1137](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1137)

statements.name: Erdos1137.erdos_1137
statements.doc:
Let $d_n=p_{n+1}-p_n$, where $p_n$ denotes the $n$th prime. Is it true that
$$\frac{\max_{n < x}d_{n}d_{n-1}}{(\max_{n < x}d_n)^2}\to 0$$ as $x\to \infty$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1137 :
    Tendsto (fun x ↦
       (((range x).sup (fun n ↦ (primeGap n) * (primeGap (n - 1))) : ℕ) : ℝ) /
       (((range x).sup primeGap : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 0)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1138
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1138](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1138)
- [Va99] Vardi, I., Prime census. (1999).
- [Kum26] Kumrawat, S., [Disproof of Erdős Problem 1138](https://sourish-kumrawat.github.io/papers/Erdos_1138.pdf).

Note that the conjecture has a claimed disproof found at:
https://sourish-kumrawat.github.io/papers/Erdos_1138.pdf,
see the discussion section on the Erdos problems website for more information.

statements.name: Erdos1138.erdos_1138
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 1138.**
Let $x/2 < y < x$ and $C > 1$. If $d = \max_{p_n < x}(p_{n+1} - p_n)$,
where $p_n$ denotes the $n$-th prime, then is it true that
$$\pi(y + Cd) - \pi(y) \sim \frac{Cd}{\log y}$$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1138 : ¬ ∀C > 1,
    primeCount_Ioc_mul_const C ~[snd_gt_half_fst] fun (x, y) ↦
      C * (sup_primeGap x) / Real.log y

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1139
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1139](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1139)

statements.name: Erdos1139.erdos_1139
statements.doc:
Let $1\leq u_1 < u_2 < \cdots$ be the sequence of integers with at most $2$ prime factors.
Is it true that $$\limsup_{k \to \infty} \frac{u_{k+1}-u_k}{\log k}=\infty?$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1139 :
    letI u := Nat.nth (fun n ↦ 0 < n ∧ Ω n ≤ 2)
    atTop.limsup (fun k : ℕ ↦ (((u (k + 1) : ℝ) - (u k : ℝ)) / Real.log (↑k + 1) : EReal)) = ⊤

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1140
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1140](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1140)
- [EpGi10] Epure, M. and Gica, A., *Principal quadratic real fields in connection with some
  additive problems*. Bull. Math. Soc. Sci. Math. Roumanie (N.S.) (2010), 251-259.
- [MoWi89] Mollin, R. A. and Williams, H. C., *Period four and real quadratic fields of class
  number one*. Proc. Japan Acad. Ser. A Math. Sci. (1989), 89-93.
- [Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference
  "Paul Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).

statements.name: Erdos1140.erdos_1140
statements.doc:
Do there exist infinitely many $n$ such that $n-2x^2$ is prime for all $x$ with $2x^2<n$?

The answer is no: see `erdos_1140.variants.at_most_one_exception`.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1140 : ¬ {n : ℕ | Erdos1140Prop n}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos1140.erdos_1140.variants.at_most_one_exception
statements.doc:
The known such $n$ are $2,5,7,13,31,61,181,199$. It is known that these are, with at most one
exception, all such $n$. An even such $n$ must be prime (take $x = 0$), so $n = 2$. Theorem 4.1
of Epure and Gica [EpGi10] implies that the only such
$n\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ are $5,13,61,181$, and their method, coupled with a result of Mollin and
Williams [MoWi89], implies that the only such $n\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ are $7,31,199$, and at most one
other exception.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1140.variants.at_most_one_exception :
    ({n : ℕ | Erdos1140Prop n} \ {2, 5, 7, 13, 31, 61, 181, 199}).Subsingleton

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1141
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1141](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1141)
- [A214583](https://oeis.org/A214583)
- [APSSV26b] B. Alexeev, M. Putterman, M. Sawhney, M. Sellke, and G. Valiant,
  [Short proofs in combinatorics, probability and number theory II](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.06609).
  arXiv:2604.06609 (2026).
- [Or26] Y. Oriike, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 1141](https://github.com/yuta0x89/ErdosProblems/blob/a1319f732cdee5140faf47d984e2c451c1184803/Erdos1141.lean) (2026)
- [Po17] P. Pollack, Bounds for the first several prime character nonresidues. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (2017), 2815--2826.
- [Me1874] F. Mertens, Ein Beitrag zur analytischen Zahlentheorie. J. Reine Angew. Math. (1874),
  46--62.
- [Va99] Various, Some of Paul's favorite problems. Booklet produced for the conference "Paul Erdős
  and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).

statements.name: Erdos1141.erdos_1141.variants.pollack_1_3
statements.doc:
**Theorem 1.3 of [Po17]**: for a quadratic character to a large enough modulus, the primes below
$m^{1/4+\varepsilon}$ on which the character is $1$ outnumber any fixed power of $\log m$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1141.variants.pollack_1_3 (ε A : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hA : 0 < A) :
    ∃ m₀ : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, m₀ < m → ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ m, MulChar.IsQuadratic χ →
      Real.log m ^ A ≤ ((residuePrimesUpTo m χ ε).card : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1141.erdos_1141.variants.mertens_third
statements.doc:
**Mertens' third theorem** [Me1874], in the weakened form the linked proof assumes: the product
over the primes up to $n$ of $1 - 1/p$ is at least $1/(3\log n)$.

The true asymptotic is $e^{-\gamma}/\log n$, and $e^{-\gamma} > 1/3$, so this bound is weaker than
the theorem and is what the deduction needs.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1141.variants.mertens_third (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) :
    1 / (3 * Real.log n) ≤ ∏ p ∈ (Finset.range (n + 1)).filter Nat.Prime, (1 - 1 / (p : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos1141.erdos_1141
statements.doc:
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that $n-k^2$ is prime for all $k$ with $(n,k)=1$ and $k^2 < n$?

In [Va99] it is asked whether $968$ is the largest integer with this property, but this is an
error, since for example $968-9=7\cdot 137$.

The list of $n$ satisfying the given property is [A214583] in the OEIS. The largest known such $n$
is $1722$.

The answer is negative: [APSSV26b] proves a stronger finiteness theorem, deducing it from
Pollack [Po17]. Oriike [Or26] formalised the deduction in Lean.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1141 :
    ¬ Infinite { n | Erdos1141Prop n }

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1142
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1142](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1142)
- [A039669](https://oeis.org/A039669)
- [Va99] Various, Some of Paul's favorite problems. Booklet produced for the conference "Paul Erdős
  and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).
- [MiWe69] Mientka, W. E. and Weitzenkamp, R. C., On f-plentiful numbers, Journal of
  Combinatorial Theory, Volume 7, Issue 4, December 1969, pages 374-377.

statements.name: Erdos1142.erdos_1142
statements.doc:
Are there infinitely many $n > 2$ such that $n - 2^k$ is prime for all $k \geq 1$ with $2^k < n$?

The only known such $n$ are $4, 7, 15, 21, 45, 75, 105$ (OEIS [A039669](https://oeis.org/A039669)).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1142 :
    Infinite { n | Erdos1142Prop n }

statements.name: Erdos1142.erdos_1142.variants.mientka_weitzenkamp
statements.doc:
Mientka and Weitzenkamp [MiWe69] proved that the only $n \leq 2^{44}$ such that $n > 2$ and
$n - 2^k$ is prime for all $k \geq 1$ with $2^k < n$ are $4, 7, 15, 21, 45, 75, 105$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1142.variants.mientka_weitzenkamp :
    { n : ℕ | n ≤ 2 ^ 44 ∧ Erdos1142Prop n } = {4, 7, 15, 21, 45, 75, 105}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1145
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/28](https://www.erdosproblems.com/28)
- [erdosproblems.com/1145](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1145)

statements.name: Erdos1145.erdos_1145
statements.doc:
Let $A=\{1\leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots\}$ and $B=\{1\leq b_1 < b_2 < \cdots\}$ be sets of integers with
$a_n/b_n\to 1$.

If $A+B$ contains all sufficiently large positive integers then is it true that
$\limsup 1_A\ast 1_B(n)=\infty$?

A conjecture of Erdős and Sárközy.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1145 : Erdos1145Prop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1146
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1146](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1146)
- [Ru99] Ruzsa, I., Erdős and the Integers. Journal of Number Theory (1999), 115-163.

statements.name: Erdos1146.erdos_1146
statements.doc:
Is $B=\{2^m3^n : m,n\geq 0\}$ an essential component?

In [Ru99] Ruzsa states "The simplest set with a chance to be an essential component is the
collection of numbers in the form $2^m3^n$ and Erdős often asked whether it is an essential
component or not; I do not even have a plausible guess."
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1146 :
    IsEssentialComponent { k | ∃ m n : ℕ, k = 2 ^ m * 3 ^ n }

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1147
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1147](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1147)
- [Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference "Paul
  Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).
- [Ko16b] Konieczny, Jakub, *Sets of recurrence as bases for the positive integers*. Acta Arith.
  (2016), 309-338.

statements.name: Erdos1147.erdos_1147
statements.doc:
Let $\alpha>0$ be an irrational number. Is the set
$$A=\left\{ n\geq 1: \| \alpha n^2\| < \frac{1}{\log n}\right\},$$
where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the distance to the nearest integer, an additive basis of order $2$?

This was disproved by Konieczny [Ko16b], and is false both for almost every $\alpha>0$, and also
is false specifically for $\alpha=\sqrt{2}$.

More generally, given any $\epsilon(n)\to 0$, the set
$A=\{ n\geq 1: \| \alpha n^2\| < \epsilon(n)\}$ is not an additive basis of order $2$ for almost
every $\alpha>0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1147 : ¬ ∀ α : ℝ, 0 < α → Irrational α →
    (recurrenceSet α fun n ↦ 1 / Real.log n).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2

statements.name: Erdos1147.erdos_1147.variants.sqrt_two
statements.doc:
Konieczny [Ko16b] showed that the set is not an additive basis of order $2$ for
$\alpha=\sqrt{2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1147.variants.sqrt_two :
    ¬ (recurrenceSet (√2) fun n ↦ 1 / Real.log n).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2

statements.name: Erdos1147.erdos_1147.variants.almost_every
statements.doc:
Konieczny [Ko16b] showed that, given any $\epsilon(n)\to 0$, the set
$\{ n\geq 1: \| \alpha n^2\| < \epsilon(n)\}$ is not an additive basis of order $2$ for almost
every $\alpha>0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1147.variants.almost_every : ∀ ε : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto ε atTop (nhds 0) →
    ∀ᵐ α : ℝ, 0 < α → ¬ (recurrenceSet α ε).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1148
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1148](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1148)
- [Ch26] P. Chojecki, [Bounded Representations by $x^2 + y^2 - z^2$](https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos1148-full.pdf) (2026)
- [Va99] Various, Some of Paul's favorite problems. Booklet produced for the conference "Paul Erdős
  and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).

statements.name: Erdos1148.erdos_1148
statements.doc:
Can every large integer $n$ be written as $n=x^2+y^2-z^2$ with $\max(x^2,y^2,z^2)\leq n$?

This was proved affirmatively by Chojecki [Ch26], using a Duke-type equidistribution theorem.
A Lean formalisation of the reduction (conditional on a Duke-type equidistribution theorem) exists;
see the [forum discussion](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/1148#post-4849). The linked
formal proof (plby/lean-proofs) removes the Duke hypothesis; it is stated over `ℤ`, as
`∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∃ x y z : ℤ, n = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 - z ^ 2 ∧ max (x ^ 2) (max (y ^ 2) (z ^ 2)) ≤ n`,
which gives the statement below by taking absolute values.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1148 : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, Erdos1148Prop n

statements.name: Erdos1148.erdos_1148.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc: The integer $6563$ cannot be written as $x^2 + y^2 - z^2$ with $\max(x^2, y^2, z^2) \leq 6563$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1148.variants.lower_bound : ¬ Erdos1148Prop 6563

statements.name: Erdos1148.erdos_1148.variants.weaker
statements.doc: [Va99] reports this is 'obvious' if we replace $\leq n$ with $\leq n+2\sqrt{n}$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1148.variants.weaker : ∀ n, erdos_1148_weaker_prop n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1149
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1149](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1149)
- [BeRi17] Bergelson, Vitaly and Richter, Florian Karl, *On the density of coprime tuples of the
  form $(n,\lfloor f_1(n)\rfloor,\dots,\lfloor f_k(n)\rfloor)$, where $f_1,\dots,f_k$ are
  functions from a Hardy field*. Number Theory - Diophantine Problems, Uniform Distribution and
