  Applications, Springer (2017), 109-135. [arXiv:1611.08044](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.08044)
- [Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference "Paul
  Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).

statements.name: Erdos1149.erdos_1149
statements.doc:
Let $\alpha>0$ be a real number, not an integer. The density of integers $n\geq 1$ for which
$(n,\lfloor n^\alpha\rfloor)=1$ is $6/\pi^2$.

This is true, and was proved by Bergelson and Richter [BeRi17].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1149 (α : ℝ) (hα : 0 < α) (hα' : α ∉ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)) :
    {n : ℕ | 1 ≤ n ∧ n.Coprime ⌊(n : ℝ) ^ α⌋₊}.HasDensity (6 / Real.pi ^ 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1150
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1150](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1150)
- [OAI26a] OpenAI, *Asymptotically minimal maxima of real Littlewood polynomials*. OpenAI Math
  Release preprint (2026).
  https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/Asymptotically-minimal-maxima-of-real-Littlewood-polynomials-September-23-2026/paper.pdf

statements.name: Erdos1150.erdos_1150
statements.doc:
Is there some constant $c > 0$ such that, for all large enough $n$ and all polynomials $P$ of
degree $n$ with coefficients in $\{-1, 1\}$,
$$\max_{|z|=1} |P(z)| > (1 + c) \sqrt{n}?$$

No. This was disproved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26a]; see the linked
Lean proof.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1150 :
    ¬ ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ P : ℂ[X],  (∀ i ≤ P.natDegree, P.coeff i = - 1 ∨ P.coeff i = 1) → P.natDegree = n →
        ⨆ z : Metric.sphere (0 : ℂ) 1, ‖P.eval (z : ℂ)‖ > (1 + c) * Real.sqrt n

statements.name: Erdos1150.erdos_1150.variants.parseval_lower_bound
statements.doc:
The trivial lower bound from Parseval's identity: for any polynomial $P$ of degree $n$ with
coefficients in $\{-1, 1\}$, we have $\max_{|z|=1} |P(z)| \geq \sqrt{n+1}$.

This follows from Parseval's identity:
$$\frac{1}{2\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} |P(e^{i\theta})|^2 d\theta = \sum_{k=0}^{n} |a_k|^2 = n+1$$
since each $|a_k|^2 = 1$. The circle average is bounded by the pointwise supremum squared, so
$\max_{|z|=1} |P(z)|^2 \ge n+1$, whence $\max_{|z|=1} |P(z)| \ge \sqrt{n+1}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1150.variants.parseval_lower_bound (P : ℂ[X]) (n : ℕ)
    (hcoeff : ∀ i ≤ P.natDegree, P.coeff i = -1 ∨ P.coeff i = 1)
    (hdeg : P.natDegree = n) :
    ⨆ z : Metric.sphere (0 : ℂ) 1, ‖P.eval (z : ℂ)‖ ≥ Real.sqrt (n + 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1152
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1152](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1152)
- [EKS89] Erdős, P., Kroó, A. and Szabados, J., *On convergent interpolatory polynomials*.
  J. Approx. Theory 58 (1989), 232-241. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1989-16.pdf)
- [Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference
  "Paul Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).

statements.name: Erdos1152.erdos_1152
statements.doc:
For $n\geq 1$ fix some sequence of $n$ distinct numbers $x_{1n},\ldots,x_{nn}\in [-1,1]$. Let
$\epsilon=\epsilon(n)\to 0$.

Does there always exist a continuous function $f:[-1,1]\to \mathbb{R}$ such that if $p_n$ is a
sequence of polynomials, with degrees $\deg p_n<(1+\epsilon(n))n$, such that
$p_n(x_{kn})=f(x_{kn})$ for all $1\leq k\leq n$, then $p_n(x)\not\to f(x)$ for almost all
$x\in [-1,1]$?

This is Problem 2.42 in [Va99]. The $n$ nodes of the $n$-th row form the finite set `nodes n`.
We take $\epsilon(n)>0$. A smaller $\epsilon$ only shrinks the class of $p_n$, so this is
equivalent to allowing any real $\epsilon(n)\to 0$. We impose the degree bound only for
$n\geq 1$, since for $n=0$ the bound `natDegree < 0` can never hold. We read
"$p_n(x)\not\to f(x)$ for almost all $x$" as: for almost every $x$, the sequence $p_n(x)$ does
not converge to $f(x)$.

For $\deg p_n<n$ the interpolating polynomial is unique (the Lagrange polynomial). Erdős, Kroó
and Szabados [EKS89, pp. 232-233] give necessary and sufficient conditions on the nodes under
which, for every continuous $f$ and every fixed $\epsilon>0$, there are interpolating polynomials
of degree at most $\lfloor n(1+\epsilon)\rfloor$ approximating $f$ at the rate of the best
uniform approximation (in particular converging uniformly to $f$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1152 :
    ∀ nodes : ℕ → Finset ℝ, (∀ n, (nodes n).card = n) →
      (∀ n, ∀ x ∈ nodes n, x ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) →
      ∀ ε : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ n, 0 < ε n) → Tendsto ε atTop (𝓝 0) →
        ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) ∧
          ∀ p : ℕ → ℝ[X],
            (∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ((p n).natDegree : ℝ) < (1 + ε n) * n) →
            (∀ n, ∀ x ∈ nodes n, (p n).eval x = f x) →
              ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1)),
                ¬ Tendsto (fun n => (p n).eval t) atTop (𝓝 (f t))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1154
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1154](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1154)
- [ErVo66] Erdős, Paul and Volkmann, Bodo, Additive Gruppen mit vorgegebener Hausdorffscher
  Dimension. J. Reine Angew. Math. (1966), 203--208.
- [EdMi01] Edgar, G. A. and Miller, Chris, Hausdorff dimension, analytic sets and transcendence.
  Real Anal. Exchange (2001/02), 335--339.
- [EdMi03] Edgar, G. A. and Miller, Chris, Borel subrings of the reals. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (2003), 1121--1129.
- [Ma16b] Mauldin, R. Daniel, Subfields of ℝ with arbitrary Hausdorff dimension. Math.
  Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (2016), 157--165.

statements.name: Erdos1154.erdos_1154.parts.i
statements.doc:
Does there exist, for every $\alpha \in [0, 1]$, a ring in $\mathbb{R}$ with Hausdorff dimension
$\alpha$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1154.parts.i :
    ∀ a ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ≥0∞) 1, ∃ R : Subring ℝ, dimH (R : Set ℝ) = a

statements.name: Erdos1154.erdos_1154.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Does there exist, for every $\alpha \in [0, 1]$, a field in $\mathbb{R}$ with Hausdorff dimension
$\alpha$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1154.parts.ii :
    ∀ a ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ≥0∞) 1, ∃ R : Subfield ℝ, dimH (R : Set ℝ) = a

statements.name: Erdos1154.erdos_1154.variants.group
statements.doc:
For every $\alpha \in [0, 1]$, there exists an additive group in $\mathbb{R}$ with Hausdorff
dimension $\alpha$. This is proved in [ErVo66].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1154.variants.group {a : ℝ≥0∞} (ha : a ∈ Icc 0 1) :
    ∃ R : AddSubgroup ℝ, dimH (R : Set ℝ) = a

statements.name: Erdos1154.erdos_1154.variants.analytic_ring
statements.doc:
If a subring is analytic, then it is either equal to $\mathbb{R}$ or its Hausdorff dimension is
equal to $0$. This is proved in [EdMi03], superseding the earlier result of [EdMi01] that a real
closed analytic subfield of $\mathbb{R}$ has Hausdorff dimension $0$ or $1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1154.variants.analytic_ring {R : Subring ℝ} (hR : AnalyticSet (R : Set ℝ)) :
    R = ⊤ ∨ dimH (R : Set ℝ) = 0

statements.name: Erdos1154.erdos_1154.variants.continuumHypothesis_field
statements.doc:
Assume the continuum hypothesis, then for every $\alpha \in [0, 1]$, there exists a field in
$\mathbb{R}$ with Hausdorff dimension $\alpha$. This is proved in [Ma16b].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1154.variants.continuumHypothesis_field {a : ℝ≥0∞} (ha : a ∈ Icc 0 1)
    [Fact (ℵ₁ = 𝔠)] :
    ∃ R : Subfield ℝ, dimH (R : Set ℝ) = a

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1157
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1157](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1157)
- [BES73] Brown, W. G. and Erdős, P. and S\'os, V. T., Some extremal problems on {$r$}-graphs.
  (1973), 53--63.

statements.name: Erdos1157.erdos_1157
statements.doc:
Let $s,k,r\geq 2$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the family of all $r$-uniform hypergraphs with $k$ vertices
and $s$ edges. Determine
$$\mathrm{ex}_r(n,\mathcal{F}).$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1157 :
    ∀ r k s : ℕ, 2 ≤ r → 2 ≤ k → 2 ≤ s → ∀ n : ℕ,
      Hypergraph.configurationExtremalNumber n r k s = erdos_1157.answer n r k s

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1158
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1158](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1158)
- [Er64f] Erdős, P., On extremal problems of graphs and generalized graphs. Israel J. Math. (1964),
  183--190.

statements.name: Erdos1158.erdos_1158
statements.doc:
Let $K_{t}(r)$ be the complete $t$-partite $t$-uniform hypergraph with $r$ vertices in each class.
Is it true that
$$\mathrm{ex}_t(n,K_t(r)) \geq n^{t-r^{1-t}-o(1)}$$
for all $t,r\geq 2$? The restriction $r\geq 2$ excludes forbidding a single edge.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1158 :
    ∀ t r : ℕ, 2 ≤ t → 2 ≤ r →
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (n : ℝ) ^ ((t : ℝ) - (r : ℝ) ^ (1 - (t : ℝ)) - ε) ≤
        (Hypergraph.partiteExtremalNumber n t r : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1159
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1159](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1159)
- [ESS83] Erdős, P. and Silverman, R. and Stein, A., *Intersection properties of families containing
  sets of nearly the same size*. Ars Combin. (1983), 247--259.
- [Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.

statements.name: Erdos1159.erdos_1159
statements.doc:
Determine whether there exists a constant $C>1$ such that the following holds.

Let $P$ be a finite [projective plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Projective_plane). Must there exist a set of points $S$ such that $1\leq \lvert S\cap \ell\rvert \leq C$ for all lines $\ell$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1159 :
    ∃ C : ℕ, 1 < C ∧
      ∀ (P L : Type) (_ : Membership P L) (_ : Fintype P) (_ : Fintype L),
        ∀ _ : ProjectivePlane P L, ∃ S : Set P, ∀ l : L,
          1 ≤ (S ∩ {p : P | p ∈ l}).ncard ∧ (S ∩ {p : P | p ∈ l}).ncard ≤ C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1160
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1160](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1160)
- [Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference
  "Paul Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).
- [BNV07] Blackburn, S. R., Neumann, P. M. and Venkataraman, G., *Enumeration of finite groups*.
  Cambridge Tracts in Mathematics 173, Cambridge University Press (2007), xii+281.
- [Pa03] Pantelidakis, I., *On the Number of Non-isomorphic Groups of the Same Order*. DPhil
  thesis, University of Oxford (2003).

statements.name: Erdos1160.erdos_1160
statements.doc:
Let $g(n)$ denote the number of groups of order $n$. If $n\leq 2^m$ then
$g(n)\leq g(2^m)$.

This is [Va99, 5.71] and an open problem (Question 22.16) in [BNV07], where its origin could not
be traced. It has been attributed to Erdős, Higman and others. Pantelidakis [Pa03] proved it for
odd $n$ and $m\geq 3619$.

It is a conjecture, not a question. We take $n\geq 1$; for $n=0$ it holds trivially, since
$g(0)=0$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1160 : ∀ n m : ℕ, 0 < n → n ≤ 2 ^ m → g n ≤ g (2 ^ m)

statements.name: Erdos1160.erdos_1160.variants.sum
statements.doc:
Question 22.18 of [BNV07] suggests the even stronger conjecture
$$\sum_{n<2^m}g(n) \leq g(2^m)$$
for all sufficiently large $m$ (perhaps even as soon as $m\geq 7$).

The sum is over $1\leq n<2^m$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1160.variants.sum :
    ∀ᶠ m : ℕ in atTop, ∑ n ∈ Finset.Ico 1 (2 ^ m), g n ≤ g (2 ^ m)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1161
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1161](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1161)
- [Be25d] Beker, Adrian, *The most probable order of a random permutation*.
  [arXiv:2510.11698](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11698) (2025).
- [Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference
  "Paul Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).

statements.name: Erdos1161.erdos_1161
statements.doc:
Let $f_k(n)$ count the number of elements of $S_n$ of order $k$. For which values of $k$ will
$f_k(n)$ be maximal? [Va99, 5.72]

Beker [Be25d, Theorem 1.2] proved that, for all large $n$, $f_k(n)$ is maximal if and only if
$k\geq 1$ is minimal such that $[1,\ldots,n-k]\mid k$, where $[\cdot]$ is the least common
multiple. The last clause on erdosproblems.com/1161 reads "$f_k(n)=(n-1)!$" instead of "$f_k(n)$
is maximal"; we follow [Be25d]. For $k > n$ we read $n-k$ as $0$, which does not change the
least such $k$, because $k = n$ qualifies.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1161 :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, {k : ℕ | ∀ j : ℕ, f j n ≤ f k n} = erdos_1161.answer n

statements.name: Erdos1161.erdos_1161.variants.max_asymptotic
statements.doc:
Beker [Be25d, Theorem 1.1] proved that
$$\max_{k\geq 1} f_k(n)\sim (n-1)!.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1161.variants.max_asymptotic :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (maxF n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((n - 1).factorial : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos1161.erdos_1161.variants.threshold
statements.doc:
Beker [Be25d, Theorem 1.1] also proved that, if $n$ is sufficiently large and
$f_k(n)\geq (n-1)!$, then $[1,\ldots,n-k]\mid k$. The statement also records $1\leq k\leq n$,
since [Be25d] writes such $k$ as $n-k'$ with $0\leq k'\leq n-1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1161.variants.threshold :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ k : ℕ, (n - 1).factorial ≤ f k n →
      k ≤ n ∧ 0 < k ∧ Nat.lcmUpto (n - k) ∣ k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1162
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1162](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1162)
- [Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference
  "Paul Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).
- [Py93] Pyber, L., *Asymptotic results for permutation groups*. Groups and computation
  (New Brunswick, NJ, 1991), DIMACS Ser. Discrete Math. Theoret. Comput. Sci. 11 (1993),
  197-219.
- [RoTr25] Roney-Dougal, C. M. and Tracey, G., *Subgroups of symmetric groups: enumeration and
  asymptotic properties*. [arXiv:2503.05416](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05416) (2025).

statements.name: Erdos1162.erdos_1162
statements.doc:
Give an asymptotic formula for the number of subgroups of $S_n$. Is there a statistical theorem
on their order?

A problem of Erdős and Turán [Va99, 5.73]. We state the first question: `erdos_1162.answer` is a
function asymptotically equivalent to the number $f(n)$ of subgroups of $S_n$ (an explicit
formula is intended, not $f$ itself). The second question is too vague to state.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1162 :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] erdos_1162.answer

statements.name: Erdos1162.erdos_1162.variants.pyber
statements.doc:
Pyber [Py93] proved that
$$\log f(n)\asymp n^2.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1162.variants.pyber :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (f n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos1162.erdos_1162.variants.roney_dougal_tracey
statements.doc:
Roney-Dougal and Tracey [RoTr25] have proved that
$$\log f(n)=\left(\frac{1}{16}+o(1)\right)n^2.$$
Here $\log$ is the logarithm to base $2$, as in [RoTr25].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1162.variants.roney_dougal_tracey :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.logb 2 (f n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 16

statements.name: Erdos1162.erdos_1162.variants.roney_dougal_tracey_bounds
statements.doc:
Roney-Dougal and Tracey [RoTr25, Theorem 1] proved that there are absolute constants
$\alpha>0$ and $\beta$ such that for all integers $n>1$
$$2^{n^2/16+\alpha n\log n}\leq f(n)\leq 2^{n^2/16+\beta n^{3/2}},$$
where $\log$ is the logarithm to base $2$. This implies the previous variant.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1162.variants.roney_dougal_tracey_bounds :
    ∃ α > (0 : ℝ), ∃ β : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, 1 < n →
      (2 : ℝ) ^ ((n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 16 + α * n * Real.logb 2 n) ≤ f n ∧
        (f n : ℝ) ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ ((n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 16 + β * (n : ℝ) ^ ((3 : ℝ) / 2))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1164
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1164](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1164)
- [Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference
  "Paul Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).
- [ErTa60] Erdős, P. and Taylor, S. J., *Some problems concerning the structure of random walk
  paths*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 11 (1960), 137--162.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1960-17.pdf)
- [Re90] Révész, P., *Random walk in random and non-random environments*. World Scientific,
  Singapore (1990).
- [DPRZ04] Dembo, A., Peres, Y., Rosen, J. and Zeitouni, O., *Cover times for Brownian motion and
  random walks in two dimensions*. Ann. of Math. (2) 160 (2004), 433--464.
  [arXiv:math/0107191](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0107191)

statements.name: Erdos1164.erdos_1164
statements.doc:
Let $R_n$ be the maximal integer such that almost every random walk from the origin in
$\mathbb{Z}^2$ visits every $x\in\mathbb{Z}^2$ with $\lVert x\rVert\leq R_n$ in at most $n$ steps.

Is it true that
$$\log R_n \asymp \sqrt{\log n}?$$

A problem of Erdős and Taylor, see [ErTa60, p. 153] and [Va99, 6.76]. This is true, as proved
independently by Révész [Re90] and Kesten, see [DPRZ04, Section 1.3], which reports that they
proved the following. The probability that the disc of radius $n$ is covered by time
$e^{t(\log n)^2}$ has $\liminf_{n\to\infty}$ at least $e^{-b/t}$ and $\limsup_{n\to\infty}$ at
most $e^{-a/t}$ for every $t>0$, where $0<a<b<\infty$ are constants. The exact limit is in
`erdos_1164.variants.dembo_peres_rosen_zeitouni`.

We take the simple random walk (`IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps`). Read literally, $R_n$ would be $0$:
for every $n$ some walk misses a neighbour of the origin, and such walks have positive
probability. So $R_n=R_n(\omega)$ is the random variable `coveringRadius`, and
$\log R_n\asymp\sqrt{\log n}$ means tightness: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are constants
$c>0$ and $C$ such that $c\sqrt{\log n}\leq\log R_n\leq C\sqrt{\log n}$ with probability at least
$1-\varepsilon$ for all large $n$. This is the sense of the results above and of
`erdos_1164.variants.dembo_peres_rosen_zeitouni`, which are about probabilities, not almost sure
bounds. [ErTa60, p. 153] asks an almost sure question about the time needed to cover the disc of
radius $n$; we follow the results in probability reported in [DPRZ04, Section 1.3].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1164 {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ} (hX : IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X) :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ c C : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      1 - ε ≤ (ℙ {ω | c * Real.sqrt (Real.log n) ≤ Real.log (coveringRadius X n ω) ∧
        Real.log (coveringRadius X n ω) ≤ C * Real.sqrt (Real.log n)}).toReal

statements.name: Erdos1164.erdos_1164.variants.dembo_peres_rosen_zeitouni
statements.doc:
Dembo, Peres, Rosen and Zeitouni [DPRZ04, Theorem 1.4] proved a conjecture of Kesten and Révész:
if $T_n$ is the time it takes the simple random walk in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ to cover the disc of
radius $n$, then
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\left(\log T_n\leq t(\log n)^2\right)=e^{-4/t}$$
for every $t>0$.

The disc is $D_n=D(0,n)\cap\mathbb{Z}^2$ (`openDisc`). Since $T_n$ is an integer,
$\log T_n\leq t(\log n)^2$ holds if and only if $T_n\leq\lfloor e^{t(\log n)^2}\rfloor$, that is,
if the disc is covered by that time.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1164.variants.dembo_peres_rosen_zeitouni {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω]
    [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)] {X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ}
    (hX : IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦
      (ℙ {ω | Covers X ⌊Real.exp (t * Real.log n ^ 2)⌋₊ ω (openDisc n)}).toReal)
      atTop (𝓝 (Real.exp (-4 / t)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1165
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1165](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1165)
- [Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference
  "Paul Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).
- [HLOZ24] Hao, C., Li, X., Okada, I. and Zheng, Y., *Favorite sites for simple random walk in
  two and more dimensions*. [arXiv:2409.00995](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00995) (2024).
- [To01] Tóth, B., *No more than three favorite sites for simple random walk*.
  Ann. Probab. 29 (2001), 484--503.

statements.name: Erdos1165.erdos_1165
statements.doc:
Given a random walk $s_0,s_1,\ldots$ in $\mathbb{Z}^2$, starting at the origin, let $f_n(x)$ count
the number of $0\leq k\leq n$ such that $s_k=x$.

Let
$$F(n)=\{ x: f_n(x) = \max_y f_n(y)\}$$
be the set of 'favourite values'. Find
$$\mathbb{P}(\lvert F(n)\rvert=r\textrm{ infinitely often})$$
for $r\geq 3$.

A problem of Erdős and Révész [Va99, 6.77]. We take the simple random walk, on any probability
space (`IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps`). Hao, Li, Okada and Zheng [HLOZ24, Theorem 1.1] showed that the
probability is $1$ for $r=3$ and $0$ for $r\geq 4$, see `erdos_1165.variants.hao_li_okada_zheng`.
The value of `erdos_1165.answer` for $r<3$ is not used.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1165 {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ} (hX : IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X) (r : ℕ) (hr : 3 ≤ r) :
    ℙ {ω | ∃ᶠ n in atTop, (favouriteSites X n ω).encard = (r : ℕ∞)} = erdos_1165.answer r

statements.name: Erdos1165.erdos_1165.variants.hao_li_okada_zheng
statements.doc:
Hao, Li, Okada and Zheng [HLOZ24, Theorem 1.1] proved that, for the simple random walk on
$\mathbb{Z}^2$, almost surely
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty} \#K^{(2)}(n) = 3,$$
where $K^{(2)}(n)$ is the set of favourite sites at time $n$. The cardinalities are natural
numbers, so almost surely there are eventually at most three favourite sites, and exactly three
infinitely often. Tóth [To01] proved the corresponding bound for the one-dimensional walk, see
[HLOZ24, Section 1].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1165.variants.hao_li_okada_zheng {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω]
    [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)] {X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ} (hX : IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X) :
    ∀ᵐ ω, limsup (fun n ↦ (favouriteSites X n ω).encard) atTop = 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1166
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1166](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1166)
- [Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference
  "Paul Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).
- [ErTa60] Erdős, P. and Taylor, S. J., *Some problems concerning the structure of random walk
  paths*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 11 (1960), 137--162.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1960-17.pdf)
- [DPRZ01] Dembo, A., Peres, Y., Rosen, J. and Zeitouni, O., *Thick points for planar Brownian
  motion and the Erdős-Taylor conjecture on random walk*. Acta Math. 186 (2001), 239--270.
  [doi:10.1007/BF02401841](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02401841)
- [HLOZ24] Hao, C., Li, X., Okada, I. and Zheng, Y., *Favorite sites for simple random walk in
  two and more dimensions*. [arXiv:2409.00995](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00995) (2024).

statements.name: Erdos1166.erdos_1166
statements.doc:
Given a random walk $s_0,s_1,\ldots$ in $\mathbb{Z}^2$, starting at the origin, let $f_k(x)$ count
the number of $0\leq l\leq k$ such that $s_l=x$.

Let
$$F(k)=\{ x: f_k(x) = \max_y f_k(y)\}$$
be the set of 'favourite values'. Is it true that
$$\left\lvert \bigcup_{k\leq n}F(k)\right\rvert \leq (\log n)^{O(1)}$$
almost surely, for all but finitely many $n$?

A problem of Erdős and Révész [Va99, 6.78]. The answer is yes. Almost surely there are at most
three favourite sites at all large times [HLOZ24, Theorem 1.1], see
`Erdos1165.erdos_1165.variants.hao_li_okada_zheng`, and the maximal local time is
$O((\log n)^2)$ [ErTa60, p. 162], see `erdos_1166.variants.erdos_taylor`. A favourite
site stays a favourite site for as long as the maximal local time does not change. So for each
value of the maximal local time, the sites that are favourite at some time while it has that value
are all favourite at the last such time, and there are at most three of them, up to finitely many
exceptions. This gives the bound $O((\log n)^2)$ stated on the problem page.

We take the simple random walk (`IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps`). We read $O(1)$ as a single exponent
`C` that works for almost every walk. The cardinality is `Set.encard`, so an infinite union would
not satisfy the bound.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1166 {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ} (hX : IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X) :
    ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ᵐ ω, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ((⋃ k ≤ n, favouriteSites X k ω).encard : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (Real.log n ^ C)

statements.name: Erdos1166.erdos_1166.variants.erdos_taylor
statements.doc:
Erdős and Taylor [ErTa60, p. 162] proved that, for the simple random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, if
$T_n$ is the maximal number of visits to a point in the first $n$ steps, then almost surely
$$\frac{1}{4\pi}\leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{T_n}{(\log n)^2}
  \leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{T_n}{(\log n)^2}\leq\frac{1}{\pi}.$$
They conjectured that the limit exists and equals $1/\pi$, see
`erdos_1166.variants.dembo_peres_rosen_zeitouni`.

We use `maxLocalTime`, which also counts the visit at time $0$. This changes $T_n$ by at most one.
The bounds are stated with $\varepsilon$ to avoid the junk values of `liminf` and `limsup`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1166.variants.erdos_taylor {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω]
    [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)] {X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ}
    (hX : IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X) :
    ∀ᵐ ω, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
      (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, 1 / (4 * π) - ε ≤ (maxLocalTime X n ω : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) ∧
      (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (maxLocalTime X n ω : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2 ≤ 1 / π + ε)

statements.name: Erdos1166.erdos_1166.variants.dembo_peres_rosen_zeitouni
statements.doc:
Dembo, Peres, Rosen and Zeitouni [DPRZ01, Theorem 1.1] proved the conjecture of Erdős and Taylor:
for the simple random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, if $T_n^*$ is the maximal number of visits to a
point in the first $n$ steps, then almost surely
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{T_n^*}{(\log n)^2}=\frac{1}{\pi}.$$

`maxLocalTime` counts the visit at time $0$. Whether this visit is counted changes $T_n^*$ by at
most one, so the limit is the same.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1166.variants.dembo_peres_rosen_zeitouni {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω]
    [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)] {X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ}
    (hX : IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X) :
    ∀ᵐ ω, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (maxLocalTime X n ω : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 (1 / π))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1167
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1167](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1167)
- [EHMR84] P. Erdős, A. Hajnal, A. Máté and R. Rado, *Combinatorial set theory: partition
  relations for cardinals*. Studies in Logic and the Foundations of Mathematics 106,
  North-Holland (1984).

The original Erdős–Hajnal problem list gives the additional conditions $\gamma \geq 2$, $r < \omega$,
and $\kappa_\alpha > r$. Without $\gamma \geq 2$, the statement is false: taking $\gamma = 1$ and
$\kappa_0 = \aleph_1$ with $\lambda = \aleph_0$ gives a counterexample, since the partition relation
with one color degenerates to a cardinality comparison (see `erdos_1167.unrestricted_is_false`).
Without $\kappa_\alpha > r$ it is also false: with $r = 2$, $\lambda = \aleph_0$ and targets
$(2, \aleph_1)$, the premise $2^{\aleph_0} \to (3, \aleph_1)^3$ holds, but a constant colouring
of the pairs of $\aleph_0$ has neither a red pair nor a blue set of size $\aleph_1$.

statements.name: Erdos1167.erdos_1167
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 1167.** Let $r \geq 2$ be finite, $\gamma \geq 2$, and $\lambda$ be an infinite
cardinal. Let $\kappa_\alpha > r$ be cardinals for all $\alpha < \gamma$. Is it true
that
$$2^\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha + 1)_{\alpha < \gamma}^{r+1}$$
implies
$$\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha)_{\alpha < \gamma}^r?$$
Here $+$ means cardinal addition, so that $\kappa_\alpha + 1 = \kappa_\alpha$
if $\kappa_\alpha$ is infinite.

A problem of Erdős, Hajnal, and Rado.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1167 :
    ∀ (r : ℕ), 2 ≤ r →
    ∀ (lam : Cardinal.{u}), ℵ₀ ≤ lam →
    ∀ (γ : Ordinal.{u}), 2 ≤ γ →
    ∀ (κ : γ.ToType → Cardinal.{u}), (∀ α, (r : Cardinal.{u}) < κ α) →
      cardinalPartitionRel ((2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ lam) (r + 1) γ (fun α => κ α + 1) →
      cardinalPartitionRel lam r γ κ

statements.name: Erdos1167.erdos_1167.variants.finite_targets
statements.doc:
**Finite-target case.** When all $\kappa_\alpha$ are finite, $\kappa_\alpha + 1$
is the ordinary natural-number successor. Special case of `erdos_1167`.

This case was proved by Erdős, Hajnal, Máté and Rado [EHMR84], using the Erdős–Rado tree
argument and the negative stepping-up lemma. The statement omits the condition $n_\alpha > r$.
This is harmless, since a colouring that witnesses
$\lambda \not\to (n_\alpha)^r_{\alpha < \gamma}$ can only use colours $\alpha$ with $n_\alpha > r$.
statements.statement:
theorem finite_targets (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) (lam : Cardinal.{u}) (hlam : ℵ₀ ≤ lam)
    (γ : Ordinal.{u}) (hγ : 2 ≤ γ) (n : γ.ToType → ℕ) :
    cardinalPartitionRel ((2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ lam) (r + 1) γ
        (fun α => (n α : Cardinal.{u}) + 1) →
    cardinalPartitionRel lam r γ (fun α => (n α : Cardinal.{u}))

statements.name: Erdos1167.erdos_1167.variants.binary_colors
statements.doc: **Binary-color case.** The $\gamma = 2$ specialization (two color classes).
statements.statement:
theorem binary_colors (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) (lam : Cardinal.{u}) (hlam : ℵ₀ ≤ lam)
    (κ : (2 : Ordinal.{u}).ToType → Cardinal.{u}) (hκ : ∀ α, (r : Cardinal.{u}) < κ α) :
    cardinalPartitionRel ((2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ lam) (r + 1) 2 (fun α => κ α + 1) →
    cardinalPartitionRel lam r 2 κ

statements.name: Erdos1167.erdos_1167.variants.infinite_targets
statements.doc:
**Infinite-target case.** When all $\kappa_\alpha \geq \aleph_0$ are infinite and bounded by
$\lambda$, $\kappa_\alpha + 1 = \kappa_\alpha$, so the hypothesis simplifies to a "pure"
stepping-down lemma:
$$2^\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha)_{\alpha<\gamma}^{r+1} \implies
   \lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha)_{\alpha<\gamma}^r.$$
The condition $\kappa_\alpha \leq \lambda$ is needed to avoid a size obstruction: without it, the
conclusion would require a subset of $\lambda$ of size $\kappa_\alpha > \lambda$, which is impossible
(see `infinite_targets_needs_bound`).
statements.statement:
theorem infinite_targets (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) (lam : Cardinal.{u}) (hlam : ℵ₀ ≤ lam)
    (γ : Ordinal.{u}) (hγ : 2 ≤ γ) (κ : γ.ToType → Cardinal.{u}) (hκ : ∀ i, ℵ₀ ≤ κ i)
    (hκ_le : ∀ i, κ i ≤ lam) :
    cardinalPartitionRel ((2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ lam) (r + 1) γ κ →
    cardinalPartitionRel lam r γ κ

statements.name: Erdos1167.erdos_1167.variants.r_eq_two
statements.doc:
**$r = 2$ case.** The stepping-down from 3-uniform to 2-uniform partition
relations: $2^\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha + 1)_{\alpha<\gamma}^3$ implies
$\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha)_{\alpha<\gamma}^2$. Generalises the classical
Erdős–Rado stepping-up/down theorem for pairs.
statements.statement:
theorem r_eq_two (lam : Cardinal.{u}) (hlam : ℵ₀ ≤ lam)
    (γ : Ordinal.{u}) (hγ : 2 ≤ γ) (κ : γ.ToType → Cardinal.{u})
    (hκ : ∀ α, (2 : Cardinal.{u}) < κ α) :
    cardinalPartitionRel ((2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ lam) 3 γ (fun α => κ α + 1) →
    cardinalPartitionRel lam 2 γ κ

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1168
problems.doc:
*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/1168](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1168)
* [EHR65] Erdős, P., Hajnal, A. and Rado, R., *Partition relations for cardinal numbers*.
  Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1965), pp. 93–196.

statements.name: Erdos1168.erdos_1168
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 1168.** Prove that
$$\aleph_{\omega+1} \not\to (\aleph_{\omega+1}, \underbrace{3, 3, \ldots}_{\aleph_0})^2_{\aleph_0}$$
without assuming the generalized continuum hypothesis.

A problem of Erdős, Hajnal, and Rado [EHR65]: the negative arrow is known under GCH;
the open problem asks for a ZFC proof. Here `ω = Ordinal.omega0`, so `ℵ_ (ω + 1)` is
the successor cardinal of the singular `ℵ_ω`.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1168 : ¬ CardinalCountableColorRamsey (ℵ_ (ω + 1))

statements.name: Erdos1168.erdos_1168.variants.under_GCH
statements.doc:
**Erdős–Hajnal–Rado theorem under GCH** [EHR65]: the negative partition relation
$\aleph_{\omega+1} \not\to (\aleph_{\omega+1}, 3, 3, \ldots)^2_{\aleph_0}$ holds
assuming GCH.
statements.statement: theorem under_GCH (hGCH : GCH) : ¬ CardinalCountableColorRamsey (ℵ_ (ω + 1))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1169
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1169](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1169)

*References:*
- [Ha71] Hajnal, A. *A negative partition relation.* Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 68 (1971),
  pp. 142–144.

statements.name: Erdos1169.erdos_1169
statements.doc:
Is it true that $\omega_1^2 \not\to (\omega_1^2, 3)^2$?

A problem of Erdős and Hajnal. Hajnal [Ha71] proved this assuming the continuum hypothesis.
The source's displayed relation has blue target $3$; its introductory $k$ does not occur
in that relation. See also [erdosproblems.com/592](https://www.erdosproblems.com/592).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1169 :
    ¬ OrdinalRamsey ((ω_ 1) ^ (2 : ℕ)) ((ω_ 1) ^ (2 : ℕ)) (3 : Ordinal)

statements.name: Erdos1169.erdos_1169.variants.finite_blue_target
statements.doc:
The finite-blue-target form asks whether $\omega_1^2 \not\to (\omega_1^2, k)^2$
for every $k \ge 3$. The restriction excludes $k \le 2$, where the positive relation holds.
A colouring witnessing the negative relation with blue target $3$ also witnesses this form.
statements.statement:
theorem finite_blue_target :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k →
      ¬ OrdinalRamsey ((ω_ 1) ^ (2 : ℕ)) ((ω_ 1) ^ (2 : ℕ)) (k : Ordinal)

statements.name: Erdos1169.erdos_1169.variants.hajnal_under_ch
statements.doc:
**Hajnal (1971), assuming CH.** Under the Continuum Hypothesis,
$\omega_1^2 \not\to (\omega_1^2, k)^2$ holds for every finite $k \ge 3$.
statements.statement:
theorem hajnal_under_ch (hCH : 𝔠 = ℵ_ 1) :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k → ¬ OrdinalRamsey ((ω_ 1) ^ (2 : ℕ)) ((ω_ 1) ^ (2 : ℕ)) (k : Ordinal)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1171
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1171](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1171)

statements.name: Erdos1171.erdos_1171
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 1171.** Is it true that for all finite $k < \omega$,
$$\omega_1^2 \to (\omega_1 \cdot \omega, \underbrace{3, \ldots, 3}_{k})^2_{k+1}?$$

In any $(k+1)$-coloring of the pairs of the complete graph on $\omega_1^2$, either
there is a color-0 set of order type $\omega_1 \cdot \omega$, or there is a
monochromatic triangle $K_3$ in some non-zero color. The case $k = 1$
(`erdos_1171.variants.k_one`) is the Erdős–Hajnal theorem [EH74].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1171 :
    ∀ k : ℕ, OrdinalMultiColorRamsey (ω_ 1 ^ 2) (ω_ 1 * ω) 3 k

statements.name: Erdos1171.erdos_1171.variants.k_one
statements.doc:
**Erdős–Hajnal theorem** [EH74]: the case $k = 1$,
$\omega_1^2 \to (\omega_1 \cdot \omega, 3)^2$.
statements.statement: theorem k_one : OrdinalMultiColorRamsey (ω_ 1 ^ 2) (ω_ 1 * ω) 3 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1173
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1173](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1173)

statements.name: Erdos1173.erdos_1173
statements.doc:
**Erdős–Hajnal Problem 1173** [EH74]. Assume GCH. Let
$f : \omega_{\omega+1} \to [\omega_{\omega+1}]^{\leq \aleph_\omega}$
be a set mapping such that $|f(\alpha) \cap f(\beta)| < \aleph_\omega$ for all
$\alpha \neq \beta$. Does there exist a free set of cardinality $\aleph_{\omega+1}$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1173 :
    GCH →
    ∀ f : (ω_ (ω + 1)).ToType → Set (ω_ (ω + 1)).ToType,
      IsSetMapping f →
      ∃ Y : Set (ω_ (ω + 1)).ToType, IsFreeSet f Y ∧ #Y = ℵ_ (ω + 1)

statements.name: Erdos1173.erdos_1173.variants.free_set_mono
statements.doc: Free sets are downward-closed under inclusion.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1173.variants.free_set_mono
    (f : (ω_ (ω + 1)).ToType → Set (ω_ (ω + 1)).ToType)
    {Y Z : Set (ω_ (ω + 1)).ToType}
    (hYZ : Z ⊆ Y) (hY : IsFreeSet f Y) : IsFreeSet f Z

statements.name: Erdos1173.erdos_1173.variants.image_lt_aleph_succ
statements.doc: Under `IsSetMapping f`, each image has cardinality `< ℵ_{ω+1}`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1173.variants.image_lt_aleph_succ
    (f : (ω_ (ω + 1)).ToType → Set (ω_ (ω + 1)).ToType)
    (hf : IsSetMapping f)
    (α : (ω_ (ω + 1)).ToType) :
    #(f α) < ℵ_ (ω + 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1174
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1174](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1174)
- [Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference
  "Paul Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999), problem 7.91.

statements.name: Erdos1174.erdos_1174.parts.i
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 1174, part (i)** [Va99, 7.91]. A problem of Erdős and Hajnal:
does there exist a graph $G$ with no $K_4$ such that every edge colouring of $G$
with countably many colours contains a monochromatic $K_3$?

For simplicity the colourings are given on all unordered pairs $\operatorname{Sym}_2(V)$;
only the values on the edges of $G$ matter, since a monochromatic triangle is witnessed by
edges alone.

Shelah proved that a graph with this property can consistently exist, so the
problem is not disprovable in ZFC; whether such a graph exists outright remains open.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1174.parts.i :
    ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.CliqueFree 4 ∧
      ∀ c : Sym2 V → ℕ, ∃ x y z : V,
        G.Adj x y ∧ G.Adj y z ∧ G.Adj x z ∧
        c s(x, y) = c s(y, z) ∧ c s(y, z) = c s(x, z)

statements.name: Erdos1174.erdos_1174.parts.ii
statements.doc:
**Erdős Problem 1174, part (ii)** [Va99, 7.91]. A problem of Erdős and Hajnal:
does there exist a graph $G$ with no $K_{\aleph_1}$ (that is, every clique of $G$
is countable) such that every edge colouring of $G$ with countably many colours
contains a monochromatic $K_{\aleph_0}$ (an infinite clique all of whose edges
receive the same colour)?

For simplicity the colourings are given on all unordered pairs $\operatorname{Sym}_2(V)$;
only the values on the edges of $G$ matter.

Shelah proved that a graph with this property can consistently exist, so the
problem is not disprovable in ZFC; whether such a graph exists outright remains open.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1174.parts.ii :
    ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V),
      (∀ S : Set V, G.IsClique S → #S ≤ ℵ₀) ∧
      ∀ c : Sym2 V → ℕ, ∃ S : Set V, G.IsClique S ∧ S.Infinite ∧
        ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, x ≠ y → c s(x, y) = k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1175
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1175](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1175)

- [KoSh88] Komjáth, Péter and Shelah, Saharon, *Forcing constructions for uncountably chromatic
  graphs*. J. Symbolic Logic (1988), 696--707.

## Formalization notes

- **Chromatic cardinal**: `SimpleGraph.chromaticCardinal` is the cardinal-valued chromatic number
  defined in `FormalConjecturesForMathlib`. It extends the finite `chromaticNumber` (which takes
  values in `ℕ∞`) to a `Cardinal`, and is therefore able to distinguish between different infinite
  chromatic numbers.
- **Triangle-free subgraph**: a subgraph `H : G.Subgraph` is triangle-free when `H.coe.CliqueFree 3`.
  This is the standard Mathlib formulation: `CliqueFree 3` means the graph has no `K₃` as a clique.
- **Subgraph**: we use `G.Subgraph` (an arbitrary subgraph record) rather than an induced subgraph
  since the problem asks for any subgraph, not just induced ones.

statements.name: Erdos1175.erdos_1175
statements.doc:
Let $\kappa$ be an uncountable cardinal. Must there exist a cardinal $\lambda$ such that every
graph with chromatic number $\lambda$ contains a triangle-free subgraph with chromatic number
$\kappa$?

Shelah proved that a negative answer is consistent when
$\kappa = \lambda = \aleph_1$ (see `erdos_1175.variants.aleph_one`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1175 :
    ∀ (κ : Cardinal), ℵ₀ < κ →
      ∃ (μ : Cardinal),
        ∀ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = μ →
          ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), H.coe.CliqueFree 3 ∧ H.coe.chromaticCardinal = κ

statements.name: Erdos1175.erdos_1175.variants.aleph_one
statements.doc:
The case $\kappa = \lambda = \aleph_1$ of Problem 1175: does every graph with chromatic number
$\aleph_1$ contain a triangle-free subgraph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$?

Shelah proved that a negative answer is consistent with ZFC [KoSh88, Theorem 1]: there is a
model of ZFC containing a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ all of whose triangle-free
subgraphs have countable chromatic number. Consistency results about models of ZFC are not
directly formalizable inside Lean's fixed model, so only the underlying question is recorded
here. Note that this concerns only the choice $\lambda = \aleph_1$; it does not rule out a
larger $\lambda$ in `erdos_1175`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1175.variants.aleph_one :
    ∀ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 →
      ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), H.coe.CliqueFree 3 ∧ H.coe.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1

statements.name: Erdos1175.erdos_1175.variants.threshold_formulation
statements.doc:
**Threshold reformulation variant.** Replaces `chromaticCardinal = λ` in the hypothesis
of `erdos_1175` with `λ ≤ chromaticCardinal` (a graph of chromatic number ≥ λ has a
triangle-free subgraph of chromatic number κ). This is a strengthening of `erdos_1175`
(see `erdos_1175.test.threshold_implies_exact`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1175.variants.threshold_formulation :
    ∀ (κ : Cardinal), ℵ₀ < κ →
      ∃ (μ : Cardinal),
        ∀ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V), μ ≤ G.chromaticCardinal →
          ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), H.coe.CliqueFree 3 ∧ H.coe.chromaticCardinal = κ

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1176
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1176](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1176)

statements.name: Erdos1176.erdos_1176
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$. Is it true that there is a colouring of the
edges with $\aleph_1$ many colours such that, in any countable colouring of the vertices, there
exists a vertex colour containing all edge colours?

A problem of Erdős, Galvin, and Hajnal. The consistency of this was proved by Hajnal and Komjáth.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1176 :
    ∀ {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = aleph 1 →
      ∃ (EColor : Type) (_ : mk EColor = aleph 1) (c_edge : G.edgeSet → EColor),
        ∀ (VColor : Type) (_ : mk VColor ≤ aleph 0) (c_vert : V → VColor),
          ∃ (vc : VColor),
            ∀ (ec : EColor), ∃ (u v : V) (h : G.Adj u v),
              c_vert u = vc ∧ c_vert v = vc ∧ c_edge ⟨s(u, v), h⟩ = ec

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1177
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1177](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1177)
- [Li26] Li, E., *A Resolution of Erdős Problems 593 and 1177: Obligatory Triple Systems
  and Exact Spectra*. [arXiv:2606.24882v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24882v2) (2026),
  Corollary 1.4.

statements.name: Erdos1177.erdos_1177.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a finite $3$-uniform hypergraph, and let $F_G(\kappa)$ denote the collection of
$3$-uniform hypergraphs with chromatic number $\kappa$ not containing $G$. If
$F_G(\aleph_1)$ is non-empty, then it contains a hypergraph on at most
$2^{2^{\aleph_0}}$ vertices. Li [Li26, Corollary 1.4(1)] proved this.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1177.parts.i :
    ∀ (W : Type) [Fintype W] (G : UniformHypergraph W 3),
    G.HasAvoidingChromaticCardinal ℵ₁ →
      ∃ (V : Type) (_ : DecidableEq V) (X : UniformHypergraph V 3),
        X.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₁ ∧ ¬ G.Appears X ∧
          Cardinal.mk V ≤ (2 : Cardinal) ^ ((2 : Cardinal) ^ ℵ₀)

statements.name: Erdos1177.erdos_1177.parts.ii
statements.doc:
The assertion that two non-empty avoidance families $F_G(\aleph_1)$ and $F_H(\aleph_1)$
always have non-empty intersection is false. Li [Li26, Corollary 1.4(2)] gives a
counterexample using two triples sharing a pair and the loose seven-cycle.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1177.parts.ii :
    ¬ ∀ (W U : Type) [Fintype W] [Fintype U]
    (G : UniformHypergraph W 3) (H : UniformHypergraph U 3),
    G.HasAvoidingChromaticCardinal ℵ₁ → H.HasAvoidingChromaticCardinal ℵ₁ →
      ∃ (V : Type) (_ : DecidableEq V) (X : UniformHypergraph V 3),
        X.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₁ ∧ ¬ G.Appears X ∧ ¬ H.Appears X

statements.name: Erdos1177.erdos_1177.parts.iii
statements.doc:
If $\kappa,\lambda$ are uncountable cardinals and $F_G(\kappa)$ is non-empty then
$F_G(\lambda)$ is non-empty. Li [Li26, Corollary 1.4(3)] proved this.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1177.parts.iii :
    ∀ (W : Type) [Fintype W] (G : UniformHypergraph W 3)
    (κ μ : Cardinal), ℵ₀ < κ → ℵ₀ < μ →
      G.HasAvoidingChromaticCardinal κ → G.HasAvoidingChromaticCardinal μ

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1178
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1178](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1178)
- [BES73] Brown, W. G. and Erdős, P. and S\'os, V. T., Some extremal problems on {$r$}-graphs.
  (1973), 53--63.
- [CGLS23] Conlon, David and Gishboliner, Lior and Levanzov, Yevgeny and Shapira, Asaf, A new bound
  for the {B}rown-{E}rd\H os-S\'os problem. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (2023), 1--35.
- [EFR86] Erdős, P. and Frankl, P. and Rödl, V., The asymptotic number of graphs not containing a
  fixed subgraph and a problem for hypergraphs having no exponent. Graphs Combin. (1986), 113-121.
- [Er75b] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Journ\'{e}es
  Arithm\'{e}tiques de Bordeaux (Conf., Univ. Bordeaux, Bordeaux, 1974) (1975), 295-310.
- [RuSz78] Ruzsa, I. Z. and Szemer\'{e}di, E., Triple systems with no six points carrying three
  triangles. Combinatorics (Proc. Fifth Hungarian Colloq., Keszthely, 1976), Vol. II (1978), 939-945.
- [SaSe05] Sárk\"ozy, Gábor N. and Selkow, Stanley, An extension of the {R}uzsa-Szemer\'edi theorem
  . Combinatorica (2005), 77--84.
- [SoSo17] Solymosi, David and Solymosi, Jozsef, Small cores in 3-uniform hypergraphs. J. Combin.
  Theory Ser. B (2017), 897--910.

statements.name: Erdos1178.erdos_1178
statements.doc:
For $r\geq 3$ let $d_r(e)$ be the minimal $d$ such that
$$\mathrm{ex}_r(n,\mathcal{F})=o(n^2),$$
where $\mathcal{F}$ is the family of $r$-uniform hypergraphs on $d$ vertices with $e$ edges. Prove
that
$$d_r(e)=(r-2)e+3$$
for all $r,e\geq 3$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1178 :
    ∀ r e : ℕ, 3 ≤ r → 3 ≤ e →
    Hypergraph.sparseConfigurationThreshold r e = (((r - 2) * e + 3 : ℕ) : ℕ∞)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1179
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1179](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1179)
- [Er73] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of
  combinatorial theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971)
  (1973), 117-138.
- [ErRe65] Erdős, P. and Rényi, A., *Probabilistic methods in group theory*. J. Analyse Math.
  (1965), 127-138.
- [ErHa76] Erdős, P. and Hall, R. R., *Probabilistic methods in group theory. II*. Houston J.
  Math. (1976), 173-180.

statements.name: Erdos1179.erdos_1179
statements.doc:
Let $0<\epsilon<1$ and let $g_\epsilon(N)$ be the minimal $k$ such that if $G$ is an abelian
group of size $N$ and $A\subseteq G$ is a uniformly random subset of size $k$, and
$$F_A(g) = \#\left\{ S\subseteq A : g = \sum_{x\in S}x\right\},$$
then, with probability $\to 1$ as $N\to \infty$,
$$\left\lvert F_A(g)-\frac{2^k}{N}\right\rvert \leq \epsilon \frac{2^k}{N}$$
for all $g\in G$.

Estimate $g_\epsilon(N)$ - in particular, is it true that for all $\epsilon>0$
$$g_\epsilon(N)=(1+o_\epsilon(1))\log_2N?$$

It is trivial that $g_\epsilon(N)\geq \log_2N$ for all $0<\epsilon<1$. Erdős and Rényi [ErRe65]
proved that for all $0<\epsilon<1$, $g_\epsilon(N) \leq (2+o(1))\log_2N+O_\epsilon(1)$. Erdős and
Hall [ErHa76] proved that, for all $0<\epsilon<1$,
$$g_\epsilon(N)\leq \left(1+O_\epsilon\left(\frac{\log\log\log N}{\log\log N}\right)\right)
\log_2N.$$

The upper bound $g_\epsilon(N)\leq (1+o(1))\log_2 N$ is formalised as: there is a choice of sizes
$k(N) = (1+o(1))\log_2 N$ such that, along any sequence of abelian groups with $|G|\to\infty$,
the probability that a random $k(|G|)$-subset is $\epsilon$-balanced tends to $1$. The matching
lower bound is `erdos_1179.variants.lower_bound`.

See also [543](https://www.erdosproblems.com/543).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1179 : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε < 1 → ∃ k : ℕ → ℕ,
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ (k N : ℝ) / Real.logb 2 N) atTop (nhds 1) ∧
      ∀ (G : ℕ → Type) [∀ i, AddCommGroup (G i)] [∀ i, Fintype (G i)],
        Tendsto (fun i ↦ Fintype.card (G i)) atTop atTop →
          Tendsto (fun i ↦ successProbability (G i) ε (k (Fintype.card (G i)))) atTop
            (nhds 1)

statements.name: Erdos1179.erdos_1179.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
It is trivial that $g_\epsilon(N)\geq \log_2N$: an $\epsilon$-balanced set $A$ with
$\epsilon < 1$ must satisfy $|G| \leq 2^{|A|}$, since every $g$ has a representation.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1179.variants.lower_bound : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε < 1 →
    ∀ A : Finset G, IsBalanced ε A → Fintype.card G ≤ 2 ^ A.card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1180
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1180](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1180)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Sh02] Shparlinski, Igor E., *On a question of Erdős and Graham*. Arch. Math. (Basel) (2002),
  445-448.
- [Gl06] Glibichuk, A. A., *Combinatorial properties of sets of residues modulo a prime and the
  Erdős-Graham problem*. Mat. Zametki (2006), 384-395.
- [PALOMAR-2026-10-12-000005](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-12-000005&version=1)

statements.name: Erdos1180.erdos_1180
statements.doc:
Let $\epsilon>0$. Does there exist a constant $C_\epsilon$ such that, for all primes $p$, every
residue modulo $p$ is the sum of at most $C_\epsilon$ many elements of
$$\{ n^{-1} : 1\leq n\leq p^\epsilon\}$$
where $n^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $n$ modulo $p$?

The original question was answered in the affirmative by Shparlinski [Sh02], who proved that
$\ll \epsilon^{-3}$ summands suffice for all sufficiently large primes. This was improved to
$\ll \epsilon^{-2}$ by Glibichuk [Gl06]. It is trivial that at least $\gg \epsilon^{-1}$
summands are required, and it may be that $C_\epsilon\leq \epsilon^{-1-o(1)}$ is possible.

See also [540](https://www.erdosproblems.com/540).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1180 : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p,
    ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, s.card ≤ C ∧ Represents ε p a s

statements.name: Erdos1180.erdos_1180.variants.shparlinski
statements.doc:
Shparlinski [Sh02] proved that $\ll \epsilon^{-3}$ summands suffice for every residue modulo
every sufficiently large prime, where the threshold on $p$ may depend on $\epsilon$. No bound
polynomial in $\epsilon^{-1}$ can hold for all primes, since when $p^\epsilon < 2$ the only
admissible denominator is $1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1180.variants.shparlinski : ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 →
    ∃ P : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, P ≤ p → p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p,
      ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, (s.card : ℝ) ≤ K * ε⁻¹ ^ 3 ∧ Represents ε p a s

statements.name: Erdos1180.erdos_1180.variants.glibichuk
statements.doc:
Glibichuk [Gl06] improved the bound to $\ll \epsilon^{-2}$ summands, again for every
sufficiently large prime.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1180.variants.glibichuk : ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 →
    ∃ P : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, P ≤ p → p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p,
      ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, (s.card : ℝ) ≤ K * ε⁻¹ ^ 2 ∧ Represents ε p a s

statements.name: Erdos1180.erdos_1180.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc: It is trivial that at least $\gg \epsilon^{-1}$ summands are required.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1180.variants.lower_bound : ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 →
    K * ε⁻¹ ≤ C ε

statements.name: Erdos1180.erdos_1180.variants.optimal
statements.doc:
Is $C_\epsilon\leq \epsilon^{-1-o(1)}$? Here $C_\epsilon$ is the number of summands needed for
every sufficiently large prime, as in `erdos_1180.variants.shparlinski` and
`erdos_1180.variants.glibichuk`. For all primes no such bound holds, since when $p^\epsilon < 2$
the only admissible denominator is $1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1180.variants.optimal : ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ →
    ∀ᶠ ε : ℝ in nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0), ∃ P : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, P ≤ p → p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p,
      ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, (s.card : ℝ) ≤ ε⁻¹ ^ (1 + δ) ∧ Represents ε p a s

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1182
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1182](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1182)
- [Er78] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory*. Proceedings of the Ninth Southeastern Conference on Combinatorics, Graph Theory, and
  Computing (Florida Atlantic Univ., Boca Raton, Fla., 1978) (1978), 29-40.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1978-36.pdf)
- [BEFRS80] Burr, S. A., Erdős, P., Faudree, R. J., Rousseau, C. C. and Schelp, R. H., *An extremal
  problem in generalized Ramsey theory*. Ars Combin. 10 (1980), 193-203.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-04.pdf)
- [Br96] Brandt, S., *Expanding graphs and Ramsey numbers*. Freie Universität Berlin, preprint
  A 96-24 (1996).
- [BBH98] Brandt, S., Brinkmann, G. and Harmuth, T., *All Ramsey numbers $r(K_3,G)$ for connected
  graphs of order 9*. Electron. J. Combin. 5 (1998), #R7.
- [Ch77] Chvátal, V., *Tree-complete graph Ramsey numbers*. J. Graph Theory 1 (1977), 93.
- [NiRo09] Nikiforov, V. and Rousseau, C. C., *Ramsey goodness and beyond*. Combinatorica 29
  (2009), 227-262.

statements.name: Erdos1182.erdos_1182.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that there is a connected graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $f(n)$ edges
such that
$$R(K_3,G)= 2n-1.$$
Let $F(n)$ be maximal such that every connected graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $\leq F(n)$ edges
has
$$R(K_3,G)= 2n-1.$$
Estimate $f(n)$ and $F(n)$. In particular, is it true that $F(n)/n\to \infty$?

This is the first part: estimate $f(n)$. The problem is due to Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and
Schelp [BEFRS80] and appears in [Er78, p. 33]. We read "estimate" as the order of magnitude
`=Θ`. Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp [BEFRS80, Theorem 2] proved
$n^{3/2}(\log n)^{1/2}\ll f(n)\ll n^{5/3}(\log n)^{2/3}$ (`erdos_1182.variants.f_lower`,
`erdos_1182.variants.f_upper`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1182.parts.i :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_1182.parts.i.answer

statements.name: Erdos1182.erdos_1182.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that there is a connected graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $f(n)$ edges
such that
$$R(K_3,G)= 2n-1.$$
Let $F(n)$ be maximal such that every connected graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $\leq F(n)$ edges
has
$$R(K_3,G)= 2n-1.$$
Estimate $f(n)$ and $F(n)$. In particular, is it true that $F(n)/n\to \infty$?

This is the second part: estimate $F(n)$. As an order of magnitude, `=Θ`, this is known:
$F(n)=\Theta(n)$, by $F(n)\ge n-1$ (`erdos_1182.variants.F_ge_pred`, from Chvátal's theorem
[Ch77]) and the linear upper bounds of `erdos_1182.variants.brandt` and
`erdos_1182.variants.nikiforov_rousseau`. The finer question of the asymptotic behaviour of
$F(n)/n$ is open, see `erdos_1182.variants.brandt_expects`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1182.parts.ii :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (F n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_1182.parts.ii.answer

statements.name: Erdos1182.erdos_1182.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that there is a connected graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $f(n)$ edges
such that
$$R(K_3,G)= 2n-1.$$
Let $F(n)$ be maximal such that every connected graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $\leq F(n)$ edges
has
$$R(K_3,G)= 2n-1.$$
Estimate $f(n)$ and $F(n)$. In particular, is it true that $F(n)/n\to \infty$?

This is the third part, asked in [BEFRS80, Section 5] and in [Er78, pp. 33-34], where Erdős says
it seems certain. The answer is no: Brandt [Br96] proved $F(n)\le 84n$ (as recorded on the problem
page, see `erdos_1182.variants.brandt`), and [NiRo09, Theorem 5.1] implies $F(n)<50n$ for large
$n$ (see `erdos_1182.variants.nikiforov_rousseau`).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1182.parts.iii :
    ¬ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (F n : ℝ) / n) atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos1182.erdos_1182.variants.ramsey_ge
statements.doc:
It is trivial that $R(K_3,G)\geq 2n-1$ for any connected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices
([BEFRS80, p. 193]).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1182.variants.ramsey_ge {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (hG : G.Connected) :
    2 * n - 1 ≤ SimpleGraph.graphRamsey (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) G

statements.name: Erdos1182.erdos_1182.variants.chvatal
statements.doc:
By a result of Chvátal [Ch77], $R(K_3,T)=2n-1$ whenever $T$ is a tree on $n$ vertices (as stated
in [BEFRS80, p. 193]).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1182.variants.chvatal {n : ℕ} (T : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (hT : T.IsTree) :
    IsTriangleGood T

statements.name: Erdos1182.erdos_1182.variants.F_ge_pred
statements.doc:
Every connected graph with at most $n-1$ edges is a tree, so Chvátal's theorem [Ch77] gives
$F(n)\geq n-1$ ([BEFRS80, p. 193]).
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1182.variants.F_ge_pred {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : n - 1 ≤ F n

statements.name: Erdos1182.erdos_1182.variants.befrs_lower
statements.doc:
Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp [BEFRS80, Theorem 1(a)] proved
$$\frac{17n+1}{15}\leq F(n),$$
the lower bound for all $n\geq 4$.

We state the integer-part version $n+\lfloor (2n+1)/15\rfloor\le F(n)$, which is what the proof
gives (the number $k$ of extra edges there is an integer with $0\le k\le (2n+1)/15$) and which
follows from the printed bound because $n+\lfloor (2n+1)/15\rfloor\leq(17n+1)/15$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1182.variants.befrs_lower {n : ℕ} (hn : 4 ≤ n) :
    n + (2 * n + 1) / 15 ≤ F n

statements.name: Erdos1182.erdos_1182.variants.befrs_upper
statements.doc:
Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp [BEFRS80, Theorem 1(b)] proved
$$F(n)\leq \left(\frac{27}{4}+o(1)\right)n(\log n)^2.$$
This is superseded by the linear bounds of `erdos_1182.variants.brandt` and
`erdos_1182.variants.nikiforov_rousseau`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1182.variants.befrs_upper :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (F n : ℝ) < (27 / 4 + ε) * n * Real.log n ^ 2

statements.name: Erdos1182.erdos_1182.variants.brandt
statements.doc:
The upper bound was improved to $F(n)\leq 84n$ by Brandt [Br96]. (This resolves the final
question in the negative.)

We have not seen the preprint [Br96]; the bound is as recorded on the problem page, and we state
it for all large $n$. Brandt's method uses expander graphs: almost all regular graphs of large
degree are not $3$-good. In [BBH98, p. 6], of which Brandt is a coauthor, it is stated without
proof that it gives $F(n)<12n$ for large $n$ (there $F(n)$ is called $f(K_3,n)$).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1182.variants.brandt :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, F n ≤ 84 * n

statements.name: Erdos1182.erdos_1182.variants.nikiforov_rousseau
statements.doc:
Nikiforov and Rousseau [NiRo09, Theorem 5.1] proved that for $n$ sufficiently large almost all
connected $100$-regular graphs of order $n$ are not $3$-good. Such a graph has $50n$ edges (and
connected $100$-regular graphs of order $n$ exist for all $n\geq 101$), so $F(n)<50n$ for all
large $n$. This gives a proved linear upper bound for $F$, answering the third part.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1182.variants.nikiforov_rousseau :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, F n < 50 * n

statements.name: Erdos1182.erdos_1182.variants.brandt_expects
statements.doc:
Brandt [Br96] expects that for all large $n$ we have $2n<F(n)<6n$ (as recorded on the problem
page).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1182.variants.brandt_expects :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, 2 * n < F n ∧ F n < 6 * n

statements.name: Erdos1182.erdos_1182.variants.f_lower
statements.doc:
Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp [BEFRS80, Theorem 2] proved that there is a constant
$A>0$ with
$$n^{3/2}(\log n)^{1/2} \ll f(n),$$
more precisely $An^{3/2}(\log n)^{1/2}<f(n)$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1182.variants.f_lower :
    ∃ A > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      A * (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) * Real.sqrt (Real.log n) < (f n : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1182.erdos_1182.variants.f_upper
statements.doc:
Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp [BEFRS80, Theorem 2] proved that there is a constant
$B>0$ with
$$f(n)\ll n^{5/3}(\log n)^{2/3},$$
more precisely $f(n)<Bn^{5/3}(\log n)^{2/3}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1182.variants.f_upper :
    ∃ B > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (f n : ℝ) < B * (n : ℝ) ^ (5 / 3 : ℝ) * Real.log n ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1182.erdos_1182.variants.small_values
statements.doc:
The first few values of $F(n)$ and $f(n)$ (beginning with $n=2$) are $1,2,5,7,8$ and $1,2,5,8,12$
respectively, as reported in [BEFRS80, Table I]. Brandt, Brinkmann and Harmuth [BBH98, Table 2]
extended these (by computer) to all $n\le 12$:
$$F(n):\ 1,2,5,7,8,11,11,16,18,23,23,\qquad f(n):\ 1,2,5,8,12,16,20,27,33,41,49$$
for $n=2,\ldots,12$. (The value for $n=2$ is from [BEFRS80]; [BBH98] start at $n=3$.)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1183
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1183](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1183)
- [Er78] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory*. Proceedings of the Ninth Southeastern Conference on Combinatorics, Graph Theory, and
  Computing (Florida Atlantic Univ., Boca Raton, Fla., 1978) (1978), 29-40.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1978-36.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos1183.erdos_1183.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that in any $2$-colouring of the subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ there is
always a monochromatic family of at least $f(n)$ sets which is closed under taking unions and
intersections. Estimate $f(n)$.

Let $F(n)$ be defined similarly, except that we only require the family be closed under taking
unions. Estimate $F(n)$. In particular, is it true that $F(n)\geq n^{\omega(n)}$ for some
$\omega(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$, and $F(n)<(1+o(1))^n$?

This is the first part, a problem of Erdős and Ulam [Er78, p. 39]. We read "estimate" as
$f(n)=\Theta(\text{answer})$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1183.parts.i :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_1183.parts.i.answer

statements.name: Erdos1183.erdos_1183.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that in any $2$-colouring of the subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ there is
always a monochromatic family of at least $f(n)$ sets which is closed under taking unions and
intersections. Estimate $f(n)$.

Let $F(n)$ be defined similarly, except that we only require the family be closed under taking
unions. Estimate $F(n)$. In particular, is it true that $F(n)\geq n^{\omega(n)}$ for some
$\omega(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$, and $F(n)<(1+o(1))^n$?

This is the second part. We read "estimate" as $F(n)=\Theta(\text{answer})$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1183.parts.ii :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (F n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_1183.parts.ii.answer

statements.name: Erdos1183.erdos_1183.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that in any $2$-colouring of the subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ there is
always a monochromatic family of at least $f(n)$ sets which is closed under taking unions and
intersections. Estimate $f(n)$.

Let $F(n)$ be defined similarly, except that we only require the family be closed under taking
unions. Estimate $F(n)$. In particular, is it true that $F(n)\geq n^{\omega(n)}$ for some
$\omega(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$, and $F(n)<(1+o(1))^n$?

This is the third part, the "in particular" question: both conjuncts must hold. We state it as
printed in [Er78, p. 39]: $F(n) > n^c$ for every $c$ if $n > n_0(c)$, and
$F(n) < (1+\varepsilon)^n$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$ if $n > n_0(\varepsilon)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1183.parts.iii :
    (∀ c : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (n : ℝ) ^ c < (F n : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (F n : ℝ) < (1 + ε) ^ n

statements.name: Erdos1183.erdos_1183.variants.f_ge
statements.doc:
It is trivial that $f(n)\geq \frac{n+1}{2}$, since there is a sequence of $n+1$ many nested
subsets.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1183.variants.f_ge (n : ℕ) : ((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2 ≤ (f n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1185
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1185](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1185)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf)
- [Fu81] Furstenberg, H., *Recurrence in ergodic theory and combinatorial number theory*.
  M. B. Porter Lectures, Princeton University Press (1981), xi+203.

statements.name: Erdos1185.erdos_1185
statements.doc:
Let $\delta>0$ and $k\geq 3$. Is it true that there exists $m\geq 1$ (depending only on $\delta$
and $k$) such that, for all large $N$, if $A,B\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$\lvert A\rvert \geq \delta N$ and $\lvert B\rvert \geq m$ then there is a non-trivial $k$-term
arithmetic progression in $A$ whose common difference is in $B-B$?

A problem of Erdős and Mauldin [Er80, p. 92], who ask the case $k=3$ and say that the same
probably holds for $k$ terms. The answer is no, already for $k=3$: to disprove it suffices to give
an infinite set $B$ such that $B-B$ is not $2$-intersective (a set $S$ is $k$-intersective if
every subset of $\mathbb{N}$ with positive density contains an arithmetic progression of length
$k+1$ whose common difference is in $S$), which was provided by Furstenberg [Fu81]. The statement
below is the negation of the claim for all $\delta>0$ and $k\geq 3$, with $m$ chosen before the
threshold $N_0$ for "large $N$".
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1185 :
    ¬ (∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k →
      ∃ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m ∧ ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N →
        ∀ A B : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N → B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
          δ * (N : ℝ) ≤ (A.card : ℝ) → m ≤ B.card → HasAPWithStepInDiff k A B)

statements.name: Erdos1185.erdos_1185.variants.k_three
statements.doc:
The answer is already negative for $k=3$: there is a density $\delta>0$ such that for every
$m\geq 1$ and every $N_0$ there are $N\geq N_0$ and $A,B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$\lvert A\rvert\geq\delta N$, $\lvert B\rvert\geq m$, and no non-trivial $3$-term arithmetic
progression in $A$ whose common difference is in $B-B$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1185.variants.k_three :
    ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → ∀ N₀ : ℕ, ∃ N : ℕ, ∃ A B : Finset ℕ,
      N₀ ≤ N ∧ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N ∧ B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N ∧
        δ * (N : ℝ) ≤ (A.card : ℝ) ∧ m ≤ B.card ∧ ¬ HasAPWithStepInDiff 3 A B

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1186
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1186](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1186)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf)
- [PRS08] Parrilo, Pablo A. and Robertson, Aaron and Saracino, Dan, *On the asymptotic minimum
  number of monochromatic 3-term arithmetic progressions*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (2008),
  185-192. [arXiv:math/0609532](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0609532)

statements.name: Erdos1186.erdos_1186
statements.doc:
Let $\delta_k$ be such that in any $2$-colouring of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ there exist at least
$(\delta_k+o(1))n^2$ many monochromatic $k$-term arithmetic progressions. Give reasonable bounds
(or even an asymptotic formula) for $\delta_k$.

We read "reasonable bounds" as determining the order of magnitude of $\delta_k$ as $k \to \infty$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1186 : δ =Θ[atTop] erdos_1186.answer

statements.name: Erdos1186.erdos_1186.variants.van_der_waerden
statements.doc:
Van der Waerden's theorem implies $\delta_k\gg_k 1$.

For fixed $k$ this says $\delta_k > 0$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1186.variants.van_der_waerden (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) : 0 < δ k

statements.name: Erdos1186.erdos_1186.variants.probabilistic
statements.doc:
The probabilistic method implies
$$\delta_k \leq \frac{1}{(k-1)2^{k}}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1186.variants.probabilistic (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    δ k ≤ 1 / (((k : ℝ) - 1) * 2 ^ k)

statements.name: Erdos1186.erdos_1186.variants.prs_bounds
statements.doc:
Parrilo, Robertson, and Saracino [PRS08] have proved
$$0.0511\approx \frac{1675}{32768}\leq \delta_3 \leq \frac{117}{2192}\approx 0.0533,$$
and conjectured the upper bound is correct.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1186.variants.prs_bounds : 1675 / 32768 ≤ δ 3 ∧ δ 3 ≤ 117 / 2192

statements.name: Erdos1186.erdos_1186.variants.prs_conjecture
statements.doc:
Parrilo, Robertson, and Saracino [PRS08] have proved
$$0.0511\approx \frac{1675}{32768}\leq \delta_3 \leq \frac{117}{2192}\approx 0.0533,$$
and conjectured the upper bound is correct.

This is the conjecture $\delta_3 = \frac{117}{2192}$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1186.variants.prs_conjecture : δ 3 = 117 / 2192

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1187
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1187](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1187)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [GrTa08] Green, Ben and Tao, Terence, *The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic
  progressions*. Ann. of Math. (2) (2008), 481-547.

statements.name: Erdos1187.erdos_1187.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 3$. Is it true that, in any finite colouring of the integers, there are monochromatic
arithmetic progressions of primes of length $k$?

It follows from the theorem of Green and Tao [GrTa08] (that any set of primes with positive
relative density contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions) that the answer to the first
question is yes for any $k\geq 3$.

See also [219](https://www.erdosproblems.com/219).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1187.parts.i : ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k →
    ∀ (κ : Type) [Finite κ] (c : ℤ → κ), ∃ S : Set ℤ, S.IsAPOfLength k ∧
      (∀ n ∈ S, ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ (p : ℤ) = n) ∧
        ∃ γ : κ, ∀ n ∈ S, c n = γ

statements.name: Erdos1187.erdos_1187.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $k\geq 3$. In any finite colouring of the integers, are there monochromatic arithmetic
progressions of length $k$ whose common difference is a prime?

The answer to the second question is trivially no: colouring the integers by their residue modulo
$4$ creates a colouring in which there is not even any monochromatic pair of integers whose
difference is a prime. Alternatively, one can just use $2$ colours and avoid any $3$-term
progressions whose difference is a prime by colouring $0,1\pmod{4}$ red and $2,3\pmod{4}$ blue.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1187.parts.ii : ¬ ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k →
    ∀ (κ : Type) [Finite κ] (c : ℤ → κ), ∃ (a : ℤ) (p : ℕ) (S : Set ℤ), p.Prime ∧
      S.IsAPOfLengthWith k a p ∧ ∃ γ : κ, ∀ n ∈ S, c n = γ

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1188
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1188](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1188)

statements.name: Erdos1188.erdos_1188
statements.doc:
Call a set of distinct integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ with associated congruence
classes $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ a distinct covering system if every integer satisfies at
least one of these congruences. A minimal distinct covering system is one such
that no proper subset forms a covering system. Let $F(x)$ count the number of
minimal distinct covering systems with all moduli in $[1,x]$. Estimate $F(x)$.

The estimate is `log(log F(x)) / log x → 1`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1188 :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => Real.log (Real.log (coveringCount x : ℝ)) / Real.log (x : ℝ))
      atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1189
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1189](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1189)
- [Er80] Erdős, P., *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math. 6
  (1980), 89-115. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf)
- [Si85] Simpson, R. J., *Regular coverings of the integers by arithmetic progressions*. Acta Arith.
  45 (1985), 145-152.
- [Su07] Sun, Z.-W., *On covering numbers*. Combinatorial Number Theory, de Gruyter (2007),
  443-453. [arXiv:math/0601017](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0601017)
- [BBMST24] Balister, P., Bollobás, B., Morris, R., Sahasrabudhe, J. and Tiba, M., *The structure
  and number of Erdős covering systems*. J. Eur. Math. Soc. 26 (2024), 75-109.
  [arXiv:1904.04806](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04806)

See also [erdosproblems.com/1188](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1188), which counts minimal
covering systems with bounded moduli.

statements.name: Erdos1189.erdos_1189.parts.i
statements.doc:
Call a set of distinct integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ a covering set if there is a choice of
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ such that every integer satisfies at least one of these
congruences. A set is an irreducible covering set if no proper subset is a covering set.

How many irreducible covering sets of size $k$ are there?

This is the first part of the questions of Erdős [Er80, p. 95]. We read "how many" as asking for
the asymptotics of $\log I(k)$, where $I(k)$ is the number of irreducible covering sets of size
$k$; this is the scale on which the number of minimal covering systems is known [BBMST24].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1189.parts.i :
    (fun k : ℕ ↦ Real.log (irreducibleCount k : ℝ)) ~[atTop] erdos_1189.parts.i.answer

statements.name: Erdos1189.erdos_1189.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Call a set of distinct integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ a covering set if there is a choice of
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ such that every integer satisfies at least one of these
congruences. A set is an irreducible covering set if no proper subset is a covering set.

What is the minimum and maximum that $n_k$ can be?

This is the second part. Here $n_k$ is the largest element of an irreducible covering set of
size $k$. The answer is a pair (minimum, maximum), stated for each $k$ for which an irreducible
covering set of size $k$ exists.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1189.parts.ii (k : ℕ)
    (hk : ∃ M : Finset ℕ, IsIrreducibleCoveringSet M ∧ M.card = k) :
    IsLeast (largestModulus k) (erdos_1189.parts.ii.answer k).1 ∧
      IsGreatest (largestModulus k) (erdos_1189.parts.ii.answer k).2

statements.name: Erdos1189.erdos_1189.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Call a set of distinct integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ a covering set if there is a choice of
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ such that every integer satisfies at least one of these
congruences. A set is an irreducible covering set if no proper subset is a covering set.

Determine or estimate $\max \sum\frac{1}{n_i}$, where the maximum ranges over all irreducible
covering sets of size $k$.

This is the third part. We read "determine or estimate" as an estimate up to constant factors.
In [Er80, p. 95] the maximum is taken over the irreducible covering sets
$1<n_1<\cdots<n_k\leq x$, as a function of $x$; we follow the problem page, which takes it over
the irreducible covering sets of size $k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1189.parts.iii :
    maxReciprocalSum =Θ[atTop] erdos_1189.parts.iii.answer

statements.name: Erdos1189.erdos_1189.parts.iv
statements.doc:
Call a set of distinct integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ a covering set if there is a choice of
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ such that every integer satisfies at least one of these
congruences. A set is an irreducible covering set if no proper subset is a covering set.

Are there infinitely many $n$ such that the divisors of $n$ (which are $>1$) form an irreducible
covering set?

This is the fourth part. Sun [Su07, Theorem 1.4(i) and Corollary 1.3] proved that the answer is
yes: see `erdos_1189.variants.sun`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1189.parts.iv :
    {n : ℕ | IsIrreducibleCoveringSet (n.divisors.filter (1 < ·))}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos1189.erdos_1189.variants.sun
statements.doc:
The divisors of $12$ (which are $>1$) are an example of an irreducible covering set. Sun [Su07]
proved more generally that, for any odd prime $p$, the divisors (which are $>1$) of $2^{p-1}p$
form an irreducible covering set, settling the final question.

That $n=12$ is an example is already noted in [Er80, p. 95].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1189.variants.sun (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hodd : Odd p) :
    IsIrreducibleCoveringSet ((2 ^ (p - 1) * p).divisors.filter (1 < ·))

statements.name: Erdos1189.erdos_1189.variants.simpson
statements.doc:
Simpson [Si85] proved $n_k\leq 2^{k-1}$.

Here $n_k$ is the largest element of an irreducible covering set of size $k$. The bound follows
from Simpson's theorem [Si85] (see [BBMST24, Theorem 2.4]), as stated in [BBMST24, Section 1].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1189.variants.simpson (M : Finset ℕ) (hM : IsIrreducibleCoveringSet M) :
    ∀ n ∈ M, n ≤ 2 ^ (M.card - 1)

statements.name: Erdos1189.erdos_1189.variants.bbmst
statements.doc:
Let $I(k)$ count the number of irreducible covering sets of size $k$. Balister, Bollobás, Morris,
Sahasrabudhe, and Tiba [BBMST24] proved that
$$I(k) \leq \exp\left((c+o(1))\frac{k^{3/2}}{(\log k)^{1/2}}\right)$$
by proving that the right-hand side is an asymptotic for the number of minimal covering systems
on $k$ moduli.

Here $c = 4\sqrt{\tau}/3$ [BBMST24, Theorem 1.1]. The bound for $I(k)$ follows because each
irreducible covering set is the set of moduli of a minimal covering system. The $o(1)$ is stated
with an arbitrary $\varepsilon > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1189.variants.bbmst (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, (irreducibleCount k : ℝ) ≤
      Real.exp ((4 * Real.sqrt bbmstTau / 3 + ε) *
        ((k : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) / Real.sqrt (Real.log k)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1190
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1190](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1190)
- [BFV13] de la Bretèche, Régis and Ford, Kevin and Vandehey, Joseph, *On non-intersecting
  arithmetic progressions*. Acta Arith. (2013), 381-392.
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.

statements.name: Erdos1190.erdos_1190
statements.doc:
Let
$$\epsilon_m=\max \sum \frac{1}{n_i}$$
where the maximum is taken over all finite sequences $m<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ for which there exist
congruences $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ such that no integer satisfies two such congruences.

Estimate $\epsilon_m$.

The resolution of [202] by GPT-5.4 Pro implies via the same reduction that
$$\epsilon_m=L(m)^{-1+o(1)},$$
where $L(m)=\exp(\sqrt{\log m\log\log m})$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1190 : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ m : ℕ in atTop,
    scaleL m ^ (-1 - ε : ℝ) < eps m ∧ eps m < scaleL m ^ (-1 + ε : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1190.erdos_1190.variants.lt_one
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er80] seems to credit Mirsky and Newman with the result that $\epsilon_m<1$, but gives no
reference.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1190.variants.lt_one (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (S : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℤ)
    (hS : ∀ n ∈ S, m < n)
    (hdisj : ∀ n ∈ S, ∀ n' ∈ S, n ≠ n' → ¬ ∃ x : ℤ, x ≡ a n [ZMOD n] ∧ x ≡ a n' [ZMOD n']) :
    (∑ n ∈ S, (n : ℝ)⁻¹) < 1

statements.name: Erdos1190.erdos_1190.variants.tendsto_zero
statements.doc: He could not even decide whether $\epsilon_m\to 0$ as $m\to \infty$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1190.variants.tendsto_zero : Tendsto eps atTop (𝓝 0)

statements.name: Erdos1190.erdos_1190.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc:
The work of de la Bretèche, Ford, and Vandehey [BFV13] implies
$$L(m)^{-1+o(1)}< \epsilon_m < L(m)^{-\sqrt{3}/2+o(1)},$$
where $L(m)=\exp(\sqrt{\log m\log\log m})$. The lower bound is implicit in their construction.
