statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1190.variants.lower_bound : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ m : ℕ in atTop,
    scaleL m ^ (-1 - ε : ℝ) < eps m

statements.name: Erdos1190.erdos_1190.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
The work of de la Bretèche, Ford, and Vandehey [BFV13] implies
$$L(m)^{-1+o(1)}< \epsilon_m < L(m)^{-\sqrt{3}/2+o(1)},$$
where $L(m)=\exp(\sqrt{\log m\log\log m})$. The upper bound follows immediately from their upper
bound as reported in [202] and partial summation.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1190.variants.upper_bound : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ m : ℕ in atTop,
    eps m < scaleL m ^ (-(sqrt 3 / 2) + ε : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1191
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1191](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1191)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [HaRo66] Halberstam, H. and Roth, K. F., *Sequences. Vol. I*. (1966), xx+291.

statements.name: Erdos1191.erdos_1191.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite Sidon set. Is it true that
$$\liminf_{x\to \infty} \frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{x^{1/2}}(\log x)^{1/2}=0?$$

Here $x$ runs over $\mathbb{N}$ and the $\liminf$ is taken in `ℝ≥0∞`, so that it is $\infty$
rather than $0$ when the sequence tends to infinity.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1191.parts.i : ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → IsSidon A →
    liminf (fun x : ℕ ↦ ENNReal.ofReal
      ((A ∩ .Icc 1 x).ncard / (x : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) * log x ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))) atTop = 0

statements.name: Erdos1191.erdos_1191.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Does there exist an infinite Sidon set $A$ such that
$$\liminf_{x\to \infty} \frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{x^{1/2}}(\log x)^c>0$$
for some $c>0$?

A positive answer would also give a positive answer to Erdős Problem 39.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1191.parts.ii : ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ IsSidon A ∧
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), 0 < liminf (fun x : ℕ ↦ ENNReal.ofReal
      ((A ∩ .Icc 1 x).ncard / (x : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) * log x ^ c)) atTop

statements.name: Erdos1191.erdos_1191.variants.liminf_le
statements.doc:
Erdős proved (see for example [HaRo66]) that if $A$ is an infinite Sidon set then
$$\liminf_{x\to \infty} \frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{x^{1/2}}(\log x)^{1/2}\leq c$$
for some constant $c>0$. See also `erdos_158.variants.isSidon'`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1191.variants.liminf_le {A : Set ℕ} (hAinf : A.Infinite) (hAsid : IsSidon A) :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), liminf (fun x : ℕ ↦ ENNReal.ofReal
      ((A ∩ .Icc 1 x).ncard / (x : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) * log x ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))) atTop ≤
        ENNReal.ofReal c

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1192
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1192](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1192)
- [Ru90] Ruzsa, Imre Z., A just basis. Monatsh. Math. (1990), 145--151.
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory.
  Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89--115.

statements.name: Erdos1192.erdos_1192
statements.doc:
Does there exist, for all $r\geq 2$, a basis $A$ of order $r$ (so that $f_r(n)>0$ for all
large $n$) such that $$\sum_{n\leq x}f_r(n)^2 \ll x$$ for all $x$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1192 :
    ∀ r ≥ 2, ∃ A : Set ℕ,
      (∀ᶠ n in atTop, f_r A r n > 0) ∧
      (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ ∑ n ∈ range (x + 1), (f_r A r n : ℝ) ^ 2) =O[atTop]
        (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (x : ℝ))

statements.name: Erdos1192.erdos_1192.variants.renyi
statements.doc:
Erdős and Rényi proved by the probabilistic method that there exists a set $A$ such that
$$\sum_{n\leq x}f_r(n)^2 \ll x$$ and $$\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert\gg x^{1/r}$$ for all $x$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1192.variants.renyi :
    ∀ r ≥ 2, ∃ A : Set ℕ,
      ((fun (x : ℕ) ↦ ∑ n ∈ range (x + 1), (f_r A r n : ℝ) ^ 2) =O[atTop]
        (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (x : ℝ))) ∧
      ((fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (x : ℝ) ^ (1 / (r : ℝ))) =O[atTop]
        (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (count (· ∈ A) x : ℝ)))

statements.name: Erdos1192.erdos_1192.variants.ruzsa
statements.doc: Ruzsa [Ru90] proved that the answer is yes for $r=2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1192.variants.ruzsa :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ,
      (∀ᶠ n in atTop, f_r A 2 n > 0) ∧
      (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ ∑ n ∈ range (x + 1), (f_r A 2 n : ℝ) ^ 2) =O[atTop]
        (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (x : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1193
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1193](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1193)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.

statements.name: Erdos1193.erdos_1193.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ and let $g(n)$ be a non-decreasing function of $n$ which is always $>0$.

Is the lower density of
$$\{ n : 1_A\ast 1_A(n)=g(n)\}$$
always $0$?

The answer is trivially no to both questions: indeed if $A=\mathbb{N}$ (assuming $0\in\mathbb{N}$)
then $1_A\ast 1_A(n)=n+1$ for all $n$. Presumably Erdős had some additional restrictions on either
$g$ or $A$ in mind, but these are not recorded in [Er80].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1193.parts.i :
    ¬ ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (g : ℕ → ℕ), Monotone g → (∀ n, 0 < g n) →
      {n : ℕ | sumRep A n = g n}.lowerDensity = 0

statements.name: Erdos1193.erdos_1193.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ and let $g(n)$ be a non-decreasing function of $n$ which is always $>0$.

Is the upper density of
$$\{ n : 1_A\ast 1_A(n)=g(n)\}$$
always $<c$ for some constant $c<1$?

The answer is trivially no to both questions: indeed if $A=\mathbb{N}$ (assuming $0\in\mathbb{N}$)
then $1_A\ast 1_A(n)=n+1$ for all $n$. Presumably Erdős had some additional restrictions on either
$g$ or $A$ in mind, but these are not recorded in [Er80].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1193.parts.ii :
    ¬ ∃ c < (1 : ℝ), ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (g : ℕ → ℕ), Monotone g → (∀ n, 0 < g n) →
      {n : ℕ | sumRep A n = g n}.upperDensity < c

statements.name: Erdos1193.erdos_1193.variants.sumRep_univ
statements.doc: Indeed if $A=\mathbb{N}$ (assuming $0\in\mathbb{N}$) then $1_A\ast 1_A(n)=n+1$ for all $n$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1193.variants.sumRep_univ (n : ℕ) : sumRep (Set.univ : Set ℕ) n = n + 1

statements.name: Erdos1193.erdos_1193.variants.upper_density_pos
statements.doc: Erdős writes the upper density can be positive, but he believes it is bounded away from $1$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1193.variants.upper_density_pos :
    ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (g : ℕ → ℕ), Monotone g ∧ (∀ n, 0 < g n) ∧
      0 < {n : ℕ | sumRep A n = g n}.upperDensity

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1194
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1194](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1194)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  6 (1980), 89-115. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf)
- [HaRo66] Halberstam, H. and Roth, K. F., *Sequences. Vol. I*. Oxford University Press, Oxford
  (1966), xx+291.
- [Le04] Lev, Vsevolod F., *Reconstructing integer sets from their representation functions*.
  Electron. J. Combin. 11 (2004), Research Paper 78, 6 pp.
  [Link](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/view/v11i1r78)

statements.name: Erdos1194.erdos_1194
statements.doc:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ be such that every integer $n\geq 1$ can be written uniquely as
$a_n-b_n$ for some $a_n,b_n\in A$. How fast must $a_n/n$ increase?

A question of Erdős [Er80, p. 100]. Here $a_n$ is the larger element of the representation of
$n$, not the $n$th element of $A$. We read "must increase" as: the answer is the set of
non-decreasing $G$ such that every such $A$ has $a_n \geq c\,n\,G(n)$ for infinitely many $n$,
for some $c>0$ depending on $A$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1194 :
    {G : ℕ → ℝ | Monotone G ∧ ∀ A : Set ℕ, IsPerfectDifferenceSetInt A →
      ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), HasLargeElement A (fun n ↦ c * G n * n)} = erdos_1194.answer

statements.name: Erdos1194.erdos_1194.variants.exists_perfect_difference_set
statements.doc:
Such a set is called a perfect difference set; they can be constructed, for example, by a greedy
approach (as detailed by Lev [Le04]).

Erdős [Er80, p. 100] remarks that it is easy to construct such a sequence, and [Le04, Section 3]
constructs a perfect difference set $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ (positive integers) greedily.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1194.variants.exists_perfect_difference_set :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, IsPerfectDifferenceSetInt A

statements.name: Erdos1194.erdos_1194.variants.greedy_upper_bound
statements.doc:
The greedy construction achieves $a_n\ll n^3$.

In the greedy construction of [Le04, Section 3], step $k$ adds $z_k$ and $z_k+d_k$, where $d_k$ is
the least non-negative integer that is not yet a difference and $z_k$ is the least admissible
positive integer. There are $O(k^3)$ excluded choices for $z_k$ and $d_k=O(k^2)$, so every element
added by step $k$ is $O(k^3)$. As $d_1=0$ and the $d_k$ increase, $n$ is represented by step
$n+1$, which gives $a_n\ll n^3$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1194.variants.greedy_upper_bound :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, IsPerfectDifferenceSetInt A ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
      ∀ a, IsLargerElement A n a → (a : ℝ) ≤ C * (n : ℝ) ^ 3

statements.name: Erdos1194.erdos_1194.variants.limsup_eq_top
statements.doc:
Erdős [Er80, p. 100] wrote it is 'easy to see' that
$$\limsup_{n\to \infty}\frac{a_n}{n}=\infty.$$
Indeed, since $A$ must be a Sidon set, if $a_n \leq f(n)n$ for all $n$, then all differences in
$[1,x/f(x)]$ can be realised by differences from $A\cap [1,x]$, and hence
$\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert^2 \gg x/f(x)$. Erdős (see for example [HaRo66]) proved that for
infinitely many $x$, $\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert \ll (x/\log x)^{1/2}$, which is a contradiction for
a suitable choice of $f$.

Formally: for every perfect difference set $A$ and every $C$, $a_n \geq Cn$ for infinitely many
$n$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1194.variants.limsup_eq_top :
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, IsPerfectDifferenceSetInt A → ∀ C : ℝ, HasLargeElement A (fun n ↦ C * n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1195
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1195](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1195)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf)
- [Ha70] Haight, J. A., *A linear set of infinite measure with no two points having integral
  ratio*. Mathematika (1970), 133--138.
- [HoGPT] Ho, Boon Suan and GPT-5.4 Pro, comments on Erdős Problem 1195. erdosproblems.com forum
  thread. [Forum](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/1195)
- [Sc69] Schmidt, W. M., *Disproof of some conjectures on Diophantine approximations*. Studia Sci.
  Math. Hungar. (1969), 137-144.
- [Sz71] Szemerédi, E., *On a problem of W. Schmidt*. Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. (1971), 287--288.

statements.name: Erdos1195.erdos_1195
statements.doc:
Let $S\subset \mathbb{R}$ be a set of infinite measure such that $x/y$ is never an integer for all
distinct $x,y\in S$.

How fast can $\lvert S\cap (0,x)\rvert$ tend to infinity?

A question of Erdős [Er80, p. 101]. Ho Boon Suan and GPT-5.4 Pro [HoGPT] settled this: if
$F:[1,\infty)\to [0,\infty)$ is a non-decreasing function tending to infinity, then there exists
such a set $S$ with
$\lvert S\cap (0,x)\rvert \geq F(x)$ if and only if
$$\int_1^\infty \frac{F(x)}{x^2}\mathrm{d}x < \infty.$$
Here $\lvert\cdot\rvert$ is Lebesgue measure, $S$ is measurable, and the inequality is required for
all sufficiently large $x$. The statement says that the set of such $F$ is exactly the answer.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1195 :
    {F : ℝ → ℝ | IsGrowthRate F ∧ HasSet F} = erdos_1195.answer

statements.name: Erdos1195.erdos_1195.variants.exists_set
statements.doc:
Schmidt [Sc69] asked whether such a set exists. Haight [Ha70] constructed a measurable set
$E\subset(0,\infty)$ of infinite Lebesgue measure such that $x_1/x_2$ is never an integer for
distinct $x_1,x_2\in E$, and Szemerédi [Sz71] independently constructed such a set.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1195.variants.exists_set :
    ∃ S : Set ℝ, MeasurableSet S ∧ S ⊆ Set.Ioi 0 ∧ volume S = ⊤ ∧ IntegerRatioFree S

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1196
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1196](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1196)

statements.name: Erdos1196.erdos_1196
statements.doc:
Is it true that, for any $x$, if $A\subset [x,\infty)$ is a primitive set of integers (so that no distinct elements of $A$ divide each other) then$$\sum_{a\in A}\frac{1}{a\log a}< 1+o(1),$$where the $o(1)$ term $\to 0$ as $x\to \infty$?
-
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1196 :
    ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[Filter.atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ x > (0 : ℕ), ∀ A ⊆ Set.Ici x, IsPrimitive A →
       ∑' (a : A), (1 / ((a.val : ℝ).log * a)) < 1 + o x

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1197
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1197](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1197)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [BuMa99] Buczolich, Zoltán and Mauldin, R. Daniel, *On the convergence of
  $\sum^\infty_{n=1}f(nx)$ for measurable functions*. Mathematika (1999), 337--341.

statements.name: Erdos1197.erdos_1197
statements.doc:
Let $E\subset (0,\infty)$ be a set of positive measure. Is it true that, for almost all $x>0$,
for all sufficiently large (depending on $x$) integers $n$ there exists an integer $r\geq 1$ such
that $nx\in r\cdot E$?

A problem of Haight, who constructed a set $E\subset (0,\infty)$ of infinite measure such that,
for all $x\in E$, $x\not\in r\cdot E$ if $r\geq 2$, and also for all $x>0$, if $n$ is large enough
then $nx\not\in E$ (see [1195](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1195)).

This is trivially true if $E$ contains an interval $(a,b)$ with $a<b$, since for any $x>0$, for
all large $n$, the interval $(\frac{nx}{b},\frac{nx}{a})$ has length $>1$ so contains at least
one integer $r\geq 1$.

Buczolich and Mauldin [BuMa99] proved that there exists an open set $E\subset (0,\infty)$ and two
intervals $I,J\subset [1/2,1)$ such that, for all $x\in I$, $x\in \frac{1}{n}\cdot E$ for
infinitely many $n\geq 1$, and for almost all $x\in J$, $x\not\in \frac{1}{n}\cdot E$ for all
sufficiently large (depending on $x$) $n$.

This was solved in the negative by ebarschkis in the comments, who constructed a counterexample
using a variant of the Buczolich-Mauldin construction.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1197 : ¬ ∀ E : Set ℝ, MeasurableSet E → E ⊆ Set.Ioi 0 → 0 < volume E →
    ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume.restrict (Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ))), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∃ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r ∧ (n : ℝ) * x ∈ (r : ℝ) • E

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1198
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1198](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1198)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [Hi74] Hindman, Neil, *Finite sums from sequences within cells of a partition of $\mathbb{N}$*.
  J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. A (1974), 1-11.
- [Sm95] Smith, Gregory L., *Partitions and ($m$ and $n$) sums of products*. J. Combin. Theory
  Ser. A (1995), 77-94.

statements.name: Erdos1198.erdos_1198
statements.doc:
If $\mathbb{N}$ is $2$-coloured, must there exist an infinite set $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}$ such that
all expressions of the shape
$$\sum_{j=1}^{k}\prod_{i\in S_j}a_i,$$
for $k\geq 1$ and pairwise disjoint nonempty finite sets of indices $S_1,\ldots,S_k$ (excluding the
trivial expressions $a_i$, that is $k=1$ and $|S_1|=1$), have the same colour?

Erdős [Er80, p.104] wrote that "one would perhaps guess that the answer must be 'no' but no
counterexample is in sight". The case where every $S_j$ is a singleton is Hindman's theorem [Hi74].
The answer is no: a counterexample was given by Smith [Sm95].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1198 :
    ¬ ∀ c : ℕ → Fin 2, ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a ∧ 0 < a 0 ∧ ∃ col : Fin 2,
      ∀ (k : ℕ) (S : Fin k → Finset ℕ), 0 < k → (∀ j, (S j).Nonempty) →
        Pairwise (fun j j' => Disjoint (S j) (S j')) → ¬ (k = 1 ∧ ∀ j, #(S j) = 1) →
        c (∑ j, ∏ i ∈ S j, a i) = col

statements.name: Erdos1198.erdos_1198.variants.hindman
statements.doc:
The case where every $S_j$ is a singleton (Hindman's theorem [Hi74]): for every $2$-colouring of
$\mathbb{N}$ there is an infinite set all of whose finite sums of distinct elements have the same
colour.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1198.variants.hindman :
    ∀ c : ℕ → Fin 2, ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a ∧ 0 < a 0 ∧ ∃ col : Fin 2,
      ∀ T : Finset ℕ, T.Nonempty → c (∑ i ∈ T, a i) = col

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1199
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1199](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1199)
- [Hi79] Hindman, Neil, Partitions and sums of integers with repetition.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1979), 19--32.
- [Ow74] J. Owings, E2494. Amer. Math. Monthly (1974), 902.

statements.name: Erdos1199.erdos_1199
statements.doc:
Is it true that in any 2-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there exists an infinite set $A$
such that all elements of $A+A$ are the same colour?

A conjecture of Owings [Ow74].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1199 :
    ∀ (color : ℕ → Fin 2), ∃ (A : Set ℕ),
    A.Infinite ∧ ∀ n ∈ (A+A), ∀ m ∈ (A+A), color n = color m

statements.name: Erdos1199.erdos_1199.variants.three
statements.doc: Hindman [Hi79] has shown that this is false for 3-colourings.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1199.variants.three :
    ∃ (color : ℕ → Fin 3), ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
    A.Infinite → ∃ n ∈ (A+A), ∃ m ∈ (A+A), color n ≠ color m

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1201
problems.doc: *Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1201](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1201)

statements.name: Erdos1201.erdos_1201
statements.doc:
Is it true that for every $\epsilon,\eta>0$ there exists a $k$ such that the density of $n$
for which $P(n(n+1)\cdots(n+k))>n^{1-\epsilon}$ is at least $1-\eta$ (where $P(m)$ is the greatest
prime divisor of $m$)?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1201 :
    ∀ ε > 0, ∀ η > 0, ∃ k : ℕ,
      atTop.liminf (fun x : ℕ ↦
        (((count (· ∈ Erdos1201Set ε k) x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ)) : EReal)) ≥ (1 - η : EReal)

statements.name: Erdos1201.erdos_1201.variants.epsilon_half
statements.doc: Erdős wrote he could prove this for $\epsilon=1/2$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1201.variants.epsilon_half :
    ∀ η > 0, ∃ k : ℕ,
      atTop.liminf (fun x : ℕ ↦
        (((count (· ∈ Erdos1201Set (1 / 2 : ℝ) k) x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ)) : EReal)) ≥ (1 - η : EReal)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1202
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1202](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1202)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [Gr24] [Ben Green's 100 Open Problems, Problem 44](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.44)

statements.name: Erdos1202.erdos_1202
statements.doc:
Let $\epsilon > 0$. Does there exist $k$ such that, for every $n$, any primes
$p_1 < \cdots < p_k < n^{1-\epsilon}$ and any sets $A_i$ of $\frac{p_i - 1}{2}$ residue classes
modulo $p_i$, the number of $m \le n$ that avoid $A_i \pmod{p_i}$ for every $i$ is at most
$\epsilon n$?

The answer is negative: according to [erdosproblems.com/1202](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1202),
Price (with GPT-5.4 Pro) gave a construction in which the $A_i$ are intervals of residues and at
least $(1/2 - c) n$ integers in $[1, n]$ survive. The large sieve gives a positive answer when
$p_k < n^{1/2}$ instead. See also `Green44` for a related special case.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1202 :
    ¬ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ (n : ℕ) (p : Fin k → ℕ) (A : (i : Fin k) → Finset (ZMod (p i))),
      (∀ i, (p i).Prime) →
      StrictMono p →
      (∀ i, (p i : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε)) →
      (∀ i, (A i).card = (p i - 1) / 2) →
      ((((Finset.Icc 1 n).filter (fun m => ∀ i, (m : ZMod (p i)) ∉ A i)).card : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ ε * n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1203
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1203](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1203)

statements.name: Erdos1203.erdos_1203
statements.doc: Prove that $F(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1203 :
    Tendsto F atTop atTop

statements.name: Erdos1203.erdos_1203.variants.lower_bound
statements.doc: It is easy to prove that $F(n)\geq 1-o(1)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1203.variants.lower_bound :
    ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, F n ≥ 1 - ε

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1204
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1204](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1204)
- [El65] Elliott, P. D. T. A., *On sequences of integers*. Quart. J. Math. Oxford Ser. (2) 16
  (1965), 35-45.
- [Er80] Erdős, P., *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math. 6
  (1980), 89-115.
- [Po14c] Polymath, D. H. J., *Variants of the Selberg sieve, and bounded intervals containing
  many primes*. Res. Math. Sci. 1 (2014), Art. 12.
  [arXiv:1407.4897](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.4897)

statements.name: Erdos1204.erdos_1204.parts.i
statements.doc:
We call a sequence of integers $0\leq a_1<\cdots <a_k$ admissible if it is missing at least one
congruence class modulo every prime $p$. Let $A(k)=\min a_k$. Estimate $A(k)$ - in particular, is
it true that
$$A(k)\sim k\log k?$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1204.parts.i :
    (fun k : ℕ ↦ (A k : ℝ)) ~[atTop] fun k : ℕ ↦ (k : ℝ) * Real.log k

statements.name: Erdos1204.erdos_1204.parts.ii
statements.doc:
We call a sequence of integers $0\leq a_1<\cdots <a_k$ admissible if it is missing at least one
congruence class modulo every prime $p$. Estimate
$$B(k)=\min \frac{a_1+\cdots+a_k}{k}.$$

We read "estimate" as finding an asymptotic formula, since $B(k)\asymp k\log k$ already follows
from the known bounds for $A(k)$ (as $a_j\geq A(j)$).
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1204.parts.ii : B ~[atTop] erdos_1204.parts.ii.answer

statements.name: Erdos1204.erdos_1204.variants.A_lower
statements.doc:
It is known that $(1/2+o(1))k\log k \leq A(k)$. This lower bound is originally due to Elliott
[El65], but was rediscovered by the Polymath project on bounded gaps between primes [Po14c].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1204.variants.A_lower :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, (1 / 2 - ε) * k * Real.log k ≤ (A k : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1204.erdos_1204.variants.A_upper
statements.doc: It is known that $A(k)\leq (1+o(1))k\log k$, by taking the $k$ smallest primes $>k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1204.variants.A_upper :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, (A k : ℝ) ≤ (1 + ε) * k * Real.log k

statements.name: Erdos1204.erdos_1204.variants.B_upper
statements.doc: Taking the first $k$ primes which are $>k$ implies $B(k)\leq (1/2+o(1))k\log k$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1204.variants.B_upper :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, B k ≤ (1 / 2 + ε) * k * Real.log k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1205
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1205](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1205)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos1205.erdos_1205
statements.doc:
Let $F(x)$ be maximal such that there exists, for all $n\leq x$, a congruence class
$a_n\pmod{n}$ such that every $m\leq x$ satisfies at least $F(x)$ of these congruences.

Estimate $F(x)$.

Erdős [Er80, p. 108] describes $F(x)\to\infty$ as a simple exercise and asks how fast $F(x)$
tends to infinity. The estimate $F(x)\sim\log x$ comes from the argument given on
erdosproblems.com/1205 (a pigeonhole upper bound and a probabilistic lower bound), not from a
paper.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1205 : (fun x : ℕ ↦ (F x : ℝ)) ~[atTop] erdos_1205.answer

statements.name: Erdos1205.erdos_1205.variants.upper_bound
statements.doc:
The pigeonhole principle implies $F(x)\leq \sum_{n\leq x}\frac{1}{n}= \log x+O(1)$.

We state the exact pigeonhole bound $F(x)\leq H_x+1$, where $H_x=\sum_{n\leq x}\frac{1}{n}$ is
the $x$-th harmonic number. The $+1$ is needed, since $F(3)\geq 2>H_3$. By Mathlib's
`harmonic_le_one_add_log` this gives $F(x)\leq\log x+2$.
statements.statement: theorem erdos_1205.variants.upper_bound (x : ℕ) : (F x : ℝ) ≤ (harmonic x : ℝ) + 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1206
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1206](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1206)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [GGK26] M. Garaev, F. Garayev, and S. Konyagin, *On Sidon sets with squares, cubes, and quartics
  in short intervals*. arXiv:2602.08807 (2026).
- [GaKo24] Gabdullin, M. R. and Konyagin, S. V., *Trigonometric polynomials with frequencies in the
  set of cubes*. Math. Notes (2024), 336--340.

statements.name: Erdos1206.erdos_1206.parts.i
statements.doc: Does $\{1,2^3,\ldots,N^3\}$ contain a Sidon set of size $\gg N$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1206.parts.i :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, ∃ S : Finset ℕ,
      S ⊆ (Finset.Icc 1 N).image (fun n => n ^ 3) ∧
      IsSidon (S : Set ℕ) ∧ c * (N : ℝ) ≤ (S.card : ℝ)

statements.name: Erdos1206.erdos_1206.parts.ii
statements.doc: Is there an infinite set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ of positive density such that $\{a^3 : a\in A\}$ is a Sidon set?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1206.parts.ii :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ 0 < A.lowerDensity ∧
      IsSidon ((fun a : ℕ => a ^ 3) '' A)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1207
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1207](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1207)
- [BMP05] Brass, Peter and Moser, William and Pach, János, *Research problems in discrete geometry*.
  (2005), xii+499.
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [LPZ26] Lee, S., Pohoata, C., and Zhu, D. G., *The Minkowski grid has robustly many repeated
  distances*. [arXiv:2607.05374](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05374) (2026).
- [PaTa02] Pach, János and Tardos, Gábor, *Isosceles triangles determined by a planar point set*.
  Graphs Combin. (2002), 769--779.

statements.name: Erdos1207.erdos_1207
statements.doc:
Let $P_d(n)$ be such that in any set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ there exist at least $P_d(n)$ many points which do not contain an isosceles triangle. Estimate $P_d(n)$ - in particular, is it true that $$P_2(n)<n^{1-c}$$ for some constant $c>0$?

Lee, Pohoata, and Zhu [LPZ26] proved the stated planar bound. Their isosceles-free subsets
also exclude degenerate triangles of equally spaced collinear points.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1207 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (P 2 n : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1209
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/429](https://www.erdosproblems.com/429)
- [erdosproblems.com/1102](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1102)
- [erdosproblems.com/1209](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1209)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.

statements.name: Erdos1209.erdos_1209.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}$ be a sequence of integers which tends to infinity sufficiently fast.
If there is an $n$ such that all $n+a_k$ are primes then must there exist infinitely many such $n$?

Erdős [Er80] wrote 'unless I overlook a trivial way of getting a counterexample these questions
are quite hopeless'. There is indeed a trivial counterexample (a variant of the construction in
[erdosproblems.com/429]): define $a_1=2$ and for $k\geq 2$ let $a_k>a_{k-1}$ be a prime such that
$a_k+k\equiv 0\pmod{q_k}$, where $q_k$ is some prime not dividing $k$. This sequence can be made to
grow arbitrarily fast

See also [erdosproblems.com/429] and [erdosproblems.com/1102].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1209.parts.i :
    ¬ ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a → (∀ k, f k ≤ a k) →
      (∃ n, ∀ k, (n + a k).Prime) →
      {n | ∀ k, (n + a k).Prime}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos1209.erdos_1209.parts.ii
statements.doc:
What if we ask for $n+a_k$ to be squarefree instead of prime?

A similar construction provides a counterexample to the squarefree question.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1209.parts.ii :
    ¬ ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a → (∀ k, f k ≤ a k) →
      (∃ n, ∀ k, Squarefree (n + a k)) →
      {n | ∀ k, Squarefree (n + a k)}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos1209.erdos_1209.parts.iii.a
statements.doc:
Are there $n$ such that $n+2^{2^k}$ is always a prime?

ebarschkis and GPT have proved that there are no $n$ such that $n+2^{2^k}$ is always prime: let
$n\geq 3$ be any odd integer. If $k$ is chosen sufficiently large, and $p=n+2^{2^{k}}$ is prime,
then the multiplicative order of $2^{2^k}\pmod{p}$, say $m$ is odd, and hence if $l$ is chosen such
that $2^l\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ then $p\mid n+2^{2^{k+rl}}$ for all $r\geq 1$.

This was formalized in Lean by Barschkis using ChatGPT.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1209.parts.iii.a :
    ¬ ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ k : ℕ, (n + 2 ^ (2 ^ k)).Prime

statements.name: Erdos1209.erdos_1209.parts.iii.b
statements.doc: Are there $n$ such that $n+2^{2^k}$ is always squarefree?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1209.parts.iii.b :
    ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ k : ℕ, Squarefree (n + 2 ^ (2 ^ k))

statements.name: Erdos1209.erdos_1209.parts.iii.c
statements.doc: Are there $n$ such that $n+2^{2^k}$ is infinitely often a prime?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1209.parts.iii.c :
    ∃ n : ℕ, {k | (n + 2 ^ (2 ^ k)).Prime}.Infinite

statements.name: Erdos1209.erdos_1209.parts.iii.d
statements.doc: Are there $n$ such that $n+2^{2^k}$ is infinitely often squarefree?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1209.parts.iii.d :
    ∃ n : ℕ, {k | Squarefree (n + 2 ^ (2 ^ k))}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1210
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1210](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1210)
- [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III. Number theory day
  (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.

statements.name: Erdos1210.erdos_1210
statements.doc:
Let $A\subseteq [1,n)$ be a set of integers such that $(a,b)=1$ for all distinct $a,b\in A$.
Is it true that $\sum_{a\in A}\frac{1}{n-a}\leq \sum_{p < n}\frac{1}{p}+O(1)$?
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1210 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset ℕ,
      (∀ a ∈ A, 1 ≤ a ∧ a < n) →
      (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, a ≠ b → a.Coprime b) →
      ∑ a ∈ A, (1 / ((n : ℝ) - a)) ≤ (∑ p ∈ (range n).filter Prime, (1 / (p : ℝ))) + C

statements.name: Erdos1210.erdos_1210.variants.er80_correction
statements.doc:
In [Er80] he claims he "did not state this quite correctly" in [Er77c]. The problem in [Er77c] which
Erdős is presumably referring to states that if $n < q_1 < \cdots < q_k\leq m$ is the set of primes
in $(n,m]$ then $\sum \frac{1}{q_i-n} < \sum_{p < m-n}\frac{1}{p}+O(1)$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1210.variants.er80_correction :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n m : ℕ, n < m →
      ∑ q ∈ (Ioc n m).filter Prime, (1 / ((q : ℝ) - n)) <
      (∑ p ∈ (range (m - n)).filter Prime, (1 / (p : ℝ))) + C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1211
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1211](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1211)
- [CFP22] Conlon, David and Fox, Jacob and Pham, Huy Tuan, *The upper logarithmic density of
  monochromatic subset sums*. Mathematika 68 (2022), 1292--1301.
  [arXiv:2105.15195](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.15195)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos1211.erdos_1211
statements.doc:
Let $\mathbb{N}=A\cup B$ where $A$ and $B$ are disjoint. Let $S(A)$ be those integers which are the
sum of finitely many distinct elements of $A$, and similarly for $S(B)$.

If
$$
\overline{\delta}(X)=\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{1}{\log x}
  \sum_{\substack{n\in X\\ n<x}}\frac{1}{n}
$$
is the upper logarithmic density of $X$ then how large must
$$\max(\overline{\delta}(S(A)),\overline{\delta}(S(B)))$$
be?

A question of Erdős [Er80]. Conlon, Fox, and Pham [CFP22, Theorem 1] proved that the least
possible value of $\max(\overline{\delta}(S(A)),\overline{\delta}(S(B)))$ is
$\frac{2+\sqrt{3}}{4}\approx 0.93301$, and that it is attained.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1211 :
    (∀ A B : Set ℕ, IsNatPartition A B → erdos_1211.answer ≤ partitionValue A B) ∧
      ∃ A B : Set ℕ, IsNatPartition A B ∧ partitionValue A B = erdos_1211.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1212
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1212](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1212)
- [Er80] Erdős, P., _Some notes on problems and results in number theory_ (1980), p. 114.

This file also records machine-checked cores of verified partial results (2026):
a composite-anchor sufficient reduction and an impossibility theorem for periodic
certificates; see the corresponding lemmas below.

statements.name: Erdos1212.erdos_1212
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be the graph with vertex set those pairs $(x,y)\in \mathbb{N}^2$ with
$\mathrm{gcd}(x,y)=1$, in which we join two vertices if the differ in only one coordinate, and
there by $\pm 1$.

Is there a path going to infinity on $G$, say $P$, such that for all $(x,y)\in P$ both
$\min(x,y)>1$ and at least one of $x$ or $y$ is composite?

The weaker version (only $\min(x,y) > 1$) was solved by C. Stewart via the prime-pair path
$(p_k, p_{k+1}) \to (p_{k+1}, p_{k+2})$, as recounted in [Er80]; the compositeness condition
forbids those anchors.

The strengthened problem was solved by Alex Chengyu Li; see
[Li's construction](https://crabresearch.com/research/erdos-1212-algebraic-corridors)
and the accompanying
[Lean formalization](https://github.com/crabsatellite/erdos-1212-visible-lattice-path).
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1212 :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ × ℕ, Function.Injective f ∧ (∀ n, Adj (f n) (f (n + 1))) ∧
      (∀ n, Valid (f n)) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n => (f n).1 + (f n).2) atTop atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1213
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1213](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1213)
- [He86] Hegyvári, N., *On consecutive sums in sequences*. Acta Math. Hungar. (1986), 193-200.

statements.name: Erdos1213.erdos_1213
statements.doc:
Let $a,K\geq 1$. Does there exist $f(a,K)$ such that if $a=a_1<\cdots <a_s$ is a sequence of
integers with $a_s> f(a,K)$ and with bounded gaps $a_{i+1}-a_i\leq K$ then there are two distinct
intervals $I$ and $J$ such that
$$\sum_{i\in I}a_i=\sum_{j\in J}a_j?$$

Hegyvári [He86] has proved the answer is yes, and gives an explicit bound of the shape
$f(a,K) \ll ae^{O(K)}$. Hegyvári believes that the exponential dependence on $K$ here is not best
possible.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1213 : ∀ a K : ℕ, 1 ≤ a → 1 ≤ K → ∃ f : ℕ,
    ∀ (s : ℕ) (A : ℕ → ℕ), 0 < s → A 0 = a → StrictMonoOn A (Set.Iio s) →
      (∀ i, i + 1 < s → A (i + 1) - A i ≤ K) → f < A (s - 1) → HasEqualIntervalSums A s

statements.name: Erdos1213.erdos_1213.variants.hegyvari
statements.doc: Hegyvári [He86] proved that one can take $f(a,K) \ll ae^{O(K)}$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1213.variants.hegyvari : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ a K : ℕ, 1 ≤ a → 1 ≤ K →
    ∀ (s : ℕ) (A : ℕ → ℕ), 0 < s → A 0 = a → StrictMonoOn A (Set.Iio s) →
      (∀ i, i + 1 < s → A (i + 1) - A i ≤ K) → C * a * Real.exp (C * K) < A (s - 1) →
        HasEqualIntervalSums A s

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1214
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1214](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1214)
- [CoSc97] Corrales-Rodrigáñez, Capi and Schoof, René, The support problem and its
  elliptic analogue. J. Number Theory (1997) [Volume 64, Issue 2], 276--290.

statements.name: Erdos1214.erdos_1214
statements.doc:
Let $x,y\geq 1$ be integers such that, for all $n\geq 1$, the set of primes dividing $x^{n}-1$ is
equal to the set of primes dividing $y^n-1$. Must $x=y$?

Erdős asked this at a 1988 number theory conference in Banff.

A positive answer was given by Corrales-Rodrigáñez and Schoof [CoSc97].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1214 :
    ∀ x y : ℕ, x ≥ 1 → y ≥ 1 →
      (∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 1 → { p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ p ∣ x ^ n - 1 } = { p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ p ∣ y ^ n - 1 }) →
      x = y

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1217
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1217](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1217)
- [ABLLPSTT26] B. Alexeev, K. Barreto, Y. Li, J. D. Lichtman, L. Price, J. I. Shah, Q. Tang, and
  T. Tao, *Primitive sets and von Mangoldt chains: Erdős Problem #1196 and beyond*.
  arXiv:2605.00301 (2026).
- [DaEr51] Davenport, H. and Erdős, P., *On sequences of positive integers*. J. Indian Math.
  Soc. (N.S.) (1951), 19--24. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1951-07.pdf)
- [ESS66] Erdős, P. and Sárközi, A. and Szemerédi, E., *On divisibility properties of sequences of
  integers*. Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. (1966), 431--435.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1966-09.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos1217.erdos_1217
statements.doc:
Let $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}$ be an infinite sequence of positive integers with positive lower
logarithmic density.

Must there exist a sequence $n_1<\cdots$ such that
$$a_{n_i}\mid a_{n_{i+1}}$$
for all $i\geq 1$ and
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{1}{\log\log x}\sum_{a_{n_i}<x}1 \geq
  \limsup_{x\to \infty} \frac{1}{\log\log x}\sum_{a_n<x}\frac{1}{a_n\log a_n}?$$

A problem of Erdős, Sárközi, and Szemerédi [ESS66, p. 432, (5)]. The answer is yes, proved by
Alexeev, Barreto, Li, Lichtman, Price, Shah, Tang, and Tao [ABLLPSTT26, Theorem 1.6]. Sequences
are indexed from $0$ here.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1217 :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a → (∀ i, 0 < a i) → 0 < lowerLogDensity (Set.range a) →
      ∃ n : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono n ∧ (∀ i, a (n i) ∣ a (n (i + 1))) ∧
        weightedRate (Set.range a) ≤ chainRate (a ∘ n)

statements.name: Erdos1217.erdos_1217.variants.without_density
statements.doc:
The answer to `erdos_1217` is yes even without the assumption that $A$ has positive lower
logarithmic density [ABLLPSTT26]: it suffices that the doubly harmonic rate on the right-hand
side is positive, which holds whenever the lower logarithmic density is positive.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1217.variants.without_density :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a → 0 < weightedRate (Set.range a) →
      ∃ n : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono n ∧ (∀ i, a (n i) ∣ a (n (i + 1))) ∧
        weightedRate (Set.range a) ≤ chainRate (a ∘ n)

statements.name: Erdos1217.erdos_1217.variants.abllpstt
statements.doc:
The set form of [ABLLPSTT26, Theorem 1.6]: if $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ has positive upper doubly
logarithmic density
$$\Delta=\limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{1}{\log\log x}\sum_{n\in A,\ n<x}\frac{1}{n\log n},$$
then $A$ contains a strictly increasing infinite divisibility chain $d_0\mid d_1\mid\cdots$ with
$$\limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{1}{\log\log x}\sum_{d_i<x}1\geq\Delta.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1217.variants.abllpstt (A : Set ℕ) (hA : 0 < weightedRate A) :
    ∃ d : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono d ∧ (∀ i, d i ∈ A) ∧ (∀ i, d i ∣ d (i + 1)) ∧
      weightedRate A ≤ chainRate d

statements.name: Erdos1217.erdos_1217.variants.davenport_erdos
statements.doc:
Davenport and Erdős [DaEr51] proved that (assuming $A$ has positive lower logarithmic density)
there exists a sequence $n_1<\cdots$ such that $a_{n_i}\mid a_{n_{i+1}}$ for all $i\geq 1$
(as stated in [ESS66, p. 431]). This also follows from `erdos_1217`.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1217.variants.davenport_erdos :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a → (∀ i, 0 < a i) → 0 < lowerLogDensity (Set.range a) →
      ∃ n : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono n ∧ ∀ i, a (n i) ∣ a (n (i + 1))

statements.name: Erdos1217.erdos_1217.variants.erdos_sarkozi_szemeredi
statements.doc:
Erdős, Sárközi, and Szemerédi [ESS66, Theorem 2] proved that if
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{1}{\log\log x}\sum_{a_n<x}\frac{1}{a_n\log a_n}=c>0,$$
then there exists such a sequence with
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{1}{\log\log x}\sum_{a_{n_i}<x}1\gg_c 1.$$
Here $\gg_c 1$ means a lower bound $\kappa>0$ depending only on $c$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1217.variants.erdos_sarkozi_szemeredi :
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ κ : ℝ, 0 < κ ∧ ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a →
      weightedRate (Set.range a) = ENNReal.ofReal c →
        ∃ n : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono n ∧ (∀ i, a (n i) ∣ a (n (i + 1))) ∧
          ENNReal.ofReal κ ≤ chainRate (a ∘ n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1219
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1219](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1219)
- [ErHa71] Erdős, Paul and Hajnal, András, Unsolved problems in set theory. Axiomatic Set
  Theory, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. XIII Part I (1971), 17-48.
- [Ko25b] Komjáth, Péter, The Erdős–Hajnal problem list. Bull. Symb. Log. (2025), 418-461.
- [Sh75] Shelah, Saharon, Notes on partition calculus. Infinite and finite sets (Colloq.,
  Keszthely, 1973), Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai 10, North-Holland (1975), 1257-1276.

statements.name: Erdos1219.erdos_1219
statements.doc:
Let $(n_k)$ be an increasing sequence of integers such that $2^{\aleph_{n_k}}$ is strictly
increasing, and $2^{\aleph_{n_0}} > \aleph_\omega$. Is it true that
$$\sum_k 2^{\aleph_{n_k}} \to (\aleph_\omega)^2?$$

Here $\sum_k 2^{\aleph_{n_k}}$ is the cardinal sum, and the partition relation is the classical
one with two colours: every $2$-colouring of the pairs of a set of that cardinality has a
monochromatic set of cardinality $\aleph_\omega$.

A problem of Erdős, Hajnal, and Rado [ErHa71], proved by Shelah [Sh75].
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1219 :
    ∀ n : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono n →
      StrictMono (fun k => (2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ ℵ_ (n k)) →
      ℵ_ ω < (2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ ℵ_ (n 0) →
      cardinalPartitionRel (sum fun k => (2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ ℵ_ (n k)) 2 2 (fun _ => ℵ_ ω)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1221
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1221](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1221)
- [dBEr49] de Bruijn, N. G. and Erdős, P., *Sequences of points on a circle*. Nederl. Akad.
  Wetensch., Proc. (1949), 14-17 = Indagationes Math. 11 (1949), 46-49.
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1949-13.pdf)

statements.name: Erdos1221.erdos_1221.parts.i
statements.doc:
Let $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ be points, ordered consecutively, around the circle (normalised to have
circumference $1$). Let
$$M_r(a)=\max_r \lvert a_{i+r}-a_i\rvert$$
and
$$m_r(a)=\min_r \lvert a_{i+r}-a_i\rvert,$$
where the indices are interpreted in a cyclic fashion and the distance is around the circle (in
other words, the maximum and minimum distance between $r$-consecutive points).

Let
$$\Lambda_r=\inf_a \limsup_n n M_r(a_1,\ldots,a_n),$$
$$\lambda_r = \sup_a \liminf_n nm_r(a_1,\ldots,a_n),$$
and
$$\mu_r=\inf_a \limsup_n \frac{M_r(a)}{m_r(a)},$$
where the outer $\inf/\sup$ is over all infinite sequences $a=(a_1,\ldots)$.

Is it true that $r(\Lambda_r-1)$, $r(1-\lambda_r)$, and $r(\mu_r-1)$ tend to infinity as
$r\to \infty$?

This is the first part, conjectured by de Bruijn and Erdős [dBEr49, §6]. We read $\Lambda_r$ and
$\lambda_r$ as in `bigLambda` and `smallLambda`, that is, as printed. The sequences are required
to have pairwise distinct points modulo $1$ (see `bigLambda`). Then $nM_r\geq r$ [dBEr49, §1],
so $r(\Lambda_r-1)\to\infty$ would hold trivially. Also $m_r\geq r\,m_1$, so the sequence
$a_k=\log_2(2k-1)$ of [dBEr49, §2] gives $\lambda_r\geq r/\log 4$, which exceeds $1$ for $r\geq2$,
so $r(1-\lambda_r)$ would be negative for $r\geq2$. The intended conjectures are about the
quantities normalised by $r$, so $r(\Lambda_r/r-1)=\Lambda_r-r$, and the first part asks whether
$\Lambda_r-r\to\infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1221.parts.i :
    ∀ K : ℝ, ∀ᶠ r : ℕ in atTop, ENNReal.ofReal ((r : ℝ) + K) < bigLambda r

statements.name: Erdos1221.erdos_1221.parts.ii
statements.doc:
Let $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ be points, ordered consecutively, around the circle (normalised to have
circumference $1$). Let
$$M_r(a)=\max_r \lvert a_{i+r}-a_i\rvert$$
and
$$m_r(a)=\min_r \lvert a_{i+r}-a_i\rvert,$$
where the indices are interpreted in a cyclic fashion and the distance is around the circle (in
other words, the maximum and minimum distance between $r$-consecutive points).

Let
$$\Lambda_r=\inf_a \limsup_n n M_r(a_1,\ldots,a_n),$$
$$\lambda_r = \sup_a \liminf_n nm_r(a_1,\ldots,a_n),$$
and
$$\mu_r=\inf_a \limsup_n \frac{M_r(a)}{m_r(a)},$$
where the outer $\inf/\sup$ is over all infinite sequences $a=(a_1,\ldots)$.

Is it true that $r(\Lambda_r-1)$, $r(1-\lambda_r)$, and $r(\mu_r-1)$ tend to infinity as
$r\to \infty$?

This is the second part. As in the first part, we normalise $\lambda_r$ by $r$, so
$r(1-\lambda_r/r)=r-\lambda_r$, and the second part asks whether $r-\lambda_r\to\infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1221.parts.ii :
    ∀ K : ℝ, ∀ᶠ r : ℕ in atTop, smallLambda r < ENNReal.ofReal ((r : ℝ) - K)

statements.name: Erdos1221.erdos_1221.parts.iii
statements.doc:
Let $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ be points, ordered consecutively, around the circle (normalised to have
circumference $1$). Let
$$M_r(a)=\max_r \lvert a_{i+r}-a_i\rvert$$
and
$$m_r(a)=\min_r \lvert a_{i+r}-a_i\rvert,$$
where the indices are interpreted in a cyclic fashion and the distance is around the circle (in
other words, the maximum and minimum distance between $r$-consecutive points).

Let
$$\Lambda_r=\inf_a \limsup_n n M_r(a_1,\ldots,a_n),$$
$$\lambda_r = \sup_a \liminf_n nm_r(a_1,\ldots,a_n),$$
and
$$\mu_r=\inf_a \limsup_n \frac{M_r(a)}{m_r(a)},$$
where the outer $\inf/\sup$ is over all infinite sequences $a=(a_1,\ldots)$.

Is it true that $r(\Lambda_r-1)$, $r(1-\lambda_r)$, and $r(\mu_r-1)$ tend to infinity as
$r\to \infty$?

This is the third part. The quantity $\mu_r$ needs no normalisation, and the third part asks
whether $r(\mu_r-1)\to\infty$, that is, whether $\mu_r>1+K/r$ for every $K$ and all large $r$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1221.parts.iii :
    ∀ K : ℝ, ∀ᶠ r : ℕ in atTop, ENNReal.ofReal (1 + K / (r : ℝ)) < mu r

statements.name: Erdos1221.erdos_1221.variants.r_one
statements.doc:
De Bruijn and Erdős [dBEr49, §§2-5] proved that $\Lambda_1=\frac{1}{\log 2}$,
$\lambda_1=\frac{1}{\log 4}$, and $\mu_1=2$. A sequence which witnesses this is
$a_k=\log_2(2k-1)$. For $r=1$ the normalisation by $r$ plays no role.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1221.variants.r_one :
    bigLambda 1 = ENNReal.ofReal (1 / Real.log 2) ∧
      smallLambda 1 = ENNReal.ofReal (1 / Real.log 4) ∧ mu 1 = 2

statements.name: Erdos1221.erdos_1221.variants.bigLambda_ge
statements.doc:
De Bruijn and Erdős [dBEr49, (3.3)] proved that, for any $r\geq 1$,
$$\Lambda_r \geq \frac{1}{\log(1+1/r)}.$$
Here $\Lambda_r$ is as in `bigLambda`, with no normalisation by $r$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1221.variants.bigLambda_ge {r : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) :
    ENNReal.ofReal (1 / Real.log (1 + 1 / (r : ℝ))) ≤ bigLambda r

statements.name: Erdos1221.erdos_1221.variants.smallLambda_le
statements.doc:
De Bruijn and Erdős [dBEr49, (4.3)] proved that, for any $r\geq 1$,
$$\lambda_r \leq \frac{r}{r+1}\frac{1}{\log(1+1/r)}.$$
Here $\lambda_r$ is as in `smallLambda`, with no normalisation by $r$.
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1221.variants.smallLambda_le {r : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) :
    smallLambda r ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal ((r : ℝ) / ((r : ℝ) + 1) * (1 / Real.log (1 + 1 / (r : ℝ))))

statements.name: Erdos1221.erdos_1221.variants.mu_ge
statements.doc:
De Bruijn and Erdős [dBEr49, §1 and (5.7)] proved that, for any $r\geq 1$,
$$\mu_r \geq 1+\frac{1}{r}.$$
statements.statement:
theorem erdos_1221.variants.mu_ge {r : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) :
    ENNReal.ofReal (1 + 1 / (r : ℝ)) ≤ mu r

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 1
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 1](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.1 Problem 1)
- [Be25] Bedert, Benjamin, Large sum-free subsets of sets of integers via $L^1$-estimates for
  trigonometric series. [arXiv:2502.08624](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08624) (2025).

statements.name: Green1.green_1
statements.doc:
Let $A$ be a set of $n$ positive integers. Does $A$ contain a sum-free set
of size at least $\frac n 3 + Ω(n)$, where $Ω(n) → ∞$ as $n → ∞$?

Bedert [Be25] proved that every set of $n$ integers contains a sum-free subset of size at least
$\frac n 3 + c \log\log n$ for some absolute constant $c > 0$, so the answer is yes.
statements.statement:
theorem green_1 : ∃ Ω : ℕ → ℝ, atTop.Tendsto Ω atTop ∧
     ∀ n, ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), (∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a) → A.card = n →
     ∃ (S : Finset ℕ), S ⊆ A ∧ IsSumFree (S : Set ℕ) ∧ ((n : ℝ) / 3) + Ω n ≤ S.card

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 2
problems.doc:
References:
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.2)
- [Er65] P. Erdős. Extremal problems in number theory, In Proc. Sympos. Pure Math., Vol. VIII,
  pages 181–189. Amer. Math. Soc., Providence, R.I., 1965.
- [Sa21] Sanders, Tom. "The Erdős–Moser Sum-free Set Problem." Canadian Journal of Mathematics 73.1
  (2021): 63-107.
- [Ru05] I. Z. Ruzsa, Sum-avoiding subsets. Ramanujan J., 9 (2005) (1-2):77–82.
- [Ch71] S. L. G. Choi. On a combinatorial problem in number theory. Proc. London Math. Soc. (3),
  23:629–642, 1971. doi:10.1112/plms/s3-23.4.629.
- [BSS00] A. Baltz, T. Schoen, and A. Srivastav. Probabilistic construction of small strongly
  sum-free sets via large Sidon sets. Colloq. Math., 86(2):171–176, 2000.
  doi:10.4064/cm-86-2-171-176.

statements.name: Green2.green_2
statements.doc:
Let $A \subset \mathbf{Z}$ be a set of $n$ integers. Is there a set $S \subset A$ of size
$(\log n)^{100}$ such that the restricted sumset$S \hat{+} S$ is disjoint from $A$?
statements.statement:
theorem green_2 :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℤ, A.card = n →
      (maxRestrictedSumAvoidingSubsetSize A : ℝ) ≥ (Real.log n) ^ 100

statements.name: Green2.green_2_lower_bound_sanders
statements.doc: From [Sa21] it is known that there is always such an S with $|S| \gt (\log |A|)^{1+c}$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_2_lower_bound_sanders :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℤ, A.card = n →
      maxRestrictedSumAvoidingSubsetSize A ≥ Real.log n ^ (1 + c)

statements.name: Green2.green_2_upper_bound_erdos
statements.doc: From [Er65] it is known that $M(A) \le \frac{1}{3}|A| + O(1)$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_2_upper_bound_erdos :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ A : Finset ℤ, A.card = n ∧
      (maxRestrictedSumAvoidingSubsetSize A : ℝ) ≤ A.card / 3 + C

statements.name: Green2.green_2_upper_bound_choi
statements.doc: From [Ch71] it is known that $M(A) \le |A|^{2/5 + o(1)}$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_2_upper_bound_choi :
    ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : Tendsto o atTop (𝓝 0)), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ A : Finset ℤ, A.card = n ∧
      (maxRestrictedSumAvoidingSubsetSize A : ℝ) ≤ A.card ^ (2 / 5 + o A.card)

statements.name: Green2.green_2_upper_bound_ruzsa
statements.doc: From [Ru05] the best-known upper bound is $|S| \lt e^{C \sqrt{\log |A|}}$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_2_upper_bound_ruzsa :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ A : Finset ℤ, A.card = n ∧
      (maxRestrictedSumAvoidingSubsetSize A : ℝ) < Real.exp (C * Real.sqrt (Real.log A.card))

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 3
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 3](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.3 Problem 3)
- [FGY26] Franchi, Leonardo and Gowers, W. T. and Yip, Fredy, *Product-free subsets of $(0,1)$*,
  [arXiv:2607.06073](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06073), Theorem 1.1.

statements.name: Green3.green_3
statements.doc:
Suppose that $A \subset [0,1]$ is open and has measure greater than $\frac{1}{3}$. Is there a
solution to $xy = z$ with $x, y, z \in A$?

The answer is yes. [FGY26] prove that an open product-free subset of $(0,1)$ has measure strictly
less than $\frac{1}{3}$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_3 :
    ∀ A : Set ℝ,
      IsOpen A → A ⊆ Icc 0 1 → volume A > 1/3 →
        ∃ x y z, x ∈ A ∧ y ∈ A ∧ z ∈ A ∧ x * y = z

statements.name: Green4.large_green_4

In the case of large n, the problem was solved in
[On the largest product-free subsets of the alternating groups](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.15191).
Specifically, this theorem formalizes the statement of theorem 1.1 in the mentioned paper

    ∀ S, MaximalFor (ProdFree (M := alternatingGroup <| Fin n)) Set.ncard S →
    ∃ x I, S = extremalFamily x I ∨ S = (extremalFamily x I).image (·⁻¹)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 5
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.5)
- [BaSo85] Babai L, Sós VT. Sidon sets in groups and induced subgraphs of Cayley graphs.
  European Journal of Combinatorics. 1985 Jun 1;6(2):101-14.
- [Ke97] Kedlaya, K. S., *Large product-free subsets of finite groups*, J. Combin. Theory
  Ser. A 77 (1997), no. 2, 339–343.
- [Ke09] Kedlaya, K. S., *Product-free subsets of groups, then and now*, Contemp. Math., 479,
  American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI, 2009, 169–177.
- [Go08] Gowers, W. T., *Quasirandom groups*, Combin. Probab. Comput. 17 (2008), no. 3,
  363–387.

statements.name: Green5.green_5
statements.doc:
Which finite groups have the smallest biggest product-free sets?

We formalise this as: determine the supremum of exponents $\alpha$ such that every nontrivial
finite group of order $n$ contains a product-free set of size $\geq c n^{\alpha}$ for some
absolute constant $c > 0$. (The trivial group is excluded since its only product-free subset
is empty.) Kedlaya [Ke97] showed that $\alpha = 11/14$ is admissible, and Green suggests this
exponent may well be sharp; the candidate extremal family is the Ree groups ${}^2G_2(q)$,
$q = 3^{2m+1}$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_5 :
    IsLUB {α : ℝ | ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Fintype G], Nontrivial G →
      ∃ S : Finset G, IsProductFree (S : Set G) ∧
        c * (Fintype.card G : ℝ) ^ α ≤ (S.card : ℝ)}
      green_5.answer

statements.name: Green5.green_5.variants.kedlaya
statements.doc:
Kedlaya [Ke97] observed, refining some work of Babai and Sós [BaSo85], that it follows from the
classification of finite simple groups that every finite group $G$ of order $n$ has a
product-free subset of size $\gg n^{11/14}$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_5.variants.kedlaya :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Fintype G], Nontrivial G →
      ∃ S : Finset G, IsProductFree (S : Set G) ∧
        c * (Fintype.card G : ℝ) ^ ((11 : ℝ) / 14) ≤ (S.card : ℝ)

statements.name: Green5.green_5.variants.sl_two
statements.doc:
A good model problem would be to determine the largest product-free subsets of
$\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$.

statements.name: Green5.green_5.variants.gowers_sl_two
statements.doc:
For the largest product-free subsets of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ of order $n$, the
best-known upper bound is $O(n^{8/9})$, due to Gowers [Go08].
statements.statement:
theorem green_5.variants.gowers_sl_two :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], ∀ S : Finset (SL₂ p),
      IsProductFree (S : Set (SL₂ p)) →
      (S.card : ℝ) ≤ C * (Fintype.card (SL₂ p) : ℝ) ^ ((8 : ℝ) / 9)

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 12
problems.doc:
References:
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.12)

statements.name: Green12.green_12
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be an abelian group of size $N$, and suppose that $A \subset G$ has density $\alpha$.
Are there at least $\alpha^{15} N^{10}$ tuples $(x_1, \dots, x_5, y_1, \dots, y_5) \in G^{10}$
such that $x_i + y_j \in A$ whenever $j \in \{i, i+1, i+2\}$?

Note: We interpret indices modulo 5.
statements.statement:
theorem green_12 :
    ∀ {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G],
    ∀ (A : Finset G),
    let N := Fintype.card G
    let α := (A.card : ℝ) / N
    let valid_tuples : Finset ((Fin 5 → G) × (Fin 5 → G)) := Finset.univ.filter (fun t =>
      ∀ i : Fin 5, ∀ j ∈ ({i, i + 1, i + 2} : Finset (Fin 5)), t.1 i + t.2 j ∈ A)
    (valid_tuples.card : ℝ) ≥ α ^ 15 * (N : ℝ) ^ 10

statements.name: Green14.green_14_polynomial
statements.doc:
Is $W(k, r)$ a polynomial in $r$, for fixed $k$?

We formulate this as asking if $W(k, r)$ has polynomial growth in $r$.
The answer is no, already for $k = 4$. Every red $k$-term progression with $k \ge 3$ contains a
red $3$-term progression, so `mixedMonoAPGuaranteeSet k r ⊆ mixedMonoAPGuaranteeSet 3 r`, and
both sets are nonempty by van der Waerden's theorem, so $W(3, r) \le W(k, r)$. Polynomial
growth for one $k \ge 4$ would therefore force polynomial growth for $k = 3$, contradicting
`green_14_polynomial_k_eq_3` [Gr21, p.3].
statements.statement:
theorem green_14_polynomial :
    ¬ ∀ k ≥ 4, ∃ d : ℕ, (fun r => (W k r : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun r => (r : ℝ) ^ d

statements.name: Green14.green_14_polynomial_k_eq_3
statements.doc: We know $W(3, r)$ does not have polynomial growth in $r$ [Gr21, p.3].
statements.statement:
theorem green_14_polynomial_k_eq_3 :
    ¬ ∃ d : ℕ, (fun r => (W 3 r : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun r => (r : ℝ) ^ d

statements.name: Green14.green_14_quadratic
statements.doc:
Is $W(3, r) \ll r^2$?

[Gr21] proves a superpolynomial lower bound $W(3, r) \gg \exp(c(\log r)^{4/3-o(1)})$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_14_quadratic :
    ¬ (fun r => (W 3 r : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun r => (r : ℝ) ^ 2

statements.name: Green14.green_14_lower_bound_green
statements.doc: [Gr21] proved a lower bound of shape $W(3, r) \gg \exp(c(\log r)^{4/3-o(1)})$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_14_lower_bound_green :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : Tendsto o atTop (𝓝 0)),
    (fun (r : ℕ) => Real.exp (c * (Real.log r)^(4/3 - o r))) =O[atTop] fun r => (W 3 r : ℝ)

statements.name: Green14.green_14_lower_bound_hunter
statements.doc: [Hu22] improved this to $W(3, r) \gg \exp(c(\log r)^{2-o(1)})$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_14_lower_bound_hunter :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : Tendsto o atTop (𝓝 0)),
    (fun (r : ℕ) => Real.exp (c * (Real.log r)^(2 - o r))) =O[atTop] (fun r => (W 3 r : ℝ))

statements.name: Green14.green_14_lower_bound_brown_landman_robertson
statements.doc: [BLR08] proved $W(3, r) \gg r^{2 - 1/\log \log r}$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_14_lower_bound_brown_landman_robertson :
    (fun (r : ℕ) => (r : ℝ)^(2 - 1 / Real.log (Real.log r))) =O[atTop] (fun r => (W 3 r : ℝ))

statements.name: Green14.green_14_lower_bound_li_shu
statements.doc: [LiSh10] proved $W(3, r) \gg (r / \log r)^2$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_14_lower_bound_li_shu :
    (fun (r : ℕ) => ((r : ℝ) / Real.log r)^2) =O[atTop] (fun r => (W 3 r : ℝ))

statements.name: Green14.green_14_upper_bound_schoen
statements.doc: [Sc20] proves the upper bound $W(3, r) < \exp(r^{1-c})$ for some $c > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_14_upper_bound_schoen :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
    (fun (r : ℕ) => ((W 3 r) : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun r => Real.exp ((r : ℝ) ^ (1 - c)))

statements.name: Green14.green_14_upper_bound_kelley_meka
statements.doc: [KeMe23] gives a corresponding upper bound $W(3, r) \ll \exp(C(\log r)^C)$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_14_upper_bound_kelley_meka :
    ∃ C : ℝ,
    (fun (r : ℕ) => ((W 3 r) : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun r => Real.exp (C * (Real.log r)^C))

statements.name: Green14.green_14_variant_2r2
statements.doc:
It remains an interesting open problem to actually write down a colouring showing (say)
$W(3, r) \ge 2r^2$ for some $r$. [Gr24]
statements.statement:
theorem green_14_variant_2r2 :
    -- Provide a pair (r, associated coloring) that avoids the monochromatic APs
    -- To show $W(3, r) > 2r^2 - 1$, we need a coloring of $\{1, \ldots, 2r^2 - 1\}$
    -- that avoids monochromatic APs of length 3 and $r$.
    let ans : Σ r : ℕ, Icc 1 (2 * r^2 - 1) → Fin 2 := green_14_variant_2r2.answer
    let r := ans.1
    let c := ans.2
    3 ≤ r ∧
    ¬ ((∃ s : Finset (Icc 1 (2 * r^2 - 1)), ({(s' : ℕ) | s' ∈ s}).IsAPOfLength 3 ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, c x = 0) ∨
       (∃ s : Finset (Icc 1 (2 * r^2 - 1)), ({(s' : ℕ) | s' ∈ s}).IsAPOfLength r ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, c x = 1))

problems.doc:
References:
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.15)
- [BJP14] T. Brown, V. Jungić and A. Poelstra, "On double 3-term arithmetic progressions",
  Integers 14 (2014), Paper No. A43.
- [CCS14] J. Cassaigne, J. D. Currie, L. Schaeffer and J. Shallit, "Avoidance of additive cubes and
  related results", Adv. in Appl. Math. 56 (2014), 25–66.

statements.name: Green15.green_15
statements.doc:
Does there exist a Lipschitz function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ whose graph
$\Gamma = \{(n, f(n)) : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^2$ is free of 3-term progressions?
statements.statement:
theorem green_15 :
    ∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∃ f : ℕ → ℤ, LipschitzWith K f ∧
      IsAPOfLengthFree {((n, f n) : ℤ × ℤ) | (n : ℕ)} 3

statements.name: Green15.green_15_ap4
statements.doc: The answer is YES for 4-term progressions [BJP14].
statements.statement:
theorem green_15_ap4 :
    ∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∃ f : ℕ → ℤ, LipschitzWith K f ∧
      IsAPOfLengthFree  {((n, f n) : ℤ × ℤ) | (n : ℕ)} 4

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 16
problems.doc:
*References:*
* [Ben Green's Open Problem 16](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.16)
* [Ruzsa](I. Z. Ruzsa, Solving a linear equation in a set of integers. I. Acta Arith. 65 (1993), no. 3, 259–282.)
* [Schoen and Sisask](T. Schoen and O. Sisask, Roth’s theorem for four variables and additive structures in sums of sparse sets Forum of Mathematics, Sigma (2016), Vol. 4, e5, 28 pages.)
* [Yufei Zhao](Via Personal Communication with Ben Green)

statements.name: Green16.green_16
statements.doc: What is the largest subset of $[N]$ with no solution to $x + 3y = 2z + 2w$ in distinct integers $x, y, z, w$?
statements.statement:
theorem green_16 (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Icc 1 N ∧ SolutionFree A ∧
      A.card = green_16.answer N ∧
      MaximalFor (fun B => B ⊆ Icc 1 N ∧ SolutionFree B) Finset.card A

statements.name: Green16.green_16_lower_bound
statements.doc: From [Ruzsa] $f(N) \gg N^{1/2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_16_lower_bound :
    (fun N ↦ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) ≪ fun N ↦ (f N : ℝ)

statements.name: Green16.green_16_upper_bound
statements.doc: From [Schoen and Sisask] $f(N) \ll N \cdot e^{-c(\log N)^{1/7}}$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_16_upper_bound :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), (fun N ↦ (f N : ℝ)) ≪ fun N ↦ (N : ℝ) * exp (-c * (log N) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))

statements.name: Green16.zhao_question
statements.doc:
From [Yufei Zhao]: Is there a subset of $\{1, \ldots, N\}$ of size
$N^{1/3 - o(1)}$ with no nontrivial solutions to $x + 2y + 3z = x' + 2y' + 3z'$?
statements.statement:
theorem zhao_question :
    ∃ h : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto h atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
      ∀ᶠ N in atTop, (g N : ℝ) ≥ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 3 - h N)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 18
problems.doc:
*Reference:*
- [Gr26] [Ben Green's Open Problem 18](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.18)
- [Au16] Austin, Tim. "Ajtai–Szemerédi theorems over quasirandom groups." Recent trends in
  combinatorics. Cham: Springer International Publishing, 2016. 453-484.
- [So13] Solymosi, Jozsef. "Roth-type theorems in finite groups." European Journal of Combinatorics
  34.8 (2013): 1454-1458.
- [Go01] Gowers, William T. "A new proof of Szemerédi's theorem." Geometric & Functional Analysis
  GAFA 11.3 (2001): 465-588.

statements.name: Green18.green_18
statements.doc:
Suppose that $G$ is a finite group, and let $A \subset G \times G$ be a subset of density $\alpha$.
Is it true that there are $\gg_\alpha |G|^3$ triples $x, y, g$ such that $(x, y), (gx, y), (x, gy)$
all lie in $A$?

Note: A is taken as $\alpha$-dense, i.e. $|A| \ge \alpha |G|^2$ [Au16, Question 2]
statements.statement:
theorem green_18 :
    ∀ α > 0, ∃ c > 0, ∃ m₀ : ℕ,
      ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G] (A : Finset (G × G)),
      Fintype.card G ≥ m₀ →
      (A.card : ℝ) ≥ α * (Fintype.card G) ^ 2 →
      (numNaiveCorners A : ℝ) ≥ c * (Fintype.card G) ^ 3

statements.name: Green18.green_18.bmz_corners
statements.doc: [So13] proved this is true for "BMZ corners". Follows from the proof of Theorem 2.1, p.1456-1457.
statements.statement:
theorem green_18.bmz_corners : ∀ α > 0, ∃ c > 0, ∃ m₀ : ℕ,
    ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G] (A : Finset (G × G)),
    Fintype.card G ≥ m₀ →
    (A.card : ℝ) ≥ α * (Fintype.card G) ^ 2 →
    (numBmzCorners A : ℝ) ≥ c * (Fintype.card G) ^ 3

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 19
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr26] [Ben Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.19)
- [FSS20] Fox, Jacob, et al. "Triforce and corners." Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge
  Philosophical Society. Vol. 169. No. 1. Cambridge University Press, 2020.
- [Ma21] Mandache, Matei. "A variant of the Corners theorem." Mathematical Proceedings of the
  Cambridge Philosophical Society. Vol. 171. No. 3. Cambridge University Press, 2021.
- [Ch11] Chu, Qing. "Multiple recurrence for two commuting transformations." Ergodic Theory and
  Dynamical Systems 31.3 (2011): 771-792.

statements.name: Green19.green_19
statements.doc:
What is $C$, the infimum of all exponents $c$ for which the following is true, uniformly for
$0 < \alpha < 1$? Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n \times \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a set of density
$\alpha$. Write $N := 2^n$. Then there is some $d \neq 0$ such that $A$ contains $\gg \alpha^c N^2$
corners $(x,y), (x,y+d), (x+d,y)$.

This question has been resolved by [FSS20], showing that $C = 4$.
statements.statement: theorem green_19 : C = 4

statements.name: Green19.green_19.lower
statements.doc: [Ma21] showed that $3.13 \leq C$. This also follows from `green_19`.
statements.statement: theorem green_19.lower : C >= 3.13

statements.name: Green19.green_19.upper
statements.doc: [Ma21] showed that $C \leq 4$. This also follows from `green_19`.
statements.statement: theorem green_19.upper : C <= 4

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 21
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.21)
- [Ra33] Rado, Richard, *Studien zur Kombinatorik*. Math. Zeit. 36 (1933), 424-480.
- [FoKl06] Fox, Jacob and Kleitman, Daniel, *On Rado's boundedness conjecture*. J. Combin. Theory
  Ser. A 113 (2006), no. 1, 84-100.
- [ElJo23] Ellis, David and Johnson, Robert (editors), *A collection of open problems in
  celebration of Imre Leader's 60th birthday*. arXiv preprint arXiv:2310.18163 (2023).

statements.name: Green21.green_21
statements.doc:
Suppose that $a_1, \dots, a_k$ are integers which do not satisfy Rado's condition: thus if
$\sum_{i \in I} a_i = 0$ then $I = \emptyset$. It then follows from Rado's theorem that the
equation $a_1x_1 + \cdots + a_kx_k = 0$ is not partition regular. Write $c(a_1, \dots, a_k)$ for
the least number of colours required in order to colour $\mathbb{N}$ so that there is no
monochromatic solution to $a_1x_1 + \cdots + a_kx_k = 0$. Is $c(a_1, \dots, a_k)$ bounded in
terms of $k$ only?

This problem, which is known as Rado's boundedness conjecture, dates back to 1933 [Ra33]. It is
open for all $k \geq 4$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_21 : ∃ B : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ (k : ℕ) (a : Fin k → ℤ),
    ¬ RadoCondition a → minColours a ≤ B k

statements.name: Green21.green_21.variants.fox_kleitman
statements.doc:
The answer was shown to be affirmative for $k = 3$ by Fox and Kleitman [FoKl06], who showed that
$c(a_1, a_2, a_3) \leq 24$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_21.variants.fox_kleitman (a : Fin 3 → ℤ) (ha : ¬ RadoCondition a) :
    minColours a ≤ 24

statements.name: Green21.green_21.variants.fox_kleitman_sharp
statements.doc:
Green [Gr24] is not sure that the constant $24$ of [FoKl06] is sharp, and remarks that it might
be interesting to determine the sharp constant.

The largest value of $c(a_1, a_2, a_3)$ is attained, since by `green_21.variants.fox_kleitman`
the values form a non-empty set of naturals bounded above by $24$.

statements.name: Green21.green_21.variants.fox_kleitman_modular
statements.doc:
A question [FoKl06, Conjecture 5] of Fox and Kleitman, which they call a 'modular analogue' of
Rado's Boundedness Conjecture. Let $k > 0$, let $p$ be a prime, and suppose that
$a_1, \dots, a_k$ are integers with $\sum_{i \in I} a_i \equiv 0 \pmod p$ only when
$I = \emptyset$. Does there exist
an $f(k)$-colouring of $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^*$ with no monochromatic solution to
$a_1x_1 + \cdots + a_kx_k = 0$? This seems to be open even when $k = 3$; Green [Gr24] suspects
the answer may be negative.

The point of the question is that the number of colours $f(k)$ must not depend on $p$.

The arity $k$ is required to be positive, as in [FoKl06]: for $k = 0$ the empty tuple is a
monochromatic solution with sum $0$ for every colouring, so no $f(0)$ could work.
statements.statement:
theorem green_21.variants.fox_kleitman_modular : ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ,
    ∀ (k p : ℕ), 0 < k → p.Prime → ∀ a : Fin k → ℤ,
      (∀ I : Finset (Fin k), (p : ℤ) ∣ ∑ i ∈ I, a i → I = ∅) →
      ∃ col : (ZMod p)ˣ → Fin (f k), ∀ x : Fin k → (ZMod p)ˣ,
        (∀ i j, col (x i) = col (x j)) → ∑ i, (a i : ZMod p) * (x i : ZMod p) ≠ 0

statements.name: Green21.green_21.variants.milicevic
statements.doc:
Milićević [ElJo23, Conjecture 11.1] conjectures the following 2-adic variant. For any
$k \in \mathbb{N}$, there exists $K = K(k)$ such that the following is true. Let $r$ be a
positive integer, and let $a_1, \dots, a_k \in \mathbb{Z}/2^r\mathbb{Z}$. Let $d$ be the largest
integer such that $\sum_{i \in I} a_i \equiv 0 \pmod{2^d}$ for some non-empty subset
$I \subset [k]$. Then there is a $K$-colouring of $\mathbb{Z}/2^r\mathbb{Z}$ such that all
monochromatic solutions $x = (x_1, \dots, x_k)$ to the equation
$a_1x_1 + \cdots + a_kx_k = 0$ satisfy $x_i \equiv 0 \pmod{2^{r-d}}$ for all $i = 1, \dots, k$.

Milićević remarks that, if true, this would imply the Rado boundedness conjecture by a
compactness argument.
statements.statement:
theorem green_21.variants.milicevic : ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ r : ℕ, 0 < r →
    ∀ a : Fin k → ZMod (2 ^ r), ∃ col : ZMod (2 ^ r) → Fin K,
      ∀ x : Fin k → ZMod (2 ^ r), (∀ i j, col (x i) = col (x j)) →
        ∑ i, a i * x i = 0 → ∀ i, 2 ^ (r - maxDepth a) ∣ (x i).val

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 22
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr26] [Ben Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.22)
- [Mo17] Moreira, Joel. "Monochromatic sums and products in N." Annals of Mathematics 185.3 (2017):
  1069-1090.
- [GrSa25] Green, Ben, and Mehtaab Sawhney. "Bounds for monochromatic solutions to
  $\{x+ y, xy\} $." arXiv preprint arXiv:2511.09365 (2025).
- [Ri25] Richter, Florian K. "Sums and products in sets of positive density." arXiv preprint
  arXiv:2507.00515 (2025).
- [BoSa24] Bowen, Matt, and Marcin Sabok. "Monochromatic products and sums in the rationals." Forum
  of Mathematics, Pi. Vol. 12. Cambridge University Press, 2024.
- [Bo25] Bowen, Matt. "Monochromatic products and sums in 2-colorings of N." Advances in Mathematics
  462 (2025): 110095.
- [Al23] Alweiss, Ryan. "Monochromatic Sums and Products over $\mathbb {Q} $." arXiv preprint
  arXiv:2307.08901 (2023).

statements.name: Green22.green_22
statements.doc:
If $\{1, \ldots, N\}$ is $r$-coloured then, for $N \geqslant N_0(r)$, there are integers
$x, y \geqslant 3$ such that $x + y, xy$ have the same colour.

Find reasonable bounds for $N_0(r)$. The goal is to improve upon the Green-Sawhney bound.
statements.statement:
theorem green_22 :
    ∀ᶠ r in atTop, N₀ r ≤ green_22.answer r ∧
    green_22.answer =o[atTop] GreenSawhneyBound

statements.name: Green22.green_22.variants.green_sawhney_bound
statements.doc: [GrSa25, Theorem 1.1] found a permissible upper bound.
statements.statement:
theorem green_22.variants.green_sawhney_bound :
    ∀ᶠ r in atTop, N₀ r ≤ GreenSawhneyBound r

statements.name: Green22.green_22.variants.moreira_infinite
statements.doc:
[Mo17, Corollary 1.5] For any finite coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ there exist (infinitely many)
$x, y \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\{xy, x + y\}$ is monochromatic.

This guarantees that $N_0(r)$ is well-defined.

Note: [Mo17] also establishes that $x$ is of the same colour.
statements.statement:
theorem green_22.variants.moreira_infinite :
    ∀ (r : ℕ) (coloring : ℕ → Fin r),
    Set.Infinite { p : ℕ × ℕ |
      0 < p.1 ∧ 0 < p.2 ∧
      coloring p.1 = coloring (p.1 * p.2) ∧
      coloring p.1 = coloring (p.1 + p.2) }

statements.name: Green22.green_22.variants.lower_nine
statements.doc:
Since $x, y \geq 3$, we must have $xy \geq 9$, so every $N$ such that all $r$-colourings of
$\{1, \ldots, N\}$ have the monochromatic sum-product property is at least $9$. In particular
$N_0(r) \geq 9$ once $N_0(r)$ is well-defined, which follows from [Mo17].

The bound is stated for every such $N$ and not as `9 ≤ N₀ r`: since `sInf ∅ = 0` in `ℕ`, the
latter is equivalent to the existence of such an $N$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_22.variants.lower_nine : ∀ r : ℕ, r ≠ 0 →
    ∀ N : ℕ, (∀ c : Icc 1 N → Fin r, HasMonochromaticSumProduct N r c) → 9 ≤ N

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 23
problems.doc:
References:
- [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.23)
- [FrKlMo25] Frantzikinakis, N., O. Klurman, and J. Moreira. "Partition regularity of Pythagorean pairs." Forum of Mathematics, Pi 13. Cambridge University Press (2025).

statements.name: Green23.green_23
statements.doc:
Suppose that $\mathbb{N}$ is finitely coloured. Are there $x,y$ of the same colour such that $x^2 +
 y^2$ is a square?

Solved in [FrKlMo25].
statements.statement:
theorem green_23 :
    -- For every finite colouring of the natural numbers
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (c : ℕ → Fin k),
    -- there exist two numbers of the same colour whose squares sum to a square
    ∃ x y : ℕ,
      0 < x ∧ 0 < y ∧  -- Exclude trivial x^2 + 0^2 = x^2 solution
      c x = c y ∧      -- Same colour
      IsSquare (x^2 + y^2)

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 24
problems.doc:
References:
- [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.24)
- [Aa19] Aaronson, James. "Maximising the number of solutions to a linear equation in a set of integers."
  Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society 51.4 (2019): 577-594.
- [HaL28] Hardy, G. H., and J. E. Littlewood. "Notes on the theory of series (VIII): an inequality."
  Journal of the London Mathematical Society 1.2 (1928): 105-110.

statements.name: Green24.green_24
statements.doc:
If $A$ is a set of $n$ integers, what is the maximum number of affine translates of the set
$\lbrace 0,1,3 \rbrace$ that $A$ can contain?

Conjectured in [Aa19] p.579: $\left(\frac{1}{3} + o(1)\right) n^2$.
statements.statement: theorem green_24 : ∀ n, max013AffineTranslates n = green_24.answer n

statements.name: Green24.variants.upper_trivial
statements.doc: From [Aa19] p.577: the trivial upper bound is $n^2$ (non asymptotic).
statements.statement: theorem upper_trivial {n : ℕ} : max013AffineTranslates n ≤ n ^ 2

statements.name: Green24.variants.upper_HL
statements.doc: Asymptotic upper bound (1.2) in [Aa19]. Named after Hardy and Littlewood [HaL28].
statements.statement: theorem upper_HL : gamma ≤ 3/4

statements.name: Green24.variants.lower_HL
statements.doc: Asymptotic lower bound (1.2) in [Aa19]. Named after Hardy and Littlewood [HaL28].
statements.statement: theorem lower_HL : gamma ≥ 1/12

statements.name: Green24.variants.conjecture
statements.doc: Conjecture p.579 in [Aa19]: $\left(\frac{1}{3} + o(1)\right) n^2$.
statements.statement: theorem conjecture : gamma = 1/3

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 25
problems.doc:
References:
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.25)
- [ESS89] Erdős, Pál, András Sárközy, and V. T. Sós. "On a conjecture of Roth and some related
  problems I." Irregularities of partitions. Berlin, Heidelberg: Springer Berlin Heidelberg, 1989.
  47-59.
- [Ru04] Ruzsa, Imre Z. "A problem on restricted sumsets." CONTEMPORARY MATHEMATICS 342 (2004):
  245-248.

statements.name: Green25.green_25
statements.doc:
For which values of $k$ is the following true: whenever we partition $[N] = A_1 \cup \dots \cup A_k$,
$\left|\bigcup^k_{i=1} (A_i \hat{+} A_i)\right| \geq \frac{1}{10} N$?
statements.statement: theorem green_25 : {k : ℕ → ℕ | ∀ᶠ N in atTop, Property25 (k N) N} = green_25.answer

statements.name: Green25.green_25.upper
statements.doc: We conjecture that the best-known upper bound can be lowered.
statements.statement:
theorem green_25.upper :
    -- Ensure k is a valid partition size
    (∀ᶠ N in atTop, 1 ≤ green_25.upper.answer N ∧ green_25.upper.answer N ≤ N) ∧
    (fun N => (green_25.upper.answer N : ℝ)) =o[atTop] bestUpper ∧
    ¬ ∀ᶠ N in atTop, Property25 (green_25.upper.answer N) N

statements.name: Green25.green_25.lower
statements.doc: We conjecture that the best-known lower bound can be raised.
statements.statement:
theorem green_25.lower :
    (bestLower =o[atTop] green_25.lower.answer) ∧
    (∀ᶠ N in atTop, 1 ≤ green_25.lower.answer N ∧ green_25.lower.answer N ≤ N) ∧
    ∀ k : ℕ → ℕ,
      (∀ᶠ N in atTop, 1 ≤ k N ∧ k N ≤ N) ∧
      ((fun N => (k N : ℝ)) ≪ green_25.lower.answer) →
      ∀ᶠ N in atTop, Property25 (k N) N

statements.name: Green25.green_25.variants.lower_ess89
statements.doc:
For $k \ll \log \log N$, this is true [Gr24].

NOTE: [ESS89] derive a precise constant for which this is true, but $\ll$ would imply that it works
for any constant. We thus prefer a little-o statement.
statements.statement:
theorem green_25.variants.lower_ess89 :
  ∀ k : ℕ → ℕ,
    (∀ᶠ N in atTop, 1 ≤ k N ∧ k N ≤ N) ∧ -- Ensure Property25 is not False due to non-existent partitions
    (fun N => (k N : ℝ)) =o[atTop] bestLower →
    ∀ᶠ N in atTop, Property25 (k N) N

statements.name: Green25.green_25.variants.upper_ess89
statements.doc:
For $k \gg N / \log N$, it need not be true [Gr24].

We formalize by enforcing a $N / \log N$ growth rate on $k(N)$. This avoids cases like $k(N) = N$
or $N-1$, which produce trivial counter examples with singletons and thus empty restricted sumsets.
statements.statement:
theorem green_25.variants.upper_ess89 :
  ∃ k : ℕ → ℕ,
    (∀ᶠ N in atTop, 1 ≤ k N ∧ k N ≤ N) ∧
    (fun N => (k N : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] bestUpper ∧
    ¬ ∀ᶠ N in atTop, Property25 (k N) N

statements.name: Green25.green_25.variants.upper_pow_23_40
statements.doc:
For $k(N) = \lceil N^{23/40} \rceil$, it need not be true: for all sufficiently large $N$
there is a partition of $[N]$ into $\lceil N^{23/40} \rceil$ parts with
$\left|\bigcup^k_{i=1} (A_i \hat{+} A_i)\right| < \frac{1}{10} N$.
In particular, the best-known upper bound $N / \log N$ can be lowered.
statements.statement:
theorem green_25.variants.upper_pow_23_40 :
    let k : ℕ → ℕ := fun N => Nat.ceil ((N : ℝ) ^ (23 / 40 : ℝ))
    (∀ᶠ N in atTop, 1 ≤ k N ∧ k N ≤ N) ∧
    (fun N => (k N : ℝ)) =o[atTop] bestUpper ∧
    ∀ᶠ N in atTop, ¬ Property25 (k N) N

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 26
problems.doc:
References:
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.26)
- [JLP92] Jaeger, François, et al. "Group connectivity of graphs—a nonhomogeneous analogue of
  nowhere-zero flow properties." Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B 56.2 (1992): 165-182.
- [ALM91] Alon, Noga, Nathan Linial, and Roy Meshulam. "Additive bases of vector spaces over prime
  fields." Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A 57.2 (1991): 203-210.
