- [Yu25] Yu, Yang. "Note on the Additive Basis Conjecture." arXiv preprint arXiv:2510.01300 (2025).

statements.name: Green26.green_26
statements.doc:
Let $A_1, \dots, A_{100}$ be "cubes" in $\mathbb{F}^n_3$.
Is it true that $A_1 + \dots + A_{100} = \mathbb{F}^n_3$?
statements.statement:
theorem green_26 :
    ∀ n : ℕ,
      ∀ A : Fin 100 → Set (𝔽₃ n), (∀ i, IsCube (A i)) →
      ∑ i, A i = univ

statements.name: Green26.green_26.variants.yu25
statements.doc: [Yu25] has solved the original problem (with 100 replaced by 4)
statements.statement:
theorem green_26.variants.yu25 :
    ∀ n : ℕ,
    ∀ A : Fin 4 → Set (𝔽₃ n), (∀ i, IsCube (A i)) →
      ∑ i, A i = univ

statements.name: Green26.green_26.variants.alm91
statements.doc:
[ALM91] showed that if 100 is replaced by $\leq c(p) \log n$ then the result is true for
$\mathbb{F}^n_p$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_26.variants.alm91 :
    ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime],
      ∃ (k : ℕ → ℕ),
        ((fun n ↦ (k n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ Real.log n) ∧
        ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
          ∀ A : Fin (k n) → Set (𝔽 p n), (∀ i, IsCube (A i)) →
          ∑ i, A i = univ

statements.name: Green26.green_26.variants.open
statements.doc: The analogous problem in $\mathbb{F}^n_p$ remains open. [Gr24]
statements.statement:
theorem green_26.variants.open :
    ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime],
      (∃ C, ∀ n, ∀ A : Fin C → Set (𝔽 p n), (∀ i, IsCube (A i)) →
      ∑ i, A i = univ)

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 27
problems.doc:
References:
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.27)
- [Be23] Bedert, Benjamin. "On unique sums in Abelian groups." Combinatorica 44.2 (2024): 269-298.
- [CY26] Cao, Jiao-Long, and Ye Yuan. "A Second-Logarithm Lower Bound for Sets with No Unique
  Sums." arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.06728 (2026).
- [St76] Straus, E. G. "Differences of residues (mod p)." Journal of Number Theory 8.1 (1976): 40-42.

statements.name: Green27.green_27.equivalent
statements.doc:
What is the size of the smallest set $A \subset \mathbb{Z} / p\mathbb{Z}$ (with at least two elements)
for which no element in the sumset $A + A$ has a unique representation?
statements.statement:
theorem green_27.equivalent :
  green_27.equivalent.answer ~[primesAtTop] m

statements.name: Green27.green_27.lower
statements.doc:
Propose a better lower bound along primes.

Cao and Yuan [CY26, Theorem 1.1] prove $m(p) \gg \log p \log \log p$. This beats `lowerBest`,
since $\sqrt{\log \log \log p} / \log \log \log \log p = o(\log \log p)$. The exact order of
$m(p)$ remains open.
statements.statement:
theorem green_27.lower :
    (lowerBest =o[primesAtTop] green_27.lower.answer) ∧ (green_27.lower.answer =O[primesAtTop] m)

statements.name: Green27.green_27.upper
statements.doc: Propose a better upper bound along primes.
statements.statement:
theorem green_27.upper :
    (green_27.upper.answer =o[primesAtTop] upperBest) ∧ (m =O[primesAtTop] green_27.upper.answer)

statements.name: Green27.green_27.variants.lower_be23
statements.doc: We have $m(p) \geq \omega(p) \log p$ for some function $\omega(p)$ tending to infinity [Be23, Theorem 3].
statements.statement:
theorem green_27.variants.lower_be23 :
  ∃ ω : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto ω primesAtTop atTop ∧
    ∀ᶠ p in primesAtTop,
      ω p * Real.log (p : ℝ) ≤ m p

statements.name: Green27.green_27.variants.lower_cy26
statements.doc: Lower bound: $\log p \log \log p \ll m(p)$ [CY26, Theorem 1.1].
statements.statement:
theorem green_27.variants.lower_cy26 :
  (fun p ↦ Real.log (p : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (p : ℝ))) =O[primesAtTop] m

statements.name: Green27.green_27.variants.upper_be23
statements.doc: Upper bound: $m(p) \ll (\log p)^2$ [Be23, Theorem 5].
statements.statement:
theorem green_27.variants.upper_be23 :
  m =O[primesAtTop] upperBest

statements.name: Green27.green_27.variants.previous_lower
statements.doc: Previous best-known lower bound $\log p \ll m(p)$ from [St76].
statements.statement:
theorem green_27.variants.previous_lower :
  (fun p ↦ Real.log (p : ℝ)) =O[primesAtTop] m

statements.name: Green27.green_27.variants.previous_upper
statements.doc: Previous best-known upper bound $m(p) \ll \sqrt{p}$ from [Be23].
statements.statement:
theorem green_27.variants.previous_upper :
  m =O[primesAtTop] (fun p ↦ Real.sqrt (p : ℝ))

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 28
problems.doc:
References:
- [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.28)
- [Mathoverflow/339137](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/339137/why-do-polynomials-with-coefficients-0-1-like-to-have-only-factors-with-0-1) asked by user [Sil](https://mathoverflow.net/users/136794/sil)
- [MathStackexchange/3325163](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3325163/) asked by user [Emmanuel Amiot](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/403309/emmanuel-amiot)

statements.name: Green28.green_28
statements.doc:
Suppose that $X, Y$ are two finitely-supported independent random variables taking integer values,
and such that $X + Y$ is uniformly distributed on its range. Are $X$ and $Y$ themselves uniformly
distributed on their ranges?
statements.statement:
theorem green_28 :
  ∀ (X Y : PMF ℤ), -- marginals, independence is built into indepSum
    X.support.Finite ∧ Y.support.Finite ∧ IsUniformOnSupport (indepSum X Y) →
      IsUniformOnSupport X ∧ IsUniformOnSupport Y

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 29
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 29](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.29)
- [Gr12] Green, Ben. "What is... an approximate group." Notices Amer. Math. Soc 59.5 (2012): 655-656.
- [Br13] Breuillard, Emmanuel, Ben Green, and Terence Tao. "Small doubling in groups."
  Erdős Centennial. Berlin, Heidelberg: Springer Berlin Heidelberg, 2013. 129-151.
- [Sa10] Sanders, Tom. "On a nonabelian Balog–Szemerédi-type lemma." Journal of the Australian
  Mathematical Society 89.1 (2010): 127-132.
- [CrSi10] Croot, Ernie, and Olof Sisask. "A probabilistic technique for finding almost-periods of
  convolutions." Geometric and functional analysis 20.6 (2010): 1367-1396.

statements.name: Green29.green_29
statements.doc:
Suppose that $A$ is a $K$-approximate group (not necessarily abelian). Is there $S \subset A$,
$|S| \gg K^{-O(1)} |A|$, with $S^8 \subset A^4$?

The answer is negative. A counterexample is given, for arbitrarily large finite groups `H`, by
`A = ({-1} × H) ∪ ({1} × H) ∪ {(0, 1)}` in `Multiplicative ℤ × H`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_29 :
    ¬ ∃ C c : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ 0 < c ∧
      ∀ {G : Type*} [Group G] [DecidableEq G] (K : ℝ) (A : Finset G),
        1 ≤ K → IsApproximateSubgroup K (A : Set G) →
          ∃ S ⊆ A, C * K ^ (-c) * (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (S.card : ℝ) ∧
          S ^ 8 ⊆ A ^ 4

statements.name: Green29.green_29.variant
statements.doc: Such a conclusion is known with $|S| \gg_K |A|$ [Br13 Problem 6.5, CrSi10, Sa10].
statements.statement:
theorem green_29.variant :
    ∀ K : ℝ, 1 ≤ K →
      ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ -- Allow c to depend on K.
        ∀ {G : Type*} [Group G] [DecidableEq G] (A : Finset G),
          IsApproximateSubgroup K (A : Set G) →
            ∃ S : Finset G, -- No S ⊆ A requirement in this variant.
              c * (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (S.card : ℝ) ∧
              S ^ 8 ⊆ A ^ 4

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 31
problems.doc:
Write $F(N)$ for the largest Sidon subset of $[N]$.
Improve, at least for infinitely many $N$, the bounds $N^{1/2} + O(1) \le F(N) \le N^{1/2} + N^{1/4} + O(1)$.

Note: the upper bound was improved to $N^{1/2} + 0.98183 N^{1/4} + O(1)$ in [CHO25], and then to
$N^{1/2} + 0.94349\ldots N^{1/4} + O(1)$ in [HZ26].

Related to Erdős Problem 30.

*References:*
- [Gr24] [Ben Green's Open Problem 31](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.7 Problem 31)
- [Gr01] Green, Ben. "The number of squares and $ B_h [g] $ sets."
  Acta Arithmetica 100.4 (2001): 365-390.
- [BFR23] Balogh, József, Zoltán Füredi, and Souktik Roy. "An upper bound on the size of Sidon sets."
  The American Mathematical Monthly 130.5 (2023): 437-445.
- [CHO25] Carter, Daniel, Zach Hunter, and Kevin O’Bryant. "On the diameter of finite Sidon sets."
  Acta Mathematica Hungarica 175.1 (2025): 108-126.
- [HZ26] Hou, Jianfeng, and Hongbin Zhao. "An Improved Upper Bound for Finite Sidon Sets via
  Vector-Valued Smoothing." [arXiv:2607.01169](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01169) (2026).
- [ET41] Erdos, Paul, and Pál Turán. "On a problem of Sidon in additive number theory, and on some
  related problems." J. London Math. Soc 16.4 (1941): 212-215.
- [Li69] Lindström, Bernt. “A remark on B4-Sequences.” Journal of Combinatorial Theory,
  Series A 7 (1969): 276-277.
- [CLZ01] Cohen, G.D., Litsyn, S., & Zémor, G. (2001). Binary B2-Sequences : A New Upper Bound.
  J. Comb. Theory A, 94, 152-155.
- [BS85] Babai, László, and Vera T. Sós. "Sidon sets in groups and induced subgraphs of Cayley
  graphs." European Journal of Combinatorics 6.2 (1985): 101-114.
  [doi:10.1016/S0195-6698(85)80001-9](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0195-6698%2885%2980001-9)

statements.name: Green31.green_31.lower
statements.doc: Can we improve the lower bound $N^{1/2} + O(1)$, at least for infinitely many $N$?
statements.statement:
theorem green_31.lower :
    -- Break the O(1) barrier
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N ↦ green_31.lower.answer N - Real.sqrt (N : ℝ)) atTop atTop ∧
    ∃ᶠ N in atTop, green_31.lower.answer N ≤ F N

statements.name: Green31.green_31.variants.lower_eventually
statements.doc: Can we improve the lower bound $N^{1/2} + O(1)$, for all sufficiently large $N$?
statements.statement:
theorem green_31.variants.lower_eventually :
    -- Break the O(1) barrier
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N ↦ green_31.variants.lower_eventually.answer N - Real.sqrt (N : ℝ)) atTop
      atTop ∧
    ∀ᶠ N in atTop, green_31.variants.lower_eventually.answer N ≤ F N

statements.name: Green31.green_31.upper
statements.doc:
Can we improve the upper bound $N^{1/2} + 0.94349 N^{1/4} + O(1)$ [HZ26], at least for infinitely
many $N$?
statements.statement:
theorem green_31.upper :
    (∃ᶠ N in atTop, F N ≤ green_31.upper.answer N) ∧
    ∃ c < (0.94349 : ℝ), ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, green_31.upper.answer N - Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) ≤ c *
      (N : ℝ) ^ (4⁻¹ : ℝ) + C

statements.name: Green31.green_31.variants.upper_eventually
statements.doc:
Can we improve the upper bound $N^{1/2} + 0.94349 N^{1/4} + O(1)$ [HZ26], for all sufficiently
large $N$?
statements.statement:
theorem green_31.variants.upper_eventually :
    (∀ᶠ N in atTop, F N ≤ green_31.variants.upper_eventually.answer N) ∧
    ∃ c < (0.94349 : ℝ), ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, green_31.variants.upper_eventually.answer N -
      Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) ≤ c * (N : ℝ) ^ (4⁻¹ : ℝ) + C

statements.name: Green31.green_31.variants.upper_li69
statements.statement:
theorem green_31.variants.upper_li69 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, F N ≤ Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) + (N : ℝ) ^ (4⁻¹ : ℝ) + C

statements.name: Green31.green_31.variants.upper_bfr23
statements.doc:
[BFR23] obtained a small improvement, getting an upper bound of $F(N) \le N^{1/2} + 0.998 N^{1/4}$
for large $N$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_31.variants.upper_bfr23 :
    ∀ᶠ N in atTop, F N ≤ Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) + (0.998 : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (4⁻¹ : ℝ)

statements.name: Green31.green_31.variants.upper_cho25
statements.doc: The upper bound was further improved to $N^{1/2} + 0.98183 N^{1/4} + O(1)$ [CHO25].
statements.statement:
theorem green_31.variants.upper_cho25 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, F N ≤ Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) + (0.98183 : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (4⁻¹ : ℝ) + C

statements.name: Green31.green_31.variants.upper_hz26
statements.doc:
[HZ26] improved the upper bound to $N^{1/2} + \gamma_0 N^{1/4} + O(1)$ with
$\gamma_0 = 0.94349\ldots < 0.9435$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_31.variants.upper_hz26 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, F N ≤ Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) + (0.9435 : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (4⁻¹ : ℝ) + C

statements.name: Green31.green_31.variants.zmod_p
statements.doc:
It is not known whether or not there exists a Sidon subset of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ of size
$(1 + o(1))\sqrt{p}$, for all $p$ [Gr24].
statements.statement:
theorem green_31.variants.zmod_p :
    ∃ S : (n : ℕ) → Finset (ZMod n),
    ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ,
      (o =o[atTop] fun _ : ℕ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧
      (∀ p, p.Prime → IsSidon (S p : Set (ZMod p))) ∧
      (∀ p, p.Prime → ((S p).card : ℝ) = (1 + o p) * Real.sqrt (p : ℝ))

statements.name: Green31.green_31.variants.abelian
statements.doc:
It is not known whether, if $G$ is an abelian group of size $n$, there always exists a Sidon subset
of $G$ of size $0.01\sqrt{n}$ [Gr24].

Green defines a Sidon set by $r_A(n) \le 1$ [Gr24, Section 4]. Read literally, this forbids
$a + a = b + b$ with $a \ne b$, and the answer is trivially negative: a Sidon subset of a group
of exponent $2$ then has at most one element. We use the definition of Babai and Sós [BS85]
instead, see `IsGroupSidon`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_31.variants.abelian :
    ∀ (G : Type) [AddCommGroup G] [Fintype G],
      ∃ S : Finset G, IsGroupSidon (S : Set G) ∧
        0.01 * Real.sqrt (Fintype.card G) ≤ S.card

statements.name: Green31.green_31.variants.sidon_01n
statements.doc:
Another very nice old problem is whether there is a Sidon subset of $\{0, 1\}^n$ of size $N^{0.51}$,
where $N = 2^n$ [Gr24].
statements.statement:
theorem green_31.variants.sidon_01n :
    ∃ S : (n : ℕ) → Finset (𝔽₂ n),
      (∀ n, IsBinarySidon (S n : Set (𝔽₂ n))) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ((2 : ℝ) ^ n) ^ (0.51 : ℝ) ≤ (S n).card

statements.name: Green31.green_31.variants.sidon_01n_clz01
statements.doc: The best-known upper bound for a Sidon subset of $\{0, 1\}^n$ ($N = 2^n$) is $N^{0.5753}$ [CLZ01].
statements.statement:
theorem green_31.variants.sidon_01n_clz01 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n, ∀ S : Finset (𝔽₂ n),
      IsBinarySidon (S : Set (𝔽₂ n)) →
        (S.card : ℝ) ≤ C * ((2 : ℝ) ^ n) ^ (0.5753 : ℝ)

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 32
problems.doc:
*Reference:*
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.32)
- [Sh20] Shakan, George. "A Large Gap in a Dilate of a Set." SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics
  34.4 (2020): 2553-2555.

statements.name: Green32.green_32
statements.doc:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $A \subset \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ be a set of size $\lfloor \sqrt{p} \rfloor$.
Is there a dilate of $A$ containing a gap of length $100\sqrt{p}$?
statements.statement:
theorem green_32 :
    HasLargeGapDilate (fun p ↦ Real.sqrt p)

statements.name: Green32.green_32.variants.sh20_general
statements.doc: [Sh20, Theorem 1] implies a gap of at least $\lfloor 2p/|A| - 2 \rfloor$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_32.variants.sh20_general :
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → -- Theorem 1 is for any prime p, not just asymptotically
      ∀ A : Finset (ZMod p), 1 < A.card →
      ∃ c : (ZMod p)ˣ, HasGap (c • A) ⌊2 * (p : ℝ) / A.card - 2⌋₊

statements.name: Green32.green_32.variants.sh20_sqrt
statements.doc:
[Sh20] has used the polynomial method to show that this is true with 100 replaced by 2 [Gr24].

Note: More precisely [Sh20, Theorem 1] implies a gap of at least $\lfloor 2p/|A| - 2 \rfloor$.
For a set $A$ of size $\lfloor \sqrt{p} \rfloor$, this guarantees a gap of at least
$\lfloor 2\sqrt{p} \rfloor - 2$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_32.variants.sh20_sqrt :
    ∀ᶠ p in atTop, p.Prime →
      ∀ A : Finset (ZMod p), A.card = ⌊Real.sqrt p⌋₊ →
      ∃ c : (ZMod p)ˣ, HasGap (c • A) (⌊2 * Real.sqrt p⌋₊ - 2)

statements.name: Green32.green_32.variants.szemeredi_regime
statements.doc: In the regime $\omega(p) \sim c p$, this is Szemerédi's theorem [Gr24].
statements.statement:
theorem green_32.variants.szemeredi_regime :
    ∀ c, 0 < c ∧ c < 1 → ∀ ω : ℕ → ℝ, ω ~[atTop] (fun p ↦ c * p) →
      HasLargeGapDilate ω

statements.name: Green32.green_32.variants.dirichlet_regime
statements.doc:
In the regime $\omega(p) \le c \log p$, this is basically Dirichlet's lower bound for the size of
Bohr sets [Gr24].

The lower bound $101 \le \omega(p)$ makes the set size $\lfloor \omega(p) \rfloor$ exceed $100$.
With only $100 < \omega(p)$, a function with $100 < \omega(p) < 101$ asks for sets of size $100$
with a gap of length $p - 1$ in some dilate, which is impossible.
statements.statement:
theorem green_32.variants.dirichlet_regime :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ ω : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ᶠ p in atTop, 101 ≤ ω p ∧ ω p ≤ c * Real.log p) →
      HasLargeGapDilate ω

statements.name: Green32.green_32.variants.log_regime
statements.doc: Even what happens in the regime $\omega(p) \sim 10 \log p$ is unclear [Gr24].
statements.statement:
theorem green_32.variants.log_regime :
    (∀ ω : ℕ → ℝ, ω ~[atTop] (fun p ↦ 10 * Real.log p) →
      HasLargeGapDilate ω)

statements.name: Green32.green_32.variants.finite_field
statements.doc:
Tom Sanders' finite field variant [Gr24].
If $N = 2^n$ and $A$ is a subset of size $\lfloor \sqrt{N} \rfloor$, then $A^c$ contains a coset of
size at least $100\sqrt{N}$ for sufficiently large $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_32.variants.finite_field :
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∀ A : Finset (𝔽₂ n), A.card = ⌊Real.sqrt (2^n : ℝ)⌋₊ →
      HasCosetHole A ⌊100 * Real.sqrt (2^n : ℝ)⌋₊

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 33
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Ben Green's Open Problem 33](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.33)
- [CaHa20] Caprace, Pierre-Emmanuel, and Pierre de la Harpe. "Groups with irreducibly unfaithful
  subsets for unitary representations." Confluentes Mathematici 12.1 (2020): 31-68.
- [CrLe07] Croot, Ernie, and Vsevolod F. Lev. "Open problems in additive combinatorics."
  Additive combinatorics 43.207-233 (2007): 1.

statements.name: Green33.green_33
statements.doc:
Are there infinitely many $q$ for which there is a set $A \subset \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$,
$|A| = (\sqrt{2} + o(1))q^{1/2}$, with $A + A = \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$? [Gr24]
statements.statement:
theorem green_33 :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
      ∃ᶠ q : ℕ+ in atTop,
        ∃ A : Finset (ZMod q),
          A + A = Finset.univ ∧
          |((A.card : ℝ) / Real.sqrt q - Real.sqrt 2)| < ε

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 35
problems.doc:
Estimate the infimum of the $L^p$ norm of the self-convolution of a nonnegative integrable
function supported on $[0,1]$ with total integral $1$.

We model a function `f : [0,1] → ℝ≥0` as a function `f : ℝ → ℝ` that is nonnegative, integrable,
supported on `[0,1]`, and has total integral `1`.

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 35](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.35)
- [Gr01](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/number-of-squares-and-Bh%5Bg%5D.pdf)
  B. J. Green, *The number of squares and $B_h[g]$-sets*, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), no. 4, 365-390.
- [CS17](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.7988)
  A. Cloninger and S. Steinerberger, *On suprema of autoconvolutions with an application to Sidon
  sets*, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 145 (2017), no. 8, 3191-3200.
- [MV10](https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.1379)
  M. Matolcsi and C. Vinuesa, *Improved bounds on the supremum of autoconvolutions*,
  J. Math. Anal. Appl. 372 (2010), 439-447.
- [AE25](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13131)
  A. Novikov et al., *AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery*,
  arXiv:2506.13131 (2025), Appendix B.1.
- [GGTW25](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02864)
  B. Georgiev, J. Gómez-Serrano, T. Tao and A. Z. Wagner, *Mathematical exploration and discovery
  at scale*, arXiv:2511.02864 (2025), Section 6.2.

The constants of [CS17], [MV10], [AE25] and [GGTW25] are stated for functions supported on
$[-1/4, 1/4]$; rescaling to $[0, 1]$ halves them.

statements.name: Green35.green_35.lower
statements.doc:
Lower bound for $c(p)$ for $1 < p \le \infty$, improving the known value $\sqrt{4/7}$ at
$p = 2$ or the known value $0.64$ at $p = \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_35.lower :
    (∀ p, 1 < p → green_35.lower.answer p ≤ c p) ∧
      (ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (4 / 7)) < green_35.lower.answer 2 ∨
        0.64 < green_35.lower.answer ∞)

statements.name: Green35.green_35.upper
statements.doc:
Upper bound for $c(p)$ for $1 < p \le \infty$, improving the best-known value $0.7516$ at
$p = \infty$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_35.upper :
    (∀ p, 1 < p → c p ≤ green_35.upper.answer p) ∧ green_35.upper.answer ∞ < 0.7516

statements.name: Green35.variants.c_2_lower
statements.doc: Lower bound for $c(2)$ from Green's first paper ([Gr01]); the constant is `sqrt(4/7)` (about 0.7559).
statements.statement: theorem c_2_lower : ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (4 / 7)) ≤ c 2

statements.name: Green35.variants.c_inf_lower
statements.doc: Best-known lower bound for $c(\infty)$ due to Cloninger and Steinerberger ([CS17]).
statements.statement: theorem c_inf_lower : 0.64 ≤ c ∞

statements.name: Green35.variants.c_inf_upper
statements.doc:
Upper bound for $c(\infty)$ due to Matolcsi and Vinuesa ([MV10]); their step function has
autoconvolution supremum $1.50972\ldots$, which rescales to $0.75486\ldots$.
statements.statement: theorem c_inf_upper : c ∞ ≤ 0.7549

statements.name: Green35.variants.c_inf_upper_ae25
statements.doc:
Upper bound for $c(\infty)$ found by AlphaEvolve ([AE25]) and recorded in Green's 2025
update; the step function there has autoconvolution supremum at most $1.5053$, which rescales to
$0.75265$.
statements.statement: theorem c_inf_upper_ae25 : c ∞ ≤ 0.75265

statements.name: Green35.variants.c_inf_upper_ggtw25
statements.doc:
Best-known upper bound for $c(\infty)$ ([GGTW25], §6.2): a step function with autoconvolution
supremum at most $1.5032$, which rescales to $0.7516$.
statements.statement: theorem c_inf_upper_ggtw25 : c ∞ ≤ 0.7516

statements.name: Green35.variants.c_inf_lower_young
statements.doc: A comparison bound from Young's inequality.
statements.statement: theorem c_inf_lower_young : (c 2) ^ 2 ≤ c ∞

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 36
problems.doc:
*References:*
* [Gr24] [Green's Open Problems #36](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.36)
* [CKS05] Cohn, H., Kleinberg, R., Szegedy, B., and Umans, C. "Group-theoretic Algorithms for
  Matrix Multiplication" (Problem 4.7)

statements.name: Green36.green_36
statements.doc:
Do the following exist, for arbitrarily large $n$? An abelian group $H$ with $|H| = n^{2+o(1)}$,
together with subsets $A_1, ..., A_n, B_1, ..., B_n$ satisfying $|A_i||B_i| \ge n^{2-o(1)}$ and
$|A_i + B_i| = |A_i||B_i|$, such that the sets $A_i + B_i$ are disjoint from the sets $A_j + B_k$
($j \neq k$)?

NOTE: according to [CKS05, 4.1], the conditions should be $A_i + B_j$ disjoint from $A_j + B_k$ for
$i \neq k$. See `green_36.variants.cks05`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_36 :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∃ (H : Type) (_ : AddCommGroup H) (_ : Finite H) (A B : Fin n → Finset H),
        (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε) ≤ Nat.card H ∧ Nat.card H ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (2 + ε) ∧
        (∀ i, (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε) ≤ (A i).card * (B i).card) ∧
        Green36Property A B

statements.name: Green36.green_36.variants.cks05
statements.doc: Variant using the exact simultaneous double product property from [CKS05, 4.1].
statements.statement:
theorem green_36.variants.cks05 :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∃ (H : Type) (_ : AddCommGroup H) (_ : Finite H) (A B : Fin n → Finset H),
        (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε) ≤ Nat.card H ∧ Nat.card H ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (2 + ε) ∧
        (∀ i, (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε) ≤ (A i).card * (B i).card) ∧
        SimultaneousDoubleProduct A B

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 37
problems.doc:
What is the smallest subset of `ℕ` containing, for each `d = 1, …, N`,
an arithmetic progression of length `k` with common difference `d`?

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 37](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.37)
- [Green & Tao, *The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions* (arXiv:math/0404188)](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0404188)

statements.name: Green37.green_37
statements.doc:
Given a natural number `N`, what is the smallest size of a subset of `ℕ` that contains, for each `d = 1, …, N`,
an arithmetic progression of length `k` with common difference `d`.

statements.name: Green37.green_37_asymptotic
statements.doc:
Asymptotic version: determine the asymptotic behavior of `m(N, k)` as `N` grows.
The solver should determine a function `f : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ` such that, for each `k`,
`f k` eventually equals `(fun N ↦ (m N k : ℝ))`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_37_asymptotic (k : ℕ) :
    ∀ᶠ N in atTop, (m N k : ℝ) = green_37_asymptotic.answer k N

statements.name: Green37.green_37_theta
statements.doc: Determine, for each `k`, the asymptotic equivalence class (theta) of `m(N, k)` as `N` grows.
statements.statement:
theorem green_37_theta (k : ℕ) :
    (fun N ↦ (m N k : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] green_37_theta.answer k

statements.name: Green37.green_37_lower_bound
statements.doc:
Writing `F_k(N)` for `m(N, k)`, Green conjectures that `F_k(N) ≫_k N^(1 - c_k)` for some
sequence `c_k` with `c_k → 0` as `k → ∞`.
The restriction to `0 < k` excludes the degenerate case `m(N, 0) = 0`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_37_lower_bound :
    ∃ c : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto c atTop (nhds 0) ∧
      ∀ k, 0 < k → (fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 - c k)) =O[atTop] fun N ↦ (m N k : ℝ)

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 38
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [100 open problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.38)
- [La79] Lovász, László. "On the Shannon capacity of a graph."
  IEEE Transactions on Information theory 25.1 (1979): 1-7.
- [Po20] Polak, Sven. "New methods in coding theory: Error-correcting codes and the Shannon capacity."
  arXiv preprint arXiv:2005.02945 (2020).
- [IRCR26] Itty, Nathaniel and Rosin, Christopher D. and Carstensen, Chase and Reichman, Daniel.
  "Improved lower bounds for the Shannon capacity of odd cycles." arXiv:2607.21517 (2026).
- [Ga26] Gao, Yu. "A recursive construction improving the lower bound on the Shannon capacity of
  $C_7$." arXiv:2607.27869 (2026).
- [BPZ26] Buys, Pjotr and Polak, Sven and Zuiddam, Jeroen. "Lean-verified lower bounds for the
  Shannon capacity of odd cycles." arXiv:2607.29681 (2026). Lean formalisation:
  https://github.com/spectra-research/shannon-capacity-lean

statements.name: Green38.green_38.lower
statements.doc:
Can we improve the lower bound? The answer sequence must be eventually nonnegative, since
`=O` compares norms.

Yes. Itty, Rosin, Carstensen and Reichman [IRCR26] found a valid set of size $134753$ in
$\mathbb{F}_7^{10}$ (an independent set in the tenth strong power of $C_7$). Taking products
gives valid sets of size $134753^{\lfloor n/10 \rfloor}$ in $\mathbb{F}_7^n$, see
`green_38.variants.lower_itty_rosin_carstensen_reichman`, so the growth rate is at least
$134753^{1/10} > 3.258020 > C_1$ (note $134753 > 367^2 = 134689$). Gao [Ga26] and then Buys,
Polak and Zuiddam [BPZ26] improved the rate further, to $3.258789\ldots$ and $3.2588\ldots$
respectively; the latter is formalised in Lean. The exact growth rate remains open.
statements.statement:
theorem green_38.lower :
    (∀ᶠ n in atTop, 0 ≤ green_38.lower.answer n) ∧ green_38.lower.answer ≤ᶠ[atTop]
      LargestAdmissibleCardinality ∧
    ∃ c > C₁, (fun n ↦ c ^ n) =O[atTop] green_38.lower.answer

statements.name: Green38.green_38.upper
statements.doc:
Can we improve the best upper bound? The base `c` must be positive, since `=O` compares
norms.
statements.statement:
theorem green_38.upper :
    LargestAdmissibleCardinality ≤ᶠ[atTop] green_38.upper.answer ∧
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ c < C₂ ∧ green_38.upper.answer =O[atTop] (fun n ↦ c ^ n)

statements.name: Green38.green_38.variants.best_lower
statements.doc:
The lower bound $(C_1 - o(1))^n \leqslant |A|$ where $C_1 = 367^{1/5} \approx 3.2578$, from a
valid set of size $367$ in $\mathbb{F}_7^5$ [Po20, Section 9.1]. This was the best known bound
when Green's list was written; it has since been improved, see `green_38.lower`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_38.variants.best_lower :
    ∀ ε ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) C₁, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (C₁ - ε) ^ n ≤ LargestAdmissibleCardinality n

statements.name: Green38.green_38.variants.lower_itty_rosin_carstensen_reichman
statements.doc:
Itty, Rosin, Carstensen and Reichman [IRCR26] found a valid set of size $134753$ in
$\mathbb{F}_7^{10}$. Products of copies of it, padded with zero coordinates, give
$134753^{\lfloor n/10 \rfloor} \leqslant |A|$ in $\mathbb{F}_7^n$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_38.variants.lower_itty_rosin_carstensen_reichman (n : ℕ) :
    (134753 : ℝ) ^ (n / 10) ≤ LargestAdmissibleCardinality n

statements.name: Green38.green_38.variants.best_upper
statements.doc:
The current best upper bound is $|A| \leqslant (C_2 + o(1))^n$ where
$C_2 = \frac{7 \cos(\pi/7)}{1 + \cos(\pi/7)} \approx 3.3177$ [La79, Corollary 5].
statements.statement:
theorem green_38.variants.best_upper :
    ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, LargestAdmissibleCardinality n ≤ (C₂ + ε) ^ n

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 39
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.39)
- [BJR11] Bollobás, Béla, Svante Janson, and Oliver Riordan. "On covering by translates of a set."
  Random Structures & Algorithms 38.1‐2 (2011): 33-67.

statements.name: Green39.green_39
statements.doc:
If $A \subset \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ is random, $|A| = \sqrt{p}$, can we almost surely cover
$\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with $100\sqrt{p}$ translates of $A$? [Gr24]
statements.statement:
theorem green_39 :
    Tendsto
      (fun p : {q : ℕ // q.Prime} ↦
        let k := Nat.sqrt p
        let c := 100 * k
        (proportionCoverable p k c : ℝ))
      atTop (𝓝 1)

statements.name: Green39.green_39.variant_101
statements.doc: "I do not know how to answer this even with 100 replaced by 1.01." [Gr24]"
statements.statement:
theorem green_39.variant_101 :
    Tendsto
      (fun p : {q : ℕ // q.Prime} ↦
        let k := Nat.sqrt p
        let c := ⌊1.01 * (k : ℝ)⌋₊
        (proportionCoverable p k c : ℝ))
      atTop (𝓝 1)

statements.name: Green39.green_39.variant_theta
statements.doc:
Similar questions are interesting with $\sqrt{p}$ replaced by $p^\theta$ for any $\theta \le 1/2$. [Gr24]

NOTE: using $C p^\theta$ translates as stated makes the conjecture trivially false by the pigeonhole
principle. Indeed for a set of size $p^\theta$, we cover at most $C p^{2\theta}$ elements, which is
strictly less than $p$ for $\theta < 1/2$. We interpret the question as asking whether
$O(p^{1-\theta})$ translates suffice. This generalizes the main conjecture where
$\sqrt{p} = p^{1-1/2}$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_39.variant_theta :
    ∀ (θ : ℝ), 0 < θ → θ ≤ 1/2 →
    ∃ C > 1, Tendsto
      (fun p : {q : ℕ // q.Prime} ↦
        let k := ⌊(p : ℝ) ^ θ⌋₊
        let c := ⌊C * (p : ℝ) ^ (1 - θ)⌋₊
        (proportionCoverable p k c : ℝ))
      atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 40
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Ben Green's Open Problem 40](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.40)
- [Da90] Davydov, Alexander Abramovich. "Construction of linear covering codes."
  Problemy Peredachi Informatsii 26.4 (1990): 38-55.
- [CHL97] Cohen, G., Honkala, I., Litsyn, S., & Lobstein, A. (1997). Covering codes (Vol. 54). Elsevier.
- [St94] R. Struik, Covering codes, PhD Thesis, Eindhoven University of Technology, the Netherlands, 106 pp, 1994.

statements.name: Green40.green_40
statements.doc: Does $f(r) \to \infty$? [Gr24]
statements.statement: theorem green_40 : Tendsto f atTop (𝓝 ⊤)

statements.name: Green40.green_40.sanity_f_one
statements.doc: The only value known is $f(1) = 1$, which follows from the existence of the Hamming code [Gr24].
statements.statement: theorem green_40.sanity_f_one : f 1 = 1

statements.name: Green40.green_40.upper_bound
statements.doc: $f(r) \le r^r / r! \sim e^r$ [Gr24].
statements.statement: theorem green_40.upper_bound (r : ℕ) : f r ≤ (r ^ r : ℝ≥0∞) / (r.factorial : ℝ≥0∞)

statements.name: Green40.green_40.f_eq_one_for_all
statements.doc: The possibility that f(r) = 1 for all r has not been ruled out [Gr24]
statements.statement: theorem green_40.f_eq_one_for_all : ∀ r, f r = 1

statements.name: Green40.green_40.f_two_eq_one
statements.doc: It is not known whether f(2) = 1 [Gr24]
statements.statement: theorem green_40.f_two_eq_one : f 2 = 1

statements.name: Green40.green_40.upper_bound_f_two
statements.doc: The best-known upper bound for $f(2)$ is $1.4238$ [CHL97].
statements.statement: theorem green_40.upper_bound_f_two : f 2 ≤ (1.4238 : ℝ≥0∞)

statements.name: Green40.green_40.variants.arbitrary_subsets
statements.doc: Does $\tilde{f}(r) \to \infty$? [Gr24]
statements.statement: theorem green_40.variants.arbitrary_subsets : Tendsto f_tilde atTop (𝓝 ⊤)

statements.name: Green40.green_40.variants.arbitrary_subsets_sanity_f_tilde_two
statements.doc: It is known that $\tilde{f}(2) = 1$ [St94].
statements.statement: theorem green_40.variants.arbitrary_subsets_sanity_f_tilde_two : f_tilde 2 = 1

statements.name: Green40.green_40.f_tilde_le_f
statements.doc: We evidently have $\tilde{f}(r) \le f(r)$ [Gr24].
statements.statement: theorem green_40.f_tilde_le_f (r : ℕ) : f_tilde r ≤ f r

statements.name: Green40.green_40.variants.all_n
statements.doc:
Does $f_{\text{all}}(r) \to \infty$? [Gr24]

The target filter is `𝓝 ⊤`, as in `green_40` and `green_40.variants.arbitrary_subsets`. On
`ℝ≥0∞`, `atTop` is the principal ultrafilter at `⊤`, so `Tendsto f_all atTop atTop` would say
that `f_all r = ⊤` for all large `r` rather than that `f_all r → ∞`.
statements.statement: theorem green_40.variants.all_n : Tendsto f_all atTop (𝓝 ⊤)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 41
problems.doc:
*References*
- [Gr24] [Ben Green's Open Problem 41](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.41)
- [Ma15] Manners, Freddie. "A solution to the pyjama problem." Inventiones mathematicae 202.1 (2015): 239-270.
- [KrLe25] Kravitz, Noah, and James Leng. "Quantitative pyjama." arXiv preprint arXiv:2510.17744 (2025).

statements.name: Green41.minCopies_set_nonempty
statements.doc:
[Ma15] proved that for any $\varepsilon > 0$, finitely many rotations of the pyjama set of width
$\varepsilon$ cover the plane. This implies that the set we are taking the infimum over in `minCopies`
is non-empty.
statements.statement:
theorem minCopies_set_nonempty (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    (coveringCopies ε).Nonempty

statements.name: Green41.green_41
statements.doc:
How many rotated (about the origin) copies of the 'pyjama set'
$\\{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : \text{dist}(x, \mathbb{Z}) \leq \varepsilon\\}$ are needed to cover
$\mathbb{R}^2$?

That is, determine the minimal number of rotations as a function of $\varepsilon > 0$.
statements.statement: theorem green_41 : ∀ ε > 0, minCopies ε = green_41.answer ε

statements.name: Green41.green_41.variants.double_exponential_bound
statements.doc:
Can the triple-exponential bound of [KrLe25] be improved by one exponential? That is, do
$\exp\exp(\varepsilon^{-C})$ rotations suffice for some $C$ and all sufficiently small
$\varepsilon > 0$? [KrLe25, Section 8.1] discusses where the three exponentials are lost and
which of them one might hope to save.
statements.statement:
theorem green_41.variants.double_exponential_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∃ ε₀ > 0, ∀ ε ∈ Ioc 0 ε₀, (minCopies ε : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp (Real.exp (ε ^ (-C)))

statements.name: Green41.green_41.variants.polynomial_bound
statements.doc: Is $\varepsilon^{-C}$ rotations enough?
statements.statement:
theorem green_41.variants.polynomial_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∃ ε₀ > 0, ∀ ε ∈ Ioc 0 ε₀, (minCopies ε : ℝ) ≤ ε ^ (-C)

statements.name: Green41.green_41.variants.kravitz_leng
statements.doc:
[KrLe25] have established the first quantitative bound, showing via an analysis of [Ma15]'s method
that $\exp\exp\exp(\varepsilon^{-C})$ rotations suffice.
statements.statement:
theorem green_41.variants.kravitz_leng :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∃ ε₀ > 0, ∀ ε ∈ Ioc 0 ε₀, (minCopies ε : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp (Real.exp (Real.exp (ε ^ (-C))))

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 42
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.42)
- [CoEl03] Cohn, Henry, and Noam Elkies. "New upper bounds on sphere packings I."
  Annals of Mathematics (2003): 689-714.
- [Vi17] Viazovska, Maryna S. "The sphere packing problem in dimension 8."
  Annals of mathematics (2017): 991-1015.
- [CKM17] Cohn, H., Kumar, A., Miller, S., Radchenko, D., & Viazovska, M. (2017).
  The sphere packing problem in dimension 24. Annals of mathematics, 185(3), 1017-1033.
- [Sa21] Sardari, Naser Talebizadeh. "Higher Fourier interpolation on the plane."
  arXiv preprint arXiv:2102.08753 (2021).
- [OAI26a] OpenAI, *A sharp Fourier certificate for planar circle packing*.
  OpenAI Math Release preprint (2026).
  https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/A-sharp-Fourier-certificate-for-planar-circle-packing-September-23-2026/paper.pdf

statements.name: Green42.green_42
statements.doc:
Can the Cohn-Elkies scheme be used to prove the optimal bound for circle-packings in 2 dimensions?

The answer is "yes". This was proved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26a]; see
the linked Lean proof, which constructs a radial Schwartz certificate normalised to minimum
distance $1$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_42 :
    CohnElkiesOptimal 2 (Real.sqrt 3 / 6)

statements.name: Green42.green_42.variants.dimension_one
statements.doc: [CoEl03] proved this when $d = 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_42.variants.dimension_one :
    CohnElkiesOptimal 1 (1 / 2)

statements.name: Green42.green_42.variants.dimension_eight
statements.doc: [Vi17] established the case $d = 8$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_42.variants.dimension_eight :
    CohnElkiesOptimal 8 (1 / 16)

statements.name: Green42.green_42.variants.dimension_twenty_four
statements.doc: In [CKM17], [Vi17] was adapted to $d = 24$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_42.variants.dimension_twenty_four :
    CohnElkiesOptimal 24 1

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 43
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Ben Green's Open Problem 43](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.43)
- [Gr18] Green, Ben. "A note on multiplicative functions on progressions to large moduli."
  Proc. Roy. Soc. Edinburgh Sect. A 148 (2018), no. 1, 63–77. (Problem 43 is formulated here,
  [Gr18, Section 4].)
- [AP92] Alon, Noga, and Yuval Peres. "Uniform dilations." Geometric and Functional Analysis
  2 (1992), no. 1, 1–28. (Source of the favourite variant in [Gr24, Comments to Problem 43].)

statements.name: Green43.green_43
statements.doc:
Let $N$ be a large integer. For each prime $p$ with $N^{0.51} \leq p < 2N^{0.51}$, pick some
residue $a(p) \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. Is it true that
$$\#\{n \in [N] : n \equiv a(p) \pmod{p} \text{ for some } p\} \gg N^{1-o(1)}?$$
statements.statement: theorem green_43 : SievedLowerBoundExp (0.51 : ℝ)

statements.name: Green43.green_43.variants.alon_peres
statements.doc:
[Gr24, Comments to Problem 43; AP92] One of Green's favourite related conjectures: if
`A ⊆ ℤ/pℤ` is a set of size `⌊p/2⌋`, does some dilation `n A` (`n` an integer) have no gaps of
length more than `p^{0.49}`?

The question is asymptotic, so it is stated for all sufficiently large primes `p` (see the
large-prime discussion in [AP92, §2]); for small primes it fails trivially, e.g. `p = 3`, `A = {0}`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_43.variants.alon_peres :
    ∀ᶠ p : ℕ in atTop, p.Prime → ∀ A : Finset (ZMod p), A.card = p / 2 →
    ∃ n : ZMod p, ∀ L : ℕ, (p : ℝ) ^ (0.49 : ℝ) < (L : ℝ) → ¬ HasGap (Dilate n A) L

statements.name: Green43.green_43.variants.range_N051_N052
statements.doc:
[Gr24, Comments to Problem 43] A minor variant of Problem 43: the same question but with `p`
ranging over `N^{0.51} ≤ p < N^{0.52}`. Obtaining the lower bound `N^{1-o(1)}` here is no harder
than Problem 43, but is not known.
statements.statement:
theorem green_43.variants.range_N051_N052 :
    SievedLowerBound (fun N => (N : ℝ) ^ (0.51 : ℝ)) (fun N => (N : ℝ) ^ (0.52 : ℝ))

statements.name: Green43.green_43.variants.range_N051_N052_linear
statements.doc:
[Gr24, Comments to Problem 43] For the range `N^{0.51} ≤ p < N^{0.52}` there may even be a
linear lower bound `c N`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_43.variants.range_N051_N052_linear :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∀ a : ℕ → ℤ,
      c * N ≤ sievedCard N a ((N : ℝ) ^ (0.51 : ℝ)) ((N : ℝ) ^ (0.52 : ℝ))

statements.name: Green43.green_43.variants.general_exponent
statements.doc:
[Gr24, Comments to Problem 43] One can replace the exponent `0.51` by any other exponent `α`:
does the lower bound `N^{1-o(1)}` hold for sieving primes in `[N^α, 2 N^α)` for every exponent
`0 < α < 1`? Problem 43 is the case `α = 0.51`; the regime `α < 1/2` is the solved special case
`green_43.variants.general_exponent_lt_half`, while progress for `α ≈ 1` would imply Kakeya.
statements.statement:
theorem green_43.variants.general_exponent :
    ∀ α : ℝ, 0 < α → α < 1 → SievedLowerBoundExp α

statements.name: Green43.green_43.variants.general_exponent_lt_half
statements.doc:
[Gr24, Comments to Problem 43] For exponents `α < 1/2` the lower bound `N^{1-o(1)}` is
straightforward (by an inclusion–exclusion or Cauchy–Schwarz argument). This is the solved
special case of `green_43.variants.general_exponent`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_43.variants.general_exponent_lt_half :
    ∀ α : ℝ, 0 < α → α < 1 / 2 → SievedLowerBoundExp α

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 44
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Ben Green's 100 Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.44)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul. "A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory."
  Annals of Discrete Mathematics 6 (1980): 89-115.

statements.name: Green44.green_44
statements.doc:
Sieve $[N]$ by removing half the residue classes mod $p_i$, for primes
$2 \leqslant p_1 < p_2 < \dots < p_{1000} < N^{9/10}$. Does the remaining set have size at most
$\frac{1}{10} N$?

We interpret "half the residue classes" as $\lfloor p_i / 2 \rfloor$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_44 :
    ∀ (N : ℕ) (p : Fin 1000 → ℕ) (A : (i : Fin 1000) → Finset (ZMod (p i))),
      let remaining := (Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (fun x => ∀ i, (x : ZMod (p i)) ∉ A i)
      (∀ i, (p i).Prime) →
      StrictMono p →
      (p 999) ^ 10 < N ^ 9 →
      (∀ i, (A i).card = (p i) / 2) →
      10 * remaining.card ≤ N

statements.name: Green44.green_44.variants.less_than_sqrt
statements.doc: The answer is affirmative if the primes are all less than $N^{1/2}$, by the large sieve. [Gr24]
statements.statement:
theorem green_44.variants.less_than_sqrt :
    ∀ (N : ℕ) (p : Fin 1000 → ℕ) (A : (i : Fin 1000) → Finset (ZMod (p i))),
      let remaining := (Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (fun x => ∀ i, (x : ZMod (p i)) ∉ A i)
      (∀ i, (p i).Prime) →
      StrictMono p →
      (p 999) ^ 2 < N →
      (∀ i, (A i).card = (p i) / 2) →
      10 * remaining.card ≤ N

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 45
problems.doc:
Can we pick residue classes $a_p \pmod{p}$, one for each prime $p \leq N$,
such that every integer $\leq N$ lies in at least 10 of them?

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 45](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.45)
- [erdosproblems.com/689](https://www.erdosproblems.com/689)

The version of this problem with $10$ replaced by $2$ is `Erdos689.erdos_689` in
`FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«689»`.

statements.name: Green45.green_45
statements.doc:
Can we pick residue classes $a_p \pmod{p}$, one for each prime $p \leq N$, such that every
integer $\leq N$ lies in at least $10$ of them?

Erdős remarks that he does not know how to answer it with $10$ replaced by $2$;
this is `Erdos689.erdos_689`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_45 :
    ∀ᶠ N in .atTop, ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N,
      10 ≤ (Finset.Icc 1 N |>.filter fun p => p.Prime ∧ a p ≡ m [MOD p]).card

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 46
problems.doc:
What is the largest $y$ for which one may cover the interval $[y]$ by residue classes $a_p \pmod{p}$, one for each prime $p \leq x$?

*References:*
- [Gr24] [Ben Green's Open Problem 46](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.46)
- [FGK18] Ford, K., Green, B., Konyagin, S., Maynard, J., & Tao, T. (2018). Long gaps between primes.
  Journal of the American Mathematical Society, 31(1), 65-105.
- [Iw78] Iwaniec, Henryk. "On the problem of Jacobsthal." Demonstratio Mathematica 11.1 (1978): 225-232.
- [OAI26a] OpenAI, *A quadratic bound for Jacobsthal's function*. OpenAI Math Release preprint
  (2026).
  https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/A-quadratic-bound-for-Jacobsthals-function-September-25-2026/paper.pdf
- [Ra38] Rankin, R. A., *The difference between consecutive prime numbers*. J. London Math. Soc.
  (1938), 242--247.

This is the same problem as Erdős Problem 687.

statements.name: Green46.green_46.improve_lower
statements.doc: We conjecture that the best-known lower bound can be improved.
statements.statement:
theorem green_46.improve_lower :
    (bestLower =o[atTop] green_46.improve_lower.answer) ∧ (green_46.improve_lower.answer ≪ maxY)

statements.name: Green46.green_46.improve_upper
statements.doc:
We conjecture that the best-known upper bound can be improved.

Yes. OpenAI [OAI26a] proved $h(k) \ll k^2 / (\log\log 3k)^2$ for Jacobsthal's function $h$
(Erdős Problem 970). By the Chinese remainder theorem $\mathrm{maxY}(x) < h(\pi(x))$, which gives
$\mathrm{maxY}(x) \ll (x+1)^2 / (\log\log 3(x+1))^2 = o(x^2)$. Whether $y \ll x^{1+o(1)}$ remains
open, see `green_46.improve_upper_conjectured`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_46.improve_upper :
    (green_46.improve_upper.answer =o[atTop] bestUpper) ∧ (maxY ≪ green_46.improve_upper.answer)

statements.name: Green46.green_46.improve_upper_conjectured
statements.doc: It seems very likely that we must have $y \ll x^{1+o(1)}$ [Gr24].
statements.statement:
theorem green_46.improve_upper_conjectured :
    ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, (o =o[atTop] fun _ : ℕ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧
      maxY ≪ fun x ↦ (x : ℝ) ^ (1 + o x)

statements.name: Green46.green_46.variants.lower
statements.doc: Best known lower bound: $y \gg x \frac{\log x \log \log \log x}{\log \log x}$ [FGK18].
statements.statement:
theorem green_46.variants.lower :
    bestLower ≪ maxY

statements.name: Green46.green_46.variants.upper
statements.doc: Best known upper bound: $y \ll x^2$ [Iw78].
statements.statement:
theorem green_46.variants.upper :
    maxY ≪ bestUpper

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 47
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Ben Green's 100 Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.47)
- [GH14] Green, Ben, and Adam J. Harper. "Inverse questions for the large sieve."
  Geometric and Functional Analysis 24.4 (2014): 1167-1203.
- [HV09] Helfgott, Harald Andrés, and Akshay Venkatesh. "How small must ill-distributed sets be."
  Analytic number theory 2 (2009): 224-234.
- [Wa12] Walsh, Miguel N. "The inverse sieve problem in high dimensions." (2012): 2001-2022.
- [Wa14] Walsh, Miguel N. "The algebraicity of ill-distributed sets."
  Geometric and Functional Analysis 24.3 (2014): 959-967.

statements.name: Green47.green_47
statements.doc:
Suppose that a large sieve process leaves a set of quadratic size. Is that set quadratic?

The following very particular instance is probably the simplest [Gr24]:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ is a set with the property that
$|A \pmod p| \leqslant \frac{1}{2}(p + 1)$ for all sufficiently large $p$.
Is it true that either $|A \cap [X]| \ll X^{1/2} / \log^{100} X$, or $A$ is contained in the
image of $\mathbb{Z}$ under a quadratic map $\phi : \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}$?
statements.statement:
theorem green_47 :
    ¬ ∀ A : Set ℕ,
      (∀ᶠ p in atTop, Nat.Prime p → Set.ncard (Set.image (fun a : ℕ => (a : ZMod p)) A) ≤ (p + 1) / 2) →
      ((fun X : ℕ => ((A ∩ Set.Iic X).ncard : ℝ)) ≪ (fun X : ℕ => Real.sqrt (X : ℝ) / (Real.log (X : ℝ)) ^ 100))
      ∨ (∃ P : Polynomial ℚ, P.degree = 2 ∧ ∀ a ∈ A, ∃ z : ℤ, (a : ℚ) = P.eval (z : ℚ))

statements.name: Green47.green_47.variants.finite_exceptions
statements.doc:
In Green and Harper's formulation [GH14, Conjecture 1.7], the quadratic containment
is allowed to fail on a finite subset of $A$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_47.variants.finite_exceptions :
    ∀ A : Set ℕ,
      (∀ᶠ p in atTop, Nat.Prime p → Set.ncard (Set.image (fun a : ℕ => (a : ZMod p)) A) ≤ (p + 1) / 2) →
      ((fun X : ℕ => ((A ∩ Set.Iic X).ncard : ℝ)) ≪ (fun X : ℕ => Real.sqrt (X : ℝ) / (Real.log (X : ℝ)) ^ 100))
      ∨ (∃ P : Polynomial ℚ, P.degree = 2 ∧ {a ∈ A | ¬∃ z : ℤ, (a : ℚ) = P.eval (z : ℚ)}.Finite)

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 49
problems.doc:
Also known as the *Marton's conjecture* or the *Polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture (PFR)*.

*References:*
- [Gr24] [Ben Green's 100 Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.49)
- [Aa19] Aaronson, James. "A counterexample to a strong variant of the Polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture." arXiv preprint arXiv:1902.00353 (2019).
- [Fa00] I. Farah, Approximate homomorphisms. II. Group homomorphisms, Combinatorica 20 (2000), no. 1, 47–60.
- [GGM25] W. T. Gowers, B. J. Green, F. Manners and T. C. Tao, On a conjecture of Marton, Ann. of Math. (2) 201 (2025), no. 2, 515–549.
- [Gr05] B. J. Green, Finite field models in additive combinatorics, Surveys in combinatorics 2005, 1–27, London Math. Soc. Lecture Note Ser., 327, Cambridge Univ. Press, Cambridge, 2005.
- [GrTa10] B. J. Green and T. C. Tao An equivalence between inverse sumset theorems and inverse conjectures for the U3 norm, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 149 (2010), no. 1, 1–19.
- [Lo12] S. Lovett, Equivalence of polynomial conjectures in additive combinatorics, Combinatorica 32 (2012), no. 5, 607–618.
- [LoRe17] S. Lovett and O. Regev, A counterexample to a strong variant of the Polynomial Freiman Ruzsa conjecture in Euclidean space, Discrete Anal.(2017), Paper No. 8, 6 pp.
- [Ma19] F. R. W. M. Manners, Formulations of the PFR conjecture over Z, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 166 (2019), no. 2, 243–245.
- [Sa12] T. Sanders, On the Bogolyubov-Ruzsa lemma, Anal. PDE 5 (2012), no. 3, 627–655.
- [Ta08] T. C. Tao, A counterexample to a strong polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture, blog post November 2008, available at http://tinyurl.com/36j6hyxv.

statements.name: Green49.green_49
statements.doc:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a set with $|A + A| \leq K|A|$. Is it true that $A$
is covered by $K^{O(1)}$ translates of a subspace of size $\leq |A|$?

Solved by [GGM25], with at most $2K^{12}$ translates. The factor $2$ cannot be omitted: for
$A = \mathbb{F}_2^n \setminus \{0\}$ one has $K = 2^n / (2^n - 1)$, so $K^C \to 1$ as
$n \to \infty$, while every subspace of size at most $|A|$ is proper and two translates are needed.
statements.statement:
theorem green_49 :
    ∃ C > 0,
      ∀ n (A : Finset (𝔽₂ n)), A.Nonempty →
      ∀ K ≥ (1 : ℝ), (#(A + A) : ℝ) ≤ K * #A →
        ∃ (W : Submodule (ZMod 2) (𝔽₂ n)) (T : Finset (𝔽₂ n)),
          Nat.card W ≤ #A ∧
          (#T : ℝ) ≤ 2 * K ^ C ∧
          (A : Set (𝔽₂ n)) ⊆ T + W

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 50
problems.doc:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a set of density $\alpha$. Does $10A$ contain a coset
of some subspace of dimension at least $n - O(\log(1/\alpha))$?

Here $kA$ denotes the $k$-fold iterated sumset, i.e., the set of all sums of $k$ elements from $A$
(with repetition allowed). In `Mathlib`, this is denoted `k • A` using pointwise scalar
multiplication on sets.

*Reference:* [Ben Green's Open Problem 50](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.6 Problem 50)

statements.name: Green50.green_50
statements.doc:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ be a set of density $\alpha > 0$. Does $10A$ contain a coset
of some subspace of dimension at least $n - O(\log(1/\alpha))$?

More precisely: does there exist an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that for all $n \geq 1$ and all
nonempty $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with density $\alpha > 0$, the sumset $10A$ contains a coset
of some subspace of dimension at least $n - C \log_2(1/\alpha)$?

The sumset $10A$ is defined as $\{a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{10} : a_i \in A\}$, using the pointwise
scalar multiplication notation `10 • A` where `•` denotes the iterated addition of a set.

Note: We model $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ as `Fin n → ZMod 2`, which is an $n$-dimensional vector space
over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_50 :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset (𝔽₂ n),
    A.Nonempty →
    let α : ℝ := A.dens
    ∃ (W : Submodule (ZMod 2) (𝔽₂ n)) (v : 𝔽₂ n),
      v +ᵥ (W : Set (𝔽₂ n)) ⊆ ↑(10 • A) ∧
      (n : ℝ) - C * Real.logb 2 (1 / α) ≤ Module.finrank (ZMod 2) W

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 51
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.51)
- [Gr13] B. J. Green, Restriction and Kakeya phenomena, notes from a 2003 course.
  Available at http://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/rkp.pdf
- [Sa11] Sanders, Tom. "Green's sumset problem at density one half."
  Acta Arithmetica 146.1 (2011): 91-101.
- [Gr02] Green, Ben. "Arithmetic progressions in sumsets."
  Geometric & Functional Analysis GAFA 12.3 (2002): 584-597.
- [Ruz91] Ruzsa, Imre Z. "Arithmetic progressions in sumsets."
  Acta Arithmetica 60.2 (1991): 191-202.

statements.name: Green51.green_51
statements.doc:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a set of density $\alpha$. What is the largest size of coset
guaranteed to be contained in $2A$?

We phrase this by asking for the exact function $F(\alpha, n)$ giving the maximum dimension
of a guaranteed coset.
statements.statement: theorem green_51 : green_51.answer = guaranteedMaxCosetDim

statements.name: Green51.green_51.lower
statements.doc: It is known that $A + A$ must contain a coset of dimension $\gg_\alpha n$ [Gr13].
statements.statement:
theorem green_51.lower :
    ∀ (α : ℝ), 0 < α → α ≤ 1 →
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, c * (n : ℝ) ≤ guaranteedMaxCosetDim n α

statements.name: Green51.green_51.upper
statements.doc: It is known that $A + A$ need not contain a coset of dimension $n - \sqrt{n}$ [Gr13].
statements.statement:
theorem green_51.upper :
    ∃ α > 0, α ≤ 1 ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, (guaranteedMaxCosetDim n α : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) - sqrt n

statements.name: Green51.green_51.one_half
statements.doc:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ has density $\alpha > 1/2 - C/\sqrt{n}$.
Does $A + A$ contain a subspace of co-dimension $O_C(1)$? [Sa11, Question 5.1]
statements.statement:
theorem green_51.one_half :
    ∀ (k : ℝ), 0 < k →
      ∃ (c : ℕ), ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
        ∀ (α : ℝ), α > (1/2 : ℝ) - k / sqrt (n : ℝ) → α ≤ 1 →
          n ≤ guaranteedMaxCosetDim n α + c

statements.name: Green51.green_51.lower_ap
statements.doc: It is known that $A + A$ must contain an arithmetic progression of length $\sim \exp(c (\log N)^{1/2})$ [Gr02].
statements.statement:
theorem green_51.lower_ap :
    ∀ (α : ℝ), 0 < α → α ≤ 1 →
      ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in atTop,
        exp (c * log (N : ℝ) ^ (1/2 : ℝ)) ≤ guaranteedMaxAPLength N α

statements.name: Green51.green_51.upper_ap
statements.doc:
It is known that $A + A$ need not contain an arithmetic progression of length
$\sim \exp(c (\log N)^{2/3 + \varepsilon})$, for any $\varepsilon > 0$ [Ruz91].
statements.statement:
theorem green_51.upper_ap :
    ∀ (α : ℝ), 0 < α → α < 1/2 → ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
      ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in atTop,
        guaranteedMaxAPLength N α ≤ exp (c * log (N : ℝ) ^ (2/3 + ε : ℝ))

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 52
problems.doc: *Reference:* [Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.52)

statements.name: Green52.green_52
statements.doc:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a set with an additive complement of size $K$.
Does $2A$ contain a coset of codimension $O_K(1)$?
statements.statement:
theorem green_52 :
    ∃ (c : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ (n K : ℕ) (A : Set (𝔽₂ n)) (S : Finset (𝔽₂ n)),
      S.card = K → A + (S : Set (𝔽₂ n)) = Set.univ →
      ∃ (V : AffineSubspace (ZMod 2) (𝔽₂ n)), (V : Set (𝔽₂ n)) ⊆ A + A ∧
        n ≤ Module.finrank (ZMod 2) V.direction + c K

statements.name: Green52.green_52_log
statements.doc:
Could $2A$ even contain a coset of codimension $O(\log K)$?

From [Green's 2025 update](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.52):

> Update 2025. Kaave Hosseini and Ryan Alweiss have independently pointed out
> that the second question is far too optimistic. To see this, let $A$ be a Hamming ball
> of radius $n/2 - \sqrt{n}$. There is a set $S$ of size $O(n)$ such that
> $A + S = \mathbb{F}_2^n$; a random choice of $S$ will work. However, every subspace
> contained in $A - A$ has codimension $\gg \sqrt{n}$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_52_log :
    ¬ ∃ (C D : ℝ), ∀ (n K : ℕ) (A : Set (𝔽₂ n)) (S : Finset (𝔽₂ n)),
      0 < K → S.card = K → A + (S : Set (𝔽₂ n)) = Set.univ →
      ∃ (V : AffineSubspace (ZMod 2) (𝔽₂ n)), (V : Set (𝔽₂ n)) ⊆ A + A ∧
        (n : ℝ) ≤ (Module.finrank (ZMod 2) V.direction : ℝ) + C * log (K : ℝ) + D

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 53
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.53)

statements.name: Green53.green_53
statements.doc:
Suppose that $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is partitioned in to sets $A_1, ..., A_K$.
Does $2A_i$ contain a coset of codimension $O_K(1)$ for some $i$?
statements.statement:
theorem green_53 :
    ∃ (c : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ (n K : ℕ) (A : Fin K → Set (𝔽₂ n)),
      (⋃ i, A i) = Set.univ →
      Pairwise (Disjoint on A) →
      ∃ (i : Fin K) (S : AffineSubspace (ZMod 2) (𝔽₂ n)),
        (S : Set (𝔽₂ n)) ⊆ A i + A i ∧
        n ≤ Module.finrank (ZMod 2) S.direction + c K

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 54
problems.doc:
*References:*

- [Ben Green's Open Problem 54](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.54)
- Original formulation: M. Talagrand, *Are All Sets of Positive Measure Essentially Convex?*, in Operator Theory:
Advances and Applications, 77, 1995 Birkhäuser Verlag Basel/Switzerland.
- [Hua–Song–Tudose, *On Talagrand's convexity conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10908) (2026)
- [M. Talagrand, *Some open problems*](https://michel.talagrand.net/Korea15.pdf), §2

Here $nK = K + \cdots + K$ ($n$ times) is the $n$-fold sumset of $K$, written `n • K` for `n : ℕ`
with `open scoped Pointwise`.

statements.name: Green54.green_54
statements.doc:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ be a balanced compact set (that is, $\lambda K \subseteq K$
whenever $|\lambda| \leq 1$) and suppose that the normalised Gaussian measure
$\gamma_\infty(K) \geq 0.99$. Does the sumset $10K = K + \cdots + K$ ($10$ times) contain a compact
convex set $C$ with $\gamma_\infty(C) \geq 0.01$?

The answer is yes: Hua, Song and Tudose proved that if $\gamma_n(A) > 5/6$ then $3(A + A + A)$
contains a symmetric convex body $C$ with $\gamma_n(C) \geq 1/4$, uniformly in $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_54 :
    ∀ K : Set (ℕ → ℝ), IsCompact K → Balanced ℝ K → (0.99 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤
    gaussianMeasureInf K → ∃ C : Set (ℕ → ℝ), IsCompact C ∧ Convex ℝ C ∧ C ⊆ (10 : ℕ) • K ∧
    (0.01 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ gaussianMeasureInf C

statements.name: Green54.green_54_known_case
statements.doc: The same statement is known to be false for the sumset $2K = K + K$ instead of $10K$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_54_known_case : ¬ (∀ K : Set (ℕ → ℝ), IsCompact K → Balanced ℝ K → (0.99 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤
    gaussianMeasureInf K → ∃ C : Set (ℕ → ℝ), IsCompact C ∧ Convex ℝ C ∧ C ⊆ K + K ∧
    (0.01 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ gaussianMeasureInf C)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 57
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [Ben Green's Open Problem 57](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8)

Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. Consider the space $\Phi(G)$ of all functions on $G$ which
are "convex combinations" (in the sense of complex coefficients $c_i$ with
$\sum |c_i| \le 1$) of functions of the form
$$\phi(g) := \mathbb{E}_{x_1 + x_2 + x_3 = g} f_1(x_2, x_3) f_2(x_1, x_3) f_3(x_1, x_2)$$
with $\|f_i\|_\infty \le 1$ (where $f_i : G \times G \to \mathbb{C}$).

Let $\Phi'(G)$ be the space defined similarly, but with $f_3(x_1, x_2)$ required to be
a function of $x_1 + x_2$. Do $\Phi(G)$ and $\Phi'(G)$ coincide?

**Note:** The "convex combination" here uses complex coefficients whose absolute values sum to
at most 1 (cf. personal communication with B. Green, April 2026). Since the base sets are
balanced (closed under multiplication by unit complex numbers), this absolutely convex hull
equals the real convex hull of the complex-valued base set.

**Motivation:** $\Phi(G)$ is a 'generalised convolution algebra' as considered by
Conlon–Fox–Zhao, whereas $\Phi'(G)$ consists of Tao's $\text{UAP}_2(G)$-functions.

statements.name: Green57.green_57.variants.z3_functional
statements.doc:
For $G = \mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}$ and the functional $a(0) = -1$, $a(1) = -3$, $a(2) = 3$,
does the support function of $\Phi$ at $a$ strictly exceed that of $\Phi'$?

Numerical evidence suggests the answer is **yes**:
$$\sup_{\varphi \in \Phi'(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})} \operatorname{Re}\langle a, \varphi \rangle
  \;<\; \sup_{\varphi \in \Phi(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})} \operatorname{Re}\langle a, \varphi \rangle.$$

The DeepMind prover agent provided a formal proof, showing that $\frac{183095}{30000}$ separates the
support functions.
statements.statement:
theorem green_57.variants.z3_functional :
    let a : ZMod 3 → ℂ := ![(-1 : ℂ), -3, 3]
    supportFn (ZMod 3) a (Φ' (ZMod 3)) < supportFn (ZMod 3) a (Φ (ZMod 3))

statements.name: Green57.green_57.variants.z3
statements.doc:
Do $\Phi(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})$ and $\Phi'(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})$ coincide?

Numerical evidence suggests the answer is **no**: the integer functional $a = (-1, -3, 3)$
separates the two spaces. A branch-and-bound verification over the phase variables shows
$\max_{\Phi'} \operatorname{Re}\langle a, \varphi \rangle < 6.112 < 6.115 \approx
\max_{\Phi} \operatorname{Re}\langle a, \varphi \rangle$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_57.variants.z3 :
    ¬ (Φ (ZMod 3) = Φ' (ZMod 3))

statements.name: Green57.green_57
statements.doc:
Is it true that for every finite abelian group $G$ the spaces $\Phi(G)$ and $\Phi'(G)$,
obtained from kernels $\phi(g) = \mathbb{E}_{x_1 + x_2 + x_3 = g} f_1(x_2, x_3)
      f_2(x_1, x_3) f_3(x_1, x_2)$ with $\lVert f_i \rVert_\infty \le 1$
(where $f_i : G \times G \to \mathbb{C}$), still coincide when the
third kernel is required to depend only on $x_1 + x_2$?

Green guesses that the answer is probably 'no'.
statements.statement:
theorem green_57 :
    ¬ ∀ (G : Type) [AddCommGroup G] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G],
      Φ G = Φ' G

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 58
problems.doc: *Reference:* [Ben Green's Open Problem 58](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8 Problem 58)

statements.name: Green58.green_58
statements.doc:
Suppose $A, B ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ both have size at least $N^{0.49}$. Must the sumset $A + B$
contain a composite number?
statements.statement:
theorem green_58 :
    ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∀ᵉ (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N) (B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N),
      (N : ℝ) ^ (0.49 : ℝ) ≤ (A.card : ℝ) →
      (N : ℝ) ^ (0.49 : ℝ) ≤ (B.card : ℝ) →
      ∃ m ∈ (A + B), m.Composite

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 60
problems.doc: *Reference:* [Ben Green's Open Problem 60](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8 Problem 60)

statements.name: Green60.green_60
statements.doc:
Is there an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that, whenever $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ is a set of squares
with $|A| ≥ 2$, the sumset $A + A$ satisfies $|A + A| ≥ |A|^{1 + c}$?
statements.statement:
theorem green_60 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ),
      ∀ (A : Finset ℕ),
        (∀ a ∈ A, IsSquare a) →
        2 ≤ A.card →
          ((A + A).card : ℝ) ≥ (A.card : ℝ) ^ (1 + c)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 61
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [Ben Green's Open Problem 61](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8 Problem 61)

This problem was originally considered by Erdős and Newman.

statements.name: Green61.green_61
statements.doc:
Suppose that $A + A$ contains the first $n$ squares. Is $|A| \geq n^{1 - o(1)}$?

It is known that necessarily $|A| \geq n^{2/3 - o(1)}$, whilst in the other direction there do
exist such $A$ with $|A| \ll_C n / \log^C n$ for any $C$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_61 :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto f atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 1 → ∀ (A : Finset ℕ),
        (Finset.Icc 1 n).image (· ^ 2) ⊆ A + A →
          (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - f n) ≤ A.card

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 62
problems.doc:
Let $p$ be a large prime, and let $A$ be the set of all primes less than $p$.
Is every $x \in \{1, \ldots, p-1\}$ congruent to some product $a_1 a_2$ where $a_1, a_2 \in A$?

This is a problem of Erdős, Odlyzko, and Sárközy [105] from 1987.

*Reference:* [Ben Green's Open Problem 62](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.62)

statements.name: Green62.green_62
statements.doc:
Let $p$ be a large prime, and let $A$ be the set of all primes less than $p$.
Is every $x \in \{1, \ldots, p-1\}$ congruent to some product $a_1 a_2$ where $a_1, a_2 \in A$?
statements.statement:
theorem green_62 :
    ∀ᶠ p in atTop, p.Prime →
      let A := (Finset.range p).filter Nat.Prime
      ∀ x : ℕ, 1 ≤ x ∧ x < p →
        ∃ a₁ ∈ A, ∃ a₂ ∈ A, (x : ZMod p) = (a₁ * a₂ : ZMod p)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 63
problems.doc:
Let $A$ be the smallest set containing $2$ and $3$ and such that $a_1a_2 - 1 \in A$
if $a_1, a_2 \in A$. Does $A$ have positive density?

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 63](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8)
- [erdosproblems.com/424](https://www.erdosproblems.com/424)

This file points to the canonical formalization in `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«424»`.

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 64
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [Ben Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.64)

Do there exist infinitely many primes $p$ for which $p - 2$ has an odd number of prime factors,
counted with multiplicity?

statements.name: Green64.green_64
statements.doc:
Do there exist infinitely many primes $p$ for which $p - 2$ has an odd number of prime factors,
counted with multiplicity (i.e. $\Omega(p - 2)$ is odd)?
statements.statement:
theorem green_64 :
    {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ Odd (Ω (p - 2))}.Infinite

statements.name: Green64.green_64.variants.p_sub_one
statements.doc:
The same question as `green_64` but with $p - 1$ instead of $p - 2$.
Green notes this is "probably more natural".
statements.statement:
theorem green_64.variants.p_sub_one :
    {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ Odd (Ω (p - 1))}.Infinite

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 65
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr26] [Ben Green's Open Problem 65](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.65)
- [Gr22] [Green, Ben. "On Sárközy's theorem for shifted primes."](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.08001)

statements.name: Green65.green_65
statements.doc:
Is there $c > 0$ such that every sufficiently large subset $A \subseteq [N]$ of size at least
$N^{1-c}$ has a difference that is a nonzero square?
statements.statement:
theorem green_65 :
    LargeDifferencePattern IsNonzeroSquare

statements.name: Green65.green_65.variants.prime_minus_one
statements.doc:
Green asks the analogous question with a nonzero square replaced by $p - 1$ for a prime $p$.
Green [Gr22, Theorem 1.1] solved this positively.
statements.statement:
theorem green_65.variants.prime_minus_one :
    LargeDifferencePattern IsPrimeMinusOne

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 66
problems.doc: *Reference:* [Ben Green's Open Problem 66](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8)

statements.name: Green66.green_66
statements.doc:
Is there always a sum of two squares between $X - \frac{1}{10}X^{1/4}$ and $X$?
We formalize this as an eventual statement for sufficiently large real $X$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_66 :
    ∀ᶠ X : ℝ in atTop,
      ∃ n : ℕ, IsSumOfTwoSquares n ∧
        (n : ℝ) ∈ Set.Icc (X - (1 / 10 : ℝ) * X ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ)) X

statements.name: Green66.green_66.variants.trivial_bound
statements.doc: Green notes that a well-known, almost trivial argument gives an $O(X^{1/4})$ bound on the left.
statements.statement:
theorem green_66.variants.trivial_bound :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ X : ℝ in atTop,
      ∃ n : ℕ, IsSumOfTwoSquares n ∧
        (n : ℝ) ∈ Set.Icc (X - C * X ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ)) X

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 68
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.68)
- [Gr14] Green, B., *Approximate algebraic structure*. Proceedings of the ICM 2014, Vol. I,
  Kyung Moon Sa, Seoul (2014), 341--367. [arXiv:1404.0093](https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.0093)
- [Vo90] Voloch, J. F., *Arcs in projective planes over prime fields*. J. Geom. 38 (1990),
  198--200.
- [BaLa19] Ball, S. and Lavrauw, M., *Arcs in finite projective spaces*. EMS Surv. Math. Sci. 6
  (2019), 133--172. [arXiv:1908.10772](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10772)

statements.name: Green68.green_68
statements.doc:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_p^2$ is a set meeting every line in at most 2 points. Is it true
that all except $o(p)$ points of $A$ lie on a cubic curve?

Such sets are called arcs. We read "cubic curve" as the zero set of a nonzero polynomial of total
degree at most $3$ in two variables over $\mathbb{F}_p$. This includes conics and lines, and unions
of these. The $o(p)$ is uniform in $A$: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and every large prime $p$, every
arc $A$ has all but at most $\varepsilon p$ of its points on one such curve. Green asked a
projective form of this question in [Gr14, Section 4.4]. [Gr24] notes that the question is more
natural in projective space, and that the analogue over $\mathbb{F}_q$ with $q = p^2$ is false,
because of Hermitian quadrics.
statements.statement:
theorem green_68 :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ p₀ : ℕ, ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], p₀ ≤ p →
      ∀ A : Finset (Fin 2 → ZMod p), MeetsLinesInAtMost 2 A →
        ∃ F : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) (ZMod p), F ≠ 0 ∧ F.totalDegree ≤ 3 ∧
          (numOffCurve F A : ℝ) ≤ ε * p

statements.name: Green68.green_68.variants.voloch
statements.doc:
**Voloch's theorem.** If $p$ is an odd prime and $A \subset \mathbb{F}_p^2$ is a set meeting every
line in at most 2 points, with $|A| > \frac{44}{45} p + \frac{8}{9}$, then $A$ lies on a conic
[BaLa19, Theorem 52], due to Voloch [Vo90]. This is the affine form of the theorem for planar arcs
in $\mathrm{PG}(2, p)$: a set of affine points is an arc in $\mathrm{PG}(2, p)$ if and only if it
meets every affine line in at most 2 points, and the affine equation $Q(x, y, 1) = 0$ of a conic
$Q = 0$ through $A$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most $2$ vanishing on $A$. We assume $p$
odd, as in [BaLa19, Section 15.3].
statements.statement:
theorem green_68.variants.voloch :
    ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], p ≠ 2 →
      ∀ A : Finset (Fin 2 → ZMod p), MeetsLinesInAtMost 2 A →
        (44 : ℝ) / 45 * p + 8 / 9 < A.card →
          ∃ F : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) (ZMod p),
            F ≠ 0 ∧ F.totalDegree ≤ 2 ∧ ∀ a ∈ A, MvPolynomial.eval a F = 0

statements.name: Green68.green_68.variants.bounded_intersection
statements.doc:
More generally than in `green_68`, one may conjecture that if $A \subset \mathbb{F}_p^2$ meets
every line in $O(1)$ points, then all but $o(p)$ points of $A$ lie on a curve of degree $O(1)$
[Gr24]. We read this as: for every $k$ there is a degree bound $d$ such that, for every
$\varepsilon > 0$ and every large prime $p$, every set meeting each line in at most $k$ points has
all but at most $\varepsilon p$ points on the zero set of a nonzero polynomial of total degree at
most $d$. The degree $d$ depends on $k$, not on $p$ or $\varepsilon$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_68.variants.bounded_intersection :
    ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ d : ℕ, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ p₀ : ℕ, ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], p₀ ≤ p →
      ∀ A : Finset (Fin 2 → ZMod p), MeetsLinesInAtMost k A →
        ∃ F : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) (ZMod p), F ≠ 0 ∧ F.totalDegree ≤ d ∧
          (numOffCurve F A : ℝ) ≤ ε * p

statements.name: Green68.green_68.variants.f_four_little_o
statements.doc:
Denote by $f_d(p)$ the size of the largest no-three-in-a-line set in $\mathbb{F}_p^d$. Is
$f_4(p) = o(p^3)$?

[Gr24] reports that $f_2(p) \sim p$ and $f_3(p) \sim p^2$, and that the best known upper bound is
$f_4(p) \le (1 - c)p^3$ for a constant $c > 0$, due to Nagy and Szőnyi, a slight improvement of
the trivial bound.
statements.statement:
theorem green_68.variants.f_four_little_o :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ p₀ : ℕ, ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], p₀ ≤ p →
      (maxNoThreeCollinear 4 p : ℝ) ≤ ε * (p : ℝ) ^ 3

statements.name: Green68.green_68.variants.f_four_polynomial
statements.doc:
Is $f_4(p) = O(p^{2+o(1)})$, where $f_d(p)$ is the size of the largest no-three-in-a-line set in
$\mathbb{F}_p^d$? We read $O(p^{2+o(1)})$ as: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $C$ with
$f_4(p) \le C p^{2+\varepsilon}$ for all primes $p$. This is stronger than
`green_68.variants.f_four_little_o`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_68.variants.f_four_polynomial :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime],
      (maxNoThreeCollinear 4 p : ℝ) ≤ C * (p : ℝ) ^ (2 + ε)

statements.name: Green68.green_68.variants.blocking_set
statements.doc:
Let $\mathrm{PG}(2, q)$ be the projective plane over $\mathbb{F}_q$. Is there a set $B \subset
\mathrm{PG}(2, q)$ (a "blocking set") meeting every line in at least 1, but at most 1000, points?

A question of this kind goes back to Erdős (see [Gr24]). For $q$ not prime such sets exist in many
cases [Gr24]. As $q$ ranges over sufficiently large primes, it is speculated that no such set
exists [Gr24]. We state this speculation. Points of $\mathrm{PG}(2, p)$ are the one-dimensional
subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_p^3$ (`Projectivization`), and lines are the two-dimensional subspaces.
statements.statement:
theorem green_68.variants.blocking_set :
    ∃ p₀ : ℕ, ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], p₀ ≤ p →
      ¬ ∃ B : Set (Projectivization (ZMod p) (Fin 3 → ZMod p)),
        ∀ W : Submodule (ZMod p) (Fin 3 → ZMod p), Module.finrank (ZMod p) W = 2 →
          1 ≤ Set.ncard {x ∈ B | x.submodule ≤ W} ∧ Set.ncard {x ∈ B | x.submodule ≤ W} ≤ 1000

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 70
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.70)
- [ABBCDHKLPW11] Abel, Z., Ballinger, B., Bose, P., Collette, S., Dujmović, V., Hurtado, F.,
  Kominers, S. D., Langerman, S., Pór, A. and Wood, D. R., *Every large point set contains many
  collinear points or an empty pentagon*. Graphs Combin. 27 (2011), 47-60.
  [arXiv:0904.0262](https://arxiv.org/abs/0904.0262)
- [KPW05] Kára, J., Pór, A. and Wood, D. R., *On the chromatic number of the visibility graph of
  a set of points in the plane*. Discrete Comput. Geom. 34 (2005), 497-506.
  [doi:10.1007/s00454-005-1177-z](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-005-1177-z)
- [PoWo10] Pór, A. and Wood, D. R., *On visibility and blockers*. J. Comput. Geom. 1 (2010),
  29-40. [arXiv:0912.1150](https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.1150)

statements.name: Green70.green_70
statements.doc:
Fix integers $k, \ell$. Is it true that, given a set of $n \geq n_0(k, \ell)$ points in
$\mathbb{R}^2$, either some $k$ of them lie on a line, or some $\ell$ of them are 'mutually
visible', that is to say that line segment joining them contains no other point from the set?

This question was first raised by Kára, Pór and Wood [KPW05]. It is called the big-line-big-clique
conjecture [PoWo10, Conjecture 1]. We read "mutually visible" as "pairwise visible". The cases
$k \leq 3$ are trivial: a set with no three collinear points has all pairs visible. For the
cases $\ell \leq 5$, see `green_70.variants.five_visible`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_70 :
    ∀ k ℓ : ℕ, ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ P : Finset (ℝ × ℝ),
      n₀ ≤ #P → HasCollinear k P ∨ HasMutuallyVisible ℓ P

statements.name: Green70.green_70.variants.five_visible
statements.doc:
The answer to `green_70` is yes for $\ell \leq 5$ [Gr24]: for every $k$, every sufficiently large
planar set contains $k$ collinear points or $5$ mutually visible points. The case $\ell = 5$ is
[ABBCDHKLPW11, Theorem 5], and it implies the cases $\ell \leq 4$ (see
`HasMutuallyVisible.mono`). According to [ABBCDHKLPW11, Section 1.4], the case $\ell = 4$ was
proved in [KPW05]. In [ABBCDHKLPW11] and [PoWo10] the letters $k$ and $\ell$ are interchanged.
statements.statement:
theorem green_70.variants.five_visible :
    ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ P : Finset (ℝ × ℝ),
      n₀ ≤ #P → HasCollinear k P ∨ HasMutuallyVisible 5 P

statements.name: Green70.green_70.variants.empty_pentagon
statements.doc:
Generalised empty pentagon theorem [ABBCDHKLPW11, Theorem 3]: for every integer $k \geq 2$,
every sufficiently large finite set of points in the plane contains $k$ collinear points or an
empty pentagon. By `HasEmptyPentagon.hasMutuallyVisible`, this implies
`green_70.variants.five_visible`, which is [ABBCDHKLPW11, Theorem 5].
statements.statement:
theorem green_70.variants.empty_pentagon :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ P : Finset (ℝ × ℝ),
      n₀ ≤ #P → HasCollinear k P ∨ HasEmptyPentagon P

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 72
problems.doc:
More commonly known as the **no-three-in-line problem**.

What is the largest subset of the grid $[N]^2$ with no three points in a line? In particular,
for $N$ sufficiently large, is it impossible to have a set of size $2N$ with this property?

The upper bound $2N$ is the easy half and is `allowedSetSize_le` below, by pigeonhole on the
columns. The open content is whether $2N$ is attained. Green records that it is for $N$ up to
around 50, that $(3/2 + o(1))N$ points are achievable for arbitrary $N$, and that his "personal
suspicion is that this is optimal". The Wikipedia reference points the same way: Guy and Kelly
conjectured $c = \sqrt[3]{2\pi^2/3} \approx 1.874$, and after an error in the heuristic was found
Guy corrected it to $c = \pi/\sqrt3 \approx 1.814$. Both are below $2$, so the expected answer to
the question above is yes.

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 72](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.72)
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No-three-in-line_problem)
- [GK2025] Grebennikov, A. Kwan, M. No $(k + 1)$-in-line problem for large constant $k$.
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.17743

statements.name: Green72.allowedSetSize_le
statements.doc:
By the pigeon hole principle, the size of a subset of an $N \times N$ grid such that no $k$
points lie on a line is bounded by $\leq (k - 1) * N$.
statements.statement:
theorem allowedSetSize_le {k : ℕ} {N : ℕ} :
    AllowedSetSize k N ≤ (k - 1) * N

statements.name: Green72.NoKInLine
statements.doc:
The **no-k-in-line problem**:
For which $k > 2$ does every $N \times N$ grid with $N \geq k$ contain a set of $(k - 1) N$ points
