with no $k$ on a line, so that `AllowedSetSize k N` is the pigeonhole bound $(k - 1) N$?

[GK2025] proves that every $k > 10^{37}$ has this property, which is `no_k_in_line_big` below,
and does not optimise this constant. At $k = 3$ it is the property that Green expects to fail
for large $N$, see `green_72`.
statements.statement: theorem NoKInLine : NoKInLine.answer = {k | 2 < k ∧ ∀ N, k ≤ N → NoKInLineFor k N}

statements.name: Green72.green_72
statements.doc:
**Green's Open Problem 72 / No-three-in-line problem**:
For $N$ sufficiently large, is it impossible to have $2N$ points in $[N]^2$ with no three in a
line? Green suspects the answer is yes, and that $(3/2 + o(1))N$ is optimal.
statements.statement: theorem green_72 : ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, ¬ NoKInLineFor 3 N

statements.name: Green72.green_72.variants.eventually
statements.doc:
Is $2N$ attained for all sufficiently large $N$?

This is not the negation of `green_72`. Negating that one gives $\exists^f N$ where this asks
$\forall^f N$, so both can be answered `False` if the behaviour oscillates. Green asks his
question in the `green_72` form.
statements.statement: theorem green_72.variants.eventually : ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, NoKInLineFor 3 N

statements.name: Green72.no_three_in_line_le
statements.doc: For $N \leq 60$, this has been verified with computers.
statements.statement:
theorem no_three_in_line_le {N : ℕ} (hN : 3 ≤ N) (hN' : N ≤ 60) :
    NoKInLineFor 3 N

statements.name: Green72.no_k_in_line_big
statements.doc:
In [GK2025] Grebennikov and Kwan prove that the pigeonhole bound $(k - 1) N$ is attained
for $k > 10 ^ {37}$ and $N \geq k$.
statements.statement:
theorem no_k_in_line_big {k : ℕ} (N : ℕ) (h : 10 ^ 37 < k) (hN : k ≤ N) :
    NoKInLineFor k N

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 75
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.75)
- [CL25] Conlon, D. and Lim, J., *Everywhere unbalanced configurations*. Adv. Math. 480 (2025),
  Paper No. 110445. [arXiv:2308.02466](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.02466)
- [Pi03] Pinchasi, R., *Lines with many points on both sides*. Discrete Comput. Geom. 30 (2003),
  415-435. [doi:10.1007/s00454-003-2826-8](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-003-2826-8)

statements.name: Green75.green_75
statements.doc:
Let $X \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points. Does there exist a line $\ell$ through at
least two points of $X$ such that the numbers of points on either side of $\ell$ differ by at
most $100$?

This is a form of the Kupitz-Perles conjecture [Gr24]. We take $n \geq 2$, since a line through
two points of $X$ needs two points. If all points of $X$ are collinear, the line through them has
no points on either side.
statements.statement:
theorem green_75 :
    ∀ X : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), 2 ≤ #X → ∃ p ∈ X, ∃ q ∈ X, p ≠ q ∧ imbalance X p q ≤ 100

statements.name: Green75.green_75.variants.exists_constant
statements.doc:
Is there a constant $C$ such that every finite set $X \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with at least two
points has a line through two points of $X$ whose sides differ by at most $C$? This is the
question of Kupitz in the form of [CL25, Section 1], where the constant is not specified.

`green_75` implies it with $C = 100$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_75.variants.exists_constant :
    ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ X : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), 2 ≤ #X →
      ∃ p ∈ X, ∃ q ∈ X, p ≠ q ∧ imbalance X p q ≤ C

statements.name: Green75.green_75.variants.pinchasi
statements.doc:
Pinchasi [Pi03] proved that the answer to `green_75` is yes if $100$ is replaced by
$C \log \log n$ for an absolute constant $C$, where $n = |X|$ [Gr24]. This is the best known bound.
[CL25, Theorem 1.1] states Pinchasi's theorem for generalised configurations (points with
pseudolines); sets of points with lines are a special case. The hypothesis $n \geq 3$ ensures
that $\log \log n > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_75.variants.pinchasi :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ X : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), 3 ≤ #X → ∃ p ∈ X, ∃ q ∈ X, p ≠ q ∧
      (imbalance X p q : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.log (Real.log #X)

statements.name: Green75.green_75.variants.alon
statements.doc:
Kupitz conjectured that one can take the difference to be at most $1$ [CL25, Section 1]. Alon
showed that this is false: there are finite point sets for which, for every line through two of
its points, the numbers of points on the two sides differ by at least $2$ [CL25, Section 1].
[Gr24] phrases this as: the answer to `green_75` is no if $100$ is replaced by $2$. Since the
sets in [CL25] have differences of at least $2$, they show that $100$ cannot be replaced by $1$.
We state the form given in [CL25].
statements.statement:
theorem green_75.variants.alon :
    ∃ X : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), 2 ≤ #X ∧ ∀ p ∈ X, ∀ q ∈ X, p ≠ q → 2 ≤ imbalance X p q

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 76
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.76)
- [AES10] Aronov, Boris, Esther Ezra, and Micha Sharir. "Small-size $\varepsilon$-nets for
  axis-parallel rectangles and boxes." SIAM Journal on Computing 39.7 (2010): 3248-3282.
  [doi:10.1137/090762968](https://doi.org/10.1137/090762968)
- [PT11] Pach, János. "Boxes and the art of $\varepsilon$-net maintenance." Invited problems,
  2nd Emléktábla Workshop (2011), Problem 5 (Pach and Tardos).
  [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~emlektab/emlektabla2withresults.pdf)
- [PT13] Pach, János, and Gábor Tardos. "Tight lower bounds for the size of epsilon-nets."
  Journal of the American Mathematical Society 26.3 (2013): 645-658.
  [doi:10.1090/S0894-0347-2012-00759-0](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0894-0347-2012-00759-0),
  [arXiv:1012.1240](https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.1240)

statements.name: Green76.green_76
statements.doc:
Let $A$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane. Can one select a set $A'$ of $n/2$ points, with the
property that any axis-parallel rectangle containing $1000$ points of $A$ contains at least one
point of $A'$?

We read "a set of $n/2$ points" as at most $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ points, and "containing $1000$
points" as containing at least $1000$ points. The points of $A'$ need not lie in $A$. If
$A' \subseteq A$ is required, then the answer is no; see `green_76.variants.subset`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_76 :
    ∀ A : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), ∃ A', #A' ≤ #A / 2 ∧ HitsRichRectangles 1000 A A'

statements.name: Green76.green_76.variants.exists_constant
statements.doc:
Is there a constant $k$ such that the answer to `green_76` is yes with $1000$ replaced by $k$?
[PT11, Problem 5] asks this in an equivalent form, with $k = C + 1$: is there a constant $C$ such
that every set of $n$ points in the plane has a set $Y$ of $n/2$ points such that every
axis-parallel rectangle disjoint from $Y$ contains at most $C$ of the $n$ points?

Each of `green_76` and `green_76.variants.weak_net` implies this.
statements.statement:
theorem green_76.variants.exists_constant :
    ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), ∃ A', #A' ≤ #A / 2 ∧ HitsRichRectangles k A A'

statements.name: Green76.green_76.variants.weak_net
statements.doc:
Do weak $\varepsilon$-nets of size $O(1/\varepsilon)$ exist for axis-parallel rectangles in the
plane? [Gr24] believes that `green_76` is an instance of this question, which he states for
axis-parallel boxes. With $k = \varepsilon n$: is there a constant $C$ such that, for every
$k \ge 1$, every set $A$ of $n$ points in the plane has a set $A'$ of at most $Cn/k$ points that
meets every axis-parallel rectangle containing at least $k$ points of $A$?

A positive answer implies `green_76.variants.exists_constant`, and it implies `green_76` if the
constant $C$ is at most $500$. [AES10, Theorem 2.2] gives such sets of size
$O(\varepsilon^{-1} \log \log \varepsilon^{-1})$, even with $A' \subseteq A$. When
$A' \subseteq A$ is required, this size is optimal [PT13, Theorem 4].
statements.statement:
theorem green_76.variants.weak_net :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → ∀ A : Finset (ℝ × ℝ),
      ∃ A', #A' ≤ C * #A / k ∧ HitsRichRectangles k A A'

statements.name: Green76.green_76.variants.subset
statements.doc:
If $A'$ is required to be a subset of $A$, then the answer to `green_76` is no, even with $1000$
replaced by any constant. [Gr24] attributes this remark to Alon. It follows from
[PT13, Lemma 4.1], which [Gr24] cites as Lemma 3.1, its number in the arXiv version.
statements.statement:
theorem green_76.variants.subset :
    ¬ ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), ∃ A' ⊆ A, #A' ≤ #A / 2 ∧ HitsRichRectangles k A A'

statements.name: Green76.green_76.variants.subset_log_log
statements.doc:
The answer to `green_76` is yes if $1000$ is replaced by $C \log \log n$ [Gr24]. This follows
from [AES10, Theorem 2.2], which gives $\varepsilon$-nets of size
$O(\varepsilon^{-1} \log \log \varepsilon^{-1})$ for axis-parallel rectangles. These nets are
subsets of $A$. The hypothesis $n \ge 3$ ensures that $\log \log n > 0$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_76.variants.subset_log_log :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ A : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), 3 ≤ #A → ∃ A' ⊆ A,
      #A' ≤ #A / 2 ∧ HitsRichRectangles ⌈C * Real.log (Real.log #A)⌉₊ A A'

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 77
problems.doc:
*Reference:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 77](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.77)

statements.name: Green77.green_77
statements.doc:
Given $n$ points in the unit disc, must there be a triangle of area at most $n^{-2+o(1)}$
determined by them?
statements.statement:
theorem green_77 :
    ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ), Tendsto o atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
      α ≪ fun n ↦ n ^ (-2 + o n)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 81
problems.doc:
Let $A$ be a set of size $n$ integers. Is there some absolute constant $c > 0$ and $\theta$
such that $\sum_{a \in A} \cos(a \theta) \leq - c \sqrt{n}$?

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 81](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.11)
- [erdosproblems.com/510](https://www.erdosproblems.com/510)

This file points to the canonical formalization in `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«510»`.

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 82
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 82](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.82)
- [An improved lower bound for a problem of Littlewood on the zeros of cosine polynomials](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.16075) (Bedert, 2025)
- [Cosine polynomials with few zeros](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.01695) (Juškevičius & Sahasrabudhe, 2020)

statements.name: Green82.green_82
statements.doc:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{Z}$ be a set of size $n$. For how many $\theta \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$
must we have $\sum_{a \in A} \cos(2\pi a\theta) = 0$? The answer is the function `minZeros`.
statements.statement: theorem green_82 : green_82.answer = minZeros

statements.name: Green82.green_82_lower_bound
statements.doc: Lower bound: every set has at least $(\log \log n)^{1-o(1)}$ zeros.
statements.statement:
theorem green_82_lower_bound :
    ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℤ, A.card = n →
        (⌊(Real.log (Real.log n)) ^ (1 - |o n|)⌋₊ : ℕ∞) ≤
        ({θ : ℝ | θ ∈ Ico 0 1 ∧ ∑ a ∈ A, cos (2 * π * a * θ) = 0} : Set ℝ).ncard

statements.name: Green82.green_82_upper_bound
statements.doc: Upper bound: there exists $A$ with at most $C(n \log n)^{2/3}$ zeros.
statements.statement:
theorem green_82_upper_bound :
    ∃ C > 0, ∀ n ≥ 1, ∃ A : Finset ℤ, A.card = n ∧
      ({θ : ℝ | θ ∈ Ico 0 1 ∧ ∑ a ∈ A, cos (2 * π * a * θ) = 0} : Set ℝ).ncard ≤
      (⌊C * (n * Real.log n) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ)⌋₊ : ℕ∞)

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 85
problems.doc:
*Carbery’s rectangle problem*

References:
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.85)
- [CCW99] Carbery, Anthony, Michael Christ, and James Wright. "Multidimensional van der Corput and sublevel set estimates." Journal of the American Mathematical Society 12.4 (1999): 981-1015 Section 6.
- [Ke00] Keleti, Tamás. "Density and covering properties of intervals of ℝn." Mathematika 47.1-2 (2000): 229-242.
- [KKM02] Katz, Nets Hawk, Elliot Krop, and Mauro Maggioni. "Remarks on the box problem." Mathematical Research Letters 9.4 (2002): 515-520.
- [Mu02] Mubayi, Dhruv. "Some exact results and new asymptotics for hypergraph Turán numbers." Combinatorics, Probability and Computing 11.3 (2002): 299-309 Conjecture 1.4.
- [CPZ20] Conlon, David, Cosmin Pohoata, and Dmitriy Zakharov. "Random multilinear maps and the Erd\H {o} s box problem." arXiv preprint arXiv:2011.09024 (2020).

statements.name: Green85.green_85
statements.doc:
Suppose that $A$ is an open subset of $[0, 1]^2$ with measure $\alpha$. Are there four points in
$A$ determining an axis-parallel rectangle with area $\gt c \alpha^2$?
statements.statement:
theorem green_85 :
  ∃ c > 0, ∀ A : Set (ℝ × ℝ),
    IsOpen A →
    A ⊆ Icc 0 1 ×ˢ Icc 0 1 →
    A.Nonempty →
    let α := (volume A).toReal
    ∃ x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂,
      {(x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₁), (x₂, y₂), (x₁, y₂)} ⊆ A ∧
      c * α ^ 2 ≤ |x₁ - x₂| * |y₁ - y₂|

statements.name: Green85.green_85_loose
statements.doc:
From [Gr24] "It is quite easy to show using Cauchy-Schwarz that there must be such a rectangle with
area $\gg \alpha^2 (\log 1/\alpha)^{-1}$."
statements.statement:
theorem green_85_loose :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ α in 𝓝[>] 0,
    ∀ A : Set (ℝ × ℝ),
    IsOpen A →
    A ⊆ Icc 0 1 ×ˢ Icc 0 1 →
    A.Nonempty →
    α = (volume A).toReal →
    ∃ x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂,
      {(x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₁), (x₂, y₂), (x₁, y₂)} ⊆ A ∧
      c * α ^ 2 * (Real.log (1/α))⁻¹ ≤ |x₁ - x₂| * |y₁ - y₂|

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 87
problems.doc:
References:
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.87)
- [BW15] Britnell, John R., and Mark Wildon. "Computing derangement probabilities of the symmetric
  group acting on k-sets." arXiv preprint arXiv:1511.04106 (2015).
- [EFG16] Eberhard, Sean, Kevin Ford, and Ben Green. "Permutations fixing a k-set." International
  Mathematics Research Notices 2016.21 (2016): 6713-6731. arXiv:1507.04465.
- [GS26] Green, Ben, and Mehtaab Sawhney. "The proportion of permutations fixing a k-set."
  arXiv preprint arXiv:2604.28116 (2026).
- [Ve26] Veljjanoski, Daniel. "p(k) for permutations fixing a k-set: values and checks for
  k ≤ 121." https://github.com/veljjanoski/green87-fixing-k-set (2026).

statements.name: Green87.green_87.variants.exists_tendsto
statements.doc:
For every $k$, $i(n, k)$ converges as $n \to \infty$ [BW15, Section 2]; the limit is
$p(k)$ in Green's notation. It is the probability that the random multiset with
$\mathrm{Pois}(1/j)$ parts of size $j$ ($1 \le j \le k$, independent) has a sub-multiset
of total size $k$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_87.variants.exists_tendsto (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto (fun n ↦ i n k) atTop (𝓝 L)

statements.name: Green87.green_87.decreasing
statements.doc:
Let $p(k)$ be the limit, as $n \to \infty$, of the probability that a random permutation of
$[n]$ preserves some set of size $k$. Is $p(k)$ a decreasing function of $k$?

This is a conjecture of Peter Cameron (2010), see [BW15]. The statement is taken in the strict
sense, as in [BW15]: they verified $p(k) > p(k + 1)$ for $k < 30$, and the values computed
numerically in [Ve26] satisfy it for $k < 121$. Note $p(0) = 1$, since the empty set is always
fixed, and $p(1) = 1 - 1/e$. The limit $p$ is quantified inside the statement; it exists and is
unique by `green_87.variants.exists_tendsto`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_87.decreasing :
    ∀ p : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ k, Tendsto (fun n ↦ i n k) atTop (𝓝 (p k))) → StrictAnti p

statements.name: Green87.green_87.variants.order
statements.doc:
$p(k)$ is bounded above and below by constant multiples of $k^{-\delta} (\log k)^{-3/2}$.
[EFG16, Theorem 1.1] proves this for $i(n, k)$ uniformly in $1 \le k \le n/2$ (with
$(1 + \log k)^{-3/2}$); letting $n \to \infty$ gives the statement for $p$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_87.variants.order :
    ∀ p : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ k, Tendsto (fun n ↦ i n k) atTop (𝓝 (p k))) →
      p =Θ[atTop] fun k : ℕ ↦ (k : ℝ) ^ (-δ) * (Real.log k) ^ (-(3 / 2 : ℝ))

statements.name: Green87.green_87.asymptotic
statements.doc:
Is $p(k) = (C + o(1)) k^{-\delta} (\log k)^{-3/2}$ for some absolute constant $C$?

Green and Sawhney [GS26] proved $p(k) = (1 + o(1)) f(\{\log_2 k\}) k^{-\delta} (\log k)^{-3/2}$
for an explicit smooth, positive $f$ on $\mathbb{R} / \mathbb{Z}$ with
$\max f / \min f < 1 + 2 \cdot 10^{-7}$. The question is therefore equivalent to whether $f$ is
constant; they conjecture that it is not, so the expected answer is no, but this has not been
proved.
statements.statement:
theorem green_87.asymptotic :
    ∀ p : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ k, Tendsto (fun n ↦ i n k) atTop (𝓝 (p k))) →
      ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
        p ~[atTop] fun k : ℕ ↦ C * (k : ℝ) ^ (-δ) * (Real.log k) ^ (-(3 / 2 : ℝ))

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 88
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Ben Green's Open Problem
  88](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.88)
- [GoLo21] [The length of an $s$-increasing sequence of
  $r$-tuples](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.08688)
  by W. T. Gowers and J. Long

statements.name: Green88.green_88
statements.doc:
[Gr24, Problem 88]: Is there an absolute constant $\delta > 0$ such that every pairwise
$2$-comparable set $S \subseteq [N]^3$ satisfies $|S| \leq N^{2 - \delta}$?
statements.statement:
theorem green_88 :
    ∃ δ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (N : ℕ) (S : Finset (Fin 3 → Fin N)),
      (S : Set (Fin 3 → Fin N)).Pairwise IsComparable₂ →
        (S.card : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 - δ)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 93
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.93)
- [BrVa19] Breuillard, E. and Varjú, P. P., *Irreducibility of random polynomials of large
  degree*. Acta Math. 223 (2019), 195--249. [arXiv:1810.13360](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.13360)
- [BSKK23] Bary-Soroker, L., Koukoulopoulos, D. and Kozma, G., *Irreducibility of random
  polynomials: general measures*. Invent. Math. 233 (2023), 1041--1120.
  [arXiv:2007.14567](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.14567)
- [Ko99] Konyagin, S. V., *On the number of irreducible polynomials with 0,1 coefficients*.
  Acta Arith. 88 (1999), 333--350.

statements.name: Green93.green_93
statements.doc:
Is a random polynomial with coefficients in $\{0,1\}$ and nonzero constant term almost surely
irreducible?

More precisely, writing $p_n$ for the probability that
$1 + a_1 x + \cdots + a_{n-1} x^{n-1} + x^n$ is irreducible, where the $a_i$ are independent and
take the values $0$ and $1$ with equal probability, does $p_n \to 1$?

The probability $p_n$ is `irreducibleProb 1 n`. The conjecture is due to Odlyzko and Poonen
[BrVa19, Section 1].
statements.statement: theorem green_93 : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ irreducibleProb 1 n) atTop (𝓝 1)

statements.name: Green93.green_93.variants.konyagin
statements.doc:
Konyagin [Ko99] proved that $p_n \ge c / \log n$ for an absolute constant $c > 0$, as stated in
[BrVa19, Section 1]. We state it for all large $n$. It is superseded by
`green_93.variants.bskk_small`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_93.variants.konyagin :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c / Real.log (n : ℝ) ≤ irreducibleProb 1 n

statements.name: Green93.green_93.variants.bskk_small
statements.doc:
Bary-Soroker, Koukoulopoulos and Kozma [BSKK23, Theorem 1(b)] proved that a random monic
polynomial of degree $n$ whose coefficients are uniform on $N$ consecutive integers in $[-H, H]$
with $2 \le N \le 34$, and with nonzero constant term, is irreducible with probability at least
$\delta$. Here $\delta > 0$ is an absolute constant, and $n$ must be at least an absolute constant
and at least $(\log H)^3$. We state it for the integers $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ with
$1 \le M \le 33$, so $N = M + 1$ and $H = M$. The condition on $(\log H)^3$ is absorbed into
$n_0$, because $M$ is bounded. The case $M = 1$ gives $p_n \ge \delta$ for large $n$ for the
polynomial of `green_93`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_93.variants.bskk_small :
    ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ M n : ℕ, 1 ≤ M → M ≤ 33 → n₀ ≤ n →
      δ ≤ irreducibleProb M n

statements.name: Green93.green_93.variants.bskk_large
statements.doc:
Bary-Soroker, Koukoulopoulos and Kozma [BSKK23, Theorem 1(a)] proved that a random monic
polynomial of degree $n$ whose coefficients are uniform on $N \ge 35$ consecutive integers in
$[-H, H]$, with nonzero constant term, is irreducible with probability at least $1 - n^{-c}$.
Here $c > 0$ is an absolute constant, and $n$ must be at least an absolute constant and at least
$(\log H)^3$. We state it for the integers
$\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ with $M \ge 34$, so $N = M + 1 \ge 35$ and $H = M$. In particular
`irreducibleProb M n` $\to 1$ for each such $M$, which is the analogue of `green_93` for
coefficients in $\{0, \dots, M\}$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_93.variants.bskk_large :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ M n : ℕ, 34 ≤ M → n₀ ≤ n → (Real.log (M : ℝ)) ^ 3 ≤ n →
      1 - (n : ℝ) ^ (-c) ≤ irreducibleProb M n

statements.name: Green93.green_93.variants.breuillard_varju
statements.doc:
**Breuillard and Varjú.** Assume the Riemann hypothesis for the Dedekind zeta functions of all
number fields $\mathbb{Q}(a)$ with $a$ a root of a polynomial with coefficients in $\{0, 1\}$
(`ZeroOneRootFieldsRH`). Then $p_n \to 1$ [BrVa19, Theorem 1].
statements.statement:
theorem green_93.variants.breuillard_varju :
    ZeroOneRootFieldsRH → Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ irreducibleProb 1 n) atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 94
problems.doc:
*Reference:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 94](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.94)
- [erdosproblems.com/120](https://www.erdosproblems.com/120)
- [OAI26a] OpenAI, *The dyadic case of the Erdős similarity conjecture*.
  OpenAI Math Release preprint (2026).
  https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/The-dyadic-case-of-the-Erdos-similarity-conjecture-September-25-2026/paper.pdf

statements.name: Green94.green_94_outer_measure
statements.doc:
Let `A ⊂ R` be a set of positive outer measure. Does $A$ contain an affine copy of `{1, 1/2, 1/4, . . . }`?

The answer is "no".
statements.statement:
theorem green_94_outer_measure :
   ¬ ∀ A : Set ℝ,
   volume A > 0 →
   ∃ a b : ℝ, a ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, a * (1 / 2^n) + b ∈ A

statements.name: Green94.green_94
statements.doc:
Let `A ⊂ R` be a set of positive measure. Does $A$ contain an affine copy of `{1, 1/2, 1/4, . . . }`?

The answer is "no": there are compact sets of measure arbitrarily close to $1$ in $[0, 1]$
that contain no affine copy of $\{2^{-n} : n \geq 1\}$. This was proved by an internal OpenAI
model in September 2026 [OAI26a]; see the linked Lean proof.
statements.statement:
theorem green_94 :
   ¬ ∀ A : Set ℝ,
   MeasurableSet A ∧ volume A > 0 →
   ∃ a b : ℝ, a ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, a * (1 / 2^n) + b ∈ A

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 97
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.97)
- [Si23] Simkin, M., *The number of $n$-queens configurations*. Adv. Math. 427 (2023),
  Paper No. 109127. [arXiv:2107.13460](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13460)
- [BoKe21] Bowtell, C. and Keevash, P., *The $n$-queens problem*.
  [arXiv:2109.08083](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.08083) (2021).
- [NAB23] Nobel, P., Agrawal, A. and Boyd, S., *Computing tighter bounds on the $n$-queens
  constant via Newton's method*. Optim. Lett. 17 (2023), 1229--1240.
  [arXiv:2112.03336](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03336)
- [EMM19] Eberhard, S., Manners, F. and Mrazović, R., *Additive triples of bijections, or the
  toroidal semiqueens problem*. J. Eur. Math. Soc. 21 (2019), 441--463.
  [arXiv:1510.05987](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.05987)

statements.name: Green97.green_97
statements.doc:
In how many ways (asymptotically) $Q(n)$ may $n$ non-attacking queens be placed on an
$n \times n$ chessboard?

This is the $n$-queens problem, see [Gr24, Problem 97]. We read "asymptotically" as: find an
explicit function `green_97.answer` with $Q(n) \sim$ `green_97.answer n`. The function
$n \mapsto Q(n)$ itself is not an explicit answer. [Gr24] notes that an asymptotic "rather than
an asymptotic for the log" is open. What is known is $Q(n) = ((1+o(1))\, n e^{-\alpha})^n$ for a
constant $1.94 < \alpha < 1.9449$ [Si23], see `green_97.variants.simkin`.
statements.statement:
theorem green_97 :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (numQueens n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] green_97.answer

statements.name: Green97.green_97.variants.simkin
statements.doc:
**Simkin's theorem.** There is a constant $1.94 < \alpha < 1.9449$ such that
$$\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{Q(n)^{1/n}}{n} = e^{-\alpha},$$
that is, $Q(n) = ((1+o(1))\, n e^{-\alpha})^n$ [Si23, Theorem 1.1]. The constant $\alpha$ is
defined in [Si23] as the solution of a convex optimisation problem over Borel probability measures
on the square $[-1/2, 1/2]^2$. The limit determines $\alpha$ uniquely. Nobel, Agrawal and Boyd
[NAB23] combined Simkin's formulation with a sharper bound of Knuth, solved the resulting convex
problems numerically, and report the tighter range
$\alpha \in [1.944000752, 1.944001082]$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_97.variants.simkin :
    ∃ α : ℝ, 1.94 < α ∧ α < 1.9449 ∧
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (numQueens n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / n) / n) atTop
        (𝓝 (Real.exp (-α)))

statements.name: Green97.green_97.variants.alpha
statements.doc:
Find an explicit value for the constant $\alpha$ of `green_97.variants.simkin`, that is, the
number with $Q(n)^{1/n}/n \to e^{-\alpha}$.

[Gr24] writes that "an explicit solution remains an open problem". The value $\alpha$ is the
solution of an entropy optimisation problem [Si23]. As for `green_97`, an explicit closed form is
intended.
statements.statement:
theorem green_97.variants.alpha :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (numQueens n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / n) / n) atTop
      (𝓝 (Real.exp (-green_97.variants.alpha.answer)))

statements.name: Green97.green_97.variants.bowtell_keevash
statements.doc:
**Bowtell and Keevash.** For $n \equiv 1, 5 \pmod 6$ the number of toroidal $n$-queens
configurations satisfies $T(n) = ((1+o(1))\, n e^{-3})^n$ [BoKe21, Theorem 1.2]. The filter
`toroidalDegrees` restricts to these $n$, because $T(n) = 0$ for all other $n \ge 1$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_97.variants.bowtell_keevash :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (numToroidalQueens n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / n) / n) toroidalDegrees
      (𝓝 (Real.exp (-3)))

statements.name: Green97.green_97.variants.toroidal
statements.doc:
Find an asymptotic for the number $T(n)$ of toroidal $n$-queens configurations, for
$n \equiv 1, 5 \pmod 6$.

[Gr24] writes, after the result of [BoKe21], that the problem of "obtaining an asymptotic (rather
than an asymptotic for the log) remains open". [BoKe21] proved the asymptotic of the logarithm, see
`green_97.variants.bowtell_keevash`. We read "asymptotic" as for `green_97`: an explicit function
is intended.
statements.statement:
theorem green_97.variants.toroidal :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (numToroidalQueens n : ℝ)) ~[toroidalDegrees]
      green_97.variants.toroidal.answer

statements.name: Green97.green_97.variants.eberhard_manners_mrazovic
statements.doc:
**Eberhard, Manners and Mrazović.** For odd $n$, the number $s_n$ of pairs $(\pi_1, \pi_2)$ of
bijections $\{1, \dots, n\} \to \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ with $\pi_1 + \pi_2$ also a bijection is
$$s_n = (e^{-1/2} + o(1))\, \frac{(n!)^3}{n^{n-1}}$$
[EMM19, Theorem 1.2]. [Gr24] refers to this paper for the variant of the toroidal question where
only $\pi_1$, $\pi_2$ and $\pi_1 - \pi_2$ are required to be bijections. Replacing $\pi_2$ by
$-\pi_2$ shows that this variant has the same count $s_n$. For even $n$, $s_n = 0$
[EMM19, Section 1], so the theorem is stated for odd $n$.
statements.statement:
theorem green_97.variants.eberhard_manners_mrazovic :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (numAdditiveTriples n : ℝ)) ~[atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {n : ℕ | Odd n}]
      fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.exp (-(1 / 2)) * ((n ! : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ 3 / (n : ℝ) ^ (n - 1)

problems.title: Hilbert's Fifth Problem and the Hilbert–Smith Conjecture
problems.doc:
The **Hilbert–Smith conjecture** states that a locally compact topological group acting
continuously and faithfully on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold must be a
Lie group. It remains open in general; Pardon proved it for 3-manifolds in 2013.
An equivalent formulation: no p-adic integer group `ℤ_[p]` can act faithfully on any
connected finite-dimensional topological manifold.

## Main statements

- `hilbert_smith_conjecture`: the Hilbert–Smith conjecture.
- `hilbert_smith_padic_formulation`: the equivalent formulation for `ℤ_[p]`.
- `hilbert_smith_conjecture.variants.dimension_three`: Pardon's theorem for 3-manifolds.
- `hilbert_smith_conjecture.variants.riemannian`: the case of isometric actions on Riemannian
  manifolds.
- `hilbert_fifth_problem`: Hilbert's fifth problem, solved by Gleason, Montgomery and Zippin.

## Implementation notes

`AdmitsLieGroupStructure G`, defined in
`FormalConjecturesForMathlib.Geometry.Manifold.LieGroupPresentation`, says that `G` is
continuously isomorphic to a finite-dimensional real-analytic Lie group. Lie groups are Hausdorff
but not assumed second countable: every discrete group is a `0`-dimensional Lie group
(`admitsLieGroupStructure_of_discreteTopology`). This matters for the Hilbert–Smith conjecture,
since uncountable discrete groups act continuously and faithfully on connected manifolds, for
instance `ℝ` with the discrete topology acting on `ℝ` by translations.

The acting group is not assumed Hausdorff: a topological group acting continuously and
faithfully on a Hausdorff space is Hausdorff, because the closure of the identity acts trivially.

The hypotheses on the manifold `X` are written in each theorem. A section variable
`[ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) X]` is included only in a theorem that mentions `n`,
so it would be dropped silently from a statement that mentions only `X`.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%E2%80%93Smith_conjecture)
- [Tao's blog](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/)
- [Pardon 2013] J. Pardon, *The Hilbert–Smith conjecture for three-manifolds*,
  J. Amer. Math. Soc. 26 (2013), 879–899. https://doi.org/10.1090/S0894-0347-2013-00766-3,
  [arXiv:1112.2324](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2324)
- [Myers–Steenrod 1939] S. B. Myers, N. E. Steenrod, *The group of isometries of a Riemannian
  manifold*, Ann. of Math. 40 (1939), 400–416. https://doi.org/10.2307/1968928
- [van den Dries–Goldbring 2015] L. van den Dries, I. Goldbring, *Hilbert's 5th problem*,
  Enseign. Math. 61 (2015), 3–43. https://doi.org/10.4171/LEM/61-1/2-2

statements.name: Hilbert5.hilbert_smith_conjecture
statements.doc:
**Hilbert–Smith conjecture**: every locally compact topological group acting continuously
and faithfully on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold is a Lie group.
statements.statement:
theorem hilbert_smith_conjecture {X : Type*}
    [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [ConnectedSpace X]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) X]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [LocallyCompactSpace G]
    [MulAction G X] [ContinuousSMul G X] [FaithfulSMul G X] :
    AdmitsLieGroupStructure G

statements.name: Hilbert5.hilbert_smith_conjecture.variants.riemannian
statements.doc:
The Hilbert–Smith conjecture holds for actions by isometries of a connected smooth Riemannian
manifold `X`: the isometry group of `X` is a Lie group by the Myers–Steenrod theorem, so `G` has
no small subgroups and is a Lie group by the Gleason–Montgomery–Zippin theorem.

Here `X` carries its Riemannian distance (`IsRiemannianManifold`), so the metric topology of `X`
is its manifold topology.
statements.statement:
theorem hilbert_smith_conjecture.variants.riemannian {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X]
    [ConnectedSpace X] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) X] [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ X]
    [Bundle.RiemannianBundle (fun x : X ↦ TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x)]
    [IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle (𝓡 n) ∞ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
      (fun x : X ↦ TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x)]
    [IsRiemannianManifold (𝓡 n) X]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [LocallyCompactSpace G]
    [MulAction G X] [ContinuousSMul G X] [FaithfulSMul G X]
    (hiso : ∀ g : G, Isometry (g • · : X → X)) :
    AdmitsLieGroupStructure G

statements.name: Hilbert5.hilbert_smith_conjecture.variants.dimension_three
statements.doc:
**Pardon's theorem** (2013): the Hilbert–Smith conjecture holds for connected 3-manifolds,
see [Pardon 2013].
statements.statement:
theorem hilbert_smith_conjecture.variants.dimension_three {X : Type*}
    [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [ConnectedSpace X]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) X]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [LocallyCompactSpace G]
    [MulAction G X] [ContinuousSMul G X] [FaithfulSMul G X] :
    AdmitsLieGroupStructure G

statements.name: Hilbert5.hilbert_smith_padic_formulation
statements.doc:
**p-adic formulation**: the p-adic integers `ℤ_[p]` cannot act continuously and faithfully
on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold. This is equivalent to
`hilbert_smith_conjecture` by the Gleason–Yamabe theorem together with Newman's theorem on
periodic transformations of manifolds.
statements.statement:
theorem hilbert_smith_padic_formulation {X : Type*}
    [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [ConnectedSpace X]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) X]
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [AddAction ℤ_[p] X] [ContinuousVAdd ℤ_[p] X] :
    ¬ FaithfulVAdd ℤ_[p] X

statements.name: Hilbert5.hilbert_fifth_problem
statements.doc:
**Hilbert's fifth problem** (Gleason–Montgomery–Zippin, 1952): every Hausdorff topological
group modeled on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space is continuously isomorphic to a real-analytic
Lie group.

The input `ChartedSpace` supplies only a topological atlas. The compatible analytic atlas and
analytic group operations belong to the output `LieGroupPresentation`.
statements.statement:
theorem hilbert_fifth_problem
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [T2Space G]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) G] :
    Nonempty (LieGroupPresentation G n)

problems.title: Hilbert's 17th problem
problems.doc:
Let $f(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ be a multivariable polynomial with real coefficients that takes only
nonnegative values for all real inputs.
Hilbert's 17th problem asks whether there exist rational functions $g_1, \dots, g_m$ such that
$f = g_1^2 + g_2^2 + \cdots + g_m^2$. Resolved affirmatively by Artin in 1927.
*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%27s_seventeenth_problem)
- Motzkin, "The arithmetic-geometric inequality". In Shisha, Oved (ed.). Inequalities. Academic Press. pp. 205–224.

statements.name: Hilbert17.hilbert_17th_problem
statements.doc:
Hilbert's 17th problem: every non-negative multivariate polynomial is a sum of
squares of rational functions.
statements.statement:
theorem hilbert_17th_problem {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℝ)
    (h : ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, 0 ≤ f.eval x) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → MvRatFunc (Fin n) ℝ), algebraMap _ _ f = ∑ i, (g i) ^ 2

statements.name: Hilbert17.f_nonneg
statements.doc: The Motzkin polynomial is non-negative everywhere.
statements.statement: theorem f_nonneg : ∀ x y : ℝ, 0 ≤ f.eval ![x, y]

statements.name: Hilbert17.f_not_sum_of_squares
statements.doc: The Motzkin polynomial cannot be written as a sum of squares of polynomials.
statements.statement:
theorem f_not_sum_of_squares :
    ¬∃ (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (S : Fin n → MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℝ), f = ∑ i, S i ^ 2

statements.name: Hilbert17.hilbert_17th_problem_poly
statements.doc:
Hilbert's 17th problem for homogeneous polynomials: characterization of dimensions and degrees
where non-negative polynomials are sums of squares of polynomials.
statements.statement:
theorem hilbert_17th_problem_poly {n d : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hd : 0 < d) :
    Hilbert17thProblemHomogenousPoly n d ↔ n = 1 ∨ n = 2 ∨ d = 1 ∨ n = 3 ∧ d = 2

problems.title: Conjecture 1.35(c)
problems.doc:
by A. I. Mal'cev and L. Fuchs

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

statements.name: Kourovka.«1.35c».kourovka_1_35c
statements.doc: Do there exist simple pro-orderable groups?
statements.statement:
theorem kourovka_1_35c :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), IsSimpleGroup G ∧ ProOrderable G

problems.title: Conjecture 1.40
problems.doc:
by Sh. S. Kemkhadze

Is a group a nilgroup if it is the product of two normal nilsubgroups?

Here a nilgroup (Engel group) is a group in which every element is an Engel
element. This is the Engel-group analogue of Fitting's theorem, which
guarantees that the product of two normal nilpotent subgroups is nilpotent.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v40)

statements.name: Kourovka.«1.40».kourovka_1_40
statements.doc:
Is a group a nilgroup if it is the product of two normal nilsubgroups?

Since $H$ and $K$ are normal, the product $HK$ coincides with the join
$H \sqcup K$, so "$G$ is the product of $H$ and $K$" is stated as
$H \sqcup K = G$.
statements.statement:
theorem kourovka_1_40 :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G),
      H.Normal → K.Normal → IsEngelGroup H → IsEngelGroup K → H ⊔ K = ⊤ →
      IsEngelGroup G

problems.title: Conjecture 1.74 (Minimal topological groups)
problems.doc:
by V. P. Platonov

Describe all "minimal topological groups", that is, non-discrete Hausdorff
topological groups all of whose proper closed subgroups are discrete. The
minimal locally compact groups can be described without much effort, but the
problem is probably complicated in the general case.

A Tarski monster group equipped with a non-discrete Hausdorff group topology
is a minimal topological group in this sense, since all its proper subgroups
are finite (hence discrete in any Hausdorff group topology). Such topologizable
Tarski monsters exist by a theorem of Klyachko, Olshanskii and Osin.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v40)
- A. A. Klyachko, A. Yu. Olshanskii, D. V. Osin, *On topologizable and
  non-topologizable groups*, Topology Appl. 160 (2013), 2104–2120,
  [arXiv:1210.7895](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.7895), Theorem 1.4.

statements.name: Kourovka.«1.74».kourovka_1_74
statements.doc:
Describe all minimal topological groups, that is, all non-discrete Hausdorff
topological groups whose proper closed subgroups are all discrete.
statements.statement:
theorem kourovka_1_74 :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G],
      IsMinimalTopologicalGroup G ↔
        kourovka_1_74.answer G

statements.name: Kourovka.«1.74».kourovka_1_74.variants.tarski_monster
statements.doc:
There exists a Tarski monster group that admits a non-discrete Hausdorff group
topology. This follows from Theorem 1.4 of Klyachko, Olshanskii and Osin, which
gives a topologizable Tarski monster of every sufficiently large odd exponent $n$;
taking $n$ to be a prime $p$ makes every non-trivial proper subgroup cyclic of
order $p$. Any such group is a minimal topological group.
statements.statement:
theorem kourovka_1_74.variants.tarski_monster :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : TopologicalSpace G),
      IsTarskiMonster G ∧ IsTopologicalGroup G ∧ T2Space G ∧
      ¬ DiscreteTopology G

problems.title: Conjecture 8.8
problems.doc:
by R. I. Grigorchuk

Both parts of the problem are due to D. V. Anosov.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

statements.name: Kourovka.«8.8».kourovka_8_8a
statements.doc:
Does there exist a non-cyclic finitely-generated group $G$ containing an
element $a$ such that every element of $G$ is conjugate to a power of $a$?

Here a power of $a$ means $a^n$ for some $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

Answered affirmatively by V. S. Guba, Math. USSR-Izv. 29 (1986), 233–277.
statements.statement:
theorem kourovka_8_8a :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), ¬ IsCyclic G ∧ Group.FG G ∧
      ∃ a : G, ∀ g : G, ∃ n : ℤ, IsConj g (a ^ n)

statements.name: Kourovka.«8.8».kourovka_8_8b
statements.doc:
Does there exist a non-cyclic finitely presented group $G$ which contains an
element $a$ such that each element of $G$ is conjugate to some power of $a$?

Here a power of $a$ means $a^n$ for some $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.
statements.statement:
theorem kourovka_8_8b :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), ¬ IsCyclic G ∧ Group.IsFinitelyPresented G ∧
      ∃ a : G, ∀ g : G, ∃ n : ℤ, IsConj g (a ^ n)

problems.title: Conjecture 19.25
problems.doc:
by B. Curtin, G. R. Pourgholi

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v40)

- [vDJMM26] W. van Doorn, E. Judin, P. Monticone and D. Morrison,
  *On Some Problems from the Kourovka Notebook*,
  [arXiv:2607.17477v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17477v1), Theorem 4.1.

statements.name: Kourovka.«19.25».kourovka_19_25
statements.doc:
Let $G$ and $H$ be finite groups of the same order with
$\sum_{g \in G} \phi(|g|) = \sum_{h \in H} \phi(|h|)$,
where $\phi$ is the Euler totient function. Suppose that $G$ is simple. Is
$H$ necessarily simple?

The answer is negative by [vDJMM26, Theorem 4.1]. The groups
$G = \operatorname{PSU}(3,3)$ and $H = C_6 \times S_4 \times (C_7 \rtimes C_6)$
both have order $6048$ and totient sum $23984$, but only $G$ is simple.
In the semidirect product, a generator of $C_6$ acts on $C_7$ by multiplication
by $3$ modulo $7$.
statements.statement:
theorem kourovka_19_25 :
    ¬ ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H] [Fintype G] [Fintype H],
       Fintype.card G = Fintype.card H →
       ∑ g : G, φ (orderOf g) = ∑ h : H, φ (orderOf h) →
       IsSimpleGroup G → IsSimpleGroup H

problems.title: Conjecture 20.76
problems.doc:
by L. Pyber
*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v40)
*Solution:* K. Muliarchyk, [Abelian subgroups of finite 2-groups: counterexamples to
Problems 20.75 and 20.76](https://kourovkanotebookorg.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/kourovka_20_75-20_76_solution.pdf), Proposition 6.1.
!

statements.name: Kourovka.«20.76».kourovka_20_76
statements.doc:
Let $G$ be a finite $p$-group and assume that all abelian normal subgroups of $G$
have order at most $p^k$. Is it true that every abelian subgroup of $G$ has order at most
$p^{2k}$?

The answer is no. Muliarchyk's Proposition 6.1 gives a finite $2$-group of order
$2^{145}$ whose abelian normal subgroups have order at most $2^{42}$, but which
contains an elementary abelian subgroup of order $2^{85} > 2^{84}$.
statements.statement:
theorem kourovka_20_76 :
    ¬ (∀ᵉ (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (hg : IsPGroup p G) (_ : Finite G) (k : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ H: Subgroup G, H.Normal ∧ IsMulCommutative H → Nat.card H ≤ p ^ k),
    (∀ H : Subgroup G, IsMulCommutative H → Nat.card H ≤ p ^ (2 * k)))

problems.title: Conjecture 21.149
problems.doc:
by A. V. Zenkov

The problem is due to V. M. Kopytov and N. Ya. Medvedev. Its original form asked for an order
automorphism of a Dlab group that is not inner (`kourovka_21_149.variants.not_inner`). After that
form was solved, the problem was revised to the stronger question below [vDJMM, Appendix A].
[GYZ] answered the revised question for order-preserving embeddings and rank-one slope groups.

The Notebook does not define Dlab groups. We follow [Dl] and [GYZ]: the Dlab groups with slope
group $H$ are four groups of order automorphisms of $I = [0, 1]$ and two groups of order
automorphisms of the extended real line $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$. All six are viewed as subgroups
of the order automorphisms of $\mathbb{R}$ (`IsDlabGroup`).

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 21.149. The original
  wording is in [arXiv:1401.0300v43](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v43).
- [GYZ] T. Gong, Y. Yang and M. R. Zeng, *An order automorphism of a Dlab group not induced by
  conjugation*, [arXiv:2609.18630](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18630).
- [vDJMM] W. van Doorn, E. Judin, P. Monticone and D. Morrison,
  [arXiv:2607.17477](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17477).
- [Dl] V. Dlab, *On a family of simple ordered groups*, J. Austral. Math. Soc. 8 (1968), 591–608.

statements.name: Kourovka.«21.149».kourovka_21_149
statements.doc:
Are there order automorphisms of Dlab groups that are not induced by conjugation by elements of
a (possibly bigger) Dlab group?

A Dlab group $G$ (on $I$ or on $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$) carries Dlab's order, and $\alpha$ is an
automorphism of $G$ that preserves it. The automorphism $\alpha$ is induced by conjugation in a
bigger Dlab group $A$ if $G$ embeds into $A$ by an injective homomorphism $e$ and some $u \in A$
satisfies $e(\alpha(f)) = u^{-1} e(f) u$ for all $f \in G$. This includes the inclusions and the
order-preserving embeddings of [GYZ]. The slope groups are arbitrary.
statements.statement:
theorem kourovka_21_149 :
    ∃ (K : Subgroup NNRealˣ) (G : Subgroup (ℝ ≃o ℝ)), IsDlabGroup K G ∧
      ∃ α : G ≃* G, (∀ f g : G, DlabLt (α f) (α g) ↔ DlabLt f g) ∧
        ¬ ∃ (H : Subgroup NNRealˣ) (A : Subgroup (ℝ ≃o ℝ)), IsDlabGroup H A ∧
          ∃ e : G →* A, Function.Injective e ∧ ∃ u : A, ∀ f : G, e (α f) = u⁻¹ * e f * u

statements.name: Kourovka.«21.149».kourovka_21_149.variants.not_inner
statements.doc:
The original form of the problem: are there order automorphisms of Dlab groups that are not inner
automorphisms?

This was answered affirmatively by the formal reasoning agent Aristotle (Harmonic), as reported
in [vDJMM, Appendix A].
statements.statement:
theorem kourovka_21_149.variants.not_inner :
    ∃ (K : Subgroup NNRealˣ) (G : Subgroup (ℝ ≃o ℝ)), IsDlabGroup K G ∧
      ∃ α : G ≃* G, (∀ f g : G, DlabLt (α f) (α g) ↔ DlabLt f g) ∧
        ¬ ∃ u : G, ∀ f : G, α f = u⁻¹ * f * u

problems.title: Lam--Litt conjecture
problems.doc:
A conjecture of Lam and Litt on algebraic solutions of algebraic ODEs.

Let $g \in \mathbb{Q}(z, y_0, \dots, y_{n-1})$ be a rational function in
$n + 1$ variables. Let $f$ be a power series over $\mathbb{Q}$ such that
$f^{(n)}(z) = g(z, f(z), f'(z), \dots, f^{(n-1)}(z))$.
Also, assume that $g(0, f(0), f'(0), \dots, f^{(n-1)}(0))$ is defined.
Then the following are equivalent:

1) $f$ is algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}[z]$.
2) There exists $N$ such that for all $n$, the $n$-th coefficient of $f$ is in $\mathbb{Z}[1/N]$.
3) There exists an integer-valued function $\omega$ on the set of primes with
$\lim_{p \to \infty} \omega(p) / p = \infty$ such that, for each prime $p$,
the rational numbers $a_0, a_1, \dots, a_{\omega(p)}$ are in $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$.

The implication 1) => 2) is due to Eisenstein, and 2) => 3) is trivial.

*References:*
- [Litt's problem 1](https://www.problemsilike.com/1)
- Yeuk Hay Joshua Lam, Daniel Litt, "Algebraicity and integrality of solutions to differential equations",
  [arxiv/2501.13175](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13175)
- Gotthold Eisenstein. "Über eine allgemeine Eigenschaft der Reihen-Entwicklungen aller algebraischen Funktionen",
  Bericht der Königl. Preuss. Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Berlin, 1852

TODO:
- Lam-Litt conjecture implies Grothendieck p-curvature conjecture.
- Examples in Remark 1.1.3 and 1.1.5 on the conditions of the conjecture.

statements.name: LamLitt.lam_litt.variants.eisenstein
statements.doc:
Eisenstein's theorem (1852): an algebraic power series over $\mathbb{Q}[z]$ has bounded
denominators, i.e., there exists $N$ such that all coefficients lie in $\mathbb{Z}[1/N]$.
statements.statement:
theorem lam_litt.variants.eisenstein (f : PowerSeries ℚ) (hAlg : IsAlgebraic (Polynomial ℚ) f) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, IsCoeffIntegralAdjointInvNat f N

statements.name: LamLitt.lam_litt.variants.integrality_implies_omega_integrality
statements.doc: Textbook implication: integrality (2) trivially implies ω(p)-integrality (3).
statements.statement:
theorem lam_litt.variants.integrality_implies_omega_integrality
    (f : PowerSeries ℚ) (N : ℕ) (hN : IsCoeffIntegralAdjointInvNat f N) :
    ∃ ω : Nat.Primes → ℤ, omegaSuperlinear ω ∧ omegaIntegral ω (PowerSeries.coeff · f)

statements.name: LamLitt.lam_litt.variants.omega_integrality_implies_algebraicity
statements.doc:
3) implies 2): if the coefficients of $f$ satisfy the $\omega$-integrality condition for some superlinear $\omega$,
then there exists $N$ such that for all $n$, the $n$-th coefficient of $f$ is in $\mathbb{Z}[1/N]$.
statements.statement:
theorem lam_litt.variants.omega_integrality_implies_algebraicity {n : ℕ} (f : PowerSeries ℚ)
    (g : MvRatFunc (Fin (n + 1)) ℚ) (hODE : IsSolutionOfAlgebraicODE n f g)
    (ω : Nat.Primes → ℤ) (hω : omegaSuperlinear ω ∧ omegaIntegral ω (PowerSeries.coeff · f)) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, IsCoeffIntegralAdjointInvNat f N

statements.name: LamLitt.lam_litt.variants.integrality_implies_algebraicity
statements.doc:
2) implies 1): if the coefficients of $f$ are in $\mathbb{Z}[1/N]$ for some $N$, then $f$ is algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}[z]$.
Also the version of conjecture of Litt's problem 1 on his website.
statements.statement:
theorem lam_litt.variants.integrality_implies_algebraicity {n : ℕ} (f : PowerSeries ℚ)
    (g : MvRatFunc (Fin (n + 1)) ℚ) (hODE : IsSolutionOfAlgebraicODE n f g)
    (N : ℕ) (hN : IsCoeffIntegralAdjointInvNat f N) :
    IsAlgebraic (Polynomial ℚ) f

problems.title: Mathoverflow 1973

problems.title: Optimal monotone families for the discrete isoperimetric inequality
problems.doc:
*References:*
- [mathoverflow/10799](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/10799)
  asked by user [*Gil Kalai*](https://mathoverflow.net/users/1532/gil-kalai)
- [Optimal Monotone Families for the Discrete Isoperimetric Inequality](https://gilkalai.wordpress.com/ai/optimal-monotone-families-for-the-discrete-isoperimetric-inequality/)
  by *Gil Kalai* (2026), a Polymath project with AI agents
- [An Isoperimetric Inequality for the Hamming Cube and Integrality Gaps in Bounded-Degree
  Graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0603218) by *Jeff Kahn* and *Gil Kalai* (2006)
- [A Proof of the Kahn–Kalai Conjecture](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.17207) by *Jinyoung Park*
  and *Huy Tuan Pham* (2022)

statements.name: Mathoverflow10799.mathoverflow_10799
statements.doc:
Problem: For every monotone increasing family $F$, given an interval $[s,t]$ of real numbers so
that $t/s > 1000 \log n$ we have some $p$ in the interval $[s,t]$ so that $F$ is optimal with
respect to $\mu_p$.

This was a "missing lemma" in the work of Kahn and Kalai on threshold behavior of monotone
properties. The related [Kahn–Kalai conjecture](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0603218) was
[settled by Park and Pham](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.17207).

**This conjecture is false** without the additional assumption $\mu_t(F) = 1/2$.
A counterexample was found by Shlomo Perles (April 7, 2026).
statements.statement:
theorem mathoverflow_10799 :
    ¬ ∀ (n : ℕ) (_ : 2 ≤ n)
    (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (_ : IsMonotoneIncreasing F)
    (s t : ℝ) (_ : 0 < s) (_ : s ≤ t) (_ : t < 1)
    (_ : t / s > 1000 * Real.log n),
    ∃ p, s ≤ p ∧ p ≤ t ∧ IsOptimal p F

statements.name: Mathoverflow10799.mathoverflow_10799.variants.kahn_kalai_conjecture_7
statements.doc:
Conjecture 7 from Kahn–Kalai 2006: a fixed-`1000` variant of the original
conjecture, with the additional assumption that $t$ is the critical probability for $F$,
namely $\mu_t(F) = 1/2$.

This variant is false by a counterexample due to Sahar Diskin and Uri Kreitner;
see the [MathOverflow discussion](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/10799/optimal-monotone-families-for-the-discrete-isoperimetric-inequality)
and the [counterexample note](https://gilkalai.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/dual_tribes_more_readable.pdf).
Their construction was adapted to this exact Formal Conjectures statement and
[formalized in Lean](https://github.com/KitaKen1/kahn-kalai-conjecture-7-counterexample)
by Kenta Kitamura (KitaKen1).
statements.statement:
theorem mathoverflow_10799.variants.kahn_kalai_conjecture_7 :
    ¬ ∀ (n : ℕ) (_ : 2 ≤ n)
    (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (_ : IsMonotoneIncreasing F)
    (s t : ℝ) (_ : 0 < s) (_ : s ≤ t) (_ : t < 1)
    (_ : μFamily t F = 1 / 2)
    (_ : t / s > 1000 * Real.log n),
    ∃ p, s ≤ p ∧ p ≤ t ∧ IsOptimal p F

statements.name: Mathoverflow10799.mathoverflow_10799.variants.weak_kahn_kalai
statements.doc:
Weaker version proven by Kahn–Kalai (2006): for every fixed $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a constant
$C = C_\varepsilon$ such that for every monotone increasing family $F$ with critical probability
$t$, i.e. $\mu_t(F) = 1/2$, there is some $p \in [n^{-\varepsilon} t, t]$ for which $F$ is
$(C \log(1/p), p)$-optimal.
statements.statement:
theorem mathoverflow_10799.variants.weak_kahn_kalai :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (n : ℕ) (_ : 2 ≤ n)
    (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (_ : IsMonotoneIncreasing F)
    (t : ℝ) (_ : 0 < t) (_ : t < 1) (_ : μFamily t F = 1 / 2),
    ∃ p, (n : ℝ) ^ (-ε) * t ≤ p ∧ p ≤ t ∧ IsOptimalWith C p F

statements.name: Mathoverflow10799.discrete_isoperimetric_inequality
statements.doc:
Now a famous isoperimetric relation asserts that
(IR) $I^p(F) \ge \frac{1}{p} \mu_p(F) \log_p \mu_p(F)$
This relation holds for monotone increasing families $F$ and $0 < p < 1$.
It is especially famous and simple when
$p=1/2$ and $\mu_p(F)=1/2$. In this case, it says that given a set of half the vertices of the
discrete cube $2^X$, the number of edges between $F$ and its complement is at least $2^{n-1}$.

*Note on translation:* We use `Real.logb p m` to represent the logarithm base $p$ directly.
The factor of $p$ in the denominator (equivalent to $1/p$ in front) is consistent with the
definition of `IsOptimal` used in the counterexample proof.
statements.statement:
theorem discrete_isoperimetric_inequality (n : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p) (hp' : p < 1)
    (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hF : IsMonotoneIncreasing F) :
    let m := μFamily p F
    edgeBoundary n p F ≥ m * Real.logb p m / p

statements.name: Mathoverflow31809.mathoverflow_31809
statements.doc:
Does there exist a category that is pretriangulated but not triangulated?

Yes. Theorem 1.2 of [CLLZ26] twists the triangulated structure on the category of finitely
generated projective modules over the preprojective algebra of type $A_5$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$.

    [Pretriangulated C], IsTriangulated C)

problems.title: Mathoverflow 34145
problems.doc:
Can the unit square be covered by $1/k$-by-$1/(k+1)$ rectangles (across $1 \le k$ natural)?

I am deliberately not requiring that the rotations can only be $0^\circ, 90^\circ, 180^\circ, \text{ or } 270^\circ$.

Because of indexing, since `n : ℕ` starts at 0, we change the side lengths to $1 / (n + 1)$ and
$1 / (n + 2)$, so that the first rectangle is $1/1$ by $1/2$, the second is $1/2$ by $1/3$, etc.

*Reference:* [mathoverflow/34145](https://mathoverflow.net/q/34145)
asked by user [*Kaveh*](https://mathoverflow.net/users/7507/kaveh)

statements.name: Mathoverflow34145.rectangles_cover_unit_square
statements.doc: Can a unit square be covered by rectangles of width `1 / (n + 1)` and height `1 / (n + 2)`?
statements.statement:
theorem rectangles_cover_unit_square :
    ∃ c : Configuration, ∀ p ∈ unitSquare, ∃ n, p ∈ (c.rect n).toSet

statements.name: Mathoverflow34145.rectangles_pack_unit_square
statements.doc:
Equivalently, can a unit square be packed with rectangles of width `1 / (n + 1)` and height
`1 / (n + 2)`?

theorem rectangles_pack_unit_square :
    ∃ c : Configuration, (∀ n, (c.rect n).toSet ⊆ unitSquare) ∧ c.IsPacking

statements.name: Mathoverflow34145.rectangles_pack_square_133_div_132
statements.doc:
It is known that packing the rectangles into a square of side length `133/132` is possible.

Reference: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0097316594901163
statements.statement:
theorem rectangles_pack_square_133_div_132 :
    (∃ c : Configuration,
      (∀ n, (c.rect n).toSet ⊆ Rectangle.toSet ⟨133/132, 133/132, (0, 0), 0⟩) ∧
      c.IsPacking)

statements.name: Mathoverflow34145.rectangles_pack_square_501_div_500
statements.doc:

Reference: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167506008706009

problems.title: Mathoverflow 75792
problems.doc:
Various questions about integer complexity, which is the minimum number of `1`s needed to express a natural number using addition, multiplication, and parentheses.

Let `‖n‖` denote the integer complexity of `n > 0`.
* It is known that `‖3^n‖ = 3n` for `n > 0`.
* Is it true that `‖2^n‖ = 2n` for `n > 0`?
* The corresponding conjecture for `5` is false, because
  `5^6 = 15625 = 1 + 2^3 * 3^2 * (1 + 2^3 * 3^3)`!

We have chosen to formalise this using an inductive type.

*References:*
 - [mathoverflow/75792](https://mathoverflow.net/a/75792) by user [Harry Altman](https://mathoverflow.net/users/5583)
 - http://arxiv.org/abs/1203.6462 by Jānis Iraids, Kaspars Balodis, Juris Čerņenoks, Mārtiņš Opmanis, Rihards Opmanis, Kārlis Podnieks
 - http://arxiv.org/abs/1207.4841 by Harry Altman, Joshua Zelinsky
 - https://oeis.org/A5245 : Mahler-Popken complexity.

statements.name: Mathoverflow75792.complexity_five_pow
statements.doc: Is `5n` the complexity of `5^n` for `0 < n`? Answer: No.
statements.statement: theorem complexity_five_pow : ¬ ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → complexity (5 ^ n) = 5 * n

statements.name: Mathoverflow75792.complexity_three_pow
statements.doc:
Is `3n` the complexity of `3^n` for `0 < n`? Answer: Yes, by John Selfridge.

Reference: https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.4841
statements.statement: theorem complexity_three_pow : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → complexity (3 ^ n) = 3 * n

statements.name: Mathoverflow75792.complexity_two_pow
statements.doc: Is `2n` the complexity of `2^n` for `0 < n`?
statements.statement: theorem complexity_two_pow : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → complexity (2 ^ n) = 2 * n

problems.title: Mathoverflow 339137
problems.doc:
Why do polynomials with coefficients 0,1
 like to have only factors with 0,1
 coefficients?

*Reference:* [mathoverflow/339137](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/339137)
asked by user [*Sil*](https://mathoverflow.net/users/136794/sil)

statements.name: Mathoverflow339137.mathoverflow_339137
statements.doc:
Let $P(x), Q(x) ∈ ℝ[x]$ be two monic polynomials with non-negative coefficients.
If $R(x) = P(x)Q(x)$ is a $0,1$ polynomial (coefficients only from $\{0,1\}$), then $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$
are also $0, 1$ polynomials.
statements.statement:
theorem mathoverflow_339137 (P Q R : ℝ[X]) (hP: P.Monic) (hQ : Q.Monic)
    (hp : ∀ c ∈ P.coeffs, 0 ≤ c) (hq : ∀ c ∈ Q.coeffs, 0 ≤ c)
    (h : R = P * Q) (hR : IsZeroOne R) :
    IsZeroOne P ∧ IsZeroOne Q

statements.name: Mathoverflow339137.mathoverflow_339137_probabilistic
statements.doc:
Green's Open Problem 28 is the probabilistic reformulation of Mathoverflow 339137.

Suppose that $X, Y$ are two finitely-supported independent random variables taking integer values,
and such that $X + Y$ is uniformly distributed on its range. Are $X$ and $Y$ themselves uniformly
distributed on their ranges?

Mathematically, this equivalence is established via Probability Generating Functions (PGFs),
shifting the support to $\mathbb{N}$, and appropriately scaling the coefficients.
statements.statement:
theorem mathoverflow_339137_probabilistic :
    type_of% Mathoverflow339137.mathoverflow_339137 ↔ type_of% Green28.green_28

problems.title: Mathoverflow 347178
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [mathoverflow/347178](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/347178)
asked by user [*Biagio Ricceri*](https://mathoverflow.net/users/149235/biagio-ricceri)

statements.name: Mathoverflow347178.mathoverflow_347178
statements.doc:
Let $f : \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,  n \geq 2$ be a $C^1$ function. Is it true that
$$\sup_{x \in \mathbb R^n}f(x) = \sup_{x\in \mathbb R^n} f(x+\nabla f(x))$$?

Answer: No. A counterexample in $\mathbb R^2$ is recorded in the linked formal proof.
statements.statement:
theorem mathoverflow_347178 :
    ¬ ∀ᵉ (n ≥ 2) (f : ℝ^n → ℝ) (_ : ContDiff ℝ 1 f),
        (BddAbove (range f) ↔ BddAbove (range (fun x ↦ f (x + gradient f x)))) ∧
        (⨆ x, (f x : EReal)) = ⨆ x, (f (x + gradient f x) : EReal)

statements.name: Mathoverflow347178.mathoverflow_347178.variants.bounded_iff
statements.doc:
Let $f : \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,  n \geq 2$ be a $C^1$ function. Is the boundedness of
$\sup_{x \in \mathbb R^n}f(x)$ and $\sup_{x\in \mathbb R^n} f(x+\nabla f(x))$ equivalent?

Answer: No. The same counterexample is recorded in the linked formal proof.
statements.statement:
theorem mathoverflow_347178.variants.bounded_iff :
    ¬ ∀ᵉ (n ≥ 2) (f : ℝ^n → ℝ) (_ : ContDiff ℝ 1 f),
        BddAbove (range f) ↔ BddAbove (range fun x ↦ f (x + gradient f x))

statements.name: Mathoverflow347178.mathoverflow_347178.variants.bounded_only
statements.doc:
Let $f : \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,  n \geq 2$ be a $C^1$ function. Does the equality
$$\sup_{x \in \mathbb R^n}f(x) = \sup_{x\in \mathbb R^n} f(x+\nabla f(x))$$
hold when both suprema are finite?

Answer: Yes. Upper boundedness of $f$ alone suffices.
statements.statement:
theorem mathoverflow_347178.variants.bounded_only :
    ∀ᵉ (n ≥ 2) (f : ℝ^n → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f)
        (h : BddAbove (range f)) (h' : BddAbove (range (fun x ↦ f (x + gradient f x)))),
        (⨆ x, f x) = ⨆ x, f (x + gradient f x)

problems.title: Are prime numbers among sums of prime numbers distributed as $\frac n{2\ln(n)}$?
problems.doc:
*Reference:*

[mathoverflow.net/questions/434111](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/434111/are-prime-numbers-among-sums-of-prime-numbers-distributed-as-frac-n2-lnn)

[Me18] Meštrović, R., *Curious Conjectures on the Distribution of Primes
Among the Sums of the First `2n` Primes*, [arXiv:1804.04198](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.04198)
(2018), Conjecture 3.3.

statements.name: MathOverflow434111.restricted_prime_number_theorem
statements.doc:
The conjecture claims that $\pi_n\sim\frac n{2\ln(n)}$.

In other words, primes are distributed among the much sparser sequence $(S_n)_n$
with essentially the same density as in the positive integers, up to a factor of $2$.

[MathOverflow 434111](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/434111/are-prime-numbers-among-sums-of-prime-numbers-distributed-as-frac-n2-lnn).

[Me18] Meštrović, R., *Curious Conjectures on the Distribution of Primes
Among the Sums of the First `2n` Primes*, [arXiv:1804.04198](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.04198)
(2018).
statements.statement:
theorem restricted_prime_number_theorem :
    ((fun n : ℕ => (piRestricted n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) / (2 * Real.log n)))

statements.name: MathOverflow434111.restricted_prime_number_theorem.variants.even_subsequence
statements.doc:
Meštrović's original formulation [Me18, Conjecture 3.3]: the sequence of sums of the
first $2m$ primes satisfies the Restricted Prime Number Theorem, $\pi(m, (S_{2m})) \sim \frac{m}{\ln m}$.
statements.statement:
theorem restricted_prime_number_theorem.variants.even_subsequence :
    ((fun m : ℕ => (((Finset.Icc 1 m).filter (fun k => Nat.Prime (S (2 * k)))).card : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
      (fun m : ℕ => (m : ℝ) / Real.log m))

problems.title: Mathoverflow 486451
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [mathoverflow/486451](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/486451)
asked by user [*Junyan Xu*](https://mathoverflow.net/users/3332/junyan-xu)

statements.name: Mathoverflow486451.exists_semiring_unique_left_maximal_not_unique_right_maximal
statements.doc: There exists a semiring with a unique left maximal ideal but more than one right maximal ideals.
statements.statement:
theorem exists_semiring_unique_left_maximal_not_unique_right_maximal :
    ∃ (R : Type) (_ : Semiring R), (∃! I : Ideal R, I.IsMaximal) ∧
      ∃ I J : Ideal Rᵐᵒᵖ, I.IsMaximal ∧ J.IsMaximal ∧ I ≠ J

statements.name: Mathoverflow486451.exists_semiring_unique_left_right_maximal_ne
statements.doc:
There exists a semiring with a unique left maximal ideal and a unique right maximal ideal
which are not the same as sets.

This has been shown by Goran Žužić and Moritz Firsching using an experimental pipeline:
An example is the monoid algebra of the monoid of maps from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathbb{N}$
over $\mathbb{N}$.
statements.statement:
theorem exists_semiring_unique_left_right_maximal_ne :
    ∃ (R : Type) (_ : Semiring R) (hI : ∃! I : Ideal R, I.IsMaximal)
      (hJ : ∃! J : Ideal Rᵐᵒᵖ, J.IsMaximal),
        (hI.choose : Set R) ≠ MulOpposite.op ⁻¹' hJ.choose

problems.title: Mathoverflow 507128
problems.doc:
*Reference:* [mathoverflow/507128](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/507128/embeddability-order-on-picard-groups)
asked by user [*Junyan Xu*](https://mathoverflow.net/users/3332/junyan-xu)

statements.name: Mathoverflow507128.exists_isFractionRing_self_ideal_ne_top_invertible
statements.doc:
There exists a proper ideal `I` in a (commutative) total ring `R` of fractions that is an invertible module.
If `I ⊊ R` is such an example, `I` must have infinite order in the Picard group.
Moreover, `R` must not be Noetherian (otherwise it must be semi-local and therefore have trivial Picard group).

The linked formal proof gives the following explicit construction.

Let `D = ℂ[X, Y] / (Y² - X³)` be the coordinate ring of the cuspidal cubic.
Let `P = (X - 1, Y - 1)`, which is an invertible ideal.
Let `M` be the direct sum of the evaluation fibres at cusp parameters `r ≠ 1`.
Form the idealization `R = D ⋉ M`.
The desired ideal is the range of the multiplication map `R ⊗[D] P → R`.
statements.statement:
theorem exists_isFractionRing_self_ideal_ne_top_invertible :
    ∃ (R : Type) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : IsFractionRing R R) (I : Ideal R),
      I ≠ ⊤ ∧ Module.Invertible R I

problems.title: MathOverflow 508539
problems.doc:
Edge-vertex inequality $EV \geq 4^{n-1}$.

*References:*
- [MathOverflow 508539](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/508539), asked by
  [Paata Ivanisvili](https://mathoverflow.net/users/50901/paata-ivanisvili).
- [DIRX26] Durcik, P., Ivanisvili, P., Roos, J., and Xie, X.,
  *Sharp isoperimetric inequalities on the Hamming cube II: The critical exponent* (2026),
  [arXiv:2602.20462](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20462), inequality (1.2).

statements.name: Mathoverflow508539.mathoverflow_508539
statements.doc:
For any set $A \subset \{0,1\}^n$ of half size $2^{n-1}$, we have $EV \geq 4^{n-1}$,
where $E$ denotes the edge boundary (the number of edges between $A$ and its complement), and
$V$ denotes the inner vertex boundary (the number of points in $A$ having a neighbor outside $A$).

This is the half-size case of [DIRX26, (1.2)]. The hypothesis $n > 0$ is necessary: in dimension
zero the cardinality hypothesis allows the whole cube, whose boundaries are empty.
statements.statement:
theorem mathoverflow_508539 {n : ℕ} (A : Finset (Fin n → Bool))
    (hA : #A = 2 ^ (n - 1)) (hn : 0 < n) :
    4 ^ (n - 1) ≤ #((hypercube n).edgeBoundary A) *
      #((hypercube n).innerVertexBoundary A)

problems.title: Existence And Smoothness Of The Navier–Stokes Equation
problems.doc:
This file formalizes the Clay Mathematics Institute millennium problem concerning
the existence and smoothness of solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations in three
spatial dimensions. While the definitions are generalized to arbitrary dimension n,
the millennium problem specifically concerns the case n = 3.

## References
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navier%E2%80%93Stokes_existence_and_smoothness)
- [Clay Mathematics Institute](https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/navierstokes.pdf)
- [OpenAI, *Finite Time Blowup for Navier–Stokes*](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/32d9f210-8b73-45e0-91bc-82a30aef8a9a/navier-stokes.pdf)

## Main Theorems (Clay Millennium Problem for n = 3)

The Clay Millennium Problem asks for a proof of one of the following four statements:

- `navier_stokes_existence_and_smoothness_R3`: (A) Global existence on ℝ³
- `navier_stokes_existence_and_smoothness_periodic`: (B) Global existence on ℝ³/ℤ³
- `navier_stokes_breakdown_R3`: (C) Existence of breakdown scenario on ℝ³
- `navier_stokes_breakdown_periodic`: (D) Existence of breakdown scenario on ℝ³/ℤ³

In September 2026, an internal OpenAI model proved alternatives (C) and (D) by constructing
solutions that develop finite-time singularities under smooth forcing.

## Variable conventions

Fefferman writes the velocity as $u(x,t)$, the initial velocity as $u^\circ(x)$, the
pressure as $p(x,t)$, the force as $f(x,t)$, and the viscosity as $\nu$. In Lean,
`u₀ : ℝ^n → ℝ^n` denotes the initial velocity, while `v : ℝ^n → ℝ → ℝ^n`
denotes the solution velocity. The curried order `v x t`, `p x t`, and `f x t`
keeps the source convention that position comes before time.

Since the Clay statement gives equation (1) on the closed time half-line $t \ge 0$,
the time derivative is encoded with `derivWithin` relative to `Set.Ici 0`. The Clay
PDF also includes errata; in particular, we include spatial 1-periodicity of the
pressure in the periodic case. The sign correction to the weak-solution identity in
the errata is not represented here, since this file formalizes the four prize
alternatives rather than the later weak-solution discussion.

statements.name: NavierStokes.navier_stokes_existence_and_smoothness_R3
statements.doc: (A) Existence and smoothness of (unforced) Navier–Stokes solutions on ℝ³.
statements.statement:
theorem navier_stokes_existence_and_smoothness_R3 (nu : ℝ) (hnu : nu > 0)
    (u₀ : ℝ³ → ℝ³) (hu₀ : InitialVelocityConditionDecay u₀) :
    ∃ v p, NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessRn nu u₀ (f := 0) v p

statements.name: NavierStokes.navier_stokes_existence_and_smoothness_periodic
statements.doc: (B) Existence and smoothness of (unforced) Navier–Stokes solutions in ℝ³/ℤ³.
statements.statement:
theorem navier_stokes_existence_and_smoothness_periodic (nu : ℝ) (hnu : nu > 0)
    (u₀ : ℝ³ → ℝ³) (hu₀ : InitialVelocityConditionPeriodic u₀) :
    ∃ v p, NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessPeriodic nu u₀ (f := 0) v p

statements.name: NavierStokes.navier_stokes_breakdown_R3
statements.doc:
(C) Breakdown of (forced) Navier–Stokes solutions on ℝ³.

This was proven by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026.
statements.statement:
theorem navier_stokes_breakdown_R3 (nu : ℝ) (hnu : nu > 0) :
    ∃ (u₀ : ℝ³ → ℝ³) (f : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³),
    InitialVelocityConditionDecay u₀ ∧ ForceConditionDecay f ∧
    ¬ (∃ v p, NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessRn nu u₀ f v p)

statements.name: NavierStokes.navier_stokes_breakdown_periodic
statements.doc:
(D) Breakdown of (forced) Navier–Stokes solutions on ℝ³/ℤ³.

This was proven by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026.
statements.statement:
theorem navier_stokes_breakdown_periodic (nu : ℝ) (hnu : nu > 0) :
    ∃ (u₀ : ℝ³ → ℝ³) (f : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³),
    InitialVelocityConditionPeriodic u₀ ∧ ForceConditionPeriodic f ∧
    ¬ (∃ v p, NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessPeriodic nu u₀ f v p)

problems.doc:
References:

statements.name: PoincareConjecture.poincare_conjecture.variants.smooth_known_cases

The smooth version of the Poincaré conjecture is known to hold in dimensions
